basis: Deficient adrenal cortical hormone production defines it. Autoimmunity is only one cause; hypotension and electrolyte changes do not establish other organ damage.
Hereditary isolated hair loss; autoimmune mechanisms do not apply across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Inherited platelet dysfunction causes bleeding; additional organ disease is subtype-specific.
Partial loss of colour vision is an ocular functional disorder.
Inherited complement immunodeficiency; associated autoimmune disorders and infections are separately diagnosed diseases.
Nocturnal loss of urinary continence is a bladder-function disorder; the psychiatric ancestor does not override its urinary phenotype.
Hereditary infantile liver failure; extrahepatic manifestations vary across subtypes.
Inherited focal epilepsy producing sleep-related hypermotor seizures; movement manifestations are neurologic.
Inherited susceptibility to febrile seizures is a neurologic disorder; fever does not establish infection.
Inherited phosphate dysregulation with defective bone mineralization and rickets; renal phosphate wasting does not itself establish destructive kidney disease.
Congenital thyroid hormone deficiency; neurological injury depends on delayed treatment and is not universal across this umbrella.
Isolated pituitary GH deficiency; short stature, delayed bone age and reduced muscle mass do not establish additional destructive organ disease.
Microcephaly and osteodysplastic skeletal growth abnormalities define the umbrella; vascular complications are subtype-dependent.
Isolated developmental hypoplasia of the eye; syndromic extraocular disease is excluded by definition.
Respiratory-chain energy metabolism defect; encephalopathy and skeletal myopathy are common across the group, approximately >=30%; other organ involvement varies by subtype.
Craniosynostosis and polysyndactyly define skeletal malformations; other organ disease varies across subtypes.
Renal phosphate wasting with hypophosphatemia, nephrolithiasis and osteoporosis defines this disease group.
Pelvic organ prolapse includes structural descent of the bladder/urethra and rectum, as well as reproductive organs; urinary and intestinal labels reflect prolapse itself, not symptoms alone.

decisions.renal: primary: bladder/urethral prolapse is a core anatomical form of pelvic organ prolapse, rather than merely associated urinary symptoms.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: rectal descent into the vaginal wall is a core anatomical form; the prolapsed bowel itself establishes the axis.

basis: Congenital cerebral cortical malformation with abnormal gyration and cognitive dysfunction.
Premature activation of sexual maturation is an endocrine disorder involving gonadal hormones or their central regulation.
Mitochondrial myopathy causes progressive extraocular muscle weakness and ptosis; additional neurologic and systemic damage varies across subtypes.
Inherited microcytic anemia with intrinsic iron-handling defects and iron overload; common hepatic or cardiac functional injury is not established across the umbrella.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this inherited anemia group includes intrinsic disorders of iron transport/utilization; the metabolic defect is part of the disease, rather than treatment-induced overload.

basis: Inherited erythrocyte disorder causing nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
External-ear, mandibular condyle and oral malformations define the syndrome. Sleep apnea is separately diagnosed; hearing loss and developmental delay occur in fewer than 30%.

decisions.pulmonary: none: sleep apnea (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed consequence of craniofacial obstruction; respiratory distress alone does not establish direct airway or lung damage.

basis: Congenital clefting of the nose, which belongs to the pulmonary axis; associated hypertelorism is a minority finding.
Camptodactyly defines this congenital contracture syndrome umbrella; additional organ damage is not established across its subtypes.
Cerebellar parenchymal disease; the listed subtypes are cerebellar and spinocerebellar neurologic disorders.
Structural malformation of the cerebellum and brainstem; associated hydrocephalus is also neurologic.
Umbrella of hereditary reticulate skin pigmentation disorders; no common extracutaneous damage is established.
Umbrella for inherited structural congenital heart defects.
Skeletal dysplasia with valve disease, airway obstruction and thickened stiff skin, each 30-79%; conductive hearing impairment (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: characteristic thickened, stiff skin is frequent (30-79%); retained with severe valve and airway disease under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing impairment qualifies at 30-79% but is omitted at the cap, prioritizing characteristic skin disease and severe valve/airway disease.

basis: Inherited axonal degeneration directly affects peripheral nerves and sometimes the CNS; weakness and gait impairment are neurologic consequences.
Neurologic injury is common in predominant GA I and severe GA II, supporting an overall rate above ~30%; GA III is usually benign and muscle involvement varies.

decisions.neurologic: involved: striatal injury or metabolic encephalopathy is common across the major symptomatic forms, exceeding approximately 30%; subtype variability limits certainty.

basis: Immunodeficiency defines ICF; developmental impairment/hydrocephalus, cytopenias and malabsorption each occur in 30-79%; recurrent infections do not establish chronic lung damage.
Follicular hyperkeratosis and scarring alopecia define the disease; explicit polyamine-metabolism ancestry supports a metabolic axis. Corneal dystrophy and blepharitis occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the explicit parent 'disorder of polyamine metabolism' supports classification as a metabolic disorder, beyond the cutaneous phenotype.

basis: Hereditary cerebral white-matter disease with megalencephaly; no common extra-neurologic organ damage is established.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia; Pyle disease ancestry confirms bone involvement.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; damaging eye abnormalities and muscular dystrophy annotated 80-99%. Tumor predisposition does not establish affected tumor organs.
The represented subtypes involve multiple intestinal or gastric polyps; subsequent cancer risk does not add another organ.
Telomere disorder defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or bone marrow failure; other organ damage is not established across the umbrella.
Congenital fusion of interphalangeal joints; extra-skeletal manifestations are not shared across the umbrella.
Defined as thiamine metabolism/transport disorders comprising hereditary encephalopathies; anemia and deafness are subtype-specific.
Congenital malposition of the great arteries arising from the heart.
Triglyceride storage causes myopathy in >50% and hepatic steatosis with liver injury in roughly >=30% overall; ichthyosis is concentrated in type 1.
audit_reason: Add hepatic involvement: intrinsic hepatic steatosis with liver injury is common across neutral triglyceride storage diseases and meets the approximately 30% threshold; subtype variability alone does not justify exclusion.

basis: Premature metopic suture fusion produces a triangular skull; a cranial bone development disorder.
Developmental abnormality of the hip joint, acetabulum and femoral head relationship.
Marrow failure defines this umbrella; additional syndromic organ abnormalities are not established across most patients.
Cortical myoclonus and epilepsy are neurological; involuntary muscle movements do not establish skeletal muscle disease.
Acute postinfectious brain dysfunction; an infectious trigger alone does not establish direct CNS infection or an immune-mediated disease across this umbrella.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: postinfectious triggering is established, but direct infection or a shared immune-mediated pathogenesis is not established across this umbrella.

basis: Umbrella of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by progressive cerebral dysfunction.
Isolated developmental eye disorder defined by microphthalmia and ocular coloboma; no extraocular disease is established.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; muscular, cerebral and retinal abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Type B dystroglycanopathies typically combine congenital muscular dystrophy with intellectual impairment; major eye malformations characterize type A.
Type C dystroglycanopathies primarily cause limb-girdle muscular dystrophy; cardiac, respiratory and CNS damage are not consistently common across subtypes.
Serine biosynthesis disorder with major brain malformations and ichthyosis; muscle hypoplasia, atrophy and contractures occur in 30-79%. Other malformations omitted under cap.
Microcephaly and chorioretinal disease define this inherited neurodevelopmental syndrome; inflammatory ancestry alone does not establish immune causation.
Congenital neuromuscular-junction dysfunction with defining structural abnormalities in skeletal myofibers; this is not autoimmune myasthenia.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: tubular aggregates are defining skeletal-myofiber pathology in this specific syndrome, rather than weakness alone.

basis: Inherited glucose transport disorder causing cerebral energy deficiency and epileptic encephalopathy.
Ventricular electrical dysfunction directly impairs cardiac pumping; secondary hypoxic injury is not intrinsic organ involvement.
Abnormal glycogen metabolism produces polyglucosan accumulation and skeletal myopathy. Cardiomyopathy and immunodeficiency vary by subtype and are not established in most.
Defective cortisol regeneration causes adrenal hyperandrogenism; supplied HPO annotations report hypertension in 30-79%, supporting cardiovascular involvement.
Defining gingival fibromatosis and nail/terminal-phalangeal hypoplasia; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%. Hepatosplenomegaly occurs in only 5-29%.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and glucose dysregulation define disease; scoliosis and osteoporosis each reported in 1/3 patients.
Prenatal motor neuron disease with congenital fractures and contractures; both nervous and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome.
Inherited thiopurine metabolism disorder; myelosuppression following thiopurine exposure is a treatment effect and is excluded.
Striatal neurodegeneration causes bradykinesia, rigidity and dysarthria; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Inherited calcium dysregulation; direct renal calcium deposition is common in symptomatic infants and can cause persistent renal injury in ≥30% over the course.
Umbrella of hereditary infantile multisystem autoimmune diseases; no additional organ is established as commonly damaged across the group.
Inherited manganese metabolic disorder defined by dystonia; hepatic disease and polycythemia are subtype-dependent and not established across most of the umbrella.
Gonococcal infection of the seminal vesicle; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Defined by acquired disruption of carbohydrate metabolism; no specific organ damage established across this umbrella.
Ehrlichia directly infects monocytes/macrophages; acute hepatic inflammation and hepatocellular injury occur in approximately 70-90%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic inflammation with hepatocellular injury and aminotransferase elevation occurs in approximately 70-90% during infection.

basis: Umbrella for disordered mineral metabolism; skeletal and other organ damage varies across subtypes.
R. africae directly infects vascular endothelium, causing vasculitis; necrotic skin eschars occur in ~80-90% and represent tissue destruction rather than transient rash.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection causes dermal vasculitis ([histology](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/12/9/05-1540_article)).
decisions.dermatologic: involved: necrotic eschars occur in nearly all patients ([CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/ticks/media/pdfs/2025/03/tickborne-diseases-manual-508.pdf)).

basis: Spotted-fever rickettsial infection directly targets vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash adds no dermatologic axis.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are the defining tissue pathology of spotted-fever rickettsiosis.

basis: Endotheliotropic rickettsial infection directly causes small-vessel vasculitis. Transient exanthem and minority severe organ complications do not support additional axes.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are the disease's direct tissue pathology, rather than a later cardiovascular risk.

basis: Spotted-fever rickettsiosis directly infects vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not establish skin damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are defining tissue pathology of spotted-fever rickettsiosis.

basis: Rickettsia honei infection targets vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not establish additional dermatologic damage.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular to primary: spotted-fever rickettsiae infect vascular endothelium and cause small-vessel vasculitis, a defining disease process. A transient rash alone would not support dermatologic involvement.

basis: Rickettsial endothelial infection causes systemic small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash and eschar do not independently justify dermatologic involvement.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular to primary: Rickettsia japonica infects vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis, a defining disease process distinct from its transient rash.

basis: Rickettsial endothelial infection causes vasculitis; the defining necrotic inoculation eschar establishes skin injury. Transient rash and headache add no axes.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular to primary: spotted-fever rickettsiae directly infect vascular endothelium and cause vasculitis, including in the defining cutaneous eschar.

basis: Anthrax infection of the oropharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis. Intestinal involvement is not required.
Fungal infection directly involving the lungs.
Invasive Aspergillus infection damages lung tissue; extrapulmonary dissemination does not consistently meet the 30% threshold.
The supplied definition specifies cardiomyopathy caused by selenium deficiency together with Coxsackievirus; the mineral deficiency supports the metabolic axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: selenium deficiency is a defining nutritional mineral disorder underlying the cardiomyopathy.

basis: Dermatophyte infection of beard hair and associated skin.
Dermatophyte infection directly involving the hair surface.
Dermatophyte infection directly invades hair shafts.
Trichophyton concentricum infection of the skin.
Dengue infection with hemorrhagic abnormalities and defining vascular leakage causing circulatory shock.
Intestinal secretion and absorption dysfunction defines the diarrhea; electrolyte disturbances are consequences rather than a defining metabolic disorder.
Intestinal water absorption is impaired by poorly absorbed luminal solutes; electrolyte loss does not establish a separate metabolic disorder.
Bowel motility dysfunction causing diarrhea.
Defined by intestinal mucosal inflammation; inflammation alone does not establish infection, autoimmunity or another immune-mediated etiology.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: the umbrella establishes intestinal inflammation, without establishing an infectious or immune-mediated cause across the group.

basis: Superficial fungal infection directly occupies hair shafts.
Fungal infection directly involves skin, hair or nails.
Fungal infection directly occupies skin and subcutaneous tissue.
Systemic fungal infection; affected organs vary across subtypes, without sufficient evidence that any particular organ meets the group-wide threshold.
Acute intestinal dysfunction; infectious causation is not established for the entire concept.
Asymptomatic dengue infection; no organ damage established.
Usually infectious inflammation of the pharyngeal tonsil in the upper respiratory tract.
Fungal infection of the external auditory canal.
Usually infectious inflammation of the larynx and trachea; infectious ancestry supports the mechanism axis.
Aspiration directly injures and inflames the lungs; the supplied concept includes chemical injury from gastric contents without established infection.
Aspergillus infection involving the lung.
Disease of the lower respiratory tract, including lungs, bronchi, trachea and pleura.
Tuberculous infection of the fallopian tube; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Defined here as Kunjin viral encephalitis with infection and inflammation of the brain.
Powassan viral infection causes encephalitis, directly affecting the central nervous system.
Arenavirus infection with defining hemorrhagic manifestations involving hemostasis; headache and myalgia do not establish organ damage.
Seoul hantavirus infection causes the defining renal and hemorrhagic syndrome, including characteristic thrombocytopenia and hemostatic abnormalities.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the hemorrhagic syndrome with characteristic thrombocytopenia and disordered hemostasis is part of the disease definition.

basis: Puumala infection causes the defining renal and thrombocytopenic hemorrhagic syndrome; thrombocytopenia occurs in roughly 70-90%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: thrombocytopenia and hemorrhagic dysfunction are defining features of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome; thrombocytopenia occurs in roughly 70-90%.

basis: Epstein-Barr virus infection causing liver inflammation; the skin ancestry does not establish damaging cutaneous disease.
Parasitic echinococcal infection producing predominantly hepatic polycystic lesions; common direct damage elsewhere is not established.
Naegleria fowleri directly infects and destroys brain and meningeal tissue.
Direct amoebic infection and destructive inflammation of the brain; other sites are not consistently involved.
Philophthalmus eye-fluke infection occupies and inflames the conjunctival tissues.
Larval Taenia tissue infection; CNS cysts directly injure neural tissue in roughly half of reported human cases. Ocular and subcutaneous sites are less frequent.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS coenuri cause direct neural injury in roughly half of reported human cases, exceeding the approximate 30% threshold.

basis: Mesocestoides tapeworm infection usually occupies the intestine; extraintestinal disease is uncommon in humans.
Thorny-headed worms infect the intestine and attach to its mucosa.
Larval migration causes destructive CNS inflammation in most recognized symptomatic cases (>30%); ocular and visceral injury are less consistently documented.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neural larva migrans causes lasting brain injury in most recognized symptomatic cases, exceeding 30%; subclinical infections create uncertainty.

basis: Dioctophyme renale infection characteristically occupies and destroys renal tissue; ectopic infections do not establish another common organ axis.
Thelazia nematodes occupy the conjunctival sac and lacrimal system, causing ocular infection.
Parasitic infestation of the ocular surface or internal eye by fly larvae.
Basidiobolus infection predominantly affects skin and subcutaneous tissue; gastrointestinal and systemic forms are variable subtypes.
Conidiobolus fungal infection typically involves nasal mucosa and adjacent facial subcutaneous tissue, causing chronic rhinofacial disease.
Direct skin lesions ~60-80%, lung involvement ~30-60%, and marrow infiltration with cytopenias >30%; hepatic involvement (~30-50%) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: disseminated infection commonly infiltrates marrow with impaired blood-cell production (>30%); isolated anemia alone would not suffice.
decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic involvement (~30-50%) can qualify, but skin, pulmonary and marrow injury receive priority under the four-axis cap.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: direct pulmonary infection with infiltrates occurs in approximately 30-60%; this exceeds the threshold independently of respiratory symptoms alone.

basis: Trichosporon fungal infection; superficial and disseminated forms affect different sites, with no additional organ established as common across the umbrella.
Human disease is predominantly rhinosporidiosis; persistent nasal/nasopharyngeal lesions affect about 70-90%, directly occupying upper airways.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: human Ichthyosporea disease is predominantly rhinosporidiosis, with nasal/nasopharyngeal lesions in about 70-90%.

basis: Primary systemic fungal infection; direct pulmonary infection occurs in most patients across the major endemic mycoses (>30%). Other dissemination sites vary.
Ocular disorder causing unequal perceived image size or shape between the eyes.
Viral hemorrhagic fever with thrombocytopenia and bleeding; hepatocellular injury occurs commonly (>30%). Neurologic complications affect a minority.
Phosphate electrolyte disorder; chronic skeletal or other organ damage is not established across this broad concept.
Umbrella category of primary bacterial infections; no single anatomical organ is consistently affected across the group.
Infection by normally commensal bacteria; the anatomical site varies across this umbrella.
Umbrella for opportunistic bacterial infections; no single anatomical organ is consistently affected across the group.
Bacterial infection involving lymph nodes; lymphadenitis does not establish blood-cell or marrow disease.
Systemic Francisella infection with bacteremia; circulating bacteria and constitutional symptoms do not establish blood-cell or other organ damage.
Mycobacterium ulcerans infection directly causes necrotizing skin ulcers.
Elevated phosphate is a mineral/electrolyte metabolism disorder; blood concentration does not make it a blood-cell disease.
Rickettsia typhi infects vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not establish skin damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are intrinsic disease pathology; vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Rickettsia helvetica infection; no specific organ injury is established as common or diagnostically required.
Neorickettsia sennetsu directly infects monocytes and causes a mononucleosis-like illness; common additional organ damage is not established.

decisions.haematologic: primary: direct infection of circulating monocytes establishes blood-cell involvement, rather than a nonspecific blood-count response.

basis: Hepatitis, osteochondritis/periostitis and infection-related anemia each affect roughly 30-60% of symptomatic early cases. Transient rash excluded; persistent CNS injury less consistently common.

decisions.haematologic: involved: infection-related hemolysis and marrow dysfunction cause anemia in roughly 30-60% of symptomatic early cases.

basis: Multiple nodules arise within the thyroid gland.
Syphilitic meningoencephalitis directly destroys cerebral cortical parenchyma.
Syphilitic infection causes inflammation and thrombosis of cerebral or spinal arteries with nervous system injury.
HHV-6/7 infection; the brief, self-limited exanthem is a transient rash without lasting skin damage. Neurologic injury is uncommon.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the characteristic rash is transient and does not establish lasting cutaneous damage.

basis: Variola major causes destructive pustular skin infection, commonly leaving scars; the skin lesions are more than a transient exanthem.
Poliovirus damages spinal motor neurons, causing paralysis; denervation does not establish a separate primary skeletal muscle disorder.
Poliovirus damages bulbar and spinal motor neurons; paralysis and respiratory weakness arise from neurologic injury.
Poliovirus infection destroys central motor neurons; paralysis reflects neuronal injury rather than primary muscle or lung disease.
Alphavirus infection; rash and arthralgia are usually transient and do not establish lasting skin or joint damage.
Barmah Forest alphavirus infection; common arthralgia and transient rash do not establish lasting joint or skin damage in at least 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent arthralgia does not establish damaging arthritis; persistent objective joint damage in at least 30% is not established.

basis: Ross River virus infection causes inflammatory polyarthritis in approximately 80-90% of symptomatic patients, often prolonged. Transient rash does not qualify for dermatologic involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: inflammatory polyarthritis affects approximately 80-90% of symptomatic patients; the supplied concept is defined by viral infection, with arthritis a common organ manifestation.

basis: Oropouche viral infection; fever, rash and arthralgia do not establish lasting organ damage, and neurologic complications are uncommon.
Hantavirus infection defined by renal injury and a hemorrhagic syndrome with thrombocytopenia; additional organ damage is not established as common.
Inherited methionine catabolic defects; hepatic and neurologic damage vary by subtype, with insufficient evidence of qualifying damage across most of the umbrella.
Muscular dystrophy and joint contractures define disease; esotropia is annotated in 30-79%. Respiratory failure reflects diaphragmatic weakness rather than direct pulmonary disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure occurs in 30-79%, but the demonstrated lesion is respiratory skeletal-muscle weakness, without intrinsic lung or airway damage.

basis: Developmental cleft of the lip/palate affects oral structures and the facial skeleton; associated middle-ear disease is separately diagnosed.
Congenital vertebral and rib malformations. Restricted ventilation from thoracic deformity does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Tertiary syphilitic infection with destructive gummas; skin, bone and liver sites vary, without an established organ-specific frequency of at least 30%.
Congenital glaucoma directly damages ocular structures and the optic nerve, causing progressive visual loss.
Taenia tapeworm infection occupies the intestine; extraintestinal cysticercosis is a distinct disease.
Tuberculosis outside the lung; affected anatomical sites vary across subtypes, so no single additional organ applies across the group.
Tuberculous infection predominantly involves bowel and abdominal peritoneal tissues. Hepatic, splenic, and renal sites represent subsets, without evidence each affects most patients.
In situ carcinoma originates in oral mucosa, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the pharynx, which maps to the pulmonary axis under these rules.
Carcinoma in situ arising in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Carcinoma in situ occupies bile duct epithelium; intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Carcinoma in situ originates in bronchial epithelium.
Malignant neoplasm arising in the respiratory system; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Malignancy of steroid-producing Leydig endocrine cells of the gonad; metastatic sites are not established as commonly involved.
Malignant tumor of testicular or ovarian Sertoli cells; reproductive origin without specified endocrine dysfunction or a consistent metastatic organ.
Malignant sex cord-stromal tumor with Sertoli-Leydig differentiation arises from the gonadal endocrine compartment; hormone excess is not required to establish endocrine tumor origin.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: Sertoli-Leydig differentiation establishes gonadal endocrine tissue origin; absence of documented hormone excess does not make an endocrine-origin tumor purely reproductive.

basis: Carcinoma originates in paranasal sinus epithelium, within the upper respiratory tract; bone carcinoma ancestry does not establish bone origin.
Infiltrating urothelial carcinoma originating in the renal pelvis.
Benign tumor occupies the respiratory tract or pleura; all supplied anatomical subtypes fall within the pulmonary axis.
Umbrella of benign reproductive organ tumors; endocrine tumors listed among children do not establish endocrine involvement across most of the group.
Benign neoplasm originating in the urinary bladder, included in the renal axis.
Benign digestive tract neoplasm umbrella; hepatobiliary origins apply to particular subtypes rather than most patients.
Tumors predominantly originate in digestive tract mucosa; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease or a metabolic disorder.
Anemia defined by small, hypochromic red blood cells.
Severe skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and structural airway disease cause direct respiratory impairment in >30% across the group.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia and laryngotracheobronchomalacia commonly cause respiratory failure (>30% across types), beyond thoracic restriction alone.

basis: Prenatal alcohol exposure causes defining CNS dysfunction and neurodevelopmental impairment; growth deficiency and facial features do not establish additional organ damage.
The supplied definition includes cognitive developmental injury from prenatal alcohol exposure; structural defects in other organs vary across this broad concept.
Cerebral motor pathway injury causes spasticity; increased muscle tone alone does not establish direct skeletal muscle disease.
Cerebellar injury causes the defining motor coordination disorder.
Cerebral motor disorder producing combined spasticity and involuntary movements; altered muscle tone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Site-variable carcinoma umbrella predominantly arising in lung. Neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease; metastases vary.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the anal canal.
Malignant tumor originates in the pleura.
Prenatal alcohol injury causes defining cognitive and neurodevelopmental deficits; other structural malformations are not common across the spectrum.
Classified as bacterial infection of the fetal membranes; the obstetric site has no anatomical axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Infection-associated inflammation of the umbilical cord; the supplied definition establishes leukocyte migration, without establishing vascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: leukocyte migration from umbilical vessels does not itself establish vasculitis or vascular damage.

basis: Epilepsy syndrome beginning in adolescence or adulthood; defined by abnormal cerebral electrical activity.
Inherited serine biosynthesis defect; neurologic dysfunction, including developmental impairment, microcephaly and seizures, occurs in most affected patients.
X-linked inheritance umbrella spans unrelated diseases; no organ or listed mechanism axis applies across most members.
audit_reason: No organ changes: this inheritance umbrella has no shared organ axis. Raise confidence from low to high because its meaning is explicit; low is reserved for uncertainty about the concept's identity.

basis: Inheritance-pattern umbrella spanning unrelated diseases; no organ or qualifying mechanism axis applies across the group.
Mature T/NK-cell hematopoietic malignancy and lymphoma; skin, liver and other extranodal sites vary across subtypes.
B-cell lymphoma involving marrow, lymph nodes and spleen, commonly with an IgM paraprotein; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis.
Ataxia results from pathology of the cerebellum, its connections or proprioceptive sensory pathways.
Disorder of systemic acid-base balance; no specific causative organ disease is implied.
Midfacial skeletal dysplasia classified as an osteochondrodysplasia.
Multiple liver cysts define the disease; multiple renal cysts occur in 30-79% and represent direct structural renal involvement, even when filtration remains preserved.

decisions.renal: involved: HPO reports multiple renal cysts in 30-79%; cystic occupation is direct structural involvement and does not require established renal failure.

basis: Neoplasm of autonomic paraganglionic neuroendocrine tissue; hormone secretion and secondary vascular effects vary across subtypes.
Progressive immune-mediated CNS demyelination; direct optic nerve involvement with visual dysfunction occurs in roughly half over the MS course. Neurogenic bladder is secondary.
Immune-mediated CNS demyelination with progressive neurologic disability.
Immune-mediated CNS demyelination includes direct optic nerve injury in roughly half over the MS course; frequency in this progressive subtype is less certain.

decisions.ocular: involved: optic nerve demyelination is an integral MS lesion, with clinical optic neuritis in roughly 50% over the course; subtype-specific frequency is uncertain.

basis: Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with shortened QT interval and arrhythmias; syncope does not establish neurologic damage.
Inherited degeneration of retinal cone photoreceptors causes central visual and color vision loss.
Inborn creatine metabolism disorders defined by cerebral creatine deficiency and neurodevelopmental impairment; myopathy is not common across the group.
Glioblastoma is a primary malignant CNS tumor.
Molecular subtype of a malignant glial tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Molecular subtype of glioblastoma, a primary central nervous system tumor.
Molecular subtype of glioblastoma, a malignant CNS tumor.
Nutritional metabolic deficiency; dermatitis/alopecia are common (>30%) in overt disease. Direct neurologic injury in >=30% of nutritional cases is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: neuropsychiatric complaints do not establish direct neurologic injury; neuropathy or other qualifying dysfunction lacks an established >=30% frequency in nutritional deficiency.

basis: Defined by disease of ocular adnexa, including eyelids, conjunctiva and lacrimal apparatus.

Defining neuropathic bladder dysfunction and abnormal facial motor control support urinary and neural disease. Recurrent UTIs are separate infections; constipation alone does not establish gut damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the defining neurogenic bladder and characteristic facial motor dysfunction reflect intrinsic urofacial neuropathy, rather than merely secondary urinary injury.

basis: Disorder of atrioventricular cardiac conduction.
Delayed atrioventricular conduction is a cardiac conduction disorder.
Intermittent failure of cardiac atrioventricular electrical conduction.
Complete failure of atrioventricular electrical conduction is a cardiac conduction disorder.
Disorder of the heart's sinoatrial node and cardiac conduction system.
Disease of the endocardium; infection and other mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Disease of the tricuspid heart valve; the umbrella does not establish an immune mechanism.
Defined by structural or functional disease of arteries; downstream organ injury is not uniform across this umbrella.
Disease of the pericardium; the umbrella includes inflammatory and noninflammatory causes.
An isolated neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Focal dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal contractions do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Neurologic movement disorder affecting multiple noncontiguous body regions; dystonic contractions alone do not establish skeletal muscle damage.
Neurologic movement disorder affecting adjacent body regions; contractions alone do not establish primary muscle damage.
Focal dystonia of pelvic floor skeletal muscle causes impaired defecation; no direct intestinal tissue damage is established.
Focal neurologic movement disorder; abnormal neck contractions and soreness do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Focal neurologic movement disorder causing involuntary hand contractions, without primary skeletal muscle damage.
Focal dystonia affecting control of eye movement; ocular tissue damage is not intrinsic.
Focal neurologic dystonia directly disrupts laryngeal function; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Focal movement disorder affecting control of head, facial and neck muscles; muscle contraction does not establish primary muscle damage.
Neurologic movement disorder causing dystonia of the ipsilateral arm and leg; no primary skeletal muscle disease.
Adenoma arising in the periampullary duodenal mucosa.
Defined by structural and functional brain injury associated with diabetes; the underlying diabetes is a separate disease.
Scarring and sclerosis of kidney glomeruli; local glomerular vessels do not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Impaired limb perfusion defines a vascular disorder; muscle necrosis, neuropathy and skin loss are not established across the concept.
Chronic venous dysfunction; edema alone is not skin damage. Persistent damaging skin changes are not established at ≥30% across the umbrella.
Glomerulosclerosis and tubulointerstitial fibrosis directly damage the kidneys.
Psychiatric behavioral disorder without intrinsic organ damage.
Inflammation and bleeding of the urinary bladder; neither infection nor immune mediation is established for the entire concept.
Suppurative uterine infection with myometrial inflammation; the uterine location has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Immune-mediated arteritis causes ischemic injury of the anterior optic nerve and visual loss.
Ischemic injury of the optic nerve, which belongs to the ocular axis; systemic vascular disease is not intrinsic to this diagnosis.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in the tongue, an oral gastrointestinal structure.
Most villous adenomas originate in gastrointestinal mucosa; urinary and vaginal sites are uncommon variants of this umbrella concept.
Localized adenocarcinoma occupies lung epithelium without stromal, vascular or pleural invasion.
Myopathy, Paget bone disease and frontotemporal degeneration define the syndrome. Cardiac, hepatic and ocular damage are occasional, below 30%.
Intellectual disability defines this umbrella; additional organ abnormalities vary across its constituent syndromes.
Isolated intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder.
Alpha-synuclein accumulation causes neuronal and glial degeneration; proteostasis ancestry alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Odontogenic epithelial tumor arising in tooth-forming tissues and occupying bone; dental origin and bone location support both axes.
Definition specifies squamous cell carcinoma involving bone; a sinus subtype does not establish airway involvement across the group.
Chondrosarcoma arising in bone.
Benign cartilaginous tumour involving a phalangeal bone.
Medulloblastoma involving the brainstem.
Chordoma originates in the sacrum; adjacent nerve or pelvic-organ impairment is not established as common by this record.
Glial tumor involving the corpus callosum of the brain.
Ependymal tumor arising in the parietal lobe of the brain.
Carcinoma originating in major or minor salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Villous adenoma arising in the glandular epithelium of the cecal mucosa.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in the colon.
Adenoma arising in rectal epithelium.
Carcinoma arising in the bronchus.
Combined small cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma arising in the lung.

Substance-induced psychotic disorder without a defined organ-damaging disease.
Malignant neoplasm arising in the tongue, an oral cavity organ.
Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm; the lymphoma mechanism also warrants infectious_immune.
Disease of veins; additional organ involvement depends on the specific subtype and is not shared across the umbrella.
Cancer of the postcricoid hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Carcinoma in situ of the lip, classified here as an oral cavity site.
Malignant tumor of the aryepiglottic fold; both laryngeal and hypopharyngeal sites belong to the pulmonary axis.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphocyte neoplasm and qualifies for the lymphoma mechanism axis; no consistent extranodal site is specified.
Neonatal intestinal mucosal injury and necrosis; multifactorial pathogenesis does not establish a primary infection or immune-mediated disease.
Alcohol directly injures and inflames gastric mucosa; alcohol exposure does not establish hepatic or other organ disease.
Carcinoma confined to cutaneous epithelium.
Cancer originates in the tonsillar pillar of the oropharynx, which belongs to the upper-airway axis.
Clonal myeloid proliferation in marrow, peripheral blood and spleen; these sites belong to the haematologic axis.
Monocytic leukemia affects blood and marrow; additional organ infiltration is not established above the threshold.
Malignant neoplasm of buccal mucosa; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Pressure-induced skin and underlying soft-tissue necrosis; deep muscle or bone injury is not universal.
Cerebrovascular disease causes ischemic brain injury and persistent cognitive decline; both cerebral vessels and brain define the condition.
Anaerobic bacterial infection of lung parenchyma.
Malignant neuroendocrine tumor of the carotid-body paraganglion. The adjacent carotid artery is not its tissue of origin; metastatic sites are unspecified.
Variola infection causes destructive cutaneous pustules, commonly leaving permanent scars.
Bacterial infection directly involving lung parenchyma.
Myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm of blood and marrow, principally involving neutrophils.
Rubella virus infection; the characteristic rash is transient. Congenital rubella organ damage does not apply to most cases.
Disseminated choroidal and retinal inflammation encompasses infectious and immune-mediated uveitis; disseminated describes ocular distribution, not systemic spread.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: chorioretinitis encompasses infectious and immune-mediated inflammation of the choroid and retina, supporting the mechanism axis.

basis: Carcinoma confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Carcinoma in situ is located in the eye.
Carcinoma in situ arising in lung or bronchial epithelium.
Carcinoma confined to the tracheal mucosal epithelium.
Intestinal fluke infection occupies and injures intestinal mucosa; ectopic organ infection is occasional.
Carcinoma in situ arising in the colonic epithelium.
Parasitic worm infection, predominantly occupying the intestine; other organ sites depend on subtype.
Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm and meets the lymphoma mechanism rule; common extranodal organ damage is not established.
Intestinal fluke infection directly occupies intestinal mucosa; ectopic organ infection is occasional.
Malignant tumour arising in the sublingual salivary gland.
Liver flukes invade hepatic tissue and inhabit bile ducts and gallbladder; ectopic organ involvement is uncommon.
Malignancy occupying salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis; lymphoma is only a minority histologic subtype.
Autoimmune lupus umbrella includes skin-limited and systemic disease; arthritis and cytopenia rates from systemic lupus cannot establish common involvement across all forms.

decisions.haematologic: none: cytopenias occur in roughly half of systemic lupus cases, but are not established in at least 30% across the umbrella including cutaneous lupus.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: inflammatory arthritis is common in systemic and drug-induced lupus, but is not a defining or established common feature across the umbrella including skin-limited lupus.

basis: Carcinoma in situ of the penis is a reproductive-organ neoplasm outside the axes.
Fasciolopsis buski infection directly occupies and injures the small intestine.
Malignancy of the lower lip, an oral cavity site.
Inflammation damages the choroid and adjacent retina; usually infectious, with immune-mediated causes also represented.
Mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction directly causes both nervous system and skeletal muscle disease; additional organ involvement varies by subtype.
Superficial fungal infection confined to the skin.
Dermatophyte infection directly affects keratinized skin, hair and nails.
Disease confined to vaginal mucosa; reproductive organs have no axis.
Autoimmune blood disorder defined by platelet depletion; ancestors and children establish its immune mechanism.
Specific neurodevelopmental impairment of learning and information processing falls within the neurologic axis.
Malignancy of the retromolar oral cavity; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Plantar fascial fibromatosis; persistent loss of skin elasticity is annotated 80-99%, with subcutaneous nodules in 30-79%. Peripheral neuropathy occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent skin tethering/loss of elasticity (80-99%) supports direct cutaneous impairment; subcutaneous nodules occur in 30-79%.

basis: Cancer of the tonsillar ring in the pharynx, included in the pulmonary axis. The concept does not specify lymphoma.
Corneal stromal dystrophy directly impairs the cornea and vision.
Established diabetic retinal microvascular injury; this concept does not establish damage to other organs affected by diabetes.
Umbrella of inherited mineral-processing disorders; specific organ damage varies across subtypes.
Cancer of the tonsillar fossa in the oropharynx; pharyngeal structures belong to the pulmonary axis.
Renal cystic disease defines ADPKD. Hepatic cysts occur in 80-99% but usually preserve function; damaging liver involvement is a minority. Hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic cysts occur in 80-99%, but clinically damaging liver involvement is below ~30%; cyst presence alone does not establish impaired function.

basis: Diagnostic syndrome combines liver disease, intrapulmonary vascular dilatation and impaired pulmonary oxygenation; brain complications are uncommon.
Liver-origin lymphoma occupies hepatic tissue, is a malignant lymphoid blood-cell disorder, and receives the required lymphoma mechanism axis.

decisions.haematologic: primary: lymphoma is a neoplasm of lymphoid blood cells even when its primary anatomical site is extranodal liver.

basis: Carcinoma in situ originates in the larynx, included in the airway axis.
Epithelial hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis of the esophagus; associated carcinoma is a separate minority complication.
In situ epithelial carcinoma originates in the intestine.
Lymphoid malignancy arises predominantly in the gastrointestinal tract; lymphoma warrants both hematologic and immune axes.
Malignancy occupies the parotid salivary gland; lymphoma is only one possible histology.
Benign lesion confined to the endometrium or endocervix; reproductive organs have no axis.
Hyperkeratosis confined to uterine cervical mucosa; reproductive organs have no axis.
Carcinoma confined to urinary bladder urothelium; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Solitary fibrous tumor originating in the liver; the definition establishes hepatic origin despite the endocrine ancestor.
Autoimmune discoid lupus causes inflammatory, potentially scarring skin disease of the eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the anal canal.
Carcinoma in situ confined to esophageal epithelium, without nodal or distant metastasis.
Tumour located in the cerebral occipital lobe; visual processing deficits do not imply eye damage.
Carcinoma in situ confined to the uterus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Herpes simplex infection directly causes vesicular skin lesions; eyelid involvement is not universal.
Cancer arising in lower gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defined by skeletal muscle volume loss and atrophy. Peripheral nerve disease causes only a subset and is not required across this umbrella.
Carcinoma in situ located in the liver.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the gastric epithelium.
Hepatic vascular disease defined by abnormal blood-filled spaces in liver tissue.
Xerotic dermatitis of eyelid skin; eyelids are explicitly included in the ocular axis.
Malignant neoplasm of the hard palate, an oral cavity site.
Variola minor causes a characteristic destructive vesiculopustular skin eruption, potentially leaving scars.
Benign smooth muscle tumour arising in liver; definition provides no endocrine involvement despite an endocrine parent.
Malignancy originates in the submandibular salivary gland, included in the gastrointestinal axis.
Carcinoma in situ located in rectal mucosa.
Fibroblastic neoplasm arising in the liver; accompanying inflammatory cells do not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Cancer originates in the oral vestibule; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Retinal vascular leakage injures the macula; the underlying diabetes is a separate disease, not an additional organ affected by macular edema.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: macular edema is a localized retinal complication; underlying diabetes and metabolic ancestry do not make it an intrinsic metabolic disorder.

basis: Disordered motor function of the esophageal body or sphincters.
Developmental communication disorder affecting speech function; no common direct damage to the mouth or larynx is established across this umbrella.
Defined by sleep-related failure of central respiratory drive and ventilation; cardiovascular sequelae are risks or separate diseases.
Carcinoma in situ located in the kidney or renal pelvis.
Malignant tumor occupying the pyriform sinus of the hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Umbrella of inherited amino acid metabolic disorders; additional organ damage varies substantially by subtype.
Neurologic injury common; ocular damage ~70-90% in classic disease; thromboembolism approaches 50% by adulthood untreated. Skeletal disease omitted at cap; frequencies vary by subtype.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular for common intrinsic thromboembolic injury over the untreated course. Remove musculoskeletal under the four-axis cap, prioritizing severe vascular injury while retaining common neurologic and ocular damage.

basis: Inborn ammonia-detoxification defect; hyperammonemic encephalopathy and neurodevelopmental injury affect >=30% over the disease course.
Tyrosine metabolism disorder umbrella including transient neonatal cases; hepatic/renal injury chiefly type I and ocular/skin disease type II are not common across the whole group.
Disordered homocysteine metabolism; thrombosis and cardiovascular events are increased risks and separately diagnosed conditions.
Glaucoma-spectrum ocular condition; borderline status does not establish damage outside the eye.
Persistent erection affects penile erectile tissue, outside these axes; altered local blood flow does not by itself establish a disease of vessels.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: the affected organ is penile erectile tissue; vascular ancestry and abnormal local flow alone do not establish intrinsic arterial or venous disease.

basis: Direct disease of extraocular skeletal muscles, affecting the ocular adnexa and muscle function; immune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
Congenital structural defect of the upper lip, part of the mouth.
Lip disease falls within the mouth and oral structures axis.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the myocardium.
Developmental impairment of language is a neurodevelopmental disorder; it does not imply structural oral or airway disease.
Disorder of the orbit and ocular adnexa.
Nerve sheath neoplasm arising in and occupying the heart; both cardiac site and peripheral nerve origin are defining.
Mechanical restriction of ocular movement causes strabismus.
Structural prolapse of the rectum through the anus.
Intestinal Moniezia tapeworm infection; the supplied definition concerns ruminants rather than a human disease.
Neoplasm originates in the nasal cavity, an upper airway site. Lymphoma is only one subtype.
Chronic inflammation of ethmoid sinus mucosa; infection or immune mediation is not universal.
Localized loss of visual field defines ocular visual dysfunction; an underlying neurologic cause cannot be assumed.
Purely psychiatric paraphilic disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
Structural abnormal passage involving the urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
Pelvic venous reflux or obstruction and varicosities define the disorder, despite its uterine classification.
Dissection directly damages the carotid arterial wall; ischemic stroke is a separately diagnosed complication.
Localized bursitis affecting the fibular collateral ligament region.
Nonallergic asthma causes chronic immune-mediated airway inflammation and obstruction; absence of allergy does not exclude immune mediation.
Severe exacerbation of immune-mediated inflammatory airway disease with persistent bronchial obstruction.
Seminal-vesicle inflammation affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; the umbrella definition does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Corneal and conjunctival inflammation; the umbrella includes infectious, immune and nonimmune causes.
Immune-mediated orbital inflammation involving ocular adnexa, often extraocular muscles or lacrimal glands.
Anterior displacement of the eye within the orbit defines this ocular disorder.
Recurrent hypertensive anterior uveitis defines the ocular disorder. CMV-associated cases form a subset; a disease-wide infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not established.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: ocular inflammation alone does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease; CMV association applies to a subset rather than the syndrome universally.

basis: Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body; anterior uveitis is usually immune-mediated.
Gonococcal infection causing inflammation of the iris and ciliary body.
Lens-induced inflammation of the iris and ciliary body involves an immune response to lens material.
Acute inflammation of the larynx, most commonly caused by viral infection; vocal strain is another cause.
Usually infectious inflammation of the epididymis and testes; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis.
Usually infectious inflammation of the epididymis; reproductive anatomy has no axis, and associated urinary infection is a separate condition.
Acute infarction directly damages the posterior myocardium.
Acute ischemic necrosis of heart muscle.
Vasopressin and water-balance disorder; intrinsic renal resistance characterizes the nephrogenic subtype rather than most patients across the umbrella.
Asthma affects the bronchial airways and is explicitly mediated by type I hypersensitivity.
Inflammation of the eyelid margin; this umbrella includes infectious and noninfectious causes, without a universal immune mechanism.
Persistent inflammation of the bile ducts; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not specified.
Benign papilloma arising in the uterine cervix; reproductive organs have no axis.
Benign squamous papilloma of the uterine cervix; reproductive organs have no axis.
Biliary inflammation is hepatic; bacterial infection accounts for most clinical cholangitis, with immune-mediated forms also represented.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most clinical cases are bacterial infections; immune-mediated forms also qualify, although inflammation alone would not establish this axis.

basis: Defined by triglyceride accumulation within hepatocytes; associated metabolic diseases are not intrinsic to every fatty liver subtype.
Cancer originating in the fallopian-tube isthmus; reproductive anatomy has no axis.
Exposure causes corneal and conjunctival injury; this is not intrinsically infectious or autoimmune.
Infection directly inflames the external ear and auditory canal.
Infection directly inflames the meninges of the brain or spinal cord.
A focal peripheral nerve disorder of the lower limb; no specific infectious or autoimmune mechanism is established.
Ulcerative eyelid-margin inflammation is characteristically associated with staphylococcal infection; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Chronic inflammation of the lacrimal gland; a specific infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not established by this diagnosis.
Unilateral loss of labyrinthine function affects the inner-ear vestibular organ.
Eosinophilic inflammatory infiltration of lung tissue; tissue eosinophils do not by themselves establish a blood or marrow disorder.
Hypereosinophilic inflammatory collagen disease supports blood and immune axes; evidence does not establish common cardiac, skin or locomotor damage.
audit_reason: Add infectious_immune for eosinophil-mediated inflammatory tissue injury. Collagenopathy ancestry alone does not establish locomotor involvement, and common cardiac damage is not established.

basis: Inflammation of the lacrimal gland; the umbrella diagnosis does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Umbrella disorder of white blood cells; infection, immunodeficiency and immune mediation do not apply to every subtype.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation damages pulmonary interstitium and alveoli; reactive blood eosinophilia is not a separate blood disorder.
Benign mammary dysplasia is confined to breast tissue, which has no axis.
Acute infectious inflammation of the ethmoid sinuses; orbital and intracranial complications are uncommon.
Chronic inflammation of the conjunctiva; no specific infectious or immune-mediated cause established.
Acute lacrimal gland inflammation; this etiologically unspecified concept does not establish infection or autoimmune disease.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: lacrimal inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism; acute dacryoadenitis also has noninfectious causes.

basis: Tuberculous pulmonary or pleural infection causes rupture into the pleural space and pneumothorax.
Plasma-cell neoplasm with defining osteosclerotic bone lesions; peripheral neuropathy accompanies roughly half of cases as a manifestation of the plasma-cell process.

decisions.neurologic: involved: peripheral neuropathy occurs in approximately 50% and reflects the plasma-cell disease, commonly expressed within POEMS.

basis: Refractory plasma-cell malignancies are predominantly myeloma: destructive bone lesions affect most and disease-related renal impairment about 30-50%. Treatment effects excluded.

decisions.renal: involved: myeloma dominates refractory plasma-cell malignancies; direct light-chain-related renal impairment affects approximately 30-50% over the course.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive bone involvement affects most patients with myeloma, the predominant refractory plasma-cell malignancy.

basis: Plasma cell malignancy; destructive bone lesions occur in most patients. Renal insufficiency is less common than in secretory myeloma and does not clearly meet 30%.
Smoldering plasma-cell neoplasm lacks myeloma-defining end-organ damage; bone lesions and renal injury must not be inferred from active myeloma.
Benign tumor arising from Schwann cells of peripheral nerves; individual anatomical subtypes do not establish other organs across the group.
Disorder of the nasopharynx, included in the upper respiratory airways; infection is not shared across this umbrella.
Irreversible bronchial dilation and impaired clearance; infection may cause or complicate it but is not intrinsic to every case.
Neonatal Candida infection; the concept does not specify a site or establish common damage to any particular organ.
Calculus located in the urethra, part of the urinary axis.
Benign squamous epithelial neoplasm arising in the esophagus.
Calculi occupy the lower urinary tract, which belongs to the renal axis.
Ovarian signet-ring metastasis usually originates in the gastrointestinal tract; tumour-origin rule supports gastrointestinal. Ovary and breast have no axis.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: most Krukenberg tumours originate in stomach or bowel; the tumour-origin rule applies despite the defining ovarian metastatic site.

basis: Inflammation of locomotor connective-tissue fascia; infectious and autoimmune mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Benign fibroblastic proliferation occupies fascia and subcutaneous tissue; no metastatic or systemic organ involvement.
Benign smooth muscle tumor arising in the esophageal wall; smooth muscle origin does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Disorder of the plantar fascia, a locomotor connective tissue; usual biomechanical degeneration does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Reactive fibroblastic and myofibroblastic lesion centered in deep subcutaneous tissue.
Bacterial necrotizing infection directly destroys fascia, subcutaneous tissue and skin; systemic organ failure is not required.
The definition identifies a benign fibroblastic neoplasm arising within vessels; the fasciitis name does not establish skeletal involvement.
Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor arising within the esophagus.
Posture-dependent urinary protein loss is a renal condition; it does not establish progressive renal damage or another affected organ.
Acquired cystic lesion of the kidney.
Enlargement of the renal parenchyma defines the condition.
Inflammation directly affects oral mucosa; the umbrella includes diverse causes and does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Ocular motility disorder; an underlying neurologic or vestibular disease cannot be assumed for this umbrella.
Keratotic lesion of oral mucosa; malignant transformation is a later risk.
Recurrent oral mucosal ulceration is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease, despite its unknown initiating cause.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: recurrent aphthous stomatitis has a recognized immune-mediated mucosal injury mechanism; an unknown trigger does not exclude this axis.

basis: Placental and obstetric disorder; no covered organ is intrinsically affected.
Age-related opacity of the ocular lens.
Ulcerative inflammation of oral mucosa; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not intrinsic to this umbrella concept.
Destruction of alveolar walls and loss of functional lung tissue define emphysema.
Toxin-mediated myocardial injury; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Gonococcal infection directly damages the cornea; skin-related ancestors do not establish cutaneous involvement.
Gonococcal infection involving ocular tissues.
Neonatal conjunctival inflammation, usually infectious and classified under gonococcal conjunctivitis; definition also encompasses chemical cases.
Inflammation of tendon sheaths; the umbrella includes mechanical, infectious and rheumatic causes.
Rosacea-associated inflammation of the conjunctiva; associated cutaneous rosacea is a separate condition.
Inflammation or degeneration of a tendon, usually from mechanical overuse; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Obstruction of the gallbladder; gallbladder and bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Gallbladder distension from retained noninfected secretions; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Disease localized to the vitreous humor; infection is confined to particular subtypes.
Nodular ocular inflammation caused by embedded irritant hairs or similar foreign material; no additional organ involvement is established.
Purulent infection forms an abscess within the vitreous body.
Suppurative infection and inflammation within the eye.
Allergen-mediated inflammation and effusion of the middle ear.
Middle-ear mucoid effusion; infection or an immune mechanism is not required by this umbrella concept.
Disease of the eustachian tube, part of the middle-ear apparatus.
Defined disease of the upper respiratory tract, included within the pulmonary axis.
Biliary tree disease; intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts and gallbladder belong to the hepatic axis.
Pathologic dilatation of pelvic veins; reproductive or anorectal location does not change the vascular origin.
Thrombosis and hematoma of the external anal venous plexus; anus is gastrointestinal and venous thrombosis cardiovascular.
Pathologically enlarged vascular cushions and dilated veins of the anal canal; vascular and anorectal sites define the disease.
Disease of the anal vascular cushions above the dentate line; both anorectal location and abnormal vessels define it.
Cystic lesion arising from joint synovium, tendon sheath or bursa.
Destructive xanthogranulomatous inflammation of the gallbladder; infection or autoimmune disease is not established by this diagnosis.
Prolonged myocardial contractile dysfunction after transient severe ischemia.
Neonatal platelet deficiency defines the condition; an immune cause is not specified.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis.
Degeneration and atrophy of the ocular choroid; no systemic vascular or neurologic disease is established.
Defined by dysfunction of the lower digestive tract.
Fibrosing inflammation within skeletal muscle; the definition does not establish autoimmune or infectious causation.
Hereditary degeneration of the choroid; broad neurodegenerative ancestry does not establish extraocular neurologic disease.
Degeneration is localized to the eye; neurologic or systemic involvement in selected children does not apply across this umbrella.
Degeneration and sclerosis involve the ocular choroid; ancestry does not establish extraocular neurologic or systemic vascular damage.
Degeneration and atrophy of the ocular choroid; broad ancestors do not establish extraocular neurologic disease.
Hereditary choroidal dystrophy and atrophy directly affect the eye.
Choroidal atrophy within the inherited chorioretinal dystrophy spectrum.
Localized central choroidal dystrophy affecting the eye.
Refractive error caused by ocular anatomy.
Defective ocular focusing on the retina defines this group of visual disorders.
Permanent vertical ocular misalignment is an eye motility disorder.
Torsional strabismus is an ocular alignment and motility disorder.
Accommodative inward ocular misalignment, a form of strabismus.
Disorder of ocular alignment with medial deviation of one or both eyes.
Permanent downward deviation of an eye is an ocular alignment disorder.
Hereditary choroidal dystrophy and atrophy are confined to the eye.
Ocular alignment and binocular vision disorder within the strabismus spectrum.
Peripheral vestibular dysfunction arises in the inner ear.
A neurologic movement disorder affecting orofacial movements; the location of abnormal movements does not establish intrinsic oral tissue damage.
Interstitial keratitis is generally immune-mediated corneal stromal inflammation, often triggered by infection, causing scarring and visual impairment.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: the characteristic stromal inflammation is generally immune-mediated, including infection-triggered forms.

basis: Inflammation of the deep cornea; the umbrella does not establish a uniform infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Toxic injury and degeneration of the retinal macula.
Intestinal brush-border enzyme deficiency causing disaccharide malabsorption; explicitly a carbohydrate metabolism disorder.
Hair loss defines this umbrella disorder; autoimmune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
Infectious abscess of the urethral glands; urethral disease belongs to the renal axis.
Structural mitral leaflet abnormality, often with regurgitation; no common direct damage outside the cardiovascular axis.
Syphilitic infection directly damages the aorta, aortic valve and coronary arteries.
Alternating inward ocular misalignment, a form of strabismus.
Bacterial infection of an eyelid meibomian gland; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Ulceration directly damages the central cornea; infectious or autoimmune etiology is not specified.
Active microbial infection of a reproductive sac; the infection mechanism has an axis although the anatomical site does not.
Fluid collection around the testis is confined to the reproductive system; infection is not intrinsic to the umbrella concept.
Neurodevelopmental disorder of motor coordination; no primary skeletal muscle or joint disease established.
Chronic inflammation affects the lacrimal drainage apparatus; infection or autoimmunity is not established for the entire umbrella.
Chronic actinomycotic infection of the lacrimal canaliculus, supported by the lacrimal and eye-infection parents.
Chronic infection and inflammation of the lacrimal sac, usually associated with nasolacrimal obstruction.
Inflammation of the lacrimal sac, typically caused by bacterial infection associated with nasolacrimal obstruction.
Mucocele of the lacrimal sac caused by lacrimal drainage obstruction; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Lymph-node lymphoid-tissue disorder; no specific infectious, autoimmune, immunodeficiency or lymphoma mechanism is established across this umbrella.

decisions.haematologic: primary: lymph nodes contain lymphoid blood-cell tissue; haematologic is the best anatomical axis for this broad disorder umbrella.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: lymph-node location alone does not establish the required mechanism; infectious lymphadenitis and lymphoma are specific subtypes.

basis: Persistent proptosis classified as a disorder of the orbital eye adnexa.
Glaucoma damages the eye; corticosteroid exposure identifies its cause without adding another organ axis.
Established steroid-induced glaucoma damages the eye and optic nerve; treatment causation does not remove the defining organ of this disease.
A lymphoblastic leukemia affecting hematopoietic cells and marrow; no additional common organ damage is established.
Congenital hypoplasia and obstruction of left-sided cardiac structures and the aorta.
Inflammation of bone periosteum; infection characterizes some forms, not the whole group.
Uterine obstetric disorder lies outside the axes; associated postpartum hemorrhage does not establish a blood-cell or coagulation disease.
Vitamin D excess causes disordered calcium metabolism; renal injury and nephrocalcinosis are complications without established >=30% involvement across the concept.
Substance-use disorder has no axis; organ injuries associated with particular substances are separate diseases.
Substance dependence is a psychiatric condition; no direct organ damage is specified.
Acute infection and inflammation of the pelvic peritoneum associated with pelvic inflammatory disease.
Eosinophilia and immune-mediated myofascial injury define disease; persistent skin sclerosis ~30-50%; neuropathy near 30% omitted because of cap.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in orbital structures; lymphoma warrants the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Malignant soft-tissue tumor arising within the orbit.
Treponema pallidum infection of the brain or spinal cord; ocular damage is not established in at least 30% across the umbrella.
Low circulating glucose is a metabolic disorder; permanent neurologic injury is not present in most cases.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma involves blood or marrow; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 30-50%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic leukemic infiltration causing hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 30-50% and represents direct tumour occupation.

basis: Mature B-cell leukemia and non-Hodgkin lymphoma; blood, marrow and splenic involvement fall within haematologic.
Mature B-cell neoplasm umbrella includes lymphomas and leukemias; no additional organ is consistently damaged across the group.
Carcinoma originates in gastric epithelium; metastatic sites are not defining involvement across the umbrella.
Malignant B-cell lymphoid neoplasm, primarily nodal; lymphoma qualifies for the immune mechanism axis. No additional organ is commonly directly damaged.
Primary breast carcinoma is outside the axes; metastatic organ damage is not established for this umbrella concept.
Bone is occupied by metastases in roughly 80-90% of metastatic prostate cancer, providing the dominant applicable site; the prostate itself has no axis.
Squamous carcinoma originates in oral mucosa; HPV association and regional nodal spread do not establish another axis.
Clonal plasma-cell proliferation; bone and renal damage are not established across this umbrella, which includes MGUS and localized plasmacytoma.
Hematologic disorder defined by monoclonal immunoglobulins; renal, neurologic and skeletal damage is not common across the umbrella.
Stage I carcinoma confined to the uterine body, potentially involving cervical glands; these reproductive tissues have no axis.
Carcinoma confined to uterine body and cervical stroma; both are reproductive sites outside the axes.
Malignant T-cell precursors occupy blood and marrow; leukemic liver infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly half. A thymic mediastinal mass does not establish pulmonary involvement.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic leukemic infiltration causing hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 40-60%; direct malignant occupation qualifies without requiring hepatic failure.

basis: Mature T-cell lymphoma is a blood-cell malignancy and meets the lymphoma mechanism axis; no additional organ site is consistently specified.
Acinar carcinoma includes pancreatic and salivary origins, mapped to GI; this site-unspecified umbrella also includes breast/prostate primaries.
Inflammation of gastric mucosa; this umbrella does not establish a specific infectious or autoimmune cause.
Marrow/blood lymphoblast malignancy within the lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma spectrum; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 30-60%.
Acquired skeletal myopathy with muscle atrophy and myosin loss; critical illness and treatments are triggers, not additional affected organs.
Most tumors originate in salivary glands. Direct perineural tumor invasion occurs in approximately 40-70%; minority primary sites are not generalized across the umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct tumor infiltration along peripheral nerve sheaths occurs in approximately 40-70%; this is tumor occupation, beyond pain alone.

basis: Primary lung carcinoma with both malignant glandular and squamous components.
Adrenal medullary endocrine tumor; secondary hypertension is a separately diagnosed disease. Direct myocardial injury affects fewer than 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension (~80-90%) is a separately diagnosed secondary disease; catecholamine cardiomyopathy affects a minority below 30%.

basis: Progressive neuronal loss in the brain causes cognitive decline and dementia.
Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; progressive denervation causes muscle atrophy in most patients; respiratory failure reflects neuromuscular loss.
Mature T-cell lymphoma; no additional organ has sufficiently established common direct damage here. Rash or organ enlargement alone is insufficient.
Chronic immune-mediated airway inflammation and variable airflow obstruction define asthma.
Chronic immune-mediated eczema; asthma and allergic rhinitis are separate diseases; damaging ocular complications are not common enough.
Atrial electrical dysfunction defines this cardiac arrhythmia; stroke is a separate disease whose risk is increased.
Inflammation of the exocrine pancreas; endocrine failure and autoimmune mechanisms do not apply to most patients across this umbrella.
Isolated failure of sperm production affects reproductive function; endocrine dysfunction is not intrinsic to this umbrella.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast lies outside the axes, and metastatic risks do not establish additional involvement.
Bipolar disorder is a psychiatric mood disorder without an intrinsic organ-damage axis under these rules.
Carcinoma originates in urinary bladder epithelium; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Neoplasm occupying the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
Adenocarcinoma originating in breast glandular epithelium; breast is explicitly outside the axes.
Carcinoma originates in breast epithelium, outside the thirteen axes; metastatic sites are not intrinsic labels for this umbrella.
Breast carcinoma; breast has no axis, and gene-expression subtype does not establish damage to another organ.
Small minimally invasive adenocarcinoma arising in lung tissue.
Site-unspecified cancer umbrella; no organ or mechanism axis applies to most cancers across this group.
Site-unspecified epithelial malignancy spanning many organs; no organ axis applies across this umbrella. Empty axes reflect unspecified origin.
Disease of cardiac myocardium; cardiac muscle belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Defined as disease involving the cardiovascular system.
Malignancy of myeloid blood cells and marrow; no additional organ has established common functional damage.
Benign cartilage-producing neoplasm arising predominantly in long-bone epiphyses; metastasis is rare.
Chronic inflammation of the stomach; infectious or autoimmune causation is not universal across this umbrella.
Chronic destructive disease of airways and alveoli; cardiovascular comorbidities and pulmonary hypertension are separately diagnosed conditions.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is a separately diagnosed disease.
Malignant epithelial tumour originating in the kidney; distant metastases are separately diagnosed.
Primary kidney sarcoma; distant metastases are not sufficiently common to label additional organs.
Invasive mucin-producing adenocarcinoma originating in the colon.
Malignant glandular epithelial tumor originating in the colorectum.
Cardiac pump failure; pulmonary congestion, edema and hepatic congestion alone do not establish direct lasting damage to additional organs.
Disease of coronary arteries with stenosis and myocardial ischemic consequences, all within the cardiovascular axis.
Immune-mediated transmural intestinal inflammation and fibrosis; individual extraintestinal organ complications do not reliably meet the 30% threshold.
Primary melanoma arising from skin melanocytes; metastatic organ involvement is not characteristic across all cases.
Primary malignant cartilage-forming bone tumour; metastases are not defining organ involvement.
Disordered insulin production or action causes hyperglycemia; retinopathy, nephropathy and neuropathy are separately diagnosed complications.
Diabetic metabolic disease with defining glomerular injury; local glomerular microvascular damage is included under renal.
Adenocarcinoma originates in and diffusely infiltrates the stomach; metastatic organ involvement is not assumed.
Autoimmune skin fibrosis; GI fibrosis/dysmotility >70% and interstitial lung disease ~50-80%. Renal crisis <30%; Raynaud alone does not establish lasting vascular damage.
Umbrella for disorders affecting the small or large intestine; no mechanism or additional organ is shared across its subtypes.
Ventricular dilation and myocardial contractile dysfunction define this cardiomyopathy; other organ complications are not intrinsic across the umbrella.
Carcinoma confined to mammary ducts; breast has no axis.
Defined by endocardial inflammation; the umbrella includes infective and sterile forms without a shared infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Tumour originates in female reproductive organs, which have no axis.
Brain disorder defined by recurrent abnormal neuronal discharges and seizures.
