Epiglottic inflammation is predominantly an acute bacterial infection of the upper airway.
Generalized epilepsy characterized by tonic-clonic seizures.
Ethmoid sinus mucosal inflammation is an upper-airway disorder. The umbrella definition establishes neither a specific infection nor an autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: nonspecific sinus mucosal inflammation alone does not establish infection or an autoimmune/immune-mediated disease across this acute/chronic umbrella.

basis: Chronic fungal infection of deep dermis and subcutaneous tissue; bone invasion occurs in advanced disease and is not established in most patients.
Absent or undeveloped testes cause deficient testicular hormones; endocrine hypogonadism provides an axis despite reproductive involvement.
Fascioloides magna infection causes extensive hepatic parenchymal destruction; the supplied definition describes disease in herbivores.
Parasitic lymphatic infection with defining elephantiasis of skin/subcutis; hyperkeratosis occurs in 30-79%. Renal and pulmonary abnormalities are below 30%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: chronic enlargement and thickening of skin/subcutis constitute the named elephantiasis phenotype; hyperkeratosis occurs in 30-79%.

basis: Filoviral hemorrhagic fevers feature thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy; direct hepatocellular injury is common (>30%).
Umbrella for Flaviviridae infections; no single anatomical organ is directly damaged in most patients across the group.
Dendritic-cell neoplasm grouped with hematolymphoid tumors; extranodal sites vary. It is not lymphoma, and EBV association is not universal.
Fungal infection directly involving the lungs; no additional organ damage applies across this umbrella.
Clostridial infection causes defining skeletal-muscle necrosis with destructive skin and soft-tissue involvement.
Mycobacterial infection directly involves the gastrointestinal tract; hepatic involvement is subtype-specific.
Varicella-zoster infection involving the facial nerve and ear defines the syndrome; the transient vesicular eruption adds no dermatologic axis.
Herpes simplex infection producing genital cutaneous and mucocutaneous vesicles and ulcers.
Migratory glossitis affects the tongue's oral mucosa.
Geotrichum fungal infection has pulmonary, mucosal, cutaneous and disseminated presentations; the supplied evidence does not establish pulmonary damage in at least 30% across the concept.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary disease is a recognized presentation, but a reliable frequency of at least 30% across geotrichosis is not established.

basis: Cognitive and perceptual deficits associated with focal parietal white matter damage.
Burkholderia mallei infection; pulmonary, localized cutaneous and disseminated forms vary, with no additional organ reliably established at >=30%.
Inherited carbohydrate enzyme deficiency affecting erythrocyte redox metabolism and causing susceptibility to hemolysis; most patients remain asymptomatic.
Nematode infection; sustained larval occupation and inflammation of subcutis occur in most patients (>30%). CNS, ocular and pulmonary invasion are minority manifestations.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous/subcutaneous larval migration causes direct tissue inflammation in most cases; it is a common manifestation of the broader infection.

basis: Klebsiella infection causes destructive genital cutaneous ulcers, establishing infection and skin axes.
Gastrointestinal blood-feeding nematode infection with defining blood-loss anemia.

decisions.haematologic: primary: anemia from direct intestinal blood loss is an explicit defining manifestation of this infection.

basis: Enteroviral infection defined by cutaneous vesicular lesions and painful oral mucosal sores; neurologic complications are uncommon.
Hantavirus infection umbrella; renal and pulmonary damage characterize different syndromes and are not established across most patients in this group.
Blood accumulates in the pericardial sac; this does not itself imply a blood-cell or coagulation disorder.
Hantavirus infection defined by renal injury, thrombocytopenia and hemorrhagic coagulopathy; blurred vision alone does not establish ocular damage.
Clinically apparent Nipah/Hendra infections commonly cause encephalitis; pneumonitis and respiratory failure occur in roughly >=30%, with substantial variation between outbreaks.
Human hepadnaviral disease is hepatotropic hepatitis B infection, directly involving the liver.
Mycobacterial infection directly occupies and inflames the liver; unrelated endocrine ancestry does not support endocrine involvement.
Hepatitis E virus directly causes liver inflammation; extrahepatic injury is not common enough to qualify.
Hepatitis delta virus directly causes hepatic inflammation; bleeding and confusion are minority complications.
Hepatitis A virus causes acute inflammatory liver injury; arthralgia does not establish joint damage.
Enteroviral infection produces characteristic vesicles and ulcers of the posterior oral mucosa and soft palate.
HSV infection directly inflames and ulcerates the oral mucosa and gums.
Herpesvirus infection umbrella; no anatomical organ is directly damaged in most patients across its diverse subtypes.
HIV-associated enteric mucosal dysfunction causes chronic diarrhea after exclusion of other enteric infections.
HIV-associated syndrome defined by muscle wasting with myofiber degeneration; malabsorption reflects intestinal dysfunction in 30-79%.
HIV-associated glomerular and tubular injury defines the nephropathy; renal and infectious mechanisms are primary.
Definition excludes Ancylostoma and Necator, the usual human intestinal hookworms. Remaining animal-associated genera do not establish a consistent intestinal site in humans.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the restricted definition excludes usual human intestinal hookworms; animal intestinal tropism does not establish gastrointestinal localization in human infection.

basis: Localized bacterial infection or abscess of an eyelid gland.
HTLV-1 infection; leukemia, myelopathy, uveitis and dermatitis are separately diagnosed minority outcomes, not universal consequences despite the definition's wording.
Intestinal tapeworm infection; gastrointestinal occupation defines its site even when asymptomatic. Anemia is not established as common.
The definition describes congenital pancreatic hyperinsulinism; persistent hypoglycemic neurodevelopmental injury affects roughly 30-50% of congenital cases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: congenital hyperinsulinism, as defined here, causes lasting neurodevelopmental injury in roughly 30-50%, beyond transient hypoglycemic symptoms.

basis: Excess prolactin secretion is an endocrine disorder.
Hypoderma larvae infest and migrate through skin/subcutis. Ocular infestation is a subtype rather than involvement established in most cases.
Malignancy affecting the hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis under the specified mapping.
Immunodeficiency defined by persistent CD4-positive lymphocytopenia; opportunistic infections are separate diseases.
Chlamydia trachomatis infection directly inflames the conjunctiva.
EBV infects lymphocytes with lymphoid proliferation; hepatic inflammation with hepatocellular injury occurs in ~80-90%. Transient pharyngitis does not establish lasting airway damage.

decisions.hepatic: involved: EBV-associated hepatic inflammation and hepatocellular injury occur in ~80-90%, as part of the acute disease rather than a later disease risk.
decisions.pulmonary: none: pharyngitis is a transient manifestation; lasting airway damage is not common, and serious airway obstruction is a minority complication.

basis: Viral respiratory tract infection; conjunctival inflammation and myalgia are transient, while myocardial and CNS complications are uncommon.
Malignancy of interdigitating dendritic cells, a hematopoietic leukocyte lineage; this sarcoma is not a lymphoma.
Malignant neoplasm of the intestine; metastatic organ involvement is not established across this umbrella concept.
Neoplasm arising in the endocrine pancreas; exocrine pancreatic involvement is not established.
Behavioral and cognitive syndrome caused by bilateral temporal brain damage; infectious and traumatic causes vary, so infection is not intrinsic to the syndrome.
Tuberculous infection of the larynx; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis despite the extrapulmonary tuberculosis terminology.
Lassa virus infection; hearing impairment and abnormal bleeding are occasional (5-29%); acute pharyngitis and systemic symptoms do not establish lasting organ damage.
Hutchinson teeth and interstitial keratitis are major diagnostic stigmata; sensorineural deafness completes the defining triad. Skeletal stigmata omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: Hutchinson teeth are a major diagnostic feature of late congenital syphilis; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.ocular: primary: interstitial keratitis is a major diagnostic feature of late congenital syphilis, supporting primary ocular involvement.

basis: Asymptomatic persistent Treponema pallidum infection; later symptomatic organ disease is a separate stage and is not labelled here.
Legionella infection includes pneumonic Legionnaires' disease and nonpneumonic Pontiac fever; pulmonary damage is not established as typical across the umbrella.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pneumonia defines one subtype; nonpneumonic Pontiac fever prevents assuming pulmonary damage is typical across legionellosis.

basis: Legionella pneumonia; frequent arrhythmia alone does not establish direct cardiac injury. Myocarditis, renal injury and encephalitis are reported in only 5-29%.
Leptospiral infection; thrombocytopenia occurs in 30-79%. Hepatitis, kidney injury and meningitis occur in <30%; frequent enzyme elevations alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Direct lung injury from aspirated or inhaled fatty substances; chemical pneumonitis does not establish infection or an immune-mediated disease.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss with insulin-resistant diabetes and dyslipidemia; hepatic steatosis affects most (~80% or more).
Listeria infection; direct CNS infection and meningitis are annotated in 30-79%. Bacteremia does not establish blood-cell damage.
Veterinary concept: bovine poxvirus infection defined by nodular skin lesions.
Mycobacterial infection of lymph nodes; lymph node involvement alone does not establish blood or marrow disease.
Inflammation of lymphatic vessels, classified as vasculitis and usually infectious. Overlying red streaks do not establish separate skin damage.
Broad hematolymphoid-system disorder encompassing nodal and splenic disease; no shared infectious, autoimmune or immunodeficiency mechanism is established.

decisions.haematologic: primary: hematolymphoid tissue is the closest applicable axis for this broad nodal, splenic and lymphatic-system category.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: lymphatic anatomy alone does not establish infection, immunodeficiency, autoimmunity or lymphoma across the umbrella.

basis: Infectious lymphatic disease; organism attribution in the definition conflicts with the chlamydial name and ancestry; proctitis is presentation-dependent.
Hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome; other cancers are separate risks. Reported very frequent skin/CNS tumours conflict with the typical Lynch umbrella phenotype.
Malignancies of male reproductive organs; endocrine dysfunction is not defining, and skin-origin subtypes do not represent most cases.
Malignant neoplasm involving the mandibular bone.
Mansonella nematode infection; pruritus, arthralgia and eosinophilia do not establish common lasting skin, joint or blood damage.
Tumor of the maxillary bone; a sinus subtype does not establish airway involvement across the umbrella concept.
Inflammation of maxillary sinus mucosa; this umbrella does not establish an infectious or autoimmune cause in every case.
Mediastinum is not a specified axis. This mixed-site umbrella does not establish lung, airway, heart, nerve or blood-organ origin across most subtypes.
Blocked meibomian gland produces an eyelid lesion; this is not inherently infectious or autoimmune.
Inflammation directly affects brain and meninges, generally through infection.
Microsporidial intestinal infection causes chronic diarrhea and malabsorption; diarrhea is reported in 30-79%. Other organ infections are uncommon; immunodeficiency usually predates infection.
Chronic right middle-lobe atelectasis and pneumonitis; infection is not required across cases.
Disseminated TB with defining pulmonary micronodules; hepatic inflammation with biochemical dysfunction occurs in roughly half. Secondary anemia alone does not establish marrow damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia is often secondary to systemic inflammation; direct marrow or functionally significant splenic damage is not established in at least 30%.

basis: Pseudocowpox is a localized parapoxvirus infection producing characteristic cutaneous nodules.
Autoimmune neurologic syndrome causing ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia; ocular motor nerve dysfunction does not establish intrinsic eye disease.
Structural narrowing of the mitral valve orifice.
Site-unspecified histologic umbrella spanning reproductive, salivary, pulmonary and other sites; no organ axis applies across most cases.
Autoimmune overlap with arthritis and scleroderma; pulmonary fibrosis annotated 80-99%. Common gastrointestinal disease and ocular sicca omitted under the four-axis cap.
Poxvirus infection produces cutaneous lesions; conjunctival infection is occasional.
Broad viral infection umbrella; no single damaged organ is shared across its respiratory, hemorrhagic and neurotropic subgroups.
Morbillivirus infection umbrella; transient rash and respiratory symptoms do not establish lasting organ damage. Persistent neurologic complications are uncommon.
Site-variable tumor includes pancreatic and appendiceal origins; ovarian origin has no axis. Lung origin is rare; exact organ assignment depends on tumor site.
Leishmania infection with destructive skin ulcers. Supplied definition describes cutaneous disease and does not establish common destructive mucosal involvement.
Tuberculosis resistant to rifampicin and isoniazid; pulmonary disease predominates, without a common additional extrapulmonary site.
Malignant neoplasm arising in skeletal or smooth muscle.
Hypersensitivity-mediated alveolar and interstitial lung inflammation caused by inhaled mushroom-associated organic antigens.
MAC causes infection; chronic pulmonary infection directly damages lungs in a substantial share (>30%). Nodal and disseminated forms do not imply uniform other-organ injury.
Mycoplasma infection directly causes pneumonia and bronchial inflammation.
Marrow replacement by fibrosis, tumour or granulomas impairs blood-cell production; other organs depend on the underlying cause.
Necator hookworms occupy and injure small-intestinal mucosa. Blood-loss anemia depends on worm burden and is separately diagnosed.
Nematode infection umbrella; tissue sites vary by organism and subtype, without a particular organ damaged in most patients across the group.
Malignant neoplasm involving the nervous system; subtype-specific sites do not establish additional axes across this umbrella.
Aspergillus directly infects the nervous system; possible extracranial sources do not establish common additional organ involvement.
Schistosomal infection directly involves brain, spinal cord or meninges.
Human Newcastle virus infection characteristically localizes to the conjunctiva. Respiratory and intestinal symptoms do not establish additional common organ damage.

decisions.ocular: primary: conjunctivitis represents characteristic direct conjunctival infection; the exclusion of transient signs does not remove the primary site of infection.

basis: Viral infection umbrella encompassing different tissue tropisms; no single damaged organ is established across the group.
Onchocerca infection directly affects the eye; additional organ damage is not established for this ocular concept.
Toxoplasma infection of the retina and adjacent ocular tissues.
Oesophagostomum helminth infection directly involves the intestinal tract.
Obstetric disorder of amniotic fluid volume; fetal renal disease and pulmonary hypoplasia are not defining organ damage across this umbrella.
VZV infection of the ophthalmic trigeminal division and its cutaneous territory; keratitis, uveitis or other ocular disease develops in roughly 50%.
Opisthorchis flukes inhabit and inflame the biliary tract; cholangiocarcinoma is a later risk and separate disease.
Usual optic neuritis is immune-mediated optic-nerve inflammation; toxic/nutritional forms are minority exceptions. The optic nerve maps to ocular; associated MS is separate.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most usual optic neuritis is immune-mediated demyelinating inflammation; the broader umbrella's toxic/nutritional exceptions do not dominate.

basis: Candida infection directly involves oral mucosa; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Tuberculous infection of the mouth, tongue or salivary glands.
Chlamydia psittaci infection characteristically causes respiratory infection and atypical pneumonia.
Hyperparathyroid metabolic bone disease defined by bone resorption, fibrous replacement, cysts and fractures.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: osteitis fibrosa is a metabolic bone disorder defined by excessive parathyroid hormone action, rather than an unrelated endocrine association.

basis: Veterinary parasitic disease: Ostertagia worms infect and damage the stomach; the supplied definition concerns herbivorous mammals.
Middle-ear effusion defines the disorder; active infection or an immune-mediated mechanism is not required.
Carcinoma of the endocrine pancreas; metastatic sites and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction are not defining involvement.
Systemic mycosis characteristically affects lungs and oral mucosa; destructive skin lesions occur in ~30-50%. Bone disease is uncommon.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: destructive oral mucosal infection is a characteristic, definition-level manifestation.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent destructive cutaneous lesions occur in approximately 30-50%, near the inclusion threshold.

basis: Paragonimus infection causes chronic pulmonary disease; reactive eosinophilia does not establish a separate blood disorder.
Viral-family umbrella with respiratory, salivary and neurologic subtypes; the supplied evidence does not establish common direct damage to another organ across the group.
Infection of the periungual soft tissues defines the supplied concept.
Disease of the parotid salivary gland; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inflammation of the parotid salivary gland; infection or autoimmunity is not required by the umbrella definition.
Pasteurella infection most commonly causes direct skin and soft-tissue infection (>50%); pulmonary and invasive presentations are less common.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis directly infects and inflames the pericardium.
Pericardial inflammation defines the disease; inflammation alone does not establish infection, autoimmunity or another qualifying immune mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this etiologically broad umbrella does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism across most patients.

basis: Neurologic sleep-related movement disorder; repetitive muscle contractions do not establish skeletal muscle damage.
Bacterial abscess surrounding the palatine tonsil in the pharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Chronic cognitive dysfunction supports neurologic classification; muscle/joint pain and other multisystem symptoms do not establish direct damage to additional organs.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: myalgia and arthralgia are symptom domains without established direct muscle or joint injury.

basis: Defined by pestivirus infection; no consistent human organ damage pattern is established by the supplied record.
Defective bactericidal function of phagocytic leukocytes defines this immunodeficiency; no additional organ damage is established across the umbrella.
Adenoviral infection defined by pharyngeal inflammation and conjunctivitis; both sites are intrinsic to the syndrome.
Substance-use disorder defined by psychological symptoms and impaired functioning; no specific organ damage is established.
Acute sandfly-transmitted viral infection; fever and influenza-like symptoms do not establish organ damage.
Picornavirus infection umbrella; no single damaged organ is shared across its diverse infections.
Superficial Malassezia infection of skin; systemic infection is exceptional.
Abnormal placental attachment or invasion of the uterine wall; obstetric and reproductive tissues have no axis.
Placental disease is obstetric and outside the thirteen axes.
Placental implantation disorder is obstetric; bleeding does not make this a primary blood or coagulation disease.
Obstetric placental dysfunction; associated maternal autoimmune diseases and separately diagnosed offspring neurodevelopmental disorders do not add axes.
Plasmodium falciparum infects and destroys erythrocytes. Cerebral malaria, renal failure and pulmonary injury affect a minority overall.
Plasmodium vivax infection directly parasitizes and destroys erythrocytes; severe injury to other organs is a minority complication.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection directly inflames the pleura, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Fungal infection predominantly causing interstitial pneumonia; extrapulmonary infection is rare.
The supplied definition describes bovine bacterial fibrinous bronchopneumonia, directly affecting the lungs.
Polyomavirus infection umbrella; renal/urinary disease and CNS disease depend on viral species and host context, without established >=30% involvement across the group.
Chronic venous valve damage defines the syndrome; persistent stasis dermatitis and skin induration are major diagnostic features. Ulceration alone affects a minority (<10%).

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent stasis dermatitis and induration are major diagnostic skin manifestations of chronic venous injury; this does not rely on ulcer frequency (<10%).

basis: Postpartum depressive disorder; no intrinsic organ disease within the axes is established.
Herpesvirus infection defined by central nervous system involvement.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the lung; mesenchymal differentiation does not establish another organ of origin.
Recurrent pulmonary infection; supplied definition specifies nontuberculous mycobacterial infection.
Neurologic parasomnia involving failure of normal REM motor inhibition; later neurodegenerative disease is a separate diagnosis and risk.
Mycobacterial infection directly affects the kidney; pulmonary involvement is not required for renal tuberculosis.
Viral infection umbrella; gastrointestinal, hematologic and other tissue involvement varies among the constituent infections.
Respiroviruses cause infection of respiratory tract mucosa, including upper airways, larynx and lungs.
Retroperitoneal space has no dedicated axis; this heterogeneous cancer umbrella does not establish a particular visceral organ, vascular or locomotor tissue origin.
Acute metabolic syndrome defined by encephalopathy/cerebral edema, hepatic fatty change and hypoglycemia.
Umbrella for rhabditid nematode infections; affected organs vary across subtypes, without a shared organ site established for most patients.
Umbrella for rhabdoviral infections; rabies-associated neural damage cannot be generalized across the entire group.
Klebsiella infection causes granulomatous respiratory tract disease; extension to skin or lips is not established as common.
Chronic granulomatous infection predominantly involving nasal mucosa; ocular and disseminated lesions are minority manifestations.
Rickettsial infection directly causes pulmonary inflammation; no additional common organ damage is established for this concept.
Roseolovirus infection; typical exanthem is transient, and encephalitis is a minority manifestation across the group.
Salmonella infection directly causes intestinal inflammation; systemic complications are not defining or sufficiently common.
Streptococcal infection usually centered in the pharynx; the characteristic toxin-mediated rash is transient.
Screwworm myiasis is a parasitic infestation typically invading wounds and destroying skin and underlying soft tissue; other sites vary.
Yersinia pestis infection of the bloodstream defines septicemic plague, with blood explicitly identified as its location.
Setaria nematode infection; aberrant ocular migration can cause blindness, but common ocular damage is not established.
Respiratory and airway complaints support pulmonary. An immune mechanism is not established across the syndrome; headache, dry skin and mucosal irritation do not establish additional organ damage.
audit_reason: Remove infectious_immune: sick building syndrome is a heterogeneous exposure-associated symptom syndrome, without a defining immune or infectious mechanism. Listed allergic diseases and the pneumonitis parent do not establish that mechanism across the umbrella.

basis: Inhaled silica directly causes pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis; associated infection and autoimmune disease are separate conditions.
Paranasal sinus mucosal inflammation belongs to the pulmonary axis. The umbrella definition does not establish infection or a specific immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: sinusitis encompasses infectious and noninfectious inflammation; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious, autoimmune or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Tuberculous infection directly damages bones or joints; pulmonary disease is not required for this extrapulmonary concept.
Spirometra larval infection; destructive subcutaneous invasion with inflammatory nodules occurs in roughly 30-50%. CNS and ocular frequencies vary geographically.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous larval invasion causes inflammatory nodules in roughly 30-50%; this common site does not define every form of sparganosis.

basis: Usually infectious inflammation of sphenoid sinus mucosa; paranasal sinuses belong to the airway axis, and the bone itself is not the defined site.
Structural narrowing of the vertebral canal. Pain or claudication alone does not establish lasting neural damage; separately diagnosed radiculopathy or myelopathy is not added.
Malignancy occupies the spleen, a blood organ; this broad concept does not specify lymphoma or another immune mechanism.
Mycobacterial infection directly occupies and damages the spleen, covered by the haematologic axis.
Fungal infection predominantly produces persistent cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions; extracutaneous disease is uncommon.
Staphylococcal infection directly involving lung tissue.
Staphylococcal enterotoxin-mediated foodborne gastrointestinal disease; muscle weakness does not establish muscle injury.
Streptococcal infection directly inflames lung parenchyma; extrapulmonary complications do not qualify across typical cases.
Strongylid infection umbrella ([MeSH](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/68017206)); intestinal hookworms dominate human cases; extraintestinal sites depend on species.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: most human strongylid infections are intestinal, especially hookworm; rare extraintestinal species do not determine umbrella labels.

basis: Strongyloides infection occupies intestinal mucosa; migratory skin eruptions are transient, and pulmonary injury or dissemination is not common across patients.
Suppurative infection of the middle ear.
Treponemal infection; early sores and rash are transient, while destructive neurologic or cardiovascular involvement is a minority and separately classified.
Syphilitic degeneration of spinal posterior columns and sensory roots; destructive arthropathy and optic atrophy are minority complications.
Theileria infects leukocytes and/or erythrocytes. The supplied definition describes livestock infection.
Brachial plexus compression predominates (~90-95%); vascular compression occurs in minority subtypes.
Tick ectoparasitic infestation of skin; paralysis is a minority subtype.
Tick infestation produces a salivary neurotoxin causing paralysis; neurologic dysfunction and the parasitic mechanism define the condition.
Fungal infection of skin and its appendages; otologic disease is limited to a subtype.
Chronic fungal infection of skin and scalp follicles causes crusting and scarring alopecia.
Dermatophyte infection of foot skin; no direct musculoskeletal involvement.
Viral infection umbrella; sustained damage to a particular organ is not shared across the group.
Torovirus infection in humans characteristically causes intestinal infection and gastroenteritis.
Defined by Toxascaris nematode infection; the supplied concept does not establish common damage to a particular organ.
Larval parasitic infection; hepatic, pulmonary and ocular damage vary by clinical form, with no established >=30% frequency across the umbrella.
Toxoplasma infection; most infections do not cause organ damage. Cerebral and ocular damage belong to specific subtypes rather than most patients.
Defined as bacterial infection and inflammation of the tracheal mucosa.
Bartonella quintana infection; transient splenomegaly and shin pain do not establish lasting organ damage.
Trichomonas infection predominantly affects genital mucosa, outside the anatomical axes. Urinary disease occurs in subtypes and is not established across most patients.

decisions.renal: none: the definition describes vaginitis; urinary ancestry and a cystitis subtype do not establish urinary involvement across this umbrella concept.

basis: Parasitic nematode infection predominantly occupying the gastrointestinal tract; pulmonary and hematologic damage are not universal across this group.
Intestinal nematode infection; adult Trichostrongylus occupy the small intestine.
Whipworms occupy and injure colonic mucosa; substantial blood-loss anemia is mainly associated with heavy infections.
Structural narrowing of the tricuspid valve; infection or immune-mediated disease is not intrinsic to this concept.
Cutaneous infestation by trombiculid mite larvae; carriage of the scrub-typhus agent does not establish systemic infection.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection produces empyema in the pleural space.
Mycobacterial infection directly inflames and occupies peritoneal surfaces; pulmonary tuberculosis is not required.
Schistosomal infection directly injures the bladder and urinary tract; subsequent bladder cancer is a separate disease risk.
Tuberculous infection commonly occupies kidneys and urinary tract; genital involvement has no separate reproductive axis.
Malignancy originates in the uterine body, a reproductive organ outside the listed axes.
Nonallergic nasal mucosal disease caused by abnormal vasomotor regulation; the definition does not support an allergic immune mechanism.
Oral cavity is the predominant origin across this histologic umbrella. Upper-airway and cutaneous origins belong to minority site-specific forms.

decisions.pulmonary: none: nasal and laryngeal origins occur in minority subtypes and do not characterize most patients across the umbrella.
decisions.dermatologic: none: plantar and other cutaneous forms are minority subtypes; skin origin does not characterize most patients.

basis: Abnormal function of the bladder-ureter junction; the renal axis includes bladder and ureters.
Inflammation of the peripheral vestibular nerve defines this vestibular disorder; idiopathic neuritis alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
Viral infection causing inflammation of brain tissue.
Viral infection directly inflames liver parenchyma; extrahepatic damage is not common across this umbrella.
Viral infection directly inflames the lung parenchyma.
Candida infection of vulva and vagina; reproductive location has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism qualifies.
Bacterial infection with massive adrenal hemorrhage, adrenal insufficiency and defining DIC. Circulatory shock alone does not establish direct cardiac or vascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: shock reflects sepsis and adrenal failure; separate direct cardiac or vascular injury is not established by the syndrome.

basis: Systemic inflammatory rheumatic syndrome; arthralgia, transient exanthema and reactive leukocytosis do not establish joint, skin or blood damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the supplied definition establishes arthralgia, without persistent arthritis, structural injury or muscle dysfunction.

basis: Treponemal infection causes persistent papillomatous and ulcerative skin lesions; destructive bone disease is not established in >=30% across all stages.
Coronary arterial vasospasm causes myocardial ischemia; associated migraine, Raynaud phenomenon and asthma do not establish other organ involvement.
Acid-base imbalance defines this metabolic axis condition; respiratory and renal causes do not establish shared lung or kidney damage across the umbrella.
Inheritance-pattern umbrella rather than an organ-defined disease; no organ axis applies consistently across its heterogeneous members.
Urinary bladder disease; bladder belongs to the renal axis. No mechanism applies across the umbrella.
Primary tumour of the breast, which has no axis; sarcoma histology does not establish locomotor involvement.
Glandular epithelial malignancy arising in the cecum.
Carcinoma arising in the caecal epithelium.
Definition specifies recurrent urinary bladder infections; bladder is included in the renal axis.
Chronic disease of nasal and paranasal sinus mucosa; a specific infectious or immune-mediated cause is not inherent to the umbrella.
Urinary bladder inflammation; bacterial infection accounts for most patients across this umbrella, although noninfectious subtypes exist.
Primary neuroglial malignancy arising in the pons.
Malignant epithelial tumor originating in the stomach.
Adenocarcinoma originating in the stomach; metastatic sites are not inherent organ involvement.
Tumor of hormone-producing gonadal granulosa cells, classified as an endocrine gland neoplasm.
Severe brain, limb and airway malformations define the syndrome; cardiac malformations occur in 30-79%. Oral clefts (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease with colonic inflammation that cannot be classified as Crohn disease or ulcerative colitis.
Viral or bacterial infection directly inflames the colon.
Defined metabolic acid-base disorder with lactate accumulation; underlying hypoxic organ diseases are separate causes.
Neuroendocrine tumour arising in the lung; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the meninges; the definition overrides the erroneous salpingitis ancestry.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Mesenchymal differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle or bone origin.
Sclerosis of renal arteries and arterioles causes renal ischemia and fibrosis; both renal tissue and its vasculature are affected.
Ovarian epithelial malignancy affects a reproductive organ; associated hypercalcemia does not establish common endocrine involvement.
Ovarian epithelial malignancy; reproductive tumour origin has no axis. No qualifying extraovarian damage is established across the concept.
Exocrine pancreatic primary; liver metastases directly occupy and damage hepatic tissue in roughly 50% or more over the usual course.

decisions.hepatic: involved: liver metastases occur in roughly 50% or more over the course and represent spread of the same malignancy.

basis: Primary lung adenocarcinoma with papillary architecture.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Metastatic organ involvement is not established by this concept.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection localized to the lungs; extrapulmonary tuberculosis is a separate disease localization.
Benign smooth muscle neoplasm arising in the kidney; smooth muscle histology does not imply skeletal muscle involvement.
Reproductive-system tumor umbrella has no applicable axis across most patients; endocrine-origin tumors are subtypes.
Sex cord-stromal tumors arise from gonadal endocrine/supporting lineages, including granulosa, theca, Sertoli and Leydig cells; hormone excess is not required for endocrine tumor origin.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: gonadal sex cord/stromal endocrine lineage establishes the axis; secretion is variable ([NCI](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/sex-cord-gonadal-stromal-tumor)).

basis: Carcinoma originates in breast parenchyma, which has no axis; squamous histology does not imply skin origin.
Embryonal tumor arising in the kidney in the vast majority; extrarenal origins are rare.
Carcinoma originates in nasal cavity mucosa; the nasal airway belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the nasopharynx; pharyngeal airways belong to the pulmonary axis.
Dissection directly damages cervical arterial walls; associated cerebral infarction is a separately diagnosed complication.
Intestinal lactase deficiency causes impaired lactose digestion; an inherited carbohydrate metabolic disorder.
Prostate epithelial carcinoma; reproductive origin has no axis. Urinary invasion or metastatic injury is not intrinsic to this histologic variant.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; urinary tract invasion is not established as common.
Most tumors cause sustained cortisol excess; skin atrophy/fragility affects >50%, and myopathy or bone loss roughly 50-80%. These are direct hormonal manifestations; silent tumors are a minority.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent skin atrophy and fragility commonly (>50%) result directly from tumor-driven cortisol excess, rather than representing only a future disease risk.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: cortisol-mediated myopathy and bone loss commonly affect roughly 50-80%; hormone excess is the usual functional expression of this tumor.

basis: Carcinoma originating in the pituitary endocrine gland; Cushing disease and metastatic organ damage are not assumed.
Definition restricts this benign epithelial-stromal neoplasm to female reproductive organs, outside the axes.
Odontogenic origin maps to gastrointestinal; the vast majority of tumors directly occupy and expand jaw bone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: the vast majority are intraosseous, directly occupying jaw bone; tumor occupation qualifies without a separate skeletal diagnosis.

basis: Benign adrenal tumour; its mature hematopoietic tissue does not establish a blood or marrow disorder.
Neuroblastoma originates in the adrenal medulla; the adrenal gland belongs to the metabolic_endocrine axis.
Hyperplasia directly involves the adrenal medulla, an endocrine gland component.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the CNS; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis, and the disease is associated with HIV.
Malignant odontogenic epithelial tumour arising in the tooth-bearing jaws, typically with destructive intraosseous growth.
Melanoma arising in the anus; gastrointestinal site determines the organ label.
Squamous carcinoma arising predominantly in the anal canal; perianal skin origin is a subset. HPV association does not make the carcinoma an infection.
Benign adipose neoplasm usually arising in subcutis. Prominent intratumoral vessels do not establish a cardiovascular disorder.
Benign connective and soft tissue neoplasm; vascular proliferation within the tumor does not establish cardiovascular disease.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the glandular epithelium of the appendix.
Glandular epithelial neoplasm arising in the appendix.
Hyperplastic mucosal polyp arising in the appendix.
Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor originating in the appendix; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Villous epithelial adenoma arises in the appendix.
Low-grade neuroendocrine neoplasm originating in ascending colon; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Tumor arises in thoracic wall soft tissues/periosteum and may occupy pleura, which belongs to pulmonary; lung parenchyma is spared.
Atypical carcinoid principally denotes a pulmonary neuroendocrine tumor. No endocrine-gland origin or metabolic disorder is established; the supplied definition does not specify a site.
audit_reason: Add pulmonary as primary: atypical carcinoid is principally a pulmonary tumor. Remove metabolic_endocrine: neuroendocrine histology alone establishes neither endocrine-gland origin nor a metabolic disorder.

basis: Hyperplasia is confined to the uterine endometrium, a reproductive tissue outside the available axes.
Locally aggressive adipocytic tumor typically arising in deep extremity soft tissue; superficial synonyms do not establish predominantly subcutaneous disease.

decisions.dermatologic: none: subcutaneous variants occur, but this unrestricted concept does not establish common skin or subcutaneous involvement.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: atypical lipomatous tumor typically originates in deep extremity soft tissue associated with the locomotor system.

basis: Lobular epithelial neoplasia confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Adrenal medullary tumour; secondary hypertension (~80-90%) is separately diagnosed. Direct cardiomyopathy occurs in a minority (<15%). Neural crest origin does not imply neurologic injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: secondary hypertension (~80-90%) is a separate diagnosis; direct cardiac injury such as catecholamine cardiomyopathy is uncommon (<15%).

basis: Localized neuroendocrine tumor of peripheral paraganglionic tissue; proximity to the carotid artery does not establish vascular damage.
