Breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Receptor negativity does not establish endocrine-organ disease.
Acute inflammation and necrosis of exocrine pancreatic tissue; distant organ failure occurs in a minority.
Age-defined cancer umbrella has no shared organ of origin; selecting blood, CNS or bone would extrapolate from distinct subtypes.

decisions.haematologic: none: leukemia and other blood malignancies are subtypes; a blood origin does not characterize most cancers across this umbrella.
decisions.neurologic: none: CNS tumors are a subset, not a shared defining site across childhood malignancies.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: bone and soft-tissue sarcomas are subtypes, not a shared organ of origin across this umbrella.

basis: Malignant neoplasm involving the rectum; lymphoma is only a subtype of this umbrella.
Recurrent localized subcutaneous finger hematomas; spontaneous resolution and no established systemic coagulation or vascular disease.
Acne-like cutaneous inflammation; infectious causes represent only part of this etiologically heterogeneous group.
Acquired pathological thickening of skin; heterogeneous causes do not establish a shared infectious or immune mechanism.
Acral dermatitis defines the concept; associated viral infections do not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism throughout this umbrella.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation and association with viral infection alone do not establish infection, autoimmunity or immune-mediated disease across the umbrella.

basis: Chronic cutaneous Borrelia infection causes skin atrophy; associated local peripheral neuropathy occurs in approximately 40-60%.
Allergen-specific delayed hypersensitivity directly causes dermatitis.
Urticarial skin disease defined by type I hypersensitivity.
Loss of sweating is dysfunction of the cutaneous sweat apparatus; no consistent additional organ damage is defined.
A bacterial infection-associated cutaneous eruption defines the condition.
Destructive keratinizing epithelial lesion predominantly occupying the middle ear and mastoid; rare sinus subtypes do not characterize the umbrella.
Cholesteatoma occupies the epitympanic attic of the middle ear.
Destructive keratinizing lesion localized to the external ear.
Destructive keratinizing epithelial lesion of the middle ear; preceding infections do not make the lesion itself an infection.
Mast cell-mediated inducible urticaria is defined by cutaneous wheals triggered by sweating.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss defines this metabolic disorder; intrinsic ectopic hepatic fat accumulation affects most patients, roughly 80-90%.
Pigmented lesions or deposits arise in the conjunctiva.
Diffuse neoplastic overgrowth of adipose tissue, commonly subcutaneous; associated liver disease and treatment exposures are not affected organs.
Recurrent immune-mediated vesicular eczema affecting palms and soles; no qualifying extracutaneous damage.
Skin fragility and blistering define the group; substantial mucosal and other extracutaneous damage varies by subtype.
Blistering and scarring of skin and mucous membranes define DEB, including oral mucosa. Severe esophageal injury varies by subtype and is not assumed across the umbrella.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal blistering and scarring belong to the defining mucocutaneous disease; severe esophageal disease is not required.

basis: Parvovirus B19 infection defined by its cutaneous exanthem; significant blood-cell complications are not typical of fifth disease.
Immune-mediated targetoid skin disease; erosive oral mucositis occurs in roughly 25-60%, near the threshold; lasting ocular damage is uncommon.
Scaly inflammatory disease of the scalp and facial skin; no defined systemic immune mechanism.
Defined by widespread skin eruption; this umbrella does not establish a specific infectious or immune mechanism.
Facial skin disease, supported by its skin-disorder parent; no established extra-cutaneous damage.
Anal fibroepithelial polyp; perianal skin is an alternative origin without evidence that cutaneous disease applies to most cases.

decisions.dermatologic: none: perianal skin is an alternative site; this anal-polyp umbrella does not establish cutaneous origin or involvement in most patients.

basis: Benign polyp arising in the urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
Follicular mucin deposition causes cutaneous lesions and alopecia; associated lymphomas are separate diseases.
Hair-follicle inflammation is usually infectious, most often bacterial. The umbrella rule follows the usual infectious phenotype despite inclusion of sterile subtypes.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most ordinary folliculitis is infectious, usually bacterial; the umbrella rule requires the majority phenotype rather than universal infection.

basis: Chronic disorder of cutaneous apocrine sweat glands and surrounding skin; no established systemic immune mechanism or extra-organ injury.
Immune-mediated granulomatous skin disease; no common direct extracutaneous damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: granuloma annulare is mediated by a cutaneous cellular immune response; an unknown initiating cause does not exclude immune mediation.

basis: Antigen-driven, immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation directly occupies and damages skin.
The supplied definition specifies neutrophilic dermatosis, an immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease; associated systemic illnesses are separate conditions.
Benign blood-vessel neoplasm arising in subcutaneous tissue; both its vascular origin and subcutaneous location are defining.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease associated with pregnancy; pregnancy association does not make it an axis-free obstetric condition.
Chronic immune-mediated follicular skin inflammation causes abscesses, sinus tracts and permanent scarring.
Pigmentation disorder confined to the eyelid, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Benign keratotic tumour arising from follicular structures in the skin.
Direct irritant injury to skin; inflammation does not establish an autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease in children. Associated coeliac enteropathy is a separately diagnosed disease.
Defined by hypertrophy of the skin's stratum corneum; other organ involvement is not shared across this umbrella.
Alloimmune red-cell destruction causes bilirubin brain injury; permanent auditory neuropathy/hearing loss is a major defining feature of chronic kernicterus.

decisions.otologic: involved: permanent auditory neuropathy/hearing loss is a major feature of chronic kernicterus, supporting inclusion independently of a prevalence estimate.

basis: Cutaneous lesions localized to the leg.
Cutaneous lichen encompasses predominantly immune-mediated lichenoid disease, including lichen planus. Genital skin remains dermatologic; common damaging oral involvement is unproven.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immune-mediated cutaneous inflammation characterizes the major lichenoid forms, particularly lichen planus; an identified autoantigen is not required.

basis: Chronic immune-mediated lichenoid inflammation produces persistent cutaneous papules; no common extracutaneous damage.
Immune-mediated skin disease; oral mucosal inflammation or erosions affect ~30-70%. Associated hepatitis C is a separate disease.
Disorder of adipose tissue loss or redistribution, classified as cutaneous and metabolic; systemic complications are not shared across localized and generalized forms.
Diffuse mature adipose tissue overgrowth, predominantly involving subcutaneous tissue; internal organ involvement varies by subtype.
Bacterial cellulitis of the mouth floor and adjacent submandibular spaces; airway compromise is a complication rather than defining airway infection.
Keratinizing lesion originates in maxillary sinus mucosa; sinuses are pulmonary. Possible bone erosion and secondary infection lack qualifying frequency.
Overgrowth arises in mediastinal adipose tissue, outside the listed axes; lung, airway, pleural or cardiovascular damage is not established.
Benign cutaneous proliferation of keratinocytes and melanocytes.
Cutaneous sweat duct obstruction with characteristic skin lesions.
Epidermal sweat-duct obstruction and inflammation cause the defining cutaneous papules.
Congenital dermal melanocytosis confined to skin.
Chronic cutaneous collagen degeneration with granulomatous inflammation, atrophy and ulceration; associated diabetes is a separate disease.
Repeated scratching produces chronic lichenified skin damage; the name does not establish neurologic disease or an immune mechanism.
Repetitive excoriation directly produces skin lesions; the cutaneous damage establishes an organ axis despite the psychiatric mechanism.
Workplace contact dermatitis affects skin; the umbrella includes irritant disease and does not uniformly imply an immune mechanism.
Hyperkeratotic thickening of palmar and plantar skin defines the umbrella; syndromic extracutaneous findings are subtype-dependent.
Inflammation of subcutaneous fat; the umbrella does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Chronic T-cell-mediated inflammatory skin disease; progression to cutaneous lymphoma is a separate later risk.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: parapsoriasis is an immune-mediated cutaneous inflammatory disorder, despite uncertain initiating etiology.

basis: Deep pelvic soft-tissue adipose overgrowth; bladder/ureter compression with obstructive dysfunction occurs in ~30-50%. Constipation alone does not establish bowel damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the proliferating fat is in deep pelvic connective tissue, outside the skin and subcutis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: this deep pelvic mesenchymal soft-tissue proliferation is assigned to the connective-tissue axis.

basis: Autoimmune blistering disease; damaging oral erosions occur in >30% across the group, particularly its common vulgaris form. Other mucosal sites are less consistently affected.
Perinatal jaundice explicitly results from hepatocellular damage.
Immune-mediated delayed hypersensitivity causing eczematous inflammation of light-exposed skin.
Abnormal cutaneous reactions to light; definition excludes ocular photosensitivity and photosensitive epilepsy. Immune mechanisms do not apply across the umbrella.
UV-associated skin injury; phototoxicity is not inherently immune mediated, although the definition also includes photoallergic reactions.
Physical stimuli induce mast-cell-mediated urticaria of the skin; no additional organ damage defines the umbrella.
Self-limited papulosquamous skin disease; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not sufficiently established for an additional mechanism label.
Abnormal epidermal keratinocyte proliferation produces persistent keratotic skin lesions.
Benign cutaneous collagen overgrowth during wound healing.
Chronic facial dermatosis; persistent blepharitis, meibomian dysfunction and ocular surface inflammation affect approximately 30-50%, beyond transient redness.

decisions.ocular: involved: chronic eyelid and ocular surface inflammation occurs in approximately 30-50%; severe corneal destruction is not required for involvement.

basis: Disease of the scalp skin.
Dermal mucin deposition causes skin induration; associated diabetes, infections and malignancies are separate conditions.
Disorder of cutaneous sebaceous glands; eyelid-specific disease is only a subtype.
Chronic inflammatory scaling disorder of skin; not inherently an infection or autoimmune disease.
Seborrheic dermatitis of infant scalp; no defining systemic immune disorder or invasive infection.
Degeneration and thinning of the epidermis and dermis.
Immune-mediated cutaneous granulomas; pulmonary involvement from the same systemic sarcoid process occurs in roughly 50-70% of cutaneous cases, despite some remaining skin-limited.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary granulomatous disease accompanies roughly 50-70% of cutaneous cases and reflects the same sarcoid process; involvement need not be universal.

basis: Diffuse overgrowth of subcutaneous adipose tissue; steroid association alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Pigmentation is located in the corneal stroma and epithelium; no systemic underlying disorder is specified.
Chronic immune-mediated sterile pustular skin disease; associated thyroid disease, arthritis and myeloma are separate disorders and occur in a minority.
Disease of cutaneous sweat glands; these are exocrine skin appendages.
Urushiol causes immune-mediated allergic contact inflammation of the skin.
Defined by skin blistering; infectious, autoimmune and genetic mechanisms vary across subtypes.
Vibration-triggered mast-cell-mediated urticaria and angioedema define a cutaneous immune-mediated disorder; transient swelling does not establish other organ damage.
Viral infection defined by a cutaneous eruption; skin is a defining primary site.
Benign fibroepithelial stromal polyp of the vulva; reproductive organ lesion without an applicable axis.
Benign keratotic neoplasm arising from vulvar skin follicles; cutaneous origin provides an axis despite genital location.
Benign epidermal keratinocytic neoplasm of vulvar skin; the supplied definition establishes a skin lesion despite misleading carcinoma parents.
Urinary bladder dysfunction with urgency and abnormally frequent detrusor contractions.
Altitude-related hypoxemia defines this respiratory disorder; cerebral edema and other severe organ injuries occur in a minority.
Defined by peripheral or autonomic nerve damage; diabetes is the separate underlying disease, and local nerve microangiopathy does not establish another organ disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: diabetic neuropathy labels the nerve complication; the underlying diabetes does not independently establish endocrine organ damage within this concept.

basis: Degenerative structural disease of the hip joint; no infectious or autoimmune mechanism is intrinsic.
Degenerative disease of spinal articular cartilage and adjacent bone; neurologic injury is not intrinsic or established as common.
Degenerative disease of toe joints and adjacent bone.
Degenerative disease of hand joints; an autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Gallbladder inflammation without stones. The definition overrides the erroneous urinary-bladder ancestry; infection is not required.
Adenoma originates in the anterior pituitary endocrine gland; visual or neurologic compression is not established as common across this category.
Bacterial infection with variable anatomical sites; no single organ site is established across the umbrella concept.
Bacterial infection defined by Actinobacillus; no consistent anatomical site is specified.
Necrosis of renal tubular cells causes acute kidney failure.
Herpetic necrotizing retinitis, usually caused by VZV or HSV; retinal vasculitis and detachment remain within the ocular axis.
Carcinoma originates in the adrenal cortex. Metastatic organ damage is not established at >=30%; hypertension, diabetes and lung adenocarcinoma are separate diagnoses.
Defined by excess adrenal cortical hormone production; no other directly damaged organ is established across this umbrella.
Mechanical obstruction of the afferent jejunal loop defines this postoperative gastrointestinal syndrome.
Delirium is acute organic cerebral dysfunction and explicitly belongs to the neurologic axis; autonomic signs do not establish cardiovascular damage.
Alcohol-induced dilated cardiomyopathy directly damages myocardium; other alcohol-associated diseases are separate conditions.
Alcohol-induced fibrosis and cirrhosis directly damage the liver; alcohol exposure alone does not establish other organ disease.
Alcohol-associated damage to peripheral nerves; liver disease and nutritional disorders are separate conditions.
Benign perivascular smooth muscle tumor arising in dermis or subcutis; vascular arrangement alone does not establish cardiovascular disease.
Brain tissue necrosis in the anterior cerebral artery territory; the definition establishes cerebral injury rather than intrinsic arterial disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: the artery identifies the infarct territory; intrinsic vessel disease or thrombosis is not established by this concept.

basis: Compartment pressure causes ischemic necrosis of anterior tibial skeletal muscle.
Optic disc infarction causes permanent visual loss; associated systemic arteritis is a separate disease and not universal.
Anterior spinal arterial ischemia causes infarction and loss of spinal cord function.
Inflammation of the iris/anterior chamber, predominantly immune-mediated; infectious forms also meet the mechanism axis.
Ischemic necrosis of the anterior or anterolateral myocardium.
Inhaled carbon and silica cause pulmonary parenchymal fibrosis.
Coal dust deposition damages lung parenchyma, causing nodules and emphysema.
Structural displacement of aortic valve cusps with potential valvular regurgitation.
Inflammation of the aortic wall is vasculitis, commonly immune-mediated or infectious.
Arteriolar wall thickening narrows vascular lumina; downstream organ ischemia is not universal or specified.
Atherosclerotic obstruction directly damages arteries; hyperlipidemia and hypertension are risk factors rather than additional affected organs.
Localized immune-complex vasculitis characteristically arises in skin/subcutis, producing tissue inflammation and sometimes necrosis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the characteristic lesion is localized cutaneous/subcutaneous immune-complex vasculitis, rather than an incidental transient rash.

basis: Inflammation of the meninges, most commonly from viral infection; no other organ is consistently damaged.
Perinatal gas-exchange failure includes hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy in this record. Direct hypoxic-ischemic renal dysfunction occurs in approximately 40-50%.

decisions.renal: involved: direct renal hypoperfusion and ischemic injury affect approximately 40-50% over the course of clinically significant perinatal asphyxia.

basis: Congenital communication between the atria; respiratory infections are occasional and stroke is very rare.
Persistent gastric gland atrophy; this etiologically unspecified concept does not itself establish an active infection or autoimmune mechanism.
Degeneration and atrophy directly affect the thyroid endocrine gland; an autoimmune cause is not specified.
Bacterial infection and inflammation of the conjunctiva.
Bacterial infection of the endocardium and cardiac valves; embolic organ injuries are minority complications.
Bacterial infection and inflammation of the meninges; lasting hearing damage does not meet the 30% threshold across the umbrella.
Bacteroides bacterial infection; anatomical sites vary, and no particular organ is established across this umbrella.
Inflammation confined to the glans penis, a reproductive organ; this umbrella includes noninfectious causes and does not establish an immune mechanism.
Anterior pituitary epithelial adenoma; basophilic staining does not imply a leukocyte or hematopoietic neoplasm despite erroneous ancestors.
Thiamine deficiency defines the metabolic disorder; peripheral neuropathy and cardiac dysfunction define its dry and wet clinical forms.
Bile reflux affects the stomach, esophagus or pancreas; the definition does not establish liver or bile duct damage.
Calculus located in the urinary bladder.
Obstruction affects the bladder outlet and urinary flow; bladder and urethra belong to the renal axis.
Benign melanocytic neoplasm arising within the dermis.
Umbrella for Borrelia infections; no additional organ damage is established as common across the group.
Immune-mediated inflammatory brachial plexus neuropathy; weakness reflects nerve injury rather than primary muscle disease.
Brachial peripheral nerve plexus disorder; weakness reflects nerve dysfunction rather than primary muscle damage.
Pathologic fluid accumulation and swelling directly affect brain tissue.
Hypoxia and reduced perfusion directly injure the brain; an underlying cardiovascular cause does not establish cardiovascular damage from this concept.
Cerebrovascular ischemic disease causing infarction of brainstem tissue.
Defined oral burning/dysesthesia; taste symptoms are common, but do not establish additional lasting neural damage across this heterogeneous syndrome.
Cotton-dust occupational airway disease; no defining infection or autoimmune mechanism.
Thrombosis directly occupies the carotid artery; cerebral infarction is a separately diagnosed complication, and transient ischemic symptoms do not establish damage.
Direct pontine demyelination. Preceding hyponatremia is a separate electrolyte disorder, not an additional organ affected by myelinolysis.
Defined by disease of intracranial arteries; brain infarction or other neural injury depends on subtype.
Atherosclerotic disease of cerebral arteries; stroke and vascular cognitive impairment are separate potential sequelae.
Epithelial erosion confined to the uterine cervix; reproductive organs have no axis.
Gallstones located in the gallbladder, included in the hepatic axis.
Gallstones occupy the common bile duct; extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Malignant neoplasm of the ocular choroid; vascular ancestry does not establish systemic cardiovascular involvement.
Adenoma originating in the anterior pituitary gland; visual pathway compression is size-dependent and not established as common across this concept.
Immune-mediated demyelination of peripheral nerves and roots; weakness results from neuropathy rather than direct muscle disease.
Autoimmune CNS demyelination defines the group; damaging optic neuritis occurs in roughly 50% over the course of multiple sclerosis, the predominant subtype.

decisions.ocular: involved: optic nerve demyelination directly impairs vision; optic neuritis affects roughly 50% over the course of MS, the predominant disease in this umbrella.

basis: Bacterial infection umbrella with variable anatomical sites; no single organ is consistently affected across the group.
Bacterial infection umbrella without a shared organ site; bacterial vaginosis affects reproductive anatomy outside the organ axes.
Bacterial infection umbrella without a specified organ site shared across the group.
Neoplasm of the extrahepatic common bile duct; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Focal epilepsy with impaired awareness arises from cerebral seizure activity; psychic and motor manifestations do not establish other organ damage.
Pericardial fibrosis and thickening directly restrict cardiac filling; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established.
Edema directly affects the cornea.
Pathological vascular ingrowth into the cornea; infectious and immune causes are alternatives, not defining mechanisms.
Structural aneurysmal dilatation of coronary vessels; an inflammatory cause is not universal.
Narrowing of coronary arteries directly affects the cardiovascular system.
Thrombus within coronary vessels; myocardial injury remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Fibrohistiocytic neoplasm arising in the dermis.
Treponema pallidum infection specifically defined by cutaneous lesions; skin is the primary disease site despite transient secondary eruptions.
Stenosing wrist tenosynovitis affects tendons and their sheaths; association with rheumatoid arthritis does not make this inherently autoimmune.
Developmental dental enamel injury from excess fluoride. Teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis; skeletal fluorosis is a separate condition.
Oral mucosal inflammation from denture irritation; the definition does not establish infection or an immune-mediated mechanism.
Structural abnormality of the diaphragm, a skeletal muscle; elevation alone does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Myocardial relaxation and cardiac filling dysfunction define the disease.
Subaortic fibrous obstruction impairs left ventricular outflow.
Substance-induced psychotic disorder; no specific neurological tissue injury or other axis disease is established.
A drug-induced neurologic movement disorder; medication causation does not exclude the disease's primary axis.
Drug-induced dysfunction of motor control; abnormal muscle movements do not establish primary muscle damage.
Tear-film deficiency and corneal/conjunctival disease; the umbrella is not necessarily autoimmune.
Nonmetastasizing neoplasm originating in the duodenal wall.
Retrograde movement of duodenal contents into the stomach; bile in reflux does not indicate hepatobiliary disease.
Premalignant epithelial dysplasia confined to the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Difficult obstetric labor is outside the 13 axes.
Cutaneous neoplasm arising from eccrine sweat glands.
Experimental transplantable mouse mammary carcinoma, not a human disease; its breast origin has no mapped axis.
Flattening or damage of the pituitary gland defines the condition; its location at the brain base does not establish neural injury.
Localized destruction and atrophy of brain parenchyma.
Iodine deficiency causes thyroid enlargement; no additional organ damage defines endemic goiter.
Mycobacterial infection directly occupies endocrine glands; hepatic involvement is not established across the concept.
Endolymph accumulation distorts cochlear and vestibular structures, causing sensorineural hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction.
Tumor originates in uterine or other reproductive stromal tissue, outside the organ axes.
Endocardial fibrosis causes restrictive cardiomyopathy and atrioventricular valve dysfunction.
Melanocytic malignancy assigned to the usual cutaneous origin; the supplied definition specifies histology without establishing an ocular site.
Organism-defined bacterial infection; most human cases (>50%) involve direct cutaneous infection as erysipeloid. Endocarditis is uncommon.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: localized cutaneous erysipeloid accounts for most human infections (>50%); this genus-wide concept is defined by its pathogen rather than a required skin location.

basis: Erysipelothrix infection most commonly presents as localized cutaneous erysipeloid; systemic infection and endocarditis are minority presentations.
E. coli infection directly inflames the meninges; neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary injury.
Multiple structural diverticula of the esophagus.
Altered thyroid hormone metabolism during non-thyroidal illness; underlying illnesses do not establish additional organ involvement.
Obstruction of extrahepatic bile flow; extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Mycobacterial infection warrants the infectious mechanism axis; the affected reproductive organs have no anatomical axis.
Disease of the femoral peripheral nerve.
Maternal alloantibodies cause fetal or neonatal red-cell destruction; permanent neurologic injury is a minority complication.
Structural arterial-wall disease; renal-artery involvement remains cardiovascular. Renal damage and stroke are not established in at least 30%.
Fibrosis and adhesion of the shoulder joint capsule cause persistent restriction of movement; no established autoimmune mechanism.
Fungal infection of the meninges; immunodeficiency may predispose but is not inherent to every case.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable sites; no single anatomical organ is established as commonly affected across the group.
Disordered cerebral planning of walking; the definition excludes primary sensory impairment or muscle weakness.
Pathologic ectasia of gastric antral vessels; associated liver, renal and autoimmune diseases are separate conditions.
Defined by impaired gastric motility and delayed stomach emptying.
Localized giant-cell-rich lesion arising within bone.
Inflammation of the tongue; oral tissues belong to the gastrointestinal axis. Infection or autoimmunity is not inherent.
Neoplasm defined by gonadal germ-cell, sex-cord or stromal tissue; no covered anatomical site or endocrine dysfunction is specified.
Recurrent spontaneous pregnancy loss is an obstetric/reproductive condition outside the axes.
Defective desquamation and elongated filiform papillae affect the tongue, an oral gastrointestinal structure.
Cutaneous melanocytic nevus with immune-mediated melanocyte destruction producing the characteristic depigmented halo.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immune-mediated destruction of nevus and surrounding melanocytes produces the defining halo; this is intrinsic to the lesion.

basis: Structural aneurysmal abnormality of the myocardial wall.
Helicobacter infection directly involves gastric and proximal duodenal mucosa.
Blood retained within the uterus is a reproductive-organ disorder, not a blood-cell or coagulation disease.
Air and blood occupy the pleural cavity; pleural bleeding does not itself constitute a blood-cell or coagulation disorder.
Vitamin K deficiency causes defective coagulation; impaired factor production does not establish intrinsic liver damage. Intracranial injury is not universal across forms.
Thrombosis of hepatic veins defines a vascular disorder obstructing liver venous outflow; fibrosis is not required.
Benign cystic proliferation of cutaneous sweat glands.
Biochemical enzyme elevation without established pancreatic or salivary injury; serum location does not imply blood-cell, marrow or coagulation disease.
Excess cementum formation is a disorder of tooth hard tissue.
Defined by severe, intractable vomiting with dehydration, weight loss and electrolyte derangement; digestive dysfunction and metabolic disturbance have axes despite the obstetric setting.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: severe intractable vomiting defines pathological digestive dysfunction; primary classification does not require structural gastrointestinal injury.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: electrolyte imbalance and dehydration are explicit defining manifestations; electrolyte disorders fall within this axis.

basis: Immune-complex cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis causes recurrent purpura; elevated polyclonal globulins do not establish a blood-cell disorder.
Anterior pituitary hormone hypersecretion; downstream organ damage varies with the hormone and subtype.
Immune-mediated small-vessel inflammation with characteristic cutaneous disease; internal-organ damage is not common across the umbrella.
Splenic hyperfunction causes excessive blood-cell destruction; spleen as a blood organ belongs to the hematologic axis.
Brain dysfunction caused by severe hypertension defines this hypertensive neurovascular disorder.
Vitamin A excess is a nutritional metabolic disorder; damaging skin, liver and skeletal manifestations vary across acute and chronic presentations.

decisions.dermatologic: none: persistent epithelial injury is characteristic of chronic toxicity, but a frequency of at least 30% across this umbrella is not established.

basis: Neoplasm occupying the hypothalamus, a brain structure; endocrine dysfunction is not established across this umbrella.
Acquired impairment of learned motor actions from disruption of cortical motor-planning connections.
Neoplasm arising in the ileal wall; lymphoma is only one possible subtype.
Inappropriate ADH secretion produces disordered water and sodium balance; underlying tumour location and transient neurologic symptoms do not add axes.
Infarction directly damages the inferior myocardial wall.
Defining dermal lymphatic tumour infiltration causes persistent skin edema and induration. Breast origin has no axis; the name does not indicate immune inflammation.
Unstable angina is a coronary artery disease syndrome; no other organ is intrinsically affected.
Predominantly immune-mediated inflammation of the intermediate uvea; macular edema remains within the ocular axis; systemic associations are separate diseases.
Rupture directly damages the small or large intestinal wall.
Disease of intracranial arteries; brain infarction or other parenchymal damage is not required across this vascular umbrella.
Embolic obstruction of intracranial vessels classified as ischemic stroke; vascular obstruction and cerebral ischemic injury define the disease.
Elevated intracranial cerebrospinal fluid pressure defines the condition; this is not systemic vascular hypertension. Permanent visual injury is not universal.
Disorder of cerebrospinal fluid pressure. Occasional hearing loss or abducens palsy does not establish common additional organ damage.
Intracranial arterial constriction and resulting cerebral ischemia define the condition; permanent hypoxic-ischemic injury is not required for primary neurologic assignment.
audit_reason: Add neurologic to primary: cerebral ischemia is explicitly part of the definition. Defining brain dysfunction does not require permanent infarction; cardiovascular remains primary for arterial vasospasm.

basis: Benign proliferation of melanocytic nevus cells within the dermis.
Inflammation directly affects the iris; the generic concept does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated etiology.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: iris inflammation alone does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease; the generic concept also includes traumatic and etiologically unspecified forms.

basis: Malignant neoplasm originating in the jejunum.
Defined as a disorder of skeletal joints; immune mechanisms do not apply to every subtype.
Malignant bone-forming tumour arising on the bone surface.
Necrosis directly destroys the renal cortex; possible causes do not establish additional affected organs.
Necrosis of renal papillae, potentially impairing concentration and obstructing urinary drainage.
Primary testicular endocrine failure defines the syndrome; developmental language and learning impairments occur in over 50%.
Acquired transmissible prion infection causing progressive cerebellar and cerebral neuronal loss.
Protein deficiency with defining skin/hair abnormalities and hepatic fatty infiltration, necrosis or fibrosis; both organ manifestations appear in the disease's own definition.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic fatty infiltration and associated liver injury are explicitly part of the disease definition.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: nutritional skin and hair abnormalities are defining features, also reflected in the supplied synonyms.

basis: Vertebral or PICA vascular occlusion produces lateral medullary infarction; dysphagia reflects brainstem injury rather than gastrointestinal damage.
Destructive nasal/sinus lesion is predominantly NK/T-cell lymphoma, a blood-cell neoplasm. Palatal destruction is explicitly part of the defining lesion, qualifying without a frequency estimate.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the vast majority are malignant NK/T-cell lymphoproliferations, constituting a disease of blood cells even at an extranodal site.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: palatal destruction is part of the explicit disease definition; three primary slots are occupied by nasal origin and mandatory lymphoma mechanism axes.

basis: Reactive marked leukocytosis with immature neutrophil forms; the supplied definition overrides the erroneous plasma-cell-neoplasm ancestry.
Localized keratotic epithelial lesion of glans/preputial skin; genital location does not exclude a cutaneous lesion. Infection is only a risk factor.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: leukoplakia affects the surface epithelium of the glans or prepuce, rather than reproductive function.

basis: Leukocyte aggregates obstruct microvessels; pulmonary injury and cerebral ischemic dysfunction each occur in roughly 30% or more of symptomatic cases.
Enlargement of ectopic thyroid tissue defines the disease; tongue location does not establish oral tissue damage. Airway obstruction is not established as common.
Malignancy of the lip is classified here as oral cavity cancer; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Immune-mediated podocyte injury causes nephrotic syndrome; edema and lipid abnormalities do not establish additional directly damaged organs.
Listeria infection directly inflames the meninges and may involve brain tissue.
Glaucomatous optic nerve injury with visual loss despite normal intraocular pressure; optic nerve disease belongs to ocular here.
Cutaneous tuberculosis; nasal and buccal mucosal infection described as typical in supplied definition; conjunctival involvement omitted at four-axis cap.
Defined by atrial septal defect combined with acquired mitral stenosis; an immune etiology is not required.
Structural dilatation of lymphatic vessels, classified as vascular ectasia; organ-specific involvement depends on location.
Benign cutaneous lymphatic vessel proliferation producing persistent skin plaques.
Neoplasm featuring lymphatic vessel proliferation and associated smooth muscle; pulmonary involvement is site-dependent, not universal.
Structural defect of the retinal macula.
Magnesium deficiency is a mineral and electrolyte disorder; cramps, nausea and confusion do not establish common additional organ damage.
Mycobacterial infection of male reproductive organs; renal or pulmonary disease is not established by this genital-site concept.
Severe hypertension with acute vascular injury; renal dysfunction occurs in >30%, and advanced retinopathy is a classic defining criterion. Encephalopathy is less common.
Definition specifies malignant lymphoid tissue, supporting lymphoma axes; the misleading name does not establish a vascular-origin tumour.
Severe protein-energy deficiency causes skeletal-muscle catabolism and wasting in most patients.
Breast is outside the organ axes; mastitis includes sterile obstructive inflammation, so infection or autoimmunity is not defining.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this umbrella includes noninfectious obstructive inflammation; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Neoplasm of the maxillary sinus, an upper respiratory site; jaw involvement and lymphoma are not universal across this umbrella.
Meconium directly obstructs and inflames neonatal lungs; pulmonary hypertension is occasional and encephalopathy very rare.
Malignant cartilage-forming tumor arises in bone or soft connective tissue; unspecified distant metastases do not establish another organ.
Mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm involving connective tissues; no specific visceral organ of origin is established.
Mesenteric vessel obstruction; qualifying bowel injury is not established in >=30% across this broad concept. Ischemic bowel disease can be separately diagnosed.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: obstruction or stenosis alone does not establish bowel damage; >=30% qualifying injury is unsupported, and ischemic bowel disease is a distinct consequence.

basis: Pleural origin predominates across mesothelial tumours; peritoneal and other locations represent minority subgroups.
Cerebral arterial disease causing infarction and permanent injury of brain tissue in the middle cerebral artery territory.
Defined by disease of the mouth, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Tumor of immature myeloid blood cells; extramedullary sites vary, with no single additional organ established as commonly involved.
Defined by skeletal-muscle trigger points and regional myofascial dysfunction; referred pain does not establish other-organ damage.
Malignant mesenchymal soft-tissue tumor; no specific visceral or cutaneous site is established.
Necrotizing lesion of minor salivary glands; local ischemic inflammation does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease.
Bacterial infection directly causes necrosis and ulceration of gingival tissue; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Maternal antibodies impair neuromuscular transmission; respiratory and swallowing weakness do not establish intrinsic lung or gastrointestinal damage.
Intestinal evacuation dysfunction is defined as resulting from impaired neural control or nerve damage.
Nodular enlargement arises within the thyroid gland, regardless of hormone production.
Predominantly ovarian or testicular germ-cell tumor, outside the axes; pineal origin is a minority. Potential metastatic sites do not establish common organ involvement.
Umbrella of nutrient and energy deficiencies; specific blood, bone, eye or other organ damage is subtype-dependent rather than common across the group.
Obstruction of intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts causes cholestasis and jaundice; both belong to the hepatic axis.
Elevated intraocular pressure is an eye disorder; it is not systemic arterial hypertension.
Tuberculous infection directly involves ocular tissues; pulmonary disease is not inherent to this extrapulmonary diagnosis.
Ovarian inflammation is generally infectious; autoimmune forms share the immune mechanism axis. Ovarian reproductive anatomy has no axis.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable anatomical sites; no single organ site is established across the group.
The supplied definition describes optic-disc edema with potential visual loss; it does not establish an autoimmune mechanism or primary brain disease.
Defined by intracellular edema and structural changes of the buccal mucosa.
Infection of orbital tissues; adjacent sinus infection is a source rather than an obligatory manifestation.
Defined as viral or bacterial infection of the testes; reproductive location has no axis, and common endocrine failure is not established.
Malignancy originating in the lung apex; possible Pancoast syndrome does not establish direct nerve damage in at least 30% across this concept.
Suppurative infection involving the eye with scleral necrosis and possible orbital extension.
Carcinoma originates in the thyroid gland.
Parametrial infection is a form of pelvic inflammatory disease; its reproductive anatomical site has no axis.
Paraneoplastic peripheral nerve injury, generally mediated by an immune response to the distant tumor.
Entrapment of the penile foreskin affects reproductive anatomy outside the axes; urinary tract disease is not defining.
Benign tumour arising in the parathyroid gland. Bone and renal complications belong to associated hyperparathyroidism and are not intrinsic tumour occupation.
Focal epilepsy defined by motor seizures; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Focal cerebral seizures; sensory manifestations do not establish damage to eyes or ears.
Pasteurella infection with hemorrhagic sepsis; human data do not establish common lasting damage to any specific additional organ.
A disorder defined by pain and dysfunction of the patellofemoral joint; cartilage damage is not required.
Neoplasm of a reproductive organ; urethral or skin involvement is not established across this umbrella.
Reflux causes direct inflammatory injury of the oesophageal mucosa; this is not an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Chronic inflammatory destruction around a dental root, usually driven by infection of necrotic pulp.
Inflammation affects periarticular tissues. Inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.
Localized bacterial infection and inflammation of gingiva surrounding a tooth crown; gingiva belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inflammation of tissues surrounding the kidney; nonspecific inflammation alone does not establish infection or an immune-mediated mechanism.
Neoplastic occupation of the peritoneum; no additional organ involvement is established across this heterogeneous group.
Loss of peripheral peroneal nerve function; resulting weakness does not establish a separate primary muscle disorder.
Constriction of the penile foreskin is a reproductive disorder; urinary tract damage is not intrinsic or established as common.
Benign melanocytic proliferation located in the skin.
Benign cutaneous epithelial neoplasm arising from the follicular sheath.
Pituitary infarction/hemorrhage; chiasmal dysfunction causes hemianopia in 80-99%, and cranial nerve paralysis occurs in 30-79%. These localize to neurologic structures.

decisions.ocular: none: typical bitemporal hemianopia arises from optic chiasm compression; ocular motor palsies reflect cranial nerve injury rather than direct eye damage.

basis: Pituitary growth hormone deficiency causes proportionate growth failure; short stature alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Gas-filled cysts within the intestinal wall; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to this concept.
Pneumococcal infection directly affects the meninges; lasting hearing loss is generally below 30% overall, although rates vary by age and severity.
Peripheral nerve and nerve-root injury defines the concept; immune-mediated forms are subtypes, and the umbrella does not specify an immune mechanism.
Postcholecystectomy biliary syndrome; the urinary-bladder parent is inconsistent with the definition. Abdominal symptoms alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Ischemic brain necrosis in a cerebral arterial territory; visual field loss reflects brain injury rather than direct ocular damage.
Inflammation damages the choroid, retina and vitreous; infectious or immune-mediated ocular disease.
Potassium depletion is an electrolyte disorder; severe muscle injury and hypokalemic nephropathy are not established in at least 30% across the condition.
Disordered glucose metabolism; future diabetes and vascular complications are risks rather than defining organ damage.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable anatomical sites; no additional organ is consistently affected across the group.
Bacterial infection targets circulating leukocytes; hepatocellular injury with elevated aminotransferases occurs in roughly 50-90% of common human anaplasmosis/ehrlichiosis cases.

decisions.hepatic: involved: direct hepatocellular injury occurs in roughly 50-90% of the common human infections represented by this umbrella.

basis: Bacterial infection umbrella with variable anatomical sites; no additional organ is consistently affected across the group.
Bacterial infection umbrella; no particular damaged organ is consistently established across its clinical forms.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable anatomical sites; no single organ consistently affected across the group.
Bacterial infection umbrella with diverse sites; no single anatomical organ is established across the group.
Rickettsiaceae infection characteristically targets vascular endothelium, causing small-vessel vasculitis. Transient rash does not establish additional skin damage.
Proteus infections predominantly affect the urinary tract (>30%); direct cystitis or pyelonephritis supports urinary-organ involvement.

decisions.renal: involved: urinary infections are the predominant clinical presentation (>30%); these are direct Proteus infections, rather than a later disease risk.

basis: Upper motor neuron injury affecting bulbar function; swallowing impairment does not itself establish gastrointestinal tissue damage.
A solitary pulmonary tissue lesion; infection and malignancy are alternative causes, not universal mechanisms.
Fluid accumulation in lung tissue impairs gas exchange. Heart failure is a possible underlying cause, not an organ damaged by pulmonary edema.
Tumor-like lesion occupies lung; inflammatory histology alone does not establish infection or an immune-mediated disorder.
Congenital obstruction within the right ventricular outflow tract; pulmonary refers to cardiac outflow, not lung disease.
Structural narrowing of a cardiac valve obstructs right ventricular outflow; pulmonary in the name identifies the valve, not lung disease.
Inflammation of dental pulp, usually driven by bacterial infection; classified here as a bacterial infectious disease.
Inflammation of the renal pelvis, usually caused by bacterial urinary tract infection.
Bacterial or fungal infection directly inflames the kidney; the definition overrides the inconsistent uterine parent and synonym.
Direct lesion of the radial peripheral nerve; associated weakness is neurologic rather than primary skeletal muscle disease.
Bacterial infection with inflammatory arthritis in 30-79%; rash is transient, while septic arthritis and cardiac or CNS complications are uncommon.
Inherited amino-acid transport disorders impair proximal renal tubular reabsorption; renal location and inborn metabolic mechanism define the group.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: inherited defects of amino-acid transport qualify as inborn metabolic disorders, even without systemic metabolic complications.

basis: Obstruction affects renal arteries; kidney parenchymal injury is not inherent, and ischemic nephropathy is a separately diagnosed consequence.
Disordered bone mineralization and remodeling define this metabolic bone disease; chronic kidney disease is its separately diagnosed underlying cause.

decisions.renal: none: kidney disease causes the osteodystrophy; osteodystrophy does not itself directly damage the kidneys.

basis: Renal artery stenosis and resulting hypertension are vascular disease; renal parenchymal damage is not required.
Occlusion of a retinal artery directly defines both an ocular and arterial vascular disorder.
Deposits beneath retinal pigment epithelium define an ocular condition; no other organ involvement is established.
Inflammation of retinal blood vessels defines ocular vasculitis; underlying systemic diseases are separate diagnoses.
Occlusion of retinal venous circulation defines both an ocular disorder and a vascular occlusive disease.
Retinal vascular disease with potential scarring and detachment; prematurity does not establish other organ involvement.
Alloimmune sensitization against red-cell Rh antigens defines this blood-group incompatibility; fetal complications are not assumed.
Poststreptococcal immune-mediated cardiac injury causes characteristic valvular damage.
Broad infectious umbrella; vascular, blood-cell and other organ involvement varies by pathogen and is not established across most of the group.
Cariogenic bacterial biofilm causes destruction of tooth-root cementum and dentin; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Disease of the sciatic nerve; pain and weakness reflect neuropathy rather than a separate primary muscle lesion.
Infectious prion disease causing fatal nervous-system degeneration in sheep and goats; this is not a human disease.
Sebaceous gland carcinoma arises in skin or ocular adnexal glands; eyelid origin is common. Metastatic sites are not inherent organ labels.
Benign or malignant tumor arising from sebaceous glands of the skin.
Secondary PTH excess commonly causes skeletal demineralization/high-turnover bone injury (~30-60%); underlying kidney disease is a cause, not direct involvement.
Periostitis, osteitis and arthropathy define the disease; underlying pulmonary or cardiac conditions are separate diseases.
Secondary dysfunction of central motor pathways causing parkinsonism; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to the umbrella concept.
Mechanical compression and inflammation of rotator cuff tendons and the subacromial bursa.
Definition specifies infection of salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Calculus within a salivary gland or duct; salivary structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Neoplasm arising in the sigmoid colon.
Inhaled nitrogen oxides directly injure the lungs, causing toxic alveolitis/pneumonitis.
Carcinoma originates in cutaneous sweat glands, sebaceous glands or hair follicles.
Mesenchymal malignancy encompassing bone and soft-tissue sarcomas; no other organ site is shared across the umbrella.
Delta-cell NET originates in endocrine pancreas (~60%) or bowel (~40%); direct somatostatin-mediated gallbladder dysfunction occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: sustained somatostatin-mediated gallbladder dysfunction represents direct loss of function; HPO frequency 30-79%.

basis: Benign epididymal cyst confined to the male reproductive system.
Splenic tissue necrosis caused by failure or obstruction of its arterial or venous blood supply.
Ovarian teratoma containing thyroid tissue; reproductive origin has no axis, and functional thyrotoxicosis occurs in a minority.
Bacterial infection of the endocardium; embolic and renal complications do not consistently meet the involvement threshold.
Postviral immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation destroys thyroid follicles and disrupts hormone function; a proven active infection or autoimmune antibody is not required.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: subacute granulomatous thyroiditis involves immune-mediated follicular destruction, usually after a viral illness; the axis includes non-autoimmune immune-mediated disease.

basis: Subclavian arterial stenosis with reversed vertebral flow; neurologic symptoms are transient without chronic neurologic damage.
Suppurative infection in the intracranial or spinal subdural space.
Thyroid enlargement defines the disease; direct tracheal compression and narrowing occur commonly, approximately 30% or more.
Structural narrowing of the left ventricular outflow tract below the aortic valve.
Abnormal sulfur-containing hemoglobin impairs blood oxygen carriage; cyanosis alone does not establish pulmonary or cardiovascular damage.
Infectious abscess in tissues surrounding a tooth root; teeth and periodontal tissues fall within gastrointestinal.
Suppurative intraocular infection, usually bacterial and occasionally fungal.
Treponema pallidum infection directly damages the aorta and potentially the aortic valve.
Myocardial systolic dysfunction defines the disease; congestion alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Compression neuropathy of the posterior tibial nerve and its branches; surrounding tissue inflammation does not establish a separate damaged organ.
Spinal cord tethering causes progressive neurologic dysfunction. Incontinence and leg weakness do not alone establish intrinsic bladder or muscle damage.
Severe thyrotoxicosis; heart failure occurs in roughly 40%, and encephalopathy is a major diagnostic feature. Tachycardia alone does not qualify.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: acute cardiac decompensation, including heart failure in roughly 40%, represents direct organ dysfunction during the storm.
decisions.neurologic: involved: toxic encephalopathy, delirium or impaired consciousness is a major diagnostic feature and represents cerebral dysfunction.

basis: Tibial peripheral nerve injury causes sensory loss and weakness; weakness does not establish a primary muscle disorder.
Malignant neoplasm of the tonsil, a pharyngeal structure. Lymphoma is only one subtype and does not define this umbrella.
Teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis under the supplied mapping, despite the skeletal ontology parent.
Treponemal bacterial infection umbrella; persistent damage to a particular organ is not shared across most patients.
Tricuspid valve leaflet prolapse causes valvular insufficiency.
Disease of the fourth cranial nerve; impaired eye movement does not establish direct damage to the eye.
Immune-complex-mediated tissue injury; no additional organ consistently affected across this umbrella.
Immune-mediated ulcerative inflammation of the rectum and sigmoid colon; no additional organ is commonly directly damaged.
Peripheral mononeuropathy directly affecting the ulnar nerve.
Ureaplasma infection of the urethra, supported by the urethritis and bacterial urinary infection ancestry.
Renal failure causes retention of uremic toxins. Separately diagnosed neuropathy, pericarditis and other variable complications do not justify additional axes.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: retained metabolic waste reflects failed renal clearance; it does not independently establish an endocrine or metabolic disease.

basis: Calculus located in the ureter, which is covered by the renal axis; mineral composition does not establish a metabolic disease.
Sarcoid inflammation of uvea and parotid defines the syndrome; facial nerve palsy is a major diagnostic feature of Heerfordt syndrome.
Acquired transmissible prion disease causing progressive spongiform degeneration of the brain.
Defined by defective penile arterial inflow or venous occlusive function, establishing vascular dysfunction.
Vibrio infections predominantly occupy the intestinal tract and cause enteric dysfunction, especially cholera; wound infection and septicemia characterize a smaller subset.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal infection is the predominant disease location across Vibrio infections, including cholera; it represents the infection site rather than a secondary complication.

basis: Viral infection directly inflames the meninges surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
Vitamin deficiency with retinal dysfunction, night blindness and xerophthalmia explicitly included in its definition and cardinal clinical manifestations.

decisions.ocular: primary: night blindness and xerophthalmia are cardinal defining manifestations explicitly included in the disease definition.

basis: Separation of vitreous from retina is confined to the eye; inherited-neurologic ancestry does not establish extraocular disease.
Inflammation confined to the reproductive vulva; generic inflammation alone does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease.
Generic inflammation of vulva and vagina, both reproductive sites; an infectious or immune-mediated cause is not specified.
Thiamine-deficiency encephalopathy damages brainstem and diencephalic tissue; ophthalmoplegia reflects central neurologic injury.
Chronic bacterial infection directly destroys renal parenchyma.
Enteric Yersinia infections account for most clinical yersiniosis; direct intestinal inflammation exceeds 30% across the group. Plague-specific damage is not generalized.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: enterocolitica and pseudotuberculosis enteric infections dominate clinical yersiniosis, making intestinal inflammation common overall (>30%).

basis: Yersinia pseudotuberculosis typically causes intestinal infection with terminal ileitis and mesenteric lymphadenitis.
Primary syphilitic infection defined by a localized indurated, eroded cutaneous or mucocutaneous sore.
Steatosis with hepatocyte injury and inflammation defines liver disease; associated obesity and diabetes are separate conditions.
Rotator cuff tendon and skeletal muscle injury localized to the shoulder.
Hearing and ear malformations plus renal malformations define the syndrome; renal hypoplasia/aplasia is frequent. Other organ defects are occasional.
Faciodigitogenital syndrome with defining skeletal and digital abnormalities; genital abnormalities do not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Inherited aneurysmal disease of the abdominal aortic wall.
Urinary malformations and absent abdominal musculature define disease; lung hypoplasia is annotated at 80-99%. Xerostomia in a selected 6-patient series is not established across the syndrome.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: xerostomia in 6/6 reflects a small, selected CHRM3-associated series; common salivary dysfunction across the prune-belly umbrella is not established.

basis: Sixth cranial nerve dysfunction causes impaired eye movement; this does not establish direct injury to ocular tissue.
Scalp aplasia and limb/skull defects define AOS; cardiac malformations and hydrocephalus each annotated 30-79%. Ocular defects (30-79%) omitted at cap, prioritizing severe cardiac and brain disease.

decisions.neurologic: involved: hydrocephalus is annotated 30-79%; retained for potentially severe brain injury despite less frequent intellectual disability and seizures.
decisions.ocular: none: cataract and microphthalmia are annotated 30-79%, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of cardiac malformations and hydrocephalus.

basis: Defined cutaneous thickening and pigmentation; associated endocrine disorders or malignancies are separate conditions.
Connective-tissue syndrome defined by arachnodactyly, joint laxity and craniofacial skeletal abnormalities.
Defining skeletal dysplasia; hearing impairment 30-79%. Spinal stenosis alone does not establish neural damage; isolated severe pulmonary findings are not typical.
Inherited dysregulation of the light-triggered sneeze reflex; no ocular injury or chronic airway damage established.
Neural tumors define disease; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%, cataracts in 81/148, and cutaneous schwannomas in ~60%. Pigment spots alone do not qualify.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous schwannomas occur in approximately 60% and constitute direct tumor occupation of skin; this does not rely on cafe-au-lait spots.

basis: Craniosynostosis, limb skeletal defects and congenital heart defects define the syndrome; respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Craniosynostosis and syndactyly define it; hearing loss 80-99%, strabismus 23/34, intellectual disability 30-79%; dental malocclusion 11/13 omitted at cap.
Craniosynostosis, syndactyly, ptosis and strabismus define disease. Hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%; external ear shape alone does not establish functional damage.
Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define the syndrome; ptosis occurs in 80-99%, and tracheal cartilaginous sleeve in 20/20 annotated patients.
Skeletal dysplasia and hormone resistance define disease. Developmental delay 2/2; hearing impairment 1/2. Renal agenesis 1/3 omitted under cap; estimates use small samples.
Craniofacial/limb dysostosis, microcephaly and frequent dental caries are defining features; intellectual disability and dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: frequent caries are explicitly part of the defining phenotype; dental and palatal abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: defining microcephaly, the intellectual-disability parent and intellectual disability in 80-99% establish a neurodevelopmental component.

basis: Persistent palmoplantar keratotic papules and plaques with hair changes; associated atopic tendency does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Inherited keratoderma with epidermal hyperkeratosis and dermal elastic-fiber abnormalities; intestinal synonyms conflict with the definition.
Inherited keratinization disorder affecting skin and nails.
Hereditary symmetric acral depigmentation; no supplied evidence establishes another affected organ.
Defining scalp folds, corneal leukoma and skeletal overgrowth/periostosis. Acromegaloid appearance alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Defining skeletal changes, joint hypermobility and thickened intraoral mucosa; intellectual disability reported in 1/5, below threshold.
Hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma; acromegaly and associated cardiovascular diseases are separately diagnosed consequences.
Congenital skin dimples over the acromial region; no skeletal disease is established.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; decreased nerve conduction velocity in 30-79% supports peripheral nerve dysfunction.
Degeneration and resorption of the distal phalangeal bones.
Osteolysis and osteoporosis define disease; periodontitis occurs in 80-99% and conductive hearing impairment in 9/9; renal and cardiovascular damage is not established as common.
Skeletal dysplasia with carpal/tarsal fusion and digital anomalies; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%; thoracic shape alone is not lung injury.
Distal limb and renal malformations define the syndrome; ocular and palatal abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and globozoospermia; reproductive function lies outside the axes.
Congenital unilateral digital and metacarpal reduction; nail remnants accompany the absent or hypoplastic digits.
