decisions.neurologic: involved: intrinsic metabolic neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in roughly 30-50%; motor delay 1/1 supports this, independently of infectious complications.

basis: Hereditary anemia attributed to erythrocyte ATPase deficiency; the supplied evidence establishes a red-cell disorder without a distinct metabolic disease.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: an erythrocyte ATPase defect causing anemia does not alone establish a metabolic disorder warranting this additional axis.

basis: Inherited pyruvate metabolism abnormality expressed in erythrocytes, with increased red-cell ATP and polycythemia.
Purine metabolic disorder defined by developmental impairment and seizures; strabismus in 4/7 patients does not establish direct ocular damage or visual loss.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus affects 4/7 patients, but misalignment alone does not demonstrate direct ocular damage or visual loss.

basis: Painful subcutaneous lipomas define disease. Arthralgia and abdominal pain do not establish tissue damage; neuropathy is occasional, and metabolic conditions may co-occur.
Congenital chronic primary adrenal cortical insufficiency; no autoimmune mechanism or additional organ damage is established.
Skin/nail dysplasia, limb malformations and dental defects define syndrome; nasolacrimal obstruction occurs in 80-99%.
Tongue hypoplasia and limb reduction define the syndrome. Nail morphology abnormalities (30-79%) lack evidence of functional damage; intellectual disability is below 30%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: abnormal fingernail morphology occurs in 30-79%, but this nonspecific finding does not establish direct skin or nail damage or loss of function.

basis: Constricting cutaneous fibrotic band causes progressive destruction and autoamputation of a digit.
Congenital lacrimal apparatus dysfunction causing absent tears and possible corneal epithelial damage.
Defined by congenital sensorineural deafness and generalized skin, hair and ocular hypopigmentation.
Hormone resistance and AHO skeletal defects; intellectual disability and cataracts each 30-79%. Subcutaneous ossification (2/2) and enamel defects (30-79%) omitted under cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts are damaging lens disease reported in 30-79%; retained under the cap because of their visual consequences.
decisions.dermatologic: none: characteristic subcutaneous ossification qualifies, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of common cognitive and visual impairment.

basis: Substance-use disorder; alcoholic liver disease, neuropathy and other organ complications are separately diagnosed conditions.
Inherited aldosterone excess with defining hypertension in 80-99%. Stroke, retinopathy and ventricular hypertrophy are occasional, separately recognized complications.
Autoimmune injury to hair follicles causes patchy or extensive alopecia; associated nail changes remain dermatologic.
Keratoderma, alopecia and nail disease define it; frequent hand-contracture annotations conflict with the definition excluding hand complications.
Permanent universal alopecia, intellectual disability/epilepsy and destructive periodontal disease define the syndrome; hearing impairment is occasional.
Inherited glomerular basement-membrane disease. Subtype-specific hearing loss occurs in 5-29%; damaging ocular abnormalities are rare.
Central neurologic disorder with episodic paralysis, seizures and intellectual disability; nystagmus does not establish primary eye damage.
APP-associated Alzheimer neurodegeneration; vascular amyloid deposition alone does not establish common functional vascular damage.
Alzheimer neurodegeneration with dementia and neurofibrillary tangles; APOE association alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Ureteral triplication and the characteristic vertebral, hip and limb malformations define urinary and skeletal involvement. Cardiac and neurologic frequencies are unknown; amastia has no axis.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the constellation of hemivertebrae, scoliosis, congenital hip dislocation and limb malformations constitutes the syndrome's skeletal dysmorphism.

basis: Congenital absence or transverse reduction of limbs defines musculoskeletal malformation; no additional organ disease is documented.
Inherited dental enamel hypoplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Developmental dental enamel disorder; enamel hypoplasia in 11/11 patients. Teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited dental enamel hypoplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defining enamel defects and nail/sweat-gland abnormalities, predominantly reported at 80-99%; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Amenorrhea with galactorrhea is an endocrine syndrome of prolactin excess and suppression of gonadal function.
Inherited amyloid disorder with corneal and nerve disease; skin disease 80-99%. Hearing, salivary and cardiac involvement (30-79%) omitted by cap; severe renal disease uncommon overall.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: arrhythmias occur in 30-79%, but more prevalent skin disease takes the remaining place under the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutis laxa and other persistent cutaneous amyloid manifestations are very frequent (80-99%).
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary gelsolin amyloidosis is an inherited disorder of protein processing and amyloid accumulation.

basis: Cerebral arterial amyloid deposition with recurrent intracerebral hemorrhage defines the disease. Systemic deposits alone do not establish functional damage elsewhere.
Hereditary amyloid protein deposition predominantly damages kidneys; GI involvement 30-79%; liver dysfunction, heart failure and neuropathy <30%.
Hereditary amyloid storage defines neuropathy and cardiomyopathy; nephropathy occurs in 30-79%. Ocular disease also 30-79%, omitted under the four-axis cap.
Amyloid deposition is localized to skin; this cutaneous disorder does not imply systemic amyloidosis or systemic metabolic dysfunction.
Spastic paraplegia, dystonia and intellectual disability establish neurologic disease. Muscle wasting and sphincter dysfunction are neurogenic; intrinsic muscle disease is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy accompanying this neurologic syndrome does not establish direct skeletal muscle disease; frequency of independent muscle pathology is unspecified.

basis: Motor-neuron degeneration involving anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts. Muscle wasting is secondary to denervation, not direct muscle disease.
Neurodegenerative complex involving motor neurons, parkinsonism and dementia; muscle weakness reflects denervation.
Frontotemporal and motor-neuron degeneration; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Developmental abnormality of the anal sphincter; the anus belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Myopathy is confined to the internal anal sphincter, a gastrointestinal smooth muscle rather than locomotor skeletal muscle.
Carcinoma arises from anal canal epithelium; HPV association does not make the carcinoma itself an infectious disease.
Ineffective erythropoiesis and abnormal marrow erythroblasts cause anemia; bilirubin and iron elevations alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Inherited red-cell aplasia; congenital thenar muscle hypoplasia, recorded as small thenar eminence, occurs in 7/10. Cardiac and renal malformations are uncommon.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: small thenar eminence in 7/10 supports common congenital thenar muscle hypoplasia, a persistent structural musculoskeletal defect.

basis: Aneurysmal disease of cerebral arteries; neurological injury from rupture is not established in at least 30%.
Congenital aneurysm of the interventricular septum; associated conduction abnormalities remain cardiovascular.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus/astigmatism and scoliosis each annotated 30-79%. Hypopigmentation lacks functional damage; reflux/constipation alone do not establish tissue injury.
Phalangeal and hip epiphyseal dysplasia define disease; hypodontia and delayed tooth eruption occur in 30-79%.
Cutaneous capillary malformation involving dermal blood vessels.
Defined by vascular angiomatous lesions in brain and skin; cerebral lesions cause seizures, hemorrhage and focal deficits.
Inherited loss of sweat gland function causes generalized anhidrosis; heat intolerance does not establish another damaged organ.
Isolated congenital iris malformation with associated ocular abnormalities; systemic involvement is excluded.
Aniridia and patellar aplasia or hypoplasia define the syndrome; cataract and glaucoma remain within the ocular axis.
Aniridia, microcornea and cataract are intrinsic ocular abnormalities.
Unequal pupil size defines an ocular abnormality; neurologic disease is an alternative cause rather than a universal component.
Eyelid fusion and cleft palate define the named syndrome; palate involvement is defining despite its low annotation frequency.
Skin defects, ankyloblepharon and oral clefts define AEC; conductive hearing loss occurs in 80-99%. Choanal atresia omitted at the four-axis cap.
Congenital attachment restricting tongue movement; tongue and floor of mouth fall within the gastrointestinal axis.
Supplied definition includes vertebral hyperostosis and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis; keratoderma occurs in 30-79%.
Hereditary annular erythematous skin disorder; no established systemic involvement or autoimmune mechanism.
Congenital absence of teeth defines the disorder; teeth and associated oral clefts belong to gastrointestinal.
Abnormal pulmonary venous drainage is cardiovascular; pulmonary hypertension shares that axis, while respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
Defined by nail aplasia and persistent skin abnormalities. Caries in 80-99% is a separate dental disease; intrinsic developmental tooth damage is not established.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: frequent caries (80-99%) is separately diagnosed dental disease; the evidence does not establish intrinsic tooth malformation or direct syndromic dental injury.

basis: Congenital absence of nails and ectrodactyly define nail and skeletal limb abnormalities.
Defining nail absence/dystrophy and congenital digital skeletal malformations.
Defining congenital nail hypo/aplasia and distal phalangeal hypo/aplasia directly affect nails and bones.
Isolated congenital nail absence and dystrophy; distal phalangeal abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Hereditary malformations of the anus and rectum, including anal atresia and rectovaginal fistula, define gastrointestinal involvement.
Congenital loss of smell from abnormal olfactory development; smell belongs to the neurologic axis.
PITX3-related ocular developmental disorder with posterior polar cataract in 98/98 patients.
Anal, ear and thumb malformations define the syndrome; renal insufficiency occurs in 30-79%. Lesser skin findings omitted under the four-axis cap.
Defining triad comprises interrupted aortic arch, facial nerve palsy and retinal coloboma; nevus frequency is unspecified.
Localized skin absence defines ACC. Calvarial defects occur in roughly 20% and spinal dysraphism is uncommon; supplied 80-99% annotations conflict with the umbrella phenotype and definition.

decisions.neurologic: none: spinal dysraphism is an uncommon associated anomaly, below 30%; the 80-99% annotation conflicts with usual ACC and the definition's occasional anomalies.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: underlying calvarial defects occur in roughly 20%, below threshold; the supplied 80-99% annotation does not represent the usual umbrella phenotype.

basis: Recurrent upper-airway obstruction defines disease; cardiovascular complications are separately diagnosed conditions, and somnolence is a symptom.
Localized corneal lipid deposition defines the disease; systemic dyslipidemia is not intrinsic to arcus senilis.
Congenital radial and ulnar hypoplasia with radioulnar synostosis.
Right ventricular myocardial fibrosis and fatty replacement cause ventricular dysfunction and arrhythmias.
Inherited arterial abnormalities; no additional organ involvement specified.
Malformation of cerebral arteries and veins; cerebral hemorrhage and seizures are frequent. Central visual deficits do not establish ocular damage.
Familial granulomatous arteritis with juvenile polyarthritis defines inflammatory disease of arteries and joints; no additional organ involvement established.
Arthritis affects the sacroiliac joints; the sparse hereditary record does not establish a specific infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Congenital distal joint contractures and limb deformities define the condition; hearing impairment is very rare.
Congenital limb contractures and ocular dysfunction define DA5; restrictive ventilation in 3/3 reflects thoracic mechanical restriction without established direct lung or airway injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: restrictive ventilation is documented in 3/3, but chest-wall restriction does not establish direct pulmonary tissue or airway disease.

basis: Defining congenital hand contractures and sensorineural deafness; joint stiffness and hearing impairment occur in 80-99%.
Vitreoretinopathy and skeletal dysplasia define disease; sensorineural hearing loss 19/25, cleft palate 30-79%; reported mitral prolapse omitted under cap.
Isolated failure of sperm production causes male infertility; reproductive function alone has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Asymmetric skeletal growth and short stature identify the apparent affected axis; no definition or phenotype data establish additional organs.
Cerebellar channelopathy causing episodic and progressive ataxia; central nystagmus, diplopia and vertigo do not establish separate eye or ear damage.
Spastic ataxia is neurological; supranuclear gaze palsy and dysphagia reflect neural dysfunction without establishing primary eye or gastrointestinal damage.
Spastic ataxia and congenital fixed miosis with impaired pupillary reaction define the syndrome; optic atrophy is occasional (5–29%).
Hereditary neurological disorder defined by ataxia and fasciculations; no independent muscle pathology is established.
Severe lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79% and directly compromises lung development and function.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease. Respiratory insufficiency is frequent (30-79%) but does not establish direct lung disease; direct airway malacia is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.pulmonary: none: frequent respiratory insufficiency can result from skeletal restriction; direct pulmonary pathology is not established, and laryngotracheomalacia occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Congenital external auditory canal obstruction with conductive hearing loss and associated middle-ear abnormalities.
Atrial electrical and mechanical failure with associated cardiac conduction abnormalities and atrial cardiomyopathy.
Congenital atrial septal defect; associated structural and conduction abnormalities remain cardiovascular.
Congenital atrial septal malformation with atrioventricular conduction disease; both affect the heart.
Cardiac conduction disorder defined by a short PR interval and atrial tachyarrhythmias.
Inherited variation in cardiac atrioventricular conduction, measured by the PR interval.
Progressive retinal and choroidal atrophy causes visual loss; optic-disc proximity does not establish extraocular neurologic disease.
Skeletal dysplasia and characteristic external ear malformations define the syndrome; both occur in 80–99%.
Craniosynostosis, syndactyly, hearing impairment and intellectual disability characterize the syndrome; cardiac abnormalities lack sufficient frequency evidence.
Autoimmune mechanism defines the umbrella; affected anatomical organs depend on the specific autoimmune disease.
Defining eye anomalies, hydrocephalus/callosal abnormalities and skeletal malformations. Hearing impairment is reported without an established frequency.
Axial skeletal mineralization disorder; renal and hepatic cyst annotations lack frequencies sufficient to establish common involvement.
Central and peripheral neurodegeneration defines SCA3. Ophthalmoplegia (34/57) reflects neural ocular-motor dysfunction; muscle atrophy reflects denervation.

decisions.ocular: none: common ophthalmoplegia and nystagmus arise from neurologic degeneration; direct disease of the eye or optic nerve is not established.

basis: Familial azotemia reflects abnormal renal urea handling; isolated elevated urea does not establish progressive renal failure or damage to other organs.
Androgenetic hair-follicle miniaturization and alopecia; androgen sensitivity does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Carpal synostosis and characteristic metacarpal and finger abnormalities define this skeletal syndrome.
Gastric reflux causes esophageal dysfunction and possible mucosal injury; cough alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Basal cell carcinomas, odontogenic jaw keratocysts and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; falx calcification generally causes no neurologic impairment.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: defining odontogenic keratocysts arise from dental epithelium; their intraosseous location does not exclude their dental origin.

basis: Congenital craniovertebral skeletal defect; brainstem/cranial nerve dysfunction supported by oculomotor and bulbar abnormalities in 30-79%; no independent ocular damage.
Hereditary susceptibility specifically to chronic lymphocytic leukemia; no additional organ involvement established.

Hereditary abnormality of renal beta-amino-acid transport; renal transport and amino-acid handling define the concept.
Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts leading to biliary cirrhosis.
Congenital bicuspid aortic valve with associated valve dysfunction and aortopathy, all within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital nasal malformation; the nose belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Structural diverticulum of the urinary bladder; stones and infections are separate complications.
Defining triad comprises eyelid blepharochalasis, duplicated oral lip mucosa, and variable thyroid enlargement; goiter is a major syndrome feature.
Blepharochalasis affects the upper eyelids, which belong to the ocular axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ovarian failure is restricted to type I females; amenorrhea 2/3 does not establish >=30% involvement across the BPES umbrella.

basis: Ptosis, high myopia and lens dislocation define the syndrome; structural fingernail dysplasia is reported in 30-79%.
Cutaneous and gastrointestinal venous malformations define disease; HPO coagulation dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Bone pain alone does not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.haematologic: involved: HPO coagulation abnormalities in 30-79% support impaired coagulation; bleeding alone would not suffice.

basis: Bone fragility and craniosynostosis define it; hydrocephalus in 2/2 and dentinogenesis imperfecta in 1/2 support brain and dental involvement. Proptosis alone does not establish eye injury.
Bone dysplasia and bone sarcoma syndrome classified under polyamine metabolism disorders; cataract frequency is unspecified, so ocular involvement is omitted.
Hereditary periodic bone pain is localized to the skeleton; no evidence supports additional organ involvement.
Ectodermal dysplasia defined by premolar aplasia, abnormal sweating and premature hair graying. Small hands alone do not establish locomotor impairment.
Severe skeletal dysplasia with pulmonary hypoplasia in 30-79%; abnormal growth hormone testing alone does not establish endocrine damage.
Defining bent-bone dysplasia; intellectual disability is frequent (30-79%). Dental, thyroid and blood abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
Microcephaly and developmental delay define neurologic involvement; metatarsus adductus is a defining skeletal deformity.

Defining heart-hand syndrome combines digital and joint malformations with cardiac conduction defects.
Defined by hypoplastic distal phalanges and shortened metacarpals.
Defining digital bone shortening and hallux varus; nonspecific palate and nail morphology do not establish functional damage to additional organs.
Congenital shortening or hypoplasia of digital phalanges, sometimes with fusion and short stature; confined to the skeletal axis.
Congenital hypoplasia or absence of finger phalanges defines this skeletal malformation.
Congenital shortening and abnormal shape of the fifth-finger middle phalanx, with clinodactyly.
Congenital shortening or absence of middle phalanges, sometimes with joint fusion; skeletal malformation.
Skeletal dysplasia with shortened middle phalanges, mesomelic limb shortening and carpal/tarsal abnormalities; intelligence is generally normal.
Type B brachydactyly features distal phalangeal hypoplasia or absence with hypoplastic or absent nails; other reported abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Congenital phalangeal and metacarpal malformations. Nail morphology changes occur in 30-79%, but intrinsic nail damage or functional loss is not established.
Congenital shortening and broadening of terminal phalanges define the skeletal disorder.
HOXD13-related shortening of metacarpals and metatarsals; impacted teeth have no frequency supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Type E brachydactyly and atrial septal defect are defining components of the syndrome.
Congenital skeletal malformations involving the fibula, digits and other limb bones define the syndrome.
Brachydactyly and cerebellar dysfunction define the syndrome; nystagmus does not establish intrinsic eye damage. Strabismus frequency is unspecified.

decisions.ocular: none: defining nystagmus is consistent with cerebellar ocular motor dysfunction; intrinsic ocular damage or common independent visual impairment is not established.

basis: Brachydactyly and symphalangism with characteristic spinal and foot deformities.
The supplied syndrome description defines severe limb shortening, glomerulocystic renal dysplasia and corneal opacities.
Congenital shortening of the fourth metatarsal is a skeletal abnormality.
Defined skeletal anomalies and Kallmann hypogonadism/anosmia; absent or hypoplastic toenails occur in 80-99%; pigmentation alone does not imply damage.
Vertebral skeletal dysplasia with kyphoscoliosis and adult joint degeneration; spinal cord compression is not established as common.
Congenital lateral cervical soft-tissue cyst or fistula; embryologic pharyngeal origin alone does not establish airway damage.
Myoclonus, spastic paraparesis and cerebellar ataxia define a neurological disorder; no independent muscle disease is established.
Ocular, branchial skin and characteristic lip defects define BOFS; hearing impairment occurs in 5/6 and conductive loss in 80-99%. Renal anomalies are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft/pseudocleft upper lip is part of the major characteristic facial criterion; tooth agenesis and microdontia additionally occur in 30-79%.

basis: Ear malformations/hearing loss and congenital renal tract abnormalities define BOR1; renal abnormalities remain defining despite variable penetrance.
Breast hypertrophy has no axis. Associated skin necrosis and skeletal changes are not established as common direct manifestations.
Isolated absence of mammary glands; breast has no axis.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder causing blistering and progressive hyperkeratosis.
Inherited progressive disease of the cardiac conduction system, potentially causing complete heart block.
Familial complete right bundle branch block is a cardiac conduction disorder.
Hereditary butyrylesterase enzyme abnormality provisionally assigned to metabolism; no definition or evidence of specific organ damage supplied.
Mature B-cell lymphoma; oral cavity neoplasm is frequent (30–79%), supporting gastrointestinal occupation. Hepatic and pancreatic abnormalities are occasional.
Infantile cortical hyperostosis with periosteal inflammation and new bone formation; transient soft tissue swelling does not establish lasting skin damage.
Inherited isolated cutaneous pigmentation disorder; definition explicitly excludes neurofibromatosis and systemic manifestations.
Calcific aortic valve disease with stenosis/regurgitation; elevated immunoglobulins alone do not establish autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency.
Childhood cerebral calcification; supplied Aicardi-Goutieres and inborn-error-of-immunity ancestry supports an immune-mediated neurologic disorder.
Inherited palmoplantar keratoderma produces painful hyperkeratotic skin lesions at pressure points.
Congenital shortened digits, interphalangeal contractures and syndactyly; nail abnormalities are occasional and vaginal anomalies have no axis.
Permanent finger joint flexion contracture; explicitly non-neurogenic.
Skeletal dysplasia and cleft palate define the syndrome; airway malacia occurs in 80-99%; conductive hearing impairment in 3/5. Genital anatomy alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate is an explicit defining structural malformation, reported in 80-99%; the palate belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Congenital distal contractures define disease. Eyelid ptosis occurs in 5/15 (~33%). Cleft palate is occasional; high palate alone does not establish functional damage.
Breast malignancy; breast has no axis. Metastatic organ involvement is not universal or defining.
Malignant tumor arising from hepatocytes; metastases and associated viral hepatitis do not establish additional axes.
Inherited chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis is defined by Candida infection of skin, nails and oral mucosa. Endocrine findings lack adequate frequency evidence.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: chronic oral mucosal Candida infection is part of the defining mucocutaneous disease; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Skeletal anomalies, cutis laxa and intellectual disability define the syndrome; cardiac anomalies, including PDA and cardiomegaly, occur in 30-79%.
Rare inherited bleeding disorder; abnormal bleeding supports a haemostatic axis despite limited descriptive information.
Developmental dental anomaly; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Disorder of cardiac impulse generation or conduction; subtype-specific extracardiac findings do not apply across the umbrella.
Defining cardiac, skin/hair and neurodevelopmental disease; ocular abnormalities common, including ptosis 13/20 (65%); common chest skeletal anomalies omitted by cap.
TNNT2-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects cardiac muscle.
TPM1-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium.
MYBPC3-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; pulmonary edema reflects heart failure, and stroke is a minority complication.
Isolated LMNA cardiomyopathy with conduction disease. Lipodystrophy is a separately diagnosed laminopathy phenotype despite its 30-79% annotation; muscular dystrophy occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: lipodystrophy represents a separate LMNA-associated disorder; its 30-79% annotation does not establish fat loss caused by this isolated cardiomyopathy.

basis: Inherited isolated restrictive cardiomyopathy directly affects the myocardium.
Dermal collagenous nevi define disease; cardiomyopathy, heart failure and septal defects are occasional (5-29%).
Inherited carotene-to-vitamin A metabolic disorder; skin discoloration alone does not establish skin damage.
Defining tumors arise in adrenal medulla and autonomic paraganglia. Renal carcinoma and GIST are separate tumor risks; hypertension alone does not establish cardiovascular damage.
Hereditary displacement of the carpal bones affects the wrist skeleton and joints.
Compression and dysfunction of the median peripheral nerve.
Ocular, anorectal and cardiac malformations define CES; renal defects are frequent (30-79%). Frequent intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies omitted at cap; hearing impairment <30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital cardiac malformations are an organ system explicitly included in the supplied disease definition and are frequent (30-79%); retained within the three-primary cap.

basis: Cataracts and abnormal oral frenula define disease; cavernous vascular tumors occur in 30-79%. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Inherited non-syndromic lens cataract; no extraocular disease is established.
Inherited developmental cataract causes lens opacity and reduced visual acuity.
Nonsyndromic congenital lens opacity; nuclear cataract reported in 41/41 patients.
CRYGD-related cataract directly affects the ocular lens.
Inherited cataract affecting the ocular lens.
Nonsyndromic inherited cataract; lens opacity reported in 10/10 patients.
CRYGS-associated nonsyndromic cataract affects the ocular lens.
GJA8-associated cataract directly affects the ocular lens.
VIM-related nonsyndromic early-onset cataract affecting the lens.
Isolated early-onset nuclear cataract; other WFS1-associated syndromes do not apply.
EPHA2-related nonsyndromic cataract; posterior polar cataract reported in 12/12.
Inherited developmental cataract; the associated adult i blood-group phenotype does not itself cause blood-cell dysfunction.
HSF4-related nonsyndromic lens cataract.
Neutrophil adhesion defect; intrinsic destructive periodontal inflammation affects most survivors (>50%). Skin ulcers occur in 5/19, below 30%.
Congenital structural skeletal myopathy; mitral valve prolapse annotated frequent (30-79%). Respiratory insufficiency is very rare; malignant hyperthermia is a susceptibility.
Childhood focal epilepsy; ictal drooling, laryngospasm and apnea do not establish lasting gastrointestinal or pulmonary damage.
Cerebellar degeneration causes ataxia and central nystagmus; hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%, below the involvement threshold.
Cerebral vascular amyloid deposition and neurodegeneration define disease; early cataracts and progressive hearing loss occur in most classically affected patients.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ITM2B-related cerebral amyloid deposition is not, by itself, an endocrine disease or an established inborn metabolic disorder.
decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss is a characteristic manifestation in most affected patients over the typical course.

basis: Congenital cerebellar disorder; oculomotor dysfunction reflects neurologic disease. Strabismus 3/3 and ptosis 4/4 are selected small samples, insufficient to establish common intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: cerebellar eye-movement abnormalities are neurologic; sparse strabismus/ptosis reports do not establish intrinsic ocular damage in ≥30% overall.

basis: Sarcoma involving the telencephalon; the affected organ is the brain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%; its potentially substantial lifelong impairment gives it priority under the four-axis cap.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: ear-canal atresia and conductive hearing impairment occur in 30-79%; severe airway and neurodevelopmental impairment take priority.

basis: Regional hypertrichosis and underlying kyphoscoliosis define the syndrome.
Congenital accessory cervical rib; most are asymptomatic, and nerve or vascular compression does not meet the 30% threshold across the concept.
Structural cervical vertebral bridging, supported by the vertebral-column phenotype.
Cervical vertebral dysplasia, facet hypoplasia and atlanto-occipital instability define a skeletal disorder; spinal cord damage is not established.
Congenital cervical vertebral fusion defines disease; hearing impairment 20/24 and kidney abnormalities 16/45 meet threshold. Nervous system abnormalities 5/19 fall below 30%.

Peripheral axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; chronic denervation causes distal muscle atrophy in 20/20 reported patients.
Inherited peripheral demyelinating neuropathy; muscle atrophy and fixed foot deformity are frequent (30-79%). Hearing and respiratory involvement lack supporting frequency.
Hereditary peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness and wasting from denervation do not independently establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Demyelinating neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy and pes cavus occur in 30-79%. Deafness is variable; a 1/1 report does not establish a population frequency of >=30%.
Peripheral neuropathy, parkinsonism and ptosis define syndrome; chronic distal muscle wasting and foot deformity affect most (>50%) patients with typical CMT. Subtype-specific data are sparse.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic denervation atrophy and structural foot deformities affect most (>50%) patients with CMT; this subtype's frequency is undocumented.

basis: Defined by chronic inflammation of labial minor salivary glands and oral lip tissue. Unknown inflammatory cause does not establish immune mediation; associated carcinoma is separate.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the defining lesion concerns labial salivary glands and oral tissue; lip swelling and the skin-disorder parent do not establish independent cutaneous disease.

basis: Paraganglionic endocrine tumors plus cutaneous angiolipomas; endocrine classification: [NCI](https://seer.cancer.gov/seer-inquiry/inquiry-detail/20210003/).
Autoinflammatory fibro-osseous jaw disease; missing and abnormal teeth occur in 30-79%. Visual and airway complications are under 30%.
Hindbrain malformation; skeletal findings (30-79%) are associated anomalies or secondary scoliosis. Vestibular findings (30-79%) do not establish direct inner-ear damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: vertebral anomalies are associated malformations; scoliosis is secondary and separately diagnosed. The 30-79% annotations do not establish direct skeletal injury.
decisions.otologic: none: vestibular symptoms and eighth-nerve abnormalities are predominantly neurologic; 30-79% functional annotations do not establish direct, persistent ear damage.

basis: Biliary, cardiac and ocular abnormalities define disease; corneal dystrophy annotated 80-99%. Renal abnormalities affect ~40%; vertebral defects omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: involved: renal dysplasia and other intrinsic renal abnormalities occur in approximately 40%; retained for their potential functional severity.
decisions.ocular: primary: ocular abnormalities are defining; supplied corneal dystrophy frequency is 80-99%, beyond nonimpairing posterior embryotoxon alone.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: vertebral segmentation defects are defining and frequent (30-79%), but commonly asymptomatic; omitted at cap in favor of renal disease.

basis: Inherited pyrophosphate metabolism disorder causes cartilage crystal deposition and destructive arthropathy; joint disease documented in 11/11.
Apatite crystal deposition in cartilage; ancestry identifies an arthritic and metabolic bone disorder.
Skeletal dysplasia with epiphyseal stippling and contractures; frequencies of cataracts and skin disease are insufficiently established across this group.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by epiphyseal stippling and tibial/metacarpal shortening; no additional organ damage established.
Hereditary progressive movement disorder with choreoathetosis, pyramidal signs and possible dementia or seizures.
Lipoprotein clearance disorder causing chylomicronemia. Pancreatitis is a separate complication; splenomegaly alone does not establish functional injury or autoimmune disease.
Bilateral benign ossifying tumors of the ocular choroid; ectopic bone formation does not establish skeletal-system disease.
Familial or cryptogenic hepatic cirrhosis; sparse reports of varices and pulmonary hypertension do not establish additional common direct organ damage.
Congenital clavicular nonunion; dextrocardia and situs inversus are positional anomalies without established cardiovascular damage.
Congenital digital and long-bone deficiencies define the disorder; cupped ears do not establish hearing damage.
Defining lower lip pits and common cleft lip/palate affect the mouth, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Clefting, limb contractures and restrictive skin webs define the syndrome; ankyloblepharon occurs in 30-79%; hyperglycinemia is not an established IRF6 manifestation.
Congenital cleft lip with or without cleft palate affects oral structures.
Isolated congenital defect of the oral palate; nonspecific neurological annotations do not define this nonsyndromic concept.
Cleft palate and intraoral adhesions define the disorder; mandibular hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement. Voice changes alone do not establish airway damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: micrognathia represents structural mandibular underdevelopment and is explicitly annotated as frequent (30-79%).

basis: Congenital cleft of the oral soft palate; hearing impairment and otitis are occasional, and language delay alone does not establish neurologic damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: finger syndactyly is a direct congenital structural abnormality of the digits, reported in 30-79%; additional locomotor disability is not required.

basis: Bone and dental developmental defects define CCD; hearing impairment and chronic middle-ear disease occur in 30-79%. Respiratory infections are secondary.

Congenital structural foot deformity; neurologic and palatal findings in small syndromic samples do not characterize the clubfoot umbrella.
Isolated nail and terminal soft-tissue clubbing; no additional skeletal or systemic disorder is established.
Inherited trigeminal autonomic headache disorder; tearing, rhinorrhea and ptosis do not indicate separate organ damage.
Congenital aortic narrowing; associated cardiac abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis. Stroke is very rare (1-4%).
Defining cochleosaccular degeneration and cataracts; frequent ataxia may reflect vestibular dysfunction already covered by otologic, without established CNS damage.
Cold-triggered autoinflammatory disease; rash, conjunctivitis and arthralgia are usually transient. Renal amyloidosis occurs in 1/26; isolated uveitis reports lack robust frequency.
Congenital ocular coloboma and associated eye malformations define disease; renal and cerebral findings lack qualifying frequencies.
Developmental absence or atrophy of macular tissues impairs vision; associated syndromes do not define this isolated eye disorder.
Renal hypodysplasia and optic nerve dysplasia define the syndrome. Scoliosis reported in 2/4 supports skeletal involvement, though evidence is limited; hypertension is secondary to renal disease.
Macular coloboma and brachydactyly define the syndrome; nail aplasia or dysplasia occurs in 30-79%. Renal agenesis is below 30%.
Congenital optic disc/optic nerve malformation; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis under these rules.
Coloboma, cleft lip/palate and intellectual disability define syndrome; hearing loss in 10/11. Hematuria alone does not establish direct renal damage.
Hereditary colorectal cancer predisposition; other associated cancers are later risks, not direct organ involvement.
Varicose veins localized to the colon define the disease; portal hypertension and hepatic disease are explicitly absent.
Inherited cutaneous disorder characterized by dyskeratotic comedones.
Congenital pits of the oral commissures are structural mouth abnormalities; preauricular pits do not establish hearing or vestibular damage.
Branchiootic syndrome defined by ear malformations and hearing impairment; renal disease is not part of this concept.
Complement regulatory protein deficiency; recurrent angioedema is transient, and associated lupus is a separately diagnosed disease.
Inherited retinal degeneration affecting cones and rods, causing visual loss.

KCNQ3-related neonatal epilepsy; focal clonic seizures reported in 21/22 patients.
Inherited susceptibility to febrile seizures defines a neurologic disorder.
Copper transport disorder; seizures and acne occur in 30-79%, with characteristic seborrheic dermatitis. Anemia and skeletal changes occur in 5-29%.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: abnormal immune physiology in 80-99% is nonspecific and does not establish immunodeficiency, infection or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Congenital anomalous articulation between the coracoid process and clavicle; isolated joint abnormality.

Inherited flattening of the cornea with altered corneal refractive function.

Corneal epithelial basement membrane disease causing recurrent erosions.

Corneal stromal deposits cause progressive visual impairment and recurrent erosions; disease is confined to the eye.
Inherited corneal endothelial and Descemet membrane dystrophy; associated iris and anterior chamber abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy; confined to the eye despite often limited visual impairment.
Corneal dystrophy causes scarring, erosions and progressive visual impairment; definition specifies no systemic manifestations.
Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy causing recurrent erosions, opacities and scarring.
Corneal/retinal disease, deafness and intellectual disability define syndrome; aganglionic megacolon occurs in 30-79%. PDA also 30-79%, omitted at cap in favor of severe bowel dysfunction.

decisions.cardiovascular: none under cap: PDA occurs in 30-79%, but chronic aganglionic bowel dysfunction takes the fourth axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: congenital aganglionic megacolon causes direct bowel dysfunction in 30-79%; prioritized over PDA under the cap.

basis: Corneal dystrophy, keratoderma/nail abnormalities and skeletal defects define syndrome; dental enamel abnormalities affect 80-99%, supporting oral GI involvement. Hearing loss is <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: gastroesophageal reflux occurs in 25/40 but is usually diagnosed and coded as a separate disease; feeding symptoms alone do not establish direct GI damage.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects ~85-90%, with structural ear abnormalities ([consensus](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7136165/)).

basis: Congenital ligament shortening fixes the scapula to the first rib and alters shoulder anatomy; no pulmonary malformation is established.

Inherited resistance to coumarin anticoagulation concerns regulation of coagulation; it does not establish damage to other organs.
Structural deformity of the proximal femur and hip.
Defining skeletal dysplasia with hip dislocation and external-ear malformations/hearing impairment; both occur in 80-99%.
Cranioacral malformations and contractures with congenital septal and pulmonary-valve defects form the reported syndrome; cardiac frequency is unquantified.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: inferred core congenital cardiac component (VSD/pulmonic stenosis), alongside cranioacral abnormalities; frequency is unquantified.

basis: Deafness and hand contractures define it; lacrimal duct atresia and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%.
Osteosclerosis and skeletal dysplasia; dental/enamel defects 80-99% and tooth agenesis 30-79%; cerebral calcification and proptosis lack established functional damage.
Bone dysplasia; hearing loss 4/5, facial palsy 4/5, optic atrophy 2/3; dental anomalies and choanal stenosis (1/3) omitted by cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: nasolacrimal duct agenesis is a defining malformation of the lacrimal drainage system.

basis: Cranial suture fusion defines disease; aortic valve stenosis is reported in 1/2 patients, supporting cardiovascular involvement, although the sample is very small.
Defining foot malformations and craniosynostosis; strabismus and ptosis occur in 30-79%, supporting ocular functional involvement.

Hereditary hyperCKemia with muscle cramps, myopathic abnormalities and muscle-fiber pathology; elevated CK is not itself a metabolic disorder.
Inherited prion-mediated CNS degeneration causes dementia, ataxia and neuronal loss; visual dysfunction is predominantly central, and weakness does not establish muscle disease.
Microcephaly and severe developmental disability define disease; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Characteristic cry alone does not establish lasting airway damage; heart defects occur in 5-29%.
Craniosynostosis defines disease; strabismus 30-79%, conductive hearing loss 7/7, and Chiari/cerebellar abnormalities 30-79%. Dental abnormalities omitted by cap; optic atrophy <30%.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus causes ocular motor dysfunction in 30-79%. Proptosis reflects shallow bony orbits and does not independently establish primary eye disease.

basis: Cold-precipitating plasma fibrinogen disorder; acrocyanosis alone does not establish lasting vascular injury. Renal findings are transient or lack frequency evidence.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: thrombotic vascular injury is not established as defining or present in at least 30% of this familial form; acrocyanosis alone is insufficient.

basis: Immune-complex vasculitis with defining skin disease; neuropathy ~50-60% (HPO 30-79%). Renal injury ~30%, GI infarction and arthritis (HPO 30-79%) omitted by cap; viral hepatitis is separate.

decisions.renal: none: renal injury qualifies (HPO 30-79%, usually about 30%), but more prevalent neuropathy and defining skin disease take the remaining slots.
decisions.neurologic: involved: direct peripheral neuropathy is common, roughly 50-60%, consistent with the supplied frequent (30-79%) HPO annotations.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: vasculitic purpura is part of the defining triad; skin ulcers in 80-99% confirm direct cutaneous injury.

basis: Familial congenital malformation of the external ear.

Congenital absence or malformation of eyelids with ocular coverage and often microphthalmia; isolated ocular disorder.
Inherited skin elastic-tissue defect; emphysema and bronchiectasis each 2/3; cardiac defects/failure 1/3 and pulmonary arterial stenosis 1/1 support vascular involvement.

Destructive osteolysis with abnormal lymphatic vascular proliferation defines disease; hearing loss and pleural effusions occur in only 5-29%.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; hepatic dysfunction/fibrosis 2/2, developmental impairment 1/1 and brain lesions 1/2, renal tubular dysfunction with aminoaciduria 1/2.
Aristolochic acid-associated chronic tubulointerstitial kidney injury; urothelial cancer is a separate disease risk.
Skin/nail keratinization disorder; chronic blepharitis or keratoconjunctivitis sicca and anal mucosal leukoplakia are each reported as frequent (30-79%).

Stapedial malformations cause profound conductive deafness; facial nerve paralysis is a defining feature.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (30-79%) qualifies, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining organs and cognitive impairment.

basis: Hereditary progressive sensorineural hearing loss; no evidence of a broader neurologic disorder.

Unilateral deafness is loss of auditory function.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic abnormal dentition is a defining component of anhidrotic ectodermal dysplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Congenital hearing loss defines syndrome; temporal hypotrichosis and tongue/palate anomalies occur in 80–99%, PDA in 30–79%. Evidence derives from one family.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: temporal hypotrichosis occurs in 80–99%, representing persistent hair abnormality; it is an associated feature rather than a defining diagnostic component.

basis: Multiple eruptive milia are keratin-containing cutaneous cysts.

Inherited structural disease of the mitral valve; no additional organ disease defines this umbrella.
Valvular disease, skeletal fusions and hearing impairment define the syndrome. Reflux is separately diagnosed; singleton gastroparesis does not establish population frequency.
Congenital facial and abducens palsies define it; limb/muscle malformations occur in 30-79%, dental abnormalities in 37%; hearing impairment is occasional.
Fusion of dental cementum to alveolar bone prevents tooth eruption; occasional limb abnormalities do not meet the involvement threshold.
Obesity, intellectual disability and ocular defects define syndrome; femoral bowing/abnormal ossification occur in 30-79%. Dental abnormalities, also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Hair-shaft dysplasia, hypotrichosis and nail abnormalities; dental, ocular and cognitive abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
Congenital skeletal abnormality with a single phalanx of the great toe.
Developmental impairment and cranioskeletal malformations define syndrome; congenital heart defects occur in roughly 35%. Frequent blepharophimosis lacks demonstrated visual impairment.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac malformations occur in approximately 35%, supporting inclusion beyond the single-patient HPO annotations.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis is frequent, but eyelid morphology alone does not establish impaired vision or ocular function.

basis: Vestibular motion-processing disorder; nausea and vomiting do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Defining muscle-tendon shortening causes trismus and finger contractures; occasional ptosis does not meet the involvement threshold.
Skin, oral epithelial and corneal/lens disease define HMD; pulmonary fibrosis occurs in 30-79%. Bladder abnormalities (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Defined by sebaceous skin neoplasms and visceral malignancy, predominantly gastrointestinal; colon cancer reported in 2/3. Other cancer sites are variable.
Hyperandrogenism defines endocrine disease; frontal balding represents hair loss in 80-99%. Renal agenesis is occasional (5-29%) overall despite an isolated 1/1 annotation.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: frontal balding is direct hair loss, reported in 80-99%; hirsutism alone would not establish tissue damage.

basis: Multiple bony exostoses and spastic tetraparesis are the two defining manifestations.
Characteristic cutaneous/oral hamartomas and GI hamartomatous polyposis; benign thyroid structural lesions occur in roughly 50-70%. Cancer risks are excluded.
Inherited disorder defined by recurrent skeletal muscle cramps; no supplied evidence establishes a separate peripheral nerve disorder.
Ataxia, retinitis pigmentosa and diabetes define the syndrome; direct myopathy with muscular atrophy occurs in 80-99%.
Hereditary motor neuropathy; vocal cord paresis/paralysis is a defining type 7 manifestation causing laryngeal dysfunction.
HSPB8-related motor neuron disease causes distal paresis and neurogenic EMG changes; weakness reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Lower motor-neuron disease with characteristic proximal lower-limb denervation and muscle atrophy in most affected patients.
Neurogenic muscular atrophy defines nerve and skeletal muscle disease; respiratory paralysis reflects motor weakness, not intrinsic lung disease.
Muscular dystrophy with myopathy and myotonia; no evidence of common direct damage to additional organs.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy with joint contractures. Skin findings occur in under 30%; hypoventilation reflects muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy; disabling retinal disease, clinically significant hearing loss and respiratory failure affect minorities, generally below 30%.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy; hearing impairment occurs in 6/33 patients, below 30%. Facial weakness does not establish peripheral nerve disease.
Skeletal muscular dystrophy with characteristic muscle pathology; common cardiac involvement is not established for this specific rare phenotype.
Congenital generalized skeletal muscle hypoplasia; no evidence supporting additional organ involvement.
Autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. Limb and ocular weakness reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission; associated autoimmune diseases are separate.
Congenital myelination abnormality of retinal optic nerve fibres; confined to the ocular axis.
Defined by cerebellar degeneration and cytopenias/marrow dysfunction. Recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic pulmonary damage.
HTLV-1-associated immune-mediated spinal cord inflammation; bladder and bowel dysfunction reflect neurologic injury rather than direct visceral disease.
Neonatal clonal myeloid proliferation; clinically significant hepatic injury is a minority complication, and later leukemia is a separate disease.
Myoclonic epilepsy syndrome; no additional organ involvement is established.
Cerebellar dysfunction, myoclonus and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; amyotrophy accompanies neuropathy.
SGCE-related myoclonus and dystonia are neurologic; psychiatric manifestations add no organ axis.
Motor-neuron disease, epilepsy and progressive muscle atrophy define this sphingolipidosis; atrophy 6/6. Respiratory muscle weakness does not establish lung damage; aspiration pneumonia is separate.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: progressive muscular atrophy is explicitly part of the disease definition and documented in 6/6; denervation explains the muscle tissue loss without removing this defining organ.

basis: Metabolic myopathy with episodic muscle breakdown and myoglobinuria; acute renal failure is occasional and excluded.
Neuronal channelopathy causing ataxia and peripheral nerve hyperexcitability; spasms, visual symptoms and vertigo do not establish separate organ damage.
Structural skeletal myopathy; ptosis 12/14 and ophthalmoparesis 3/4 impair ocular function. Neuropathy and respiratory insufficiency occur in only 5-29%.
Inherited distal skeletal-muscle disease; no separate nerve involvement is established.
Primary skeletal myopathy with distal weakness and atrophy; cardiomyopathy is occasional (5-29%). Isolated atrial enlargement in one patient does not establish common cardiac damage.
Defined by skeletal-muscle weakness and tubular aggregates; no common extra-muscular damage established.
Inherited glycoprotein/glycosaminoglycan storage myopathy; muscle and metabolic storage disease are defining, without supported extra-organ damage.
Inherited high myopia; retinal detachment remains within the ocular axis. Unspecified nervous-system annotation does not establish common injury.
Autoimmune skin and muscle inflammation; vasculitis occurs in 30-79%. Restrictive ventilation can reflect muscle weakness; pulmonary fibrosis is 5-29%.
Skeletal muscle chloride-channel disorder causing myotonia and hypertrophy; no primary nerve or central nervous system disease.
Muscular dystrophy with defining conduction disease and cataracts (80-99% each); cognitive impairment 30-79%. Baldness omitted at cap; supplied hypogonadism frequency is 5-29%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: arrhythmia and cardiac conduction disease are explicit defining manifestations; conduction abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
decisions.ocular: primary: cataract is an explicit defining manifestation, with posterior subcapsular cataract in 80-99%.

basis: Endocrine lesions, characteristic skin lesions and cardiac myxomas are major diagnostic features; cardiac myxoma reported in 6/11.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with characteristic muscle inclusions; associated neurologic abnormalities lack evidence of frequency above 30%.
Ectodermal dysplasia defined by skin, sweat gland, nail and dental abnormalities. Dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%; joint contractures are occasional.
Inherited isolated nail dysplasia and dystrophy; rare autoimmune associations do not establish an immune mechanism.
Nail and skeletal dysplasia define disease; renal involvement in ~30-50%; iris pigmentation is non-damaging and glaucoma is a minority complication.
Hypocretin-related sleep regulation disorder with cataplexy, sleep attacks and REM abnormalities; muscle tone loss is neurologic.
Bilateral collapse of the nasal alae affects the nasal airway, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Congenital absence of nasal bones is a skeletal malformation; accompanying nasal shape findings do not establish airway dysfunction.
Inherited transverse crease of the skin over the nasal dorsum; no airway disease established.
Familial transverse hyperpigmentation affects nasal skin; no airway disease is described.
Hereditary susceptibility is specific to nasopharyngeal carcinoma; the nasopharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis. Susceptibility does not establish additional organ damage.
Adult Leigh disease is mitochondrial metabolic encephalomyelopathy; supplied periosteal/skin HPO findings are discordant with this diagnosis.
ACTA1 skeletal-muscle myopathy includes respiratory and bulbar muscle weakness; intrinsic lung damage is not established; cardiomyopathy occurs in 5-29%.
Progressive nephropathy and hypertension are defining features; renal failure, proteinuria and hematuria support kidney disease.
UMOD-related progressive tubulointerstitial nephropathy with hyperuricemia; gout (~42%) and hypertension (~58%) are separately diagnosed complications.
Multiple peripheral and spinal nerve-sheath tumors define disease; hearing loss, cataracts and skeletal abnormalities are minority findings.
Hereditary recurrent brachial plexus neuropathy; muscle weakness and atrophy result from denervation.
Spinal nerve-root neurofibromas define disease (8/8). Pigment spots do not establish skin damage; cutaneous neurofibromas occur in only 1/5; Lisch nodules are non-damaging.

decisions.dermatologic: none: cafe-au-lait spots in 5/8 do not establish skin damage; cutaneous neurofibromas occur in only 1/5, and skin disease does not define this spinal subtype.

basis: Defined by neurofibromatosis, adrenal pheochromocytoma and duodenal carcinoid; cutaneous neurofibromas affect most adults with the associated NF1 phenotype.
Central/peripheral neural tumors and cutaneous neurofibromas define this historical phenotype; common hearing dysfunction is not established, and Lisch nodules are non-damaging.

decisions.otologic: none: vestibular schwannomas establish neural tumors, but the supplied evidence does not establish hearing or vestibular organ dysfunction in at least 30%.

basis: Historical neurofibromatosis subtype with neural tumors and cutaneous manifestations; no common additional organ injury established.
Endocrine neoplasia and oral/enteric neural proliferation define MEN2B. Structural skeletal abnormalities and joint laxity occur in approximately 65-75%; tall habitus alone is insufficient.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural skeletal abnormalities and joint laxity affect approximately 65-75%; persistent deformities support this axis beyond tall or slender habitus.

basis: Lipopigment storage disorder with defining neurodegeneration; vascular deposits alone do not establish vascular dysfunction.
Congenital peripheral neuropathy with defining multiple joint contractures, muscle wasting and skeletal deformity.
Axonal neuropathy from disordered sphingolipid biosynthesis; muscle wasting reflects denervation. Singleton cataract does not establish common ocular disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy/weakness reflects motor denervation, not direct muscle disease; the 1/1 observation does not establish common intrinsic myopathy.

basis: Peripheral demyelinating neuropathy; weakness and scoliosis are secondary to nerve dysfunction. Hearing and respiratory complications occur in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is annotated 30-79%, but is secondary to neuropathy; neurogenic weakness does not establish direct muscle or skeletal disease.

basis: Neuropathy defines peripheral nerve dysfunction. Paraprotein alone does not establish blood-cell disease, renal damage or an immune mechanism.
Inherited chronic reduction in neutrophils; periodontal disease and tooth loss are reported without frequencies sufficient to establish common involvement.
Cyclic neutrophil deficiency impairs innate immunity; recurrent oral ulceration and gingivitis cause mucosal injury in 30-79%. Secondary infections are separate diseases; periodontitis is <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent oral ulceration and gingivitis directly injure oral tissues in 30-79%; these are intrinsic mucosal manifestations, beyond pain or transient redness.

basis: Persistent inherited neutrophil proliferation with splenomegaly; blood, marrow and spleen fall within the same axis. No established immunodeficiency.
Benign epidermal overgrowth located in skin; extracutaneous nevus syndromes are not implied.
Congenital cutaneous capillary malformations define the disease; glaucoma and neurologic complications occur in <30%.
Localized cutaneous capillary vascular anomaly producing persistent pale macules; both skin and its vessels define the lesion.
Localized cutaneous capillary malformation of the nape; no systemic organ involvement established.
Sebaceous nevus with CNS malformations and seizures; microphthalmia/coloboma and vertebral/limb defects each reported at 80-99%; renal and endocrine damage not established as common.
Mesomelic skeletal dysplasia with synostoses and restricted joints; skin dimples do not establish skin damage; ocular and neurologic findings are occasional.
PDE6B-associated retinal phototransduction dysfunction causes stationary night blindness; broad nervous-system ancestry does not establish additional neurologic disease.
Isolated inverted nipples affect the breast, which is outside the defined axes.
Isolated familial breast/nipple malformation has no axis; genitourinary anomalies occur in only 5-29%.
Inherited sinus-node dysfunction; associated arrhythmias, ventricular noncompaction and valve abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Multiple cutaneous nodules and urinary tract abnormalities define the syndrome; annotations include hydronephrosis and duplicated collecting systems.
Cardiac and skeletal abnormalities define Noonan syndrome; ptosis occurs in 77/136 (~57%), and bruising susceptibility supports hemostatic dysfunction in 32/56 (~57%).

decisions.haematologic: involved: hemostatic dysfunction is common; bruising susceptibility occurs in 32/56 (~57%). Overt abnormal bleeding at 3/18 measures a narrower manifestation.

basis: Congenital nasal structural anomaly; the nose belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Congenital ocular motor disorder with persistent nystagmus and reduced visual acuity; no independent brain disorder is established.
Isolated inherited vertical nystagmus is an ocular motor disorder; no broader neurologic disease is established.
Eye, CNS and skin malformations define the triad; skull defects and rib abnormalities are frequent (30-79%), supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Autoimmune conjunctival inflammation causes scarring and vision loss; other mucosal or skin damage is possible but not established at >=30% for this ocular subtype.
Eye, dental and digital defects define disease; neurologic deficits frequent (30-79%); bladder dysfunction (12/20), hearing loss and hair defects omitted by cap.
Cleft palate, eyelid blepharophimosis and male urethral hypospadias are defining malformations; intellectual disability occurs in under 30%.
Purely psychiatric obsessive-compulsive disorder; no qualifying organ damage.
Digital malformations, microcephaly and gastrointestinal atresias are defining features; intellectual impairment ~51%. Cardiac, renal and hearing abnormalities are minorities.
Progressive myopathy with defining eyelid and pharyngeal dysfunction; direct tongue atrophy and weakness occur in 30-79%, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: defining pharyngeal muscle dysfunction affects the pharynx, explicitly assigned to pulmonary by the guide.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: tongue atrophy and weakness occur in 30-79%; these directly affect oral tissue beyond the defining pharyngeal dysfunction.

basis: Odontomas and esophageal obstruction define syndrome; supplied annotations report hepatic failure and atherosclerosis in 80-99%; myocarditis below 30% excluded.
Progressive cerebellar, brainstem and peripheral nerve degeneration; eye-movement abnormalities are neurologic, while optic atrophy is occasional.
Inherited disorder of toenails, plantar skin keratinization and hair.
Skeletal dysplasia; cleft lip/palate reported in 1/2 patients supports gastrointestinal involvement, with limited precision. Ear shape alone does not establish functional damage.
Omphalocele is a congenital abdominal-wall closure defect with defining herniation of bowel; reported in 9/9.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: congenital bowel herniation is part of the defining structural lesion; intrinsic intestinal injury is not required for primary assignment.

basis: Inherited isolated nail disorder with distal onycholysis.
Defining corneal opacity with blindness and limb/joint malformations; impaired mastication results from temporomandibular ankylosis.
Inherited static impairment of ocular motility with ptosis and pupillary abnormalities; no generalized neurologic or muscular disease established.
Total ophthalmoplegia, ptosis and iris abnormalities define an ocular disorder; no established extraocular neurologic disease.
Defining intellectual disability, ophthalmoplegia with retinal abnormalities, and congenital furrowed tongue; each is annotated as very frequent.
Mitochondrial optic atrophy-plus disorder; optic atrophy and neuropathy define organ disease. Hearing loss is part of the defining triad, placed in involved because primary is capped at three.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine because the supplied ancestry identifies a mitochondrial disease. Retain ocular and neurologic as primary; move otologic to involved solely to respect the three-primary cap, since hearing loss remains defining.

basis: Leber-plus mitochondrial disorder defined by optic atrophy and CNS demyelination; autoimmune causation is not established by the supplied record.
Optic atrophy with mitochondrial dysfunction; cerebellar atrophy and neuropathic findings in 30-79%; hearing impairment in 5/14 (~36%).
Mitochondrial optic atrophy; hearing loss and sensorimotor neuropathy each annotated 30-79%. Myopathy is annotated <30%; systemic features may overrepresent the classic form.
Optic atrophy in 18/18 with retinal/foveal dysfunction; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis. No extraocular neurological disease established.
Isolated developmental optic nerve abnormality with visual impairment; optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis. Inconsistent cancer ancestors are unsupported.
Defined by cleft palate and oral frenula together with digital anomalies, radial shortening, fibular agenesis and tarsal fusion; facial spacing does not establish ocular disease.
Orbital bony margin agenesis and malformations of eyelids and lacrimal drainage define the syndrome.
Defined by osteosarcoma, limb malformations and erythroid macrocytosis. Caries is reported in 80-99%, but direct syndromic dental damage is not established.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: caries frequency (80-99%) alone does not establish direct dental involvement; caries is a separate disease without demonstrated intrinsic dental pathology here.

basis: Ossification affects external-ear cartilage; no evidence of generalized skeletal or metabolic disease.
Congenital middle-ear ossicular malformations cause conductive hearing impairment; ossicles belong to the ear axis.
Inherited phalangeal epiphyseal osteonecrosis with subsequent joint degeneration and restricted mobility.
Multiple enchondromas directly affect bone. Vascular HPO entries suggest Maffucci overlap and conflict with isolated Ollier disease; malignant transformation is a separate disease.
Bone fragility defines OI type I. Hearing loss affects roughly 30-50% over adulthood; blue sclerae do not impair function, and dentinogenesis imperfecta is only 5-29%.
Lethal bone fragility disorder; pulmonary hypoplasia and severe respiratory insufficiency affect most cases. Blue sclerae do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Bone fragility defines OI IV; dentinogenesis imperfecta damages teeth in roughly half. Hearing loss is not reliably ≥30%; scleral coloration is non-damaging.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dentinogenesis imperfecta affects roughly half and directly damages teeth; it is variable rather than required for the type IV bone-fragility diagnosis.

basis: Bone abnormalities and opalescent teeth define this osteogenesis imperfecta subtype; teeth are gastrointestinal, while blue sclerae do not establish visual damage.
Skeletal dysplasia and multiple unerupted teeth define disease; tooth agenesis and impaction occur in 80–99%. Intellectual disability is only occasional.
Dysplasia affects jaw and long bones. Mandibular osteomyelitis is annotated in 30-79% but is a separately diagnosed infection.
Carpotarsal osteolysis and nephropathy define syndrome; renal insufficiency 15/19. Corneal opacity 3/9 (~33%) supports ocular involvement, with small-sample uncertainty.

decisions.renal: primary: nephropathy is explicitly named and included in the disease definition; renal insufficiency in 15/19 confirms it is a central manifestation despite variable expression.

basis: Progressive ossification begins in skin/subcutis and extends into fascia and muscle, restricting joints; endocrine dysfunction is not defining and is occasional.
Benign bone tumours arising in the mandible.
Axial skeletal dysplasia with patchy osteosclerosis and common vertebral deformities; no common extraskeletal injury is established.
HPO reports cranial palsy 80-99%, optic atrophy and anemia 30-79%; dental abnormalities omitted by cap. Osteomyelitis is a separate infection; frequency annotations conflict.
Defined by skeletal osteopoikilosis and cutaneous connective tissue nevi.
Lacrimal canal stenosis with dacryocystitis and osteosclerotic skeletal lesions define the syndrome.
Metabolic bone disorder causing loss of bone strength after menopause; estrogen deficiency contributes to pathogenesis.
Osteosclerosis with recurrent fractures and ichthyosis defines bone and skin disease.
Defined by malformed enlarged teeth and sensorineural hearing loss, both usually present. Ocular malformations occur in only 5–29%.
Ear malformations/hearing loss, cervical muscle and shoulder-girdle defects, and developmental impairment define the syndrome; renal hypoplasia is occasional (5-29%).
Localized otic-capsule bone remodeling causes stapes fixation and hearing impairment.
Inherited erythrocyte membrane disorder; jaundice reflects hemolysis rather than liver damage. Renal tubular acidosis is occasional and separately diagnosed.
Teratoma originates in the ovary as a reproductive organ; its hair and sebaceous contents do not constitute skin disease or endocrine dysfunction.
Fibrous ovarian tumour is reproductive; reactive effusions do not establish direct pleural damage, and associated syndromic tumours are separate diseases.
Defining skeletal dysplasia, callosal agenesis/hydrocephalus and thrombocytopenia; hypertension is also a defining feature, though frequency is unspecified.
Ovarian malignancy arises in a reproductive organ; hormone dysfunction and damage to another axis are not defining features across this umbrella.
Calculus within the kidney or urinary collecting system; a systemic metabolic disorder is not required across the umbrella.
Periosteal bone thickening and pachydermia define the disorder; both occur in 2/2 annotated patients. Diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Nail dystrophy and palmoplantar keratoderma define disease; persistent oral leukokeratosis is common and present in 1/1 annotated patients.
KRT17-related nail dystrophy, palmoplantar keratoderma and cutaneous cysts define the disease. Natal teeth occur in only 1/4.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia with epiphyseal stippling and osteolysis; patent ductus arteriosus is annotated in 80-99%.
Inherited metabolic bone disorder with abnormal remodeling, osteolysis and sclerosis. Hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Malignant Paget cells infiltrate the skin, including genital or perianal skin; associated internal malignancies are separate diseases.
Myopathy, Paget bone disease (~50%) and frontotemporal degeneration (~one-third) define the syndrome; cardiac and lung damage are not established as common.
Pain-channel dysfunction affects sensory and autonomic nerves; ocular and rectal pain, flushing and constipation do not establish local tissue damage.
Soft-palate and pharyngeal closure dysfunction; associated hearing impairment reported in 30-79%.
Defined by eyelid colobomas and nasopalpebral subcutaneous lipomas; cutaneous hamartomas and lacrimal abnormalities reinforce these axes.
Congenital pancreatic ring surrounds the duodenum, commonly causing stenosis or obstruction; endocrine pancreatic dysfunction is not defining.
Agenesis removes pancreatic exocrine tissue and endocrine islets. [Report](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11160984/)
Definition explicitly specifies irreversible injury to both exocrine and endocrine pancreas. Diabetes is occasional (5-29%); vascular complications are also occasional.
Pancytopenia and occlusive vascular disease directly define blood-cell and vascular involvement; no other organ damage is established.
Familial panic disorder is a psychiatric anxiety disorder; the neurological ancestor does not establish neurologic damage.
Confluent and reticulated papillomatosis is a keratinization disorder producing hyperkeratotic skin lesions.
Breast duct origin has no axis, but the defining erosive, crusting lesion directly damages the overlying epidermis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent epidermal erosion and crusting characterize the lesion itself; this is direct skin damage despite its breast duct origin.

basis: Defined by adrenal chromaffin and autonomic paraganglial tumors; renal carcinoma and GIST are separate tumor risks, and common lasting ear damage is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: primary: paragangliomas arise in autonomic paraganglia, supported by the autonomic nervous system neoplasm ancestry; tumor origin qualifies without separate nerve injury.

basis: Juvenile parkinsonian-pyramidal disease affects central motor pathways.
A developmental dental tubercle anomaly; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Skeletal muscle sodium-channel disease causing myotonia and weakness; dysphagia and stridor reflect muscle dysfunction without established intrinsic organ damage.
Chondrodysplasia with severe skeletal deformity, kyphoscoliosis and joint contractures.
Defective parietal bone ossification with persistent skull openings; neurologic complications are not established as common.
Developmental defects of parietal bones and clavicles; the definition explicitly reports no dental abnormalities.
Neurodegenerative parkinsonism; swallowing, bowel, bladder and ocular motor symptoms do not establish direct damage to those organs.
SNCA-associated neurodegenerative parkinsonism; motor disability and autonomic symptoms reflect nervous system disease.
Neurodegeneration causes parkinsonism and central hypoventilation; common respiratory failure reflects loss of central drive, without direct lung damage.
Hereditary bilateral enlargement of the parotid salivary glands; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Hereditary coagulation factor defect causing a bleeding tendency; no additional organ disease is established.
Isolated congenital absence or hypoplasia of the patella; an unspecified skin abnormality lacks evidence of common involvement.
Neurologic ocular-motor disorder with ataxia; transient gaze deviation and nystagmus do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Localized patellar articular-cartilage disease; the familial definition remains confined to the skeletal axis.
Inherited recurrent patellar dislocation directly affects knee joint stability.
PDA and hand malformations define the syndrome; eyelid ptosis occurs in 80-99%. Dental, hearing and developmental abnormalities are occasional.
PRPH2-related retinal pigment epithelial and macular dystrophy; visual impairment documented.
Adrenal dysfunction, severe intellectual disability and cutis laxa define syndrome; skeletal deformities 80-99%; bladder diverticula 80-99% omitted by cap.
Rare factor-deficiency bleeding disorder; supplied abnormal bleeding supports a haemostatic axis, but the specific defect is poorly characterized.
Developmental deformity of the sternum and thoracic skeleton; clinically significant cardiac or pulmonary impairment is not established in most patients.
Classic dominant disease affects neutrophil nuclear morphology. ID in 4/12 annotated cases may reflect rare severe forms and does not establish common neurologic damage across dominant PHA.
Central demyelination and autonomic degeneration define disease; bladder dysfunction and muscle weakness reflect neurologic impairment.
Crossed renal ectopia is a defining urinary malformation; pelvic lipomatosis involves deep pelvic fat, not necessarily skin or subcutis.
Brain malformations, coloboma/microphthalmia and hydronephrosis each 30-79%; cap omits oral malformations and microtia, also annotated 30-79%.
Inherited epidermal acantholysis causes chronic erosions and blistering; this is not autoimmune pemphigus.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; destructive oral mucosal blistering and erosions occur in 80-99%.
Peptide metabolic defect with skin ulcers and immune dysfunction; hearing loss 80-99%. Cap excludes cytopenias/splenomegaly (~65-75%) and hepatic, dental, skeletal and ocular findings.

decisions.haematologic: none: cytopenias in 3/4 and splenomegaly in 15/23 qualify, but the cap favors defining metabolic, skin and immune disease plus hearing loss in 80-99%.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immune dysfunction is frequent (80-99%), with recurrent infections in 4/4; this supports an intrinsic immune disorder.

basis: Skeletal muscle channelopathy and ventricular arrhythmias define the syndrome. Frequent dental morphology abnormalities do not establish functional oral damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental crowding and unspecified dentition abnormalities lack established functional damage; oligodontia and retained primary teeth are occasional (5-29%).

basis: Skeletal muscle channelopathy with obligate episodic hypokalemia and frequent muscle abnormalities; arrhythmia and respiratory weakness occur in <30%.
Skeletal-muscle channelopathy with episodic hyperkalemia; cardiac/respiratory complications are below 30%. Cerebral-palsy annotation conflicts with the established phenotype.
Skeletal-muscle channelopathy causing periodic paralysis; normal potassium does not establish a systemic electrolyte or metabolic disorder.
Infection-associated periodontal inflammation directly destroys dental attachment and alveolar jaw bone; rapid alveolar bone loss is a defining diagnostic feature.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the definition explicitly requires destructive alveolar bone loss; jaw bone is skeletal tissue, and defining bone destruction qualifies regardless of its dental location.

basis: Acromelic skeletal dysplasia with abnormal phalanges and epiphyses; hip osteoarthritis remains within the same axis.
Megaloblastic anemia from autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells and B12 malabsorption. Neurologic injury is variable and not reliably present in at least 30%.
An inherited anatomical variant of a peripheral nerve; no additional organ disease established.
Fibrosis of penile tunica albuginea is reproductive disease outside the axes; urethral constriction is not common defining damage, and Dupuytren disease is separate.
Inherited plasma-related impairment of phagocytosis is an immune-function disorder; no intrinsic blood-cell abnormality or other organ damage established.
