Adrenal medullary endocrine tumor; hypertension occurs in ~80-90% but does not itself establish direct cardiovascular injury. Cardiomyopathy occurs in <30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: common catecholamine-mediated hypertension (~80-90%) does not establish direct cardiovascular damage; cardiomyopathy occurs in <30%.

basis: Endocrine neoplasia syndrome involving thyroid, adrenal and parathyroid glands; hypertension is reported in 13/54, below 30%.
Pheochromocytoma and pancreatic islet-cell tumors define endocrine involvement. Frequencies of cardiovascular injury are unspecified; episodic hypertension alone does not establish damage.
Localized abnormal dilation of lip veins; vascular disease without evidence of separate oral mucosal damage.
Limb reduction defects, ear malformations with conductive deafness, and sinus arrhythmia are defining components.
Poorly characterized phosphoglucomutase-related hereditary entry; metabolic assignment is provisional because no clinical disease phenotype is supplied.
Inherited pentose phosphate pathway enzyme deficiency associated with hemolytic anemia.
Cerebral dysfunction, diabetes and nephropathy define the syndrome; defining deafness qualifies without a prevalence estimate and occupies involved because primary is capped at three.

decisions.renal: primary: nephropathy is an explicit defining component; prioritize intrinsic kidney damage within the three-primary cap.
decisions.otologic: involved: deafness is a defining component, retained through the diagnostic-feature exception after the primary cap.

basis: Frontotemporal neuronal degeneration with tau-containing Pick bodies causes dementia.
Congenital skin and hair depigmentation; white eyebrows and eyelashes do not establish ocular damage. Hearing and neurologic abnormalities occur in under 30%.
Skin hypopigmentation, neurologic impairment and progressive sensorineural deafness define the syndrome. Hearing loss occurs in 30-79%; megacolon is only 5-29%.

decisions.otologic: primary: progressive sensorineural deafness is a defining component of the syndrome, supported by HPO frequency of 30-79%.

basis: Retinal and choroidal atrophy with characteristic paravenous pigmentation.
Defined by mandibular and limb skeletal defects together with glossoptosis and cleft palate; oral structures fall within gastrointestinal.
Chronic pigmented purpuric dermatosis affects skin; localized capillary leakage does not establish systemic vasculitis or a coagulation disorder.
Congenital pituitary growth hormone deficiency; short stature is an endocrine consequence, and one scoliosis report does not establish common skeletal damage.
Familial PRP is an immune-mediated inflammatory keratinization disorder affecting skin and nails; ocular and oral abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: familial PRP has an autoinflammatory, immune-mediated cutaneous mechanism involving dysregulated CARD14 signaling.

basis: Record identifies an inherited platelet enzyme-activity phenotype; platelet biology maps to haematologic, but a clinical disease definition is absent.
Inherited abnormal spontaneous platelet aggregation; vascular injury is not established.
Platelet aggregation defect with thrombocytopenia and abnormal bleeding; listed neoplasms do not establish common additional organ damage.
Inherited platelet procoagulant activity deficiency causing a haemostatic disorder.
The annotated inherited trait concerns platelet membrane properties; no other organ involvement is established.
Inherited impairment of platelet responsiveness is a blood-cell functional disorder.
Intrinsic platelet signaling and aggregation defect causes abnormal hemostasis; epistaxis does not establish airway disease.
Familial pleural air accumulation and lung collapse; associated syndromes do not establish additional organ involvement.
Oral inflammation/leukoplakia affects 8/11; esophageal strictures and persistent finger deformities occur in 30-79%. Urethral stenosis affects only 4/22.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: camptodactyly is persistent finger contracture and is annotated at 30-79%; this supports locomotor involvement beyond cutaneous webbing alone.

basis: Hereditary poikiloderma with cutaneous sclerosis; no additional organ damage is established as common.
Pectoral muscle and hand defects define syndrome; subcutaneous tissue absence occurs in 80-99%, renal hypoplasia in 30-79%; cardiac anomalies are occasional.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: absence of subcutaneous fat in 80-99% represents structural tissue loss; subcutis belongs to this axis.

basis: PKD1-related renal cystic disease; mitral regurgitation in 51/163 (~31%) supports cardiovascular involvement; hepatic cysts usually preserve function.
Inherited tubulointerstitial kidney disease with progressive renal dysfunction; hyperuricemia is not universal across this umbrella.
Numerous hepatic cysts define the disease; renal cysts have unspecified frequency and do not establish common renal functional damage.
Congenital digit duplication and syndactyly; cutaneous fusion is part of the limb malformation.
Defining oral and digital malformations; intellectual disability 8/8 and hearing impairment 2/3. Cardiac and ocular defects reported in 1/3 omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 8/8 and developmental delay in 5/5 support common intrinsic neurodevelopmental impairment beyond the defining oral-digital malformations.

basis: Four-limb postaxial polydactyly and progressive myopia define the syndrome, both in 80-99%. Hernias do not establish bowel damage; cryptorchidism is outside the axes.
Congenital duplication of skeletal components of the thumb.
Congenital thumb and digit skeletal malformations; associated systemic syndromes are separate diagnoses.
Isolated congenital digit malformation with preaxial polydactyly and triphalangeal digits.
Congenital duplication and fusion of digits, with abnormal phalanges.
Immune-mediated chronic photodermatosis; persistent cheilitis affects ~60-70% and chronic conjunctivitis ~30-50%, sometimes with scarring. Renal injury is not established as common.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent inflammatory cheilitis affects ~60-70%, constituting chronic lip/oral mucosal disease.
decisions.ocular: involved: chronic conjunctival inflammation affects ~30-50% and may scar; this is persistent ocular disease rather than transient conjunctival injection.

basis: Fibro-osseous replacement affects multiple bones; associated endocrinopathy defines the separate McCune-Albright syndrome.
Expansile skeletal osteolysis; conductive hearing loss in 16/20 from ossicular destruction; premature tooth loss affects most and is a defining manifestation.
Juvenile gastrointestinal polyposis, predominantly colorectal; blood-loss anemia is a separately diagnosed consequence.
Neoplastic or non-neoplastic polyp arising from the stomach.
GI polyps and vascular malformations define syndrome; pulmonary AVMs cause shunting in 7/10. Hepatic AVMs (4/7) need not impair liver; anemia reflects blood loss.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia occurs in 12/14 (~86%), but is secondary to bleeding and separately diagnosed; no intrinsic blood-cell or marrow disorder is established.

basis: Gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyposis and characteristic mucocutaneous pigmentation define the syndrome; additional cancers are separate diseases or risks.
Hereditary polyposis directly occupies the intestinal mucosa.
Intestinal polyposis and multiple bony exostoses are the defining manifestations.
GI polyposis and characteristic alopecia, nail dystrophy and pigmentation define the syndrome. Anemia reflects GI losses/malabsorption; vascular damage is insufficiently specified.
Multiple recurrent gastrointestinal inflammatory fibroid polyps and stromal tumors; inflammatory terminology does not establish immune-mediated disease.
Congenital digital and limb malformations; abnormal dermatoglyphics do not establish skin dysfunction; hearing and ocular findings occur in 5-29%.
Polysyndactyly defines syndrome; developmental delay 14/45 (~31%) and callosal hypoplasia 4/12 support neurologic involvement near the threshold.
Synovial cyst arising from the knee joint or semimembranous bursa.
Cerebral small-vessel disease causes hemorrhage and porencephaly. Retinal tortuosity alone is non-damaging; retinal hemorrhage occurred in 1/6.
Inherited cutaneous keratinization disorder with porokeratosis in 9/9 patients; the causal gene alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Porokeratosis with persistent keratotic lesions of palms, soles and other skin; no qualifying extracutaneous involvement.
Isolated palmoplantar epidermal keratoderma with characteristic spiny projections.
Inherited cutaneous keratinization disorder with porokeratotic lesions; MVK involvement alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disease.
Hepatic heme-synthesis disorder with defining neurovisceral attacks; renal insufficiency occurs in 30-79%. Episodic autonomic hypertension does not establish cardiovascular damage.
audit_reason: Add hepatic to primary: the disease arises in hepatic heme synthesis and is explicitly an acute hepatic porphyria. Primary location does not require the common tissue damage required for an involved organ.

basis: Acquired hepatic uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency causes porphyrin accumulation and defining photosensitive blistering with skin fragility.
Inherited hepatic porphyrin metabolism disorder with photosensitive skin fragility and blistering; cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma are separate complications.
Hepatic heme-synthesis disorder; motor polyneuropathy and blistering skin erosions each occur in 30-79%. Abdominal pain alone does not establish GI damage.

decisions.hepatic: primary: explicitly an acute hepatic porphyria, located in hepatic heme synthesis; primary location does not require frequent liver injury.

basis: Isolated congenital absence or reduction of postaxial digits and associated hand and foot bones.
Posterior-column dysfunction causes sensory ataxia and impaired proprioception; scoliosis frequency is unspecified.
Hypothalamic-pituitary and neurodevelopmental dysfunction define PWS; scoliosis occurs in 150/180 (~83%) and strabismus in 30-79%.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent strabismus causes ocular alignment dysfunction and is annotated frequent (30-79%).

basis: Defining congenital limb abnormalities, urethral hypospadias and absent second-toe nails affect skeletal, urinary and nail structures.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central origin does not establish neurologic damage.
Autonomous testicular androgen production causes precocious puberty; accelerated skeletal maturation reflects hormone action rather than intrinsic skeletal disease.
Anorectal and sacral malformations define the triad; anterior sacral meningocele occurs in 30-79%; urinary anomalies are generally below 30%.
Cerebral vascular amyloid deposition and progressive neurodegeneration define British familial dementia.
Presenile dementia establishes neurologic loss of function; the supplied phenotype confirms dementia.
Familial idiopathic priapism affects erectile reproductive tissue; no independent vascular disease or urinary-organ damage is established.
Inherited platelet secretion defect causes impaired haemostasis; bleeding sites do not establish separate organ involvement.
Defining skin and skeletal disease; progressive arterial damage affects most over the course; hearing impairment 80-99%. Endocrine and oral abnormalities omitted by cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: progressive arterial degeneration affects most over the typical course; skin and skeletal abnormalities establish the clinical syndrome.

basis: Defining skin changes, immunodeficiency and gonadal failure; visual loss/cataracts 80-99%. Cap omits neurologic, skeletal, dental, hepatic and cardiac involvement.

decisions.neurologic: none: cognitive impairment and thalamic abnormalities at 80-99% qualify, but the four-organ cap prioritizes defining skin, immune and endocrine disease plus progressive visual loss.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and gonadal hormone deficiency occur in 80-99%, supporting endocrine gland failure.

basis: Mandibular skeletal malposition and dental malocclusion define the disease; open bite occurs in 80-99%. Craniosynostosis is occasional.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental malocclusion is the supplied definition, with open bite in 80-99%; teeth and dental occlusion belong to this axis

basis: Inherited impairment of forearm rotational movement defines a locomotor disorder.
Prostate malignancy arises in a reproductive organ outside the axes; metastatic disease does not establish shared organ involvement.
Inherited anticoagulant protein deficiency; thromboses are separately diagnosed complications, and warfarin skin necrosis is treatment-related.
Poorly characterized inherited plasma proteolytic-activity phenotype; provisional blood-axis assignment, with no defined additional organ damage.
Definition includes skeletal, skin and CNS overgrowth; vascular malformations occur in 80-99%. Ear-canal exostoses (30-79%) omitted at cap; lung lobation alone adds no axis.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the supplied definition explicitly includes central nervous system overgrowth among the defining affected tissues.

basis: Heme synthesis defect causes cutaneous phototoxic injury. Liver failure affects ~5%; anemia frequency is variable and not securely above 30%; gallstones are a separate diagnosis.
Medial protrusion of the acetabulum causes structural hip disease and contracture.
Hereditary localized cutaneous pruritus is the only documented manifestation; no evidence establishes a neuropathy or systemic organ damage.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, epiphyses and joints, with short limbs, deformity and frequent osteoarthritis.
Renal tubular sodium transport disorder defined by hypertension and hypokalemia; cerebral ischemia is a separately diagnosed vascular complication.
Hereditary contracture disorder resembling arthrogryposis; no supplied evidence establishes additional organ damage.
Inherited cutaneous disorder with abnormal skin; no evidence of other organ involvement.
Defined by abnormal fibrillar material in anterior eye tissues; subsequent glaucoma remains within the ocular axis.
Hereditary open-angle glaucoma with optic nerve injury and visual field loss.
Kidney-restricted mineralocorticoid resistance causes renal salt wasting, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia and metabolic acidosis.
Hair-shaft abnormality with irregular nodular thickening and fragility; hair belongs to the dermatologic axis.
Inherited platelet dysfunction and thrombocytopenia cause bleeding; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate skin or gastrointestinal damage.
PXE is an elastic-tissue disorder of skin, ocular tissues and arterial walls, with attenuated expression here. Gastrointestinal and cerebral hemorrhage are minority complications.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: arterial elastic-tissue disease is a defining location of PXE; the record supports arterial mineralization and occlusive stenosis.

basis: ID and skeletal defects define syndrome; severe hypermetropia and delayed puberty 80-99%, hypothyroidism 30-79%; oral, ear and cardiac anomalies omitted by cap.
Isolated congenital cervical skin webbing; associated facial morphology does not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Conjunctival fibrovascular growth extending onto the cornea; neurological ancestry does not establish nervous system disease.
Defining contractures, skeletal fusions and cutaneous pterygia; ptosis in 5/9 supports ocular involvement. Ventricular septal defect in 2/7 is below 30%.
Antecubital skin webbing with restricted elbow extension and radioulnar joint maldevelopment defines the syndrome.
Congenital eyelid dysfunction; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Defined by eyelid ptosis, strabismus and ectopic pupils; all are ocular abnormalities.
Developmental dysplasia of the pubic bone directly affects the skeleton.
Congenital cardiac outflow, pulmonary valve/arterial and ventricular septal malformations; pulmonary vessels belong to cardiovascular.
Recurrent alveolar hemorrhage and iron-deficiency anemia form the defining clinical triad with infiltrates; anemia affects 80-99%. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not show hepatic damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: iron-deficiency anemia is a major diagnostic feature of idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis and occurs in 80-99%; diagnostic criteria qualify despite blood-loss causation.

basis: Benign reactive lymphoid nodules occupy lung tissue; not lymphoma, and immunodeficiency or autoimmune findings occur in only 1-4%.
Pulmonary valve stenosis, atrial septal defect and ECG abnormalities are cardiac features; pulmonary valve disease is cardiovascular.
Pulmonic valve stenosis and hearing loss define the syndrome; the pulmonary valve belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Persistent embryonic pupillary membrane, with associated corneal and lens abnormalities confined to the eye.
Pregnancy-associated inflammatory skin eruption; pregnancy does not remove its defining dermatologic axis.
Cutaneous purpura from small-vessel fragility defines the condition; platelet and coagulation function are generally normal.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous bruising/purpura is the defining disease manifestation, rather than an additional incidental or transient rash.

basis: Hypertrophic pyloric obstruction; vomiting-related alkalosis does not establish additional lasting organ damage.
Inherited posterior radial-head dislocation with restricted elbow extension and antecubital pterygium.
Defining radial/thumb malformations, urethral hypospadias and maxillary dental diastema. Dermatoglyphic differences do not establish skin damage.
Defining triad of radial hypoplasia, choanal atresia and convergent strabismus affects skeleton, nasal airway and eyes.
Limb reduction and renal malformations define the syndrome; supplied phenotypes report pleural effusions/chylothorax and respiratory failure in 80-99%.
Absent radius and cleft lip/palate define the syndrome; palate and oral structures fall under gastrointestinal.
Allergic hypersensitivity to ragweed; sensitivity alone does not establish airway or ocular damage.
Inherited skin hypopigmentation; no additional organ involvement is supplied.
Peripheral arterial vasospasm; episodic skin discoloration is not lasting skin damage. Autoimmunity applies only to some secondary cases.
Defining heart, neurodevelopmental and urinary malformations; dental abnormalities 80–99%, gingival overgrowth 30–79%. Hearing and skeletal defects also 30–79%, omitted at cap.
Inherited permeability abnormality of red blood cell membranes; no evidence establishes common damage to another organ.
Hereditary erythrocyte membrane phospholipid abnormality causing hemolysis; jaundice reflects red-cell destruction rather than liver damage.
Renal acidification defect with metabolic acidosis; nephrocalcinosis is renal. Osteomalacia occurs in only 1/18 patients.
Proximal tubular bicarbonate loss causes hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis; ocular, skeletal and neurologic damage is occasional (5-29%) and excluded.
Reticulate pigmentation and hyperkeratosis define the skin disorder; glycosylation defects concern particular subtypes. Arthritis is very rare at 1–4%.
Congenital absence or severe developmental failure of the retina causes visual loss.
Disorder of retinal arteries, with retinal hemorrhage in 2/3 reported patients.
Retinal cone degeneration causes progressive visual and color-vision loss.
Separation of retinal layers directly threatens visual function; neurological ancestry does not indicate additional brain or nerve disease.
Hereditary structural abnormality of retinal veins defines both ocular location and venous involvement; systemic vascular disease is not required.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the lesion directly affects veins, which belong to this axis even when confined to the retina.

basis: RP1-related retinal photoreceptor degeneration with night blindness, visual field constriction and reduced acuity.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration; no evidence of common extraocular disease.
IMPDH1-related retinal degeneration causing night blindness, visual field constriction and reduced acuity.
Malignant retinal tumor; secondary nonocular cancers are separate diseases, and intracranial tumors or extension affect a minority.
Progressive pigmentary retinal degeneration causing visual loss.
Inherited splitting and degeneration of retinal layers.
Autoimmune erosive synovitis defines RA. Clinically significant lung disease, vasculitis and other extra-articular damage are minority or separately coded conditions.
Immune-mediated rheumatoid variant defined by polyarthritis, subchondral bone cysts and subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules.
Anterior segment dysgenesis and dental hypoplasia define the syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Limbal dermoids extending into cornea and conjunctiva; skin-like histology does not establish skin disease.
Isolated lifelong hair-shaft abnormality; hair is within the dermatologic axis.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; gingival overgrowth and oral/dental malformations occur in 30-79%. External genital anomalies do not establish endocrine damage.
Defined by cutaneous atrophy, milia, hypotrichosis and skin tumors; cutaneous vasodilation does not establish separate cardiovascular damage.
Hereditary sensorimotor neuropathy; fixed pes cavus, talipes and scoliosis occur in 30-79%. Nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Developmental disability and broad digits define RSTS; ocular defects/strabismus >50% and dental/palatal abnormalities >30%; renal anomalies near 30% omitted at cap.
Growth restriction and limb asymmetry define SRS; recurrent hypoglycemia and insulin resistance occur in 30-79%. Motor delay alone does not establish neural damage.
Skeletal dysplasia and intellectual/developmental disability define it; ptosis occurs in 80-99%. Dental crowding alone does not establish oral dysfunction; retinal abnormalities are 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental crowding and narrow mouth are dysmorphic findings without demonstrated oral tissue damage or loss of function.

basis: Defining triad comprises corneal dystrophy, gingival fibromatosis and failure of tooth eruption.
Congenital absence or hypoplasia of lacrimal and salivary glands defines the disorder; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Calculi occupy and can obstruct salivary ducts, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Benign neoplasm arising predominantly in salivary glands; uncommon respiratory tract sites do not characterize most patients.
Cleft palate, microcephaly and skeletal growth defects define it; ptosis occurs in 30-79%. Nail hypoplasia omitted at cap; renal damage frequency unknown.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis represents eyelid dysfunction and occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining prenatal short stature and skeletal abnormalities; delayed skeletal maturation occurs in 80-99%, muscle atrophy in 30-79%.

basis: Scalp aplasia and postaxial polydactyly define the syndrome; encephalocele is reported in 30-79%.
Defining scalp defects and external-ear hypoplasia; renal insufficiency 5/15 (~33%), cataracts 30-79%. Dental abnormalities and syndactyly omitted by cap.
Neurogenic scapuloperoneal disorder with intrinsic myofibrillar pathology: rimmed vacuoles in 6/8 and shoulder atrophy in 13/15. Dysphagia affects only 2/15.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myofibrillar disease ancestry and intrinsic muscle pathology, including rimmed vacuoles in 6/8, establish muscle as a defining site.

basis: Motor neuron disease with defining progressive scapular and peroneal muscle wasting in most patients; common intrinsic pulmonary disease is not established.
Myosin-storage skeletal myopathy with weakness and structural muscle abnormalities; reduced vital capacity occurs in 25% and does not establish direct lung disease.
Osteochondrosis of vertebral epiphyses causes structural vertebral deformity and kyphosis.
Ulnar defects and apocrine, hair and nail abnormalities define it; delayed puberty indicates endocrine dysfunction in 30-79%; other organ defects are occasional.
Intestinal schistosome infection; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish common hepatic functional injury.
Schizophrenia is a psychiatric disorder without an axis. Listed congenital anomalies lack evidence of common direct organ involvement.
Keratoderma, cutaneous sclerosis and nail hypoplasia define Huriez syndrome; sclerodactyly here reflects skin fibrosis.
Congenital corneal opacity and scleralization define sclerocornea.
Familial systemic sclerosis; esophageal fibrosis/dysmotility affects ~80% and interstitial lung disease ~40–60%; renal crisis is a minority complication.
Benign epidermal skin neoplasm.
Defining microstomia/palatal, external-ear and eyelid anomalies; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Skin and hair findings are predominantly morphology without established damage.
Inherited ineffective erythropoiesis with ring sideroblasts and anemia; common extrahematologic damage is not established.
Sinoatrial node dysfunction and high myopia jointly define the syndrome.
Bony bridging of the sella turcica is a skeletal anomaly; pituitary dysfunction is not established.
Omphalocele, laryngopharyngeal hypoplasia and scoliosis define syndrome; developmental impairment occurs in 80-99%. Eyelid and eyebrow morphology alone does not establish damage.
Craniosynostosis, skeletal abnormalities, intellectual disability and cardiac anomalies define SGS; strabismus and ptosis occur in 30–79%.
Optic nerve hypoplasia, pituitary dysfunction and midline brain defects define disease; cleft palate is annotated as frequent (30-79%).
Interferonopathy with defining aortic calcification and skeletal disease; dental dysplasia is a defining diagnostic feature. Psoriasiform skin disease omitted at cap.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by delayed epiphyseal and carpal ossification and characteristic bone abnormalities.
Primary lung carcinoma; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine gland disease. Metastases and paraneoplastic syndromes are separate diagnoses.
Neurodevelopmental and skeletal abnormalities define SMS; dental defects and tracheobronchial anomalies each occur in 80-99%. Recurrent otitis is a separate infection.
Noninflammatory vasculopathy defined by cerebral ischemia and persistent cutaneous vascular disease; reduced GFR annotated 30-79% supports renal involvement.
Corticospinal tract degeneration defines SPG3A. Weakness and amyotrophy are neurogenic; urinary symptoms do not establish urinary-organ damage, and skeletal deformity frequency is unspecified.
Progressive corticospinal tract disease; weakness and urinary urgency reflect neurologic dysfunction, without evidence of common direct muscle or urinary tract damage.
Spastic paraplegia, epilepsy and intellectual disability define a hereditary neurological syndrome.
Paraplegia, intellectual disability, nephropathy and deafness define the syndrome (80-99%). Hypertension (30-79%) is a secondary renal complication, without established direct vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension is annotated in 30-79%, but is a separately diagnosed consequence of nephropathy rather than direct cardiovascular involvement.

basis: Spastic paraplegia and extrapyramidal dysfunction define a neurologic disorder.
Spastic paraplegia, demyelinating neuropathy and atrophic poikiloderma define the syndrome; distal amyotrophy reflects denervation.
Progressive spastic paraplegia and intellectual disability accompany precocious puberty from hormone-producing Leydig cell hyperplasia.
Spastic paraplegia and dementia define neurological disease; optic atrophy defines ocular involvement.
Speech developmental delay and strabismus define the syndrome; ptosis is also present in 80-99%. Earlobe creases and ear position do not establish hearing or vestibular dysfunction.
Sperm protamine entry concerns reproductive biology, outside the axes; the record does not establish a clinical disease or other organ damage.
Red-cell membrane disease causes hemolytic anemia; splenic involvement remains on the blood axis. Jaundice is not liver injury; gallstones are a separate disease.
Congenital neural-tube and vertebral closure defect; bladder dysfunction is not established across the umbrella, which includes occult forms.
Adhesive inflammation and fibrosis of spinal arachnoid injure nerve roots/spinal cord; infection or autoimmunity is not intrinsic to all cases.
Anterior horn cell degeneration defines disease; weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation. Structural foot damage at a frequency of at least 30% is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: denervation weakness and wasting do not establish direct muscle disease; frequency of damaging skeletal deformities is unspecified.

basis: Anterior horn disease with near-universal denervation atrophy; persistent skeletal-muscle tissue loss and functional impairment are integral manifestations, not a separate disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: characteristic, near-universal denervation atrophy represents persistent muscle tissue loss, beyond weakness alone.

basis: Anterior horn motor-neuron disease; proximal amyotrophy occurs in 6/8 (75%), establishing persistent structural muscle loss from denervation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: proximal amyotrophy in 6/8 (75%) documents actual muscle loss integral to the disease; primary pathology remains in motor neurons.

basis: Intradural spinal arachnoid cysts occupy the central nervous system and can compress the spinal cord or nerve roots.
Segmental anterior horn cell disease; muscle wasting results from denervation rather than direct disease of skeletal muscle.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: defining hand muscle atrophy is secondary to motor-neuron loss and denervation; direct muscle injury is not established.

basis: Spinocerebellar dysfunction and peripheral neuropathy define disease; muscle atrophy is neurogenic, without evidence of a separate direct myopathy.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; nystagmus, diplopia and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct ocular or gastrointestinal damage.
Cerebellar and brainstem degeneration; abnormal eye movements, dysphagia and muscle weakness reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Spinocerebellar degeneration and defining loss of pupillary function; limited phenotype detail supports no additional axes.
Limb/jaw dysostosis, splenic fusion and oral malformations define syndrome. Individual oral HPO findings are 5-29%; lung/cardiac defects also 5-29%; unspecified skin findings lack damage evidence.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate and microglossia belong to the defining orofacial phenotype; mouth is gastrointestinal, despite individual oral HPO frequencies of 5-29%.

basis: Defining splenic disease with germinal-center hypoplasia and reduced helper T cells indicates a combined splenic and immune disorder.
Congenital lower-lip abnormality with dental findings; lips and dentition belong to the mouth axis.
Congenital split hands and feet plus absent teeth define the syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital limb malformation; cleft palate in 30-79%, hearing impairment in 35%, intellectual disability in 33%. Cardiovascular malformations in 13% are excluded.
Mandibulofacial and limb dysostosis define it; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Hearing impairment is occasional; abnormal pinna shape alone is insufficient.
Split-hand/split-foot malformations and congenital ocular dysfunction, especially nystagmus, define the syndrome.
Defining split limbs, spinal defects, obstructive urinary anomalies and spina bifida; pulmonary hypoplasia and hydrocephalus are occasional (<30%).
Spondyloepimetaphyseal bone dysplasia and congenital hypotrichosis are defining features.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia and punctate corneal dystrophy are defining components.
Congenital vertebral and epiphyseal dysplasia; myopia in 42/93 (~45%) and hearing impairment in 32/87 (~37%). Retinal detachment and cord compression are minority complications.
Skeletal dysplasia, sensorineural deafness and myopia form the defining syndrome described by the name and synonym.
Skeletal dysplasia involving vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses, with osteoporosis and joint degeneration.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae and epiphyses, with abnormal bone growth and early joint degeneration.
Structural displacement of a vertebra; neurological compression is not an obligatory or established common component.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; myopia and hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%; spinal cord compression and airway disease are occasional.
Defining vertebral, metaphyseal, pelvic and joint abnormalities constitute a skeletal dysplasia.
Vertebral and metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia; myopia, palatal defects and auditory canal stenosis are occasional, each 5-29%.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, metaphyses and hips; visual impairment and other ocular findings occur in only 5–29%.
Degenerative cervical vertebral and joint disease. Radiculopathy or myelopathy is not established in at least 30% by the supplied evidence.
Congenital elevated scapula with shoulder muscle hypoplasia and impaired shoulder anatomy; thoracic ancestry alone does not establish lung disease.
Inherited persistent developmental speech-fluency disorder; no additional organ damage established.
Stapes fixation with conductive hearing loss and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; hypermetropia affects 80-99%.
Multiple dermal sebaceous duct cysts define the disease; kidney stones are occasional and separately diagnosed.
Defined by multiple cutaneous steatocystomas and natal teeth; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Ovarian endocrine dysfunction and hyperandrogenism define PCOS. Hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage; diabetes is a separate disease.
Brain/radial defects define syndrome; nasal aplasia and auditory canal atresia each 80-99%. Cap excludes defining cardiac/renal defects and ocular, oral and gallbladder anomalies.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: defining cardiac defects qualify, but the four-axis cap prioritizes brain, limbs and nasal/auditory atresia; specified cardiac lesions occur in 5-29%.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: nasal aplasia affects 80-99%, a permanent structural defect of the upper airway.
decisions.ocular: none: microphthalmia affects 30-79%, but is omitted under the cap in favor of more frequent nasal and auditory canal defects.

basis: Premature fusion of sternal sutures is a structural bone disorder; no other organ involvement is established.
Defined by skeletal/joint dysplasia, sensorineural hearing loss and cleft palate; ocular abnormalities are explicitly absent.
Immune-mediated CNS inhibitory dysfunction; spasms and rigidity do not establish intrinsic muscle damage; endocrine autoimmune comorbidities are separate.
Skin/fascial fibrosis and fixed contractures define disease; myopia 6/8 supports ocular dysfunction. Reflux lacks established direct GI injury; neuropathy 2/8 is below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: fixed joint contractures and restricted mobility are defining manifestations; elbow contractures occurred in 8/8 and knee contractures in 7/8.

basis: Red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolytic anemia. Thromboembolism is particularly associated with splenectomy; jaundice does not establish liver damage.
Inherited red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolytic anemia; pseudohyperkalemia is an artifact rather than systemic electrolyte disease.
Defective platelet granules cause impaired haemostasis; bleeding sites do not establish separate organ damage.
Defining platelet dysfunction/asplenia, myopathy and ichthyosis (80-99%). Characteristic dyslexia and speech abnormalities (80-99%) support neurologic involvement; miosis lacks functional injury.

decisions.neurologic: involved: characteristic dyslexia and speech abnormalities (80-99%) support neurodevelopmental dysfunction; migraine alone would not qualify.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent ichthyosis is explicitly part of the defining syndrome and occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Skeletal defects, GH deficiency and dextrocardia/PDA define syndrome; renal hypoplasia/aplasia 80-99%; anorectal atresia and neurological deficits also 80-99%, omitted at cap.
Familial striae represent structural changes of the dermis.
Defining cerebral and facial capillary malformations; ocular damage includes glaucoma and optic atrophy, each frequent (30-79%).
Inherited abnormal hemoglobin impairs red-cell oxygen carriage; cyanosis does not establish pulmonary or cardiovascular damage.
Congenital suprabulbar cerebral palsy causes oropharyngeal weakness. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction; glue ear and respiratory infections are separate conditions.
Structural stenosis of the aorta and sometimes other arteries; pulmonary artery involvement remains cardiovascular.
Congenital fusion of toe phalangeal joints is a skeletal disorder.
Congenital skeletal fusion involving the hand and first metacarpal.
Defined by fusion and ankylosis of distal interphalangeal joints; nail findings have unspecified frequency.
Congenital fusion and malformation of finger/toe bones and joints; dermatoglyphic variants do not establish skin damage; hearing loss only 5-29%.
Congenital joint ankylosis and carpal/tarsal fusion; hearing impairment is frequent (30-79%).
Non-syndromic congenital skeletal malformation causes fused and additional digits.
Isolated congenital finger fusion with associated digital skeletal abnormalities; cutaneous syndactyly is a limb malformation.
Congenital limb malformation with complete syndactyly, polydactyly and associated skeletal abnormalities.
Congenital syndactyly with metacarpal and metatarsal fusion; cutaneous webbing does not establish separate skin damage.
Defined by digital skeletal malformations, syndactyly and abnormal earlobes; no evidence of other organ damage.
Carpal and tarsal synostoses cause skeletal stiffness and immobility; nail abnormalities have unspecified frequency.
Multiple skeletal synostoses; hypermetropia in 4/5 and ptosis in 2/5 support ocular involvement. Hearing-loss annotations each report 1/5; overlap is unclear.
Elbow, wrist and digit skeletal dysplasia defines disease; structural fingernail abnormalities are reported in 80-99%.
Fusion of carpal, tarsal and phalangeal bones defines the syndrome; hearing abnormality occurs in only 1/20 patients.
Familial synovial cartilage proliferation with skeletal growth impairment; disease is localized to the locomotor system.
Immune-mediated granulomatous arthritis and uveitis define disease; granulomatous dermatitis occurs in 42/44 (~95%). The three-primary cap places skin involvement in the involved tier.

decisions.ocular: primary: granulomatous uveitis is a defining diagnostic feature, present in 39/54 (~72%), with potential permanent visual damage.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: granulomatous dermatitis occurs in 42/44 (~95%); the primary cap reserves three positions for immune mechanism, arthritis and uveitis.

basis: Multiple benign cutaneous sweat-duct tumours.
Spinal cord syrinx causes sensory and motor dysfunction; scoliosis frequency is insufficiently established for an additional axis.
Congenital coalition of talus and navicular with associated skeletal fusion abnormalities.
Abnormal bony, cartilaginous or fibrous union between tarsal bones.
Hereditary abnormal tooth morphology; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Natal teeth are a dental developmental abnormality; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Supernumerary teeth are a dental developmental disorder; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Persistent widespread dilatation of cutaneous small blood vessels defines this skin vascular disorder.
Vascular malformations and characteristic cutaneous telangiectases define HHT1; pulmonary AVMs occur in ~45% and cause shunting. Hepatic AVMs alone do not establish hepatic dysfunction.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: characteristic mucocutaneous telangiectases are a major diagnostic criterion of HHT and remain defining in HHT1. Pulmonary involvement is supported by common shunting AVMs.

basis: Abnormal positioning of the medial eyelid canthi; an eyelid disorder.
Immune large-vessel vasculitis; permanent visual loss <30%; ischemia annotations and visual symptoms do not establish common lasting brain or eye damage.
Defining finger extensor tendon malformation; multiple subcutaneous lipomas occur in 80-99%, supporting dermatologic occupation.
Torsion directly injures reproductive testicular tissue; persistent endocrine failure is not a typical defining consequence.
Defined by four congenital cardiac abnormalities; the supplied extracardiac HPO features are not characteristic of most patients with isolated tetralogy.
Tetralogy of Fallot and developmental glaucoma are the defining structural cardiac and ocular abnormalities.
Congenital skeletal limb malformation with one digit on each extremity; typically isolated.
Silent beta-thalassemia allele reduces beta-globin synthesis; no evidence of common damage outside blood.
Severe skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia/respiratory failure in most, profound intellectual disability annotated 80-99%, hearing impairment 30-79%; redundant skin alone is not damage.
Skeletal dysplasia; lung hypoplasia and cognitive impairment each 80-99%, hearing impairment 30-79%. Redundant skin alone does not establish skin damage.
Defining skeletal dysplasia of ribs and pelvis with structural laryngeal stenosis.
Inherited platelet number and function disorder causing macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; petechiae do not establish independent skin disease.
Inherited platelet deficiency and dysfunction cause bleeding; bruising and epistaxis do not establish independent skin or airway damage.
Inherited sustained thrombocytosis with platelet dysfunction; the limb-reduction parent conflicts with the definition and phenotype evidence.
Cyclic reduction in circulating platelets defines a blood-cell disorder; an immune mechanism is not established for this concept.
Platelet and megakaryocyte disorder; intellectual disability and cardiovascular malformations each occur in 30-79%.
Autoimmune platelet destruction; petechiae/purpura are bleeding signs. Arterial thrombosis is a separate complication, and the supplied 30-79% frequency is not clinically credible.
Inherited coagulation disorder; the supplied definition explicitly includes venous thrombus, supporting cardiovascular classification beyond susceptibility.
Inherited coagulation abnormality causing activated protein C resistance; venous thrombosis is a separate disease whose risk is increased.
Congenital thumb aplasia or hypoplasia; unspecified cardiovascular abnormalities lack evidence of >=30% prevalence.
Thumb malformations, alopecia and pigmentation define it; intellectual/developmental disability and dental abnormalities each occur in 30-79%.
Thumb ankylosis, brachydactyly and intellectual disability define the syndrome; obesity alone adds no direct organ damage.
Thymic immunodeficiency, congenital heart defects and hypoparathyroidism define disease; intellectual disability 72/78. Scoliosis 37/78 omitted at cap.
Cyst of the embryonic thyroid migration tract; classified as a thyroid developmental disorder.
Follicular or papillary carcinoma arising in the thyroid gland.
Familial nonmedullary thyroid carcinoma arises in an endocrine gland; the unrelated syndromic parent does not establish neurologic or pulmonary involvement.
Thyroid hormone transport disorder with euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia and possible goiter; no established extra-endocrine damage.
Generalized thyroid hormone resistance; speech and language developmental delay in 2/2 annotated patients supports neurologic involvement, although the sample is small.
Disordered proximal tibial growth with genu varum and epiphyseal abnormalities.
Congenital limb dysostosis with tibial hypoplasia/aplasia, polydactyly and triphalangeal thumbs.
Bilateral structural rotational deformity of the tibiae; associated findings are also skeletal.
Substance dependence has no axis; tobacco-associated pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases are separately diagnosed conditions.
Inherited abnormality of fifth-toe phalangeal number affects the skeleton.
Hereditary toe deformity with an annotated skeletal abnormality.
Congenital rotational deformity of the fifth toe; nail abnormality has no frequency or evidence of substantial functional damage.
Hereditary variation in relative toe length; skeletal anatomy is the specified phenotype.
Inherited structural foot anomaly characterized by an increased first-to-second toe gap.
Dental malposition with variable congenital tooth absence; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defining hypodontia and dental dysplasia affect the gastrointestinal axis; nail hypoplasia and dysplasia affect the dermatologic axis.
The definition specifies fibromatosis within the sternocleidomastoid muscle, causing congenital muscular torticollis.
Benign bony exostoses of the hard palate and mandible; the affected tissue is bone.
Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, hepatic injury and systemic microvascular endothelial injury define HELLP; glomerular injury with proteinuria occurs in 30-79%. AKI is rare.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: systemic endothelial injury and thrombotic microangiopathy define the syndrome; cardiovascular labeling does not depend solely on associated hypertension.
decisions.renal: involved: proteinuria in 30-79% reflects direct glomerular endothelial injury within the syndrome; rare severe AKI is not the basis for inclusion.

basis: Congenital oesophageal discontinuity and tracheoesophageal communication directly affect the digestive tract and airway; fistula occurs in 80-99%.
Osteocartilaginous nodules occupy and may obstruct the trachea and bronchi; their composition does not indicate locomotor skeletal disease.
Inherited movement disorder causing chin myoclonus; mentalis contractions do not establish a separate muscle disease.
Intention tremor and ataxia define neurologic dysfunction; lipofuscin deposition alone does not establish a metabolic disorder. Premature graying does not establish skin damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: nonspecific metabolism/homeostasis annotation and lipofuscin accumulation do not establish a defined inborn metabolic disorder.

basis: Inherited essential tremor is a neurologic movement disorder.
Defined by tremor/movement disorder and duodenal ulceration; nystagmus accompanies the neurologic syndrome without established intrinsic eye damage.
Defining hair/nail abnormalities, dental enamel defects and taurodontism, and increased bone density involve all three axes.
Abnormal eyelash hair growth; cataract frequency is unspecified and does not establish common ocular damage.
Benign dermal tumors; definition explicitly excludes systemic organ involvement.
Multiple benign cutaneous tumors of hair-follicle origin.
Defining skeletal dysplasia and sparse hair; dental abnormalities, including supernumerary teeth, occur in 30-79%.
Hair shaft abnormalities, sparse brittle hair and dry skin define disease; sparse eyelashes do not establish ocular damage.
Trigeminal nerve dysfunction defines the disorder. Vascular compression does not establish vascular damage; feeding difficulty and ocular pain do not establish organ injury.
Mechanical flexor tendon impingement with pulley narrowing and tendon sheath thickening.
Inherited triglyceride storage disorder; supplied findings do not establish common functional damage to another organ.
Triglyceride storage disorder supported by metabolic ancestors; obesity alone does not establish damage to another organ.
Metopic craniosynostosis defines the skeletal disorder; speech/language developmental delay is reported in 1/1, supporting neurologic dysfunction with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.neurologic: involved: speech/language developmental delay is documented in 1/1; this supports neurologic dysfunction, although the denominator leaves its usual frequency uncertain.

basis: Congenital skeletal malformation with a triphalangeal thumb and duplicated distal phalanx.
Congenital thumb skeletal malformation with an additional phalanx and loss of opposition; polydactyly is within the same axis.
Defined by congenital digital abnormalities and recurrent patellar dislocation; borderline intelligence is not established as a common defining feature.
Congenital skeletal malformations of the thumbs, fingers and toes define the syndrome.
Intellectual disability and skeletal/joint abnormalities define the syndrome; heart malformations affect ~40-50%, and dental structural abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Congenital triple rows of eyelashes; eyelid and eyelash abnormalities belong to the ocular axis.
Congenital retinal cone dysfunction causing selective loss of blue color vision.
Congenital humeral trochlear deformity; occasional ulnar nerve palsy does not establish neurologic involvement in at least 30%.
Brain and skin hamartomas define TSC1 disease; renal angiomyolipomas occur in 12/15. Pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis is below threshold (20/78).
Tuftsin deficiency impairs phagocyte function and causes recurrent infections; common functional splenic damage is not established.
Congenital amusia impairs central musical pitch processing; it does not establish peripheral ear damage.
Immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; no common direct extraintestinal damage established for this subtype.
Defining ulna/fibula dysplasia and limb deformities; ocular abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); skin dimples do not establish skin damage.
Primary skeletal dysplasia involving ulnar and other metaphyses; dental abnormalities and kidney stones occur in only 5-29%.
Isolated forearm skeletal dysplasia with ulnar hypoplasia and radial bowing.
Isolated scalp hair shaft dysplasia; characteristic hair abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Hair, retinal/cataract and dental abnormalities define syndrome; brachydactyly occurs in 80-99%. Intellectual deficit lacks sufficient frequency evidence.
Hip dysplasia, premature epiphyseal fusion and cartilaginous bone lesions define the disease.
Congenital bifurcation or duplication of the ureter; ureters belong to the renal axis.
Malignant neoplasm of the ureter, included in the urinary tract axis.
Congenital cystic dilation of the distal ureter within the bladder; both belong to the renal axis.
Inherited uric-acid stone disease of the urinary tract; a systemic urate metabolic disorder is not established.
Autonomic bladder dysfunction defines the disorder. Pupillary slowing in 4/5 reflects autonomic dysfunction without documented eye damage; urinary tract findings share the renal axis.
Water-induced urticaria is a mast-cell-mediated skin disorder; uncertainty about the initiating trigger does not exclude its immune effector mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: mast-cell-mediated urticaria qualifies as immune-mediated disease even without an established autoimmune or IgE-mediated trigger.

basis: Autoinflammation with defining deafness; uveitis and arthritis each HPO 80-99%. Rash is transient; renal AA amyloidosis is separate. Cranial neuropathy omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none: renal AA amyloidosis is annotated at 30-79%, but represents a separately diagnosed secondary disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: inflammatory arthritis is annotated at 80-99%, supporting common direct joint involvement.

basis: Familial heat-induced urticaria is a mast-cell-mediated skin disorder; no additional organ damage established.
Uterine structural anomalies affect reproductive anatomy outside the 13 axes.
Ipsilateral renal agenesis or urinary tract anomaly is a defining component; associated uterine and vaginal anomalies have no axis.
Congenital cleft of the uvula and soft-palate region of the mouth.
Pathologic dilation and tortuosity of veins define a vascular disorder; no other organ is consistently damaged across the umbrella.
Lymphocyte-mediated inflammation damages cutaneous blood vessels and skin; systemic organ involvement occurs in a minority.
Small-vessel disease defines retinal and cerebral injury; nephropathy/glomerulosclerosis 30-79%. Hepatic lesions and anemia also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Defining anorectal and airway/lung defects 80-99%; vertebral/limb defects 30-79%. Renal agenesis 30-79%; cardiac defects 30-79% omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac defects qualify at 30-79%, but are omitted at the four-axis cap, prioritizing frequent airway/lung defects and irreversible renal agenesis.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: tracheoesophageal malformation is a defining criterion; tracheal stenosis and lung hypoplasia are annotated at 80-99%.
decisions.renal: involved: renal malformations are a major diagnostic criterion; agenesis and ectopic kidney each occur in 30-79%. Primary tier is capped at three.

basis: Defining palatal, cardiac and neurodevelopmental abnormalities; intellectual disability 31/38. Supplied T-cell defects 2/38 and hypocalcemia 5/38 do not support extra axes.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is explicitly defining, supported by intellectual disability in 31/38 patients (~82%).

basis: Defined by ventricular arrhythmias, digital skeletal defects and Pierre-Robin sequence with oral malformations; impaired smell reported in 80-99%.
MYH7-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects cardiac muscle; the gene alone does not establish skeletal myopathy.
Inherited ventricular rhythm disorder; ventricular tachycardia and conduction abnormalities involve the heart.
Systemic venular dysfunction is a vascular disorder; cyanosis alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Lumbosacral vertebral fusion and congenital eyelid ptosis define the syndrome; sacral dimples do not establish additional skin damage.
Vertebral hypoplasia and lumbar kyphosis define a structural skeletal disorder.
Congenital talonavicular dislocation and fixed foot deformity; definition specifies isolated disease, so associated neurologic syndromes are excluded.
Inherited vesicoureteral reflux affects the urinary tract; unspecified skeletal abnormalities lack sufficient evidence for inclusion.
Cerebellar ataxia with sensory and oculomotor dysfunction; central nystagmus does not establish direct ocular damage.
Progressive hearing loss and vestibular areflexia define cochlear and vestibular dysfunction; no independent central neurologic disease established.
Inherited haptocorrin transport deficiency usually causes low measured B12 without functional deficiency; common neurologic injury or anemia is not established.
FGF23-mediated renal phosphate wasting, hypophosphatemia and rickets/osteomalacia define disease; iron deficiency anemia and tooth abscess are separate diagnoses.
Autoimmune destruction of cutaneous melanocytes causes depigmentation; associated autoimmune disorders are separate diseases.
Inherited vitreoretinochoroidal disease with ocular developmental abnormalities, retinal degeneration, glaucoma and cataract.
Inherited degeneration of the vitreous and retina with common cataracts; disease is confined to the ocular axis.
Defined by recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis, bilateral eyelid ptosis and vocal cord dysfunction; laryngomalacia is present in 80-99%.
Congenital intestinal malrotation with midgut volvulus and possible obstruction; facial findings do not establish other organ injury.
CNS, retinal and renal tumors are defining manifestations. Adrenal tumors are frequent (30-79%) in supplied HPO; ear tumors 5-29%, with hearing data from a selected series.

decisions.renal: primary: renal cell carcinoma is a characteristic tumor and part of VHL diagnostic criteria, not merely an unrelated later cancer risk.
decisions.otologic: none: endolymphatic sac tumors occur in 5-29%; the 34/35 hearing-loss series does not establish prevalence across the VHL population.

basis: Inherited quantitative VWF deficiency causes a coagulation disorder; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish separate lasting organ damage.
Allergic hypersensitivity to seminal proteins; affected reproductive tissues have no organ axis.
Auditory-pigmentary syndrome: sensorineural hearing loss 12/14 and characteristic hair/skin pigmentation changes; heterochromia alone does not impair ocular function.
Pulmonary valve stenosis and cafe-au-lait lesions define Watson syndrome; developmental delay and pectus carinatum each occur in 2/3 reported patients; Lisch nodules are non-damaging.
Defining skeletal malformations, nail dysplasia and dental/oral anomalies, generally present in 80-99%; cardiac disease is not characteristic.
Contractures and functionally restrictive microstomia define disease; dental defects occur in 80-99%. Strabismus/ptosis and hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%; motor delay is mechanical.
Hereditary oral mucosal keratinization disorder; oral leukoplakia reported in 8/8 patients. Skin involvement is not established.
Neurodevelopmental, arterial and connective-tissue defects define the syndrome; hypercalcemia is annotated 80-99%. Hyperacusis alone does not establish ear damage.
WT1-related renal tumour and nephropathy spectrum; genitourinary abnormalities do not establish common additional endocrine damage.
Hereditary Wilms tumor is a nephroblastoma arising in the kidney.
Aniridia, ID and urethral malformations are defining features; hearing abnormalities occur in 30-79%; Wilms tumour risk alone is excluded.
Defined by diffuse mesangial sclerosis, nephropathy and Wilms tumor. Genital differences have no axis; gonadal dysgenesis is occasional and hypertension is separately coded.
Hereditary Wilms tumor is a renal nephroblastoma.
Defining neurodevelopmental impairment; immunodeficiency 69%, hypodontia 80-99%, skeletal malformations 30-79%; strabismus and ear malformations omitted at cap.
Accessory cardiac conduction pathway causing ventricular pre-excitation and tachyarrhythmias.
Isolated structural hair disorder; ocular abnormalities are occasional (5–29%), below the involvement threshold.
Inherited marrow failure with defining radial, ulnar and thumb malformations; lymphoma is a possible associated malignancy.
Hereditary red-cell dehydration and hemolysis; hepatic findings occur in 5-29%. Pseudohyperkalemia does not establish an electrolyte disorder.
Mild inherited photodermatosis; no evidence that damaging ocular or neurologic manifestations commonly occur in this specific subtype.
Lipoprotein disorder defined by malabsorption and neurologic dysfunction; progressive visual loss occurs in 30-79%. Anemia in 30-79% omitted at cap; hepatic injury uncommon.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal fat malabsorption is an explicit defining manifestation, present in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: neurologic dysfunction is explicit in the definition and disease ancestry; nervous-system abnormalities occur in 80-99%.

basis: Eyelid, mouth and skin malformations define syndrome; developmental delay in ~2/3; hearing loss and limb contractures (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Intellectual disability, progressive quadriplegia, absent hair and glaucoma define syndrome; joint stiffness and skull ossification defect occur in 80-99%.
Neurodegeneration with characteristic erythrocyte acanthocytosis; myopathy and muscle-fiber atrophy occur in 30-79%. Oral injury is secondary mechanical trauma from dyskinesia.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: tongue/lip injury is reported in 2/2 but results from mechanical self-trauma due to dyskinesia, rather than direct gastrointestinal disease.

basis: Defined by acanthosis, insulin resistance, severe muscle cramps and acral hypertrophy. Renal enlargement lacks evidence of functional damage.
Oesophageal motor disorder with impaired lower sphincter relaxation and persistent swallowing dysfunction.
Esophageal achalasia, microcephaly and intellectual disability define the syndrome; dermatoglyphic differences do not establish skin damage.
Congenital absence of distal limb bones, hands and feet; definition explicitly reports no other systemic manifestations.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99% and causes respiratory failure.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Specific damaging ocular lesions occur in 5-29%; nonspecific eye morphology is insufficient.
Limb-confined skeletal dysplasia with severe shortening, deformity and bone fusions; facial features and intelligence are normal.
SCID with defining skeletal dysplasia and profound T/B lymphocyte depletion (80-99%); recurrent infections are separate diseases and anemia is occasional.

decisions.haematologic: primary: absence of T and B lymphocytes is explicitly defining, with decreased lymphocyte counts in 80-99%; this is a direct blood-cell defect, independent of occasional anemia.

basis: Lysosomal enzyme deficiency classified as an inherited storage disorder; the supplied record establishes no additional organ damage meeting the frequency threshold.
Molar-root abnormalities and taurodontism are consistent defining findings. Glaucoma, hypotrichosis and digital anomalies are variable, without an established frequency of at least 30%.

decisions.ocular: none: the definition describes glaucoma only in some relatives; it is not required for diagnosis and its frequency is not established at 30% or more.

basis: Limb/jaw malformations and renal agenesis define it; pulmonary hypoplasia and olfactory dysfunction each occur in 30-79%.
Callosal agenesis, intellectual disability and limb malformations define it; hypospadias affects the urethra in 10/18 (~56%). Cardiac anomalies occur in only 5/22 (~23%).

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral malformation, explicitly within the renal axis, reported in 10/18 (~56%).

basis: Skeletal defects, renal dysplasia and thickened skin define disease; pancreatic fibrosis occurs in 30-79%. Microtia 80-99% omitted by cap; organ enlargement alone is insufficient.
Craniosynostosis and polysyndactyly define Carpenter syndrome; intellectual disability affects roughly half or more. Cardiac defects are around 20-30% in RAB23-related cases.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac defects occur in approximately 20-30% of RAB23-related cases; evidence does not securely establish the threshold.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability affects roughly half or more; it is variable rather than a defining skeletal criterion.

basis: Craniosynostosis, limb skeletal malformations and congenital heart disease define the described syndrome; intellectual impairment is variable.
Skeletal dysostosis, cleft palate and mixed deafness define syndrome; ptosis 80-99%, myopia 30-79%; nail abnormalities and choanal atresia omitted under cap.
Inherited zinc malabsorption defines the metabolic, skin and intestinal disease; cortical atrophy annotated 80-99%; ocular inflammation omitted by cap.
Defining skeletal defects and cleft palate; CNS/cardiac malformations each 30-79%. Microtia 80-99% omitted at cap for severity; renal defects 5-29%; lung injury frequency unclear.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: severe cleft palate is part of the defining mandibulofacial malformation; the palate belongs to the mouth axis.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: microtia occurs in 80-99%, but defining skeletal/palatal defects and severe CNS/cardiac malformations take priority.

basis: Dysostosis and severe ID define syndrome; cleft palate and eyelid coloboma/ptosis each 80-99%. Nail/skin defects omitted by cap; genitourinary anomalies 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate causes direct oral structural dysfunction in 80-99%; associated craniofacial manifestation rather than the defining dysostosis/ID axes.

basis: Skin atrophy defines disease. Joint hypermobility 80-99% and scoliosis 30-79%; supplied HPO also reports intellectual disability at 30-79%.
Limb skeletal dysplasia with shortened or fused bones and dislocations; definition explicitly states normal intelligence, conflicting with the cognitive HPO annotation.
Acquired autoimmune central, peripheral and autonomic nervous system disease, commonly associated with CASPR2 antibodies.
Acrorenal syndrome is defined by congenital limb and urinary tract malformations.
Congenital pituitary ACTH deficiency causing adrenal insufficiency. Hypoglycemic seizures and neonatal jaundice do not establish lasting brain or liver damage.
Fatty acid oxidation defect; decreased liver function occurs in 30-79%. Myopathy and neurologic complications are reported in 5-29%.
Fatty-acid oxidation defect; most individuals are asymptomatic. Neurologic and myopathic frequencies in selected symptomatic cohorts do not establish ≥30% across all patients.
Fatty-acid oxidation defect; hepatic steatosis 2/2 and cardiomyopathy 3/3 in supplied small cohorts support involvement; rhabdomyolysis annotated 5-29%.
Congenital contractures and myopathy, cerebral dysmyelination and microcephaly, and cleft palate define the syndrome; respiratory weakness alone does not establish lung damage.
Defective steroidogenesis causes adrenal and gonadal hormone failure; pigmentation, vomiting and salt wasting do not establish other organ damage.
Skeletal anomalies and steroidogenesis defects define disease; choanal stenosis 1/3. Hypertension 1/3 is sparse evidence; single umbilical artery is fetal anatomy.
Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; urethral hypospadias occurs in 30-79% and falls within the renal axis. Hormonal salt wasting does not establish intrinsic kidney injury.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral malformation annotated in 30-79%; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra. Salt wasting alone would not qualify.

basis: Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; premature epiphyseal fusion occurs in 30-79%, causing permanent growth restriction. Salt wasting reflects hormone deficiency, not kidney damage.
Adrenal steroid synthesis disorder explicitly defined by mineralocorticoid-mediated hypertension (80-99%). Accelerated skeletal maturation alone does not establish bone damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertension is explicitly part of the definition and identifies the hypertensive CAH form; supplied frequency is 80-99%.

basis: Adrenal steroidogenesis defect with hypogonadism and hypokalemia; severe hypertension is defining and occurs in 80-99%.
Congenital adrenal hypoplasia and deficient pituitary luteinizing hormone are defining endocrine abnormalities.
Congenital adrenal cortical hypoplasia causes primary adrenal insufficiency; unrelated neurologic ancestor entries do not establish involvement.
Primary adrenal glucocorticoid deficiency; pigmentation, hypotension and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish damage to additional organs.
Carcinoma originates in the adrenal cortex. Renal ancestry is inconsistent with the definition; choroid plexus carcinoma is a separate tumour.
Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment, visual disease and hearing loss each commonly exceed 30% in milder Zellweger spectrum disease. Hepatic involvement omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment and neurologic dysfunction commonly exceed 30%; the defining disorder is peroxisomal metabolism.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment commonly exceeds 30% in milder Zellweger spectrum disease, although subtype-specific frequencies are limited.

basis: Absent fibrinogen causes a coagulation disorder; bleeding sites and joint swelling alone do not establish lasting organ damage; cerebral hemorrhage is <30%.
Congenital absence of enteric ganglia defines the disease, directly affecting peripheral nervous tissue and intestinal motility.

decisions.neurologic: primary: enteric ganglia belong to the peripheral nervous system; their complete absence is the defining lesion.

basis: Congenital absence of cerebral white matter with intellectual disability.
Mandibular agenesis, brain malformations and fused ears define syndrome; severe ocular defects occur in 80-99%; oral and airway malformations omitted by cap.
Lung/heart malformations and agonadism define syndrome; renal dysplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Diaphragmatic and abdominal-wall defects omitted by cap.
Congenital neutropenia is an immunodeficiency; recurrent oral ulceration and periodontal injury occur in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed infections do not establish other organ involvement.
Microcephaly and severe intellectual disability, diabetes and metabolic abnormalities, and dental enamel defects define the syndrome; aminoaciduria alone is not kidney damage.
Nasal alar cartilage hypoplasia and clefting define disease; upper-lip clefts occur in 80-99%. Coloboma refers to nasal cartilage; telecanthus alone is not eye damage.
Inherited tyrosinase-dependent melanin synthesis defect defines skin/hair depigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with impaired vision.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorder defining skin and hair hypopigmentation, foveal hypoplasia and visual impairment; optic pathway misrouting belongs to the ocular phenotype.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorder defining skin, hair and ocular pigmentation abnormalities, with nystagmus in 30–79%.
Platelet dysfunction and oculocutaneous albinism define HPS1; pulmonary fibrosis develops in most adults; granulomatous colitis affects a minority.
PTH resistance causes hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia without Albright osteodystrophy; hypocalcemic seizures do not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Microcephaly, cutaneous albinism and digital skeletal defects define the syndrome. Oculocutaneous albinism affects visual development; iris hypopigmentation occurs in 80-99%.

decisions.ocular: involved: defining oculocutaneous albinism affects visual development; ocular pigmentation abnormalities occur in 80-99%; three primary slots are occupied.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: digital phalangeal hypoplasia/aplasia is named and explicitly defining, occurring in 80-99%.

basis: Adrenal aldosterone biosynthesis deficiency causes salt wasting and electrolyte abnormalities; renal salt loss reflects hormone deficiency, not intrinsic kidney damage.
Astrocytic neurodegeneration defines disease. Scoliosis, despite HPO frequency of 80-99%, is secondary to motor dysfunction; eye-movement and swallowing abnormalities are neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is a secondary, separately diagnosed deformity rather than direct skeletal injury by the astrocytic disease, despite its 80-99% annotation.

basis: Ochronotic arthropathy defines disease; aortic stenosis 30-79%, hearing abnormalities 80-99%. Visual abnormality 80-99% omitted under cap; pigmentation alone is nondamaging; stones separately coded.
audit_reason: Retain the axes, but acknowledge ocular involvement omitted under the four-axis cap: the supplied visual abnormality frequency is 80-99% and cannot be dismissed as pigmentation alone.

basis: Alopecia, skeletal contractures/fusions and intellectual disability define the syndrome; myopia occurs in 30-79%. Dental enamel abnormalities omitted by cap.
Congenital alopecia, early epilepsy and intellectual disability define the syndrome; delayed bone development lacks frequency evidence.
Alopecia and intellectual disability define it; hearing loss 80-99%, skeletal malformations 30-79%. Hypogonadism 30-79% omitted by four-axis cap.
Definition explicitly identifies immune-mediated alopecia areata with complete hair loss, despite conflicting HR-related congenital atrichia annotations.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by neurodegeneration, seizures and hepatic failure; cerebral visual impairment reflects brain damage.
Krebs-cycle defect with defining developmental and movement dysfunction; muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%. Hepatomegaly and salivary morphology alone do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay is part of the definition; ataxia and developmental impairment occur in 80-99%, with hereditary neuropathy ancestry.

basis: Inborn defect of ketone utilization and isoleucine catabolism causes ketoacidosis; acute altered consciousness is common, but lasting neurologic injury is under 30%.
The defining syndrome comprises progressive nephropathy, sensorineural hearing loss and characteristic ocular defects; lenticonus is diagnostic despite infrequent vision loss.

decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic ocular abnormalities are part of the defining syndrome; lenticonus is a major diagnostic feature, rather than merely incidental retinal flecks.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss is a defining component of Alport syndrome and is frequent (30-79%) in the supplied annotations.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, hearing loss and metabolic dysfunction define disease; cardiomyopathy in ~60%. Cap excludes hepatic, renal and other less consistent damage.
GUCY2D-related congenital retinal disease; extraocular annotations lack frequencies and are not established common features.
RPE65-related retinal degeneration causes severe visual loss; intellectual disability is reported in only 2/13.
Severe congenital retinal dystrophy and characteristic generalized hypertrichosis define the syndrome.
Lysosomal storage neurodegeneration; progressive retinal degeneration and visual failure affect nearly all typical cases; cardiac involvement is variable and age dependent.
Lysosomal storage disorder causing progressive dementia, seizures and ataxia; Kufs phenotype lacks the characteristic retinal degeneration of childhood forms.
TPP1 lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss develop in most patients over the typical course.
Inherited dental enamel defect; teeth are gastrointestinal under these axes.
Enamel defects, gingival fibromatosis and nephrocalcinosis define this enamel-renal syndrome; renal dysfunction is also frequent.
KLK4-related enamel hypomaturation directly affects teeth, included in the gastrointestinal axis.
Acidosis/aminoaciduria, intellectual disability, muscular dystrophy and osteoporosis define the phenotype. Aminoaciduria can reflect metabolic overflow; renal tubular dysfunction is not established.

decisions.renal: none: aminoaciduria and acidosis do not distinguish metabolic overflow from renal tubular dysfunction; intrinsic renal disease is not established.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is an explicitly defining feature of the syndrome, supported by its HPO annotation.

basis: Inherited lysine metabolism disorder; developmental delay reported in 2/2 annotated patients supports neurologic involvement, although clinical expression is variable and many individuals are asymptomatic.
The named syndrome is defined by gingival and conjunctival amyloidosis with intellectual disability.
Localized corneal amyloid deposition causes corneal opacity and visual impairment; no systemic amyloidosis is implied.
Cutaneous amyloid deposition causes bullous skin disease; systemic organ involvement is not established by the supplied concept.
Defined by multiple congenital joint contractures. Neurologic causes occur in some subtypes but are not universal across the umbrella.
Motor-neuron degeneration defines disease; contractures and scoliosis in 2/3 and muscle atrophy in 1/3 follow denervation and spasticity rather than direct muscle or joint disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contractures/scoliosis (2/3) and atrophy (1/3) are consequences of denervation and spasticity; they do not establish direct myopathy or arthropathy.

basis: Motor neuron degeneration with progressive dementia; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
ALS subtype with motor-neuron degeneration and polyglucosan bodies; muscle wasting from denervation does not establish primary muscle disease.
Neuropathy, nail dystrophy and ectropion each 30-79%; liver/spleen enlargement lacks established dysfunction; atherosclerosis is a separate disease.
Inherited sideroblastic anemia affects erythropoiesis; iron indices alone do not establish hepatic or other organ damage.
Sideroblastic anemia is a disorder of erythropoiesis and heme synthesis. Common independent hepatic injury is not established for this subtype.
Defined by congenital microcytic anemia, defective iron transport and progressive hepatic iron overload; liver involvement is intrinsic rather than treatment-related.
Inherited iron metabolism disorder causing persistent hypochromic microcytic anemia.
Red-cell membrane disorder causing nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia; nonspecific homeostasis annotation adds no metabolic axis.
Congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia; proposed porphyrin-metabolism defect is unconfirmed. Jaundice does not establish liver damage.
Absence of brain, cranial vault and covering skin defines the malformation; adrenal insufficiency is annotated as very frequent, 80-99%.
Benign subcutaneous angiolipomas; the definition explicitly excludes infiltration of adjacent muscles, tendons and joint capsules.
Corticomeningeal vascular malformation with cerebral degeneration defines the disease. Marbled skin lacks established tissue damage; hemianopia reflects cerebral dysfunction.
Hereditary absence or abnormal development of cutaneous sweat glands causes generalized anhidrosis.
Aniridia, cerebellar ataxia and intellectual disability define Gillespie syndrome; sparse extracranial case counts do not establish common additional organ damage.
Aniridia/glaucoma, renal agenesis and developmental delay define syndrome; craniosynostosis occurs in 80-99% in supplied HPO.
Complete developmental absence of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Isolated congenital absence of nails; anonychia reported in 4/4 patients.
Defining eye and esophageal defects; tracheoesophageal fistula occurs in 80-99%. Callosal agenesis occurs in 30-79%; hearing impairment (30-79%) omitted under cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: tracheoesophageal fistula is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 80-99%, directly affecting the trachea.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%; defining eye, esophageal and tracheal defects plus substantial CNS abnormalities take priority.

basis: Eye and limb malformations define disease; developmental delay in 3/4 and intellectual disability in 30-79%; cleft upper lip in 30-79% affects the mouth.
Selective inherited loss of smell perception; olfactory function belongs to the neurologic axis.
Inherited hemorrhagic diathesis is a coagulation disorder; no specific additional organ damage is established.
Defining skeletal malformations; cardiovascular abnormalities 80-99%, choanal atresia and renal anomalies 30-79%. Steroidogenesis defects are subtype-specific.
Limb/vertebral, urinary and rectal dysgenesis define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia 30-79%; PDA and anonychia, also 30-79%, omitted under cap.
Skin aplasia and intestinal lymphangiectasia; calvarial defects 80-99%, lymphopenia 30-79%. Hypogammaglobulinemia (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
