decisions.haematologic: involved: persistent enteric lymphocyte loss causes lymphopenia in 30-79% and is explicitly described in the syndrome definition.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: antibody loss occurs in 30-79%, but ranks below frequent calvarial defects and defining lymphopenia under the four-axis cap.

basis: Polyneuropathy and congenital absence or hypoplasia of digital extensor muscles and tendons define the syndrome; hypohidrosis reflects autonomic dysfunction.
Inherited chylomicron metabolism disorder; pancreatitis (5/8) is a separately diagnosed complication; organ enlargement and lipemia retinalis do not establish functional damage.
Forebrain absence, eye malformations and preaxial limb defects define the syndrome; anal atresia occurs in 30-79%; pharyngeal/nasal anomalies omitted at the four-axis cap.
Ectodermal defects, renal abnormalities and lipoatrophic diabetes define syndrome; sideroblastic anemia 80-99%. Frequent dental and skeletal defects omitted by cap.
Arachnoidal cyst within the intracranial or spinal central nervous system.
Urea-cycle defect; developmental impairment very frequent (80-99%) and progressive spasticity frequent. Single-case hepatic fibrosis/cholestasis does not establish common involvement.
Neurodevelopmental injury, hepatic dysfunction and intrinsic NO-related hypertension each occur in 30-79%. Monilethrix (30-79%) omitted for cap; renal insufficiency is <30%.
Congenital hindbrain displacement with associated neural tube and CNS abnormalities; dysphagia and apnea do not establish separate organ damage.
An inherited extracellular pyrophosphate metabolism disorder causes arterial calcification and stenosis. Rickets is occasional (5-29%); renal artery stenosis is cardiovascular.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: deficient extracellular pyrophosphate metabolism is the established disease mechanism, supporting an inborn metabolic disorder.

basis: Arterial disease, joint hypermobility (12/14) and inherited cutis laxa define ATS; cleft palate is annotated frequent (30-79%). Keratoconus occurs in 3/14; refractive errors alone lack tissue injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is a direct structural defect of the mouth and is annotated frequent (30-79%).
decisions.ocular: none: myopia (6/15) and astigmatism (5/15) alone do not establish ocular tissue injury; keratoconus affects 3/14 (~21%).
decisions.dermatologic: primary: inherited cutis laxa ancestry and characteristic skin laxity/hyperextensibility establish a defining cutaneous connective-tissue disorder.

basis: Severe juvenile arteriosclerosis is a structural disease of arteries; no other organ damage established.
Distal joint contractures and intellectual disability define the syndrome.
Defining contractures, renal tubulopathy and cholestasis; ichthyosis in about 50%. Clinical bleeding occurs in 11/62, below threshold.
Congenital joint contractures and muscle wasting arise from neurogenic atrophy; chronic denervation occurs in 80-99%.
Multiple joint contractures and pulmonary hypoplasia define the sequence; neurologic causes vary and are not universal.
Contractures, severe CNS dysfunction and restrictive microstomia define it. Blepharophimosis is annotated in 80-99%, but functional ocular damage is not established.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent blepharophimosis describes eyelid morphology; the record does not establish impaired lid function, visual loss or other direct functional ocular damage.

basis: Congenital joint contractures and fissured hyperkeratosis define the syndrome; severe posterior-column hypoplasia is a characteristic reported feature.
Noninflammatory skeletal dysplasia with progressive joint destruction, contractures and vertebral abnormalities; not an autoimmune arthropathy.
Non-inflammatory arthropathy with camptodactyly and coxa vara; pericarditis and valve abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Chylous fluid accumulates in the peritoneal cavity; underlying liver disease or malignancy is a separate cause, and skin nodules do not establish functional damage.
Lysosomal storage disorder; intellectual disability, scoliosis and gingival overgrowth each occur in 80-99%. Additional dental and skeletal abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Short-rib thoracic skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and lasting respiratory impairment commonly exceed 30%. Renal, hepatic and retinal damage are not established at >=30% for this subtype.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory impairment affect >30%; they result from the defining restrictive thoracic skeletal dysplasia.

basis: Complex cardiac malformations and congenital asplenia define the syndrome; asplenia (5/5) removes splenic blood and immune functions. Organ position and lung lobation add no axis.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: defining congenital asplenia causes an intrinsic deficiency of splenic immune function; this is not merely a later infection risk.

basis: Defining renal, hepatic and pancreatic dysplasia; renal failure and cirrhosis each reported in 2/2 patients; pancreatic fibrosis and cysts affect exocrine tissue.
Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease combines asthma and nasal polyposis with immune-mediated airway inflammation.
Asthma defines immune-mediated airway disease. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine damage; elevated IgA alone does not establish immunodeficiency.
Ataxia, myoclonic epilepsy, dementia and polyneuropathy are neurologic manifestations.
Ataxia, sensorineural deafness and cardiomyopathy define the syndrome; skin abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Ataxia, intellectual disability and deafness define the syndrome; strabismus affects 80–99%, and structural scoliosis affects 30–79%.
Ataxia, microcephaly and cataracts define the syndrome.
Ataxia, immunodeficiency and cutaneous telangiectasia define disease; gonadal dysfunction/delayed puberty 80-99%. Eye movements are neurologic; liver enzymes alone insufficient.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent cutaneous telangiectasia is a defining diagnostic feature; the primary tier includes defining organs without requiring secondary functional damage.

basis: Ataxia and generalized skin pigmentation define this variant; the parent disorder includes combined immunodeficiency. Common pulmonary damage is not established here.
Cerebellar and axonal degeneration define AOA1; characteristic lipid metabolic dysfunction occurs in 9/12 (~75%). Wasting and skeletal deformities are secondary to neuropathy.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: characteristic lipid metabolic dysfunction with hypercholesterolemia in 9/12 (~75%).
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy (14/14), pes cavus (6/11) and scoliosis (6/12) reflect denervation and secondary deformity rather than direct muscle or bone disease.

basis: Defining vascular, metabolic and neurologic disease; progressive nephropathy 30-79%. Cap prioritizes renal severity over deafness/anemia 80-99% and skeletal abnormalities 30-79%.

decisions.renal: involved: progressive nephropathy/nephrotic syndrome occurs in 30-79% and is a defining feature; potentially severe renal failure merits the fourth axis.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: sensorineural deafness occurs in 80-99%, but severe progressive renal disease is prioritized after the three defining primary axes.

basis: Inherited platelet adhesion and aggregation dysfunction causing abnormal bleeding.
Atonic-astatic neurologic syndrome characterized by hypotonia, ataxia and inability to stand or walk; no intrinsic muscle disease established.
Transferrin deficiency causes anemia and disordered iron transport; cardiac/endocrine abnormalities are <30%; hepatic functional injury frequency is unclear.
Irreversible generalized hair loss and cutaneous papular lesions define the disorder.
Disorder of cardiac electrical conduction.
Follicular skin disease causing persistent pitted atrophic scars in 80-99%; heart block is occasional, below 30%.
Ear atresia, intellectual disability and VSD define syndrome; skeletal deformities occur in 30-79%; anorectal anomaly and strabismus omitted at cap.
Skin dysplasia, ectropion and oral malformation define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%, with auditory canal stenosis in 6/12.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly are defining features; intellectual disability occurs in 26/33 (~79%). Renal disease is less consistent in BBS1.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining severe malabsorption and protracted diarrhea in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed respiratory infections and infectious hepatobiliary disease are excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: severe malabsorption is a defining intestinal loss of function, supported by protracted diarrhea in 30-79%; recurrent enteric infections alone would not qualify.

basis: Hydrocephalus, cardiac malformations and dense bones define it; thrombocytopenia 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct lung injury.
Defining optic atrophy and neurologic degeneration; ancestry identifies an inborn mitochondrial metabolism disorder. Constipation and dysphagia do not establish direct gut injury.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: supplied ancestry identifies an inborn mitochondrial metabolism disorder; this classification, rather than the OPA1 gene alone, supports the mechanism axis.

basis: Defining aneurysms, cirrhosis and emphysema; cerebral calcification with developmental delay/seizures is a major component supporting neurologic involvement.
Inherited biochemical trait of beta-aminoisobutyric acid metabolism; urinary metabolite excretion does not establish renal damage.
Leucine catabolic defect; most identified patients are asymptomatic. Severe neurologic findings in tiny HPO series do not establish involvement in >=30% overall.
Inborn leucine catabolism defect; developmental delay in 20/20 annotated patients supports neurologic involvement, although clinical penetrance is variable.
Intellectual disability, coloboma and hypogonadism define syndrome; polydactyly and mandibulofacial dysostosis occur in 80-99%.
Progressive chorioretinal degeneration causes visual loss; corneal deposits are within the same ocular axis.
Congenital cleft malformation of the nose; the nasal structures fall within the pulmonary axis.
Obliterative disease of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts; fat malabsorption and prolonged clotting reflect impaired bile delivery and vitamin absorption.
The defining abnormalities are biliary tract malformation and renal tubular dysfunction; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability, primordial dwarfism and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; additional organ defects lack reliable frequencies.
Skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly/ID and hair/skin defects define syndrome; dental/palatal defects and pyloric atresia reported at 80-99%; ptosis omitted at cap.
Defining skeletal dysplasia and cerebral malformations; ocular/auditory deficits lack established >=30% frequency; renal and cardiac defects each reported in 1/10.
Skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly and dental defects define disease; insulin resistance occurs in ~40-70%. Hearing loss 30-79% omitted by cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: abnormal dentition is defining; tooth agenesis occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: insulin resistance affects ~40-70%, especially with increasing age; retained as a systemic manifestation under the primary cap.

basis: Primordial skeletal growth disorder with osteodysplasia, microcephaly and neurodevelopmental impairment; no other organ involvement established.
Polyendocrinopathy and progressive ataxia define syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Short stature and finger deviation do not establish functional skeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short stature and finger deviation (80-99%) are reported, but skeletal dysfunction, destructive disease or fixed contractures are not established.

basis: Defining eyelid, ocular alignment and skeletal abnormalities; cranial nerve malformation reported in 80-99%. Intellectual disability and anosmia are under 30%.
Photosensitive dermatosis and antibody deficiency define syndrome. Insulin resistance lacks established injury; diabetes/ovarian insufficiency are separate diagnoses; steatosis is a single report.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: insulin resistance (30-79%) alone does not establish organ injury; diabetes and premature ovarian insufficiency are separately diagnosed conditions.

basis: Amino-acid transport disorder defined by hypercalcemia and nephrocalcinosis; diarrhea alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; the severely shortened thorax causes respiratory failure/asphyxia in the characteristic neonatal course.
Severe developmental impairment, microcephaly, joint contractures and foot deformities define the syndrome; cardiac and pulmonary malformations occur in <30%.
Congenital skeletal dysplasia with bowed, shortened bones and thoracic abnormalities; a narrow bony thorax alone does not establish lung damage.
Congenital angular deformity and shortening of long bones.
Brachydactyly and microcephaly define skeletal and brain abnormalities; seizures support neurologic involvement. Diabetes frequency is unknown.
Ocular anomalies, shortened bones and ectodermal defects define the syndrome; congenital anodontia is a major defining feature in the reported sibship.
Intellectual disability, skeletal anomalies and cleft/dental defects define the syndrome; strabismus occurs in 80-99%. Hearing loss lacks support in the supplied definition/HPO.
Brittle, sparse hair and intellectual disability characterize Sabinas syndrome; intellectual disability is a defining component despite unspecified HPO frequency.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is a characteristic defining component of Sabinas syndrome, rather than an incidental or minority complication.

basis: Bronchiectasis and chronic bronchitis directly affect the airways; occasional elevated sweat chloride does not establish another organ disorder.
Congenital deficiency of bronchial cartilage causes bronchomalacia and bronchiectasis.
Inflammatory thrombotic vasculitis; sensory neuropathy and ischemic skin ulcers/gangrene each reported in 80-99%.
Progressive bulbar motor neuron degeneration; dysphagia and muscle weakness reflect denervation rather than intrinsic gastrointestinal or skeletal muscle disease.
Riboflavin transport defect causes motor neuron disease and deafness; muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Respiratory failure is neuromuscular; optic injury occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: documented skeletal muscle atrophy in 30-79% represents structural tissue loss within the neuromuscular disease, beyond weakness alone.

basis: Inherited hepatocellular bile-transport disorder; chronic intestinal malabsorption/diarrhea in roughly half; rickets in 25/33. Pruritus alone does not establish skin damage.
Craniosynostosis and developmental disability define it; gingival overgrowth 80-99%, anal and cardiac anomalies 30-79%; strabismus 30-79% omitted at cap.
Cataract, hypertrichosis and intellectual disability define the syndrome; dental/palatal anomalies occur in 80-99%. Pectus excavatum, also 80-99%, omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: microdontia and palatal abnormalities occur in 80-99%; direct dental/oral malformations retained as the fourth axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pectus excavatum occurs in 80-99%, but omitted at four-axis cap; severity or associated cardiopulmonary impairment is not documented.

basis: Defining arterial calcification with occlusion and periarticular calcification causing arthritis; paresthesias alone do not establish nerve damage.
Skeletal, renal and lymphatic malformations define the syndrome; cleft palate/pancreatic anomalies occur in 80–99%. Myelodysplasia (30–79%) omitted under cap; hepatomegaly alone insufficient.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular to primary for defining lymphatic malformation: cystic hygroma occurs in 80–99%. Remove haematologic under the four-axis cap because myelodysplasia is less frequent than the retained defining malformations.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; dental eruption and occlusion defects 80-99%; developmental impairment/seizures 30-79%. Microtia and microcornea lack documented functional impairment.

decisions.otologic: none: microtia is reported in 80-99%, but external-ear shape and size alone do not establish hearing loss or other functional ear damage.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia and fixed limb deformities define the syndrome; microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction.
Skeletal dysplasia and contractures define the syndrome; mild intellectual disability accompanied the sole reported family of three affected siblings.

decisions.neurologic: involved: mild intellectual disability accompanies the reported three-sibling phenotype; it is associated rather than a defining skeletal feature.

basis: Muscle hypoplasia, weakness, contractures and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome. Abnormal dermatoglyphics do not imply skin damage; valve involvement has unspecified frequency.
Malignant neoplasm arising in the lung; no additional organ is consistently occupied across this cancer umbrella.
Congenital skeletal disorder characterized by bowed long bones and limb shortening.
Glycosylation defect with cerebellar disease; coagulation dysfunction ~80-90%, hepatic disease ~60%. Cap omits ocular findings (80-99%), renal cysts (11/16) and skeletal disease.

decisions.haematologic: involved: glycosylation-related coagulation factor deficiencies affect approximately 80-90% and impair coagulation.
decisions.ocular: none: strabismus at 80-99% supports involvement, but the cap prioritizes coagulation dysfunction and hepatic injury alongside metabolic and neurologic disease.

basis: Glycosylation defect with defining developmental impairment; VSD and gingival/dental overgrowth each reported in 2/3. Bleeding is occasional (5-29%).
Congenital glycosylation disorder with a prominent seizure/infantile-spasm phenotype; pigmentation alone does not establish skin damage.
Defective inflammatory-mediator regulation causes defining angioedema and chronic urticaria. Common intrinsic airway disease is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: chronic urticaria and cutaneous angioedema constitute the defining skin disease phenotype, rather than an incidental passing rash

basis: Familial cardiac lipidosis is a metabolic cardiomyopathy; microcephaly has no frequency sufficient to support additional neurologic involvement.
Congenital cardiac septal defects and aortic coarctation are confined to the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital cardiac valve and associated structural heart defects; urinary anomalies lack evidence of a frequency reaching 30%.
Cardioauditory syndrome is defined by ventricular hypertrophy and hearing impairment; dermatoglyphic patterns do not establish skin damage.
Cardiomyopathy and hormonal gonadal failure define disease; ptosis and toe phalangeal aplasia each annotated at 80–99%; contractures/dislocation also reported. Neurologic findings are <30%.
Cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy are the defining manifestations.
Congenital cardiac malformations and skeletal dysplasia with limb shortening jointly define this syndrome.
Cardiomyopathy/arrhythmia, encephalopathy/developmental impairment and rhabdomyolysis each occur in 80-99%; common hepatic biochemical injury is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic biochemical injury occurs in 80-99%, but failure is 5-29%; omitted at the cap in favor of common severe cardiac, brain and muscle injury.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: rhabdomyolysis occurs in 80-99%, establishing frequent direct skeletal-muscle injury and supporting retention under the cap.

basis: Carnitine transport disorder with defining cardiomyopathy/myopathy; hepatic dysfunction annotated 80-99%. Acute neurologic crises omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases are annotated 80-99%, supporting common hepatic dysfunction.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: childhood cardiomyopathy is a defining classical manifestation; reported in 2/5 patients.
decisions.neurologic: none: acute hypoglycemic encephalopathy may reverse; cardiac, muscle and hepatic dysfunction take precedence at the four-axis cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic skeletal myopathy with weakness/hypotonia; muscle weakness is annotated 80-99%.

basis: Disordered carnitine metabolism with deficient muscle carnitine and defining skeletal myopathy.
Carnosinase deficiency disrupts peptide metabolism; seizures, intellectual disability and regression annotated in 80-99%. Carnosinuria alone is not renal damage.
Mitochondrial disease defined by cataracts and cardiomyopathy; myopathy occurs in 80-99%. Sparse neurologic and haematologic findings omitted under the four-axis cap.
Congenital alopecia and keratoderma define disease; cataracts with visual impairment and joint stiffness each occur in 80–99%, with progressive sclerodactyly.
Congenital cataract and ichthyosis jointly define the syndrome.
Juvenile cataract defines the disease; supplied phenotypes show arrhythmia in 14/19 (~74%), despite the nonsyndromic designation.
Brain degeneration, cataracts/microphthalmia and contractures define COFS; sensorineural hearing loss 30-79%; hypogonadism and immune dysfunction omitted at cap.
Optic disc malformations and macular/chorioretinal atrophy directly impair vision.
Defining cataracts, cerebellar/peripheral neurological dysfunction and progressive sensorineural deafness.
Defining limb synostoses and syndactyly; nail absence 11/12, renal agenesis 4/12 and hypoplasia 3/12. Dental loss 2/7 is borderline; other dental defects are <30%.
Inherited lipid storage disorder; intellectual disability and splenic abnormalities are reported without frequencies or evidence of splenic dysfunction.
Cerebellar degeneration, sparse hair and hypodontia define the syndrome; pes cavus occurs in 30–79%.
Progressive cerebellar disease with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; optic atrophy and retinal dysfunction are annotated at 80-99%.
Cerebellar dysfunction and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; pes cavus has no established common frequency.
Cerebellar ataxia, impaired temperature sensation and axonal loss establish nervous system disease.
Progressive cerebellar and pyramidal disease; abnormal eye movements are neurologic, while skeletal and cardiac abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Cerebellar underdevelopment with epilepsy and developmental impairment; scoliosis occurs in 2/5. Abnormal eye movements reflect cerebellar dysfunction.
Hepatic fibrosis, renal dysplasia and ID define syndrome; visual defects/coloboma 30-79%, ptosis 80-99%. Hearing and respiratory dysfunction 30-79% omitted by cap.
Cerebellar degeneration and developmental impairment define disease. Eye-movement abnormalities and weakness are neurologic; flat feet alone do not establish damage.
Defining cerebellar/brainstem malformation and developmental impairment; retinal dysplasia and renal cysts are occasional. Hepatic fibrosis 2/7 is borderline and omitted.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration with ataxia and myoclonus; other described lesions remain within the nervous system.
Dysphoric cerebral angiopathy affects cerebral vessels and adjacent brain tissue; supplied phenotype supports nervous system involvement.
Brain calcification with neurodegeneration; neither a systemic calcium disorder nor intrinsic vestibular damage is established.
Sterol storage with defining CNS/tendon disease; cataracts impair vision in 80-99%; osteoporosis occurs in 30-79%. Diarrhea alone does not establish gut damage.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts and visual impairment occur in 80-99%; the three primary slots retain the metabolic mechanism and named cerebral and tendon sites.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: tendon xanthomata are a defining, named site; osteoporosis in 30-79% additionally establishes common skeletal damage.

basis: Cerebral malformation with seizures, hypertrichosis and overlapping fingers are the defining neurologic, hair and skeletal abnormalities.
Inherited cerebral neurodegenerative disease; the nonspecific metabolism/homeostasis annotation does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Infantile degeneration of the cerebral cortex; supplied information establishes no additional organ involvement.
Severe peroxisomal disorder with defining cerebral and hepatic disease; hearing impairment 4/4. Ocular disease omitted at cap; renal cysts alone do not establish dysfunction.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic dysfunction is a defining component of severe Zellweger disease, supported by transaminase elevation in 2/2 and hepatomegaly/jaundice.
decisions.neurologic: primary: cerebral malformations and profound neurodevelopmental impairment define severe Zellweger disease; developmental delay is reported in 4/4.

basis: Severe peroxisomal disease with defining encephalopathy; hepatic dysfunction in most and vision loss ~59%; renal cysts ~42% and hearing loss ~37% omitted under cap.

decisions.renal: none: renal cysts ~42% qualify but are omitted under the cap in favor of more frequent, functionally severe ocular disease. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9221082/)
decisions.neurologic: primary: severe Zellweger disease is defined by profound developmental impairment, neuronal migration defects and seizures.
decisions.ocular: involved: vision loss ~59% in severe Zellweger cohorts; prioritized over renal cysts under the cap. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9221082/)

basis: Brain, eye and skeletal defects define COFS1. Sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 1/3 (~33%); dental disease and metabolic findings omitted by cap. Recurrent pneumonia is a separate infection.
Congenital absence of cervical vertebrae is a structural skeletal disorder.
Defined by congenital cervical vertebral fusion and associated skeletal anomalies; hearing, cardiac and palatal abnormalities lack qualifying frequencies.
Neuropathy, intellectual disability and congenital deafness define disease. Persistent lower-limb amyotrophy occurs in 80-99% and structural pes cavus in 30-79%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent muscle wasting occurs in 80-99%, with fixed foot deformity in 30-79%; these are intrinsic functional and structural consequences of this syndrome.

basis: Sensorimotor neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy and foot deformities in 80-99%; persistent vocal cord paresis in 30-79% affects laryngeal function.
Skin/hair hypopigmentation and neurologic impairment define GS1; retinopathy occurs in 80-99%. Hyperlipidemia is a separately diagnosed metabolic condition; immunodeficiency is absent.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hyperlipidemia, although annotated in 30-79%, is a separately diagnosed metabolic condition rather than direct endocrine organ damage.

basis: Immune/blood-cell defects and ocular albinism define CHS; neurologic decline affects most long-term survivors. Cap omits skin findings, hepatic dysfunction and periodontitis (30-79%).

decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive neuropathy/neurodegeneration affects most long-term survivors; ocular albinism takes the third primary slot as a defining congenital hallmark.
decisions.ocular: primary: oculocutaneous albinism defines CHS; ocular albinism occurs in 8/9 and reduced visual acuity in 30-79%, establishing functional ocular disease.

basis: Intestinal chloride transport disorder defined by secretory diarrhea and hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.
Ear, eye and cranial nerve/developmental defects define CHARGE; hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurs in 80-99%. Common choanal and cardiac defects omitted under the four-axis cap.

Cholestasis and severe chronic subcutaneous lymphedema define the syndrome; frequent lipomas further support skin/subcutis involvement. Nutritional sequelae do not establish other direct organ injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic dysfunction does not establish disease of the heart or blood vessels covered by this axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: defining chronic lymphedema affects skin/subcutis; pigmentation changes and subcutaneous lipomas are also frequent (30-79%).

basis: Bile acid synthesis disorder with defining liver disease; encephalopathy/neuropathy and pigmentary retinopathy each frequent (30-79%).
Named syndrome is defined by hepatobiliary cholestasis, ataxia and visual dysfunction; no evidence establishes an additional metabolic mechanism.
Cholesterol-containing lipid accumulation causes pulmonary inflammation; the record does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder or infection.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and cataract each reported at 80-99%. Coarctation excluded: aggregate frequency 5-29% despite a 2/2 case series.
Metaphyseal chondrodysplasia defines the disorder; isolated mucopolysacchariduria does not establish a metabolic disease.
Peroxisomal lipid disorder with defining skeletal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities; cataracts affect >80%. Respiratory involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe neurodevelopmental impairment is a defining major feature, supported by intellectual disability, CNS atrophy and delayed myelination.
decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts affect >80%; retained as the fourth axis after metabolic, skeletal and defining neurodevelopmental disease.

basis: Epiphyseal stippling, ocular colobomata and developmental delay characterize syndrome; reported cardiac malformations lack an established >=30% frequency.
Sterol synthesis defect with lethal skeletal dysplasia; airway calcification lacks demonstrated functional damage; leukocyte shape changes alone do not qualify.
Skeletal dysplasia and sensorineural hearing loss define disease; cleft palate affects 30-79%, supporting oral involvement. Ocular findings are 1-4%.
Abnormal glycosaminoglycan metabolism, cellular immunodeficiency and nephrotic syndrome define it; frequencies of corneal, hepatic and skeletal damage are unclear.
Malignant cartilage-producing mesenchymal tumour arising predominantly in bone and locomotor connective tissues.
Malignant notochordal tumor arising in the axial skeleton; neurologic invasion or compression is not established as common across all sites.
NKX2-1-related chorea; intrinsic thyroid dysfunction affects roughly 50-70% and developmental/surfactant-related lung disease roughly 40-60%; expression varies.
Defining triad of cerebellar degeneration, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and chorioretinal dystrophy; amyotrophy accompanies neurologic disease.
Inherited macular and chorioretinal degeneration causing progressive visual loss.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction; persistent hearing loss affects ~30% in PCD cohorts, with chronic middle-ear dysfunction much more frequent; subtype data sparse.

decisions.otologic: involved: persistent hearing loss ~30% in PCD, from chronic middle-ear dysfunction; subtype extrapolation. [Cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11843728/).

basis: Respiratory ciliary dysfunction defines disease; chronic middle-ear disease with conductive hearing impairment affects over 50% in typical primary ciliary dyskinesia.

decisions.otologic: involved: impaired middle-ear clearance causes chronic effusions and conductive hearing impairment in over 50% of typical primary ciliary dyskinesia patients.

basis: Placental disease is outside the axes; the undefined syndrome's extra-placental findings have no frequencies or established diagnostic status.

decisions.neurologic: none: intracranial hemorrhage is reported without frequency or evidence that it defines this syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: none: unspecified skin abnormalities lack evidence of defining or common direct skin damage.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: unspecified skeletal abnormalities lack frequency and diagnostic detail sufficient to establish this axis.

basis: Urea-cycle enzyme deficiency; hepatic failure is frequent (30-79%). Supplied neurological injury annotations are occasional, so neurologic involvement is not added across the umbrella.
Inherited citrulline transport defect with metabolic/homeostatic abnormality; no evidence establishes additional organ damage.
Congenital cleft between the laryngeal/tracheal airway and oesophagus; aspiration follows the structural defect.
Named limb-heart-cleft triad defines syndrome; lung hypoplasia 80-99%. Cap omits ear canal atresia and parathyroid anomalies (80-99%) and renal anomalies (30-79%).

decisions.pulmonary: involved: lung hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%; retained for severity, with the three primary slots assigned to the named limb-heart-cleft triad.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft lip and palate are defining malformations in the syndrome's name and definition; cleft palate occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Skeletal malformations, microcephaly/intellectual disability and oral clefting define the syndrome; horseshoe kidney and urethral malformation occur in 30-79%.
Defined by cleft palate and tooth agenesis, stapes fixation with deafness, and carpal/tarsal skeletal fusions.
Inherited skeletal dysplasia affecting cranial and clavicular development; no additional organ damage is established.
Skeletal defects and severe CNS disease characterize the syndrome; sparse hair 26/27 and nail hypoplasia 22/24 support skin involvement. Isolated cardiac reports lack cohort prevalence.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: tetralogy in 1/1 assessed is an isolated report, not evidence that cardiac defects affect at least 30% of the syndrome population.
decisions.neurologic: primary: severe CNS disease is a defining feature, including neuronal loss and brain malformations. [FIG4 study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3644641/)

basis: Neurologic degeneration and cutaneous photosensitivity characterize disease; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Calcification alone does not establish vascular dysfunction.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: premature atherosclerosis (30-79%) is a separate disease; vascular calcification alone does not demonstrate functional vascular damage.

basis: Developmental impairment, retinal dystrophy and neutropenia define Cohen syndrome; dental agenesis, tongue hypoplasia and gingival abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Inherited cutaneous collagen disorder with transepidermal elimination and recurrent keratotic lesions; no established systemic immune mechanism.
The defining triad comprises macular coloboma, cleft palate and hallux valgus; palate belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited retinal and optic disc colobomas with reduced vision and additional ocular abnormalities.
Inherited cone dysfunction causes absent color vision and reduced visual acuity, with retinal abnormalities.
Classical complement immunodeficiency. SLE in approximately 60% and recurrent respiratory infections are separately diagnosed diseases; their organ effects are not assigned here.
Classical complement immunodeficiency; infections and autoimmune diseases are separately diagnosed consequences. Lupus affects only about 10-20%.
Defining combination of cone-rod retinal dystrophy and amelogenesis imperfecta; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Heart defects, tongue hamartoma and polysyndactyly define the syndrome. Benign CNS neoplasms are frequent (30–79%), supporting neurologic involvement.
Fibrinolytic protein deficiency causes damaging mucosal membranes: ocular disease 80-99%, gingival disease 30-79%. Hydrocephalus generally affects <15%, despite a selected 2/2 series.

decisions.neurologic: none: hydrocephalus generally occurs in <15%; the selected 2/2 report does not represent its frequency across this disease.

basis: Congenital discontinuity of the aortic arch; associated cardiac defects remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Arthrogryposis, myopathy and cutaneous pterygia define it. Cleft palate and conductive hearing loss each occur in 30-79%; ptosis (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis occurs in 30-79%, but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of defining skin webs, cleft palate and hearing impairment.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: multiple cutaneous pterygia are named defining malformations; webbed neck is reported in 80-99%.

basis: Familial early-onset seizures with intellectual disability and myoclonus define a neurologic disorder.
Congenital corneal flattening, opacity and reduced visual acuity; confined to the eye.
Congenital endothelial corneal dystrophy and progressive sensorineural hearing loss are defining, each reported in 80-99%.
Corneal calcium deposition causes pain and visual impairment; local calcification does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Hereditary band-shaped spheroidal degeneration affects the cornea.
Corneal stromal dystrophy defines the disease, even though its opacities generally do not impair vision.
Congenital corneal endothelial dysfunction causes edema, opacity and impaired vision; hearing impairment occurs in only 5–29%.
Inherited keratan-sulfate sulfation defect causes corneal deposits, stromal opacification and visual loss; a metabolic disorder need not cause systemic injury.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defective keratan-sulfate sulfation is an inborn glycosaminoglycan metabolic disorder, despite predominantly ocular injury.

basis: Brain, palate and cardiac defects define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%; facial and eyelid morphology alone does not establish ocular damage.
Congenital absence of a central nervous system structure; associated findings do not establish common damage outside the nervous system.
Cortical blindness and intellectual disability are neurologic; polydactyly is defining. No intrinsic eye damage or established immunodeficiency.
Steroid metabolism disorder with defining severe hypertension. Nephrocalcinosis occurs in 30-79% as a separate complication; renal insufficiency occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.renal: none: nephrocalcinosis (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed complication; direct renal functional impairment is documented in only 5-29%.

basis: Developmental, skin and skeletal/joint abnormalities define syndrome; cardiac defects/cardiomyopathy have HPO frequencies of 30-99%. Frequent ocular and dental defects omitted by cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cardiac malformations/cardiomyopathy are common, with HPO frequencies of 30-99%; retained alongside the three defining phenotype axes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: joint laxity and skeletal growth abnormalities define the faciocutaneoskeletal phenotype; congenital myopathy is also a synonym.

basis: Defined by deficient skull ossification, absent clavicles and vertebral anomalies; cleft palate affects 80-99%. Brain anomalies occur in only 5-29%.
Congenital cranial-nerve paresis with facial palsy; unspecified pinna morphology does not establish functional ear damage.
Recurrent cranial nerve paresis and peripheral neuropathy; ophthalmoplegia is neurogenic, and diabetes is a separate diagnosis with unspecified frequency.
Generalized skeletal hyperostosis; intellectual disability 80–99%; auditory canal stenosis and conductive hearing loss 30–79%. Optic atrophy only 5–29%.
Skeletal/ectodermal dysplasia with nephronophthisis; hepatic fibrosis affects ~30-50%. Dental defects (80-99%) omitted at cap in favor of severe visceral damage.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic fibrosis affects approximately 30-50% and causes substantial visceral damage; retained under the four-axis cap.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none at cap: dental defects affect 80-99%, but hepatic fibrosis is prioritized for its greater functional severity.

basis: Callosal abnormalities, ID and ocular colobomas define syndrome; brachydactyly 80–99% with other skeletal defects; aortic aneurysm 30–79%.
Craniosynostosis defines disease; developmental delay 80-99% and hydrocephalus 30-79%; auditory canal stenosis and strabismus each 30-79%. Cardiac defects 5-29%, excluded.
Cranial hyperostosis and metaphyseal dysplasia define disease. Hearing impairment, optic atrophy and facial palsy lack evidence establishing a frequency of at least 30%.

decisions.otologic: none: mixed hearing impairment is reported without frequency; involvement in at least 30% of this recessive subtype is not established.

basis: Defining congenital heart defect, craniosynostosis and developmental disability; structural tracheal abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Craniosynostosis with cranial-base and digit malformations defines a skeletal disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
Craniosynostosis and fibular aplasia define the syndrome; cryptorchidism is outside the axes and palmar creases do not indicate skin damage.
Craniosynostosis and radial-ray defects define disease; malabsorption occurs in 30-79% and poikiloderma in 2/6. Proptosis alone does not establish eye damage.
Craniosynostosis and intellectual disability are the defining skeletal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities.
Craniosynostosis, ID/seizures and cleft lip/palate define syndrome; renal dysplasia is a defining feature; ocular coloboma omitted because of cap.
Craniosynostosis and severe brain malformations define disease; microphthalmia, optic atrophy and visual impairment occur in 30-79%.
Generalized thyroid hormone resistance defines the disorder; peripheral hormone resistance alone does not establish structural damage to additional organs.
Hepatic bilirubin conjugation enzyme deficiency. Kernicterus and hearing impairment are annotated at 5-29%, below threshold across both types.
Congenital cataracts, renal tubular necrosis and severe encephalopathy define the syndrome and occurred in both reported infants.
Cryptophthalmos, syndactyly and renal malformations are major criteria; renal defects 80-99%. Laryngeal stenosis/hypoplasia 30-79%; GI and ear anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal agenesis/hypoplasia is a major diagnostic criterion, supported by renal hypoplasia/aplasia and urinary abnormalities in 80-99%.

basis: Abnormal testicular descent is a reproductive structural disorder; endocrine dysfunction and common renal damage are not established.
Congenital nail disorder; associated distal phalangeal shortening has no frequency supporting additional skeletal involvement.
Adrenal cortisol excess; proximal amyotrophy/osteoporosis and dermal striae/fragility each occur in 30-79%. Hypertension and kidney stones are separately diagnosed complications.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension occurs in 30-79%, but is a separately diagnosed secondary condition; direct cardiovascular tissue injury is not established.

basis: ACTH/cortisol excess causes bone loss/myopathy, skin atrophy and secondary hypertension, each 30-79%. Endogenous immunodeficiency (30-79%) is omitted at the four-organ cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: secondary hypertension (30-79%) is a direct manifestation of cortisol excess; no later cardiovascular complications are inferred.
decisions.infectious_immune: none under cap: endogenous immunodeficiency is reported in 30-79%, but bone/muscle, skin and cardiovascular damage take priority.

basis: Defined by severe inflammatory colitis and early photosensitive vesicular skin lesions; classified as inflammatory bowel disease.
Cutis laxa defines disease; emphysema in 6/6 and pulmonary artery stenosis/aortic regurgitation each in 1/2 support lung and cardiovascular damage. Bladder diverticula 1/4 excluded.
Proline/ornithine metabolism disorder with neurodevelopmental impairment and cutis laxa; cataracts 80-99%. Joint hypermobility and hip dislocation omitted under cap.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and high myopia occur in 80-99%; muscle loss 80-99%, delayed fontanelle closure 100%. Dental caries 80-99% omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment and cortical abnormalities occur in 80-99%; the supplied concept is defined primarily by inherited cutis laxa.

basis: Congenital cutaneous vascular malformation; supplied HPO reports seizures and limb defects at 80-99%; retinal detachment 30-79% omitted by cap.
Scalp skin thickening and folding with intellectual disability are the defining manifestations.
Hepatic disease is explicit; available information does not establish whether cyanosis reflects pulmonary, cardiovascular or blood pathology.
Usually benign cystathionine metabolism defect. Despite frequent HPO annotations, the definition describes neurologic findings as associations without established pathogenic relevance.
Abnormal cysteine/glycine peptide handling supports a metabolic disorder; intellectual disability frequency is unspecified, and urinary excretion alone does not establish renal damage.
Hereditary pulmonary cysts with neonatal pneumothorax; recurrent infections alone do not establish a separate immunodeficiency mechanism.
Defining obstructive airway disease and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (80-99%). Hepatic abnormalities occur in 5-29%; secondary infections do not make CF an immune disorder.
CF, gastritis and anemia define syndrome; intellectual disability 80-99%. H. pylori infection and renal disease (30-79%) omitted under four-axis cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: cystic fibrosis defines the syndrome and causes intrinsic airway disease; recurrent respiratory infections occur in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%; retained for its common, substantial neurodevelopmental impairment.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: defining H. pylori infection qualifies, but the four-axis cap prioritizes pulmonary, gastrointestinal, haematologic and neurologic damage.

basis: Defining cerebral ventriculomegaly and cystic renal disease; cardiac abnormalities occur in only 1/6.
Inherited cystine transport disorder confined to cornea/conjunctiva, with photophobia and visual impairment; no systemic manifestations.
Lysosomal cystine storage causes nephropathy; corneal abnormalities affect 80-99%, with photophobia 2/2 and ocular pain 30-79% indicating functional involvement.
Inherited renal tubular amino acid transport defect with recurrent cystine stones. Hypertension and urinary infections are separate complications.
Mitochondrial Leigh syndrome; cardiomyopathy and liver dysfunction each occur in 30-79%. Frequent skeletal myopathy omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Progressive encephalopathy 80-99%; optic nerve hypoplasia and patent ductus arteriosus each 1/3. Small samples limit certainty. Reflux is separately diagnosed.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: patent ductus arteriosus is an annotated structural cardiovascular defect in 1/3 patients, approximately 33%; the small denominator limits certainty.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic nerve hypoplasia represents structural ocular injury in 1/3 patients, approximately 33%; the small denominator limits certainty.

basis: Inherited proximal tubular urate transport defect with defining hypouricemia; renal complications remain within the renal axis.
Cerebellar vermis malformation, posterior fossa cyst and hydrocephalus define the disease; associated skull remodeling does not establish direct skeletal damage.
Cerebellar/posterior fossa malformations, developmental impairment and congenital heart defects define the cranio-cerebello-cardiac syndrome.
Brain malformation, intellectual disability, severe myopia and brachytelephalangy define syndrome; dental and palatal abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Hair and nail findings are cosmetic.
Cerebellar malformation and postaxial polydactyly define the syndrome; cardiac and ocular abnormalities have no established qualifying frequency.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; any associated vestibular dysfunction remains within the otologic axis.
Congenital hearing loss and myoclonic epilepsy define the syndrome.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, deafness and osteodystrophy define DOORS; nail hypoplasia ~100% retained as involved under the primary cap. Gingival overgrowth 3/3 omitted by total cap.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: diagnostic nail hypoplasia occurs in essentially 100%; retained here because the three primary slots prioritize neurologic, hearing and skeletal disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: osteodystrophy defines DOORS, with short distal finger phalanges in 30/30; skeletal involvement is a core diagnostic component.

basis: Split hand/foot malformation and sensorineural hearing loss are defining and each present in 2/2.
Congenital deafness and generalized albinism define the syndrome; ocular dysfunction, hypogonadism and intellectual disability lack frequency evidence.
High myopia and progressive sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome and are present in 7/7 patients.
External/middle ear malformations and hearing loss define disease; hypogonadism and global developmental delay each occur in 30-79%.
Ear atresia/deafness, ptosis and skeletal defects define syndrome; enamel/dental dysplasia occurs in 80-99%. Hair dysplasia omitted at the four-axis cap.
Deafness, vitiligo and achalasia define the syndrome; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%. EEG abnormalities alone do not establish additional neurologic damage.
Defined by progressive deafness, sensory neuropathy and bowel diverticulosis/dysmotility. Frequent ptosis is a neurologic manifestation without established direct ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis occurs in 30-79%, but is attributable to neurologic dysfunction; independent eyelid or eye pathology is not established.

basis: Congenital sensorineural hearing impairment defines the disease.
Defined by sensorineural deafness and persistent atopic dermatitis; atopic dermatitis is immune-mediated.
Sensorineural deafness and missing teeth define the syndrome and each occur in 80-99%; vestibular symptoms remain within the otologic axis.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss classified as a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; no additional systemic damage established.
Combined pituitary hormone deficiency, rigid cervical spine/kyphoscoliosis and sensorineural hearing loss define syndrome; hearing and spinal findings occur in 80-99%.
Progressive leukodystrophy with dementia and polycystic bone lesions causing recurrent fractures define the disease.
Progressive leukodystrophy and thickened, hyperkeratotic skin are defining manifestations, both reported in 80-99%.
Skin nodules, osteochondrodystrophy and visually impairing corneal dystrophy define the syndrome; core features occur in 80-99%. Gingival frequency unknown.
Skin ulceration, osteolysis and oligodontia are defining features; keratitis caused visual impairment or blindness in 3/5 siblings (~60%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oligodontia is explicitly part of the defining syndrome and annotated 80-99%; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

basis: Congenital persistence of fetal ocular vasculature with severe vitreoretinal maldevelopment and vision loss in 31/31 patients.
Dextrocardia, microphthalmia and neurologic impairment define the syndrome; cleft palate is an additional defining feature affecting the oral cavity.
Renal concentrating failure and cerebral dysfunction define syndrome; dental damage and joint restriction occur in 80-99%. Hearing loss (30-79%) is omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint restriction occurs in 80-99%, with skeletal hypoplasia; prioritized over less frequent hearing impairment.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: conductive hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%, below the frequency of retained dental and musculoskeletal damage.

basis: Diabetes, optic atrophy and deafness are cardinal; hearing loss 60-90%. Hydronephrosis 8/10 (80%); neurologic dysfunction ~33-50% omitted at cap.

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural deafness is a cardinal component of Wolfram/DIDMOAD, with hearing impairment in 60-90% in the supplied series.

basis: Inherited biochemical disorder with urinary excretion of diaminopentane (cadaverine); abnormal urinary metabolites alone do not establish renal damage.
Congenital diaphragm defect; associated pulmonary hypoplasia directly impairs lung development in well over 30%.
Brain malformation, visual disease and deafness define syndrome; renal proximal tubulopathy/proteinuria ~100%; common diaphragmatic defects (~69%) omitted by cap.
Enteropathy, hair abnormalities and immunodeficiency define the syndrome; hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis occurs in 30-79%. Neurodevelopmental impairment (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Congenital split spinal cord; associated vertebral malformations and scoliosis affect roughly half or more.
Sulfate transport/metabolism defect causing skeletal dysplasia and joint contractures; cleft palate affects 8/12. Blue sclerae and ear shape changes do not establish damage.
Renal dibasic amino-acid transport disorder; intellectual deficit reported in one homozygote, while 25 heterozygotes were asymptomatic; common neuro damage unproven.
Amino acid transport disorder; developmental delay 10/10, osteoporosis 5/6, renal dysfunction 30-79%. Common pulmonary, hepatic and blood damage omitted by cap.
Inherited renal amino-acid transport defect; intellectual disability is occasional; nephrolithiasis is a separate complication despite 1/2 reported cases.
Pyrimidine metabolism disorder; intellectual disability 12/19 and seizures 30-79%; feeding problems alone do not establish GI injury, and villous atrophy occurs in 5-29%.
Plasmalogen synthesis defect with skeletal dysplasia and cataracts; severe intellectual disability is characteristic (1/1 annotated). Isolated cardiac report lacks group prevalence.
Inherited erythrocyte enzyme defect causing abnormal red-cell physiology, including erythrocytosis or hemolysis; splenic involvement shares the blood axis.
Inherited intestinal brush-border enzyme deficiency causing carbohydrate maldigestion and malabsorption.
Inherited intestinal lactase deficiency causes impaired lactose digestion and severe neonatal diarrhea; an inborn carbohydrate metabolic disorder.
Disseminated sclerosis denotes immune-mediated CNS demyelination; associated narcolepsy is also neurologic.
Diverticula arise in the small-intestinal wall.
Defined by visceral diverticula, marfanoid skeletal/connective-tissue abnormalities with hernias, and retinal detachment; aortic disease is not established.
Defining upper-limb phocomelia, encephalocele and thrombocytopenia occur in 80-99%; urinary abnormalities occur in only 5-29%, with other urogenital findings reproductive.
Leukocyte inclusions, anemia and leukemia define the blood disorder; atrial septal defect has no established frequency supporting inclusion.
Catecholamine synthesis defect causes autonomic failure and severe hypotension; defining eyelid ptosis occurs in 4/6; renal biochemical findings alone do not establish lasting damage.
Intellectual disability and eczema define syndrome; thumb hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%, palatal cleft in 30-79%. Eyelid narrowing lacks established dysfunction; otitis is separately coded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: submucous cleft hard palate occurs in 30-79% and represents a direct structural oral defect.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis is reported in 20/20, but the supplied evidence establishes eyelid dysmorphism without visual loss or impaired eyelid function.

basis: Congenital absence of the duodenal lumen; vascular anomalies and metabolic alkalosis are occasional, below 30%.
Growth-hormone unresponsiveness defines impaired endocrine growth signaling. Hearing impairment and intellectual disability have unspecified frequencies.
Intellectual disability and eye abnormalities define this syndrome. Unspecified dwarfism does not establish skeletal dysplasia or endocrine disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: dwarfism alone does not specify bone, joint or muscle pathology; no skeletal abnormalities are supplied.

basis: Skeletal growth disorder defined by proportionate dwarfism and hip dislocation; no evidence of an endocrine cause.
Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia with characteristic intellectual disability defines DMC and distinguishes it from Smith-McCort dysplasia.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is a defining diagnostic feature, rather than an incidental complication of the skeletal dysplasia.

basis: Sensory/autonomic neuropathy; alacrima 80-99% and corneal erosion 30-79%; scoliosis 30-79%; BP instability reflects neural autonomic dysfunction.
Autonomic dysfunction, peripheral neuropathy and intellectual disability establish a neurologic disorder; no direct extra-neural damage is documented.
Cerebellar hypoplasia and intellectual disability define disease; strabismus and muscle atrophy each occur in 30-79%, but direct ocular or muscle pathology is unestablished.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus occurs in 30-79% but does not establish direct ocular damage; cataract and visual abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79%, but this cerebellar disorder does not establish direct myopathy rather than secondary disuse or neurologic effects.

basis: Dyserythropoietic anemia with a glycosylation defect. Gallstones are separately coded; iron loading alone does not establish hepatic functional injury in at least 30%.
Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis and hemolytic anemia; hepatomegaly and jaundice alone do not establish hepatic damage. Syndactyly is below 30%.
Skin/nail abnormalities, marrow failure and oral leukoplakia are defining dyskeratosis congenita features; marrow failure 1/3. Other organ complications lack qualifying frequencies.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral leukoplakia is part of the major diagnostic mucocutaneous triad of dyskeratosis congenita; oral mucosa maps to gastrointestinal.

basis: Dysmyelination establishes neurologic disease; jaundice of unspecified mechanism does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.hepatic: none: jaundice alone cannot distinguish hepatic dysfunction from hemolysis or isolated bilirubin handling abnormalities; liver damage is unestablished.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; regression/intellectual disability, optic atrophy and hearing loss each annotated 80-99%. Dental, cardiac and skin abnormalities omitted at cap.
Defining vertebral and long-bone dysplasia with restricted joints; supplied CNS, ocular and palatal abnormalities lack evidence of frequency at or above 30%.
Severe skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia reported in 2/2 with lethal respiratory compromise. Broader annotations place cataract and encephalocele below 30%.
Progressive dystonia is neurologic; dysphagia and blepharospasm reflect motor dysfunction without demonstrated gastrointestinal or ocular damage.
Syndrome defined by dystonia and ringbinden, the abnormal ring-fiber architecture of skeletal muscle.
Patellar aplasia and microtia define syndrome; intellectual disability in 1/2 and emphysema in 1/3 support involvement, with uncertainty from small samples.
Congenital tricuspid valve malformation. Respiratory insufficiency and cyanosis reflect abnormal circulation; cerebral ischemia is a minority complication.
Defining features include palmoplantar keratoderma, hair/nail abnormalities, eyelid hidrocystomas and hypodontia.
Ectodermal defects, deafness and finger contractures define the syndrome; cognitive impairment occurs in 30-79%. Dental disease in 30-79% omitted under the four-axis cap.
Defining sweat-gland and hair abnormalities affect skin; missing, small and conical teeth affect the gastrointestinal axis.
Ectodermal dysplasia, oral clefting and intellectual disability characterize the syndrome. Eyelid fusion is optional in this definition, without an established >=30% frequency.

decisions.ocular: none: fused eyelids are an additional possible feature; the AEC parent alone does not establish their frequency or diagnostic necessity in this specific syndrome.

basis: Defining ectodermal and CNS abnormalities; enamel defects and microdontia occur in 80-99%. Nonspecific immune annotation does not establish immunodeficiency.
Skin, thyroid and airway ciliary defects define syndrome; lacrimal dysfunction 30-79%. Enteropathy is described but its frequency is unclear and the four-axis cap favors ocular evidence.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: enteropathy is described without frequency; the four-axis cap favors ocular dysfunction with explicit 30-79% frequency.
decisions.ocular: involved: lacrimal dysfunction affects 30-79%, supporting loss of lacrimal function; ophthalmic complications also appear in the definition.

basis: Skin/hair/nail dysplasia and oral cleft/dental defects define disease; intellectual disability and hypogonadism each occur in 30-79%. Defining syndactyly is cutaneous.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypogonadism is reported in 30-79% and represents gonadal endocrine dysfunction, beyond reproductive anatomy alone.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: defining syndactyly is explicitly cutaneous; facial skeletal dysmorphism does not establish additional locomotor dysfunction.

basis: Isolated hereditary lens dislocation; no systemic connective-tissue disease is established.
Isolated displacement of the lens and pupil, with associated ocular structural abnormalities.
Congenital thyroid dysgenesis and hypothyroidism; individual cardiac findings occur in 1/4 and do not establish common cardiac damage.
Defining hair/ectodermal abnormalities, ectrodactyly and macular dystrophy; dental malformations in 80-99% support gastrointestinal involvement.
Congenital digital and limb malformations define the disorder; cutaneous syndactyly is part of the limb anomaly.
Congenital skeletal malformation of hands and feet, with missing digits and syndactyly.
Defined by joint hypermobility, abnormal skin extensibility/scarring and platelet dysfunction; mitral valve prolapse frequency is unestablished.
Valve disease, joint hypermobility and skin fragility define subtype; myopia, strabismus and ptosis annotated 30-79%; dental crowding alone excluded.
Skin fragility and joint laxity define dEDS; hiatus hernia/reflux 80-99% and gingival disease support GI; myopia 3/4 and other ocular defects 30-79%. Bruising reflects tissue fragility.
Skeletal/ectodermal dysplasia with heart defects; dental/oral abnormalities 80–99%. HPO renal/urinary, lung and strabismus findings 30–79% omitted under cap.
Multilocular destruction of brain tissue with intellectual disability and spastic diplegia.
Named syndrome comprises axonal encephalopathy, necrotizing myopathy, cardiomyopathy and cataracts; cataracts are a defining component.
Interferon-mediated encephalopathy; thrombocytopenia 12/17 and inflammatory chilblains 40/90. Hepatic involvement (transaminases 6/19) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia and prenatal contractures define PCH4; contractures occur in 2/4. Central apnea and neurogenic dysphagia do not establish lung or gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: prenatal contractures are explicitly part of the disease definition, supported by contractures in 2/4 and frequent arthrogryposis.

basis: Encephalopathy, retinal degeneration and growth hormone deficiency define the syndrome; visual impairment need not accompany early retinal disease.
Cerebral proliferative vasculopathy causes destructive brain malformations; fixed joint contractures occur in 6/7 and talipes in 5/7.
Endocardial thickening causes cardiomyopathy; supplied syndromic endocrine and neurologic annotations are not general features of isolated fibroelastosis.
Endocardial fibroelastosis and abdominal aortic coarctation both directly affect cardiovascular structures.
Congenital corneal endothelial dystrophy and nail hypoplasia define the disorder.
Inflammation of small intestine and colon; infectious or immune mechanisms are not universal across causes.
Intestinal enteropeptidase deficiency causes defective protein digestion and malabsorption; associated celiac or pancreatic disorders are separate diseases.
Definition covers intestinal protein loss across causes. CHAPLE-associated immunoglobulin depletion (11/11) does not establish common immunodeficiency across this broader concept.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: the broad definition describes immune depletion in severe cases; CHAPLE-specific frequencies cannot establish >=30% immune dysfunction across all protein-losing enteropathies.

basis: Immune-mediated fascial inflammation with defining cutaneous/subcutaneous induration and fibrosis. Reactive eosinophilia does not establish a blood disorder.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: progressive skin/subcutaneous induration and disabling cutaneous fibrosis are defining clinical features of eosinophilic fasciitis.

basis: Inherited susceptibility to chronic cutaneous HPV infection with persistent skin lesions; subsequent skin cancer is a separate disease.
Junctional skin blistering, intellectual disability and characteristic dental defects define this syndrome; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental enamel defects are part of the syndrome definition ([MedGen](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/341663)); the supplied synonym also describes anodontia.

basis: Rare skin/nail dystrophy with characteristic congenital sensorineural deafness; hearing loss is treated as part of the defining phenotype, although frequencies are unavailable.

decisions.otologic: primary: congenital sensorineural deafness is characteristic of this rare neurotrophica phenotype alongside skin atrophy and nail dystrophy.

basis: Cutaneous and oral/GI blistering define disease; contractures occur in 80-99%, ocular erosions/scarring in 30-79%. Secondary anemia excluded; renal/cardiac injury <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: mucosal blistering and scarring are defining manifestations, including oral erosions and gastrointestinal inflammation.
decisions.ocular: involved: ocular disease occurs in 30-79%, including erosions and scarring; visual loss need not occur for direct injury to qualify.

basis: Skin fragility and nail dystrophy define the disease; oral blistering and enamel hypoplasia are defining gastrointestinal-axis manifestations.
Blistering and muscular dystrophy define disease; ocular motor impairment is annotated at 80-99%, enamel defects at 30-79%. Language annotations are discordant with established EBS-MD.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental enamel abnormalities are annotated at 30-79%; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.neurologic: none: aphasia/echolalia annotations conflict with established EBS-MD; myopathic ocular weakness does not establish separate neurologic damage.

basis: Defining skin and oral mucosal erosions; oral abnormalities and enamel hypoplasia occur in 80-99%. Structural airway abnormalities occur in 5-29%; stridor alone is insufficient.

decisions.pulmonary: none: stridor and hoarseness are symptoms; documented laryngeal stenosis and upper respiratory tract abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: mucosal blistering is part of the definition, with characteristic oral erosions and enamel defects; mouth and teeth map to gastrointestinal.

basis: Skin blistering and pyloric atresia define disease; urinary tract dysplasia, obstruction and hydronephrosis are frequent (30-79%). Skin infections are secondary.
Defining abnormalities are skin blistering and a congenital defect of the muscular diaphragm; common pulmonary damage is not established.
Epilepsy, intellectual deterioration and dental enamel defects define the syndrome; impaired sweating occurs in 30-79%.
Photosensitive epilepsy, spastic diplegia and intellectual disability define neurologic dysfunction.
Defined by autoimmune intestinal disease together with epilepsy and cerebral calcifications.
Epilepsy, intellectual disability, IgA deficiency and congenital fifth-finger shortening define the syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 30–79%. Conjunctival telangiectasia is non-impairing.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: developmental dental abnormalities affect 30–79%; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital fifth-finger shortening is part of the syndrome's defining phenotype and occurs in 80–99%.

basis: Epiphyseal and joint dysplasia caused by defective sulfate transport/cartilage sulfation; explicitly classified as an inborn metabolic disorder.
The defining syndrome combines femoral epiphyseal dysplasia, high myopia and hearing impairment.
Epiphyseal dysplasia and microcephaly define it; retinal dysfunction/field loss reported in 1/3. Restriction in 1/3 does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Neonatal diabetes, epiphyseal dysplasia and recurrent liver failure define WRS; neutropenia occurs in 30-79%. Renal and neurologic findings occur in under 30%.

decisions.hepatic: primary: recurrent acute liver failure is explicitly part of the disease definition; liver abnormalities affect 80-99% and acute hepatic failure 30-79%.

basis: Keratinizing squamous epithelial dysplasia directly affects the urinary tract.
Record conflates IRF8 deficiency and CAEBV; immune and blood-cell abnormalities define it. Liver dysfunction is described as common, with hypoalbuminemia in 1/1.
Hereditary acral erythema defines skin involvement; frequencies and functional effects of dental abnormalities and clubfoot are unspecified.
Defined pigmentary abnormalities and sensorineural deafness; intellectual disability reported in 1/1 annotated patient. Ocular abnormalities are occasional.
Self-limited suppression of erythroid marrow production causes anemia and reticulocytopenia; an infectious or immune cause is not established.
Exfoliative skin disease; malabsorption 80-99%; respiratory insufficiency alone does not establish direct lung damage. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/sign/1954)
Defined by eyebrow hair duplication and finger/toe syndactyly; eyebrow abnormalities do not establish ocular damage.
Kyphoscoliosis and intellectual disability are defining skeletal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities; facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
Dermal defects and distichiasis (19/21) define it; sacroiliac anomalies occur in 80-99%, anal atresia in 2/3 assessed. Urinary anomalies (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none: upper urinary tract anomalies occur in 30-79%, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent skeletal anomalies and severe anorectal defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural sacroiliac joint abnormalities are reported in 80-99%, supporting common skeletal involvement.

basis: Limb hypoplasia and cardiac malformations define the syndrome; structural tongue hypoplasia affects 80-99%.
Heart defects, horseshoe kidney and intellectual disability define the syndrome; cleft palate and hypodontia occur in 80–99%.
Inherited deficiency of coagulation factors V and VIII causes a bleeding disorder.
Combined coagulation factor V and VIII deficiency causes abnormal bleeding; no additional organ is intrinsically affected.
Facial and thoracic structural anomalies suggest skeletal involvement; genital anomalies have no axis. Detailed phenotype data are unavailable.
Defining digital and skeletal malformations; dental open bite is persistent malocclusion reported in 30-79%. Hearing impairment and intellectual disability occur in 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental open bite in 30-79% represents persistent defective occlusion; high palate and facial appearance alone would not justify this axis.

basis: Inherited factor V coagulation deficiency; joint hemorrhage is annotated in 30-79%, directly affecting joints. Epistaxis alone does not imply airway damage.
Factor VII coagulopathy; intracranial and gastrointestinal hemorrhage affect <30% overall, despite the inconsistent supplied HPO frequency labels.
Inherited coagulation factor deficiency; common mucosal bleeding does not establish lasting organ damage. Joint and muscle hemorrhage occur in <30%.
Inherited marrow failure; absent thumbs in 2/4 and absent radius in 1/3 support skeletal involvement. Pigment changes alone do not establish skin damage.
Marrow failure; intellectual disability 31%, microphthalmia 61% and thumb malformations >=31%. Pigment changes lack demonstrated tissue injury; renal anomalies individually <30%.
FANCA-related marrow failure; congenital skeletal/radial-ray defects occur in roughly 30-50%. Renal anomalies are about 20-30%; pigmentation alone is not damaging.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital skeletal/radial-ray malformations affect roughly 30-50%; they are associated structural manifestations rather than the defining marrow disease.

basis: GLUT2 metabolic disorder with defining renal tubular dysfunction and hepatic glycogen accumulation; phosphate-wasting rickets affects 30-79%.
Pancytopenia, immunodeficiency and cutaneous malignancies are explicitly defining features; pulmonary and bone complications lack frequency evidence.
Arthritis and subcutaneous granulomas occur in 80-99%; laryngeal granulomas causing hoarseness are a classic criterion. Neurologic injury (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Congenital fascial fibrosis with stiff skin, restricted joints and contractures; unspecified respiratory findings do not establish common direct lung damage.
Synonyms and ancestry establish congenital fatal hepatic steatosis; no specific metabolic defect or common extrahepatic damage is established.
Congenital limb-bone reduction and malformation; internal organs and intellectual function are usually normal.
Defined by femoral bifurcation and limb reduction defects.
Luteinizing hormone deficiency causes gonadal hormone insufficiency; sparse body hair reflects androgen deficiency rather than skin damage.
Fetal iodine imbalance causes thyroid dysfunction and irreversible neurodevelopmental injury; sensorineural hearing impairment is very frequent, 80-99%.
Tentative metabolic assignment: proposed abnormal steroid-metabolite handling causes persistent fever; mechanism uncertain. [Report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4951423/)
Skeletal dysplasia defines FBCG1; pulmonary hypoplasia and severe thoracic restriction commonly cause neonatal respiratory failure (>30%). Other organ frequencies are unestablished.
audit_reason: Add pulmonary involvement: fibrochondrogenesis commonly causes pulmonary hypoplasia and severe respiratory insufficiency in its usual perinatal course, exceeding 30%. Thoracic restriction can cause direct loss of pulmonary function.

basis: Myofibromas characteristically arise in skin, subcutis, muscle and bone; visceral disease affects a minority.
Defining gingival fibromatosis with frequent dental abnormalities; gums and teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis. Facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
Defining hyaline deposition causes skin nodules (34/35), gingival overgrowth (33/35), contractures and osteolysis. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: gingival fibromatosis is a defining manifestation, present in 33/35 patients; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: IgG4-related retroperitoneal fibroinflammation; ureteric encasement causes obstructive urinary dysfunction in roughly half or more. Other fibrotic sites vary.

decisions.renal: involved: the retroperitoneal fibrosis parent supports direct ureteric encasement and obstruction, occurring in approximately 50% or more.

basis: Congenital limb-bone and joint dysplasia defines the disease; small nails (30-79%) alone do not establish damaging skin or nail disease.
Congenital limb and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; no other axis has established common damage.
Fibuloulnar dysostosis and renal anomalies define the syndrome; cardiac defects are occasional (5–29%); respiratory failure lacks a defined lung lesion.
Inherited contact-pathway coagulation protein deficiency with prolonged aPTT; absence of bleeding diathesis precludes inferred organ injury.
Retinal disorder defined by bilateral flecks; remains ocular despite preserved vision and normal electrophysiology.
Retinal dystrophy with characteristic flecks and frequently mild stationary night blindness.
Heck disease is HPV-associated focal epithelial proliferation of oral mucosa; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Folate transport defect causes malabsorption and megaloblastic anemia; neurodevelopmental impairment 80-99%. Common immune dysfunction omitted because of cap.
FSH deficiency causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; delayed skeletal maturation alone does not establish bone damage.
Inherited histidine/folate metabolic defect; anemia and developmental impairment are occasional (5-29%), despite historical anemia parentage.
Intellectual disability, deafness and skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; persistent subcutaneous nodules and abnormal skin elasticity are frequent (30-79%).
Corneal fragility defines disease; joint abnormalities occur in 80-99% and hearing loss in 30-79%. These are extraocular involvement; skin laxity alone does not establish injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint connective-tissue abnormalities occur in 80-99%; they are extraocular manifestations accompanying the defining corneal disease.

basis: Available phenotype description identifies structural subglottic stenosis and finger joint contracture; ovarian cysts have no applicable axis.
Selective inherited loss of smell perception; olfactory function belongs to the neurological axis.
The syndrome is defined by hereditary ataxia and congenital glaucoma; additional organs cannot be inferred from ordinary Friedreich ataxia.
Craniofacial skeletal, eyelid/eye and oral cleft defects define disease; encephalocele and olfactory tract hypoplasia occur in 30-79%. Choanal atresia is occasional.
Inherited sugar intolerance with hypoglycemia establishes a metabolic disorder; seizures alone do not establish lasting brain damage.
Inherited fructose metabolism defect; supplied hepatic failure and renal insufficiency frequencies are 5-29%; common gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish tissue damage.
Gluconeogenesis defect causing hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis; hepatic and neurologic abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish damage.
Fructokinase deficiency is a benign fructose-metabolism disorder; urinary fructose and erythrocyte enzyme findings do not indicate organ damage.
Lung, diaphragm and distal limb defects define it; renal dysplasia and severe developmental impairment each 80-99%. Cardiac, ocular, oral and nail anomalies omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: severe developmental impairment occurs in 80-99%, with frequent brain malformations; the defining core comprises diaphragm, lung and distal limb abnormalities.

basis: Neurodegeneration defines this storage disease; dysostosis in 3/3 and hearing loss in 80-99%. Skin disease omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone does not prove liver dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive neurologic deterioration is a defining feature of fucosidosis, supported by regression, CNS hypomyelination and intellectual disability.

basis: Galactose metabolism defect defined by early cataracts; hepatic and neurologic manifestations are occasional (<30%).
Inappropriate breast milk secretion; breast has no axis. Hyperprolactinemia is a possible underlying diagnosis rather than an intrinsic feature of every case.
