Umbrella includes predominantly asymptomatic peripheral GALE deficiency; supplied hepatic, neurologic and cataract frequencies reflect the rare generalized phenotype.
Galactose metabolism defect with defining neonatal liver disease; neurologic abnormalities 80-99% and cataracts 30-79%; common coagulopathy omitted at the four-axis cap.
Glutathione synthesis defect with hemolytic anemia; supplied HPO lists neuropathy/spinocerebellar degeneration and myopathy at 80-99%; aminoaciduria alone is insufficient.
Infantile storage neurodegeneration with defining dysostosis; blindness 80-99%. Hearing loss 80-99% and cardiomyopathy 30-79% omitted by cap; organomegaly alone lacks functional impairment.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: dysostosis multiplex (4/4) and skeletal dysplasia are defining infantile GM1 features, also reflected in its skeletal-involvement parent.

basis: Lysosomal disorder with neuroregression; skeletal dysostosis and vertebral/joint abnormalities are common (~30%+); hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive CNS dysfunction; skeletal dysplasia includes scoliosis and platyspondyly (1/1 reported). Ocular damage frequency is uncertain.
Alopecia, failed tooth eruption and ocular disease define GAPO; delayed skeletal maturation and joint hypermobility occur in 80-99%.
Congenital musculofascial abdominal-wall defect with exposed, eviscerated bowel defines disease; intestinal atresia, volvulus and perforation are minority complications.
Lysosomal storage with defining cytopenias and bone disease; hepatic storage/hepatomegaly 80-99%. Valve findings (33/69) omitted at cap; neurologic disease not characteristic.
Acute neuronopathic storage disease; splenic involvement 80-99%, cytopenias 30-79%, hepatic infiltration 80-99%. Pulmonary involvement 30-79% omitted at cap.
Neuronopathic storage disease with defining splenic/marrow involvement; destructive bone disease 80-99%. Hepatic storage and aortic calcification omitted at cap; gaze palsy is neurologic.

decisions.haematologic: primary: macrophage storage in spleen and marrow with cytopenias is a defining systemic component; the blood-organ mechanism rule applies.

basis: Metabolic storage with defining cardiac calcification and supranuclear ophthalmoplegia; thrombocytopenia 30-79%. Corneal opacity and hepatic involvement (30-79%) omitted at four-axis cap.
audit_reason: Replace primary ocular with neurologic: the defining ophthalmoplegia reflects supranuclear oculomotor dysfunction. Corneal opacity supports ocular involvement, omitted alongside hepatic involvement at the four-axis cap.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia, valvular disease and thick skin (10/15) are defining features; airway stenosis 6/13 (46%). Intellectual disability 6/15 (40%) omitted by cap.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent thickened skin is a characteristic diagnostic feature of geleophysic dysplasia, supported by 10/15 patients (67%).

basis: Defined by gonadal dysgenesis, cleft palate and congenital heart defects; kidney, brain and skeletal malformations are occasional, 5-29%.
Glycosylation disorder with skin laxity and severe osteoporosis. Intellectual disability in 7/8 supports neurologic involvement despite the definition describing it as rare.
Arthrogryposis, neurodevelopmental impairment and lymphedema define syndrome. GI: dysphagia 80-99%, clefts 30-79%. Ocular strabismus 80-99% and hearing abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary for defining chronic lymphedema. Move gastrointestinal to involved under the three-primary cap. Remove ocular under the total cap, prioritizing defining lymphedema and severe swallowing dysfunction.

basis: Recurrent gestational trophoblastic disease confined to the reproductive/placental domain; the gene does not establish immune disease.
Defining diaphyseal bone sclerosis and marrow dysfunction with anemia/cytopenias. Nonspecific immune-system annotations do not establish immunodeficiency.
Neonatal liver failure with iron overload, usually caused by gestational alloimmune liver injury. Extrahepatic iron deposition alone does not establish functional organ damage.
Inherited platelet adhesion defect with macrothrombocytopenia; mucosal and skin bleeding reflect haemostatic failure rather than intrinsic disease of those organs.
Congenital glaucoma damages ocular outflow structures and the optic nerve; no extraocular organ disease is established.
Adrenal insufficiency, achalasia and alacrima define the triad; neurologic dysfunction affects roughly one-third or more over time. Frequent keratoderma omitted at four-axis cap.
Organic acid metabolism defect defined by striatal injury and dystonic encephalopathy; feeding and swallowing dysfunction reflect neurologic disease.
Fatty acid and amino acid oxidation disorder; myopathy with proximal weakness and elevated CK occurs in 30-79%. Hepatic and cardiac damage is occasional across the umbrella.
Inherited organic acid metabolism disorder without a consistent damaging phenotype; developmental and white-matter abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis deficiency causes hemolysis. Oxoprolinuria and neurologic annotations conflict with this restricted subtype and suggest generalized disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: intellectual disability in 2/4 accompanies contradictory oxoprolinuria annotations; these do not reliably describe the erythrocyte-restricted, non-oxoprolinuric subtype.

basis: Glutathione metabolism defect; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2. Asthma and eczema are separate diagnoses; incontinence does not establish urinary tract injury.
Congenital absence of gluteal skeletal muscles.
Glucose metabolism defect with hepatic glycogen storage. Renal storage causes common tubulopathy and hyperfiltration (>30%); stones and other separately diagnosed complications excluded.
Metabolic defect with neutropenia and impaired neutrophil function; hepatic glycogen storage and dysfunction in most (>80%). Bowel inflammation and bone disease omitted by cap.
Lysosomal glycogen-storage myopathy; cardiac enlargement/hypertrophy occurs in 30-79% in supplied HPO. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness, not intrinsic lung damage.
Debrancher deficiency defines hepatic and muscle glycogenosis; cardiac hypertrophy occurs in roughly 50-70%. Listed immune/ID frequencies are atypical for GSD III.
Glycogen metabolic disorder; liver dysfunction 80-99%, myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy each 30-79%. Neurologic disease varies by subtype; nonspecific skin findings lack demonstrated damage.

decisions.hepatic: involved: liver dysfunction occurs in 80-99%, but this umbrella includes nonhepatic forms and is defined by the glycogen metabolic defect.

basis: Hepatic glycogen metabolism defect with liver dysfunction; osteopenia/osteoporosis reported in 30-79%; renal and cardiac damage are rare.
Phosphofructokinase deficiency directly affects skeletal muscle glycolysis and erythrocytes, causing metabolic myopathy and hemolytic anemia.
Lysosomal glycoprotein storage disorder. Splenomegaly and gout lack frequencies sufficient to establish common direct organ damage.
Inherited renal glucose transport defect causing isolated glucosuria; usually benign, with no common additional organ damage.
Gonadal endocrine failure is obligate; reduced bone density and impaired skeletal maturation are frequent (30-79%); hearing loss is occasional.
Sensorineural deafness and gonadal endocrine failure define Perrault syndrome; neuropathy and intellectual disability occurred in 2/2, cerebellar atrophy in 1/2.
Complete gonadal dysgenesis with streak gonads entails loss of gonadal endocrine function; reproductive malformations have no additional axis.
Gonadal, cardiac and renal defects define syndrome; ear-canal atresia 80-99%. Cap omits mild developmental impairment and skeletal defects (80-99%), clefts (30-79%) and scalp defects.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac malformations are part of the syndrome's definition; VSD is annotated in 80-99%.
decisions.renal: primary: renal malformations are part of the definition; ureter defects occur in 80-99% and renal hypoplasia/aplasia in 30-79%.
decisions.neurologic: none at cap: mild intellectual disability/developmental delay occurs in 80-99%; severe structural cardiac, renal and ear defects take priority.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal atresia occurs in 80-99%, directly compromising the conductive hearing apparatus.

basis: Autoimmune basement membrane disease defined by glomerulonephritis and pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage.
Granulocytopenia, immunodeficiency and hypoglycemia define syndrome; malabsorption/chronic diarrhea 1/1; arteritis 1/1 omitted by cap.
Defining skin granulomas and combined immunodeficiency with depleted T- and B-cell populations; recurrent respiratory infections alone do not establish pulmonary damage.
audit_reason: Add haematologic: the inherited T-B- combined immunodeficiency directly affects blood-cell populations, supported by decreased T- and B-cell counts. Skin granulomas and the immune mechanism remain primary.

basis: Inherited neutrophil functional defect causing phagocyte immunodeficiency; organ-specific infections are separate diagnoses.
An intrinsic phagocyte oxidative-burst defect defines this blood-cell immunodeficiency. Organ infections are separately diagnosed complications.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a functional disease of blood phagocytes, with defective neutrophil oxidative burst; the blood-cell mechanism rule applies.

basis: Phagocyte functional disorder with defective neutrophil oxidative burst in 6/6; recurrent organ infections do not establish common intrinsic organ damage.
Intrinsic neutrophil oxidative-burst dysfunction; granulomatous intestinal inflammation affects roughly 30-50% in CGD. Secondary organ infections are separately diagnosed.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is an intrinsic functional disease of blood phagocytes, with defective neutrophil oxidative burst documented in 7/7 patients.

basis: Disease is located in the retinal pigment epithelium; no extraocular disease is established.
Growth-factor deficiency with lipodystrophy and skin thickening; contractures/joint stiffness 80-99%. Atherosclerosis is a separately diagnosed vascular disease.
Delay, distal limb hypoplasia and eczema define syndrome; dental anomalies occur in 80-99%; ocular motility abnormalities omitted at cap.
Inherited coagulation factor XII deficiency; thrombosis and retinal vascular occlusion are occasional (5-29%), so no additional axes.
Ocular disease, skin atrophy/hypotrichosis and dental defects are cardinal features; bone loss/rib defects occur in 80-99%, recurrent fractures in 30-79%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic dental malformations are major diagnostic features; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal abnormalities qualify; with three primary slots occupied by cardinal ocular, skin and dental disease, bone loss (80-99%) supports involvement.

basis: CoA metabolic neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration/visual impairment 80-99%. Acanthocytosis lacks blood dysfunction; osteopenia can reflect immobility rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: acanthocytosis is annotated in 30-79%, but abnormal red-cell morphology alone does not establish anemia, hemolysis or other blood dysfunction.

basis: Severe neurodevelopmental impairment and spondylometaepiphyseal dysplasia define syndrome; frequent hair texture and growth changes do not establish tissue damage.
Congenital skeletal malformations of the toes, metatarsals and phalanges.
Halothane-associated hepatitis causes hepatocellular injury through an immune response to drug-modified hepatic proteins.
Defined by defective renal and intestinal amino-acid transport; ataxia and other neurologic dysfunction reported in 80-99%. Photosensitive dermatitis omitted by cap.
Congenital atrioventricular conduction disease; the umbrella includes immune and nonimmune causes, so an immune mechanism is not universal.
Cutaneous hemangiomatosis is vascular proliferation in skin, defining skin and blood-vessel disease. Associated extracutaneous features and their frequencies are unspecified.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangiomas are blood-vessel proliferations; vascular tissue is the lesion's origin, while cutaneous location also supports dermatologic.

basis: Pulmonary venous/capillary vascular disease with defining infiltration of lung interstitium, bronchioles and pleura; impaired gas transfer is very frequent.
Defined as a malignant tumor of capillary-associated pericytes; specific anatomical sites and metastatic organ involvement vary.
Asymmetric limb overgrowth; supplied HPO reports intellectual disability and dental abnormalities in 30-79%. Renal and hepatic tumors are risks, not intrinsic involvement.
Umbrella for blood disorders present at birth; immune or skeletal abnormalities do not apply across most subtypes.
Fatal hepatic failure 3/3; renal anomalies, pulmonary lymphangiectasia and VSD 80-99%. Polydactyly 80-99% and protein-losing enteropathy 30-79% omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: ventricular septal defect occurs in 80-99%, supporting structural cardiac involvement independently of lymphatic abnormalities.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary lymphangiectasia occurs in 80-99% and is a major organ manifestation of the defining lymphatic malformation.
decisions.renal: primary: renal anomalies are explicitly defining, with abnormal renal morphology and hydronephrosis reported in 80-99%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: defining polydactyly occurs in 80-99%, but hepatic, renal, pulmonary and cardiac disease carry greater functional severity.

basis: Hereditary red-cell membrane disorder causing thermally sensitive erythrocytes and hemolytic anemia.
Pulmonary hemosiderosis with defining IgA deficiency; lung injury and immunodeficiency are intrinsic to the concept.
Generalized lymphatic vascular dysplasia and intestinal lymphangiectasia (7/7); pulmonary lymphangiectasia 6/7 and pleural involvement 4/7. Developmental delay only 1/7.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: generalized lymphatic vascular malformation with lymphedema in 7/7 defines the syndrome; this label reflects lymphatic vessels rather than the uncommon cardiac defect.
decisions.dermatologic: none: lymphedema in 7/7 reflects lymphatic vascular dysfunction; independent skin injury or fibrosis is not established by the supplied evidence.

basis: Defining hepatic venous occlusion and combined immunodeficiency; pulmonary fibrosis and neurologic injury occur in fewer than 30%.
Bile-acid synthesis defect with cholestatic liver injury. Malabsorption and coagulopathy (each 30-79%) reflect deficient bile, vitamin K or hepatic synthesis, without direct gut/blood injury.

decisions.haematologic: none: coagulopathy occurs in 30-79% but follows deficient hepatic factor synthesis/vitamin K; direct blood-cell or coagulation-system disease is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: fat malabsorption occurs in 30-79% because bile acids are deficient; intrinsic intestinal damage or loss of intestinal function is not established.

basis: Erythrocyte glycolytic enzyme deficiency causes chronic hemolytic anemia; jaundice does not establish liver damage, and gallstones are a separate disease.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy and Hirschsprung disease define the syndrome; cardiac malformations affect ~58% and strabismus ~57%; skeletal abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Bowel aganglionosis, deafness and polydactyly define syndrome; renal agenesis 30-79%; intellectual disability 30-79% omitted because of cap.
Defining combination of intestinal aganglionosis, limb polysyndactyly and ventricular septal defect.
Hirschsprung disease, nail hypoplasia and distal limb hypoplasia define the syndrome. Hydronephrosis is reported without an established common frequency.
Histidase deficiency causes elevated histidine, generally without clinical consequences; neurologic findings occur in only 1–4%.
Tubular histidine transport defect; brain atrophy/ID and hearing loss 80-99%; skeletal and nail abnormalities also 80-99%, omitted by cap.
Inherited phagocytic-cell dysfunction defines both immune and blood-cell disease; evidence does not establish common damage to additional organs.
audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary: inherited phagocytic-cell dysfunction is a disease of blood cells as well as an immune defect.

basis: Malignant B-cell lymphoma; extranodal organ damage is not common enough across the group to add another axis.
Alobar forebrain malformation; hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, particularly diabetes insipidus, affects roughly 50-70% of HPE. Craniofacial defects vary.
Defining renal, cardiac and palatal defects; lung hypoplasia 80-99%. Cap omits skeletal defects (polydactyly 80-99%) and callosal defects (30-79%), prioritizing severe organ dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: defining cleft palate occurs in 80-99%; its feeding and oral functional burden warrants retention with the severe renal, cardiac and pulmonary defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: polydactyly occurs in 80-99% and other skeletal defects in 30-79%; the retained axes generally carry greater organ dysfunction.

basis: The described syndrome includes a metabolic defect, spastic diplegia, intellectual disability and retinitis pigmentosa; clinical findings affected 3/4 relatives, with biochemical causality uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: primary: spastic diplegia and intellectual disability define the reported syndrome (3/4 relatives); association with the biochemical defect remains uncertain.
decisions.ocular: primary: retinitis pigmentosa defines the reported syndrome (3/4 relatives); association with the biochemical defect remains uncertain.

basis: CBS deficiency with defining lens and skeletal disease (80-99%); neurologic involvement supported by ID in 14/14. Vascular disease (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: vascular disease qualifies at 30-79%, but the four-axis cap retains metabolic disease and more frequent ocular, skeletal and neurologic involvement.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 14/14 and brain atrophy in 3/3 support common CNS injury; primary slots retain metabolic, lens and skeletal hallmarks.
decisions.ocular: primary: lens disease is a defining hallmark and ontology parent; ectopia lentis occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic skeletal disease defines the syndrome; osteoporosis and recurrent fractures occur in 80-99%.

basis: Folate-remethylation disorder defined by CNS dysfunction and peripheral neuropathy; thrombosis occurs in only 5-29%.
Cobalamin remethylation defect with megaloblastic anemia; developmental impairment and brain injury 30-79% or higher. Eye findings nonspecific; blindness and thrombosis <30%.
Congenital fusion of humerus and radius defines the disorder; renal insufficiency and external ear anomalies lack frequencies supporting additional axes.
Congenital humeroradial bony fusion with craniofacial skeletal abnormalities.
Core syndrome combines severe intellectual disability, skeletal dysplasia with short stature, and nephrotic renal disease.
Brain and renal malformations define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia in 11/11 and arthrogryposis in 12/12 support additional involvement.
Congenital hydrocephalus directly affects the brain; seizures and intellectual disability are neurologic manifestations.
Congenital cerebral aqueduct stenosis causes obstructive hydrocephalus.
Hydrocephalus and pulmonary hypoplasia define the core syndrome; intestinal malrotation and limb/bone malformations each occur in 80-99%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: limb undergrowth and long-bone bowing occur in 80-99%; these are associated structural abnormalities alongside the defining brain and lung defects.

basis: Hydrocephalus, joint laxity and spinal deformity define it; aortic regurgitation is annotated frequent (30-79%).
Congenital O-mannosylation disorder with muscular dystrophy and brain malformations; defining eye malformations (retinal dysplasia 2/2) occupy involved because primary is capped at three.

decisions.ocular: involved: structural eye malformations are defining; retinal dysplasia occurs in 2/2 annotated patients. The three-primary cap requires placement here.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the established congenital O-mannosylation defect is an inborn glycosylation disorder, supported by the supplied ancestry rather than the gene alone.

basis: Defining hydrocephalus and skeletal malformations; microphthalmia 49/56; tracheal stenosis 29/38, laryngeal hypoplasia 32/56 and abnormal lung lobation 35/56.
Hydrocephalus causes gait impairment and cognitive decline; urinary and bowel incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction without intrinsic urinary or intestinal damage.
Polydactyly and genitourinary malformations define syndrome; urinary anomalies and hydronephrosis occur in 30-79%. Cardiac and bowel defects are occasional.

decisions.renal: primary: the defining genitourinary malformations include urinary sinus/urethral abnormalities; frequent urinary tract findings support this axis.

basis: Congenital bladder innervation and facial motor dysfunction define urofacial syndrome, with urinary obstruction and upper tract injury. Secondary UTIs and constipation do not establish additional axes.
audit_reason: Add neurologic to primary: urofacial syndrome is a congenital peripheral/autonomic neuropathy with characteristic facial motor dysfunction and impaired bladder innervation, retaining its parent's defining neurologic component.

basis: Severe subcutaneous edema, pleural effusion and pericardial effusion are major diagnostic fluid compartments. Underlying anemia or intrinsic organ diseases vary across this umbrella.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: pericardial effusion is a major diagnostic compartment of hydrops; this does not imply universal intrinsic heart disease.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: pleural effusion is a major diagnostic compartment of hydrops, and pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: severe generalized subcutaneous edema is a major diagnostic manifestation; subcutis belongs to the dermatologic axis.

basis: Organic acid disorder defined by leukoencephalopathy, developmental impairment and ataxia. The discordant infectious encephalitis annotation does not establish an infectious mechanism.
Valine organic aciduria with defining cerebral anomalies. Microtia is a congenital external-ear defect occurring in 30-79%; hypogonadism shares the endocrine axis.

decisions.otologic: involved: microtia represents structural hypoplasia of the external ear, which this axis includes, and is annotated frequent (30-79%).

basis: Tryptophan metabolic defect with encephalopathy; renal tubular acidosis and congenital hearing loss each 30-79%; stomatitis (30-79%) omitted at four-axis cap.
Hydroxylysine metabolic disorder defined by seizures and intellectual disability; aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal damage.
Hydroxyproline catabolic defect is generally benign; intellectual disability and hematuria are not established common direct consequences.
Congenital obstruction of the hymen is a reproductive tract disorder outside the listed axes.
Urea-cycle defect causes hyperammonemic brain injury; seizures occur in 80-99%, with developmental impairment common. Respiratory findings do not establish lung injury.
Urea cycle defect causes ammonia neurotoxicity: seizures 3/3 and coma 2/3 reported patients. Reduced hepatic enzyme activity alone does not establish liver injury.
Inborn beta-alanine metabolism disorder explicitly defined by neurotoxic accumulation with encephalopathy and convulsions; numerical frequencies are unavailable.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurotoxicity, encephalopathy and convulsions are explicitly defining manifestations of the described disease.

basis: Inherited hepatic bilirubin transport disorder; jaundice and urinary pigment excretion do not establish skin or kidney damage.
Inherited hepatic bilirubin transport disorder; gastric mucosal morphology alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Inherited conjugated bilirubin handling disorder localized to hepatic bilirubin transport/metabolism; jaundice does not establish other organ injury.
Primary shunt hyperbilirubinemia reflects bilirubin overproduction from ineffective erythropoiesis; erythroid hyperplasia supports marrow involvement. No established hepatic damage.
Transient impairment of hepatic bilirubin conjugation; kernicterus can occur, but evidence does not establish damage in at least 30%.
Leydig cell hypoplasia causes LH resistance and deficient gonadal hormone production with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.
Inherited biochemical disorder with elevated leucine and isoleucine; supplied evidence does not establish additional organ damage.
A developmental reading and language disorder classified under learning disability and hereditary neurologic disease.
Inherited triglyceride metabolism disorder; pancreatitis is a separate diagnosis. Xanthomas and lipemia retinalis do not establish functional organ damage.
Lysine metabolism disorder; developmental impairment and seizures annotated in 30-79%. Optic hypoplasia in 1/2 is insufficient to establish common ocular involvement.
Inherited mitochondrial lysine transport defect causing hyperlysinemia; intellectual disability is reported without an established frequency.
Amino-acid handling disorder with hyperammonemia and hyperlysinuria; frequencies of lasting neurologic damage and malabsorption are unspecified.
Luft disease is a mitochondrial myopathy with uncoupled oxidative phosphorylation causing hypermetabolism and skeletal muscle dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: this is Luft mitochondrial myopathy; defective oxidative phosphorylation in skeletal muscle and muscle dysfunction characterize the disease.

basis: High hyperopia is a refractive disorder of the eye.
Urea-cycle transport defect; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in 80-99%, with frequent encephalopathy; liver dysfunction and hepatitis occur in 30-79%.
Inherited metabolic bone remodeling disease with characteristic deafness; optic atrophy 30-79%. Dental abnormalities lack documented dysfunction; hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: nonspecific dental abnormalities in 80-99% do not establish impaired dentition or oral function; the four-organ cap also prioritizes established damage.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary hyperphosphatasia is an inherited metabolic bone disorder with profoundly dysregulated bone resorption and deposition.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss is a characteristic manifestation explicitly included in the disease definition, rather than an incidental complication.

basis: Generalized skeletal hyperostosis; facial palsy and sensorineural hearing loss each occur in 30-79% from cranial nerve compression. Optic damage frequency is uncertain.
Neonatal parathyroid/calcium disorder; nephrocalcinosis and renal tubular acidosis are reported, but involvement in at least 30% is not established.
Severe neonatal hyperparathyroidism; fractures and renal tubular aminoaciduria each occur in 80-99%. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish functional injury.

decisions.renal: involved: aminoaciduria in 80-99% supports common intrinsic tubular reabsorptive dysfunction, beyond hypercalciuria or stone risk alone.

basis: GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with intellectual disability and short distal phalanges (7/7); sensorineural hearing loss 2/3. Rectal anomalies 4/7 omitted by cap.
Hyperphosphatemia and seizures define the syndrome; polyuria alone does not establish renal tissue damage.
Proline metabolism defect; developmental disability and seizures common in annotated cohorts; nephropathy frequent (30-79%), despite often benign presentation.
Inherited proline metabolism defect; seizures, intellectual disability and developmental delay annotated at 80-99%. Renal insufficiency is only 5-29%.
Craniofacial and limb dysostosis with common urethral malformations; glaucoma and eyelid coloboma occur in 30-79%; cortical malformations are occasional.
Tetralogy of Fallot is the defining organ malformation; hypertelorism alone does not establish ocular damage.
Microtia and cleft palate define it; developmental delay 20/20 and thenar atrophy 30-79%. Renal fusion/ectopia occurs in 30-79%, but functional renal damage is not established.

decisions.renal: none: horseshoe kidney and crossed fused ectopia are positional/fusion abnormalities; common functional renal damage is not demonstrated.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay occurs in 20/20 and intellectual disability in 30-79%; these directly impair neurologic function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: thenar muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79% and represents direct skeletal-muscle tissue loss.

basis: Hypertrichosis and neuropathy define it; skeletal deformities reported in 3/4 cases and periostitis in 30-79%. Retinal anomalies lack documented functional damage.

decisions.ocular: none: retinal anomalies are reported in familial cases (3/4), but their nature and damaging effect are unspecified.

basis: Hypertrichosis, skeletal dysplasia and cardiomegaly define syndrome; intellectual disability is frequent (30-79%).
Peripheral hypertrophic neuropathy and cataracts are the defining manifestations.
Infantile hyperuricemia with intellectual disability and absent speech defines a metabolic-neurodevelopmental syndrome; dental and lacrimal frequencies are unknown.
Defining endocrine autoimmunity/oral candidiasis (68/68); ocular damage 30-79%, reduced acuity 4/5. Cap omits skin/hair/nails 36-49%, asplenia 40% and tympanosclerosis 32%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: chronic oral candidiasis is a cardinal manifestation (68/68); enamel hypoplasia also affects 67/93.
decisions.ocular: involved: keratoconjunctivitis, cataract and corneal stromal opacity occur in 30-79%; reduced visual acuity is reported in 4/5.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: nail dystrophy 35/72 and alopecia 38/106 qualify, but defining endocrine/immune/oral disease and more consequential ocular damage take priority.

basis: Vitamin C deficiency causes skin fragility/hemorrhage and gingival breakdown, each commonly exceeding 30%. Anemia is often secondary to bleeding or accompanying nutrient deficiencies.

decisions.haematologic: none: reported anemia (~30-80%) commonly reflects blood loss or accompanying iron/folate deficiency; common direct blood-cell or marrow injury is not established.

basis: Inherited antibody deficiency; recurrent respiratory and ear infections are separate infections. Frequency of structural pulmonary damage is unspecified.
Defective hepatic glycogen synthesis causes fasting hypoglycemia; glycosuria does not establish renal damage, and neurologic complications are <30%.
Leucine-triggered hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; persistent neurologic damage is not established in at least 30%.
Hypoinsulinemic hypoglycemia and body hemihypertrophy define disease; hypoglycemic seizures/coma do not establish lasting brain injury; hepatic glycogen lacks dysfunction.
Hypogonadism and cataracts define the syndrome; osteoporosis occurs in 80-99% and fractures in 30-79%.
Hypogonadism, intellectual disability and microcephaly define the syndrome; syndactyly frequency is unspecified.
Endocrine dysfunction, neurodevelopmental/movement disorder and alopecia define it; hearing loss in 4/7 and HPO 80-99%. Frequent osteopenia omitted under cap.
Gonadal failure and alopecia define syndrome; osteopenia/osteoporosis 80-99%, skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability 30-79%; hearing impairment <30%.
Deficient gonadal endocrine function defines male hypogonadism; genital developmental findings do not add another axis.
Reduced sweat glands and sweating, with abnormal palmar dermatoglyphics, define a skin disorder.
Inherited renal tubular dysfunction causes defining hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis; muscle spasms do not establish muscle damage.
Renal tubular salt wasting defines the disease, with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis in 9/9 and nephrocalcinosis in 7/8.
Craniofacial dysostosis, oral/tongue defects and airway hypoplasia define disease; cognitive impairment 80-99%; optic disc coloboma 30-79% omitted by cap.
Congenital hypoparathyroidism and intellectual disability define SSS; dental/enamel defects occur in 30-79%. Growth delay alone does not establish bone injury; ocular defects are usually 5-29%.
Renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia with defining intracerebral calcifications; clinical detail is limited.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intracerebral calcifications are a defining structural brain lesion of this syndrome, rather than an incidental finding.

basis: Disordered phosphate metabolism with defining skeletal mineralization failure; hearing loss frequency unspecified; phosphate wasting alone does not establish kidney damage.
Renal phosphate transport dysfunction causes hypophosphatemia and defining rickets or osteomalacia.
Congenital pituitary hormone deficiency with deficient central vasopressin secretion; no intrinsic renal or additional neurologic damage established.
Congenital underdevelopment of left-sided cardiac structures defines this hypoplastic left heart syndrome subtype.
Defective albumin/IgG recycling causes hypercatabolism and immunodeficiency. Bronchiectasis (2/2) is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis (2/2) is secondary structural disease following recurrent infections, rather than direct pulmonary injury from the protein-recycling defect.

basis: Intellectual disability and urethral hypospadias define syndrome; joint stiffness 80-99%, nail abnormalities 30-79%. Palatal abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap.
Hypothalamic hamartoma with defining seizures and endocrine dysfunction; polydactyly occurs in 2/2 annotated syndromic cases. Other malformations lack usable frequencies.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: central precocious puberty and hypothalamic endocrine dysfunction are explicitly defining clinical presentations in the supplied definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: postaxial polydactyly occurs in 2/2 annotated patients, with syndactyly in 1/2; these are direct skeletal malformations.

basis: Thyroid dysgenesis, cleft palate and frequent choanal atresia define the syndrome; intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%; hair abnormalities omitted by cap.
Inherited renal tubular urate/calcium handling disorder with defining hypouricemia, hypercalciuria and decreased bone density.
Congenital keratinization disorder; ectropion affects 7/8 patients and directly disrupts eyelid function.
Skin, cornea and hearing define the syndrome; developmental delay 3/3 and intellectual disability 2/2 support neurologic involvement; hepatic injury uncertain, also beyond cap.
Inherited keratinization disorder; persistent eyelid ectropion in 16/17 supports ocular involvement. Contractures occur in fewer than 30%.
Congenital ichthyosis and biliary atresia define the syndrome; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Ichthyosis with defining severe ectropion and eclabium; hearing abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Joint restriction reflects tight skin rather than direct joint or muscle damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: defining eclabium deforms the lips and oral aperture; the mouth maps to gastrointestinal.
decisions.ocular: primary: severe eyelid ectropion is explicitly part of the disease definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint restriction from tight skin does not establish direct skeletal muscle or joint damage.

basis: Ichthyosis/alopecia, intellectual disability and eyelid ectropion define syndrome. Eclabion at 30-79% reflects cutaneous contracture without established oral mucosal damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: eclabion occurs in 30-79% but represents lip eversion from skin contracture; direct gastrointestinal tissue damage or loss of function is not established.

basis: Ichthyosis, hepatic enlargement and cerebellar degeneration define syndrome. Splenomegaly (80-99%) lacks evidence of impaired splenic blood function.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenomegaly is defining and occurs in 80-99%, but enlargement alone does not establish impaired splenic blood function or hematologic damage.

basis: Ichthyosis, intellectual disability and renal impairment define syndrome; cataracts 30-79%; dental abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap; short stature alone adds no axis.
Skin/hair and amino-acid abnormalities define the syndrome; intellectual impairment affected 1/2 reported siblings ([report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/843456/)). Renal damage is unestablished.

decisions.renal: none: aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal injury or a specific tubular transport defect; its mechanism is unspecified.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the defining amino-acid handling abnormality establishes a metabolic phenotype, although the biochemical mechanism remains unspecified.

basis: Inherited amino-acid transport disorder defined by defective renal tubular reabsorption. Usually asymptomatic; neurologic and ocular involvement not established as common.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; chronic middle-ear dysfunction with hearing impairment affects roughly 30% or more in primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Primary ciliary dyskinesia damages respiratory airways; chronic middle-ear disease with conductive impairment affects >30% in PCD, though subtype data are limited.
Congenital thymic aplasia causes defining quantitative and functional T-cell deficiency. Pneumonias and gastrointestinal infections are separate secondary diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defining T-lymphocyte deficiency includes reduced blood-cell numbers, satisfying the explicit blood-cell disease rule alongside the immune mechanism.

basis: Callosal agenesis 27/27; immune deficiency and cardiomyopathy 80-99%; cataracts 22/27 (~81%). Cap omits renal anomalies/RTA and myopathy (9/27); hypopigmentation alone is non-damaging.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy is a principal defining feature (80-99%); its severity supports prioritization within the three-primary cap.
decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts affect 22/27 (~81%); retained as the fourth axis after prioritizing defining neurologic, immune and cardiac disease.

basis: DNMT3B-related immunodeficiency defines ICF1. Lasting pulmonary, intestinal and neurologic damage lacks sufficient frequency evidence; recurrent infections are separate diseases.
Combined immunodeficiency with erythroid/myeloid hypoplasia and reduced IgG; no additional common organ damage established.
Inherited immunoglobulin D deficiency concerns humoral immunity; no evidence supports blood-cell disease or other organ damage.
Skeletal dysplasia, T-cell deficiency and nephropathy define SIOD; strokes occur in 30–79%; cap excludes frequent cytopenias and vascular involvement.
Sensory channelopathy causing absent pain perception and anosmia; fractures and neuropathic arthropathy follow unrecognized injury rather than direct skeletal disease.
Abnormal indolylacroylglycine metabolism with defining intellectual disability; urinary metabolite excretion does not establish kidney damage.
Isolated sperm structural abnormalities and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease.
Purine salvage enzyme deficiency defines the metabolic and immune axes; intrinsic developmental and motor neurologic impairment occurs in approximately two-thirds of patients.
audit_reason: Add neurologic involvement: purine nucleoside (inosine) phosphorylase deficiency causes intrinsic developmental and motor neurologic impairment in approximately two-thirds of patients, meeting the 30% rule.

basis: Congenital underdevelopment of the internal carotid arteries; neurologic infarction is not established as common.
Defective T-cell immune function defines an immunodeficiency; no cytopenia or specific damaged organ is established.
Multiple congenital intestinal obstructions define the disorder; immunodeficiency belongs to a specific subtype and is not established across the umbrella.
Defining features are intestinal pseudo-obstruction, natal teeth and patent ductus arteriosus; teeth and intestine share the gastrointestinal axis.
Raised intracranial pressure and diagnostic optic-disc edema define IIH. Papilledema is a major criterion; visual loss occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: sustained papilledema is optic-nerve involvement and a major diagnostic criterion; the 5-29% frequency of visual loss does not negate this defining feature.

basis: Inherited ATP8B1 lipid/bile transport disorder causes recurrent hepatic cholestasis. Hearing loss and pancreatitis lack qualifying frequencies; jaundice and pruritus do not establish eye or skin damage.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine as primary: BRIC1 is an inherited lipid/bile transport disorder within the inborn metabolic cholestasis spectrum. The hepatic primary axis remains appropriate.

basis: Brain malformations/developmental impairment and coloboma/ptosis define the syndrome. Sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in roughly 30-40%; cardiac defects are less common.

decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment affects approximately 30-40% over the usual course and represents lasting auditory dysfunction.

basis: Congenital gastrointestinal B12-binding protein deficiency causes cobalamin malabsorption and megaloblastic anemia; neurologic damage has no established qualifying frequency.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: absent gastric intrinsic factor is a defining gastrointestinal secretory defect causing cobalamin malabsorption.

basis: Inherited slow acetylation is a xenobiotic metabolic phenotype; it does not itself establish damage to another organ.
Microtia and aortic/cardiac malformations define the syndrome; CNS malformations/developmental impairment and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: hydrocephalus, posterior fossa abnormalities and developmental impairment occur in 30-79%; ear and aortic abnormalities define the core syndrome.

basis: Hereditary selective loss of smell for isovaleric acid; olfactory function belongs to the neurologic axis.
Organic acid metabolism disorder; developmental delay 80-99% and intellectual disability/seizures 30-79% support neurologic injury. Pancreatitis 5-29%; renal disease rare.
The supplied definition specifies apple-peel atresia with deficient mesenteric arterial supply; persistent vascular malformation is integral and annotated at 30-79%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: the defined apple-peel form has persistent deficient mesenteric arterial anatomy, not merely a hypothesized past trigger; vascular abnormalities occur in 30-79%.

basis: Defining triad comprises intestinal atresia, microcephaly and ocular malformations; renal/cardiac involvement lacks established frequency of at least 30%.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining chronic cutaneous disease. Bronchiectasis affects 57/135 (~42%) but is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent respiratory infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis (~42%) is separately diagnosed secondary disease; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic pulmonary involvement.

basis: Pancreatic/dental disease and deafness define JBS; intellectual disability 30-79%, alopecia 80-99%. Lacrimal defects 30-79% omitted by cap; hepatic reports sparse.
Brain, retinal and renal disease define this subtype; hepatic fibrosis in 5/5 and cirrhosis in 3/4. Anemia (5/5) omitted because of the cap.
Pathological exaggerated startle with involuntary motor responses supports neurologic classification; its cultural and behavioral basis remains debated.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; olfactory bulb aplasia in 4/6 and hyposmia in 5/10 establish common neurologic loss of function. Renal and hearing abnormalities lack qualifying frequency.
Intellectual disability and intestinal/cardiac anomalies define the syndrome. Coloboma and microphthalmia occur in 80-99%; ocular involvement follows the three definition-based primaries.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac anomalies are explicitly defining; individual lesion frequencies of 5-29% do not measure their combined frequency.
decisions.ocular: involved: structural coloboma and microphthalmia occur in 80-99%; the three primary slots prioritize organs explicitly named in the definition.

basis: Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; chronic middle-ear disease/hearing loss affects most (>50%). Recurrent infections are secondary.
Developmental disability and ocular malformations define disease; respiratory failure is annotated at 80-99%. Thin skin and sparse hair lack documented functional impairment.

decisions.dermatologic: none: thin skin and sparse hair occur in 4/4, but these descriptive anomalies do not establish skin damage or functional loss.

basis: Defining congenital hypoparathyroidism and skeletal dysplasia; microcephaly occurs in 30-79%. Hypocalcemic seizures alone do not establish brain damage; caries is separate.

decisions.neurologic: involved: microcephaly is a structural neurodevelopmental abnormality reported in 30-79%; the label does not rely on transient hypocalcemic seizures.

basis: Keratoconus and congenital hip dysplasia are the defining corneal and skeletal abnormalities.
Posterior corneal ectasia and opacity define the disorder; associated skeletal and developmental abnormalities have unspecified frequencies and no established diagnostic status.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental delay is reported without frequency; neither occurrence in approximately 30% nor status as a major diagnostic criterion is established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: reported skeletal anomalies lack frequencies or established major diagnostic status sufficient to label this entire concept.

basis: Isolated inherited diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma without associated systemic manifestations.

Destructive periodontitis and intrinsic neutrophil dysfunction define PLS; keratoderma/nail disease occurs in 80-99%, placed in involved under the primary cap. No systemic metabolic injury established.
audit_reason: Add primary haematologic for the intrinsic functional neutrophil disorder. Move dermatologic to involved to respect the three-primary cap; keratoderma and nail abnormalities occur in 80-99%.

basis: CTSC deficiency impairs neutrophil antimicrobial function; periodontitis and keratoderma define the syndrome; destructive acroosteolysis occurs in 30-79%.
audit_reason: Replace metabolic_endocrine with infectious_immune: CTSC deficiency impairs neutrophil antimicrobial function. Lysosomal localization alone does not establish a metabolic disorder. Common destructive skeletal involvement remains supported.

basis: Ketone-utilization defect causes recurrent ketoacidosis; vomiting, tachypnea and ketonuria do not establish organ damage. Cardiomegaly and coma occur in <30%.
Neurodegeneration, deafness and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism define syndrome; distal amyotrophy represents muscle wasting in 80-99%.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to involved: distal amyotrophy is actual muscle wasting, reported in 80-99%, and is part of the syndrome rather than an isolated symptom or separate disease.

basis: Skeletal/cartilage defects and pulmonary artery stenoses define it; airway abnormalities 80-99%, hearing loss 12/17 (~71%). Developmental delay 10/17 (~59%) omitted by cap.
The syndrome is defined by skeletal dysplasia and ectopia lentis; pursed lips alone do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Familial seizure disorder with intellectual disability; transient psychotic episodes add no organ axis.
Severe skeletal dysplasia; atrial septal defect and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%. A narrow skeletal thorax alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Lysosomal disease damages CNS and peripheral myelin; visual and sensorineural hearing impairment each occur in 80-99%; feeding symptoms do not establish gut damage.
Metabolic skeletal myopathy with exertional rhabdomyolysis; erythrocyte transport findings do not establish blood-cell disease.
Pyruvate metabolism defect with defining neurologic dysfunction; retinal degeneration is annotated in 30-79%, supporting direct ocular involvement.
PDHX-related metabolic enzyme deficiency defined by lactic acidosis and neurologic dysfunction; seizures, spasticity and callosal abnormalities occur in 30–79%.
Metabolic encephalomyopathy; hepatic steatosis and transaminase elevation occur in 30-79%. Hearing impairment reported in 1/1 is omitted under cap.
Inherited D-lactate metabolism defect; urinary lactate does not indicate renal injury. Frequencies of neurologic and ocular abnormalities are unestablished; gout is separate.
Intrinsic neutrophil granule and bactericidal defect causing primary immunodeficiency.
Bile-duct paucity, intellectual disability and meatal atresia define syndrome; clubfeet are major diagnostic defects. VSD and low immunoglobulins (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: VSD occurs in 30-79% and qualifies, but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of defining hepatic, neurologic, otologic and skeletal defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: clubfeet are explicitly defining structural defects, meeting the major-diagnostic-feature exception without a numerical frequency.
decisions.otologic: primary: external auditory meatal atresia is part of the defining branchial dysplasia, establishing structural ear involvement.

basis: Epileptic encephalopathy with acquired language loss and auditory verbal agnosia; impaired recognition is cerebral rather than otologic.
Proteoglycan glycosylation disorder with skeletal dysplasia and characteristic congenital cardiac defects; blue sclerae alone do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Multiple joint dislocations and respiratory insufficiency from tracheomalacia or lung hypoplasia define the syndrome; brain abnormalities occur only in some.
Skin/nail, upper airway and conjunctival granulation define disease; enamel hypoplasia 6/6 and oral blisters 30-79% support gastrointestinal involvement.
Neuropathy, pituitary dysfunction and chorioretinal dystrophy define it. Renal insufficiency 30-79%; hearing loss 30-79% and frequent digital anomalies omitted by cap.
Complete LCAT deficiency with defining hemolytic anemia and corneal dystrophy; renal lipid deposition causes proteinuria in most. Renal retained as fourth axis under primary cap.

decisions.haematologic: primary: hemolytic anemia is a defining component of complete LCAT deficiency.
decisions.renal: involved: renal lipid deposition causes proteinuric nephropathy in most, with progressive renal failure; assigned here because primary is capped at three.

basis: Limb malformation and cataract with optic nerve dysplasia define the syndrome; anal atresia occurs in 30-79%.
Insulin resistance; cardiomyopathy and cholestasis 3/3; lipoatrophy/hyperkeratosis 80-99%. Neurologic and muscle findings (30-79%) and renal findings omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental disability occurs in 30-79%, but more frequent cardiac, hepatic and cutaneous disease exhaust the four-organ cap.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous fat loss and hyperkeratosis occur in 80-99%, establishing persistent cutaneous involvement.

basis: Disseminated histiocytic neoplasm with defining marrow/splenic, skin and hepatic infiltration; destructive bone lesions are common (~50% or more). Other sites excluded by cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly and possible jaundice is explicitly part of this disseminated disease's definition.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: infiltrative skin lesions are a defining presentation of Letterer-Siwe disease, rather than a transient rash.

basis: Ketogenesis/leucine defect; hepatic injury in 14/20 (70%), developmental delay in 17/35 (~49%), and anemia/coagulation abnormalities annotated frequent (30-79%).

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia is annotated frequent (30-79%), supported by frequent coagulation abnormalities; these are manifestations of metabolic decompensation.

basis: Acute myeloid leukemia, colonic polyposis and colon cancer define the syndrome; unspecified genitourinary abnormalities do not establish another axis.
Skin/hair abnormalities, hypodontia and intellectual disability define syndrome; delayed puberty in 80-99% supports endocrine involvement. Kidney stones are separately coded disease.
Constitutional neutropenia, immunoglobulin deficiency with recurrent infections, and osteoporosis/fractures with bone anomalies define the syndrome.
Severe intellectual disability, spastic paraplegia and structural limb defects are defining manifestations.
Limb/jaw and mouth malformations define disease; renal dysfunction and intellectual disability 30-79%; hearing loss and myopia (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Fibular aplasia, tibial bowing and digit reduction define FATCO; cardiac abnormalities are not established as common.
Combined lipase deficiency disrupts lipid metabolism; subcutaneous fat loss reported in 1/1 patient supports skin involvement. Pancreatitis is a separate diagnosis.
Defective intestinal lipid export causes malabsorption; retinopathy 80-99%; hepatic enzyme injury 80-99% with lipid accumulation 30-79%; neurologic damage rare.
Metabolic deficiency with defining neurologic and hepatic presentations; developmental delay 80-99%, hepatic encephalopathy 30-79%. Cardiomyopathy occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.hepatic: primary: liver disease is explicitly a defining presentation, supported by hepatomegaly and hepatic encephalopathy at 30-79%; it is not merely a later risk.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment and later-onset neurologic dysfunction explicitly define presentations; neurodevelopmental delay occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Defining hyaline infiltration affects skin, larynx and oral mucosa. Dystonia is reported in 30-79%, supporting neurologic dysfunction; calcification alone would not qualify.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: characteristic early hoarseness reflects direct laryngeal infiltration; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal and gingival infiltration with tongue nodules is a defining mucocutaneous manifestation.
decisions.neurologic: involved: dystonia is annotated as frequent (30-79%), supporting functional CNS involvement rather than asymptomatic calcification alone.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the historical lipid-metabolism classification is misleading; ECM1-related extracellular matrix deposition is not an established metabolic or endocrine defect.

basis: Lissencephaly defines disease. Clinodactyly in 10/24 is minor dysmorphism without established dysfunction; specific cardiac malformations occur in 6/27 despite a broader frequent annotation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: clinodactyly in 10/24 does not establish functional skeletal damage; hand contractures occur in 6/27, below 30%.

basis: Hypoparathyroidism, nephropathy and mitral prolapse define syndrome; skin/nail dysfunction 80-99%. Skeletal defects (80-99%) and cataracts (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Immune deficiency defined by chronic Candida infection of skin, nails and mucosa, particularly oral mucosa.
Intrinsic immune defect causing chronic Candida infection of skin, nails and oral mucosa; nonspecific metabolic annotation does not establish metabolic disease.
Immune-mediated lymphoplasmacytic infiltration damages lung interstitium; eczema and systemic autoimmune diseases are associated conditions, not direct spread of LIP.
Progressive lymphoid-system deterioration indicates immunodeficiency; the sparse record does not establish specific blood-cell abnormalities or other organ damage.
Acute lymphoblastic leukemia with an explicit lymphomatous component; no additional organ damage meeting the threshold is documented.
Immune deficiency with chronic Candida infection of skin, nails and mucosa, including oral mucosa; nonspecific metabolic annotation adds no endocrine diagnosis.
Antibody deficiency, lymphopenia, autoimmune hemolytic anemia and glomerulonephritis define the syndrome. Pneumonia is a secondary infection.
Inherited lysine transport disorder involving intestinal absorption and renal tubular reabsorption; intellectual disability frequency is unspecified, so neurologic involvement is not established.
Microcephaly, seizures and developmental disability define disease; finger contractures/brachydactyly and hydronephrosis are frequent (30-79%). Genital hypoplasia has no axis.
Patellar subluxation in 2/2; myopia in 2/2 and strabismus in 1/2. Nephrolithiasis and celiac disease are separately diagnosed conditions.
Syndrome defined by epiphyseal dysplasia, osteoporosis and abnormal wrinkled skin; no other organ involvement established.
Name indicates congenital adiposity with excessive growth; absent definition and phenotype data limit certainty and do not support additional organs.
Microphthalmia, hepatomegaly and cleft palate characterize the syndrome; respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79%; cranial skeletal anomalies omitted at cap.
Defined by renal magnesium wasting, hypomagnesemia, nephrocalcinosis and severe structural retinal abnormalities.
Progressive inherited retinal dystrophy causing severe visual loss; developmental and gait abnormalities are occasional.
Renal Mg wasting, nephrocalcinosis and renal failure define disease; enamel defects in 4/6 and amelogenesis imperfecta in 5/6 support dental involvement.
Record supports an inherited magnesium-homeostasis abnormality; elevated red-cell magnesium alone does not establish blood-cell damage.
Palmoplantar keratoderma defines the disease; flexion contractures and autoamputation are reported in 30-79%, producing lasting digit and locomotor impairment.
Blepharophimosis 6/7 and oral clefts 3/7; abdominal muscle-wall defect, diastasis recti, 3/7; radioulnar synostosis 2/7 and developmental delay 1/7 excluded.
Defining dental malocclusion maps to gastrointestinal. Short stature alone establishes neither skeletal pathology nor an endocrine disorder.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage; no skeletal dysplasia or other structural locomotor abnormality is supplied.

basis: Organic acid metabolism defect; intellectual disability 5/6 and developmental impairment very frequent; dilated cardiomyopathy 5/9.
Defining osteolysis, lipodystrophy and frequent skin atrophy; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury, nor dental crowding intrinsic tooth damage.
Mandibulofacial dysostosis, ear abnormalities and lower eyelid coloboma define the phenotype. Cleft palate occurs in 1/2 annotated patients, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.

decisions.ocular: primary: lower eyelid coloboma is a characteristic diagnostic malformation of Treacher Collins syndrome, present in 2/3 annotated patients.

basis: Mandibulofacial skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability define the disease.
Defining eyelid coloboma, abnormal hair pattern and anorectal malformations; developmental delay occurs in only 1/10.
Lysosomal storage with immunodeficiency and neurodevelopmental damage; hearing loss 80-99%; skeletal dysplasia and ocular disease also 80-99%, omitted at cap.
Lysosomal disease defined by developmental impairment and hearing loss; abdominal muscle hypoplasia is annotated in 80-99%. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay is explicitly defining; intellectual disability and very frequent seizures reinforce neurologic disease.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing loss is explicitly defining and annotated as very frequent (80-99%).

basis: Branched-chain amino acid metabolism defect; neurotoxicity with seizures and developmental impairment in 80-99%. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish lung injury.
Contractures, muscle hypoplasia, blepharophimosis and palatal defects define syndrome. Neurodevelopmental impairment and microcephaly occur in 80-99%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: palatal clefts are explicitly defining structural oral abnormalities; submucous cleft palate occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay, learning disability and microcephaly occur in 80-99%; three primary slots retain defining musculoskeletal, eyelid and palatal disease.

basis: Microcephaly/intellectual disability, glomerulonephritis/CKD and marfanoid skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome.
Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; cardiac abnormalities are occasional.
Cerebellar ataxia, cataracts and myopathy define the syndrome; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism occurs in 19/21 annotated patients.
Progressive central motor and cognitive degeneration. Dysphagia (9/14) and weakness reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct gut or skeletal muscle disease.
Skin mastocytosis, hearing loss and microcephaly define syndrome; optic atrophy 80-99%; scoliosis 2/3 and contractures omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: none: mastocytosis is cutaneous; blood-cell, marrow or coagulation dysfunction is not established.
decisions.neurologic: primary: microcephaly is defining and present in 3/3; intellectual disability occurs in 2/3.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic atrophy is annotated in 80-99% and represents direct visual-system damage.

basis: Intellectual disability, congenital heart defects and skeletal/muscle malformations define the syndrome; strabismus 80-99% and ptosis 30-79%. Dental abnormalities omitted at cap.
Cystic renal dysplasia, encephalocele and polydactyly define Meckel syndrome; hepatic ductal plate malformation with congenital fibrosis occurs in most.
Autoinflammatory disease with defining recurrent peritonitis (94%); inflammatory pleuritis occurs in 47% and arthritis in 39%. Renal amyloidosis is a minority complication.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: recurrent inflammatory peritonitis is a major diagnostic manifestation, documented in 164/175 (~94%); this is serosal inflammation rather than abdominal pain alone.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia with enlarged epiphyses and severe short stature; lens subluxation and cleft palate have no established frequency or major-criterion status in the supplied evidence.

decisions.ocular: none: lens subluxation is reported, but its frequency and status as a major diagnostic criterion are not established.

basis: Cerebral enlargement and dysmyelination with seizures, ataxia and spasticity define a brain disorder.
Defining anemia, diabetes and sensorineural deafness; optic atrophy frequent (30-79%). Cardiac and other neurologic damage are occasional.
Congenital enlargement of the cornea; an ocular disorder.
Megalocornea and intellectual disability define syndrome; scoliosis/kyphosis 30-79%; immune annotation nonspecific; retinal detachment 20%.
CNS melanocytic proliferation and congenital cutaneous nevi define disease; damaging ocular abnormalities are occasional, while papilledema alone does not establish visual damage.
Skeletal anomalies, megalocornea and developmental delay define syndrome; mitral prolapse occurs in 80-99%; skin thickening in 80-99% omitted because of the four-axis cap.
PRSS12-related nonsyndromic intellectual disability, severe in 5/5 patients; ocular findings lack qualifying frequencies.
Intellectual disability and epilepsy accompany defining hypogonadism and diabetes; muscle atrophy is occasional and facial dysmorphism does not establish another damaged organ.
Corneal opacity, elbow contractures with forearm bone abnormalities, and intellectual/developmental impairment are defining, very frequent features.
Defining eye, cognitive, hearing and dental defects; dental hypoplasia 80-99%. Cap omits renal proteinuria (80-99%)/bladder defects (30-79%) and cardiac septal defects (30-79%).

decisions.renal: none under the four-axis cap: proteinuria is annotated 80-99% and bladder diverticula 30-79%; defining dental malformations take the remaining slot.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental hypoplasia is a defining structural defect affecting 80-99%; placed here because primary is limited to three axes.

basis: Septal and skeletal/bone-density abnormalities in 80-99%; hydronephrosis in 30-79%. Common dental and nail/hair abnormalities omitted by four-axis cap.
Inherited metabolic encephalopathy; skeletal abnormalities and strabismus each occur in 30-79%; dry skin alone does not establish substantial skin damage.
Mesoaxial polydactyly and congenital cardiac malformations define the syndrome; intellectual disability has no supplied frequency supporting additional involvement.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by severe limb shortening and abnormalities of long bones and joints.
Limb dysplasia, contractures and cleft palate define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Skin dimples do not establish skin damage.
Saposin B deficiency causes sphingolipid storage with central and peripheral demyelination; weakness reflects neuropathy.
Sulfatide storage causes central and peripheral demyelination; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%; hearing loss and cholecystitis are <30%.
Metaphyseal and epiphyseal skeletal dysplasia; developmental delay and alopecia occur in some cases without an established frequency of at least 30%.
Skeletal dysplasia with inherited glutathione metabolism defect; AV block/arrhythmia 80-99%, cerebellar hypoplasia 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency may reflect thoracic restriction.
Defined by metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia, scoliosis and structural tracheobronchomalacia.
Skeletal dysplasia, hypotrichosis and immunodeficiency define CHH; neutropenia annotated 80-99%. Ocular and cardiopulmonary annotations omitted under the four-axis cap.
Metaphyseal chondrodysplasia establishes skeletal disease; the nonspecific metabolism/homeostasis annotation does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia; associated structural dentition abnormalities are frequent (30–79%), supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Skeletal dysplasia and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; developmental delay/intellectual disability occur in 30-79%; renal, cardiac and skin findings are below 30%.
Defining metaphyseal dysplasia, intellectual disability and conductive hearing loss; ocular abnormalities occur only in 5-29%.
The defining triad directly affects metaphyseal bone, dermal elastic tissue and optic nerves.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia with short bones; this subtype lacks documented hair abnormalities or immunodeficiency.
The defining phenotype combines metaphyseal bone abnormalities, skin lesions and spastic paraplegia.
Organic aciduria defined by progressive neurodegeneration; strabismus and vertebral abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. A single cardiac report does not establish common involvement.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus is annotated frequent (30-79%) and represents persistent impairment of ocular alignment and binocular function.

basis: Defective erythrocyte methemoglobin reduction defines a blood disorder; generalized metabolic or neurologic disease is not established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: a blood-cell reductase deficiency does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.

basis: Cytochrome b5 deficiency causes methemoglobinemia and impaired androgen steroidogenesis; low DHEAS and elevated LH were documented in 1/1.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: impaired androgen steroidogenesis is an intrinsic biochemical defect of cytochrome b5 deficiency, supported by low DHEAS and elevated LH in 1/1.

basis: Inherited redox-enzyme deficiency impairs hemoglobin function. Neurologic injury occurs mainly in minority generalized type II (<30% overall); the 1/1 HPO sample does not represent both types.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: methemoglobin reductase deficiency is an inborn disorder of enzymatic redox metabolism, as well as a blood disorder.

basis: Methionine metabolism defect is usually benign; neurologic injury is rare and intellectual disability <30%; hepatic enzyme localization is not liver damage.
Intestinal methionine transport disorder; intellectual disability and seizures are characteristic neurologic manifestations, although frequencies are unspecified.
Cobalamin remethylation defect with megaloblastic anemia; developmental impairment is common and seizures occur in ~50%; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Inborn leucine metabolism defect; white matter abnormalities in 4/6 and developmental delay in 30-79% support neurologic damage. Optic atrophy is only 1/10.
Organic aciduria with developmental disability, seizures and spasticity in 80-99%; hepatic, cardiac, hearing, ocular and platelet abnormalities are each only occasional.
Organic aciduria with developmental/intellectual impairment in 30-79%. Cytopenias are typically reversible during crises; renal insufficiency is annotated 5-29%; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: none: leukopenia is annotated 30-79%, but typically reflects reversible marrow suppression during metabolic crises rather than lasting haematologic damage.

basis: MMAA-related cobalamin-processing disorder causes organic acidemia. Persistent neurologic injury is not established at >=30% in this responsive subtype; acute hypotonia alone is insufficient.

decisions.neurologic: none: supplied phenotypes lack evidence of persistent neurologic injury in >=30%; acute metabolic encephalopathy or hypotonia does not establish lasting damage.

basis: Cobalamin metabolic defect; developmental neurologic injury commonly exceeds 30%, and CKD affects roughly half or more in cblB disease; cardiomyopathy reported in one patient is insufficient.
MCEE deficiency causes methylmalonic acid accumulation and possible acidosis. Neurological findings in isolated reports do not establish damage in at least 30%.
Skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly/ID and immunodeficiency define syndrome; cataracts 80-99%; enamel hypoplasia 80-99% and neutropenia 30-79% omitted by cap.
Primary microcephaly and intellectual disability affect brain development; short stature is uncommon.
Severe intellectual disability, microcephaly and dilated cardiomyopathy define syndrome; minor ear and digit shapes do not establish functional organ damage.
Microcephaly and severe limb reduction define the syndrome. Pulmonary hypoplasia is reported, but neither a frequency of at least 30% nor diagnostic-criterion status is established.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary hypoplasia is reported without frequency; the supplied evidence does not establish occurrence in at least 30% or its status as a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Developmental impairment and immunodeficiency; skeletal dysplasia/contractures and hypogonadism each 30-79%. Panniculitis (30-79%) omitted at cap; ocular disease 5-29%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: panniculitis occurs in 30-79% but is omitted at the four-axis cap, prioritizing persistent skeletal abnormalities and gonadal endocrine dysfunction.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypogonadism occurs in 30-79% and represents direct loss of gonadal endocrine function.

basis: Microcephaly, intellectual disability and cervical fusion define disease; ptosis occurs in 30–79%. Unspecified ureter, reticulocyte and dental morphology do not establish functional damage.
audit_reason: Remove renal: an unspecified ureter abnormality at 30–79% establishes frequency but does not establish direct damage or impaired function required for involved. Persistent frequent ptosis supports ocular involvement.

basis: Microcephaly, intellectual disability and digital skeletal malformations define the syndrome; congenital absence of nails occurs in 7/7 patients.
Immunodeficiency and microcephaly define NBS. Anal malformations are rare despite suspect HPO frequencies; malignancies and autoimmune cytopenias are separate diseases.
audit_reason: Remove gastrointestinal: anal atresia and stenosis are rare associations of Nijmegen breakage syndrome. The supplied 80-99% annotations conflict with its established phenotype and do not establish the required common involvement.

basis: Microcephaly and chorioretinal disease define syndrome; scoliosis is annotated in 30-79%.
Brain malformation with microcephaly, epilepsy and spastic quadriplegia; visual impairment in 3/3 does not establish damage to the eye itself.
Congenital cerebral calcification, microcephaly, seizures and developmental impairment; resembles infection but has no established infectious cause.
Nephrotic disease and CNS malformations define the syndrome; congenital hiatal hernia is a recognized syndromic structural abnormality in 30-79%.
Skeletal dysplasia with joint abnormalities defines disease; intellectual disability occurs in 3/4. Neonatal respiratory distress in 3/9 does not establish lasting pulmonary damage.
Isolated ocular malformation with coloboma in 185/196 and microcornea in 155/196 patients.
Isolated congenital eye underdevelopment, including microphthalmia or anophthalmia.
Defined by structural eye abnormalities with retinal degeneration and dental anomalies; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Developmental lens and corneal disease with ectopia lentis and possible glaucoma; extraocular abnormalities are occasional.
External and middle ear malformations with meatal atresia and conductive hearing loss define the disorder.
Intestinal epithelial disease causing severe secretory diarrhea; frequent renal findings may reflect dehydration or parenteral nutrition, and nephrocalcinosis is separately coded.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder of hepatocerebral type; liver failure in 19/19 and characteristic encephalopathy/cerebral injury.
Skeletal myopathy caused by an inborn mitochondrial metabolic defect; additional organs vary across the many subtypes.
Inherited mitochondrial protein-transport defect causing skeletal myopathy, weakness and exercise intolerance; no additional organ damage established.
Oral malformations and limb skeletal defects define OFD2; conductive hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Neurologic malformations are occasional.
Inborn cofactor deficiency with defining destructive encephalopathy; lens dislocation and renal stones are not established as common.
Molybdenum cofactor deficiency causes destructive encephalopathy with seizures and cerebral atrophy; lens displacement and renal stones lack qualifying frequency evidence.
Monocyte immune dysfunction causes chronic Candida infection of skin, nails and mucosa, particularly oral mucosa.
Marrow myelodysplasia with monosomy 7 and frequent AML; no defining extrahematologic organ damage is documented.
Morquio-type mucopolysaccharidosis is a storage disorder with defining skeletal dysplasia; subtype-specific evidence for other commonly damaged organs is lacking.
Motor/autonomic neuropathy with defining esophageal achalasia; denervation muscle atrophy and joint stiffness occur in 80-99%. Sweating and acrocyanosis do not establish skin injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: esophageal achalasia is an explicit defining component, with persistent organ dysfunction in 80-99%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal muscle atrophy and joint stiffness occur in 80-99%, documenting structural locomotor injury beyond weakness alone.

basis: Occlusive cerebral arteriopathy defines disease. Stroke may occur in >30% but is separately diagnosed; transient ischemic symptoms alone do not establish lasting brain damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke may affect >30% but is a separately diagnosed complication; arterial occlusion and transient ischemic symptoms alone do not establish brain damage.

basis: Lysosomal disease with defining skeletal and developmental impairment; valve dysfunction 80-99%. Skin/gingiva (80-99%) and airway/hearing disease (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is explicitly defining; global developmental delay occurs in 7/9 and cognitive impairment in 30-79%.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining skeletal and joint disease; myopia occurs in 3/3. Functionally significant cardiac involvement is not established in >=30%; retinitis pigmentosa is rare.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac complications are rarely clinically significant ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK24701/)); common valve thickening alone is insufficient.

basis: Lysosomal disease defined by neurodevelopmental and visual impairment; achlorhydria occurs in nearly all; abdominal muscle hypoplasia omitted under the cap.
Lysosomal storage with defining neurodegeneration; hearing impairment affects 27/73 (~37%). Diarrhea in 59/72 alone does not establish intestinal injury; skeletal damage frequency is uncertain.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea affects 59/72 (~82%), but the evidence does not establish direct intestinal injury or persistent intestinal loss of function rather than a symptom.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining neurodegeneration; dysostosis multiplex 16/16 and hearing impairment in roughly half. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.

decisions.otologic: involved: conductive and/or sensorineural hearing impairment affects roughly half over the usual course, exceeding 30%; it is part of the storage disorder.

basis: Lysosomal storage with neurodevelopmental decline; hearing impairment 5/11 (~45%). Dysphagia 4/11 may be neurogenic; documented skeletal abnormalities are <30%.
Lysosomal storage with defining neurodegeneration; contractures 2/3 and hearing impairment 1/3. Mitral regurgitation 1/3 omitted by cap; small series.
Lysosomal storage with defining skeletal and spinal cord deficits; obstructive airway disease affects >30%; ocular, hearing and valve disease omitted by cap.
Lysosomal storage disorder defined by skeletal dysplasia; mitral regurgitation 5/9 and corneal opacity 3/9 support involvement; neurologic findings reported in <30%.
Storage disorder defined by dysostosis/contractures and corneal clouding (28/28 each); valve damage in 27/28 (~96%). Cap omits common airway, ear and skin involvement.

decisions.ocular: primary: corneal stromal clouding is a defining MPS VI feature, present in 28/28, with direct visual impairment.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic dysostosis multiplex and progressive joint contractures define the phenotype; contractures occur in 28/28.

basis: Storage disease with defining dysostosis (26/29); intellectual disability and corneal opacity each 80-99%. Airway/pleural involvement omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone lacks dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal dysplasia is a defining component, supported by the skeletal-involvement parent, dysostosis in 26/29 and joint restriction in 22/26.

basis: Inspissated mucus obstructs the respiratory tract.
Peroxisomal growth disorder with muscle hypoplasia and pericardial constriction; hepatic involvement is common (37/42 hepatomegaly), with associated fibrosis.
