Neurologic dysfunction ~70%; optic atrophy 17/31; sensorineural hearing loss 30-79%. Alopecia/skin disease ~70-77% omitted at cap in favor of severe sensory injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none at cap: alopecia affects 24/31 and rash 21/31; irreversible neurologic, visual and auditory injury take priority.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 30-79% and may persist despite treatment; retained for its severity.

basis: Biotin-dependent carboxylase deficiency; seizures, perioral eczema and keratoconjunctivitis each reported in 80-99%.
Inborn O-glycosylation disorder with defining muscular dystrophy and brain malformations. Retinal dysplasia occurs in 20/20; ocular disease is placed in involved because of the primary cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: defining structural eye disease, including retinal dysplasia in 20/20; the three-primary cap places ocular involvement here.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an inborn disorder of protein O-glycosylation, so the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Contractures, skeletal defects and skin webs define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia is common (>30%) in the lethal form; cardiac defect frequency uncertain.
Severe infantile motor-neuron degeneration with defining progressive muscle weakness and atrophy; respiratory failure reflects muscle denervation rather than primary lung damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: severe progressive skeletal muscle weakness and atrophy define this SMA subtype and occur in essentially all patients.

basis: Defining fetal akinesia and contractures accompany anterior horn neuron loss, severe muscle hypoplasia and pulmonary hypoplasia (80-99%).
Intellectual disability, congenital myopathy and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; myopia, ptosis and ophthalmoparesis occur in 80-99%.
Spinal and brainstem motor-neuron degeneration; denervation causes skeletal muscle wasting and loss of function in nearly all patients.
Lower motor neuron degeneration; denervation causes skeletal muscle atrophy in nearly all patients. Respiratory weakness does not establish direct lung damage.
Muscular dystrophy and cerebral white-matter disease define the syndrome; seizures and ataxia support neurologic involvement.
Progressive skeletal muscle dystrophy with weakness, atrophy and contractures; cardiac involvement is explicitly absent.
Dysferlin-related skeletal muscle dystrophy. Cardiac findings are occasional (5-29%); respiratory involvement is excluded by the definition.
Progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy; right ventricular hypertrophy reported in 30-79%. Restrictive ventilation reflects respiratory muscle weakness, not lung damage.
Congenital muscle-brain-eye dystroglycanopathy; myopia occurs in 30-79%, with other structural eye anomalies variably present; cardiomyopathy is occasional.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with multiple joint contractures; neuromuscular ancestry alone does not establish nervous tissue disease.
The defining triad is congenital muscular dystrophy, infantile cataract and hypogonadism; skeletal muscle disease does not itself establish neurologic damage.
Collagen VI muscular dystrophy causes muscle degeneration, contractures and scoliosis; hypoventilation reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Congenital muscular dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle; the supplied evidence does not establish intrinsic nerve or brain disease.
Progressive skeletal muscle dystrophy; paresthesia alone does not establish peripheral nerve damage, and respiratory muscle weakness is muscular.
Lethal hypertonia with hypokinesia and dyskinesia supports neurologic motor dysfunction; respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Primary muscular dystrophy causing distal skeletal muscle weakness and atrophy; no established common damage to other axes.
Inherited selective inability to perceive musk is an olfactory functional deficit; unspecified blindness lacks evidence of common involvement.
Inherited neuromuscular junction dysfunction; weakness, ptosis and ophthalmoplegia do not establish separate primary muscle or ocular injury.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction disease; ocular and bulbar weakness are neurologic. Myositis is a separate overlap disorder; respiratory failure occurs in 5-29%.
Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder; apnea, bulbar weakness and ophthalmoparesis reflect transmission failure rather than direct lung or eye damage.
DOK7-related postsynaptic NMJ disease; structural muscle involvement includes tongue atrophy in 4/10 (40%). Ptosis and reduced vital capacity reflect neuromuscular weakness.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: tongue atrophy in 4/10 (40%) establishes common structural muscle loss; the defining lesion is at the NMJ rather than a primary dystrophy.

basis: Cutaneous neoplasm of T lymphocytes and a lymphoma; marrow, splenic and hepatic involvement are each annotated at 5-29%.
Marrow fibrosis and clonal myeloproliferation; hepatic extramedullary hematopoietic infiltration with hepatomegaly is frequent (30-79%). Spleen is haematologic.
Marrow plasma-cell malignancy; destructive bone disease affects most patients, and direct paraprotein-associated kidney damage occurs in roughly 30% or more.
Functional neutrophil defect impairing antimicrobial activity; infection-related organ damage is not common enough to add another axis.
Inherited myeloproliferative neoplasm affecting myeloid blood cells and bone marrow.
Generalized epilepsy syndrome; nonspecific mouth and eye-movement annotations do not establish direct oral or ocular damage.
Glycogen metabolism disorder causing progressive epilepsy and neurological decline; hepatic failure occurs in 5-29%; aspiration pneumonia is a separate secondary disease.
Progressive myoclonic epilepsy with seizures, ataxia and variable cognitive decline directly affects the nervous system.
Progressive myoclonus epilepsy and primary glomerular disease define the syndrome; anemia and effusions can follow renal failure; other organ damage is not commonly established.
Intrinsic skeletal muscle disease with granulovacuolar pathology, atrophy, weakness and electrical myotonia.
Metabolic shuttle defect presenting as skeletal muscle disease; no additional organ involvement established.
Lipid metabolic myopathy directly affects skeletal muscle; respiratory weakness is muscular, while cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia occur in under 30%.
Fatty-acid oxidation defect with defining skeletal myopathy and frequent muscle-fibre atrophy; renal insufficiency 5/28 is below 30%.
Hepatic fatty-acid oxidation disorder; supplied phenotypes report neurologic dysfunction and muscle atrophy at 80-99%. Renal and cardiac lesions are occasional.
Metabolic skeletal myopathy; singleton cytopenia and ophthalmoparesis reports do not establish common involvement across ISCU disease.
Inherited myopathy establishes skeletal-muscle disease; abnormal mitochondrial morphology alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Skeletal myosin-storage myopathy; cardiomyopathy in 3/3 and heart failure in 2/3. Restrictive ventilation reflects muscle/skeletal dysfunction.
Centronuclear skeletal myopathy; ophthalmoplegia in 25% and respiratory insufficiency in 20% do not meet the involvement threshold.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy causing myotonia; cardiac abnormalities and dysphagia are very rare, not defining manifestations.
Structural skeletal-muscle myopathy; respiratory and swallowing impairment arise from muscle weakness, without established intrinsic lung or gastrointestinal damage.
Structural skeletal myopathy and defining external ophthalmoplegia; respiratory weakness reflects muscle disease, without established direct lung injury.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive disorder.
Collagen VI myopathy causes muscle fibrosis, weakness and contractures; reduced vital capacity can reflect respiratory muscle weakness.
Skeletal muscle chloride channelopathy causes myotonia, stiffness and weakness; no primary nerve or neuromuscular junction lesion.
Myotonia, skeletal dysplasia and profound intellectual disability define the syndrome; dysphagia reflects neuromuscular dysfunction without demonstrated gut damage.
Chondrodysplasia and defining neuromuscular junction hyperexcitability/myotonia; ocular involvement includes visual impairment 80-99% and cataract 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: defining neuromuscular hyperexcitability involves the neuromuscular junction, included in this axis; skeletal dysplasia and muscle involvement also remain primary.

basis: Severe hypothyroidism with characteristic myxedematous skin thickening from dermal glycosaminoglycan deposition; autoimmune causation is not universal.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic myxedematous skin thickening reflects dermal glycosaminoglycan deposition and forms part of this disease's defining phenotype.

basis: Cardiac myxoma is obligate; embolic and hepatic complications occur in fewer than 30%.
Skeletal anomalies and hearing loss define it; intellectual disability occurs in 8/10 and cardiac anomalies in 30-79%. Ptosis and nail defects (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Deafness, cataracts and skeletal/muscle abnormalities define the syndrome; arrhythmia occurs in 80-99%.
Myopathy, cleft palate and ptosis are defining features; ptosis and cleft palate occur in 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness; malignant hyperthermia is anesthesia-triggered.

decisions.ocular: primary: ptosis is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 30-79% (also 2/2 reported patients); eyelids are ocular.

basis: Mitochondrial encephalopathy; optic atrophy and cardiomyopathy each frequent (30-79%); frequent hearing loss omitted at four-axis cap.
Inherited glomerulopathy with progressive renal failure; common secondary hypertension is separately diagnosed. No defining nail or skeletal disease.
NEB-related skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Autoinflammatory dermatosis with inflammatory subcutaneous fat loss; myositis, muscle wasting and fixed contractures commonly affect at least ~30%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: inflammatory loss of subcutaneous fat supports dermatologic disease; lipodystrophy alone does not establish a common metabolic or endocrine disorder.

basis: Sulfate-transport metabolic bone dysplasia with cleft palate; pulmonary hypoplasia and structural airway disease occur in 30-79%.
Progressive renal tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis cause kidney failure; anemia is secondary to renal disease, not direct blood-cell damage.
Nephropathy, sensorineural deafness and parathyroid hyperplasia define the syndrome; bone cysts occur in 30-79%. Anemia is only occasional.
Nephrosis and urinary tract anomalies, deafness, and thumb/hallux skeletal malformations define the syndrome; corresponding anomalies are reported in 30-79%.
Congenital NPHS1-related glomerular filtration-barrier dysfunction causes protein loss and progressive renal damage; secondary lipid changes add no damaged organ.
WT1-associated nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis and frequent renal failure; gonadal tumors are uncommon.
ABCC8-related insulin excess causes persistent hypoglycemia; lasting neurodevelopmental impairment affects roughly 30-50% in severe congenital hyperinsulinism cohorts.
Skin/hair disease with immune dysfunction; isolated reports of gut, renal, hearing or CNS findings do not establish damage in >=30% of patients.
Serine synthesis defect with severe brain malformation and ichthyosis (2/3); limb contractures/deformities common (>=30%); ocular and cleft anomalies (~1/3) omitted by cap.
Lysosomal storage with defining dysostosis and ocular disease; intellectual disability/seizures ~80-99%. Hearing loss ~80-99% omitted by cap; hepatosplenomegaly <30%.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by developmental impairment and dysostosis; nephropathy occurs in 80-99%. Ocular damage and hearing loss, also 80-99%, omitted by cap.
Neurologic and acrorenal defects define syndrome; auditory canal atresia in 80-99%. Ocular disease and cardiovascular malformations omitted under four-axis cap.
Hereditary predisposition to sympathetic nervous system tumors; no additional organ damage inferred from susceptibility or possible tumor spread.
Neurologic impairment and skin/hair pigment abnormalities define disease. Persistent refractive dysfunction from myopia occurs in 30-79%; optic atrophy and macular dystrophy occur in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: involved: syndrome-associated myopia causes persistent ocular functional impairment in 30-79%; optic atrophy and macular dystrophy alone would fall below threshold.

basis: The concept explicitly identifies infantile neurologic disease and bone fragility; unspecified multisystem involvement cannot establish additional axes.
Lysosomal disorder with neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most classic cases (>30% overall); vascular deposits alone do not establish damage.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration causes progressive visual loss, reported in 2/2.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy with defining anhidrosis and frequent sweat-gland aplasia; fractures, osteomyelitis and oral injuries are secondary complications.
Hepatocerebral mitochondrial depletion defines metabolic, hepatic and neurologic disease. Retinopathy 2/2, hearing loss 1/1 and tubulopathy 1/1 do not establish >=30% disease-wide prevalence.

decisions.ocular: none: retinopathy in 2/2 selected reported patients does not establish >=30% prevalence across MPV17-related hepatocerebral disease; ocular disease is not a defining criterion.

basis: Sensory-autonomic neuropathy and spastic paraplegia define disease; skin ulcers occur in 80-99%. Muscle wasting is neurogenic; osteomyelitis occurs in 25%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy in 4/4 reflects denervation from neuropathy, without evidence of direct skeletal-muscle disease.

basis: Central/peripheral axonopathy; persistent tendon abnormalities 80-99% and skeletal deformities 30-79% support musculoskeletal involvement. Hair morphology lacks demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: pili canaliculi and woolly hair are characteristic morphology without demonstrated loss of hair or skin function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: tendon abnormalities occur in 80-99%, with persistent scoliosis and foot deformities in 30-79%, supporting structural involvement.

basis: Hereditary motor and sensory peripheral neuropathy with abnormal myelin folding.
Inherited sensory peripheral neuropathy causing sensory ataxia; definition excludes ulcerating acropathy and autonomic abnormalities.
Hereditary painful neuropathy is a peripheral nerve disorder; no additional organ injury is documented.
Severe congenital neutropenia causes a blood-cell deficiency and impaired innate immunity; eosinophilia is also hematologic.
Definition and parents describe dysplastic melanocytic nevi despite the conflicting name and HPO; melanoma is a later risk.
Storage disease defined by hepatic injury and neurodegeneration; lung infiltration 80-99%, respiratory failure 30-79%. Splenic/blood involvement omitted by cap; cherry-red spots alone do not qualify.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatosplenomegaly is defining, with hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases in 10/10; liver failure occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: rapidly progressive neurodegeneration defines type A; developmental regression/delay occurs in 10/10, not merely as an optional complication.

basis: Lysosomal lipid storage disorder; progressive neurologic damage in most and common hepatic disease, with hepatomegaly in 7/13. Splenic/marrow storage lacks established common functional impairment.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenomegaly in 4/13 and marrow histiocytosis demonstrate storage, but do not establish blood-organ dysfunction in at least 30%.

basis: GRM6-related retinal signaling dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness; no separate CNS disease is established.
Microcephaly in 9/9 and characteristic developmental impairment establish neurologic disease; individual cardiac and renal lesions are uncommon; cancer predisposition is a risk.
Lissencephaly, microcephaly and severe developmental impairment define the syndrome; retinal and cardiac abnormalities occur in <30%.
Cystic malformation/neoplasm of lymphatic vessels; classified under cardiovascular organ benign neoplasms.
Isolated congenital motor nystagmus impairs ocular fixation; the record does not establish additional neurologic disease.
Obesity with chronic alveolar hypoventilation and respiratory failure; associated sleep apnea and secondary cardiovascular diagnoses are assessed separately.
Central saccade-initiation disorder; ataxia 80-99% and cerebellar abnormalities 30-79%. Intrinsic eye damage is not established; strabismus is only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: impaired central initiation of saccades defines the disease; ataxia occurs in 80-99% and cerebellar malformations in 30-79%.
decisions.ocular: none: impaired gaze reflects central motor control rather than intrinsic eye disease; strabismus and nystagmus occur in only 5-29%.

basis: Myopathy localized to extraocular skeletal muscles; curare sensitivity alone does not establish a separate neurologic disorder.
Brain and ocular abnormalities define syndrome; hearing impairment and anemia each occur in 80-99%. Skin hypopigmentation and immune abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: hypochromic anemia occurs in 80-99%; retained over pigmentation changes because it represents greater functional impairment.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: generalized hypopigmentation occurs in 80-99%, but brain, ocular, hearing and blood abnormalities take priority by functional severity.

basis: Defining skin, eye and CNS abnormalities; anemia occurs in 30-79%. Dental/palatal and joint abnormalities also frequent but omitted under the four-axis cap.
Eye, tooth and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; developmental delay occurs in 1/2. Sparse hair (1/2) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Eye, palate and cerebral abnormalities define syndrome; nail aplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Asthma is separately diagnosed; joint laxity and small extremities do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: asthma, despite an 80-99% annotation, is a separately diagnosed airway disease; direct pulmonary involvement by this malformation syndrome is not established.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: nail aplasia/hypoplasia is direct structural loss of a cutaneous appendage, reported in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility, small hands and short feet (30-79%) do not by themselves establish skeletal injury or loss of function.

basis: Developmental disability, eyelid malformations and oral clefts characterize 3MC syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 5/6 assessed patients.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft lip/palate is a characteristic defining malformation, reported in 4/6; oral structures belong to gastrointestinal.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment represents functional ear damage in 5/6 assessed patients, beyond the defining craniofacial-developmental features.

basis: Retinitis pigmentosa, hair/nail dysplasia and dental anomalies define the syndrome; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Retinal/optic degeneration, progressive glomerulopathy and cerebellar impairment define the syndrome. Hypermobility alone does not establish joint damage; scoliosis is occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility in 80-99% does not itself establish damage or functional loss; scoliosis occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Skin, hair, nail and tooth dysplasia define disease. Photophobia in 3/10 does not establish ocular tissue damage.
OEIS defines bladder exstrophy, bowel/anorectal defects and spinal dysraphism. Associated structural hip, vertebral and limb abnormalities occur in 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: spinal dysraphism is a defining component of OEIS; frequent myelomeningocele confirms that the spinal defects include neural tissue.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: associated hip, vertebral and limb malformations occur in 30-79%; bladder, bowel and neural spinal defects occupy the three primary slots.

basis: Inherited retinal dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness; both supplied retinal features occur in 6/6 patients.
Isolated impaired sperm production and male infertility; no evidence of gonadal hormone dysfunction or another covered organ disorder.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy and postaxial polydactyly define the syndrome; oral, skin and ear anomalies are occasional or nondamaging.
Hereditary degeneration of the inferior olives, pons and cerebellum.
Skeletal dysplasia with limb shortening and elbow dislocation. Intellectual disability and cardiovascular malformations are occasional, below 30%.
Omphalocele and oral clefting define the syndrome; hydrocephalus in 1/3, annotated frequent. Uterine anomalies have no axis.
Hair/nail dysplasia and chronic neutropenia with recurrent infections define the syndrome; developmental and conjunctival findings lack reliable prevalence or diagnostic-criterion evidence.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental delay and mild ID are reported, but frequency is unspecified and neither >=30% prevalence nor major diagnostic-criterion status is established.

basis: Congenital ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, miosis and associated amblyopia define ocular dysfunction; no separate neurologic lesion is established.
Mitochondrial extraocular myopathy defines PEO; muscle pathology 2/2, ataxia/cerebellar atrophy 1/1. Hearing loss 1/1 omitted at cap; cardiomyopathy 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: PEO is an extraocular skeletal-muscle myopathy; ragged-red fibers in 2/2 and limb weakness support defining muscle disease.

basis: Muscle weakness and abnormal muscle mitochondria support myopathy; ophthalmoplegia and ptosis (20/20) define ocular dysfunction. Independent nerve damage is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: the unquantified cranial-nerve morphology annotation does not establish a defining neuropathy or common independent nerve damage beyond myopathic ophthalmoplegia.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; respiratory insufficiency 8/8, renal phosphate wasting 5/6 and hypophosphatemia 5/6 support additional axes. Proptosis alone is not ocular damage.
Hereditary optic nerve atrophy with visual impairment in 4/4; optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Organic aciduria defined by optic atrophy and choreoathetosis; optic atrophy 10/10 and movement abnormalities 80-99%.
Optic atrophy, hearing loss and peripheral neuropathy are the three defining manifestations.
Defining degeneration affects optic nerves, cochlea and CNS, with visual loss, deafness, spastic tetraplegia and mental deterioration.
Hereditary impairment of oral sensation and coordination; no evidence of structural oral tissue disease.
Ichthyosis, congenital mouth/lip abnormalities and digital anomalies form the defining triad. Oral structural abnormalities support primary localization without requiring secondary dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: congenital small mouth and lip malformations constitute the syndrome's defining oral component; the mouth is explicitly within the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Oral, ocular and digital anomalies define the syndrome; severe intellectual disability is also a defining feature, supporting neurologic involvement without a frequency estimate.
Oral and limb defects define OFD4; intellectual disability and airway malformations each 80-99%; hearing loss (80-99%) and eye movement abnormalities omitted by cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: choanal atresia and laryngomalacia are structural airway defects, each annotated 80-99%; severe airway compromise takes priority at the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing impairment qualifies at 80-99%, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining oral/limb defects, neurologic impairment and airway compromise.

basis: Oral malformations, digital skeletal defects and retinal dysplasia/coloboma define it; intellectual impairment is a defining feature. Aspiration frequency is unspecified.
Ornithine metabolism defect causing progressive chorioretinal degeneration; aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal damage; hearing loss is under 30%.
UMP synthesis defect with anemia and T-cell dysfunction (30-79%); developmental delay 80-99%. Ureter, hip and cardiac abnormalities (30-79%) omitted at cap; crystalluria alone is not injury.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: T-cell dysfunction with recurrent infections, annotated at 30-79%, supports immunodeficiency; qualifying mechanism axes belong in primary.

basis: ID, myopathy and calcified pinnae define syndrome; hearing loss 12/14; cataracts 80-99%. Hypogonadism and anemia, each HPO 80-99%, omitted at cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myopathy is named in the syndrome synonym; progressive muscle wasting and contractures are characteristic structural manifestations.
decisions.otologic: primary: calcified external ears are defining; hearing impairment occurs in 12/14 patients (~86%).

basis: Adolescent tibial growth disorder causing progressive bowing and knee deformity.
Skeletal and dental developmental defects define the syndrome; hypertension occurs in 80–99%. Hyperuricemia alone does not establish an additional metabolic disorder.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting long bones, pelvis and digits; respiratory infections do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Prenatal bone fragility, microcephaly and bilateral cataracts define the syndrome; cardiac malformations are occasional.
Severe bone fragility and deformity define type III; dentinogenesis imperfecta is explicitly a main defining feature. Scleral color alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: the supplied definition explicitly includes dentinogenesis imperfecta among the main features of type III; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Bone fragility and deformity define OI9; dentinogenesis imperfecta affects 10/11; blue sclerae do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Inherited skeletal dysplasia with osteoporosis, fractures and congenital joint contractures; no established additional organ damage.
Malignant bone-forming mesenchymal tumor; pulmonary metastases are not sufficiently common across all cases to add pulmonary.
Benign bone-forming neoplasm arising in skeletal bone.
Osteolysis, arthropathy and subcutaneous nodules define MONA; gingival overgrowth 4/5 and corneal opacity 2/5 support involvement; mitral prolapse 1/5 excluded.
Distal osteolysis and intellectual disability define the named syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is part of the explicit syndrome synonyms and definition, supported by an 80-99% HPO frequency.

basis: Benign bone-forming neoplasm of the middle ear; both its ear location and skeletal tissue of origin are primary.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: an osteoma is a bone neoplasm; skeletal tissue of origin qualifies even when the lesion is localized to the middle ear.

basis: Sterile autoinflammatory bone disease with osteitis and osteolysis; skin, bowel, vascular and neurologic manifestations are occasional.
Osteopenia with fractures, intellectual disability and sparse hair define the syndrome; hearing impairment is only occasional.
Bone sclerosis causes marrow failure (anemia 3/6), visual impairment (2/5) and hypocalcemia (3/6). Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Osteopetrosis causes marrow compromise with anemia in 6/6 and hydrocephalus in 3/6. Hepatomegaly alone lacks proven dysfunction; blindness occurs in 1/6.
Neurodegenerative osteopetrosis; marrow failure with anemia/thrombocytopenia ~67-75% and optic atrophy ~50-67%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
CA2 deficiency defines osteopetrosis and renal tubular acidosis; neurologic dysfunction with cerebral calcification is a defining feature, with developmental delay in 30-79%.
Severe osteoporosis/fractures and congenital vitreoretinal disease define syndrome; intellectual disability reported in 3/4, supporting neurologic involvement.
Osteosclerosis and brain abnormalities define disease; lung hypoplasia 4/7 (~57%), cleft palate 80-99%, gingival fibromatosis 30-79%. Hearing/urinary defects <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate (80-99%) and gingival fibromatosis (30-79%) are common structural oral disease, accompanying the defining bone and brain disorder.

basis: Defining skeletal, nail and external-ear malformations; intellectual disability reported in 80-99%.
Glyoxylate metabolic disorder with defining renal oxalate injury; stones occur in 80-99%. Hepatic enzyme deficiency does not establish liver damage; anemia need not reflect direct blood injury.

decisions.renal: primary: nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis and progressive renal injury define the clinical disease; stones occur in 80-99%.

basis: Glyoxylate metabolic disorder defined by renal oxalate deposition and recurrent stones; systemic oxalosis is not sufficiently common.
Glutathione-cycle defect; developmental delay reported in 30-79%. Urinary metabolite elevation does not establish kidney damage.
Syndrome defined by cleft palate, intellectual disability and limb abnormalities; oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Parkinsonism and pyramidal degeneration define disease; structural talipes occurs in 10/10. Neurogenic bladder reflects neural dysfunction without established direct urinary damage.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder occurs in 30-79%, but reflects neurologic dysfunction; direct urinary tract damage is not established.

basis: Pancreatic malignancy is predominantly exocrine; endocrine carcinoma and lymphoma are minority subtypes and do not determine labels for the umbrella.
Congenital absence of pancreatic tissue affects the organ's exocrine and endocrine compartments.
Persistent measles infection causes progressive encephalitis; directly damaging chorioretinitis is frequent (30-79%), supporting ocular involvement.
Defining pancreatic inflammation, biliary sclerosis and sicca-related lacrimal/salivary dysfunction; immune mechanism unspecified.
Choroid plexus brain tumor, commonly causing hydrocephalus. Visual impairment occurs in 5-29%; osteosarcoma is a separate tumor.
Diffuse rigid skin defines disease; respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79% through restricted chest expansion, without established direct pulmonary injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 30-79% reflects external restriction by rigid skin; direct lung, airway or pleural damage is not established.

basis: Neurodegenerative parkinsonian syndrome; gaze palsy and abnormal eye movements reflect CNS dysfunction rather than direct eye damage.
Cohen alias ([Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/2829)); ID, retinal dystrophy and neutropenia define it; joint laxity >30%, a major criterion; obesity omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: primary: Orphanet merges this historical entity into Cohen syndrome, where neutropenia is a defining blood-cell disorder.
decisions.ocular: primary: Cohen syndrome includes defining progressive retinal dystrophy and high myopia, rather than only non-damaging ocular signs.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint hypermobility is common (>30%) and a major criterion ([cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1181995/)).

basis: Encephalopathy and optic atrophy define PEHO; syndromic gingival overgrowth is annotated 30-79%; contractures do not establish direct muscle or joint disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent gingival overgrowth is a recognized syndromic phenotype annotated at 30-79%; gingiva belongs to this axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contractures and restricted mobility occur in 30-79%, but reflect severe neurologic impairment without established direct muscle or joint pathology.

basis: Autoinflammation with abnormal neutrophil morphology/function; recurrent aphthous mucosal ulceration in 3/3. Skin infections are secondary infectious diagnoses.
CNS hypomyelination; fixed contractures and kyphoscoliosis each affect 6/7. Visual impairment in 7/7 may be central; nystagmus and strabismus do not establish direct ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 7/7 can reflect CNS disease; no retinal, optic-nerve or other direct ocular damage is established.

basis: Synonyms define pellagra-like skin disease with neurologic manifestations; a metabolic defect or gastrointestinal involvement is not established.
Pelvic/scapular and limb dysplasia define disease; hearing impairment with auditory canal stenosis in 2/2; strabismus and blepharophimosis annotated 30-79%.
An inborn pentose metabolism disorder; urinary L-xylulose excretion does not indicate kidney damage.
Chronic fluid accumulation in the pericardial space defines a pericardial disorder.
Chronic scalp follicular inflammation causes abscesses, sinus tracts and scarring alopecia; secondary infections do not define its underlying mechanism.
MVK-related autoinflammation; oral ulcers 60%, GI hemorrhage 80-99%, arthritis 67%; vasculitis 30-79% omitted by cap; transient rash and organomegaly do not establish lasting damage.
Chronic periodontal destruction affects tooth-supporting oral tissues through a dysbiotic bacterial biofilm and host immune response.
Peripheral axonal neuropathy and degenerative, necrotizing brain disease define the condition.
Gastric intrinsic-factor secretory deficiency causes B12 malabsorption and megaloblastic anemia; dementia/learning disability 30-79% supports neurologic involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: congenital loss of gastric intrinsic-factor function directly defines B12 malabsorption; gastric mucosal atrophy is not required for a secretory functional defect.

basis: Inherited intestinal B12 malabsorption causes megaloblastic anemia; renal tubular protein reabsorption dysfunction causes proteinuria in 30-79%; neurologic findings occur in <30%.
Congenital absence of a skeletal muscle, with possible foot dorsiflexor weakness.
Defining encephalopathy; retinal dysfunction 17/22, liver disease with hepatomegaly 32/73. Cap omits hearing loss 29/64, renal cysts 4/12 and skeletal stippling 12/12.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neonatal seizures and profound developmental impairment define the disease; developmental delay affects 126/126 and seizures 79/85.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with eye and limb malformations; developmental impairment 80-99%; cap excludes frequent cleft palate, pulmonic stenosis and microtia.
Isolated reproductive differentiation disorder with persistent uterus/fallopian tubes in otherwise normally virilized males.
Progressive joint stiffness, enamel hypoplasia and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Frequent eyelid and pinna dysmorphism lacks documented functional impairment.

decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis occurs in 30-79%, but the described narrow fissures and epicanthus do not establish damaging ocular dysfunction.

basis: Limb/vertebral defects, heart malformations and ear anomalies define PHAVER; myelomeningocele occurs in 30-79%, supporting neurologic involvement.
Inherited phenformin hydroxylation defect is a drug-metabolism phenotype; lactic acidosis is annotated. Intrinsic hepatic injury is not established.
Untreated neurotoxicity and eczematous dermatitis are frequent (30-79%); osteopenia excluded because dietary treatment substantially confounds attribution.
BH4 recycling deficiency with defining CNS neurotransmitter depletion and neurodevelopmental disease; developmental delay 20/20. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: primary: CNS neurotransmitter and folate deficiency with severe neurologic dysfunction defines this neurometabolic disease; developmental delay 20/20.

basis: BH4 synthesis deficiency causes hyperphenylalaninemia and central neurotransmitter depletion; progressive cognitive and motor deficits are explicitly defining, with developmental delay in 11/12.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive cognitive and motor deficits are explicitly part of the disease definition; developmental delay occurs in 11/12 (~92%).

basis: Gluconeogenesis disorder with hypoglycemia and a classic hepatic steatosis/failure phenotype; quantitative frequencies are unavailable. Renal steatosis alone does not establish kidney dysfunction.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic steatosis and liver failure characterize the classic reported hepatometabolic presentation; precise frequencies are unavailable.

basis: PGAM2 deficiency is a muscle glycolytic disorder. Hemolysis in the definition conflicts with its usual phenotype and supplied HPO; acute kidney injury occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.haematologic: none: hemolytic anemia is not characteristic of muscle-specific PGAM2 deficiency and is unsupported by HPO; the supplied definition appears erroneous.

basis: Gluconeogenesis defect; hepatic dysfunction/steatosis is common, with failure in 1/1 annotated. Neurologic injury is mainly described in severe cases, without reliable frequency.
Cardiac glycogen storage causes lethal cardiomyopathy; renal enlargement and macroglossia lack demonstrated functional damage; effusions reflect heart failure.
Glycogen metabolism disorder with predominant hepatic storage, hepatomegaly and frequent fibrosis. Muscle weakness occurs in 3/15, below 30%.
Cleft palate, glossoptosis and mandibular hypoplasia define the sequence; upper airway obstruction and respiratory distress occur in 30-79%.
Twisted fragile hair defines disease; dental and enamel abnormalities are annotated in 30-79%, supporting gastrointestinal involvement; hearing impairment is only 5-29%.
Hair defects, developmental impairment and joint laxity define the syndrome; valve regurgitation reported in 1/1 supports cardiac involvement. Microdontia omitted at cap; sample is tiny.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: joint laxity is part of the syndrome's explicit synonym; joint hypermobility and multiple skeletal abnormalities support this defining component.

basis: Deafness and pili torti define this mitochondrial metabolic disorder. Eye abnormalities lack evidence of damage; hypogonadism and intellectual disability occur in 5–29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the established mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder is an inborn metabolic disease, independently of occasional hypogonadism.

basis: Hair and skin dysplasia, abnormal or missing teeth, and refractive errors define the syndrome.
Extreme insulin resistance with characteristic skin/nail disease; developmental disability and dental abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Recurrent infections do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic persistent skin, hair and nail abnormalities help define the syndrome, supported by hypertrichosis ancestry and HPO frequencies of 30-79%.

basis: Inherited retinal cone dysfunction causes achromatopsia, photophobia and reduced visual acuity.
Congenital isolated growth hormone deficiency. Short stature reflects hormone deficiency; treatment-induced antibodies do not establish intrinsic immune disease.
GH resistance with low IGF-I; skeletal growth and maturation impaired in >80%; tooth agenesis, microdontia and eruption defects in 80-99%.
PROP1-related deficiency of multiple anterior pituitary hormones; short stature and hypoglycemia do not establish separate organ damage.
Biologically inactive growth hormone causes impaired growth signaling; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation do not establish destructive bone disease.
Defined by congenital pituitary hormone deficiency and cerebellar malformation; small sella and delayed bone age do not establish separate locomotor damage.
Pituitary growth hormone deficiency with hypothyroidism; enlarged sella and growth delay do not establish separate skeletal damage.
Deficiency of a plasma factor responsible for clot retraction indicates a haemostatic disorder; no additional organ involvement established.
Inherited fibrinolytic bleeding disorder; joint hemorrhage 80-99%, muscle hematomas and hemothorax 30-79%. Hematuria alone does not establish urinary organ injury.
Inherited platelet receptor dysfunction; claudication lacks frequency and evidence establishing common direct vascular damage.
Inherited platelet procoagulant dysfunction; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish intrinsic skin or airway disease.
Inherited skeletal myopathy; salt craving alone does not establish an endocrine or metabolic disorder.
Alveolar macrophage accumulation and interstitial inflammation injure lungs; smoking-related inflammation does not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Defined by polycystic kidneys together with cataracts and congenital blindness.
Collecting-duct cysts and congenital hepatic fibrosis define ARPKD; hepatic fibrosis occurs in 80-99%, pulmonary hypoplasia in 30-79%.

decisions.hepatic: primary: congenital hepatic fibrosis and ductal plate abnormalities are defining components of ARPKD; fibrosis occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with skeletal dysplasia; lung hypoplasia 9/9 and renal dysplasia 9/10. Hepatic fibrosis 6/8, heart anomalies 6/8 and microcephaly omitted by cap.
Clonal marrow overproduction of blood cells; thromboses are minority complications; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Congenital erythrocytosis; thrombosis is a separate complication. Pulmonary hypertension reported in 1 patient does not establish a population frequency of >=30%.
Congenital skeletal digit abnormality with postaxial polydactyly and possible metacarpal synostosis.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia is usual and cystic renal dysplasia is common (approximately >=30%). Hepatic, cardiac and CNS abnormalities are mostly <30%.

decisions.renal: involved: cystic renal dysplasia is a characteristic, common visceral lesion of severe Majewski/SRTD6 (approximately >=30%); HPO gives no exact frequency.

basis: Defined by digital and vertebral malformations and dental abnormalities; ear shape and skin folds do not establish functional damage.
Infantile myoclonus, ataxia and opsoclonus constitute a neurologic movement syndrome; abnormal eye movements do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Glycogen storage disease defined by central/peripheral neurodegeneration and progressive neurogenic bladder (80-99%); skin ulcers are secondary.

decisions.renal: primary: progressive neurogenic bladder is a defining urinary-organ loss of function (80-99%), integral to APBD despite its neural cause.

basis: Idiopathic excess amniotic fluid is an obstetric condition; no disease of an included organ axis is established.
Polysyndactyly and complex cardiac malformations define syndrome; hepatic ductal plate malformation in 30-79%; renal and ocular abnormalities below 30%.
Limb webbing/contractures, ectodermal defects and oral synechiae/clefts define syndrome; corneal ulceration reported in 4/4 supports ocular damage.
UROS deficiency causes erythropoietic porphyrin accumulation, hemolysis and destructive photosensitive skin disease. Erythrodontia alone is not dental damage; ocular injury is 5-29%.
Defining limb, craniofacial, eyelid and ear malformations; cleft palate in 30-79%; cardiac malformations reported in 30-79% omitted under the four-axis cap.
Renal salt transport defect with hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia and alkalosis. Weakness and QT prolongation do not establish direct muscle or cardiac damage.
Intellectual disability, skeletal abnormalities and obesity define the syndrome; hypogonadism occurs in 80-99%. Strabismus occurs in 30-79%; elevated IgE alone does not establish immune disease.
audit_reason: Move metabolic_endocrine from involved to primary: obesity is part of the syndrome's definition, supported by hypogonadism in 80-99%. Retain ocular involvement for strabismus in 30-79%.

basis: Congenital bowing of long bones defines the disease; unspecified skin abnormalities lack evidence of common functional damage.
Congenital retinal vessel malformation forming loops anterior to the optic disc; both ocular location and intrinsic vascular abnormality define the disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the lesion is a blood-vessel malformation; the cardiovascular axis includes local arteries and veins without requiring systemic vascular disease.

basis: BH4 recycling defect with usually benign hyperphenylalaninemia; developmental delay is 5-29%. Oculogyric crises at 30-79% do not alone establish lasting neurologic damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: oculogyric crises (30-79%) are episodic signs without established lasting impairment; developmental delay is only 5-29%.

basis: Resistance to progesterone represents impaired endocrine hormone signaling, with infertility as its reported manifestation.
Hereditary lipodystrophy with skin and hair abnormalities; generalized muscle atrophy in 3/3 and slender bones in 7/7; entropion reported in 80-99%.
Isolated deficiency of the pituitary hormone prolactin.
Prolactin deficiency and obesity define endocrine dysfunction; borderline intellectual disability has no documented frequency.
Defining urinary tract defects, absent abdominal musculature, pulmonic stenosis and intellectual disability retained. Defining deafness also qualifies but is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability is defining and retained; urinary, abdominal muscle and cardiac defects occupy the three primary slots.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital abdominal wall muscle deficiency is a defining component of prune belly, not secondary neurogenic weakness.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: defining deafness qualifies, but urinary tract, abdominal muscle, cardiac and neurodevelopmental disease take the four available slots.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia with limb shortening, joint dislocations and vertebral abnormalities; cardiovascular abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Defining humeral, radial-head and jaw abnormalities are obligate. Genital malformations and amenorrhea alone do not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Testicular steroidogenesis defect; urethral malformation includes hypospadias (80-99%) and urogenital sinus anomaly (30-79%). Other genital features are reproductive.
Mineralocorticoid resistance causes renal salt wasting, hyperkalemia and acidosis; frequent respiratory infections are separate infections, not established lasting lung damage.
Inherited retinal degeneration with hemorrhage, exudation and progressive visual loss; pseudoinflammatory does not establish immune mediation.
Peroxisomal neurodegeneration; retinal dysfunction and sensorineural hearing loss each 80-99%; hypodontia (80-99%) omitted by cap; hepatomegaly alone insufficient.
Limb, hearing and eyelid abnormalities define syndrome; dental defects 30-79%. Skin abnormalities omitted by cap; pseudopapilledema alone does not imply visual damage.
Brain/digital malformations define disease; microphthalmia 80-99%, endocrine defects 30-79%. Cap omits GI, cardiac and urethral defects (30-79%); lobation alone lacks lung damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: anal atresia and oral clefts qualify at 30-79%, but are omitted under the cap, prioritizing very frequent eye defects and multigland endocrine malformations.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: adrenal/thyroid hypoplasia and hypothalamic-pituitary abnormalities occur in 30-79%; substantial endocrine malformations are retained under the cap.

basis: Abnormal pseudouridine metabolism and intellectual disability define the disorder; urinary metabolite excretion does not establish kidney damage.
Testosterone-to-DHT conversion defect; defining posterior/perineal hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies affect urethral development (HPO 80-99%). Other genital anomalies have no axis.

decisions.renal: primary: posterior/perineal hypospadias is explicitly part of the defining phenotype; urethral malformations fall within renal and are annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Vitamin D metabolic defect with defining rickets; cardiomyopathy and hypochromic anemia each have HPO frequency 30-79%. Aminoaciduria alone does not establish direct renal injury.

decisions.haematologic: involved: hypochromic anemia represents blood-cell dysfunction and is annotated frequent (30-79%); no separate cause is established in this record.
decisions.renal: none: aminoaciduria (80-99%) alone does not establish direct kidney injury or clinically significant tubular failure from this disease.

basis: Elastic-tissue mineralization affects skin, retina and arteries; GI hemorrhage 5/16 (~31%); reduced DLCO 11/35 (~31%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Contractures and skin webs define syndrome; oral clefts 30-79%, malocclusion 2/3 and ptosis 2/2. Hypogonadism (30-79%) omitted at cap; neonatal distress may be transient.

decisions.ocular: involved: characteristic congenital ptosis is a persistent eyelid defect, reported in 2/2 patients.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypogonadism is annotated 30-79%, but characteristic ocular and oral abnormalities take priority under the four-axis cap.

basis: Ptosis 100%, ID 70%, craniosynostosis 60% and synostosis 40%; hearing impairment 60%. Oral clefts 40% omitted at the four-axis cap.
Alveolar calcium-phosphate deposits directly injure lung tissue; right ventricular failure occurs in 5-29%, and extrapulmonary damaging deposits are rare.
Inherited surfactant metabolism defect causes alveolar phospholipid accumulation in 5/5 and respiratory failure; pulmonary hypertension is a separately diagnosed secondary complication.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: congenital SP-B deficiency is an inherited disorder of surfactant metabolism, with abnormal alveolar phospholipid accumulation in 5/5 patients.

basis: Congenital pulmonary valve/artery atresia with right ventricular and tricuspid hypoplasia; cyanosis and tachypnea do not establish lung disease.
Pulmonary bullae and recurrent pneumothoraces directly affect lungs and pleura.
Pulmonary lymphatic maldevelopment causes lung and pleural disease; chylopericardium directly involves the pericardium in 30–79%. Reflux is a separate disease.
Developmental pulmonary capillary/venous disease with severe pulmonary hypertension; intestinal malrotation in 30-79%; renal anomalies below 30%.
Pulmonary arterial vascular disease with right ventricular failure in 3/5; both fall within cardiovascular, without established lung parenchymal damage.
Primary congenital pulmonary parenchymal hypoplasia with severe respiratory dysfunction; other structural anomalies are minority findings.
Occlusive disease of pulmonary veins and capillaries causing pulmonary hypertension and impaired pulmonary gas exchange.
Congenital narrowing of the pulmonary heart valve.
The defining abnormalities are pulmonary valve stenosis and congenital nephrosis; pulmonic stenosis is cardiac, not pulmonary.
Lysosomal skeletal disease; dental abnormalities and conductive hearing loss each 30-79%. Nail abnormalities (30-79%) omitted by cap; blue sclerae do not establish visual damage.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia with generalized osteosclerosis and abnormal ossification; edema and facial morphology do not establish additional organ damage.
Metaphyseal bone dysplasia; structural dental malocclusion occurs in 30-79%. Caries is separate; sinus hypoplasia alone does not establish airway dysfunction.
Congenital obstruction from atresia of the gastric pylorus; no evidence of additional intrinsic organ disease.
Inborn metabolic epilepsy defined by pyridoxine-responsive seizures; neonatal respiratory distress does not establish pulmonary damage.
Inherited erythrocyte pyrimidine-metabolism defect causing hemolysis; jaundice does not establish hepatic injury; neurologic findings are rare.
Glutathione synthesis defect causes organic acid accumulation, acidosis and hemolytic anemia; neurologic injury affects roughly half of systemic cases.
Inherited erythrocyte membrane disorder causing severe hemolytic anemia through partial spectrin deficiency.
Neurometabolic disease defined by lactic acidosis and developmental impairment; developmental delay in 17/17. Hepatomegaly is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures are defining manifestations; developmental delay occurs in 17/17.

basis: Erythrocyte glycolytic enzyme deficiency causes chronic hemolysis. Hepatomegaly and indirect jaundice do not establish liver damage; gallstones are a separate disease.
Radiculoneuropathy identifies disease of spinal nerve roots and peripheral nerves; no additional organ involvement is established.
Hearing abnormalities 80-99% and multicystic renal dysplasia 30-79%; strabismus 80-99% and dental defects 30-79% omitted at the four-axis cap.
Glycosylation disorder with defective leukocyte adhesion; severe intellectual disability and developmental delay 2/2, cerebral atrophy 30-79%; infections are sequelae.
Defined by cherubism/osteolysis, gingival fibromatosis and intellectual disability with seizures. Retinal pigmentation lacks documented functional damage; hirsutism alone adds no axis.
Radial/patellar defects and joint dislocations define the syndrome, alongside palatal malformations and chronic diarrhea; immune abnormalities occur in <30%.
Inherited skin pigmentation anomaly with hair findings; nystagmus and photophobia lack frequencies or evidence establishing common lasting visual impairment.
Retinal dysplasia with persistent fetal ocular vasculature.
Phytanic acid disorder with defining retinal degeneration and neuropathy/ataxia; cardiomyopathy annotated 80-99%. Common hearing, skin and skeletal involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: polyneuropathy, anosmia and ataxia are defining diagnostic manifestations; neuropathy/ataxia are annotated 80-99%.
decisions.ocular: primary: early-onset retinitis pigmentosa explicitly characterizes the disease and is a major diagnostic feature; retinal disease is annotated 80-99%.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; developmental impairment/ataxia, retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss are characteristic, each documented in 1/1 annotated patient.
NOD2-associated immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; no common direct extraintestinal damage established.
Renal hypoplasia is defining; Mullerian reproductive tract hypoplasia falls outside the axes.
Senior-Loken syndrome is defined by nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy; retinal disease occurs in 5/6 and advanced kidney disease in 6/8 reported patients.
Renal dysplasia and limb/rib malformations define the syndrome; lethal pulmonary hypoplasia occurred in all three described infants.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia caused fatal respiratory failure in 3/3 infants; it is a downstream manifestation of the defining renal and skeletal syndrome.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia, nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy define Mainzer-Saldino syndrome; hepatic fibrosis in one reported patient does not establish common involvement.
Renal hamartomas/nephroblastomatosis and pancreatic islet hyperplasia define disease; developmental impairment in 80-99%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Renal-hepatic dysplasia and Dandy-Walker malformation define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Pancreatic/intestinal anomalies (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79% and represents severe structural loss of lung capacity; prioritized under the cap.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none at cap: pancreatic abnormalities and intestinal malrotation occur in 30-79%; severe pulmonary hypoplasia takes the remaining slot.

basis: Renal tubular bicarbonate wasting causes acid-base and potassium abnormalities; rickets and osteomalacia lack frequencies establishing common bone damage.
Renal acidification defect causes metabolic acidosis and electrolyte disturbance; progressive sensorineural hearing loss is defining.
Renal hypoplasia/aplasia and middle-ear ossicular anomalies with hearing impairment define the syndrome; genital abnormalities have no axis.
Developmental renal tubular failure causes fetal anuria; pulmonary hypoplasia is common (>30%) in the characteristic oligohydramnios sequence.
Surfactant deficiency and lung immaturity cause alveolar collapse and respiratory failure; DIC is not an established common defining feature.
Impaired respiratory responsiveness indicates dysfunction of neural ventilatory control; intrinsic airway or lung injury is not established.
Profound immune deficiency, agranulocytosis/marrow hypoplasia and defining sensorineural deafness (11/11). Liver disease and intestinal stenosis are single reports, not established as common.
Inherited immune dysregulation with hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; hepatic inflammation/dysfunction occurs in most and CNS inflammation in roughly 30-70% of familial HLH.
Definition identifies a non-Hodgkin lymphoma of large lymphocytes; no specific extranodal organ involvement is established as common.
Retinal degeneration and epilepsy are the two defining manifestations, supported by the supplied phenotypes.
Retinal degeneration, small eyes, macular disease and glaucoma are confined to the ocular axis; optic atrophy is also ocular.
Progressive retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy causing visual loss; associated structural findings are also confined to the eye.
Retinal vascular abnormality and hypogammaglobulinemic immunodeficiency are defining features; retinal vessels are captured by ocular.
Retinal degeneration and hearing loss are the defining components.
Retinopathy, intellectual disability and endocrine dysfunction define the syndrome; sensorineural deafness occurs in 80-99%. Skin and skeletal abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hypogonadism and insulin-resistant diabetes are defining endocrine disorders, both reported in 80-99%.
decisions.otologic: involved: defining sensorineural deafness occurs in 80-99%; retained here because primary is capped at three and the endocrine mechanism requires primary status.

basis: Inherited retinal degeneration presenting in late adulthood.
The defining triad comprises progressive cone dystrophy, degenerative liver disease and endocrine dysfunction.
Pigmentary retinal degeneration and intellectual disability define the syndrome.
Inherited retinal disease with splitting of the foveal retina.
Retinopathy, marrow failure and skin/nail abnormalities define syndrome; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in 30-79%, cerebellar hypoplasia in 2/2; oral leukoplakia omitted at cap.
LPIN1-related metabolic disease causes recurrent skeletal muscle breakdown; myoglobinuria does not itself establish kidney injury, whose frequency is unspecified.
Sarcoma with skeletal muscle differentiation; anatomical sites vary, with no additional organ consistently affected across the group.
Malignant soft-tissue tumour with skeletal-muscle differentiation, usually arising in the extremities; alveolar describes histology.
Skeletal dysplasia, heart defects and developmental impairment define it; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Hair/skin abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital heart defects are defining features; pulmonic stenosis is annotated in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is a defining feature, with cognitive impairment annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Defining skeletal, palatal and dental malformations; airway obstruction occurs in 30-79%; global developmental delay in 11/25 (44%) supports neurologic involvement beyond speech delay.

decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay occurs in 11/25 (44%); this exceeds the threshold and is broader than speech impairment from craniofacial defects.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; dental abnormalities affect 80-99%, gingival overgrowth and bifid tongue 17/22. Proptosis alone does not prove eye damage.
Retinal degeneration, hearing loss and Fanconi renal dysfunction define the syndrome; phosphate-wasting rickets affects 4/6 patients.
Ocular malformations/blindness, hypotrichosis and intellectual disability define syndrome. Dental abnormalities occur in 80-99% and occupy the fourth axis; hearing loss is occasional.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: structural dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%; teeth are gastrointestinal. The three primary slots prioritize blindness, hair abnormalities and intellectual disability.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly part of the disease definition and occurs in 80-99%; retained among the three primary axes.

basis: Poikiloderma and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%; juvenile cataracts are occasional (5-29%).
Limb defects, ectodermal dysplasia and oral/dental defects define disease; lacrimal defects 80-99%, corneal disease 30-79%; renal anomalies 30-79% omitted at cap.
Inherited lysine metabolism disorder. Neurologic impairment is occasional (5-29%); urinary amino acid abnormalities do not establish kidney damage.
GM2 storage causes neurodegeneration; blindness and hearing impairment each occur in 80-99%. Kyphosis omitted at the four-axis cap; organ enlargement alone does not establish dysfunction.
Intellectual disability, ptosis and cleft lip define it; skeletal anomalies affect 80-99%. Hearing abnormalities and shagreen patches, also 80-99%, omitted at cap.
Sarcosine degradation defect; neurologic, ocular, cardiac and hearing abnormalities are each occasional (5-29%); sarcosinuria is not kidney damage.
Severe developmental impairment, hydronephrosis and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; heart defects occur in 30-79%. Ocular and skin findings omitted by cap.
Congenital cerebral clefts cause neurologic dysfunction; strabismus in 80-99% reflects impaired alignment and does not establish direct ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent strabismus can arise from cerebral motor dysfunction; it does not establish direct damage to the eye.

basis: Autoimmune adrenal failure with thyroid and/or islet disease defines APS2; celiac disease, alopecia and vitiligo are separately diagnosed associated disorders.
Glycosylation disorder with lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia is usual (>30%) with severe thoracic restriction. Nail changes in 30-79% lack demonstrated dysfunction.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is usual (>30%) in this lethal thoracic dysplasia; inclusion relies on the usual disease course, beyond narrow-chest morphology alone.
decisions.dermatologic: none: nail hypoplasia and abnormal morphology occur in 30-79%, but do not establish functional nail or skin damage.

basis: Craniotubular skeletal dysplasia with characteristic dental hypoplasia in its definition. Proptosis and curly hair alone do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic dental hypoplasia is part of the defined syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: PXDN-related anterior segment malformation with corneal opacity, cataract and impaired vision.
Skeletal hyperostosis defines disease; facial nerve compression and hearing loss each affect >30%. Ocular damage is less common; singleton eye annotations cannot establish prevalence.
audit_reason: Remove ocular: visual loss and optic atrophy in one assessed patient do not establish involvement in at least 30%, and neither is a major diagnostic criterion. Common facial nerve compression and hearing loss qualify.

basis: Lipid storage with marrow histiocytes, thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly; liver enzyme data are limited to 1 patient and common functional liver damage is unestablished.
Skeletal syndrome with metacarpal abnormalities, carpal/tarsal synostosis and platyspondyly.
Deficiency of mucosal secretory IgA transport defines an immunodeficiency; intestinal symptoms and candidiasis lack frequencies establishing common direct gut damage.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss with metabolic dysfunction; hepatic steatosis 2/4; intellectual impairment is common in BSCL2 disease (~80%).
Inherited neonatal epilepsy; no additional organ involvement established.
Senile plaques are cerebral neuropathologic deposits; sparse supplied information supports brain localization without additional axes.
Primary combined immunodeficiency; respiratory and gastrointestinal infections are separately diagnosed consequences, not intrinsic organ lesions.
Defining severe skeletal thoracic dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia commonly causes early death and brain defects are described as common; visceral cysts lack evidence of >=30% frequency.
Obesity supports the metabolic axis; sparse syndrome information. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Lipodystrophy/insulin resistance, Rieger anomaly and skeletal features define SHORT; hearing loss is annotated at 80-99%. Dental and skin/subcutis abnormalities omitted at cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none under cap: dental delay occurs in 6/6 and enamel defects in 30-79%; retained axes capture greater functional burden.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal growth abnormalities, delayed bone maturation and joint hypermobility are defining features; hypermobility occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Infantile lysosomal storage with defining severe neurodevelopmental disease and skeletal dysplasia; common hepatic or renal functional damage is not established.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly alone does not establish function-impairing storage; conjugated hyperbilirubinemia has no stated frequency
decisions.renal: none: nephrotic syndrome is reported, but its frequency is unspecified and involvement in at least 30% is uncertain
decisions.neurologic: primary: severe developmental impairment and progressive CNS disease characterize the infantile phenotype
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal dysplasia is supported by the explicit skeletal-involvement parent and characteristic skeletal abnormalities

basis: Sialic acid metabolic defect; liver injury, ID/seizures and dysostosis reported in 80-99%; airway obstruction and coagulopathy omitted by cap.
Mirror positioning of heart, liver and gut defines condition; pulmonary situs omitted at the three-primary cap. Reversal alone does not establish functional organ damage.

decisions.hepatic: primary: mirror positioning of the liver is a defining abdominal anatomical feature of complete situs inversus.
decisions.pulmonary: none: reversed pulmonary situs is omitted under the three-primary cap; position alone does not establish lung damage warranting involved.

basis: Autoimmune lacrimal and salivary destruction; tubulointerstitial nephritis annotated 30-79%. Pulmonary fibrosis also annotated 30-79%, omitted at cap.
Lipid metabolism defect with ichthyosis and CNS disease; retinal atrophy in 5/9 and reduced visual acuity in 19/19 support common ocular damage.
Inherited ichthyosis; the concept explicitly excludes CNS and eye involvement. No established metabolic disorder is specified.
Generalized inherited skin peeling; atopy characterizes only some subtypes and does not establish a shared immune mechanism.
Cholesterol synthesis defect with intellectual disability and characteristic syndactyly; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Ocular involvement omitted by cap; liver reports are sparse.
Congenital intestinal secretory dysfunction; choanal atresia affects 10/22 (45%) and corneal erosion 9/22 (41%).
Record concerns inherited red-cell sodium-potassium pump activity; clinical consequences are poorly specified, without evidence of systemic metabolic organ damage.
IGF-I resistance; intellectual disability 30-79%; delayed skeletal maturation 80-99% with pectus and digital deformities 30-79%.
Congenital heart defects and intellectual disability define syndrome; urethral malformation through hypospadias occurs in 30-79%. Pigment changes do not establish skin damage.
Spastic ataxia and intellectual disability define neurologic disease; optic atrophy is a defining ocular lesion.
Neurodegenerative ataxia; pes cavus in 8/18 (~44%); mitral valve prolapse annotated 30-79%. Retinal hypermyelination lacks established visual damage; urinary symptoms are neurogenic.
Spastic diplegia and intellectual disability define neurologic dysfunction; no intrinsic muscle disease is established.
Corticospinal and peripheral motor neuron disease; distal weakness and muscle wasting result from denervation rather than direct muscle disease.
Spastic paraplegia and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; retinal degeneration occurs in 3/7 (~43%). Neurogenic bladder symptoms do not establish direct urinary injury.

decisions.ocular: primary: retinal degeneration is explicitly part of the disease definition and syndrome synonyms; documented in 3/7 patients (~43%).

basis: Defining spastic paraplegia and persistent pigment/hair abnormalities; kyphoscoliosis is frequent (30-79%). Bowel dysfunction is neurologic; horseshoe kidney is occasional.
Oxysterol metabolism disorder with corticospinal degeneration; muscle atrophy/pes cavus 30-79%. Incontinence 10/16 reflects neural dysfunction, without proven urinary damage.
Progressive spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability and glaucoma define the syndrome; each is reported at 80-99%.
Spasticity, intellectual disability and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; infantile sensorineural hearing loss is frequent (30-79%).
Isolated failure of spermatogenesis and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction established.
Red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolytic anemia; pigment gallstones are a separately diagnosed complication.
Motor-neuron disease with intellectual disability; sustained denervation causes actual skeletal-muscle wasting in most patients, integral to the syndrome.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent neurogenic muscle atrophy affects most patients; structural muscle wasting is integral to this disease, beyond weakness alone.

basis: Spinal motor neuron disease with microcephaly and intellectual disability; muscle atrophy reflects denervation.
Adult-onset lower motor neuron degeneration; sustained denervation causes muscle wasting, with quadriceps atrophy in 5/6 patients.
Anterior horn motor-neuron disease with defining proximal amyotrophy in the usual course; persistent denervation causes actual muscle loss. Skeletal deformity frequencies are unspecified.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: proximal amyotrophy is a defining manifestation, expected in most affected patients; persistent denervation produces structural muscle loss, not weakness alone.

basis: Anterior horn motor neuron disease; scapular and peroneal muscle wasting are defining manifestations, establishing substantial skeletal muscle loss.
Mitochondrial disorder with central and peripheral degeneration; hearing impairment and optic atrophy 80-99%. Isolated transaminase elevation does not establish hepatic damage.
Ataxia, developmental delay and skeletal deformities define syndrome; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Skin hyperextensibility alone does not establish tissue injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: skin hyperextensibility occurs in 80-99%, but no skin fragility, wounds, scarring or functional loss establishes direct damage.

basis: Defined by vision-impairing corneal dystrophy and progressive spinocerebellar degeneration; both are core disease components.
Spastic ataxia and cataract/corneal dystrophy define it; hypogammaglobulinemia in 30-79% supports immune involvement.
Spinocerebellar neurodegeneration; slow eye movements reflect neurologic oculomotor dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Congenital absence of splenic function directly affects a blood organ and constitutes primary immunodeficiency.
Splenoportal venous malformation defines disease. Hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis are reported without frequencies establishing >=30% or major diagnostic status; splenomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.hepatic: none: fibrosis and cirrhosis establish possible hepatic damage, but the supplied evidence does not establish their frequency or status as defining criteria.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia and marrow failure are in the supplied definition; intellectual disability in 12/20 (~60%); airway and ocular abnormalities occasional.
Vertebral/rib dysostosis, anal atresia and genitourinary malformations including urethral atresia define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia frequency is unclear.
Skeletal dysplasia with platyspondyly, abnormal vertebral endplates and short-trunk stature.
Skeletal dysplasia involving vertebrae and epiphyses, with associated osteoarthritis.
Spinal and epiphyseal dysplasia with intellectual disability explicitly defining the Kohn subtype, despite lower individual HPO frequencies.
Vertebral skeletal dysplasia with platyspondyly and spinal deformity; corneal opacities lack documented frequency and functional visual impairment.
Glycosylation disorder causing skeletal dysplasia; myopia 20/20 and atrial septal defect 5/5. Cleft palate 10/15 and skin changes omitted under the four-axis cap.
Skeletal dysplasia involving vertebrae, epiphyses, metaphyses and joints, with common osteoarthritis and impaired mobility.
Primary skeletal dysplasia; motor delay can reflect skeletal limitations. Cord damage and functionally significant airway calcification lack established >=30% frequency.
Skeletal dysplasia; myopia, hearing impairment and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%. Retinal detachment and cataract are occasional.
ASPA metabolic leukodystrophy; optic atrophy occurs in 80-99% and hearing impairment in 30-79%; feeding difficulty does not establish GI injury.
Progressive striatal degeneration defines the disease; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Dysphagia and weakness reflect neurologic dysfunction.
A subaortic membrane causes structural obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract.
Subaortic stenosis and short stature define syndrome; scoliosis/kyphosis occur in 30-79%. Vocal cord malformations occur in 80-99%, with respiratory insufficiency in 30-79%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: short stature is a defining named feature, supported by structural spinal abnormalities occurring in 30-79%.

basis: Inherited GABA metabolism disorder defined by developmental impairment, ataxia and epilepsy; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Defining triad comprises abnormal sucrose handling, hiatus hernia and intellectual disability; sucrosuria alone does not establish renal damage.
Inflammatory immune-mediated CNS demyelinating disease; ocular symptoms are occasional and do not establish common independent eye damage.
Congenital malformation of finger and toe bones and joints.
Storage disorder with defining neurodegeneration and ichthyosis; visual impairment 80-99%. Skeletal and hearing disease (30-79%) omitted at cap; organomegaly alone insufficient.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive neurologic deterioration and developmental impairment are defining manifestations, present in 80-99%.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: ichthyosis is a defining manifestation in 80-99%, supported by the integumentary-system parent.

basis: Sulfite metabolism defect causing destructive encephalopathy; ectopia lentis affects roughly half of surviving patients. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.

decisions.ocular: involved: characteristic ectopia lentis occurs in roughly half of surviving patients and directly disrupts ocular function.

basis: Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define the skeletal disorder; marked obesity is a defining metabolic feature.
Autonomic thermoregulatory dysfunction and congenital contractures define the syndrome. Respiratory crises and sudden death do not establish intrinsic lung or cardiac damage.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability, syndactyly and digital malformations define syndrome; cutaneous fusion is a defining skin lesion. Optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous syndactyly is explicitly a defining feature; frequent nail hypoplasia provides additional skin-appendage evidence.

basis: Syndesmodysplasic dwarfism denotes a hereditary skeletal/connective-tissue dysplasia; supplied evidence does not establish another affected axis.
Skeletal fusion dysplasia; enamel hypoplasia and hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%.
Ataxia and tapetoretinal degeneration are the defining neurologic and retinal components, despite inconsistent low-frequency phenotype annotations.
Persistent dyskinesia is a neurological movement disorder; medication causation does not change the affected primary organ.
Inherited coagulation protein disorder with abnormal bleeding and impaired prothrombin consumption.
Structural dental anomaly involving enlarged pulp chambers and shortened roots; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
GM2 storage with defining neurodegeneration; progressive retinal ganglion-cell injury and visual loss commonly affect >30% in the severe infantile course, beyond cherry-red deposits alone.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal ganglion-cell degeneration with progressive visual loss commonly exceeds 30% in the usual severe infantile course; not based on cherry-red spots alone.

basis: GM2 storage causes neurodegeneration; retinal visual impairment occurs in 30-79%. Muscle wasting is neurogenic; aspiration pneumonia is a separate disease.
Defining skeletal abnormalities, hair/sweat-gland dysplasia and oligodontia; cardiac defects 5-29%; renal abnormalities lack established frequency.
Congenital tooth absence and taurodontia define dental involvement; sparse or absent hair defines dermatologic involvement.
Congenital fusion of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Dental noneruption and maxillary hypoplasia with severe genu valgum define the syndrome; rotated ears alone do not establish otologic damage.
Teratoma arises in the pineal region of the central nervous system; common additional endocrine or ocular damage is not established.
Rudimentary testes with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism establish gonadal endocrine failure.
Germ cell tumor originating in the testis, a reproductive organ; endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Limb absence, ectodermal dysplasia and lacrimal drainage malformations define the syndrome. Intellectual disability is reported without a reliable frequency.
Limb aplasia, lung hypoplasia, hydrocephalus and oral clefts each 80-99%; anal atresia 30-79%. Renal, ocular, cardiac and ear anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: major pulmonary malformations are in the definition; lung aplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: CNS malformations are in the definition; hydrocephalus occurs in 80-99% and callosal agenesis in 30-79%.

basis: Limb defects, hair/nail dysplasia and abnormal teeth define the syndrome; nasolacrimal obstruction is also defining. Ear shape alone does not establish hearing loss.
Symmetric infantile degeneration of the thalami is a central nervous system disorder.
