The Glasgow variant combines lethal skeletal dysplasia with characteristic cataracts and anemia; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: primary: anemia is a characteristic component distinguishing the Glasgow variant, rather than a minority complication of ordinary thanatophoric dysplasia.
decisions.ocular: primary: cataracts are a characteristic defining component of the Glasgow variant.

basis: Thoracic skeletal dysplasia and hydrocephalus define it; conductive hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Restrictive respiratory failure does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure occurs in 30-79%, but thoracic restriction does not demonstrate direct lung or airway damage.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia with short ribs, limb shortening and joint abnormalities; narrow thorax alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Skeletal dysplasia with slender bones, vertebral abnormalities and joint laxity; hypospadias is a structural urethral anomaly reported in 10/11 patients.
Inherited amino acid metabolic disorder; evidence does not establish common damage to another organ.
Inherited platelet deficiency and dysfunction; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate skin or airway damage.
ADAMTS13 deficiency causes hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and microvascular thrombosis. Stroke 25/120; direct renal injury at ≥30% is not established.

decisions.renal: none: renal dysfunction is variable, with no supplied frequency establishing ≥30%; it is not required for diagnosis of congenital TTP.

basis: Hereditary hyperextensibility of the thumb joint.
Defining limb defects, chorioretinal coloboma and ear/hearing abnormalities; global developmental delay in 80–99% supports neurologic involvement.
Thymic aplasia disrupts T-cell development and defines an immune developmental defect; additional organ damage is not established by the supplied record.
Thymic epithelial tumour; thymus has no specified anatomical axis. Thymoma itself is neither lymphoma nor an immune mechanism disorder; associated autoimmune diseases are separate.
Renal, cerebellar and thyroid disease define syndrome; thrombocytopenia 30-79%. Hearing loss (30-79%) omitted by four-axis cap.

Renal dysgenesis, thymic aplasia and anal atresia define the syndrome. Named lung dysplasia qualifies as a core malformation despite unspecified frequency; the three-primary cap places it in involved.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: lung dysplasia is a named core malformation, satisfying the defining-feature exception despite unspecified frequency; three primary axes are retained.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: anal dysplasia/atresia is a named defining malformation, corroborated by the anal-atresia HPO annotation.

basis: Inherited pyrimidine catabolism defect; seizures and developmental impairment occur in 30-79%, with intellectual disability in 10/22; drug toxicity excluded.
Defective thyroid-hormone responsiveness defines an endocrine disorder; isolated antibody findings do not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Congenital thyroid hormone synthesis failure; neurodevelopmental delay and abnormal/delayed epiphyseal ossification each occur in 30-79%; hearing loss is rare.
Thyroid peroxidase deficiency impairs thyroid hormone synthesis, causing congenital hypothyroidism and goitre; no qualifying additional organ damage established.
Sensorineural deafness and thyroid dyshormonogenesis/goiter define Pendred syndrome; renal and neurologic abnormalities are occasional.
Inherited thyroid hormone synthesis failure causes goitrous hypothyroidism; small reports of motor delay do not establish common lasting neurologic damage.
Inherited thyroid hormone synthesis defect causing hypothyroidism and goiter; neurologic impairment has no established qualifying frequency.
Inherited thyroid hormone synthesis defect causing congenital hypothyroidism; frequency of permanent neurologic impairment is not established.
Excess circulating thyroid hormone defines the syndrome; tachycardia, tremor and sweating do not establish lasting organ damage.
Congenital TSH deficiency; neurodevelopmental delay and skeletal maturation/epiphyseal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%.
Hypothalamic TRH deficiency causes central hypothyroidism; isolated hormonal dysfunction does not establish additional neurologic damage.
Inherited disorder of isoleucine metabolism with tiglic acid accumulation; supplied evidence does not establish common damage to another organ.
Congenital tibial deficiency with frequent foot deformity and knee contracture; other organ abnormalities are rare.
Absence of the tibia and congenital hearing loss are the defining abnormalities.
Inflammatory dermatophyte infection of scalp hair follicles and skin, with suppuration and possible scarring alopecia; lymphadenopathy is reactive.
Pigmentation is localized to fungiform papillae of the tongue, an oral structure within the gastrointestinal axis.
Structural dilation of trachea and bronchi impairs clearance; recurrent respiratory infections are secondary, separately diagnosed infections.
Cobalamin transport defect causes megaloblastic cytopenias and frequent hypogammaglobulinemia; acute kidney injury annotated at 80-99%.
Common origins include oral cavity/lip/salivary glands and pharyngeal/laryngeal/nasal airways; rare ocular and external-ear subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Inherited tricarboxylic acid cycle energy-metabolism defect; supplied evidence does not establish common damage to a particular additional organ.
Chorioretinal degeneration, hypopituitarism and hair abnormalities define the syndrome; ID/ataxia 30-79% and axonal neuropathy 3/7 support neurologic involvement.
Defined by hair, nail and skin abnormalities, enamel hypoplasia with tooth loss, and frontoparietal bone deficiency.
Defined by cranial, mandibular and acral skeletal anomalies. Macrostomia and external nasal dysmorphism do not establish gastrointestinal or airway dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: macrostomia describes mouth shape; no oral tissue disease, impaired feeding or other gastrointestinal dysfunction is established.

basis: Lipid storage with ichthyosis; progressive muscle weakness 80-99%, hepatic steatosis 30-79%; ocular, otologic, neurologic and cardiac findings 30-79% omitted by cap.
Spastic paraplegia with distal amyotrophy and characteristic skeletal deformities defines this syndrome; constipation and dysphagia do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: distal amyotrophy is a defining feature, including in the synonym; skeletal deformities are also characteristic (30-79%; several in 2/2).

basis: Tryptophan-handling disorder with characteristic intellectual disability and ataxia; short stature and photosensitivity alone do not establish additional tissue damage.
[MedGen](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/338528) documents metabolic abnormality, growth delay and intellectual disability; the erythrocyte T-antigen interpretation is unsupported.

decisions.haematologic: none: OMIM 276200 refers to a poorly characterized metabolic/neurodevelopmental phenotype; evidence does not support an erythrocyte T-antigen disorder.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is a documented characteristic of this poorly characterized syndrome.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: documented metabolic/homeostatic abnormality and the historical urinary T-substance phenotype support a metabolic disorder.

basis: MLH1 mismatch repair cancer syndrome is defined by brain tumors, colorectal polyposis/cancers and hematological malignancies. Cafe-au-lait spots do not establish damaging skin involvement.
audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary: hematological malignancies are an explicitly defining component of this cancer syndrome alongside brain tumors and colorectal polyposis. Excluding only its hematological cancer spectrum is inconsistent with the primary-tier definition rule.

basis: Tyrosine metabolism defect with defining corneal disease and palmoplantar keratoderma; intellectual disability is reported in 80-99% by supplied HPO annotations.
FAH deficiency causes defining liver disease and renal tubulopathy; porphyria-like neuropathic crises affect roughly 40% of untreated patients. Rickets is occasional.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct peripheral and autonomic neuropathic crises affect roughly 40% of untreated patients and are characteristic of the disease.

basis: Inherited tyrosine metabolism defect; developmental delay in 3/5 and intellectual disability/seizures at 30-79% support neurologic involvement. Urinary metabolites are not renal damage.
Historical tyrosine-metabolism disorder; sparse information does not establish a specific hepatic, renal or neurologic phenotype.
Severe limb and pelvic skeletal malformations define disease; nail dysplasia occurs in 80-99%. Genital malformations fall outside the axes.
Defining limb hypoplasia and clubfeet, severe developmental impairment, and congenital absence or hypoplasia of nails.
Defined by congenital absence of the ulna and endocardial fibroelastosis; finger aplasia further supports skeletal involvement.
Histidine metabolism disorder explicitly defined by encephalopathy, intellectual disability and ataxia; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.neurologic: primary: encephalopathy is explicit in the definition; intellectual disability and cerebellar dysfunction characterize reported cases.

basis: Congenital sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive retinal dystrophy define the syndrome; sensory-related developmental delays do not establish brain damage.
Usher syndrome combines retinal rod-cone degeneration with congenital sensorineural hearing loss.
Usher syndrome combines sensorineural hearing loss and retinal rod-cone dystrophy, both 2/2; vestibular dysfunction belongs to the otologic axis.
Usher type I combines retinal rod-cone degeneration with congenital sensorineural deafness and vestibular dysfunction.
Hydrocephalus, gut atresias, renal defects and tracheoesophageal fistula occur in 80-99%; severe airway defects retained. Ocular (80-99%), skeletal/cardiac (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: tracheoesophageal fistula directly malforms the trachea in 80-99%; retained for frequency and severity under the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: none: corneal/optic nerve anomalies occur in 80-99% but are omitted at the cap in favor of severe brain, gut, renal and airway defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: vertebral and radial malformations occur in 30-79%; omitted at the cap in favor of more frequent, severe organ defects.

basis: Type 1 explicitly denotes isolated uterovaginal aplasia, outside the axes. Renal annotations conflict with this definition and should not override the isolated subtype.
Inherited valine catabolic disorder; developmental delay is reported without an established frequency of at least 30%. Vomiting and poor feeding do not establish GI damage.
Brain, oral and digital malformations define syndrome; conductive hearing impairment 30-79%; frequent ocular abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Small-vessel hyalinosis defines vascular, gut and renal disease; subarachnoid hemorrhage occurred in 3/3; skin disease and retinal ischemia omitted by cap.
Isolated absence of the vas deferens affects the reproductive tract; CFTR association alone does not establish cystic fibrosis organ involvement.
Congenital right ventricular hypoplasia with intracardiac shunting and ventricular dysfunction; hypoxemia does not establish pulmonary damage.
Vertebral and rib segmentation defects; thoracic restriction causes respiratory insufficiency in 80-99%. Nonspecific immune annotation does not establish immunodeficiency.
Ophthalmoplegia, intestinal visceral myopathy and skeletal myopathy define it; neuropathy frequency is unspecified and valve abnormalities occur in 5–29%.
Inherited vitamin A metabolic disorder; night blindness and Bitot spots are characteristic ocular manifestations, typically >=30%; skin involvement frequency is unknown.

decisions.dermatologic: none: follicular hyperkeratosis is documented, but its frequency is unspecified and cannot confidently be placed at >=30% or treated as a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Cobalamin metabolic defect with defining anemia and neurodevelopmental impairment; cardiac malformations 30-79% by HPO. Stomatitis 4/12 omitted by four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay, intellectual disability and seizures explicitly characterize the disease in its definition.

basis: Cobalamin metabolism defect with defining anemia and neurodevelopmental impairment; retinal/optic damage in 30-79%. Glomerulopathy and oral inflammation omitted by cap.
Cobalamin processing defect with megaloblastic marrow disease (80-99%); intellectual disability and movement impairment occur in 80-99%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: intrinsic megaloblastic marrow disease, annotated 80-99%, makes this a blood/marrow disorder as well as an inborn metabolic disorder.

basis: Vitamin D resistance causes hypocalcemic rickets; alopecia affects roughly half to two-thirds. Hearing loss in 1 annotated patient does not establish common involvement.
Inherited combined coagulation-factor deficiency; cerebral and joint hemorrhage each occur in 1/4 patients, below the involvement threshold.
Vitamin E metabolic defect causes neurodegeneration; nyctalopia and skeletal deformities each occur in 30-79%; cardiomyopathy is occasional.
The defining syndrome combines progressive vitiligo, intellectual disability and urethral duplication; an autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Pontocerebellar developmental and degenerative disease. Common dysphagia and visual impairment reflect neurologic dysfunction, without established gut or eye damage.
Severe inherited coagulation disorder from near-absent VWF; joint hemorrhage is occasional (5-29%).
Defined by intestinal aganglionosis, sensorineural deafness and skin/hair pigment abnormalities; iris pigmentation alone does not impair vision.
Skeletal overgrowth/dysplasia and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; persistent skin laxity and nail dysplasia are common (roughly 67-99%).
Defining skeletal dysplasia and lens abnormalities; aortic and pulmonic stenosis each reported in 2/6 patients (~33%).
Skin/hair abnormalities and cataracts define the syndrome; osteoporosis ~90% and hypogonadism 80-99%; diabetes and atherosclerosis are separate age-related disorders.
Freeman-Sheldon phenotype comprises congenital limb and facial contractures with defining microstomia, trismus and oral malformations.
Thiamine-deficiency brain injury causes encephalopathy and amnesia; ophthalmoplegia and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction, not intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: this concept denotes thiamine-deficiency brain injury; its nutritional cause does not itself establish an intrinsic metabolic or endocrine disease.

basis: Poliosis, septal defect and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; respiratory abnormalities occur in 80-99%, with bronchomalacia reported. Ocular dysfunction at 30-79% is omitted by cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: respiratory abnormalities occur in 80-99%, with bronchomalacia reported; retained under the cap because involvement is more frequent than ocular dysfunction.
decisions.ocular: none under cap: myopia and strabismus occur in 30-79% and qualify, but pulmonary involvement is more frequent; blue sclera alone does not establish functional damage.

basis: Copper metabolism disorder with hepatic injury; neurologic damage occurs in about half. Kayser-Fleischer rings do not impair ocular function.
Osteolysis, arthropathy and subcutaneous nodulosis define the supplied MMP14-related MONA concept; gingival findings lack a qualifying frequency.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: subcutaneous nodulosis is a defining component of the supplied disease concept; hirsutism alone would not justify this axis.

basis: Severe intellectual disability and skeletal contractures define the syndrome; hypospadias 80-99%, oral/intestinal defects 30-79%. Strabismus and nail abnormalities omitted at the cap.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias affects the urethra, explicitly within renal, and occurs in 80-99%; it is not solely a reproductive-organ anomaly.
decisions.ocular: none: strabismus occurs in 30-79% but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent or consequential abnormalities.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: joint contractures, restricted mobility and skeletal developmental defects are defining features, with multiple findings in 80-99%.

basis: Isolated inherited hair disorder with sparse, dry, woolly scalp hair in 14/14 patients.
Woolly sparse hair defines the disorder. Protruding ears and an everted lip do not establish hearing impairment or intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Cutis laxa with skeletal defects and a glycosylation disorder; developmental impairment in 80-99%. Frequent dental disease omitted by cap.
Purine metabolic enzyme deficiency; urinary biochemical abnormalities do not establish renal damage; stones are a separate complication and renal failure is uncommon.
UV-related skin disease; neurodegeneration affects >50% in XPA, chronic ocular surface damage >50%, and sensorineural hearing loss approximately 30-50% over the course.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss is a common component of XPA neurodegeneration, affecting approximately 30-50% over the typical course.

basis: Defective UV damage repair causes cutaneous photodamage; chronic ocular surface injury, including keratitis and eyelid damage, affects a majority. Neurologic degeneration is atypical of group C.
UV-induced skin injury defines XP-D; neurodegeneration affects roughly half and cumulative ocular surface injury exceeds 30%. Individual ocular lesions are 5-29%; hearing frequency is uncertain.

decisions.ocular: involved: cumulative UV-related ocular surface injury exceeds approximately 30%; frequencies of 5-29% for individual lesions do not represent total ocular involvement.

basis: UV-related cutaneous injury defines XP-E. Ocular abnormalities are listed without frequencies; damaging ocular disease at >=30% is not established for this subtype.
Genetic photodermatosis with chronic cutaneous damage; keratitis is frequent (30-79%), supporting direct ocular involvement.
UV repair defect with cutaneous photosensitivity and freckling; neurologic, hearing and ocular abnormalities are annotated below 30%.
UV-sensitive skin DNA-repair disorder; cataract 1/1 and microphthalmia 1/3 support ocular damage; developmental delay/microcephaly 1/3 support neurologic involvement.
XP, neurodegeneration and hypogonadism define syndrome; equinovarus 2/2, coxa valga 1/2. Optic atrophy and hearing loss each 1/2 omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: none at cap: optic atrophy in 1/2 qualifies, but structural skeletal deformity is more frequent (2/2).
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: equinovarus deformity in 2/2 and coxa valga in 1/2 support common structural skeletal involvement.

basis: Gonadal endocrine failure is supported by low testosterone and elevated LH/FSH in 2/2; reproductive anatomy and infertility add no other axis.
Defining chronic sinobronchial disease; recurrent otitis (30-79%) is a separate infection and hearing impairment is only 5-29%. Reproductive obstruction has no axis.

decisions.otologic: none: recurrent otitis (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed infection; persistent hearing impairment is only 5-29%.

basis: GPI-anchor disorder with ID/seizures and ichthyosis; coloboma 8/8. Cap omits hearing loss 8/8, cardiac defects 30-79%, and dental anomalies 80-99%.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal coloboma in 8/8; retained as the fourth axis after the three-primary cap.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent ichthyosiform dermatosis is a defining feature, present in 8/8.

basis: Defining laryngotracheoesophageal malformations and urethral hypospadias; developmental delay occurs in 19/37 (~51%), with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia in 3/7.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: esophageal malformations form part of the defining laryngotracheoesophageal defects; dysphagia in 6/7 supports functional involvement.

basis: Inherited ichthyosis affects skin; no steroid sulfatase deficiency or other established metabolic defect is specified.
Callosal agenesis defines disease; scoliosis/hip abnormalities and strabismus occur in 30-79%, supporting skeletal and ocular dysfunction. Renal defects are 5-29%; optic atrophy frequency unknown.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus is a functional ocular abnormality annotated 30-79%; nystagmus is also frequent. This does not depend on the unspecified frequency of optic atrophy.

basis: Renal proximal tubular disorder with proteinuria, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis; rickets is variable and not established in at least 30%.
RPGR-related retinal degeneration with night blindness, reduced visual acuity and visual field loss.
Nonsyndromic congenital sensorineural hearing loss.
Congenital absence or severe underdevelopment of scalp or body hair; isolated cutaneous disorder.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder.
Nonsyndromic inherited intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder; no other organ involvement is established.
Chronic intestinal neuromuscular dysfunction causes pseudo-obstruction; CNS manifestations and hydronephrosis are occasional (5–29%).
Neuronal migration disorder; cardiac/vascular abnormalities occur in approximately 65% of FLNA-related cases; isolated 1/1 reports do not establish other organ prevalence.
Intellectual disability and pyramidal dysfunction define it; heart failure is annotated frequent (30-79%); skeletal deformities have isolated reports.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability; speech impairment and seizures also fall within neurologic.
Intellectual disability and syndromic cranial skeletal abnormalities define the disease; bradycardia alone does not establish cardiac damage.
SMPX-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
DCX-related cortical malformation defines the disease. Contractures occur in 30-79% but reflect neurologic motor impairment rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: flexion contractures occur in 30-79%, but are secondary to cerebral motor dysfunction; direct musculoskeletal pathology is not established.

basis: Inherited retinal signaling dysfunction causing stationary night blindness and reduced visual acuity.
Fetal akinesia deformation syndrome with defining brain malformations, including callosal agenesis and arrhinencephaly; no established additional functional organ damage.
Immunodeficiency and neurologic dysfunction define disease; night blindness in 4/4 supports ocular loss. Bladder dysfunction lacks evidence of direct urinary-organ damage.
audit_reason: Remove renal: bladder dysfunction accompanies the neurologic disease and does not establish direct urinary-organ damage. Retain ocular because night blindness documents visual functional loss in 4/4 patients.

basis: Social cognitive function locus with a nervous-system phenotype annotation; supplied record does not clearly define a clinical disease.
Inherited degeneration of retinal cone and rod photoreceptors.
PCDH19-related epilepsy with developmental impairment and intellectual disability.
Peroxisomal metabolic disease defined by cerebral demyelination; adrenal insufficiency occurs in 80-99%. Hearing and visual impairment are occasional.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses, with characteristic limb and joint abnormalities.
Syndromic intellectual disability with common seizures and structural brain abnormalities; ocular and skeletal abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual developmental disorder.
Defined by intellectual disability and pituitary hormone deficiency, including panhypopituitarism.
Intellectual disability defines disease; strabismus affects ocular alignment in 2/5 (40%); joint hypermobility alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Prostate malignancy is reproductive-organ disease; urinary invasion or obstruction is not inherent to this hereditary concept.
Severe neurodevelopmental disease with defining hypogonadism and obesity; talipes equinovarus in 30-79% supports skeletal involvement. Nystagmus alone does not establish eye damage.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration.
Congenital lower-limb joint contractures and arthrogryposis define the disorder; no neurologic lesion is established.
Eye, dental and cardiac septal defects define OFCD; skeletal synostosis/contractures occur in 30-79%. Intellectual disability (1/3) omitted at cap.
Hypotonia, ataxia and abnormal auditory brainstem responses define neurologic dysfunction; nystagmus alone establishes neither intrinsic eye damage nor hearing loss.

decisions.ocular: none: congenital nystagmus can arise from central neurologic dysfunction; no independent ocular lesion or visual loss is established.

basis: Defining glomerulopathy, intellectual disability and elliptocytosis; sensorineural hearing loss in 2/4 patients. Ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Adrenal hypoplasia with adrenal insufficiency and frequent hypogonadism; pigmentation and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish direct organ damage.
Severe intellectual disability, limb defects and cleft palate/GI malformations characterize the syndrome. Unspecified genitourinary anomalies do not establish renal disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate and gastrointestinal malformations are explicit components of the defining phenotype; the oral cavity belongs to this axis.

basis: Nonsyndromic intellectual disability, present in 6/6; singleton ocular, nail and dental findings do not establish common direct damage to additional organs.
Inherited episodic skeletal-muscle dysfunction with obligate muscle weakness; no additional organ disease is established.
Lissencephaly, callosal agenesis and epilepsy define the disorder; malabsorption occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac and exocrine pancreatic defects occur in 5-29%.
Isolated retinal telangiectasia with damaging exudation and frequent retinal detachment; no systemic vascular involvement established.
Intellectual disability and hypogonadism define syndrome; dental malformation/malposition in 30-79%. Weakness alone does not establish muscle injury.
Severe congenital myopathy and defining urethral malformation: hypospadias in 2/2. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness without established intrinsic lung damage.

decisions.renal: primary: hypospadias is a urethral malformation, reported in 2/2, forming part of the defining genital abnormalities; urethra belongs to the renal axis.

basis: Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; both hematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes apply.
Testicular germ-cell malignancy affects a reproductive organ; an endocrine disorder is not established.
Skeletal dysplasia with hypomyelinating leukodystrophy defines disease; optic nerve abnormalities and visual impairment occur in 30-79%.
Radioulnar fusion and radial ray malformations define structural disease of the limb skeleton; unspecified severe malformations cannot support further axes.
Intellectual disability and obesity define syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 4/7. Eyelid dysmorphism lacks demonstrated functional impairment; macroorchidism is reproductive.

Severe neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus occurs in 11/11 and ophthalmoplegia in 30-79%; pectus excavatum in 30-79%. Neurogenic feeding difficulties do not establish direct gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia and feeding difficulties are neurogenic manifestations; direct gastrointestinal tissue damage or intrinsic dysfunction is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: pectus excavatum is a persistent structural skeletal deformity annotated as frequent (30-79%).

basis: Defined by limb skeletal malformations, pigmentary skin lesions and digital fibromatosis; accessory oral frenula do not establish functional damage.
Hereditary congenital dysfunction of eyelid elevation.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy; intellectual disability in 8/10. Visual impairment reported in 30-79% omitted at cap.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; HPO reports eyelid ptosis/blepharophimosis and urethral hypospadias at 80-99%. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral defect, within the renal axis, reported as very frequent (80-99%).
decisions.infectious_immune: none: recurrent infections in 9/12 establish susceptibility, but do not independently establish intrinsic immunodeficiency or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Intellectual disability and seizures define syndrome; cataract/glaucoma in 3/6 (50%) and cleft palate in 2/6 (33%). Small hands/feet alone do not establish skeletal dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: small hands/feet and short stature are descriptive growth traits; substantive skeletal or joint dysfunction is not established as common.

basis: Intellectual disability and microcephaly define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Small testes alone do not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Intellectual disability with characteristic orofacial clefting; cleft lip occurs in 6/8 and cleft palate in 5/8. Genital anomalies do not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Inherited spastic paraplegia; visual loss occurs in 30-79%. Bladder and bowel control abnormalities lack evidence of direct urinary or intestinal disease.

decisions.ocular: involved: visual loss is annotated in 30-79%, supporting substantial visual functional impairment; nystagmus alone would not suffice.

basis: Adrenal failure, myopathy and severe developmental delay define disease; potentially fatal megacystis 80-99%. Cap excludes intestinal abnormalities 80-99% and hepatic steatosis 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe psychomotor delay is explicitly defining; severe global developmental delay occurs in 80-99%, with seizures in 30-79%.

basis: X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 9/9 and seizures in 3/9; stature and head-shape findings do not establish another damaged organ.
Multinodular enlargement of the thyroid, an endocrine gland, even when thyroid hormone production remains normal.
Defining myopathy and skeletal deformities with cardiac disease; mitral regurgitation and ventricular hypertrophy each in 2/3. Transaminases alone do not establish liver damage.
Immunodeficiency with defining sweat-gland, hair and dental abnormalities; conical teeth occur in 80–99%. Colitis affects the same gastrointestinal axis in 30–79%.
Congenital neutropenia and monocytopenia define a cellular immunodeficiency with recurrent bacterial infections.
Immunodeficiency, ectodermal dysplasia and osteopetrosis define disease; lymphatic malformation causes defining lymphedema. Dental defects omitted at the four-axis cap.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular for the defining congenital lymphatic malformation and lymphedema. Remove gastrointestinal under the four-axis cap: dental defects have weaker syndrome-specific evidence than the defining lymphatic disease.

basis: Antibody deficiency defines the disease; recurrent ear and respiratory infections are separate infections, without established lasting organ damage.
FG syndrome is defined by neurodevelopmental impairment and hypotonia; constipation alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Purine disorder with defining neurologic dysfunction; nephrocalcinosis 13/17, renal insufficiency 30-79%, anemia 30-79%; gout is separately diagnosed.
Purine metabolism disorder; nephropathy annotated at 30-79%. Grade I denotes the hyperuricemia phenotype without overt neurologic dysfunction; conflicting neurologic annotations excluded.
audit_reason: Remove neurologic: grade I/HPRT-related hyperuricemia is the subtype without overt neurologic dysfunction. The conflicting intellectual-disability and dystonia annotations should not establish common involvement in this subtype.

basis: Nonsyndromic neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 8/8 patients.
Neurocutaneous pigmentary mosaicism; structural skeletal abnormalities occur in roughly 30-50%. Ocular abnormalities are less consistently above 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital skeletal abnormalities, including scoliosis, limb asymmetry and digit malformations, affect roughly 30-50%; estimates vary by series.

basis: Brain creatine transport defect causes developmental impairment; bowel dysmotility/aganglionosis reported in 30-79%; prolonged QT in 7/18 (~39%).
ID, muscle wasting, kyphosis and joint hyperextensibility define syndrome; amyotrophy 7/12. Obesity and small testes alone do not establish direct endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity (15/19) and small testes (10/15) do not establish endocrine gland dysfunction or an intrinsic metabolic disorder.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: muscle wasting, kyphosis and joint hyperextensibility are explicit defining features; distal amyotrophy occurs in 7/12.

basis: Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability.
Inherited platelet deficiency and dysfunction, sometimes with dyserythropoietic anemia; bleeding signs do not establish other organ disease.
Nonsyndromic inherited intellectual disability.
Progressive skeletal muscle degeneration; cardiac muscle disease affects roughly 50-70% over the course. Transaminase elevation can originate from muscle.
Congenital deficiency of radial forearm and hand skeletal structures.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with speech delay and hyperreflexia; no established metabolic disorder.
Bilateral perisylvian cortical malformation with seizures, cognitive impairment and pseudobulbar dysfunction.
Combined immune deficiency with profound T/NK-cell depletion; pneumonia and enteric infections are separately diagnosed infections, and diarrhea alone does not establish bowel damage.
Intellectual disability occurs in 6/6. Persistent bowel dysfunction with chronic constipation occurs in 3/3; joint contractures in 2/3. Fine/sparse hair alone is cosmetic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint contractures impair joint function in 2/3; broad digits are dysmorphic features rather than evidence that skeletal disease defines FG syndrome 3.

basis: Intellectual disability defines disease. Pes planus 3/4 lacks documented functional damage; hearing loss 1/4 is below threshold. Incontinence alone does not establish urinary tract injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes planus in 3/4 establishes common foot morphology, but no damaging deformity or musculoskeletal functional loss is documented.

basis: Syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder; sensorineural hearing impairment in 4/6 (~67%). Scoliosis in 2/8 (25%) falls below threshold.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy and progressive neurologic abnormalities define the syndrome; skeletal deformities and ventricular hypertrophy are occasional.
OFD1-associated retinal degeneration; other OFD1 syndromes do not establish extraocular involvement in this retinal subtype.
Non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability; listed minor physical features do not establish additional organ damage.
Intellectual disability defines syndrome; dental abnormalities/microdontia 80-99%. Obesity and macroorchidism alone do not establish endocrine organ dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder.
Syndromic intellectual disability; strabismus and structural skeletal abnormalities including clubfoot, kyphosis and hip dislocation each occur in 30-79%.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by neurodegeneration and cardiomyopathy; retinopathy with progressive visual loss occurs in 30-79%.
Acquired alpha-thalassemia with marrow myelodysplasia and cytopenias; dyspnea does not establish pulmonary damage.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability defines a neurodevelopmental disorder; no additional organ injury is established.
Intellectual disability and marked cubitus valgus define the syndrome. Common benign nevi and facial morphology do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: nevi occur in 80-99%, but benign nevi alone do not establish damaging skin disease or a primary dermatologic disorder.

basis: Callosal agenesis, coloboma and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; hearing loss 80-99%. Cap omits cardiac defects, choanal atresia and cleft palate (30-79%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: named micrognathia and defining skeletal anomalies, including scoliosis in 80-99%, establish a core skeletal component.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects 80-99%; the three primary slots retain the named neurologic, ocular and skeletal components.

basis: Severe neurodevelopmental disease and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; optic atrophy occurs in 2/6 and strabismus in 5/6.
Inherited retinal cone and rod dysfunction causes progressive visual impairment; no extraocular disease is established.
Defining oral, limb and epiglottic malformations occupy three primary slots. Intellectual deficit is also explicitly defining and retained as involved under the cap; frequency unspecified.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: epiglottic hypoplasia is an explicit defining airway malformation.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual deficit is explicitly defining, satisfying the diagnostic-feature exception; placed here because primary is capped at three.

basis: Intellectual disability and cerebellar malformation define the disease; strabismus affects 30-79% and impairs ocular alignment.
Distal motor neuropathy; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than a separate primary muscle disease.
SYN1-related epilepsy with learning disability and neurodevelopmental manifestations.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability; supplied dysmorphic features do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability defines a neurodevelopmental disorder.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and delayed puberty in 2/2 patients.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins; gonadal hormone failure belongs to the endocrine axis.
Marrow failure; limb aplasia 5/6, ventriculomegaly 6/6 and hypogonadism 4/4. Cap omits renal agenesis 3/6 and cardiac, gut and optic defects around 2/6.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability; skeletal findings lack evidence of involvement in at least 30%.
Deafness and intellectual disability define syndrome; pancytopenia 2/3, renal dysplasia/insufficiency 30-79%. Dental, ocular and thyroid findings omitted by cap.
Thyroid hormone transport defect defines neurodevelopmental impairment and muscle hypoplasia; hypertension reported in 30-79%.
Intellectual disability defines disease; patchy alopecia occurs in 80-99% and strabismus in 11/29 (~38%). Skeletal dysmorphism lacks demonstrated functional impairment.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: maxillary hypoplasia (80-99%), pectus excavatum and cubitus valgus (2/2 each) establish dysmorphism, without demonstrated locomotor or skeletal functional impairment.

basis: Inherited renal water-excretion defect causing hypotonic hyponatremia. Acute electrolyte-related seizures and elevated blood pressure do not establish lasting extra-organ damage.
CLCN5-related proximal renal tubulopathy causes phosphate wasting, hypophosphatemia and defective skeletal mineralization; all three axes define the disease.
Proximal renal tubulopathy; developmental delay 3/4 and phosphate-wasting hypophosphatemia 3/5 support involvement. CK/transaminase elevations alone establish neither muscle nor liver damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypophosphatemia in 3/5 is a common intrinsic consequence of renal phosphate wasting; electrolyte disorders belong to this axis.

basis: Young-onset Parkinson disease is a neurodegenerative movement disorder.
PAK3-related intellectual developmental disorder; associated facial and palatal features do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Muscle glycogen metabolism disorder with myopathy and progressive weakness; myoglobinuria alone does not establish kidney damage.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability with universal developmental delay; other organ damage lacks sufficient frequency evidence.
Intellectual disability and severe early retinal degeneration define the syndrome and affect all five reported patients.
Congenital structural skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness. Cardiomyopathy is reported without an established frequency of at least 30%.
FG neurodevelopmental syndrome; metopic synostosis and strabismus each occur in the single reported patient (1/1). Chronic constipation alone does not establish bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: chronic constipation is reported in 1/1 patient, but no structural bowel disease or established intrinsic intestinal dysfunction is supplied.

basis: Primary bone dysplasia with normal growth hormone; the ketoacidosis annotation conflicts with the defined SHOX skeletal disorder.
Congenital nystagmus is an ocular motor disorder with impaired stereopsis and associated strabismus; additional CNS damage is not established.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and characteristic hand/limb skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; cardiomyopathy is 5-29%; reflux is separately diagnosed.
Inherited retinal dysfunction with foveal hypoplasia, reduced visual acuity and impaired dark adaptation.
Ovarian endocrine failure defines disease. Osteoporosis (2/5) is a separate hypoestrogenic complication; unspecified dentition abnormalities (2/5) do not establish damaging dental involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dentition abnormalities occur in 2/5 (40%), but their unspecified nature does not establish structural injury or loss of function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: osteoporosis in 2/5 (40%) is a separately diagnosed complication of estrogen deficiency, rather than defining skeletal disease.

basis: Inherited retinal degeneration causing progressive visual loss.
ARHGEF9-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causes seizures, hyperekplexia and intellectual disability; no separate systemic metabolic defect is established.
Inherited myopia is a refractive and ocular growth disorder.
Defined by sensory/autonomic axonal neuropathy and hearing loss; hearing impairment in 16/16. Myopia in 4/16 is below 30%.
Monoamine metabolism disorder with defining cognitive impairment/intellectual disability; behavioral features do not make it purely psychiatric.
Cataract, ataxia and intellectual disability define disease; short stature and hypotonia alone do not establish skeletal muscle damage.
Clonal blood-cell glycosylation defect exposes Tn antigen, enabling antibody-mediated polyagglutination and immune destruction of affected blood cells.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: antibody recognition of exposed Tn antigen mediates the defining polyagglutination; this supports an immune mechanism alongside the blood-cell defect.

basis: Progressive central and peripheral neurodegeneration; common bladder symptoms reflect autonomic dysfunction rather than demonstrated direct urinary-organ injury.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; joint hypermobility and pes planus 80-99%, scoliosis 30-79%; otitis and reflux are separate diagnoses.
Congenital malposition of the urethral opening; the urethra belongs to the renal axis. AR involvement alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Immunodeficiency with cytopenias and hemophagocytosis; hepatitis in 8/9 and jejunoileal ulceration in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed Crohn disease is not the basis.
Inherited immunodeficiency; dental abnormalities include conical teeth in 4/5 and hypodontia in 1/3. Pneumonia is a separate infection.
Epilepsy, intellectual disability, speech dyspraxia and possible perisylvian polymicrogyria are neurologic manifestations.
Inherited ocular melanin disorder defined by visual impairment and late-onset sensorineural deafness; visual and hearing impairment each occur in 80-99%.
Cutaneous capillary malformation involving dermal vessels; associated hyperkeratosis and hair/nail abnormalities remain within the skin axis.
Glycolytic defect with defining hemolytic anemia and myopathy; neurodevelopmental impairment and ataxia occur in 30-79%. Renal and retinal damage occur in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myopathy is an explicitly defining manifestation of PGK deficiency; myopathy and rhabdomyolysis occur in 30-79%.

basis: BRWD3-related intellectual disability; external ear morphology does not establish hearing damage.
Purine metabolic disorder; renal insufficiency 30-79%. Neurologic/hearing damage belongs to severe disease (~25%); HPO overrepresents this subtype. Gout and stones are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurodevelopmental damage characterizes the severe form (~25% overall); the predominant mild form lacks it. HPO ataxia frequencies reflect severe-case enrichment.
decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing loss belongs to the severe form (~25% overall); the HPO 80-99% annotation is not representative across the mild-predominant umbrella.

basis: CDKL5 developmental epileptic encephalopathy; scoliosis affects 4/5 patients. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; reflux/constipation alone lack direct gut damage.
Severe MECP2 encephalopathy; frequent apnea and respiratory insufficiency reflect central hypoventilation without established intrinsic lung injury. Reflux is a separate disease.
Syndromic intellectual disability; facial dysmorphism does not establish functional skeletal damage, and scoliosis occurs in 3/11 (<30%).
Glycerol kinase deficiency, adrenal insufficiency and muscular dystrophy define this contiguous-gene syndrome; neurodevelopmental impairment 80-99%; persistent strabismus 30-79%.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent strabismus/esotropia is an ocular alignment disorder with impaired binocular function; HPO frequency 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: muscular dystrophy is a defining component of complex Xp21 deletion syndrome; myopathy occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Scapuloperoneal skeletal muscle degeneration defines the disease; cardiac conduction abnormality occurred in only 1/14.
Primary muscular dystrophy; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 4/7 (~57%); respiratory insufficiency in 2/7 does not establish direct lung damage.
GRIA3-related intellectual disability with developmental delay and frequent seizures; renal and eyelid abnormalities are occasional.
Congenital sensorineural deafness and cutaneous piebald pigmentation define syndrome; definition explicitly excludes ocular albinism.
Cerebellar developmental disease; nystagmus and pursuit abnormalities are central motor signs. Frequent strabismus does not establish intrinsic ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus occurs in 30-79%, but the evidence supports cerebellar ocular-motor dysfunction without direct eye damage or established visual loss.

basis: Hereditary prostate cancer involves a reproductive organ outside the axes; metastatic sites are not defining involvement.
X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 10/10; macrocephaly alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Intellectual disability defines syndrome; strabismus 13/21 and blepharophimosis 12/21; persistent skeletal abnormalities include brachydactyly 12/21 and overlapping toes 9/21.
Limb, anal and renal malformations define syndrome; cardiac septal defects reported in 30-79%. Most ocular defects are occasional; isolated Duane report omitted at cap.
Severe intellectual disability, microcephaly and strabismus define the syndrome; strabismus is reported in 80–99%. Short stature alone adds no skeletal axis.

decisions.ocular: primary: strabismus is explicitly part of the defining clinical association and occurs in 80–99%, supporting intrinsic ocular alignment dysfunction.

basis: Androgenetic scalp hair follicle miniaturization; androgen responsiveness does not itself establish endocrine gland disease.
Inherited hypertrophic narrowing of the gastric pylorus.
Intellectual disability and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; bilateral eyelid ptosis occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac, renal and airway abnormalities individually occur in 5-29%.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability with delayed speech and language development.
Intrinsic skeletal myopathy with reducing bodies, weakness and contractures. Respiratory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung disease.
Reducing-body skeletal myopathy; dilated cardiomyopathy in 1/2 patients. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness, without established intrinsic lung damage.
Deafness, cataract and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; sperm abnormalities are reproductive and outside the axes.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia and intellectual disability define disease; visual impairment and sensorineural hearing loss each frequent (30-79%); feeding difficulty alone adds no GI axis.
Pure hereditary spastic paraplegia affects descending motor pathways, with spasticity, hyperreflexia and sensory abnormalities.
Heme metabolism disorder defined by cutaneous photosensitivity; liver abnormalities, gallstones and anemia are occasional (5–29%).
Inherited immunodeficiency caused by B-cell maturation failure; circulating B cells are depleted in 44/44. Infections and secondary bronchiectasis are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the defining maturation defect affects blood cells, with near-absent B cells in 44/44; the blood-cell mechanism rule applies alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Alzheimer disease subtype defined by cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Penoscrotal hypospadias is a structural abnormality of the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis; reported in 4/4 patients.
Hereditary alveolar proteinosis with defective surfactant clearance and impaired gas exchange; the supplied phenotype establishes pulmonary disease.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: CSF2RA-related alveolar proteinosis reflects defective macrophage surfactant clearance; the metabolism wording alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.

basis: Primary dystrophy of the corneal epithelium; visual impairment need not be frequent to assign its organ of origin.
Corneal endothelial dystrophy with corneal opacity and reduced visual acuity in 80-99%.
Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal habitus define the syndrome; strabismus lacks evidence of common involvement.
Name, ancestry and HPO identify duplication syndrome; cobalamin definition is discordant. Precocious puberty 7/11; structural foot abnormalities 30-79%. No corroborated blood-cell disorder.

decisions.haematologic: none: megaloblastic anemia appears only in a discordant cobalamin-disease definition; ancestry and HPO support the chromosomal duplication syndrome.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: precocious puberty affects 7/11, supporting common endocrine dysfunction; the discordant definition does not establish a primary metabolic disease.

basis: SYP-related nonsyndromic intellectual developmental disorder; intellectual disability reported in all annotated patients.
Non-syndromic intellectual disability with speech and motor developmental impairment; obesity does not establish a defining endocrine disorder.
Joubert cerebellar malformation and intellectual disability; polydactyly in 6/9 (~67%) and rod-cone dystrophy in 3/8 (~38%). Hearing loss reported in only one assessed patient.

decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing loss in 1/1 assessed patient does not establish prevalence ≥30% across this subtype and is not a diagnostic criterion.

basis: Factor IX gain of function causes inherited hypercoagulability. Venous thrombosis is a separately diagnosed consequence rather than universal vessel damage.
Usually arises in deep mesenchymal soft tissues of the extremities near joints; visceral primary sites and metastases do not characterize most patients.
Inherited ocular nystagmus with foveal/retinal abnormalities and reduced visual acuity in 6/6; no independent CNS disease established.
Syndromic X-linked intellectual disability is the shared defining manifestation; additional organ damage is not established across the duplication group.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with neurodegeneration, neuropathy and muscle wasting in nearly all; respiratory failure is attributable to muscle weakness.
Acquired clonal blood-cell disease causing complement-sensitive hemolysis; thrombosis is a separately diagnosed complication, not direct defining vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: thrombosis may affect approximately 30-40% over untreated courses, but is a separately diagnosed complication excluded by the rules.

basis: Fatal fetal cardiomyopathy is defined by myocardial calcification; no systemic metabolic disorder is established.
Inborn cholesterol biosynthesis disorder with cortical malformations; strabismus and kyphoscoliosis each occur in 80-99%. Dental crowding alone does not establish functional damage.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: CK syndrome is an inborn error of cholesterol biosynthesis. Retain neurologic primary and ocular/musculoskeletal involvement, each supported by 80-99% phenotypes.

basis: Isolated testicular sex development in a 46,XX individual; no endocrine dysfunction or damage to another axis is established.
Inherited macular and cone-rod degeneration causing visual loss.
Inherited erythroid, platelet and neutrophil abnormalities, with marrow hypocellularity; all belong to the haematologic axis.
Cone dysfunction, myopia and impaired color vision define an ocular disorder.
Intellectual disability defines the disease; scoliosis affects 4/6 patients, supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Defining cerebral arteriopathy and hypogonadism; cerebral ischemic/hemorrhagic injury is frequent, with stroke-like episodes 5/7; cataracts 4/7. Hair graying alone is insufficient.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral injury follows the defining arteriopathy; stroke-like episodes occur in 5/7, with ischemic stroke and hemorrhage frequent. The defining lesion is vascular.

basis: Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability with developmental and language delay.
GDI1-related nonsyndromic intellectual disability; neurologic dysfunction defines the disorder.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; persistent strabismus affects 3/8 patients (~38%). Hypotonia does not establish primary muscle disease.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability; ocular abnormalities occur in 2/8 patients, below 30%; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with seizures in 5/9; both affect the neurologic axis.
Combined immunodeficiency with persistent EBV; bronchiectasis and lymphoma are separate diagnoses; splenic enlargement alone does not establish dysfunction.
Renal epithelial malignancy associated with Xp11/TFE3 rearrangement; no common additional site established.
Developmental, cardiac and skeletal disease define syndrome; dermatitis 4/8 and cutis laxa 3/8 support skin involvement. Hepatic steatosis in one assessed case has uncertain prevalence.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: dermatitis occurs in 4/8 and cutis laxa in 3/8; the three primary slots prioritize defining neurologic, cardiac and skeletal disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal anomalies are explicitly defining; scoliosis and delayed cranial suture closure are frequent (30-79%).

basis: Hypospadias is a congenital abnormality of the urethral opening; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.
Motor neuron degeneration, sometimes with frontotemporal dementia; weakness and dysphagia reflect neurologic injury rather than separate muscle or gut disease.
Defining intellectual disability and lacrimal failure occur in 5/5; esophageal achalasia, a named syndrome feature, occurs in 3/5.
ID and nail/skin abnormalities define disease; urinary reflux and VSD each annotated 30-79%; common foot deformities omitted under four-axis cap.
Intellectual disability and seizures with characteristic hypogammaglobulinemia; frequency of structural skeletal involvement is unspecified.
Defining chondrodysplasia, hydrocephalus and microphthalmia; each supported by 80-99% phenotype frequencies.
Brain malformations and vision-impairing ocular coloboma define the syndrome; abnormal breathing does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Developmental and skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; hypodontia 2/4, cleft palate 1/3 and hearing loss 1/3. Cap excludes strabismus in 15/48.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis defect with encephalopathy; contractures in 7/7 support musculoskeletal involvement. Severe hepatic and cardiac findings in isolated reports do not establish >=30% frequency.
audit_reason: Remove hepatic: steatosis/failure reported in one assessed patient does not establish involvement in at least 30% or a major diagnostic criterion. Musculoskeletal involvement remains supported by contractures in 7/7.

basis: Developmental disability and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation do not establish skeletal injury.
An intracranial arterial aneurysm is vascular disease; brain injury after rupture is a potential complication rather than intrinsic established damage.
Developmental disability and limb abnormalities define syndrome; limited elbow extension in 4/5. Ptosis affects eyelid function in 2/5; hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
ALG13 glycosylation disorder with developmental epileptic encephalopathy; bleeding, hepatomegaly and optic atrophy in isolated cases do not establish common organ damage.
Defined by intellectual disability, cardiac abnormalities/heart failure and joint contractures with thumb abnormalities.
Skin aplasia 4/4; developmental delay 15/20 and callosal agenesis 2/4 support neurologic damage. Ocular damage is 1/4 or occasional despite the umbrella syndrome name.
Pituitary hormone dysfunction causes central hypothyroidism, frequent prolactin deficiency and altered pubertal development.
Inherited brain iron accumulation disorder with developmental impairment and neurodegeneration; optic atrophy is occasional (5-29%), and eye movement abnormalities are neurologic.
Intellectual disability and blepharophimosis define the syndrome; hearing loss 3/5, auditory canal stenosis 4/5, joint hypermobility 5/5; microdontia 2/4 omitted at cap.
Glycosylation disorder with encephalopathy; skeletal anomalies 80-99%, scoliosis and ocular defects 30-79%. Other broad HPO annotations do not establish organ damage.
Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; fixed foot deformities and distal muscle atrophy in 5/5; hearing impairment 1/5 is below threshold.
Pentose phosphate enzyme deficiency causing chronic hemolytic anemia. Splenic involvement is hematologic; hemolytic jaundice does not establish liver damage.
Defined by deep dermal/subcutaneous edema. The umbrella does not establish an immune mechanism; episodic mucosal swelling does not establish additional lasting organ damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: angioedema alone does not establish immune-mediated disease; this umbrella includes nonimmune bradykinin-mediated and drug-induced forms.

basis: Genetic parkinsonism with pyramidal tract dysfunction; spasticity and rigidity reflect neurologic disease rather than primary muscle damage.
Syndromic neurodevelopmental impairment; strabismus 7/7 supports ocular dysfunction. Reflux and nephrotic syndrome are separate diagnoses; hypotonia is neurologic.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss with cochlear malformation in 4/4 patients.
Microphthalmia with coloboma and intellectual disability define syndrome; kyphoscoliosis occurs in 4/4 patients.
Mutilating palmoplantar and periorificial keratoderma; reported blepharitis lacks sufficient frequency evidence for ocular involvement.
Non-syndromic intellectual disability; hypotonia is neurological. Broad thumbs alone do not establish skeletal damage; other organ findings occur in 1/5.
Defined by intellectual disability; developmental delay and seizures are neurologic manifestations.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease; strabismus affects 4/6 (~67%); optic atrophy only 1/6.
Glycosylation defect with universal neurodevelopmental impairment; strabismus occurs in 80-99%. Feeding difficulty, vomiting and reflux do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal injury.
audit_reason: Remove gastrointestinal: feeding aversion, vomiting and reflux do not establish direct intrinsic gastrointestinal damage. Retain ocular for common functional impairment from strabismus.

basis: Pituitary GH excess defines disease. Acral overgrowth (8/12) does not establish skeletal damage; skeletal abnormalities and visual-field defects are occasional; arthralgia 1/12.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: acral overgrowth occurs in 8/12, but skeletal disease is annotated as occasional (5-29%) and arthralgia occurs in 1/12; overgrowth alone does not establish locomotor damage.

basis: Growth hormone-secreting pituitary endocrine neoplasm; additional organ damage is not established by the supplied phenotype.
Red-cell aplasia with mandibulofacial dysostosis; conductive hearing loss and cleft palate each occur in 2/2 patients.
Defining skin and eye defects; cardiomyopathy/arrhythmia and structural brain abnormalities/developmental delay each reported in 1/2 patients.
Brittle sulfur-poor hair and severe neurodevelopmental disease 2/2; infections 2/2 with IgG1 deficiency 1/2; panhypopituitarism 1/2. Retinal/optic defects 1/2 omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: profound intellectual disability, cerebellar abnormalities and progressive microcephaly in 2/2 establish a core neurodevelopmental phenotype.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal dystrophy and optic nerve hypoplasia occur in 1/2, but are excluded by the four-organ cap.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: recurrent infections in 2/2 with documented chronic IgG1 deficiency in 1/2 support syndromic immunodeficiency, requiring the mechanism axis.

basis: Intellectual disability and cerebral abnormalities define the syndrome. Short stature and overweight do not establish skeletal or endocrine damage; ocular impairment is under 30%.
Intellectual disability and neurological dysfunction define it; strabismus in 2/5 supports ocular involvement. Hypotonia alone is not muscle damage.
Sterol biosynthesis disorder with neurologic defects; cataracts and aortic stenosis each 30-79%; less severe skin/renal anomalies omitted at four-axis cap.
Developmental brain disease and cardiac defects define syndrome; skeletal contractures in 2/2 and glaucoma in 1/2 support additional axes; samples small.
Neurodevelopmental and sacral defects define syndrome; strabismus 8/12, myopia 4/7 and hearing loss 5/9. Aplasia cutis 5/10 omitted at cap; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia and constipation do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage; swallowing dysfunction is attributable to neurologic impairment.
decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus in 8/12 and myopia in 4/7 establish common ocular dysfunction.

basis: Developmental disability and cardiac malformations define it. Skeletal defects reported in 3/3 and strabismus in 2/3; dental crowding (3/3) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Hearing loss 65%, scoliosis 65%/hip dysplasia 47%, anal atresia 53%; cap excludes choanal atresia 35% and thyroid dysfunction 35%.
Transient antenatal renal tubular salt-wasting disorder with characteristic sodium, potassium and chloride disturbances.
Glycosylation disorder with immunodeficiency and defining hepatopathy; intellectual disability/seizures in 6/11. Leukopenia 6/11 and splenic involvement omitted under cap.
Intellectual disability, early balding and patellar/acral abnormalities are defining features; hypogonadism causes endocrine dysfunction in 30-79%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: premature balding is a named, defining manifestation and occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypogonadism occurs in 30-79%; the three primary slots prioritize the defining intellectual, hair and skeletal abnormalities.

basis: Intellectual disability and speech delay define the disorder; hair and facial differences do not establish additional organ damage.
Intellectual disability affects 33/33; CNS malformations and seizures are frequent. Facial dysmorphism and hypotonia do not establish other organ damage.
KLHL15-related intellectual disability; developmental delay, seizures and cerebral malformations remain within the neurologic axis.
FRMPD4-related intellectual and motor developmental disorder; strabismus in 3/7 (~43%) supports ocular dysfunction, with limited sample size.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual developmental disorder.
Congenital absence of the vas deferens causes reproductive infertility; no affected organ belongs to the specified axes.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; mitral valve prolapse reported in 2/6. Reflux is separately diagnosed; flat feet alone do not establish locomotor damage.
Combined immunodeficiency with characteristic lymphopenia and neutropenia. Eczema affects roughly half of reported cases; recurrent infections alone do not establish other organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: characteristic lymphopenia and persistent or intermittent neutropenia are defining cellular defects, supporting blood-cell disease.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic eczematous dermatitis affects roughly half of reported patients and represents inflammatory skin disease, rather than a transient rash.

basis: Aortic aneurysm and skeletal connective-tissue disease define the syndrome; gingival overgrowth affects 2/3. Proptosis and ventriculomegaly alone do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: gingival overgrowth is direct structural involvement of the gums, reported in 2/3 patients (~67%).

basis: Defining elliptocytosis, hearing loss and nephrocalcinosis; cleft palate 2/2. Clubfoot (1/2) and PDA (1/1) omitted at cap; facial hypoplasia alone does not establish locomotor damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft hard palate/submucous cleft palate in 2/2 assessed patients is a direct structural oral defect, prioritized under the four-axis cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none under cap: clubfoot is reported in 1/2; palatal defects in 2/2 receive the fourth axis. Midface hypoplasia alone is dysmorphism without established locomotor impairment.

basis: Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis; chronic middle-ear disease occurs in 4/4. Recurrent infections reflect impaired clearance, not intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Defining immunodeficiency, microthrombocytopenia and eczema; frequent diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal tissue damage.
Intellectual disability and alpha-thalassemia define ATR-X; talipes and visual impairment each occur in 30-79%. Reflux (80-99%) alone does not establish direct GI damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: reflux is annotated in 80-99%, but direct GI injury or intrinsic dysmotility is not established by the supplied phenotype.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: talipes equinovarus is a structural skeletal defect occurring in 30-79%; spinal deformities provide additional support.

basis: Hereditary basement membrane nephropathy; hearing loss and anterior lenticonus each occur in 30-79%; hypertension is secondary to renal disease.
Inherited dental enamel hypoplasia and hypomaturation; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cutaneous interferonopathy; bronchiectasis 13/14 and colitis 9/14. Corneal scarring 7/14 and urethral stricture 5/14 omitted because of the cap.
Inherited mitochondrial iron-sulfur/heme metabolic defect causes defining anemia and cerebellar disease; ocular motor signs reflect neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: inherited mitochondrial iron-sulfur/heme metabolism defect warrants the metabolic mechanism axis. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/2802)

basis: Neural tube closure defects define disease; spina bifida includes defective vertebral arch formation, while anencephaly includes cranial and brain maldevelopment.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the spina bifida parent and anencephaly/spina bifida phenotype include defining vertebral or cranial skeletal defects.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease; renal, cardiac and small-fiber nerve damage in most. Common skin, cochleovestibular and intestinal involvement omitted at cap.
Loss of smell maps explicitly to neurologic function; nasal or infectious causes are not inherent to every case.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration, sensorineural deafness and optic atrophy are defining features; hearing impairment and optic atrophy occur in 80-99%.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is explicitly part of the disease definition and occurs in 80-99%; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.

basis: Defining contractures, ectodermal defects and oral clefts; developmental and cognitive impairment in 80-99%. Lacrimation abnormality in 80-99% omitted under cap.
Purine synthesis disorder with defining neurologic disease and deafness; optic atrophy in 80-99%. Infection susceptibility omitted at the four-axis cap.
Progressive cerebellar and pyramidal disease with adult dementia; manifestations remain within the neurologic axis.
Hereditary follicular atrophoderma and hypotrichosis with basal cell tumor predisposition; paraneoplastic Bazex findings and nonspecific anemia do not establish other involvement.
Unresolved gene/protein-like legacy entry without a disease phenotype; no organ assignment is defensible from 'tubulin, beta' alone.

decisions.neurologic: none: neither definition nor ancestors supply a neurologic phenotype; a tubulin name alone cannot establish neurologic disease.

basis: ID, hypogonadism and digital malformations define disease; ptosis/blepharophimosis occur in 30-79%. Sparse hair (80-99%) omitted at cap for functional eyelid abnormalities; hearing loss <30%.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis and blepharophimosis occur in 30-79% and affect eyelid function; prioritized over sparse hair at the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: sparse hair occurs in 80-99%, but functional eyelid abnormalities carry greater organ impact; retain the defining neurologic, endocrine and skeletal axes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: tapered fingers and short toes are in the disease definition; digital skeletal anomalies and toe contractures occur in 80-99%.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia with brachydactyly, abnormal thumbs and great toes, fibular overgrowth and bowlegs.
Mandibulofacial dysostosis, bilateral hearing loss and learning disability define the syndrome. Cardiac lesions occur in 5-29%; a high palate alone does not establish GI dysfunction.
Blistering, intellectual disability and digital malformations define the syndrome; corneal opacity occurs in 30-79%. Pneumonia is a separate infection; cardiac anomalies occur in 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual deficit is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: digital malformations are included in the definition; short and tapered fingers each occur in 30-79%.

basis: Isolated calvarial bone hyperostosis; no common neurologic or sensory-organ damage is established.
DMD-related isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; muscle histology and gene identity alone do not establish common skeletal muscle functional damage.
Phospholipid defect with cardiomyopathy and neutropenia; skeletal myopathy occurs in 80-99%. Oral ulcers in 30-79% omitted at the four-axis cap.
Early-onset nonsyndromic cataract directly affects the lens and vision.
Congenital cataracts and dental anomalies define syndrome; intellectual disability annotated 30-79%; isolated short metacarpals lack demonstrated impairment.
Congenital absence of central incisors; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Progressive cerebellar and peripheral nerve degeneration; scoliosis, pes cavus and distal amyotrophy occur in 30-79%. Abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Hereditary cerebellar ataxia with extrapyramidal dysfunction defines a neurologic disease.
Peripheral neuropathy with persistent distal amyotrophy and pes cavus in 80-99%; Achilles contractures in 5/8. Hearing impairment is below 30%.
Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; structural pes cavus and distal muscle atrophy occur in 30-79%. Ocular and hearing damage occur in <30%.
Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy and foot deformities occur in 30-79%; respiratory involvement is below 30%.
Axonal neuropathy and congenital scalp aplasia define the disorder; calvarial skull defects occur in 3/3 reported patients.
Cleft palate, coloboma and deafness define syndrome; urethral hypospadias occurs in 80-99%. Radioulnar synostosis (30-79%) omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a urethral malformation, within the renal axis, reported in 80-99%; occasional ectopic kidney is not the basis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: radioulnar synostosis qualifies at 30-79%, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent urethral malformation.

basis: ARSL enzyme deficiency causes skeletal dysplasia; mixed hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Airway disease, cord compression and developmental delay are under 30%.
X-linked skeletal dysplasia with punctate cartilage calcification and a metabolic classification. Skin and ocular disease vary by subtype and are not established across most of the umbrella.
Progressive degeneration of choroid, retinal pigment epithelium and retina; ocular vascular changes remain within the ocular axis.
Retinal degeneration, deafness and obesity define it; hypopituitarism occurs in 30-79%. Intellectual disability affects 5/5 reported patients, supporting neurologic involvement.
Intellectual disability, aphasia and spastic paraplegia define the neurologic phenotype; adducted thumbs are a defining structural feature.
Cleft palate, ankyloglossia and associated dental abnormalities affect the oral cavity; digital abnormalities are not established as common damaging manifestations.

Intellectual disability and progressive skeletal abnormalities define disease; hypodontia/dental defects occur in 80-99%; hearing impairment is annotated in 1/1, with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is documented in 1/1 assessed; supplied HPO frequency supports inclusion, although the small denominator limits confidence.

basis: Congenital interruption of the colonic lumen causing intestinal obstruction.
Retinal L- and M-cone dysfunction causes impaired color discrimination and visual acuity.
Inherited retinal cone photoreceptor dysfunction causing impaired red-green discrimination.
Inherited retinal cone dysfunction causes loss of red color discrimination.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with visual loss.
Inherited retinal cone degeneration; no established extraocular involvement.
Defined by callosal agenesis, infantile spasms and chorioretinal lacunae; vertebral/rib malformations and scoliosis are frequent (30–79%).
Callosal dysgenesis defines disease; pes planus 2/2 and radial dislocation 1/2; strabismus 1/2; congenital enteric aganglionosis with megacolon 1/2. Estimates are from very small samples.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: congenital enteric aganglionosis with megacolon occurs in 1/2; this is direct developmental bowel involvement, not merely a later disease risk.

basis: Defining skeletal and oral malformations; intellectual disability and sensorineural hearing loss each 30-79%. Common nail/hair dysplasia omitted by cap in favor of greater functional damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability is documented in 30-79% and represents persistent neurodevelopmental impairment.
decisions.dermatologic: none by cap: defining nail/hair dysplasia is common, but skeletal/oral malformations, intellectual disability and hearing loss have greater functional consequences.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment is documented in 30-79%; retained under the cap because it causes lasting functional loss.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia, hearing loss and oral/dental malformations define disease; pulmonary hypoplasia 80-99%; hydrocephalus 30-79% omitted because of cap.
Copper transport defect with cutis laxa and occipital exostoses; bladder diverticula 4/4. Neurologic, GI, vascular and hepatic manifestations omitted under the four-axis cap.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic primary for defining cutis laxa and hair abnormalities. Remove neurologic under the four-axis cap: neurological disease is generally milder in this subtype, while skeletal and bladder abnormalities are characteristic.

basis: The defining triad comprises scalp skin hypertrophy, thyroid aplasia and intellectual disability.
CNS malformation and intellectual disability; myopathy 30-79% and muscle atrophy 80-99%; persistent strabismus 80-99%.
Mixed hearing loss and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; delayed skeletal maturation alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Nonsyndromic hearing loss caused by structural inner ear abnormalities and stapes fixation.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; PRPS1 alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Defining progressive sensorineural deafness, dystonia/neurodegeneration and optic neuronopathy; optic atrophy is frequent (30-79%).
Congenital corneal dermoids cause opacity and visual impairment; definition explicitly excludes systemic abnormalities.
Autoimmune enteropathy and endocrinopathy define IPEX; eczematoid dermatitis occurs in 97/116 (~84%); autoimmune cytopenias and nephritis are under 30%.
Renal vasopressin resistance causes impaired urinary concentration and disordered water balance. Neurologic injury is not established as common.
X-linked Dyggve-Melchior-Clausen phenotype combines spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with intellectual disability.
Telomere disorder defined by nail dystrophy, skin pigmentation, oral leukoplakia and common marrow failure; cancer risks do not add axes.
Defining sweat gland and hair abnormalities with hypodontia and malformed teeth; endocrine abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Skin hyperextensibility and joint hypermobility define EDS; structural cardiovascular abnormalities annotated at 80-99%. Reflux is a separate condition.
Inherited susceptibility to persistent cutaneous HPV infection produces epidermodysplasia verruciformis lesions; later skin cancer is a risk.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease with peripheral retinal avascularity and retinal detachment; no extraocular involvement established.
Acromelic skeletal and joint abnormalities define disease; ptosis 9/16 (56%) and developmental delay 5/13 (38%). Hormone findings in one patient do not establish common endocrine damage.
