Intellectual disability and anal atresia (4/5) define FG1; optic nerve hypoplasia and auditory canal stenosis each 30-79%. Broad digits alone do not establish locomotor damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: broad digits and skeletal shape differences do not establish functional locomotor damage; hypotonia is attributable to the neurodevelopmental disorder.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal stenosis is a structural ear lesion reported in 30-79%; this supports involvement independently of cosmetic pinna differences.

basis: Congenital skeletal-muscle disorder with weakness and fingerprint inclusions; nonspecific metabolic annotation does not establish a metabolic disease.
Dermal, limb and eye malformations define syndrome; dental defects 30-79%. Neurologic features (ID 30-79%, microcephaly 80-99%) omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: microphthalmia and ocular colobomas (30-79%) are characteristic malformations in the defining skin-limb-eye syndrome.

basis: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis is an immune/complement-mediated glomerular disease; no common extrarenal damage is established.
Lysosomal storage with renal failure and cerebral degeneration in the original reported patient (1/1); extremely limited case numbers constrain frequency estimates.
audit_reason: Add renal and neurologic involvement: tissue storage caused progressive renal failure and cerebral degeneration in the original patient ([case report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3786260/)). These are direct disease manifestations.

basis: Hepatic glycogen metabolism disorder with hepatomegaly in 10/15 and biochemical liver injury; reduced erythrocyte enzyme activity does not establish blood-cell damage.
Congenital cerebral granulomas localize to brain; supplied evidence does not establish an infectious, immune or metabolic cause.
Inherited phagocyte oxidative-burst defect; intrinsic granulomatous bowel inflammation affects roughly 30-50%, especially X-linked disease. Secondary organ infections are separate diagnoses.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intrinsic granulomatous enterocolitis affects approximately 30-50%; it reflects CGD inflammatory dysfunction rather than coincidental inflammatory bowel disease.

basis: Factor VIII coagulation deficiency; recurrent hemarthrosis (96/151, ~64%) directly damages joints. Bruising and mucosal bleeding alone do not establish other organ damage.
Inherited coagulation disorder with an explicitly defining vascular abnormality; no evidence supports additional common organ damage.
Factor IX deficiency; recurrent hemarthroses cause joint damage (80-99% annotated). Intracranial hemorrhage is clinically uncommon despite the supplied HPO frequency.
Proliferation of hematopoietic cells; supplied phenotypes localize the disorder to blood and blood-forming tissues.
Congenital structural defect of the diaphragm, a skeletal muscle. Common intrinsic lung or bowel damage is not established for the anterior subtype.
Congenital cardiac and splenic defects define heterotaxy; asplenia occurs in 7/12. Anal atresia occurs in 1/2, supporting GI involvement with limited sampling.

decisions.haematologic: primary: splenic absence/malformation is a defining heterotaxy feature; asplenia occurs in 7/12 and eliminates splenic function.

basis: Seizures and hemiparesis establish neurologic disease. Hemi­atrophy and unspecified skeletal abnormalities lack anatomical detail or frequency to establish another axis.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: unspecified skeletal abnormality and hemiatrophy have no frequencies or supporting definition; a defining skeletal lesion or damage in at least 30% is not established.

basis: Holoprosencephaly and congenital joint contractures define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%; renal anomalies occur in 5-29%.
Hydrocephalus and severe neurologic dysfunction define HSAS; characteristic adducted thumbs and structural thumb contractures are defining features, reported in 20/20.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: adducted thumbs are explicitly part of the disease definition, with structural thumb contractures documented in 20/20.

basis: Cerebellar agenesis, ataxia and intellectual disability with cataracts are defining features; each occurs in 80-99%.
Glycerol metabolism defect; developmental delay 12/14 (~86%) and intellectual disability 2/4 support neurologic involvement. Complex deletions enrich these data; pancreatitis 1/4 excluded.

decisions.neurologic: involved: supplied HPO reports developmental delay in 12/14 (~86%) and intellectual disability in 2/4; these exceed 30%, despite enrichment for complex deletions.

basis: Congenital generalized hair overgrowth defines the disorder; dental anomalies and deafness are kindred-specific, and scoliosis occurs in 5-29%.
Congenital growth hormone deficiency with absent B cells and hypogammaglobulinemia in 3/4 patients; delayed bone maturation is not independent skeletal damage.
Hypogonadism, intellectual disability and congenital vertebral/rib anomalies define the syndrome; diabetes also falls within the endocrine axis.
Parathyroid agenesis causes hormone deficiency and hypocalcemia; provoked seizures and hypercalciuria do not establish brain or kidney damage.
Defining renal phosphate wasting, hypophosphatemia and rickets. Dentin defects/odontodysplasia occur in 30-79%; nephrocalcinosis is often treatment-related.
Inherited renal tubular urate-handling defect causing hypouricemia.
Sterol biosynthesis disorder defined by ichthyosiform skin lesions and limb defects; isolated renal agenesis report does not establish common renal involvement.
Steroid sulfatase deficiency causes sterol metabolic dysfunction and ichthyosis. ADHD (30-79%) is a separate associated diagnosis; corneal deposits usually do not impair vision.

decisions.neurologic: none: ADHD at 30-79% is a separately diagnosed association, not established direct neurologic injury; intellectual disability occurs in only 2/35.

basis: Ichthyosis defines skin involvement and male hypogonadism defines gonadal endocrine dysfunction.
Inherited immunodeficiency with abnormal T-cell function and recurrent infections; no common lasting organ injury is established.
CD40L immunodeficiency; intrinsic neutropenia in 39/62 (63%) and oral ulceration in 25/56 (45%). Separately diagnosed infections excluded; cholangitis occurs in 20%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent oral ulceration represents mucosal breakdown in 25/56 (45%), associated with intrinsic neutropenia; mouth belongs to this axis.

basis: Inherited immunodeficiency with abnormal lymphocyte proliferation; lymphoma and hemophagocytic syndromes are separate diagnoses, not additional organ labels.
IgM-level quantitative trait; no defined immunodeficiency, immune-mediated disease or other qualifying organ disease is documented.
audit_reason: Remove infectious_immune: an inherited IgM-level trait alone does not establish infection, immunodeficiency, autoimmunity or lymphoma. The record documents no qualifying disease axis.

basis: Multiple impacted and supernumerary teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Poorly specified hereditary retinoblastoma-related concept; retinal tumor association supports ocular assignment, but the imprinting phenotype is unclear.
Skin and dental dysplasia characterize IP. Corneal opacity and seizures each occur in 30-79% by HPO, supporting ocular and neurologic involvement despite the broader definition's wording.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental abnormalities are characteristic ectodermal defects explicitly included in the definition; hypodontia and abnormal dental morphology occur in 30-79%.

basis: ARX developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; microphthalmia reported in only 1/1 does not establish ocular damage in >=30% across this disorder.
Iris hypoplasia and hereditary glaucoma directly affect the eye; the neurological ancestor does not establish extraocular nervous-system disease.
Familial neonatal obstructive/nonhemolytic jaundice indicates hepatobiliary dysfunction; no specific metabolic defect or other organ damage is established.
GnRH deficiency and olfactory developmental defects define ANOS1-related Kallmann syndrome; unilateral renal agenesis occurs in approximately 30%.
GnRH deficiency with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, olfactory developmental defects and spastic paraplegia; common renal involvement is not established.
Follicular hyperkeratosis and scarring alopecia define disease. Photophobia alone is insufficient; damaging corneal disease is recognized but not established in at least 30%.

decisions.ocular: none: keratitis and corneal dystrophy are reported without frequencies; characteristic photophobia does not establish damaging ocular disease in at least 30%.

basis: Generalized follicular keratosis, alopecia and cerebral atrophy define the syndrome. Proportionate dwarfism alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine pathology.
Permanent laryngeal paralysis and intellectual disability define the syndrome; obligate bronchiectasis falls within the pulmonary axis.
Alport nephropathy, sensorineural deafness and esophageal leiomyomatosis define syndrome; cataract occurs in 3/4. Airway leiomyomatosis is occasional (<30%).

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural deafness is explicitly part of the defining Alport phenotype, with HPO frequency 30-79%.

basis: Lesch-Nyhan-like neurologic syndrome with hyperuricemia despite normal HGPRT; no evidence of common direct renal damage.
Malignant hematopoietic blasts occupy marrow and peripheral blood; additional organ infiltration is not consistently common across this umbrella.
Inherited proximal tubulopathy with proteinuria and nephrocalcinosis; urinary calcium loss does not establish a separate systemic metabolic disorder.
Inherited transport/metabolic disorder with cataracts and renal tubulopathy; intellectual disability and neurologic dysfunction 80-99%. Skeletal disease (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Inherited dystrophy of the retinal macula.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and azoospermia affect reproductive function; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Hereditary bipolar affective disorder; purely psychiatric phenotype despite neurological ancestry.
Isolated developmental abnormality of the cornea and anterior eye segment; associated complications remain ocular.
Skeletal dysplasia; airway malacia 2/2, urinary obstruction 1/1 and hearing impairment 1/1 support involvement, although samples are small. Cardiac prevalence is uncertain.

decisions.renal: involved: ureteral stenosis and hydronephrosis each reported in 1/1 assessed; obstructive urinary malformations are recognized syndrome features, with small-sample uncertainty.

basis: Copper disorder with neurodegeneration and marked skeletal/connective tissue defects; vascular dilatation 80-99%, arterial stenosis 30-79%. Hair/skin abnormalities (80-99%) omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: vascular dilatation occurs in 80-99% and arterial stenosis in 30-79%; intrinsic vascular disease can cause severe injury.
decisions.dermatologic: none: characteristic hair/skin changes occur in 80-99%, but omitted at cap to retain more consequential skeletal and vascular damage.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: marked connective tissue anomalies define Menkes disease; joint hypermobility and chest/abdominal muscle defects occur in 80-99%.

basis: Intellectual disability, seizures and psoriasiform dermatitis define the syndrome, each annotated 30-79%; an immune mechanism is not established by psoriasiform morphology.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: the evidence establishes psoriasiform dermatitis, which does not by itself establish psoriasis or an immune-mediated syndrome.

basis: Intellectual disability defines it; muscle atrophy 80-99%, alopecia 30-79%, and urethral hypospadias 30-79% support involvement. Renal hypoplasia itself is uncommon.
audit_reason: Add renal involvement: urethral hypospadias is frequent (30-79%) and is a direct urinary malformation. Occasional renal hypoplasia does not negate this qualifying manifestation.

basis: Intellectual disability and dystonia define this neurological syndrome; spasticity, dysarthria and seizures also belong to the neurologic axis.
Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal disease define the syndrome; atrial septal defect is annotated at 30-79%. Dental crowding and high palate alone do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental crowding (5/6) and high palate (5/5) establish morphology, without demonstrated dental loss, oral dysfunction or tissue damage

basis: IQSEC2-related intellectual disability and epilepsy; ocular findings are occasional or lack qualifying frequencies.
Cobalamin metabolic disorder with defining neurodevelopmental impairment; intellectual disability is an explicit parent and synonym, with developmental delay in 12/14 and seizures in 9/14.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is an explicit parent and synonym; developmental delay in 12/14 and seizures in 9/14 support a core neurodevelopmental phenotype.

basis: Severe intellectual disability and epilepsy define the syndrome; recurrent infections (30-79%) do not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Intellectual disability and language-development impairment define the disorder; dysmorphic features do not establish other organ dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability and developmental delay; isolated minor skeletal findings do not establish substantial skeletal disease.
Defining severe intellectual disability, optic atrophy and profound hearing impairment; structural joint abnormalities are occasional.
Intellectual disability, spastic paraplegia, palmoplantar keratoderma and pes cavus are defining features; cone-shaped epiphyses occur in 80-99%. Ocular findings are occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: bilateral pes cavus is explicitly part of the defining syndrome; cone-shaped epiphyses (80-99%) and frequent digital/joint abnormalities reinforce skeletal disease.

basis: Severe intellectual disability defines the syndrome; seizures occur in 35%; other organ abnormalities lack established qualifying frequencies.
Polyamine disorder with intellectual disability, osteoporosis and kyphoscoliosis; cleft palate 30-79%, dental crowding 2/2; ptosis 2/2 omitted at cap.
Intellectual disability and hypogonadism/obesity define the syndrome; structural foot deformities occur in 80-99%. Microtia alone does not establish hearing loss.
Intellectual disability, patellar abnormalities and abnormal dentition define the syndrome; ocular dysfunction, including strabismus and abnormal fundus, occurs in 30–79%.
Skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability define it; intrinsic glucose intolerance in 3/4 cases supports endocrine involvement. Anal atresia is below 30%.
Congenital fusion and shortening of the fourth and fifth metacarpals; explicitly nonsyndromic.
Intellectual disability and spastic quadriparesis define a neurologic syndrome; spasticity alone does not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Syndromic microphthalmia with intellectual disability; scoliosis, syndactyly and pectus deformity each reported in 4/4. Other visceral defects lack frequency support.
Eye and skin defects define syndrome; cardiac defects/cardiomyopathy 30-79%; diaphragmatic defects 80-99% support muscle involvement; hearing loss <30%.
Poorly characterized modifier concept; its name and sole phenotype identify nervous-system dysfunction, with no evidence for other organs.
Storage disease defined by skeletal and cardiac involvement; neurologic deterioration 30-79%. Cap omits common airway dysfunction, hearing loss and retinal degeneration.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac involvement is explicitly defining; abnormal heart morphology occurs in 80-99%, with valve abnormalities in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal abnormalities define the disease; dysostosis multiplex occurs in 99/126 and limited joint mobility in 80-99%.

basis: Muscular dystrophy with defining cardiomyopathy; both skeletal and cardiac muscle disease are intrinsic.
Muscular dystrophy with a limb-girdle phenotype; no evidence establishing another affected organ.
Muscular dystrophy is a primary degenerative skeletal muscle disorder; no evidence establishes additional organ involvement.
Progressive muscular dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle; a neuromuscular classification alone does not establish nerve involvement.
Skeletal and cardiac muscle degeneration define DMD; cognitive impairment reported in 80-99%; respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness.
Muscular dystrophy, contractures and cardiac conduction or myocardial disease define Emery-Dreifuss dystrophy. Neurogenic and treatment-related complications are not inferred.
Leukopenia and abnormal neutrophil maturation with recurrent bacterial and viral infections support hematologic and immune insufficiency.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; ventilation is required in ~80% because of respiratory muscle weakness, without established direct lung damage. Pneumonia is a separate disease.
Autophagic skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency and extraocular movement limitation occur in only 5-29%.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Intellectual disability, visual impairment and sensorineural deafness occur in 80-99%; leukemia is a separately diagnosed malignancy associated with the syndrome.
Inherited proximal renal tubulopathy with nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis and progressive renal failure.
Inherited progressive sensory peripheral neuropathy with loss of myelinated nerve fibers.
Axonal neuropathy; hearing loss in 3/7 (~43%); pes cavus in 80-99% and scoliosis/kyphosis in 30-79%. Elevated transaminases alone do not establish liver disease.
NYX-related retinal dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness, commonly with high myopia.
Cochlear abnormalities, intellectual disability and venous insufficiency each 30-79%; hearing loss is age-dependent despite its 5-29% HPO annotation.
Congenital ocular motor disorder causing nystagmus and reduced visual acuity; no additional neurologic dysfunction established.
Hereditary localized loss of occipital hair pigmentation; no additional organ disease described.
Congenital umbilical abdominal-wall closure defect with herniated bowel; no intrinsic skeletal muscle or locomotor connective-tissue disease is established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: an umbilical closure defect does not by itself establish skeletal muscle or locomotor connective-tissue disease.

basis: Ophthalmoplegia, myopia and chorioretinal degeneration define the ocular disorder; frequency of associated neurologic abnormalities is unspecified.
Hereditary optic nerve degeneration with visual loss; additional neurologic manifestations are occasional, 5-29%, below threshold.
Purine-metabolism disorder defined by peripheral neuropathy and profound deafness; progressive optic neuropathy/atrophy occurs in 80-99%; muscle wasting reflects denervation.
Optic atrophy and spastic paraplegia define the syndrome; abnormal glucose tolerance has unspecified frequency.
Oral, digital and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define OFD1; polycystic kidney dysplasia in 3/7. Common milia/alopecia omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Urea-cycle defect; hyperammonemic encephalopathy and seizures occur in 30-79%; hepatic failure is annotated in 80-99%. Splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ damage.
Skeletal, hearing and palatal defects define the named triad; cleft palate 18/18. Intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%, retained as involved under the three-primary cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: palatal defects define the named syndrome; cleft palate occurs in 18/18 and tooth agenesis in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%; the three primary slots retain the defining skeletal, ear and palatal triad.

basis: Ovarian endocrine failure with increased gonadotropins; distinct from purely reproductive structural disease.
Developmental disability, oral clefts and skeletal malformations define syndrome; esotropia 80-99%; acne and hair abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Parkinsonism and intellectual disability define the disorder; persistent strabismus affects ocular alignment in 30–79%.
Defined by digital and mandibular skeletal abnormalities together with cleft palate and glossoptosis affecting oral structures.
Cardiac defects, clubfoot and Robin/cleft palate define it; neurodevelopmental impairment 30-79%; hepatic failure reported in 1/2, omitted by cap.
Combined pituitary hormone deficiency defines the disease; no common additional organ damage is established.
Inherited complement immunodeficiency; meningococcal infection is a separately diagnosed consequence, not intrinsic neurologic damage from properdin deficiency.
CNS hypomyelination defines PMD. Visual impairment in 80-99% can be central; optic atrophy in one assessed patient does not establish common ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent visual impairment does not distinguish central dysfunction from ocular injury; optic atrophy in 1/1 does not establish its usual frequency.

basis: Joint contractures, amyoplasia and cutaneous webs define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia is a common, major lethal manifestation.
Pyruvate oxidation defect defined by lactic acidosis and neurodevelopmental dysfunction; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage.
Radial reduction and anorectal/urethral malformations define syndrome; hydrocephalus occurs in 80-99%. Hypospadias affects the urethra, within the renal axis.

decisions.renal: primary: hypospadias is a defining urethral malformation; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.

basis: Inherited abnormal radiosensitivity of natural killer immune activity; no additional organ damage is established.
Androgen resistance defines the endocrine disorder. Hypospadias is a urethral malformation, annotated 30-79% and perineal hypospadias 5/5; urethra belongs to renal.

decisions.renal: involved: frequent hypospadias directly affects urethral anatomy (30-79%; perineal form 5/5); the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.

basis: Reticuloendothelial disorder with anemia and splenic involvement. Hepatomegaly and jaundice alone do not establish direct hepatic injury; frequencies are unspecified.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatosplenomegaly and jaundice lack evidence of functional hepatic injury or damaging infiltration; jaundice does not distinguish hepatic disease from hemolysis.

basis: Inherited retinal dysplasia with falciform retinal folds; retinal disease belongs to the ocular axis.
RP2-related retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction, visual field loss and chorioretinal atrophy.
Inherited retinal splitting and macular degeneration cause progressive visual impairment; complications remain within the ocular axis.
Scoliosis affects ~52% and muscle atrophy 30-79%; central breathing abnormalities are neurologic; constipation/reflux alone do not establish direct GI damage.
Silver-Russell phenotype includes growth restriction and skeletal/body asymmetry; additional organ dysfunction is not established for this X-linked subtype.
Skeletal defects, cutis laxa and intellectual disability define syndrome; ptosis/strabismus occur in 30-79%. Enamel defects omitted at cap; hepatic adenoma is a separate neoplasm.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: enamel defects occur in 30-79% but are omitted at the four-axis cap, prioritizing ocular functional impairment.
decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis and strabismus are annotated in 30-79%, supporting common eyelid and ocular motor dysfunction.

basis: Intellectual disability, movement disorder, deafness and ophthalmoplegia define the syndrome; renal abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Combined immunodeficiency with a defining T-lymphocyte defect and reduced CD4/CD8 populations supports immune and blood-cell axes. Associated respiratory infections are separate diseases.
audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary: the defining T-lymphocyte developmental and functional defect is a blood-cell disorder, requiring this mechanism axis alongside infectious_immune. Associated respiratory infections remain separate diseases.

basis: Skeletal abnormalities and characteristic macroglossia define the syndrome; renal dysplasia and VSD annotated 80-99%. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not demonstrate damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic macroglossia is part of the defining overgrowth phenotype; cleft palate additionally supports structural oral involvement.

basis: Spastic neurodegeneration and sensorineural deafness define disease; cataract/visual impairment and hypogonadism each occur in 30-79%.
Inherited leukodystrophy; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Bladder and bowel symptoms reflect neural dysfunction without documented intrinsic urinary or intestinal injury.
Synonyms identify an inherited visuospatial/neurocognitive phenotype; the supplied nervous-system annotation supports the neurological axis.
Motor neuron degeneration and defining muscle wasting (80-99%); functional androgen resistance in ~86%. Diabetes and lipid disorders are minority or separate diagnoses.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hormonal evidence of partial androgen resistance in 86%, beyond reproductive signs alone. [Endocrine study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12161529/)
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: proximal and bulbar muscle wasting is explicitly defining; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Congenital skeletal malformations of the hands and feet; no established extra-skeletal organ damage.
Vertebral and epiphyseal dysplasia with premature osteoarthritis; unquantified corneal opacity does not establish common ocular involvement.
Primary skeletal dysplasia with vertebral and metaphyseal abnormalities and contractures; associated intellectual disability lacks a demonstrated frequency of at least 30%.
Inherited structural tooth abnormalities; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Selective congenital tooth absence defines disease; maxillary aplasia reported in 5/5 supports associated skeletal involvement. No common skin disease is established.
Defining cardiac/pericardial, sternal, diaphragmatic and abdominal wall defects; pulmonary hypoplasia 30-79%. Omphalocele is an abdominal wall defect without established intrinsic bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the defining omphalocele is an abdominal wall defect; herniated bowel location alone does not establish bowel disease or dysfunction.

basis: Inherited platelet deficiency; bleeding signs reflect thrombocytopenia. WAS mutation alone does not establish clinically significant immunodeficiency.
Thrombocytopenia and glomerular renal disease define the syndrome; elevated IgA alone does not establish immunodeficiency or an autoimmune mechanism.
Platelet dysfunction, thrombocytopenia, thalassemic anemia and splenomegaly are hematologic; petechiae do not establish separate skin damage.
Congenital thumb contracture/deformity; unspecified nervous-system findings lack evidence of common direct injury.
Neurodegenerative basal ganglia disorder causing dystonia and parkinsonism; swallowing and respiratory complications are occasional.
Muscular torticollis, keloids and renal dysplasia define syndrome; frequencies of additional vascular and neurologic abnormalities are unspecified.
Craniosynostosis and developmental delay define the syndrome; ventricular septal defect reported in 30-79%, based on very few patients.
Defining congenital limb defects include ulnar hypoplasia, absent fingers and split feet.
Hereditary variation in green color perception; supplied phenotype identifies the eye.
GI, vertebral/limb and cardiac defects are major criteria; airway involvement includes tracheoesophageal fistula in 11/11. Renal defects and variable hydrocephalus omitted under the cap.
Inherited multivalvular dysplasia with regurgitation; extracardiac findings are occasional or very rare.
Intellectual disability, chorioretinal atrophy and keratosis/anhidrosis define the syndrome; skeletal deformities are also defining features.
Inherited vesicoureteral reflux directly affects the urinary tract.
Inherited haemostatic disorder characterized by abnormal bleeding and prolonged bleeding time.
Sparse record identifies a hairline-related syndrome; dermatologic assignment is provisional, with no evidence establishing other organ involvement.
Neurodevelopmental disability, congenital contractures and muscle atrophy define syndrome. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic; structural eye findings are occasional.
Defining triad: cervical vertebral fusion, Duane ocular motility disorder and congenital sensorineural deafness.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration.
Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; no common extranodal organ damage established for this subtype.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and male infertility affect reproductive function without established endocrine dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Gonadal dysgenesis causes deficient gonadal hormone production and hypogonadism; the anomalous cardiomyopathy parent does not establish cardiac involvement.
Isolated spermatogenic failure causes azoospermia and infertility; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Germ cell/sex cord-stromal tumor of reproductive gonads; endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Hereditary excessive hair growth on the pinnae; no intrinsic hearing or vestibular disorder.
Apparent gene/enzyme entry without a defined disease or phenotype; supplied information supports no organ assignment.
Arrhythmogenic myocardial disease classified as an inborn mitochondrial metabolic disorder; extracardiac structural abnormalities are rare.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder defined by optic atrophy and neurologic dystonia/striatal disease.
Mitochondrial myopathy and diabetes define disease; pyramidal dysfunction is supported by Babinski sign (1/1) and lower-limb hyperreflexia (30-79%). Neuropathy is only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: Babinski sign plus frequent lower-limb hyperreflexia (30-79%) supports central motor-pathway dysfunction; inclusion does not depend on occasional neuropathy.

basis: Mitochondrial disease with infantile striatal degeneration. Retinal dysfunction and muscle histology lack frequencies; ophthalmoparesis may reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Retinal degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; mitochondrial inheritance alone adds no metabolic axis.
Inherited syndrome defined by magnesium and lipid abnormalities plus hypertension; renal damage is not established by hypomagnesemia alone.
Infantile hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects heart muscle; no additional organ disease is established.
Defined by recurrent functional gastrointestinal vomiting; migraine association does not establish neurologic damage or endocrine disease.
Isolated sensorineural hearing loss caused by an inherited mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder defined by myopathy; respiratory insufficiency is muscular, while intrinsic neurologic and liver abnormalities are occasional.
Ataxia and polyneuropathy define neurologic disease; supplied ancestry explicitly classifies the underlying disorder among inborn errors of metabolism.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the supplied ancestry explicitly identifies an inborn metabolic disorder, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Mitochondrial myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia are defining manifestations.
The supplied phenotype identifies chloramphenicol-associated aplastic anemia and marrow toxicity as the defining organ injury.
Mitochondrial diabetes and sensorineural deafness define disease; intrinsic retinal degeneration with field constriction in 20/20 supports ocular involvement. Cardiomyopathy is occasional.
Mitochondrial enteropathy with defining renal insufficiency; hepatic steatosis is a defining feature, frequency unreported. Later neurologic, ocular and hearing frequencies are unknown.

decisions.renal: primary: renal insufficiency is explicitly included among the syndrome's defining manifestations, rather than described as a later complication.

basis: Mitochondrial disorder with defining ocular myopathy and pigmentary retinopathy; heart block 80-99%. Ataxia and hearing loss (30-79%) omitted under cap.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary for defining extraocular skeletal myopathy. Move cardiovascular to involved to respect the primary cap; retain common severe heart block. Remove neurologic under the total cap because defining muscle involvement takes priority.

basis: Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder causing optic neuropathy and visual loss; extraocular neuropathy, myopathy and arrhythmia are each below 30%.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy and lactic acidosis define MELAS; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Visual loss may be cortical; cardiac damage less common.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with epilepsy and ragged-red fibers; sensorineural hearing loss in 80-99%. Optic atrophy and lipomas in 30-79% omitted by cap.
Inborn metabolic disease causes recurrent skeletal muscle destruction; direct myoglobin-related renal impairment is described as common, supporting approximately 30% or more.
Mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis; cardiomyopathy and renal insufficiency each 30-79%; developmental delay omitted under cap; ophthalmoplegia reflects muscle disease.
Chronic tubulointerstitial nephropathy directly damages renal tubules and interstitium; no extrarenal involvement is established.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder defined by neuropathy, ataxia and retinopathy; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Neurogenic weakness does not establish muscle damage.
Mitochondrial form of parkinsonian neurodegeneration; no defined systemic metabolic disorder or common additional organ damage is provided.
Mitochondrial marrow-pancreas disease with acidosis; hepatic failure 3/5. Renal, cardiac, neurologic and corneal involvement (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Tubulopathy, diabetes and cerebellar disease define syndrome; retinopathy/blindness in 1/1. Myopathy, osteoporosis and deafness also reported, omitted by cap.
Inherited mitochondrial disorder manifesting as isolated sensorineural hearing loss; explicit oxidative-phosphorylation ancestry supports the metabolic mechanism.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the record explicitly classifies this as an inborn mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation disorder; a systemic phenotype is not required.

basis: Diabetes and optic atrophy define Wolfram; hearing loss ~60% and neurologic dysfunction ~50-60% in the broader syndrome. Subtype frequencies uncertain; urinary disease excluded at cap.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly 60% in Wolfram overall; diabetes and optic atrophy are the core diagnostic features.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defined by vertebral flattening, scoliosis and finger contractures.
Diabetes, heart defects and pancreatic hypoplasia with exocrine failure define disease; developmental delay 7/15 (~47%); diaphragm defects omitted at cap; gallbladder absence 4/15 (<30%).
Skeletal dysplasia with delayed ossification; dental eruption failure and oligodontia reported in 1/1 assessed patient, with uncertain prevalence. Isolated Chiari finding excluded.
Bladder evagination and pelvic, pelvic-floor and abdominal-wall defects define the condition. Anal positional anomalies alone do not establish bowel damage; UTIs are separate infections.
PRPF8-related retinal degeneration; reported manifestations remain ocular.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss with possible vestibular dysfunction; both belong to the otologic axis.
Inherited prion neurodegeneration; dysautonomia, dysphagia and sleep apnea reflect neural dysfunction rather than direct damage to additional organs.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inherited PRNP-associated protein misfolding causes this disease; potential prion transmissibility does not establish an infectious etiology in affected families.

basis: Familial infantile myeloid leukemia affects marrow and circulating myeloid cells.
Vitamin D activation defect causes mineral imbalance and defining rachitic skeletal damage; hepatic enzyme localization does not imply liver injury.
Prostatic hyperplasia affects a reproductive organ. Urinary symptoms or outflow obstruction do not establish direct urinary-tract injury in at least 30%.

decisions.renal: none: prostate has no axis; urinary symptoms alone do not demonstrate urinary-tract damage. Retention, bladder injury and obstructive nephropathy are not established in >=30%.

basis: Familial enlargement of red blood cells; nonspecific homeostasis annotation does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Agenesis of endocrine pancreatic beta cells causes neonatal insulin-dependent diabetes; exocrine pancreatic disease is not established.
Chondrodysplasia and gonadal endocrine failure define it; CNS hypoplasia occurs in 3/4 and ocular malformations in 2/2. Nail dysplasia omitted at cap.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia. Developmental delay and microcephaly are reported without frequencies or established major diagnostic status.

decisions.neurologic: none: unquantified developmental delay and microcephaly do not establish involvement in at least 30% or a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Defining developmental impairment, skeletal maturation abnormalities and muscle fiber disproportion. Constipation (80-99%) alone does not establish intrinsic bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation occurs in 80-99%, but no direct intestinal injury or established primary motility disorder is documented.

basis: Nonsyndromic KCNQ4-related hearing loss.
CRB1-related retinal degeneration with progressive visual loss; findings are confined to the ocular axis.
Inherited ELOVL4-related macular dystrophy with macular atrophy and impaired vision.
PRKN-associated degeneration of dopaminergic motor pathways; rigidity and gait abnormalities reflect neurologic disease rather than primary muscle damage.
Neurodevelopmental speech and language disorder with verbal apraxia; hearing is explicitly normal.
Warburg micro syndrome is defined by severe neurodevelopmental abnormalities, cataracts/microphthalmia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Plasmalogen synthesis defect with defining rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia and cataracts; severe developmental impairment occurs in most patients.
Intellectual disability and hypogonadism define disease; skeletal defects/bone loss and severe hearing loss each occur in 80-99%. Ocular anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: none: defining ocular malformations qualify, but frequency is unspecified; the cap prioritizes severe hearing loss and skeletal disease documented in 80-99%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: reduced bone density, kyphosis and genu valgum occur in 80-99%, establishing common structural skeletal disease.

basis: Septal, eyelid and radial defects define syndrome; anal atresia/malposition in 30-79%. Hearing and additional neurologic abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Generalized epilepsy defined by frequent absence seizures; pallor and seizure-associated movements do not establish other organ damage.
TULP1-related rod-cone retinal degeneration; retinal dysfunction and cataracts are documented in all five annotated patients.
PRPF31-associated retinal degeneration causes progressive visual impairment.
Cerebral arteriopathy, leukoencephalopathy and premature alopecia define CARASIL; alopecia 5/6. Intrinsic spondylosis and localized osteoporosis occur in 30-79%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: premature scalp alopecia is a defining clinical hallmark explicitly included in the definition, supported by 5/6 patients.

basis: Neuronal lysosomal storage disease; progressive visual loss in 6/6 supplied cases supports ocular involvement, although the northern epilepsy variant may spare vision.
Defined by caudal skeletal, anorectal and urinary malformations. Individual neural abnormalities occur in 1/4; aggregate neurologic frequency is unclear.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly are defining features; developmental delay 12/12 and intellectual disability 13/19. Renal hypoplasia only 1/12.
Defining cervical skin webbing, intellectual disability and digital skeletal anomalies; persistent eyelid ptosis occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: pterygium colli is an obligate congenital skin web and a named defining feature; primary structural malformations do not require acquired skin injury.

basis: Isolated bilateral small eyes; no other organ involvement established for this concept.
Parathyroid hormone excess; skeletal bone loss is common (about 30% or more); kidney stones are a minority and separately diagnosed.
Complete absence of gonads entails loss of their endocrine function as well as reproductive function.
Congenital motor neuronopathy with defining muscle atrophy and fixed joint contractures; arthrogryposis occurs in 15/20 and scoliosis in 12/20.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital muscle atrophy and fixed contractures define this phenotype; arthrogryposis affects 75% and scoliosis 60%.

basis: Pachygyria, arachnoid cysts, intellectual disability and epilepsy define a neurologic disorder; skeletal involvement lacks supporting frequency.
Sensorineural hearing loss and hair pigmentation abnormalities in 36/36; iris heterochromia does not establish ocular damage.
Venous malformations occupying skin and oral mucosa define the condition. Intestinal bleeding alone does not establish common intestinal involvement.
COL9A2-related epiphyseal cartilage and joint disease; tooth agenesis occurs in only 1/4 reported patients.
Hereditary multiple osteochondromas are bone lesions.
Cerebellar ataxia and sensory neuropathy affect the central and peripheral nervous systems; impaired pursuit does not establish ocular disease.
Cerebellar degeneration defines SCA5; nystagmus and impaired pursuit reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than primary eye damage.
Inherited palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with blistering and ulceration; associated tinea is a separate infection.
Defining oculomaxillofacial cleft affects facial skeleton, upper lip/palate and lower eyelid/orbit; cleft palate and microphthalmia are reported.
Craniosynostosis, glaucoma and severe developmental delay define the syndrome; cardiac malformations occur in 30-79%. Cleft palate/dental defects (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Named BOR-Duane-hydrocephalus syndrome defines ear, urinary and CNS abnormalities; Duane ocular motility defect is a defining component. Trapezius aplasia omitted by cap.
Eye dermoids/skin aplasia define OES; CNS malformations 80-99%, bowel aganglionosis 30-79%. Cap omits hearing, renal, cardiac, laryngeal and skeletal defects.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: aganglionic megacolon is reported in 30-79% and directly impairs intestinal function; its severity supports retention under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment qualifies at 30-79%, but the four-axis cap prioritizes similarly frequent, more severe aganglionic bowel disease.

basis: Tarsus denotes the eyelid tarsal plate; eyelid hypoplasia and absent lower eyelashes define this ocular adnexal syndrome.
Severe polycystic renal disease and TSC define the syndrome; cortical and cutaneous lesions are major TSC criteria. Lymphangioleiomyomatosis is not common across all patients.
Anterior temporal neurodegeneration causes progressive loss of semantic knowledge; visual agnosia reflects cerebral dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Craniosynostosis, limb defects and intellectual disability define disease. Eyelid dysmorphism (30-79%) lacks demonstrated functional injury; renal anomalies are 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent blepharophimosis/proptosis are described as dysmorphism without established functional injury; ophthalmoplegia is only 5-29%.

basis: Defined by osteopetrosis and structural/neurodegenerative brain abnormalities; hearing impairment is only occasional (5-29%).
Defining congenital poikiloderma/alopecia, mandibular retrognathism and cleft palate.
Inherited skeletal muscle hyperirritability with rippling contractions, mounding, stiffness and cramps.
Motor neuron degeneration and dementia define disease; associated ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic dysfunction without established intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: ophthalmoplegia in this neurodegenerative syndrome reflects impaired neurologic control of eye movement; intrinsic ocular disease is not established.

basis: Distal skeletal muscle dystrophy with tibialis anterior weakness and atrophy in 71/71 patients; no common additional organ damage is established.
Succinic acidemia is a biochemical metabolic disorder with reported lactic acidosis; respiratory distress alone does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Polycystic developmental disease of the parotid salivary glands; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital cerebral neuronal migration disorder with heterotopia, cortical malformations, developmental impairment and frequent seizures.
Familial intestinal enteropathy with villous edema and defining IgG2 immunodeficiency.
Familial periarticular cutaneous fibromatosis causing thickened finger skin; underlying joints and bones are generally preserved.
Congenital absence of limb skin with residual scarring; associated epidermolysis bullosa is a separate condition.
Hereditary motor-sensory axonal neuropathy; distal weakness, neurogenic wasting and foot deformities follow denervation rather than direct muscle or skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness, wasting and associated foot deformities are downstream effects of neuropathy; direct musculoskeletal injury is not established.

basis: Corticospinal degeneration defines SPG6; pes cavus, muscle atrophy and fixed joint limitation are frequent (30-79%). Bladder symptoms alone do not establish urinary damage.
Defines brain, cataract and skeletal disease; dental/enamel defects occur in 80-99%. Cap excludes hearing impairment (30-79%) and vocal cord paresis (3/4).
Vascular and skin telangiectases plus recurrent nasal bleeding define HHT; GI lesions 60% with melena 30% support GI injury. Hepatic AVMs alone do not establish liver dysfunction.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent spontaneous nasal bleeding, present in 10/10, is a major diagnostic criterion; nasal mucosa belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic persistent skin telangiectases, present in 8/10, are defining vascular skin lesions and a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Skeletal fusions, palatal defects and ptosis define syndrome; hydronephrosis occurs in 3/4 patients (75%). Cardiac defects omitted at cap; hearing loss only 1/5.

decisions.ocular: primary: ptosis is explicitly defining and present in 5/5 patients; myopia in 2/5 additionally supports ocular dysfunction.

basis: Limb malformations, microcephaly and intellectual disability define the syndrome; nail hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%, with absent nails in 30-79%.
Pectus deformity and nail dysplasia define the syndrome; motor delay explicitly resolves during childhood, without established lasting neurologic damage.
Inherited muscular dystrophy directly affects scapular and upper-arm skeletal muscles.
Cutaneous angiokeratomas and arteriovenous fistulas define this hereditary vascular disorder.
Developmental disability and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; eczematoid dermatitis occurs in 30-79%. Obesity alone does not establish endocrine damage.
Localized excess hair on anterior neck skin; the laryngeal prominence describes location, not airway disease.
Endometrial tissue within uterine myometrium affects a reproductive organ; bleeding does not establish intrinsic hematologic disease.
Arterial dissection, medial necrosis and lentigines define syndrome. Hemiparesis occurs in 30-79%, but persistent direct CNS injury is not established.
Limb malformations, congenital heart defects and intellectual disability define syndrome; cleft lip/palate affects 30-79%.
Lethal nonimmune hemolysis; ureter abnormalities 80-99%, renal and lung hypoplasia 30-79%. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury; only two cases described.
HNF1A-associated monogenic diabetes; diabetic organ complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Albinism, intestinal aganglionosis and deafness define syndrome. Polycythemia in one infant lacks evidence of persistent blood dysfunction; fundus hypopigmentation alone is non-damaging.

decisions.haematologic: none: polycythemia in 1/1 is an isolated observation without evidence of persistent intrinsic blood disease or functional impairment.

basis: Iris pigment dispersion is an intrinsic eye disorder; subsequent pigmentary glaucoma remains within the ocular axis.
Genetic schizophrenia subtype is a psychiatric disorder; nonspecific nervous-system annotation does not establish neurologic damage.
Focal temporal epilepsy; auditory symptoms arise from cerebral seizure activity rather than ear damage.
CHRNA4-related focal epilepsy arising during sleep.
Seckel-spectrum disorder with microcephaly and developmental delay; pancytopenia reported, but its frequency is unclear.
Hydrocephalus, endocardial fibroelastosis and cataracts define the syndrome. Respiratory insufficiency may be secondary; intrinsic pulmonary damage is not established.
Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia; neurologic compromise from odontoid anomalies and cervical instability is a defining manifestation. Respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
Premature cranial-suture fusion with additional hand and foot skeletal abnormalities.
Familial benign setting-sun eye positioning is an ocular motility phenotype; associated structural brain disease is not established.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration; hearing, cognitive and gonadal annotations lack frequencies supporting common involvement.
BMP4-associated cleft lip/palate is a structural disorder of the mouth; additional BMP4-associated syndromes are not assumed.
Inherited tryptophan metabolism disorder with defining intellectual disability; other organ findings lack evidence of common direct damage.
Hair anchoring disorder; structural iris coloboma is reported frequent (30-79%) in the supplied annotations.
Inherited photodermatosis with photosensitivity and persistent pigmentary skin changes; no other organ damage established.
Persistent nocturnal urinary incontinence defines a disorder of bladder control; no additional organ damage established.
Pituitary endocrine tumour; compressive progressive visual loss and hypogonadal bone loss are each annotated frequent (30-79%). Headache alone adds no neurologic axis.
Congenital ocular motility impairment arises from cranial dysinnervation; brain malformations and neuropathy further support neurologic disease. Limb contractures are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental oculomotor nerve/nuclear abnormalities underlie CFEOM ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1348/)).

basis: Congenital intrahepatic bile duct dilatation; renal dysplasia occurs in 5-29%; cholangitis is a separate complication.
Fatty-acid oxidation disorder with defining infantile hepatic and cardiac disease; myopathy occurs in 30-79%. Neurologic injury is occasional.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic dysfunction characterizes the severe infantile hepatocardiomuscular form despite occasional frequency tags on individual hepatic phenotypes.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy and serious arrhythmias characterize the severe infantile hepatocardiomuscular phenotype.

basis: Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss; no extra-aural involvement is defining.
Renal cystic disease; hepatic cystic occupation in 15/19 (~79%), although reduced liver function is occasional. Hypertension is separately diagnosed.
Hereditary calcium pyrophosphate deposition disorder affecting cartilage and joints, with chondrocalcinosis and osteoarthritis.
Inherited susceptibility to severe recurrent varicella; transient varicella rash does not establish lasting skin damage.
External ear malformation with frequent canal atresia and hearing impairment; speech delay secondary to hearing loss does not establish neurologic injury.
Nasal dermoid cysts arise in nasal skin/subcutis; the nose also belongs to the pulmonary axis. Intracranial extension is a minority finding.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: a nasal dermoid is a congenital cutaneous/subcutaneous cyst or sinus, making skin/subcutis a site of the lesion.

basis: Skeletal abnormalities, alopecia and malabsorption define the syndrome; ovarian hypoplasia/amenorrhea are annotated 80-99%. Renal DI is not established as a common feature.
audit_reason: Replace renal with metabolic_endocrine under the cap: characteristic ovarian insufficiency has support from the phenotype and ancestry. Nephrogenic DI is not an established common manifestation despite the anomalous HPO frequency.

basis: Hereditary proximal skeletal myopathy with muscle weakness and elevated creatine kinase.
Organic acid metabolic disorder defined by neurologic disease; developmental delay in 80-99%; cardiomyopathy occurs in only 5-29%.
Defining limb/joint malformations and palatal/velopharyngeal abnormalities; dental abnormalities also occur in 30-79%. Facial spacing does not establish ocular disease.
Inherited calcium-sensing disorder with hypercalcemia; renal impairment and stones occur in 5-29%. Common structural bone damage is not established.
Isolated cleft lip or palate affects oral structures; no additional organ involvement is established.
Familial dwarfism with painful muscle spasms defines skeletal and muscle involvement; no evidence establishes an endocrine or neurologic disorder.
Cranial suture fusion; developmental language delay in 1/2 and raised intracranial pressure in 9/26; optic nerve hypoplasia in 1/2. Ectopic pituitary alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Eye agenesis, oral clefts and neural tube defects are defining anomalies; choanal atresia affects the airway in 30-79%. Rotated ears alone do not establish ear damage.
Vitamin D resistance causes defective skeletal mineralization and rickets; alopecia is occasional (5-29%).
Progressive macular and nasal chorioretinal atrophy causes visual impairment; no independent neurologic disease is established.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss with enlarged vestibular aqueduct; thyroid disease is not part of this concept.
Frontotemporal and motor neuron degeneration; secondary weakness and urinary incontinence do not establish separate muscle or urinary tract damage.
Concept describes a vascular response to isoproterenol; no definition or evidence establishes additional organ disease.
SCID with profound T-cell lymphopenia and usually absent NK cells; recurrent organ infections are separate diseases.
Biliary phospholipid transport disorder causing recurrent gallstones and intrahepatic cholestasis; pancreatitis occurs in only 5–29%.
Recurrent nocturnal urinary incontinence defines a bladder function disorder within the renal axis.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration; no established extraocular involvement.
PRKAG2 cardiac glycogen storage disease causes myocardial hypertrophy, ventricular preexcitation and conduction abnormalities.
Hepatic venous outflow obstruction directly affects hepatic vessels and liver; renal insufficiency occurs in <30%.
Isolated inherited cataract; lens opacity is the defining lesion.
Axonal neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy/foot deformities and recurrent trophic foot ulcers are characteristic, commonly >30%; secondary infections are separate.
Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with impaired myocardial function and possible arrhythmia.
Inherited ferritin-regulation disorder with early cataracts; hyperferritinemia occurs without iron overload or demonstrated liver or blood-cell damage.
Inherited marrow failure; developmental delay reported in 20/20; structural limb anomalies affect approximately 35% in usual Fanconi anemia, with limited FANCE-specific frequency data.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: functionally significant radial/thumb malformations affect approximately 35% in usual Fanconi anemia; subtype-specific frequency remains uncertain.

basis: Reported dominant Wiskott-Aldrich phenotype comprises immunodeficiency, thrombocytopenia and eczema; molecular characterization is limited.
Named syndrome defines ectodermal abnormalities, intellectual disability and syndactyly; no evidence supports additional organs.
Defining dental enamel hypoplasia, cataracts and cerebral aqueductal stenosis affect teeth, eyes and CNS respectively.
Inherited cardiac electrical dysfunction causing arrhythmias; syncope does not establish neurologic injury.
Joint contractures and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome, together with blepharophimosis, a characteristic eyelid malformation.
Unresolved legacy protocadherin entry without a defined disease phenotype; no organ assignment is supported. Requires ontology review.

decisions.neurologic: none: a protocadherin name does not establish neurologic disease; no definition, clinical phenotype or informative disease ancestor supports it.

basis: Prohormone-processing defect; congenital malabsorptive enteropathy affects most; cholestasis annotated 30-79%; pigment changes do not establish skin damage.
Isolated inherited palmoplantar keratoderma; fungal infections are separate diseases, and tendon or joint abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; WFS1 association alone does not establish other organ involvement.
Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia causes abnormal ossification, joint restriction and osteoarthritis; associated myopathy remains within the same axis.
Isolated hereditary hearing impairment, reported in 15/15 patients.
Sulfate-transport metabolic defect causing lethal skeletal dysplasia; lung hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%; cardiovascular abnormalities occur below 30%.
TMC1-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Primary congenital glaucoma affects the eye and damages the optic nerve.
Inherited retinal cone-rod degeneration causing impaired acuity, color vision and central vision.
Defining cardiac malformations, cleft palate and neurodevelopmental impairment; digital malformations are also defining. Isolated pulmonary findings omitted at cap.
Congenital collecting-system malformations cause multicystic kidneys and renal insufficiency; hypertension and urinary infections are secondary complications.
Hydrocephalus and scapular/costovertebral defects define syndrome; dental enamel defects occur in 30-79%. Pigmentation, photosensitivity and obesity do not establish additional organ injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: pigmentation and photosensitivity occur in 30-79%, but persistent skin injury or loss of function is not demonstrated.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity in 30-79% does not establish direct endocrine or metabolic dysfunction; obesity alone is a separately diagnosed condition.

basis: Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Inherited podocyte disease causes nephrotic syndrome and progressive kidney failure; secondary lipid abnormalities do not establish another organ disease.
Inherited basal epidermal fragility and blistering; oral mucosal blisters occur frequently, 30-79%, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Skeletal-muscle calcium-pump dysfunction causes exercise-induced stiffness and impaired relaxation; no independent nerve or systemic metabolic disease is established.
Cavernous transformation affects the portal vein and causes extrahepatic portal hypertension; liver parenchymal injury is not established.
Long QT, syndactyly and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define disease; hypoglycemia 7/17 and hypocalcemia 6/17 support metabolic involvement. Microdontia 17/17 omitted at cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: microdontia occurs in 17/17, but dental involvement is less severe than the retained cardiac, neurologic, limb and metabolic abnormalities; omitted at cap.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypoglycemia in 7/17 (41%) and hypocalcemia in 6/17 (35%) establish common metabolic dysfunction.

basis: Hypopituitarism and limb malformations define the syndrome. Unspecified midline malformations do not securely establish another organ axis.
Tibial absence/hypoplasia and polydactyly define skeletal disease; the retrocerebellar arachnoid cyst is a defining CNS anomaly.
The syndrome is defined by ichthyosis with abnormal epidermal keratohyalin granules and intellectual disability.
Inherited glucose transport disorder causing dystonia, choreoathetosis and progressive spastic paraplegia; episodic diplopia does not establish direct eye damage.
Usher type I is defined by sensorineural hearing loss, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal dystrophy.
Familial cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; bilateral tonic-clonic seizures in 79/105 patients.
OTOF-related inner-ear auditory synaptic dysfunction causes nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no separate generalized neuropathy.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss affects the auditory system.
Defined by congenital skin aplasia and retinal dysfunction/high myopia; calvarial skull defects occur in 80-99%.
Renal dysplasia or agenesis and vertebral segmentation abnormalities are defining MURCS features. Reproductive aplasia has no axis; hearing defects occur in 5–29%.
Hereditary heterotaxy with congenital cardiovascular malformations; organ malposition alone is not damage, and asplenia frequency is unestablished.
Cataracts 14/15, deafness and ID 15/15 define syndrome; pericarditis 6/15 (40%); brachydactyly 12/15 and dental anomalies 6/15 omitted at cap.

Demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy; pes cavus (1/2) and distal amyotrophy are consequences of denervation, without established direct skeletal or muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes cavus (1/2) and muscle wasting result from neuropathic denervation; the record does not establish direct muscle, bone or joint disease.

basis: Inherited vascular malformations and persistent cutaneous telangiectases define HHT; additional organ damage is insufficiently established for this subtype.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: persistent cutaneous telangiectases are defining vascular malformations and a major diagnostic feature of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

basis: Degenerative brain disease causes parkinsonism, dementia and supranuclear gaze palsy; gaze dysfunction does not establish direct ocular damage.
Glycosylation defect with severe CNS disease; ocular abnormalities and liver dysfunction occur in 30-79%. GI findings lack specified direct injury; bone and hearing findings omitted at cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: decreased liver function is explicitly frequent (30-79%), establishing functional hepatic involvement.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the 80-99% annotation is nonspecific; feeding difficulties do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage. Definite hepatic dysfunction takes priority.

basis: Defining congenital heart defects and profound intellectual disability; minor facial and digital anomalies do not establish additional functional organ damage.
Appears to be a gene/pseudogene entry rather than a defined human disease; no disease phenotype or organ damage is supplied.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with ventricular arrhythmias; syncope does not itself establish neurologic damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: vocal cord paresis occurs in 4/10 but reflects neural dysfunction rather than direct airway disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting and weakness reflect denervation; intrinsic muscle disease or common structural skeletal damage is not established.

basis: Isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with conduction disease and arrhythmia; stroke 6/21 is below 30% and a separately diagnosed complication.
