Poorly characterized Edwards-like syndrome; neurodevelopmental and skeletal abnormalities are inferred from the syndrome designation; no phenotype data supplied.
P5CS-deficiency spastic paraplegia; persistent pes cavus is frequent (30-79%). Cataracts, hearing impairment and urinary manifestations are below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent pes cavus is a structural skeletal deformity reported in 30-79%; weakness alone would not qualify.

basis: Diaphragmatic, limb and skull defects define the syndrome; severe pulmonary hypoplasia occurred in all four fetuses. Omphalocele alone does not establish bowel damage.
Cleft palate and severe congenital heart defects define the syndrome; mandibular hypoplasia occurs in 80-99% and clinodactyly in 30-79%, supporting persistent skeletal involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: micrognathia is mandibular hypoplasia in 80-99%, accompanied by clinodactyly in 30-79%; these are persistent skeletal malformations.

basis: Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining severe CNS atrophy and loss of large myelinated nerve fibers.
Eye/lung malformations and intellectual disability (80-99%) define the phenotype; cardiovascular malformations occur in 30-79%. Most renal/GI defects are occasional.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiovascular malformations occur in 30-79%; eye/lung and near-universal neurodevelopmental involvement take the three primary slots.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly in the definition and occurs in 80-99%, making neurodevelopmental impairment a major defining feature.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia, epilepsy and intellectual disability define the syndrome; structural dental abnormalities and malocclusion occur in 80-99%.
Iron overload with defining hepatic fibrosis and necrosis; cardiac and pancreatic abnormalities occur in only 5-29%. Viral hepatitis is a separate infection.

Calcium-sensing/electrolyte disorder. Nephrocalcinosis 12/27 may reflect treatment or non-impairing deposits; reduced GFR occurs in only 2/20. Hypocalcemic spasms/seizures do not prove lasting damage.

decisions.renal: none: nephrocalcinosis in 12/27 does not establish untreated functional damage; treatment can contribute, and reduced GFR is reported in only 2/20.

basis: Malignancy originates in lung and/or pleura; associated tumors and cysts are separate lesions and collectively occur in only about 25%.
Anterior polar cataract in all reported patients, with amblyopia in 16/17.
Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair define Naxos disease; vertigo does not establish ear damage.
Defining vertebral and skeletal dysplasia with enamel defects and tooth agenesis; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
The defining triad is congenital total alopecia, intellectual disability and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, each reported in 80-99%.
Defined by osteoporosis and oculocutaneous hypopigmentation; retinal abnormalities and visual impairment occur in 80-99%.
Dysplasia of enteric neural ganglia causes intestinal dysmotility and pseudo-obstruction.
Exostoses, skull defects and neurodevelopmental disability characterize the syndrome; developmental delay 80-99%, ID 7/10. Strabismus (30-79%) impairs ocular alignment/binocular function.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental disability is a characteristic syndrome component, supported by developmental delay in 80-99% and intellectual disability in 7/10.
decisions.ocular: involved: persistent strabismus occurs in 30-79% and impairs ocular alignment and binocular function; nystagmus alone would be insufficient.

basis: Mixed colorectal polyposis defines disease. Frequent anemia is secondary to gastrointestinal bleeding and separately diagnosed; cancer risk adds no axis.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; associated celiac enteropathy is a separately diagnosed disease.
Congenital cerebellar dysfunction; muscle atrophy in 3/5 and pes planus in 5/5 support musculoskeletal involvement. Strabismus and nystagmus reflect ocular motor dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus (4/5) and nystagmus are ocular motor manifestations of cerebellar disease; direct damage to the eye is not established.

basis: Congenital ichthyosis defines skin disease; ectropion directly affects eyelids in 14/15 patients.
Genetic type 2 diabetes; retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy and vascular complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Skeletal dystrophy and frequently associated cardiomyopathy are explicit defining features; respiratory muscle impairment does not establish pulmonary damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy is explicitly included in the disease definition and supported by its familial dilated cardiomyopathy parent.

basis: Defined as nonsyndromic EYA4-related sensorineural hearing loss; gene-associated syndromic cardiac disease is not this concept.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; associated vestibular dysfunction also belongs to the ear axis.
Defined by abnormal dentition and nail development; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Neurocutaneous disease with defining heart defects; scoliosis 9/22 and pectus 4/8 support skeletal damage. Cap excludes frequent ptosis and bleeding dysfunction; Lisch nodules non-damaging.
Defining porencephaly and cerebellar malformations; associated cardiac defects and corneal clouding have no established frequency supporting the 30% threshold.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac malformations are reported associated findings, without an established frequency of at least 30% or evidence that they are major diagnostic criteria.

basis: Ataxia, optic atrophy and sensorineural deafness define CAPOS; pes cavus is a defining skeletal deformity, reported in 3/10 patients.
Familial cutaneous disorder producing varioliform atrophic scars; macular atrophy here refers to skin.
Vertebral dysplasia, scoliosis, coxa vara and hand osteoarthritis define a skeletal disorder.
Ectodermal disease defined by skin changes and missing or abnormal teeth; hair, sweat-gland and nail abnormalities share the dermatologic axis.
Myelodysplasia, immunodeficiency and psychomotor delay define the syndrome; short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Defining limb reduction defects, mandibular hypoplasia and congenital heart disease.
Defining microcephaly, microphthalmia and limb defects; oral clefts occur in 80-99%. Cardiac defects are occasional; four-axis cap reached.
Osteochondrodysplasia defines the syndrome. Horseshoe kidney occurs in 30-79%, but fusion alone does not establish renal damage or dysfunction.

decisions.renal: none: horseshoe kidney is frequent (30-79%), but the supplied evidence establishes an anatomical variant without functional injury.

basis: Deafness, skeletal dysplasia and developmental disability define the syndrome; myopia and nasolacrimal obstruction are frequent (30-79%); retinal detachment is occasional.
Epilepsy, microcephaly, intellectual disability and skeletal dysplasia define the syndrome. Hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
Developmental impairment, cataract and deafness define syndrome; cleft palate and oligodontia occur in 30–79%. Common skeletal abnormalities omitted by cap.
Microcephaly, cardiac defects and lung malformation define the syndrome; renal hypoplasia/agenesis 30-79%; cleft palate omitted at four-axis cap.
Osteosclerotic skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and pulmonic stenosis each occur in 30-79%. Thick skin and hypertrichosis lack demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: thickened skin and hypertrichosis occur in 30-79%, but neither establishes destructive skin pathology or functional loss.

basis: Limb absence, oral clefts and major forebrain malformations define syndrome; ocular coloboma is reported as occasional (5-29%), without established obligatory criteria.
Intellectual disability/epilepsy, sparse hair and brachydactyly with skeletal and joint abnormalities define the syndrome.
Congenital limb absence defines the skeletal disorder; the supplied full syndrome synonym also identifies pulmonary hypoplasia as a defining malformation.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the supplied syndrome synonym explicitly includes pulmonary hypoplasia; the definition does not contradict this defining feature

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder; hearing impairment, strabismus and cardiac malformations each occur in 30-79%; nail hypoplasia (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Hereditary Wilms tumor is a nephroblastoma originating in the kidney.
Defined by disease of brain-supplying vessels and impaired cerebral blood flow, including cerebral ischemia and infarction.
COCH-related cochlear degeneration causes hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction, both within the otologic axis.
Holoprosencephaly and craniosynostosis define the syndrome; strabismus (80-99%) supports common impairment of ocular alignment and binocular function.
Developmental cataract affects the lens; the definition explicitly describes a nonsyndromic eye disorder.
Hereditary chorea with defining nystagmus and cataracts; cataracts establish intrinsic ocular disease.
Severe forebrain and cerebellar malformations; retinal dysplasia and craniosynostosis each in 2/2 reported patients; bifid uvula alone lacks demonstrated functional damage.
Hair and nail dysplasia with cardiac rhythm abnormalities defines syndrome; arrhythmia retained as defining despite HPO frequency of 5–29%.
Lethal osteochondrodysplasia primarily affects skeletal development; no additional common organ injury is established.
Craniosynostosis and intellectual disability are defining features; distal skeletal anomalies reinforce musculoskeletal involvement.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy causes lasting distal muscle atrophy in 20/20 patients and frequent foot deformities; respiratory involvement is not established as common.
Nonsyndromic severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss; prelingual hearing impairment in 6/6 patients.
Defining skeletal malformations, anal atresia and urethral obstruction; renal dysplasia/hypoplasia also reported. Autoimmune thrombocytopenia frequency is unknown.
Developmental/brain abnormalities, skeletal malformations and hearing loss define the syndrome; renal hypoplasia occurs in 3/4. Tracheomalacia is only 1/4.
Inherited thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction; hematologic malignancy is a predisposition, not obligatory disease.
Inherited type 2 diabetes; diabetic vascular, renal, retinal and nerve complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Neonatal insulin deficiency and hyperglycemia define the disease. Frequent macroglossia lacks documented functional damage; other organ abnormalities occur in <30%.
Progressive high-frequency nonsyndromic hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease established.
PRPF3-associated retinal degeneration causing rod-cone dysfunction and progressive visual-field loss.
Desmin-related skeletal myopathy with defining cardiomyopathy and conduction disease, supported by cardiac HPO frequencies of 30-79%. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy and conduction disease are defining manifestations in the definition and cardiomyopathy ancestry, with frequent cardiac HPO findings.

basis: Microcephaly and corpus callosum dysgenesis define brain involvement; cleft lip/palate defines an oral structural defect.
Ocular dysgenesis, cerebellar malformation/developmental disability and hypothyroidism define it. Tracheal stenosis 80–99%; skeletal anomalies omitted at cap.
Primary skeletal dysplasia affecting humeri, hips, digits and vertebrae; facial configuration alone does not establish other organ damage.
Stapes fixation causes bilateral conductive hearing impairment in 80-99%; the affected ossicle belongs to the middle ear.
Hip dislocation and joint laxity define the syndrome; cardiac septal/valvular defects and hearing abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Urinary abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Defining craniofacial dysostosis, ocular lesions and ear defects; encephalocele occurs in 30-79%; VSD and cleft lip also occur in 30-79% but are omitted by the four-axis cap.
Abnormal hair and developmental dental anomalies define the syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Demyelinating neuropathy with characteristic progressive deafness (3/3); lasting foot deformities 2/2 and muscle atrophy support musculoskeletal involvement. Glaucoma is separate.

decisions.ocular: none: glaucoma in 2/3 is a separately diagnosed association; intrinsic ocular damage from CMT4D is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: neurogenic muscle atrophy and persistent skeletal deformities are common; pes cavus 2/2 and claw hands/hammertoes 2/3.
decisions.otologic: primary: progressive sensorineural deafness is a defining feature of this subtype, reported in 3/3 and typically developing by adulthood.

basis: Profound T- and B-cell deficiency defines SCID. Recurrent respiratory and enteric infections are separate diseases; diarrhea alone does not establish direct intestinal damage.
Genetic subtype of immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; intestinal inflammation defines the condition.
Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction disease; hand muscle atrophy in 3/4 supports muscle involvement. Diaphragm weakness does not establish lung damage.
Congenital intrahepatic portosystemic shunt diverts portal blood away from hepatic perfusion; common persistent neurologic damage is not established.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the intrahepatic shunt and diversion of hepatic portal perfusion define this congenital liver vascular anomaly.

basis: Isolated congenital facial palsy results from maldevelopment of the facial nucleus or cranial nerve.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; sustained distal muscle wasting in 20/20 patients constitutes common muscle tissue loss, even though caused by denervation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal amyotrophy in 20/20 patients is persistent muscle tissue loss caused by the neuropathy; a primary myopathy is not required for this tier.

basis: Defined by long-bone diaphyseal sclerosis; a small study's cardiac association does not establish common direct cardiac involvement.
Hyaluronidase deficiency is a lysosomal storage disorder; synovitis, periarticular masses and skeletal abnormalities define the phenotype.
Inherited cardiomyopathy with ventricular dilation, hypertrophy and sometimes noncompaction; no common extracardiac disease is established.
Isolated inherited myocardial disease with ventricular dilation, systolic dysfunction and sometimes noncompaction.
Primary antibody deficiency. Recurrent infections and arthritis are separately diagnosed conditions; bronchiectasis and malabsorption occur in <30%.
Anterior-segment dysgenesis defines type 2; dental anomalies are reported without frequencies. Common dental, auditory, cardiac or CNS dysfunction is not established for this subtype.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: hypodontia/microdontia are reported, but type 2 prevalence >=30% or status as major diagnostic criteria is not established.

basis: Hereditary prostate cancer arises in a reproductive organ outside the axes; metastases are not defining involvement.
Brainstem dysfunction, deafness and gaze palsy define the syndrome; carotid malformations are a major feature, with cardiovascular abnormalities in >50%.
Defining microcephaly, retinal degeneration and cataract establish neurologic and ocular disease.
Peroxisomal disorder with defining developmental impairment (20/20); retinal degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss usually >30%. Common hepatic disease omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: none (cap): hepatic fibrosis/dysfunction is common (>30%), but neurologic impairment and the characteristic disabling retinal and hearing degeneration take priority.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment in 20/20 and the NALD/IRD neurodevelopmental phenotype define this peroxisomal syndrome.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss is a characteristic common manifestation (>30%). [GTR](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/conditions/C0282527/)

basis: Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss without established extra-auditory disease.
CRYBB2-related cataract directly affects the lens; cataract is obligate.
Congenital lacrimal dysfunction causes absent tears and corneal epithelial erosions.
Lens and anterior-segment defects define disease. Malocclusion 12/12, arachnodactyly 4/5 and laxity/pes planus 1/2 establish morphology but not additional functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: arachnodactyly 4/5 and joint hypermobility/pes planus 1/2 establish common skeletal features, without demonstrated tissue injury or functional loss.

basis: Congenital hypotrichosis and progressive macular degeneration define the syndrome; skeletal dysplasia occurs in only 5-29%.
Defining epiphyseal dysplasia and skeletal abnormalities; cleft palate in 80-99% affects the mouth.
Syndrome defined by skeletal dysplasia, vertebral abnormalities and glaucoma.
Genetically defined Wilms tumour arising in the kidney; radial aplasia is not established as a common feature of this concept.
Demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy and defining severe early scoliosis; hearing, ocular and respiratory abnormalities each occur in <30%.
Inherited multiple benign hair-follicle tumors affecting the skin.
Defined by spastic paraplegia and Evans syndrome: autoimmune hemolytic anemia with autoimmune thrombocytopenia.
Lung agenesis, congenital cardiac defects and thumb malformations define the syndrome, despite lower reported frequencies for individual thumb findings.
Hereditary structural anomaly of iris pigment epithelium, with iris cysts.
Acute leukemia involving distinct blast populations; lymphoid differentiation does not make this a lymphoma or immune-mediated disease.
Developmental abnormality of the iris and anterior chamber angle; extraocular disease is subtype-specific.
Neural tube closure disorder classified as isolated spina bifida, involving spinal dysraphism and vertebral closure defects; folate sensitivity alone adds no metabolic axis.
Hereditary tumours of neuroendocrine paraganglia, predominantly head and neck; local nerve or ear complications lack established common frequency.
Disorder of excess adiposity; associated diabetes, fatty liver and cardiovascular diseases are separate diagnoses.
Skeletal dysplasia and oligodontia with abnormal incisors jointly define the syndrome; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Photosensitive brittle-hair disease; neurodevelopmental impairment affects ~70-85%. Common damaging ocular disease or intrinsic immunodeficiency is not established.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental/intellectual impairment affects ~70-85%; it is a common associated manifestation rather than required to define photosensitive TTD1.

basis: Name denotes an insulin-secretion/endocrine metabolic trait; empty definition and nonspecific ancestry leave its disease status and phenotype unclear.
Distal arthrogryposis with congenital joint contractures and skeletal abnormalities; facial and palatal morphology does not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Hereditary glaucoma causes ocular pressure abnormalities and glaucomatous optic nerve damage.
Familial sebaceous gland hyperplasia is confined to cutaneous sebaceous glands.
Ectodermal defects, cataracts and kyphoscoliosis define the syndrome. Dental defects, clefting and diabetes have unspecified frequencies, insufficient for additional involvement.
FOXN1 deficiency is defined by severe T-cell deficiency, congenital alopecia and nail dystrophy; reduced circulating T-cell counts occur in 80-99%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defining deficiency of circulating T cells is a blood-cell disorder; decreased total T-cell count occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Defining pigment, ocular and hearing abnormalities; macrodontia and delayed tooth eruption occur in 80-99%. Gait disturbance alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Defining skeletal, brain and atrophic skin defects; microphthalmia 30-79%, iris coloboma 40%. Bowel malrotation 40% and chronic constipation 30% omitted by cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: malrotation 4/10 and chronic constipation 3/10 support gastrointestinal involvement, but the axis is omitted under the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia occurs in 30-79% and iris coloboma in 4/10; retain common structural eye abnormalities under the cap.

basis: Familial ligament calcification/ossification defines the disease; associated suprascapular nerve entrapment has no established frequency.
Inherited platelet granule and fibrinolytic bleeding disorder; joint bleeding is not established as common chronic joint damage.
ABCA4-associated retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction and progressive visual loss.
Preaxial digit duplication is a skeletal malformation; diabetic embryopathy reflects maternal diabetes, not established endocrine disease in the affected child.
Folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia with abnormal folate metabolism; the stated folate-transporter-deficiency parent includes immunodeficiency.
Glycosylation disorder with defining joint contractures and skin fragility; retinal detachment occurs in 30-79%. Bruising reflects tissue fragility, not a blood disorder.
GUCY2D-related cone-rod degeneration causes retinal and macular atrophy with progressive visual loss; retinal vessel attenuation remains within the ocular disease.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and progressive visual loss are common, exceeding 30% in childhood CLN6 disease.
Defining ocular malformations, hypogonadism and intellectual disability; each is supported by frequent phenotype annotations.
Neurodevelopmental and hallmark cutaneous abnormalities define PKS; visual impairment 17/22; skeletal delay/hypermobility 80-99%. Delayed dentition omitted at cap.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic pigmentary mosaicism and temporal alopecia are hallmark diagnostic features; supplied hair and sweat abnormalities occur in 80-99%.

basis: Neurodevelopmental/myelination disorder; hearing loss 43-50%, skeletal abnormalities and GH deficiency 30-79%. Cardiac and ocular findings omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac defects are annotated 30-79%, but the cap favors characteristic hearing, skeletal and endocrine dysfunction across the syndrome.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: secondary growth hormone deficiency is annotated frequent (30-79%) and represents endocrine loss of function, beyond short stature alone.

basis: Defining skeletal dysostosis, arthrogryposis, pulmonary hypoplasia and persistent cutaneous webbing across joints.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: multiple cutaneous pterygia are explicitly defining structural skin malformations that restrict joints.

basis: Severe developmental delay, diabetes and osteoporosis/osteosarcoma characterize the syndrome. Cataracts are a defining feature, with frequency unreported; macrocytosis alone is not injury.
Acroosteolysis and keloid-like skin disease define Penttinen syndrome. Posterior fossa cysts in 2/4 lack demonstrated functional damage; eye/hearing findings each 1/4.
Retinal vascular developmental disorder with exudation and detachment. Osteopenia is reported, but frequency across this subtype is insufficiently established.
Serine biosynthesis deficiency with defining developmental impairment and seizures; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Cataracts occur in only 5-29%.
Pancreatic beta-cell hyperinsulinism causes hypoglycemia; common permanent neurologic injury is not established.
Defined by acrofacial dysostosis with dental and ectodermal abnormalities. Oligodontia occurs in 80-99%, sparse hair in 30-79%; cutis aplasia and pili torti are occasional.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oligodontia is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 80-99%; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: the definition includes cutis aplasia and hair abnormalities; frequent sparse hair supports the defining ectodermal phenotype.

basis: Biopsy-supported rimmed-vacuole muscular dystrophy; supplied phenotypes do not establish peripheral nerve damage. Dysphagia alone does not establish GI damage.
Inherited bile-salt transport disorder causing progressive intrahepatic cholestasis; definition explicitly states no extrahepatic features.
Defining cerebellar malformation, trigeminal dysfunction and scalp alopecia; corneal opacity occurs in 80-99%, strabismus in 31/39 and visual impairment in 30-79%.
Defective lymphocyte apoptosis causes autoimmune lymphoproliferation, splenic enlargement and characteristic autoimmune cytopenias.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; COL11A2 does not justify adding skeletal manifestations from other syndromes.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 17/17 patients.
GJA3-related nonsyndromic cataract affects the ocular lens.
Fibronectin deposition directly damages glomeruli. Hypertension in 7/8 is secondary and does not establish direct vascular injury.
Atrial septal defect and congenital lower-limb lymphedema are defining features; persistent lymphatic dysfunction affects subcutaneous tissue.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: congenital persistent lymphedema affects the subcutis and defines this syndrome alongside the cardiac defect.

basis: Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder affecting skin and nails; finger deformities arise from cutaneous constriction.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy with progressive weakness and atrophy; definition explicitly reports no cardiac or respiratory involvement.
Defining abnormalities affect teeth, hair and nails, and the bones of the hands and feet.
Named syndrome indicates ear and skeletal abnormalities; no definition or phenotypes establish endocrine dysfunction from the gonadal component.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: gonadal abnormalities alone do not establish hormonal dysfunction; reproductive structural disease has no axis, and confirming endocrine evidence is absent.

basis: Inherited megakaryocyte proliferation and sustained thrombocytosis; thrombotic complications are not established as common.
Zinc dysregulation/autoinflammation; chronic cytopenias >80% and persistent inflammatory skin lesions >30%. Arthritis omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury.

decisions.haematologic: involved: chronic anemia and neutropenia affect >80% and reflect intrinsic inflammatory marrow/blood dysfunction.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic ulcerative or pyoderma-like inflammatory lesions affect >30%; these represent persistent tissue inflammation.

basis: Friedreich phenotype: neural degeneration with cardiomyopathy (~60-70%) and skeletal deformities (>50%); estimates extrapolate from the parent disease; diabetes is a minority.
Intestinal magnesium malabsorption and renal magnesium wasting cause hypomagnesemia and secondary hypocalcemia; lasting neurologic injury is not established in ≥30%.
audit_reason: Add renal to primary: this disorder combines impaired intestinal magnesium absorption with defective renal magnesium reabsorption; renal wasting is intrinsic to the disease.

basis: Defining hair and nail dysplasia, including alopecia and congenital nail dystrophy in 8/8 patients.
Defined by infantile epilepsy and subsequent paroxysmal movement disorder.
Familial enlargement of distal finger and toe phalanges is a skeletal disorder.
Congenital cranial dysinnervation causes fixed ophthalmoplegia, extraocular muscle fibrosis and ptosis.
Disordered trimethylamine metabolism; urinary, sweat and breath excretion causes odor without intrinsic renal, skin or pulmonary damage.
Inherited high-turnover metabolic bone disease; hearing loss 1/1 and characteristic early tooth loss support involvement (estimated >=30%); neurologic compression frequency unclear.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine: this is a hereditary metabolic bone disorder, with hypercalcemia reported in 1/1. The metabolic mechanism axis does not require an endocrine-gland defect.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment of speech motor planning and language; oromotor apraxia does not establish structural oral disease.
Corneal dystrophy causing opacities, recurrent erosions and progressive visual impairment.
Usher syndrome is defined by sensorineural deafness and retinal degeneration; hearing loss 15/15, rod-cone dystrophy 14/15 and vestibular dysfunction 7/8.
Congenital postaxial extra digits are skeletal malformations.
Inherited right ventricular cardiomyopathy with myocardial necrosis and ventricular arrhythmias.
Inherited right ventricular myocardial disease with ventricular arrhythmias.
INVS-related cystic tubulointerstitial kidney disease; kidney failure in 5/5. Secondary hypertension is a separate condition; pulmonary damage frequency unspecified.
Benign capillary endothelial tumor typically located in skin; uncommon visceral lesions do not justify additional organs.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; the USH1C association does not establish retinal disease in this concept.
GUCA1A-related cone or cone-rod retinal degeneration causes progressive visual dysfunction.
Inherited early-onset Alzheimer disease causes progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Usher type I is defined by congenital sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal dystrophy.
SPG11-related motor neuron degeneration; amyotrophy in 23/23 reflects denervation. Respiratory insufficiency occurs in only 2/23 and reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy in 23/23 is secondary to motor neuron degeneration and denervation, rather than direct skeletal muscle disease.

basis: Hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness reflects nerve dysfunction.
Vertebral, epiphyseal and metaphyseal dysplasia with limb deformity and osteoarthritis; supplied phenotypes are skeletal.
Progressive tubulointerstitial nephropathy and cholestatic liver disease define this syndrome; an immune mechanism is not established.
Inherited focal dystonia, predominantly cervical; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish direct skeletal muscle damage.

Inherited progressive disease of the cardiac conduction system.

HLA-I expression deficiency causes immunodeficiency; destructive granulomatous skin ulcers occur in roughly 40-50%. Secondary respiratory infections are separate diseases.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic destructive granulomatous skin ulcers affect roughly 40-50% and represent direct immune dysregulation

basis: PAX9-related absence of permanent teeth; molar agenesis and oligodontia in 16/16.
Developmental disability, cardiac defect and anal atresia define syndrome; ocular ptosis is also a defining feature, retained as involved because primary is capped at three.
Autonomic neurotransmitter transport dysfunction causes defining orthostatic tachycardia; visual and respiratory symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Premature cranial suture fusion defines the disorder; ocular abnormalities, seizures and oral malformations are occasional, below 30%.
Defined as isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; no evidence here for accompanying skeletal myopathy or neuropathy.
Polycystic bone disease identifies a skeletal disorder; supplied information does not establish another affected organ.
Inherited cardiac arrhythmia with possible cardiac dysfunction; syncope and seizure-like events do not establish independent neurologic damage.
Inherited keratinization disorder with scaling and hyperkeratosis; supplied subtype phenotypes do not establish common ocular damage.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy with contractures; respiratory failure results from respiratory muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Progressive brain degeneration; fixed flexion contractures occur in 30-79% and cause lasting joint restriction. Incontinence reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Primary microcephaly with cortical maldevelopment and intellectual disability; hearing loss in one annotated patient cannot establish >=30% involvement across the disease.

decisions.otologic: none: mixed hearing impairment in 1/1 selectively annotated patient is insufficient to establish a >=30% disease-wide frequency; it is not a defining criterion.

basis: Corticospinal degeneration defines disease; structural pes cavus/amyotrophy occur in 30-79%, and bladder sphincter dysfunction in 11/27. Isolated ocular reports lack established association.

decisions.renal: involved: bladder sphincter dysfunction in 11/27 (~41%) represents sustained urinary functional loss, beyond urgency alone.

basis: Chronic destructive bronchiolar inflammation; associated sinus disease is within the same axis; secondary airway infection does not define an infectious cause.
Mandibulofacial dysostosis establishes craniofacial skeletal involvement; supplied evidence does not establish frequencies for other organs.
Vitreoretinal and skeletal disorder; HPO hearing loss 80-99% and cleft palate 30-79%. Subtype-specific hearing annotations outweigh the generic definition's 10% estimate.
Named inherited hyaluronan metabolic defect; definition and organ phenotype evidence are absent, preventing additional organ assignment.
Type II collagen skeletal disorder with defining early generalized osteoarthritis and vertebral dysplasia; no common extra-skeletal damage is documented.
Inherited intrahepatic cholestasis progressing to hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis; portal hypertension reflects liver disease.
Becker nevus with defining ipsilateral muscular or skeletal hypoplasia; micromelia and shoulder muscle atrophy 80-99%. Breast abnormalities have no axis.
Defining skeletal dysplasia with fractures and dentinogenesis imperfecta; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Diabetes and optic atrophy define the syndrome (16/16). Deafness affects 14/16 (~88%); characteristic peptic ulceration 11/16 (~69%). Platelet dysfunction omitted under the cap.

decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects 14/16 (~88%); diabetes and optic atrophy are the defining diagnostic pair.

basis: Defective cortisol regeneration causes ACTH-driven androgen excess; hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
Severe congenital CNS malformation defines disease. Amyotrophy in 2/2 accompanies profound motor impairment; scalp folds in 2/2 do not establish skin dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy in 2/2 accompanies severe spastic tetraplegia; evidence does not establish direct muscle disease rather than secondary wasting.

basis: ANGPTL3-related lipid metabolism disorder with low LDL cholesterol and triglycerides; common hepatic or neurologic injury is not established.
Inherited epilepsy with developmental impairment, dysarthria and ataxia; manifestations remain neurologic.
Congenital autoimmune diabetes defines endocrine pancreatic dysfunction with an autoimmune mechanism; no additional organ evidence supplied.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; familial occurrence does not establish additional organ involvement.
Inherited mild elevation of LDL cholesterol is a lipid metabolic disorder; cardiovascular disease is a later risk and a separate diagnosis.
Developmental impairment, contractures and characteristic skin/hair findings define the syndrome; myopia 5/6, optic/retinal atrophy and coloboma 30-79%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: defining forehead nevus flammeus and hypertrichosis are reported in 80-99% and 6/7, respectively.

basis: Defining abnormalities affect the clavicles, zygomatic arches, and mandible.
Defining skin appendage tumours; salivary neoplasms and hearing or visual damage occur in a small minority, below 30%.
Familial cerebral neurodegeneration with amyloid, neurofibrillary tangles and spongiform pathology; prion pathology alone does not establish an infection.
Congenital absence of the tricuspid valve with right ventricular hypoplasia and associated cardiac or great-vessel malformations.
Mineralocorticoid receptor gain of function causes defining early hypertension and disordered hormonal/electrolyte regulation; no intrinsic renal injury established.
Intellectual disability and characteristic hypertrichosis define the syndrome; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation alone do not establish skeletal damage.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; renal involvement is not established as common in this concept despite an unquantified reflux annotation.
Genetically associated immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; no additional commonly damaged organ established.
Spastic paraplegia with motor axonal neuropathy; structural pes cavus affects 80-99%, supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Retinopathy, obesity and polydactyly 7/7; diabetes 4/7. Intellectual disability 6/7 supports neurologic involvement; renal cysts 2/7 fall just below 30%.
Immune dysregulation with pathological lymphocyte proliferation, lymphadenopathy and/or splenomegaly defines the disorder.
Carney complex is defined by characteristic skin lesions, cardiac/cutaneous myxomas and endocrine overactivity or tumors.
Congenital peripheral hypomyelination; typical distal muscle atrophy and fixed foot deformity (>30%) cause lasting structural loss. Respiratory weakness alone is not lung damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent distal muscle atrophy and structural foot deformities are typical in most patients, constituting tissue loss/deformity within CMT rather than weakness alone.

basis: Antibody deficiency with defective class switching; recurrent respiratory and gastrointestinal infections do not establish lasting intrinsic organ damage.
Cerebellar degeneration and neurodevelopmental impairment define SCA13. Nystagmus is neurologic; optic atrophy and hearing impairment occur in under 30%.
Congenital limb and pelvic skeletal dysplasia; intellectual disability annotated 30-79%, with developmental delay reported in 1/3 patients.
Cardiac and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; developmental impairment 60-67%, cutis laxa/hyperkeratosis 57%; ptosis 38% omitted at cap.
Hereditary corticospinal degeneration; sphincter dysfunction is neurologic and does not establish intrinsic urinary tract damage.
Skeletal glycosylation disorder with defining developmental impairment (6/9); dental defects in 10/10. Severe hearing loss (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: structural dental abnormalities affect 10/10; retained for their near-universal frequency within the four-axis cap.
decisions.neurologic: primary: delayed mental and motor development defines the syndrome; global developmental delay occurs in 6/9.
decisions.otologic: none: severe sensorineural hearing loss qualifies at 30-79%, but is omitted at cap in favor of universal skeletal/dental and major neurologic disease.

basis: Hereditary motor-sensory neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy in 21/21 and pes cavus in 19/21. A biochemical glycolytic disorder is not established for this HK1 neuropathy.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the HK1-associated neuropathy lacks an established biochemical metabolic phenotype; glycolysis ancestry alone does not establish metabolic disease.

basis: Split hands and feet with absent or hypoplastic digital bones define this TP63-associated subtype.
Hereditary optic nerve atrophy; optic nerve disease belongs to the ocular axis.
Macrocephaly, autism and developmental impairment define disease; freckling is non-damaging, and associated tumours are risks.
Craniosynostosis and ocular/eyelid malformations characterize the syndrome; developmental impairment and cardiac defects lack established frequencies.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental delay and intellectual disability have unspecified frequencies and are not established major diagnostic criteria in the supplied evidence.

basis: Structural skeletal myopathy with progressive weakness, atrophy and contractures; motor delay is muscular, and respiratory weakness does not establish lung damage.
Cerebellar degeneration defines SCA14. Frequent Achilles morphology annotations do not establish direct tendon damage; hypotonia and nystagmus are neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: Achilles morphology is annotated in 30-79%, but direct tendon injury or functional impairment is not established.

basis: Syndrome defined by progressive dilated cardiomyopathy and childhood sensorineural hearing loss, both present in 80-99%.
Defined by autonomic paraganglial and adrenal neuroendocrine tumors; renal carcinoma and GIST are additional tumor risks, not involved organs.
Inherited focal epilepsy with sleep-related hypermotor seizures.
Congenital cardiac/laterality disorder; intestinal malrotation 2/3, asplenia 1/3 and callosal agenesis 1/3 support additional axes. Frequency estimates rely on only three patients.
CHMP4B-associated nonsyndromic cataract affects the ocular lens.
Ataxic cerebral palsy with cerebellar atrophy; gait abnormalities and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Isolated hereditary hair deficiency; sparse hair in 19/19 patients.
The defining triad comprises gingival fibromatosis, excessive hair growth and intellectual disability.
Inherited dopamine-synthesis disorder causes dystonia/parkinsonism. Foot findings reported in 30-79% can reflect dystonic posturing; common fixed skeletal damage is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes cavus/talipes annotations are frequent (30-79%), but this dystonia commonly produces foot posturing; persistent structural damage is not established.

basis: Schizophrenia is a psychiatric disorder; no qualifying organ damage is described.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia and radioulnar synostosis define the syndrome; hearing loss is occasional (5–29%).
Classified as an inherited neurodegenerative disorder; radiation sensitivity and chromosome instability alone do not establish another organ axis.
Usher syndrome is defined by retinal degeneration and congenital sensorineural hearing impairment.
Inherited bile-acid transport disorder causing recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis; pruritus does not establish direct skin damage.
Inherited Alzheimer disease causing progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
SNCA-associated neurodegeneration causes parkinsonism, dementia and autonomic dysfunction; orthostatic hypotension does not establish intrinsic cardiovascular damage.
Hereditary fibrous overgrowth of gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited retinal cone and rod degeneration with progressive visual loss.
Metabolic syndrome involves abdominal obesity and metabolic abnormalities; hypertension is a major diagnostic component.
Abdominal obesity/metabolic syndrome defines the metabolic axis; hypertension is explicitly annotated and is a major diagnostic component, rather than merely a later cardiovascular risk.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertension is an explicitly annotated cardinal component of the metabolic syndrome phenotype and a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with myocardial dysfunction; heart failure occurred in 5/9.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 23/23 patients.
Axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy; persistent muscle atrophy and structural foot deformities occur in 30-79%; LMNA alone does not imply cardiac disease.
Axonal peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; distal weakness and amyotrophy result from denervation rather than a direct skeletal muscle disease process.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common distal wasting is secondary to axonal denervation; direct muscle or skeletal pathology is not established.

basis: Defined by sensorineural deafness and dentinogenesis imperfecta; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Tetralogy of Fallot is a congenital structural heart malformation; no additional organ phenotype is supplied.
Defining CNS, eye and nasal malformations; cleft palate in 12/20 (60%) supports gastrointestinal involvement; frequent skeletal malformations omitted by cap.
Autonomous adrenal aldosterone production and hypertension define the disease; hypokalemia shares the metabolic axis.
Hereditary MYH2 myopathy with defining external ophthalmoplegia; not autoimmune myositis. Dysphagia reflects muscle dysfunction.
Thyroid and renal papillary neoplasia define the syndrome; neck-vessel morphology alone does not establish vascular injury.
Inherited retinal dystrophy with photoreceptor degeneration, chorioretinal atrophy and progressive visual loss.
Cerebellar ataxia and gonadal hormone failure define the syndrome.
Cardiomyopathy, woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma define this cardioectodermal syndrome.
Inherited mitochondrial metabolic defect; encephalopathy/regression occurs in 30-79%, pulmonary arterial hypertension in 7/10. Respiratory failure alone does not establish intrinsic lung damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy and developmental regression occur in 30-79%, with leukoencephalopathy supporting direct CNS injury; the defining disease is a mitochondrial metabolic defect.

basis: Amyloid damages cerebral vessels and causes brain hemorrhage; stroke and cerebellar hemorrhage reported in 4/4.
Fanconi marrow-failure syndrome; microcephaly 3/7 does not establish neurologic dysfunction. Anal atresia 2/7 is below 30%; pigment spots are nondamaging and cancers are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly in 3/7 establishes small head size, without documented brain dysfunction; subsequent brain tumours are separate diseases.

basis: Hereditary motor neuron disease; sustained denervation causes distal muscle atrophy and weakness in 3/3 annotated patients, with limb deformities.
Otosclerosis affects the otic capsule and stapes, causing hearing loss; localized ear bone disease does not warrant a musculoskeletal axis.
Inherited early-onset lens cataract.
Inherited platelet aggregation and thromboxane synthesis defect; bleeding sites do not establish additional organ damage.
Isolated congenital microphthalmia with coloboma affects the eye.
Breast asymmetry; breast has no axis.
Isolated inherited early-onset cataract affects the lens.
Vitreoretinal vascular disease causing retinal folds, exudation, detachment and visual impairment.
Familial infantile epilepsy; tonic-clonic and focal seizures are defining neurologic manifestations.
Hypergonadotropic ovarian hormone failure and recurrent metabolic acidosis both fall within the endocrine-metabolic axis; short stature alone adds no skeletal axis.
Congenital nail dysplasia defines the disease; associated phalangeal malformations and distal phalanx duplication occur in 30-79%.
Immune-mediated posterior uveitis directly damages the choroid and retina; retinal vascular changes remain within the ocular axis.
Slow-channel acetylcholine receptor dysfunction causes impaired neuromuscular transmission and characteristic degenerative endplate myopathy; respiratory weakness does not establish lung injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: prolonged receptor opening causes characteristic degenerative endplate myopathy, establishing intrinsic skeletal muscle injury.

basis: Citrin-related hepatic metabolic disease; coagulation-factor deficiency with prolonged prothrombin time in 80-99% supports common coagulation dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Inherited sialic acid biosynthesis disorder causes degenerative skeletal myopathy; hypothyroidism is separately diagnosed and cardiomyopathy occurs in only 1-4%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defective sialic acid biosynthesis is an inborn metabolic disorder, supported by the glycosylation-disorder ancestry; hypothyroidism is not the justification.

basis: Osteoporosis/vertebral disease and cataract/retinal detachment define syndrome; hearing loss 3/4; cardiac valve/septal defects 2/2 and VSD frequent.
Follicular skin hamartomas, hypotrichosis and palmoplantar pits define this cutaneous syndrome.
Pelvic skeletal dysplasia; no additional organ involvement established.
Glycine metabolism defect described in one patient; fatigability and elevated CK do not firmly establish damaging myopathy. Odor does not indicate skin injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: fatigability and elevated CK are annotated at 80-99% but derive from one case; lasting muscle damage or a defined myopathy is not established.

basis: Callosal agenesis/intellectual disability, microphthalmia and heminasal hypoplasia define brain, eye and nasal defects. Unspecified atypical clefting does not establish oral/palatal involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: heminasal hypoplasia is a defining nasal malformation; the nose belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the record does not localize atypical clefting to the mouth or palate; a gastrointestinal malformation cannot be assumed.

basis: Glycine metabolism defect with defining encephalopathy and seizures; breathing dysregulation reflects neurologic dysfunction, not direct lung injury.
PINK1-related Parkinson disease is neurodegenerative; urinary urgency does not establish intrinsic urinary tract damage.
Ketogenesis defect; hepatic steatosis 4/5 and transaminase elevation 13/16 support liver injury. Lasting neurologic damage is not established in ≥30%.

decisions.neurologic: none: encephalopathy (9/10) and seizures (13/14) occur during metabolic crises; patients are usually asymptomatic between episodes, without established common lasting brain injury.

basis: Inherited coagulation protein disorder causing bleeding.
Forebrain malformation; central diabetes insipidus affects about 70% in classic holoprosencephaly. HPE6-specific endocrine frequency is uncertain.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, especially central diabetes insipidus (~70%), is common in holoprosencephaly; subtype-specific frequency is uncertain.

basis: Hereditary erosive joint disease; no evidence supplied for an autoimmune mechanism or other organ involvement.
Ear, oral/palatal and jaw/digit malformations define the syndrome; mild developmental delay is a defining associated feature. Sparse hair omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: mild developmental delay is a defining syndromic feature; three primary slots prioritize the structural ear, oral and skeletal malformations.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: micrognathia and digit anomalies are defining structural components of this malformation syndrome.

basis: Defining metaphyseal and long-bone dysplasia; premature tooth loss occurs only occasionally.
Defining limb and sternal malformations; intellectual disability occurs in only 5-29%.
Pentose phosphate defect with defining cirrhosis and cytopenias (80-99%); renal abnormalities 30-79%. Skin changes omitted at cap; individual cardiac defects occur in <30%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: anemia and thrombocytopenia are explicit defining manifestations, each present in 80-99%; they establish disease of blood cells.

basis: Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic progressive hearing loss.
Overgrowth and acromegaloid skeletal features with defining cleft palate; the name does not establish growth hormone excess or another endocrine disorder.
Organic acidemia; developmental delay 20/20 and arrhythmia 30-79%; cardiomyopathy 5-29%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Glycosylation disorder defined by neurologic dysfunction and hypogammaglobulinemia. Pooled hepatic enlargement, optic atrophy and hearing loss are each under 30%.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration causing night blindness and progressive visual field loss.
Iron-transport disorder defined by hepatic iron deposition; arthritis, cardiomyopathy and diabetes are minority manifestations.
MATR3 motor neuron disease also has direct myopathy: rimmed vacuoles in 5/6 and abnormal muscle fibers; bulbar and respiratory weakness do not establish GI or lung damage.
Neuropathy with defining laryngeal dysfunction and hearing loss; muscle atrophy occurs in 39/42 (93%) and scoliosis in 26/40 (65%). Vocal paresis is 11/42 but is a defining feature.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the definition specifically identifies vocal-cord anomalies and respiratory impairment; laryngeal loss of function is defining despite paresis in 11/42.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss is explicitly a defining component of this CMT subtype; HPO provides no separate frequency estimate.

basis: Skeletal myopathy with mechanically induced muscle contractions; immune mechanisms apply to acquired subtypes rather than the entire umbrella.
Inherited multinodular enlargement of the thyroid, an endocrine gland.
Inherited pure red-cell aplasia defines Diamond-Blackfan anemia; no common additional organ damage is established for this subtype.
Inherited iron-handling disorder with damaging brain iron accumulation and progressive movement disorder; low serum ferritin alone is not hematologic damage.
Red-cell aplasia with mandibulofacial dysostosis; cleft palate and developmental delay each 2/2. Hearing/canal abnormalities in 1/2 omitted at cap.
Patellar defects, neurodevelopmental impairment and renal anomalies define syndrome; laryngomalacia 6/19 (~32%); hair abnormalities omitted by cap.
Refers to absence of a penile reproductive structure; humans normally lack a baculum, so this unusual entry does not establish damage to an organ axis.
The supplied definition describes defective intermediary metabolism, impaired glucose homeostasis and intrinsic muscle loss of function.
Immune-mediated intermediate uveitis affecting the pars plana; associated systemic autoimmune diseases are separate conditions.
Cerebellar ataxia and motor neuropathy define neurologic disease; defining laryngeal paralysis impairs airway function.
Inherited Alzheimer neurodegeneration causing progressive cognitive loss.
Meningeal tumor; radiation identifies its cause, not an additional affected organ.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the neurologic phenotype; skeletal abnormalities and joint dislocations also define the syndrome.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; nail hypoplasia 80-99%, hypohidrosis 30-79%, and strabismus/ptosis 30-79%. Reflux is a separately diagnosed condition.
Familial nonmedullary carcinoma arising in the thyroid, an endocrine gland.
Intellectual disability, microcephaly and joint contractures define the syndrome. Frequencies and functional significance of additional skin and eyelid findings are unclear.
Deep extremity soft-tissue sarcoma; lung metastases directly occupy pulmonary tissue in roughly 50-70% over the course. Brain and bone metastases are less common.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary metastases occur in roughly 50-70% over the usual course and constitute direct occupation by the same malignancy.

basis: Metabolic bone disease with abnormal remodeling and osteolysis; hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
PARK7-related neurodegenerative parkinsonism; rigidity and dystonia reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Heterotaxy with congenital heart defects; asplenia/hyposplenism affects roughly half across heterotaxy, with subtype uncertainty. Malrotation alone does not establish bowel dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: involved: absent or functionally deficient spleen occurs in roughly half of heterotaxy patients; this is organ loss, with limited subtype-specific frequency data.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: malrotation is common (~50-70%) but often asymptomatic; malposition alone is not damage, and volvulus is a minority complication.

basis: MYO6-related nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss; the gene alone does not establish other organ involvement.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease associated with chromosome 5q31 variation; extraintestinal diseases are not intrinsic common organ damage.
A psychiatric gambling disorder without intrinsic damage to an organ covered by the axes.
Progressive upper motor neuron degeneration defines disease. Weakness and dysphagia are neurologic manifestations; skeletal muscle atrophy is reported in <30%.
Villous atrophy 2/2, dermatitis 3/3, pulmonary lymphocytic infiltration 1/1; small samples. Cap omits reported endocrine and blood autoimmunity.
PDX1-associated monogenic diabetes; diabetic end-organ complications are separate diseases.
NEUROD1-related monogenic diabetes; neurologic abnormalities are not established as common in heterozygous MODY6.
Amino-acid transport/endocrine disorder with cystinuria and defining neuromuscular hypotonia; developmental delay 7/7, seizures 5/7. One abnormal muscle biopsy does not establish common myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: defining congenital hypotonia reflects neuromuscular dysfunction; developmental delay 7/7 and seizures 5/7 further establish neurologic disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage; ragged-red fibers in one tested patient cannot establish common myopathy. No frequent skeletal lesions are documented.

basis: Joint instability and skin hyperextensibility define the syndrome; sensory/peripheral neuropathy occurs in 30-79%. Cardiovascular and gastrointestinal lesions are under 30%.
Inherited neurodegeneration causes movement disorder and cognitive decline; neuroacanthocytosis classification does not establish common blood dysfunction.
Persistent polyclonal blood B-cell proliferation; usually asymptomatic, without established common hepatic injury or immunodeficiency.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Inherited peripheral neuropathy; denervation causes distal muscle wasting and weakness in 20/20 patients. Cataracts and neutropenia are not established as common.
Peripheral motor-sensory neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy in 20/20 and pes cavus in 3/7 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Facial haemangioma, arterial/cardiac anomalies and brain malformations define PHACE; damaging ocular anomalies are major criteria and reported in 30-79%.
Usher-hyperinsulinism syndrome defines endocrine, auditory and retinal disease; retinal degeneration is age-dependent. Enteropathy/tubulopathy occurred in ~3/18 and may be unrelated.
audit_reason: Add ocular to primary: retinal degeneration is part of the defining Usher phenotype; adolescent onset explains low pediatric counts. [Cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3579360/).

basis: Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines the umbrella; additional organ disease varies by subtype.
Inherited epidermal barrier disorder with ichthyosis and impaired sweating; ectropion occurs in only 2/11.
Vestibulocerebellar dysfunction causes ataxia, vertigo and abnormal eye movements; these do not establish intrinsic eye or inner-ear damage.
Episodic ataxia and interictal myokymia define neural dysfunction; vertigo and tinnitus do not establish intrinsic ear damage.
Melanin metabolism disorder defined by skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental defects with visual loss; optic misrouting belongs to ocular phenotype.
Combined immunodeficiency, pancytopenia and microcephaly/developmental impairment define LIG4 syndrome; hypothyroidism is a separately diagnosed associated disease.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypothyroidism in 2/4 meets the numerical threshold but is a separately diagnosed associated disorder, without evidence of direct thyroid injury by LIG4 deficiency.

basis: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent distal amyotrophy occurs in 7/7 and structural foot deformity in 6/7, integral to the disease course.
Congenital muscular dystrophy from defective dystroglycan glycosylation. Structural brain abnormalities are 5-29%; intellectual disability frequency is uncertain.
Progressive diaphyseal hyperostosis with muscle weakness; cardiac and endocrine findings lack established frequencies in this single-family disorder.
Familial motor neuron degeneration with bulbar dysfunction and weakness; these do not establish intrinsic muscle, gastrointestinal or pulmonary disease.
Cerebellar degeneration causes ataxia, tremor and oculomotor abnormalities; dysphagia is neurologic, without established gastrointestinal tissue injury.
Susceptibility is defined specifically by the uveal tumor site; this label does not establish that a carrier currently has melanoma or ocular damage.
Hereditary susceptibility specifically targets uveal melanoma; this label identifies the defined organ, without assuming an existing tumor or other BAP1-associated disease.
Defined by congenital sensorineural deafness and skin/hair pigmentation defects; iris pigmentation differences do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Methionine metabolism disorder; definition explicitly describes hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases without liver disease. Neurologic problems are a risk, not established common damage.
Inherited susceptibility form of immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; no qualifying extraintestinal damage specified.
Genetic subtype of immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; no additional common organ damage established.
Genetic susceptibility subtype of immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; intestinal inflammation defines the disease.
Defined as isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; heart failure in 7/7. Sarcoglycan ancestry does not establish skeletal muscle disease in this subtype.
Inherited PRNP prion disease causes spongiform brain degeneration and dementia in 9/9. Infectious prion propagation supports the mechanism axis despite genetic initiation.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: this is a transmissible prion disease involving infectious prion propagation; hereditary initiation does not remove its prion mechanism.

basis: LAM-cell proliferation produces cystic pulmonary destruction and pleural disease; associated renal angiomyolipoma is a separate tumour.
Neurodegeneration classified within brain iron accumulation and inherited metabolic disorders; gaze palsy and incontinence are neurologic manifestations.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss confined to the auditory system.
Congenital split-hand/foot malformation is a structural limb skeletal disorder.
Neurodevelopmental language disorder with impaired phonologic memory and speech development.
Neurodevelopmental language disorder with impaired expressive language, phonologic memory and nonword repetition.
Oral malformation syndrome with cleft palate in 22/27, cleft lip in 15/27 and lip pits in 14/27.
Hereditary tumor syndrome defined by cutaneous melanoma and exocrine pancreatic cancer; other associated tumor risks do not establish additional involvement.
Subcutaneous fat loss 4/5; cataracts and neurodegeneration define syndrome. Pulmonary/vascular findings (1/2) omitted at cap; pancreatitis is a separate complication.
Microcephalic primordial skeletal dwarfism defines the subtype. Ocular and oral defects are singleton observations without established >=30% prevalence; renal ectopia is occasional.
audit_reason: Remove ocular and gastrointestinal: microphthalmia and microdontia/microglossia in one assessed patient do not establish involvement in at least 30% of this subtype. Microcephalic skeletal dwarfism remains defining.

basis: Fulminant immune-mediated hemorrhagic demyelination of brain and spinal cord.
Hyperinsulinism and hyperammonemia define the metabolic disorder; developmental impairment and intrinsic epilepsy occur in 30-79%.
Defining chronic airway disease; persistent middle-ear inflammation/effusion affects most PCD patients (>50%). Hearing impairment here is 5-29%; situs reversal alone causes no cardiac damage.

decisions.otologic: involved: chronic middle-ear disease affects >50% in the usual PCD course; the 5-29% hearing-loss annotation does not measure the frequency of persistent otitis.

basis: Stromal tumour arising in the gastrointestinal tract; anemia and liver abnormalities are occasional, and syndromic associations are separate conditions.
Isolated failure of sperm production or motility affects reproductive function; endocrine gonadal dysfunction is not established.
Dysferlin-related skeletal myopathy with distal and progressive proximal weakness; no independent nerve disease established.
Intellectual disability and eye/skin anomalies define syndrome; structural jaw and toe abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Obesity and dental abnormalities omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none at cap: defining obesity occurs in 30-79%, but structural skeletal abnormalities receive the remaining slot based on direct organ impairment.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: hallux valgus, cone-shaped toe epiphyses and jaw abnormalities occur in 30-79%; retained within the four-axis cap.

basis: Developmental facial muscle overgrowth; eyelid ptosis in 4/5 supports ocular involvement. Septal deviation alone does not establish airway dysfunction.
Inherited glucose transport defect causes defining encephalopathy and epilepsy; erythrocyte morphology alone does not establish blood dysfunction.
Deficient hepatic bilirubin conjugation causes unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia; permanent neurologic injury is uncommon in type 2.
Peripheral arterial occlusive disease directly affects arteries; no additional organ damage is established.
Focal dystonia defined by involuntary eyelid closure; neurologic motor dysfunction and the eyelids are the defining sites.
TCA-cycle disorder defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment and cerebral malformations; hepatic failure/cholestasis in 2/2 selected cases does not establish typical prevalence.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic failure/cholestasis in 2/2 selected cases is insufficient to establish >=30% across this predominantly neurologic disease.
decisions.neurologic: primary: psychomotor impairment, seizures and cerebral malformations define the disease; encephalopathy is frequent (30-79%).

basis: Inherited intestinal glucose-galactose transport defect causes severe malabsorption and diarrhea; renal insufficiency and stones occur in only 5–29%.
Inherited digital skeletal dysplasia with brachydactyly and progressive small-joint arthropathy in essentially all reported patients.
Sleep-related movement disorder with bruxism and myoclonus. Dental damage is not established as common for this specific syndrome.
Defined by cardiomyopathy, neuropathy with distal sensory loss, and skeletal myopathy with nemaline bodies; respiratory insufficiency does not establish direct lung damage.
CD40 class-switch immunodeficiency; intrinsic neutropenia occurs in roughly half or more of patients. Secondary infections do not independently establish organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic neutropenia affects roughly half or more of patients with CD40 deficiency, exceeding the 30% threshold.

basis: Intellectual disability with developmental delay in 20/20 patients; frequencies of associated skeletal, oral and ocular malformations are unspecified.
Inherited Parkinson disease subtype causing degeneration of central motor pathways.
Cortical malformation with developmental disability and epilepsy. Esotropia (5/5) reflects abnormal neurologic gaze control; intrinsic ocular damage is not established.

decisions.ocular: none: esotropia in 5/5 establishes gaze misalignment, but not direct eye injury; the defining pathology is cerebral.

basis: The supplied definition specifies familial pancreatic carcinoma, establishing an exocrine pancreatic tumor rather than susceptibility alone.
GIST and neuroendocrine paragangliomas define the syndrome; tumor-related cranial nerve paralysis and hearing impairment each occur in 30–79%.
PSEN2-associated cortical neurodegeneration; cerebral amyloid angiopathy is a distinct disease, and vascular deposits alone do not establish functional damage.
Intraosseous venous malformations deform bone; oral bleeding/ectopic teeth 8/8 and visual loss 5/6. Secondary blood-loss anemia omitted at the four-axis cap.
Defining intestinal atresia and volvulus with absent mesentery and superior mesenteric artery.
Defined by distal joint fusion, carpal abnormalities, microdontia and dental pulp calcification; nail anomaly frequencies are unspecified.
Usher type 1G is defined by sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal dystrophy.
Partial tyrosinase deficiency is an inborn melanin-synthesis disorder, defining skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with impaired vision.

Photosensitive epilepsy phenotype defined by abnormal cerebral electrical responses; light sensitivity does not indicate eye damage.

audit_reason: Add neurologic primary: congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles with synergistic divergence is a congenital cranial dysinnervation disorder, involving abnormal ocular motor innervation as well as ocular motility.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; retinal detachment frequency is unspecified.
Inherited cardiac channelopathy causing shortened repolarization and potentially lethal atrial or ventricular arrhythmias.
Cardiac channelopathy causing shortened repolarization and atrial or ventricular arrhythmias.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common clinodactyly is minor digit dysmorphism without demonstrated functional damage; significant skeletal lesions are occasional.

basis: Autoinflammatory osteomyelitis and congenital dyserythropoietic anemia define disease; dermatosis is transient and organomegaly alone does not establish damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: inferred from central DI in ~70% of classic HPE; ZIC2-specific frequency is uncertain. [Cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16355806/)

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure in 30-79% establishes frequency, but its mechanism is unspecified and direct pulmonary injury is not demonstrated.

basis: Defining eye/pituitary defects; developmental delay and auditory canal atresia each 80-99%. Limb anomalies omitted at the four-axis cap; individual digit defects and renal hypoplasia are <30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: defining limb abnormalities qualify but are omitted at the four-axis cap, prioritizing severe eye/pituitary defects and frequent CNS and auditory canal abnormalities.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal atresia is a direct structural ear abnormality reported in 80-99%; occasional hearing impairment does not negate that lesion.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no other organ disease is established.
Nonsyndromic inner-ear hearing disorder; profound sensorineural hearing impairment in 9/9 patients.
Keratin-filled cyst arising from the hair follicle outer root sheath, usually in scalp skin.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft lip/palate has no supplied frequency or established status as a major diagnostic criterion; facial dysmorphism alone does not establish gastrointestinal disease.

basis: Defining osteolysis of tali, patellae and scaphoids with joint inflammation; renal disease explicitly absent.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; COL11A2 does not justify adding skeletal involvement to this defined phenotype.
Spastic paraplegia, auditory hearing loss and symptomatic hiatal hernia define SPG29. Structural pes cavus occurs in 30-79%; bilirubin elevation alone does not establish hepatic damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: symptomatic hiatal or paraesophageal hernia is part of the syndrome's definition; hiatus hernia is annotated in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed structural pes cavus occurs in 30-79%; this is musculoskeletal deformity within the syndrome, beyond weakness or spasticity alone.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing impairment from auditory neuropathy is a defining manifestation; hearing loss belongs to the otologic axis and occurs in 30-79%.

basis: POMC deficiency causes obesity and ACTH/adrenal failure; cholestatic liver dysfunction occurs in 30-79%; hair and skin pigmentation do not establish damage.
CRYBB3-related nonsyndromic lens cataract; no extraocular disease is defined.

Familial aneurysmal disease of the abdominal aorta.
Familial Alzheimer disease causes cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
TGM5-related acral epidermal peeling is a skin disorder. Frequent hypermetropia annotation does not establish disease-caused ocular injury; allergy is separate.

decisions.ocular: none: despite the 30-79% annotation, hypermetropia is not an established direct manifestation of TGM5-related acral peeling skin syndrome.

basis: Inherited epilepsy characterized by febrile and generalized seizures.
Congenital fibrolipomatous hamartomas occupy precalcaneal subcutaneous tissue.
CEL-related monogenic diabetes; intrinsic exocrine pancreatic dysfunction affects most patients (>30%) and often precedes diabetes.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: exocrine pancreatic dysfunction affects most patients and is intrinsic to CEL-MODY; the supplied definition identifies the primary disease as diabetes.

basis: Vertebral segmentation and rib defects define the skeletal disease; explicit fucoglycosan-synthesis ancestry identifies an inherited glycosylation disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the supplied fucoglycosan-synthesis-disorder ancestry establishes a metabolic mechanism, beyond the LFNG gene name alone.

basis: Complement-mediated glomerulopathy with factor H deficiency and impaired immune defense; associated infections and autoimmune diagnoses are separate diseases.
Isolated syndactyly is a congenital structural abnormality of the digits.
Immune-mediated lymphocytic inflammation of cutaneous small vessels defines skin and vascular involvement.
Inherited erythrocytosis defined by increased red-cell mass; vascular complications are not defining or established as common.
Inherited platelet P2Y12 receptor dysfunction impairs aggregation; bruising and mucosal bleeding do not establish additional organ damage.
TRIOBP-related nonsyndromic severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss.

Inherited thyrotropin resistance causing congenital hypothyroidism; no common extra-endocrine damage is established for this subtype.
PLN-related isolated dilated cardiomyopathy directly impairs cardiac structure and systolic function.
Inherited retinal photoreceptor degeneration causing progressive visual loss.
Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; cardiac involvement reported in 16/16 patients.
Hereditary gallbladder disorder; the gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Hereditary gallbladder disease; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
TOPORS-related retinal degeneration causes visual field loss and abnormal retinal function.
Amino-acid metabolic defect with defining neurologic manifestations; encephalopathy is frequent (30–79%); hearing loss in one patient does not establish prevalence.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Heart defects, developmental disability and pectus deformity characterize KRAS Noonan syndrome; strabismus 8/14 and ptosis 7/12; leukemia 1/5 excluded.
Ectodermal dysplasia and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; frequencies of additional ocular and skeletal abnormalities are unspecified.
Limb-bone malformations define disease; reported hearing, renal, ocular and developmental abnormalities lack frequencies supporting the 30% threshold.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; hearing impairment documented in 5/5 patients.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 4/4 patients.
Hereditary fibrous overgrowth of gingival tissue; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 16/16 patients.
Insulin-receptor dysfunction causes hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; episodic coma and seizures do not establish lasting brain injury.
HADH-related hyperinsulinism; hepatic steatosis/transaminitis and hypoglycemic encephalopathy each 80-99% in supplied HPO; retinal and peripheral nerve damage <30%.
Defining NK-cell deficiency and adrenal insufficiency occur in 6/6. Developmental delay 5/6 and microcephaly 3/4 support neurologic involvement; pigmentation alone is not skin damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: reduced NK-cell count in 6/6 is a defining deficiency of a blood-cell population; the blood-cell rule applies alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Familial panic disorder is an anxiety disorder; hereditary classification does not establish neurologic damage.
