decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, not an isolated hair disorder ([clinical report](https://doi.org/10.1002/ajmg.a.20411)).

basis: Defined by sclerosing bone dysplasia, ichthyosis and premature ovarian endocrine failure, each reported in 80-99%.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Congenital multiple joint contractures and deafness define the syndrome; inguinal hernias do not establish intrinsic intestinal damage.
Neuronal lipid-storage disease with epilepsy and cognitive decline; supplied phenotypes report progressive visual loss and retinal/optic dysfunction in 30-79%.
Isoleucine degradation disorder, usually asymptomatic; neurologic findings occur in 5-29%, and muscle findings from one patient do not establish common involvement.
Glutamine synthesis defect with congenital brain dysgenesis and seizures; micromelia and fixed contractures each reported in 1/2 patients.
Multiple congenital bone and joint fusions define the syndrome; hearing impairment is not established for this subtype.
Inherited cataract affecting the lens.
Pancreatic beta-cell dysregulation causes exercise-induced hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; hypoglycemic seizures do not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Brachydactyly and structural ocular malformations define the syndrome; hearing loss and developmental delay lack established frequencies.
Retinal cone dysfunction causes impaired colour vision and reduced visual acuity; the neurologic ancestor adds no separate brain involvement.
Cortical and other brain malformations with developmental impairment; ocular abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Cortical developmental disorder with epilepsy and intellectual impairment; strabismus reported in 3/3 assessed patients; constipation alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Congenital corneal stromal dystrophy causes corneal opacity and visual loss.
Hereditary mixed colonic polyposis directly occupies intestinal mucosa; cancer susceptibility adds no other axis.
Familial primary hyperparathyroidism; skeletal mineral loss is common (~30% or more), supported by the mineralization-disorder ancestry.
PNPO deficiency is an inborn vitamin B6 metabolic disorder causing neonatal epileptic encephalopathy; sideroblastic anemia is occasional (5-29%).
Isolated developmental eye disease with microphthalmia, coloboma and sometimes cataract.
Isolated developmental eye disorder; microphthalmia and corneal stromal opacity in 6/6 patients.
Progressive skeletal muscle degeneration defines the myopathy; distal sensory impairment in 30-79% supports additional peripheral neurologic dysfunction.
Hereditary axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle wasting and foot deformities follow denervation rather than direct skeletal disease. Cardiomyopathy frequency is unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy and foot deformities are consequences of motor denervation; direct disease of muscle, bone or joints is not established.

basis: Complement C7 immunodeficiency; recurrent Neisserial infections are consequences, not intrinsic damage to another organ.
Ocular malformations and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define the syndrome; pituitary hypoplasia (5/5) and hormone deficiencies support common endocrine dysfunction.
Lysosomal storage neurodegeneration; rod-cone dystrophy in 5/5 supports common direct retinal damage; vascular deposits lack demonstrated dysfunction.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: conduction abnormalities and ventricular bigeminy in 1/1 assessed patient establish possibility, but insufficient evidence of involvement in at least 30% of patients.

basis: Defined by cardiac conduction disease/cardiomyopathy and digital skeletal malformations; myopathy occurs in only 1/14 and adds no separate axis.
Inherited nonsyndromic prelingual sensorineural hearing loss.

Nonsyndromic profound prelingual sensorineural deafness.
ADCY1-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.

Inherited corneal endothelial degeneration with corneal guttata and edema.

audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary: the defining T-lymphocyte defect, with documented lymphopenia, meets the blood-cell disease rule. Retain dermatologic for erythroderma reported in 1/1.

basis: Arterial aneurysms and skeletal/skin connective-tissue abnormalities; exotropia affects 6/10. Blue sclerae and asymptomatic dural ectasia do not establish additional damage.
Hereditary kyphoscoliosis is a structural spinal disorder; common intrinsic damage to another organ is not established.
RNASEH2B-related interferonopathy with defining encephalopathy, cerebral atrophy and intracranial calcification.
Cerebellar malformation/atrophy and intellectual disability define the disease; sensorineural hearing impairment in 1/2 supports ear involvement, with limited sampling.
Diaphragm defect; lung hypoplasia and pulmonary hypertension 2/2; intestinal malrotation 2/2; neurologic findings omitted by four-axis cap.
Oculorenal Joubert subtype: cerebellar malformation and developmental impairment, congenital blindness 11/19, and kidney failure 11/12.
Senior-Loken syndrome combines nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy; kidney failure and rod-cone dystrophy each documented in 2/2.
Inherited arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with ventricular myocardial disease and arrhythmias.
Metabolic disorder defined by cardiomyopathy and ataxia; anemia in 12/18 (~67%); hepatic steatosis 5-29% and optic atrophy 4/18 excluded.
Diabetes and hypothyroidism define syndrome; hepatic fibrosis 50%, glaucoma/buphthalmos ~67%, renal cystic disease ~33%; neurodevelopmental impairment ~33% omitted by cap.
Early-onset nonsyndromic cataract; associated abnormalities are also confined to the eye.
Severe congenital pontocerebellar hypoplasia with microcephaly and seizures.
Bile-duct, cardiac and vertebral defects define the syndrome; renal malformations/dysfunction occur in roughly 40%+. Posterior embryotoxon usually preserves vision.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: butterfly vertebrae are a major diagnostic skeletal feature explicitly included in the definition.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 8/8; other DCDC2-associated diseases are separate concepts.

Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ disease is defined.
Inherited epidermal disorder with seborrhea-like dermatitis, acanthosis and hyperkeratosis; no established systemic immune disease.
Nonsyndromic congenital fusion and duplication of digits.
Hereditary corticospinal tract degeneration causes spastic paraplegia; weakness and abnormal gait do not establish primary muscle damage.
Cerebellar degeneration with ataxia and sensory dysfunction; abnormal saccades reflect neurologic control rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Mitochondrial disorder causing cerebellar degeneration; ophthalmoparesis, abnormal saccades and ptosis reflect neurologic motor dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye injury.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation directly affects the esophagus.
Isolated hereditary hearing impairment without syndromic organ involvement.
Corticospinal tract degeneration with possible peripheral neuropathy; weakness and amyotrophy are neurogenic rather than evidence of primary muscle disease.

Neurodevelopmental disability defines the syndrome; hearing impairment and structural heart defects/arrhythmias are frequent (30-79%). Renal disease is occasional.
Congenital absence of the lens with associated developmental defects confined to ocular structures.
Inherited hypertrophy of the gastric pylorus causes gastric outlet obstruction.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 13/13 patients.
Cortical malformation with developmental impairment and seizures; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Incontinence reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration causing progressive visual loss.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration causing progressive visual loss.
GPI biosynthesis defect with defining hypercoagulability and venous thrombosis; seizures occur in 2/3. Hepatomegaly reflects portal vascular disease without established hepatic injury.

decisions.neurologic: involved: seizures occur in 2/3; the three primary slots prioritize the metabolic defect, coagulopathy and defining vascular thrombosis.

basis: Autonomic sweating disorder with sensorimotor neuropathy; scoliosis, restricted elbow extension and skeletal anomalies reported in 1/1 patient.
The defining constellation combines rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia and scoliosis with retinal degeneration.
Inherited myopia is an ocular growth and refractive disorder.
Hereditary prostate malignancy; the prostate is outside the specified axes. Metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ labels.
Interferonopathy with destructive encephalopathy; inflammatory chilblain lesions occur in roughly 40% of AGS. Hepatic and blood findings may be transient; subtype frequencies uncertain.
Type I interferonopathy causes destructive encephalopathy and leukodystrophy; persistent hepatic, blood or skin damage in at least 30% is not established for AGS4.
Congenital anomalous pulmonary artery origin and associated cardiac malformations; pulmonary arteries belong to the cardiovascular axis.
Inherited focal epilepsy; nocturnal seizures occur in 10/10 reported patients.
Inherited retinal photoreceptor dysfunction causes progressive visual impairment; no established extraocular disease.
Motor pathway degeneration and neuropathy define disease; lasting distal muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%). Abnormal saccades reflect neurological dysfunction.
Inherited retinal degeneration with rod-cone dysfunction and progressive visual impairment.
Structural cleft of the lip and/or palate affects the mouth.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defining absence of intestinal hormone-producing enteroendocrine cells is intrinsic endocrine dysfunction, independently of separately diagnosed diabetes.

basis: ABCC8-related transient neonatal diabetes is an endocrine pancreatic insulin-secretion disorder.
Metabolic autoinflammation with defining neurodevelopmental impairment; cataracts 3/3. Myopathy, anemia and hepatosplenic involvement omitted at four-axis cap.

basis: Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with macular atrophy and progressive visual loss.

Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease is established.
Isolated congenital accessory auricular tag, an external-ear malformation; no syndromic organ involvement is specified.
The defining manifestations are generalized alopecia and intellectual disability.
Nonsyndromic inherited cataract with microcornea; disease is confined to the eye.
Congenital retinal photoreceptor synaptic dysfunction causes stationary visual impairment and abnormal electroretinography.
Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia is a lymphoplasmacytic B-cell lymphoma involving marrow and monoclonal immunoglobulin production.
Microliths in testicular seminiferous tissue are reproductive pathology; endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability define this NANS-related sialic acid biosynthesis disorder; cerebral atrophy occurs in 4/6.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; ptosis/strabismus 30-99%, hip dysplasia/dislocation 30-79% and ventricular septal defect 30-79% support additional axes.

RHO-related retinal dysfunction causing congenital stationary night blindness.
Immune-mediated ulcerative chilblain lupus; digital autoamputation in 1/3 (~33%) establishes destructive limb involvement. Arthralgia alone would not qualify.

basis: Inherited calcification disorder with calcinosis cutis in 8/8 patients; qualifying frequency or damage is not established for gingivitis or conjunctivitis.
Inherited thiopurine metabolism defect; marrow toxicity requires thiopurine exposure and is excluded as a treatment effect.
Defining skeletal abnormalities and hearing loss; intellectual disability in 11/12 and global developmental delay in 13/22 support neurologic involvement.
Cortisol elevation occurs in 3/4. In overt hypercortisolism, hypertension affects ~70%, skin atrophy/striae >50% and bone loss ~50%; subtype-specific frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypertension is a direct manifestation of cortisol excess in roughly 70% of overt cases; subtype-specific frequency is unavailable.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: sustained cortisol excess directly causes skin atrophy and striae in over 50% of overt cases; these are tissue changes rather than transient rash.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: cortisol directly causes bone loss in approximately 50% of overt cases; osteopenia, osteoporosis and kyphosis are supplied phenotypes.

basis: DSC2-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy; definition specifies isolated cardiac disease. Skin and hair findings are not established as common.
Inherited retinal photoreceptor dysfunction causing cone or cone-rod dystrophy and visual impairment.
B-cell maturation defect and severe dermatitis; developmental impairment 30-79%. Cap omits craniosynostosis, cleft palate, choanal stenosis and eyelid defects, each 30-79%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defective B-cell maturation with reduced B-cell count in 80-99% directly affects blood cells.
decisions.neurologic: involved: microcephaly and developmental delay occur in 30-79%; retained after the three-primary cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: craniosynostosis occurs in 30-79%, but immune/blood-cell disease, severe dermatitis and neurodevelopmental impairment take priority.

basis: Adrenal cortisol excess causes bone loss (~50-80%) and skin atrophy (~50%) in overt disease; subtype frequencies uncertain. Hypertension is separately diagnosed.
Mitochondrial lactic acidosis with defining brain defects and brachydactyly; PDA 1/1. Hepatic enzyme/complex abnormalities alone do not establish functional liver damage.

decisions.hepatic: none: transaminase elevation and reduced respiratory-chain activity in liver do not establish sustained hepatic dysfunction or structural damage.
decisions.cardiovascular: involved: patent ductus arteriosus is a structural cardiovascular abnormality reported in 1/1 patient; frequency evidence is limited to this case.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: brachydactyly is explicitly part of the defining syndrome and occurs in 1/1 patient; it represents structural bone abnormality.

basis: Obstetric disorder of the chorioamniotic membranes; no covered organ is intrinsically affected.
OXPHOS disorder with defining hepatic insufficiency and encephalopathy (1/2); hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 1/2. Muscle injury/rhabdomyolysis 1/2 also qualifies but is omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic insufficiency is explicitly part of the defining clinical description, establishing functional liver disease.
decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy occurs in 1/2; primary slots prioritize metabolic disease, defining hepatic insufficiency and encephalopathy.

basis: Monogenic diabetes; separately diagnosed diabetic organ complications are excluded.
CNS/PNS hypomyelination and congenital cataract define disease; scoliosis occurs in 4/10 and lower-limb muscle atrophy in 9/10; auditory conduction delay is central.

Storage disorder; cytopenias/splenic involvement and hepatomegaly 80-100%; seizures/neurodegeneration 30-79%. Osteopenia (~50%) omitted at four-axis cap.
Defined by a glycosylation defect, neuromuscular transmission failure and tubular-aggregate muscle pathology. Retinoschisis is reported in 2/4 patients (50%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: tubular-aggregate muscle pathology is part of the named disease and parent concept, beyond weakness from junction dysfunction.

basis: Developmental disability and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; heart and urinary anomalies each occur in 30-79%. Common gastrointestinal dysfunction omitted by the cap.
Severe insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia and androgen excess define the endocrine disorder; persistent acanthosis nigricans is part of its defining triad.
HSV directly infects and damages brain tissue; ventilation needs and transient electrolyte abnormalities do not establish additional organ damage.
Transient neonatal diabetes from impaired insulin secretion; no common neurologic or other organ damage is established for this subtype.
PRCD-associated retinal photoreceptor degeneration.
Aldosterone synthesis deficiency causing hyperkalemia, hyponatremia and salt wasting; no intrinsic renal tissue disease is established.
Inherited retinal dystrophy causes congenital blindness; no extraocular disease is established.
Defined by subcutaneous, visceral and upper-airway angioedema; F12-associated disease is bradykinin-mediated rather than allergic or autoimmune.
Defined as nonsyndromic early-onset cataract; unquantified neurologic annotations do not establish syndromic involvement.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and developmental olfactory dysfunction define the Kallmann phenotype; hyposmia 2/4, anosmia 1/4. Osteoporosis 2/8 is below threshold.

decisions.neurologic: primary: olfactory developmental dysfunction is a defining Kallmann component, explicitly represented by anosmia in the name; hyposmia 2/4 and anosmia 1/4.

basis: RPS24-related congenital red-cell aplasia; supplied phenotypes establish hematologic disease without common extrahematologic damage.
Palmoplantar keratoderma defines skin disease. Sex reversal alone has no axis; endocrine dysfunction is not established and lipid abnormalities have no frequency.
XP-B commonly has Cockayne-like neurologic degeneration and damaging ocular disease, generally >30%; hearing-loss frequency is insufficiently established.

Vascular malformations and mucocutaneous telangiectases define HHT; recurrent nasal bleeding is a major criterion supporting pulmonary involvement. HHT4-specific visceral injury frequencies are unknown.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: characteristic mucocutaneous telangiectases define HHT, and this genetic subtype has no evidence of excluding that defining manifestation.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining destructive encephalopathy. Respiratory failure does not establish intrinsic lung injury; muscle enzyme defects alone do not establish myopathy.
Bone fragility, fractures and skeletal deformity define CRTAP-related osteogenesis imperfecta; blue sclerae alone do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Congenital limb skeletal malformations include ectrodactyly and long-bone deficiency.
Structural skeletal myopathy with nemaline bodies and weakness; respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung disease.
Cerebellar malformation defines disease; hepatic fibrosis 2/5; TMEM67-associated coloboma and nephronophthisis each affect roughly one-third or more.
Macular degeneration directly damages the retina; CFH association alone does not establish an immune disease.
Inner-ear aplasia, microtia and congenital deafness define ear involvement; microdontia and dental abnormalities define oral involvement.
Hereditary optic nerve degeneration with optic atrophy in 4/4; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Defined by shortened or absent phalanges, toe syndactyly and metacarpal/metatarsal abnormalities.
Lipid-storage myopathy; cardiomyopathy and hepatic steatosis occur in 30-79%. Intellectual disability and pancreatitis have sparse reports and are omitted under the cap.
PLCE1-related glomerular disease causes nephrotic syndrome and commonly kidney failure; no immune mechanism is established.
Cardiac and skeletal defects define syndrome; ptosis 16/16 and bleeding 6/17 support involvement. Keratosis pilaris 9/17 omitted at cap in favor of more consequential organ dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: involved: eyelid ptosis occurs in 16/16 annotated patients and represents a persistent structural and functional eyelid defect.
decisions.dermatologic: none at cap: keratosis pilaris occurs in 9/17, but cardiac, skeletal, eyelid and coagulation defects take priority for severity.

basis: Severe neutropenia causes immunodeficiency; developmental delay affects 3/8 (~38%); sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 2/2 assessed, with limited sampling.
Progressive cerebellar and motor-neuron disease. Muscle wasting (30-79%) is neurogenic; ocular pursuit abnormalities reflect CNS dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy (30-79%) reflects denervation from motor-neuron disease, without evidence of direct muscle pathology; skeletal deformities occur in under 30%.

basis: The supplied concept concerns hereditary iris pattern; ocular localization is supported, but functional impairment is unspecified.
Alopecia areata is autoimmune injury to hair follicles, including total or universal hair loss.
Endocrine tumor syndrome; renal angiomyolipoma, skin tumors and pulmonary carcinoid each annotated 30-79%; GI ulceration omitted by cap.
COFS defines brain, eye and skeletal abnormalities; hearing impairment reported in 1/1. Skin/hair findings omitted under the four-axis cap; photosensitivity alone is not injury.
COFS phenotype includes severe brain malformations, bilateral microphthalmia and extensive skeletal malformations with contractures.
Developmental disability and limb defects define syndrome; intrinsic reflux 11/16 and hearing impairment 7/13. Myopia 5/11 omitted under four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intrinsic oesophageal dysfunction with reflux in 11/16 (~69%) is a common syndrome manifestation.
decisions.ocular: none: myopia in 5/11 (~45%) qualifies, but less frequent ocular impairment is omitted under the four-axis cap.

basis: Glycosylation defect with cardiomyopathy (80-99%) and ichthyosis (3/4); seizures and developmental delay occur in 30-79%. Elevated transaminases alone do not establish liver damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder defined by hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis and skeletal muscle dysfunction.
Epiphyseal dysplasia with abnormal bone development, absent hand bones and joint deformities.
Immunodeficiency with constitutional neutropenia and defining partial albinism, each 80-99%. Recurrent infections alone do not establish chronic pulmonary damage.
Congenital structural abnormalities of the kidneys and urinary tract define this disease.
Forebrain malformation defines disease; microphthalmia and cleft lip each reported in 2/4. Panhypopituitarism 1/8 does not meet threshold.
Forebrain/callosal malformation; maxillary hypoplasia 20/20, dental malocclusion 11/14. Panhypopituitarism 3/11 (~27%, near 30%) supports endocrine involvement in this pituitary-associated phenotype.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine involvement: panhypopituitarism occurs in 3/11 (~27%, approximately 30%), and pituitary anomalies characterize the GLI2 phenotype. The rule allows an approximate threshold.

basis: Skeletal disorder defined by multifocal bone destruction and excessive bone formation; no supported extraskeletal involvement.
Marrow failure defines FANCN; thumb hypoplasia 3/8 and microphthalmia 3/7 support involvement. Microcephaly alone lacks functional CNS evidence; associated tumors are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly in 16/18 does not establish functional brain damage; medulloblastoma is a separately diagnosed malignancy.

basis: Inherited myxomatous mitral valve prolapse with regurgitation is a structural cardiac valve disorder.
Skin elastic-fiber damage and clotting-factor deficiency define disease. Intrinsic arterial lesions reported at 30-79%; cerebral artery dilation 1/2. Angioid streaks alone lack visual loss.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic sinonasal and airway disease; recurrent infections reflect impaired clearance rather than immunodeficiency.
Inherited vesicoureteral reflux affects the urinary tract; associated renal hypoplasia remains within the renal axis.
Airway abnormality/apnea 80-99%; cardiovascular malformations and scoliosis 30-79%. Frequent high hypermetropia omitted by four-axis cap.
Branchiootorenal syndrome is defined by ear/hearing and renal developmental abnormalities; hearing impairment 4/4 and renal dysplasia 2/4.
Progressive supranuclear palsy is a neurodegenerative movement disorder; supranuclear gaze dysfunction arises centrally.

Inherited surfactant metabolism disorders cause alveolar accumulation and impaired gas exchange; autoimmunity is not the mechanism of this hereditary umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental delay reported in 1/2 is insufficient to distinguish direct neurodevelopmental disease from limitations caused by severe skeletal disease.

basis: Inherited surfactant phospholipid metabolism dysfunction causes alveolar accumulation and interstitial lung disease; recurrent infections do not establish immunodeficiency.
Selective congenital absence of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited coronary atherosclerotic disease; diabetes in 11/15 is a separately diagnosed disease, as are osteoporosis and gout.
Lysosomal storage disease causing neurodegeneration; progressive retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients.

Neurodevelopmental disease; refractive impairment, chronic bowel dysfunction/dental malposition and foot deformities each 80-99% in supplied HPO. Central breathing spells do not establish lung damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent intestinal dysmotility causes functional impairment; constipation and dental malposition are annotated 80-99%, reflux 4/4.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent pes valgus in 80-99% and pes planus in 4/4 represent common structural foot deformities, beyond neurologic hypotonia alone.

Inherited paroxysmal movement disorder causing dystonia, chorea and dyskinesia.

Isolated microphthalmia with retinal degeneration, foveoschisis and impaired vision; manifestations remain within the ocular axis.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurological dysfunction is explicit in the definition and encephalopathy occurs in 3/4 patients.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none under cap: direct myopathy occurs in 30-79%, but defining cardiac/CNS disease and hepatic involvement take priority.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia causes respiratory impairment, a major feature of asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy; thoracic skeletal dysplasia is primary.

basis: Hereditary juvenile open-angle glaucoma damages the ocular optic nerve.
Inborn error of valine metabolism; cardiomyopathy and developmental impairment are occasional, below 30%, and most screened patients lack such damage.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining T/B lymphopenia and microcephaly; recurrent respiratory infections are separately diagnosed infections.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy at 30-79% reflects neurogenic muscle wasting; direct skeletal muscle disease is not established.

basis: Persistent fetal vitreous and its vasculature cause congenital structural eye disease.

Degeneration of the retinal macula causes loss of central vision.
Inherited cortisol-binding and transport disorder. Anemia in one annotated patient does not establish common blood damage; hypotension alone is not vascular damage.

Inherited cardiac rhythm disorder defined by atrial fibrillation.

GLIS2-related nephronophthisis causes renal tubular atrophy and progressive kidney failure.

TYK2-related immunodeficiency; recurrent infections do not establish common lasting damage to another organ.
Isolated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy; ventricular disease and arrhythmias define the condition.

Inherited bipolar affective disorder; a purely psychiatric condition without established damage to an organ axis.

CRYBB1-related nonsyndromic cataract affects the lens.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: characteristic structural chest-wall deformities affect approximately 50% in Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines; RAF1-specific estimates are limited.

basis: Defining renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis and intellectual disability; skeletal damage includes scoliosis 4/4, osteopenia 3/3 and femoral necrosis 2/4.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic ductal-plate malformation is a core Meckel feature; bile duct proliferation occurs in 3/3.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia is a structural eye defect reported in 3/3; retained for its substantial functional consequences.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none due to cap: polydactyly 3/3 and bowed long bones 2/3 qualify, but severe renal, CNS, hepatic and ocular defects take priority.

basis: Localized otic-capsule remodeling causes conductive or mixed hearing impairment; this is an ear disorder rather than generalized skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: rickets is variable, not a defining criterion, and a >=30% frequency is not established for this subtype.

basis: Inherited cataract affecting the lens; no established extraocular damage.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia and characteristic blepharophimosis define it; nail dysplasia and structural external-ear hypoplasia each occur in 30-79%.

decisions.otologic: involved: microtia is permanent external-ear hypoplasia, annotated in 30-79%; hearing loss is not required to recognize this structural defect.

basis: Renal magnesium wasting defines the electrolyte disorder; intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures were reported in 2/2 patients.

Lysosomal storage encephalopathy. Hepatosplenomegaly in 2/2 does not establish functional organ damage; respiratory insufficiency lacks direct lung evidence; optic atrophy is 5-29%.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenomegaly in 2/2 establishes enlargement, but no hypersplenism, cytopenia or other splenic functional impairment is documented.
decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly in 2/2 without demonstrated hepatic dysfunction or fibrosis does not establish function-impairing storage.

basis: Sphingolipid storage disorder with central dysmyelination and peripheral neuropathy; central apnea and respiratory failure do not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Progressive neurodegeneration with NCL/metabolic ancestry; optic atrophy in 1/2 supports ocular damage (~50%), although visual loss is annotated 5-29%; small sample limits certainty.
audit_reason: Add ocular involvement: optic atrophy is direct damage reported in 1/2 patients, exceeding the approximate 30% threshold. Occasional visual loss is a distinct annotation and does not negate that evidence.

basis: Congenital retinal degeneration defines LCA10; seizures reported in 2/4 support neurologic involvement, with uncertainty from the small sample.
Innate immune autoinflammatory disease; sensorineural hearing impairment in 2/3 reported patients. Episodic urticaria and arthralgia do not establish lasting damage.

Angiopathy, nephropathy and muscle disease define HANAC; cerebral white-matter injury/stroke in 44-56%; retinal hemorrhage <30%, tortuosity alone need not impair vision.
Immune-mediated medium-vessel vasculitis; transient mucocutaneous findings, reactive blood counts and proteinuria do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited cardiac conduction and ventricular rhythm disorder.
Inherited erythrocytosis; thromboses are separately diagnosed complications, and isolated 1/1 reports do not establish a population frequency of at least 30%.
ACTA2-associated thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection; no common direct injury outside the vascular axis is established for this phenotype.
Inherited erythrocyte membrane disorder causing elliptocytosis and possible hemolysis; jaundice does not establish liver damage.
Essential tremor and normal pressure hydrocephalus are defining neurologic manifestations.
BEST1-associated retinal dystrophy with central visual loss and impaired retinal electrophysiology.
Defining renal, adrenal and lung dysgenesis; oral clefts 2/3 and bowel malrotation 30-79%. Cardiac defects 30-79% omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac malformations qualify at 30-79%, but are omitted under the cap; oral clefts have a specific 2/3 estimate plus frequent bowel malrotation.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate/lip in 2/3 and bowel malrotation in 30-79% establish common structural gastrointestinal involvement.

basis: Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder causing QT prolongation and arrhythmias; syncope alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder with prolonged QT and arrhythmia susceptibility.
Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder with prolonged QT and arrhythmia susceptibility.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: absent fingernails and toenails are permanent structural losses of skin appendages, annotated frequent (30-79%).
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal anomalies, including clinodactyly, are explicitly part of the syndrome definition; clinodactyly and pes planus are annotated in 30-79%.

basis: Hereditary prostate cancer arises in a reproductive organ; no qualifying additional organ involvement established.

Inherited cardiac electrical disorder causing arrhythmias; syncope does not establish neurological damage.

Isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular dysfunction and heart failure.

Anterior horn motor-neuron disease with congenital contractures and muscle atrophy; respiratory failure reflects neuromuscular weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Familial aneurysmal disease of the abdominal aorta.

ANG-related motor neuron degeneration; muscle wasting results from denervation rather than direct muscle disease.

basis: Isolated nanophthalmia: congenital reduction in eye size.

Hereditary prostate cancer arises in a reproductive organ, outside the defined axes.
Skeletal and muscle developmental abnormalities define the syndrome; intellectual disability and symblepharon each 30-79%. Numerous nevi do not establish skin dysfunction.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental impairment; dental abnormalities 30-79%, pes planus 2/4. Obesity 3/5 alone does not establish direct endocrine injury; major eye and heart defects are occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural pes planus occurs in 2/4 (50%); hypotonia alone would not establish primary muscle damage.

basis: Inherited ventricular arrhythmia. Syncope and seizure-like events from transient hypoperfusion do not establish primary neurologic damage.

basis: CoQ10 deficiency with cerebellar degeneration; myopathic proximal weakness occurs in 30–79%; ocular findings in 1/2 do not establish typical prevalence.

basis: Central movement disorder with dystonia and parkinsonism; swallowing and laryngeal manifestations arise from abnormal motor control.

basis: SUCLA2 metabolic encephalomyopathy with muscle atrophy in 12/12; hearing impairment 12/13. Ocular dysfunction annotated at 80-99% omitted because of the four-axis cap.

Glucose transport disorder causing dystonia and other neurologic dysfunction; direct hemolysis with anemia occurs in 4/4 annotated patients, although broader prevalence is uncertain.
Ectodermal sweat-gland, hair and dental defects with T-cell immunodeficiency; conical teeth in 1/1 and hypodontia are defining dental abnormalities. Organomegaly alone adds no axis.

decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing loss in 30-79% qualifies, but the four-axis cap prioritizes defining skeletal/skin disease, hydrocephalus and airway obstruction.

Defined by capillary and lymphatic malformations, a persistent cutaneous lip lesion, and asymmetric limb or tissue overgrowth.
Asphyxiating skeletal dysplasia with defining respiratory failure (80-99%); renal malformations and hepatic fibrosis each 30-79%. Cardiovascular anomalies (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: respiratory failure is a defining feature of asphyxiating thoracic dysplasia, with insufficiency reported in 80-99%.

basis: REN-associated tubulointerstitial kidney disease with defining early hypoproliferative anemia. Hyperuricemia reflects impaired renal urate handling rather than an independent metabolic disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hyperuricemia results from renal urate handling abnormalities; the disease is not defined by a separate systemic metabolic or endocrine defect.

basis: PDE6C-related retinal cone degeneration causes visual impairment; no extraocular disease is established.
Microphthalmia defines the disorder. Polydactyly occurs in 1/3, but associated musculoskeletal damage or functional impairment is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: polydactyly in 1/3 meets the frequency threshold, but an additional digit alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage or loss of function.

basis: Renal cystic disease; hepatic cysts occur in 6/8, but clinically significant hepatic damage affects <30%. Cysts alone do not establish impaired liver function.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic cysts occur in 75%, but usually preserve function; damaging or functionally significant hepatic disease occurs in <30%.

basis: Spinal motor pathway disease with peripheral neuropathy; urinary symptoms and weakness reflect neurologic dysfunction. Skeletal abnormalities occur in under 30%.
Inherited susceptibility specifically concerns cutaneous melanoma; no current tumor or additional organ injury is inferred from susceptibility alone.
Hereditary open-angle glaucoma causes optic nerve damage within the ocular axis.
Cytotoxic immune defect with cytopenias; hepatic inflammation/dysfunction common (>50%); STXBP2 enteropathy affects roughly 30-40%. Hearing/lung singleton reports lack population support.
Inherited hypotrichosis and recurrent epidermal blistering define the disorder.
PRPH2-related chorioretinal dystrophy causes ocular degeneration; neurovascular ancestry does not establish separate brain or systemic vascular disease.
Inherited peripheral vestibular disorder; the vestibular organ belongs to the otologic axis.
Congenital neutrophil deficiency is both a blood-cell disorder and an innate immunodeficiency.
Inherited antifungal immune deficiency causing chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, including fungal nail disease; vulvovaginal disease has no anatomical axis.
Sensory-autonomic neuropathy with characteristic trophic injury: acral ulcers in 4/4 and distal phalangeal osteolysis in 3/3 patients.
Inherited coagulation disorder; thromboembolism is a separately diagnosed complication, with no supplied >=30% frequency. Osteonecrosis ancestry alone is insufficient.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: thrombophilia is a coagulation disorder; thromboembolism is a separately coded complication and its frequency is unspecified.

basis: Inherited coagulation inhibitor deficiency; DVT and pulmonary embolism are separately diagnosed thrombotic complications, not additional organ labels.
Cardiac electrical disorder causing characteristic ST elevation and potentially lethal ventricular arrhythmias.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with Brugada-pattern abnormalities and atrial arrhythmias.
Isolated NEXN-associated dilated cardiomyopathy; ventricular dilation and impaired systolic function are consistently documented.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with ventricular tachycardia and characteristic conduction/ECG abnormalities.
Gracile bones and limb/thoracic hypoplasia establish skeletal disease. Pulmonary and adrenal hypoplasia have unspecified frequencies; hydrops alone establishes no additional axis.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary hypoplasia is reported without frequency or evidence that it is a major diagnostic criterion; common involvement cannot be established.

basis: Infantile parkinsonism, dystonia and developmental impairment define the disease; constipation and reflux do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Central choroidal and retinal atrophy defines the dystrophy.
IL10RA immune dysfunction causes early enterocolitis; destructive pyoderma and folliculitis are characteristic, each reported in 1/1 annotated patients.
Muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; cleft palate directly affects oral structure in 1/3 reported patients (33%), with limited precision.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is a structural oral malformation reported in 1/3 patients (33%); the supplied frequency meets the threshold, although the cohort is small.

basis: Congenital muscular dystrophy with intellectual disability caused by defective protein O-glycosylation; ocular abnormalities lack sufficient frequency evidence.
Congenital muscular dystrophy; cerebral white-matter abnormalities reported in 1/1 annotated patient, supporting neurologic involvement despite preserved intellect.
Inherited O-glycosylation disorder with muscular dystrophy and brain malformations; defining structural eye abnormalities occur in 1/1. Ocular tier reflects the three-primary cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: defining microphthalmia, coloboma and corneal opacity occur in 1/1; retained as the fourth axis because primary is capped at three.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an inherited disorder of alpha-dystroglycan O-glycosylation, supported by its metabolic ancestry.

basis: Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; retinal dysplasia, cataract and optic atrophy are documented.
Congenital dystroglycan glycosylation disorder with muscular dystrophy and intellectual disability; myopia affects 3/5 (60%). Cardiomyopathy and cataracts occur in 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defective O-mannosyl glycosylation of dystroglycan constitutes an inborn glycosylation disorder, supported by the disease ancestry.

basis: Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining intellectual disability and brain malformations; defective dystroglycan glycosylation is an inherited metabolic disorder. Ocular findings 25%; cardiac <30%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: POMT2-related dystroglycanopathy is an inherited O-glycosylation disorder, qualifying for the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Muscular dystrophy from defective O-glycosylation; high myopia is characteristic and reported in 1/1 annotated patient, supporting ocular involvement with limited data.
POMT2-related skeletal muscular dystrophy; cognitive and learning impairment occur in 30-79%. Cardiomyopathy and ventricular dysfunction occur in only 5-29%.
Renal tubular disease; syndromic seizures/ID, sensorineural hearing loss and chronic pancreatic injury each 2/5. Secondary hypertension excluded.
Pyrimidine metabolism defect; seizures, intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 30-79%. Reduced hepatic enzyme activity alone is not liver damage.
Progressive spastic paraplegia; fixed knee/ankle/toe contractures in 80-99% and skeletal muscle atrophy in 8/10. Optic atrophy is occasional (5-29%).
Inborn GABA metabolic defect defined by obligate epileptic encephalopathy; cerebral dysmyelination and severe developmental delay occur in 80–99%.
Parkinson disease subtype; defining pathology and functional loss are neurologic.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular systolic dysfunction.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability occur in all reported patients; long fingers and high palate alone do not establish damaging skeletal or oral disease.
Defining cutis laxa 4/4, emphysema 3/3 and bladder diverticula 3/3; GI malformations include pyloric stenosis 2/4. Joint hypermobility 4/4 omitted under cap.

decisions.renal: primary: urinary anomalies are defining; bladder diverticula occur in 3/3 and hydronephrosis in 2/4.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: pyloric stenosis occurs in 2/4; the three-primary cap prioritizes the more consistently affected skin, lung and urinary organs.

basis: Purine metabolic immunodeficiency; intrinsic neurologic dysfunction affects roughly 30-79%. Autoimmune cytopenias and secondary infections are separately diagnosed.
Cortical and brainstem malformations with severe neurodevelopmental impairment and defining optic nerve hypoplasia.
Intellectual disability, microcephaly and brain abnormalities define the disorder; obesity alone does not establish intrinsic endocrine damage.
Defective airway cilia cause bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 3/5 patients. Situs inversus alone does not establish cardiac damage.
BEST1-associated rod-cone retinal degeneration causes progressive visual dysfunction.
Lens and anterior chamber abnormalities with short stature/acromelic dysplasia define the syndrome; skin involvement is not established by the phenotype record.
Primary skeletal-muscle dystrophy; intellectual disability reported in 1/3 supports neurological involvement, with a small denominator; respiratory weakness is muscular.
Skeletal muscle dystrophy and contractures; respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness (60%), not intrinsic lung disease; cardiac involvement <30%.
Hypomyelinating CNS disease; pes cavus in 3/3 and sensorineural hearing loss in 30-79%. Gaze and sphincter findings do not establish direct ocular or urinary-tract damage.

decisions.renal: none: sphincter dysfunction occurs in 30-79%, but reflects neurologic dysfunction without established direct urinary-tract damage.
decisions.ocular: none: strabismus and slow saccades accompany CNS dysfunction; intrinsic eye damage or loss of vision is not established.

basis: Inherited dental enamel hypomaturation; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis. Common renal involvement is not established here.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with developmental delay and central hypotonia in 80-99%; scoliosis 2/7 (<30%); other structural organ defects are occasional.
Retinal dysfunction defines disease; dry skin in 3/6 lacks established causal tissue damage. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2775833/)
Intestinal epithelial disease causes villous atrophy and irreversible intestinal failure; ocular, skin and joint abnormalities occur in <30%.
Cardiac and skeletal malformations characterize NS6; motor delay 9/12 and intellectual disability 2/5 support neurologic involvement. Cosmetic skin findings lack functional damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: keratosis pilaris in 4/9 and pigmentary changes exceed 30%, but do not establish significant inflammation, tissue injury or impaired skin function.

basis: Inherited coagulation factor XIII A deficiency; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish additional organ damage. Intracranial hemorrhage is a minority complication.
Cerebellar ataxia and intellectual disability define this neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus frequency is unspecified.
Compulsive hair pulling directly causes defining hair loss; the physical hair injury supports the dermatologic axis.
Inherited coagulation factor XIII B-subunit deficiency; bruising and bleeding do not establish a separate skin disorder.
Inherited INF2-associated glomerular disease causes proteinuria and renal failure; a genetic podocytopathy does not establish an immune mechanism.
Inherited hair-shaft abnormality producing apparent alternating bands.
TNNC1-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium; conduction abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome; other tumor risks do not establish direct organ involvement.
MYH6-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium and cardiac function.
Isolated MYH6-related dilated cardiomyopathy directly damages myocardial function.
Brain and skin lesions define TSC2 disease; renal lesions occur in ~45-50% and cardiac rhabdomyomas in ~50%. Retinal hamartomas, also a major criterion, omitted under cap.
VCL-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis and outflow obstruction affect the cardiovascular axis.
Waardenburg-Shah phenotype combines sensorineural deafness, intestinal aganglionosis and skin/hair pigmentation abnormalities; iris color changes do not establish ocular damage.
Waardenburg-Shah syndrome combines sensorineural deafness, intestinal aganglionosis and pigmentary abnormalities; iris color changes do not impair vision.
TCF4-associated corneal endothelial degeneration causes guttata, edema and visual impairment.
Fuchs endothelial dystrophy directly damages the corneal endothelium and impairs vision.
Inherited corneal endothelial dystrophy; disease is confined to the eye.
Inherited Fuchs corneal endothelial dystrophy.
Manganese transport defect with dystonia 14/15 and defining polycythemia (30-79%); cirrhosis 5/6 is retained as involved because primary is capped at three.

decisions.haematologic: primary: polycythemia is a named, defining blood-cell disorder, reported in 30-79%; the haematologic mechanism axis therefore applies.
decisions.hepatic: involved: direct manganese-related hepatic injury includes cirrhosis in 5/6; the three-primary cap retains the metabolic, neurologic and blood-cell axes.

basis: Hepatic steatosis, inflammation and fibrosis define the disease. Associated diabetes, dyslipidemia and other cardiometabolic conditions are separately diagnosed disorders.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: metabolic dysfunction qualifies this hepatic disease; associated diabetes and lipid disorders do not establish a separate endocrine/metabolic axis.

basis: GRXCR1-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ disease is established.
Isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular enlargement and impaired systolic function.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy occurs in 4/7 (~57%). Hearing impairment has no established frequency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: denervation causes established muscle tissue loss in 4/7 (~57%); this is structural atrophy rather than weakness alone.

basis: Inherited intestinal bile-acid transport defect causing chronic diarrhea and fat malabsorption; no hepatic injury established.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; associated speech delay reflects impaired hearing rather than independent neurologic damage.
RPS10-related congenital erythroid aplasia; anemia in 5/5. No common direct extrahematologic damage established.
Congenital red-cell aplasia; hearing loss/external canal atresia, ventricular septal defect and cleft palate each reported in 2/4; renal anomalies below 30%.
Inherited retinal vascular disease with exudation, retinal folds and potential retinal detachment.
Disordered phosphate homeostasis causes rickets; phosphate wasting alone does not establish renal damage; nephrocalcinosis occurred in 1/5.
Inherited iron metabolism disorder; hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis in 2/2; cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-50% of juvenile cases. Pigmentation alone does not establish skin injury.

decisions.hepatic: involved: iron deposition causes hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis in 2/2; hepatic injury is an organ manifestation of the systemic iron metabolism disorder.

basis: Distal muscular dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle.
ANO5-related distal muscular dystrophy causes progressive skeletal muscle weakness and atrophy; no common extra-muscular damage established.
Spondylometaphyseal bone dysplasia defines disease. Hypertension, cardiomegaly and developmental delay are reported, but their frequencies are unestablished.
The supplied definition describes actual familial rhabdoid tumors; CNS and kidney are tumor-origin sites, each documented in 1/2 patients.

decisions.renal: primary: renal rhabdoid tumor is a tumor-origin manifestation of the defined familial tumor syndrome, documented in 1/2 patients.

basis: Generalized fat loss, metabolic dysfunction and characteristic myopathy define CGL4; abnormal muscle histology 5/5. Hepatic steatosis 1/3 supports hepatic involvement; atrial fibrillation 1/5 excluded.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic congenital myopathy is a defining feature of CGL4, supported by abnormal skeletal muscle histology in 5/5 and weakness in 3/5.

basis: Immunodeficiency with defining optic and skeletal anomalies; developmental impairment and seizures occur in 30–79%. Renal agenesis (30–79%) omitted under cap.
Inherited hyperfibrinolytic bleeding disorder; bruising does not establish lasting skin damage, and intracranial or gastrointestinal hemorrhage is occasional (5-29%).
Vertebral, epiphyseal and metaphyseal dysplasia define disease; hydrocephalus and microcephaly each reported in 1/3 support CNS involvement.
Reflex epilepsy with focal or generalized seizures triggered by hot water exposure.
Inherited reflex epilepsy triggered by hot water.
LRAT-associated congenital retinal dystrophy causing severe visual loss; no systemic metabolic disease established.
Chondrodysplasia with progressive destructive arthropathy, predominantly affecting the hips and other joints.
Primary skeletal dysplasia with hip degeneration, epiphyseal abnormalities and variable vertebral involvement.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy with hypokalemia and episodic paralysis; dyspnea alone does not establish intrinsic pulmonary injury.
Despite the susceptibility wording, the definition specifies familial pancreatic carcinoma; pancreatic tumour origin establishes the gastrointestinal axis.
Despite the susceptibility wording, the definition specifies familial pancreatic carcinoma, an exocrine pancreatic tumour.
Developmental delay, congenital heart defects and limb abnormalities define the syndrome. Hearing impairment occurs in 2/7, below 30%.
Corticospinal degeneration defines pure spastic paraplegia; weakness, neurogenic amyotrophy and urinary urgency do not establish direct muscle or urinary-organ damage.
Monogenic diabetes due to impaired insulin production; diabetic vascular, retinal and renal complications are separate diseases.
Progressive cerebellar ataxia; nystagmus and abnormal saccades reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than primary eye damage.
Monogenic diabetes with impaired endocrine pancreatic function; diabetic organ complications are separate diseases.
Hereditary motor neuronopathy; established upper- and lower-limb muscle atrophy in 1/2 (50%) represents tissue loss within the disease, beyond weakness alone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: established muscle atrophy in 1/2 (50%) represents structural muscle loss from disease-related denervation; it is not merely weakness or a separately coded comorbidity.

basis: Brachydactyly with shortened metacarpals and metatarsals. Dental abnormalities occur in only 5-29%; the gene does not establish endocrine disease.
Autoimmune developmental syndrome; global delay 11/11 is defining. Chronic lung disease 9/10 and persistent finger contractures 11/11 qualify; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is a defining component of this syndromic disorder, supported by the intellectual-disability parent and global developmental delay in 11/11.

basis: Inherited proximal tubulopathy with defining phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia; rickets, osteomalacia, osteopenia and recurrent fractures reported in 2/2 patients.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: persistent electrolyte and phosphate disturbances are defining features of this inherited tubular transport disorder, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Fanconi anemia; anal atresia 2/2, renal abnormalities at least 1/3 including severe renal failure, and radial/thumb defects 1/3; estimates derive from very small cohorts.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural deafness with vestibular dysfunction; both hearing and vestibular function belong to the otologic axis.
Nonsyndromic prelingual sensorineural hearing loss.
Microcephaly, developmental impairment and cochlear hearing loss are core features; singleton cardiac and ocular findings do not establish common involvement.
PNKP-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with microcephaly, seizures and developmental impairment.
Defining joint contractures, renal tubulopathy and cholestasis; ichthyosis affects roughly half of ARC patients; CNS and platelet abnormalities are variable.
Developmental disability and skeletal/digital anomalies define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 4/13 (~31%). Singleton strabismus data do not establish common eye involvement.
GRK1-related retinal phototransduction disorder causing congenital stationary night blindness.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of the esophagus; eosinophilia does not independently establish a blood-cell disorder.
ACTC1-associated isolated cardiomyopathy with ventricular dilation and myocardial fibrosis; no established extracardiac disease.
Isolated inherited cardiomyopathy with ventricular noncompaction, fibrosis and systolic dysfunction.
Inherited retinal photoreceptor degeneration with progressive visual impairment.
Motor neuron degeneration; muscle weakness, dysphagia and respiratory failure result from denervation rather than separate organ disease.
MEF2C-related neurodevelopmental impairment with severe intellectual disability, motor delay and seizures; minor dysmorphic features do not establish other organ damage.
Developmental disorder; retinal dystrophy 80–99%; renal malformations/dysfunction and aganglionic megacolon 30–79% in supplied annotations; obesity omitted at cap.
Defines craniofacial dysplasia, alopecia and hypogonadism. Intellectual disability/encephalocele 80-99%; ocular and dental defects also frequent, omitted at cap.
SERPINB6-related nonsyndromic progressive hearing loss; no additional organ disease established.
Defining craniofacial dysplasia, microphthalmia and facial/palatal clefting; callosal agenesis 30-79%; cap omits hearing loss (30-79%) and hair anomalies.
Developmental impairment and hand/foot malformations define the syndrome; developmental delay 9/12 and camptodactyly 4/12. Individual cardiac defects are below 30%.
TTC8-associated retinal rod-cone degeneration; this retinal subtype does not establish multisystem ciliopathy.
Glycolytic enzyme deficiency causes chronic hemolytic anemia; neurologic impairment and gallbladder complications are under 30%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Autoimmune biliary disease and cutaneous sclerosis define it; GI dysfunction/mucosal abnormalities 80–99%. Ocular sicca and arthritis 30–79% omitted at cap.
SPTAN1-related encephalopathy with brain atrophy and hypomyelination; reflux in 2/3 is a separate condition and does not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
GJC2-related primary lymphatic vessel dysfunction; cellulitis is a separate infection, and edema alone does not establish skin damage.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with prolonged QT and arrhythmias; syncope does not establish neurologic damage.
Adipocytic sarcoma typically arising in deep soft tissues of the extremities; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ involvement.
Glycosylation defect with defining neurodevelopmental disease; cirrhosis, thrombocytopenia and coagulation abnormalities each reported in 30-79%.
Inherited plasma-protein metabolic disorder defined by emphysema and hepatic injury; panniculitis is very rare (1-4%).
CD19-related antibody immunodeficiency; recurrent otitis and respiratory infections are separate infections, without documented chronic organ damage.
Primary antibody deficiency; recurrent pneumonia and sinusitis are separately diagnosed infections, without evidence of intrinsic chronic lung damage.
MS4A1-associated antibody immunodeficiency; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic airway or lung damage.
CD81 antibody deficiency; immune-complex nephritis/CKD and autoimmune thrombocytopenia, each reported in 1/1, are separately diagnosed autoimmune complications.

decisions.haematologic: none: autoimmune thrombocytopenia (1/1 reported patient) is a separately diagnosed autoimmune complication.
decisions.renal: none: immune-complex nephritis and resulting CKD (1/1 reported patient) constitute separately diagnosed renal disease complicating antibody deficiency.

basis: B-cell developmental arrest with absent circulating B cells defines an immune and blood-cell disorder; recurrent otitis, pneumonia and meningitis are separate infections.

decisions.haematologic: primary: absent circulating B cells reflect a defining blood-cell developmental defect, meeting the explicit blood-cell disease rule.

basis: CD79A-related B-cell maturation arrest with absent circulating B cells and antibodies; recurrent respiratory and ear infections are separately diagnosed diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: absent circulating B cells (1/1) reflect the defining B-cell maturation defect, a blood-cell disease; inclusion does not depend on nonspecific neutropenia.

basis: BLNK antibody deficiency; protein-losing enteropathy in 1/1 supports intestinal dysfunction, with limited sampling. Neutropenia in 1/2 lacks evidence of persistence; infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: none: neutropenia in 1/2 does not establish persistent intrinsic blood-cell dysfunction; transient infection-associated neutropenia is insufficient.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: protein-losing enteropathy in 1/1 documents intestinal loss of function beyond infection susceptibility; the tiny sample limits confidence.

basis: Inherited antibody immunodeficiency; supplied findings do not establish common additional organ damage.
Glycogen metabolism disorder defined by skeletal myopathy and cardiac storage with cardiomyopathy and ventricular arrhythmias.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; limb hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Hearing loss in one reported patient does not establish a syndrome-wide frequency of at least 30%.

decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing loss is reported in only 1/1 patient; this isolated observation does not establish involvement in at least 30% of patients.

basis: Isolated developmental eye disorder with microphthalmia and high hypermetropia in 9/9.
FGFR1-rearranged hematopoietic neoplasm; associated lymphoblastic lymphoma is a common, defining presentation and warrants the lymphoma mechanism axis.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: lymphoblastic lymphoma is a common defining component of the FGFR1-rearranged stem-cell neoplasm, often accompanying its myeloid presentation.

basis: Progressive skeletal muscle dystrophy; the definition explicitly excludes cardiac and oculofacial-bulbar muscle involvement.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 80-99%; ear, digital and unspecified dental dysmorphism do not establish functional organ damage.
Congenital cleft of the oral commissure produces an abnormally wide mouth; mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Estrogen synthesis deficiency; osteopenia/osteoporosis occur in 80-99%. Steatosis is frequent, but common functional hepatic damage is not established.
Inherited nephronophthisis; hepatic fibrosis in 7/7 patients supports direct liver involvement; retinal degeneration only 1/7.
Inherited qualitative von Willebrand factor dysfunction; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish separate organ damage.
Defined as isolated progressive postlingual hearing loss; the chromosome-duplication synonym does not establish a multisystem syndrome.
Mitochondrial disease with neuroregression and optic atrophy; muscle atrophy in 80-99%. Cap excludes paralytic ileus reported in 2/3.
Mitochondrial myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia define MLASA2; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 1/3 patients meets the frequency threshold.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and joint/skeletal abnormalities characterize the syndrome; joint hypermobility 20/20. JMML is a separately diagnosed predisposition; cardiac frequency unclear.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: joint and skeletal abnormalities are defining manifestations, supported by joint hypermobility in 20/20 patients.

basis: Defective steroidogenesis with adrenal hormone deficiency and defining skeletal malformations; skeletal abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Defining hair and skin dysplasia plus malformed teeth and enamel hypoplasia; syndactyly is explicitly cutaneous.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the definition specifies partial cutaneous syndactyly, without established bone, joint or muscle involvement.

basis: ARL6-related rod-cone retinal degeneration; other ciliopathy manifestations cannot be inferred from the gene.
Ectodermal skin/hair abnormalities and defining syndactyly; frequencies of enamel hypoplasia and cardiomegaly are insufficient to establish additional involvement.
Inherited retinal degeneration with visual loss; retinal vessel attenuation and cataracts remain within the ocular axis.
PDE6G-related rod-cone retinal degeneration with visual field and acuity loss.
Macular retinal dysfunction causes progressive bilateral visual loss.
Primary ventricular arrhythmia causing torsade de pointes and ventricular fibrillation.
Cardiac electrical disorder defined by early repolarization associated with ventricular fibrillation.
ID/developmental delay 4/4; aganglionic megacolon 2/4 (50%), microtia 4/4 (100%), and zygomatic bone hypoplasia 3/4 (75%) support gastrointestinal, otologic and musculoskeletal involvement.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal: zygomatic bone hypoplasia in 3/4 patients is a common structural skeletal defect. Its inclusion brings the total to four organs, within the cap.

basis: Developmental delay/ID 5/5; camptodactyly 2/5 supports skeletal involvement. Otitis is a secondary diagnosis; hearing impairment only 1/5.

decisions.otologic: none: recurrent/chronic otitis (80-99%) is a separate secondary disease; intrinsic hearing impairment is reported in only 1/5.

basis: Familial cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; tremor and gait disturbance are neurologic manifestations.
Cranioskeletal and ectodermal dysplasia includes defining dental defects (2/2); progressive renal disease affects ~50-80% of CED. Ocular defects (1/2) omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: involved: progressive renal tubulopathy is a common complication, approximately 50-80% across cranioectodermal dysplasia, rather than a required defining feature.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental dysplasia is a defining ectodermal component; microdontia, fused teeth and abnormal spacing occurred in 2/2 patients. Teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

basis: Defining lymphatic vascular dysfunction causes lymphedema in 5/7; posterior nasal airway atresia occurs in 7/7.
Glycosylation disorder with intellectual disability in 7/7; hearing impairment and neurogenic bladder each occur in 2/7, below 30%.
Nephronophthisis and retinal degeneration define Senior-Loken syndrome; intellectual disability occurs in 6/19 (~32%), just above threshold.
Glyoxylate metabolic disorder defined by renal oxalate disease; nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis and abnormal renal physiology occur in 80-99%.
ZNF513-related retinal degeneration; visual impairment and retinal abnormalities in 4/4 reported patients.
Familial congenital clubfoot defines the condition; nail abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
Callosal agenesis and congenital lymphatic vascular dysfunction define the syndrome; lymphatic disease is mapped to cardiovascular.
Inherited combined factor V and VIII deficiency directly impairs coagulation.
Skeletal defects, microcephaly/intellectual disability and hearing loss define the syndrome; ptosis is a defining eyelid defect, with frequency unspecified.
Developmental hypoplasia of the cervical odontoid process; neurologic injury is a possible complication, not established in at least 30%.
Defining skin encasement, limb/muscle hypoplasia and severe oral defects; microphthalmia 2/2. Cardiac/renal defects (1/2) omitted at cap; CNS cysts/lung lobation lack proven functional injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: severe oral malformation and omphalocele are defining developmental defects, each reported in 2/2 patients.
decisions.neurologic: none: intracranial cysts occur in 2/2, but functional impact is unclear; four systems with clearer tissue defects fill the cap.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia in 2/2 directly impairs eye development; the three primary slots prioritize defining skin, limb/muscle and severe oral defects.

basis: Inherited absence of tuberculin-specific delayed hypersensitivity is an immune-response phenotype; no evidence establishes infection or other organ injury.
Developmental delay/ID define disease; strabismus and pectus excavatum each 30-79%. GI complaints lack clear lasting damage; optic nerve defects <30%.
Sphingolipid-biosynthesis disorder causing neuropathy; ulcers (4/7) follow insensate injury rather than direct skin disease; osteomyelitis (3/5) is a separate infection.

decisions.dermatologic: none: ulcers affect 4/7 but arise through trauma to insensate tissue, rather than direct cutaneous damage by the disease process.

basis: Peripheral demyelinating/axonal neuropathy with developmental impairment; vestibular schwannoma is a nerve tumor, without documented hearing damage.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy; respiratory distress reflects cardiac failure, and SDHA causation alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Inherited cobalamin uptake disorder causing methylmalonic acidemia; patients are usually asymptomatic. Reported retinal vascular disease is not common.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive corticospinal degeneration. Bladder dysfunction is neurogenic; intrinsic urinary tract damage is not established.
Classical complement immunodeficiency; associated SLE and lupus-related skin or kidney disease are separately diagnosed conditions.
Organic acid metabolism disorder; developmental impairment and seizures affect most patients, and cardiomyopathy occurs in approximately half of type 2 cases.
Inherited retinal photoreceptor degeneration with progressive visual loss in 6/6 patients.
Glycosylation defect with defining encephalopathy and gastric bleeding; hearing loss 30-79%. Frequent visual impairment may be cerebral; intrinsic ocular damage is unconfirmed.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: persistent vomiting and gastric bleeding are explicit defining manifestations; bleeding establishes gastrointestinal injury.
decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment (30-79%) does not localize damage to the eye in this encephalopathy; strabismus is only 5-29%.

basis: Mitochondrial disease with defining neuropathy and intestinal failure; destructive myopathy in 2/2. Ophthalmoplegia reflects muscle dysfunction; hearing impairment is occasional.
Progressive cerebral and cerebellar disease with seizures and profound developmental impairment; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated digestive-organ damage.
FOXP1 neurodevelopmental disorder; persistent strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: anterior maxillary protrusion is a defining skeletal abnormality, supported by maxillary hyperplasia in 6/7; not inferred from hypermobility alone.

basis: Inherited mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder with spastic ataxia; optic atrophy in 4/4 assessed patients.
Ineffective erythropoiesis and hemolysis; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage. Cardiomyopathy and hypothyroidism are separately diagnosed conditions.
Inherited vesicoureteral reflux with urinary tract malformations; constipation in 2/4 does not establish intestinal damage.
Joint hypermobility 21/29 and vertebral changes 30-79%; progressive visual loss 30-79%; cardiac defects/HTN 30-79% omitted by cap. Lisch nodules alone are non-damaging.

decisions.cardiovascular: none under cap: cardiac abnormalities and hypertension are reported in 30-79%; retain more frequent skeletal abnormalities and progressive visual loss with explicit functional damage.
decisions.ocular: involved: progressive visual loss is reported in 30-79%, establishing functional eye damage; Lisch nodules alone would not qualify.

basis: Microcephalic primordial dwarfism with severe growth restriction and skeletal abnormalities; short stature does not establish endocrine disease.

Skeletal dysplasia with platyspondyly and scoliosis in 80-99%; falx cerebri abnormalities are occasional.
Factor II coagulopathy; supplied HPO reports joint and intracranial hemorrhage each in 30-79%, supporting joint and CNS injury; epistaxis alone adds no airway damage.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; dental abnormalities 80-99%, heart malformations 30-79%, myopia 2/4; kidney abnormalities classified occasional, so renal excluded.
Mesomelic skeletal dysplasia with limb malformations; pendular nystagmus in 2/2 does not establish intrinsic ocular damage or a defined neurologic lesion.

Platelet defect and vision-impairing albinism define HPS9; immune dysfunction has leukopenia/infections in 1/1. Cutaneous hypopigmentation is a core, usually common feature; primary cap applies.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular albinism with reduced acuity and nystagmus is defining; ocular albinism is reported in 1/1.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous hypopigmentation is part of the core albinism phenotype, expected in >=30%; the three primary slots prioritize blood, vision and immune dysfunction.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: leukopenia and recurrent infections in 1/1, together with inborn-immunity ancestry, support an immunodeficiency mechanism.

basis: Cytopenic immunodeficiency; hearing loss 80-99% and optic abnormalities/visual loss 30-79%. Respiratory failure lacks evidence of direct intrinsic pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure is annotated 80-99%, but intrinsic lung injury is not established; recurrent infections are separately diagnosed complications.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic nerve abnormalities with visual loss are annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting structural and functional eye involvement.

basis: TCTN1-related Joubert syndrome with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and molar tooth sign in 2/2 patients; no other common organ damage documented.

CLRN1-related retinal degeneration; this concept does not establish syndromic hearing loss.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: characteristic progressive valvular disease is a major diagnostic feature of geleophysic dysplasia, not merely a minority complication.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: thickened skin is a defining feature of geleophysic dysplasia and belongs with its skeletal and cardiac diagnostic manifestations.

basis: KCNJ13-related congenital retinal dystrophy; reduced visual acuity and cataracts are reported in 3/3 patients.

Craniosynostosis and dental defects define disease; papilledema 7/7 and Chiari/syringomyelia 1/2 support involvement. Hearing defects 1/2 omitted at cap.
Primary adrenal cortical nodular disease with adrenal hyperplasia and cortisol excess.
Anterior segment dysgenesis defines disease; CNS malformations/hydrocephalus and severe sensorineural hearing loss each reported in 1/3. Small pituitary alone lacks functional evidence.
Genetic podocyte disease causing proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome; edema and hypoalbuminemia do not establish other organ damage.
Inherited postsynaptic transmission disorder and SCN4A myopathy with periodic paralysis; ptosis, ophthalmoplegia and apnea reflect muscle transmission failure.
Progressive nephrotic glomerular disease; reduced visual acuity in 8/8, retinal detachment in 5/9 and pigmentary retinopathy in 3/9 support common direct ocular damage.
Inherited platelet collagen-receptor dysfunction causing defective haemostasis; bruising does not establish independent skin damage.
Inherited platelet GPVI dysfunction impairs collagen-induced aggregation; bruising and mucosal bleeding do not establish damage to additional organs.
MAN1B1 glycosylation disorder with intellectual disability; cutis laxa 5/7 and strabismus 5/12; joint hypermobility 7/19 omitted by cap.
VPS35-related Parkinson disease causes progressive degeneration of the motor nervous system.

Skeletal growth disorder with severe short stature and characteristic bone abnormalities. Microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction.
GPI-anchor disorder with ID; shortened phalanges 2/2 and severe enteric malformations 1/2. Strabismus 2/3, hearing loss and ASD 1/2 omitted by cap, prioritizing severe bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: anal stenosis and aganglionic megacolon each occur in 1/2 assessed patients and represent substantial structural or functional bowel damage.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: strabismus 2/3 qualifies, but skeletal abnormalities 2/2 and severe enteric malformations 1/2 take priority.

basis: Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic intellectual disability, sometimes accompanied by seizures.
Renal dysplasia, encephalocele and limb malformations define phenotype; hepatic ductal-plate malformation/fibrosis occurs in most Meckel cases (>30%); subtype data are sparse.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic ductal-plate malformation with fibrosis occurs in most Meckel syndrome cases (>30%); this subtype has no established exception.

basis: Lung-specific hereditary cancer predisposition; pulmonary denotes the target organ, without assuming existing cancer or additional organ damage.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss without established extra-auditory disease.
Hereditary sensory neuropathy with acral ulceration in 8/8 and destructive digit loss in 7/8; weakness alone does not establish primary muscle disease.
Scalp aplasia and limb defects define AOS; brain/developmental damage and visual impairment each reported in 1/2. Optic atrophy alone is 3/12; small samples limit certainty.

decisions.ocular: involved: visual impairment is reported in 1/2 (50%), supporting functional involvement; optic atrophy at 3/12 (25%) alone would not qualify.

basis: Subtype of autoimmune primary biliary cholangitis, which destroys intrahepatic bile ducts.
Primary biliary cholangitis is an autoimmune disease damaging intrahepatic bile ducts.
Warburg micro syndrome combines severe neurodevelopmental disease, congenital ocular abnormalities and characteristic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Retinal arterial macroaneurysms and supravalvular pulmonic stenosis define the syndrome and occur in all assessed patients.
Warburg micro syndrome combines severe neurodevelopmental impairment, congenital ocular abnormalities and characteristic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
CDON-related forebrain cleavage malformation; frequencies of cleft palate and other extra-neural abnormalities are unspecified.
Inherited tubulointerstitial nephropathy with renal insufficiency and concentrating defects; hyperuricemia reflects abnormal renal urate handling.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hyperuricemia is a manifestation of the renal urate-handling defect; an independent metabolic disorder is not established.

basis: Axonal peripheral neuropathy; fixed pes cavus deformity in 10/12 (~83%) supports musculoskeletal involvement beyond weakness alone.
Cerebellar atrophy, ataxia and developmental impairment; nystagmus and impaired pursuit are neurologic, and dysphagia does not establish intrinsic digestive damage.
