decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic ptosis is explicitly included in the syndrome definition and occurs in 80-99%; corneal disease and cataracts provide additional ocular evidence.

basis: Progressive inherited skin hyperpigmentation; oral and conjunctival pigmentation does not establish functional damage.
Inherited hypotrichosis affecting scalp and body hair in all reported patients.
Isolated hereditary hypotrichosis affects scalp and body hair, eyebrows and eyelashes.
Intellectual disability and encephalopathy define disease; atrial and ventricular septal defects each reported in 1/2 assessed patients; limited cardiac sample.
Hereditary narcolepsy-cataplexy; associated obstructive sleep apnea and diabetes are separate diseases. MOG mutation alone does not establish autoimmunity.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm is vascular disease; cerebral injury from rupture is a separately diagnosed complication.
GRIN1-related neurodevelopmental disease causes intellectual disability, movement abnormalities and brain malformations; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.

Nonsyndromic inherited intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous capillary malformations are a defining feature, present in 10/10.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none under four-axis cap: short distal phalanges occur in 19/20, but severe optic atrophy takes priority over this limited skeletal anomaly.

decisions.pulmonary: none: asthma in 3/3 is a separately diagnosed associated disease; no intrinsic pulmonary malformation or other direct syndrome-related lung injury is established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: congenital pyloric stenosis in 2/3 directly impairs gastrointestinal function and is a structural component of the syndrome.

basis: Organic acid metabolism defect; seizures are annotated frequent (30-79%). Other neurologic features are individually occasional; hepatic enzyme elevation is under 30%.
Metaplastic epithelial lesion of the oesophagus; subsequent adenocarcinoma is a separate disease risk.
Testicular steroid-synthesis deficiency impairs gonadal hormone production and causes abnormal sexual development.

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss is a core diagnostic feature of this Stickler subtype, present in 8/8 patients.

basis: Developmental and cognitive impairment with neuronal migration abnormalities define the syndrome; renal and skeletal malformations are minority findings.
High myopia, cataracts and vitreoretinal degeneration directly affect the eye; no extraocular disease established.
Recurrent complete hydatidiform mole is a gestational trophoblastic disorder confined to reproductive and obstetric tissues.
Developmental delay in 2/3 and congenital diaphragmatic muscle defects in 3/5 characterize the syndrome. Individual cardiac and renal anomalies occur in 1/5.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital diaphragmatic hernia in 3/5 is a major defining structural muscle defect in this deletion syndrome.

basis: Diabetes, progressive hearing loss and optic atrophy define the syndrome; conflicting neurologic HPO entries are not retained because the definition describes neurologic findings as rare.
Inherited brain iron accumulation disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; optic atrophy in 20/23 patients.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; CNS injury and cardiomyopathy each frequent (30-79%); respiratory failure alone does not establish intrinsic lung damage.

Inherited corneal, iris and lens abnormalities; keratoconus and cataracts reported in 18/18.

Developmental delay occurred in 3/3; optic nerve hypoplasia and amblyopia in 1/1 examined support direct ocular impairment, although evidence is limited.
Peroxisomal metabolic defect defined by adult cognitive decline, seizures and neuropathy; pigmentary retinopathy occurs in 1/2 reported patients. Infantile liver disease is rare.

decisions.neurologic: primary: adult cognitive decline, seizures and sensorimotor neuropathy explicitly characterize the disease in its definition.

basis: Familial vesicoureteral reflux is a urinary tract disorder; infection and renal scarring are separate potential complications.
Familial vesicoureteral reflux affects the urinary tract; infection is a potential complication, not an intrinsic mechanism.
Familial reflux from the bladder into the ureters; all affected structures belong to the renal axis.
The definition specifies familial pancreatic carcinoma, establishing pancreatic tumour origin despite susceptibility wording in the name.
Progressive distal skeletal muscle degeneration; palpitations alone do not establish cardiac damage, and elevated AST can originate in muscle.
Cerebellar ataxia, epilepsy and intellectual disability define SCAR12; retinal degeneration and optic atrophy occur in only 5-29%; nystagmus is neurologic.
Persistent patterned skin hyperpigmentation defines LWNH; neurologic, skeletal and cardiac abnormalities are isolated reports.
Ovarian dysgenesis causes endocrine gonadal failure with elevated gonadotropins and delayed puberty, each reported in 3/3.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment and frequent epileptic encephalopathy define this syndrome; other organ abnormalities lack qualifying frequencies.

Characteristic BAP1-inactivated melanocytic skin tumors are a defining manifestation; associated visceral cancers are separately diagnosed tumors, not automatic organ involvement.
Skin and bowel autoinflammation define disease; blepharitis in 2/2 supports ocular involvement. Otitis externa in 2/2 omitted by the four-axis cap.
An isolated inherited intellectual disability; no additional organ injury or specific metabolic disorder is established.
Hereditary colorectal cancer subtype; no additional organ involvement is established, and the gene alone does not justify vascular labels.
Neurodevelopmental deletion syndrome; strabismus in 6/11 and hearing impairment in 3/4 support involvement. Single-case organ anomalies do not establish common damage.
Nonsyndromic neurodevelopmental disorder with severe intellectual disability and absent speech in 5/5; no established systemic metabolic disease.
Congenital distal joint contractures and foot deformities define the disorder; no additional organ damage is established.

Inherited lipase deficiency causes exocrine pancreatic dysfunction and fat malabsorption; skeletal and ocular complications occur in only 5–29%.
LINS1-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, microcephaly and absent speech; no established metabolic disease.
Defined as nonsyndromic intellectual disability; skeletal findings lack frequency evidence, and a transport-related ancestor alone does not establish metabolic disease.
Nonsyndromic severe intellectual disability with microcephaly. Broad carbohydrate-transport ancestry does not establish a metabolic disorder; macroglossia lacks evidence of GI dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the broad transport-disorder ancestor alone does not establish a metabolic disease in this nonsyndromic intellectual disability concept.

basis: Nonsyndromic intellectual disability affects 3/3; the supplied ancestry alone does not establish a clinical metabolic disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: carbohydrate-transport ancestry without biochemical or clinical metabolic abnormalities does not establish metabolic organ disease.

basis: Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with motor delay; no disease-specific evidence establishes an inborn metabolic defect or endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: broad carbohydrate-transport ancestry alone does not establish a metabolic disorder; supplied disease-specific features are exclusively neurodevelopmental.

basis: Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay; no established additional organ damage.

Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay and microcephaly; no established systemic metabolic phenotype is supplied.
Hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer syndrome; other tumour sites represent cancer risks, not established organ damage.

audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine: inherited failure of surfactant catabolism is a defining metabolic disorder. Pulmonary disease and intrinsic alveolar macrophage dysfunction support the existing primary axes.

basis: Lectin complement pathway deficiency; recurrent infections do not establish common lasting damage to a particular additional organ.
SIGMAR1-related motor neuron disease; muscle weakness and wasting reflect denervation rather than an independent primary muscle lesion.
Inherited aneurysmal disease of the abdominal aortic wall.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia with defining respiratory restriction; renal failure and cataract each occur in 1/1 assessed patient. Evidence is sparse; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: restrictive respiratory insufficiency is a defining component of asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy; a restrictive ventilatory defect is documented in 1/1.

basis: Inherited fibrosing renal disease; hepatobiliary structural involvement includes intrahepatic bile duct dilatation in 6/6 and hepatic cysts in 1/2. Pancreatic cysts occur in 1/6.
Skeletal and ectodermal dysplasia; rod-cone dystrophy with visual impairment 2/2, stage 5 kidney disease 1/2. Marrow hypocellularity 1/2 omitted by cap.
Classical complement pathway immunodeficiency; recurrent infections are separately diagnosed consequences, and singleton reports do not establish common direct organ damage.
Inherited complement immunodeficiency; lupus and glomerulonephritis are separately diagnosed associated diseases, with no supplied qualifying frequencies.
Hypomyelination, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and dental abnormalities define the syndrome; myopia affects 3/4, with optic atrophy also reported.
Hereditary colorectal carcinoma defines the affected organ; other cancer risks do not establish direct involvement.
Mitochondrial/peroxisomal disorder with severe encephalopathy; myopathy and hepatic steatosis each reported in 1/1 assessed patients; small denominators limit certainty.
Donor immune attack damages skin in 80-99%; oral/GI epithelial disease and hepatitis occur in 30-79%. Eye and lung findings are only 5-29% here.

decisions.neurologic: involved: structural brain malformations and developmental delay occur in 1/1; they accompany the defining microphthalmia rather than define its primary organ.

basis: Brain malformations and cardiac conduction block define syndrome; fixed digital contractures/deformities are typical in reported cases, supporting >30% involvement.

Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; no extraotologic disease is specified.

Defining skeletal dysplasia and craniosynostosis with occipital encephalocele.
Inherited focal epilepsy arising in the temporal lobe; no other organ damage is established.
DNASE1L3-related systemic lupus retains defining autoimmune, cutaneous and articular manifestations; nephritis occurs in 11/17 (~65%).

basis: Inherited developmental cerulean cataract affecting the ocular lens.
Oculorenal Joubert subtype: cerebral malformations, renal cysts in 15/18 and ocular dysfunction in most; hypertension is a separately diagnosed complication.
GATA4-related atrioventricular septal malformation; pancreatic disease in the broader parent concept is not established for this subtype.

Congenital atrial septal defect; anomalous pulmonary venous return also belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Cutis laxa defines disease; scoliosis and mitral regurgitation have unspecified frequencies, insufficient to establish involvement in at least 30%.
Congenital hypoplasia of left-sided cardiac structures defines the disease.

basis: Cutis laxa and arterial disease define ARCL1B; joint hypermobility 1/3 and skeletal malformations support musculoskeletal involvement. Emphysema 1/1 cannot establish typical frequency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint hypermobility 1/3, arachnodactyly 2/2 and reported bone/chest malformations support common structural involvement; samples are small.

basis: Proline-biosynthesis disorder with defining cutis laxa and intellectual disability; osteopenia 10/11 and hip dislocation 15/22. Cataract 2/22; glaucoma evidence limited to singletons.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: PYCR1 deficiency is an inborn disorder of proline biosynthesis, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Periostosis and pachydermia define disease; persistent secretory diarrhea in 7/7 supports direct intestinal dysfunction.
THRA resistance commonly causes skeletal maturation defects, neurodevelopmental impairment and anemia, each >30%; constipation alone does not establish GI damage.
Peripheral neuropathy and glomerulosclerotic nephropathy define the syndrome; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 4/12 patients.
Defined cutaneous melanoma predisposition; renal and pancreatic cancers are additional risks, not established organ involvement.
Inherited lipid biosynthesis disorder with ichthyosis and severe neurologic impairment; joint contractures 2/4. High myopia 1/2 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Thiamine activation defect causes encephalopathy, dystonia and ataxia; left ventricular hypertrophy occurs in only 1/5.

Lipoic acid synthesis defect with defining lactic acidosis and encephalopathy. Cardiomyopathy in 1/1 assessed patient does not establish usual prevalence; respiratory insufficiency need not be pulmonary.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is reported in 1/1 assessed patient, insufficient to establish that it affects at least about 30% over the usual disease course.

basis: Cerebellar malformation and developmental impairment define disease. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic; retinal dystrophy occurs in only 5-29%.

Immunodeficiency with defining cold urticaria in 27/27; recurrent infections and associated asthma are separate diseases.
Autoimmune cytopenias, monocytosis and lymphoproliferation define RALD; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage or functional impairment.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly is characteristic, but enlargement alone does not establish function-impairing infiltration or hepatic injury in at least 30%.

basis: Inherited extracellular pyrophosphate deficiency causes pathological arterial mineralization and cardiac injury. Nephrocalcinosis and hypophosphatemic rickets occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: generalized arterial calcification is an inherited disorder of extracellular pyrophosphate metabolism, independently of occasional hypophosphatemic rickets.

basis: GATA6-associated atrioventricular septal defect; pancreatic disease is not established for this specific concept.
Defined by a congenital atrial septal defect; the broader GATA6 association does not establish pancreatic disease in this subtype.
Hypertriglyceridemia with defining hepatic steatosis and fibrosis; splenomegaly alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Acetyl-CoA transport disorder with severe neurodegeneration and cataracts; hearing impairment occurs in 5/5 patients.
Cerebral small-vessel disease causes hemorrhage, porencephaly and developmental brain injury; esotropia alone does not establish direct ocular damage.
Metopic craniosynostosis defines the disorder; global developmental delay is reported in 1/3 patients, meeting the threshold in a very small series.
Inherited coagulation disorder; venous thromboses are separately diagnosed complications rather than intrinsic vascular disease.
Spastic ataxia, epilepsy and sensorimotor neuropathy define the disease; weakness and amyotrophy are neuropathic, and oculomotor apraxia is neurologic.
Renal tubular salt-handling disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and hypertension.
Renal tubular electrolyte-handling disorder defined by hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis and hypertension; hypertension reported in 10/10 patients.
Wiskott-Aldrich phenotype comprises immunodeficiency, thrombocytopenia and eczema; each is documented in the reported patient.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with night blindness and visual impairment; no established extraocular involvement.
Renal tubular salt-handling disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and hypertension.
Renal tubular transport disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and hypertension; hypertension is typically early and severe in CUL3 disease.

basis: Isolated ocular developmental disorder with iris and chorioretinal colobomas in all eight reported patients.
Severe developmental epileptic encephalopathy; joint contractures occur in 2/2 assessed patients. Apnea and bradycardia reflect autonomic dysfunction; optic atrophy is under 30%.
CRADD-related intellectual disability with megalencephaly and cortical developmental abnormalities; no supported extra-neural disease.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration; postaxial polydactyly in 2/6 (~33%) does not establish functionally damaging skeletal involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: polydactyly reaches ~33% in a small cohort, but no associated skeletal dysfunction or destructive lesion is documented; frequency alone is insufficient.

basis: Severe neurodevelopmental impairment and epilepsy define disease; laryngomalacia causes structural airway dysfunction in 26/35.
Usher syndrome defines retinal and hearing impairment; truncal ataxia, hyperreflexia and motor developmental delay are reported in 3/3 patients.
Glycosylation defect with defining neurodevelopmental and hepatic dysfunction; coagulation abnormalities 80-99%. Common ocular and bone findings omitted at cap.
Congenital motor pathway disorder causing mirror movements; bimanual synkinesia documented in 10/18.
Severe recessive protein S coagulopathy; neonatal microvascular thrombosis and necrotic purpura occur in most severe cases; cerebral hemorrhage in 1/1. Ocular frequency unknown.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: severe biallelic deficiency typically causes neonatal microvascular thrombosis; vascular occlusion is integral to this presentation rather than merely a later risk.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: necrotic neonatal purpura fulminans is characteristic in most severe biallelic cases, representing ischemic skin injury rather than transient purpura alone.

basis: Cerebral vascular rupture causes bleeding directly into brain tissue with neurologic injury.

Inherited platelet overproduction; ischemic stroke in 2/6 is a separately diagnosed thrombotic complication.
COL11A2-related skeletal dysplasia with short bones, vertebral abnormalities and thoracic hypoplasia; intrinsic pulmonary disease is not established.

Renal dysplasia, diabetes and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define this deletion syndrome; individual neurologic HPO findings can be less frequent.
Developmental delay in 6/6 and hypotonia in 15/16 establish neurologic disease; facial, palatal and digit dysmorphism alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Kyphoscoliosis/myopathy, fragile hyperextensible skin and hearing loss define subtype; myopia 4/7. Bladder diverticula 2/2 and tricuspid regurgitation 2/5 omitted by cap.
SCN8A-related epileptic encephalopathy with developmental impairment; no independent metabolic disorder is established.
Tricarboxylic acid cycle disorder defined by neurodegeneration and retinal dystrophy; hearing impairment occurs in 2/8 patients, below 30%.
Defining leukoencephalopathy, cerebral calcifications and intracranial cysts occur in 80-99%, with common seizures and cognitive deterioration.
Cortical malformations, developmental disability, seizures and peripheral neuropathy are neurologic; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Persistent cutaneous capillary ectasia defines disease. Caries (7/12) and predisposed cancers are separate diseases; intrinsic enamel/tooth defects are reported in only 2/12.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: caries in 7/12 is a separately diagnosed dental disease; intrinsic tooth defects occur in 2/12 (~17%); oropharyngeal cancer is a predisposition outcome.

basis: GPR179-related retinal dysfunction causing congenital stationary night blindness.
Defining enchondromas with bone deformities and cutaneous vascular lesions; other organ tumours are minority risks.
Glycosylation defect; developmental delay 7/7, cholestasis 5/9 and thrombocytopenia 5/5; common cardiac, skin, infection and gut manifestations omitted by cap.
Defining mitochondrial defect, cardiomyopathy and psychomotor delay; hepatic injury in 4/5. Single reported renal lesion omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: psychomotor delay is a defining manifestation; global developmental delay is documented in 1/1 annotated patient.

basis: Brain malformations and ocular defects define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 5/6 and structural skull abnormality (trigonocephaly) in 7/7 patients.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal involvement: trigonocephaly is a structural skull abnormality reported in 7/7 patients, meeting the threshold for common direct organ involvement.

basis: Primary torsion dystonia; muscle spasms and blepharospasm reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than separate muscle or eye damage.

Syndromic enteropathy and liver disease; immunodeficiency in 3/6 supports immune axis; hair-shaft damage with trichorrhexis nodosa in 6/6 supports skin axis.
Developmental disability and fifth-digit/nail defects define CSS; cleft palate 2/3. Visual impairment 1/2 and hearing loss 1/3 omitted by cap.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: visual impairment affects 2/3; retain defining axes and hearing impairment, reported in 3/4.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic sparse scalp hair and abnormal hair distribution form part of the defining Coffin-Siris phenotype.

basis: Coffin-Siris neurodevelopmental, digit and hair/nail abnormalities; visual impairment 5/11 and ptosis 9/12. Cap excludes hearing impairment 4/12 and cleft palate 4/12.
Defining skeletal dysplasia; intellectual disability and speech delay in 4/4. Endocrine abnormalities are occasional (5-29%) and not universal.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 10/10 patients.

Congenital intestinal secretory dysfunction; chronic diarrhea in 32/32. Crohn disease is separately diagnosed and occurred in 4/32.
Hereditary glycinergic startle disorder; supplied ancestry explicitly includes neurotransmitter-deficiency metabolic disease. Apnea in 1/6 does not support pulmonary involvement.

basis: Glycinergic neurologic disorder causing exaggerated startle and stiffness; esotropia impairs ocular alignment in 7/9 annotated patients.
UV-sensitive photodermatosis with photosensitivity and freckling; no documented extracutaneous damage.

audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine for the congenital dystroglycan glycosylation disorder. Move ocular to involved to meet the three-primary cap; cataracts affect 4/6 and microphthalmia 3/6.

decisions.pulmonary: none: apnea and vocal cord paresis reflect neural dysfunction; direct pulmonary or airway tissue damage is not established.

basis: CoQ10 biosynthesis disorder with encephalopathy and cardiomyopathy; renal tubular dysfunction is a defining feature, qualifying despite sparse frequency data.

decisions.renal: involved: renal cortical cystic dysplasia is common (>30%) in classic Zellweger disease and represents direct structural involvement.

Inherited phosphohydroxylysine degradation defect; urinary metabolite excretion does not establish kidney damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the record supplies no thyroid phenotype or frequency; the usual PTEN-associated Cowden thyroid frequency cannot confidently be assigned to this KLLN subtype.

basis: Cowden mucocutaneous and GI hamartomas define it; benign thyroid lesions occur in roughly 50-70% of Cowden patients, with limited subtype data; ID is 12%.
Cowden cutaneous and oral hamartomas define disease; thyroid nodules in 1/2 support gland occupation. Associated carcinomas are separate predisposition outcomes.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: benign thyroid nodular lesions are part of Cowden disease and reported in 1/2; gland occupation qualifies independently of cancer risk.

basis: Congenital urinary dysfunction with reflux in 4/5; constipation in 3/5 does not establish intestinal damage, and facial grimacing does not establish neuropathy.
Isolated developmental eye malformation with microphthalmia or anophthalmia and associated visual pathway abnormalities.
Complex IV deficiency with defining cardiac and cerebral disease; retinopathy in 1/1 annotated patient supports ocular damage, with limited numbers. Hypotonia alone does not prove skeletal myopathy.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinopathy is direct retinal damage, reported in 1/1 annotated patient; accept provisionally given the very limited frequency evidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the definition specifies encephalocardiomyopathy; hypotonia and spasticity can reflect CNS disease and do not establish common skeletal-muscle damage.

basis: Inherited neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; weakness and ptosis reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission. Respiratory insufficiency occurs in only 5-29%.
CD27 immune deficiency with lymphoid proliferation. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury; cytopenias and inflammatory organ complications are below 30%.
Familial cortical myoclonus, tremor and epilepsy define a neurologic disorder; muscle movements do not indicate primary muscle damage.
Cutaneous melanoma is the specified tumor phenotype of this susceptibility syndrome; glioma predisposition alone does not establish neurologic involvement.
Mild branched-chain amino acid metabolism disorder; supplied findings establish biochemical abnormalities without common lasting neurologic injury.
Immunodeficiency and characteristic livedo/telangiectases define FILS. Recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic lung damage; bronchiectasis occurs in 2/14.
Microphthalmia, coloboma and visual impairment occurred in 2/2 patients; developmental impairment is reported without a qualifying frequency.
Retinol transport disorder causes retinal dystrophy; comedonal acne and follicular hyperkeratosis occurred in 2/2 patients.
Congenital skeletal dysplasia with dislocations, coalitions and spinal abnormalities; hearing impairment and developmental delay are reported in only 1-4%.
Mitochondrial myopathy with defining progressive external ophthalmoplegia and ptosis; weakness and gait disturbance reflect muscle disease.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; peripheral axonal degeneration in 3/4 and cerebellar atrophy in 2/4; muscle atrophy and hearing impairment each 1/4.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; hepatomegaly and elevated liver transaminases in 1/1 reported patient support hepatic injury.
Defined by mitochondrial complex III deficiency due to UQCRQ; severe intellectual disability, dystonia and ataxia occur in 20/20 patients.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct neurologic dysfunction affects 20/20 patients; the concept is defined by its respiratory-chain defect rather than a neurologic diagnostic criterion.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental delay 2/3 and atrial septal defect 1/3 (~33%). Small samples; hepatic dysfunction frequency is not established.

decisions.hepatic: none: liver dysfunction has no frequency estimate; hyperammonemia and hypoglycemia alone do not establish direct hepatic damage in at least 30%.

basis: Ulnar hypoplasia and intellectual disability define the syndrome; microtia is permanent external-ear hypoplasia in 30-79%. Hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.

decisions.otologic: involved: microtia is structural hypoplasia of the external ear in 30-79%, exceeding a positional or cosmetic ear variant.

basis: Inherited degeneration of retinal cones and rods causing visual loss.
Defining congenital finger and toe malformations with contractures and ankylosis.
Inherited melanin-production disorder defined by skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular dysfunction; reduced visual acuity, nystagmus and iris transillumination occur in 9/9 reported patients.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with brain and eye malformations defines this type A dystroglycanopathy.
Inborn metabolic disorder with nearly universal epileptic encephalopathy and developmental impairment; apnea and hypotonia do not establish lung or muscle damage.
Defined as isolated dilated cardiomyopathy. Elevated CK alone does not establish skeletal myopathy; other CRYAB phenotypes are not inherent.
Inherited peripheral neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy in 7/7 and characteristic foot deformities support musculoskeletal involvement.
Isolated inherited lens cataract; developmental cataract reported in 7/7.
Telomere disorder with marrow failure and immunodeficiency; cerebellar hypoplasia/developmental delay occur in 80-99%. Nail and GI lesions occur in only 5-29%.
Brain malformations and developmental impairment define the disease; optic atrophy is annotated at 30-79% despite the subtype name; cataract and hearing loss are under 30%.
Inherited macrothrombocytopenia affects platelet production; epistaxis in 2/13 does not establish airway damage.
Metaphyseal osteosclerosis defines disease; developmental delay in 1/1 does not establish usual neurologic involvement; seizures and intellectual disability are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.neurologic: none: isolated developmental delay does not establish >=30%; neurologic expression is variable. [Case series](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34798323/)

basis: Combined T/B-cell functional immunodeficiency; reported pneumonias are separately diagnosed infections rather than intrinsic pulmonary disease.
Defining immunodeficiency and cholangitis; enteric infection 4/4 with chronic diarrhea 2/4; bronchiectasis 2/5 establishes pulmonary damage. Otitis evidence limited and omitted under cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: enteric infections affect 4/4 and chronic diarrhea 2/4; intestinal disease is a common manifestation rather than the syndrome's defining hepatobiliary lesion.

basis: Primary antibody deficiency; neutropenia reported in 1/1 patient supports blood-cell involvement. Respiratory infections alone do not establish chronic pulmonary damage.
Cerebellar degeneration and axonal neuropathy define disease; amyotrophy (4/4) reflects denervation rather than direct muscle disease. Eye movement abnormalities are neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy occurs in 4/4 but is secondary to axonal denervation; direct skeletal muscle disease is not established.

basis: Congenital hydrocephalus and brain malformations; chorioretinal coloboma in 2/4 patients supports ocular involvement. Cardiac anomalies reported in only 1/4.
Inherited bone fragility with recurrent fractures; blue sclerae do not establish eye dysfunction; developmental delay in 1/9 does not meet the threshold.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with vertebral, epiphyseal and joint abnormalities; no established extraskeletal organ disease.
Inherited disorder of circadian sleep timing; associated migraine remains within the neurologic axis.
Corneal dyskeratosis, palmoplantar keratoderma and laryngeal dyskeratosis define the syndrome; visual impairment and nail dystrophy support eye and skin disease.
Congenital postaxial polydactyly of hands and feet with abnormal phalangeal development.
ATP synthase deficiency; encephalopathy, seizures and cerebellar hypoplasia each 2/2; pulmonary hypoplasia 2/2. Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: this is defined by mitochondrial ATP synthase deficiency; encephalopathy, seizures and cerebellar hypoplasia each affect 2/2 reported patients.

basis: Inherited retinal degeneration with visual field loss, reduced acuity and night blindness.
Congenital iron-utilization disorder defines anemia with iron overload. Hepatic iron alone does not establish damage; hepatic and gonadal injury cannot be separated from transfusional loading here.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: this congenital iron-utilization disorder has defining iron overload, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis. Uncertain attribution of subsequent organ damage to transfusions does not negate that axis.

basis: Isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction in 3/3 patients.
Neurologic, phalangeal and nail defects define syndrome; optic atrophy 2/2. Ventricular septal defect 1/3 omitted at four-axis cap.
Congenitally short intestine causes malabsorption. Cognitive impairment (30-79%) does not establish direct CNS involvement; nutritional sequelae and syndromic subtypes may account for it.

decisions.neurologic: none: cognitive impairment is annotated 30-79%, but direct CNS disease is unestablished; malnutrition or selected syndromic subtypes may explain it.

basis: Subcutaneous fat loss and insulin resistance define disease; ectopic hepatic steatosis/hepatomegaly reported in 1/1; pancreatitis is a separately diagnosed complication.
Genetic podocyte disease causing nephrotic syndrome and glomerular sclerosis; neurologic and hearing findings have no established qualifying frequency.
MYPN-related cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium; supplied phenotypes are confined to cardiac structure and function.
Defined by congenital muscular dystrophy with brain and eye anomalies; lissencephaly, severe developmental delay and retinal degeneration documented.
Hypogonadotropism defines disease; olfactory loss is a major Kallmann diagnostic feature. Hearing impairment 3/14 and dental or bone abnormalities 2/14 are below 30%.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with defining olfactory dysfunction, anosmia 8/8; hearing impairment 6/8. Dental defects 2/8 and occasional bone loss fall below threshold.

decisions.neurologic: primary: olfactory dysfunction is a defining component of the Kallmann phenotype and anosmia is documented in 8/8 patients.

basis: Cerebellar ataxia, intellectual disability and cerebral/cerebellar atrophy define this neurodevelopmental disorder.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; dental abnormalities 2/5 and osteopenia 2/5 support involvement; hearing impairment 1/5; anosmia frequency unestablished.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism defines disease; congenital anosmia and osteopenia each occur in 2/3 reported patients, supporting sensory and skeletal involvement.
GnRH deficiency defines the endocrine disorder. Anosmia is optional; subtype frequencies for olfactory, hearing and skeletal impairment are not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: olfactory dysfunction is optional, and neither the supplied HPO annotations nor subtype evidence establishes a frequency of at least 30%.

basis: Marrow hypocellularity 2/2; biliary atresia, esophageal atresia and primum ASD each 1/2. Absent thumb (1/2) omitted at cap in favor of visceral defects; very small sample.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: primum atrial septal defect occurs in 1/2 reported patients (50%); prioritize this potentially serious cardiac defect under the cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: absent thumb occurs in 1/2 patients (50%), but marrow disease and potentially severe hepatic, gastrointestinal and cardiac defects take priority.

basis: MIP-related nonsyndromic cataract affecting the lens.
Nonsyndromic inherited cataract; associated abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Cardiac, ectodermal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define CFC. Ocular dysfunction, including strabismus and refractive errors, affects >30% across CFC; KRAS-specific estimates are limited.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ocular dysfunction affects >30% in the usual CFC course; myopia and ptosis support this axis, although KRAS-specific frequencies are uncertain.

basis: Cardiac, cutaneous and developmental abnormalities define CFC; skeletal involvement includes pectus excavatum in 3/3 and scoliosis in 2/3.
Cardiac, cutaneous and developmental defects define CFC; ocular defects include cataract and optic hypoplasia, each 1/1 assessed. Skeletal findings omitted at cap.
Leukodystrophy affects brainstem and spinal pathways; optic disc pallor indicates optic nerve damage in 3/10 (~30%). Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Defining cortical malformations; fixed joint contractures/arthrogryposis reported in 1/1, with fetal akinesia in 3/3, support musculoskeletal involvement.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy affects 3/3 and scoliosis 12/13 annotated patients; ocular and urinary findings are occasional.
Neutropenia, marrow fibrosis, immune deficiency and nephromegaly define VPS45 deficiency; hepatomegaly in 7/7 does not establish liver injury or functional impairment.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly in 7/7 and extramedullary hematopoiesis in 5/5 establish enlargement/hematopoietic activity, without demonstrated hepatic damage or loss of function.

basis: Intellectual disability and strabismus define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 22/24 patients. Hearing impairment and endocrine abnormalities are occasional.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; retinal dysplasia in 2/4. Renal dysplasia in 1/4 is below threshold.
Motor neuron disorder with defining muscle atrophy and contractures; Achilles contractures occur in 10/18. Respiratory impairment is uncommon.
Infantile myofibroblastic tumors characteristically arise in skin, subcutis and skeletal soft tissues; common visceral damage is not established for this subtype.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction defines disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation is characteristic of PCD and reported in 1/1 annotated patient.
Scalp aplasia cutis and terminal limb reduction define Adams-Oliver syndrome; individual cardiac defects occur in 1/5 reported patients.
Congenital fusion of proximal finger joints with associated skeletal abnormalities; no evidence of common extraskeletal damage.
Defining sensorineural deafness and ovarian endocrine failure; neurologic abnormalities occur in a minority.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorder affecting skin and hair pigmentation, with defining foveal hypoplasia and impaired vision.
Premature cranial suture fusion defines the disease; strabismus (11/72) and neurodevelopmental abnormalities are below 30%.
Reticulate pigment disorder with explicit fucoglycosan-synthesis disorder ancestry; inherited glycosylation defect supports the metabolic mechanism axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: explicit fucoglycosan-synthesis disorder ancestry identifies an inborn glycosylation disorder; systemic endocrine damage is not required for this mechanism axis.

basis: Defining keratoderma/hypohidrosis, enamel defects and intellectual disability; hepatitis is occasional; respiratory infections do not establish immunodeficiency.
Metabolic disease with leukodystrophy; joint contractures occur in 30-79%. Visual impairment may be cerebral; optic atrophy occurs in only 5-29%. Respiratory failure does not establish lung damage.
audit_reason: Remove ocular: visual impairment does not establish direct eye damage in a leukodystrophy; optic atrophy is occasional (5-29%), below the involvement threshold.

basis: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with cerebral atrophy; optic atrophy is occasional (5-29%); feeding difficulty alone adds no organ.
Heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension directly affects pulmonary arteries; lung parenchymal or airway damage is not established.
Pulmonary arterial vasculopathy with elevated vascular resistance; pulmonary arteries belong to the cardiovascular axis.
Heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension damages pulmonary vessels; no separate lung parenchymal disease established.
Premature activation of the reproductive endocrine axis; accelerated skeletal maturation alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure (28/29) and dysphagia (23/24) arise from respiratory and bulbar muscle weakness without established intrinsic lung or GI injury.
Skeletal dysplasia and abnormal skin define this glycosylation disorder; blue sclerae/proptosis do not establish ocular damage; aortopathy is not established at 30%.
Muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye anomalies; intellectual disability 7/8 and cataract 3/8; hearing loss 1/8 excluded.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with intellectual disability defines disease; ocular motor dysfunction includes strabismus in 3/4 and ptosis in 2/4.
Muscular dystrophy with defining developmental impairment and seizures; cataract and cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/3. Respiratory weakness does not establish lung damage.
Noonan cardiac and skeletal diagnostic features; short stature 8/24. Cutis laxa 10/19 and ptosis 3/6 support skin and eye involvement; intellectual disability 4/18 is below 30%.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary: the subtype retains Noonan skeletal diagnostic features, with short stature also reported in 8/24. Individual sternal findings below 30% do not negate the defining skeletal axis.

basis: Muscle dystrophy with defining intellectual disability and movement disorder; cataracts frequent (30–79%). Hepatic steatosis <30%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
GDF6-related congenital retinal dystrophy causing profound visual impairment; no additional organ disease is established.
Inherited calcium regulation disorder. Paresthesia and spasms are hypocalcemic symptoms; basal ganglia calcification occurs in <30%.
Lysosomal storage disease with dementia and cerebral atrophy in 4/4 patients; adult Kufs-type disease does not establish retinal involvement.
Estrogen-receptor resistance; delayed skeletal maturation and osteoporosis occur in 80-99%. Coronary atherosclerosis is a separate disease rather than intrinsic organ involvement.
Congenital myopathy, contractures, cerebral and retinal hemorrhages define syndrome. Respiratory insufficiency in 3/3 reflects neuromuscular failure rather than direct airway or lung disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 3/3 results from severe neuromuscular weakness; direct pulmonary pathology is not established.

basis: CHD2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causes seizures, cognitive regression and intellectual disability.
PRDM16-related isolated cardiomyopathy with ventricular noncompaction and myocardial dysfunction.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with reduced visual acuity and central visual dysfunction.
Axonal/demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy in 6/6, pes cavus in 5/5 and hammertoes in 3/5 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Inherited atrial rhythm disorder; reported valve disease and atrial enlargement remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Familial atrial fibrillation is a cardiac rhythm disorder.
Mandibular defects, deafness and lipodystrophic endocrinopathy define MDPL; dermal/subcutaneous atrophy 4/4. Hepatic steatosis 2/3 and dental crowding 4/4 omitted at cap.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: dermal and subcutaneous atrophy affects 4/4; the three primary slots cover named skeletal/hearing disease and the required metabolic mechanism.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is a lipodystrophic metabolic disorder with insulin resistance in 4/4, hypertriglyceridemia in 3/4 and hypogonadism in 3/3 assessed males.

basis: Cystic tubulointerstitial kidney disease; associated aortic valve stenosis occurs in 4/7 patients (~57%); hepatic abnormalities occur in 1/7.
Cerebellar degeneration, developmental delay and intellectual disability; abnormal saccades and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
T-cell deficiency defines an immune and blood-cell disorder; neutropenia occurs in 2/2. Vitiligo and alopecia are separately diagnosed autoimmune diseases; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the defining defect is in T blood cells, supporting the blood-cell mechanism axis; neutropenia in 2/2 provides additional evidence.
decisions.dermatologic: none: vitiligo and alopecia (each 1/2) are distinct autoimmune diseases associated with immune dysregulation, rather than direct skin damage from the T-cell deficiency.

basis: Familial vesicoureteral reflux directly affects the bladder-ureter urinary tract; infection is a separate complication.
MYBPC3-related structural cardiomyopathy; ventricular noncompaction occurs in all reported patients.
Cystic renal dysplasia, encephalocele and polydactyly define Meckel syndrome; hepatic ductal-plate malformation with fibrosis is common (>30%) across the syndrome.
Glycosylation disorder with defining CNS and skeletal disease; hydroureter 3/4, nephrocalcinosis 30-79%. Ocular findings 4/4, hearing and heart defects 30-79% omitted at cap; visual loss is cerebral.

decisions.renal: involved: hydroureter affects 3/4 and nephrocalcinosis 30-79%; intrinsic urinary structural disease takes the remaining slot.
decisions.ocular: none under cap: cerebral visual impairment belongs to neurologic; hypermetropia/strabismus 4/4 are less severe than the retained urinary structural disease.

basis: PIGT-related clonal blood disorder causing complement-sensitive erythrocytes and hemolysis; listed systemic symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Familial cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; visual seizure phenomena are neurologic, not ocular damage.
T-B+ SCID entails profound T-cell lymphopenia and impaired adaptive immunity; respiratory, oral and ear infections are separately diagnosed consequences.

decisions.haematologic: primary: profound T-cell lymphopenia defines T-B+ SCID, with reduced lymphocyte count in 1/1 annotated patient; this directly affects blood cells.

basis: Inherited cutaneous pigmentation disorder defined by hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules.
Congenital cortical and other brain malformations with seizures and developmental delay; nystagmus is occasional and does not establish ocular damage.
Cortical malformations cause developmental impairment and seizures; cataract in 1/3 meets the approximate 30% threshold, although the cohort is small.
Isolated failure of sperm production affects reproductive function; no endocrine gland dysfunction is established.
Primary congenital microcephaly defines abnormal brain development; short stature alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine damage.
Defines renal, hepatic and pancreatic dysplasia; truncus arteriosus in 2/3. Cap excludes femoral bowing (3/3) and pulmonary hypoplasia (1/3); severe cardiac defects prioritized.
Mitochondrial cardiomyopathy; muscle weakness 1/2 with atrophy/myopathic biopsy 1/1; intellectual disability 1/1. Cataract 1/1 omitted by cap; evidence comprises very few patients.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability is reported in 1/1 assessed patient; retain lifelong neurodevelopmental impairment under the cap, with substantial sampling uncertainty.
decisions.ocular: none: cataract in 1/1 assessed patient qualifies by supplied frequency but is omitted under the four-axis cap.

basis: Neurodevelopmental/neurodegenerative syndrome; strabismus occurs in 80-99%, and scoliosis or clubfoot in 30-79%. Constipation alone does not establish gut damage.
Inherited high myopia, present in 8/8 annotated patients.
Myopathy and Pagetic bone lesions affect 5/5; frontotemporal degeneration is an explicitly defining, variable component, with cognitive impairment in 2/5 (~40%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: frontotemporal degeneration is explicitly included in the syndrome's name and definition, although variably expressed; cognitive impairment occurs in 2/5.

basis: Inclusion-body myopathy and Paget bone disease characterize this subtype; dementia is optional and not established in the supplied HNRNPA1 cohort.

decisions.neurologic: none: despite the generic parent-derived definition, dementia is optional and unreported in the supplied subtype cohort; a characteristic neurologic phenotype is not established.

basis: Inherited skin fragility with blistering and nail dystrophy from BP230 deficiency; this is not autoimmune epidermolysis bullosa.
HNRNPA1-associated motor neuron degeneration; denervation weakness does not establish primary muscle disease, and reported myopathy lacks a common frequency.
ELMOD3-related nonsyndromic hearing loss; mixed hearing impairment in 6/6 patients.
Inherited high myopia with increased globe axial length and impaired visual acuity.
Neurodevelopmental language-processing disorder; language delay occurs in 26/26 and cerebral white-matter abnormalities in 22/31.
Developmental and skeletal abnormalities characterize the syndrome; urinary abnormalities are annotated 80-99%. Myopia 4/8 and strabismus 6/14 support ocular involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal abnormalities are explicitly characteristic in the definition; frequent structural hand/chest abnormalities and joint stiffness reinforce this assignment.

basis: Retinal degeneration defines the disease. Bronchiectasis occurred in 1/4 patients (25%); situs inversus alone does not establish organ damage.
Inherited aortic aneurysm and dissection; additional arterial manifestations remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 5/5 and developmental delay in 3/5. Hearing loss in 1/5 is below threshold.
Ventricular arrhythmia defines disease; intrinsic proximal skeletal muscle weakness occurs in 1/3 (~33%), meeting the threshold in a small cohort.
Defective respiratory ciliary clearance causes chronic airway disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation affects 28/36 (~78%); situs inversus alone causes no cardiac damage.
Defective respiratory ciliary clearance causes chronic airway disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 4/12 (~33%), supporting otologic involvement.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; acute hepatic failure and progressive neurologic deterioration each occur in 1/2 (~50%). Isolated ptosis does not establish intrinsic ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis occurs in 1/2, but this isolated sign does not establish visual impairment or intrinsic ocular damage.

basis: Microcornea, myopia and chorioretinal atrophy occur in 8/8 patients; rotated ears are dysmorphic features without demonstrated ear dysfunction.
Holoprosencephaly, ectrodactyly and cleft lip/palate define the syndrome; microphthalmia and ptosis reported in 80-99%; endocrine frequency unspecified.
Immunodeficiency, bronchiectasis and inflammatory gastrointestinal disease are defining features; bronchiectasis 3/3, oral ulcers 2/2 and esophageal stricture 1/1.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent pulmonary infections leading to bronchiectasis explicitly define the disease; bronchiectasis reported in 3/3.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: inflammatory gastrointestinal disease is explicitly defining, supported by oral ulceration 2/2 and esophageal stricture 1/1.

basis: Encephalomyopathic mitochondrial depletion with lactic acidosis defines metabolic, brain and muscle disease. Isolated renal or immune reports do not establish common involvement.
GNAO1-associated developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, profound developmental impairment and structural brain abnormalities.
CACNA1D neurodevelopmental disorder with aldosteronism; ventricular hypertrophy 80-99%, conduction disease 30-79%. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; stones are separate.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; aortic regurgitation and atrial septal defect each reported in 1/3 patients, meeting ~30% in a small sample.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 9/12; recurrent middle-ear inflammation affects 8/12 patients.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear inflammation in 9/12. Situs inversus alone is not cardiovascular damage.
Primary familial brain calcification affects basal ganglia and other cerebral structures; no systemic metabolic disorder is established.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus occurs in 7/12 (~58%) and skeletal abnormalities in 30-79%. Feeding difficulty and hypotonia alone do not establish gastrointestinal or muscle damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal-system abnormalities are explicitly annotated as frequent (30-79%), supporting skeletal involvement independently of hypotonia.

basis: Inherited interstitial lung and liver disease; pulmonary fibrosis in 12/18 and liver enlargement with biochemical injury in most.
Age-related degeneration of the retinal macula; complement-associated variation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy defines disease; hand muscle atrophy and pes cavus occurred in 1/1 annotated patients; pulmonary frequency is unclear.
Progressive neurodegeneration and blinding optic atrophy define disease; structural skeletal abnormalities include pes cavus in 3/3 and pectus carinatum in 2/3.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural skeletal deformities are common, with pes cavus in 3/3 and pectus carinatum in 2/3; this exceeds motor symptoms alone.

basis: Syndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay, central hypotonia, spasticity and frequent seizures; no primary muscle damage established.
Defective respiratory ciliary clearance causes chronic airway disease; middle-ear inflammation occurs in 3/4 patients.
Molybdenum cofactor deficiency causes defining severe encephalopathy, seizures and developmental impairment; brain malformations are documented.
Strabismus 30-79%; ASD 7/10 and PDA 30-79%. Macrodontia lacks established functional damage; cleft palate 1/4 and hearing loss 10/42 are below threshold.
audit_reason: Remove gastrointestinal: frequent macrodontia and unspecified dental abnormalities do not establish functional oral damage; feeding difficulty alone is insufficient, and cleft palate is reported in only 1/4.

basis: Short-rib skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and restrictive respiratory impairment are major manifestations of asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy.
Defective airway ciliary clearance with bronchiectasis in 4/4; middle-ear clearance dysfunction manifests as recurrent otitis media in 3/3.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; recurrent otitis media affects 9/11 patients (~82%). Situs inversus alone does not damage organs.
Defining mucocutaneous vascular malformations (3/3); portal hypertension with elevated transaminases supports hepatic involvement (1/3), though the cohort is small.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: persistent mucocutaneous telangiectases are defining HHT lesions, reported in 3/3 patients. Hepatic involvement is supported by functional abnormalities in 1/3.

basis: Severe dermatitis and allergies define syndrome; malabsorption and developmental delay each 3/3; cardiac defects 1/3 omitted by cap; hypernatremia reflects fluid loss.
GMPPA glycosylation disorder with developmental disability and achalasia; lacrimal failure 15/15. Hearing impairment 4/12 omitted by cap.
Skeletal muscle purine metabolism defect causes myopathy; areflexia alone does not establish peripheral nerve damage.
Glycolytic defect defined by hemolysis and neurodegeneration; muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%; immune dysfunction omitted at cap; respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
Primary immunodeficiency with chronic airway destruction: bronchiectasis 12/16 (75%). Gut nodules occur in 30-79%, but malabsorption/diarrhea only 5-29%; enlargement alone is insufficient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: frequent intestinal lymphoid nodules do not establish damaging or function-impairing infiltration; diarrhea and malabsorption occur in only 5-29%.

basis: Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; muscle wasting and respiratory weakness reflect denervation, without evidence of intrinsic muscle or lung disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and muscle wasting are secondary to motor neuron loss and denervation; intrinsic muscle pathology is not the disease process.

basis: Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability, autistic features and neurologic gait instability; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Inherited iron-metabolism disorder; elevated hepatic iron alone does not establish function-impairing liver damage.
Persistent CD4 T-cell depletion defines this immunodeficiency; associated infections and bronchiectasis are separate diseases.
Defining hypopigmentation and palmoplantar keratoderma; ectopic calcification in 4/8 has no established additional damaged organ.
Inherited corneal endothelial dystrophy with corneal guttata in 12/12 patients.
Defining microphthalmia, pulmonary hypoplasia (4/5) and diaphragm defect (6/6); major neurologic impairment includes ID (1/1). Malrotation (2/7) is below 30%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: severe neurodevelopmental impairment is a major clinical feature; intellectual disability was present in 1/1 assessed patient
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital diaphragm skeletal-muscle defect is part of the defining triad and occurred in 6/6 patients

basis: Inherited mucocutaneous candidiasis with oral thrush and dermatitis in 2/2; blepharitis represents direct eyelid inflammation in 1/2, with substantial small-cohort uncertainty.

decisions.ocular: involved: blepharitis is direct eyelid inflammation reported in 1/2 patients (50%); the supplied phenotype evidence supports inclusion despite the small cohort.

basis: DNAJC6-related juvenile parkinsonism; abnormal saccades and muscle tone reflect neurologic dysfunction.
SYNJ1-related neurodegenerative parkinsonism; dysphagia, rigidity and gaze abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated separate organ injury.
Reticulate cutaneous hyperpigmentation with palmoplantar pitting and epidermal changes.
Chromosomal syndrome with seizures in 2/2 and developmental delay in 1/2; facial features do not establish additional organ damage.
Dermatan-sulfate biosynthesis disorder with contractures, joint abnormalities and skin fragility; isolated PFO and blue sclerae do not establish functional damage.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss, present in 6/6 reported patients.
Syndromic intellectual disability; kyphoscoliosis in 3/3 and dental malocclusion in 2/3 support skeletal and dental involvement.
Partial gonadal dysgenesis impairs testicular endocrine development; congenital heart disease is a named syndrome component, with tetralogy of Fallot in 1/3.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital heart disease is explicitly a named syndrome component; tetralogy of Fallot occurs in 1/3 reported patients.

basis: Neuronal migration disorder with seizures and developmental delay; persistent strabismus reported in 1/1 patient, with limited frequency evidence.
Despite the susceptibility name, the definition specifies PAX5-related precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
Brain, skeletal and ear/hearing abnormalities characterize the syndrome; renal hypoplasia occurs in 6/6. Four-axis cap; lesser cutaneous and oral anomalies omitted.

decisions.otologic: primary: congenital ear abnormalities and hearing loss are characteristic components of van Maldergem syndrome; hearing impairment is reported in 3/3.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment, distal contractures and pituitary/hypogonadal dysfunction define the syndrome; feeding difficulty does not establish intrinsic gut damage.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy with defining chronic intestinal dysmotility. Fractures and wounds are secondary injuries; hyperhidrosis alone is not skin damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: gastrointestinal dysfunction is explicit in the definition and synonyms; intestinal dysmotility is a defining loss of digestive function.

basis: Inherited red-cell aplasia; triphalangeal thumb and ventricular septal defect each occur in 1/1 annotated patient. Organ frequencies are uncertain given the tiny sample.
Inherited peripheral sensory channelopathy causing episodic neuropathic pain and dysesthesia; no other organ damage is established.
Inherited sensory-neuron channel disorder causing episodic pain and autonomic dysfunction; painful limbs do not imply muscle or joint damage.
Congenital glycosylation disorder defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and distal arthrogryposis.
Benign fibroadenomas confined to the breast, which has no designated axis; PRLR association alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Inherited prolactin-signalling disorder with persistent hyperprolactinemia; bone loss is occasional (5-29%). The neurological ancestry does not reflect its phenotype.
APOB lipid disorder; hepatic steatosis with biochemical injury commonly affects over 30%. Severe intestinal, neurologic and retinal disease chiefly affects the biallelic minority.
Inherited complement deficiency causing susceptibility to recurrent bacterial infections; pneumonia and meningitis are separately diagnosed infections.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration.
COQ8B-related coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis deficiency causes renal disease; steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome in 15/15 and FSGS in 12/13.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an established coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis disorder, not merely a renal disease associated with an unspecified gene.

basis: Asparagine synthesis defect causes microcephaly and progressive encephalopathy; visual loss is often cerebral; optic nerve hypoplasia in 1/1 does not establish a common ocular phenotype.
Hereditary motor neuron/peripheral nerve disease; weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation rather than a separate primary muscle disorder.
Central adrenal insufficiency 4/4; alopecia totalis and nail dystrophy each 2/4; recurrent infections are separate episodes; Chiari anatomy alone does not establish functional damage.
Aortic aneurysms and skeletal connective-tissue abnormalities define LDS5; cleft palate occurs in 5/43, below threshold.
Developmental disability and congenital heart defects define syndrome. Skeletal involvement includes hypermobility 5/6; optic nerve hypoplasia 2/6 and visual impairment 30-79%.
Otosclerosis affects the otic capsule and hearing apparatus; localized ear-bone disease does not establish systemic skeletal involvement.
ADAM10-related Alzheimer disease causes cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Combined immune dysfunction with profound antibody deficiency; oral thrush and other secondary infections are separately diagnosed diseases.
Combined T/B-cell immunodeficiency; Kaposi sarcoma remains a separately diagnosed malignancy despite occurring in 3/3 reported patients.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; hepatic steatosis/injury and muscle-fiber pathology each occur in 1/2. Respiratory distress alone does not demonstrate intrinsic pulmonary damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: hypotonia/head lag in 1/2 do not establish brain or nerve damage; elevated brain/CSF lactate alone is metabolic evidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: muscle-fiber abnormalities in 1/2 support direct mitochondrial myopathy ([original report](https://doi.org/10.1093/hmg/ddt295)).

basis: Glycosylation disorder defined by developmental impairment and seizures; cerebellar atrophy in 2/2. Feeding difficulty and impaired pursuit do not establish other organ damage.
Glycosylation disorder defined by neurodevelopmental disease and optic atrophy; thrombocytopenia reported in 1/1. Respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic nerve atrophy is explicitly part of the disease definition and documented in 1/1; optic nerve belongs to ocular.

basis: Inherited palmoplantar keratoderma directly affects the epidermis; no extracutaneous organ damage is established.

Ferritin iron-storage defect; alopecia 10/11 and seizures 1/2 support involvement. Neurologic frequency is uncertain because of the small sample; normal blood counts exclude a blood-cell disorder.

decisions.neurologic: involved: seizures in 1/2 assessed patients meet the supplied frequency threshold; small sample and variable dominant/recessive expression reduce confidence.

basis: Inherited proximal tubular wasting with metabolic acidosis. Rickets and leg bowing are reported, but subtype-specific prevalence >=30% or a required skeletal criterion is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: phosphate-wasting rickets is reported, but frequency is unspecified and it is not a required diagnostic criterion; >=30% is not established for this subtype.

basis: Immunodeficiency with defining T-cell lymphopenia; anoperineal fistula and chronic diarrhea in 2/2 support GI involvement. Recurrent infections and autoimmune anemia are separate diseases.
audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary: selective T-cell lymphopenia is explicitly defining, making this a disease of blood cells as well as an immunodeficiency. Retain gastrointestinal involvement for reported fistulas and chronic diarrhea.

basis: Congenital hip dysplasia with joint deformity and subsequent hip osteoarthritis.
Intrinsic T-cell deficiency with lymphopenia and impaired proliferation; recurrent infections do not establish lasting lung, intestinal or ear damage.
CD3D SCID directly impairs T-cell development, with defining T-cell lymphopenia in 3/3. Infections and diarrhea do not establish additional direct organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: intrinsic failure of T-cell development with lymphopenia in 3/3 is a defining blood-cell defect, alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Hereditary susceptibility specifically concerns bile-duct cancer, defining the hepatic site; this does not establish an existing malignancy or injury.
