decisions.renal: involved: urinary bladder sphincter dysfunction is documented functional loss in 30-79%, rather than a later risk of urinary disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes cavus (30-79%) reflects secondary motor imbalance; direct skeletal damage is not established by the foot-shape finding.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 11/11 patients.
Skeletal ciliopathy; nephronophthisis/CKD and hepatic fibrosis each affect roughly >=30% of reported cases. Retinal frequency is uncertain; thoracic restriction is secondary to skeletal disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: thoracic skeletal hypoplasia causes restrictive breathing; common direct airway or pulmonary parenchymal disease is not established.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal degeneration has no supplied frequency; nyctalopia is occasional (5-29%), leaving >=30% direct ocular involvement unestablished.

basis: Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis causes anemia; hepatomegaly and jaundice alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Sensory axonal neuropathy; neuropathic arthropathy and metatarsal fractures each affect 5/7 patients, supporting substantial skeletal damage.
Short-rib thoracic dysplasia causes characteristic respiratory insufficiency and pulmonary hypoplasia in most; renal and retinal findings are occasional, 5-29%.
Joubert brain malformation with developmental delay in 19/19; persistent eyelid dysfunction affects 15/18. Pulmonary, skeletal and renal abnormalities are below 30%.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ptosis in 15/18 represents loss of eyelid function; eyelids explicitly belong to the ocular axis.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disability defines the syndrome; hypotonia and minor dysmorphism do not establish muscle damage. Pneumonia and organomegaly occur in <30%.
Inborn coenzyme A metabolism disorder causing progressive brain degeneration and axonal neuropathy; distal wasting is neurogenic.
Nonsyndromic hereditary hearing loss affects the auditory system.
White matter disease with cerebellar dysfunction; optic neuropathy in 2/6 and visual field defects in 4/6 support ocular involvement.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 20/20 patients.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; nonspecific palate and pinna morphology do not establish functional organ damage; heart anomalies occur in under 30%.
Spastic paraplegia, peripheral neuropathy and optic atrophy define the syndrome; muscle wasting in 2/2 reflects denervation rather than a primary muscle process.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting in 2/2 is neurogenic; the nonspecific Achilles tendon finding does not establish direct musculoskeletal damage.

basis: Warburg micro syndrome is defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment, cataracts/microphthalmia and hypogonadism; contractures occur in 2/7.
Cerebellar malformation defines Joubert syndrome; polydactyly 11/11, microphthalmia 2/3 with retinal dysfunction, and renal hypoplasia 1/3 support involvement.
Developmental disability and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome despite conflicting limb descriptions. Visual impairment occurs in 3/4; cardiac defects each in 1/4 are below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: limb and digit abnormalities are defining features in the definition; HPO also supports a major skeletal phenotype despite conflicting morphology.

basis: Multiple peripheral or spinal nerve schwannomas; schwannomas in 23/23. Subcutaneous nerve tumors do not establish a separate skin disorder.
Myopathy and neurodevelopmental/extrapyramidal dysfunction define the syndrome. Transaminase elevation alone does not establish liver injury.
Inherited reticulate pigment disorder; skin pigmentation abnormalities occur in 11/11. Broad glycosylation ancestry alone does not establish a clinical metabolic disorder in this subtype.
Hereditary motor-pathway degeneration; skeletal muscle atrophy in 3/3 assessed patients is persistent muscle tissue loss. Contractures and scoliosis are only occasional (<30%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal muscle atrophy in 3/3 assessed patients documents common persistent tissue loss; neurogenic origin does not negate it. Contractures/scoliosis alone are <30%.

basis: Central motor and neurodevelopmental disease; amyotrophy is neurogenic, and delayed puberty alone does not establish endocrine gland damage.
Spastic paraplegia and polyneuropathy with destructive acropathy and terminal digit loss define disease; structural skeletal involvement exceeds weakness or gait symptoms.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: acropathy with loss of terminal digits is explicitly defining structural damage, supported by frequent knee and Achilles abnormalities (30-79%).

basis: Corticospinal and cerebral white-matter disease defines SPG63. Frequent muscle atrophy (30-79%) reflects neurologic dysfunction, without evidence of a separate muscle lesion.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%) but is secondary to neurologic dysfunction; direct myopathic damage is not established.

basis: Autoinflammatory vasculitis with immunodeficiency and marrow defects; stroke in 12/15. Skin ulceration in 18/34 omitted by cap; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
POGLUT1-related reticulate pigmentation and epidermal abnormalities define this cutaneous disease; the glycosylation ancestor does not clearly establish a metabolic phenotype.
Inherited temporal lobe epilepsy; reported manifestations are seizures.
Inherited obesity with metabolic abnormalities. Steatosis, hypertension and coronary disease are separately diagnosed obesity-associated conditions despite reported frequencies.
Defining poikiloderma, contractures, myopathy and pulmonary fibrosis; hepatic and pancreatic dysfunction are variable and not established above 30% here.
Inherited cerebellar ataxia with epilepsy and intellectual disability; nystagmus and pursuit abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction without established eye damage.
Defined by external-ear and mandibular malformations; question-mark ears 9/9 and mandibular hypoplasia 4/9. Other organ abnormalities are minority findings.
Defective NK-cell cytotoxicity defines immunodeficiency; recurrent infections do not establish lasting damage to additional organs.
Sacral and vertebral malformations define disease; anal atresia and renal agenesis each in 1/3. Neurologic injury is not established despite neural-tube ancestry.
Genetic Alzheimer disease causes cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Syndrome defined by trilineage marrow failure and developmental delay; microcephaly occurs in 2/3 reported patients.
GPI-anchor metabolic disorder with defining developmental impairment and seizures; cleft palate affects 2/5 patients (40%).
Bilateral renal agenesis in 4/4; pulmonary hypoplasia reported in 1/1 and characteristic of the resulting severe oligohydramnios sequence.
Optic nerve abnormalities with visual impairment and developmental delay/intellectual disability define the syndrome; hearing impairment is occasional.
Ovarian endocrine failure with low estradiol and elevated gonadotropins occurs in 5/5; this is gonadal hormone dysfunction.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated FSH and LH in 3/3 establishes gonadal hormone-organ dysfunction.
Inherited retinal degeneration with rod-cone dystrophy, retinal atrophy and visual loss.
Nail dystrophy and palmoplantar keratoderma define the disease; persistent oral leukoplakia affects 7/10 patients.
KRT6B-related nail dystrophy, palmoplantar keratoderma and cutaneous cysts.
Primary skeletal muscle disease with weakness and nemaline bodies; respiratory insufficiency is occasional and reflects muscle weakness.
Inherited palmoplantar epidermal keratinization disorder; oral leukoplakia occurs in only 1/17 patients.
GABRA1 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. Optic atrophy in one assessed patient does not establish involvement in at least 30% across the disease.
Inherited atrial myocardial and electrical dysfunction; stroke is a separately diagnosed complication with unspecified frequency.
Intracranial arterial disease and achalasia define the syndrome; ischemic stroke with brain injury occurs in 4/9, with stroke also annotated as obligate.
Inherited metabolic disorder defined by hyperammonemic encephalopathy; liver injury is not established by hyperammonemia alone.
Cortical malformation with epilepsy and developmental impairment; exotropia occurs in only 1/5 patients.
Immunodeficiency with anemia/thrombocytopenia, retinal vasculitis and pericarditis each reported in 1/1; panniculitis omitted at cap. Organ-frequency estimates have tiny denominators.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia and thrombocytopenia each reported in 1/1 support blood-cell involvement; prioritized over panniculitis.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: panniculitis is direct subcutaneous inflammation, reported in 1/1, but blood, retinal and cardiac involvement take priority.

basis: Progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, seizures and profound developmental impairment define the disorder; hypotonia is neurologic.
Syndromic intellectual disability; myopia and astigmatism each reported in 1/2, supporting common visual dysfunction with limited sampling. Dental crowding alone is insufficient.
TUBB2A-related brain malformations, severe developmental delay and seizures define this neurodevelopmental disorder.
IL21-related immunodeficiency with defining infantile inflammatory bowel disease; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Cerebellar degeneration and ataxia; eye movement findings are neurologic. Digit morphology alone does not establish damage; hypogonadism/hearing loss are occasional.
Inherited atrial arrhythmia; atrial fibrillation in 5/5 patients.
Developmental brain malformations define the disease; microphthalmia and retinal dysplasia occur in 1/3 reported patients.
Oocyte structural defect causes infertility with normal hormone levels; purely reproductive disease.
Skeletal dysplasia and defective glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis define this linkeropathy; intellectual disability occurs in 5/7. Neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine: this XYLT1-related linkeropathy is an inborn disorder of glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis. Dermatologic damage is not established for this subtype.

basis: NR2F2-related congenital structural heart disease, particularly atrioventricular septal defects.
KIZ-related rod-cone retinal degeneration; no extraocular disease established.
KRT13-related white sponge nevus is a keratinization disorder principally affecting oral mucosa; the skin-disorder ancestry does not establish cutaneous disease.
Skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly/developmental impairment and hair/pigment abnormalities; anemia in 1/2 patients; ocular findings omitted at the four-axis cap.
GPI-anchor remodeling disorder with neurodevelopmental impairment; retinal dystrophy 2/2 and pulmonic stenosis 1/2. Enamel hypoplasia 1/1 omitted at cap; denominators are small.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none at cap: enamel hypoplasia 1/1 supports dental involvement, but retinal dystrophy and pulmonic stenosis take priority for severity.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: PGAP1 deficiency is an inborn GPI-anchor remodeling disorder, establishing a metabolic mechanism beyond the gene name alone.

basis: Pontocerebellar malformation and neuropathy; structural kyphoscoliosis in 2/2 reported patients. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; gastrointestinal symptoms lack damage evidence.
Primordial skeletal growth disorder with microcephaly, developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2; ectopic kidney in 1/2 does not establish renal impairment.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia with severe neurodevelopmental impairment; optic atrophy in 4/8 supports direct ocular damage. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited metabolic syndrome with obesity, diabetes and dyslipidemia; hypertension in 27/27 is a defining vascular feature. Infarction is a separately coded disease.
PGM3 glycosylation immunodeficiency; CNS damage ~60-88%, eczema 80-99%. Bronchiectasis 11/17 follows separate infections; hearing loss 4/8 and cutaneous vasculitis 30-79% omitted by cap.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis (11/17) follows recurrent respiratory infections, separately diagnosed complications; direct glycosylation-related lung injury is not established.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent eczematoid dermatitis in 80-99% reflects intrinsic cutaneous immune inflammation, beyond separately diagnosed skin infections.

basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease; strabismus occurs in 1/2 assessed patients, supporting ocular dysfunction with limited sampling.
Dilated cardiomyopathy, woolly hair/keratoderma and tooth agenesis are defining manifestations; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Respiratory-chain defect; seizures 2/2 and developmental delay 1/1 support neurologic damage; renal tubular acidosis and sensorineural hearing loss each 1/1. Small cohort.
DEAF1-associated intellectual disability and developmental dysfunction; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency, and joint laxity is not tissue damage.
Intellectual disability and obstructive apnea define the syndrome. Visual dysfunction: astigmatism 2/2, amblyopia 1/1, nystagmus 3/3; skeletal damage prevalence remains uncertain.

decisions.ocular: involved: HPO documents visual impairment, including astigmatism 2/2 and amblyopia 1/1; these support the threshold, with limited denominators.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal malformations are reported in selected 1/1-2/2 samples; substantial skeletal impairment in >=30% of the syndrome is not established.

basis: Adrenal cortisol excess; myopathy/bone loss occurs in roughly 50-80%, skin atrophy/fragility in >50%, and hypertension in about 70% of overt Cushing cases.

Syndromic developmental disability with defining skeletal anomalies, including contractures; strabismus and bilateral ptosis each occur in 30-79%. Feeding difficulty alone does not establish GI damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal anomalies, including kyphosis/scoliosis and arthrogryposis, are explicitly defining features; arthrogryposis is also reported in 2/2 assessed patients.

basis: Nonsyndromic bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 3/3 patients.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining leukoencephalopathy and developmental impairment in 7/7; optic pallor and visual impairment in 5/7. Weakness does not establish intrinsic myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: leukoencephalopathy and neurodevelopmental impairment define the clinical syndrome, with white-matter abnormalities and intellectual disability in 7/7.

basis: TAF4B-related spermatogenic failure affects reproduction; elevated FSH alone does not establish impaired gonadal hormone production.
Isolated spermatogenic failure affects reproduction; elevated FSH reflects impaired spermatogenesis rather than a separate endocrine disorder.
Interferonopathy with destructive CNS disease; thrombocytopenia occurs in 2/5. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury; steatosis is 1/5.
Organ assignments reflect the defining familial melanoma and glioma susceptibility; established tumors or damage are not assumed, and additional cancer risks are excluded.
Pituitary deficiency and polydactyly define syndrome; developmental delay/seizures 2/2 and cleft palate 1/3. Urinary reflux 1/1 omitted at four-axis cap; samples small.

decisions.renal: none: vesicoureteral reflux is reported in 1/1; omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of defining endocrine/skeletal features, severe neurologic impairment and cleft palate.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate occurs in 1/3, meeting ~30%; it is an intrinsic structural manifestation explicitly supported by the syndrome definition.

basis: Pontocerebellar and cerebral degeneration with severe developmental impairment and seizures; optic atrophy in 1/2 supports ocular involvement.

Inherited cone and rod degeneration with reduced visual acuity in 5/5 patients.
EMP2-associated glomerular podocyte disease causing nephrotic syndrome; a genetic cause does not establish immune-mediated disease.
Renal disease in 6/6; cholestasis and intellectual disability each 2/6 (~33%); ocular abnormalities below 30%; hypertension is a separate diagnosis.
DGAT1 triglyceride synthesis deficiency causes intestinal villous injury and protein-losing enteropathy; hyperlipidemia in 2/2. Immunoglobulin depletion follows enteric protein loss.
ID/microcephaly and Coffin-Siris nail/digital abnormalities define the phenotype; nail hypoplasia and clinodactyly 2/2. Delayed puberty alone does not establish common hypogonadism.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: fifth-finger/toe nail hypoplasia in 2/2 is a defining Coffin-Siris feature.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypogonadism is optional; delayed puberty in 1/2 does not establish hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in at least 30%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: digital skeletal abnormalities are characteristic of the Coffin-Siris phenotype; clinodactyly occurs in 2/2.

basis: HCN1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; the supplied metabolic ancestor does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 15/15; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish an intrinsic immune disorder.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; persistent swallowing and intestinal motility dysfunction occur in 30-79%. Developmental incontinence and joint laxity do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: chronic dysphagia and intestinal dysmotility are persistent losses of gastrointestinal function reported in 30-79%; reflux alone is not the basis.

basis: Developmental eye defects and rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia define the syndrome; intellectual disability occurs in 2/6 (~33%); precocious puberty is 1/6.
Inherited hepatobiliary transport/metabolic disorder causing intrahepatic cholestasis and progressive liver failure; no common extrahepatic damage established.
Intellectual disability and skeletal overgrowth define syndrome; scoliosis occurs in 4/13; isolated cardiac reports do not establish common involvement.
Tubular aggregate skeletal myopathy; hypocalcemia in 5/5 supports electrolyte involvement. Miosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
Isolated inherited hair growth disorder affecting scalp and body hair, eyebrows and eyelashes; eyelash loss alone does not establish ocular damage.
Enamel hypomaturation affects teeth; nail dysplasia reported in one patient does not establish common nail involvement across this otherwise dental disorder.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect; epistaxis, bruising and dental bleeding do not establish separate organ damage.
Progressive white-matter degeneration and ovarian endocrine failure define the disorder; muscle histochemistry alone does not establish damaging myopathy.
Cleft lips, gingival/labial mucosal fusion and abnormal dentition define an oral malformation; nonspecific facial morphology does not establish additional skeletal damage.
Glycogen storage myopathy with immunodeficiency; cardiomyopathy is defining and reported in 1/3. Colitis (2/3) and hepatic fibrosis (1/3) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Isolated hair disorder causing sparse, woolly hair and sparse eyelashes; eyelashes belong to the hair axis.
Defective T- and B-cell proliferation defines immunodeficiency; respiratory infections are separate infectious episodes without established chronic lung damage.
Inherited citrate transport disorder with epileptic encephalopathy; enamel defects and hypodontia affect most patients with erupted teeth.
Inherited lymphatic vascular malformation causing lymphedema; hyperkeratosis reported in one assessed patient does not establish common skin damage.
Inherited pure red-cell aplasia caused by RPS29 variants; no common direct extrahematologic injury is established.
Frontotemporal degeneration and motor neuron disease; weakness and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction; hearing loss occurs in 2/8.
An isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy; ventricular dysfunction, heart failure and mitral regurgitation occurred in 10/10 patients.
Mitochondrial disorder; brain abnormalities/seizures, cardiomyopathy and muscle weakness each reported in 1/1. Ophthalmoplegia/ptosis omitted under four-axis cap; denominators are small.

decisions.ocular: none: ophthalmoplegia and ptosis occur in 1/1, but ocular involvement is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of brain, heart and broader muscle disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: mitochondrial muscle dysfunction with weakness occurs in 1/1; prioritized over ocular motor manifestations under the cap.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder with defining developmental impairment and structural CNS abnormalities. Muscle enzyme deficiency alone does not establish myopathy; hepatic frequency is unknown.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: respiratory-chain deficiency in a muscle sample does not establish damaging myopathy; axial hypotonia can arise from the defining CNS disease.

basis: Neurodegeneration and photosensitive skin disease define ATLD2; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 4/4. Ocular telangiectasia and photophobia do not establish functional injury.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: photosensitive cutaneous disease with telangiectasia in 4/4 is a defining component of this DNA repair syndrome.

basis: Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with visual loss; retinal vessel attenuation remains within the ocular axis.
Skeletal overgrowth and epiphyseal dysplasia with scoliosis, osteopenia and enlarged great toes; no endocrine gland disorder is established.
Encephalopathy, metabolic dysfunction and subcutaneous fat loss define disease; hepatic steatosis occurs in 30-79%. Myopathy and respiratory failure occur in only 5-29%.
Ghrelin receptor deficiency impairs growth hormone signaling; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation reflect endocrine growth dysfunction.
Brain disease, pituitary insufficiency and blindness define syndrome; neurogenic bladder, reflux and hydronephrosis in 6/6. Hip dislocation (6/6) omitted by cap.
Autoinflammatory small-vessel disease with destructive skin lesions; pulmonary fibrosis 6/10. Myositis 2/5 omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Pancreatic agenesis causes both exocrine insufficiency and diabetes in 14/14; developmental delay occurs in only 1/14.
Defining cerebral overgrowth, cortical malformation and hydrocephalus with postaxial polydactyly; skin findings lack frequency evidence.
Defining cerebral malformations, hydrocephalus and developmental disability; postaxial polydactyly occurs in 11/12.
METTL23-related intellectual disability; pes planus in 4/4 lacks evidence of functional skeletal injury. Minor facial features and bifid uvula do not establish additional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes planus in 4/4 meets frequency, but flat feet alone do not demonstrate functional damage or a clinically significant skeletal malformation.

basis: Cerebellar degeneration defines disease; sensorineural hearing impairment is frequent (30-79%); eye movement abnormalities are neurologic.
Inherited high myopia; all reported patients have ocular refractive and growth abnormalities.
Inherited chylomicron metabolism disorder; pancreatitis and atherosclerosis are separately coded diseases. Lipemia retinalis and organ enlargement alone do not establish damage.
Brain, oral and digital malformations define OFD14. Cardiac defects occur in 30-79%; retinal coloboma, epiglottic and urethral defects also meet frequency thresholds but exceed the cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: PDA and VSD are annotated at 30-79%; potentially serious cardiac malformations receive the remaining slot under the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal coloboma occurs in 30-79%, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of cardiac malformations.

basis: Immune dysregulation with cytopenias 46-85%; endocrine pancreatic autoimmunity 4/5 and enteropathy/exocrine failure 38-40%. Dermatitis 2/5 omitted at cap; pneumonitis 3/13 below threshold.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: endocrine pancreatic autoimmunity occurs in 4/5 annotated patients as direct multisystem disease; endocrine disease does not define the whole syndrome.

basis: Adrenal macronodular hyperplasia causes autonomous cortisol excess. Osteoporosis frequency is unspecified for this subtype; hypertension is a separately coded complication.
Cerebellar degeneration and neuropathy within an inherited fatty-acid biosynthesis disorder; nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction, not eye damage.
Centronuclear skeletal myopathy; dilated cardiomyopathy in 2/3 patients. Motor delay and respiratory weakness do not establish separate brain or lung damage.
Defined neuro-ophthalmological syndrome with cerebellar dysplasia and functional eye abnormalities, including frequent retinal atrophy and amblyopia.
Defective circulating IGF complex causes endocrine growth impairment and insulin resistance. Reduced bone density occurs in only 5-29%; short stature alone is not skeletal damage.
Glucocorticoid resistance causes endocrine feedback abnormalities; hypertension is frequent (30-79%). Hirsutism does not establish skin damage.
Urinary reflux/collecting-system defects define disease. Hypermobility in 2/2 lacks documented tissue injury or functional loss; UTIs are separate infections.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility in 2/2 does not by itself establish damaging joint disease or impaired locomotor function.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency defined by absent T and B lymphocytes; neurologic, visual and hearing abnormalities are only occasional (5-29%).
Congenital small eyes with hypermetropia and reduced visual acuity in all reported patients.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with visual loss.
Nonsyndromic hereditary profound hearing impairment.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability in 5/5 patients; facial dysmorphism does not establish additional organ damage.
Defining subcutaneous fat loss and insulin resistance; hepatic lipid deposition in 80-99%; muscle atrophy in 3/3 and myopathy in 1/3. Hypertension is separately coded.
Retinal dystrophy and intellectual disability 14/14; obesity 14/14, diabetes 13/14; CKD 2/2. Polydactyly 14/14 omitted by cap.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and digit anomalies define BBS4; renal abnormalities are major BBS criteria. Intellectual disability in 1/3 omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: structural renal abnormalities are major BBS diagnostic criteria and are documented in BBS4, despite unspecified frequency here.
decisions.neurologic: none under cap: intellectual disability in 1/3 qualifies, but retinal, endocrine, skeletal and potentially severe renal disease take priority.

basis: Retinal degeneration, obesity/hypogonadism and digit malformations define the syndrome; intellectual disability 3/3. Hypodontia omitted under the four-axis cap.
Retinal dystrophy 6/7, obesity 11/11, hypogonadism 5/5 and polydactyly 9/9 define disease; intellectual disability in 6/6 supports neurologic involvement.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and developmental delay define disease. Polydactyly occurs in 8/8 and is a major criterion; renal dysplasia is only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is a defining feature and global developmental delay occurs in 8/8; prioritized within the three-primary cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: polydactyly occurs in 8/8 and is a major diagnostic criterion; retained as the fourth axis after prioritizing visual, endocrine and neurologic disease.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity and digital anomalies are core features; developmental delay 2/2, intellectual disability 2/4. Renal insufficiency 1/3 omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none: renal insufficiency in 1/3 qualifies, but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent defining manifestations.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is a major BBS criterion; brachydactyly and syndactyly each occur in 2/2 reported patients.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and renal disease are cardinal BBS features; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in ~60% (1/1 annotated). Skeletal features omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: structural or functional renal abnormalities are a major BBS diagnostic criterion, and renal disease is prominent in BBS10.

basis: Retinopathy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly define BBS; renal structural or functional disease is a major diagnostic criterion, although subtype frequency is uncertain.
Retinal dystrophy 7/8, obesity 8/8 and polydactyly 8/8 are defining features. Neurologic impairment: intellectual disability 3/3 and developmental delay 5/7. Renal frequency unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 3/3 and developmental delay in 5/7 establish common functional damage; three primary slots hold core diagnostic features.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is a major BBS diagnostic feature and occurs in 8/8 reported subtype patients.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity and renal disease are defining BBS features; developmental/intellectual impairment in 1/1. Polydactyly omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal disease is a major BBS diagnostic feature; renal insufficiency is reported in 1/1 annotated patient.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay and intellectual disability occur in 1/1; retained alongside the defining retinal, metabolic and renal axes.

basis: BBS retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly are defining; renal abnormalities ~50% and a major criterion. Neurodevelopmental involvement omitted by cap.
Retinal dystrophy, hypogonadism/obesity and developmental impairment define the syndrome; stage 5 CKD occurs in 3/4. Polydactyly (2/2) omitted by cap; situs alone is noninjurious.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability and developmental delay are major diagnostic features of Bardet-Biedl syndrome and are present in 2/2 annotated patients.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity and renal disease are major Bardet-Biedl criteria; renal failure and intellectual disability each 1/1 in this subtype. Brachydactyly omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal disease is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic feature, with renal insufficiency and stage 5 kidney disease documented in the reported subtype case (1/1).

basis: Retinal dystrophy 23/23, obesity 24/24, polydactyly 19/23. Renal anomalies are a major BBS criterion despite insufficiency in 6/23; neurologic features omitted under cap.
Inherited abnormal albumin binding alters circulating thyroid hormone measurements; patients are euthyroid, without intrinsic thyroid injury or other organ damage.
Inherited albumin synthesis disorder; subcutaneous lipodystrophy occurs in 30-79%, and osteoporosis is reported in 2/2 assessed patients; skeletal estimate is uncertain.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: osteoporosis represents bone damage reported in 2/2 assessed patients; supplied HPO frequency supports inclusion despite the small denominator.

basis: Defined as isolated breast/nipple malformation, outside the axes; meatal stenosis in 1/2 reported males does not establish a typical renal phenotype.
Genetic glomerular disease with proteinuria and progressive kidney failure; other PAX2-associated phenotypes are not established for this concept.
Inherited functional fibrinogen disorder. Despite HPO thrombosis frequency of 30-79%, thrombotic events are separately diagnosed complications; bleeding sites do not imply local disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: HPO reports venous thrombosis in 30-79%, but these are separately diagnosed thrombotic events whose risk is raised by the coagulation disorder.

basis: Global developmental delay 30-79%, despite conflicting rare annotation. Bronchiectasis is a separate infection sequela; intestinal hyperplasia lacks common functional injury.

decisions.haematologic: none: immune-cell abnormalities and lymphoproliferation do not establish a separate blood disorder or impaired splenic blood function.
decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis is reported in 30-79%, but represents a separately diagnosed sequela of recurrent infections rather than direct intrinsic lung injury.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal lymphoid hyperplasia occurs in 30-79%, but functional injury is not established; diarrhea and malabsorption are only 5-29%.

basis: Intestinal lymphangiectasia and ID define syndrome; microtia 8/8 and camptodactyly 5/8; blepharophimosis 6/9 omitted at cap. Hearing impairment alone occurs in only 2/9.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic dysplasia alone does not establish heart or blood-vessel damage within this axis; pericardial lymphangiectasia has no frequency.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is a defining Hennekam feature, present in 7/9 patients.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis in 6/9 qualifies structurally but is omitted at the cap in favor of universal microtia and functionally limiting contractures.

basis: Mitochondrial/GH disorder with cataracts and deafness; sensory neuropathy 3/3; skeletal dysplasia and achalasia (80-99%) omitted at cap.
Congenital neutrophil deficiency with marrow maturation arrest constitutes an innate immunodeficiency; infections do not establish additional intrinsic organ damage.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder defined by intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures; elevated alkaline phosphatase alone does not establish liver disease.
Renal Fanconi dysfunction with endocrine/metabolic abnormalities; rickets and hepatomegaly with elevated transaminases each reported in 1/1 patients; frequency evidence is limited.
Scalp aplasia and terminal limb defects define AOS. Congenital cutaneous capillary malformation occurs in 4/6; individual cardiac and portal lesions occur in 1/6.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita in 4/6 is a structural capillary malformation, not transient mottling; capillaries belong to this axis.

basis: Defining skin, nail and dental defects; sensorineural hearing impairment 3/6. Esophageal strictures 2/6 share the GI axis. Asthma 3/6 is a separate associated disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: asthma in 3/6 meets the frequency threshold but is a separately diagnosed association; direct syndromic airway damage is not established.

basis: Gonadotropin deficiency defines the endocrine disorder; anosmia is a defining Kallmann feature and occurs in 4/4 annotated patients.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the Kallmann syndrome parent establishes defining olfactory dysfunction, supported by anosmia in 4/4 patients.

basis: Inherited ANLN-associated glomerular disease with proteinuria and kidney failure; no immune mechanism established.
Metabolic leukodystrophy with progressive encephalopathy; optic atrophy reported in 1/1. Renal tubular acidosis has no established common frequency.
Airway ciliary dysfunction causes chronic respiratory disease; middle-ear clearance dysfunction with recurrent otitis occurs in 2/5 (40%). Situs inversus alone is not damage.
Serine synthesis disorder with brain malformations and ichthyosis; foot deformities 12/12 and toe syndactyly 7/12. Ablepharon 9/12 omitted at the four-organ cap.

decisions.ocular: none at cap: ablepharon affects 9/12, but universal limb malformations take the remaining slot.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: rocker-bottom feet in 12/12 and toe syndactyly in 7/12 establish common structural limb involvement.

basis: Peripheral neuropathy classified as a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; weakness and foot deformity reflect denervation rather than a separate primary myopathy.
Presynaptic neuromuscular transmission disorder with motor neuropathy; distal amyotrophy in 40% and fixed foot deformities in 70-80%. Hearing impairment only 20%.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss with vestibular dysfunction in 2/2; both cochlear and vestibular disease belong to the ear axis.
Nonsyndromic progressive hearing impairment in 19/19; no other organ involvement established.
ATP synthase metabolic defect; encephalopathy/neuropathy, cardiomyopathy and muscle weakness each 30-79%; respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
NLRC4 autoinflammation with enterocolitis and macrophage activation/cytopenias; alveolar hemorrhage 1/3; meningitis 1/3 omitted by cap.
Microcephaly with primordial dwarfism/slender-bone skeletal disorder; restrictive cardiomyopathy and subglottic stenosis each occur in 1/2 patients. Frequency estimates are fragile.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the explicit primordial dwarfism/slender-bone disorder ancestry supports defining skeletal disease; metaphyseal sclerosis occurs in 1/2.

basis: Skeletal muscular dystrophy; cardiac dysfunction is frequent (30-79%; reduced contractility in 3/4 children). Reduced vital capacity reflects respiratory muscle weakness, not lung injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: HPO 30-79%; reduced contractility in 3/4 children confirms direct cardiac dysfunction. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4582941/)

basis: Degenerative pontocerebellar disease causes ataxia and pyramidal signs; gaze abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Hereditary episodic ataxia; weakness and abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than muscle or ocular tissue disease.
KCNB1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; no evidence of a separate metabolic disorder or direct muscle damage.
Congenital abnormal motor pathway control produces involuntary mirror movements; there is no primary skeletal muscle disease.
Inherited disseminated actinic porokeratosis affects skin keratinization.
Complete or partial gonadal dysgenesis compromises testicular endocrine function; the cardiac ancestry and gene alone do not establish cardiac involvement.
Autoinflammatory skin and bowel disease defines it; structural aortic coarctation and hypertension occur in 1/1 annotated patient, supporting cardiovascular involvement with limited precision.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: coarctation and hypertension are documented in 1/1; the supplied frequency supports inclusion, although a singleton gives uncertain population frequency.

basis: SETBP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder; visual impairment occurs in 14/29 (~48%), hypermetropia in 9/29 (~31%) and ptosis in 3/4.
Inherited retinal dysfunction with visual loss and optic disc pallor; retinal ganglion cells and optic disc belong to the ocular axis.
Congenital brain growth disorder with microcephaly and intellectual disability in 10/10 patients.
Hearing and visual impairment each affect 9/11; muscle atrophy affects 8/11. Respiratory failure reflects neuromuscular dysfunction rather than direct lung injury.
Defined by intellectual disability, speech delay and developmental dysfunction; hypotonia does not independently establish muscle disease.
Defining anemia, B-cell deficiency and developmental delay; renal tubular dysfunction 7/9, nephrocalcinosis 3/7. Retinal dystrophy 3/6, deafness 5/11 and lactic acidosis 3/4 omitted by cap.
Genetic type 2 diabetes; retinopathy, nephropathy and vascular complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Muscular dystrophy caused by an inherited dystroglycan glycosylation disorder; borderline intellectual disability in 2/2 patients supports neurologic involvement.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: established defective alpha-dystroglycan O-glycosylation is an inborn metabolic disorder, supported by the disease ancestry.

basis: Ketone transport/metabolism disorder with ketoacidosis in 9/9; intellectual disability in 3/9 supports neurologic involvement.
BCL10-related combined immunodeficiency; infectious encephalitis is a separate infection; colitis in one case does not establish direct immune-mediated gut damage.
Hereditary keratoderma with hair and nail abnormalities; the definition explicitly states cardiomyopathy is absent.
Immune dysregulation with lymphopenia and autoimmune cytopenias; inflammatory dermatitis 30-79%. Direct intestinal lesions and bronchiectasis are annotated at 5-29%; diarrhea alone is insufficient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea occurs in 30-79%, but documented colorectal infiltration, colitis and atrophic gastritis are each 5-29%; common direct intestinal damage is not established by these HPO data.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: atopic dermatitis is annotated in 30-79%; persistent inflammatory skin disease in this immune dysregulation syndrome qualifies beyond a transient rash.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, cataracts and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Dental malocclusion occurs in 3/3; brachydactyly in 30-79%. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: brachydactyly occurs in 30-79%, supporting congenital skeletal involvement; short stature alone does not establish a primary skeletal disorder.

basis: Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; developmental delay, brain cysts and muscle weakness occur in the reported patient (1/1). Isolated hypermetropia lacks evidence of direct ocular injury.
Multiple endocrine deficiencies and polyneuropathy define the syndrome; progressive hearing impairment and alopecia each occur in 30-79%.
Inherited autoinflammatory disease; episodic urticaria, fever and arthralgia do not establish lasting skin or joint damage.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay in 8/8; seizures in 5/8. Ocular and skeletal abnormalities are below 30%.
Disease of atrial cardiac electrical conduction; associated cardiomyopathy remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Inherited early macular degeneration with visual loss; FBN2 alone does not establish systemic connective-tissue disease.
Congenital cerebellar maldevelopment defines the disease; structural distal thumb phalanx abnormalities are annotated frequent (30-79%). Oculomotor findings reflect neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal thumb phalanx malformation is direct skeletal involvement and is annotated frequent (30-79%); hypotonia alone would not qualify.

basis: Sensorineural deafness and ovarian endocrine failure define Perrault syndrome; ataxia and axonal neuropathy affect most reported TWNK cases.
GRIN2B-related developmental encephalopathy with infantile spasms, severe developmental delay and absent speech.
CNS hypomyelination with developmental impairment and motor dysfunction; nystagmus reflects neurologic disease rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Digital skeletal defects and cleft palate/glossoptosis define disease; ventricular septal defects occur in 30-79%. Chronic otitis media is a separately diagnosed secondary disease.

decisions.otologic: none: chronic otitis media occurs in 30-79%, but is a separate secondary disease associated with palatal dysfunction, rather than intrinsic ear damage from the syndrome.

basis: Inherited macular dystrophy with vitelliform lesions and reduced visual acuity.
Inherited macular retinal dystrophy with reduced visual acuity in 8/8 patients.
Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; definition explicitly specifies chondrodysplasia despite absent skeletal HPO findings. Severe CNS disease in 3/3; cataracts in 2/3 (~67%).

decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts cause intrinsic lens dysfunction in 2/3 (~67%); three defining axes already occupy the primary cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the supplied definition explicitly specifies rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata, reinforced by skeletal-dysplasia ancestry; skeletal HPO support is absent.

basis: Axonal peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle weakness reflects denervation, while scoliosis and talipes occur in only 5-29%.
Neurodevelopmental encephalopathy; neonatal central respiratory dysfunction and feeding difficulty do not establish intrinsic lung or gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency in 21/21 is due to muscle weakness, without intrinsic lung damage. Ophthalmoplegia is 6/21.
Familial aortic aneurysm/dissection; dural ectasia (3/4) lacks documented neural dysfunction, and arachnodactyly (2/6) alone does not establish locomotor damage.
Macular cone dystrophy causes central visual loss in 6/6. MFSD8 association alone does not establish a neurologic storage disorder in this phenotype.
Microcephaly and chorioretinopathy define the syndrome; intellectual disability occurs in 7/7. Genetic retinal disease does not establish an immune mechanism.
Inherited epilepsy with febrile and afebrile seizures; additional developmental manifestations remain neurologic.
Inherited platelet-number and function disorder; epistaxis and hematomas are bleeding manifestations rather than intrinsic airway or skin disease.
Ovarian endocrine failure causes low estradiol and elevated FSH; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation do not establish skeletal damage.
Progressive myoclonic epilepsy with seizures, myoclonus and frequent cognitive deterioration; manifestations are neurological.
Retinal degeneration and obesity define the syndrome; supplied phenotypes confirm both in the reported patient.
Syndrome defined by diabetes, central/peripheral neurodegeneration and sensorineural hearing loss, each reported in 5/5; autoimmune mechanism is not established.
FMN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 5/5. Mitral valve prolapse in 1/5 does not meet threshold.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; cardiomyopathy 80-99%, developmental delay 4/12; hypotonia 4/12 with COX-negative muscle fibers 4/4 supports direct muscle dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: COX-negative muscle fibers in 4/4 tested plus hypotonia in 4/12 support direct mitochondrial muscle dysfunction at approximately the 30% threshold.

basis: Disordered glycogen metabolism causes polyglucosan accumulation and weakness in skeletal muscle.
Progeroid lipodystrophy and skeletal abnormalities; muscle atrophy 2/2; cataract 1/3 (~33%); hepatocellular carcinoma is a separately diagnosed predisposed malignancy.
Atrial conduction dysfunction and chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction define the syndrome; both present in 17/17.
Cerebellar and dental malformations define the syndrome; scoliosis and slender long bones occur in 6/6. Sparse hair alone does not establish functional skin damage.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; optic disc pallor in 1/3 supports ocular damage near the threshold. Nystagmus and oculomotor apraxia are neurologic.
Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; muscle wasting is secondary to denervation. Associated frontotemporal dementia remains within the neurological axis.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder causing skeletal myopathy. Restrictive ventilation reflects muscle weakness without established direct lung disease.
Severe developmental epileptic encephalopathy; abnormal electroretinogram indicates retinal dysfunction in 7/17 (~41%); optic atrophy alone is below 30%.
Congenital cerebral malformation with microcephaly, abnormal cortical development, developmental impairment and seizures.
Inherited abnormal proinsulin processing or secretion; no other organ damage established.
Inherited platelet production disorder with lifelong thrombocytopenia and macrocytosis; malignancy predisposition adds no organ axis.
Inherited renal tubulointerstitial disease; cholestasis in 2/2 and hepatic fibrosis or ductal abnormalities in 1/2 support direct hepatic involvement.
Congenital cranial dysinnervation causes restricted ocular movement and ptosis; affected extraocular muscles belong to the ocular apparatus.

decisions.neurologic: primary: CFEOM5 is a congenital cranial dysinnervation disorder; abnormal motor innervation is intrinsic to the ocular motility disease.

basis: Genetic podocyte/glomerular disease with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; no immune mechanism established.
Inherited dental enamel formation disorder; teeth and dental malocclusion fall within the gastrointestinal axis.
Temple syndrome features motor developmental delay, precocious puberty and obesity. Joint hypermobility (12/19) lacks documented tissue damage; scoliosis occurs in 7/30 (<30%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypermobility in 12/19 establishes laxity without demonstrated joint damage or functional loss; scoliosis in 7/30 is below threshold.

basis: Neuromuscular junction disease within ALG14 glycosylation disorders; multiple joint contractures in 6/7 support musculoskeletal involvement; ptosis only 1/7.
Glycosylation disorder affecting neuromuscular transmission; intrinsic muscle pathology and knee contractures in 3/5 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Bone fragility defines OI16; tooth agenesis and prolonged bleeding time each reported in 1/1 assessed. Hearing loss lacks frequency evidence; blue sclerae are non-damaging.
Ceramide synthesis disorder causing progressive epilepsy and neurodegeneration; nystagmus alone does not establish direct ocular damage.
Calsequestrin-containing inclusions directly affect skeletal muscle; myopathy occurs in 80-99%; no separate neural or systemic metabolic dysfunction is established.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease; abnormal muscle fibers 2/2, muscle atrophy 1/2, intellectual disability/seizures 1/2. Hearing-loss frequency is insufficiently established.

decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment is reported without frequency; a ≥30% rate in syndromic COXPD24 is not established by the supplied evidence.

basis: Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder causing ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac arrest; no defining extracardiac organ disease.
Congenital contractures and arthrogryposis occur in 3/3. An absent fetal stomach bubble does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage; no neural lesion is documented.
Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder with prolonged QT and ventricular arrhythmias; seizures are uncommon and may reflect arrhythmic syncope.
Skeletal growth disorder with proportionate short stature; no evidence of endocrine gland disease.
Defining brain malformations, renal/ureteral agenesis or hypoplasia, and generalized arthrogryposis; reproductive malformations have no axis.
Noninflammatory generalized skin scaling and superficial peeling; no immune mechanism or other organ damage established.
Contractures and neurodevelopmental impairment define CLIFAHDD; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Constipation/reflux lack evidence of direct bowel injury; breathing abnormalities may be central.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation (5/6) and reflux (9/11) do not establish direct intestinal injury or primary dysmotility; reflux is also a separate diagnosis.
decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus is frequent (30-79%) and represents persistent ocular alignment dysfunction.

basis: Cerebellar degeneration and peripheral neuropathy define AOA4. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic; hypercholesterolemia in 5/9 is a biochemical feature without demonstrated additional organ injury.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypercholesterolemia in 5/9 is characteristic, but does not by itself establish direct endocrine injury or a damaging metabolic disorder within AOA4.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental disorder and cardiac defects; esodeviation in 4/5 supports ocular dysfunction, and limb amyotrophy in 4/5 supports muscle involvement.
Inherited amino acid transport disorder with intellectual disability and tremor; duplicated urinary anatomy lacks demonstrated functional damage; hypothyroidism is below 30%.
AMBN-related defective dental enamel formation; enamel hypoplasia and amelogenesis imperfecta occur in 4/4 patients.
Organic aciduria with universal developmental impairment and neutropenia in 80-99%; cataracts 80-99%; renal cysts/nephrocalcinosis 80-99% omitted under four-axis cap.
CoQ10 deficiency with defining encephalomyopathy and cardiomyopathy; muscle weakness 1/1 supports myopathy. Hearing loss 10/14 omitted by cap; respiratory weakness does not establish lung injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy explicitly defines the syndrome; severely reduced ventricular ejection fraction reported in 1/2.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal myopathy is part of the named phenotype; weakness 1/1 and distal arthrogryposis 2/4 support muscle involvement.
decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment 10/14 qualifies, but omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining encephalomyopathy and cardiomyopathy.

basis: Metabolic enzyme deficiency with common neurologic dysfunction (>30%); cardiomyopathy reported in 1/2 assessed patients. Cardiac frequency is uncertain because of the small sample.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 1/2 assessed patients supports inclusion under the supplied HPO evidence, with limited precision.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment and brain degeneration are common manifestations of the metabolic defect; brain atrophy is reported in 1/2.

basis: Inherited bile acid synthesis defect with hepatic fibrosis and failure; iron deficiency anemia is separate, and prolonged clotting time reflects hepatic dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic cataract; posterior subcapsular cataract in 9/9 patients.
Axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness and wasting reflect denervation rather than direct skeletal muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent muscle atrophy is downstream of peripheral nerve damage, without evidence of direct muscle or skeletal disease.

basis: Inherited transaminase deficiency causes neurodevelopmental impairment, microcephaly and spasticity. Contractures occur in 3/14, below threshold.
Pure corticospinal tract degeneration; weakness, mild atrophy and urinary dysfunction are neurologic consequences rather than direct muscle or urinary tract disease.
Congenital arthrogryposis with defining hypomyelinating neuropathy, paralysis and fetal akinesia.
Hypomyelinating neuropathy and congenital joint contractures define the syndrome. Vocal cord paralysis causes laryngeal functional loss in 1/1 assessed patient; evidence is sparse.
Isolated optic atrophy with visual loss in 2/2; explicitly classified as mitochondrial disease, reflecting an inherited mitochondrial metabolic defect.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an inherited mitochondrial metabolic disorder, supported by its mitochondrial-disease ancestry, despite its isolated ocular presentation.

basis: Syndrome combines cerebellar ataxia with sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 3/3 patients; cafe-au-lait pigmentation does not establish skin damage.
Bone fragility and craniosynostosis define the disorder; hydrocephalus occurs in 5/6 (~83%). Proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
Skin peeling, nail abnormalities, keratoses and cheilitis define PLACK. Cheilitis occurs in 2-3/4 and oral leukoplakia in 2/4.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cheilitis is explicitly part of the syndrome's defining name; associated oral leukoplakia occurs in 2/4 patients.

basis: Interferonopathy with acro-osteolysis and defining aortic calcification (5/7); glaucoma in 10/11. Psoriasiform skin disease (7/11) omitted by cap.
Inherited lipoate metabolism defect; neurologic regression, white-matter disease and cerebellar atrophy in reported cases (1/1). Hepatic and cardiovascular frequencies unclear.
Asphyxiating skeletal dysplasia defines thoracic and pulmonary disease; cerebellar malformation and tongue hamartoma each 1/2. Renal anomaly frequency is unspecified.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy includes defining pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory insufficiency.

basis: Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction; weakness, feeding difficulty and ptosis reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission.
Nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy define Senior-Loken syndrome; structural intrahepatic bile duct disease occurs in 4/6. Pancreatic cysts and polydactyly each occur in 1/4.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with microcephaly; skeletal and ocular abnormalities each occur in only 1/6.
Inherited neuromuscular junction defect; direct endplate myopathy with muscle atrophy, fiber abnormalities and contractures is reported in 1/1.
Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction; respiratory and feeding impairment reflect muscle activation failure rather than lung or gut damage.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disease; respiratory weakness, dysphagia and ptosis do not establish separate lung, intestinal or eye injury.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction defines CMS3B. Ptosis, ophthalmoplegia and respiratory weakness reflect impaired transmission rather than intrinsic eye or lung disease.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and ophthalmoplegia in 1/1 reflect neuromuscular junction dysfunction; they do not establish direct disease of ocular structures.

basis: Inherited neuromuscular junction dysfunction; bulbar, eyelid and respiratory weakness do not establish separate organ damage.
Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction. Ophthalmoplegia and muscle weakness reflect junction dysfunction rather than separate eye or muscle disease.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction disease; ocular and generalized weakness reflect transmission failure. Scoliosis 1/2 and hyperlordosis 2/5 are secondary skeletal manifestations.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis 8/8 and ophthalmoplegia 6/6 reflect neuromuscular transmission failure, without direct disease of ocular structures.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and amyotrophy reflect neuromuscular dysfunction; scoliosis 1/2 and hyperlordosis 2/5 are secondary deformities, not direct skeletal disease.

basis: Postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; weakness and ptosis reflect transmission failure, not independent muscle or eye damage. Respiratory distress is 1/4.
Monogenic diabetes with impaired insulin secretion; diabetic organ complications are separate diseases, and antibody positivity alone does not establish autoimmunity.
Presynaptic NMJ and CNS disorder; fixed knee flexion contracture in 1/1 reported patient supports structural musculoskeletal involvement, with substantial small-sample uncertainty.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed knee flexion contracture is structural joint dysfunction, reported in 1/1 patient; weakness alone would not qualify.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; gingival overgrowth 13/15, oligodontia 3/3 and hearing loss 6/12 support involvement. Neurologic findings in 1/1 lack representative frequency.
Defining microcephaly and chorioretinal dysplasia, with developmental delay and visual impairment.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with structural skeletal involvement: rocker-bottom feet in 3/3 and hip dislocation in 2/3. No established systemic metabolic phenotype.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: AARS-related encephalopathy concerns tRNA aminoacylation; the amino-acid-transport ancestor does not establish a metabolic disorder in this concept.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no other organ involvement established.
SIK1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; respiratory distress in 3/6 does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

IRF7-related primary immunodeficiency; severe influenza susceptibility does not establish common intrinsic pulmonary damage.
DNM1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causes seizures, developmental impairment and cerebral atrophy; no established extracerebral damage.

decisions.ocular: involved: bilateral ptosis is persistent eyelid dysfunction, reported in 1/3 patients; cerebral visual impairment belongs to neurologic.

basis: Marrow failure and characteristic skin/nail/oral lesions define dyskeratosis congenita; cerebellar hypoplasia and developmental delay occurred in 4/4.
Cerebellar disease and developmental impairment define syndrome; contractures/brachydactyly in 6/7. Hearing loss 5/22 (23%) conflicts with 30-79% SNHL annotation; otologic involvement uncertain.
audit_reason: Remove otologic: the explicit hearing-impairment count is 5/22 (23%), below 30%. The conflicting 30-79% sensorineural annotation leaves common involvement unestablished; no defining hearing criterion overrides the threshold.

basis: Intellectual disability and central hypotonia define the disorder; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Unspecified eye abnormalities do not establish functional damage.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 3/3 patients.
Inherited Parkinson disease with bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor and postural instability reflects central neurodegeneration.
Developmental brain disorder; scoliosis is frequent (30-79%). Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; intrinsic ocular abnormalities are occasional.
Intellectual disability, microcephaly and strabismus define the syndrome. Feeding symptoms alone do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
KCNA2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures, developmental impairment and ataxia are neurologic.
Craniofacial dysostosis, alopecia and ear defects with hearing loss define syndrome; cleft palate affects 3/4. Eyelid coloboma and cardiac/urinary defects each occur in 1/4.
Skeletal dysplasia occurs in 80-99%; cap excludes renal anomalies (~2/3), GI dysfunction (~2/3) and hearing impairment (30-79%).
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining leukodystrophy and optic degeneration; eye-degenerative ancestry, optic atrophy in 6/6 and visual loss in 80-99% support ocular primary.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic degeneration is a defining component, supported by the eye-degenerative parent, optic atrophy in 6/6 and visual loss in 80-99%.

basis: PARN-related telomere disorder defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or marrow failure; measured pulmonary dysfunction in 8/8 patients.
Telomere disorder defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or marrow failure; pulmonary fibrosis reported in 15/20.
Retinal rod dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness; nervous-system ancestry does not establish extraocular involvement.
Photosensitive ichthyosis and abnormal brittle hair define disease; maxillary lateral incisor agenesis occurs in 1/2 reported patients.
Neurodevelopmental disease; clubfoot in 1/2 reported patients is a functional skeletal deformity. Facial dysmorphism and central hypotonia do not add organs.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: clubfoot is a functionally important structural deformity in 1/2 patients; the small sample limits confidence.

basis: Retinal degeneration defines RP71; scoliosis is documented in 1/2 patients (50%), supporting skeletal involvement, with uncertainty from the small sample.
Photosensitive brittle-hair disorder; intellectual disability 3/3, cataracts 2/3, hearing impairment 1/3. Singleton immune and GI findings have weaker support and are omitted at the cap.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: immune abnormalities and recurrent infections have singleton evidence (1/1), weaker than the retained manifestations under the four-axis cap.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment in 1/3 (~33%) meets the threshold for functional damage, although the sample is very small.

basis: Central movement disorder causing myoclonus and dystonia; blepharospasm and torticollis do not establish separate ocular or muscle disease.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder; KCND3-associated neurologic diseases are separate phenotypes.
Isolated focal hyperkeratosis of palms and soles.
Primary microcephaly with severe intellectual disability, developmental delay, cerebellar hypoplasia and seizures.
Mechanical restriction of eye movement from an abnormal superior oblique tendon sheath.
Defined by developmental impairment and epileptic encephalopathy; no independent metabolic disorder is established.
Progressive cerebellar ataxia with cerebellar vermis atrophy.
Isolated dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; laryngeal and limb contractions do not establish intrinsic airway or skeletal muscle disease.
Primary brain calcification with movement and cognitive dysfunction; no systemic metabolic disorder is established.
Autoimmune interstitial lung disease and inflammatory arthritis define the syndrome; variable renal involvement is not consistently established at >=30%.
NTHL1-related adenomatous intestinal polyposis. Associated cancers and meningiomas are separately diagnosed tumors arising through predisposition.

audit_reason: Add renal to primary: intrinsic renal tubular magnesium wasting is part of this familial hypomagnesemia syndrome. Functional tubular impairment qualifies without structural kidney injury.

basis: Defective proline biosynthesis causes hypomyelinating neurodegeneration; skeletal muscle atrophy in 4/4 patients supports musculoskeletal involvement.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: PYCR2 deficiency is an inborn defect of proline biosynthesis, warranting the metabolic mechanism axis. Retain neurologic disease and muscle atrophy documented in 4/4 patients.

basis: Generalized epilepsy with developmental impairment and cognitive regression; no other organ has qualifying common damage.
