decisions.renal: involved: perineal hypospadias affects 2/5 patients (40%) and directly malforms the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the complete/partial gonadal dysgenesis parents establish defective testicular endocrine differentiation, beyond an isolated external genital malformation.

basis: Isolated developmental eye disease with microphthalmia, anophthalmia and coloboma; the causal gene alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease; cerebellar atrophy/developmental impairment and sensorineural hearing loss each affect 2/2. Pectus alone lacks functional damage; aspiration pneumonia is secondary.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pectus carinatum in 2/2 is a structural finding without demonstrated functional damage; hypotonia does not establish direct muscle disease.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with direct T-cell depletion in 3/5 (60%). Pneumonia in 2/5 is a separate infection; thrombocytopenia and intrinsic organ lesions occur in only 1/5.

decisions.haematologic: involved: T-cell lymphopenia is a direct quantitative blood-cell deficit, reported in 3/5 (60%), exceeding the 30% threshold.

basis: Inherited marrow failure; facial palsy, hearing impairment and thumb malformations each reported in 1/2 patients. Frequencies are uncertain in this tiny cohort; AML is separate.
Temporal lobe epilepsy; auditory seizure symptoms arise centrally and do not establish ear damage.
Frontotemporal degeneration and motor neuron disease; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
TBK1-associated cortical and motor-neuron degeneration; muscle wasting and swallowing weakness result from denervation.
IL17RC immunodeficiency causes chronic candidiasis of skin, nails and oral mucosa, which are defining sites; Candida esophagitis is reported in 1/3.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosa is a defining site of chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis; esophageal candidiasis is additionally documented in 1/3.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental, cataract and skin/hair disease; ASD 2/6 (~33%). Mild toe syndactyly 3/5 and cleft palate 2/6 omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: atrial septal defect in 2/6 (~33%) is direct structural cardiac disease; retained for potential functional severity.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: toe syndactyly occurs in 3/5 but is a minor skeletal defect; more consequential cardiac disease takes the final slot.

basis: Spastic paraplegia, neuropathy and defining optic involvement; persistent distal amyotrophy and pes cavus occur in 30-79%, supporting musculoskeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal amyotrophy and structural pes cavus each occur in 30-79%; persistent tissue wasting and deformity qualify despite their neurogenic origin.

basis: Congenital immunodeficiency with defining polyclonal B-cell expansion, lymphoid hyperplasia and splenomegaly; recurrent infections do not establish lasting organ damage.
Gingival overgrowth, developmental disability and absent nails define the phenotype; sensorineural hearing loss in 1/2; kyphosis in 1/2 omitted by cap.
CAD deficiency has a defining neuro-metabolic and erythrocyte phenotype: anemia 5/5, anisopoikilocytosis 6/6. Renal tubular acidosis in one assessed patient does not establish usual prevalence.

decisions.haematologic: primary: characteristic anemia and abnormal erythrocyte morphology are cardinal features of CAD deficiency, documented in 5/5 and 6/6 respectively.

basis: Developmental disability defines disease; brachydactyly/joint hypermobility and atrial septal defect each 3/3. Hypopigmentation and constipation alone do not establish tissue damage.
Intellectual disability and microcephaly in 2/2; sensorineural hearing impairment in 1/2 supports ear involvement, with uncertainty from the small sample.
Inherited temporal lobe epilepsy; gastrointestinal and auditory auras are cerebral seizure manifestations, not damage to those organs.
Dysostosis; seizures 5/5, hearing impairment 2/2, vocal cord paralysis 2/2. Cardiovascular and renal findings from single cases omitted by cap; small samples limit certainty.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease with retinal vascular abnormalities, detachment and degeneration; no systemic vascular disease established.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with visual loss; reported additional findings remain within the ocular axis.
Skeletal muscle dystrophy with contractures and joint laxity; hypoventilation in 1/3 reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Mitochondrial myopathy with external ophthalmoplegia; cerebellar atrophy in 2/4 supports neurologic involvement; cardiac conduction abnormality in 1/4 excluded.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis and chronic sinonasal disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 5/5 annotated patients.
Defining skeletal dysplasia, CNS impairment and acanthosis; hearing loss 1/3. Heart failure/pulmonary hypertension are not established as direct syndrome damage.
NBAS-related recurrent infantile liver failure; cardiomyopathy and seizures each 1/10. Metabolic abnormalities and coagulopathy are consequences of liver failure.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly and brain hypoplasia; bilateral structural clubfoot reported in 2/3 patients.
Skin blistering and severe nail dystrophy define this subtype; muscular dystrophy is not established by its broader spectrum parent.
Sensory-autonomic neuropathy with defining sweat-function loss; corneal scarring occurs in 15/20 (75%). Recurrent skin infections are secondary.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: hypohidrosis is a named, defining loss of cutaneous sweat function, present in 9/20; its autonomic origin does not remove the skin manifestation.

basis: Severe growth restriction and skeletal dysmorphism define the phenotype. No endocrine dysfunction is established; developmental delay occurs in 1/4 (25%) and cardiac defects in 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: growth restriction and IGF2 association alone do not establish endocrine gland dysfunction or a metabolic disorder in the supplied phenotype.

basis: Joubert neurodevelopmental disorder; eye movement and breathing abnormalities reflect central dysfunction. Coloboma and hearing loss occur in fewer than 30%.
Painful axonal peripheral neuropathy with sensory loss and hyporeflexia; the NAGLU association alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
CNS hypomyelination defines disease; developmental dental abnormalities and myopia each occur in 3/8 (~38%). Endocrine involvement is not established.
Mitochondrial complex IV deficiency with defining encephalocardiomyopathy; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 2/2. Separate skeletal muscle dysfunction is not established.
Mitochondrial complex IV deficiency defining fatal cardiomyopathy and encephalopathy. Hypotonia alone does not establish direct skeletal muscle damage.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with macular atrophy and visual loss.
Congenital joint contractures define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 1/4, below the threshold.
Hereditary peripheral axonal neuropathy; optic atrophy with visual impairment occurs in 3/6 patients. Respiratory failure is very rare.
Bone fragility defines OI17; syringomyelia and intraventricular hemorrhage each reported in 1/2 patients support neurological involvement, with limited sample size.
Nonsyndromic lens cataract with visual loss; LSS causation alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
APPL1-related monogenic diabetes; separately diagnosed diabetic complications are excluded.
Isolated prelingual sensorineural hearing impairment in 6/6 patients; absent auditory responses do not establish brain disease.
Muscular dystrophy, early contractures and cardiac conduction disease define EDMD; cardiac abnormalities 30-79%. Lipid abnormalities may represent separate dyslipidemia.
ATF6-related cone/retinal disorder with impaired color vision, reduced acuity, foveal hypoplasia and macular atrophy.
MYT1L-related intellectual and developmental disability. Obesity (7/12) is separately diagnosed; singleton strabismus does not establish common ocular involvement.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity occurs in 7/12 (~58%), but is a separately diagnosed associated condition; hyperphagia alone establishes no endocrine organ injury.

basis: Brain malformations and arthrogryposis define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 2/3. Fetal pyelectasis in 2/3 does not establish renal functional damage.
Nonmedullary carcinoma originates in the thyroid endocrine gland; other reported cancers are separate diseases and each occurs in 1/4.
Nonmedullary carcinoma originating in the thyroid endocrine gland.
Congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations and retinal dystrophy define this subtype; all three systems are affected in the reported patients.
Cirrhosis, muscle weakness and spasticity each occur in 2/2. Cardiac, renal and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction each occur in 1/2 and are omitted at the four-axis cap.
Progressive epilepsy; scoliosis 2/2 and generalized amyotrophy 1/2 support musculoskeletal involvement. Microglossia lacks documented functional damage.
Microcephaly, endocrine dysfunction and primordial skeletal growth disorder define it; cardiomyopathy reported in 1/2 assessed patients; renal anomalies individually 1/5.
HGSNAT-related isolated retinal dystrophy with retinal atrophy in 6/6; the gene association alone does not establish systemic storage disease.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia and Joubert brain malformation define subtype; pulmonary hypoplasia/asphyxiation is a major feature. Retinal coloboma occurs in 2/8 (25%), below threshold.
Vertebral fusion and congenital myopathy define the syndrome; persistent ptosis occurs in 2/2. Microcephaly alone does not establish CNS damage; cardiomyopathy frequency is unknown.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly in 2/2 does not alone establish brain dysfunction; motor delay and hypotonia can be explained by the defining congenital myopathy.

basis: Telomere disorder with marrow failure (2/3); nail dystrophy and oral leukoplakia are defining dyskeratosis congenita features; common lung or liver injury is not established.
Noonan cardiac and skeletal phenotype; prolonged PT 2/2 and developmental delay 2/5 support involvement. Keratosis pilaris 3/5 omitted under the four-axis cap.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal: the genetic subtype retains Noonan's defining skeletal phenotype. Remove dermatologic under the four-axis cap; keratosis pilaris is less consequential than coagulation and neurodevelopmental dysfunction.

basis: Rod-cone retinal dystrophy defines this BBS2-related phenotype; polydactyly and obesity each occur in only 1/9 and do not justify syndromic extrapolation.
Defining cardiac/skeletal syndrome; ptosis 14/16; cutis laxa/hyperkeratosis 4/7. Coagulation findings (PTT 2/2, factor XI deficiency 1/3) omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: none: PTT prolongation 2/2 and reduced factor XI 1/3 support involvement, but omitted at cap; ocular and skin abnormalities have stronger prevalence evidence.
decisions.ocular: involved: congenital ptosis affects 14/16 (88%); eyelids belong to the ocular axis.

basis: Congenital vertebral segmentation abnormalities define the disease; spinal canal stenosis alone does not establish neurologic damage.
COFS defines cerebral, ocular and skeletal anomalies; microcephaly and arthrogryposis each 5/5. Microphthalmia is only 5-29%, but ocular disease is part of the syndrome definition.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular malformations define COFS and its syndromic-microphthalmia ancestry; the primary tier does not require microphthalmia itself to exceed 30%.

basis: Primary antibody deficiency; pneumonia in 40% represents separate infections. Chronic obstruction 20% and bronchiectasis 10% do not establish common direct lung damage.
Brain dysfunction and deafness define the syndrome; immunodeficiency 4/12 (~33%); visual loss predominantly cerebral; scoliosis and reflux <30%.
CHAMP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder; persistent ocular dysfunction includes hypermetropia in 4/4 and strabismus in 2/5; feeding symptoms alone add no gastrointestinal axis.
Neurodevelopmental, skeletal and cardiac defects define the parent syndrome; hydronephrosis/reflux occur in 30-79%. Oral/dental abnormalities omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital cardiac defects are part of the defining parent syndrome and a recognized major feature; HPO reports heart defects in 30-79%.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia affects vertebrae, epiphyses and joints; no established extra-skeletal organ damage.
P5CS metabolic deficiency causes spastic neurodevelopmental disease. Muscle atrophy (4/6) and incontinence (4/6) reflect neural dysfunction; cataract occurs in only 1/6.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting in 4/6 reflects denervation from the neurologic disease, without evidence of direct myopathy; kyphoscoliosis is occasional (5-29%).

basis: Scalp aplasia and terminal limb defects define Adams-Oliver syndrome. Cardiac defects, renal hypoplasia and hepatic fibrosis are minority findings in the supplied cohort.
Defining skeletal overgrowth/scoliosis, fragile hyperelastic skin (2/2), and white-matter lesions with neurologic impairment; proptosis alone adds no ocular damage.
Cranial suture fusion defines disease; strabismus 5/9 and ptosis 3/9 support ocular dysfunction. Brain malformations individually <30%; developmental-delay frequency unknown.
Definition specifies inherited predisposition to myeloid blood/marrow neoplasms; this does not imply an existing neoplasm or damage to other organs.

Intellectual disability, seizures, retinal and skin pigmentary disorders are explicitly definitional. Pigmentary findings are uncommon in HPO; recurrent infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.

decisions.ocular: primary: retinal pigmentary disorder is explicitly included in the disease definition; the 5-29% annotation does not exclude a definitional primary organ.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent skin pigmentation disorder is explicitly included in the disease definition, despite its low annotated frequency.

basis: Inherited peripheral neuropathy; persistent pes cavus and structural foot abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Renal failure 8/8 and retinal dystrophy 7/8 define the syndrome; developmental delay 3/8 supports neurologic involvement. Hepatic fibrosis 2/8 is below threshold.
Inherited cutaneous keratinization disorder; porokeratosis in 4/4 patients. FDPS variation alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Microcephaly, seizures and developmental impairment define the syndrome; optic atrophy in 3/4 supports ocular damage. Bronchiectasis 25%; immunodeficiency occasional.
Innate antiviral immunodeficiency; organ-specific viral infections are separate diseases. Encephalopathy is occasional; isolated ALT elevation does not establish liver damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and thoracic hypoplasia define it; quantitative IgA deficiency in 11/11 supports common humoral immune dysfunction. Pigment spots do not establish skin damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: involved: decreased IgA in 11/11 supports a common quantitative humoral immune deficit; clinical severity remains uncertain.

basis: Progressive myoclonic epilepsy with neurologic deterioration; Lafora bodies alone do not establish functional damage in other organs.
SLC12A5-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, regression and structural brain abnormalities.
ITPA-related purine metabolic disorder with epileptic encephalopathy; cataracts in 3/7 (~43%); cardiomyopathy annotated only 5-29%.
Mitochondrial optic atrophy; deafness and myopathy each 30-79%. Impaired neuromuscular transmission (30-79%) omitted at cap; neuropathy and ataxia only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: none at cap: impaired neuromuscular transmission occurs in 30-79%, but deafness and myopathy are more characteristic; neuropathy and ataxia occur in 5-29%.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an inherited mitochondrial disease affecting cellular energy metabolism.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia, retinal dystrophy and antibody deficiency define syndrome; developmental delay 5/6. Dermatitis and hypogonadism (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Developmental impairment/neuropathy; heart and renal malformations each 30-79%, strabismus 6/15 (40%). Skeletal findings omitted at cap; constipation alone lacks direct injury.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent strabismus occurs in 6/15 (40%), establishing common ocular dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy is neurogenic; frequent foot abnormalities/hypermobility are lower priority than the retained organ abnormalities under the four-axis cap.

basis: Joubert brain malformations define disease; hand/foot polydactyly reported in 1/1 patient. Hypermetropia alone does not establish ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: hypermetropia in 1/1 patient does not demonstrate ocular tissue injury or significant visual loss; nystagmus can reflect the cerebellar disorder.

basis: Serine transport disorder with defining neurodevelopmental injury; ankle contracture in 1/2 is secondary to spasticity and does not establish direct musculoskeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: ankle contracture is reported in 1/2, but reflects secondary mechanical consequences of neurologic spasticity rather than direct musculoskeletal injury.

basis: Axonal peripheral neuropathy; established skeletal deformities include pes cavus in 23/29, kyphoscoliosis in 17/29 and ankle contractures in 14/29.
IFNAR2-related immunodeficiency; reported vaccine-associated measles does not establish common direct injury to another organ.
Mitochondrial epileptic encephalopathy; hearing impairment 2/2 and progressive visual loss 30-79%. Muscle pathology (30-79%) and hepatic steatosis (1/1) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive epileptic encephalopathy is the central clinical phenotype, with myoclonus 3/3, mental deterioration 2/2 and structural brain abnormalities.

basis: Complex spastic paraplegia; optic disc pallor in 30-79% and reduced acuity in 3/3 establish ocular dysfunction. Distal amyotrophy is neurogenic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy in 3/3 reflects denervation from the neurologic disease; direct skeletal-muscle disease is not established.

basis: Congenital microcephaly with brain malformations; adducted thumbs 11/12 and knee contracture 1/2 support skeletal involvement; glaucoma 1/2 supports ocular involvement. Pigment macules are non-damaging.
Glycosylation disorder with seizures and scoliosis; renal dysfunction/proteinuria ~50%; cap omits VSD 2/3, intestinal malrotation 2/4 and strabismus 2/4.
Contractures 20/20; optic atrophy and sensorineural hearing loss each 30-79%. Neurogenic bladder (30-79%) omitted under cap; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Mitochondrial disorder with demyelinating neuropathy; progressive distal muscle atrophy and functional loss are defining and affect most. Hearing-loss prevalence is unspecified.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent distal muscle atrophy represents actual tissue and functional loss, is defining/common (>30%), and belongs to this neuropathy's course.

basis: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent foot deformities, including pes cavus and hammertoes, occur in 4/5 patients.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy affects 80-99%, with structural hand/finger contractures in 30-79%.
Inherited red-cell membrane/channel disorder causing hemolysis; splenic involvement shares the blood axis; hepatomegaly alone does not prove liver injury.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 9/9 patients.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, present in 10/10 annotated patients.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; strabismus and impaired vision occur in 30-79%. Constipation and nonspecific respiratory findings do not establish organ damage.
CHCHD2-associated neurodegenerative parkinsonism; constipation is an autonomic symptom without demonstrated separate gastrointestinal damage.
Peroxisomal metabolic skeletal dysplasia; developmental impairment, seizures and neuropathy occur in 4/4, cataracts in 4/4. Asthma is a separate disease.
Liver failure/fibrosis and cerebellar degeneration with sensorimotor neuropathy define the syndrome; muscle wasting is neurogenic, and splenomegaly alone does not establish splenic damage.
Neuromuscular-junction disorder; pectus deformity 3/3 and spinal rigidity 2/3 support structural skeletal involvement. Ptosis and respiratory weakness reflect impaired transmission.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis in 3/3 reflects neuromuscular-junction dysfunction rather than direct eyelid or ocular tissue disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent pectus deformity in 3/3 and spinal rigidity in 2/3 support substantial skeletal involvement beyond weakness.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with severe developmental impairment and cerebellar atrophy; strabismus in 7/8 and osteopenia in 2/3 support ocular and skeletal involvement.
Inherited retinal dystrophy with iris coloboma and variable cataract; all defining lesions are ocular.
Skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability define the syndrome; both documented in 5/5. Proptosis and external ear morphology do not establish functional damage.
Selective congenital absence of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; middle-ear dysfunction with persistent effusions and conductive hearing loss commonly affects >30% in primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Developmental and palatal/dental abnormalities define it; strabismus and joint/digital abnormalities each affect 2/3. Nail hypoplasia 2/3 omitted under cap.
NUP107-related nephrotic syndrome directly damages glomeruli; FSGS in 8/10. Cardiac abnormalities are very rare; other syndromic findings lack frequencies.
CoQ10 biosynthesis disorder; neuropathy and neurodevelopmental impairment occur commonly (>30%). Supplied renal, cardiac, pulmonary and hearing findings lack established frequencies.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neuropathy/neurodevelopmental impairment is common (>30%) across COQ7 deficiency; the disease is defined by CoQ10 biosynthesis deficiency rather than a required neurologic lesion.

basis: Defining congenital skin creases; intellectual disability 4/4 and callosal hypoplasia 2/2; microphthalmia 4/4; cleft palate 3/4. Ureterocele 1/4 excluded.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability 4/4 and callosal hypoplasia 2/2 establish common neurodevelopmental involvement accompanying the defining skin disorder.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia in 4/4 establishes common structural eye involvement accompanying the defining skin disorder.

basis: Hereditary essential tremor is a neurologic movement disorder; tongue tremor does not establish oral tissue damage.
Macrothrombocytopenia and neurodevelopmental disease; hearing loss and camptodactyly 2/2; ocular abnormalities (2/2) and cardiac defects (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Radioulnar fusion and marrow failure define syndrome; hearing loss 2/3; intellectual disability 1/3; cleft palate 1/3 omitted because of cap.
Defined as nonsyndromic intellectual disability; HNMT enzyme function alone does not establish a separate metabolic disorder.
Combined immunodeficiency; thrombocytopenia 4/4 and anemia 2/4 support blood involvement. Diarrhea and recurrent infections alone do not establish other organ damage.
Complex congenital heart malformations dominate MMP21-related heterotaxy; intestinal malrotation frequency is unspecified, and polysplenia need not impair function.
Retinal dystrophy, skeletal deformities/dislocations and sensorineural hearing loss each occur in 30-79%; urinary incontinence is occasional and does not establish renal damage.
Isolated inherited hair-shaft disorder with woolly, sparse and fragile hair.
Leukodystrophy, acquired microcephaly and profound developmental impairment; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular tissue damage.
Primordial skeletal growth disorder with microcephaly and developmental delay in 3/3; respiratory infections and asthma are separate diagnoses.
Cerebral small-vessel arteriopathy with defining brain infarcts and leukoencephalopathy; white-matter abnormalities 11/11 and lacunar stroke 10/11.
Inherited failure of oocyte maturation is a reproductive disorder without established endocrine dysfunction.
Joubert brain malformation and developmental impairment; retinal dysfunction suggested by abnormal electroretinogram in 1/3, at the threshold with limited data.
Cerebellar malformation and developmental delay define Joubert syndrome; cleft palate affects 1/3 patients; pituitary dysfunction frequency is unspecified.
Cleft lip and palate define the disease; lagophthalmos and lower-eyelid ectropion impair eyelid function in 2/2 patients.
MED13L syndrome is defined by neurodevelopmental impairment; cardiac defects are variable and listed below 30%; facial and oral dysmorphism alone is not organ damage.
Hereditary susceptibility to neuroblastoma, a sympathetic neural tumour; the defining target axis is neurologic, without assuming existing tumour or additional damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; myopathy affects most reported cases and severe cardiac failure approximately a third; estimates derive from a very small series.
Cerebellar degeneration and ataxia define SCA42; dysphagia, urgency and abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than separate organ damage.
UNC80 encephalopathy causes profound developmental impairment and central hypotonia; esotropia affects 3/4 patients. Contractures and scoliosis are occasional.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus affects 30-79%, supporting ocular dysfunction. Optic atrophy and skeletal abnormalities individually occur in fewer than 30%.
REST-associated Wilms tumor originates in the kidney; the definition specifies the tumor rather than susceptibility alone.
GPI-anchor disorder with developmental disability; skeletal defects and cataracts each 2/2. Lung disease 1/2 omitted at cap; renal echogenicity alone does not prove dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: osteopenia, hip dysplasia, shortened distal phalanges and contractures occur in 2/2, supporting skeletal damage accompanying the metabolic/neurodevelopmental syndrome.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with severe neurodegeneration; retinopathy/optic neuropathy and gastrointestinal dysmotility requiring tube feeding each occur in 80-99%.
Skeletal muscular dystrophy and cardiac conduction disease define the syndrome; atrioventricular block reported in 3/3.
Congenital myopathy, developmental delay and cardiac septal defects define the syndrome; congenital strabismus is a defining ocular feature.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and impaired glucose regulation define the disorder; quantified renal and hearing abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Defining intellectual disability, callosal agenesis and cerebellar abnormalities; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Hirsutism and facial features do not establish skin damage.
Progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy and dilated cardiomyopathy are defining manifestations.
Glycosylation disorder; hepatic injury in 5/5 and liver failure in 2/5; developmental delay in 3/4 supports neurologic involvement.
Glycosylation disorder with hepatic steatosis in 5/5 and fibrosis in 5/7; elevated CK alone does not establish muscle damage.
SETD2-related neurodevelopmental syndrome with developmental delay and intellectual disability; overgrowth alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Metabolic bone disease with disordered remodeling, fractures and osteoarthritis. Renal and cardiovascular findings are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: Paget disease is a metabolic bone disorder, explicitly supported by its ancestry; the metabolic mechanism axis accompanies the skeletal location.

basis: Sterol biosynthesis defect with defining microcephaly, developmental impairment and cataract; dermatitis/ichthyosis in 1/1. Skeletal maturation abnormalities omitted by cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: congenital/developmental cataract is a defining feature, reported in 1/1 annotated patients.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: defining psoriasiform dermatitis and ichthyosis occur in 1/1; assigned here because primary is capped at three axes.

basis: Patellar aplasia and microtia define it; speech/motor delay 2/3; emphysema and airway malacia 1/3 support pulmonary damage. Reflux is separately diagnosed.
Riboflavin-responsive mitochondrial metabolic myopathy; exercise intolerance and ragged-red muscle fibers establish skeletal muscle disease.
Neurodegenerative parkinsonism with dementia and neuronal loss; dysphagia and urinary incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Generalized lymphatic vessel malformation; splenomegaly (55%) lacks demonstrated splenic dysfunction. Thoracic and intestinal involvement are individually <30%.
Digital skeletal hypoplasia defines the disease; speech and language developmental delay reported in 1/2, with limited sample size.
SIPA1L3-related early-onset nonsyndromic cataract directly affects the lens.
Progressive skeletal muscle disease with atrophy, weakness and contractures; reduced reflexes do not establish peripheral nerve damage.
Skeletal dysplasia and microtia define it; anal atresia and ASD each occur in 2/3. Skin aplasia (2/3), brain and urinary anomalies (~1/3) omitted by cap.
Cowden mucocutaneous and gastrointestinal hamartomas are defining; thyroid disease is a core syndrome manifestation, with papillary thyroid carcinoma in 6/7 reported cases.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: thyroid neoplasia is a defining Cowden manifestation and particularly prominent in this subtype, with papillary thyroid carcinoma in 6/7 supplied cases.

basis: Lipoate biosynthesis defect with hyperglycinemia and progressive spastic CNS disease; optic atrophy and visual impairment occur in 30-79%. Cardiac hypertrophy is very rare.
Inherited mitochondrial iron-sulfur metabolism defect causing sideroblastic anemia; hepatic iron deposition alone is insufficient, and cirrhosis is 5-29%.
Defining neurodevelopmental disorder; ocular dysfunction, including strabismus and refractive abnormalities, affects roughly half or more. Hypotonia alone adds no muscle axis.
Motor neuron disease with congenital fractures and contractures; cardiomyopathy 2/4, patent ductus 3/4; pulmonary hypoplasia 2/4.
Intestinal sodium transport dysfunction causes congenital secretory diarrhea; stool electrolyte abnormalities do not establish endocrine disease.
Defined by hereditary predisposition to marrow and blood malignancy, sometimes with cytopenias or dysplasia; listed autoimmune and skin disorders do not establish common involvement.
IKZF1-related combined immunodeficiency with B-cell deficiency and a named pancytopenic phenotype; leukemia is an uncommon separate disease.
Neurodevelopmental degeneration and visual dysfunction define the syndrome; abnormal electroretinogram 3/6; scoliosis 5/7 and gingival overgrowth 4/7 support additional involvement.
CNS hypomyelination defines disease; optic atrophy 2/6 (~33%) supports ocular damage. Contractures 2/6 reflect secondary effects of spasticity rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint contractures in 2/6 exceed the frequency threshold but arise secondarily from neurologic spasticity; direct musculoskeletal disease is not established.

basis: Inherited disorder of circadian sleep-wake regulation; associated depression is psychiatric and adds no organ axis.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability, severe in 7/7; a carbohydrate-transport ancestor does not establish a separate metabolic phenotype.
Defining limb malformations, sensorineural hearing loss in 80-99% and nail abnormalities in 30-79% establish skeletal, ear and nail axes.
Inherited podocyte disease causing steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome and glomerulosclerosis; no established immune mechanism.
Genetic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with glomerulosclerosis and possible kidney failure; no immune mechanism established.
Defining skeletal dysplasia; oral malformations include cleft palate in 75% and dental agenesis in 50%; ventricular septal defect in 50%. Eye appearance alone does not establish damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with profound encephalopathy and cardiomyopathy; optic atrophy 2/2. Muscle atrophy 1/2 and hearing impairment 1/2 omitted by cap.
Severe skeletal dysplasia with rib fractures in 20/20; pulmonary and structural CNS abnormalities lack established >=30% frequencies or clear major diagnostic status.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary hypoplasia is reported without frequency; thoracic hypoplasia and lethality alone do not establish direct lung involvement in >=30%.
decisions.neurologic: none: cerebellar hypoplasia and ventriculomegaly are reported without frequencies; >=30% direct CNS involvement or major diagnostic status is not established.

basis: Developmental delay/ID; palatal defects ~75% and congenital heart defects ~50% in deletion series ([study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30291340/)).
Neurodevelopmental and degenerative disease; osteoporosis in 9/12 and distal muscle atrophy in 8/8 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Reported phenotype centers on developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism and seizures; aniridia occurs in only 5-29%.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia; pes cavus in 5/8 and skeletal muscle atrophy in 30-79%. Bladder dysfunction occurs in fewer than 30%.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; intellectual disability in 2/5 supports neurologic involvement. Recurrent otitis in 4/5 is a separately diagnosed infection.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; intellectual disability in 3/4 and motor delay in 4/6 support common neurologic involvement.
Inherited thrombocytopenia with platelet secretion dysfunction; mucocutaneous bleeding reflects the blood disorder rather than separate organ disease.
Defining lipodystrophy affects subcutis and metabolism; marfanoid skeleton is defining. Aortic aneurysm/MVP 1/1; ocular disease 1/1 and neurologic findings omitted at cap; tiny cohort.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary because generalized loss of subcutaneous fat defines the syndrome. Remove ocular under the four-axis cap, retaining the defining axes and severe aortic involvement.

basis: PIGG-related GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with severe developmental impairment and epilepsy; joint hypermobility alone does not establish damaging musculoskeletal involvement.
Heart/brain malformations define syndrome; visual impairment and finger contractures each 1/2. Contractures affect locomotor function; cleft lip 1/2 omitted at cap. Small samples.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none at four-axis cap: cleft lip occurs in 1/2, but functionally significant ocular impairment and joint contractures take priority.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: camptodactyly in 1/2 supports structural joint involvement (~50% of assessed patients); confidence limited by the small denominator.

basis: Striatal degeneration causes chorea, parkinsonism and cognitive impairment; no additional organ involvement is established.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; lower-limb amyotrophy in 4/4 reflects denervation. Frequent direct myopathy is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: wasting is neurogenic; muscle biopsies in six patients showed no myopathic features. [Cohort study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8685631/).

basis: Inherited platelet and megakaryocyte disorder with thrombocytopenia and possible marrow fibrosis; osteoporosis is occasional (5-29%).
Coffin-Siris syndrome is defined by developmental impairment and distal phalangeal/nail hypoplasia. Other organ abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Childhood chorea, developmental delay and intellectual disability establish a neurologic disorder; involuntary movement does not imply muscle disease.
B-cell developmental immunodeficiency with reduced B-cell counts and agammaglobulinemia in 4/4; recurrent otitis is a separate infection.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defective B-cell development with reduced B-cell counts in 4/4 is a disease of blood cells as well as an immunodeficiency.

basis: Brittle hair and ichthyosis define TTD6; developmental delay in 2/2 supports neurologic involvement; microcytosis/HbA2 alone do not establish blood dysfunction.
Defined by intellectual disability and developmental impairment; seizures also fall within the neurologic axis.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with amenorrhea and elevated FSH; gonadal hormone failure belongs to the endocrine axis.
Primary ovarian insufficiency is gonadal endocrine failure; ocular annotations lack frequency evidence supporting involvement in at least 30%.
Hereditary cerebellar degeneration with ataxia, spasticity and developmental impairment; nystagmus is a central neurologic manifestation.
Inherited cerebellar ataxia, epilepsy and intellectual disability; other findings lack evidence of common direct organ damage.
Isolated spermatogenic maturation arrest and azoospermia; no endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement established.
Kyphoscoliosis 3/6, hearing impairment 30-79%, great-vessel anomalies 30-79%; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic rather than ocular.
Retinal degeneration and erythrocytic microcytosis define the syndrome; both documented in all three annotated patients.
Inherited calcium/phosphate metabolic disorder; intrinsic renal phosphate wasting and nephrocalcinosis in 15/15 establish common renal involvement.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 8/8 patients.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment in 11/11 patients.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures; strabismus affects 4/13 (~31%), supporting borderline ocular involvement. Feeding difficulties alone do not establish GI damage.
Myopathy with hypotonia 2/2; liver injury markers 2/2; polymicrogyria 1/2. Hearing loss and LV hypertrophy, each 1/2, omitted at cap; respiratory failure may be muscular.
Named neurodevelopmental syndrome with eye and heart anomalies, each frequent (30-79%); congenital urinary tract dysfunction includes vesicoureteral reflux in 3/10.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: heart anomalies are an explicitly named syndrome component; abnormal heart morphology is frequent, with VSD in 4/10.
decisions.ocular: primary: eye anomalies are an explicitly named syndrome component and frequent (30-79%), including structural ocular and optic-nerve abnormalities.

basis: HIVEP2 neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus in 3/6 and hip dysplasia in 2/4 support involvement. Reflux is separately diagnosed; skeletal estimates are small.
FRRS1L developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causes seizures, regression, intellectual disability and movement abnormalities; no separate organ damage is established.
SEC63-associated polycystic liver disease is supported by parent and hepatic cyst phenotypes; isolated kidney wording in the definition conflicts with these.

basis: Pentose phosphate metabolic defect with developmental disability and congenital heart defects; cataracts in 2/5 and uveitis in 30-79% support ocular involvement.

basis: Platelet dysfunction, immunodeficiency and severe CNS impairment define HPS10; ocular albinism/nystagmus 1/1. Pulmonary interstitial abnormality 1/1 and cutaneous albinism excluded at cap.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental disorder, dermal melanocytosis and strabismus; reduced GFR/chronic kidney disease occurs in 30-79%, supporting intrinsic renal involvement.

basis: Intellectual disability and micrognathia define the syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, crowding in 3/4. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: micrognathia is a defining mandibular skeletal abnormality explicitly named in the syndrome; scoliosis also occurs in 30-79%.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability and brain abnormalities; constipation and feeding symptoms do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Inherited mitochondrial metabolic myopathy with ophthalmoplegia and ptosis; muscle pathology in 2/2. Dysphagia reflects muscle dysfunction rather than separate GI injury.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe developmental impairment and epilepsy in 2/2, with cortical atrophy, constitute the defining clinical phenotype.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic disc pallor and retinal vessel attenuation in 1/1 assessed support ocular pathology; cerebral visual impairment alone would be neurologic.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment in 1/1 assessed, representing at least 1/2 reported cases, meets the frequency threshold.

basis: Mitochondrial/peroxisomal dysfunction causes encephalopathy; optic atrophy is frequent, with visual impairment and optic disc pallor in 3/4 patients.
Axonal neuropathy; limb amyotrophy in 3/3 and structural foot deformity in 2/3; hearing impairment in 2/3. Optic atrophy frequency is unspecified.
Short-rib skeletal dysplasia; cleft upper lip 2/3, atrioventricular canal defect 1/3, and epiglottic aplasia 1/3 support additional axes, with small denominators.
Primary microcephaly, brain malformations and developmental disability define disease; renal agenesis has no established common frequency.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis and chronic rhinosinusitis in 3/3; infertility has no covered axis.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease and bronchiectasis; chronic middle-ear inflammation occurs in 3/3 reported patients.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: vasculitis directly injures vessels and is reported in 1/3 (~33%); this meets the threshold, with substantial small-series uncertainty.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea 3/3 and chronic diarrhea 1/3 establish symptoms, but the supplied evidence does not establish direct inflammatory or structural bowel injury.

basis: Developmental disability and persistent fetal hemoglobin define the syndrome. Strabismus causes ocular dysfunction in 8/8; hypermobility in 7/8 lacks documented joint damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility in 7/8 establishes laxity, but associated instability, injury or functional loss is not documented.

basis: Callosal hypoplasia and retinal abnormalities each reported in 1/1; evidence is sparse. Respiratory distress alone does not establish direct lung damage.
Epileptic encephalopathy with amino-acid transport disorder ancestry. Nephrocalcinosis in 1/3 does not establish direct renal injury attributable to this disease.
Developmental impairment and epileptic encephalopathy occur in 5/5; nystagmus is a central motor sign without established eye damage.
Intellectual disability and renal anomalies define it; persistent neutropenia and hearing loss each 30-79%; camptodactyly omitted by cap.
Defined by serrated intestinal polyposis; subsequent cancer risk adds no other organ axis.
Inherited macular and retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy with macular atrophy and visual impairment.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures and intellectual or developmental impairment.
Structural myopathy with muscle atrophy in 4/4; global developmental delay in 1/2 supports neurologic involvement. Dysphagia alone does not establish GI injury.
Inherited epidermal disorder causing skin peeling, scaling and hyperkeratosis; scaling reported in 7/7.

Genetic focal epilepsy, sometimes with focal cortical dysplasia, is confined to the neurologic axis.
Obesity/hypogonadism, retinal dystrophy and polydactyly define the phenotype; intellectual disability in 1/2 supports neurologic involvement. Renal damage unestablished.
Joubert brain malformation and developmental impairment; retinopathy in 1/2 supports ocular damage. Renal pelvic dilation in 1/2 lacks demonstrated functional injury.
Joubert CNS malformation with developmental impairment; the ocular-defect parent and retinal disease or optic pallor in 1/2 support a defining ocular component.

decisions.ocular: primary: explicitly classified as Joubert syndrome with ocular defect; pigmentary retinopathy and optic disc pallor each occur in 1/2 reported patients.

basis: Isolated inherited retinal degeneration; POMGNT1 involvement does not imply muscular dystrophy in this concept.
ZC3H14-related nonsyndromic intellectual disability, present in 6/6; the definition does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Intellectual disability in 4/4 and developmental delay in 2/2 define neurodevelopmental involvement; hirsutism and broad halluces alone do not establish organ damage.
Oral, digital and major brain malformations characterize the reported phenotype; hydronephrosis occurred in 1/1 patient, with substantial uncertainty from the tiny cohort.
UBA5-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; developmental impairment, seizures and movement abnormalities are neurologic.
Inherited cerebellar degeneration defines the disease; cataracts directly affect the eyes in 2/2 reported patients.
Skeletal dysplasia; hearing loss 15/16, keloids 8/18 and subglottic stenosis 6/15 indicate direct involvement. Cleft palate 5/17 is below 30%.
Strabismus 55%; skeletal anomalies 83%; renal malformations 38%; cardiac defects 33% omitted by cap. [Cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34521999/)

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural joint/limb abnormalities occur in 40/48 (83%); joint hypermobility is also annotated 30-79%; this extends beyond central hypotonia.

basis: Aniridia/iris coloboma with associated ocular abnormalities; discordant cancer and renal parents are unsupported by the disease phenotype.

Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder; fixed arthrogryposis occurs in 2/5 (40%). Ophthalmoparesis, dysphagia and hypoventilation reflect neuromuscular dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and ophthalmoparesis in 5/5 reflect neuromuscular junction dysfunction, without evidence of intrinsic ocular damage.

basis: Neurodegenerative syndrome; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism in 2/2 assessed and hearing impairment in 3/9 (~33%); gaze palsy and incontinence are neurologic.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 6/6 is typically neonatal and transient, reflecting neuromuscular dysfunction rather than demonstrated lasting pulmonary injury.

basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic, without evidence of intrinsic eye damage.
Mitochondrial depletion with liver failure in 2/2; congestive heart failure in 1/2. Hepatocerebral name alone and lethargy do not establish CNS damage.
Skeletal dysplasia, developmental disability and defining obesity (4/6); renal, gastrointestinal and airway anomalies reported in single patients do not establish cohort prevalence.
Distal skeletal muscle degeneration with rimmed vacuoles and myopathic EMG; facial weakness does not independently establish peripheral nerve disease.
Developmental and cardiac defects define syndrome; hearing impairment 4/5, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism 3/4 assessed. Ocular abnormalities and cervical fusion (2/5) omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: ocular abnormalities are common, but damaging findings lack frequencies; quantified hearing and endocrine dysfunction take priority.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurs in 3/4 assessed; even with male limitation, this supports roughly 30-40% overall involvement.

basis: GRIN2D encephalopathy causes seizures and developmental impairment. Pes planus in 2/2 does not establish skeletal dysfunction; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes planus in 2/2 meets the frequency threshold but does not by itself demonstrate damaging skeletal disease; abnormal tone is neurologic.

basis: Rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; ocular and cardiac abnormalities individually reported in 1/4.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; optic disc pallor and retinal vessel attenuation each reported in 1/2 support ocular involvement. Cerebral visual impairment remains neurologic.
Inherited thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection; extra-vascular abnormalities are individually below 30%.
Defined as APC2-related non-syndromic intellectual disability; minor skeletal and facial variants do not establish additional functional organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy and extrapyramidal dysfunction define the syndrome; constipation and recurrent infections do not establish direct additional organ damage.
Developmental disability and sinus-node dysfunction define the syndrome; retinal dysfunction on ERG occurs in 30-79%, although retinal degeneration is reported in 2/9.
Defining periodontal destruction, joint hypermobility/dislocations and skin fragility; bruising reflects connective tissue fragility rather than a blood disorder.
Retinal dystrophy; ovarian insufficiency 3/5 and goiter 3/10 support endocrine involvement; intellectual disability 3/10; lung fibrosis only 1/10.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and sinus-node dysfunction (9/9); nystagmus does not establish intrinsic eye damage; reflux is a separate disorder.
Defining neurodevelopmental disease with neuropathy; optic atrophy and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each occur in 3/8. Frequent amyotrophy does not establish direct muscle disease.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining cardiomyopathy (4/7); skeletal myopathy with muscle mtDNA depletion in 5/5. Seizures 2/7 are below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal myopathy with muscle mtDNA depletion in 5/5 is common direct muscle disease; cardiomyopathy defines this named subtype.

basis: Progressive encephalopathy with edema/leukoencephalopathy defines PEBEL; both subtypes are inborn disorders of NAD(P)HX metabolite repair.

basis: Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm and infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay in 16/16, with common seizures and abnormalities of muscle tone; no independent muscle disease.
Developmental impairment 6/6; atrial septal defect and persistent ptosis each 3/6 support involvement. Hypoglycemia 3/6 lacks evidence of persistent metabolic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypoglycemia occurs in 3/6, but the supplied evidence does not establish recurrent or lasting intrinsic endocrine/metabolic dysfunction.

basis: Peripheral nodal dysfunction causes fetal akinesia and congenital joint contractures; structural pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 5/6 patients (~83%).
Neuronal heterotopia and developmental delay in 7/7; toe syndactyly in 5/7 and cleft palate in 4/7 establish common skeletal and oral malformations.

basis: Pentose metabolism defect; supplied HPO reports arthrogryposis 100%, renal dysfunction and cholestatic liver disease 30-79%; CNS and anemia findings omitted by cap.

Inherited defective dental enamel maturation; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

Inherited mitochondrial pyrophosphatase deficiency disrupts pyrophosphate metabolism and causes myocardial fibrosis with alcohol-triggered cardiac failure.

basis: Neurodegeneration with fixed pes cavus and neurogenic bladder, each 30-79%, causing skeletal deformity and urinary dysfunction. Eye movement signs reflect neurologic disease.

basis: Mitochondrial encephalocardiomyopathy; hypotonia 4/4 with muscle pathology 3/3 supports myopathy; cataract 1/3 omitted by the four-axis cap.

basis: Inherited high myopia affects the eye; retinal detachment remains within the same axis.

basis: Inherited marrow failure with anemia, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia; short stature and microcephaly alone do not establish additional organ damage.

Inherited hair-shaft disorder; the supplied juvenile cataract annotation has no frequency establishing involvement in at least 30%.
Inherited hair-shaft disorder with pili canaliculi, brittleness and uncombable hair.

basis: Defining cortical malformation and developmental impairment; talipes equinovarus in 2/6 (~33%) supports skeletal involvement; cataract in 2/8 is below threshold.

basis: Developmental delay and callosal defects define syndrome; renal dysplasia/cysts 2/3 and clubfoot 2/4. Respiratory insufficiency 3/4 lacks evidence of direct lung disease; cardiac defects each 1/4.

basis: Intellectual developmental disorder with central motor abnormalities; cardiac and structural ocular defects are reported only in some individuals.
Progressive renal tubulointerstitial disease; scoliosis is a structural skeletal manifestation in 3/8 patients (~38%).

Selective congenital absence of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with structural brain abnormalities; optic atrophy is very rare (1-4%).
Inherited mitochondrial fatty-acid/lipoic-acid biosynthesis disorder defined by dystonia, basal ganglia abnormalities and optic atrophy.
KMT2B-related neurodevelopmental dystonia; astigmatism affects 3/6 (~50%), supporting ocular functional involvement. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited pyridoxal phosphate metabolic disorder with early epilepsy and developmental impairment; respiratory insufficiency does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
KLHL24-related skin fragility with scarring and hair loss; intrinsic cardiomyopathy is reported in roughly 40%, with age-dependent expression.
Spastic paraplegia and intellectual disability define CNS disease; defining ocular findings include nystagmus 3/3 and refractive defects; syndromic obesity occurs in 3/4.
Inherited dental enamel hypoplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Glycine metabolism disorder with encephalopathy; optic atrophy occurs in 12/20 patients (60%). Contracture frequencies are unspecified.

basis: Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with visual loss; retinal vessel attenuation remains part of the ocular disease.

Inherited bile acid synthesis defect with hepatocellular injury; developmental impairment and ataxia in 1/1 annotated patient. Steatorrhea alone does not establish GI injury.
Anterior ocular segment malformation with corneal abnormalities, synechiae and developmental glaucoma.

Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and ataxia; strabismus affects 11/13. Dysphagia and facial weakness reflect neuromotor dysfunction.

basis: Hypogonadism and developmental disability predominate; skeletal and structural dental defects each 30-79%; ocular findings omitted by cap; asthma/otitis are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: extraneural perineurial differentiation does not establish origin within, occupation of, or damage to a peripheral nerve.

basis: Benign perineurial nerve-sheath neoplasm characteristically arising in dermis or subcutis; both tissue origin and anatomical site qualify.

decisions.neurologic: primary: perineurial nerve-sheath origin qualifies under tumour-origin rules; extraneural growth does not require demonstrable nerve dysfunction.

audit_reason: Remove neurologic: this extraneural subtype lacks identifiable nerve association. Perineurial differentiation alone does not establish peripheral nerve involvement; its predominant dermal and subcutaneous sites support dermatologic primary.

basis: Benign perineurial tumor arising within a peripheral nerve; associated weakness reflects nerve injury.
Cerebral vascular amyloid deposition with hemorrhagic strokes and dementia defines this disorder; no systemic organ involvement is established.
Defined by cerebral cortical malformation and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia.

basis: Intestinal lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma producing abnormal alpha heavy chains; intestinal abnormalities and malabsorption in 80-99%.
Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma producing truncated heavy chains; hepatic enlargement from infiltration and tongue neoplasm each occur in 30-79%; nonspecific rash excluded.
Inherited hypoplastic dental enamel disorder; teeth are included in the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited hypomaturation of dental enamel; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

Congenital esophageal duplication; respiratory symptoms from compression do not establish common direct airway damage.
Congenital duplication of the esophagus; respiratory symptoms and recurrent pneumonia do not establish common direct pulmonary damage.
Subcutaneous, intestinal and upper-airway edema are defining disease sites. Bradykinin-mediated C1-inhibitor deficiency is neither autoimmune disease nor immunodeficiency.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: upper-airway edema is explicitly a defining site; the exclusion for transient additional manifestations does not remove a defining disease site.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: hereditary C1-inhibitor deficiency causes bradykinin-mediated edema, without defining infection, immunodeficiency or autoimmune/immune-mediated disease.

basis: Defining bradykinin-mediated edema affects subcutis, bowel and upper airway; C1-inhibitor dysfunction does not itself establish infection, immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: upper-airway edema is explicitly part of the disease definition and can directly obstruct breathing.
