decisions.infectious_immune: none: attacks result from bradykinin excess; complement-regulator dysfunction alone does not establish an infectious, immunodeficient or immune-mediated mechanism.

basis: Anti-C1-inhibitor autoimmunity causes defining subcutaneous and bowel-wall edema; less common upper-airway attacks omitted under the primary cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: bowel-wall angioedema is a defining visceral location of the disease itself; episodic reversibility does not exclude a primary disease site.

basis: Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency defines immune-mediated subcutaneous angioedema. Reversible bowel and airway edema does not establish lasting extra-cutaneous damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: episodic upper-airway edema can be severe but does not establish lasting airway damage; transient swelling is excluded.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: recurrent bowel-wall edema is reversible; abdominal attacks do not establish persistent gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Subcutaneous, oral/visceral and upper-airway edema are defining disease sites. Bradykinin-mediated RAAS-blocker angioedema is not inherently immune-mediated.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: upper-airway edema is explicitly a defining disease location; the 5-29% obstruction frequency does not exclude a primary site.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral tissues and viscera are disease sites; tongue and lip edema are annotated at 30-79%. Transience does not exclude the disease's primary location.

basis: Frontotemporal neurodegeneration causes progressive aphasia, agrammatism and speech apraxia.
Growth and skeletal abnormalities anchor the variable phenotype. Intellectual disability, hearing loss, ocular and cardiac defects are each 5-29%; pinna dysmorphism alone is insufficient.
Brachial plexus compression defines neurogenic TOS; rib anomalies predispose to compression, while pain alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor arising in the stomach; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Tumor originates in the duodenum. Neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish a functional endocrine disorder.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in the jejunum; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Ileal tumor; extrahepatic cholestasis and arterial occlusion each reported in 30-79%, supporting biliary and vascular damage; flushing is transient and anemia separately coded.
Tumor originates in the appendix; neuroendocrine differentiation alone adds no endocrine axis. Hepatic and cardiac involvement are minority findings.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in the colon; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Tumor originates in rectal mucosa; neuroendocrine differentiation alone adds no endocrine axis. Pulmonary carcinoid is a separate tumor; carcinoid complications are rare.
Tumor originates in anal canal. Liver findings lack established infiltration or functional damage; pulmonary carcinoid is a separate tumor. Carcinoid syndrome is very rare.
Tumor originates in the larynx, an airway site; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Neuroendocrine tumour originates in the middle ear; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Carcinoma originates in liver; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease. Other frequent findings are symptoms, not organ injury.
Benign or malignant neoplasm originating in the thyroid, an endocrine gland.
Carcinoma originates in the thyroid endocrine gland; metastatic organ involvement is not universal.
Umbrella for multiple endocrine gland tumors; additional tumor sites depend on the constituent syndrome.
Alopecia and antibody deficiency define the syndrome; common respiratory infections are separate infections, without documented chronic pulmonary damage.
Paralysis originates in ocular motor nuclei or cranial nerves; impaired eye movements alone do not establish intrinsic ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: the lesion is in ocular motor nuclei or nerves; eye movement dysfunction does not independently establish disease of the eye.

basis: Originally delineated through developmental delay, supporting a neurologic assignment. Phenotype remains uncertain; delay is annotated in only 5-29%, and no other organ damage is established.
Congenital ichthyosis; supplied HPO reports digit autoamputation and ectropion each in 30-79%, supporting limb loss and eyelid dysfunction.
Craniosynostosis and thoracic skeletal dysplasia define the syndrome; mechanical chest restriction alone does not establish direct lung damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: direct pulmonary hypoplasia or injury is unestablished; asphyxiating chest restriction alone is insufficient. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/100978)

basis: Hereditary degeneration of motor pathways causes spastic paraplegia; additional organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
P5CS-related metabolic spastic paraplegia. Cataracts vary by pedigree; early cataracts reported in 2/15 dominant cases in one series do not establish >=30% across the umbrella.

decisions.ocular: none: early cataracts reported in 2/15 dominant cases; not obligatory across SPG9. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4553756/).

basis: Congenital defect of the oral hard palate; hearing impairment is 5-29%. Associated sleep apnea is a separately diagnosed condition.
A neuronal migration disorder with subcortical heterotopia and frequent epilepsy; spasticity and weakness reflect central neurologic dysfunction.
Neuronal migration malformation; associated skull/ethmoid bone defects and encephaloceles are frequent (30-79%) in supplied phenotypes.
Anterior segment dysgenesis with Peters anomaly and cataract; both defining abnormalities affect the eye.
Inherited quantitative fibrinogen deficiency is a coagulation disorder; mucosal bleeding does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal or airway damage.
Congenital dysplasia of the aortic valve causing valvular stenosis.
Congenital cerebral cortical malformation causing common developmental impairment, seizures and hemiparesis; no additional organ damage established.
Aregenerative anemia classified under myelodysplastic syndrome; blood and marrow disease.
Facial nerve synkinesis produces involuntary eyelid closure during jaw movement; nerve dysfunction and abnormal eyelid function define the syndrome.
Nonsecretory neuroendocrine tumour arising in carotid body paraganglia; proximity to the carotid artery does not establish vascular damage.
Congenital cardiac malformation; bronchial compression and bronchomalacia cause respiratory impairment in a substantial proportion (~50% or more).
Hepatic porphyrin metabolism disorder defined by bullous photodermatitis and skin fragility; associated infections and other diseases do not add axes.
Congenital structural abnormality of the mitral valve's subvalvular apparatus.
Umbrella disease of multiple endocrine glands; autoimmunity and extraendocrine injury are not established across the group.
Deficiency of pituitary hormone production defines an endocrine disorder.
Primary failure of adrenal hormone production; autoimmune causation does not apply to every subtype.
Chronic adrenal cortical hormone deficiency; autoimmune disease is only one subtype. Pigmentation and electrolyte changes do not establish other organ damage.
Combined immunodeficiency intrinsically impairs T- and B-lymphocyte function, satisfying immune and blood-cell axes; infections are separate diseases and other organ damage varies across subtypes.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the definition specifies intrinsic dysfunction of blood lymphocytes. The blood-cell disease rule does not require reduced cell counts.

basis: Congenital neutrophil deficiency causes impaired innate immunity; additional organ damage varies across the umbrella's subtypes.
Autoinflammatory periodic fever umbrella; fever alone does not establish damage to another organ.
Progressive cerebral neurodegeneration with dementia and cortical atrophy; occasional visual findings do not establish common ocular damage.
Classic lissencephaly is a congenital cerebral cortical malformation; additional organs affected in particular syndromic subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Umbrella of congenital cortical malformations with lissencephaly; additional skeletal or systemic findings depend on subtype.
Uncomplicated hereditary corticospinal tract degeneration; spasticity and weakness reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Hereditary corticospinal degeneration defines this umbrella; additional organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Inherited dystrophic degeneration of skeletal muscle; cardiac and respiratory involvement varies across dominant subtypes and is not established for most of the umbrella.
Inherited skeletal muscle degeneration; cardiac and respiratory involvement varies across subtypes and is not established in most patients.
HHV-8-associated neoplastic disorders share a viral mechanism; skin, lymphoid and serosal sites differ across subtypes.
Autoinflammatory periodic fever syndrome; recurrent fever alone does not establish damage to another organ.
Intellectual disability defines this umbrella; other congenital anomalies vary across its many subtypes.
Heterogeneous congenital syndrome umbrella characterized by variable intellectual disability; no additional organ lesion is established across most subtypes.
Myeloid neoplasia with marrow dysplasia, failure and cytopenias; infections are secondary complications.
Therapy-related myeloid neoplasm directly affects marrow and blood-cell production; extramedullary damage is not established as common.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a blood and marrow neoplasm; this translocation does not establish common damage to another axis.
Constricting skin bands and limb disruption define the syndrome. Hydrocephalus is annotated frequent (30-79%); other visceral defects are minority findings.
Congenital multiple joint contractures with muscle weakness/fibrosis define this umbrella; neurologic causes vary across subtypes.
Intestinal carbohydrate-digestion enzyme deficiency causing malabsorption and chronic diarrheal disease.
Congenital intestinal sodium-transport dysfunction causes severe diarrhea with defining hyponatremia and metabolic acidosis.
Enterocyte defect causes severe protein-losing enteropathy and secretory diarrhea. Hypoalbuminemia and edema reflect enteric loss, not hepatic or renal injury.
Autoimmune injury of intestinal mucosa defines this enteropathy.
Autoimmune inflammation of the exocrine pancreas; extra-pancreatic involvement varies by subtype, and diabetes is a separate disease.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease with unclassifiable intestinal inflammation.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia with limb shortening, bowing, osteopenia and joint stiffness.
Insufficient functional small intestine causes intestinal failure and malabsorption. Nutritional consequences do not establish a separate primary metabolic disorder.
Multiple intestinal polyps define the syndrome; extraintestinal findings vary among subtypes and do not apply across the umbrella.
Intestinal smooth muscle dysfunction causes chronic pseudoobstruction; visceral smooth muscle belongs to the affected intestinal organ.
Defined by severe fetal fluid accumulation involving subcutis and pleural/pericardial spaces; underlying immune and blood disorders are subtype-specific.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pleural fluid accumulation is a defining diagnostic manifestation; pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: pathological subcutaneous edema is a defining manifestation of fetal anasarca.

basis: Disordered erythropoiesis with marrow ring sideroblasts; syndromic organ abnormalities and systemic iron injury are not universal across this umbrella.
Congenital urethral obstruction directly affects the urinary tract and renal function. Recurrent urinary infections are separate diseases.
Defining cerebral venous arteriovenous malformation; venous hypertension produces hydrocephalus and cerebral dysfunction in roughly 30-50% over the disease course.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral venous hypertension causes hydrocephalus and associated brain dysfunction in roughly 30-50%; intracranial location alone is insufficient.

basis: Aortic sinus aneurysm and associated regurgitation are cardiovascular; stroke is very rare and dyspnea does not establish pulmonary damage.
Defined by aniridia and other ocular malformations, intellectual disability and familial obesity; cardiac and hair abnormalities are annotated as occasional.
Aniridia, cataracts, lens dislocation and optic nerve hypoplasia accompany defining intellectual disability; each is annotated at 80-99%.
Anisakis larvae infect and penetrate the gastrointestinal wall, causing local inflammation and eosinophilic granulomas.
Defining eyelid fusion and anal atresia; tooth agenesis also supports gastrointestinal involvement. Additional CNS anomalies are not established as common.
Congenital structural abnormality of the coronary arteries.
Congenital cerebral cortical malformation with severe microcephaly, developmental impairment and seizures.
Cerebral cortical malformation with developmental impairment and seizures; feeding difficulty does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital heart defects and short stature with craniofacial skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; intellectual disability frequency is unclear.
Umbrella for congenital multiple joint contracture syndromes; neurologic and other organ abnormalities vary by subtype.
Characteristic neurodevelopmental impairment; radioulnar synostosis, finger contractures and strabismus each occur in 30-79%. Cardiac defects and delayed puberty occur in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: associated structural skeletal abnormalities, including radioulnar synostosis and finger contractures, occur in 30-79%.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and neurodevelopmental impairment define BBS; CKD 30-79%; skeletal and dental abnormalities omitted because of cap.
Defined by major ocular malformations, cardiac valve disease and skeletal/muscular abnormalities; external ear morphology alone does not establish ear dysfunction.
Renal tubular salt wasting with defining hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis; hearing loss is limited to particular subtypes.
Congenital skeletal malformation involving radial deficiency and tibial hypoplasia.
Defining short terminal phalanges, sensorineural deafness and intellectual disability; reproductive anomalies have no axis.
Skeletal malformations and intellectual disability define syndrome; epiglottic aplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Feeding difficulty alone adds no gastrointestinal axis.
Intellectual disability and pronounced arachnodactyly define the syndrome; genital abnormalities lack an axis, and facial appearance alone adds no damaged organ.
Congenital aortic arch abnormalities; airway or oesophageal compression affects selected subtypes rather than most patients across the group.
Congenital absence of nasal structures/airways; microphthalmia or eyelid coloboma and microtia each occur at 30-79%; olfactory defects lack frequency evidence.
Congenital abnormal origin of a major artery; airway effects are subtype dependent.
Congenital distal joint contractures and deformities of the hands and feet define the disorder.
Congenital lifelong joint contractures with skeletal deformities and localized muscle atrophy; no common independent nerve damage established.
Aspergillus hypersensitivity causes bronchopulmonary inflammation and bronchiectasis; cortical atrophy annotation does not represent characteristic direct ABPA damage.
Cerebellar and spinal cord degeneration or abnormal development define this neurologic umbrella; other organ disease varies by subtype.
Immune-mediated neurologic syndrome; opsoclonus reflects disordered central eye-movement control, not ocular damage. Associated cancers are separate diseases.
Defining ataxia, photosensitive skin and skeletal growth anomalies; cardiac/aortic valve anomalies 30-79%; ocular and dental anomalies 30-79% omitted at cap.
Congenital complete atresia of the mitral valve.
Bulbospinal degeneration with defining external ophthalmoplegia, pupillary dysfunction and deafness. Muscle wasting is neurogenic; intrinsic muscle disease is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscular atrophy results from motor-neuron degeneration and denervation; no separate direct skeletal-muscle pathology is established.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome historically named for microphthalmia; ocular malformations occur in 30-79%. Scoliosis and hypodontia each occur in 80-99%.

decisions.ocular: primary: microphthalmia is a defining feature in the historical syndrome name; microphthalmia and iris coloboma are annotated in 30-79%.

basis: Congenital erythroid marrow failure defines the disease; specific skeletal, cardiac, renal and neurologic abnormalities are generally below 30%.
Parasitic infection; intestinal and urinary injury varies by species and stage, with no established >=30% damaging organ manifestation across the umbrella.

decisions.renal: none: urinary inflammation and scarring characterize particular species/forms; damaging urinary disease in >=30% across this umbrella is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal injury is species-dependent; damage in >=30% across all schistosomiasis, including asymptomatic infections, is not established.

basis: Defining blepharoptosis affects eyelids, cleft palate and dental anomalies affect the oral apparatus, and ectrodactyly affects the skeleton.
Sinoatrial conduction block is a cardiac rhythm disorder.
Skeletal abnormalities, intellectual disability and cardiac defects define the syndrome; tooth agenesis occurs in 80-99%, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Intestinal tapeworm infection; clinically significant B12-deficiency anemia occurs in a small minority, approximately 2%, and is separately diagnosed.
Scarring alopecia affects scalp hair follicles and skin; no established systemic involvement.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by vertebral flattening, short trunk and scoliosis across the group.
Cardiac channelopathy defined by characteristic ECG changes and susceptibility to ventricular arrhythmias.
Idiopathic organizing injury of pulmonary airspaces causes consolidation and restrictive dysfunction; infection or an autoimmune cause is not established.
Irreversible fibrosing bronchiolar obstruction defines disease; the predominant chronic lung-allograft form involves alloimmune injury. Associated infections are separate diseases.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: the definition identifies chronic lung-allograft dysfunction as the predominant setting, supporting alloimmune disease across most cases despite non-transplant forms.

basis: Digital malformations, microcephaly and characteristic gastrointestinal atresias define syndrome; atresia is variable and absent in the rare type 2.
Congenital renal collecting-duct ectasia; distal renal tubular acidosis is separately diagnosed despite its 30-79% annotation. Urinary infections are separate complications.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: distal renal tubular acidosis is a separately diagnosed associated disorder; hypercalciuria alone does not establish additional endocrine or metabolic damage

basis: Thalamic neuronal injury defines disease. Arrhythmia is reported in 30-79%, but intrinsic or sustained cardiac injury is unestablished; respiratory insufficiency does not establish lung damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: arrhythmia occurs in 30-79%, but the record does not establish direct cardiac damage or persistent cardiac dysfunction.

basis: Inherited drug-metabolism enzyme deficiency; apnea follows anesthetic exposure and does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Defined by fatty degeneration of paraspinal muscles. Frequent neurologic annotations mix secondary etiologies and do not establish neural injury caused by idiopathic myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: none: HPO lists neural findings at 30-79%, but these reflect heterogeneous secondary causes; direct neural damage from the defined idiopathic muscle disease is not established.

basis: Permanent digital contractures and abnormal taurine/amino-acid excretion define the syndrome; aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal injury.
Congenital cardiac septal and valve defects; pulmonary venous hypertension is vascular. Congestive hepatomegaly does not establish intrinsic liver damage.
Beryllium-specific cell-mediated hypersensitivity causes granulomatous interstitial lung disease; extrapulmonary damage is uncommon.
Congenital atrioventricular septal and valve malformation; respiratory symptoms do not establish direct lung damage.
Carcinoma of thyroid C cells; diarrhea and dysphagia do not establish gastrointestinal damage, and distant organ metastases are occasional.
Exocrine pancreatic carcinoma; direct biliary obstruction causes extrahepatic cholestasis in 30-79%. Diabetes and liver neoplasms are minority findings.
Immune deficiency with chronic Candida infection of skin, nails and oral mucosa; these sites define the syndrome. Other listed organ involvement is below 30%.
Heart defects, skin/hair abnormalities and developmental disability define CFC; visual impairment 80-99%. Frequent skeletal abnormalities omitted by cap.
Loss of atrial electrical and mechanical activity defines disease; associated muscular dystrophy is separate; embolic neurologic complications are occasional.
The defining triad comprises cardiomyopathy, cataracts and degenerative hip/spine disease; each has very frequent supporting phenotypes.
Mitochondrial cardiomyopathy/deafness; ataxia and developmental dysfunction 80-99%; myopathy (weakness 80-99%) and ophthalmoparesis (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Upper-limb skeletal malformations and cardiac arrhythmias define the syndrome; both occur in 80-99%.
Endocrine overactivity, characteristic skin lesions and cutaneous/cardiac myxomas are defining diagnostic manifestations; schwannomas and other sites are minority findings.
Inborn glycosylation disorders; neurologic impairment affects most patients (>50%). Other organ involvement varies substantially across this broad group.
Herpes simplex infection directly damages the corneal epithelium, producing dendritic ulcers.
Infection directly inflames and damages the corneal epithelium.
Corneal sensory loss and degeneration define keratopathy; fifth-nerve abnormalities (80-99%) describe antecedent denervation, not additional neurologic injury caused by the corneal disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: trigeminal dysfunction is the cause of corneal degeneration; the keratopathy does not itself produce a separate cranial neuropathy despite the 80-99% HPO association.

basis: Definition specifies HSV stromal keratitis with corneal inflammation, ulceration and possible necrosis; vesicles do not establish lasting skin damage.
The HSV keratitis ancestry identifies corneal endothelial inflammation, rather than systemic vascular endotheliitis.
Epidermal nevi, lipomatosis and vascular malformations define the syndrome; reduced bone mineral density occurs in 30-79%; cancer risks are excluded.
Cutaneous fibrosis with common (>30%) fascial involvement and disabling contractures; renal impairment is a predisposing condition, not damage caused by this disease.
Intractable intestinal disease, choanal atresia and chronic corneal inflammation define the syndrome; cytopenia frequency is unspecified.
Defined by ventricular noncompaction, bradycardia, pulmonary valve stenosis and atrial septal defect; laterality alone adds no damaged organ.
Corneal thinning and ectasia define this degenerative eye disorder.
Intrauterine adhesions affect reproductive anatomy; menstrual and fertility disturbances do not establish endocrine disease.
Congenital cataract and microcornea define the syndrome; explicitly lacks systemic anomalies.
Localized amyloid deposition produces cutaneous disease; systemic organ involvement is not characteristic.
Amyloid deposition is localized to dermis and subcutis; associated autoimmune conditions are separate diseases.
Localized cutaneous amyloid deposition produces chronic pruritic skin lesions; associated atopic dermatitis is a separate disease.
Chronic arachnoid inflammation; hearing and visual impairment are each annotated in 80-99%. Generic arachnoiditis includes noninfectious, nonautoimmune causes.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: arachnoiditis may follow chemical or mechanical injury as well as infection; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Defined by oropharyngeal infection and septic internal jugular thrombophlebitis, commonly with pulmonary septic emboli.
Motor neuron degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss define the disease; hearing loss occurs in 80-99%. Limb atrophy reflects denervation; optic atrophy is occasional.
Severe insulin resistance and dyslipidemia together with skeletal myopathy define this laminopathy.
Autistic neurodevelopmental impairment and a persistent facial cutaneous capillary malformation define the syndrome.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the defining port-wine angioma is a structural capillary malformation; capillaries belong to the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Congenital unilateral obstruction of the posterior nasal airway; nose is included in the pulmonary axis.
Congenital bilateral obstruction of the posterior nasal airway; the nasal airway belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Congenital lymphatic malformation occupying the larynx, an upper airway structure; dysphagia does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Brainstem disease causes swallowing, laryngeal and autonomic dysfunction; direct gastrointestinal, airway or cardiac injury is not established.

decisions.pulmonary: none: abnormal laryngeal sensation and motility reflect impaired brainstem control; intrinsic airway damage is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: swallowing dysfunction and reflux reflect impaired neural control; defining symptoms alone do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Congenital vocal cord paralysis is defined by laryngeal motor nerve dysfunction and loss of vocal cord movement. Feeding symptoms do not establish gastrointestinal injury.
Vascular neoplasm arising in and occupying the laryngeal/tracheal airway. Facial hemangioma occurs in only 5-29%; feeding difficulty does not establish digestive injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: angioma is a neoplasm of blood vessels, giving vascular origin in addition to its laryngeal/tracheal location.

basis: Cataracts, intellectual disability and anal atresia define the syndrome; urinary tract defects, including rectovesical fistula and hypospadias, are defining features.
Cataracts, sensorineural deafness and hypogonadism define the syndrome; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%. Hypertrichosis omitted at the four-axis cap.
Retinal dysfunction and skeletal abnormalities define disease; cognitive impairment is annotated at 30-79%. Caries is a separate disease; palate morphology alone does not establish damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: caries (80-99%) is separately diagnosed dental disease; abnormal palate morphology without demonstrated dysfunction does not establish direct damage.

basis: Umbrella of developmental anomalies caused by metabolic disease; no additional organ is consistently affected across the group.
Premature skin/subcutaneous aging and skeletal abnormalities characterize most major progeroid syndromes; vascular, endocrine, ocular and neurologic damage vary by subtype.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal hypoplasia, osteolysis, osteoporosis or contractures are core features across most major progeroid forms, although the particular lesions differ.

basis: Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines disease; neurologic or visual damage is not established in most isolated cases.
Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines the group; additional organ abnormalities depend on the particular syndrome.
Peroxisomal metabolic disease defined by spinal cord and peripheral nerve degeneration, often with adrenal dysfunction; sphincter symptoms are neurologic.
Hypersensitivity with defining rash and blood-cell abnormalities; hepatic injury ~60-80%. Pneumonitis annotated 30-79% omitted at cap; renal and cardiac injury occasional.
audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary because eosinophilia and lymphocyte abnormalities are defining diagnostic features. Remove pulmonary under the four-axis cap, prioritizing more frequent hepatic injury.

basis: Congenital cutaneous hamartoma composed of malformed hair follicles within the dermis.
Inflammatory, usually immune-mediated spinal cord demyelination; weakness and autonomic symptoms reflect cord injury rather than direct muscle or urinary-organ damage.
Immune-mediated inflammatory demyelination directly affects the spinal cord.
Epilepsy syndrome defined by absence seizures and perioral myoclonia; muscle movements do not indicate primary muscle disease.
Generalized reflex epilepsy; eyelid myoclonia and photosensitivity reflect seizures rather than intrinsic ocular damage.
Histiocytic skin nodules and destructive arthritis define the disease, each occurring in 80-99%; blood-cell or marrow dysfunction is not established.

decisions.haematologic: none: tissue histiocytic proliferation in skin and joints does not itself establish disease of circulating blood cells, marrow or coagulation.

basis: Cerebral white matter disease and temporal cysts define the disorder; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Strabismus alone does not establish ocular damage.
audit_reason: Remove ocular: strabismus alone does not establish direct eye damage or visual loss. Retain otologic for sensorineural hearing impairment in 30-79%. Leukodystrophy ancestry alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.

basis: Progressive cavitating white-matter disease causes neurological deterioration.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; enamel abnormalities occur in 30-79%, and scalp alopecia in 2/2 reported patients. Ocular and cardiac defects are below 30%; hair evidence is limited.
Peripheral neuropathy and sensorineural hearing impairment are both defining features.
Distal motor neuron degeneration defines disease; progressive denervation produces persistent distal skeletal muscle atrophy in most patients (>50%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic denervation causes actual muscle tissue loss in most patients (>50%); this exceeds weakness alone and is part of the disease.

basis: Hereditary motor neuron/peripheral nerve disease; weakness and muscle atrophy reflect denervation. Skeletal deformities are occasional.
Defining sensory-autonomic axonal neuropathy, developmental impairment and sensorineural hearing loss.
Motor neuropathy with defining persistent vocal cord paresis and impaired laryngeal function; distal muscle wasting is secondary to motor denervation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal weakness and wasting result from motor denervation; the evidence does not establish direct muscle disease independent of the neuropathy.

basis: Parathyroid secretory failure; nephrocalcinosis is commonly treatment-related or separately coded; basal ganglia calcification alone does not establish functional damage.
Inherited motor and sensory peripheral nerve disease; ocular and metabolic manifestations belong to particular subtypes.
Inherited distal motor neuron or axonal degeneration; muscle weakness and wasting result from denervation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common distal muscle wasting is secondary to motor neuron/axon degeneration; direct muscle or skeletal disease is not established.

basis: Distal motor neuron or axon degeneration defines this neuropathy; muscle wasting and weakness result from denervation rather than direct muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common muscle wasting reflects denervation from motor neuron or axon disease, without evidence of direct skeletal muscle pathology.

basis: Inherited sensory and autonomic peripheral neuropathy; ulcers and skeletal complications are not established across most subtypes.
Limb and mandibular malformations with oral clefts and tooth agenesis define the syndrome; fingernail and toenail abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Mandatory midbrain-hindbrain malformation defines the umbrella; retinal dystrophy affects approximately 30%. Renal disease (~25%) and hepatic fibrosis remain below threshold across the group.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal dystrophy causes direct visual-system damage in approximately 30% across Joubert syndrome and related disorders; this is a borderline frequency call.

basis: Localized dermal atrophy and linear hyperpigmentation define the disease; no systemic inflammation or scleroderma is described.
Inherited platelet disorder with congenital thrombocytopenia and enlarged platelets; no common extra-haematologic damage established.
Immune-mediated vasculitis confined to CNS vessels, with frequent cerebral infarction and neurologic impairment; ocular findings are occasional.
Oral and digital malformations define the group. Renal cystic disease and brain abnormalities vary by subtype; group-wide involvement above 30% is uncertain.
Congenital first-cleft cyst or fistula associated with the external auditory canal and periauricular region.
Congenital branchial cyst or fistula typically communicating with the hypopharyngeal pyriform sinus; secondary thyroiditis does not establish intrinsic endocrine disease.
Defined as a cutaneous dermoid neoplasm; possible swallowing or airway compression does not establish common direct gastrointestinal or pulmonary damage.
Defined as a benign cutaneous dermoid neoplasm; periorbital or nasal proximity alone does not establish ocular or airway damage.
Congenital fistula of the labial commissure lined by oral mucosa; susceptibility to infection is only a risk.
Congenital fistulae involve lower-lip oral mucosa and sometimes accessory salivary glands; infection is an optional complication.
Congenital cervicofacial cutaneous fibrocartilaginous remnants; cartilage within a skin lesion does not establish locomotor disease.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: cervicofacial fibrochondromatous remnants are cutaneous/subcutaneous lesions.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: ectopic cartilage within cutaneous remnants does not establish disease of the locomotor system.

basis: Congenital duplication cyst occupies the tongue; possible breathing difficulty does not establish airway damage.
Teratoma originates in oral tissues; airway obstruction depends on tumor size. Direct airway involvement in at least 30% is not established by the supplied evidence.

decisions.pulmonary: none: the defining origin is intraoral; size-dependent airway obstruction does not establish common direct airway occupation or injury.

basis: Congenital lacrimal drainage cyst; intranasal extension directly obstructs the nasal airway, with congestion and dyspnea reported in 30-79%.
Congenital nasal malformation; nose belongs to the pulmonary axis. Associated ocular and other structural defects are uncommon.
Nasal/sinus maldevelopment defines disease; eyelid/ocular defects and CNS malformations each occur in 30-79%. Facial dysmorphism alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Teratoma located in the nasopharynx, which is included in the airway axis.
Heterotopic tissue occupies the nose and may obstruct the airway; there is no communication with the CNS.
Tumour arises in the nasal region; neuronal/glial histology alone does not establish brain or peripheral nerve involvement.
Herniation of intracranial contents through a congenital cranial/skull-base defect into the nasal region defines neural, skeletal and nasal involvement; no ear disease is established.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary: encephalocele entails a defining congenital cranial or skull-base defect, retained in the nasal subtype. Nasal and neural locations remain primary; the ENT parent does not establish ear involvement.

basis: Congenital narrowing of the subglottic airway; larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Congenital cyst occupies the larynx or supraglottic airway; feeding difficulty does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Craniofacial, ear and limbal abnormalities define spectrum; renal malformations occur in 30-79%. Neurodevelopmental delay (30-79%) omitted at cap, prioritizing structural renal defects.

decisions.renal: involved: renal malformations occur in 30-79%; structural renal involvement is retained within the four-axis cap.
decisions.neurologic: none under cap: neurodevelopmental delay is reported in 30-79%, but structural renal abnormalities are prioritized after the three defining axes.

basis: Congenital intraoral band fixes the tongue to the palate or alveolar ridge, directly affecting oral function.
Frontonasal arterial-to-venous malformation defines the disease; optional bleeding, skin changes and blurred vision do not establish common additional organ damage.
Arteriovenous malformation occupies the maxillary jaw and its vessels. Possible dental mobility, epistaxis and ocular/ear pain do not establish additional common organ damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the named maxillary malformation involves the bony jaw as its anatomical site, alongside the abnormal arterial and venous connections.

basis: Arteriovenous malformation occupying the mandible defines vascular and jaw involvement; gingival bleeding alone does not establish additional GI damage.
Persistent congenital tumor of cutaneous blood vessels; cardiac failure, thrombocytopenia and visceral lesions are occasional (<30%).
Congenital vascular tumor typically occupies skin and subcutis; heart failure and thrombocytopenia occur in fewer than 30%.
Arteriovenous malformations of cerebral, orbital and facial territories define the syndrome; additional tissue involvement varies across subtypes.

decisions.ocular: primary: orbital vascular malformations are expressly included in the syndrome's defining anatomic spectrum.

basis: CAMS1 comprises AVMs in the medial forebrain and nasal territory; these defining sites map to vascular, neurologic and pulmonary axes.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: nasal AVMs are part of the defining medial prosencephalic territory of CAMS1; the nose belongs to this axis.

basis: Segmental arteriovenous malformations involving the hindbrain and corresponding lower facial territory define CAMS3; no additional organ damage established.
Diffuse lymphatic malformation; destructive bone lesions occur in ~75%, pleuropulmonary involvement in ~50%, and splenic lymphatic infiltration in roughly half.

decisions.haematologic: involved: splenic lymphatic lesions occupy and replace splenic tissue in roughly half of patients; this is direct structural involvement.

basis: Congenital fusion of the jaws or oral mucosa directly restricts mouth opening; respiratory difficulty does not establish separate airway damage.
Dermoid cyst occupies nasal dorsal skin/subcutis; intracranial extension alone does not establish brain damage, and neurologic complications lack a qualifying frequency.
Congenital craniofacial fusion defect classified as a facial skeletal disorder; oral, nasal and eyelid involvement varies by subtype.
Congenital cleft directly affects the upper lip/oral structures and maxillary bone; associated CNS and nasal abnormalities are variable.
Congenital structural cleft of the nose; the pulmonary axis explicitly includes the nose.
Oblique facial cleft traverses the upper lip and maxilla to the lower eyelid and orbital floor, defining oral, skeletal and eyelid malformations.
Zygomaticomaxillary cleft and lower-eyelid coloboma are defining structural lesions. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_141265)
Congenital cervical skin and subcutaneous defect; neck restriction results from local scarring. Other malformations are occasional associations.
The defining cleft directly affects the upper lip and tooth-bearing alveolar bone. Nasal shape abnormalities alone do not establish airway damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the alveolar ridge is maxillary bone, and its cleft is a defining structural lesion rather than a secondary manifestation.

basis: Oral, digital/skeletal and CNS malformations define this subtype; cardiac septal hypertrophy is another defining feature, retained as the fourth axis.
Severe skeletal dysplasia defines disease. Fatal respiratory distress reflects thoracic restriction; intrinsic pulmonary hypoplasia or injury is not established.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory distress is common (30-79%; most deaths), but a narrow bony thorax does not itself establish direct lung damage.

basis: Defining skeletal dysplasia; glaucoma and intellectual disability each 80-99%, ventricular septal defect 30-79% in supplied HPO.
Umbrella of episodic neurologic movement disorders; metabolic causes apply only to particular subtypes.
Choroidal atrophy and ectodermal hair/nail abnormalities define the syndrome; middle-ear disease is occasional.
Developmental impairment defines the syndrome; persistent ptosis in 80-99% supports ocular involvement. Clinodactyly in 80-99% lacks demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: fifth-finger clinodactyly occurs in 80-99%, but this minor shape difference alone does not establish skeletal damage or impaired function.

basis: ID defines syndrome; HPO lists renal hypoplasia, aganglionic megacolon and microphthalmia at 80-99%, despite sparse case data. Hypocalcemia and skeletal findings omitted by cap.
Developmental delay is obligate. Clinodactyly (30-79%) and dermatoglyphic variation do not establish functional damage; significant skeletal and cardiac defects are occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent clinodactyly is a minor skeletal variant without established functional damage; other skeletal lesions occur in <30%.

basis: Intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures define the phenotype; cafe-au-lait spots and retinal flecks do not establish functional damage.
