decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the definition explicitly identifies growth hormone deficiency among common defining features; occasional hypothyroidism does not negate this endocrine involvement.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing loss and aural atresia are explicitly common features in the syndrome's own definition.

basis: Developmental and intellectual impairment define the symptomatic syndrome despite variable penetrance; hearing, skin and limb abnormalities are each reported in 5-29%.
Characteristic epilepsy, status epilepticus and cognitive deterioration; renal and cardiac malformations are rare.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and seizures occur in 30-79%; skeletal and immune abnormalities are occasional; common thrombocytopenia is not established.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; neurofibromas and toenail dysplasia are annotated 30-79%; simple toe syndactyly does not establish locomotor injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent 2-3 toe syndactyly is a minor structural variant without demonstrated functional impairment; large hands alone add no axis.

basis: Developmental delay, intellectual disability and microcephaly define the syndrome; split hand occurs in 80-99% and radial hypoplasia in 30-79%.
CNS and skeletal developmental defects define the syndrome. Respiratory insufficiency and urogenital fistula each 80-99%; variable ocular anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: short neck and delayed bone age are in the defining phenotype; short distal phalanges occur in 80-99%, supporting intrinsic skeletal malformation.

basis: Developmental brain and skin abnormalities define syndrome; hypogonadism and ptosis each occur in 80-99%; murmur alone does not establish cardiac damage.
Intellectual disability is characteristic; ureter abnormalities and hydronephrosis occur in 80-99%. Finger deviation and facial morphology do not establish functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: finger deviation occurs in 80-99%, but isolated digit morphology does not establish impaired skeletal or joint function.

basis: Congenital narrowing of the aorta.
Aortic and branch-artery narrowing defines the disease; renal-artery involvement is vascular. Renal failure is an unquantified complication, and underlying arteritis is a separate diagnosis.
Carcinoma arising in the thyroid gland; no additional organ involvement established across differentiated thyroid carcinomas.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder. Neurologic, muscle, hepatic, renal and cardiac injury vary by subtype; no additional axis clearly meets 30% across the umbrella.
Congenital malformation of cardiac connections; respiratory insufficiency reflects cardiac physiology without established intrinsic lung damage.
Congenital atrial membrane divides an atrium into two chambers.
Congenital single-ventricle cardiac malformation; respiratory distress does not establish direct lung damage.
Developmental disability and fifth-digit bone/nail defects define CSS; visual impairment 30-79%; cardiac anomalies and dental delay (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Autoimmune keratitis and vestibuloauditory dysfunction define the disease; vasculitis and aortic injury occur in fewer than 30%; blood changes are inflammatory.
Biotin metabolic defect; seizures/developmental impairment and persistent dermatitis/alopecia each affect roughly 30% or more of symptomatic patients across the main forms.
Gonococcal infection directly inflames the conjunctiva.
Defined by agenesis of the corpus callosum and duplication of the urinary collecting system; both are congenital structural organ defects.
Callosal hypoplasia, intellectual disability, preauricular skin tags and camptodactyly define disease. Nonspecific immune annotations do not establish immunodeficiency; pneumonia is separate.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent preauricular skin tags are explicitly named and defining cutaneous malformations.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: the 80-99% nonspecific immune-physiology annotation and recurrent pneumonia do not establish an intrinsic immunodeficiency or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Carcinoma originates in nasopharyngeal epithelium, within the airway axis; EBV association alone does not establish an infectious disease.
Thoracic and limb skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia with respiratory dysfunction is common (>30%). Renal and hepatic disease vary substantially by subtype.
Skeletal dysplasia with rib, long-bone and pelvic abnormalities in 80-99%; unspecified palate morphology does not establish oral functional damage.
Syndactyly and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Hirsutism, thick hair and dermatoglyphic differences do not establish damaging skin disease.
Craniosynostosis and pectoral/limb malformations define syndrome; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Nail and hair morphology alone does not establish tissue damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: frequent nail and hair variants lack evidence of functional impairment or destructive skin disease.

basis: Cranial hyperostosis and metaphyseal dysplasia define it; hearing loss, visual impairment and cranial neuropathy are each occasional (5-29%).
Defining cranial ossification defects, periostosis and arthropathy; mottled pigmentation alone does not establish skin damage; dermatitis is occasional.
Cranial-suture fusion and hand/foot syndactyly define the syndrome; long palpebral fissures do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Craniosynostosis and cataracts are the defining skeletal and ocular abnormalities.
Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines a skeletal disorder; neurologic or ocular damage is not established across most of this umbrella.
A focal epilepsy syndrome; its benign and transitory course does not alter its neurologic classification.
ID, muscle/skeletal defects and lung hypoplasia define the syndrome; lung hypoplasia and strabismus each occur in 80-99%. Dental anomalies in 30-79% are omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: hypoplastic bronchial/lung development is an explicit defining structural malformation, with lung hypoplasia reported in 80-99%.

basis: Cryptosporidium directly infects intestinal epithelium; extraintestinal disease is not common across patients.
Developmental cysts and fistulae affect oral tissues and facial or cervical skin/subcutis; other ENT organs are not consistently affected across this umbrella.
Congenital auricular sinus or cyst; associated renal anomalies are not established as common, and infection is a complication.
Congenital structural defect of the oral palate. Hearing impairment and otitis media are occasional (5-29%).
Congenital structural defect of the upper eyelid; associated syndromic abnormalities are not intrinsic to the isolated concept.
Congenital structural defect of the inferior eyelid; associated facial clefts or syndromes are not intrinsic to every case.
Definition specifies craniofacial skeletal hypoplasia, lower-eyelid coloboma and microtia; these are intrinsic developmental abnormalities.
Larval tissue infection; CNS abnormalities occur in 80-99%, and intramuscular cystic lesions/abnormal muscle morphology in 30-79%. Muscle lesions may be asymptomatic; ocular disease is <30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: larval cysts directly occupy muscle, with abnormal skeletal muscle morphology in 30-79%; absence of symptoms does not negate cystic tissue occupation.

basis: Structural corneal thinning and ectasia impair vision.
Mitochondrial COX deficiency defines cardiac and brain disease; skeletal myopathy is a defining component supported by the mitochondrial myopathy parent.
Immune-complex vascular inflammation; cutaneous small-vessel inflammation affects most patients across the listed subtypes. Renal and gut involvement vary by subtype.
Autoimmune necrotizing vasculitis; glomerulonephritis affects ~70-90% and airway/lung inflammation ~50-80% across the principal subtypes.
Lipodystrophy, diabetes, skin papules, cardiomyopathy and liver steatosis define it. Hepatic involvement occupies the fourth axis under the primary cap; frequencies unspecified.

decisions.hepatic: involved: steatosis is a defining manifestation, retained as the fourth axis because primary is capped at three; no frequency estimate is supplied.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is explicitly syndrome-defining and warrants priority among the three primary axes.

basis: Isolated neurologic movement disorder; abnormal contractions do not establish primary skeletal-muscle disease.
Structural enlargement of the tongue; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defining oral and tongue malformations accompany mandibular and limb skeletal anomalies; additional organs vary across subtypes.
Abnormal facial arterial-to-venous communications define the disease; other tissue damage varies by lesion location and extent.
Umbrella of inherited endocrine disorders affecting growth; other organ abnormalities vary by subtype.
Fatty-acid oxidation defect; muscle weakness 80-99% and myopathy 30-79%; hepatic, cardiac and renal damage is concentrated in uncommon severe forms.
Congenital hand and foot reduction defects affect bones, joints, muscles, tendons and ligaments; cutaneous webbing is part of the limb malformation.
Primary antibody deficiency defines disease; associated infections, bronchiectasis and autoimmune conditions are separately diagnosed diseases.
Direct degeneration and necrosis of basal ganglia cause regression, dystonia and progressive spastic quadriparesis.
Congenital or early infantile vanishing white matter disease directly affects cerebral white matter.
Late-infantile form of vanishing white-matter leukodystrophy; cerebral white-matter degeneration defines the disease.
Juvenile/adult vanishing-white-matter leukoencephalopathy directly damages cerebral white matter. Ovarian endocrine dysfunction is variable and sex-limited.
Malignant endothelial blood-vessel neoplasm; organ sites vary and are not consistently shared across the umbrella concept.
Defined by multiple colorectal serrated or hyperplastic polyps; associated cancers are separate diseases or rare.
Congenital failure of bony union with pseudarthrosis of limb bones.
Hereditary autonomic neuropathy causing abnormal thermoregulatory sweating; sweating alone does not establish skin damage.
Congenital tumor of gingival tissue along the alveolar ridge; oral gingiva determines the axis despite nonspecific nervous-system ancestry.
Primary trigeminal autonomic headache disorder; tearing, conjunctival redness, ptosis and rhinorrhea are attack-related signs without direct organ damage.
Primary trigeminal headache disorder; cranial autonomic signs do not establish ocular or vascular damage.
Heterogeneous disorders of histiocyte accumulation; skin, liver, skeletal and neurologic damage vary by subtype, without a reliably shared additional organ.
Cutaneous histiocytic proliferation causes characteristic dermal papules. Blood abnormalities occur in 5-29%; leukemia is a separate disease reported in 1-4%.

decisions.haematologic: none: tissue histiocytes proliferate in skin; hematopoietic lineage alone does not establish blood or marrow disease. Blood abnormalities are occasional.

basis: Localized cutaneous histiocytic proliferation with papules in 80-99%; systemic blood or immune dysfunction is not characteristic.
Benign dermal histiocytic tumor; ocular and other extracutaneous involvement occur in fewer than 30%. Dermal histiocytes alone do not establish blood or marrow disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: the defined lesion is a dermal histiocytic tumor without defining blood-cell, marrow or coagulation dysfunction.

basis: Cutaneous histiocytic proliferation; supplied HPO supports osteolysis in 80–99% and pituitary diabetes insipidus in 30–79%. Individual airway abnormalities are occasional.
audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary: this is a proliferative disorder of histiocytes, retaining the blood-cell disease axis. Supplied osteolysis and diabetes insipidus frequencies support the existing involved organs.

basis: Localized cutaneous histiocytic infiltration; normolipidemic and usually without systemic disease. Oral lesions are rare.
Cutaneous histiocytosis; periocular skin lesions alone do not establish ocular dysfunction at >=30%; associated monoclonal gammopathy is separate.
Hematopoietic dendritic-cell neoplasm typically arising in skin with papules, nodules and plaques; systemic involvement is uncommon.
Progressive histiocytic proliferation occupies dermis and subcutis; systemic disease is not usual and conjunctival or mucosal lesions are rare.
Immune hyperactivation with cytopenias and hemophagocytosis; direct inflammatory hepatitis or hepatic dysfunction occurs in most cases, roughly 70-90%.
Immune dysregulation with hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; liver dysfunction and renal dysfunction each 30-79%; clinical neurologic disease 5-29%; respiratory damage unspecified.
Immune hyperactivation with hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; hepatic inflammation and dysfunction occur in most patients, commonly >50%.
Hyperinflammatory hemophagocytosis with cytopenias; renal dysfunction occurs in 80-99%, and hepatic injury with elevated transaminases and bilirubin in 30-79%.
Immune hyperactivation with hemophagocytosis, cytopenias, coagulopathy and defining liver dysfunction; encephalopathy occurs in only 5-29%.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the deletion syndrome; strabismus occurs in 80-99%. Epicanthal folds and palmar creases alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited dementia is defined by progressive cognitive dysfunction; additional organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Umbrella of hereditary neurodegenerative Huntington phenocopies; dementia and movement disorders are neurologic.
Inherited epidermal fragility with suprabasal blistering; additional organ involvement is not established across the group.
Predominantly acral skin blistering; esophageal stricture is annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Nail-limited dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa; dystrophic or absent nails without blistering.
Cutaneous mastocytosis consists of clonal mast-cell proliferation and accumulation in skin.
Cutaneous mastocytosis is a clonal hematopoietic mast-cell proliferation producing skin plaques; systemic organ infiltration is not implied.

decisions.haematologic: primary: mastocytosis is a hematopoietic mast-cell neoplasm; skin localization does not remove its hematologic identity.

basis: Cutaneous mastocytosis is a clonal mast-cell proliferation occupying skin; systemic organ involvement is not implied.
Clonal marrow mast-cell neoplasm; persistent cutaneous mast-cell infiltrates commonly occur in >30%. Visceral enlargement without dysfunction does not establish damage.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation confined predominantly to bone marrow; no defining skin disease or common additional organ damage.
Aggressive systemic mast-cell neoplasm with eosinophilia; hepatic infiltration can occur, but damaging hepatic involvement in >=30% of this subtype is not established.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly or infiltration alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction; a >=30% frequency of damaging liver involvement is not established for this subtype.

basis: Brain/limb defects define syndrome; cardiac defects and optic atrophy occur in 80-99%. Respiratory insufficiency and microtia (80-99%) omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone is not liver damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac septal abnormalities and patent ductus arteriosus are reported in 80-99%.
decisions.pulmonary: none under cap: respiratory insufficiency is 80-99%, but definite brain, skeletal, cardiac and optic pathology take priority.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic atrophy is direct, irreversible visual-system damage reported in 80-99%.

basis: Lymph-node lymphoproliferation with immune dysregulation; anemia is frequent (30-79%); substantial visceral injury is uncommon across the umbrella.
Inflammatory colorectal polyps define disease; associated gastritis remains gastrointestinal. An autoimmune or infectious mechanism is not established by inflammation alone.
Developmental impairment, limb malformations and cleft palate occur in 80-99%; cataract, microphthalmia and coloboma occur in 30-79%. Cardiac involvement lacks a qualifying frequency.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate is a major structural manifestation, annotated in 80-99%; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining limb malformations include syndactyly, abnormal phalanges and camptodactyly, each annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Bilateral congenital cataracts and subsequent glaucoma define an ocular syndrome.
Congenital narrowing of the nasal airway; nose and upper airways belong to the pulmonary axis.
Defined by congenital nasal airway stenosis together with holoprosencephaly.
Congenital middle-ear ossicular malformation causes conductive hearing loss; speech delay is secondary to hearing impairment.
Developmental/learning impairment defines the spectrum; heart malformations annotated 80-99% and kyphoscoliosis 30-79%; growth hormone deficiency is subtype-dependent.
Autoimmune cutaneous lupus; systemic organ damage is not characteristic of this cutaneous subtype.
Chronic autoimmune cutaneous disease affecting skin and sometimes subcutis; systemic lupus manifestations are not intrinsic to this concept.
Severe alpha-thalassemia; heart failure occurs in 80-99% and hydrocephalus in 30-79%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Brain and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; calvarial abnormalities 80-99%. Oral clefts and strabismus each 30-79%; nonspecific immune physiology does not establish immune damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining skeletal malformations include abnormal digits and caudal deficiency; calvarial abnormalities and micrognathia occur in 80-99%.

basis: Developmental disability, renal cystine transport dysfunction and mitochondrial metabolic abnormalities define the syndrome; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.
Refractory epileptic encephalopathy; preceding febrile illness does not establish ongoing infection or autoimmune disease. Sinusitis is a separate preceding infection.
Epilepsy syndrome with clustered spasms, other seizures and cognitive deterioration.
Epilepsy and developmental speech dysfunction define this neurologic syndrome; drooling does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Immune-mediated inflammation of the limbic brain defines the condition; an associated neoplasm is a separate disease.
Immune-mediated paraneoplastic inflammation damages the limbic brain; the underlying cancer is a separate disease.
Immune-mediated inflammation damages the limbic brain; the associated cancer is a separate disease.
LGI1-mediated autoimmune limbic encephalitis; obstinate SIADH-associated hyponatremia occurs in ~50-60%, representing intrinsic electrolyte dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: obstinate disease-associated hyponatremia occurs in ~50-60%; this axis explicitly covers electrolyte disorders without requiring gland destruction.

basis: Posttransplant limbic encephalitis is typically associated with HHV-6 reactivation; associated SIADH does not establish direct endocrine-organ damage.
Immune-mediated inflammation and lesions of the limbic brain; infectious causes are excluded.
Chronic immune-mediated pustular skin disease; associated arthritis and thyroid dysfunction are separate diseases.
Chronic allergic inflammation directly affects cornea and conjunctiva; associated atopic dermatitis is a separate disease.
Intellectual disability and primary testicular hormone failure define the syndrome; craniosynostosis and delayed skeletal maturation occur in 80-99%.
Intellectual disability and hypogonadism define the syndrome. Microtia is frequent (80-99%), but hearing loss or other functional ear damage is not established.

decisions.otologic: none: microtia in 80-99% is external-ear dysmorphism; the supplied evidence does not establish associated hearing loss or functional damage.

basis: Developmental, skeletal and urethral defects define syndrome; hypospadias 30-79%, microtia 80-99%. Dental defects 30-79% omitted at cap; cardiac defects 5-29%.

decisions.renal: primary: hypospadias is a urethral malformation (30-79%); frequent genitourinary abnormalities are part of the syndrome's definition.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%; omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of defining urethral defects and more frequent ear malformations.

basis: Ichthyosis, intellectual disability and hypogonadism are defining features; ocular abnormalities in 30-79%. Chondrodysplasia omitted by four-axis cap.
Y-chromosome microdeletion causes impaired spermatogenesis and infertility; reproductive dysfunction without established endocrine disease has no axis.
Radiation-associated myeloid neoplasia directly affects marrow and blood cells; prior radiation is its cause, not an additional organ label.
Disorder of neurologic circadian sleep-wake regulation; no additional organ damage is established.
Acquired marrow failure causes cytopenias and is predominantly mediated by immune destruction of hematopoietic stem cells.
Triglyceride storage disorder; myopathy roughly 50-100% and hepatic disease roughly 40-80%, varying by subtype. Ichthyosis is subtype-specific; its pooled frequency is uncertain.

decisions.dermatologic: none: ichthyosis defines NLSDI but is absent from NLSDM; a qualifying frequency across the umbrella population is not established.

basis: Primary proximal tubulopathy; persistent renal hypophosphatemia and recurrent fractures each annotated 80-99% support mineral and skeletal involvement. Rickets/osteomalacia individually 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: renal phosphate wasting causes persistent hypophosphatemia (HPO 80-99%); this is secondary mineral imbalance from the defining proximal tubulopathy.

basis: Abnormal dentin and tooth-root development define disease; supplied HPO records structural bony exostoses in 30-79%. Increased bone density alone would not establish damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: HPO explicitly reports exostoses in 30-79%; these are structural bony lesions, beyond an isolated bone-density measurement.

basis: Autoimmune blistering skin disease. Associated celiac enteropathy is separately diagnosed; anemia and fractures do not establish direct blood or bone injury.
Fly larvae infest cutaneous wounds and damage local skin and soft tissue.
Dipteran larval infestation defines the disease; affected cavities and organs vary, with no single anatomical axis established in most patients.
Diffuse endocrine pancreatic insulin hypersecretion; lasting hypoglycemic brain injury is not established in at least 30% across this responsive subgroup.
Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction causes profound hypoglycemia; persistent hypoglycemic neurodevelopmental injury affects roughly 30-50% in severe congenital hyperinsulinism.

decisions.neurologic: involved: severe, refractory congenital hyperinsulinism causes direct hypoglycemic brain injury with persistent developmental impairment in roughly 30-50%.

basis: Inherited peripheral neuropathy; chronic denervation causes distal muscle atrophy and structural foot deformities in most patients.
Primary epiphyseal bone dysplasia causes joint abnormalities and degeneration; rare myopathy remains within the same axis. No common extraskeletal injury is established.
Inherited qualitative von Willebrand factor defect causing impaired haemostasis; bleeding sites are not additional primary organ diseases.
Inherited VWF dysfunction causes defective haemostasis and platelet clearance; bleeding locations do not establish additional organ disease.
Inherited VWF functional defect causing impaired platelet adhesion and bleeding; no additional organ is inherently damaged.
Defective von Willebrand factor binding to factor VIII causes an inherited coagulation disorder.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disease defined by infantile encephalomyopathy, affecting brain and skeletal muscle.
Isolated skeletal sclerosis with characteristic bone islands; extra-skeletal abnormalities are occasional or very rare.
Congenital eccrine duct hamartomatous lesions produce persistent keratotic skin papules and plaques.
Dirofilaria infection commonly occupies subcutaneous tissue, producing persistent parasitic nodules in >30% of human cases; pulmonary and ocular frequencies vary geographically.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous parasitic nodules account for >30% of human cases overall and represent direct tissue occupation and inflammation.

basis: An infantile epilepsy syndrome defined by recurrent seizures.
Infantile focal epilepsy; development is normal and ictal apnea does not establish pulmonary disease.
Infantile epilepsy with focal seizures progressing to generalized convulsions; development remains normal.
Self-limited infantile seizure syndrome; gastroenteritis is an associated acute illness, without established direct intestinal damage by the seizure disorder.
Infantile focal epilepsy defined by seizures and characteristic sleep EEG findings.
Visually triggered epilepsy; the triggering stimulus does not imply eye damage.
Reflex epilepsy triggered by sound; acoustic triggering does not imply ear damage.
Reflex epilepsy triggered by eating; gastrointestinal stimuli do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Reflex epilepsy defined by orgasm-triggered seizures; the trigger does not establish reproductive-organ disease.
Reflex epilepsy triggered by cognitive tasks; disease is confined to neuronal seizure activity.
Reflex epilepsy with associated central motor and intellectual impairment; auditory triggers do not establish ear damage.
Reflex epilepsy triggered by urination; the trigger does not indicate urinary tract injury.
Epileptic brain disorder; metabolic, infectious and immune causes apply only to particular subtypes.
Genetically caused epilepsy; no additional organ damage shared across most subtypes.
Destructive developmental brain disorder with cortical loss and severe neurologic impairment; skull/scalp changes do not establish separate functional damage.
Congenital right-sided cardiac position defines the condition; situs reversal alone does not imply organ damage, and other organ malformations are under 30%.
Hypothalamic tumour with hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction defines the syndrome; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage; optic atrophy is under 30%.
Developmental dilatation of the pulmonary artery is vascular disease; airway compression occurs only in severe cases.
Defining cutaneous mucinosis and monoclonal gammopathy; myopathy in 30-79%. Dysphagia alone does not establish direct gut damage; documented hypoperistalsis is 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia occurs in 30-79%, but may reflect myopathy; direct gastrointestinal abnormalities and hypoperistalsis are reported in 5-29%.

basis: Congenital right atrial dilatation with cardiac functional abnormalities; hepatic vascular anomalies remain on the cardiovascular axis.
Acute malignant myeloid proliferation in marrow and blood; other organ infiltration is not consistent across the group.
Craniofacial and ocular duplication define disease; anencephaly and cardiac septal abnormalities each 80-99%. Cleft palate, also 80-99%, omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular duplication is part of the defining facial malformation, with eye and visual abnormalities annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease defined by progressive neurodegeneration, epilepsy and retinal degeneration with vision loss.
Fluke infection umbrella; hepatic, pulmonary and intestinal sites depend on the parasite and are not shared across the group.
Congenital ventricular diverticulum is a cardiac structural malformation; extracardiac defects are occasional.
Localized skeletal dysplasia with delayed and irregular femoral head ossification.
Neurodevelopmental regression causes loss of language and adaptive function; incontinence does not establish direct urinary or intestinal damage.
Carcinoma originates in the peritoneal lining of the abdominal cavity; ovarian involvement is absent or limited by diagnostic criteria.
Clonal eosinophilic blood/marrow neoplasm; cardiac, pulmonary and skin infiltration vary and are not established at ≥30% for this concept.
Clonal hematopoietic neoplasms with eosinophilia; lymphoma presentations and eosinophilic damage to other organs are not established across most subtypes.
Clonal blood and marrow neoplasm, often involving the spleen; no additional organ has established damage in at least 30%. Cardiac fibrosis is described as rare.
Clonal hematopoietic neoplasm involving blood and marrow; splenic involvement shares this axis; other tissue infiltration is not established at 30%.
Eosinophilic blood disorder with immune-mediated tissue injury; skin involvement ~50-60% and pulmonary ~30-40%. Gastrointestinal involvement ~30% omitted by cap; cardiac frequency varies.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none under cap: direct gastrointestinal infiltration affects roughly 30%; retain the more frequent skin and pulmonary involvement alongside the two defining mechanism axes.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: eosinophil-mediated inflammatory tissue injury defines HES and supplies the immune-mediated mechanism, alongside its defining blood-cell abnormality.

basis: Myeloid marrow neoplasm with dysplasia, anemia and excess blood or marrow blasts.
Major mucosal origins are sinonasal airways and oral/anorectal mucosa; genital primaries have no axis. Mucosal origin does not imply skin involvement.
Immunodeficiency, congenital myopathy and ectodermal dysplasia define the syndrome; enamel defects occur in 80-99%; iris hypoplasia omitted by cap. Infections are separate diseases.
Thymoma-associated combined immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis is annotated at 30-79% but is a separately diagnosed complication, as are recurrent infections.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; no common direct damage to another organ is established.
Transient primary humoral immunodeficiency; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish direct chronic pulmonary damage.
Classical complement-pathway immunodeficiency; associated infections and autoimmune diseases do not establish common direct damage to another organ across this umbrella.
Terminal complement deficiency is an immunodeficiency; meningococcal or gonococcal infections are separate diseases.
Immunodeficiency defined by deficient T-cell development and lymphopenia; other organ manifestations are occasional or separate infections.
SCID with defining profound T-lymphocyte deficiency affects immune function and blood cells; secondary infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the T-B+ phenotype is defined by absent or profoundly reduced T lymphocytes, a blood-cell deficiency, alongside combined immunodeficiency.

basis: SCID defined by deficient T-cell numbers and function; lymphopenia occurs in 30–79%. Site-specific infections and hepatitis occur in only 5–29% and are separately diagnosed infections.

decisions.haematologic: primary: deficient T-cell development and numbers constitute a blood-cell disorder; decreased total lymphocytes and T cells are frequent (30–79%).

basis: Familial syndromic craniosynostosis affecting skull bones; CNS malformations are subtype dependent rather than established across the umbrella.
Congenital skeletal myopathy defined by centrally placed muscle nuclei. Respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness; ocular and cardiac abnormalities are occasional.
Very rare, variable chromosomal malformation syndrome with CNS/developmental and skeletal abnormalities. Individual supplied findings are only 5-29%; no additional involvement is established.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment and congenital brain malformations are part of the syndrome's variable phenotype; their individual 5-29% frequencies make this assignment uncertain.

basis: Umbrella of disorders combining primary immunodeficiency with skeletal dysplasia; renal and marrow disease are subtype-dependent.
Developmental impairment, skeletal abnormalities and ocular malformations define the syndrome; eye hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac and urinary anomalies occur in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular malformations explicitly characterize the syndrome in its definition; eye aplasia/hypoplasia is annotated in 30-79%.

basis: Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; idiopathic form does not require structural brain disease.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; an underlying structural CNS lesion is not established by this concept.
Severe factor IX deficiency; recurrent joint bleeding causes chronic haemophilic arthropathy in well over 30% over the typical untreated course.
Factor IX deficiency defines a coagulation disorder; common destructive arthropathy is not established for this severity.
Factor IX deficiency defines a coagulation disorder; chronic joint damage is not typical of mild hemophilia.
Developmental delay is frequent (30-79%). Cardiac anomalies, pigmentary changes, scoliosis and hearing impairment are only occasional in supplied HPO data.
Severe factor VIII deficiency; recurrent joint hemorrhage occurs in 30-79% and directly injures joints. Established joint destruction is annotated less often (5-29%).
Factor VIII deficiency; joint bleeding occurs in 30-79%, but arthropathy, cartilage destruction and restricted mobility occur in only 5-29%; common lasting muscle damage is unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint bleeding and hematomas are frequent, but damaging joint sequelae are reported in only 5-29%; bleeding alone does not establish common lasting damage.

basis: Mild factor VIII deficiency defines a coagulation disorder; chronic joint damage is not common in this mild form.
Inherited coagulation factor deficiency; skeletal, vascular and intracranial complications occur in fewer than 30%.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; cardiovascular malformations occur in 30-79%. Renal and major eye defects are under 30%.
Developmental and blood-cell abnormalities define disease; limb malformations and nail hypoplasia occur in 30-79%. Dental abnormalities (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental abnormalities occur in 30-79% but are less specifically characterized than the retained limb and nail defects; omitted at the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: hypoplastic toenails and other nail abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting direct appendage abnormalities.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: postaxial polydactyly and other limb malformations occur in 30-79%; they are associated structural abnormalities rather than the defining core.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and heart malformations are very frequent; cleft palate/ectopic anus and microtia occur in 30-79%. Minor facial and eyelid dysmorphism adds no axis.
Cognitive impairment 80-99%; cardiac defects, glaucoma and hearing impairment each 30-79%. Urinary anomalies omitted at cap; lung lobation alone lacks established dysfunction.

decisions.renal: none: urinary tract anomalies occur in 30-79%, but functional severity is unspecified; omitted under the cap in favor of established cardiac, visual and hearing involvement.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%, establishing common loss of auditory function.

basis: Cardiac and brain malformations characterize the syndrome; nervous abnormalities 80-99%. Finger contractures occur in 30-79%; renal anomaly frequency is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: primary: structural brain malformations are part of the syndrome's definition, supported by nervous-system abnormalities in 80-99%.

basis: Intellectual disability and skeletal contractures are characteristic; cardiac malformations and eyelid defects occur in 30-79%; minor facial dysmorphism adds no axis.
Cardiac malformations occur in 30-79%; neurologic, renal, skeletal, pulmonary and auditory abnormalities are reported below 30%.
Definition identifies neurodevelopmental, skeletal and cardiac abnormalities as characteristic. Hearing impairment is 30-79%; scoliosis/limb asymmetry are 5-29% but explicitly defining.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: body asymmetry with leg-length difference and scoliosis are explicitly characteristic in the definition; their HPO frequencies of 5-29% would not support involved alone.

basis: Congenital anorectal agenesis, atresia or stenosis; urinary symptoms or an optional fistula do not establish common urinary organ damage.
Congenital anorectal malformation; urinary infections are potential complications, without established common urinary organ damage.
Congenital malformation of the anus and rectum.
Congenital duplication of the rectum is an intestinal malformation; associated urinary infections are separate conditions.
Congenital structural skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure and dysphagia reflect muscle weakness. Pulmonary hypoplasia and cardiomyopathy occur in 5-29%.
Structural skeletal myopathy. Respiratory failure and dysphagia occur in 30-79% but reflect respiratory and swallowing muscle weakness, without direct lung, gut or nerve damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure in 30-79% results from skeletal respiratory muscle weakness; direct pulmonary disease is not established.

basis: Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Structural skeletal myopathy; dysphagia reflects muscle dysfunction without established gastrointestinal injury. Cardiac and respiratory manifestations are below 30%.
Nemaline-body skeletal myopathy; paraproteinemia is an associated separate disorder; cardiomyopathy occurs in only 5-29%.
Developmental disability defines disease; pyloric stenosis and blepharophimosis each occur in 80-99%; unspecified finger/foot morphology does not establish functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: finger and foot abnormalities occur in 30-79%, but their unspecified morphology does not establish damaging skeletal disease.

basis: Developmental impairment and skeletal malformations define phenotype; dental defects/caries 80-99%, cardiovascular malformations 30-79%. Skin/hair variants do not establish damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the skeletal phenotype includes progressive intervertebral narrowing in 80-99% and camptodactyly in 30-79%.

basis: Necrosis of periventricular cerebral white matter; visual and motor deficits can reflect brain injury without direct eye or muscle damage.
Bilateral peripheral vestibular dysfunction; oscillopsia and imbalance reflect vestibular loss rather than separate ocular or central nervous damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize the syndrome; additional skeletal, cardiac, urogenital and gastrointestinal malformations lack evidence of frequency ≥30%.
Defined by congenital brain malformations and severe developmental impairment; respiratory distress and recurrent infections do not establish additional direct organ damage.
Isolated sperm structural dysfunction causing male infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Inherited keratinization disorder of oral mucosa; the definition supports gastrointestinal involvement rather than cutaneous disease.
Developmental delay, obesity and eye/vision anomalies are defining features; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.

decisions.ocular: primary: eye/vision abnormalities are explicitly defining features, supported by strabismus in 30-79%.

basis: Defining skeletal/CNS malformations; renal agenesis/hypoplasia 80-99%, PDA 30-79%. Laryngomalacia 30-79% omitted at cap; eyelid/ear anomalies lack demonstrated functional injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: patent ductus arteriosus occurs in 30-79%; congenital cardiovascular shunting takes priority over laryngomalacia at the four-organ cap.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis is frequent (80-99%), but associated visual impairment or other functional eye damage is not established.

basis: Severe intellectual disability, cataracts and childhood-onset kyphosis are the defining features.
Congenital skeletal myopathy affects limb, facial and respiratory muscles; respiratory muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic lung disease.
Congenital skeletal muscle myopathy with characteristic biopsy abnormalities; reduced reflexes do not establish separate nerve disease.
Umbrella for myeloid blood and marrow neoplasms; no additional organ damage applies across most subtypes.
Lymphoid proliferative disorders affect hematopoietic cells; lymphoma accounts for most of this umbrella and supports the immune axis.
T-lymphocyte lymphoma originating in skin; extracutaneous spread is subtype- and stage-dependent.
Malignant B-cell lymphoid neoplasm; lymphoma warrants the immune axis. Extranodal organ involvement varies across subtypes.
T/NK lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma warrants the immune axis. Skin and other extranodal sites vary across subtypes.
Intellectual disability in 80-99%; skeletal malformations in 30-79%. Eye/ear findings lack evidence of functional damage; kidney abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Inherited bile-formation disorder; coagulopathy and cognitive impairment each annotated 80-99%. Malabsorption 80-99% and reduced bone density 30-79% omitted at cap.
Microcephaly and motor developmental delay occur in 30-79%; specific cardiac, ocular, intestinal and skeletal malformations are mostly 5-29%; unspecified hernia adds no clear organ damage.
Spinal, neurodevelopmental and persistent pigmentary abnormalities define symptomatic cases; most mosaics are normal. Cardiac/renal anomalies are 5-29%; constipation alone adds no axis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent pigmentary skin abnormalities are explicitly defining features; the functional-damage requirement applies to involved organs.

basis: Vibrio infection of the intestine; dehydration and electrolyte changes are acute consequences. Acute kidney injury is occasional (5-29%).
Developmental impairment defines the syndrome; dental defects/caries 80-99%, scoliosis/contractures 30-79%, strabismus 30-79%; cardiac defects 5-29%.
Severe intellectual disability defines the syndrome; renal hypoplasia/aplasia, scoliosis and ptosis each occur in 80-99%. Obesity is separately coded.
Developmental delay and characteristic ocular/eyelid abnormalities define the phenotype; ptosis and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%. Renal and cardiac abnormalities occur in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic eye-region abnormalities are explicitly defining; ptosis and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%, supporting substantive eyelid involvement.

basis: Congenital gonadotropin deficiency; olfactory developmental defects cause anosmia or hyposmia in roughly half of CHH patients, the Kallmann subgroup.
Persistent pigmentary dysplasia is frequent (30-79%); supplied HPO places developmental delay, enamel defects, renal and cardiac anomalies below 30%.
Developmental delay, heart defects and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; oral clefts and tongue defects occur in 30-79%. Urethral anomalies omitted under the four-axis cap.
Limb duplication and tibial absence define the syndrome; associated sacrococcygeal teratoma does not establish occupation of another specified axis organ.
Enteric duplication; tricuspid, cord and skeletal malformations annotated 80-99%. Respiratory insufficiency alone does not establish pulmonary damage; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.
audit_reason: Replace pulmonary with cardiovascular: respiratory insufficiency alone does not establish direct lung or airway damage, whereas tricuspid malformation is annotated in 80–99%. Retain common spinal and skeletal malformations within the cap.

basis: Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias defined by stippled bone calcification; additional organ and metabolic findings vary by subtype.
Neurodevelopmental impairment affects most classic cases; microcephaly 80-99%. Cap omits ichthyosis/dental defects 80-99%; severe intellectual disability alone is annotated 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment is typical and microcephaly occurs in 80-99%; the 5-29% annotation concerns severe intellectual disability, not all neurologic impairment.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: ichthyosis occurs in 80-99%, but defining metabolic, skeletal and ocular disease plus disabling neurologic involvement take priority.

basis: Gonadal dysgenesis with endocrine dysfunction; urethral anomalies including hypospadias occur in 30-79%. Cardiac and kidney defects individually occur in fewer than 30%.
Skin/nail, oral and marrow disease define DC; cellular immunodeficiency 30-79%; cap excludes frequent neurologic, renal, skeletal and airway abnormalities.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral leukoplakia is part of the defining triad and occurs in 80-99%; esophageal stenosis and dental disease occur in 30-79%.
decisions.infectious_immune: involved: cellular immunodeficiency occurs in 30-79%; it is associated immune dysfunction rather than the defining mechanism of this telomere disorder.

basis: Joint anomalies define syndrome; ptosis 80-99%, intellectual disability and coagulation abnormalities each 30-79%. Evidence derives from two patients.

decisions.ocular: involved: eyelid ptosis occurs in 80-99%; it accompanies the defining skeletal syndrome rather than constituting a separate defining eye disorder.

basis: Severe intellectual disability, cleft palate and redundant skin define the syndrome and occur in 80–99%; damaging eye and hearing abnormalities lack frequency evidence.
Neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic endocrine dysfunction define PWS; strabismus/visual impairment and scoliosis each occur in 30-79%; hypopigmentation is not tissue damage.
Neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction define PWS; visual impairment/strabismus and scoliosis each occur in 30-79%. Hypopigmentation adds no damage axis.
Prader-Willi syndrome defines neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic/endocrine dysfunction; central hypotonia and feeding symptoms do not establish muscle or gut damage.
Prader-Willi neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic endocrine syndrome; developmental delay, hyperphagia and obesity are common.
Symptomatic factor VIII deficiency in female carriers; joint hemorrhage only 5-29%; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish lasting organ damage.
Hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal vasopressin deficiency defines endocrine dysfunction; polyuria does not establish renal damage, and broader neurologic injury is not intrinsic.

decisions.neurologic: none: isolated hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal hormone deficiency is captured by the endocrine axis; additional brain injury depends on the underlying cause.

basis: Premature sexual maturation caused by gonadotropin-independent sex hormone production.
Defined by transient deficiency of thyroid hormones in preterm infants; no common direct injury to another organ is established.
Structural congenital myopathy with muscle weakness and hand atrophy; facial weakness and hyporeflexia can be myopathic.
Congenital structural myopathy with contractures; respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness rather than direct airway or lung damage.
Primary malignant mesenchymal tumour of the liver.
Defined by acute alveolar and pulmonary endothelial injury. Infection is one possible trigger, not an obligatory mechanism.
Hereditary photodermatosis causing UV-induced skin injury and pigment changes; DNA repair deficiency alone does not establish metabolic disease.
Fibroblastic/myofibroblastic soft tissue neoplasm; visceral site varies. Inflammatory infiltrates do not make this an immune-mediated disease.
Spondylo-epi-metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia; intelligence is characteristically normal.
Osteosclerosis, craniosynostosis and developmental delay define the syndrome; ocular and hearing complications occur in only 5-29%.
The Pittsburgh antitrypsin variant causes a coagulation defect and bleeding; ordinary antitrypsin-deficiency organ disease is not implied.
Non-syndromic intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder; additional organ damage is not shared across the group.
Wound-produced bacterial toxin blocks neuromuscular and autonomic transmission; ocular, swallowing and respiratory findings reflect neural blockade rather than separate organ injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the pre-existing wound is the site of bacterial toxin production; skin damage caused by botulism is not a defining manifestation.

basis: Intestinal infection produces toxin-mediated neuromuscular junction dysfunction; respiratory weakness and ocular motor findings do not establish intrinsic lung or eye damage.
Intestinal infection produces toxin-mediated neuromuscular junction dysfunction; colonization does not establish intestinal injury or direct lung damage.
Intestinal bacterial colonization produces toxin-mediated neuromuscular-junction paralysis; respiratory and ocular motor symptoms reflect neural dysfunction, not separate organ damage.
Myopia-associated degeneration of the retinal macula; neurological ancestry does not establish separate neurologic disease.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma directly infiltrates skin and hair follicles; lymphoma supplies the blood-cell and immune mechanism axes.
Localized cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with malignant lymphocytes confined to epidermis; extracutaneous dissemination is not reported.
Primary skin lymphoma of T lymphocytes establishes cutaneous origin, hematologic neoplasia and the lymphoma mechanism axis.
Skin-origin mature T-cell lymphoma. Advanced extracutaneous spread is described, but no individual additional organ has an established frequency of at least 30%.
Skin infiltration by malignant mature T cells defines this lymphoma; collective extranodal spread does not establish any additional organ at >=30%; marrow infiltration is uncommon.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a malignant disorder of T lymphocytes, a blood-cell lineage; uncommon marrow involvement does not negate its haematologic identity.

basis: Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma: skin is the origin, B cells establish hematologic lineage, and lymphoma warrants the immune axis.
Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma, usually confined to skin; lymphoid neoplasm supplies haematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes.
Primary skin-based T-cell lymphoma: cutaneous origin, lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm and lymphoma mechanism; extracutaneous spread is not typical.
Indolent B-cell lymphoma arising in skin; lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm and lymphoma mechanism.
Primary skin lymphoma is a neoplasm of B lymphocytes; skin location, blood-cell lineage and lymphoma mechanism define the axes.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; skin and lymphoid cell origin define it. Visceral spread is not common across the typically indolent group.
Facial skeletal dysostosis, ocular defects and oral clefts define the disorder; corneal opacity and cleft/dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%; cognitive impairment is under 30%.
Defined by vertebral and rib segmentation defects; respiratory infections and cardiovascular anomalies occur in only 5-29%.
Distal tubular acidification failure with metabolic acidosis; reduced bone mineral density occurs in 80-99%; hearing loss is under 30%.
Mullerian duct aplasia affects reproductive structures outside the axes; associated renal or skeletal defects are not established across this umbrella.
Unilateral Mullerian duct aplasia produces a unicornuate uterus; this reproductive malformation has no axis.
Non-syndromic uterine and fallopian-tube malformation lies outside the axes; associated urinary malformations are separate anomalies.
Congenital uterine duplication affects reproductive anatomy; associated renal anomalies are not intrinsic to every didelphys uterus.
Uterine duplication and obstructed hemivagina affect reproductive organs; the supplied concept does not establish renal agenesis or its frequency.

decisions.renal: none: associated renal agenesis cannot be assumed to define this uterovaginal malformation; the supplied evidence establishes no renal abnormality.

basis: Congenital malformation confined to the uterus and cervices, with patent cervix and vagina; reproductive organs have no axis.
Congenital uterine shape anomaly confined to the reproductive system.
Congenital uterine septum affects a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Isolated uterovaginal malformation; urinary tract abnormalities are very rare.
Isolated uterine malformation is outside the axes; associated urinary abnormalities are very rare.
Congenital uterine malformation affects a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Isolated uterine developmental abnormality; reproductive anatomy has no axis.
Isolated developmental absence of the uterine body affects reproductive anatomy outside the axes.
Developmental absence of the uterine cervix affects reproductive anatomy outside the axes.
Vaginal developmental malformation; reproductive organs have no axis. Associated renal abnormalities are not established as common intrinsic involvement.
Isolated vaginal developmental malformation; reproductive anatomy falls outside the axes.
Accessory breast tissue is a breast developmental anomaly; breast has no axis.
Isolated congenital absence or underdevelopment of breast tissue and nipples; breast has no axis.
Listed syndromic forms share pectoral muscle or limb skeletal malformations, especially Poland syndrome; breast hypoplasia itself has no axis.
Gonadal germ-cell tumor; gonadal origin alone is reproductive, not endocrine. Neuroectodermal differentiation does not establish nervous-system occupation.
Most mixed germ cell tumors arise in testis or ovary, outside the axes. CNS and mediastinal origins are site-specific minority subtypes, not generalizable to this umbrella.
Carcinoma originates in vaginal epithelium, a reproductive site outside the axes.
Benign neoplasm arising in breast tissue, which has no axis.
Defined by malignant occupation of nipple epidermis with persistent skin injury; breast origin does not negate the defining epidermal disease.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: malignant Paget cells occupy the nipple epidermis, producing defining chronic skin lesions; this is demonstrable skin disease despite mammary origin.

basis: Benign breast ductal neoplasm; breast tissue is outside the 13 axes.
Hair and nail dysplasia with intellectual disability define the syndrome. Teeth and sweating are normal; hearing impairment occurs in 5-29%.
Defining ectodermal defects affect sweat glands, hair and skin, with dental agenesis and abnormal dentition in 80–99%.
Defective GH/IGF signaling defines this endocrine growth disorder; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage; immune disease is subtype-specific.
Abnormal adrenal or gonadal steroid production/metabolism defines the syndrome; reproductive manifestations have no separate axis.
Adrenal aldosterone deficiency is an endocrine disorder; electrolyte effects fall within the same axis.
A disorder of lipoprotein metabolism; altered coronary risk does not establish cardiovascular damage.
Inherited lipid metabolism disorder umbrella; additional organ damage varies substantially among its constituent syndromes.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting epiphyses and metaphyses; no extraskeletal involvement is established by the supplied record.
Chronic fungal infection directly damages skin and subcutis; ocular, pulmonary and skeletal involvement is very rare (1-4%).
Hypocellular marrow failure defines aplastic anemia; immune-mediated stem-cell destruction accounts for most cases, approximately 70-80%. Inherited and toxic forms also occur.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most cases, approximately 70-80%, involve immune-mediated marrow destruction; the umbrella rule concerns the usual disease rather than requiring every subtype to share its mechanism.

basis: MYH9 platelet disorder; hearing loss, nephropathy and cataracts each frequent (30-79%) in supplied HPO. Elevated liver enzymes alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Autonomic nervous system failure causes the defining loss of blood pressure regulation on standing.
Acquired peripheral nerve disease; additional organs and immune mechanisms vary across subtypes.
Disease of pulmonary arteries with elevated vascular resistance; vessels and consequent right heart dysfunction fall within cardiovascular. Dyspnea does not establish lung tissue damage.
Lung parenchymal inflammation and fibrosis define this heterogeneous group; an immune mechanism does not apply throughout.
Inhaled mineral dust produces pulmonary interstitial deposition and injury; other organ damage is not shared across this umbrella.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of lung tissue; no common extrapulmonary damage defines this condition.
Umbrella predominantly covering structural chest-wall, rib and shoulder-girdle malformations. Respiratory ancestry alone does not establish intrinsic airway or lung damage.
Extragonadal germinoma most commonly arises in intracranial midline sites; extracranial sites vary and do not define a shared additional organ.
Skeletal dysplasia, deafness and intellectual disability define the syndrome; persistent hypopigmented skin lesions occur in 80-99%. Ptosis and delayed puberty omitted by cap.
Skeletal dysplasia and hearing loss define it. Urinary obstruction/hydronephrosis and subglottic stenosis each occur in 30-79%; cardiac anomalies omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Immune vasculitis with defining eosinophilic airway/lung disease; neuropathy affects ~60-80%. Skin and renal inflammatory lesions omitted at the four-axis cap.
Defining skeletal, urinary and anorectal defects; hydrocephalus/cortical atrophy 80-99%. Cap omits lung hypoplasia (80-99%), ear, eye, hepatic and cardiac findings.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: anal atresia and rectovesical fistula are defining malformations; anorectal and intestinal anomalies have HPO frequency 80-99%.

basis: Inherited disorders of skin cornification; extracutaneous damage is subtype-specific rather than common across this umbrella.
Hereditary photosensitive skin disorders; metabolic, neurologic and other manifestations are subtype-specific rather than shared across the umbrella.
Inherited disorders of renal tubular function; extrarenal manifestations vary across subtypes and do not define the umbrella.
Single-gene diabetes defines endocrine pancreatic dysfunction; diabetic organ complications are separate diseases.
Profound functional T-cell deficiency with absent T lymphocytes, sometimes also B cells; respiratory infections are separately diagnosed complications.
Antibody immunodeficiency caused by deficient B-cell numbers or function; infections and bronchiectasis are separate complications.
Functional disease of neutrophils, impairing innate immune defense; secondary organ infections vary across subtypes.
Absent kidneys cause oligohydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia in 80-99%. Cardiac and intestinal malformations are associated defects, not direct consequences.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: associated cardiac malformations are not direct consequences of renal agenesis, despite the 30-79% annotation
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal malformations and fistulas are associated developmental defects, not direct consequences of renal agenesis

Congenital cystic renal dysplasia produces a nonfunctional kidney; respiratory distress does not establish direct lung damage across this umbrella.
Neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Urea-cycle/ammonia detoxification disorder; encephalopathy and hepatic dysfunction are common (~30%+), with frequency varying across subtypes.
Inherited degeneration of retinal cones and rods; optic disc findings remain within the ocular axis.
The syndrome explicitly combines skeletal muscular dystrophy with spongiform degeneration of CNS white matter; the isolated Atrophie blanche synonym is inconsistent.
Sclerosing bone dysplasia with limb deformities; skin abnormalities and hypertension occur in only 5-29%.
Lens displacement, cataracts, chorioretinal dystrophy and retinal detachment define this ocular syndrome.
Isolated lens displacement defines this ocular disorder. Discordant systemic HPO annotations do not establish common involvement in nonsyndromic ectopia lentis.

basis: Adrenocortical nodular hyperplasia with autonomous cortisol production; an adrenal endocrine disorder.
Isolated impaired parathyroid hormone secretion causes an endocrine and calcium-regulation disorder; other organ damage is not established.
Defined group of inborn neurometabolic disorders; neurologic dysfunction predominates. Urinary metabolite excretion does not establish renal damage.
Kyphoscoliosis, joint laxity and ocular fragility define the disease; fragile hyperextensible skin occurs in 80-99%. Arterial rupture occurs in 5-29%.
Leukocyte infection with cytopenias; hepatic inflammation with aminotransferase elevation occurs in roughly 70-90%, supporting common hepatocellular injury.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic inflammation and biochemical hepatocellular injury occur in roughly 70-90%; persistent liver failure is not required.

basis: Defining skeletal and neural malformations from prenatal exposure; cleft palate/lip occurs in 30-79%; cardiac defects occur in 5-29%.
Defined fetal toxicity includes renal dysfunction and premature ductus closure, usually reversible. Respiratory insufficiency lacks established lung damage; cerebral/GI injuries are risks.
Progressive neurologic disease and photosensitivity define syndrome; retinopathy and sensorineural hearing loss 80-99%. Musculoskeletal and dental damage 30-79% omitted by cap.
Prenatal cocaine toxicity causes neurodevelopmental dysfunction; hypertonia and hyperreflexia occur in 80-99%. Other structural defects are occasional.
Defining distal phalangeal/nail hypoplasia and developmental impairment; hearing abnormalities 80-99%. Ocular dysfunction 30-79% omitted under cap.
Neurodevelopmental disability defines syndrome; cardiac defects, strabismus/ptosis and urethral hypospadias each have HPO frequencies of 30-79%.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a urethral malformation, annotated 30-79%; urethra belongs to the renal axis. Ambiguous genitalia alone would not qualify.

basis: Nasal skeletal hypoplasia and epiphyseal stippling define embryopathy; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish direct airway or lung injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79%, but direct airway or lung damage is unestablished; nasal bone hypoplasia is a skeletal defect.

basis: CNS developmental injury defines FAS; ocular defects, atrial septal defects and skeletal abnormalities each annotated 30-79%; dental abnormalities omitted by cap.
Defined by reproductive tract malformations; breast and reproductive organs lack axes. Later cancer and ovarian insufficiency are separate outcomes.
Prenatal methylmercury causes developmental brain injury; hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%. Visual impairment is commonly cerebral, without established intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment (80-99%) commonly reflects cerebral injury; direct eye or optic-nerve damage is not established.

basis: Cardiac and skeletal malformations define structural injury; VSD and skeletal anomalies occur in 80-99%. Hypertrichosis fades; other organ malformations lack reliable frequencies.
Developmental, digital and cleft-lip malformations define affected cases; nail hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. HPO frequencies conflict with the usually asymptomatic exposure description.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft lip is an oral structural malformation explicitly included in the embryopathy definition and annotated in 30-79% of affected cases.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: congenital nail aplasia/hypoplasia is structural appendage damage, annotated in 30-79%; it is less central than the defining developmental malformations.

basis: Defining CNS injury and craniofacial/limb skeletal malformations; micrognathia occurs in 80-99%, zygomatic hypoplasia in 30-79%; hydronephrosis occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: craniofacial/limb malformations are defining features, supported by micrognathia (80-99%) and zygomatic bone hypoplasia (30-79%).

basis: Gut/airway atresia and fistula define the embryopathy; hypothyroidism 80-99%, cardiac defects 30-79%. Skin, skull and urinary malformations omitted by cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypothyroidism 80-99% and thyroid abnormalities 30-79% support thyroid dysfunction; thyroid disease does not define the characteristic embryopathy pattern.

basis: Cardiac, skeletal and CNS malformations are core patterns; renal defects occur in 80-99%. Ocular, otologic and oral malformations, also annotated 80-99%, omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: CNS malformations are a major embryopathy pattern; microcephaly is annotated 80-99%, with hydrocephalus and brain/spinal malformations in 30-79%.

basis: Immune-mediated destructive hemispheric encephalitis causes seizures, cerebral atrophy and progressive neurological loss.

Infantile epilepsy with progressive encephalopathy and cortical atrophy; hypotonia and ataxia are manifestations of the neurologic disease.
Neonatal epilepsy syndrome; ictal apnea and cyanosis are transient manifestations without direct lung damage.
Defined neurovascular disorder of peripheral vessels and sensory nerve function; episodic skin redness does not establish skin damage.
Primary tumor of sinonasal olfactory neuroepithelium; nasal airways fall under pulmonary. Orbital or intracranial extension is not established as common.
Autoimmune destruction of red cells and platelets defines disease; bruising, jaundice and dyspnea do not establish additional organ damage.
Eye and skin anomalies define syndrome; genu varum and syndactyly occur in 80-99%, muscle atrophy in 30-79%. Thyroid abnormality (30-79%) lacks specified damage or dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: unspecified thyroid gland abnormality in 30-79% does not establish destructive pathology or endocrine dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal deformities and syndactyly occur in 80-99%, with muscle atrophy in 30-79%; these accompany the defining eye and skin phenotype.

basis: Congenital hypoplasia or absence of the femur; an isolated skeletal malformation.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and limb malformations define syndrome; dental abnormalities/reflux and auditory canal abnormalities are reported in 80-99%; hearing loss is common.
Progressive ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma; visual impairment/field loss occurs in 30-79% per HPO. Pigmentation alone is non-damaging; Cushing features are separate.
Superficial fibromatoses predominantly affect palmar/plantar fascia and related connective tissues; reproductive involvement is subtype-specific.
Benign fibroblastic tumor arising characteristically in aponeuroses, fascia and tendinous soft tissues.
Superficial dermal fibrous proliferation forming digital skin nodules; no established deeper locomotor involvement.
Segmental autonomic sympathetic dysfunction; flushing and sweating abnormalities do not establish intrinsic skin damage.
Congenital structural underdevelopment of the stomach causes severe feeding intolerance; associated anomalies are variable.
Pituitary ACTH deficiency with autoimmunity annotated in 80-99%; associated autoimmune diseases are separate. GI symptoms and weakness do not establish direct injury.
Congenital upper-lip cleft affects the mouth; frequent chronic otitis media is a separately diagnosed disease, so otologic involvement is excluded.
Defining cleft affects oral structures and the bony alveolar ridge/hard palate. Recurrent otitis is separately diagnosed; hearing impairment is below 30%.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary: the defining fissure crosses the bony alveolar ridge and hard palate, establishing a structural skeletal defect alongside oral involvement.

basis: Perineal hypospadias (80-99%) is a structural urethral defect. Other genital findings are reproductive; mixed blood lineages and pigment patches do not establish functional damage.

decisions.renal: primary: supplied HPO reports perineal hypospadias in 80-99%; the malformed urethra falls explicitly within the renal axis, despite the reproductive presentation.

basis: Congenital foot and ankle bone/joint malalignment, often with lower-leg muscle hypoplasia and other lower-limb malformations.
Infection of the internal structures of the eye.
Inherited renal magnesium-wasting disorder causing hypomagnesemia. Cramps, tetany and tremor do not establish additional muscle or nervous-system damage.
audit_reason: Add renal to primary: this disorder impairs renal magnesium conservation. Normal-range urinary magnesium is inappropriate during hypomagnesemia and does not establish normal tubular function.

basis: Congenital dysferlin-related skeletal myopathy; weakness and motor delay reflect muscle disease rather than primary nervous system damage.
Cleft lip affects oral anatomy; progressive retinal degeneration is the other defining feature.
Autism spectrum neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental and social impairment.
Congenital hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis; oculomotor findings arise from neurologic dysfunction.
Isolated congenital impairment of brain growth; neurodevelopmental disorder ancestry supports the neurologic axis.
Herniation of brain through a defining skull defect; visual deficits do not establish common intrinsic ocular damage.
Paroxysmal dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal contractions do not establish primary muscle damage.
Cleft lip/palate, deafness and sacral lipoma define syndrome; meningocele reported at 80-99%; hip dislocation at 80-99% omitted because of cap.
Congenital cleft involves the laryngeal airway and its separation from the upper digestive tract; recurrent infections are secondary complications.
The definition specifies a midline lower-lip cleft, affecting an oral structure; mandibular clefting is not required or established as common.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: despite the name and skeletal ancestor, the specific definition establishes only a lower-lip cleft; mandibular involvement is variable and unquantified.

basis: Mucocutaneous/GI hamartomas define disease; goiter 80-99%, neurodevelopmental deficits 30-79%; non-impairing conjunctival hamartomas and separate cancer risks excluded.
Congenital structural defect of the oral palate; middle-ear disease is a separately diagnosed complication.
Cleft palate, vertebral malformations and intellectual disability are defining features; external ear and facial morphology do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Congenital failure of sternal fusion; respiratory symptoms and infection susceptibility do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Defined by progressive sensorineural deafness, alopecia and hypogonadism with LH and GH deficiencies.
Severe skeletal dysplasia; respiratory insufficiency from thoracic restriction, cleft palate and hearing abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Nail hypoplasia omitted at cap; proptosis alone excluded.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79%; severe thoracic restriction produces substantial pulmonary functional loss rather than an isolated symptom.

basis: Defining fibrous overgrowth of gingivae; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Skin hyaline lesions, skeletal/connective-tissue abnormalities and gingival fibromatosis define the syndrome; gingival disease is characteristic despite occasional HPO coding.
Microphthalmia defines this umbrella; associated extraocular organ abnormalities vary by syndrome and cannot be generalized across the group.
Parasitic infection; damaging skin, lymphatic and ocular manifestations vary by subtype and are not established in most patients across the umbrella.
Congenital communication between the aorta and pulmonary artery; both are cardiovascular structures.
Congenital systemic arterial-to-venous communication; no additional organ is consistently damaged across locations.
Sporadic endogenous prion misfolding causes destructive CNS degeneration. Transmissibility alone does not establish infection; aspiration pneumonia and sepsis are separate secondary diseases.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: sporadic disease arises through endogenous prion misfolding; transmission potential alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism in this subtype.

basis: Congenital fistula directly connects the tracheobronchial tree with a hepatic bile duct; both structures define the anomaly.
Nail dystrophy and recurrent pilar cysts define disease; ocular inflammation 80-99% and blepharitis 30-79%; kidney stones are separately coded.
Bone dysplasia with defining hydrocephalus; dental enamel abnormalities occur in 30–79%. Proptosis and blue sclera alone do not establish ocular damage.
Osteochondrosis with avascular necrosis and structural damage of the navicular bone.
Progressive vertebral fusion and ankylosis define disease. Skin thickening is reported in 80-99%, but functional injury or destructive skin pathology is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: none: frequent skin thickening alone does not establish inflammation, fibrosis or impaired skin function meeting the damage requirement.

basis: Purine salvage disorder; neurologic dysfunction affects most patients across the severe and intermediate forms (>30%). Gout and urinary stones are separate diseases.
Lysosomal sphingolipid disorder with CNS and peripheral demyelination. Progressive optic atrophy and visual loss commonly exceed 30%; auditory brainstem delays are neurologic.
Sphingolipid storage causes central and peripheral demyelination; visual loss and hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%.
Lysosomal lipid storage disease with CNS demyelination; muscle atrophy reflects neurologic disease. Visual loss occurs in only 5-29%.
Benign ovarian epithelial tumor affects a reproductive organ; no endocrine dysfunction is defined.
Borderline epithelial tumor arising in the ovary; reproductive epithelial tissue is outside the axes.
Malignant germ cell tumor of the vagina; reproductive organs have no axis.
Tumour originates in the vagina, outside the axes; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish origin in locomotor muscle.
Malignant germ cell tumour arising in the ovary, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Progressive dystrophin-related skeletal myopathy defines symptomatic carriers; cardiomyopathy and ventricular abnormalities are annotated 5-29%.
Autoimmune skeletal-muscle necrosis; dysphagia (30-79%) reflects swallowing-muscle dysfunction, without established separate GI damage. Lung and cardiac lesions are <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: frequent dysphagia (30-79%) is attributable to affected skeletal swallowing muscles; it does not establish direct gastrointestinal tissue disease.

basis: Immune myositis; swallowing dysfunction from pharyngoesophageal muscle involvement and sclerodactyly each occur in 30-79%. Interstitial pulmonary abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dysphagia (30-79%) reflects direct inflammatory dysfunction of swallowing/upper esophageal muscles in myositis.

basis: Immune-mediated skeletal muscle rippling combined with myasthenia gravis, an autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder.
Supplied definition describes avian Marek disease: viral infection with peripheral nerve lymphoid infiltration; other organ involvement lacks frequency evidence.
Immune-mediated peripheral nerve demyelination; weakness reflects neuropathy. Respiratory abnormalities are very rare (1-4%).
Muscle-disorder spectrum with isolated muscle-derived CK elevation; absent weakness and nonfunctional microscopic changes do not establish additional organ damage.
Acquired disease of skeletal muscle; immune mechanisms apply to some subtypes rather than the entire umbrella.
Umbrella of progressive skeletal muscle dystrophies; additional organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Muscle degeneration, cataracts and conduction defects are defining features; intrinsic endocrine dysfunction, including insulin resistance and hypogonadism, affects >30%; four-organ cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac conduction defects are explicitly part of the disease definition.
decisions.ocular: primary: cataracts are explicitly part of the disease definition and common across the principal subtypes.

basis: Inherited distal skeletal muscle disease; cardiac and respiratory manifestations vary by subtype and are not established across most patients.
Umbrella of inherited skeletal-muscle inclusion-body disorders; dementia, ophthalmoplegia and respiratory failure are subtype-dependent.
Bulbar and spinal motor-neuron degeneration causes progressive denervation, muscle atrophy and loss of skeletal-muscle function in most patients.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: progressive denervation causes actual muscle atrophy and loss of function in most patients; muscle injury need not be primary myopathy.

basis: Umbrella for disorders of skeletal muscle relaxation; multisystem damage in myotonic dystrophy cannot be generalized across all subtypes.
Periodic paralysis is a disorder of skeletal-muscle excitability; electrolyte abnormalities are not universal across the umbrella.
Viral infection directly inflames skeletal muscle; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to this umbrella.
Bacterial infection directly inflames skeletal muscle.
Parasitic infection directly involving skeletal muscle.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic infiltration damages the gastrointestinal wall; eosinophilia is not blood-cell damage, and associated allergic diseases are separate.
Fungal infection directly inflames and damages skeletal muscle.
The umbrella predominantly comprises muscular dystrophies and structural protein myopathies; neural or cardiac involvement is not shared across most subtypes.
Sarcoglycan deficiency primarily causes muscular dystrophy. Cardiomyopathy varies markedly by subtype and is not clearly common across the umbrella; respiratory weakness is muscular.
Alpha-sarcoglycan deficiency causes skeletal muscle dystrophy; neurologic ancestry does not establish nerve disease.
Beta-sarcoglycanopathy causes skeletal muscle dystrophy; cardiomyopathy affects roughly one third or more of patients across reported series.
Gamma-sarcoglycanopathy causes skeletal muscular dystrophy. Cardiomyopathy and respiratory failure are variable and do not reliably meet the 30% threshold.
Predominantly skeletal-muscle dystrophy; cardiac involvement is variable and not securely ≥30% across this umbrella. A cardiomyopathy subtype alone does not establish frequency.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy is a recognized subtype, but the evidence does not securely establish cardiac damage in ≥30% across delta-sarcoglycanopathy.
