basis: Dysferlinopathies directly damage skeletal muscle; neuromuscular classification does not establish primary nerve disease.
Caveolin-3 disorders primarily affect skeletal muscle; cardiac or neural damage is not established across most of the umbrella.
Dystrophin defects primarily damage skeletal muscle; intrinsic cardiomyopathy affects well over 30% across the usual dystrophinopathy course.
Perlecan disorders encompass skeletal dysplasia and neuromuscular dysfunction, including Schwartz-Jampel syndrome; no common additional axis established.
TRIM32 neuromuscular disease chiefly comprises skeletal muscular dystrophy. Retinal, renal and endocrine findings belong to the Bardet-Biedl subtype.
Defective alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation causes muscular dystrophy; brain and eye abnormalities characterize severe subtypes rather than the entire umbrella.
FKRP dystroglycan glycosylation disorder causes muscular dystrophy; cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-50% in predominant limb-girdle disease. Brain/eye defects characterize severe minority subtypes.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-50% of the predominant FKRP limb-girdle phenotype and reflects direct myocardial dystroglycan dysfunction.

basis: Narcolepsy type 1 entails loss of hypothalamic orexin neurons, usually attributed to immune-mediated destruction. Autonomic symptoms do not establish other organ damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: typical narcolepsy type 1 is regarded as immune-mediated loss of orexin neurons; rare inherited forms do not define the umbrella's usual mechanism.

basis: Ataxia, amyotrophy and deafness define the syndrome (80-99% each); delayed puberty/testicular abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Pigment patches (30-79%) lack demonstrated functional skin damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: hypopigmented patches occur in 30-79%, but pigment change alone does not demonstrate skin injury or loss of function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: amyotrophy is a defining component of the named syndrome, with skeletal muscle atrophy in 80-99%; persistent tissue loss qualifies despite neurogenic origin.

basis: Intellectual disability and epilepsy define this neurologic syndrome; no other organ involvement applies across the group.
Definition combines cerebral gigantism with jaw-bone cysts and basal-cell nevoid skin disease.
Frontal cortical malformation causes developmental impairment and spastic paresis; motor deficits arise from brain disease.
Cerebellar degeneration and retinal dystrophy define SCA7; congestive heart failure is annotated frequent (30-79%). Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; mucosae generally spared, and peripheral eosinophilia does not establish blood-organ damage.
Inherited deficiency of parathyroid function; autoimmune and syndromic manifestations are not shared across this umbrella.
Inherited parathyroid overactivity; bone loss commonly affects at least ~30% in sustained primary forms. Transient neonatal disease differs; renal stones are separate disease.
Glioma arises along the optic nerve and intracranial visual pathways; optic atrophy and visual impairment are characteristic. Endocrine and other neurologic complications are occasional.
Autoinflammatory spectrum; progressive sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly 40-60%. Rash is transient; destructive CNS and joint disease cluster in severe subtypes.
Paraprotein-associated, typically immune-mediated peripheral nerve/root injury; associated gammopathy alone does not establish blood-cell damage.
Loss of dermal elasticity defines the umbrella; pulmonary, vascular and skeletal disease vary substantially by subtype.
Peripheral axonal damage defines disease; immune causation is uncertain across Ig classes. Associated gammopathy is separate; muscle wasting reflects denervation.
POMT1 dystroglycanopathy combines defective O-glycosylation, muscular dystrophy and characteristic neurodevelopmental disease; ocular damage varies by subtype.
O-mannosylation defect causing dystroglycan-related muscular dystrophy; developmental/cognitive impairment is common (>30%). Severe ocular abnormalities vary by subtype.
Myofibrillar protein defects cause structural skeletal myopathy; cardiac involvement varies by subtype and is not established as common across this umbrella.
Umbrella encompasses desmin-related skeletal myopathies and cardiomyopathy; the neurogenic subtype does not establish neurologic involvement across the group.
Parent identifies alphaB-crystallin-related myofibrillar muscle disease; cardiomyopathy and cataracts vary by subtype and are not established in >=30% across this group.
Filamin C myofibrillar disease damages skeletal muscle; cardiomyopathy occurs in approximately one third of myofibrillar cases.
ZASP-related myofibrillar protein defects cause skeletal myopathy; cardiac involvement is not established in at least 30% across this concept.
The child concept identifies titin-related skeletal myopathy; a broad neurologic ancestor does not establish nerve disease, and cardiac involvement varies by subtype.
Telethonin-related muscular dystrophy predominates. Cardiomyopathy is a distinct listed subtype and is not established in most patients across this umbrella.
Alpha-actin defects cause nemaline skeletal myopathy; respiratory muscle weakness alone does not establish direct lung damage.
Nebulin-related nemaline myopathies directly affect skeletal muscle; broad nervous-system ancestry does not establish neural damage.
Umbrella of MYH7 skeletal myopathies; neither neuronal damage nor cardiomyopathy is established across most patients.
Selenoprotein N-related congenital myopathy affects skeletal muscle; respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Muscular dystrophy defines the group; epidermolysis bullosa with skin fragility affects most reported plectin muscular dystrophy cases, although isolated muscle forms occur.
SERCA1-related disorders represented by the children are intrinsic skeletal myopathies; the broad neuromuscular ancestry does not establish nerve damage.
Inherited rhegmatogenous detachment directly affects the retina.
Inherited cholesterol/bile-acid metabolism defect; cholestasis, hepatitis and hepatic steatosis reported in 80-99%. Atherosclerosis is a separately diagnosed downstream disease.
Copper-overload disorder causing hepatocyte necrosis, fibrosis and cirrhosis; urinary copper elevation does not establish kidney damage.
Defined by inflammatory retinal vasculitis, retinal arterial aneurysms and neuroretinitis; retinal vessels fall within cardiovascular.
Scleral abnormalities cause uveal effusion and retinal detachment; this syndrome is not inherently immune-mediated despite the supplied panuveitis parent.
Lens protein-induced immune inflammation directly affects intraocular structures.
Ischemic ulceration of rectal mucosa; anemia occurs in only 5-29%.
Defined neurologic disorder with recurrent nocturnal hemiplegic attacks; persistent developmental impairment is explicitly absent.
Neurologic disorder with alternating hemiplegic episodes; no additional organ damage established across the umbrella.
Urothelial carcinoma originating in the bladder; bladder is included in the renal axis.
Defining abnormalities involve nails, skin and hair; acanthosis-like lesions do not establish an endocrine disorder.
Defining triad of pulmonary fibrosis, hepatic nodular regenerative hyperplasia and marrow hypoplasia; myocardial fibrosis occurs in only 5-29%.
Cerebral motor disorder affecting all four limbs; persistent muscle-tendon shortening and fixed contractures develop in more than 30% over the typical course.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed contractures and structural muscle-tendon shortening affect >30% over the course of quadriplegic cerebral palsy, beyond altered tone alone.

basis: Primary carcinoma arising from hepatocytes; underlying viral hepatitis or cirrhosis is a separate disease.
Persistent central vestibular motion-perception dysfunction; peripheral ear damage is not established, and ocular findings are occasional (5-29%).
Immune-mediated peripheral nerve and nerve-root injury; respiratory weakness and autonomic symptoms do not establish direct lung or heart damage.
Joint laxity, pectus carinatum and genu valgum define skeletal involvement; facial appearance alone does not establish damage to another axis.
Congenital fusion of the temporomandibular joint. Feeding and breathing difficulties reflect restricted jaw opening without established additional organ damage.
Benign blood-vessel tumor arising in the dermis and subcutis.
Benign vascular neoplasm; anatomical sites vary across this umbrella, so no additional site applies consistently.
Persistent neurodevelopmental impairment of academic information processing and learning.
Developmental language disorder is a neurodevelopmental impairment, supported by learning-disability ancestry.
Inherited neurologic disorders causing episodic cerebellar dysfunction; vertigo does not establish peripheral vestibular damage.
Congenital capillary malformations are vascular lesions, predominantly located in skin; visceral disease is not shared across the umbrella.
Infiltrative vascular tumor commonly involving skin; platelet trapping, hemolysis and consumptive coagulopathy occur in 30-79%.
Cutaneous and visceral vascular tumors; hepatic involvement in most, anemia/coagulopathy 80-99% in HPO. Renal insufficiency, also annotated 80-99%, is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: thrombocytopenia, anemia and coagulation abnormalities are annotated 80-99%; substantial consumptive blood dysfunction merits priority under the cap.
decisions.renal: none under cap: renal insufficiency is annotated 80-99%, but defining vascular/skin disease, predominant hepatic tumors and severe blood dysfunction take priority.

basis: Fibroblastic soft-tissue neoplasm with variable anatomical origin; pleural and other organ-specific locations represent subtypes rather than uniform multisystem damage.
Lysosomal cystine storage with defining kidney and eye damage; myopathy 80-99% and rickets/osteomalacia 30-79%. Organ enlargement alone does not establish hepatic or splenic dysfunction.
Congenital absence or severe shortening of limb bones defines this skeletal malformation.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with persistent impairment; GI dysmotility occurs in 80–99%. Eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction; adrenal synonyms conflict with the definition.
Abnormal hemoglobin causes absent or mild hemolytic anemia; no common additional organ damage is established.
Inherited hemoglobin variant causing generally mild microcytic anemia; no common extrahematologic damage.
Complement-mediated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define aHUS; direct microvascular endothelial injury and thrombosis are intrinsic in essentially all cases.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: defining thrombotic microangiopathy directly injures capillaries in essentially all cases; cardiovascular includes microvessels, not just the heart.

basis: Inherited ovarian cancer arises in a reproductive organ; ovarian tumour origin alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Hereditary ovarian malignancy affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; additional cancer risks are not direct organ involvement.
Primary mixed epithelial and mesenchymal neoplasm of the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Lymphatic malformation, intestinal lymphangiectasia and ID define syndrome. Immune depletion occurs in 80-99%; cap excludes lymphopenia (80-99%) and glaucoma (30-79%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly part of the syndrome's definition and occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.infectious_immune: involved: immunoglobulin depletion occurs in 80-99% from lymphatic/enteric losses; secondary immune dysfunction is an organ consequence of the lymphatic disorder.

basis: Malignant mixed epithelial and fibrous tumour originating in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Primary uterine corpus malignancy; epithelial and sarcomatous histology does not change its reproductive site of origin.
Tumor originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish a locomotor muscle origin.
Tumour originates in uterine corpus smooth muscle, a reproductive site outside the axes; visceral smooth muscle is not skeletal muscle.
Tumour originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; neuroectodermal histology does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Autoimmune inflammation of liver parenchyma; arthralgia does not establish joint damage, and extrahepatic inflammatory lesions are <30%.
Carcinoma of the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no designated axis.
Carcinoma arises in the uterine corpus, outside the specified axes; bleeding alone does not establish hematologic disease.
Carcinoma of the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Primary uterine carcinoma; reproductive organs have no axis. Neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine disease; paraneoplastic syndromes are optional.
Endometrial tumor of a reproductive organ; neuroendocrine differentiation and possible ectopic secretion do not establish endocrine gland damage.
Carcinoma originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; transitional histology does not imply urinary origin.
Tumor originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; germ-cell histology does not establish endocrine disease.
Primary cervical epithelial malignancy; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Tumour originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Sarcoma arising in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ; mesenchymal histology alone does not establish musculoskeletal origin.
Hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies occur in 80-99% and directly affect urethral anatomy; reproductive tissue differences alone do not establish endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.renal: primary: frequent hypospadias and urogenital sinus malformations establish congenital urethral involvement; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.

basis: Tumour originates in the uterine cervix, outside the axes; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Tumour originates in cervical smooth muscle, a reproductive site outside the axes; metastatic tendencies do not establish common organ involvement.
Tumor originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; neural differentiation does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Carcinoma originating in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Malignant germ-cell tumor of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Developmental impairment and seizures define the syndrome alongside obesity (80-99%); delayed puberty occurs in 30-79%. Dysmorphic features do not establish additional organ damage.
Skeletal defects and intellectual impairment define the syndrome. Urinary tract anomalies and lung hypoplasia each occur in 30-79%; cap omits cleft palate (30-79%).
Cerebral neuronal migration malformation with seizures in 80-99%.
Congenital retinal signaling dysfunction causes stationary night blindness and reduced visual acuity; no independent neurologic involvement is established.
Defining intestinal aganglionosis, distal phalangeal hypoplasia and absent/hypoplastic nails; all three are core syndrome features.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by progressive neuronal and retinal degeneration; these features characterize most patients across the group.
Forebrain and defining oral malformations; clefts 80-99%. Eye defects and endocrine dysfunction 30-79%; choanal atresia (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: the definition includes facial malformation, with oral clefts in 80-99% and characteristic dental anomalies; mouth and teeth belong to this axis.

basis: Isolated genetic hearing impairment from auditory-system abnormalities; impaired spoken-language acquisition does not establish a separate neurologic disorder.
Isolated inherited hearing loss involving the auditory apparatus; no syndromic organ involvement.
Brain, caudal skeletal and severe eye malformations define syndrome; renal insufficiency affects 30-79%. Cap excludes cleft lip/palate and nasal malformations.
Congenital atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance with associated cardiac structural and conduction abnormalities.
Congenital malposition of the great arteries is a structural cardiovascular disorder.
Congenital transposition of the great arteries with associated cardiac malformation.
An inborn coenzyme A metabolic defect causes neurodegeneration; retinal dystrophy and optic pallor occur in 30-79%. Stiffness and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: PKAN is an established inborn disorder of coenzyme A metabolism, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis alongside neurologic disease.

basis: An inherited coenzyme A biosynthesis disorder causes progressive brain neurodegeneration. Retinopathy, blindness and optic atrophy occur in only 1-4% of the atypical form.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: pantothenate kinase deficiency is an inborn defect of coenzyme A metabolism, so the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Perinatal lysosomal storage disease with defining severe neonatal hepatic disease; direct pulmonary injury in >=30% is not established; neurologic disease may not emerge before early death.

decisions.hepatic: primary: severe neonatal hepatic disease defines this perinatal phenotype.
decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary infiltration can occur, but direct pulmonary injury in >=30% is not established; respiratory distress alone is insufficient.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining early neurodegeneration; hepatic storage with cholestatic injury affects roughly >=30% of severe infantile cases. Splenic enlargement alone is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenic storage and enlargement are common, but functional splenic impairment or blood-cell damage in >=30% is not established.

basis: Lysosomal lipid storage with defining late-infantile neurodegeneration; hepatic dysfunction and splenic blood dysfunction are not established in >=30% of this subgroup.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenic storage and enlargement do not by themselves establish impaired blood-organ function; qualifying dysfunction is not established in >=30%.
decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly or storage alone is insufficient; functionally damaging liver disease is not established in >=30% of this neurologic-onset subgroup.

basis: Lysosomal lipid-storage disorder with defining juvenile neurodegeneration; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish common hepatic or hematologic functional damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenic storage and enlargement are common, but damaging hypersplenism or other hematologic dysfunction in >=30% is not established for this juvenile subtype.

basis: Lysosomal lipid-trafficking disorder defined here by adult-onset neurodegeneration; supranuclear gaze palsy is neurologic. Common damaging visceral involvement is not established.
Diffuse cutaneous venous malformations; limb bone hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%, with cortical/trabecular abnormalities and muscle dysfunction in 30-79%.
The poisoning itself is defined by gastrointestinal mucosal injury, myelosuppression and alopecia; occasional hand-foot syndrome adds no additional axis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: alopecia is explicitly included among the poisoning's defining toxicities; hair is covered by this axis.

basis: Neuronopathic storage disorder; skeletal/joint disease >80% and obstructive airway disease >70%. Common valvular disease (>50%) and hearing loss omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: valvular storage disease affects >50%, but is omitted at the cap in favor of very frequent skeletal disease and severe airway involvement.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: airway glycosaminoglycan deposition and structural airway dysfunction affect >70%; direct obstruction contributes substantially to mortality.

basis: GAG storage with defining skeletal disease; valvular disease and airway obstruction each affect >50% over the course. Common hearing loss and nerve entrapment omitted at cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal disease and short stature are defining features of attenuated MPS II, supported by its skeletal-storage ancestry

basis: JC virus infection directly destroys CNS myelin. Visual deficits arise from brain injury; underlying immunodeficiency is a separate condition.
Congenital sensory/autonomic neuropathy with absent pain perception; hyperhidrosis alone does not establish skin damage.
Infantile interstitial lung disease; glycogen-containing interstitial cells do not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Infantile interstitial lung disease with pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia; no systemic endocrine disorder is defined.
Inherited surfactant metabolism disorder causing alveolar surfactant accumulation and chronic pulmonary dysfunction.
Acquired hypertrophic disease of myocardium; systemic findings of individual etiologic subtypes do not apply across this umbrella.
Contractures and skin hyalinosis define disease; immunodeficiency/thymic hypoplasia and GI malabsorption each 80-99%. Adrenal abnormalities lack demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immunodeficiency and thymic aplasia/hypoplasia are each reported in 80-99%; the mechanism axis is added whenever immunodeficiency applies.

basis: Cardiac hypertrophy/cardiomyopathy attributed to intensive athletic training.
Inherited dilated cardiomyopathy; extracardiac manifestations of individual syndromic subtypes do not characterize most patients across this umbrella.
Dilated cardiomyopathy directly impairs cardiac structure and function; underlying causes vary across this umbrella.
Inherited restrictive myocardial disease; systemic manifestations of particular listed subtypes do not apply across this umbrella.
Inherited myocardial degeneration and ventricular arrhythmias define the disease.
Absent cerebral hemispheres; sensorineural hearing impairment 80-99% and pituitary atrophy 30-79%. Cortical blindness does not establish eye damage.
Restrictive cardiomyopathy directly impairs myocardial filling; systemic deposition, inflammation and other organ injury depend on the underlying subtype.
Hydrocephalus, intellectual disability and hypogonadism define syndrome; mitral prolapse and skeletal defects each annotated 100%.
Congenital cerebral ventricular enlargement; supplied HPO annotations place structural iris coloboma and strabismus at 30-79%. Optic atrophy and hearing loss are only 1-4%.
Nephrotic FSGS and congenital hydrocephalus define organ disease. Blue sclerae and thin skin lack documented functional impairment.

decisions.ocular: none: blue sclerae are a descriptive color change without documented visual impairment or damaging ocular disease.

basis: Anti-HLA alloimmune sensitization is an immune disorder; renal failure is an associated pre-existing condition, not damage caused by sensitization.
Defining keratoderma and motor/sensory neuropathy; fixed pes cavus deformity occurs in 80-99%.
Skin disease and neurodegeneration define XP/CS; retinopathy/optic atrophy and hearing loss occur in 80-99%; arteriosclerosis (80-99%) omitted by cap.
Autoimmune skin fibrosis; lung fibrosis 30-79% and GI dysfunction in most. Musculoskeletal damage omitted by cap; renal insufficiency and heart failure each <30%.
Neonatal osteosclerotic skeletal dysplasia with abnormal cortical bone formation.
Autoimmune skin fibrosis and Raynaud-associated vasculopathy define disease; esophageal dysfunction/reflux occurs in 30-79%. Pulmonary fibrosis and PAH are only 5-29%.
Autoimmune systemic microvasculopathy without skin fibrosis; esophageal dysfunction ~70-90% and interstitial lung disease ~40-60%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: structural microvascular injury is intrinsic to systemic sclerosis; this rests on the vasculopathy, beyond transient Raynaud symptoms.

basis: Defined by macrothrombocytopenia with platelet dysfunction and mitral valve insufficiency; bruising and epistaxis are bleeding manifestations.
Colonic adenomatous polyposis defines AFAP; gastric and duodenal polyps share the same axis. Extracolonic tumors are minority findings or separate diseases.
Defined by Joubert cerebellar malformation and retinal dystrophy; respiratory abnormalities reflect central control dysfunction rather than direct airway or lung disease.
Inherited primary parathyroid overactivity; skeletal mineral loss affects about a third or more. Kidney stones are separate complications.
Embryopathy in non-PKU offspring: microcephaly/intellectual disability and congenital heart defects define it; maternal metabolic disease is not the child's diagnosis.
Autoimmune inflammatory myopathy with characteristic skin lesions; interstitial lung disease and pulmonary fibrosis occur in roughly 30% or more.
Poikiloderma and cataracts 10/10; skeletal anomalies and dental defects 30-79%. Ovarian insufficiency (2/5 females) omitted by cap.
Poikiloderma and skeletal defects define RTS2. Microphthalmia 13/13; dental delay 42/42 and hypoplasia 2/2. Intellectual disability 13/41 omitted at cap; tumors are separate risks.
Corpus callosum demyelination defines the disease; alcoholism, malnutrition and vitamin deficiency are associated conditions rather than additional organ damage caused by it.
Combined cranial-nerve hyperactivity syndrome classified as cranial neuralgia and neuropathy; no additional organ damage established.
Glossopharyngeal nerve disorder; referred ear, tongue and throat pain does not establish damage to those organs.
Facial nerve/movement disorder causing rippling contractions; contractions alone do not establish direct skeletal muscle damage.
Neuralgia and neuropathy of cranial nerves define a neurologic disorder.
Confetti-like atrophic skin macules; dermis disorder ancestry establishes cutaneous rather than retinal disease.
Severe intellectual disability and seizures define this neurodevelopmental syndrome; episodic breathing dysregulation does not establish lung damage.
Chronic erosive scalp inflammation causes scarring alopecia; inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Acquired lanugo hair growth; glossitis and tongue enlargement occur in 30-79%. Associated cancers are separate diseases; eyelid hair changes do not establish eye damage.
Generalized congenital lanugo hair; dental abnormalities and hearing impairment each occur in 80-99%.
Umbrella for inherited poikiloderma; neutropenia, tendon disease and pulmonary involvement are subtype-specific.
Renal resistance to vasopressin causes defective water conservation and hypernatremia in 80-99%; neurological sequelae are uncommon.
Hypogonadotropic hormone deficiency and frontoparietal hair loss jointly define the syndrome.
Hypogonadism, mitral prolapse and intellectual disability define the syndrome; metacarpal and ulnar abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Hair findings omitted under the four-axis cap.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and retinal degeneration define syndrome; skeletal disease/osteoporosis in 80-99% and dental abnormalities in 30-79% per HPO.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism defect; neurologic dysfunction and myopathy commonly affect roughly 30% or more; other organ involvement varies by subtype.
PTH deficiency; myopathy 80–99%, cataracts and dental enamel defects 30–79%. Provoked seizures and nonimpairing brain calcifications do not establish neurologic damage.
Neonatal insulin deficiency causes diabetes; neurologic or exocrine pancreatic abnormalities are restricted to particular subtypes.
Cerebellar hypoplasia and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; visual impairment, optic atrophy and neurologic abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Destructive bilateral basal ganglia degeneration defines disease; dysphagia and hypotonia reflect neurologic dysfunction; recurrent respiratory infections are separate episodes.
Foveal hypoplasia, cataracts and optic atrophy define ocular disease; hyperpigmentation alone does not establish skin damage.
Pontocerebellar and anterior horn degeneration define PCH1; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%, optic atrophy/visual loss in 30-79%. Respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
Severe renal hypoplasia with reduced nephron number and renal dysfunction in 80-99%; extrarenal abnormalities are very rare.
Permanent thyroid hormone deficiency present from birth; neurologic injury is not established in most patients receiving usual care.
Congenital thyroid hormone deficiency caused by dysfunction of the hypothalamic-pituitary thyroid-regulating system.
Congenital pituitary/thyroid hormone deficiency; neurodevelopmental delay and epiphyseal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%; hearing and optic abnormalities are occasional.
Congenital thyroid hormone deficiency from peripheral metabolism/action defects; neurologic damage is not established across this umbrella.
Transient congenital thyroid hormone deficiency with goiter; delayed ossification and neonatal symptoms do not establish lasting skeletal or neurologic damage.
Hypotrichosis, intellectual disability and complete finger syndactyly define the syndrome. Advanced tooth eruption alone does not establish dental damage.
Duplicated penile urethral anatomy and hypospadias affect the urinary axis (30-79%); associated anal atresia occurs in 30-79%. Other renal anomalies are occasional.
Ichthyosis and microcephaly with tetraplegia define skin and nervous-system disease; nonspecific muscle abnormalities do not establish a separate myopathy.
Cerebellar and autonomic neurodegeneration; bladder, swallowing and breathing abnormalities reflect neural dysfunction rather than direct visceral injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: stridor and central apnea reflect neural dysfunction; direct airway or lung injury is not established.
decisions.renal: none: frequent neurogenic bladder dysfunction reflects autonomic degeneration rather than direct urinary tract injury.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: neuromuscular dysphagia and constipation reflect neural dysfunction without established direct gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Hereditary carcinoma of the breast; breast has no axis, and other cancers are separate diseases.
Umbrella of inherited retinal and macular dystrophies; no common extraocular damage established.
Systemic vasculopathy and pulmonary injury define it; inflammatory muscle injury with weakness affects ~50%, and peripheral neuropathy ~32-55%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: sensory neuropathy ~55%, with direct axonal injury ([cohort](https://ehp.niehs.nih.gov/doi/pdf/10.1289/ehp.111-1241614)).
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: muscle injury with weakness affects ~50%; inflammatory myopathy is documented ([pathology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1654352/)).

basis: Autoimmune thyroid disease defines syndrome; gastritis/celiac disease and macrocytic anemia each occur in 30-79% as components of the syndrome.
Autoimmune endocrine syndrome; component atrophic gastritis/celiac disease and macrocytic anemia each occur in 30-79%; skin and liver manifestations are <30%.
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with QT prolongation define the syndrome.
Vasculitis with pulmonary artery aneurysms and venous thrombosis. Pulmonary vessels belong to cardiovascular; transient amaurosis does not establish ocular damage.
Fungal infection; skin/nail infection and sinusitis/pneumonia each annotated 30-79%. Keratitis 1-4%; neutropenia and immunodeficiency are predisposing conditions.
Aggressive autoimmune CNS demyelination causes rapidly progressive neurologic disability.
Inflammatory immune-mediated CNS demyelination with concentric cerebral lesions.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy with congenital ptosis and early cataracts explicitly defining this subtype. Occasional neutropenia is excluded.

decisions.ocular: primary: congenital ptosis and early cataract are explicitly part of this subtype's defining phenotype, rather than incidental complications.

basis: Congenital heart defects and upper-limb skeletal malformations define this group.
Deafness, psychomotor impairment and cleft palate are explicitly defining features; PDA/pulmonary arterial hypertension occur in 30-79%. Cleft palate qualifies despite its 5-29% annotation.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate is explicitly part of the disease definition; defining oral malformations qualify without meeting the involvement frequency threshold.

basis: Localized dermal elastic-tissue disorder; definition explicitly excludes systemic involvement.
Localized abnormal elastic tissue in the dermis; definition explicitly reports no systemic involvement.
Localized dermal elastic-tissue disorder causing persistent skin laxity and impaired recoil; hyperesthesia alone does not establish nerve damage.
Benign fibrous connective tissue tumor typically arising in deep infrascapular soft tissue.
Acquired cutaneous elastic tissue disorder; definition explicitly excludes the retinal and vascular manifestations of inherited PXE.
Localized dermal connective-tissue nevus involving elastic fibers; this concept excludes associated osteopoikilosis.
Localized dermal connective-tissue abnormality producing cutaneous papules, nodules or plaques.
Localized loss of dermal elastic tissue causes persistent flaccid skin.
Dermal elastin loss defines disease; joint laxity, hyperlordosis and tibial abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Irregular dentition and high palate do not establish oral functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: irregular dentition and high palate occur in 30-79%, but these annotations alone do not establish destructive or functionally damaging oral disease.

basis: Acquired loss of dermal elastic tissue causes lax skin; common extracutaneous damage is not established across acquired forms.
Localized dermal elastic tissue disorder producing persistent fibrous papules.
Acquired loss of elastic fibers confined to the papillary dermis; the definition explicitly excludes systemic involvement.
Loss of elastic fibers in the mid dermis causes persistent skin wrinkling and laxity; no established common systemic involvement.
Cold-reactive autoantibodies cause immune destruction of red blood cells; vascular symptoms alone do not establish lasting vessel damage.
Central disorder of sleep-wake regulation causing persistent hypersomnolence and sleep inertia.
Central disorder of sleep-wake regulation causing persistent excessive daytime sleepiness.
Ingested preformed botulinum toxin blocks neuromuscular and autonomic transmission; ocular, swallowing and respiratory findings reflect neural dysfunction.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: foodborne botulism is intoxication by preformed toxin, rather than infection or an immune-mediated disease; broad infectious ancestry does not override its definition.

basis: Hereditary peripheral motor and sensory axonal neuropathy; muscle weakness and atrophy result from denervation.
Polyomavirus infection directly affects cutaneous hair follicles, producing follicular papules and keratin spicules.
Severe intellectual disability, epilepsy and brain malformations define the syndrome. Ocular and skeletal abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Eyelid, eye-movement and lacrimal defects define syndrome; tricuspid regurgitation occurs in 30-79%. Common minor skeletal dysmorphism does not establish functional skeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: maxillary hypoplasia and clinodactyly occur in 80-99%, but are described as minor dysmorphism without established skeletal functional impairment.

basis: Developmental delay, hearing loss and VSD occur in 80-99%; Duane anomaly in 80-99% impairs eye movement. Urinary reflux (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Severe developmental impairment and seizures define the syndrome; constipation, hirsutism and minor skeletal variants do not establish additional organ damage.
Valve disease and intellectual disability define the syndrome; structural eyelid dysfunction from ptosis occurs in 30-79%. Short stature and delayed bone age alone do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis is structural eyelid dysfunction reported in 30-79%, meeting the supplied frequency threshold.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and delayed skeletal maturation define syndrome; myopia occurs in 30-79%. Seizures remain within the neurologic axis.
Primary B-cell deficiency impairs antibody production. Recurrent infections are separately diagnosed diseases; rash and diarrhea do not establish intrinsic organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a B-cell deficiency with impaired lymphocyte development; B lymphocytes are blood cells, so the explicit blood-cell disease rule applies.

basis: Defined by deficient antibody production within a syndrome; additional organ manifestations vary across subtypes and are not shared by most patients.
Insulin-receptor autoantibodies cause metabolic dysfunction. Acanthosis is a nondamaging skin marker; nephritis and leukopenia reflect associated autoimmune disease.

decisions.dermatologic: none: acanthosis nigricans occurs in 80-99%, but persistent pigmentation and thickening alone do not establish destructive skin disease or loss of function.

basis: Asbestos-induced pulmonary fibrosis and pleural disease; cor pulmonale occurs in <30%, and associated cancers are separate diseases.
Ear, CNS and cardiac malformations define embryopathy; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Nail hypoplasia (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Infection produces toxin causing neuromuscular junction dysfunction; respiratory weakness, ocular motor signs and constipation reflect neural dysfunction.
Defined by spontaneous medium-artery dissections; renal artery involvement is vascular and does not establish kidney injury.
Joint instability, bone fragility and abnormal skin define the syndrome. Blue sclera alone does not establish ocular damage.
Skin and nail keratinization abnormalities and persistent oral mucosal leukokeratosis define the disease; oral leukoplakia occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal leukokeratosis is explicitly part of the disease definition and occurs in 30-79%.

basis: Subcutaneous parasite causes blistering and skin ulceration; arthritis and restricted joint mobility are reported in 30-79%. GI symptoms lack organ damage.
The supplied definition centers on childhood CNS rhabdoid tumors; renal and other extraneural tumors are variable and lack a demonstrated 30% frequency here.
Autoimmune drug reaction; supplied HPO reports pericarditis and cytopenias in 80-99%. Renal labs alone do not establish nephritis, uncommon in classic DIL; muscle/joint pain alone is insufficient.
Macroglossia, abdominal wall defects, lateralized overgrowth and persistent hyperinsulinism are major diagnostic features; transient hypoglycemia and tumor risk add no organs.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: persistent hyperinsulinism is a cardinal diagnostic feature; this does not rely on transient neonatal hypoglycemia.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized skeletal overgrowth and abdominal wall defects are major defining structural abnormalities.

basis: Macroglossia and omphalocele define this subtype; abdominal-wall muscular defects and somatic overgrowth support musculoskeletal. Transient hypoglycemia and tumour risks add no damaged organ.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital abdominal-wall muscular defects, especially omphalocele, are core CDKN1C-related features; somatic overgrowth also characterizes the syndrome.

basis: Defining BWS features include macroglossia, hyperinsulinism, abdominal wall defects and lateralized overgrowth. Subtype frequencies are sparse; organ enlargement and tumor risks add no axes.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized skeletal/soft-tissue overgrowth and abdominal wall defects are cardinal BWS features. [Consensus](https://doi.org/10.1038/nrendo.2017.166)

basis: Macroglossia, hyperinsulinism and lateralized skeletal overgrowth/abdominal-wall defects are defining BWS features; tumour predisposition is a risk.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hyperinsulinism is a major BWS diagnostic criterion; transient neonatal hypoglycemia alone would not suffice.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized skeletal overgrowth and abdominal-wall defects are major structural features, rather than generalized large size alone.

basis: Skeletal growth disorder with delayed bone maturation and clinodactyly (30–79%); developmental impairment and hypoglycemia <30%; blue sclerae do not establish ocular damage.
Defines skeletal growth restriction, delayed skeletal maturation and limb asymmetry. Crowded teeth alone do not establish functional damage; neurologic and hypoglycemic features are under 30%.
Skeletal growth disorder with delayed skeletal maturation and clinodactyly in 30-79%; neurologic abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Syndromic skeletal growth restriction with characteristic fifth-finger clinodactyly. Neurologic, cardiac and hypoglycemic manifestations are annotated as occasional.
Cerebral arterial aneurysm; seizures and hemiparesis each annotated at 30-79% support neurological involvement. Hemorrhage itself is only 5-29%.
Congenital sensorineural hearing loss and progressive retinal degeneration are defining features.
Progressive hearing loss, vestibular dysfunction and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; hearing and retinal abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Ineffective erythropoiesis and marrow expansion cause skeletal deformity/osteoporosis (30–79%); hepatic, cardiac and endocrine injury is minority and often transfusion-related.
Ineffective erythropoiesis; osteoporosis 80-99% and chronic skin ulcers 30-79%. Hepatic, renal and cardiovascular damage below 30%; iron imbalance alone is insufficient.
Deficient delta/beta globin synthesis causes microcytic anemia; no common direct extrahematologic damage established.
Hemoglobinopathy causing moderate hemolytic anemia; common splenomegaly remains within the haematologic axis.
Hemoglobinopathy with anemia; immunodeficiency annotated at 80-99% supports immune involvement. Ferritin elevation alone does not establish liver or heart damage.
Immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy affecting bulbar, neck and arm motor function; weakness does not establish separate airway or muscle damage.
Autoimmune peripheral neuropathy confined predominantly to the legs; weakness reflects nerve dysfunction, without primary muscle disease.
Sensory Guillain-Barre variant causes immune-mediated peripheral sensory nerve injury.
Autoimmune autonomic ganglion injury; gastrointestinal, bladder and circulatory dysfunction reflects neural failure rather than direct injury to those organs.

decisions.renal: none: bladder dysfunction is common (~50%), but results from autonomic denervation without established direct urinary-organ injury.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysmotility is common (~70-80%), but reflects autonomic neural injury rather than direct gastrointestinal tissue damage.

basis: Immune-mediated Guillain-Barre variant directly damaging peripheral sensory nerves.
Fibrotic lung disease, platelet dysfunction and cutaneous albinism define subgroup; albinotic ocular abnormalities impair vision in nearly all. Colitis affects a minority.
Platelet granule dysfunction and ocular or oculocutaneous albinism define these subtypes; colitis is not established in ≥30%; pulmonary fibrosis is excluded.
Congenital epidermal erosions and vesicles healing with characteristic scarring.
Adrenal hyperplasia causes autonomous aldosterone secretion; moderate to severe hypertension is explicitly defining and occurs in 100%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: moderate to severe hypertension is part of the disease's own definition and is annotated as obligate (100%).

basis: Ectopic adrenocortical tumor produces aldosterone; sustained hypertension occurs in 100%; variable ectopic sites do not establish consistent renal involvement.
Syndrome defined by corneal, lenticular, retinal and fetal ocular vascular malformations; all fall within the ocular axis.
Epibulbar lipodermoids and accessory auricular appendages define the syndrome. Preauricular tags are external-ear developmental anomalies; supernumerary nipples lie outside the axes.

decisions.dermatologic: none: preauricular appendages are accessory auricular structures; their skin covering does not independently establish a dermatologic disorder. Polythelia is outside the axes.
decisions.otologic: primary: preauricular appendages represent accessory external-ear structures and are a defining branchial-arch malformation.

basis: Umbrella for congenital infections; organ injury varies substantially by pathogen, with no additional organ established across most of the group.
Defining intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies; heart defects ~40-50% and dental anomalies >30%. Qualifying ocular anomalies (HPO 30-79%) omitted at cap; dental defects are more frequent.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: hypodontia and other dental malformations occur in >30% (HPO 30-79%); oral structural defects commonly impair dentition.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: ocular structural abnormalities qualify by HPO 30-79%; defining neurologic/skeletal disease, cardiac defects and more frequent dental defects take priority.

basis: Skin fragility and dental agenesis define the syndrome; ocular dysfunction includes myopia 80-99% and ectopia lentis 30-79%; cognitive impairment 30-79%.
GnRH deficiency, olfactory dysfunction and heart malformations define it; renal agenesis 30-79%. Hearing impairment and skeletal disease also 30-79%, omitted at cap.
Definition includes skeletal dysplasia, hypoparathyroidism with hypocalcemia, and characteristic structural or refractive eye abnormalities.
Longstanding hypothyroidism with defining pseudohypertrophic myopathy; cognitive impairment reported in 80-99%. Constipation and jaundice alone do not establish organ damage.
Conotruncal cardiac malformations and spinal myelomeningocele are defining abnormalities.
Congenital respiratory tract cyst from abnormal airway budding, usually mediastinal; esophageal abnormalities and infection occur below 30%.
Heritable aldosterone excess with hypertension defining the major subtypes; hypokalemia belongs to the metabolic axis.
Intellectual disability and digital skeletal anomalies define syndrome; nail hypoplasia 80-99%; dental crowding/impaction 30-79%; visceral malformations less frequent.
Metabolic enzyme deficiency; muscle injury supported by elevated CK in 80-99% and myoglobinuria in 30-79%; palmoplantar hyperkeratosis 30-79%. Renal insufficiency occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: elevated CK in 80-99% and myoglobinuria in 30-79% establish common muscle injury; the umbrella concept is defined by the metabolic enzyme defect.

basis: Defining limb/body-wall and CNS malformations; renal and cardiac malformations each 30-79%. Exteriorized bowel alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Congenital urethral duplication; associated structural anorectal anomalies occur in 30-79%. Urinary infections are occasional.
Air-filled congenital lesion of the laryngeal wall; larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Congenital duplication of part of the digestive tract.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures and cognitive impairment; behavioral manifestations add no separate organ axis.
Inherited apolipoprotein processing/aggregation disorder produces renal amyloid nephropathy. Common functional damage in other organs is not established.
Typically autoimmune inflammation of the posterior pituitary and stalk, causing central diabetes insipidus.
Skin, hair, sweat gland and dental defects define disease; ocular surface injury occurs in 30-79%. Asthma is separate; immunodeficiency defines a rare subtype.
Pathologic lymphocyte proliferation within an umbrella of immune disorders; common direct injury to another organ is not established across subtypes.
Amino-acid transport disorder with defining renal cystinuria, hypotonia and intellectual disability; hypotonia alone does not establish separate skeletal muscle damage.
Congenital excess red-cell production; thrombotic risk does not establish common intrinsic vascular damage across the umbrella.
Acquired elevation of red-cell concentration or mass; underlying hypoxia or erythropoietin-producing disorders are causes, not additional affected organs.
Immune dysregulation with severe infantile bowel inflammation and defining arthritis; recurrent infections and lymphoma risk do not establish other organ damage.
BH4-related amino acid and neurotransmitter disorder; direct neurological dysfunction and neurodevelopmental delay occur in 30-79%, sometimes despite phenylalanine control.
IgG4-related inflammation, fat necrosis and fibrosis of the small-bowel mesentery; no additional organ involvement established.
Leukoencephalopathy and palmoplantar keratoderma define the syndrome; diaphyseal dysplasia is frequent, 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement.
A neurologic movement disorder; tremor, muscle activity and myalgia do not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle damage.
Parent BWS supports defining somatic overgrowth, macroglossia and abdominal-wall defects. Hypoglycemia is usually transient; persistent subtype-specific endocrine damage is unproven.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: parent BWS hypoglycemia (~30-50%) is usually transient; persistent dysfunction is unproven in this subtype. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1394/)

basis: Structural bladder and ureter disorder with massive vesicoureteral reflux; recurrent urinary infections are separate diseases.
Primary megaureter is a structural and functional ureteral disorder; ureters belong to the renal axis.
Congenital obstructive dilation of the ureter; ureters and resulting urinary tract damage belong to the renal axis.
Congenital ureteral dilatation with reflux; ureters are included in the renal axis.
Congenital ureteral dilatation; ureters belong to the renal axis.
Congenital deficiency of gonadotropin signaling causes endocrine hypogonadism.
Iodine exposure causes the defining thyroid dysfunction and transient neonatal hypothyroidism; no additional organ injury is established.
Congenital thyroid hormone deficiency due to maternal factors; an immune mechanism applies only to a subset.
Transient congenital thyroid hormone deficiency; lasting neurologic damage is not established as common for this subtype.
Usually isolated nail whitening; listed kidney stones and blepharitis do not establish direct organ damage from leukonychia itself.
Congenital corticospinal motor control disorder causing persistent mirror movements; muscle and skeletal damage are not defining features.
Congenital lens and corneal abnormalities cause secondary glaucoma; high palate alone does not establish another damaged organ.
The defining features are eyelid ptosis, skeletal syndactyly and neurodevelopmental learning difficulties.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with callosal agenesis and seizures; strabismus and cardiac septal abnormalities each reported in 30-79%. Renal anomalies are under 30%.
Neurodegenerative PSP variant defined by akinesia and gait freezing; motor and speech abnormalities arise from CNS dysfunction.
Neurodegenerative corticobasal and supranuclear motor syndrome; gaze abnormalities reflect central dysfunction rather than eye damage.
Neurodegeneration causing progressive aphasia and speech apraxia; supranuclear gaze abnormalities reflect brain dysfunction.
Filarial infection occupying subcutaneous tissue; transient conjunctival migration usually causes no lasting eye damage; encephalopathy is often treatment-related.
Neurologic disconnection causes paralysis, anarthria and gaze dysfunction; respiratory weakness and diplopia do not establish intrinsic lung or eye damage.
Anorectal malformation and deafness define the syndrome; hearing loss is reported in 30-79%. Renal excluded because the definition explicitly states absence, conflicting with HPO nephropathy 80-99%.

decisions.renal: none: the definition explicitly states absent renal abnormalities; conflicting nephropathy annotations and synonyms do not resolve this contradiction.
decisions.otologic: primary: deafness is a defining component in the disease synonyms, supported by sensorineural hearing impairment in 30-79%.

basis: Clonal lymphoid malignancy arising in lung parenchyma or bronchi; lymphoma requires the immune axis and malignant blood-cell lineage supports the haematologic axis.

decisions.haematologic: primary: lymphoma is a malignancy of lymphoid blood cells, including when its primary anatomical site is extranodal.

basis: Defined by intellectual disability, spastic paraplegia and major CNS malformations; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Cortical neuronal migration defect causing developmental impairment, epilepsy and pseudobulbar palsy.
Acute hepatic steatosis and failure; renal dysfunction in roughly 50-80% and coagulopathy in over 50%. Encephalopathy is secondary to hepatic failure.
Neurocutaneous syndrome defined by pigmentary macules and intellectual disability, reported in 30-79%; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Chronic upper and lower airway disease defines PCD; persistent middle-ear inflammation/effusion occurs in 30-79%. Situs inversion alone does not imply cardiac damage.
Congenital absence or malformation of central hand and foot rays; hearing impairment and aniridia occur in only 5-29%.
Biliary atresia and congenital splenic malformations define BASM; congenital cardiac defects occur in approximately 40%.
Congenital bronchiolar malformation replaces normal lung architecture with cystic tissue.
Congenital cardiac outflow tract and great-vessel malformations; associated chromosomal syndromes do not establish other organ involvement.
Congenital structural malformation of the mitral valve.
Congenital intestinal malrotation with midgut volvulus defines gastrointestinal involvement; facial dysmorphism alone adds no organ axis.
Bone dysplasia, skin atrophy and metabolic lipodystrophy define MAD; dental hypoplasia/crowding occur in 30-79%. Globe enlargement alone is not ocular damage.
Marrow mast-cell neoplasm; persistent skin infiltration ~70-80%; mast-cell-mediated bone loss ~30-50%, including osteopenia/osteoporosis.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: mast-cell-mediated osteopenia/osteoporosis affects approximately 30-50%; bone loss qualifies even without destructive focal lesions.

basis: Progressive myocardial loss and fibrofatty replacement cause ventricular dysfunction and arrhythmias; syndromic skin findings do not characterize most cases.
Acrodynia features desquamating acral skin injury, peripheral/autonomic neurotoxicity and characteristic hypertension; additional oral injury lacks frequency evidence.
Degenerative cerebellar disease; supplied HPO annotations report macular degeneration and visual loss in 30-79%, supporting direct ocular involvement.
Acquired disorder of neurological coordination; immune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
CNS hemosiderin deposition causes neurodegeneration; progressive sensorineural hearing loss is defining and occurs in 80-99%. Bleeding does not establish a coagulation disorder.

decisions.otologic: primary: progressive sensorineural hearing loss is explicitly defining and affects 80-99%; the otologic axis includes hearing.

basis: Thoracic anthrax infection; secondary meningitis affects ~33% of adults and ~40% of children. Confusion alone and nonspecific HPO terms do not establish other organ damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct secondary meningitis occurs in ~33% of adults and ~40% of children with inhalational anthrax [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/rr/rr7206a1.htm).

basis: GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with intellectual disability and seizures; distal phalangeal shortening occurs in 80-99%. Renal and ocular abnormalities occur in <30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal phalangeal shortening is a direct skeletal malformation present in 80-99%; metabolic and neurologic abnormalities define the core disorder.

basis: Congenital secondary erythrocytosis is a blood-cell disorder; thrombosis is a potential complication rather than established common organ damage.
Severe neonatal urea-cycle disorder; hyperammonemic encephalopathy is characteristic, with lasting neurologic impairment in a substantial share (>30%).
Urea-cycle disorder; hyperammonemic brain dysfunction is a typical symptomatic presentation (>30%); scotomas alone do not establish ocular injury.
Hepatic metabolic defect defined by neonatal cholestasis/hepatic dysfunction or adult hyperammonemia; lasting neurologic damage is not established across the umbrella.
Metabolic hyperammonemia with defining recurrent brain dysfunction; hepatic steatosis in 80-99% and biochemical liver dysfunction in 30-79%.
ALP deficiency causes profound skeletal hypomineralization; pulmonary hypoplasia with respiratory failure is typical of the lethal perinatal form.
Hypophosphatasia metabolic defect defined here by premature tooth loss or severe caries; skeletal abnormalities explicitly absent.
Congenital enlargement of the brain; associated genetic conditions do not justify additional organ labels.
Immune-mediated destructive macrophage infiltration of muscle fascia; skin lesions are variable with no established frequency of at least 30%.
Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy with eosinophilic muscle infiltration; eosinophilia alone does not establish a separate blood disorder.
Benign adipose tumour, typically arising in subcutaneous tissue of childhood.
Hereditary cerebellar dysfunction; anemia and deafness characterize particular subtypes rather than most patients across this umbrella.
APC-associated adenomatous polyposis predominantly affecting the colon; additional cancer risks do not establish other organ involvement.
Peroxisomal metabolic disorder defined by progressive cerebellar ataxia and motor axonal neuropathy; abnormal pursuit reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Immune-mediated oligoarticular arthritis; ANA positivity raises uveitis risk, but estimates around 20-30% do not securely meet the involvement threshold.
Immune-mediated chronic joint inflammation; uveitis does not reach 30% in the ANA-negative subgroup.
Immune-mediated juvenile polyarthritis; ANA positivity increases uveitis risk but does not establish ocular damage in at least 30%.
Immune-mediated juvenile polyarthritis; ANA negativity does not remove the immune mechanism. Uveitis is not common enough to add ocular involvement.
Developmental defects of skin, sweat glands, hair and nails, together with characteristic dental hypoplasia and malformations.
Periostosis, osteoarthropathy and pachydermia define disease; persistent eyelid involvement with ptosis occurs in 30-79%; gastrointestinal damage is occasional.
Juvenile neurodegeneration with movement disorder, cognitive decline and seizures; abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Congenital skeletal segmentation abnormality with 15 thoracic vertebrae and rib pairs.
Inherited deficiency anaemias; metabolic, intestinal and hepatic abnormalities are subtype-specific rather than shared across the umbrella.
Acquired deficiency anemia is a blood-cell disorder; additional organ damage is not uniform across this group.
Inherited platelet dense-granule dysfunction causing bleeding; mucocutaneous hemorrhage and mention of melanosomes do not establish intrinsic skin damage.
Inherited coagulation disorder with reduced amounts of functionally abnormal fibrinogen.
Limb and urethral malformations define syndrome; cardiac defects 80-99%; ureteral anomalies 30-79% reinforce renal; splenic septation does not establish dysfunction.
Limb reduction defects and cardiac anomalies define the syndrome; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct pulmonary pathology.
Meningeal CNS tumor. Supplied endocrine and visual-field findings concern sellar subsets and do not represent most patients across the meningioma umbrella.
Craniofacial bone-development disorder; hypertelorism does not establish eye damage. Ocular, hearing and CNS abnormalities are occasional.
Neurodegenerative language disorder causing progressive word retrieval and repetition impairment.
Defined by optic atrophy and peripheral neuropathy; supplied ancestry identifies a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder.
Epiphyseal skeletal dysplasia causing abnormal joints, osteochondritis and early arthrosis.
Neurodevelopmental and ocular defects with hypogonadism define syndrome; joint stiffness/contractures occur in 80-99% and kyphoscoliosis in 30-79%.
Usually phenotypically silent. Listed organ phenotypes reflect separately unmasked recessive disorders rather than direct effects of paternal chromosome 1 disomy.
Developmental disability and congenital limb/skeletal defects define syndrome. Hair morphology and hypoplastic toenails (30-79%) do not establish functional integumentary injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: frequent hair and nail morphology changes lack evidence of inflammatory, destructive or functionally impairing integumentary disease.

basis: Developmental disability and dental/palatal malformations define it; clubfoot and hyperopia each occur in 30-79%; sparse hair omitted because of cap.
Severe developmental impairment, congenital cardiac malformations and limb skeletal abnormalities are defining components.
Developmental disability defines syndrome; hydronephrosis, PDA and strabismus each occur in 30-79%. Milder skull/digital anomalies omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus impairs ocular alignment and occurs in 30-79%; prioritize functional eye disease over mild skeletal dysmorphism.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skull/digital anomalies occur in 30-99%, but are less functionally damaging than retained organs and omitted under the four-axis cap.

basis: Speech apraxia and language developmental impairment occur in 30-79%; ear infections are separate infections; structural ear and cardiac defects are occasional.
Spherocytic hemolytic anemia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; intellectual disability/developmental delay occur in 80-99%. Retinal dystrophy is only 5-29%.
Developmental disability and congenital heart defects define the syndrome; minor craniofacial and ear-shape differences do not establish additional organ damage.
Developmental impairment and congenital cardiac malformations are principal features, each frequent at 30-79%; other organ defects are occasional.
Primary brain-development disorder; renal agenesis/reflux is annotated frequent (30-79%). Short stature and unspecified cortical bone morphology do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent abnormal cortical bone morphology and short stature do not establish destructive lesions or impaired skeletal function.

basis: Autoinflammatory disease defined by panniculitis, uveitis and systemic granulomatous inflammation; other organ frequencies are unspecified.
Autoinflammatory disease defined by recurrent inflammation of the pericardium.
Autoimmune connective tissue overlap disorder; joint and connective tissue disease is central. Other organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Definition specifies immune-mediated cutaneous vasculitis with purpura, hemorrhagic blisters and ulceration.
Inflammatory syndrome classified under rheumatic disorders; no specific organ injury established by the supplied record.
Hemoglobinopathy causing sickling and hemolytic anemia; organ complications vary across beta-zero and beta-plus forms and are often separately diagnosed.
Sickling hemoglobinopathy directly affects erythrocytes and spleen. Retinopathy and osteonecrosis are separately diagnosed complications; other organ injuries lack a clear 30% rate.
Sickling hemoglobinopathy directly damages red cells and spleen; extrahematologic complications vary and are often separately diagnosed.
Inherited hemoglobinopathy causes microcytic hemolysis; vaso-occlusive renal, pulmonary and skeletal complications are very rare.
Inherited hemoglobinopathy; ocular, pulmonary and splenic complications are occasional (<30%).
Localized skin blistering and nail dystrophy; structural dental enamel defects occur in 30–79%, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Gonadal dysgenesis causes endocrine failure; urethral malformations and skeletal bone loss are annotated in 80-99%. Gonadoblastoma is a separate neoplasm.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies are annotated in 80-99%; structural urethral malformation falls within renal.

basis: Distal joint contractures and shortened Achilles tendons define the disorder.
Malignant astrocytic neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Malignant brain tumour with glial and sarcomatous differentiation; mesenchymal histology does not imply skeletal involvement.
Glioblastoma variant arising in the brain.
Diffuse glial tumour infiltrates the brain, sometimes extending into the spinal cord.
Malignant astrocytic tumor arising in the brain or spinal cord.
Low-grade astrocytic neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Astrocytic tumour originates in and diffusely infiltrates central nervous system tissue.
Diffuse astrocytic neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Diffuse astrocytic neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Diffuse astrocytic neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Astrocytic tumor arising in the cerebral hemispheres and involving the meninges.
Primary central nervous system astrocytic tumor; optic pathway and hypothalamic involvement are location-specific subsets.
Astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Astrocytic neoplasm arising in the brain ventricular wall; associated tuberous sclerosis manifestations belong to a separate syndrome.
Infiltrating glial tumour arising in the brain or spinal cord.
Malignant oligodendroglial tumour originates in the central nervous system.
Low-grade neoplasm of CNS ependymal cells.
Ependymal tumour arising in the central nervous system.
Ependymal tumor of the spinal conus/cauda equina region; bladder and bowel dysfunction reflect neural injury rather than direct urinary or intestinal damage.
Malignant ependymal tumor arises in the central nervous system; visual symptoms do not establish direct eye disease.
Primary central nervous system glioma with astrocytic and oligodendroglial components.
Malignant mixed glial tumour arising in the central nervous system.
Glial tumor arising in the central nervous system; angiocentric growth does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Neuroepithelial tumour arising in the third ventricle.
Glial tumour arising within the central nervous system.
Medulloblastoma is a primary central nervous system tumor, usually arising in the cerebellum.
Embryonal CNS malignancy involving the cerebellar/fourth-ventricular region; diplopia and papilledema do not establish lasting eye damage.
Embryonal malignant tumour originating in the cerebellum; vomiting does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Embryonal malignancy arising in the cerebellum.
Tumor directly occupies the central nervous system or dura; adjacent bone involvement is not required across the concept.
Embryonal malignancy arising in the central nervous system.
Neoplasm originating from choroid plexus epithelium within the brain ventricles.
Malignant choroid plexus tumour arising within the CNS and commonly invading adjacent brain.
ID/seizures, congenital heart disease and hypothyroidism define the syndrome; skeletal abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Ocular abnormalities omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Malignant pineal parenchymal tumor arising in an endocrine gland within the brain; visual impairment is occasional (5-29%).
Tumor originates in the pineal endocrine gland within the CNS. Gaze and visual-field abnormalities reflect central pathway effects; direct ocular damage is not established.

decisions.ocular: none: gaze palsy and visual-field defects can arise from central compression or hydrocephalus; these annotations do not establish direct eye or optic-nerve damage.

basis: CNS tumor arising from specialized ependymal cells; hydrocephalus and central visual pathway dysfunction do not establish intrinsic eye or endocrine disease.
Neuronal neoplasm arising in cerebral hemispheres or spinal cord.
Neuronal and glial neoplasms arising in the nervous system.
Neuroepithelial tumor of mature ganglion cells; hemianopia reflects central visual pathway involvement, while endocrine abnormalities are occasional.
Primary intracranial neuronal-glial tumor; vomiting and papilledema reflect intracranial pressure rather than separate organ disease.
Neuroepithelial tumor composed of neoplastic neurons and glia, arising predominantly in the central nervous system.
Malignant neuronal-glial tumour originates in the central nervous system.
Circumscribed glioneuronal tumor arising in the brain.
Glioneuronal neoplasm arising in the central nervous system, usually near the fourth ventricle.
Malignant germ cell tumor originating within the central nervous system.
Malignant germ cell tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Mixed malignant germ cell tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Neoplasm originates in the meninges of the central nervous system.
Melanocytic tumor diffusely infiltrating CNS leptomeninges; associated congenital skin nevi are not intrinsic to this concept.
Melanocytic tumor arising in the meninges; melanocytic lineage does not establish skin involvement.
Primary melanoma of CNS or meninges; melanocytic lineage does not imply a skin primary.
Predominantly CNS tumor; supplied HPO reports retinal capillary tumors in 80-99%, supporting ocular occupation. Neurogenic bladder/bowel findings do not establish direct visceral damage.

decisions.ocular: involved: supplied retinal capillary hemangioma frequency is 80-99%; direct tumor occupation meets the rule despite uncertainty about this broad annotation.

basis: Tumors arise in cranial or spinal nerves; optic pathway tumors are a subgroup and do not establish ocular involvement across the umbrella.
Microcephaly and cleft palate define the syndrome and occur in 80-99%; retinal changes and finger contractures occur in only 5-29%.
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with perineurial differentiation.
Benign neoplasm arising from peripheral nerve sheath tissue.
Peripheral nerve sheath tumor usually presenting in skin or subcutis; other organ locations and compression complications are uncommon.
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor; rhabdomyoblastic differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle origin or involvement.
Brain malformation, spasticity and developmental impairment define the syndrome alongside hypernatremia, an electrolyte disorder.
Pontocerebellar maldevelopment causes severe neurologic dysfunction. Bulbar symptoms and central visual impairment do not establish direct gastrointestinal or ocular damage.
Defining microcephaly, severe intellectual disability, spasticity and ocular malformations; hypogonadism is reported in 80-99%.
Vertebral and epiphyseal growth abnormalities define this skeletal dysplasia umbrella; extraskeletal disease is subtype-dependent.
Defined by congenital abnormalities of the cornea, pupil and macula.
Umbrella skeletal dysplasia involving vertebrae and metaphyses; additional organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Isolated congenital absence or underdevelopment of the eye; syndromic extraocular disease is outside this concept.
Developmental delay and hearing loss define syndrome; ASD/arrhythmia and scoliosis each occur in 30-79%; hypodontia also 30-79%, omitted under cap.
Immune-mediated lichenoid skin inflammation distributed along Blaschko lines; other lichen planus sites are not established for this subtype.
