Open cervicothoracic neural-tube defect with vertebral nonclosure; common bladder dysfunction is not established for this specific anatomical subtype.
Open thoracic vertebral and neural-tissue defect; neurogenic bladder with loss of urinary function affects over 80% of open spina bifida patients.
Spinal cord/meningeal herniation through a vertebral defect; neurogenic bladder (~70-90%) is separately diagnosed neural urinary dysfunction, not direct urinary tissue injury.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder (~70-90%) reflects spinal denervation and is separately diagnosed; direct renal or urinary tissue damage is not established in >=30%.

basis: Extensive myelomeningocele directly involves spinal neural tissue and vertebral closure. Neurogenic bladder is separately diagnosed; urinary tract damage is not established by this record.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed consequence of spinal dysfunction; its frequency does not establish direct urinary tract damage.

basis: Spinal cord herniation and vertebral defects define myelomeningocele. Neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed consequence of denervation, not direct urinary tract disease.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder reflects denervation and is separately diagnosed; direct renal injury is not a defining or consistently common lesion.

basis: Lumbosacral vertebral closure defect with herniated spinal neural tissue; neurogenic bladder and bowel are secondary neurologic dysfunction, not direct urinary or intestinal injury.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder reflects disrupted innervation; urinary tract damage is not intrinsic or established here.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: neurogenic bowel reflects disrupted innervation rather than direct intestinal damage.

basis: Cervical myelomeningocele combines a vertebral closure defect with herniation of spinal cord and meninges.
Cervicothoracic myelomeningocele involves spinal neural tissue and defective vertebral closure.
Upper thoracic myelomeningocele affects vertebral closure and spinal neural tissue; common neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed consequence of neural injury.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder is common (>80%) but is a separately diagnosed consequence of spinal denervation, rather than direct urinary-organ injury.

basis: Defined by meningeal herniation through a posterior vertebral closure defect; spinal cord function is generally preserved and other complications are occasional.
Congenital cystic spinal cord malformation associated with a spina bifida vertebral defect. Common additional organ damage is not established across subtypes.
Congenital neural tube defect with brain herniation through a defining skull defect.
Congenital meningeal herniation through a defining cranial bone defect.
Herniation of intracranial contents through a congenital occipital skull defect; both CNS displacement and the cranial bone defect define the condition.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: an occipital skull defect is an essential structural component of the malformation.

basis: Herniation of intracranial contents through a congenital parietal skull defect defines both neural and skeletal abnormalities.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the congenital parietal bone defect is an essential anatomical component of the encephalocele.

basis: Herniation of intracranial contents through a congenital skull-base bony defect defines basal encephalocele.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the skull-base bone defect is an essential anatomical component of the malformation.

basis: Lipomatous tethering directly affects spinal cord and roots. Neurogenic sphincter deficits do not establish direct bowel/bladder injury; qualifying skeletal involvement is uncertain.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder dysfunction reflects cord/root injury; direct urinary tract damage in >=30% is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: bowel dysfunction is neurogenic; direct intestinal injury in >=30% is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: foot deformities are described, but common direct skeletal disease rather than consequences of neurologic dysfunction is unestablished.

basis: Congenital spinal cord and column malformation with defining orthopedic changes; persistent neurogenic bladder dysfunction occurs in roughly 30-60%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: spinal-column malformation and skeletal deformities are explicitly part of the disease definition.

basis: Congenital cyst occupying the CNS, usually the spinal canal; associated vertebral anomalies vary and are not established at >=30% across all locations.
Isolated absence of the spinal cord; classified as a neural tube defect and CNS malformation.
Explicitly nonsyndromic brain overgrowth. The accompanying multisystem HPO profile conflicts with the isolated definition and cannot establish extracerebral involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: atrial septal defect (30-79%) conflicts with the explicitly isolated concept and appears to reflect syndromic annotation.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: delayed skeletal maturation (80-99%) and genu valgum (30-79%) belong to a conflicting syndromic profile, not established isolated megalencephaly.

basis: Bilateral cerebral cortical malformation; esotropia occurs in 30-79% but does not establish direct ocular injury or visual loss. Hearing impairment occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent esotropia reflects ocular alignment dysfunction; direct eye damage or loss of vision is not established.

basis: Cerebral cortical malformation with common seizures and motor impairment; ocular, hearing and vascular abnormalities are occasional or rarer.
A structural cerebral cortical malformation; neurologic location applies even when clinically asymptomatic.
Developmental malformation of cerebral cortex causing epilepsy and developmental impairment; metabolic causes do not define the umbrella.
Isolated developmental malformation of cerebral cortical architecture.
Localized developmental malformation of cerebral cortical architecture.
Developmental malformation of the cerebral cortex.
Congenital focal malformation of cerebral cortical architecture.
Defined by myeloid marrow hypoplasia, neutropenia, monocytopenia and congenital deafness, with associated immunodeficiency.
Focal developmental malformation of the cerebral cortex.
Focal developmental malformation of the cerebral cortex.
Destructive developmental brain disorders, including hydranencephaly, porencephaly and schizencephaly.
Ependymal-lined cyst arising within the central nervous system.
Retrocerebellar arachnoid cyst is a structural lesion of the central nervous system.
Isolated congenital absence of part or all of the cerebellar vermis.
Isolated congenital absence of the cerebellar vermis, a central nervous system malformation.
Isolated congenital partial absence of the cerebellar vermis.
Congenital cerebellar and posterior fossa malformation with hydrocephalus.
Isolated congenital cerebellar/posterior fossa malformation; absence of hydrocephalus does not change the neurologic location.
Congenital hypoplasia directly affects one cerebellar hemisphere; abnormal eye movements and vertigo do not establish eye or ear damage.
Isolated cerebellar hypoplasia causes motor, cognitive and language impairment; hypotonia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Congenital communicating hydrocephalus affects intracranial cerebrospinal fluid circulation and the brain.
Congenital obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid flow causes hydrocephalus.
Defining arthrogryposis, renal tubular dysfunction and cholestasis; platelet granule/aggregation defects affect 30-79%. Skin, CNS and gastrointestinal involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic platelet alpha-granule and aggregation defects occur in 30-79% and cause clinically important bleeding dysfunction.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ARC is a vesicular-trafficking disorder; the bilirubin-metabolism ancestor does not establish a primary metabolic defect beyond cholestatic liver dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: arthrogryposis is a defining component of the syndrome and occurs in 80-99%; congenital hip dislocation is also frequent.

basis: Gangrenous bacterial oral infection destroys facial soft tissues and skin; destruction of facial bone is part of the disease definition.
The syndrome identifies ocular, skeletal and renal abnormalities as its defining organ manifestations; detailed phenotype data are unavailable.
Defining hair and nail dysplasia with alopecia and dental agenesis/enamel abnormalities; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Olivopontocerebellar degeneration and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; optic atrophy and coloboma occur in only 5-29%.
Skeletal dysplasia with defining limb shortening across both major forms.
Filariae occupy skin and subcutis, causing nodules and chronic dermatitis; damaging ocular involvement is geographically variable and not established at >=30% overall.

decisions.ocular: none: ocular inflammation can cause permanent damage, but its frequency is not established at >=30% across this infection umbrella.

basis: Airway, esophageal/palatal and urethral malformations define syndrome; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in 30-79%; frequent ptosis omitted at the four-axis cap.
Defining oral cavity and mandibular abnormalities with severe distal limb defects.
Hydrocephalus, intellectual disability and spasticity define the neurologic disorder; characteristic adducted thumbs reflect congenital thumb muscle abnormalities.
Inherited hemoglobin disorders causing anemia; severe bone changes and iron-related organ injury do not apply across most of this umbrella.
Pulmonary arterial vascular disease causing elevated resistance and right heart failure; pulmonary vessels fall under cardiovascular.
Disease of pulmonary arteries with increased vascular resistance and right-heart failure; pulmonary parenchymal damage is not defining.
Pulmonary vascular hypertension affects the cardiovascular axis. Underlying lung disease or hypoxia is the cause, rather than lung damage directly produced by this condition.
Progressive frontotemporal neurodegeneration with cerebral atrophy and executive dysfunction; behavioral changes are neurologic manifestations.
Frontotemporal and motor neuron degeneration define disease; muscle wasting and dysphagia result from denervation rather than primary muscle or gastrointestinal injury.
Costovertebral dysostosis and pharyngeal atresia define the syndrome; tongue aplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Ear shape and position do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: tongue aplasia/hypoplasia affects 30-79%; the defining pharyngeal atresia belongs to pulmonary, while mandibulofacial dysostosis is skeletal.

basis: Maternal anti-Kell antibodies destroy fetal erythrocytes and suppress erythropoiesis; alloimmune blood disease.
Inborn bile acid synthesis/conjugation defect with neonatal cholestasis; fat malabsorption results from deficient bile acids rather than direct intestinal damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: fat malabsorption reflects inadequate luminal bile acids; direct intestinal injury or intrinsic intestinal dysfunction is not established.

basis: Malignant epithelial neoplasm originates in salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Benign epithelial tumor arising in salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defined by multiple endocrine gland tumors; no additional organ axis is consistently affected across MEN subtypes.
Recurrent episodes of stupor define this neurologic disorder; metabolic and toxic causes are explicitly excluded.
Rapid MPS VI has defining skeletal dysplasia; damaging corneal clouding and cardiac valvular disease each affect most (>80%). Common airway and ear disease omitted under the cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: severe dysostosis multiplex and progressive joint restriction are defining features of rapidly progressing MPS VI, affecting nearly all patients.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease with defining skeletal dysplasia and joint restriction; progressive corneal disease and valvular disease each affect >30%. Common airway disease omitted by cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal dysplasia and progressive joint restriction define the skeletal storage phenotype of MPS VI, including slowly progressing disease.

basis: Central and peripheral neurodegeneration defines disease. Frequent muscle wasting reflects denervation; ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic ocular damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%) but reflects denervation rather than direct skeletal muscle disease.

basis: Neurodegeneration defines disease; muscle atrophy (30-79%) is neurogenic rather than direct myopathy. Ophthalmoplegia reflects neural motor dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79%, but results from motor neuron/peripheral nerve degeneration rather than direct muscle disease.

basis: Neurodegenerative ataxia subtype defined by peripheral amyotrophy (80-99% HPO); ophthalmoplegia is neurologic, and bladder/vestibular dysfunction occurs in <30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: peripheral amyotrophy defines this subtype and represents established muscle wasting (80-99% HPO), despite its neurogenic origin.

basis: Subcutaneous lipomas and limb hemihyperplasia define the syndrome; cerebral vascular malformations are annotated 30-79%. Embryonal malignancy is only a later risk.
Subchondral bone necrosis and osteochondral separation directly damage bones and joints.
CASPR2-antibody-mediated encephalitis with central and peripheral neurologic dysfunction; associated malignancy is a separate disease.
Cardiac malformations, strabismus and urethral hypospadias each occur in 30-79%. Dental abnormalities (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap; their functional severity is unspecified.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral defect reported in 30-79%; urethra is explicitly within this axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, but are omitted at cap; unspecified dental severity ranks below cardiac, ocular and urethral structural dysfunction.

basis: A primary neurological headache disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
Inherited insulin excess causes hypoglycemia; persistent neurodevelopmental injury occurs in roughly 30-50% of congenital cases, which dominate this umbrella. Frequency varies by severity.

decisions.neurologic: involved: recurrent neuroglycopenia directly injures the brain; lasting neurodevelopmental impairment affects approximately 30-50% of congenital cases.

basis: Congenital hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; neurodevelopmental impairment is reported in 30-79%, supporting hypoglycemic CNS injury; cardiomyopathy occurs in 5-29%.
Excess pancreatic insulin causes hypoglycemia; neurodevelopmental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting lasting neurologic involvement; cardiomyopathy is 5-29%.
Endocrine pancreatic hyperinsulinism; neurodevelopmental impairment is annotated at 30-79%, supporting hypoglycemic brain injury; cardiomyopathy is only 5-29%.
Pancreatic beta-cell insulin excess defines disease; persistent neurodevelopmental impairment from neuroglycopenic injury affects roughly 30-50% in severe resistant congenital hyperinsulinism.

decisions.neurologic: involved: lasting neuroglycopenic injury or developmental impairment affects approximately 30-50% in severe resistant disease; this is direct metabolic injury.

basis: Focal endocrine pancreatic hyperinsulinism causes hypoglycemia; permanent neurologic injury is not established as common for this subtype.
Focal pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction causes congenital hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; lasting neurologic injury is not established in most patients of this subtype.
Pancreatic beta-cell hyperinsulinism; progressive neurologic deterioration annotated in 80-99% supports hypoglycemic brain injury.
Catecholamine-secreting chromaffin tumours; hypertension occurs in 30-79%. Retinopathy, nephropathy and cerebral haemorrhage are separately diagnosed complications.

decisions.neurologic: none: adrenal endocrine tumours predominate across this umbrella; extra-adrenal autonomic tumours are a subset, and cranial nerve compression occurs in 5-29%.

basis: Adrenal medullary endocrine tumour; hypertension does not by itself establish additional cardiovascular damage.
Catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumour of paraganglia; hypertension does not by itself establish direct cardiovascular damage.
Symptomatic Coffin-Lowry phenotype combines variable neurodevelopmental impairment and characteristic hand/skeletal abnormalities; other organ findings are occasional.
Disordered proximal tibial growth causes progressive tibial bowing and knee deformity.
Bone fragility and congenital contractures define disease. Respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79%, but skeletal restriction does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: frequent respiratory insufficiency (30-79%) generally reflects thoracic skeletal restriction; the evidence does not establish direct lung or airway disease.

basis: Bone fragility, retinopathy/optic atrophy, seizures and severe developmental disability define the syndrome and occur in 80–99%.
Defined by osteopathia striata together with persistent pigmentary dermopathy and a white forelock.
Heritable skeletal disorders defined by increased bone density; marrow failure and cranial nerve injury are not shared by most patients across this broad group.
Osteoporosis, skeletal abnormalities, joint laxity and congenital blindness define the syndrome; intellectual disability frequency is unclear.
Urethral sphincter dysfunction causes urinary retention and incomplete emptying. Polycystic ovarian morphology alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Infantile ocular motor disorder; head nodding and torticollis do not establish separate neurologic or skeletal damage.
Acute purulent infection and inflammation of intraocular tissues.
Chronic purulent infection and inflammation of the intraocular tissues.
Defined by toxic retinal and macular atrophy with persistent visual loss.
Lymphoma simultaneously occupying intraocular structures and the central nervous system; lymphoma adds the immune mechanism axis.
Lymphoid malignancy warrants blood-cell and lymphoma mechanism axes; no single anatomical organ applies across this umbrella.
Infection directly inflames and damages the posterior uvea and adjacent ocular tissues.
Infection with inflammation of the anterior uvea.
Infection causing inflammation throughout the uveal tract.
Paraneoplastic immune-mediated inflammation of the uvea; the associated malignancy is a separate disease.
Ejaculation-associated syndrome with self-limited symptoms and no established organ damage; immune causation remains hypothetical, and episodic hypertension is insufficient.
Cobalamin metabolic defect; intellectual disability/developmental delay 30-79%. Renal insufficiency <30%; hepatomegaly and crisis-related breathing changes lack intrinsic organ damage.
Disordered calcium deposition occludes small vessels and causes skin necrosis. CKD and hyperparathyroidism are underlying conditions; secondary infections are separate.
Calcification and occlusion of cutaneous arteries cause ischemic skin ulceration; associated renal disease is a separate underlying condition.
Calcifying vasculopathy with thrombosis and fibrosis chiefly affecting heart and lungs; underlying renal failure is a separate disease.
Nasal obstruction and solitary central incisor occur in 80–99%; intellectual disability in 30–79%. Typical brain cleavage defects are absent; endocrine defects occur in 5–29%.
Congenital submucosal defect of the shared laryngotracheal-esophageal partition; both airway and esophageal anatomy are defining.
Severe CNS hypomyelination; amyotrophy (80-99%) is secondary to neurologic motor impairment, without primary muscle disease. Nystagmus is neurologic; respiratory failure 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent amyotrophy reflects neurologic motor impairment; direct skeletal muscle pathology is not established.

basis: CNS hypomyelination causes developmental impairment and motor dysfunction; nystagmus does not establish intrinsic ocular damage.
CNS hypomyelination causes spasticity and intellectual disability; nystagmus reflects central neurologic dysfunction.
PLP1-related CNS hypomyelinating disease in manifesting female carriers; urinary abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Central hypomyelination and peripheral demyelinating neuropathy define disease; optic atrophy is occasional, 5–29%.
Inherited hypomyelinating leukodystrophy directly affects central nervous-system white matter.
IgG4-mediated pancreatitis with direct inflammatory bile-duct involvement in roughly 50-70%; renal involvement is generally below 30%. Compression-only jaundice does not establish hepatic damage.

decisions.hepatic: involved: direct IgG4-related bile-duct inflammation occurs in roughly 50-70% as an extrapancreatic manifestation of the same systemic process.

basis: Immune-mediated duct-centric inflammation of the exocrine pancreas. Associated bowel disease is separate; obstructive jaundice alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Speech apraxia, developmental delay and intellectual disability define the deletion syndrome; optional hypotonia and joint laxity do not establish other organ damage.
Lipodystrophy with severe metabolic dysfunction; phalangeal osteolysis occurs in 30-79%. Steatosis and atherosclerosis are separate diseases; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.

decisions.hepatic: none: steatosis (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed metabolic liver complication; hepatomegaly (80-99%) alone does not establish impaired liver function.

basis: Erythroid porphyrin-metabolism dysfunction causes phototoxic skin injury; this malignancy-associated form arises in abnormal clonal marrow erythropoiesis.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this form involves porphyrin production by the abnormal marrow erythroid clone; blood-cell pathology is intrinsic, rather than a later malignancy risk.

basis: Severe intellectual disability, regression and progressive disabling joint contractures define the syndrome; dysphagia is only occasional.
Inherited prion disease causes progressive cerebral degeneration and cognitive impairment; prion disease belongs to the transmissible infectious mechanism axis.
Defining abdominal wall defect with herniated abdominal viscera, hand abnormalities and maxillary skeletal abnormalities.
Immune-mediated crescentic glomerular injury with rapid renal failure; systemic autoimmune disorders and their other organ manifestations are separate diagnoses.
Hereditary sensorimotor neuropathy and hyperelastic skin are the defining manifestations.
Inherited hemoglobin abnormality causing neonatal anemia and cyanosis; cyanosis does not establish cardiac or pulmonary damage.
Inherited skin pigmentation disorder; oral pigmentation does not establish gastrointestinal tissue damage or impaired function.
Structural microangiopathy confined to cutaneous blood vessels; nonspecific metabolic annotations do not establish an endocrine or metabolic disorder.
Cutaneous mast-cell proliferation causing extensive blistering and erythroderma; cardiorespiratory arrest occurs in only 5-29%.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation infiltrating skin, with cutaneous mastocytosis and blistering in 80-99%; systemic involvement is not established.
Congenital nonfunctioning sequestered lung tissue; anomalous systemic arterial supply does not itself establish cardiovascular damage.
Congenital sequestered pulmonary tissue outside the normal lung lobes; anomalous blood supply alone does not establish vascular disease.
Congenital abnormal bronchopulmonary tissue communicates with the esophagus or stomach, defining both respiratory and foregut malformation.
Congenital malformation of pulmonary airways and lung tissue.
Congenital cystic malformation of pulmonary airways and lung tissue.
Congenital structural malformation of pulmonary airways; associated congenital anomalies are not intrinsic involvement.
Congenital structural malformation of pulmonary airways and lung tissue.
Congenital cystic malformation of distal pulmonary airways and lung tissue.
Inflammation throughout the uvea; infectious and immune-mediated forms account for the principal disease mechanisms.
Idiopathic anterior uveal inflammation is an immune-mediated ocular disease.
Noninfectious immune-mediated inflammation of the posterior uvea and adjacent retina; no defining systemic disease.
Idiopathic immune-mediated inflammation of the uvea, retina and vitreous; no established extraocular disease.
Ichthyosis defines the disease; developmental disability occurs in 30-79%. Typical corneal deposits usually spare vision; renal and endocrine abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Inherited skin keratinization disorder; ectropion and other extracutaneous effects vary by subtype and do not establish common functional damage across ARCI.
Inherited keratinization disorders affecting the epidermis; no common extracutaneous damage established across the group.
Congenital ichthyosis with a resolving collodion membrane; restricted joint movement from tight skin does not establish lasting joint damage.
Congenital acral ichthyosis with collodion membrane, hyperkeratosis and scaling confined to skin.
Syndromic ichthyosis defines skin disease; skeletal, neurological and endocrine abnormalities vary by subtype and are not established in most across the umbrella.
Progressive spastic paraplegia and persistent facial cutaneous lesions define the syndrome; skin abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Progressive frontotemporal cortical degeneration; muscle and bone disease occur in particular subtypes, not across the umbrella.
Developmental delay or intellectual disability is common across chromosome 12 deletion syndromes; other organ malformations vary with the deleted region.
Autoimmune destruction of multiple endocrine glands defines the group; non-endocrine organ disease varies by subtype and is not consistently common across the umbrella.
Neurodegenerative parkinsonism; rigidity and other motor manifestations do not establish primary muscle or joint damage.
Demodex infestation directly affects skin; damaging ocular or ear involvement is not established in at least 30%.
Renal caliceal abnormalities and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; both occur in 80-99%.
Invasive hepatic Echinococcus infection; extrahepatic lesions occur in <30%. Reactive eosinophilia and inflammatory anemia do not establish direct hematologic injury.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; visual impairment and abnormal heart morphology each occur in 80-99%; individual cardiac lesions vary.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the syndrome; limb and chest-wall malformations occur in 80-99%. Sparse hair and obesity do not establish additional organ dysfunction.

decisions.dermatologic: none: sparse hair (80-99%) is a dysmorphic finding without established damaging skin or follicular disease.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: truncal obesity (80-99%) alone does not establish direct endocrine or metabolic organ dysfunction from this syndrome.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: syndactyly, pectus excavatum and diaphragmatic malformation are annotated 80-99%; skeletal involvement accompanies the defining neurodevelopmental disorder.

basis: Urinary malformations, cortical atrophy and cardiomyopathy annotated 80-99%; intellectual disability ~60%. Minor skeletal dysmorphism lacks established functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pectus carinatum, micrognathia and clinodactyly are common morphological findings, but substantial skeletal dysfunction is not established.

basis: Blood dyscrasia, telangiectasias and hypoxemic pulmonary shunts define TEMPI; CNS hemorrhage 30-79%. Perinephric fluid need not damage kidneys; autoimmunity unproven.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: defining telangiectasias (100%) are vascular lesions; pulmonary vascular abnormalities occur in 80-99%, and venous thrombosis in 30-79%.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: intrapulmonary shunting is a defining manifestation with hypoxemia in 100%; pulmonary vascular abnormalities and pleural effusions occur in 80-99%.
decisions.renal: none: perinephric collections, despite the broad kidney HPO annotation, do not establish kidney tissue damage or impaired renal function.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: TEMPI is a plasma-cell dyscrasia-associated syndrome; an autoimmune parent alone does not establish a proven autoimmune or other qualifying immune mechanism.

basis: Pancreatic/salivary, biliary and orbital infiltration each annotated 30-79%; coexisting Hashimoto thyroiditis does not establish intrinsic thyroid involvement.
Interstitial mesenchymal tumour arising in fetal or neonatal lung.
Inherited hepatobiliary transport or metabolic defects cause intrahepatic cholestasis; extrahepatic damage is not shared across the umbrella.
Defined by cerebral arterial vasoconstriction; headache alone does not establish brain damage. Infarction and hemorrhage each occur in fewer than 30%.
Primary bronchopulmonary adenocarcinoma arising in lung tissue.
Severe glycerol metabolism disorder; altered consciousness may accompany acute crises. Persistent neurologic or muscle damage is not established across infantile cases.
Inborn glycerol metabolism defect causes metabolic crises; episodic vomiting and altered consciousness do not establish persistent gastrointestinal or neurologic damage.
Inherited glycerol metabolism defect producing pseudohypertriglyceridemia in otherwise healthy adults; no additional organ injury established.
Immune-mediated lymphocytic inflammation of the brainstem, particularly the pons; perivascular inflammation does not independently establish vascular disease.
Outer retinal dysfunction causes visual field loss; infectious and autoimmune causes are proposed rather than established.
Outer retinal disease; an immune cause is insufficiently established to assign the mechanism axis.
Congenital absence or cystic malformation of the pericardium.
Congenital absence of pericardium and diaphragm defines disease; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%.
The constituent tropomyosin disorders are structural skeletal myopathies; a neuromuscular classification does not establish nerve damage.
Inherited melanin pigmentation disorder affecting ocular development and vision; skin and hair pigmentation are normal or only slightly diluted.
Syndromic melanin disorders defining skin and ocular albinism; bleeding, immune and neurologic disease vary substantially among subtypes.
The metabolic umbrella includes mild forms without CNS injury. Severe untreated forms damage the brain, but established neurologic injury in >=30% across the full group is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurologic injury depends on biochemical severity and treatment; a >=30% frequency across the entire umbrella, including mild hyperphenylalaninemia, is not established.

basis: Umbrella of inborn tyrosine metabolism disorders; additional organ damage is subtype dependent.
Severe cardiovascular and skeletal disease with emphysema (100%); ectopia lentis occurs in 80-99%. Cutis laxa (80-99%) omitted because of the cap.
Aortic and skeletal disease characterize this group; Marfan predominates, with ectopia lentis in ~60%, supporting ocular damage in >=30% of patients across the umbrella.

decisions.ocular: involved: Marfan is the predominant subtype and ectopia lentis affects ~60% of Marfan patients; patient-weighted frequency plausibly exceeds 30% across this group.

basis: Sensorineural deafness and ovarian endocrine insufficiency define the syndrome; neurologic abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Folate metabolism/transport disorders commonly cause neurodevelopmental impairment or encephalopathy (>30% across the spectrum); anemia is subtype-dependent.
Arterial, skin and joint connective-tissue fragility; bowel perforation is a major diagnostic feature, annotated in 30-79%. Pulmonary complications are uncommon.
Congenital heart defects, intellectual disability and generalized skin abnormalities define the syndrome, each reported at 30-79%; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Deafness and neutrophil dysfunction with recurrent infections define syndrome; glaucoma 30-79%; craniosynostosis and ectopic anus omitted by cap.
Defining epidermal and melanocytic nevi; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Neurologic and ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Cutaneous pigmentary and vascular malformations; cortical atrophy 80-99% and glaucoma 30-79% support involvement. Reduced bone density 80-99% omitted under cap.
Inherited erythrocyte membrane disorder; most patients are asymptomatic, and skin ulcers and gallstones are minority complications.
Gluconeogenesis disorder; liver dysfunction and neurodevelopmental impairment occur in 5-29%. Frequent transaminase elevations alone do not establish lasting hepatic damage.

decisions.hepatic: none: liver dysfunction and steatosis occur in 5-29%; ALT/AST elevation at 30-79% alone does not establish lasting hepatic injury.

basis: Hair and nail dystrophy define this ectodermal dysplasia; cleft lip and palate are frequent (30–79%). Conjunctival hyperemia does not establish lasting eye damage.
Vitamin D metabolic disorders commonly impair bone mineralization; rickets is the listed subtype and abnormal bone mineral density is an explicit feature.
Defective vitamin D metabolism or action causes hypocalcemia and impaired skeletal mineralization; both axes define the disease.
Defined by phosphate metabolism disturbance, renal phosphate wasting and rickets; hearing loss 80-99%. Dental disease and malabsorption 30-79% omitted by cap.
Epileptic neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability and cerebral abnormalities; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage.
Chronic HTLV-1-associated infective eczema; nasal discharge and anterior-nares crusting do not establish airway damage. Later leukemia and myelopathy are separate diseases.

decisions.pulmonary: none: nasal discharge and anterior-nares crusting are diagnostic signs but do not establish damaging airway inflammation or loss of function.

basis: Ovarian germ-cell tumor has reproductive origin outside the axes. hCG secretion does not establish endocrine disease; listed metastatic sites lack qualifying frequencies.
Congenital reflux affects bladder and ureters; urinary infections and subsequent hypertension are separate complications.
Skeletal anomalies, congenital heart disease and intellectual disability define syndrome; cleft lip/palate is a major defining oral defect. Hypogonadism omitted under cap.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by destructive cutaneous inflammation: pyoderma gangrenosum, acne and hidradenitis.
Developmental delay and learning disability define the syndrome; associated hypothyroidism has no supplied frequency and is separately diagnosed.
ID, keratoconus and skeletal/joint anomalies define syndrome; obesity/hyperlipidemia 80-99%. Hearing loss and cleft palate 30-79% omitted by cap.
Partial CYP11A1 deficiency causes isolated primary adrenal failure; the supplied broad HPO profile conflicts with the explicitly isolated subtype.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism defects with lactic acidosis and severe developmental/white-matter disease; cardiac and optic damage vary across subtypes; hypotonia alone does not prove myopathy.
Nonsyndromic inherited epidermal disorder causing peeling, scaling and impaired skin barrier function.
Tumor originates in the nasopharynx, within the pulmonary axis. Proptosis and diplopia are frequent, but common direct ocular injury or orbital occupation is not established.
audit_reason: Remove ocular: frequent proptosis and diplopia do not establish direct ocular damage or orbital tumor occupation in at least about 30%. The frequency of adjacent invasion is unspecified.

basis: EBV-associated neoplasia; tumour sites vary across lymphoproliferative, epithelial and mesenchymal subtypes, without a shared organ of origin.
EBV-infected lymphoid cells proliferate; extranodal organs vary across this umbrella and none qualifies across most patients.
EBV-associated mesenchymal neoplasia; anatomic origin varies across the group, and mesenchymal origin alone does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
EBV-associated mature B-cell lymphoma; variable extranodal sites do not establish any additional organ as affected in at least 30%.
B-cell lymphoma; direct oral/GI tumour involvement occurs in roughly 30-50%. Other extranodal sites are less consistently affected.
Usually a subcutaneous myopericytic neoplasm; perivascular growth does not itself establish vascular damage or an infectious mechanism.
Inherited tryptophan metabolism disorder; neurological injury varies by subtype and is not established in at least 30% across this umbrella.
Inherited lysine/hydroxylysine metabolic disorder umbrella; neurologic damage is not established across most subtypes.
Glutamine metabolic disorders; severe developmental brain dysfunction or encephalopathy is characteristic across both listed subtypes, exceeding 30%.
Glycine metabolism defect with severe neonatal encephalopathy and developmental impairment; central apnea does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
An inborn glycine metabolism disorder defined by encephalopathy, developmental delay and seizures; hypotonia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited disruption of proline metabolism; neurologic and connective tissue manifestations vary across subtypes.
Inherited ornithine metabolism disorder; ocular and neurologic manifestations vary across subtypes and are not established across the umbrella.
Transient ammonia metabolism disturbance; asymptomatic forms lack demonstrated brain injury, and direct neurologic damage in >=30% across the full spectrum is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: none: asymptomatic forms lack deficits ([study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3511207/)); neurologic injury in >=30% across the whole concept is unestablished.

basis: Organic aciduria umbrella; neurologic, cardiac and ocular damage vary by subtype, without an established group-wide frequency.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurologic damage is prominent in several subtypes, but involvement in at least 30% across this heterogeneous umbrella is not established.

basis: Neurodevelopmental injury and thrombocytopenia from marrow toxicity each occur in 30-79%; renal dysfunction 5-29%; hepatomegaly alone does not prove hepatic injury.
Congenital infection; deafness/cataracts 80-99%, cardiac defects 30-79%; neurologic and haematologic damage (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Immune-mediated inflammatory peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness and atrophy reflect denervation. Respiratory involvement is occasional.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation damages lung parenchyma; blood eosinophilia is reactive, and associated atopic dermatitis is a separate disease.
Plasma-cell disorder, neuropathy and endocrinopathy define POEMS; sclerotic bone lesions occur in ~90-95% and are major criteria. Common skin and vascular involvement omitted by cap.

decisions.dermatologic: none: persistent skin changes are common, but bone lesions occur in ~90-95% and are a major diagnostic criterion; skin is omitted by the four-organ cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: osteosclerotic lesions directly occupy bone, occur in ~90-95%, and are a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Inherited blistering and poikiloderma; gingivitis and premature tooth loss occur in 80–99%. Skull shape alone does not establish damage; other skeletal and ocular lesions occur in 5–29%.
audit_reason: Remove musculoskeletal: skull shape abnormalities alone do not establish direct damaging skeletal involvement, and other skeletal findings are occasional. Gastrointestinal involvement remains supported by common gingivitis and tooth loss.

basis: Hereditary endocrine tumor predisposition; hypertension is reported at 30-79% but depends on manifest tumors. Retinopathy, glomerulosclerosis and stroke are separate complications.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension reported at 30-79% accompanies manifest secretory tumors; it does not establish direct cardiovascular damage inherent to this predisposition.

basis: Skin scars occur in 80-99%; CNS injury and limb hypoplasia in 30-79%. Ocular malformations also occur in 30-79%, omitted at cap in favor of disabling limb defects.

decisions.ocular: none: ocular malformations qualify at 30-79%, but are omitted under the four-axis cap, prioritizing characteristic disabling limb hypoplasia.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: limb hypoplasia occurs in 30-79% and causes permanent structural and functional impairment.

basis: Poliovirus infection of the nervous system, particularly anterior horn motor neurons. Muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than direct muscle infection.
Meningitis and thrombocytopenia each occur in 30-79%; rash is transient. Hepatic and cardiac injury occur in <30%; respiratory/digestive findings lack specific damage.
Immune arthritis with defining urethritis; keratoderma/nail dystrophy 80-99%. Oral ulcers 80-99%, colitis and iritis 30-79% omitted at cap; conjunctivitis transient.

decisions.renal: primary: urethritis is explicitly part of the defining classic triad, qualifying despite its occasional HPO frequency of 5-29%.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none at cap: oral ulceration (80-99%) and colitis (30-79%) qualify, but extensive skin/nail disease is retained alongside the three primary axes.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: iritis (30-79%) qualifies but is omitted in favor of more frequent skin/nail disease; transient conjunctivitis adds no axis.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: keratoderma and dystrophic nails represent direct skin/nail disease annotated in 80-99%, retained preferentially under the four-axis cap.

basis: Polydactyly, retinal/chorioretinal colobomas and intellectual disability define the syndrome; each is annotated as frequent (30-79%).
Defining polyneuropathy/intellectual disability, short-limb skeletal abnormalities and premature ovarian endocrine failure. Arrhythmia is occasional.
Defining gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyposis; anemia is secondary to intestinal blood loss, without direct blood-organ disease. Cancers are separate diagnoses.
Intrauterine HSV causes skin injury/scarring (~95%), CNS injury (~65%) and eye damage (~40%); individual CNS malformations at 5-29% do not measure aggregate CNS involvement.

decisions.neurologic: involved: aggregate CNS injury affects ~65% of true intrauterine HSV cases; occasional individual malformations do not exclude common overall CNS damage.
decisions.ocular: involved: destructive congenital ocular lesions, including chorioretinitis and microphthalmia, affect ~40% of intrauterine cases.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: congenital skin lesions and scarring occur in ~95%; this is direct fetal tissue injury, not merely a transient exanthem.

basis: Familial structural foot deformity; no additional organ involvement established.
Familial structural deformity of the foot and associated lower-limb locomotor tissues.
Immune-mediated pustular drug eruption affecting skin. Renal and hepatic complications occur in fewer than 30%; reactive blood counts do not establish blood damage.
Severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; ocular, skeletal and vascular abnormalities are minority findings.
Malignant soft-tissue tumor with skeletal muscle differentiation, usually arising in deep extremity tissues.
Epithelioid sarcoma commonly originates in extremity dermis/subcutis and fascia or tendon-associated connective tissue; these are primary tumour sites rather than metastatic complications.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: dermis and subcutis are characteristic sites of origin for the usual distal form, which predominates across the umbrella; proximal deep-tissue cases do not negate this.

basis: Compression and stenosis of the celiac artery define the disease; abdominal symptoms do not establish direct gastrointestinal injury.
Phenylalanine metabolic disorder explicitly defined by cognitive impairment, seizures and developmental dysfunction; neurological manifestations are defining features.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the supplied definition explicitly characterizes this phenotype by cognitive impairment, seizures and developmental disorders.

basis: Corneal Bowman layer and epithelial dystrophy with variable visual impairment.
Defined corneal stromal dystrophy; ocular primary applies despite the absence of visual impairment.
Blepharophimosis and intellectual disability define this syndrome group; additional abnormalities vary by subtype.
Ketamine-associated cholangiopathy directly affects extrahepatic bile ducts. Dysuria alone does not establish urinary tract injury; hallucinations do not establish neurologic damage.
Fixed drug eruption is a localized immune-mediated cutaneous hypersensitivity reaction; oral ulceration and stomatitis occur in only 5-29%.
Toxic cutaneous eruptions; the listed major subtypes are immune-mediated. Additional organ damage depends on subtype.
Synostosis, eyelid defects and learning disability define it. Hearing loss 80-99%; clefts 30-79% omitted at cap; renal involvement frequency unclear.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none under the four-axis cap: defining orofacial clefts occur in 30-79%; retain more frequent hearing impairment and skeletal/ocular defects plus disabling intellectual impairment.
decisions.neurologic: primary: learning disability is explicitly defining, supported by the intellectual-disability parent and HPO frequency of 30-79%.

basis: Frontotemporal neurodegeneration with predominant right temporal atrophy; behavioral changes arise from brain disease.
Defining intestinal atresia and pancreatic malformation, gallbladder aplasia/hypoplasia, and neonatal diabetes; cardiac anomalies are not established as common.
Inherited arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy predominantly affecting the left ventricle.
Inherited arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy directly affects both cardiac ventricles.
Inherited arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy predominantly affecting right ventricular myocardium.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; PDA and metatarsus adductus each have HPO frequencies of 80-99%. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: metatarsus adductus is a structural foot deformity annotated in 80-99%; arthralgia and weakness alone would not suffice.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder; impaired vision/refractive abnormalities and obesity each occur in 80-99%.
Defining hypogonadism, microcephaly/developmental impairment and deafness; night blindness/visual field defects 80-99%; anemia and skeletal abnormalities omitted at cap.
Pituitary deficiency and immunodeficiency define disease; alopecia/nail dystrophy occur in 30-79%. Bronchiectasis (30-79%) follows separately diagnosed respiratory infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis (30-79%) is secondary to separately diagnosed recurrent respiratory infections; neither establishes direct pulmonary involvement by this syndrome.

basis: Hypothalamic/endocrine dysfunction, dysautonomia and hypoventilation define ROHHAD; hearing loss annotated 80-99%. GI dysmotility and reduced lacrimation omitted by cap.
HPO: intellectual disability, hearing loss and cytopenias/coagulopathy each 30-79%; hepatic dysfunction and chorioretinitis also frequent but omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia, thrombocytopenia and coagulation dysfunction each occur in 30-79% per HPO; retained for direct blood dysfunction.
decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic dysfunction is annotated at 30-79%, but omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of neurologic, hearing and blood involvement.

basis: Intracerebral cavitation directly damages brain tissue, causing motor impairment, seizures and developmental disability.
Defining skin and bowel inflammation with immunodeficiency; recurrent blepharitis, otitis and bronchiolitis are secondary infections.
Congenital glycosylation disorder characterized by multiple joint dislocations, skeletal abnormalities and ligamentous laxity.
Multiple congenital skin webs and joint contractures define this arthrogryposis syndrome; lethal-subtype complications are not generalized.
Late motor-neuron dysfunction after poliomyelitis; muscle atrophy and respiratory insufficiency each occur in 5-29%; no active infection.
Defining renal, hepatic and exocrine pancreatic dysplasia; endocrine pancreatic dysfunction with diabetes occurs in 30-79%. Pulmonary hypoplasia is under 30%.
Defined by chronic intestinal loss of absorptive function; parenteral nutrition complications are treatment effects.
Congenital absence of limbs; explicitly nonsyndromic.
Isolated congenital shortening of the bones of the fingers or toes.
Nonsyndromic developmental duplication or altered patterning of skeletal digits.
Isolated congenital duplication of digits on the postaxial side of the hand.
Congenital structural deformities of the limbs and their bones.
Defining popliteal skin webs, syndactyly and contractures accompany oral clefts and lower-lip pits. Genital malformations have no applicable axis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: congenital cutaneous webbing behind the knees is the named pterygium and a defining structural skin abnormality.

basis: Congenital joint contractures define the group; underlying neurologic abnormalities vary across subtypes.

Congenital absence of the foot is a skeletal developmental defect.

Fetal parvovirus infects erythroid precursors; anemia and thrombocytopenia occur in 80–99%. Cardiomyopathy and ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Congenital hand-foot skeletal malformations with triphalangeal thumbs, polydactyly and syndactyly.
Congenital skeletal malformation with an accessory phalanx; defined as nonsyndromic.
Congenital duplication of central digits is a structural skeletal abnormality.
Congenital duplication of the preaxial skeletal elements of the foot; nonsyndromic.
Congenital fusion and malformation of fingers, phalanges and toes define this isolated limb disorder.
Isolated congenital finger angulation caused by abnormal phalangeal shape, without associated systemic manifestations.
Congenital tibial nonunion directly affects bone; associated neurofibromatosis is a separate disease.
Congenital failure of normal femoral bone continuity with a false joint; a skeletal disorder.

Congenital structural abnormality of the elbow joint and radial head.

Congenital toe overgrowth with frequent epiphyseal and metatarsal abnormalities; other organ defects are very rare.
Developmental overgrowth of the upper limb; no evidence establishes another affected organ axis.

Bilateral congenital absence of the forearm bones and hands.

Bilateral congenital deformity of the talus and associated foot alignment.

Skeletal dysostosis with brachydactyly, carpal fusion and vertebral abnormalities; spina bifida occulta alone does not establish neural damage.
Cutis laxa, neurodevelopmental impairment and corneal disease define syndrome; skeletal deformities and joint abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Dental defects omitted by cap.
Leukocyte adhesion dysfunction; lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia and inflammatory stomatitis/gingivitis each occur in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed infections are excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent aphthous stomatitis and gingivitis occur in 30-79%, supporting direct inflammatory oral injury; oral thrush alone would not qualify.

basis: Skin/skeletal overgrowth define syndrome; intellectual disability 80-99%, cataract/retinal detachment 30-79%. Vascular involvement 30-79% omitted at cap; parathyroid dysfunction unspecified.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability occurs in 80-99% and hydrocephalus in 30-79%; these accompany the defining skin and skeletal overgrowth.

basis: Tick-borne viral CNS infection; encephalitis is the defining disease localization despite many infections remaining non-neurologic. Hearing and visual sequelae are under 30%.
Defining anal atresia and urinary tract malformations. Normal ovaries and genital ambiguity do not establish endocrine disease; respiratory insufficiency alone lacks direct lung injury.
Chronic intestinal propulsion failure defines disease; supplied HPO reports nervous system structural abnormalities in 30–79%, supporting neurologic involvement.
Mitochondrial disease with neuropathy and intestinal muscular dysfunction; ophthalmoplegia 80-99%; myopathy and hearing loss 30-79% omitted by cap.
Umbrella for atypical reproductive and genital development; endocrine dysfunction is not established across the group.
Neurologic thermoregulatory dysfunction; sweating and episode-related arrhythmias do not establish lasting skin or cardiac damage.
Thiamine metabolism/transport defects; encephalopathy, seizures and neurodegeneration occur in most major subtypes. Anemia and deafness are subtype-specific.
Brain malformations, coloboma and progressive skeletal/joint abnormalities define the syndrome; hydronephrosis and hydroureter occur in 30-79%.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Obesity and limb abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); dysmorphism alone does not establish organ damage.
Anterior pituitary carcinoma; optic chiasm compression causes progressive visual field loss, annotated in 30-79%. No intrinsic ocular lesion established.
audit_reason: Replace ocular with neurologic: typical progressive field loss reflects optic chiasm compression, a CNS lesion, rather than established intrinsic eye disease. Anterior pituitary origin supports metabolic_endocrine.

basis: Defining limb and vertebral malformations; duodenal atresia in 80-99% and thymic aplasia in 30-79% support intestinal and immune involvement.
Severe skeletal disease from secondary hyperparathyroidism; dental abnormalities 80-99%, hearing loss 30-79%. Renal failure precedes the syndrome.
Defining peripheral nerve tumors, orbital neurofibromas and marfanoid skeletal habitus establish these three sites.
Generally benign tumor of the nail matrix causing localized nail thickening and sometimes pigmentation.
Tumor arising in the nail matrix.
Neoplasm originating in the nail apparatus.
Follicular inflammation directly affects bile ducts and exocrine pancreatic ducts; an autoimmune mechanism is not established by the supplied description.
Carcinoma originates in the hepatopancreatic ampulla, spanning the terminal biliary tract and duodenal interface.
Pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema define the syndrome; pulmonary hypertension is a separately diagnosed complication.
Umbrella for toxin-mediated staphylococcal diseases; skin, lung and shock manifestations differ across subtypes, with no common damaged organ established.
Upper and lower motor neuron degeneration; muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99% and joint contractures in 30-79%.
B-cell lymphoid malignancy; no additional organ is consistently affected across this lymphoma umbrella.
Malignancy of B lymphocytes; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis. No specific extranodal organ is affected across most subtypes.
B-cell hematologic malignancy arising in the CNS; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
B-cell lymphoma defines blood and immune axes; splenic/marrow disease shares the blood axis. Liver infiltration is described, but a frequency of at least 30% is not established.

decisions.hepatic: none: increased liver involvement is not a quantified frequency; the supplied evidence does not establish involvement in at least 30%.

basis: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; skin is the defining site and extracutaneous disease is uncommon.
B-cell lymphoma occupying splenic red pulp, marrow and blood; spleen is included in the haematologic axis.
Mature B-cell leukemia involving blood, marrow and spleen; these all fall within the haematologic axis.
EBV-associated mature B-cell lymphoma arising in chronically inflamed tissue; extranodal sites vary, so no additional anatomical organ is assigned.
Mature T-cell lymphoma; extranodal involvement varies by site, with no additional organ established as affected in at least 30%.
Mature T-cell lymphoma defines hematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes; no individual extranodal organ is established as commonly damaged.
Mature B-cell lymphoma; extranodal sites vary across subtypes, without a consistently affected additional organ across the umbrella.
Caudal spinal and sacral malformation; urinary anomalies and anal atresia each 30-79%, bowel dysfunction 80-99%; cardiac anomalies omitted by cap.
Defective renal tubules define disease; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%. Skull ossification defects and arthrogryposis are major features; joint hypermobility occurs in 80-99%.
Inherited epidermal fragility with blistering and erosions; muscle, renal and hearing disease belong to uncommon subtypes.
Neoplasm of the pituitary endocrine gland; visual or neurologic compression is not universal across this tumour umbrella.
Inherited skin fragility; characteristic enamel hypoplasia and oral mucosal blistering affect most patients. Airway and renal disease vary by subtype.
Syndrome defined by intellectual disability, hypotonia and skin hyperpigmentation; hypotonia alone does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
Intellectual disability, primary hypogonadism and ichthyosis define the syndrome; strabismus affects 80-99%.
Familial infantile epilepsy; associated dyskinesias are neurologic. Seizure-related apnea does not establish pulmonary damage.
Syndromic X-linked intellectual disability; supplied ancestry establishes neurodevelopmental involvement without evidence for other axes.
Acquired adult immunodeficiency, commonly associated with anti-interferon-gamma antibodies; resulting opportunistic infections are separate diseases.
Inherited intestinal disaccharidase deficiency impairs sucrose and starch digestion, causing carbohydrate malabsorption.
Inherited intestinal disaccharidase deficiency causes impaired sucrose and starch digestion and absorption.
Inherited intestinal brush-border enzyme deficiency impairs sucrose digestion and carbohydrate metabolism.
Congenital intestinal disaccharidase deficiency causes impaired carbohydrate digestion and absorption.
Inherited intestinal brush-border enzyme deficiency affecting carbohydrate digestion, even when sucrose intolerance is absent.
Mucocutaneous and GI hamartomas are diagnostic features; benign thyroid lesions occur in ~50–70%. Neurodevelopmental damage is not established at ≥30% across the umbrella; cancer risks excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral papillomas and gastrointestinal hamartomas are major diagnostic features.
decisions.neurologic: none: macrocephaly alone is not damage; neurodevelopmental disability is not established in ≥30% across the full PHTS umbrella.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: benign structural thyroid lesions, including adenomas and multinodular disease, occur in approximately 50–70%.

basis: Renal magnesium/calcium wasting and nephrocalcinosis define this electrolyte transport disorder; severe ocular disease is subtype-specific, with pooled frequency unclear.
Inherited renal tubular magnesium transport disorder causing hypomagnesemia with hypocalciuria.
Inherited magnesium transport disorder with hypomagnesemia and renal tubular magnesium-handling dysfunction; intestinal involvement varies by subtype.
The syndrome is defined by congenital facial palsy, sensorineural hearing loss and strabismus; facial dysmorphism alone adds no skeletal damage.
Localized lipogranulomatous lesions arise in sinonasal tissue and subcutis; altered erythrocytes within lesions do not establish a systemic blood-cell disease.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: subcutaneous lipogranulomatous lesions are an established disease location, reflected by the synonym subcutaneous spherulocystic disease.

basis: Spastic paraplegia and intellectual impairment define this L1-related neurologic disorder; weakness reflects upper motor neuron dysfunction.
Noninfectious immune-mediated inflammation of the iris and anterior uvea.
Hemiparkinsonism and structural unilateral body atrophy define the syndrome; scoliosis is reported in only 5-29%.
Toxic basal-ganglia encephalopathy defines manganism. Visual impairment occurs in 30-79%, but direct ocular injury is unestablished; inhalation alone does not establish lung damage.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 30-79% does not localize injury to the eye or optic nerve; central visual dysfunction remains possible.

basis: Carbon monoxide-related brain injury produces parkinsonism, cognitive impairment and white matter abnormalities.
Toxic brain lesions define parkinsonism. Contractures reflect neurologic rigidity; unspecified skin changes do not establish direct skin injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: elbow contractures occur in 30-79%, but reflect secondary shortening from neurologic rigidity, without direct joint or muscle disease.

basis: The supplied syndrome name defines intellectual disability, microcephaly and phalangeal skeletal abnormalities; facial dysmorphism adds no specific axis.
Poststreptococcal immune-mediated basal ganglia dysfunction causes chorea; associated carditis is separately diagnosed and not qualifying here.
Defined by dystonia from early cerebral injury together with ipsilateral bodily and limb tissue atrophy.
Neurologic startle disorder with hypertonia; acoustic triggers do not establish ear disease.
Hyperekplexia is a neurologic disorder of exaggerated startle and abnormal inhibitory motor control.
Inherited diffuse thickening of palmar and plantar skin; extracutaneous features are subtype-specific.
Syndromic intellectual disability defines neurologic involvement; short stature and minor dysmorphism do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Focal palmoplantar epidermal hyperkeratosis; extracutaneous disease belongs to particular subtypes rather than the umbrella.
Hereditary punctate hyperkeratotic lesions of palmar and plantar skin.
Localized palmoplantar keratoderma affects skin.
Defining intellectual disability, digital malformations and abnormal hair; conductive hearing impairment in 80-99%; nonspecific immune annotation insufficient.
Cobalamin remethylation disorder with characteristic inherited megaloblastic anemia; neurologic/developmental impairment is common (roughly >=30%); published series are small.

decisions.haematologic: primary: inherited megaloblastic anemia is a core phenotype ([JBC](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021925820770201)), consistent with its hereditary-anemia ancestry.

basis: Umbrella for inborn amino-acid metabolic disorders; neurologic damage in a particular subtype does not establish involvement across the group.
Cobalamin-processing disorder causing isolated methylmalonic acidemia; persistent neurologic or renal damage in at least 30% is not established for this responsive subtype.

decisions.neurologic: none: subtype-specific evidence does not establish persistent neurologic damage in at least 30%; severe MMA phenotypes cannot supply that estimate.

basis: Inherited aminoacylase metabolic defects classified as hereditary neurological diseases; includes Canavan disease and aminoacylase 1 deficiency.
Inherited disruption of neutral amino acid transport; no additional organ damage established across this umbrella.
Umbrella for inborn glycolytic metabolic disorders; blood, muscle and nerve involvement varies by subtype.
Fructose metabolism disorder umbrella includes benign fructosuria; hepatic or renal damage is not shared across the group.
Umbrella for inherited galactose metabolism defects; hepatic, ocular and neurologic injury vary by subtype and are not universal group features.
Peripheral GALE deficiency is a galactose metabolism disorder; erythrocyte enzyme deficiency alone does not imply blood-cell damage.
Generalized galactose metabolic defect; liver dysfunction, developmental impairment and cataracts are common, roughly >=30% each in small reported cohorts.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts are characteristic direct galactose-related lens injury in generalized GALE deficiency, approximately >=30%; reported cohorts are small.

basis: Infantile glycogen storage myopathy and cardiomyopathy; cerebral white-matter abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver dysfunction.
Glycogen branching defect specifically defined by progressive hepatic storage injury and cirrhosis.
Glycogen branching enzyme deficiency is an inborn metabolic disorder; this subtype is defined by hepatic glycogen accumulation and liver disease.
Glycogen metabolism disorder with defining severe prenatal myopathy; respiratory failure does not establish lung damage, and pulmonary hypoplasia lacks an established >=30% frequency.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure can result from severe myopathy; intrinsic pulmonary hypoplasia is not established as affecting >=30% or as a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Congenital GSD IV causes storage myopathy; dilated cardiomyopathy is characteristic and commonly reported (estimated >=30%). Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: dilated cardiomyopathy is characteristic and common in the congenital neuromuscular subtype (estimated >=30%); the exact frequency is uncertain.

basis: Glycogen metabolism disorder explicitly defined by combined hepatic disease and skeletal myopathy.
Childhood neuromuscular GBE deficiency has characteristic skeletal myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy from polyglucosan storage; hepatic and adult neurologic forms are distinct.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: dilated cardiomyopathy is a characteristic defining manifestation of childhood neuromuscular GSD IV alongside skeletal myopathy, although severity varies.

basis: Metabolic myopathy; this exact subtype includes isolated muscle disease ([MedGen](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/343525)). APBD neurologic features cannot be assumed.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the exact concept has the synonym 'adult, with isolated myopathy'; skeletal-muscle glycogen disease defines this subtype.

basis: Glyoxylate metabolic defect encompasses primary hyperoxaluria; renal oxalate deposition and nephrocalcinosis affect most patients; hepatic enzyme location is not liver damage.
Inherited focal epilepsy defined by abnormal cerebral electrical activity.
Congenital malformation of pulmonary venous drainage; pulmonary hypertension is vascular, and dyspnea alone does not establish lung damage.
Umbrella of inherited carbohydrate transport and absorption disorders; gastrointestinal, neural and other organ effects vary substantially by subtype.
Sterol biosynthesis defect with autoinflammatory periodic fever; persistent neurologic damage chiefly affects the severe mevalonic aciduria subtype.
Inherited pancreatic fat-digestion defect with exocrine insufficiency; anemia reflects secondary nutritional deficiency, not direct blood injury; gallstones <30%.
Inherited digestive enzyme deficiency causes lipid malabsorption and steatorrhea; pancreatic exocrine function is affected despite no structural pancreatic disease.
Inherited fatty-acid oxidation and ketogenesis defects; persistent liver, heart, muscle or brain damage is not established in most patients across this umbrella.
Umbrella of fatty-acid oxidation defects; hepatic, cardiac, muscular and neurologic injury vary substantially by subtype and severity.
HADH deficiency causes disordered metabolism and hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; supplied liver, cardiac and neurologic findings lack evidence of damage in >=30%.
Carnitine transport and fatty-acid oxidation disorders; muscle, cardiac and hepatic injury vary substantially by subtype and are not established across most of this umbrella.
Lysosomal ganglioside degradation disorders; progressive neuronal dysfunction and neurodegeneration affect most patients across GM1 and GM2 forms.
Lysosomal neuronal GM2 storage; retinal/optic degeneration causing visual loss is common in predominant infantile forms (>30% overall); cherry-red spots alone do not qualify.

GM2 storage causes progressive central and peripheral neurodegeneration; muscle atrophy/weakness at 30-79% is neurogenic, without established direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent muscle atrophy and weakness (30-79%) reflect motor-neuron/peripheral nerve degeneration; direct myopathy is not established.

basis: Adult GM2 storage disorder causes central and peripheral neurodegeneration. Weakness and dysphagia are neurogenic; direct muscle pathology is occasional.
GM2 storage causes progressive infantile neurodegeneration; progressive visual loss from retinal neuronal degeneration occurs in most, beyond a non-damaging cherry-red spot.
Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes GM2 storage and progressive juvenile neurodegeneration; damaging ocular involvement is not consistently common.
Adult GM2 lysosomal storage disease causing progressive neurologic dysfunction; ocular damage is not typical of the adult form.
Structural obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract; associated malformations and valve damage remain cardiovascular.
Defective GM2 degradation causes progressive neurodegeneration; common damaging ocular involvement is not established across B1 presentations.
Lysosomal sulfatide-storage disease damages central and peripheral myelin; optic atrophy occurs in 30–79%. Gallbladder and hearing abnormalities are under 30%.
Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes sulfatide storage and central/peripheral demyelination; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%; cholecystitis is occasional.
Lysosomal glycoprotein degradation disorders; neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal dysostosis each affect an estimated >30% across major forms. Organomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal dysostosis and joint abnormalities occur across multiple major mucolipidosis and oligosaccharidosis forms, supporting an estimated frequency >30%.

basis: Lysosomal disease with defining immunodeficiency and intellectual disability (80-99%); dysostosis multiplex 80-99%. Hearing impairment and cataracts (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability and developmental impairment are defining features of infantile alpha-mannosidosis, with intellectual disability reported in 80-99%.

basis: Lysosomal oligosaccharide storage disorder; intellectual disability occurs in 80–99% and ataxia in 30–79%. Hearing, skeletal and ocular damage are occasional.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by neurologic dysfunction and characteristic retinal disease with progressive visual loss; skeletal and visceral disease chiefly characterize type II.

decisions.neurologic: primary: myoclonus and progressive neurologic dysfunction in type I, and developmental impairment in type II, are central defining manifestations.
decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic macular disease and progressive visual loss are central diagnostic manifestations, rather than incidental deposits alone.

basis: Congenital obstruction of the aortic valve; ventricular hypertrophy and other defining abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Sialic acid metabolic/storage disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment is common (>30%) across principal forms. Visceral enlargement alone does not establish organ damage.
Lysosomal free sialic acid storage disorder defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment and progressive CNS dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodegeneration defines this severity subtype, rather than an optional complication ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1470/)).

basis: Lysosomal glycogen storage causes skeletal myopathy in most (>80%). Cardiomyopathy is concentrated in infantile Pompe and Danon; its frequency across the umbrella is uncertain.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy is subtype-dependent; involvement in at least 30% across the entire umbrella is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: direct storage-associated skeletal myopathy affects most (>80%); the umbrella is defined by lysosomal glycogen storage.

basis: Inherited organelle disorder; persistent pigment loss or palmoplantar keratoderma affects most major subtypes (>30%). Blood, immune and neurologic defects vary across the group.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent albinism or keratoderma is characteristic of the major subtypes and affects most patients across this umbrella.

basis: Defective N-linked glycosylation is metabolic; developmental impairment and other CNS dysfunction affect most patients. Hepatic and coagulation involvement vary across subtypes.
Protein O-glycosylation metabolic disorder; skeletal myopathy characterizes most represented subtypes. Brain and ocular involvement vary across the umbrella.
Rett-like neurodevelopmental disorder; gastrointestinal functional impairment occurs in 30-79% and reflects persistent dysmotility. Central breathing abnormalities do not establish lung injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: HPO records gastrointestinal functional abnormality in 30-79%; persistent dysmotility constitutes loss of gut function, beyond feeding symptoms alone.

basis: Umbrella disorder of glycoprotein O-glycosylation; no additional organ involvement is established across most subtypes.
Inherited glycosylation disorder; developmental disability, seizures and neurologic dysfunction occur in most subtypes. Hypercoagulability is subtype-specific.
Umbrella of inherited glycosylation defects, including neurologic, muscle and blood phenotypes; group-wide neurologic damage in most patients is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: the umbrella includes muscle- and blood-limited subtypes; the evidence does not establish neurologic damage in most patients across the group.

basis: Congenital glycosylation disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in most COG subtypes. Hepatic damage varies and lacks a reliable group frequency.
Umbrella glycosylation defect; subtype-specific skin and neurologic findings cannot establish group-wide frequencies. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/309778)

decisions.neurologic: none: neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in particular subtypes; frequency >=30% across this heterogeneous glycosylation group is unestablished.
decisions.dermatologic: none: cutis laxa characterizes specific subtypes, but the evidence does not establish it as defining or present in >=30% across the whole group.

basis: Umbrella of inherited porphyrin/heme metabolic disorders; hepatic, cutaneous, neurologic and blood damage vary across subtypes.
Inherited defects of hepatic bilirubin conjugation or excretion establish metabolic and hepatic localization; neurologic injury and renal disease are subtype-specific.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic bilirubin processing or excretion is the affected organ function across the usual subtypes; primary localization does not require hepatocyte destruction.

basis: Umbrella of inborn metabolite absorption and transport disorders; no additional organ damage applies across most subtypes.
Inborn neurotransmitter synthesis disorders affecting central or autonomic nervous system function; hypotension alone does not establish vascular damage.
Umbrella of mineral metabolism and transport disorders; no additional organ is consistently damaged across its subtypes.
Inherited copper homeostasis disorders; hepatic, neurologic and connective tissue damage vary across subtypes and cannot be generalized to the umbrella.
Umbrella of iron handling disorders. Hepatic, hematologic and neurologic damage vary by subtype; no additional organ damage is established across most patients.
Umbrella for zinc absorption, transport and metabolism disorders; additional organ damage varies by subtype.
Inherited magnesium transport disorder; renal transport abnormalities do not establish intrinsic kidney damage across this umbrella.
Manganese transport disorder; neurotoxic accumulation with dystonia characterizes both listed forms. Liver disease and polycythemia are subtype-dependent.
Poststreptococcal immune disease with carditis and inflammatory arthritis; chorea is a major diagnostic criterion (HPO 30-79%). Transient skin signs excluded.
Epilepsy with reproducible seizure triggers; organs supplying triggering stimuli are not themselves damaged.
Acquired immune deficiency; infections and their organ complications are separate diseases.
Renal malformations are a common syndromic component (30-79%); uterovaginal aplasia itself has no axis. Skeletal and hearing abnormalities are minority findings.
Erosive oral lichen planus is an immune-mediated disease causing destructive inflammation of oral mucosa; cutaneous involvement is not required.
HDL metabolism disorder; atherosclerosis is a separate disease, and storage-related organ injury is subtype-specific.
Lipoprotein metabolism disorder. Steatosis may occur, but common hepatic functional damage is not established across this umbrella; neurologic and intestinal disease vary by subtype.
Burkholderia infection directly causes pneumonia and lung abscesses in 30-79%; cutaneous, hepatic, splenic and CNS lesions are each under 30%.
Nocardia bacterial infection; pulmonary infection with pneumonia occurs in 30-79%. CNS, cutaneous and hepatic infections are occasional, below 30%.
Generalized keratinization disorder; cicatricial ectropion/lagophthalmos and limb joint contractures each occur in 30-79%; hearing impairment only 1-4%.
Lysosomal storage disorder; neurologic dysfunction, blindness and hearing impairment each annotated 80-99%. Vascular skin abnormalities 30-79% omitted under cap; spectrum heterogeneous.
Developmental disability and epilepsy define syndrome. Frequent small nails do not establish functional skin damage; ocular and limb defects are mostly occasional (5-29%).
12p12.1 deletion syndrome is associated with developmental delay and intellectual disability; the supplied record lacks evidence for additional common organ damage.
Developmental impairment and optic nerve abnormalities characterize the syndrome; vertebral fusion and spinal/chest deformities occur in 30-79%; dental crowding alone is insufficient.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic nerve hypoplasia and strabismus are explicit defining features; optic atrophy and other ocular abnormalities occur in 30-79%.

basis: Congenital cyst of the pancreas; no endocrine dysfunction is established. Jaundice and pancreatitis occur in fewer than 30%.
Gastric carcinoma defined by persistent Epstein-Barr virus infection within the tumor cells.
Neurocutaneous syndrome defined by epidermal nevi and associated developmental or epileptic abnormalities; reported eye findings lack qualifying frequency.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; strabismus and ptosis occur in 30-79%. Dental crowding and minor ear/digital morphology do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental anomalies and crowding occur in 30-79%, but impaired dentition or other direct functional injury is not established.
