basis: Leiner disease is defined by exfoliative dermatitis, immune dysfunction and persistent diarrhea with failure to thrive; supplied phenotypes occur in 80-99%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: persistent diarrheal intestinal dysfunction with failure to thrive is a defining component, supported by diarrhea in 80-99%.

basis: Congenital joint contractures and mandibular hypoplasia define skeletal involvement; webbed neck and hypoplastic nipples do not establish another organ disorder.
Localized corneal stromal inflammation; idiopathic inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Proximal gastric polyposis directly occupies the stomach; gastric cancer risk remains within the same gastrointestinal axis.
Bone fragility disorder with increased bone mineral density. Common extra-skeletal damage is not established for this subtype.
Developmental disability defines the syndrome; renal, skeletal and structural heart abnormalities each annotated at 80–99%; external-ear dysmorphism lacks functional damage.
Marfanoid skeletal habitus and advanced bone age define the syndrome; inguinal hernia reflects an abdominal-wall defect, without established intrinsic intestinal damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: an inguinal hernia alone establishes an abdominal-wall defect, not direct damage to bowel or another gastrointestinal organ.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome; generalized amyotrophy, optic disc pallor and eczematoid dermatitis each annotated at 80-99%; low IGF1 alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Odontogenic epithelial neoplasm usually arising within mandibular or maxillary bone; tooth-forming tissue and intraosseous jaw location define its origin.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: approximately 95% arise as intraosseous jaw tumors; bone is the primary anatomical site, rather than merely a site of secondary invasion.

basis: Spigelian hernia reflects an abdominal wall fascial defect. Cryptorchidism is reproductive; endocrine dysfunction or intrinsic bowel damage is not established.
Pleural effusion is a defining diagnostic component. Ovarian neoplasm has no axis; ascites alone does not establish gastrointestinal organ damage.
Pleural effusion is a defining component alongside pelvic tumour and ascites. Reproductive tumour origin has no axis; ascites alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Atypical Meigs syndrome characteristically combines a benign pelvic tumor with pleural effusion without ascites; pleural fluid occupation defines it. Ovarian tissue has no axis.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pleural effusion without ascites characterizes atypical/incomplete Meigs syndrome and directly occupies the pleural space.

basis: Ovarian stromal tumor; Meigs effusions/ascites are reactive. Peritonitis annotation conflicts with the described noninvasive phenotype; hormonal abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Neurodegenerative disorder of speech motor planning; speech impairment does not establish oral tissue or muscle disease.
Defined by leukoencephalopathy, cerebral ischemic injury and retinal degeneration; no separate vascular disorder established, and scoliosis frequency is unspecified.
Intellectual disability, pyloric stenosis and cranial skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; craniosynostosis occurs in 30-79%. Cryptorchidism is reproductive.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: brachycephaly is a named defining feature, supported by craniosynostosis in 30-79%, establishing a substantive cranial skeletal disorder.

basis: Renal anomalies and developmental impairment define disease; contractures/craniosynostosis and night blindness are annotated 80-99%. Hearing impairment is 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: contractures and craniosynostosis are annotated 80-99%; skeletal injury qualifies, while overgrowth alone does not establish a primary locomotor disorder.

basis: Pituitary/CNS malformations; hearing loss and night blindness each 80-99%. Spine/joint and oral malformations (80-99%) omitted at cap; sensory findings document functional loss.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft palate/oral defects (80-99%) qualify, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of documented hearing and visual loss.
decisions.ocular: involved: non-progressive night blindness is direct visual dysfunction, annotated in 80-99%; retained under the cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: spinal, scoliosis and joint defects (80-99%) qualify, but are omitted at the four-axis cap; hearing and visual loss establish functional damage.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is direct ear functional loss, annotated in 80-99%; retained under the cap.

basis: ATP13A2-associated neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis is a lysosomal metabolic disorder with neurodegeneration; upgaze palsy reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Hereditary amyloid disorder defined by progressive gastrointestinal dysfunction and autonomic neuropathy; renal amyloidosis/CKD occur in 30-79%. Cardiac and hepatic involvement are <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: progressive gastrointestinal dysfunction from visceral amyloid deposition is explicitly part of the disease definition.
decisions.neurologic: primary: autonomic neuropathy is explicitly defining despite its occasional HPO annotation; median nerve entrapment is additionally annotated 30-79%.

basis: PURA-related encephalopathy defines the disease; persistent ptosis represents eyelid dysfunction in 30-79%. Respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary injury.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis is persistent eyelid dysfunction, reported in 30-79%; eyelids fall within the ocular axis.

basis: Defined by fibroadipose, subcutaneous and skeletal overgrowth; capillary malformations directly affect vessels in 30-79%.
Defining developmental disability, skeletal abnormalities and ear malformations; renal hypoplasia in 30-79%. Tracheal abnormalities also frequent, omitted under cap.
Lymphoid cell malignancy arising in bone; lymphoma warrants both haematologic and infectious_immune axes.
Acquired destruction of cerebral tissue produces a porencephalic cavity.
Amyloidogenic clonal plasma-cell disorder with protein deposition; renal dysfunction ~60-70%, cardiac involvement ~50-70%. Hepatic dysfunction and neuropathy usually below 30%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: systemic AL amyloidosis is an amyloidogenic clonal plasma-cell disorder; overt multiple myeloma is not required.

basis: Localized light-chain amyloid deposition is an acquired metabolic disorder; affected sites vary, with no single organ established as involved in ≥30%.
Fibulin-4 deficiency causes severe arterial disease; supplied evidence does not establish common damage on another axis.
Developmental dental disease with abnormal dentin, enamel, tooth number and roots; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Pituitary adenoma secreting multiple hormones; endocrine gland origin defines the axis.
GH/PRL-secreting pituitary tumour; GH-driven skeletal overgrowth and arthropathy reported in 80-99%. Diabetes and hypertension are separate diseases; skin thickening alone is insufficient.
Familial adenomas originate in the pituitary endocrine gland; broad hereditary ancestry does not establish other organ damage.
Pituitary gland adenoma remains an endocrine-organ tumor despite absent hormone hypersecretion; common visual damage is not established.
Nonfunctioning adenoma arising in the pituitary endocrine gland; visual damage is not established as common across this concept.
Malignant tumor arising from peripheral nerve sheath; variable soft-tissue location does not establish another commonly damaged organ.
Renal bicarbonate wasting causes acidosis; reduced bone density occurred in 2/2 studied affected brothers, with limited sampling.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: reduced bone density in 2/2 affected brothers supports direct skeletal involvement. [Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10972690/).

basis: Aspartoacylase deficiency causes severe leukodystrophy; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Feeding and motor abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited aminoacylase deficiency causes leukodystrophy and neurodevelopmental impairment; retinal dystrophy is occasional (5-29%).
M. xenopi disease predominantly presents as chronic destructive pulmonary infection; extrapulmonary sites are uncommon.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the lungs are the predominant site occupied and damaged by clinical M. xenopi infection, rather than a downstream complication.

basis: Clonal eosinophil disorder; eosinophilic endomyocardial injury affects roughly 30-50% in myeloproliferative series. Other organ frequencies vary.
Reactive eosinophilic blood disorder with immune-mediated tissue injury; persistent cutaneous involvement ~50%. Direct pulmonary damage is not consistently >=30% across secondary causes.

decisions.pulmonary: none: reported respiratory involvement includes symptoms; direct pulmonary injury is not established in >=30% across secondary causes.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: reactive cytokine-driven eosinophilic inflammation causes immune-mediated tissue injury.

basis: Aberrant T-cell cytokines drive eosinophilia; eosinophilic skin disease affects approximately 70-90%.
Inherited keratinization disorder causing recurrent hyperkeratotic skin lesions.
MS, ichthyosis and coagulation deficiency define it; optic atrophy/neuritis occurs in 80-99%. Immune mechanism omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: optic atrophy and retrobulbar optic neuritis occur in 80-99%, establishing direct optic nerve damage.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: lamellar ichthyosis is a defining component, reported in 80-99%.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: MS is immune-mediated, but the four-axis cap prioritizes the defining affected organs and very frequent optic nerve damage.

basis: Facial palsy and hearing loss each 30-79%; nail dysplasia/cutaneous syndactyly 80-99%. Ptosis (30-79%) omitted at cap; optic atrophy <30%.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent nail dysplasia and cutaneous syndactyly occur in 80-99%, supporting structural nail and skin involvement.

basis: Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; renal salt loss reflects aldosterone deficiency rather than intrinsic renal damage.
Adrenal steroid-synthesis deficiency causes cortisol deficiency and androgen excess; genital virilization has no additional axis, and salt wasting is absent.
Defining nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy; HPO developmental delay 80-99%, ovarian insufficiency 30-79%; hypertension is secondary CKD disease; hepatic fibrosis <30%.
Congenital nonfunctioning lung tissue defines the disease; an anomalous systemic feeding artery does not itself establish cardiovascular damage.
Cutaneous lymphoma with defining circulating malignant T cells; hepatomegaly in 30-79% does not establish common hepatic infiltration or dysfunction.

decisions.hepatic: none: HPO hepatomegaly occurs in 30-79%, but enlargement alone does not establish hepatic infiltration or functional injury in at least 30%.

basis: Hereditary ataxia with pyramidal tract dysfunction; spasticity does not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Hereditary spastic ataxia affects central motor pathways and cerebellar function.
Umbrella hereditary spastic ataxia affecting central motor and cerebellar pathways; extra-neurologic findings are subtype-specific.
Respiratory disease, cataracts and malabsorption define the syndrome; progressive end-stage renal disease affected both reported siblings. Otitis omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: cataracts are a defining structural manifestation; retained within the cap alongside respiratory, intestinal and severe renal disease.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: recurrent infections do not establish an intrinsic immunodeficiency; the syndrome itself is not an infection. Four defining or severe organ manifestations take priority.

basis: Limb fusion, renal/urinary agenesis and anal atresia define syndrome, each in 80-99%; cardiovascular malformations occur in 30-79%; additional axes omitted under cap.
Chronic cutaneous hyperkeratosis defines EKV. Supplied 30-79% ocular/endocrine annotations conflict with its usual skin-limited course and do not establish common direct damage across the umbrella.

decisions.ocular: none: despite supplied 30-79% annotations, cataract/glaucoma are not established common direct manifestations across the EKV umbrella.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the supplied diabetes frequency does not establish direct endocrine damage from EKV; diabetes is not a characteristic manifestation across this umbrella.

basis: Epileptic encephalopathy and broad thumbs define the syndrome; cataracts/optic pallor and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each occur in 80-99%.
Antigen-driven immune inflammation directly affects pulmonary alveoli and interstitium.
SCID defined by absent functional T and B lymphocytes: immune deficiency and a blood-cell deficiency. Respiratory and intestinal infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: T-negative/B-negative SCID is defined by deficiency of two blood-cell lineages; the blood-cell mechanism rule applies alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Intellectual disability, epilepsy, spasticity and hemiplegia define neurologic disease; muscle stiffness reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Defining spinal dysraphism affects neural tube and vertebral arches; hypospadias is a urethral malformation. Both defining anomalies occur in 80-99%.
Acute leukemia of erythroid precursors with marrow disease and cytopenias; no common direct extramedullary organ damage established.
Gut and marrow cytotoxicity; cardiac injury and renal failure each 30-79%. Encephalopathy (30-79%) and secondary acid-base/electrolyte derangements omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: renal insufficiency and oliguric renal failure occur in 30-79%; severe organ dysfunction retained at the cap.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: acidosis (80-99%) and electrolyte abnormalities are secondary systemic derangements; severe cardiac and renal organ failure take priority at four-axis cap.

basis: Formate toxicity defines metabolic acidosis and CNS/visual-system injury; visual impairment and putaminal abnormalities are annotated at 30-79%; hypertension alone adds no organ.
Defining metabolic acidosis occurs in 80-99%; common intoxication signs do not establish neural damage. Encephalopathy occurs in 1-4%, renal insufficiency in 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: none: common ataxia/confusion/drowsiness are acute intoxication signs; damaging encephalopathy or cerebral edema is reported in only 1-4%.

basis: Characteristic caustic oral/GI injury and pulmonary toxicity; direct tubular renal injury occurs in ~40-70%. Functionally significant hepatic injury is not reliably ≥30%.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic injury varies substantially with dose and case severity; ≥30% with functional hepatic damage across the poisoning spectrum is not established.

basis: Defined by cardiac conduction toxicity and toxic cerebral dysfunction with confusion or altered mental status; nausea and visual symptoms do not establish additional organ injury.

decisions.neurologic: primary: toxic confusion and altered mental status are direct cerebral dysfunction explicitly included in the definition; delirium falls within this axis.

basis: Congenital obstruction of pulmonary veins; resulting pulmonary hypertension is vascular. Respiratory symptoms and infections do not establish common direct lung damage.
Congenital cardiac outflow obstruction. The laryngeal-stenosis annotation conflicts with the defined condition and is not accepted as typical involvement.
Congenital obstruction below the pulmonary valve affects the right ventricular outflow tract, not lung tissue.
Developmental impairment, microcephaly and postural instability define the syndrome; overbite and facial dysmorphism alone do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Developmental brain malformation with severe intellectual disability, spasticity and seizures; associated cardiac and ocular abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Skeletal dysplasia, nail dystrophy and night blindness define the syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Associated ear infections are separate conditions.
Congenital narrowing of the pulmonary arterial outflow above the pulmonary valve.
Bilateral adrenal hemorrhage directly damages endocrine glands; bleeding does not itself establish a coagulation disorder.
Viral hemorrhagic disease with thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy; hepatic injury 80-99%, renal insufficiency 30-79%. Neurologic dysfunction 30-79% omitted under cap; rash is transient.
Junin virus infection characteristically causes leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and hemostatic abnormalities; gastrointestinal symptoms alone do not establish injury.
Machupo infection is defined by hemorrhagic dysfunction and neurologic manifestations, including encephalopathic injury.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurologic manifestations are explicitly part of the disease definition; the primary tier does not require a separate >=30% estimate.

basis: Guanarito virus infection defined by haemorrhagic manifestations and haemostatic abnormalities; lasting neurologic damage is not established as common.
Sabia virus infection with defining hemorrhagic dysfunction; limited case data do not establish common direct injury to other organs.
Arenaviral hemorrhagic fever with bleeding/coagulation disturbance; severe encephalopathy with delirium, coma or seizures in about one-third untreated.
Hantavirus infection causes pulmonary capillary leak and respiratory failure; myocardial depression with circulatory failure occurs in roughly 30–50%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: myocardial depression and circulatory failure affect roughly 30–50%; this is direct cardiac dysfunction rather than an isolated transient blood-pressure sign.

basis: Viral infection usually causing self-limited fever; ocular injury occurs in <30%, while hemorrhagic, hepatic and encephalitic disease are rare.
Viral hemorrhagic fever with thrombocytopenia and bleeding; second-phase neurologic involvement occurs in a minority.
Viral infection defined by hemorrhagic manifestations; meningitis, pneumonia and nephrosis are minority complications.
Carcinoma originates in renal tubular epithelium; metastatic organ damage is not established in at least 30% across all patients.
Carcinoma arising from renal collecting-duct intercalated cells; metastases do not meet the common-involvement threshold.
Renal cell carcinoma originating in the kidney; nonspecific systemic symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Renal epithelial carcinoma; prior neuroblastoma describes the patient population rather than current neurologic involvement.
Primary renal epithelial malignancy; metastases to other organs are rare.
Congenital myopathy with weakness and joint contractures; facial weakness and hyporeflexia do not establish nerve damage. Intellectual disability is occasional.
Inherited acute myeloid leukaemia affects marrow and myeloid blood cells; connective-tissue ancestry does not establish locomotor disease.
Clonal myeloid blast malignancy of marrow and blood; other tissue infiltration is uncommon, and infections are secondary complications.
Familial carcinoma originates in thyroid; nonspecific neck vessel morphology does not establish vascular injury; other organ cancers are separate diseases.
Carcinoma originates in the thyroid endocrine gland; renal neoplasia is restricted to a subtype.
Inherited steroid metabolic liver disease with hepatic failure and defining numerical dental anomalies; enamel defects also very frequent.
Primary cutaneous amyloid deposition causes progressive pigmentary skin lesions; systemic amyloidosis is explicitly absent.
Conjunctival lymphoid malignancy defines ocular involvement; lymphoma is a haematologic neoplasm and qualifies for the immune mechanism axis.
Glutathione metabolic defect with haemolysis and phagocyte dysfunction; ID and seizures occur in 30-79% by HPO, although neurological disease concentrates in severe forms.
Inherited red-cell dehydration and hemolysis; gallstones are separately diagnosed, ferritin alone does not prove liver damage, and pseudohyperkalemia is an artifact.
Hereditary degeneration of motor pathways causes spastic paraplegia; additional organs vary across complex subtypes.
Progressive corticospinal tract disease with frequent axonal neuropathy; cardiomyopathy and diabetes occur in only 5-29%.
White matter hypoplasia, callosal agenesis and intellectual disability define the disease; facial dysmorphism does not establish other organ damage.
Bladder and urethral malformations define the spectrum; abdominal wall defects occur in 30-79%. Gastrointestinal and spinal malformations affect minority subtypes.
Deafness, synostoses and neurodevelopmental defects define syndrome; urethral hypospadias 80-99%. Alopecia and dental anomalies, each 30-79%, omitted under cap; only two reported patients.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral defect, within the renal axis, reported in 80-99%; it is not solely a reproductive abnormality.
decisions.dermatologic: none: alopecia in 30-79% qualifies but is excluded by the cap in favor of more frequent urethral malformation; abnormal dermatoglyphics alone do not establish damage.

basis: Defined by sensorineural hearing loss, salivary gland aldosterone resistance and hyponatremia; each reported in 80-99%.
Multiple skeletal joint fusions define the syndrome; conductive hearing impairment from ossicular fixation occurs in 80-99%.
CNS degeneration, deafness and anemia define syndrome; renal tubular acidosis in 1/2 (~50%); dermatitis and acid-base axis omitted at cap.
T-cell immunodeficiency with defining disseminated HPV-associated cutaneous lesions; lymphoma is a reported complication, not common involvement.
Paragangliomas and somatostatinomas are neuroendocrine tumors; polycythemia is defining. Variable vascular and neural tube malformations lack established qualifying frequency.
Primary bone dysplasia affecting tibial cortex, epiphyses and growth plates, with foot deformities.
Developmental delay and movement abnormalities define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Minor facial and ear dysmorphism does not establish additional functional damage.
Absent optic chiasm is a central visual-pathway malformation; reduced vision results from abnormal neural routing rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Mixed sclerosing bone dystrophy and increased bone density establish skeletal disease; unspecified extraskeletal manifestations cannot support additional organs or frequencies.
Inherited skeletal-muscle disease with progressive weakness, atrophy and filamentous inclusions; not autoimmune inclusion-body myositis.
Named muscle/liver syndrome with obligate cerebellar abnormalities and muscular dystrophy; retinal dysplasia occurs in 100%. Orofacial clefting (80-99%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: obligate cerebellar abnormalities, frequent major brain malformations and the intellectual-disability parent establish a defining neurologic component.

basis: Mitochondrial cardiomyopathy and renal disease define disorder; cerebral atrophy/developmental delay 30-79%. Myopathy also common but omitted at cap.
Intellectual disability, retinal degeneration and hearing loss define syndrome; laryngeal stenosis/vocal paralysis 30-79%; skeletal defects omitted by cap.
Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia defines the disease; neurodevelopmental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting neurologic injury beyond transient hypoglycemic symptoms.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory weakness and motor delay are muscular. Frequent skin thickening lacks documented functional damage.
Inherited peripheral motor and sensory neuropathy with neuropathic pain; no independently qualifying additional organ is established.
Structural skeletal myopathy with axial weakness, contractures and scoliosis. Common hypoventilation results from respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct pulmonary disease.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with pyramidal involvement; persistent denervation causes distal muscle atrophy and structural foot deformity in most patients (>30%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: lasting distal muscle atrophy and pes cavus are characteristic in most patients (>30%), representing structural damage integral to CMT2.

basis: Viral infection; inflammatory arthritis occurs in 30-79% and can persist. Rash is generally transient; neurologic damage is uncommon.
Hendra viral disease has respiratory and encephalitic forms; viral encephalitis ancestry and respiratory failure establish its principal organ targets.
Recurrent painful dermal ecchymoses with autoimmune classification; coagulation abnormalities are occasional, so no haematologic axis is added.
Invasive extraintestinal Salmonella infection; respiratory signs do not establish pneumonia in >=30%; abscesses and meningitis are occasional.
Amyloid deposition damages cerebral vessel walls, producing recurrent lobar intracerebral hemorrhage and cognitive decline.
Amyloid deposition damages cerebral vessels and brain, with hemorrhage, stroke and dementia reported in 80-99%.
Cerebral vascular amyloid deposition with defining recurrent intracerebral hemorrhage and dementia.
Cerebral vascular amyloid deposition and progressive dementia define the disease; intracerebral hemorrhage occurs in a subset.
APP-related cerebral amyloid angiopathy with progressive Alzheimer-like dementia; the definition specifically excludes intracerebral hemorrhage.
Across the main subtypes, skeletal dysplasia and sparse hair are defining; intellectual disability is concentrated in type II.
Inherited autoinflammatory disease umbrella; fever and episodic inflammatory symptoms do not establish common lasting damage to another organ across subtypes.
Defined by immune inflammation, oral ulcers and auricular chondritis; keratitis/scleritis 30-79%. Nasal chondritis and erythema nodosum omitted by cap.
Absent testes cause gonadal hormone failure with low testosterone in 80-99%; supplied urethrovaginal fistula/urogenital sinus annotations support urinary involvement at 30-79%.
Urogenital sinus and perineal urethral malformations occur in 80-99%; urethra maps to renal. Gonadal differentiation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
STAR deficiency impairs adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis, causing classic adrenal insufficiency and sex-hormone deficiency.
Inherited adrenal steroidogenesis disorder causing nonclassic lipoid adrenal hyperplasia.
Gonadal dysgenesis and impaired gonadal hormone function characterize the major sex chromosome DSD subtypes; other organ defects vary across subtypes.
Immune dysregulation with lymphoproliferation and multilineage cytopenias; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage, and hepatitis is under 30%.
Congenital fusion of the jaws and oral tissues defines syngnathia, directly restricting mouth opening; dysostosis ancestry supports skeletal involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: syngnathia is congenital fusion within the oral cavity that directly restricts mouth opening; the mouth is included in the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Congenital jaw fusion or adhesions impair mandibular movement; associated cleft palate directly affects oral anatomy.
Disabling elbow-bone fusion; ureter/upper urinary tract anomalies and cavernous vascular tumors each reported in 80-99% per supplied HPO.
Congenital fusion of radius and ulna causes restricted forearm rotation; associated syndromic disorders do not define the umbrella.
Plasmalogen synthesis defects commonly cause neurodevelopmental impairment, skeletal dysplasia and cataracts or retinal disease (>30% across major clinical phenotypes).
Intramedullary spinal cord cavities directly damage neural tissue; no additional axis is consistently affected across the umbrella.
Multifocal atrial electrical dysfunction produces a supraventricular arrhythmia; associated findings remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital cardiac conduction-system tachyarrhythmia; associated cardiomyopathy remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder causing adrenergically triggered ventricular arrhythmias; vertigo and syncope do not establish neurologic injury.
Large-vessel vasculitis; skin ulcers and arthritis each annotated at 30-79%. Retinopathy and stroke are under 30%; renal artery disease remains cardiovascular.
Autoinflammatory immunodeficiency with amylopectin storage; damaging skeletal myopathy affects most classic cases, and cardiomyopathy roughly a third or more of reported patients.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: myocardial amylopectin accumulation causes cardiomyopathy in roughly >=30% of classic reported cases; this is direct storage-related damage.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal muscle amylopectinosis with myopathy is characteristic and affects most classic reported cases, rather than being incidental storage.

basis: Thrombosis of cerebral veins and venous sinuses defines this cerebrovascular disorder; associated infections are separate conditions.
Severe obesity and insulin resistance define the metabolic disorder; developmental speech and language impairment occurs in 30–79%, supporting neurologic involvement.
Defining vertebral/rib malformations, urethral malformation (hypospadias) and intellectual disability.
Strabismus and periocular anomalies accompany defining pes cavus and skeletal malformations. Intellectual disability is not established by the supplied description.
Inherited metabolic neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation and neuroaxonal injury.
Inherited lipid biosynthesis disorder causes progressive neurodegeneration; optic atrophy and visual impairment occur in 30-79%.
Thrombocytosis and transverse limb reduction defects define the syndrome; splenomegaly is covered by the haematologic axis.
Defined by cutaneous vascular lesions with underlying muscle or bone atrophy; these constitute the characteristic syndrome.
Mitochondrial myopathy with ophthalmoplegia; hearing impairment 30-79%. Neuropathy/ataxia mostly 5-29%; respiratory weakness does not establish lung damage.
Autoimmune encephalitis; direct antibody-mediated enteric dysfunction causes persistent severe diarrhea and weight loss in approximately 50-70%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: direct enteric autoimmunity causes sustained intestinal loss of function, with severe diarrhea and weight loss in approximately 50-70%; tissue destruction is not required.

basis: Acute leukemia of megakaryocytic lineage involving blood and bone marrow.
Progressive spastic paraplegia and Paget disease of bone define the syndrome; weakness is neurogenic, without reported myopathy.
Distal skeletal myopathy with vacuoles and muscle loss; dementia and progressive neurologic deterioration are frequent, 30-79%.
BWS-like imprinting disorder with hyperinsulinism and lateralized overgrowth; macroglossia is variable, without established common gastrointestinal impairment.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: macroglossia is variable; neither a defining gastrointestinal abnormality nor common functional damage is established for this mosaic disorder.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized somatic and skeletal overgrowth is a characteristic component of the BWS-like phenotype.

basis: Immune-mediated giant-cell inflammation causes myocardial necrosis, fibrosis and ventricular dysfunction.
Hypertrophic gastric mucosal disease; associated anemia does not establish direct blood or marrow disease.
Immune-mediated myositis; inflammatory skin disease occurs in roughly 80-90% as juvenile dermatomyositis predominates; interstitial lung disease is below 30%.
Autoimmune inflammatory skeletal myopathy; overlap diseases are separately diagnosed, and cardiac damage is reported only in some patients.
Complement-mediated glomerular injury; ocular abnormalities occur in 5-29%. Secondary hypertension does not establish direct vascular injury.
Transient riboflavin-related metabolic dysfunction with acidosis and hypoglycemia; complete resolution and no established additional organ damage.
Recurrent joint effusions, typically involving the knee; a definite autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism is not established.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in the appendix; endocrine cell differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Carcinoma originates in appendix. Neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine gland disease; common spread remains gastrointestinal or outside the axes.
Amyloid cardiomyopathy; neuropathy and gastrointestinal dysmotility each annotated 30-79%. Pulmonary/hepatic congestion is secondary; renal involvement is 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: supplied HPO annotations place amyloid-associated gastrointestinal dysmotility and chronic diarrhea at 30-79%, supporting common functional involvement.

basis: Direct lead neurotoxicity; hypertension annotated at 30-79%. Anemia and renal tubular dysfunction are 5-29%; GI symptoms alone do not establish injury.
Direct neurotoxicity, acute kidney injury and interstitial pneumonitis are documented at 30-79%; blood-pressure changes alone do not establish lasting cardiovascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension is annotated at 30-79%, but the evidence does not distinguish transient toxic blood-pressure changes from persistent cardiovascular disease.

basis: Hypotrichosis and deafness are the defining manifestations.
Inherited hemoglobin disorder causing thalassemic anemia; skeletal damage is severity-dependent and iron-related organ damage may be treatment-related.
Inherited abnormal hemoglobin causes methemoglobinemia and impaired blood oxygen carriage; cyanosis alone does not establish skin or cardiopulmonary damage.
Scarring vesicular photodermatitis; ocular damage is occasional (5-29%), below threshold.
Chronic photosensitive eczema mediated by delayed cellular hypersensitivity; no common extracutaneous organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and epilepsy define the disorder. Joint hypermobility occurs in 80-99%, but accompanying joint injury or functional loss is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility (80-99%) alone does not establish damaging joint disease; generalized hypotonia can reflect the primary neurologic disorder.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease, skeletal anomalies and mosaic skin changes define the syndrome; heart failure and pulmonary arterial hypertension are annotated at 80-99%.
Inherited coagulation deficiency; cerebral hemorrhage and joint/intramuscular hemorrhage are each annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting direct brain and musculoskeletal injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint and intramuscular hemorrhage are direct tissue injuries, each annotated frequent (30-79%); these exceed superficial bruising.

basis: Developmental impairment and characteristic skeletal hypoplasia/contractures define syndrome; visual dysfunction 30-79%. Renal/biliary defects mostly 5-29%; pilomatrixoma is separate.

decisions.dermatologic: none: pilomatrixoma is a separately diagnosed associated neoplasm, despite its annotated frequency of 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal abnormalities, including distal phalangeal hypoplasia and contractures, are characteristic components of the syndrome's definition.

basis: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma directly infiltrates skin and destroys elastic tissue. Associated Hodgkin lymphoma is separate; renal findings occur in only 5-29%.
Congenital limb deficiencies define the embryopathy; cardiovascular malformations occur in 30-79%. Ear and hearing defects are annotated below 30%.
Immunodeficiency with dermatitis and recurrent respiratory infections defines the group; skeletal and dental abnormalities vary by subtype.
Selective antibody deficiency; recurrent infections are separately diagnosed consequences, while bronchiectasis and chronic sinusitis occur in only 5-29%.
Renal dysplasia or agenesis, cardiac malformations and oral clefts define the syndrome; each is reported in 80-99%.
Central disorder of sleep-wake regulation with persistent hypersomnolence; a neurologic sleep disorder despite psychiatric-style coding.
Marrow failure, cerebellar hypoplasia and immunodeficiency define disease; dermal atrophy 80-99%. Cap excludes gastrointestinal oral leukoplakia, reported in 30-79%.
Congenital thrombocytopenia, callosal agenesis/developmental delay and mandibular hypoplasia define disease; cleft palate accompanies Robin sequence in approximately 80-90%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate commonly accompanies Robin sequence (~80-90%); it is a structural oral defect rather than a feeding symptom.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: mandibular hypoplasia is a defining component of the named Robin sequence.

basis: Inherited thrombomodulin abnormality classified as a blood coagulation disorder.
Immune platelet disorder with defining hypercoagulability and common venous or arterial thrombosis; cerebral and pulmonary complications are occasional.
Congenital tibial deficiency and split-hand/foot skeletal malformations define the syndrome; other organ abnormalities are uncommon.
Chronic benign lymphocytic infiltration is confined to skin; an autoimmune mechanism is not established. Cutaneous lymphocytes do not establish a blood-cell disease.
Brittle sulfur-deficient hair defines the group; supplied neurologic, ocular and skeletal phenotypes are occasional (5-29%).
Inherited atrial rhythm disorder; stroke and thromboembolism are minority complications.
Primary hepatic malignancy; portal venous invasion with tumor thrombosis directly occupies vessels. Portal vein thrombosis is frequent (30–79%) in the supplied HPO annotations.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: HCC directly invades portal veins and produces tumor thrombus; supplied HPO places portal vein thrombosis at 30–79%.

basis: Immune-mediated lichen planus with characteristic cutaneous blistering; common damaging oral involvement is not established for this variant.
Absent or atretic trachea defines disease; cardiac septal malformations are reported in 80-99%.
Meningococcal infection of the meninges; permanent hearing loss and other extra-meningeal sequelae occur in a minority.
Inherited fibrinogen coagulation defect. Bleeding alone does not establish other organ damage; the supplied cataract, cardiac and malformation annotations are discordant.
Hair/skin appendage dysplasia and dental agenesis define the syndrome; scoliosis and hyperlordosis are frequent (30-79%). Ocular abnormalities are occasional.
Defining hair and nail dysplasia, dental abnormalities and syndactyly affect skin appendages, teeth and the skeletal system.
Recurrent inflammation of subcutaneous fat defines disease; autoimmunity and visceral enlargement occur in only 5-29%; pain and nausea do not establish organ damage.
Defined by craniosynostosis and structural abnormalities of thumbs, fingers and toes; shallow orbits alone do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Premature fusion of the metopic skull suture; developmental delay is occasional and intracranial hypertension/papilledema occur in only 1-4%.
Learning, language and developmental impairment are common; renal, cardiac and ovarian abnormalities are under 30%; tall stature and minor clinodactyly do not establish damage.
Skull ossification defects 80-99%; cataract/eye malformations and cleft palate 30-79%. Listed CNS malformations individually 5-29%; hepatomegaly alone does not show hepatic damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: supplied CNS malformations individually occur in 5-29%; common neurologic dysfunction or a major neurologic diagnostic criterion is not established.

basis: Brain, cardiac and ocular malformations define the syndrome; cleft palate 80-99% impairs oral function. Cap omits skeletal, renal and hearing abnormalities.
Developmental disability and skeletal malformations define syndrome; vesicoureteral reflux and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%. Heart abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Defined by multiple benign hair-follicle hamartomas; no extracutaneous involvement is established.
Severe developmental impairment, skeletal defects and heart malformations define the syndrome; GI atresias occur in 30-79%; choanal atresia 30-79% omitted by cap.
Congenital cardiac outflow and great-vessel malformation; pulmonary arteries are cardiovascular. Lung hypoplasia and edema are occasional.
Congenital failure of neural tube closure affecting brain or spinal cord; additional skeletal and urinary defects vary across subtypes.
Mycobacterial infection predominantly located in the lungs; individual extrapulmonary sites do not meet the common-involvement threshold across the umbrella.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: lungs are the predominant anatomical site explicitly described in the definition and characterize the usual disease.

basis: Francisella infection; pneumonia annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting direct pulmonary involvement. Localized skin lesions are annotated occasional (5-29%).
Malignant tumour of muscle and supportive soft connective tissues; specific visceral or vascular origins belong to subtypes.
Thymic epithelial tumor, classified under endocrine gland neoplasms in the supplied ancestry. Associated myasthenia and other autoimmune diseases are separately diagnosed.
Hantaviral infection with defining renal and hemorrhagic blood dysfunction; direct endothelial barrier failure causes capillary leak in 80-99%. Pulmonary disease is only 5-29%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: capillary leak in 80-99% reflects direct endothelial barrier dysfunction with circulatory impairment, rather than an isolated transient skin sign.

basis: Congenital connection between the ascending aorta and a ventricle; associated structural abnormalities and heart failure remain cardiovascular.
Transient biochemical disorder of tyrosine metabolism; definition explicitly states no clinical symptoms or organ damage.
Congenital absence of right ventricular myocardium causes ventricular dysfunction and heart failure; pleural effusion is occasional.
Intestinal atresia, umbilical-vessel ulceration and severe fetal hemorrhage define the syndrome; anemia occurs in 80-99%, cardiac malformations in 30-79%.
audit_reason: Move haematologic to primary: severe fetal hemorrhage is explicitly defining, rather than ancillary involvement. Retain gastrointestinal for atresia and cardiovascular for umbilical-vessel ulceration.

basis: Follicular keratosis and inflammation cause facial skin atrophy, scarring and eyebrow hair loss; eyebrow location does not establish eye involvement.
Viral infection defined by vascular injury and hemorrhagic/hemostatic dysfunction; specific visceral injuries vary across the umbrella.
Autoinflammatory recurrent peritoneal/pleural serositis defines FMF. Joint attacks usually resolve without damage; persistent destructive arthritis is <30%. Renal amyloidosis is separate.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent pleural serositis is a defining manifestation; pleuritis is frequent (30-79%) in the supplied HPO data.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: arthralgia and acute arthritis usually resolve without residual injury; persistent destructive arthritis affects fewer than 30%.

basis: Congenital ventricular outflow malformation; annotated clefts and developmental findings reflect syndromic associations rather than direct cardiac disease damage.
Congenital malformation of ventricular outflow and great-artery origins; associated defects remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Profound intellectual disability, microcephaly and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; cataracts occur in 30–79%.
Autoimmune panuveitis with diagnostic meningeal inflammation; persistent skin/hair pigment loss occurs in 80-99%. Hearing loss (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: meningeal inflammation is a major diagnostic domain; CSF pleocytosis and cognitive impairment are annotated at 80-99%.

basis: Arboviral infection umbrella, usually presenting with nonspecific fever; encephalitis, hemorrhage and organ damage are not common across the group.
Congenital hearing loss and skin/hair pigment abnormalities define the syndrome. Iris pigmentation does not establish visual damage; bowel and neurologic disease are minority subtype features.
Defined by intellectual disability, generalized bone hypoplasia with reduced muscle mass, and cleft palate; cleft palate reported as obligate.
Eye and skeletal abnormalities define WMS; persistent skin thickening and structural cardiovascular abnormalities each occur in 30-79% per HPO.
Infantile epileptic encephalopathy with spasms and developmental regression; nonspecific skin findings may reflect separately diagnosed underlying causes.
Defined by progressive skeletal myopathy and cardiac conduction disease, with later heart failure.
Inherited magnesium transport disorder, predominantly renal tubular wasting; intestinal transport defects vary by subtype and do not establish shared intestinal damage.
Renal magnesium-wasting disorder; persistent psychomotor delay is described as typical, supporting an inferred frequency of at least 30%, although subtype frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: typical mild-to-moderate psychomotor delay supports persistent developmental impairment in an inferred >=30%; transient electrolyte-related symptoms alone would not qualify.

basis: Inherited corneal disease; most disorders across this umbrella remain restricted to the cornea.
Chronic neutrophilic folliculitis destroys hair follicles with scarring alopecia; recurrent skin infections are annotated in 80-99%.
DM/DI, optic atrophy and deafness define DIDMOAD; ataxia/seizures occur in 30-79%; urinary tract/renal disease at 30-79% omitted by the four-axis cap.
Purine metabolism defect with defining xanthine urinary stone disease (HPO 30-79%); kidney failure and myopathy are occasional.

decisions.renal: primary: xanthine stone disease is an explicit defining manifestation, supported by nephrolithiasis frequency of 30-79%; this is intrinsic crystal disease.

basis: CMV colitis 80-99%; encephalitis/myelitis and pneumonitis 30-79%; ocular inflammation and hepatitis also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Viral acute liver failure with defining hepatic encephalopathy; impaired clotting-factor synthesis causes coagulopathy in essentially all cases and is a major diagnostic criterion.

decisions.haematologic: involved: coagulopathy is an acute liver failure diagnostic criterion, present in essentially all cases, with loss of coagulation function.

basis: Severe pneumococcal bloodstream infection; bacteremia alone is not a disease of blood cells, marrow or coagulation.
Epidermal nevi define disease; spinal cord atrophy/compression and spinal canal stenosis are each reported in 30-79%. Ocular and renal abnormalities are below 30%.
Galactose metabolism disorder; predominant classic disease has frequent hepatic injury and neurodevelopmental impairment (~50%); cataracts occur around 30%, varying substantially by subtype.
Inherited lipid biosynthesis disorder umbrella; neurologic damage is prominent in several subtypes, but its frequency across patients in the whole group is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurologic injury varies by subtype; the supplied evidence does not establish that it affects most patients across this umbrella.

basis: Mitochondrial genome maintenance disorders commonly cause myopathy and encephalopathy/neuropathy (>30% across the spectrum); hepatic disease is subtype-dependent.
The defining syndrome combines structural digital anomalies and intellectual disability; no additional organ involvement is established.
Brain malformations, intellectual disability and obesity define the syndrome; HPO reports night blindness in 80-99%; treatment-triggered malignant hyperthermia excluded.
FGF23 excess causes defining hypophosphatemic osteomalacia and renal phosphate-reabsorption dysfunction (80-99%); nephrocalcinosis may be treatment-related.

decisions.renal: primary: renal phosphate-reabsorption dysfunction is a defining diagnostic component, present in 80-99%; structural renal injury is not required for this primary label.

basis: Genetic neurological disorder with epilepsy, intellectual disability and structural cerebral and cerebellar abnormalities.
Progressive epilepsy, dystonia and cerebral degeneration; respiratory infections are separate diseases and optic atrophy is very rare.
Alveolar-capillary dysplasia with pulmonary vascular malformation and hypertension; GI malrotation/atresias occur in roughly 30% or more; urinary frequency uncertain.
Primary phalangeal osteolysis and sclerosis; associated redness does not establish a separate skin disorder.
GBA2-related sphingolipid metabolic disease with central and peripheral neurodegeneration. Ocular motor findings and dysphagia are neurologic; skeletal and hearing abnormalities <30%.
Inborn monoamine transport disorder causes central motor and developmental dysfunction; stridor and unspecified vascular findings do not establish additional organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental, cardiac and skeletal defects define the syndrome; hydronephrosis/reflux occur in 30-79%. Frequent dental malocclusion omitted at the cap.
Immunodeficiency, platelet dysfunction and neuropathy define disease; ocular albinism occurs in 80-99%; skin ulcers/hypopigmentation (80-99%) omitted by cap.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorders predominantly comprise albinism with defining ocular dysfunction and cutaneous hypopigmentation; isolated ocular forms spare skin.
Melanin synthesis disorder defining skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental defects with visual impairment.
Inherited tyrosine/melanin metabolism disorder defined by skin and hair hypopigmentation and ocular abnormalities with reduced visual acuity.
Temperature-sensitive tyrosinase deficiency impairs melanin synthesis, causing defining cutaneous and ocular albinism.
Gluconeogenesis defect causes lactic acidemia; developmental impairment and encephalopathy affect most patients with the infantile form.
Severe gluconeogenesis defect with neonatal acidosis; encephalopathy and neurologic dysfunction affect most patients.
Metabolic enzyme deficiency causes episodic acidosis; neurological development is normal or only mildly delayed, without established common neurological damage.
Congenital arteriovenous malformation of retinal vessels; no evidence of associated brain involvement in this concept.
Retinal capillary telangiectasia and aneurysms define this vascular lesion, causing macular edema, degeneration and visual loss.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: abnormal retinal capillaries and arteriolar/venular aneurysms define the disease; these vessels fall within the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Defining retinal capillary telangiectasia and occlusion cause progressive visual loss. Associated systemic or cerebral vascular disease is separate.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular to primary: juxtafoveolar capillary occlusion and telangiectasia define this vascular disease. Associated systemic or cerebral vascular diseases remain excluded as separate conditions.

basis: Defined as an intraretinal vascular tumor involving retina and local vessels; associated detachment and macular edema remain ocular.
Lysosomal neurodegeneration; skeletal lesions 80-99%, cardiac abnormalities 30-79%. Skin thickening (30-79%) omitted at cap; nystagmus alone does not establish eye damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: structural cardiac abnormalities are annotated at 30-79%, supporting common cardiac involvement.
decisions.ocular: none: nystagmus can reflect CNS disease; common damaging ocular pathology is not established across the group.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: epiphyseal, metaphyseal and diaphyseal abnormalities occur in 80-99%; skeletal disease is secondary to storage.

basis: Macrophage storage defines splenic/marrow disease; hepatic infiltration 80-99% and skeletal damage 30-79%. Neurologic findings concentrate in neuronopathic subtypes and are omitted under the cap.

decisions.haematologic: primary: Gaucher disease is a macrophage storage disease with defining splenic/marrow involvement and cytopenias, satisfying the blood-cell/marrow mechanism rule.

basis: Mitochondrial CoQ10 deficiency; neurologic dysfunction is common (>30%). Renal, muscle, cardiac and hearing damage vary by subtype without clear group-wide frequencies.
Immune-mediated choroidal inflammation causes recurrent lesions, scarring and visual loss.
Histiocytic neoplasm with defining bone lesions; endocrine dysfunction 80-99%, cardiovascular infiltration 30-79%. Renal hydronephrosis 30-79% and orbital involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cardiovascular infiltration occurs in approximately 50-70%, with aortic abnormalities annotated at 30-79%; frequency and severity favor retention.
decisions.renal: none: hydronephrosis at 30-79% supports involvement, but renal disease is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent, severe cardiovascular involvement.

basis: Structural deformity of the radius, ulna and wrist with restricted joint mobility.
Progressive upper motor neuron degeneration; dysphagia, urinary urgency and weakness do not establish direct digestive, urinary or muscle damage.
Deletion syndrome associated with neurodevelopmental impairment; absent definition and phenotype annotations limit confidence and preclude additional organ labels.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; neurologic and muscle dysfunction are common across major forms (>30% each). Hepatic damage varies by subtype; >=30% overall is uncertain.
DGKE-associated renal thrombotic microangiopathy causes hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and kidney injury; complement-independent disease.
Hereditary retinoblastoma affects the retina; other malignancies are separate diseases or later risks.
Malignant retinal tumour; non-hereditary status does not change its organ of origin.
Inborn serine biosynthesis deficiency defined by microcephaly, neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures.
Glycosylation disorder defined by cutis laxa and neurodevelopmental/brain abnormalities; high myopia 80-99%; joint hypermobility 11/12 omitted at cap.
Subclavian arterial compression and injury causing upper-extremity ischemia; neurologic TOS is a different subtype.
Thoracic outlet compression affects the subclavian vein, often with thrombosis; arm pain does not establish nerve damage.
Defining fibrosis of oral and oropharyngeal mucosa; pharyngeal abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Trismus reflects mucosal fibrosis.
Progressive scalp dermal thickening; definition explicitly excludes associated neurologic and ocular abnormalities.
Scalp folds with defining neurodevelopmental abnormalities distinguish the non-essential form. Developmental cataracts occur in 30-79%; cardiac and skeletal defects are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: associated neurologic abnormalities distinguish the non-essential form; developmental impairment, seizures and structural brain injury are annotated at 30-79%.

basis: Congenital optic disc malformation with impaired vision; optic nerve involvement belongs to the ocular axis. Extraocular anomalies are not consistently common.
Glomerular protein loss defines nephrotic syndrome; an immune mechanism is not established across all idiopathic subtypes.
Malignancy originating in ovarian germ cells; reproductive tissue has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Malignant ovarian sex cord-stromal cells constitute gonadal endocrine tissue; sex-steroid production and hormone excess characterize the group.
Opioid toxicity directly depresses consciousness and central respiratory drive; apnea does not itself establish intrinsic pulmonary injury, and miosis is not ocular damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory depression is caused by suppression of brain respiratory drive; the defining toxidrome does not establish direct lung or airway injury.

basis: Inherited glaucoma causes optic nerve damage and visual field loss; systemic features vary by subtype.
Inherited coagulation factor deficiency. Mucosal bleeding does not establish organ damage; joint and intracranial haemorrhage occur in 5-29%.
Malignant astrocytic CNS tumor; visual loss and weakness reflect central nervous system injury rather than direct eye or skeletal muscle damage.
Intestinal lymphatic abnormality causes protein-losing enteropathy; edema and hypoproteinemia do not establish direct damage to other organs.
Staphylococcal toxin-mediated infection; the scarlatiniform rash is transient and does not establish lasting skin damage.
Staphylococcal exfoliative toxins directly cause epidermal blistering and desquamation.
Staphylococcal skin infection with blistering and erosions; joint and renal complications are occasional, below 30%.
Staphylococcal infection directly destroys lung tissue; reactive blood counts and hypotension do not establish additional organ damage.
Diffuse infiltrative adenocarcinoma of the stomach wall.
Inherited amino acid transport disorder with cerebellar degeneration; optic disc pallor indicates ocular damage in 30-79%.
Inherited spinal motor-neuron disease; chronic denervation causes defining skeletal muscle atrophy and loss of function in most patients.
Adenocarcinoma of paratesticular reproductive tissues; no covered organ or qualifying mechanism axis.
Germ cell tumour arising in the testis; reproductive tumour origin does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining hepatic and cerebral dysfunction; renal tubular disease is a defining component, supporting renal involvement without a frequency estimate.
Biphasic encephalopathy with seizures and cerebral white-matter injury; infection is a trigger, not an intrinsic infectious diagnosis.
Defined as inflammation-mediated refractory status epilepticus; autoimmunity is frequent (30-79%), with persistent neurological sequelae.
Site-variable umbrella, predominantly mediastinal or retroperitoneal, without a shared listed organ axis. CNS and lung origins define particular subtypes.

decisions.pulmonary: none: mediastinum is not lung; pulmonary origin is a site-specific subtype, not a usual feature across this umbrella.
decisions.neurologic: none: CNS origin defines a subtype and cannot be generalized to most extragonadal germ cell tumours.

basis: Germ cell tumors originate in reproductive gonadal tissue, rather than hormone-producing endocrine tissue.
Cardiocutaneous degeneration defines LCPS; emphysema and intracranial hemorrhage each annotated 80-99%. Dyslipidemia omitted at cap; cancer predisposition does not add organs.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intracranial hemorrhage is annotated 80-99%, supporting common direct brain injury from the syndrome's vasculopathy rather than merely an increased future risk.

basis: Developmental disability and skeletal malformations define syndrome; gingival overgrowth and high myopia each 30-79%. Ear morphology alone does not establish hearing dysfunction.
Intellectual disability, seizures and corpus callosum abnormalities occur in 80-99%; facial dysmorphism alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited skeletal myopathy with defining severe external ophthalmoplegia; genetic myopathy does not imply immune-mediated myositis.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; vertebral fusions and contractures are variable without established frequency.
NF1 affects nerves and skin; bone cysts/scoliosis and structural heart anomalies each have supplied frequencies of 30-79%; Lisch nodules are non-damaging.
Progressive cerebral astrogliopathy defines disease. Scoliosis occurs in 30-79% but is secondary to neurologic impairment rather than direct skeletal pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is frequent (30-79%) but reflects secondary neuromuscular deformity; direct skeletal disease is not established.

basis: Astrogliopathy affecting brainstem, spinal cord and white matter; dysphagia, nystagmus and bladder symptoms reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Posterior parietal lesions cause visual processing and gaze deficits; the definition explicitly excludes underlying ophthalmologic abnormalities.
Inherited dissection directly damages cervical arteries; associated stroke is a separately diagnosed complication.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy, predominantly from sphingolipid biosynthesis defects; trophic skin damage and ulcers affect 30-79%; arthropathy and hearing loss only 5-29%.
Inherited epilepsy spectrum defined by generalized and febrile seizures; no qualifying damage outside the nervous system.
Paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes predominantly cause immune-mediated injury to the nervous system; other sites vary across subtypes.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; visual impairment ~50-75%, cardiac and renal/urinary malformations each ~25-50%. Joint laxity alone does not establish damaging skeletal disease.

decisions.renal: involved: congenital renal/urinary malformations occur in approximately 25-50%; the usual range supports inclusion near the 30% threshold.
decisions.ocular: involved: persistent visual impairment occurs in approximately 50-75%, commonly from refractive and ocular alignment abnormalities.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint laxity and minor skeletal traits are common, but damaging locomotor abnormalities are not established in >=30%.

basis: Koolen-de Vries neurodevelopmental syndrome; additional congenital anomalies are variable and not established here as common organ damage.
Inherited neurodegenerative disorder defined by cerebral atrophy.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal erythrocytes, causing severe anemia and hydrops. Edema and anemia-related circulatory stress do not establish direct cardiac injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: anemia-related high-output stress and hydrops do not establish direct cardiac injury; fluid accumulation alone is insufficient.

basis: EBV-driven T-cell lymphoma with severe cytopenias; hepatic infiltration and liver dysfunction are common, often progressing to liver failure.
EBV-associated cutaneous T-cell lymphoma: skin tumour origin, malignant lymphoid cells and lymphoma mechanism.
Mature B-cell lymphoma primarily involving lymph nodes; marrow, hepatic and gastrointestinal involvement is explicitly infrequent.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with progressive dystonia, dyskinesia and severe intellectual disability.
Immune small-vessel cutaneous vasculitis; renal disease in 30-79%. Arthritis and ocular inflammation also occur in 30-79%, omitted by cap; destructive lung disease is less frequent.
Congenital failure of talar fragments to fuse causes a structural bone and ankle disorder.
Immune-mediated skin and mucosal epithelial necrosis; destructive oral mucositis is defining and occurs in about 90%. Supplied damaging ocular phenotypes occur in 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: destructive oral mucositis is a defining mucosal manifestation, present in about 90%; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Inherited disorders of skeletal growth and development; extraskeletal involvement is subtype-specific.
Primary skeletal dysplasia; conductive hearing loss is common across OPD and frontometaphyseal forms, estimated >=30% across the spectrum. Cleft palate is subtype-dependent.

decisions.otologic: involved: conductive hearing loss from ossicular abnormalities is common across several major spectrum disorders, supporting an estimated frequency of at least ~30%.

basis: Defined by developmental abnormalities of individual bones or groups of bones; additional organ findings vary across subtypes.
Craniofacial and limb skeletal malformations define this umbrella; other organ abnormalities vary by subtype.
Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias and arthropathy; extra-skeletal TRPV4 disorders are not shared defining manifestations.
Autoimmune parathyroid failure; cataracts reported at 30-79% are separately diagnosed complications. Paresthesias do not establish nerve injury; renal stones are occasional.
Defining intellectual disability and movement disorder; muscular dystrophy/myopathy and cataracts each occur in 30-79%; pulmonary and cardiac findings are under 30%.
Inherited obesity with hyperinsulinemia; developmental delay, cognitive impairment and autonomic dysfunction are annotated in 80-99%.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and infantile hypotonia define neurological involvement; borderline lactate alone does not establish metabolic disease.
Peroxisomal neurometabolic disease with severe developmental impairment and cholestatic liver failure; hearing loss 30–79%. Cataracts 5–29%.
ID/seizures and syndromic obesity define disease; ocular dysfunction and MVP/WPW each 80-99%; hearing loss, eczema and dental defects omitted by cap.
Hyperphalangy, toe malformations and severe pectus excavatum define a skeletal malformation syndrome.
Diffuse thickening and painful fissuring of palmoplantar skin.
Palmoplantar and joint-overlying keratoses affect skin; joint keratoses do not imply joint disease.
Intellectual disability and structural hand anomalies define the syndrome; individual hand findings vary. Hearing, nail and other abnormalities are each below 30%.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses; no evidence supporting another organ.
Spondylometaphyseal skeletal dysplasia affects vertebral and metaphyseal bone development.
Myeloid leukemia with coagulopathy; leukemic skin infiltration occurs in roughly 30-40%. Hepatic infiltration reaching 30% across ages is not established by hepatomegaly alone.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly is described, but direct hepatic infiltration in at least 30% across the disease population is uncertain and varies with age.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: direct leukemic skin infiltration occurs in approximately 30-40%, meeting the threshold for substantial organ occupation.

basis: Inherited syrinx formation within the spinal cord causes neurological tissue damage.
Congenital cutaneous hair nevus; no common extracutaneous damage established by the supplied record.
Association of congenital skin aplasia and sebaceous nevus; both defining lesions affect skin.
SCALP denotes sebaceous nevus, CNS malformations, aplasia cutis, limbal dermoid and pigmented nevus; skin, brain and ocular lesions define the syndrome.
Epidermal nevus with severe extracutaneous vascular malformations, arteriovenous shunts and aneurysms defines the syndrome.
CNS defects, nail dysplasia and craniofacial skeletal anomalies define the embryopathy; cleft lip/palate is a major defining anomaly. Variable cardiac anomalies omitted at the four-axis cap.
audit_reason: Add gastrointestinal for cleft lip/palate, a major defining structural anomaly. Only three axes were retained, so the four-axis cap cannot justify omitting both palatal and cardiac anomalies.

basis: Inherited melanin metabolism disorder defined by skin and hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with reduced vision.
Variant defined by progressive dystonia, ataxia and neuropathy; immunodeficiency may be absent and is not established as common.
Combined dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; cervical muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Inherited platelet granule disorder causes macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding.
Platelet granule and aggregation defects with thrombocytopenia and bleeding.
Primary malignant soft-tissue sarcoma, commonly arising in trunk or extremity connective tissues.
Ewing-family tumor arising in bone or soft tissue; neural differentiation does not establish origin in peripheral nerves.
Glycosylation disorder with defining skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Ganglioside synthesis defect causes epilepsy and brain degeneration. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; common intrinsic ocular damage is unestablished; hearing loss 5-29%.
Muscular dystrophy defines the umbrella; brain and eye involvement varies substantially by subtype and is not established in most patients.
Dystroglycan glycosylation disorder defined by congenital muscular dystrophy and intellectual disability; ocular and respiratory abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with brain and eye anomalies defines the syndrome; individual ocular lesions are reported at 5-29%.
Primary muscular dystrophy with joint contractures and hyperlaxity; respiratory failure and intellectual impairment are explicitly rare.
Dystroglycanopathies primarily cause muscular dystrophy; brain and eye damage varies across subtypes and is not established as common across this umbrella.
Osteolysis, arthropathy and subcutaneous fibrocollagenous nodules define disease; cardiovascular abnormalities collectively affect 30-79%, despite rarer individual lesions.
Chronic bladder inflammation and dysfunction define the disease; reported autoimmunity does not establish an autoimmune mechanism across this heterogeneous syndrome.
Acquired structural abnormality of scalp hair; eyelash changes also affect hair, without established ocular damage.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by chronic urticarial dermatosis and monoclonal gammopathy; arthritis and abnormal bone remodeling reported in 80-99%; organ enlargement alone excluded.
Phagocyte dysfunction; intrinsic granulomatous lung obstruction and GI obstruction/malabsorption are supported by 80-99% HPO annotations. Secondary infections alone add no axes.
Pigmentary disease is shared; immunodeficient type 2 predominates. Cytopenias usually accompany separate HLH; substantial neurologic injury is subtype-limited.
Inherited metabolic neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation and progressive extrapyramidal dysfunction; other organs vary across subtypes.
Hamartomatous lesion arising within the liver during fetal development.
Defining absence of enteric ganglion cells causes permanent loss of intestinal innervation and colonic obstruction; enterocolitis and sepsis are minority complications.

decisions.neurologic: primary: congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells is the defining lesion of peripheral autonomic nervous tissue; generalized neurologic disease is unnecessary.

basis: Clonal dendritic-cell neoplasm; osteolysis 80-99%, infiltrative dermatitis and hepatic enlargement 30-79%; pulmonary and pituitary disease <30%.
Congenital acral skin hyperpigmentation defines the disease.
Histoplasma infection primarily affects the lungs; dissemination does not establish common damage to other organs across the umbrella.
Infantile temporal-lobe epilepsy with severe cognitive regression and intellectual disability.
Inherited osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disorder defined by reduced bone density and fractures; an independent endocrine gland disorder is not required.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine: osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disorder, supported by its ancestry. This mechanism axis does not require an independent endocrine gland abnormality.

basis: Inherited neurodegenerative disorder; a preceding viral trigger alone does not establish ongoing infection or an immune-mediated mechanism.
Chronic hepatitis and developmental delay are defining features; growth retardation alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Hereditary peripheral sensory nerve disorder causing episodic neuralgia.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and young-onset diabetes define the syndrome; hearing and dental abnormalities occur in under 30%.
Juvenile neurodegenerative parkinsonism; scoliosis and pes cavus occur in 30-79%, but reflect motor dysfunction rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis/pes cavus are frequent (30-79%) secondary deformities; rigidity and dystonia are neurologic, without established direct skeletal disease.

basis: Metabolic disease with defining neurodegeneration; blindness reported in 30-79%; cardiomyopathy and hearing impairment annotated 5-29%.
Neonatal metabolic acidosis, encephalopathy and severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy define this form; hepatic disease and coagulopathy are under 30%.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; ocular and generalized weakness reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission rather than intrinsic eye or muscle damage.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; ocular and generalized weakness reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission rather than separate eye or muscle injury.
Maternal autoantibodies impair neonatal neuromuscular junction function; respiratory and feeding weakness do not establish separate organ damage.
Most arise in dermal or subcutaneous glomus bodies, especially subungual distal extremities; perivascular cell origin alone does not establish cardiovascular organ damage.
Inherited LDL metabolism disorder; very frequent atherosclerosis and frequent hepatic steatosis are separately diagnosed diseases, excluded under rule 3.
Mucinous epithelial malignancy originating in the appendix; associated second malignancies are separate diseases.
Severe neonatal MADD commonly causes fatty hepatopathy, cardiomyopathy and cystic renal dysplasia, approximately >=30% each. Neurologic injury is less quantified and omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: cystic renal dysplasia is characteristic of the severe neonatal form with congenital anomalies and occurs in approximately >=30%.
decisions.neurologic: none: encephalopathy occurs, but lasting neurologic injury frequency is uncertain; characteristic renal, hepatic and cardiac disease take priority within the cap.

basis: Mild MADD is a fatty-acid/amino-acid oxidation disorder; lipid-storage myopathy affects most symptomatic patients, roughly 80-90%.
Persistent hiccup is an autonomic movement disorder; spasmodic muscle contractions do not establish intrinsic muscle or airway damage.
Primary immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections. Intestinal lymphoid hyperplasia (30-79%) lacks demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis occurs in 30-79% but is a separate disease arising from recurrent infections; direct pulmonary lymphoproliferative injury is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal lymphoid nodular hyperplasia occurs in 30-79%, but functional impairment or destructive enteropathy at that frequency is not established.

basis: Hereditary PrP amyloid causes defining sensory/autonomic neuropathy and chronic enteric dysfunction; neurogenic bladder reflects neuropathy rather than direct urinary tissue disease.
Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal habitus are explicit defining features. Psychiatric manifestations have no axis; facial dysmorphism does not establish further organ disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: marfanoid skeletal habitus is an explicit component of the syndrome's definition; primary structural skeletal abnormalities need not establish additional functional loss.

basis: Brainstem/cerebellar malformations, thoracic skeletal dysplasia and restrictive respiratory failure define the syndrome. Renal dysfunction and retinal dystrophy occur in 5-29%.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: respiratory failure from the narrow thorax is explicitly part of the disease definition, rather than an incidental respiratory symptom.

basis: Defined by skeletal muscle paralysis and distal motor neuropathy; mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder is an explicit parent.
Defined metabolic liver disease with neurodegeneration; skin disease 4/6 retained under primary cap. Dental defects ~50%, hearing loss and contractures 2/6 omitted by total cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the definition explicitly identifies a metabolic liver disease with iron overload; overt liver failure need not occur in 30% for primary status.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: ichthyosis/dermatitis affects 4/6; retained here because metabolic, hepatic and neurologic disease occupy the three primary slots.

basis: Glycosylation disorder defined by intellectual disability and developmental delay; cutis laxa and skeletal abnormalities are occasional.
Primary penile carcinoma affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; HPV association does not make the carcinoma an infection.
Autoimmune enteropathy with obligatory villous atrophy; deficiency anemia and associated dermatoses are separate diseases; elevated transaminases alone do not establish liver damage.
Defined endocrine and neurodevelopmental syndrome with hypogonadism, growth hormone deficiency, obesity, psychomotor delay and intellectual disability.
Neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic endocrine syndrome; strabismus and scoliosis each occur in 30-79%. Hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle disease.
Transplacentally acquired autoimmune disease umbrella; affected organs differ across subtypes, with no shared organ damage established.
Autoimmune thrombophilia with vascular thrombosis; cerebral infarction causes direct brain injury in approximately 50-60% of reported symptomatic neonatal cases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral infarction occurs in approximately 50-60% of reported neonatal APS cases, exceeding the threshold.

basis: Autoimmune destruction of neonatal red blood cells defines the disease.
Maternal autoantibody-mediated cutaneous disease; HPO reports liver and blood involvement each at 30-79%; cardiac involvement is a minority.
Neonatal autoimmune scleroderma affects skin; supplied ancestry does not establish common systemic organ involvement.
Persistent idiopathic facial pain is a neurologic pain disorder; oral burning does not establish oral tissue damage.
Congenital scar-like dermal lesions define the group; extracutaneous abnormalities are variable and concentrated in particular subtypes.
Malignancy originates in ovarian surface epithelium, a reproductive tissue outside the axes; ovarian origin does not imply endocrine dysfunction.
Malignancy originates in the reproductive ovary; endocrine effects occur only in selected sex cord-stromal subtypes.
Primary carcinoma of the abdominal peritoneal lining; ovarian classification does not establish ovarian origin in this concept.
Ovarian germ cell malignancy; reproductive tumour origin has no axis. Immature neural tissue does not establish CNS involvement.
Progressive distal myopathy defines the disease; persistent distal sensory impairment occurs in 80-99%, supporting additional neurologic functional loss.
Primary distal skeletal myopathy with weakness and nemaline bodies; cardiomyopathy is very rare and dyspnea does not establish intrinsic lung disease.
Ischemic necrosis directly destroys bone; interruption of blood supply does not itself establish a vascular disease.
Bone necrosis from interrupted blood supply; underlying causes vary and do not establish additional shared organ axes.
Trauma-associated ischemic bone necrosis; local interruption of blood supply does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Ischemic bone necrosis with joint dysfunction; associated autoimmunity and alcohol use are underlying conditions, not additional organ involvement.
Necrosis of mandibular or maxillary bone defines the disease.
Primary ischemic necrosis of bone; impaired bone perfusion does not establish an independent vascular disorder.
