Ischemic bone necrosis; the term avascular does not establish a separate disease of blood vessels.
Disordered growth and osteonecrosis affecting bone growth centers.
Disruption and displacement of the proximal femoral growth plate directly affect the hip skeleton.
Genetically caused bone necrosis defines this umbrella; mechanisms and extraskeletal manifestations vary across subtypes.
Disorder of sperm morphology and spermatogenesis is reproductive; elevated gonadotropins alone do not establish endocrine gland failure.
Parasitic cyst infection; hepatic cysts occur in 80-99% and cholestatic disease in 30-79%. Pulmonary cysts occur in 5-29%, below threshold.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic cyst occupation occurs in 80-99%, with cholestatic disease in 30-79%; the infection is not defined as exclusively hepatic.

basis: Hereditary corticospinal dysfunction defines disease; persistent talipes equinovarus occurs in 30-79%. Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular tissue damage.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia with motor neuropathy and intellectual disability; nystagmus does not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Central and peripheral neurodegenerative disorder; talipes equinovarus and lower-limb amyotrophy are frequent (30-79%), establishing skeletal/muscle involvement.
Progressive CNS motor and developmental disease. Frequent amyotrophy (30-79%) accompanies neurologic dysfunction but does not establish direct muscle disease.
Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia primarily affects central motor pathways.
Complex spastic paraplegia with developmental and structural brain abnormalities; hearing impairment and cataracts each occur in 30-79% by HPO.
Spastic paraplegia; muscle atrophy 3/3 and contractures 2/4; interstitial lung abnormalities 30-79%; sensorineural hearing impairment 1/2.
Hereditary corticospinal disease with frequent developmental impairment, abnormal myelination and peripheral neuropathy.
Inherited lipoate biosynthesis disorder; encephalopathy, developmental impairment or progressive motor pathway damage affects most patients across the principal subtypes.
Inherited neurodegenerative movement disorder with common cognitive impairment, chorea, rigidity and ataxia.
Adenomatous polyposis directly involves the colon; colorectal malignancy is a minority complication and separate diagnosis.
Intellectual disability defines syndrome; cardiac lesions, cervical/clavicular abnormalities, diabetes and hypercholesterolemia are each reported in 30-79%.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine involvement: diabetes and hypercholesterolemia are reported syndromic phenotypes at 30-79% and constitute metabolic dysfunction themselves; downstream organ damage is not required.

basis: Developmental disability defines the syndrome; skeletal abnormalities and joint hypermobility occur in 30-79%, as do congenital heart abnormalities; renal and intestinal defects <30%.
Congenital cerebral and cerebellar malformations with severe developmental impairment and intractable epilepsy.
Hereditary autonomic neuropathy; persistent contractures and progressive scoliosis affect approximately 30% or more across the spectrum. Abnormal sweating alone is not skin damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital contractures and progressive scoliosis are common persistent structural manifestations, estimated at >=30% across the spectrum.

basis: Dermal mucin deposition defines this cutaneous disorder; systemic manifestations of scleromyxedema do not apply across the umbrella.
Clonal myeloid blasts occupy marrow and blood. Extramedullary gingival involvement is not established in at least 30%; secondary infections are separate.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant marrow and myeloid blood-cell disease; no additional organ meets the involvement threshold.
Clonal myeloid blasts occupy marrow and blood. Extramedullary involvement is uncommon; recurrent infections reflect hematopoietic failure, not an infectious mechanism.
Megakaryoblast proliferation in marrow/blood; hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly is usual (>30%); splenic infiltration shares the haematologic axis.
Myeloid blast neoplasm of marrow and blood; gingival infiltration is not established in at least 30% and is not a diagnostic criterion.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation directly affects gastrointestinal tissue; circulating eosinophilia alone is not blood-organ damage.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation and infiltration of the colon; tissue eosinophils do not establish a primary blood-cell disorder.
Distal tubular acidification failure causes hypokalemic metabolic acidosis; sensorineural deafness is common across recessive forms, approximately half.
Brain, ear and cardiac malformations define embryopathy; retinal/optic nerve defects occur in 30-79%; oral, skeletal and thymic abnormalities omitted by cap.
Developmental CNS abnormalities and syndactyly define it; macular degeneration and choroidal neovascularization are frequent (30-79%), supporting ocular involvement.
Developmental delay, pulmonary cysts and Wilms tumors define GLOW; cysts and tumors reported in 2/2. Kyphosis and pectus deformity each occurred in 1/2.
Cerebellar ataxia, epilepsy and intellectual disability define a neurological syndrome.
Benign cartilaginous neoplasm arising in bone.
Tumor originates in renal cortical epithelium; usually localized and nonmetastatic.
Carcinoma originating in renal epithelium in acquired cystic kidney disease; no common additional organ involvement established.
Motor neuron disease with defining diaphragm paralysis, denervation weakness and joint contractures in most patients. Respiratory failure arises from skeletal muscle paralysis.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure is caused by denervation and diaphragm paralysis; no intrinsic lung or airway disease is established.

basis: Atypical cutaneous nevi and familial melanoma susceptibility; pancreatic carcinoma is a separate cancer risk.
Immune-mediated chronic polyarthritis; uveitis affects a minority of this subgroup and is not a defining criterion.
Calcium metabolic disorder; osteomalacia is annotated frequent (30-79%). Altered renal calcium handling does not establish kidney damage; pulmonary ancestry lacks support.
Isolated glycerol metabolism defect includes asymptomatic adults; supplied adrenal/myopathy and neurologic HPO appears conflated with complex Xp21 deletion disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: annotated 80-99% neurologic findings appear conflated with complex GKD; lasting neurologic damage in >=30% of isolated GKD is not established.

basis: Inflammatory retinal venous vasculitis with occlusion and visual damage; neurologic complications are below 30%.
Angelman neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and intellectual disability; pigmentation differences do not establish skin or eye dysfunction.
Angelman neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures; pigment differences do not establish tissue damage, and obesity is a separate metabolic diagnosis.
Purine metabolic disorder; gout and uric acid stones are separately diagnosed consequences. Renal impairment occurs in only 5-29%; neurologic disease is not characteristic.
Purine disorder with defining neurodevelopmental abnormalities (80-99%); renal insufficiency and hearing loss each 30-79%. Gout and stones are separately diagnosed.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental anomalies explicitly define the severe early-onset subtype and occur in 80-99%.

basis: Insulin autoantibodies cause dysregulated insulin activity and hypoglycemia; associated lupus and arthritis are separate diseases.
Cystine storage disease defined by renal and ocular injury; rickets occurs in 80-99%. Neurologic abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of esophageal mucosa causes esophageal dysfunction.
Mycobacterial infection directly damages pulmonary airways and parenchyma; underlying immunodeficiency is a predisposition.
Congenital absence of kidney and ureter; pulmonary hypoplasia and cardiovascular abnormalities occur in fewer than 30%.
Skin and oral mucosal keratoacanthomas define disease; ectropion causes eyelid dysfunction in 30-79%. Corneal complications are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal keratoacanthomas belong to the defining mucocutaneous neoplastic eruption; occasional dysphagia is not the basis.

basis: Inherited excessive eyelash and other hair growth; possible corneal irritation does not establish common direct ocular damage.
Lipoprotein metabolism disorder; atherosclerosis and fatty liver are separate diseases; xanthomas, corneal arcus and lipemia retinalis do not establish functional damage.
Intellectual disability, sensory dysfunction and eczema define syndrome; oligodontia and camptodactyly each 30-79%; hypermetropia omitted by cap.
Inherited neurodegeneration with obligate dementia and common motor deterioration; stiffness and gait abnormalities reflect neurologic disease.
Generalized dystonia with central and peripheral neurologic dysfunction; vocal cord structural abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting direct laryngeal involvement.
Bilirubin accumulation causes brain injury; permanent auditory neuropathy/hearing loss is a major feature of chronic kernicterus.
Inherited adrenal steroidogenesis disorder; hypertension and skeletal abnormalities are subtype-specific rather than shared across the umbrella.
Carcinoma arising in the esophagus; salivary gland type describes histology.
Carcinoma arising in the esophagus.
Alveolar surfactant accumulation impairs lung function; associated hematologic disorders, infections and immunodeficiencies are separate underlying conditions.
Semicircular canal dehiscence impairs auditory and vestibular function; associated eye movements do not indicate ocular damage.
Lysosomal glycogen storage directly damages skeletal and respiratory muscles. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness rather than intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Persistent central visual-processing dysfunction; ocular examinations are usually normal. Tinnitus and other associated symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Severe congenital neutropenia is a blood-cell disorder and an innate immunodeficiency; infections do not establish additional intrinsic organ damage.
Autoimmune encephalopathy; sleep breathing dysfunction arises from neurologic control and does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Primary skeletal dysplasia; severe intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%, with seizures and severe developmental delay in 30-79%; short nails alone lack functional significance.
Serine biosynthesis deficiency causes a neurometabolic syndrome; severe skin and skeletal abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Malignant epithelial tumor originates in the kidney; other manifestations of familial cancer syndromes are separate conditions.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy; acidosis and tachyarrhythmias are acute crisis manifestations. Renal, hepatic and coagulation injury occur in <30%.
Microcephaly and intellectual disability define it; frequencies of associated hypothyroidism and ocular abnormalities are insufficiently established.
Defining neurodevelopmental disease, retinal dystrophy and diabetes insipidus; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%.
Congenital cardiac outflow malformation with ventricular septal defect.
Complex congenital heart malformation; pulmonary stenosis concerns cardiovascular outflow. Heterotaxy alone does not establish other organ dysfunction.
Nematode larvae migrate within skin, producing inflammatory cutaneous tracks; sleep and concentration symptoms do not establish neurologic damage.
Familial gastric carcinoma arises in the stomach; associated hereditary syndromes and other cancers do not establish additional organ involvement across this group.
Gastric carcinoma with salivary-gland-type histology; the site of origin is the stomach.
Carcinoma originating in the stomach; no common additional organ involvement specified.
Mesenchymal neoplasm arising in the small intestine; intestinal location determines the organ axis.
Microcephaly and axonal polyneuropathy define the syndrome; characteristic wasting follows denervation, and scoliosis is secondary rather than direct musculoskeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting and scoliosis are characteristic but follow neuropathic denervation and weakness; their frequency does not establish direct musculoskeletal injury.

basis: Malignant squamous tumor arising in the small intestine; no additional organ involvement is established.
Neoplasm originates in the small intestine; neuroendocrine differentiation does not itself establish endocrine gland disease or a functional hormonal syndrome.
Epithelial neoplasm originates in the vermiform appendix.
Squamous carcinoma of the colon; no common direct extraintestinal involvement established.
Squamous cell carcinoma originates in the rectum.
Epithelial neoplasm arising in the anal canal.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the exocrine pancreas.
Non-metastasizing mucinous epithelial neoplasm of the exocrine pancreas.
Malignant tumor arising in exocrine pancreas; local vascular or perineural invasion does not establish separate systemic organ involvement.
Structural congenital myopathy; ptosis causes eyelid dysfunction in 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency occurs in only 1-4%; recurrent infections are separate diseases.

decisions.ocular: involved: myopathic ptosis represents direct loss of eyelid function in 30-79%; eyelids explicitly belong to the ocular axis.

basis: Carcinoma originates in hepatocytes or intrahepatic bile duct epithelium.
Primary carcinoma of the liver or intrahepatic bile ducts; metastatic potential does not establish another commonly damaged organ.
Primary squamous carcinoma arising in liver or intrahepatic bile duct epithelium.
Cystadenocarcinoma originates in the biliary tree, included in the hepatic axis.
Carcinoma originates in gallbladder or extrahepatic biliary epithelium, both within the hepatic axis.
Carcinoma originates in the gallbladder or extrahepatic bile ducts, both hepatic-axis structures. Adjacent organ invasion lacks a qualifying frequency.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by recurrent aphthous oral ulcers and pharyngitis. Infectious encephalitis is not characteristic despite the annotation.
Aldosterone biosynthesis deficiency; renal salt wasting and electrolyte disturbances reflect hormone deficiency rather than direct kidney damage.
Congenital neutrophil maturation failure causes severe chronic neutropenia and innate immunodeficiency; infections do not establish a shared damaged organ.
Calcium/PTH disorder; intrinsic nephrocalcinosis and hair/nail abnormalities each reported at 30-79%. Hypocalcemic arrhythmia does not establish intrinsic cardiac injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: arrhythmia is reported at 30-79%, but reflects hypocalcemic electrical disturbance; persistent cardiac injury is not established.
decisions.renal: involved: intrinsic renal calcium wasting causes nephrocalcinosis (HPO 30-79%); treatment can aggravate it but is not required.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disease with adrenal insufficiency and CNS demyelination/axonopathy. Visual, auditory and bladder deficits can reflect neural dysfunction without direct organ damage.
Central serotonergic toxicity with autonomic and neuromotor dysfunction; tachycardia and diarrhea do not establish organ damage; organ failure is rare.
Acute poisoning defined by cardiac conduction toxicity, arrhythmias, hypotension and central nervous system toxicity including coma.
The membrane-stabilizing toxidrome directly impairs cardiac conduction and contractility and CNS function, with characteristic seizures or coma.

decisions.neurologic: primary: direct CNS toxicity, including seizures or coma, is a characteristic component of the membrane-stabilizing poisoning syndrome.

basis: Congenital persistent bladder-to-umbilicus communication; recurrent urinary infections are separate complications.
Congenital urachal remnant belongs to the urinary system despite absent bladder continuity; infection is a possible complication, not intrinsic to the anomaly.
Congenital diverticulum communicating with the bladder. Recurrent urinary infections are separately diagnosed complications.
Obliterative pulmonary venous disease and/or pulmonary interstitial capillary proliferation directly affect lung vasculature and lung tissue.
Deficient hypothalamic-pituitary stimulation causes gonadal hormone deficiency; skeletal maturation abnormalities 80-99% and bone loss 30-79% support skeletal involvement.
Autoimmune presynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction; weakness and autonomic symptoms reflect neurologic dysfunction. Associated lung cancer is separate.
Congenital lower urinary tract obstruction directly affects the urinary system; pulmonary hypoplasia is not established as common across this umbrella.
Premature hormonal activation and sexual maturation constitute an endocrine disorder.
Congenital absence of toes is a structural skeletal malformation.
Intellectual disability, speech impairment and abnormal neurologic development define the syndrome. Hearing loss and other functional organ defects occur in only 5-29%.
Congenital remnants of the urachus, a urinary tract structure connecting the developing bladder and umbilicus. Infection is a possible complication.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease. The isolated developmental-stagnation annotation (30-79%) does not establish direct neurologic impairment in this growth disorder.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental stagnation is nonspecific in this skeletal growth disorder; the record establishes no accompanying cognitive, motor-neural or structural CNS disorder.

basis: Axonal hereditary motor and sensory peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness and wasting reflect denervation.
Contractures and sensorineural hearing loss each occur in 30-79%; laryngomalacia and hypospadias (30-79%) omitted by cap. Reflux alone does not establish tissue injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: knee/ankle contractures occur in 30-79% and impair locomotor function; prognathism alone does not make skeletal disease a defining primary axis.

basis: ALP deficiency defines defective bone and tooth mineralization. Pulmonary disease and seizures chiefly affect severe early-onset forms; renal complications are occasional.
audit_reason: Remove pulmonary: the emphysema annotation is not representative across the HPP umbrella. Significant pulmonary disease chiefly affects severe early-onset forms; the umbrella rule excludes subtype-specific involvement.

basis: Contractures, neurodevelopmental defects and Pierre Robin oral anomalies define the syndrome. OSA is reported in 30-79% but does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: OSA (30-79%) is secondary to oral/jaw anatomy and separately diagnosed; no direct lung or airway lesion is established.

basis: Intellectual disability, strabismus and structural limb/joint abnormalities are obligate defining findings. Obesity alone does not establish intrinsic endocrine or metabolic organ dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity in 80-99% does not by itself demonstrate direct endocrine injury or an intrinsic metabolic disorder; separately coded obesity is insufficient.

basis: Early adult-onset diabetes defines endocrine dysfunction; growth restriction and short stature alone do not establish skeletal disease.
Mitochondrial leukodystrophy; renal tubular dysfunction and cardiomyopathy each 30-79%; cap omits ocular, hepatic, muscle, hearing and blood involvement, also reported at 30-79%.
Defined by cutis laxa/PXE-like skin disease and vision-damaging rod-cone dystrophy, both obligate.
Autoimmune encephalomyelitis in the stiff-person spectrum, commonly associated with glycine-receptor antibodies; rigidity reflects central neural dysfunction.
Glucagon receptor dysfunction causes endocrine pancreatic alpha-cell hyperplasia and tumors. Pancreatitis and gallstones are separately diagnosed conditions.
Orthopoxvirus infection characteristically causes destructive vesiculopustular skin lesions, often with ulceration or scarring.
Cerebral arterial occlusion with brain ischemia and infarction defines the disease.
Necrolytic inflammatory skin disease; associated hepatitis C and zinc deficiency do not establish direct hepatic or systemic metabolic involvement.
Persistent birth-related brachial plexus injury is a peripheral nerve disorder.
Systemic amyloid protein-homeostasis disorder causing progressive renal dysfunction. Liver/lung deposits often lack functional injury; liver enzyme elevation occurs in only 5-29%.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine for the systemic protein-homeostasis disorder. Renal dysfunction defines its clinical presentation; hepatic and pulmonary deposits without common functional injury do not qualify as involved.

basis: Protein-misfolding amyloidosis; renal medullary abnormalities and creatinine elevation in 80-99%. Cardiac amyloid is 1-4%; ventricular dysfunction does not establish direct cardiac deposition.

decisions.renal: involved: renal medullary disease and impaired renal function occur in 80-99%; renal injury is the dominant manifestation of this protein-defined amyloidosis.

basis: Beta2-microglobulin amyloid deposition predominantly damages bones, joints and tendons; amyloid-related compressive neuropathy is a major manifestation (~30–50%). Renal failure is antecedent.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: a protein handling and deposition disorder, supported by its amyloidosis and proteostasis-deficiency ancestry.

basis: Inherited cerebral and vascular amyloid disease; hearing impairment and cataracts each occur in 30-79%. Progressive hearing loss is prioritized over cataracts under the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: cataracts occur in 30-79%, but the three defining axes and progressive hearing loss take priority.
decisions.otologic: involved: progressive hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%; its potentially permanent severity supports retaining it under the four-axis cap.

basis: Immune-mediated vasculitis of cutaneous arteries; extracutaneous symptoms are mild or transient, and neuropathy is rare.
Immune-mediated arterial vasculitis. Neuropathy and damaging skin-lesion frequencies in systemic PAN cannot reliably be generalized to this cutaneous/single-organ/systemic umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: none: neuropathy affects ~50-70% in systemic PAN; a >=30% frequency across the full primary-PAN umbrella is not established.
decisions.dermatologic: none: systemic-PAN skin findings (~40-60%) include nondamaging signs; common direct skin damage across the full umbrella is not established.

basis: Immune-mediated arterial vasculitis; neuropathy occurs in ~60-80%, renal ischemic involvement ~40-60%. GI and skin involvement omitted under the four-axis cap; hepatitis is separate.
Immune-mediated medium-artery vasculitis; cutaneous PAN predominates among single-organ presentations, supporting skin damage in >30%. Other organ sites vary.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous PAN is the predominant single-organ presentation, supporting >30% with direct inflammatory skin injury; skin is not universal across this umbrella.

basis: Necrotizing arterial vasculitis; neuropathy ~50-70% and renal ischemic involvement ~40-60%; common skin and gastrointestinal injury omitted under four-axis cap.
Bronchial casts directly obstruct airways; abnormal lymphatic flow alone does not establish immune or blood-vessel disease.
Congenital dysfunction of cranial nerve III; impaired eye movements reflect nerve palsy without established intrinsic eye damage.
Congenital sixth cranial nerve dysfunction; impaired eye movement reflects nerve palsy without established intrinsic eye damage.
Skeletal dysplasia, high myopia and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; upper-airway obstruction 80-99%. Cleft palate (80-99%; gastrointestinal) omitted by cap.
Necrotizing bacterial infection of soft tissues, encompassing skin/subcutis, fascia and muscle; tissue depth varies across forms.
Inherited surfactant protein C dysfunction causes interstitial and alveolar lung disease; no additional organ involvement is established.
Defined by familial colorectal cancer without mismatch-repair mutations. Supplied glioblastoma frequencies conflict with FCCTX and do not support neurologic involvement.
Inborn carbohydrate metabolic disorders; no additional organ damage applies consistently across this umbrella.
Peripapillary retinal nerve-fiber myelination is an ocular abnormality; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Autonomic neurodegeneration causes hypotension, anhidrosis and bowel/bladder dysfunction; these do not establish direct damage to those organs.
Nonsyndromic cataract affecting the lens.
Early-onset lamellar lens opacity; broader CRYAB spectrum ancestry does not establish myopathy or cardiomyopathy in this cataract subtype.
Thyroid hormone deficiency present from birth; permanent neurologic injury depends on prolonged untreated deficiency and is not established in most patients.
Heavy-chain amyloid disorder; nephropathy 80-99%, cardiac amyloidosis 30-79%; neuropathy only 5-29%, and goiter alone does not establish thyroid dysfunction.
Umbrella epileptic encephalopathy with seizures and developmental impairment; an amino-acid transport mechanism is not established across its diverse subtypes.
Primary trigeminal autonomic headache disorder; tearing, conjunctival injection and nasal symptoms do not establish ocular or airway damage.
Choroidal leakage causes subretinal fluid and retinal visual dysfunction; local choroidal vessels do not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Autonomic baroreflex dysfunction defined by severe blood-pressure fluctuations, including hypertension.
Hypothalamic thirst-regulation dysfunction causes adipsia and disordered sodium/water homeostasis with hypernatremia.
Indolent B-cell lymphoma involving lymphoplasmacytic blood-cell lineage; lymphoma warrants the immune mechanism axis.
Postpartum psychiatric disorder; psychosis and associated confusion do not establish an organic neurologic disease.
Spontaneous cerebrospinal fluid leakage causes intracranial CSF volume loss and neurological dysfunction.
Immune-mediated CNS inhibitory dysfunction causes rigidity and spasms; muscle symptoms do not establish primary muscle damage.
Systemic Salmonella enteric infection involving intestinal lymphoid tissue; hepatosplenomegaly and bradycardia alone do not establish other organ damage.
Cancer associated with HIV-related immunodeficiency; this umbrella does not specify a shared tumor organ or blood-cell origin.
Focal autoimmune stiff-person spectrum disorder; rigidity and spasms reflect impaired neural inhibition, without established primary skeletal-muscle damage.
Hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer syndrome; extracolonic cancers are separately diagnosed outcomes and do not establish involved organs.
Hereditary hair shaft abnormalities and progressive alopecia; eyelashes and eyebrows are hair, not ocular damage.
Global developmental delay and hypotonia occur in 30-79%; ocular, skeletal and skin abnormalities are individually reported in only 5-29%.
Defining developmental brain and hand/foot abnormalities; hearing impairment occurs in 30–79%. Unspecified eye abnormalities and facial dysmorphism do not prove ocular damage.
Inherited protein deposition; neuropathy and cardiomyopathy each common, roughly >=30% across predominant ATTR forms. Renal damage is subtype-dependent and not reliably >=30%.
Idiopathic destruction and resorption of phalangeal bone.
Immunodeficiency with autoimmune cytopenias; stroke/developmental impairment and hepatitis each occur in 80-99%. Recurrent ear/airway infections alone do not establish lasting damage.
Inherited triglyceride metabolism disorder; pancreatitis and fatty liver are separate diseases; lipemia retinalis and xanthomas do not establish functional damage.
Renal tubular aldosterone resistance causes salt wasting, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis; systemic manifestations vary by subtype.
Defining caudal skeletal, urinary tract and anorectal malformations; reported CNS anomalies are not established as common across the spectrum.
Secondary immune-mediated inflammation damages blood vessels; other organ involvement varies with the underlying cause and vessel distribution.
Combined immunodeficiency with impaired lymphoid immunity, reduced B cells and immunoglobulins; no common additional organ damage established.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis (80-99%) and ophthalmoplegia (30-79%) arise from NMJ dysfunction; they do not establish direct damage to ocular tissues.

basis: Fly larvae directly infest skin and subcutis, producing furuncular lesions.
Macrophage-mediated inflammatory lesions affect muscle and fascia; weakness is very frequent. Fatigue and myalgia do not establish additional organ damage.
Myofibrillar degeneration defines skeletal myopathy. Cardiac involvement varies by subtype without an established umbrella frequency of at least 30%; respiratory muscle disease remains muscular.
Pregnancy-related trophoblastic tumors originate in reproductive tissue; extra-reproductive organ damage is not common across this umbrella.
Neurodegeneration with intrinsic erythrocyte abnormalities; myopathy 8/10; cardiomyopathy 4/22 and AF 5/22 do not individually meet 30%; liver damage uncertain.
Cerebellar malformation defines disease. Eye and vision abnormalities are 5-29%; the 30-79% septo-optic dysplasia annotation describes a distinct associated disorder, not proven ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: explicit eye/vision abnormalities are 5-29%; associated septo-optic dysplasia is separately diagnosable and does not establish ocular loss at >=30%.

basis: Congenital skeletal myopathy defined by centrally placed muscle nuclei; respiratory muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Structural skeletal myopathy; strabismus 30-79% does not establish direct eye damage. Respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness, not pulmonary disease.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus is reported in 30-79%, but extraocular muscle dysfunction does not establish direct eye damage; ophthalmoplegia occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Group of primary skeletal muscle diseases causing distal weakness and atrophy; extra-muscular damage is not shared across most subtypes.
Leucine metabolism disorder; movement abnormalities are annotated 30-79%, but persistent neural injury is not established. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: movement abnormalities (30-79%) do not establish lasting neural injury; expression includes asymptomatic individuals and transient metabolic crises.

basis: Defining distal and laryngopharyngeal myopathy; bulbar palsy occurs in 30-79%, with hyperreflexia supporting neurologic involvement. Dysphagia alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
audit_reason: Add neurologic involvement: explicitly frequent bulbar palsy, supported by hyperreflexia, indicates neural dysfunction beyond skeletal muscle weakness. The supplied frequency meets the 30% threshold.

basis: Silver-induced dermatosis with irreversible skin and nail discoloration; mucosal silver staining alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Defined by deficient ossification of the parietal bones. Vascular and brain abnormalities occur below 30%; intellectual disability and seizures are very rare.
Vascular and skeletal connective-tissue disease; cleft palate and abnormal skin scarring each 30-79%. Asthma is a separate associated disease.
HPV infection produces recurrent airway papillomas, principally in the larynx; dysphagia alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Idiopathic bronchial dilation and wall destruction; recurrent respiratory infections are secondary infections rather than a defining infectious mechanism.
Pudendal neuropathic pain disorder; urinary, rectal and genital symptoms do not establish direct damage to those organs.
Structural skeletal myopathy defined by nemaline rods and muscle weakness. Respiratory muscle weakness does not itself establish direct lung disease.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy defined by potassium-aggravated myotonia; no intrinsic systemic electrolyte disorder.
Congenital ureteral dilation with frequent hydronephrosis; urinary infections and stones are separate complications.
Familial melanoma predominantly arises in skin; other cancers are separate diseases, and retinopathy is occasional.
Congenital intestinal rotation/fixation abnormality with a common mesentery; the affected structures belong to the digestive system.
Inherited methemoglobin disorder; aggregate nervous-system abnormalities are frequent (30-79%), with direct CNS injury in generalized reductase deficiency. Cyanosis is not skin damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: aggregate nervous-system HPO frequency is 30-79%; developmental and structural CNS injury support damage, although individual findings are occasional.

basis: Cobalamin metabolic disorder defined by megaloblastic anemia and encephalopathy; intrinsic retinopathy occurs in 30-79%.
Hereditary glomerular disease; hearing loss and reduced visual acuity each occur in 30-79% in HPO. Retinal flecks alone do not establish visual damage.
Defined by isolated growth hormone deficiency and congenital hypogammaglobulinemia; endocrine dysfunction and antibody immunodeficiency.
Defining CNS and cervico-occipital skeletal malformations; gastroschisis and cardiovascular malformations each frequent (30-79%). Renal agenesis is occasional.
Combined open cranial/spinal neural tube malformation includes defining cranial and vertebral nonclosure; cervical spina bifida occurs in 80-99%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: cranial and vertebral nonclosure are intrinsic to craniorachischisis; cervical spina bifida is annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Premature cranial suture fusion defines a skull disorder; supplied strabismus annotation lacks frequency sufficient to establish common ocular involvement.
Inherited macular and retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy.
Autoimmune blistering disease; destructive oral mucositis occurs in 80–99% and bronchiolitis obliterans in approximately 30%. Associated neoplasms are separate diseases.
Neurocutaneous disease with neurofibromas and pigmentary lesions; Lisch nodules are non-damaging. Optic glioma and major skeletal complications affect a minority.
Defining malformations include neural tube defects, oral clefts, omphalocele and diaphragmatic defects; renal and cardiac anomalies occur in only 5-29%.
Anti-MAG antibodies cause immune-mediated peripheral nerve demyelination; associated monoclonal gammopathy is a separate condition.
IgG4-mediated fibroinflammatory disease of the mediastinum; additional organ dysfunction is not established as common.
Immune-mediated peripheral motor neuropathy; weakness reflects nerve dysfunction rather than primary muscle disease.
Limb/craniofacial dysostosis, cleft lip/palate and developmental delay define the syndrome; microtia is a defining ear malformation. Blepharophimosis omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft lip and palate are explicitly included in the syndrome's defining phenotype; oral and palatal structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay and microcephaly are explicitly included in the defining phenotype of this particular acrofacial dysostosis.

basis: Neonatal epilepsy syndrome, despite generally favorable neurological outcome.
Lipid storage disease; neurodegeneration and hepatic disease 80-99%, hearing impairment 30-79%; spleen/marrow storage alone does not establish functional damage.
Immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation causes ocular motor cranial neuropathies; ophthalmoplegia reflects nerve dysfunction without established intrinsic eye injury.

decisions.ocular: none: defining ophthalmoplegia results from ocular motor cranial neuropathy; eye-movement symptoms do not establish direct damage to eye structures.

basis: Bartonella infection invades erythrocytes with hemolytic anemia; the supplied Carrion disease definition also includes defining chronic cutaneous proliferations.
Inflammatory disease confined to the breast; unknown etiology does not establish infection or an immune-mediated mechanism.
Progressive corneal endothelial disease with iris atrophy, synechiae and visual impairment; manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
Repeated acute inflammation of the exocrine pancreas; remote organ failure is not established as common, and inflammation alone does not imply immune mediation.
Intrahepatic portal venous sclerosis defines disease; anemia 80-99% and hypersplenism/leukopenia 30-79% support blood-organ involvement. Varices are vascular.
Immune-mediated thyroid inflammation and fibrosis; vocal cord paralysis and tracheal stenosis occur in <30%; extracervical fibroinflammatory diseases are rare or separate.
Inherited axonal peripheral neuropathy; denervation atrophy and foot deformities follow nerve injury rather than direct muscle or bone disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common muscle wasting and foot deformities are consequences of denervation; direct skeletal muscle or bone pathology is not established.

basis: Inherited peripheral motor and sensory neuropathy; weakness and muscle wasting reflect denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Hereditary peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; weakness and muscle wasting reflect denervation.
Cerebellar degeneration and axonal neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy in 10/10, pes cavus in 67% and scoliosis in 39%; oculomotor apraxia is neurologic.
Cardiac and skeletal defects define Noonan syndrome; hypogonadotropic hypogonadism 80-99%, developmental delay 30-79%. Platelet dysfunction (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: none: platelet dysfunction qualifies at 30-79%, but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of endocrine dysfunction and neurodevelopmental impairment.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: supplied HPO reports hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in 80-99%, supporting common endocrine loss of function.

basis: Retinal dystrophy defines LCA. Supplied HPO places seizures, neuronal migration defects and cerebellar malformations at 30-79%, supporting CNS involvement despite umbrella heterogeneity.

decisions.neurologic: involved: supplied 30-79% annotations include seizures and structural brain abnormalities; no evidence establishes that these frequencies apply only to a rare subtype.

basis: Lipid disorder defined by corneal opacification; renal dysfunction and hemolytic anemia each 30-79%. Visual impairment is 5-29%; atherosclerosis is a separate disease.

decisions.ocular: primary: diffuse corneal opacification is a defining structural corneal lesion across LCAT deficiency subtypes; overt visual impairment is only 5-29%.

basis: Cerebrospinal fluid-filled spinal nerve-root cysts; radiculopathy reflects nerve-root disease.
Dysplastic cerebellar gangliocytoma; extracerebellar tumors and mucocutaneous findings reflect associated Cowden syndrome rather than direct effects of LDD.
Defined by thyroid, adrenal and parathyroid neoplasia. Extra-endocrine structural lesions are minority features; catecholamine symptoms alone do not establish organ damage.
Embryonal malignancy arising in kidney; lung/liver metastases and hypertension occur in fewer than 30% across the disease.
Progressive renal tubulointerstitial injury; frequent retinal pigmentation alone does not establish damaging retinopathy. Anemia is secondary to renal failure.
Inherited glomerular disease causing proteinuria and commonly chronic kidney failure; familial steroid resistance does not establish an immune mechanism.
Vaginal and associated uterine developmental abnormalities are reproductive; abdominal symptoms do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Inherited bile-transport/metabolic disorder causing recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis. Hearing loss and pancreatitis occur in only 5-29%; pruritus is a symptom.
Focal cerebral cortical malformation causes epilepsy and frequent cognitive or motor impairment.
Endocrine pancreatic insulin excess causes recurrent hypoglycemia; lasting neurodevelopmental injury occurs in roughly 30-50%.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy and structural foot deformities affect most patients.
Craniosynostosis and digital malformations define disease; intellectual disability 80-99%; corneal abnormalities/strabismus and cardiac malformations 30-79%.
Recurrent subcutaneous edema defines the disorder; bradykinin mediation is not inherently immune-mediated; transient mucosal swelling adds no damaged organ.
The primary defect is the abdominal wall; pulmonary hypoplasia and restrictive dysfunction occur in 30-79%. Herniated bowel alone does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the malformation affects the abdominal wall; displacement of otherwise intact bowel does not establish gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy defines ophthalmoplegia and ptosis; respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness rather than direct lung disease.
Short metacarpals and insulin resistance define syndrome; spherocytosis is explicitly described and annotated 80-99%, supporting a primary blood-cell axis. Congestion is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: primary: spherocytosis is an intrinsic blood-cell abnormality described in the syndrome and annotated 80-99%; the haematologic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Acute myocardial dysfunction defines the condition; stroke and pulmonary edema are minority complications.
Bone fragility defines OI; supplied HPO reports dental defects and hearing loss 80-99%, visual impairment 30-79%. Cutis laxa omitted at cap; blue sclerae alone are not damage.
Defined as an autoimmune neurologic syndrome associated with streptococcal infection; tics, chorea and developmental regression establish neurologic involvement.
Defined by sensorineural hearing loss, premature hair graying and essential tremor; blue sclerae alone do not establish ocular damage.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation localized to skin; extracutaneous infiltration defines systemic mastocytosis, a separate concept.
Destructive mast-cell malignancy; reported series describe bone involvement in ~78% and gastrointestinal involvement in ~35%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: direct gastrointestinal tumor involvement is reported in approximately 35% of cases, meeting the threshold for occupation by the malignancy.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive osseous tumor involvement is reported in approximately 78% of cases.

basis: Localized mature mast-cell neoplasm; no specific extracutaneous organ is established across cases.
Defective bone resorption; anemia, optic compression and hearing impairment annotated 80-99%. Neurologic, dental and skin manifestations omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: marrow-space obliteration causes hematopoietic insufficiency; anemia is annotated 80-99%, secondary to skeletal disease.
decisions.neurologic: none at cap: hydrocephalus is annotated 80-99%; progressive degeneration is subtype-dependent. Marrow, visual and auditory dysfunction are retained.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is annotated 80-99%, reflecting bony compression or structural compromise of auditory pathways.

basis: Digital skeletal anomalies, deafness and cleft palate define the syndrome; palate belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Protozoal infection primarily located in the intestine; liver abscess and other extraintestinal damage affect a minority, below 30%.
Developmental abnormality of maxillary alveolar bone, gingiva and teeth; both skeletal and oral structures are defining sites.
Congenital platelet and erythroid production abnormalities cause thrombocytopenia, bleeding and anemia.
Intellectual disability and growth hormone deficiency are defining; structural brain and ocular motor findings are occasional and add no separate axis.
Scalp skin hypertrophy defines the umbrella; neurologic, ocular and hearing abnormalities occur in nonessential subtypes without established group-wide ≥30% frequency.
Congenital ectopic pancreatic tissue; no endocrine dysfunction or common injury to other organs is established.
Malignant tumor arising in the exocrine pancreas; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine dysfunction. Jaundice is occasional.
Definition emphasizes amoebic meningoencephalitis; infectious encephalitis occurs in 30–79%. Visual loss is occasional (5–29%); photophobia alone is insufficient.
Central neurodegeneration causes gaze palsy, dysphagia and movement impairment; these do not establish direct ocular or gastrointestinal damage.
Defined as inherited metabolic diseases causing CNS myelin abnormalities; peripheral nerve damage shares the neurologic axis; other organs vary by subtype.
Inherited globin disorders affect erythrocytes; additional organ injury is not consistent across this broad group.
Inherited biochemical or organelle metabolic defects; no additional organ is consistently damaged across this broad umbrella.
Peroxisomal metabolic disorders cause neurologic injury in well over 30% across major forms; hepatic and ocular damage varies substantially by subtype.
Congenital structural malformation of limbs; additional organs depend on the particular syndrome.
Umbrella explicitly includes peripheral nerve, neuromuscular junction and skeletal muscle disorders.
Neoplasm involving bone or articular cartilage; additional organs are not shared across the umbrella.
Inherited degeneration of motor pathways causes progressive spastic paraplegia; additional organs vary among complicated subtypes.
Amyloid proteostasis disorder; functional renal and cardiac deposition each commonly exceeds ~30% in systemic cohorts, though frequency varies across this broad umbrella.
Immune-mediated podocyte dysfunction causes steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome; edema and hypoalbuminemia do not establish additional organ damage.
Maternal alloantibodies cause fetal glomerular immune deposits, nephrotic syndrome and renal insufficiency.
Hair and nail abnormalities define the disorder; eyelash and eyebrow involvement remains dermatologic.
Impaired intrahepatic bile flow directly affects the liver and biliary system.
Defining hypotrichosis, vascular/lymphatic malformations and renal defects. Developmental delay is occasional; pulmonary lymphangiectasia has no established common frequency.
Acquired bilateral iris depigmentation and anterior chamber abnormalities; preceding infection does not establish an infectious mechanism.
Brainstem gaze dysfunction, profound sensorineural deafness and characteristic carotid/cardiac malformations define the syndrome; gaze palsy is neurologic.
Localized persistent epidermal thinning and depressed plaques affect palmar and plantar skin.
Benign follicular epithelial skin tumor; oral mucosal lesions occur in only 5-29%.
Cerebellar and cardiac malformations define syndrome; cleft palate and scoliosis/kyphosis each reported in 30-79%. Ocular damage is not established as common.
Lower motor neuron degeneration causes skeletal muscle atrophy in 80-99%. Respiratory muscle weakness is neuromuscular; aspiration pneumonia is a separate disease.
Autoimmune hair follicle disease causing complete scalp hair loss; diabetes and intestinal inflammation are separate associated diseases.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; oral blisters occur in 5-29%; diabetes is a separate comorbidity rather than direct endocrine damage.
OXPHOS disorder with Leigh encephalopathy and cardiomyopathy; skeletal myopathy is explicitly defining in supplied synonyms, qualifying without a numerical frequency; primary slots are full.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal myopathy is explicit in equivalent disease names, satisfying the defining-feature exception; three primary slots are already occupied.

basis: Radiation injury directly affects rectal tissue; local vascular and connective-tissue changes are components of the intestinal injury.
Chronic allergic inflammation directly affects conjunctiva and cornea, with keratitis and neovascularization.
Carcinoma originates in the epithelial lining of the esophagus.
Carcinoma arising in intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts, all within the hepatic axis.
Lymphoid proliferation ranging from polyclonal disease to lymphoma; specific extranodal organ damage is not consistently common.
Chronic developmental and acquired lung injury defines BPD. Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale are separate complications; diaphragmatic paralysis may be treatment-related.
Defined by cessation of respiratory airflow; central and obstructive causes vary, and bradycardia does not establish cardiac damage.
Specific antibody immunodeficiency; recurrent respiratory and ear infections are separate infections, without evidence of common lasting organ damage.
Congenital EBV infection; most infants lack manifestations, and anomalies from a single reported case cannot establish common organ damage.
Y. pestis infection; skin ulcers and destructive blistering are frequent (30-79%). Pneumonia is occasional; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish dysfunction.
Autoimmune destruction of platelets defines this blood and immune disorder.
Autoimmune inflammatory disease defined by myelitis and optic neuritis. Bladder dysfunction reflects spinal cord injury rather than direct urinary-organ disease.
A retinal vascular hamartoma directly involves the eye and its capillaries; occasional glaucoma and hemorrhage remain within the ocular axis.
Progressive unilateral exophthalmos and ipsilateral nasal turbinate mucosal hypertrophy define the syndrome; nasal airways belong to pulmonary.
Reflux-associated dystonic posturing defines the syndrome. Anemia is frequent (30-79%) but reflects secondary bleeding or iron deficiency rather than direct blood or marrow disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: despite the 30-79% annotation, bleeding-related or iron-deficiency anemia is a secondary, separately diagnosed condition rather than direct hematologic damage.

basis: Left renal vein entrapment causes venous hypertension, renal varices, hematuria and proteinuria; anemia occurs in only 5-29%.
Inherited red-cell membrane abnormality causes hemolytic anemia; hyperbilirubinemia reflects hemolysis rather than hepatic damage.
Maxillary sinus collapse and progressive enophthalmos define the disease; visual impairment is uncommon.
Immune-mediated demyelinating polyneuropathy; ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic dysfunction. IgM paraprotein alone does not establish blood-cell damage.
Inherited platelet-lineage disorder. Annotated thromboses and cerebral ischemia are separately diagnosed vascular complications; risks vary across subtypes.
Autoimmune paraneoplastic retinal dysfunction; associated extraocular cancers are separate diseases and do not establish additional organ involvement.
Paroxysmal dystonia causes episodic head posturing; vomiting and vertigo do not establish gastrointestinal or vestibular-organ damage.
The supplied definition identifies psychiatric conversion symptoms without an underlying structural or neurochemical neurologic disease.
Monogenic metabolic obesity; accelerated skeletal maturation is not destructive bone disease. Hypertension occurs in only 5-29%.
Inherited degeneration of the retina defines the umbrella; extraocular disease is confined to particular subtypes.
Defined by muscle ion-channel dysfunction; nerve or cardiac involvement is subtype-specific rather than shared across the umbrella.
Structural hair-shaft dysplasia with segmental branching and abnormal hair morphology.
Pneumocystis fungal infection directly causes pneumonia; extrapulmonary disease is uncommon. Underlying immunodeficiency is a predisposing condition.
Eosinophilic inflammatory infiltration of lungs causes acute hypoxic respiratory failure. Reactive eosinophil abnormalities do not establish a blood disorder.
Autoimmune small-vessel vasculitis; glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhagic involvement reported in 80-99%; neuropathy, GI injury and skin ulcers omitted at cap.
Auricular chondritis, arthritis and large-vessel vasculitis each 80-99% per HPO. Airway damage 30-79% and diagnostic ocular inflammation omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: supplied HPO reports destructive large-vessel vasculitis in 80-99%, supporting priority within the four-axis cap.
decisions.pulmonary: none: airway damage qualifies at 30-79%, but is omitted at the cap in favor of more frequent auricular, joint and vascular disease plus the immune mechanism.

basis: Autoimmune inflammatory skeletal myopathy; interstitial pulmonary abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Cardiac disease is occasional (5-29%).
Aplasia of Müllerian-derived reproductive structures; associated urinary anomalies are not established for this umbrella concept.
Developmental delay, osteopenia and structural skin abnormalities define the syndrome; dental and valvular abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Renal tubulopathy, dilated cardiomyopathy and defining electrolyte/acid-base abnormalities. Pulmonary edema is secondary; hepatic calcification lacks demonstrated functional damage.
Skeletal ossification defects and developmental delay define syndrome; hepatomegaly with elevated transaminases occurs in 30–79%, supporting hepatic injury.
Spinal motor-neuron disease, Dandy-Walker malformation and cataracts define the syndrome; persistent denervation-associated muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal muscle atrophy in 80-99% represents lasting muscle tissue loss from the disease's denervation, beyond weakness alone.

basis: Brain/enteric neuropathy, intestinal dysmotility and neurogenic megacystis define it; strabismus 80-99%, lacrimal stenosis 30-79%. Limb and airway malformations omitted under cap.
Primary intraventricular brain tumor; visual symptoms reflect intracranial pressure without established direct ocular damage.
Destructive arterial invasion defines the infection; sinusitis and skin infection each occur in 30-79%. Ocular, CNS and gastrointestinal manifestations are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the definition identifies destructive arterial invasion with embolization and tissue necrosis as characteristic disease pathology.

basis: Disordered neural circadian regulation causes a persistent sleep-wake disturbance; blindness is an antecedent association, not damage caused by this disorder.
Autoantibodies disable coagulation factors; bleeding sites do not establish common lasting damage to additional organs.
Hypoglycin poisoning directly disrupts intermediary metabolism and causes hypoglycemia; vomiting alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Defined by persistent keratotic skin plaques and abnormal epidermal keratinization.
Inherited heme synthesis disorders; skin and neurologic injury vary substantially by subtype, without an established majority across this umbrella. Hepatic synthesis does not imply liver damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: cutaneous injury defines particular subtypes; the evidence does not establish that it affects most patients across the inherited porphyria umbrella.

basis: Eosinophilic meningitis defines the infection; enteritis with GI eosinophilic infiltration is frequent (30-79%). Ocular invasion is uncommon.
Coagulation deficiency with defining recurrent venous thrombosis; retinal and destructive skin findings chiefly reflect severe recessive disease, not most across this umbrella.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: recurrent venous thrombosis is explicitly part of the disease definition, beyond a future vascular risk.

basis: Inherited coagulation disorder; thrombosis is a separately diagnosed consequence. Destructive skin disease chiefly concerns severe recessive forms or treatment, not most patients.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: protein C deficiency defines a coagulation defect; DVT is a separately diagnosed consequence rather than intrinsic vessel disease.

basis: Fly larvae invade tissue, predominantly skin and wounds. Nasal, ocular and ear infestation are site-specific minority forms across the umbrella.
Liver failure and intestinal malabsorption occur in 80-99%; splenic storage with anemia is common (>=30%). Developmental delay alone does not establish direct CNS injury.
Lysosomal lipid storage with defining hepatic injury. Splenomegaly alone does not prove dysfunction; hypersplenism/cytopenias are each reported in 1/1. Arteriosclerosis is a separate disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenomegaly is common, but functional hypersplenism/cytopenias are supported only by isolated 1/1 reports; impairment in at least 30% is not established.

basis: Inherited cone photoreceptor dysfunction causes reduced visual acuity and abnormal cone electroretinography; no extraocular disease is established.
Inherited retinal dysfunction causing congenital stationary night blindness.
Brain malformation, heart defects and polydactyly define syndrome; renal hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Hair/nail abnormalities omitted at four-axis cap.
Androgen hormone resistance defines an endocrine disorder; reproductive anatomy has no additional axis.
Leydig-cell dysfunction causes androgen deficiency; hypospadias is a structural urethral malformation reported in 80-99%. Delayed skeletal maturation alone does not establish bone damage.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a congenital urethral malformation reported in 80-99%; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.

basis: Congenital vascular malformations with defining bone hypoplasia, limb shortening and muscle hypotrophy.
Clonal marrow disorder with ineffective hematopoiesis and ring sideroblasts; hepatic and cardiac findings are uncommon.
Endomyocardial fibrosis causes restrictive cardiomyopathy; congestive hepatomegaly does not establish direct hepatic injury, and infection is only suspected.
Eosinophil-mediated endomyocardial injury causes restrictive cardiomyopathy and mural thrombosis; associated hematologic diseases are separate.
Progressive neurodegeneration causes freezing gait and postural instability; reported hypertension is a separate comorbidity.
Renal mineralocorticoid resistance causes salt wasting, hyperkalemia and acidosis; extra-renal manifestations are subtype-dependent.
Renal tubular electrolyte-transport disorder defining hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis and hypertension; normal filtration does not exclude tubular dysfunction.
Brain malformations and developmental disability define the syndrome; strabismus 80-99% and hypermetropia 30-79% support ocular dysfunction. Hypermobility alone lacks documented damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypermobility occurs in 30-79%, but no associated tissue injury or functional loss is established; skeletal deformities occur in 5-29%.

basis: Premature hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal activation; accelerated skeletal maturation does not establish separate skeletal damage.
Immune small-vessel vasculitis with defining cutaneous purpura; bowel involvement ~50-75%; renal involvement ~30-50% and arthritis ~60-80% omitted by cap.
Bacterial skeletal-muscle infection; cutaneous abscesses are reported in 80-99%; renal impairment occurs in <30%.
Neurometabolic energy disorder with developmental brain injury; supplied HPO reports osteolytic toe defects in 30-79%, supporting skeletal damage.
Necrotizing arteritis; neuropathy and renal involvement each occur in 30-79%. Cutaneous findings and arthritis omitted at cap, prioritizing nerve and kidney damage; GI involvement is 5-29%.
audit_reason: Replace dermatologic with renal under the cap: frequent renal ischemic injury is more consequential. Common skin morphology and livedo do not establish equally frequent destructive skin injury; ulcers are occasional.

basis: Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder; extracardiac damage is not common across the umbrella.
Congenital partial or complete absence of the iris; additional systemic features belong to specific syndromic subtypes.
Rabies virus directly causes fatal encephalomyelitis; salivation, gastrointestinal symptoms and vocal cord paresis do not establish separate organ damage.
Primary lymphatic drainage failure causes chronic dermal/subcutaneous swelling and fibrosis. Secondary infection risk does not establish immune involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic vessels are not explicitly covered by the cardiovascular axis; blood-vessel or cardiac disease is not established.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: the defining chronic edema and tissue fibrosis affect skin and subcutis.

basis: Leukodystrophy with progressive ataxia and pyramidal dysfunction plus defining dental agenesis; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defining external ear, oral cleft and vision-impairing ocular abnormalities; kyphosis, pectus excavatum and cervical ribs occur in 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement.
Developmental delay and skeletal malformations define syndrome; damaging eye anomalies and oral clefts annotated 80-99%; tumour predisposition does not establish organ damage.
Defining vascular and skin lesions; pulmonary AVMs and hepatic AVMs/portal hypertension each 30-79%. Oral lesions omitted at cap; anemia is secondary blood loss.

decisions.haematologic: none: blood-loss anemia is a separately diagnosed consequence, rather than direct disease of blood cells or marrow.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary AVMs with functional shunting occur in 30-79%; recurrent nasal mucosal bleeding adds support.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous hemorrhagic telangiectasias are defining lesions, present in 80-99%.

basis: Intellectual disability is explicitly the sole defining manifestation of this nonsyndromic neurodevelopmental umbrella.
Inherited dysregulation of appetite and energy balance; diabetes, fatty liver and cardiovascular disease are separate potential complications.
Coxiella infection commonly causes granulomatous hepatic inflammation; hepatocellular injury is supported by transaminase elevation in 30-79%. Pneumonia is 5-29%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: granulomatous hepatic inflammation is a usual disease manifestation; transaminase elevation in 30-79% supports common hepatocellular injury.

basis: Anterior segment dysgenesis defines disease; hearing impairment and cardiovascular malformations each annotated 30-79%; dental anomalies are annotated below 30%.
Neurodevelopmental and skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; damaging ocular anomalies and heart defects each occur in 30-79%. Common dental shape variants need not impair function.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart abnormalities are annotated in 30-79% and represent direct structural cardiac disease.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: talon cusps/high palate (80-99%) need not impair function; caries (30-79%) is secondary dental disease rather than direct syndromic damage.

basis: Umbrella of inherited amino acid and organic acid metabolic disorders; additional organ damage varies by subtype.
Diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis; intellectual disability is frequent (30-79%). Unspecified hemangiomas do not establish cardiovascular damage; heart defects occur in 5-29%.
audit_reason: Remove cardiovascular: unspecified hemangiomas do not establish cardiovascular functional damage or location; structural heart defects are only occasional. Retain neurologic for intellectual disability annotated at 30-79%.

basis: IgG4-mediated infiltration of lacrimal and salivary glands defines disease; renal and other systemic manifestations are uncommon or separately diagnosed.
Subcutaneous adipose loss and severe insulin resistance define disease; hepatic steatosis/hepatomegaly in 80-99% reflects ectopic lipid deposition.
Subcutaneous fat loss with insulin resistance; hepatic steatosis and cardiomyopathy each reported in 30-79%. Associated autoimmunity alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
Localized loss of subcutaneous fat defines disease; systemic metabolic dysfunction is not characteristic of localized lipodystrophy.
Inherited myopathy, joint contractures and external ophthalmoplegia define the syndrome. Respiratory distress and dysphagia lack evidence of common direct organ damage.
Spinal vascular malformation and chronic venous congestion cause necrotizing spinal cord injury.
Metabolic epileptic encephalopathy with folate/neurotransmitter abnormalities. Respiratory distress does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Autoimmune bilateral granulomatous uveitis; hearing and skin abnormalities are occasional (5-29%) and excluded.
Immune-mediated granulomatous skin inflammation with inflammatory arthritis defines the syndrome; skin and joints are primary sites.
Progressive retinal photoreceptor degeneration; hearing annotations reflect syndromic forms and do not apply to most patients across this umbrella.
Thyrotoxicosis and hypokalemia cause recurrent skeletal-muscle inexcitability and paralysis. Graves disease is an underlying cause, not an obligatory immune mechanism.
Malignant fibroblastic neoplasm arises in soft connective tissues; no additional organ site or common direct organ damage is established.
Idiopathic diffuse alveolar injury causes respiratory failure; infection or autoimmune disease is not established. Hypertension is not direct cardiovascular injury from AIP.
Smoking-related bronchiolar and interstitial lung injury; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Defining hair dysplasia and defective dental enamel; both reported in 80-99%.
Neonatal diabetes, developmental delay and epilepsy define DEND; weakness and hypotonia do not independently establish muscle damage.
Postinfectious immune-mediated brainstem encephalitis; ophthalmoplegia is neurologic. Respiratory infections are separate diseases; respiratory failure is 5-29%.
Mosquito-borne viral infection of brain and sometimes spinal motor neurons; muscle atrophy reflects denervation rather than direct muscle disease.
Isolated congenital absence or dystrophy of nails.
Persistent keratotic epidermal plaques on sun-exposed skin; subsequent carcinoma is a separate minority complication.
Umbrella for inherited carbohydrate metabolism defects; no additional organ is consistently damaged across most subtypes.
Umbrella of organic acid metabolism disorders; lasting neurologic injury varies substantially by subtype and is not established in >=30% across the group.

decisions.neurologic: none: some subtypes cause frequent brain injury, but others usually preserve development; >=30% lasting neurologic involvement across this umbrella is not established.

basis: Umbrella of inherited amino acid transport disorders; renal, intestinal and ocular damage vary by subtype and are not universal group features.
Bile-acid synthesis defects are metabolic disorders, typically with cholestatic liver injury. Neurologic disease is subtype-dependent; malabsorption need not damage bowel.
Inherited defects of neurotransmitter synthesis, metabolism or transport directly impair nervous-system function.
Inherited cobalamin handling defects commonly cause megaloblastic cytopenias and neurologic injury, each roughly >30% across the group; expression varies by subtype.
Inherited sulfur amino acid and methionine metabolism disorders; additional organ damage is not shared across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Umbrella of inborn fatty acid and ketone metabolism disorders; no additional organ injury is established across most subtypes.
Inherited disruption of gluconeogenesis; persistent organ damage is not established across most constituent disorders.
Inherited glucose transport defect; renal, neurologic and intestinal manifestations belong to different subtypes and do not apply across the umbrella.
Inherited histidine metabolic defects; common intrinsic organ damage is not established across histidinemia and urocanic aciduria.
Inherited ketone utilization defect causing metabolic ketoacidosis; lasting extra-metabolic injury is not common across the group.
Umbrella of inherited ornithine or proline metabolic defects; no additional organ injury is established as common across the group.
Umbrella of inherited pentose-phosphate metabolic disorders; hemolysis, liver disease and neurologic injury are subtype-dependent.
Umbrella of inherited peptide metabolism disorders; no additional damaged organ is shared by most patients across the group.
Metabolic beta-oxidation defects; neurologic injury typical across subtypes (inferred >30%); hepatic disease varies. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_79188)
Peroxisomal metabolic disease with defining neurologic and retinal dysfunction; hearing loss affects most (>80%). Hepatic disease is common (>30%) but omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: none under cap: hepatic dysfunction is common (>30%) and can be severe; defining neurologic, retinal and auditory dysfunction take the available organ slots.
decisions.ocular: primary: pigmentary retinal degeneration is explicitly defining and causes visual loss across the spectrum.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects most (>80%); retained as the fourth axis because primary is capped at three.

basis: Umbrella of inherited phenylalanine and tyrosine metabolic disorders; additional organ damage is not consistently shared across subtypes.
Inherited purine metabolic disorders; neurologic, renal and immune manifestations vary substantially between subtypes.
Inherited vitamin B6 metabolism disorders; both listed subtypes cause epilepsy, with neurologic dysfunction in most patients.
Pyrimidine metabolic disorders; neurologic and blood abnormalities vary across subtypes and are not established across most of the umbrella.
Serine/glycine metabolic defects; encephalopathy and neurodevelopmental impairment predominate in major clinical forms (>30% estimated overall). Benign biochemical subtypes exist.

decisions.neurologic: involved: glycine encephalopathy and serine-deficiency disorders cause direct brain dysfunction; estimated >30% across the clinical umbrella.

basis: Inherited sterol biosynthesis defect; additional organ damage varies substantially among subtypes, without sufficient evidence for a shared organ across the umbrella.
Inherited gamma-glutamyl/glutathione metabolic disorders; hemolysis and neurologic injury vary substantially across constituent diseases.
Inherited branched-chain amino-acid metabolic umbrella; neurologic injury varies substantially by subtype, and a group-wide frequency of at least 30% is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurotoxicity is prominent in MSUD and several other subtypes, but persistent neurologic damage in at least 30% across this heterogeneous umbrella is not established.

basis: Inherited disruption of energy metabolism; no additional organ damage is established in most patients across this broad umbrella.
Inherited lysosomal lipid degradation/storage disorders; neurologic, hepatic and other organ damage varies across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Lysosomal transport/storage disorder umbrella; renal and neurological damage vary by subtype and are not established across the group.
Lysosomal storage disease group explicitly defined by mental disability and skeletal malformations; additional organ damage varies by subtype.

decisions.neurologic: primary: mental disability is explicitly part of the disease group's definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal malformations are explicitly part of the disease group's definition.

basis: Lysosomal storage disorder; skeletal disease and valve damage commonly exceed 50%; CNS damage exceeds 30% across major types. Hearing and airway damage omitted at cap.
Inborn amine/neurotransmitter metabolic disorders; persistent neurologic dysfunction, including seizures or movement disorders, occurs in most patients across the group.
Lysosomal oligosaccharide storage; neurodevelopmental impairment or degeneration and skeletal dysostosis each affect >30% across the group. Other organ involvement varies.
Neurotransmitter-metabolism umbrella with defining neurologic subtypes, including seizures and hyperekplexia; no shared additional damaged organ.
Umbrella of inherited nucleotide metabolism disorders; additional organ damage varies substantially among subtypes.
Lysosomal sphingolipid degradation disorder. Neurologic, hepatic, splenic and other damage varies by subtype; no additional organ is established across most patients.
Inherited sterol metabolic disorders; additional organ damage varies across subtypes and is not established across the umbrella.
Inherited iron metabolism disorder; hepatic fibrosis occurs in 80–99%, cardiomyopathy and arthropathy in 30–79% each. Pigmentation alone does not establish skin damage.

decisions.hepatic: involved: iron deposition produces hepatic fibrosis in 80–99%; the defining primary disorder is systemic iron metabolism rather than a liver-specific disease.

basis: Partial phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency; sustained untreated phenylalanine of 600-1200 umol/L causes neurocognitive impairment in roughly >=30%; early treatment can prevent injury.

decisions.neurologic: involved: sustained untreated phenylalanine at 600-1200 umol/L commonly causes cognitive dysfunction, estimated >=30%; prevention by treatment does not exclude it.

basis: Phenylalanine metabolism disorder; untreated classic disease causes severe intellectual disability and persistent neurologic injury in most patients.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by progressive dementia, seizures and motor decline; retinal degeneration is not common across adult forms.
Lysosomal storage disease with rapid neurodegeneration; progressive retinal degeneration and blindness occur in most patients, typically over 80%.
Lysosomal storage disorder defined by neurodegeneration, seizures and vision loss from retinal degeneration.
Lysosomal disorder with defining neurologic disease; cataracts 80-99%, cardiomyopathy 30-79%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Focal pancreatic beta-cell hyperplasia causes uncontrolled insulin secretion and hypoglycemia; endocrine pancreas belongs to the metabolic_endocrine axis.
Autoinflammatory osteitis, hyperostosis and synovitis with defining pustular/acneiform skin disease; intestinal inflammation, thrombosis and vasculitis occur in 5-29%.
Mutase deficiency causes organic acidemia; developmental impairment/dystonia and immunodeficiency each 30-79%. Renal insufficiency, optic atrophy and cardiomyopathy are 5-29%.
Umbrella for diseases of the epidermis; extracutaneous manifestations do not apply across the group.
Generalized abnormal cornification and epidermal barrier dysfunction; systemic associations do not apply across most patients.
Umbrella of keratinization disorders defined by persistent erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques; systemic manifestations are subtype-specific.
Inherited palmoplantar epidermal hyperkeratosis; additional organ disease is confined to particular syndromic subtypes.
Inherited structural skin fragility with recurrent blistering. Substantial mucosal and other organ injury varies by subtype and is not established across most patients.
Disorder of hair shafts and pilosebaceous appendages; no other organ involvement defines the umbrella.
Excessive hair growth defines this umbrella concept; multisystem features of individual syndromic subtypes do not apply across the group.
Anomaly of the nail, an epidermal appendage.
Inherited isolated structural disorders of nails, without systemic syndromic involvement.
Defective skin appendages and dentition are defining and common across ectodermal dysplasias; other organ defects vary by subtype.
Umbrella disorder defined by abnormal pigmentation of the skin; syndromic complications do not apply across the group.
Skin pigmentation disorder; systemic abnormalities of individual syndromic subtypes do not apply across this umbrella.
Defined by reduced epidermal melanin; syndromic eye, hearing or neurologic abnormalities do not apply across this umbrella.
Disease of the superficial cutaneous vasculature defines both skin and vascular involvement; systemic manifestations vary by subtype.
Umbrella disorder of the dermis; extracutaneous abnormalities vary among its subtypes.
Superficial fascia and subcutaneous tissue belong to the dermatologic axis; other organs vary across subtypes.
Persistent lymphatic edema is located in skin and subcutis. Lymphatic obstruction alone establishes neither blood-vessel disease nor an immune mechanism.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic drainage obstruction does not establish disease of the heart, arteries, veins or blood capillaries covered by this axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: chronic edema directly affects skin and subcutaneous tissue, which are explicitly covered by this axis.

basis: Inherited epidermal disease; ectropion 80-99%, keratitis and corneal erosion 30-79%. Hearing impairment from external canal scaling occurs in 30-79%.
Skin fragility and defining enamel hypoplasia; oral mucosal blistering occurs in 80-99%. Anemia is secondary to wounds, inflammation or nutritional loss, without direct blood-cell disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia is frequent (30-79%) but secondary to wounds, inflammation or nutritional loss; direct hematologic injury is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: enamel hypoplasia is explicitly part of the disease definition; oral mucosal blistering also affects 80-99%.

basis: Defining blistering and erosions affect intertriginous skin and esophagus; common dental enamel defects also support gastrointestinal involvement.
Inherited skin fragility and blistering; dental enamel hypoplasia affects 30-79%. Oral mucosal blistering alone is below 30%.
Oral blistering and GI inflammation occur in 30–79%. Urinary abnormality is nonspecific; damaging urethral strictures occur in <30%.
Localized scalp hair abnormality, often with epidermal nevus; ocular, skeletal and endocrine abnormalities are below 30%.
Melanin/organelle disorder with platelet dysfunction and ocular albinism; pulmonary fibrosis 30-79%. Skin and renal findings omitted at cap; immunodeficiency is subtype-specific.
audit_reason: Add primary metabolic_endocrine for the melanin/organelle metabolic disorder. Omit dermatologic under the four-axis cap, prioritizing platelet dysfunction, ocular impairment and common severe pulmonary fibrosis.

basis: Hereditary structural or functional lymphatic vessel disorder; swelling alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Localized mast-cell proliferation occupying skin; mediator-related diarrhea does not establish direct intestinal damage.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation infiltrates and damages skin. Mediator-related diarrhea and hypotension do not establish extracutaneous damage; marrow abnormalities are only 1-4%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: mastocytosis is a proliferative disease of hematopoietic mast cells; a blood-cell neoplasm need not occupy marrow to qualify.

basis: Clonal mast-cell proliferation confined to skin defines cutaneous mastocytosis; mediator symptoms do not establish damage to other organs.
Follicular skin atrophy and cutaneous basal cell carcinoma define the condition.
