Localized inflammatory verrucous epidermal nevus; the inflammatory descriptor alone does not establish an autoimmune or immune-mediated disease.
Localized benign epidermal skin lesion; the definition does not establish systemic nevus-syndrome manifestations.
Localized verrucous cutaneous nevus; no established extracutaneous involvement.
Progeroid skin, skeletal changes and lipodystrophy define the syndrome; arterial stenosis and valve calcification annotated 80-99%. Retinal pigmentation alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: generalized lipodystrophy and marked metabolic dysfunction are core features; the axis does not depend solely on separately diagnosed diabetes.

basis: Autoimmune blistering skin disease; stomatitis and oral mucosal blisters occur in 30-79%, establishing direct oral involvement.
Autoimmune superficial blistering skin disease. Oral ulcers occur in only 5-29%; associated systemic lupus is a separate disease.
Autoimmune superficial blistering and erosive skin disease; oral mucosal involvement is uncommon, below 30%.
Dermal melanocytosis and cutaneous capillary malformations define the disorder; damaging ocular or neurologic involvement is not established above 30%.
Defined by dermal melanocytosis and cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita, a cutaneous vascular malformation; systemic involvement is variable.
Defined by speckled lentiginous nevi and cutaneous capillary malformations; common damaging ocular or neurologic involvement is not established.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: a defining capillary malformation is a structural disease of blood vessels, which are explicitly included in this axis.

basis: Structural malformation of lymphatic vessels; no consistently affected additional organ specified.
Microcystic lymphatic vessel malformation characteristically involving dermal and subcutaneous lymphatics, including lymphangioma circumscriptum.
Hair-follicle abnormality produces multiple shafts through one pilary canal.
Inherited palmoplantar epidermal hyperkeratosis; reported internal malignancies are uncommon, separately diagnosed cancers.
Pancreatic beta-cell hyperinsulinism causes hypoglycemia; permanent neurologic injury is not established in at least 30%.
Pancreatic insulin dysregulation causes hypoglycemia. Specific lasting neurologic deficits occur in 5-29%; the broad nervous-system annotation does not establish lasting damage.
Mild phenylalanine metabolism disorder; the definition does not establish neurologic damage at these untreated concentrations.
Colorectal adenomatous polyposis, osteomas and skin/soft tissue tumors define Gardner syndrome; retinal pigment lesions generally do not impair vision.
Autoimmune blistering disease of skin; mucosal damage varies substantially among subtypes and is not established as common across the umbrella.
Immune granulomas affect lungs in ~90%; uveitis and liver dysfunction are HPO frequent (30-79%). Skin involvement and cytopenias omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: decreased liver function is HPO frequent (30-79%), supporting functional injury from granulomatous involvement.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary granulomatous disease occurs in ~90%; the umbrella is defined by multisystem immune granulomas rather than a required pulmonary site.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: skin lesions are HPO frequent (30-79%), but pulmonary, ocular and hepatic functional injury take priority.

basis: Developmental and learning impairment define the syndrome; skeletal deformities and night blindness each annotated 30-79%. Asthma is a separate disease.
Autoimmune skin sclerosis; umbrella includes localized disease. Visceral fibrosis is subtype-dependent and not established in at least 30% across the group.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and skeletal defects define syndrome; glaucoma and dental defects 30-79%; sparse hair omitted by cap.
Autoimmune myositis and ILD define the syndrome; mechanic hands are a characteristic persistent hyperkeratotic lesion (~30-40%). Raynaud alone is not vascular damage.
Shigella infection directly inflames and damages intestinal mucosa. Dehydration and electrolyte changes are acute consequences; extraintestinal organ damage is rare.
Lysosomal disorder defined by myoclonus, ataxia and progressive visual loss; hearing loss 80-99% per HPO. Reported skeletal/skin findings omitted at cap.
Inherited epidermal disorder causing persistent superficial skin peeling; other organ damage does not characterize most patients across the group.
Developmental disability and skeletal overgrowth define the syndrome; cardiac and renal defects affect a minority. Single-patient HPO fractions do not establish population frequency.
Inherited red-cell membrane disease causing hemolysis; gallstones are a separate disease, and jaundice/hepatomegaly alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Spinal neural-tube and vertebral closure defects; urinary dysfunction estimates from open forms cannot establish common direct urinary damage across the isolated umbrella.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed consequence; direct urinary tract damage in ≥30% across open and occult forms is not established.

basis: Retinal and macular dystrophy causes progressive central visual loss; the frequent findings remain within the ocular axis.
Cleft palate and hearing loss frequent (30-79%) in HPO; definition gives deafness 10%, creating uncertainty; arrhythmia omitted at cap.
Autoinflammatory arthritis; pleuritis occurs in 30-79%. Hepatitis is 5-29%; enzyme elevations alone do not establish sustained liver damage. Evanescent rash excluded.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatitis occurs in 5-29%; frequent hepatomegaly and enzyme elevations alone do not establish substantial lasting hepatic damage.

basis: Urinary tract developmental malformations, including bladder exstrophy and lower urinary tract obstruction; reproductive abnormalities add no axis.
Congenital narrowing of the bony cervical canal defines the lesion; neural compression and myelopathy are predispositions rather than required established damage.
Sulfur amino acid metabolic disorder defined by progressive encephalopathy and lens dislocation; aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal damage.
Rickettsial infection of vascular endothelium causing systemic small-vessel vasculitis; rash is transient and lasting organ complications are not common enough.
Rickettsia akari infection; its self-limited vesicular eruption does not establish substantial lasting skin damage.
Rickettsia prowazekii infects vascular endothelium and causes systemic small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash and acute confusion do not establish lasting skin or brain damage.
Rickettsia felis infection; rash is transient, while neurologic dysfunction and pulmonary compromise are explicitly rare.
Orientia infection; necrotic inoculation eschars occur in roughly 40-80%, varying geographically. Uveitis and gangrene are uncommon despite supplied frequency tags; transient rash excluded.
audit_reason: Remove ocular: uveitis is an uncommon complication; its supplied frequency tag is clinically unreliable. Retain dermatologic for common necrotic inoculation eschars, rather than transient rash or rare gangrene.

basis: Lysosomal disease with defining neurodevelopmental dysfunction; muscle hypoplasia 80-99%, skeletal disease and skin ulcers 30-79%; nystagmus alone does not establish eye damage.
Localized developmental defects of enamel, dentin and pulp; teeth and gingiva belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Fibro-osseous lesions of jaw bone and dental cementum define disease; impacted teeth occur in 30-79%. Secondary infection is occasional.
Chronic neurologic pain and sensory/autonomic dysfunction define CRPS; persistent skin, hair and nail trophic abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Edema alone adds no vascular axis.
Erosive mucosal lichen planus involving gingiva and vulvovaginal tissues; obligate gingivitis and frequent skin erosion and lichenification.
Central sleep-wake regulation disorder causing excessive sleepiness and REM-related phenomena; no other organ damage is established.
Benign cystic lesion of bone; fractures remain within the skeletal axis, and neurologic abnormalities are very rare.
Tumor originates on abdominal peritoneal/omental surfaces; hepatic tumor spread is common, with hepatomegaly annotated in 30-79%. Lung and CNS tumors are <30%.
Cerebellar disease, optic atrophy and skin abnormalities define CAMOS; renal insufficiency/nephrotic syndrome 30–79%; skin-vessel abnormalities omitted at four-axis cap.
Brain malformations and polydactyly define the syndrome; cardiac septal defects and mitral regurgitation occur in 30-79%. Renal malposition alone does not establish damage.
West Nile viral encephalitis; CNS infection defines this concept despite the definition also describing non-neuroinvasive infection.
Mycoplasma-associated infectious encephalitis; preceding respiratory infection does not establish persistent pulmonary damage.
Mosquito-borne viral infection directly inflames the brain; gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish gastrointestinal injury.
Immune-mediated CNS demyelination with encephalopathy; visual loss is occasional (5-29%), below the involvement threshold.
Postinfectious or immune-mediated encephalitis with basal ganglia injury; ocular motor findings are neurologic, and pharyngitis is transient.
Autoimmune encephalopathy; supplied HPO identifies cerebral vasculitis in 80-99%, supporting direct vascular involvement. Associated Hashimoto thyroiditis is a separate disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: supplied HPO explicitly reports cerebral vasculitis in 80-99%; vascular inflammation satisfies direct damage and frequency requirements.

basis: Persistent or reactivated rubella infection causes chronic progressive inflammation and damage of the brain.
Ophthalmoplegia/ptosis, mouth malformation and preauricular skin tags define the syndrome. Actual tragus hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%; hearing impairment is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: preauricular skin tags are a named defining cutaneous malformation, reported in 30-79%.
decisions.otologic: none: preauricular skin tags and pits do not establish external-ear dysfunction; actual tragus hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Perineal cutaneous hemangioma and vesicorenal defects define syndrome; anorectal defects 30-79%; defining spinal defects 5-29% omitted under four-axis cap.
Autoimmune brain-retina-inner ear microangiopathy; damaging hearing loss is a diagnostic criterion and occurs in 30-79%. Cardiovascular axis omitted under four-axis cap.
Marrow failure; radial/thumb defects 80-99%, renal anomalies and neurodevelopmental deficits 30-79%; cardiac defects 30-79% omitted by cap; pigmentation alone is not damage.
Benign cutaneous adnexal tumour involving epidermal and dermal structures.
Abnormal bile acid synthesis causes chronic intestinal diarrhea and malabsorption; no intrinsic hepatobiliary damage is established.
Nephronophthisis and hepatic fibrosis define the syndrome. Hypertension is secondary; common direct cardiovascular or neurologic damage is not established.
Bladder outlet dysfunction with retention and structural bladder changes; neurologic deficits are absent. Recurrent UTIs are separate infections; encopresis alone is not bowel damage.
Function-impairing type III collagen deposition in glomeruli; associated hypertension does not establish separate common vascular damage.
Leukodystrophy is an inherited disorder of central nervous system white matter; unknown subtype adds no supported organs.
Immune-mediated peripheral motor nerve hyperexcitability; muscle stiffness and myokymia reflect nerve activity rather than direct muscle damage.
Protein-losing glomerular disease; steroid resistance does not establish an autoimmune mechanism across this heterogeneous group.
Beta-globin deficiency causes microcytic anemia. Umbrella includes mild forms; skeletal/endocrine annotations chiefly reflect severe disease, and iron-related injury often involves treatment.
Inherited ineffective erythropoiesis and red-cell abnormalities; common damaging liver involvement is not established across the heterogeneous CDA group.
The explicit definition specifies an extraneural soft-tissue tumor. Nerve involvement belongs to the intraneural subtype and is not assumed across the umbrella.
Progressive sensory and motor neuron degeneration; muscle atrophy (80-99%) is secondary to denervation, and dysphagia reflects bulbar dysfunction rather than gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy in 80-99% reflects motor-neuron denervation; the disease process directly affects neurons rather than skeletal muscle.

basis: Craniofacial and epiphyseal dysplasia with defining neurologic manifestations; hydrocephalus and spinal cord compression occur in 80-99%.
Skeletal dysplasia, cataracts and developmental abnormalities define it; hearing impairment 11/14. Neutropenia 11/14 omitted at the four-axis cap.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia with short limbs, defective ossification and cartilage stippling.
Primary metabolic bone disease with deficient bone mineralization and recurrent fractures; a separate systemic endocrine defect is not required.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine: osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disorder, as supported by its ancestry. A systemic endocrine defect is not required for the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Bilateral skeletal enchondromatosis involving clavicles and long bones defines disease.
Vertebral and long-bone dysplasia with enchondromas; pretibial blistering and skin erosion reported in 80-99%. Neurologic findings below 30%.
Ischial hypoplasia or aplasia and vertebral malformations define this skeletal dysplasia.
Brain, renal and optic nerve malformations are defining; alopecia occurs in 80-99%. Skeletal, hearing and gut defects (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal platelets. Intracranial and visceral hemorrhage occur in fewer than 30%; cutaneous bleeding does not establish lasting skin damage.
Intellectual disability, neurologic deterioration and antibody deficiency define it; cleft palate and kyphoscoliosis each occur in 30-79%.
Intellectual disability and precocious puberty define the syndrome; obesity reported in mothers does not establish another affected organ in patients.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy and progressive joint contractures define the syndrome; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Intellectual disability defines neurologic involvement; macroorchidism is reproductive anatomy without evidence of endocrine dysfunction.
Syndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay and seizures; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic pulmonary damage or immunodeficiency.
Intellectual disability, congenital ocular defects and hypogonadism characterize the syndrome; muscle hypoplasia/atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: microphthalmia, microcornea and cataract are characteristic structural abnormalities in the definition; cataract is annotated in 30-79%.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hypogenitalism is a defining manifestation, with hypogonadism explicitly annotated in 30-79%, supporting endocrine dysfunction.

basis: Intellectual disability and areflexia, genu valgum and small teeth are defining features; genu valgum occurs in 80-99% and microdontia in 30-79%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: small teeth are explicitly part of the syndrome's definition; microdontia occurs in 30-79%, and teeth belong to this axis.

basis: Syndromic intellectual disability; short stature, facial dysmorphism and minor clinodactyly do not establish skeletal dysfunction.
Defining intellectual disability and CNS malformations accompany acromegaly and documented growth hormone abnormalities.
Neurodegeneration defines the syndrome; macular degeneration occurs in 80-99%. Recurrent respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Hydrocephalus, intellectual disability and spastic diplegia define syndrome; scoliosis occurs frequently (30-79%). Hearing and optic abnormalities are occasional.
Neurodegeneration with severe developmental impairment, seizures and spasticity; blindness is a defining feature reported in 80-99%.
Intellectual disability, ataxia and apraxia define the syndrome; structural clubfoot occurs in 30-79%.
Thrombosis directly affects the portal venous system; neither intrinsic liver injury nor a systemic coagulation disorder is established.
Immune-mediated inflammatory polyarthritis; uveitis and anemia occur in only 5-29%, below the involvement threshold.
Immune-mediated oligoarthritis; intrinsic inflammatory uveitis is annotated frequent (30-79%).
Immune-mediated systemic arthritis; the characteristic rash is transient. Pericardial, pleural, renal and ocular damage are occasional.
Immune-mediated destructive polyarthritis defines the disease; no common direct extra-articular injury established.
Immune-mediated arthritis with defining psoriatic skin/nail disease; uveitis occurs in only 5-29%.
Immune-mediated arthritis and enthesitis define the disease; uveitis and cardiac abnormalities are occasional (5-29%) and excluded.
Clonal plasma-cell protein-deposition disorder; cardiac dysfunction 80-99%, renal dysfunction 30-79%. Hepatic, neural, GI and pulmonary findings omitted by cap.
Amyloid protein deposition with renal disease in 80-99%; hepatic cholestasis and intestinal malabsorption in 30-79%; cardiac amyloidosis only 1-4%.
Beta2-microglobulin deposits damage joints and bones; median neuropathy and axonal loss occur in 30-79%. Renal failure is antecedent; gastrointestinal and cardiac injury are <30%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: acquired beta2-microglobulin retention and amyloid deposition do not independently establish endocrine disease or an intrinsic metabolic disorder.

basis: Myocardial amyloid infiltration defines this cardiac ATTR subtype. Protein misfolding alone does not establish metabolic disease; neuropathy is 1-4% and other extracardiac damage below 30%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: amyloidogenic TTR misfolding establishes a deposition disorder, without evidence here of an endocrine or inborn metabolic disorder.

basis: Congenital abnormal connections of the great arteries and associated cardiac malformations; hypoxemia does not establish lung damage.
Trichinella directly infects intestine and skeletal muscle in its defining phases; cardiac, pulmonary and CNS complications are rare.
Benign hamartoma arising from cutaneous hair follicles.
Localized cutaneous mucin deposition with papules and variable fibrosis; definition explicitly excludes thyroid disease.
Dermal mucin deposition defines the disease; systemic involvement is inconsistent across subtypes, and monoclonal gammopathy is a separate condition.
Inherited cortical myoclonus, tremor and epilepsy; occasional transient visual symptoms do not establish ocular damage.
Defining severe brain malformations and fetal akinesia sequence, which includes congenital joint contractures.
Cerebral cortical malformation and cerebellar hypoplasia define this neurologic disorder.
Myeloproliferative neoplasm of marrow and neutrophils; splenic involvement remains within the haematologic axis.
Clonal myeloid proliferation involving blood and marrow; thrombosis and other extrahematologic complications are not defining or established as common.
Clonal marrow disease with dysplasia of multiple myeloid lineages and peripheral cytopenias.
Clonal bone marrow disease with excess myeloblasts and ineffective blood cell production; other organ damage is not common.
Acute myeloid leukemia with marrow fibrosis and pancytopenia; weakness and back pain do not establish skeletal muscle or bone damage.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood with multilineage dysplasia and cytopenias; common direct extramedullary damage is not established.
Myeloid malignancy affecting marrow and blood cells; therapy-related origin does not change its organ classification.
Acute myeloid leukemia with basophilic differentiation involves blood and marrow; no established common extrahaematologic injury.
Acute leukemia of blood and marrow; ambiguous lineage does not itself imply lymphoma or an immune-mediated mechanism.
B-cell neoplasm involving blood, marrow and spleen; supplied classification includes aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
B-cell lymphoma directly occupies spleen, marrow and often blood; associated hepatitis C and autoimmune cytopenias are separate conditions.
Clonal plasma-cell disorder causes nonamyloid immunoglobulin deposition; renal deposition with dysfunction occurs in >90%. Significant cardiac or hepatic damage is less common.

decisions.renal: involved: renal deposition and dysfunction occur in >90%, downstream of the clonal plasma-cell disorder; this umbrella is not restricted to renal deposits.

basis: Lymphoplasmacytic B-cell neoplasia; alpha HCD accounts for most cases (~60-75%) and usually infiltrates small intestine, supporting gastrointestinal involvement in over 30% overall.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: alpha HCD predominates (~60-75% of cases) and usually causes intestinal infiltration with malabsorption; this exceeds 30% across the umbrella.

basis: Clonal mature B-cell lymphoma primarily involving lymph nodes; no additional organ damage established in at least 30%.
EBV-driven B-cell lymphoproliferation predominantly infiltrates lungs; CNS lesions occur in roughly 30-40%. Skin involvement around 30-50% omitted at cap; renal involvement usually <30%.
Plasmacytoid dendritic cell malignancy defined by hematologic disease and cutaneous tumors. Its historical lymphoma terminology does not establish a current lymphoma diagnosis.
Blood/marrow T-cell leukemia; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 40-50%. Skin infiltration is generally below 30%.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this concept is a leukemia, not an infection, immunodeficiency, autoimmune disease or lymphoma; lymphoid lineage alone does not qualify.

basis: Mature T-cell blood/marrow malignancy classified within T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma; associated autoimmune diseases are separate diagnoses.
NK-cell leukemia/lymphoma involving blood, marrow and spleen; hepatic infiltration and dysfunction occur in most patients (>50%).
HTLV-1-associated mature T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; direct cutaneous infiltration occurs in roughly 40–60%.
EBV-associated NK/T lymphoid malignancy usually arising in nasal or upper-airway tissues; palatal and orbital extension are not established as occurring in at least 30%.
Mature T-cell lymphoma arising predominantly in intestinal mucosa; lymphoid malignancy supplies haematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes.
T-cell lymphoma defined by hepatic sinusoidal infiltration, with usual splenic and marrow involvement.
T-cell lymphoma arises in subcutaneous fat; lymphoid cell origin and lymphoma mechanism qualify both additional primary axes; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.
Mature T-cell lymphoma originating in skin; lymphoid-cell malignancy and lymphoma mechanism also apply.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis. No additional organ is commonly directly involved.
Malignant hematopoietic histiocytic neoplasm; no individual extranodal organ has established involvement in at least 30%. It is not a lymphoma.
Malignant hematopoietic dendritic-cell neoplasm; direct cutaneous tumors occur in roughly one third of reported patients.
Immunodeficiency-associated lymphoid proliferation or lymphoma; no individual extranodal organ is consistently affected in at least 30%.
Hypothalamic developmental malformation causes epilepsy and cognitive decline; precocious puberty affects only some patients.
Unilateral status epilepticus causes cerebral hemiatrophy and hemiplegia; inflammation alone does not establish autoimmune disease.
Childhood epilepsy with absence seizures and associated myoclonus; central neurologic disease.
Epilepsy syndrome with recurrent myoclonic status on a background of non-progressive encephalopathy.
Palmoplantar keratoderma establishes skin disease. Acrocyanosis occurs in 80-99% but does not demonstrate vascular injury or clinically important loss of vascular function.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: acrocyanosis is a defining vasomotor sign, but its 80-99% frequency does not establish vessel injury or damaging cardiovascular disease.

basis: Inherited progressive cardiac conduction disease; syncope, dyspnea and dizziness do not establish additional organ damage.
Primary neoplasm originating in the heart; embolic injury to other organs is not consistently present across this tumour umbrella.
Primary neoplasm arising in the heart or pericardium.
Defined as an endocrine-cell neoplasm with endocrine gland neoplasm ancestry; anatomical sites vary, so no additional organ applies across the umbrella.
Isolated inherited hearing loss; speech delay secondary to deafness does not establish neurologic damage.
Tunga penetrans infestation directly occupies and inflames the skin.
Gonadal failure and skeletal abnormalities define disease; cardiac/aortic abnormalities and hearing loss each 30-79%. Enzyme elevation alone does not establish liver injury.
Sensorineural deafness and progressive retinal degeneration define Usher syndrome; vestibular dysfunction is otologic. Ataxia does not establish separate CNS damage.
Non-syndromic intellectual disability defines the umbrella; a metabolic disorder is not shared across most subtypes.
Developmental abnormalities of the anterior segment of the eye define this spectrum.
Chronic inflammation affects the superior conjunctiva and corneal limbus; associated thyroid disease is separate.
Hypothyroidism, colitis and cardiac hypertrophy define syndrome; developmental delay 30-79%; craniosynostosis 30-79% omitted because of four-axis cap.
Developmental enamel disease affecting most teeth; dental structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital lip fistulae and cleft lip/palate define this oral malformation syndrome.
Immune complex inflammation damages cutaneous small vessels and skin; systemic organ damage is not established in at least 30%.
Defined by abnormal structural development of the heart; no extracardiac damage applies across the umbrella.
Hepatic sinusoidal endothelial injury and small-vein obstruction define disease. Renal and respiratory failure annotations do not establish direct extrahepatic damage.
audit_reason: Remove pulmonary and renal: failure can reflect secondary multiorgan dysfunction rather than direct extrahepatic injury; HPO frequency alone is insufficient ([review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/4298625/)).

basis: Inherited retinal vascular development disorder; extraocular hearing, skeletal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Defined by hearing loss and skin/hair pigmentation abnormalities; iris heterochromia does not impair eye function. Renal and intestinal abnormalities are below 30%.
Hirschsprung disease, deafness and pigmentary changes define syndrome; visual/macular abnormalities 80–99%; olfactory lobe agenesis 30–79% omitted by cap.
Inherited skin fragility with progressive acral-to-truncal blistering; common damaging extracutaneous involvement is not established for this subtype.
Skin blistering/scarring; direct esophageal injury and strictures occur in 30-79%. Anemia and muscle wasting reflect blood loss or malnutrition.
Renal salt-wasting tubulopathy, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and sensorineural deafness are defining features; weakness does not establish primary muscle damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and ovarian failure; skeletal abnormalities and strabismus each 30-79%. Dental abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Chronic immune-complex cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis; arthralgia alone does not establish joint damage.
Defined autoimmune disease; no particular organ has established common direct injury. Arthralgia or Raynaud symptoms alone do not establish organ damage.
Inflammatory mass occupies liver; the IgG4-related hepatopathy synonym supports an immune-mediated mechanism. No common extrahepatic damage established.
Defined by radiation-induced spinal cord white matter damage; treatment causation does not exclude the disease's primary organ.
Congenital fusion or webbing of digits is a structural locomotor malformation; cutaneous webbing does not establish a separate skin disorder.
Glutathione metabolism defect causes erythrocyte hemolysis; cataracts reported in 3/3 patients. Hyperbilirubinemia reflects hemolysis, not hepatic damage.
Warm autoantibodies destroy red blood cells; dyspnea and palpitations reflect anemia. Heart failure is occasional, and bilirubin elevation does not establish hepatic damage.
Cold-reacting autoantibodies cause intravascular red-cell destruction; hemoglobinuria alone does not establish renal damage.
Warm and cold autoantibodies destroy red cells; associated lupus and lymphoma are separate diseases; rash and arthralgia do not establish organ damage.
Drug-triggered immune destruction of red cells; dyspnea and weakness are anemia symptoms, while heart failure occurs in only 5-29%.
Infection-associated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define HUS. Endothelial injury and microvascular thrombosis are defining; neurologic injury occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: direct capillary endothelial injury and microvascular thrombosis define the thrombotic microangiopathy, meeting the diagnostic-feature exception.

basis: Inherited abnormal hemoglobin affecting erythrocytes; generally asymptomatic or mildly anemic, without common extrahematologic damage.
Relative polycythemia from reduced plasma volume; associated hypertension and vascular risks do not establish additional direct organ damage.
Alveolar hemorrhage defines pulmonary disease. Anemia in 30-79% reflects blood loss, not direct blood-cell or marrow injury; autoimmune causes are separate underlying diseases.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia occurs in 30-79% but results from pulmonary blood loss; the syndrome does not directly damage blood cells, marrow or coagulation

basis: Acute hepatic dysfunction with coagulopathy and encephalopathy defines the diagnosis, despite the lower annotated encephalopathy frequency.
Rupture of an intracranial arterial aneurysm causes subarachnoid hemorrhage; visual field loss can be cerebral, and cardiac failure occurs in <30%.
Acute CNS and cardiovascular sympathomimetic poisoning; hypertension occurs in 30-79%. Infarction, pulmonary injury, seizures and renal injury are minority complications.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiovascular sympathomimetic toxicity defines the poisoning syndrome, including hypertension in 30-79%; infarction is not required.
decisions.neurologic: primary: acute central nervous system toxicity defines this poisoning, distinct from a purely psychiatric cocaine-use disorder.

basis: CNS toxicity, myocardial dysfunction and severe metabolic acidosis define systemic poisoning; renal failure is described, but frequency >=30% or diagnostic-criterion status is not established.
audit_reason: Remove renal from involved: renal failure is an additional manifestation, but occurrence in at least 30% or status as a major diagnostic criterion is not established.

basis: Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of skin with recurrent plaques and blistering; reactive blood eosinophilia is not a blood disorder.
Inherited peripheral neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy and fixed foot deformities affect most patients, representing structural tissue loss beyond weakness alone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic distal muscle wasting and fixed foot deformities affect most patients; established tissue loss and deformity qualify beyond transient weakness.

basis: Axonal neuropathy with defining optic atrophy and hearing loss; muscle wasting, skeletal deformities and contractures are typical (>30%). Respiratory impairment is variable.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is an explicit defining feature of this specific neuropathy syndrome; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing loss is an explicit defining feature of this specific syndrome, rather than an incidental complication.

basis: Axonal neuropathy with defining acrodystrophy: persistent skin ulcers, contractures and terminal phalangeal loss. Associated osteomyelitis does not establish an intrinsic infectious mechanism.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent nonhealing ulcers are part of the defining acrodystrophy.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: contractures and mutilating loss of terminal phalanges are defining skeletal manifestations.

basis: Defined by hereditary peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy with optic atrophy.
Localized loss of subcutaneous fat; no characteristic systemic metabolic dysfunction. Lymphadenitis is occasional.
Localized loss of subcutaneous fat, sometimes with epidermal atrophy; systemic metabolic dysfunction is not characteristic.
Localized loss of subcutaneous fat defines this condition; systemic metabolic abnormalities are not established.
Panniculitis destroys subcutaneous fat; lipoatrophy is obligate. Localized fat loss does not establish a metabolic disorder.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation and abnormal immunoglobulins do not establish autoimmunity or another qualifying immune mechanism; ANA positivity is only occasional.

basis: Localized mechanically induced loss of subcutaneous fat; no systemic metabolic or endocrine dysfunction is inherent.
Chronic autoimmune cutaneous lupus; Raynaud phenomenon alone does not establish lasting vascular damage. Systemic lupus is occasional and separately diagnosed.
Autoimmune cutaneous inflammation causes scarring, dyspigmentation and alopecia; systemic lupus is a separate disease.
Hypertrophic variant of chronic cutaneous lupus, an autoimmune skin disease; systemic lupus involvement is not implied.
Skin-limited immune-mediated lupus with dermal inflammatory infiltrates; systemic lupus manifestations are not typical.
Cutaneous lupus causes autoimmune inflammation of deep dermis and subcutaneous fat; systemic lupus manifestations are not inherent to this cutaneous subtype.
Immune-mediated cutaneous fibrosis; frequent arthralgia alone is insufficient, while arthritis, myopathy and contractures occur in 5-29%.
Autoimmune cutaneous sclerosis with defining vasculopathy; esophageal dysfunction is a cardinal criterion and occurs in over 70%.
Inherited VWF coagulation defect; angiodysplasia is a separately coded vascular condition; reported mitral findings do not establish direct VWD damage.
Skin fragility, abnormal scarring and joint hypermobility define classic EDS; aortic root aneurysm reported in 14/42 (~33%). Recurrent infections are separate diseases.
Classic EDS defines joint hypermobility/dislocations and skin fragility/scarring; sinusitis is separate and haemoptysis alone is insufficient.
Neurodegeneration and cutaneous photosensitivity define Cockayne syndrome; retinopathy and hearing loss occur in 80-99%. Contractures (8/8), dental and hepatic/renal findings omitted at cap.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary because photosensitivity is a defining Cockayne feature, reported in 80–99%. Remove musculoskeletal under the four-axis cap to retain defining skin disease and frequent retinal and hearing damage.

basis: Neurocutaneous DNA-repair disorder; retinopathy 11/14, cataract 8/14 and sensorineural hearing loss 2/2. Kyphosis 2/3 omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: photosensitive, progeroid skin and subcutaneous abnormalities are defining Cockayne features; subcutaneous fat loss is reported in 3/3.

basis: Dermal elastic tissue disorder; aortic/valvular abnormalities and joint laxity/spinal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%; emphysema is occasional.
Skin laxity, emphysema and vascular defects define ARCL1; fractures and joint subluxation occur in 30-79%. GI and urinary diverticula occur in <30%.
Metabolic connective tissue disorder with defining skin laxity and skeletal anomalies; developmental delay is a defining, common neurologic feature.
Intestinal lymphatic dilation causes protein-losing enteropathy; direct enteric lymphocyte loss produces lymphopenia in 30-79%. Immune deficiency and effusions are under 30%.
Progressive scalp hair loss with follicular and epidermal abnormalities; allergic conditions are occasional and separate.
Cutaneous mastocytosis with clonal mast-cell proliferation in skin; telangiectases do not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Inherited isolated absence or dystrophy of nails.
Localized dermal mucinous nodules; no evidence of thyroid disease or systemic organ damage.
Localized cutaneous mucinosis producing chronic papules on the limbs and trunk; no defining systemic endocrine disorder.
Localized cutaneous mucin deposition produces persistent papules; no systemic organ involvement is established.
Localized cutaneous mucinosis producing persistent papules on the hands and forearms.
Localized cutaneous mucinosis; fever, arthralgia and weakness do not establish damage to additional organs.
Localized cutaneous mucinosis combining skin subtypes; systemic scleromyxedema involvement should not be extrapolated to this localized disease.
Localized cutaneous mucin deposition; gammopathy and systemic manifestations are alternative presentations without evidence that any additional organ is damaged in >=30%.
Generalized dermal mucin deposition and sclerodermoid infiltration; no established common extracutaneous damage for this specific form.
Inherited nonsyndromic hearing loss; additional organs affected in individual subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness is confined to auditory function; additional organ disease is not characteristic across the umbrella.
Deficiency of all anterior pituitary hormones; skeletal damage is reported only occasionally (5-29%).
UV injury defines skin/eye disease; supplied HPO places neuroregression and hypogonadism at 80-99%, though umbrella frequencies are uncertain. Cap omits dental/hearing findings.
Defining fracture-prone osteopenia, severe myopia and sensorineural hearing loss; ID in both reported brothers (2/2). Enamel hypoplasia omitted by four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability is defining and present in both brothers (2/2); placed here because primary is capped at three.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss is a named defining feature in both brothers, alongside osteopenia and severe myopia.

basis: Monoclonal gammopathy causes proximal tubular light-chain injury; defining bicarbonate, phosphate and other solute wasting establishes renal and metabolic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: generalized Fanconi solute wasting includes defining bicarbonate and phosphate handling defects, placing this syndrome on the electrolyte/acid-base axis.

basis: Glomerular immunoglobulin deposition causes immune-mediated renal injury. Associated lymphoproliferative disorders are separate diseases.
Monoclonal cryoproteins cause occlusive vasculopathy; acral ulcers and peripheral neuropathy each occur in 30-79%. Renal disease is 5-29%; type I is not inherently autoimmune.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: characteristic small-vessel occlusion by precipitated cryoproteins is a vascular disease process, distinct from true vasculitis reported in 5-29%.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: monoclonal protein precipitation is not inherently autoimmune or immune-complex disease; an associated lymphoma is a separate diagnosis.

basis: Persistent immune-mediated arthritis; no additional organ damage established as common across this unspecified subtype.
Peroxisomal disorder with defining brain and liver disease; retinal degeneration affects 80-99%. Cap excludes skeletal abnormalities (80-99%) and hearing loss (30-79%).
Gastrin-secreting neuroendocrine tumor and severe acid-mediated peptic disease define the syndrome; other endocrine tumors are minority associations.
TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma; compressive progressive visual loss and bone loss each annotated 30-79%; headache and palpitations do not establish organ damage.
Functioning pituitary gonadotroph tumor; compressive visual impairment and visual field defects occur in 30-79%. Other neurologic complications are occasional.
Pituitary gland tumour; chiasmal compression causes bitemporal hemianopia and progressive visual loss, annotated at 30-79%. These manifestations localize to the CNS visual pathway.
audit_reason: Replace ocular with neurologic: the characteristic bitemporal visual loss reflects optic-chiasm compression, damaging the CNS visual pathway rather than the eye.

basis: Rathke pouch cyst causes obligatory hypopituitarism; visual loss and bitemporal hemianopia occur in 30-79%, supporting ocular involvement.
Pituitary cysts with hypopituitarism; compressive visual impairment occurs in 30-79%. Avascular necrosis is not established as direct cyst damage.
Defined by pituitary hormone deficiency associated with empty sella; headache does not establish brain damage, and visual impairment is below 30%.
Ischemic pituitary necrosis causes hormone deficiencies. Anemia and visual-field defects are annotated 30-79%, but direct blood-organ or ocular injury is not established.

decisions.haematologic: none: normochromic anemia is annotated 30-79%, but does not establish direct marrow or blood-cell injury from pituitary necrosis.
decisions.ocular: none: visual-field defects are annotated 30-79%, but pituitary or chiasmal dysfunction does not establish direct injury to the eye or optic nerve.

basis: Congenital structural abnormality of the esophagus; aspiration pneumonia is a separately diagnosed complication.
Infantile interstitial lung disease; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Idiopathic inflammation and fibrosis of lung interstitium; infection or autoimmune disease is not required.
Recurrent subcutaneous and intestinal submucosal edema define HAE. Transient airway edema is excluded from involved; bradykinin excess alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
audit_reason: Add gastrointestinal to primary: recurrent bowel submucosal edema causing abdominal attacks is a defining disease manifestation. The exclusion of transient findings from involved does not remove a defining primary site.

basis: Recurrent subcutaneous edema with acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency defines the supplied concept; transient gut and airway edema excluded.
Familial thoracic aortic disease; iris morphology and cutis marmorata do not establish functional damage; neurologic complications occur in a minority.
Congenital connective-tissue bands join the eyelids and restrict eye opening.
Congenital lacrimal dysfunction; associated corneal and eyelid abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Congenital anterior segment dysgenesis involving the iris, pupil and anterior chamber; this concept is the ocular anomaly.
Congenital corneal abnormality causing corneal clouding.
Congenital iris and drainage-angle dysgenesis with glaucoma; associated neurofibromatosis is a separate disease.
Persistent fetal vitreous and hyaloid tissue cause cataract, microphthalmia and retinal traction within the eye.
HPO reports meningitis/cranial paralysis and arthritis each in 30-79%; cardiac and ocular disease are 5-29%; transient erythema does not qualify.
Borrelia infection; thrombocytopenia in 80-99% and anemia in 30-79%; hepatic injury with elevated transaminases and jaundice in 30-79%.
Absent respiratory cilia cause chronic airway disease. Chronic otitis is described as typical lifelong involvement, supporting >=30% with persistent ear inflammation; exact frequency is unavailable.

decisions.otologic: involved: typical lifelong chronic otitis supports common (approximately >=30%) persistent ear inflammation associated with ciliary dysfunction, rather than transient symptoms.

basis: Esophageal peristalsis and sphincter relaxation are impaired; bronchitis is a separate associated diagnosis and aspiration pneumonia occurs in 5-29%.
Congenital absence of one kidney and its ureter; both belong to the renal axis.
Congenital nephron deficit and small kidneys; hypertension and urinary infections are occasional.
Abnormal kidney development with common nephron, tubular and urinary functional abnormalities; hypertension and infections are minority complications.
Congenital renal calyceal malformation; urinary infections and stones are separately diagnosed complications.
Congenital urethral obstruction damages the urinary tract, all within renal; pulmonary hypoplasia is occasional and infections are separate complications.
Immune-mediated necrotizing GN with small-vessel vasculitis in 80-99%; pulmonary hemorrhage is <30%; broad skin and respiratory annotations do not establish common direct injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis is intrinsic to the disease, including renal-limited vasculitis, and is annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Vitamin D resistance causes hypocalcemia and rickets; alopecia and premature tooth loss each occur in 30-79%; kidney stones are separate and may reflect treatment.
Renal tubular aldosterone resistance causes salt wasting, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis; urinary infection is an underlying trigger rather than this disorder itself.
Abnormal development and impaired renal tissue formation in one kidney define the disease.
Abnormal, incomplete development of both kidneys; no other organ involvement established across the concept.
Congenital unilateral enlargement of renal calyces; confined to the kidney.
Congenital bilateral enlargement of renal calyces.
Severe skeletal ossification disorder; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99% and causes profound respiratory impairment.
Steroid-sensitive idiopathic nephrotic syndrome is an immune-mediated podocytopathy; focal segmental sclerosis directly damages renal glomeruli.
Minimal-change nephrotic syndrome is an immune-mediated glomerular podocyte disorder.
Immune-mediated steroid-sensitive glomerular disease with nephrotic syndrome and diffuse mesangial proliferation.
Familial nephrotic syndrome with a defined glomerular lesion; immune causation is not established.
Familial steroid-resistant nephrotic disease affects glomerular filtration; minimal-change morphology alone does not establish an immune mechanism in this inherited form.
Familial nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis is a renal glomerular disorder; immune causation is not established.
Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with focal segmental glomerular scarring; an immune mechanism is not established for all idiopathic cases.
Glomerular disease defined by nephrotic syndrome and diffuse mesangial sclerosis; an immune mechanism is not established.
Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define this subtype; proptosis alone is not ocular damage, and hearing loss occurs in 5-29%.
Chiari malformation 80-99%; structural airway defects and auditory canal atresia 30-79%. Proptosis alone is not eye damage; visual loss 5-29%.
Craniosynostosis/limb defects; Chiari/aqueduct stenosis, airway malacia and ear-canal stenosis each occur in 80-99%; proptosis alone need not injure the eye.
Severe skeletal dysplasia with short ribs and polydactyly; pulmonary hypoplasia affects most and causes lethal respiratory insufficiency.
Fibrous dysplasia directly replaces normal bone in a single skeletal site.
Skeletal dysplasia caused by an inborn sulfation metabolic defect; vertebral, epiphyseal and metaphyseal abnormalities define the disease.
Vertebral and epiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with disproportionate short stature, joint restriction and premature osteoarthritis.
Pancreatic adenoma with digestive-system neoplasm ancestry; endocrine origin or hormone dysfunction is not specified.
Severe skeletal dysplasia; thoracic restriction causes pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory failure in most affected neonates.
Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the ulna with associated upper-limb skeletal and joint abnormalities.
Congenital partial or complete absence of the radius, usually with associated hand skeletal abnormalities.
Congenital fibular deficiency with common limb deformities and gait impairment; renal, ocular, cardiac and intellectual abnormalities occur in only 1-4%.
Nonsyndromic congenital formation of an additional developed postaxial digit.
Congenital rudimentary supernumerary digit affecting limb development.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by vertebral and epimetaphyseal abnormalities, joint laxity and progressive spinal malalignment.
Distal phalangeal hypoplasia or absence and nail hypoplasia or absence define the disorder; absent fingernails occur in 80-99%.
Congenital shortening of metacarpals and phalanges; cardiac involvement belongs to a specific subtype.
Absent middle phalanges and duplicated thumb phalanx with defining nail dysplasia.
Congenital shortening and malformation of finger and toe phalanges define this skeletal disorder.
Genetic bone development disorder with multiple metaphyseal enchondromas; lesions occupy skeletal tissue despite the benign course.
Lysosomal storage disease; developmental delay and dysostosis 80-99%, cataracts 30-79%. Hearing impairment 30-79% omitted by cap; hepatosplenomegaly 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS storage disease causes developmental delay in 80-99% and seizures in 30-79%; the defining disorder is metabolic.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: dysostosis multiplex documents direct skeletal disease in 80-99%, accompanying the defining metabolic storage disorder.

basis: Lysosomal storage; developmental delay, dysostosis multiplex and hepatosplenomegaly/ascites each 30-79%. Cataract and hearing loss also 30-79%, omitted under cap; renal findings 5-29%.
Umbrella of FGFR3-related skeletal dysplasias; neurologic, hearing and respiratory complications are not shared across most subtypes.
Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias; cardiac, ocular, skin and hearing abnormalities vary by subtype and are not established across most patients.
Short-rib skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and thoracic respiratory insufficiency are common (>30%); renal and other anomalies vary by subtype.
Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias involving vertebral development; neurologic and immune abnormalities belong to selected subtypes.
Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias affecting distal limb development; endocrine and visceral abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Inherited skeletal dysplasia with shortening and deformity of limb bones; no common extraskeletal organ damage across the group.
Umbrella skeletal dysplasia defined by bowed bones; extraskeletal disease is not shared across the group.
Cartilage stippling and skeletal dysplasia define this umbrella. Ichthyosis and intellectual disability vary by subtype and are not established across most patients.

decisions.dermatologic: none: despite the broad definition mentioning ichthyosis, skin disease is subtype-dependent and does not characterize most patients across the umbrella.

basis: Umbrella skeletal dysplasia defined by neonatal osteosclerosis; additional organ disease is subtype-specific.
Umbrella of skeletal disorders characterized by bone resorption; renal, neurologic and other manifestations are subtype-specific.
Umbrella concept for isolated limb hypoplasia or absence; syndromic findings in individual children do not generalize across the group.
Congenital structural abnormalities of kidneys and urinary tract.
Disease of renal glomeruli; the umbrella includes immune and nonimmune causes.
Autoimmune disease; nephritis, cytopenias/hemolysis and inflammatory skin lesions each 30-79%. Pleural and pericardial involvement omitted under cap.
Immune-complex vasculitis; cutaneous vasculitis ~90%, neuropathy ~40-60%; renal involvement near 30% omitted at cap. Associated hepatitis is separate.
Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis with defining cutaneous vasculitic purpura. Renal and nerve injury are not established at >=30% specifically for type III.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: defining purpura represents cutaneous small-vessel inflammation and injury, rather than an incidental transient rash.

basis: Monoclonal heavy-chain deposition disorder associated with a plasma-cell clone; deposition nephropathy is its defining clinical manifestation.
Clonal immunoglobulin deposition disorder; renal deposits cause proteinuria or impaired kidney function in nearly all patients. Other organ dysfunction is less common.

decisions.renal: involved: damaging renal deposition occurs in nearly all patients; it is an organ manifestation of the underlying monoclonal immunoglobulin disorder.

basis: Monoclonal light-chain deposition arising from a plasma-cell disorder; renal deposition and dysfunction define LCDD. Symptomatic cardiac and hepatic disease are rare.
Inherited apoA-I amyloid nephropathy; hepatic deposition often preserves function. Function-impairing hepatic, cardiac and nerve involvement varies by variant without an established >=30% frequency.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic amyloid deposits do not necessarily impair function; clinically damaging liver involvement in >=30% is not established.

basis: Inherited amyloid protein-metabolism disorder prominently damages kidneys; symptomatic gastrointestinal deposition affects roughly one-third or more. Hepatic deposits may spare function.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary lysozyme amyloidosis is a disorder of protein metabolism with pathological amyloid accumulation.

basis: Hereditary fibrinogen protein-folding/storage disorder causing predominantly glomerular amyloid deposition and renal failure; clinically damaging extrarenal involvement is uncommon.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary fibrinogen amyloidosis is an inherited disorder of protein folding and deposition, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Childhood immune-mediated inflammatory skeletal myopathy; no additional directly damaged organ is established at >=30%.
Immune-mediated periarticular inflammation causes proximal stiffness and pain; muscle destruction is absent; associated giant cell arteritis is separate.
Complement-mediated glomerular injury defines disease. Retinal deposits often do not impair vision and do not justify an ocular label.
Microvascular thrombosis with hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia defines TMA; direct renal microangiopathic injury is common (>30%). Neurologic injury varies by subtype.
Complement factor H dysfunction causes immune-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy with hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury.
Anti-factor H autoantibodies cause complement-mediated microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury; extrarenal organ damage is a minority complication.
Autoimmune thrombotic microangiopathy with hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; neurologic injury 30-79%. Renal findings and intestinal ischemia (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Inherited cystic kidney disease; extrarenal manifestations are not consistent across this umbrella.
Nephronophthisis causes renal tubulointerstitial degeneration; the peptide-metabolism ancestor alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Inherited renal tubular amino-acid transport defect causing cystine wasting and urinary stone formation.
Inherited amino-acid transport disorder affecting renal tubular cystine reabsorption and causing urinary cystine stones; intestinal transport changes do not cause substantial gut damage.
Innate immune dysregulation defines this umbrella; no additional damaged organ is consistently shared across its diverse subtypes.
Pediatric Castleman disease is predominantly unicentric lymphoid proliferation; infection or immune-mediated disease is not established across this umbrella.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: predominantly unicentric pediatric disease is not necessarily infectious, autoimmune or immune-mediated; lymphoid proliferation alone does not qualify.

basis: Localized lymphoid-cell proliferation defines unicentric Castleman disease; it is not inherently lymphoma, infection, immunodeficiency or an immune-mediated disease.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: localized Castleman disease is a lymphoproliferative disorder; immune-cell proliferation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.

basis: HHV8-associated inflammatory lymphoproliferation; pulmonary interstitial involvement occurs in approximately 30-50%. Hepatomegaly alone does not demonstrate hepatic damage.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary interstitial inflammation/infiltration occurs in roughly 30-50% of HHV8-associated MCD and is explicitly described in the supplied definition.

basis: Organ-unspecified developmental umbrella; no individual organ axis can be assigned across most constituent disorders.
Forebrain malformation; diabetes insipidus, cleft palate and sensorineural hearing loss each 30-79%. Aspiration pneumonia is separate; nonspecific eye anomalies do not prove impairment.
Forebrain malformation with eye abnormalities (80-99%), hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction (~70% in classic HPE), and median cleft upper lip (30-79%). Aspiration pneumonia is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: median cleft upper lip is a direct structural oral malformation annotated in 30-79%; feeding symptoms alone would not establish GI damage.

basis: Congenital urethral malformation defines disease; pelvic girdle bone abnormalities are frequent (30–79%). Urethra and associated reflux are within the renal axis.
Congenital transverse absence of arm structures is a limb skeletal malformation.
Type 1 is confined to the supraglottic interarytenoid larynx above the vocal folds; the definition does not establish esophageal extension.
Congenital cleft of the laryngeal/postcricoid partition between airway and esophagus; swallowing dysfunction is characteristic.
Congenital cleft involves the laryngeal/tracheal and esophageal partition, causing severe swallowing dysfunction and pulmonary damage.
Airway-esophageal cleft; vertebral defects 80-99% and cardiac septal defects 30-79%. Motor-neuron anomalies 30-79% omitted at cap; unspecified spleen morphology does not establish dysfunction.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the syndrome; strabismus and frontal hair loss each occur in 30-79%; facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
Intellectual disability syndrome; atrial septal defects and nail/hair dystrophy are frequent (30-79%); macroglossia alone does not establish GI damage.
Syndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay and frequent spasticity; ocular and anal abnormalities are occasional.
Syndromic intellectual disability and epilepsy directly define nervous system involvement.
Focal neurologic dystonia; structural mandibular and temporomandibular joint abnormalities are annotated in 30-79%. Dysphagia and dysphonia alone do not establish GI or airway damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: abnormal mandibular morphology and temporomandibular joint abnormalities in 30-79% support structural skeletal involvement beyond muscle spasms alone.

basis: Segmental dystonia causes eyelid and oromandibular spasms; these do not establish intrinsic eye or skeletal muscle damage.
Vertebral closure defect with spinal cord injury. Common bladder/bowel denervation is separately diagnosed; direct urinary or intestinal damage in >=30% is not established.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder is a separate diagnosis secondary to spinal denervation; intrinsic urinary tract injury in >=30% is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: neurogenic bowel is a separate diagnosis secondary to spinal denervation; common direct intestinal damage is not established.

basis: Congenital absence of the external ear and auditory canal with conductive hearing loss; secondary language delay does not imply brain damage.
Astrocytic tumour arising in the brain or spinal cord.
Congenital fusion of the humerus and ulna.
Pathologic ocular neovascularization obstructs aqueous outflow and damages vision; diabetes and vascular occlusions are underlying causes, not additional organs damaged by this glaucoma.
Intellectual disability and osteopoikilosis define the syndrome. Hyperpigmentation does not establish skin damage; renal abnormalities occur in <30%.
Defined by intellectual disability, epilepsy, anal and phalangeal anomalies; VSD occurs in 30-79%. Nail hypoplasia (80-99%) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Immune-mediated intestinal injury defines the group; endocrine and other systemic manifestations belong to particular subtypes.

Tumor originates in autonomic neuroendocrine paraganglia; nonsecretory status does not change its origin. Catecholamine-related HPO entries contradict the definition and cannot support additional axes.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: paraganglia are neuroendocrine organs; a nonfunctioning tumor retains its endocrine tissue of origin despite lacking catecholamine secretion.

basis: Immune-mediated lymphohistiocytic panniculitis directly affects subcutaneous fat. Systemic hemophagocytosis and hepatic injury are variable, without established frequency of at least 30%.
Central dopaminergic dysfunction causes rigidity, altered consciousness and dysautonomia; acidosis is acute systemic stress; rhabdomyolysis and kidney injury occur in 5-29%.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by cerebellar ataxia and neuropathy; ophthalmoplegia is neurologic. Hashimoto thyroiditis is a separate autoimmune diagnosis.
Umbrella of predominantly cerebellar neurodegenerative disorders; occasional additional signs remain neurological.
Hereditary cerebellar degeneration with neurologic manifestations across the included subtypes.
Absent calvarial bones and scalp define disease. HPO reports cerebellar hypoplasia 80-99% and migration defects 30-79%, despite usually preserved CNS in definition.
Craniosynostosis and syndactyly define this skeletal malformation umbrella; additional organ damage varies among subtypes.
Skeletal dysplasia and developmental disability define disease; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Hormone resistance varies by subtype; nail morphology alone does not establish damage.
Defined as hepatic porphyria with a heme-synthesis defect and bullous skin injury; anemia and corneal injury occur in 5-29%; tooth pigmentation is non-damaging.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the definition explicitly identifies hepatic porphyria, locating the metabolic disease in the liver; this does not imply common hepatic failure.

basis: Acute adrenal steroid failure has diverse causes. The autoimmune HPO annotation does not establish an immune mechanism for this umbrella; hypotension and prerenal dysfunction are secondary.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: autoimmunity is an underlying etiology, not a defining mechanism of acute adrenal insufficiency; the 80-99% annotation is not applicable across its diverse causes.

basis: Loss of functional small intestine causes intestinal failure and malabsorption; other documented organ complications are uncommon or treatment-related.
Persistent cutaneous capillary malformation defines the disease; retinal vascular malformations occur in only 5-29%.
Congenital tracheal cartilage weakness causes airway collapse; extrapulmonary abnormalities are generally below 30%.
Unbalanced transfusion through placental vascular anastomoses defines the disorder; fetal blood-volume imbalance supports vascular and blood axes, without an immune mechanism.
Progressive language impairment results from cerebral neurodegeneration.
Congenital positioning anomaly of the heart.
Congenital failure of the aortic valve to open causes cardiac outflow obstruction and heart failure.
Congenital structural dysfunction of the aortic valve causing regurgitation.
Immune-mediated skin and oral mucosal necrosis define disease; ocular surface dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Airway abnormalities reported in 30-79% are omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: destruction of mucous membranes is explicitly defining, and oral mucosal blistering is a characteristic manifestation affecting the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Congenital absence of the tricuspid valve.
Congenital narrowing of the tricuspid valve defines the disease; regurgitation and heart failure remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital tricuspid valve malformation with associated structural heart defects.
Congenital accessory tissue of the tricuspid valve; associated cardiac malformations remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital mitral valve malformation causing stenosis and/or regurgitation.
Congenital structural malformation of the mitral valve.
Congenital structural malformation of the mitral valve.
Congenital cardiac malformations with a single functional ventricle.
Structural dilatation or aneurysm of the ascending aorta.
Fetal arterial duct closure causes right-heart pressure overload and structural cardiac changes; respiratory distress alone does not establish lung injury.
Congenital or hereditary deficiency of pituitary hormones; no additional organ damage established across the umbrella.
Congenital dilatation of a coronary artery; no underlying inflammatory disease.
Congenital pituitary malformation with hormone deficiencies; neurologic and optic abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Developmental anomaly of the superior vena cava or related systemic veins.
Congenital structural abnormality of the inferior vena cava.

Autoimmune infiltration of the pituitary causes endocrine deficiencies; CNS ancestry does not establish separate neurologic damage.
Congenital malformation of a vein; hepatic parenchymal injury is not established.

decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive visual-field defects in 30-79% reflect compression of the optic chiasm, a central nervous system structure.
decisions.ocular: none: the field loss is caused by chiasmal compression; direct injury to the eye or prechiasmal optic nerve is not established.

Defining pectoral muscle and hand malformations accompany renal or urinary tract developmental anomalies; reproductive findings have no axis.

Isolated penile developmental anomaly; no endocrine dysfunction or urinary tract disease established.

Primary ovarian insufficiency entails loss of gonadal endocrine function; syndromic findings are not shared across this umbrella.
Ectopic thyroid causes congenital hypothyroidism; severe intellectual disability and developmental delay are reported in 30-79%.
Absent thyroid causes congenital hypothyroidism; developmental delay and severe intellectual disability reported in 30-79%, especially before treatment.
Thyroid hormone deficiency caused by transferred maternal TSH-receptor blocking antibodies; associated transient symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Congenital thyroid hormone deficiency; neurodevelopmental delay and abnormal epiphyseal development each occur in 30-79%.
Congenital absence of one thyroid lobe, usually asymptomatic. Supplied hypothyroid phenotypes do not establish common neurologic damage in hemiagenesis itself.
Congenital thyroid underdevelopment causes permanent hypothyroidism; developmental delay and intellectual disability occur in 30-79% per HPO.
Levocardia with visceral situs inversus is commonly associated with structural congenital heart defects; reversed visceral position alone does not establish organ damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: characteristic hypo/hyperpigmentation does not establish skin injury or loss of function.

basis: Congenital heart defects, particularly VSD, are principal organ manifestations. Skeletal and CNS anomalies are variable, with no established frequency of substantial damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: cloverleaf skull and clinodactyly are variable reported anomalies; neither a defining skeletal disorder nor damaging involvement in at least 30% is established.

basis: Intellectual disability, skeletal/joint and urinary anomalies characterize the syndrome; corneal opacity occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac anomaly frequency is not established.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac malformations affect approximately half or more of reported patients and are intrinsic developmental manifestations.

basis: Intellectual disability, developmental delay and metopic craniosynostosis define the syndrome; cardiac and intestinal anomalies lack evidence of >=30% frequency.

The supplied definition includes developmental disability, congenital cardiac abnormalities and renal hypoplasia among the syndrome's defining structural features.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital cardiac abnormalities, including patent ductus arteriosus, are explicitly part of the defining phenotype.
decisions.renal: primary: renal hypoplasia is explicitly included in the syndrome definition; genital abnormalities alone would not establish this axis.

basis: Psychomotor and language delay and seizures define the syndrome; reported eye abnormalities lack evidence of involvement in at least 30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: structural GI and palatal anomalies are described as common, supporting approximately 30% or more; no precise frequency is available.

basis: Macroglossia, persistent hyperinsulinism and lateralized skeletal/soft-tissue overgrowth are cardinal BWS criteria. Tumour predisposition adds no organ.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized overgrowth involving skeletal muscle and bone is a cardinal Beckwith-Wiedemann diagnostic criterion.

basis: Neurodevelopmental and orthopedic disease define it; heart and urinary anomalies each 30–79%. Cap excludes frequent balding; unspecified eye findings lack damage detail.

audit_reason: Add renal involvement: hypospadias is a congenital urethral malformation, explicitly covered by renal, and occurs in 30-79% as part of this syndrome.

basis: Developmental/intellectual impairment and joint contractures are defining; other reported organ anomalies lack evidence of frequency >=30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: principal craniofacial skeletal malformations, including brachy/plagiocephaly and micrognathia, are explicitly defining features.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the record does not establish cutaneous origin or independent skin damage; hemangiomas are assigned to their vascular tissue of origin.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: craniosynostosis and other skeletal defects depend on deletion extent; the evidence does not establish a qualifying frequency across distal 7p deletions.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate affects roughly one-third and directly represents oral structural malformation; frequency is near the threshold.

basis: Developmental delay and intellectual disability occur in 30-79%. Cafe-au-lait spots do not impair skin function; cardiac and endocrine abnormalities are occasional.

The definition specifies no intrinsic phenotype; any unmasked recessive disorder would be a separate disease. No organ damage is established.

Congenital distal joint contractures and muscle disease define the umbrella; additional organs belong to particular subtypes.

Light-triggered mast-cell hypersensitivity causes cutaneous urticaria; wheezing, edema, dizziness and nausea are transient manifestations, not sustained organ damage.
Inherited skeletal muscle disease with mechanically triggered contractions, hypertrophy and weakness.
Progressive skeletal myopathy with reducing bodies; respiratory muscle weakness alone does not establish direct lung disease.
Structural congenital skeletal myopathy; global developmental delay reported in 80-99% supports additional neurodevelopmental involvement.

Congenital posterior fossa cerebrospinal fluid space malformation.

Endocrine pancreatic tumor with defining WDHA syndrome: sustained intestinal secretory dysfunction, reduced gastric acid secretion and hypokalemia.

basis: Lymphoid malignancy arising in thyroid. Airway obstruction and dysphagia reflect compression; common intrinsic airway or gastrointestinal damage is not established.

Thymic endocrine-cell neoplasm; vena cava abnormalities and collateral veins are frequent (30-79% HPO), supporting tumor-related venous obstruction. Cough alone adds no pulmonary axis.

basis: Osteonecrosis of the carpal lunate causes collapse and wrist dysfunction; local avascular necrosis does not establish a separate vascular disorder.

Clear cell sarcoma arising in tendons and aponeuroses; melanocytic differentiation does not establish a skin origin.

Persistent traumatic brain injury with dementia and other neurologic dysfunction.

basis: Defining skeletal dysplasia with mesomelic shortening. Renal, cardiac and dental abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); genital abnormalities have no axis.

Congenital multicystic dysplasia leaves one kidney structurally abnormal and nonfunctional.
Both kidneys are dysplastic and nonfunctional; fetal anuria causes anhydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia in most untreated pregnancies with this lethal bilateral form.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is an integral developmental consequence of fetal anuria/anhydramnios in most cases (>30%), rather than a later unrelated risk.

basis: Multiloculated cystic lesion of the kidney.
Renal tubular maldevelopment; pulmonary hypoplasia and fixed limb contractures are defining Potter-sequence consequences of persistent oligohydramnios.
Renal tubular developmental failure defines the disease; drug causation does not change its affected organ.
Collapsing glomerular injury causes steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; an immune mechanism is not established by this designation.
ANCA-mediated glomerular inflammation directly damages kidneys; extrarenal disease varies and is not established as common for this renal concept.
Immune-mediated necrotizing glomerulonephritis despite absent ANCA; extrarenal manifestations are less frequent and not established at 30%.
Immune-mediated glomerular disease with fibrillary immunoglobulin deposits causing proteinuria and renal insufficiency.
Glomerular immunoglobulin microtubular deposition causes renal injury; associated hematologic malignancy is a separate disease.
PTH resistance causes calcium-phosphate dysregulation despite normal renal function; skeletal abnormalities vary across subtypes.
Congenital narrowing of renal arteries is vascular disease; common renal parenchymal injury or functional loss is not established.
Defective peripheral thyroid hormone action; neurologic damage varies substantially across constituent disorders.
Respiratory-system malformation umbrella; additional skeletal involvement depends on the specific thoracic subtype.
Congenital pulmonary arterial absence; definition describes typical lung tissue changes, with pulmonary imaging abnormalities in 30-79%.
Defined as infection involving the nervous system; other organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Developmental malformations of the brain or spinal cord; other organ abnormalities vary across subtypes.
Major forms involve testicular endocrine differentiation, androgen synthesis or androgen action; additional organ damage is subtype-specific.

basis: Congenital hereditary cerebellar dysfunction; additional organ involvement is not established across the umbrella.
Umbrella of metabolic disorders defined by cerebellar dysfunction; additional organ damage varies among subtypes.

Cerebellar dysfunction defines this umbrella; hepatic, vestibular and metabolic abnormalities belong to particular subtypes.

Sex-chromosome anomaly umbrella includes major disorders with gonadal endocrine dysfunction; additional organ abnormalities vary substantially by subtype.

Dystonia combined with another neurologic movement disorder; other organ involvement is not shared across the umbrella.
Joint hypermobility and skin hyperextensibility/fragility define the group; severe vascular or ocular disease is subtype-specific.
Infection directly inflames and damages brain tissue; no additional organ involvement is common across this umbrella.
Postinfectious brain inflammation, commonly mediated by an immune response; no additional organ injury defines the umbrella.
Epilepsy syndrome defined by neonatal onset; no other organ involvement is shared across the subtypes.
Epilepsy syndrome beginning in infancy; no additional organ involvement applies across the group.

Progressive nervous system degeneration with myoclonic and tonic-clonic seizures; metabolic and extracerebral features vary by subtype.
Clonal myeloid proliferation in bone marrow; thrombosis and extramedullary organ damage are not uniformly common across this umbrella.
Clonal myeloid blood and marrow neoplasms with dysplastic and proliferative features.
Hematopoietic dendritic-cell neoplasm; immune-cell origin alone does not establish lymphoma or immune-mediated disease. Other sites vary by subtype.
Lymphoid proliferative disease associated with immunodeficiency; no additional organ is consistently affected across the group.
Inherited loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue with disordered adipose metabolism; additional organ disease varies across subtypes.

decisions.hepatic: none: steatosis commonly exceeds 30%, but function-impairing hepatic injury at that frequency is not established; associated steatotic liver disease is separately diagnosed.

basis: Acquired loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue is a metabolic and skin disorder. Diabetes and fatty liver are separately diagnosed associated diseases.
Inherited disorders of erythropoiesis with sideroblasts and anemia; syndromic manifestations and iron-related organ damage are not universal across this umbrella.
Inherited red-cell membrane disorders causing haemolysis; additional organ damage is not established across the umbrella.

Congenital absence or severe underdevelopment of lung tissue; associated anomalies are not established as common.
Inherited megaloblastic anemia encompassing metabolic defects such as orotic aciduria and thiamine transport deficiency; additional organ involvement varies by subtype.
Defined by increased absolute red blood cell mass; organs causing secondary erythrocytosis are not damaged by erythrocytosis itself.
Inherited platelet alpha-granule disorders cause thrombocytopenia and impaired haemostasis; no common extra-haematologic damage established across subtypes.
Defined as disease of skeletal muscle tissue; additional organ involvement is not shared across this umbrella.
Progressive skeletal-muscle degeneration defines the group; cardiac disease varies by subtype, and respiratory muscle weakness remains muscle involvement.
Immune-mediated skeletal muscle disease; interstitial lung disease causes direct pulmonary damage in approximately 30-40% overall, with substantial subtype variation.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: interstitial lung disease affects approximately 30-40% across major idiopathic inflammatory myopathy cohorts, meeting the threshold despite subtype variation.

basis: Metabolic enzyme deficiencies directly cause skeletal muscle dysfunction; additional organ disease varies by subtype.
Impaired neuromuscular junction transmission; immune mechanisms do not apply across inherited, toxic and autoimmune forms.
Inherited peripheral nerve disease; additional organ damage varies by subtype and is not shared across the umbrella.
