Acquired disease of motor neurons; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.

Group defined by hypoplasia, atrophy and degeneration of the cerebellum and pons; other organ manifestations vary by subtype.
Lysosomal lipid storage affecting the brain with dementia; additional organ damage varies across subtypes.
Congenital eyelid and ocular malformation; systemic features of Fraser syndrome do not apply across this umbrella.

Congenital eversion of the eyelid; syndromic abnormalities are not shared across the umbrella.

Benign tumor arising in eyelid epidermis; both skin and eyelids are explicitly covered axes.
Benign melanocytic tumor arising in eyelid skin; both eyelid and cutaneous sites are explicit.

basis: Benign or malignant neoplasm arising in the conjunctiva.
Dystrophies affecting the corneal epithelium, basement membrane and superficial stroma.
Inherited dystrophies with lesions of the corneal stroma.
Corneal dystrophies affecting the endothelium and Descemet membrane.
Inherited degeneration of the retinal macula; systemic abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Inherited disease of the vitreous and retina; neurologic ancestry alone does not establish extraocular nervous system damage.
Congenital vitreous and retinal developmental disease; extraocular abnormalities are not shared across the umbrella.
Degeneration of vitreous and retina; systemic manifestations of particular syndromic subtypes do not apply throughout this umbrella.
Hereditary optic nerve disease; extraocular manifestations are subtype-specific and do not apply across this umbrella.
Primary disorder of ocular alignment; no systemic muscle or neurologic disease is specified.
Lesions of central supranuclear pathways impair gaze control; direct ocular tissue damage is not established.

Congenital structural malformation of the tricuspid valve; additional organ injury is not shared across the group.
Congenital structural defects of the atrial and ventricular septa and atrioventricular valves.
Congenital hypoplasia of right-sided cardiac structures and pulmonary arteries; reduced pulmonary blood flow does not establish lung damage.
Congenital structural abnormalities of the aorta and other great vessels.

Congenital abnormal artery-to-vein connection; skin ulceration and other secondary organ damage are not established in at least 30%.
Cardiac and skeletal abnormalities characterize this umbrella; intellectual disability affects ~6-23% in typical Noonan syndrome, with higher rates in selected related syndromes.

Angelman neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual disability and seizures; pigmentation and facial features do not establish other organ damage.

Focal epilepsy syndrome; autonomic seizure manifestations do not establish damage to other organs.
Occipital focal epilepsy; visual symptoms arise from cortical seizures rather than eye disease.
Genetic focal epilepsy affects cerebral function; seizure auras do not establish separate ocular or otologic damage.
Myeloid neoplasm of blood and marrow with persistent monocytosis and myelodysplasia; no common extrahematologic organ damage established.

Acute malignancy of marrow myeloid cells; no common direct extramedullary organ damage is established.
Acute leukemia involving hematopoietic blasts and bone marrow; no additional organ involvement established as common.
Acute leukemia defined by mixed-lineage hematopoietic blasts; the lymphoma ancestor does not establish a separate lymphoma or bone lesion.
Mature B-cell lymphoma arising in the mediastinum; lymphoid-cell malignancy supports both mechanism axes. Mediastinal location alone does not establish lung or cardiac invasion.

Congenital anterior segment dysgenesis involving the cornea and iris.
