Iridocorneal endothelial disease affecting iris and cornea; secondary glaucoma remains within the ocular axis.
Progressive iris atrophy and corneal endothelial disease; associated glaucoma remains within the ocular axis.
Early-onset lens opacities along the sutures define an isolated ocular disorder.
Early-onset opacity of the anterior portion of the ocular lens.
Hereditary lens opacities cause reduced visual acuity and may require lens extraction.
Early-onset opacity of the lens nucleus; nonsyndromic cataract umbrella.
Nonsyndromic partial cataract affects the ocular lens.
Early posterior polar lens opacity defines the disease; the broader CRYAB spectrum does not establish myopathy or cardiomyopathy in this cataract subtype.
Early-onset nonsyndromic cataract affecting a zone of the lens.
Cerebellar neurodegeneration defines the umbrella; retinal and optic-nerve damage belong to particular subtypes rather than most patients.
Macular retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy with patterned lipofuscin accumulation and retinal degeneration.
Retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy causes slowly progressive visual loss; disease is confined to the ocular axis.
Pattern dystrophy directly affects the retinal pigment epithelium and macula.
Poorly defined adult non-neuronopathic sphingolipid storage disorder; frequencies of hepatic, splenic or pulmonary dysfunction are insufficiently established.
Congenital transposition of the great arteries with aortic coarctation.
Congenital ventricular outflow and septal malformation; pulmonary stenosis here affects cardiac outflow, not lung tissue.
Congenital ventricular and great-artery malformation with a subpulmonary ventricular septal defect.
Congenital cardiac outflow-tract and ventricular septal malformation; no additional organ disease is specified.
Congenital pulmonary valve, ventricular septal and ductal abnormalities are all cardiovascular; pulmonary valve refers to the heart.
Congenital abnormal origin of a pulmonary artery from the ductus arteriosus; pulmonary arteries belong to the vascular axis.
Congenital anomalous pulmonary artery origin with cardiac shunting and failure; respiratory symptoms do not establish direct lung damage.
Fibromuscular obstruction below the aortic valve is a structural cardiac outflow disorder.
Congenital fixed narrowing of the left ventricular outflow tract below the aortic valve.
Congenital obstruction of the pulmonary heart valve; pulmonary refers to the valve rather than lung disease.
Congenital tricuspid chordal malformation causing impaired leaflet mobility and regurgitation.
Congenital tricuspid valve and papillary muscle malformation; possible hepatomegaly from congestion does not establish common hepatic damage.
Congenital mitral apparatus malformation obstructs ventricular inflow; pulmonary hypertension is cardiovascular.
Congenital mitral annular hypoplasia causes mitral stenosis; associated malformations also lie within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital obstructing tissue above the mitral valve; pulmonary edema is secondary to cardiac obstruction.
Congenital absence of mitral valve leaflets and supporting apparatus directly affects cardiac structure and function.
Congenital accessory mitral-valve structures; obstruction and valvular dysfunction remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital absence or severe hypoplasia of mitral valve leaflets causes mitral regurgitation.
Congenital left-sided cardiac and aortic obstruction defines the condition.
Congenital structural malformation of the mitral valve.
Congenital atrioventricular septal defect with left-sided cardiac outflow obstruction.
Congenital atrioventricular septal malformation with ventricular hypoplasia.
Congenital atrioventricular septal malformation associated with tetralogy of Fallot.
Congenital structural heart disease involving ventricular and atrioventricular valve anatomy.
Congenital abnormal vascular communication between the aorta and right ventricle.
Congenital abnormal communication between the aorta and left ventricle.
Congenital aneurysm of the ductus arteriosus. Respiratory symptoms do not establish common direct airway damage; rupture and embolism are complications.
Congenital vascular ring directly compresses trachea and oesophagus; airway dysfunction occurs in most and swallowing dysfunction in >30%.
Congenital structural anomaly of the aortic arch.
Developmental aortic arch diverticulum; usually asymptomatic, with airway or esophageal compression insufficiently common to add other axes.
Aortic arch vascular ring; defining tracheal and esophageal compression directly impairs breathing and swallowing.
Congenital anatomical abnormality of the aortic arch; associated compression is not universal.
An aberrant aortic arch artery compresses the esophagus, producing the defining swallowing dysfunction.
Congenital hypoplasia of a great artery; pulmonary artery anatomy belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital narrowing of pulmonary artery branches; the affected structures are blood vessels.
Congenital coronary artery malformation with an intramyocardial arterial course.
Congenital anomalous origin and interarterial course of a coronary artery; pulmonary artery proximity does not establish pulmonary disease.
Congenital stenosis or atresia of the coronary artery ostium.
Congenital abnormal course of a coronary artery within myocardium.
Congenital abnormality of coronary artery openings.
Congenital malposition of a coronary artery origin; no other organ damage is intrinsic.
Ventricular septal defect with aortic cusp prolapse and regurgitation defines this congenital heart disorder; dyspnea does not establish lung damage.
Congenital left ventricular-to-right atrial communication. Endocarditis is a separate infection; edema and crackles do not establish additional organ damage.
Congenital membrane divides the right atrium.
Congenital membrane divides the left atrium; pulmonary congestion is secondary to cardiac obstruction.
Congenital structural anomaly of the atrial appendages; associated heart malformations remain within the same axis.
Structural enlargement of the right atrial appendage; dyspnea does not establish intrinsic pulmonary disease.
Congenital enlargement of the left atrial appendage; embolic events and respiratory symptoms do not establish common additional organ damage.
Congenital atrial septal defect with left-to-right shunting; dyspnea does not establish lung damage.
Congenital coronary sinus atrial septal defect; anomalous pulmonary veins are cardiovascular, and neurologic complications are rare.
Atrial septal defect with frequent anomalous pulmonary venous return; these are cardiovascular abnormalities.
Congenital atrioventricular septal defect; associated valve and chamber abnormalities remain cardiovascular. Respiratory infections are separate.
Structural aneurysmal abnormality of the atrial septum.
Persistent atrial septal opening; embolic stroke is a minority complication and a separate disease.
Congenital anomalous systemic venous drainage to the left atrium; embolization is a risk, not established organ damage.
Congenital systemic venous connection causing a right-to-left shunt; hypoxemia does not establish lung injury, and brain abscess is a separate complication.
Congenital systemic venous anomaly with persistent left superior vena cava draining to the left atrium.
Congenital absence of a great vein is a cardiovascular structural disorder, even when asymptomatic.
Congenital anomalous course of the brachiocephalic vein; associated cardiac malformations remain within the same axis.
Congenital absence of a major systemic vein; associated cardiac abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Developmental narrowing of the coronary sinus, a cardiac venous structure.
Congenital atresia of the coronary venous drainage outlet.
Congenital abnormal connection of the inferior vena cava to the left-sided atrium.
Persistent embryonic valve at the inferior vena cava–right atrial junction.
Congenital anatomical anomaly of the inferior vena cava and azygos venous circulation.
Congenital narrowing of the inferior vena cava is a structural venous disorder.
Congenital interruption of the inferior vena cava is a structural venous abnormality.
Congenital misconnection of pulmonary veins; dyspnea and respiratory infections do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Congenital absence of the pericardium is a cardiovascular malformation; dyspnea does not establish pulmonary damage.
Congenital partial absence of the pericardium; possible cardiac herniation remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital pericardial cyst, usually asymptomatic; pulmonary symptoms and severe cardiac complications are uncommon.
Inherited pentose phosphate pathway enzyme deficiency causing red-cell dysfunction and hemolytic anemia.
Inherited purine-metabolism defect causes erythrocyte destruction. Hyperbilirubinemia reflects hemolysis; the definition excludes other tissue involvement.
Inherited unstable hemoglobin causes red-cell instability and hemolysis; no common direct extrahematologic damage is established.
Acquired von Willebrand factor dysfunction causes bleeding; associated cardiac disease and neoplasms are underlying conditions, not organs damaged by this syndrome.
Congenital eyelid abnormality that can turn eyelashes against the ocular surface.
Congenital eyelid tarsal malformation causing entropion and possible corneal injury; tarsus here is part of the eyelid.
Isolated congenital outward turning of the eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Congenital eyelid malformation with ectropion; exposure keratopathy remains within the ocular axis.
Congenital eyelid anomaly; eyelids and potential corneal exposure belong to the ocular axis.
Ovarian endocrine failure and skeletal abnormalities define phenotype; cardiac defects ~30-50%, hearing loss 30-79%. Renal anomalies omitted by cap.
Gonadal failure and skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; hearing loss and learning disability each 30-79%. Thyroiditis, hypertension and steatosis are separate diseases.
Developmental, dental and gonadal abnormalities define syndrome; radioulnar defects occur in 80-99%. Acne omitted at cap; unspecified renal morphology does not establish damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: abnormal teeth and deficient enamel explicitly characterize the syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; skeletal malformations and gonadal insufficiency each occur in 80-99%; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: radioulnar synostosis, elbow abnormalities and scoliosis occur in 80-99%; associated skeletal lesions rather than the defining neurodevelopmental phenotype.

basis: Ovarian failure and skeletal abnormalities define it; hearing impairment and specific learning disability each occur in 30-79%. Hypertension, thyroiditis and steatosis are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: specific learning disability is a neurodevelopmental manifestation annotated in 30-79%, distinct from the psychiatric and behavioral findings.

basis: A skeletal dysplasia within chondrodysplasia punctata, affecting bone development.
Ectodermal dysplasia; intellectual disability/seizures, aganglionic megacolon and vertebral abnormalities each occur in 80-99%; blepharophimosis omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability and seizures occur in 80-99%; the supplied classification establishes ectodermal disease as the primary site.

basis: Temporal-lobe seizures with hippocampal sclerosis and associated memory impairment; autonomic seizure symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Arthropathy affects joints; progeria-associated features elsewhere cannot be assigned to this joint-specific concept.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disease defined by optic neuropathy plus serious neurological abnormalities.
Pituitary GH excess and pathological skeletal overgrowth define gigantism; myocardial hypertrophy/cardiomyopathy is annotated in 80-99%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: excessive skeletal growth before epiphyseal closure defines gigantism; accelerated skeletal maturation and acral/jaw overgrowth support this axis.

basis: Molybdenum cofactor deficiency causes metabolic sulfite toxicity and destructive encephalopathy; lens dislocation is variable and not established here at >=30%.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy causing myotonia; potassium sensitivity does not itself establish a metabolic disorder.
Persistent skeletal muscle channelopathy with myotonia; potassium sensitivity does not establish an electrolyte metabolic disorder.
Skeletal-muscle channelopathy causing myotonia and painful contractions. Ocular paresis, dysphagia and hypothyroidism are occasional; potassium sensitivity is not a metabolic disorder.
Congenital myopathy and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; persistent ptosis affects eyelid function in 4/5. A single assessed septal defect does not establish common cardiac involvement.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ptosis in 4/5 represents impaired eyelid elevation from the congenital myopathy; eyelids are explicitly within the ocular axis.

basis: Nonpneumonic legionellosis; cough, myalgia and headache are transient symptoms without established lung, muscle or nervous system damage.
PSP-tau neurodegeneration; gaze palsy and rigidity are neurologic. Kyphoscoliosis is annotated at 30-79%, but direct skeletal pathology is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent kyphoscoliosis reflects abnormal neurologic posture; frequency alone does not establish direct skeletal damage.

basis: Congenital neuronal migration abnormality producing heterotopic bands within the brain.
Cerebral hemispheric overgrowth and cortical malformation cause epilepsy and developmental impairment. Cranial asymmetry alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Central autonomic hypoventilation and intestinal aganglionosis define syndrome; strabismus in 80-99% represents ocular alignment dysfunction. Hypoventilation does not establish lung injury.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus in 80-99% represents impaired ocular alignment and binocular function, supporting functional ocular involvement.

basis: Defined by ocular colobomas, sensorineural hearing loss and globodontia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Progressive epileptic encephalopathy; HPO reports optic atrophy in 3/3, supporting ocular damage despite the definition excluding neuro-ophthalmic findings.
Inherited cerebral small-vessel disease with destructive brain lesions and porencephalic cavities; no common extracerebral damage established across subtypes.
Defined by colonic adenomatous polyposis and a primary CNS tumor; pigmented fundus lesions do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Nipah infection with defining encephalitis. Respiratory distress occurs in 5-29%; frequent pharyngitis alone does not establish lasting airway damage.
Viral hemorrhagic disease with blood-cell abnormalities; vascular dysfunction with capillary leak occurs in 80-99%. Hepatic and renal abnormalities are listed at 5-29%.
Viral hemorrhagic disease with thrombocytopenia; endothelial dysfunction/capillary leak 80-99%; hepatocellular injury common (>30%). Multiorgan failure is confined to severe cases.
Systemic viral infection; HPO supports hepatocellular injury at 80-99%, kidney injury and bleeding dysfunction at 30-79%. Neurologic injury and shock are occasional.

decisions.haematologic: involved: abnormal bleeding and excessive bleeding after venipuncture are frequent (30-79%), supporting common haemostatic dysfunction despite lower frequencies of specific laboratory defects.
decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatocellular injury is very frequent (ALT elevation 80-99%); hepatic disease is organ involvement of the systemic infection rather than its defining primary location.

basis: Inherited metabolic disorder with recurrent muscle destruction; renal insufficiency reported in 30-79%, consistent with myoglobin toxicity. Transaminases may originate from muscle.
Progressive brainstem and white-matter degeneration defines disease; vomiting, eye-movement abnormalities and auditory evoked changes do not establish separate organ damage.
EIF2B1-related degeneration of cerebral white matter. Blindness is annotated at 5-29%; ovarian insufficiency lacks evidence of ≥30% prevalence across all patients.
Primary syrinx formation damages the spinal cord.
A spinal cord syrinx damages sensory, motor and autonomic pathways; weakness and dysphonia do not establish separate organ damage.
Fluid-filled cavity within spinal cord tissue; sensory and motor disturbances reflect cord injury rather than independent muscle disease.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma occupies marrow; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 40-60%. CNS involvement is below 30%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: direct leukemic occupation of the liver with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 40-60%; malignant infiltration qualifies without requiring hepatic failure.

basis: Precursor T-cell malignancy affects marrow and blood; supplied synonyms and ancestry include the lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma entity.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: the supplied concept encompasses precursor T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma; lymphoma explicitly requires this mechanism axis.

basis: Testicular germ cell tumour affects reproductive tissue; no endocrine involvement is established.
Thymic neuroendocrine epithelial malignancy belongs to the endocrine-neoplasm axis; carcinoma alone does not imply an immune mechanism.
Langerhans-cell neoplasm usually producing a destructive bone lesion; skin and lung are alternative sites without established ≥30% involvement.
Congenital cutaneous Langerhans-cell histiocytic proliferation; skin lesions define this usually self-resolving variant. Systemic damage is uncommon.
Langerhans-cell neoplasm with multifocal destructive bone lesions; supplied definition specifies unisystem disease, so classic pituitary and orbital manifestations are not assumed.
Langerhans-cell histiocytic neoplasm infiltrates and damages small airways and lung parenchyma.
Severe joint hypermobility and congenital dislocations with hyperextensible, fragile skin define arthrochalasia EDS; bruising does not establish a blood disorder.
Inherited parathyroid gland adenoma; common direct damage to additional organs is not established for this tumour concept.
Neonatal diabetes with transient remission; later diabetic complications are separate diseases.
Megakaryoblastic leukemia is a marrow and blood-cell malignancy; Down syndrome does not establish additional organ involvement by the leukemia.
Endogenous cortisol causes myopathy/amyotrophy (30-99%), skin atrophy and immunodeficiency (30-79% each); hypertension is a separate secondary diagnosis.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension (30-79%) is generally a separately diagnosed secondary condition; nonspecific cardiovascular annotations establish no additional direct injury.
decisions.infectious_immune: involved: endogenous cortisol directly suppresses immune function; immunodeficiency is annotated 30-79%, beyond merely an increased future infection risk.

basis: ACTH-driven cortisol excess causes muscle wasting/bone loss in roughly 50-80% and persistent dermal atrophy/easy bruising in over 50%; hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic cortisol excess directly causes dermal atrophy, fragility and striae; characteristic skin damage affects over 50%.

basis: Adrenal cortisol excess directly causes myopathy/bone loss in roughly 50-80% and persistent skin atrophy/bruising in roughly 50-80%. Separately diagnosed hypertension is excluded.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension affects roughly 70-85% but is a separately diagnosed secondary condition; other direct cardiovascular injury is not established in at least 30%.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: cortisol directly causes persistent dermal atrophy, fragility and striae in roughly 50-80%; these represent structural skin damage.

basis: Fatty-acid oxidation defect with cardiomyopathy explicitly represented in ancestry; weakness alone does not establish common structural muscle damage.
Spirillum minus infection characteristically causes recurrent inflammation and ulceration at the bite site (>30%); this is tissue injury, unlike the transient systemic rash.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: recurrent bite-site inflammation and ulceration are characteristic and common (>30%); ulceration is direct skin injury, independent of transient rash.

basis: Systemic Streptobacillus infection; inflammatory polyarthritis occurs in ~50% and can persist. Transient rash does not establish skin damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: inflammatory polyarthritis affects ~50% and may persist; this exceeds transient joint pain and supports direct joint involvement.

basis: Immune-mediated hypersensitivity pneumonitis from inhaled domestic antigens.
Ovarian germ cell malignancy is reproductive; germ cell origin and occasional hCG production do not establish endocrine gland disease.
Ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor of hormone-producing gonadal cells; estrogenic or androgenic manifestations establish its endocrine role.
Malignant neoplasm of ovarian granulosa cells, the endocrine compartment of the gonad; no particular metastatic organ meets the threshold.
Malignant ovarian tumor of endocrine Sertoli-Leydig sex cord-stromal cells; functional tumors produce androgen excess.
Malignancy of ovarian steroid-producing endocrine cells, usually with androgen excess; endocrine function distinguishes it from purely reproductive tumors.
Streptococcal infection with defining hypotensive shock; renal failure occurs in roughly 70% and ARDS in roughly 50%. Coagulopathy and hepatic injury omitted under cap.

decisions.haematologic: none under cap: coagulopathy occurs in roughly half; renal failure and ARDS take priority because of severe organ dysfunction.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: ARDS directly injures lungs in roughly 50%, meeting the frequency threshold and taking priority under the cap.

basis: Superantigen-mediated shock; AKI and thrombocytopenia each occur in >30%. Hepatic dysfunction omitted by cap; rash and GI symptoms are transient.
Donor immune cells injure skin and gut; hepatic injury is a major diagnostic and staging target. Transplantation triggers this distinct immune disease.
Immune attack with diagnostic skin and oral lesions; ocular sicca/corneal injury occurs in 30-79%. Frequent hepatic and pulmonary involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic oral mucosal lesions are diagnostic manifestations; mouth and salivary glands belong to this axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic lichenoid and sclerotic skin lesions are diagnostic manifestations; skin thickening is reported in 80-99%.

basis: Gestational trophoblastic lesion invading uterine myometrium; reproductive and obstetric tissues have no axis.
Gestational trophoblastic malignancy originates in reproductive or placental tissue outside the axes; metastatic sites are not defining organs.
Tumor originates in gestational trophoblast at the uterine implantation site; reproductive and placental tissues have no axis.
Recurrent alveolar hemorrhage damages lung; chronic blood-loss anemia is part of the defining diagnostic triad; immune causes are not universal.
Milk-induced pulmonary hypersensitivity with hemosiderosis and defining anemia; digestive bleeding is explicitly characteristic in the supplied definition, although no numeric frequency is given.

decisions.haematologic: primary: characteristic blood-loss/iron-deficiency anemia is a defining component of the pulmonary hemosiderosis syndrome.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: digestive bleeding is explicitly a defining manifestation in the supplied definition; it represents mucosal injury rather than a nonspecific symptom.

basis: Malignant tumour arising in lung or pleural tissues.
Malignant tumour arising in lung and pleura; aggressive behaviour does not establish common damage to other organs.
Malignant solid pleuropulmonary tumor arising in lung or pleura; aggressive behavior alone does not establish common distant organ involvement.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; chronic muscle atrophy from denervation and arrhythmia are each annotated frequent (30-79%).
Lower motor neuron disease causes chronic denervation. Hand muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99% but reflects loss of neural input, without a direct muscle disease process.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy in 80-99% is secondary to motor neuron denervation; the disease directly targets neurons, without intrinsic muscle injury.

basis: Malignant CNS tumor; weakness and restricted mobility reflect neurologic disease rather than direct skeletal muscle or joint injury.
Usually originates in deep limb soft tissue; supplied HPO subcutaneous nodules (80-99%) support subcutis occupation. GI symptoms occur in only 5-29% without established tissue damage.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: HPO documents subcutaneous nodules in 80-99%; usual origin is deep limb soft tissue, supporting secondary subcutis involvement rather than primary skin origin.

basis: Usually a deep extremity soft-tissue sarcoma; supplied HPO reports subcutaneous nodules in 80-99%, supporting tumor occupation of subcutis despite usual deep origin.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous tumor nodules are annotated in 80-99%; this supports direct subcutis occupation even though the usual primary origin is deep soft tissue.

basis: Deep soft tissue sarcoma of adipocytic origin, usually retroperitoneal; no specific visceral organ involvement meets the threshold.
Developmental respiratory disorder of premature infants; episodic bradycardia and hypoxemia do not establish cardiac or neurologic damage.
Parasitic fly larvae infest and damage skin or cutaneous wounds.
Neonatal diabetes and developmental delay define intermediate DEND; epilepsy is absent in this form.
Reactivated Rickettsia prowazekii infection targets vascular endothelium and produces small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not establish skin damage.
Persistent neuropathic syndrome following peripheral nerve damage; edema and vasomotor or sweating changes do not establish separate organ damage.
Nongerminomatous germ-cell tumor arising within the central nervous system.
Ventricular tachycardia is a cardiac rhythm disorder.
Immune-mediated inflammation of cutaneous vessel walls defines both skin and vascular involvement; systemic organ damage is not required.
Germ cell tumor arising in testis or ovary; reproductive origin alone does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Mucositis usually denotes oral/GI mucosal inflammation; this broad concept does not establish another site or an autoimmune mechanism.
Benign mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm; renal and pulmonary locations are subtype-specific and are not assigned across this umbrella.
Tumor arises in a uterine supporting ligament, part of the reproductive apparatus rather than locomotor connective tissue.
Anemia due to enzyme dysfunction encompasses erythrocyte metabolic disorders; metabolic disease need not affect multiple organs to qualify.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the represented erythrocyte enzymopathies are disorders of cellular metabolism; a systemic metabolic phenotype is not required.

basis: Erythrocyte enzymopathies impair red-cell metabolism and cause anemia; additional organ manifestations vary by subtype.
Deficient factor V activity causes a blood coagulation disorder.
Coagulation disorder defined by deficient factor XI activity; an immune mechanism does not apply across the congenital and acquired umbrella.
Perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasm arising in the lung.
Germ cell tumour arising within myocardium or cardiac chambers.
Mycobacterial infection defines the umbrella; pulmonary, cutaneous and neural sites vary by subtype.
Pharyngeal disorders affect the upper airway, assigned to pulmonary; infection is not universal across this umbrella.
Benign neoplasm arising from cutaneous hair follicles.
Disease of the sixth cranial nerve; impaired eye movement reflects nerve dysfunction rather than intrinsic ocular damage.
Scrotal skin lesion defined by ectatic superficial dermal capillaries and overlying hyperkeratosis; both skin and capillaries are primary sites.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the lesion consists of abnormal dilated dermal capillaries; capillaries are explicitly included in the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Defined by impaired small-intestinal nutrient absorption; additional organ damage is not consistent across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Acquired deficiency of coagulation proteins. Liver disease and vitamin K deficiency are causes, not organs directly damaged by the factor deficiency; autoimmunity is subtype-specific.
Acute pharyngeal inflammation, usually caused by viral or bacterial infection; pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Mosquito-transmitted viral infection directly inflames the brain.
Skeletal overgrowth and macroglossia define it; developmental impairment ~60% and renal malformations ~50-60%. Cardiac defects (~30-45%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: congenital cardiac defects affect roughly 30-45% and qualify, but are omitted at the cap in favor of more frequent renal and neurologic damage.
decisions.renal: involved: structural renal malformations affect approximately 50-60%, including dysplasia and collecting-system abnormalities.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment is common; supplied motor delay is 8/13 and speech/language delay 5/7, supporting roughly 60% or more.

basis: Sterol synthesis disorder with defining skeletal and skin disease; cataracts in 6/8. Tracheal cartilage anomalies (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Renal tubular sodium transport dysfunction causes defining hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and hypertension; all reported in 3/3 patients.
Microcephaly in 10/10 and developmental delay in 4/10; cardiomyopathy in 4/9. Cafe-au-lait spots do not impair skin; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.
Microcephaly defines abnormal brain development; growth restriction alone establishes no additional axis; Bloom-specific skin and immune findings cannot be generalized.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define this encephalopathy. Cerebral visual impairment (2/6) is neurologic rather than intrinsic eye disease.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures in 11/11 and developmental delay in 10/11; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define disease; optic atrophy and iris coloboma each reported in 25%, below threshold.
Site-unspecified malignant neoplasm; anaplasia describes differentiation. No shared organ axis can be assigned across its diverse subtypes.
Malignant tumor originating in the meninges.
Malignant meningioma arising in the meninges of the central nervous system.
Melanoma originating in skin; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ labels.
Autoimmune inflammation directly affects the brain.
Neoplasm occupying the respiratory tract; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to this umbrella.
Renal cysts cause progressive kidney damage. Liver cysts are common (>70% of adults with dominant PKD) but usually preserve function; hepatic fibrosis chiefly defines recessive PKD.

decisions.hepatic: none: common dominant-PKD liver cysts usually preserve function; damaging hepatic fibrosis chiefly affects the less common recessive subtype.

basis: Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in and confined to the lung at diagnosis; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Inherited osteosclerosis from defective bone resorption. Marrow failure and cranial nerve complications do not affect most patients across dominant forms.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in ocular adnexa; ocular origin and lymphoma mechanism define the axes.
Microcephaly and renal agenesis define the syndrome. Micrognathia affects 3/3; structural limb and cardiac defects each occur in 1/3 (~33%). Very small cohort.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: micrognathia affects 3/3 and structural limb malformations occur in 1/3; skeletal disease is associated rather than a defining diagnostic axis.

basis: Rubella-associated infectious or postinfectious inflammation directly affects the brain.
Penile carcinoma arises in a reproductive organ outside the axes; HPV association alone does not make the tumour an infectious disease.
Germ cell tumour of a reproductive organ; vulvar origin alone does not establish a cutaneous tumour.
Germ cell malignancy arising in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Immature teratoma arising in the vulva, a reproductive site outside the defined axes.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Urothelial carcinoma originating in the renal pelvis or ureter.
Immune-mediated axial and peripheral joint disease; uveitis is not consistently present in at least 30% of juvenile cases.
Penile carcinoma has a reproductive site outside the axes; HPV causation alone does not classify the malignancy as an infection.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this concept is a carcinoma caused by HPV, rather than an infection, immunodeficiency, immune-mediated disease or lymphoma.

basis: Invasive urothelial carcinoma arising in the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Primary malignant bone tumor producing predominantly osteoid matrix.
Malignant mesenchymal tumor arising in soft connective tissues; no common additional organ involvement established.
Serous epithelial neoplasm originating in the ovary, a reproductive organ; no common direct damage to an included axis is established.
Histologic umbrella spanning sarcoma, carcinoma and melanoma; no common organ of origin is specified, so an organ axis cannot be assigned reliably.
Site-unspecified malignant neoplasm; no organ of origin is assignable. CNS examples among children do not establish the site across this umbrella.
Acute sarcoidosis defined by erythema nodosum and ankle arthritis/periarthritis; hilar lymphadenopathy alone does not establish lung damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining ankle arthritis/periarthritis represents direct inflammation of locomotor tissues.

basis: Craniosynostosis, limb synostoses and choanal stenosis/atresia characterize this subtype; neurologic and renal abnormalities lack established frequencies.
Malignancy occupies the paranasal sinuses, included in the airway axis; skull or neural invasion is not universal.
Defined by blood vessel occlusion; downstream organ damage depends on the site and is not universal across the umbrella.
Occlusion directly affects arteries; downstream organ injury varies with the artery and is not universal across this umbrella.
Umbrella for inadequate vascular or valvular function; no additional organ is consistently affected across subtypes.
Ischemia directly injures the intestine. Intrinsic vascular damage is not required; nonocclusive hypoperfusion also causes this disorder.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: inadequate bowel perfusion does not itself establish vessel disease; causal thrombosis or atherosclerosis is a separate condition.

basis: Acute hearing loss is an ear/hearing disorder.
Hearing loss arising in the cochlea or auditory nerve; additional neurologic disease is not intrinsic to the umbrella.
Hearing impairment from defective sound transmission through the external or middle ear.
Acute bronchiolar inflammation is usually a viral respiratory infection, especially RSV.
Dermatan-sulfate biosynthesis defect with contractures and skin fragility; ocular dysfunction 3-4/6; cap omits hearing loss 4/6, pneumothorax 3/6 and valve regurgitation 2/5.
Skeletal and skin defects define EDS; developmental delay and valve stenosis each annotated 80-99%; gingivitis 80-99% omitted by cap; proptosis alone is non-damaging.
Generic disease-course umbrella spanning organ systems; no specific organ or mechanism can be assigned.
Periodontitis and characteristic pretibial plaques define this subtype; joint hypermobility 11/24 and scoliosis 9/27 support musculoskeletal involvement.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic pretibial plaques are a major diagnostic criterion (24/25); skin fragility affects 24/32.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint hypermobility 11/24 and scoliosis 9/27 meet the threshold; skeletal findings are secondary features of this periodontal subtype.

basis: Ependymal tumor arising in the infratentorial brain.
Viral or bacterial infection of the tonsils in the pharyngeal upper respiratory tract.
Ependymal neoplasm originating in the supratentorial brain.
Reduced spinal cord perfusion defines the condition; the affected tissue is neural. Associated arterial or aortic disease is an underlying cause, not a required manifestation.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: spinal cord ischemia does not require intrinsic vessel disease; arterial/aortic disorders are possible causes rather than damage caused by this condition.

basis: HIV infection of the CNS causes white-matter injury and dementia.
Glioblastoma arises in central nervous system astrocytic tissue.
Vertebral segmentation defects and rib fusion define the disease; common intrinsic pulmonary damage is not established.
Hepatic glycogen metabolism disorder with hepatomegaly and frequent fibrosis. Muscle and neurodevelopmental injury are occasional, below 30%.
Carcinoma originates in salivary glands, usually the parotid; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cerebral motor disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle damage.
Vitamin deficiency is metabolic; anemia and neurologic injury are variable and not established in at least 30% across this broad biochemical deficiency concept.
Carcinoma arising in bronchial epithelium.
Biotin metabolism defects cause multiple carboxylase deficiency; neurologic dysfunction and dermatitis/alopecia each affect roughly >30% of symptomatic patients.
Biotin deficiency commonly causes encephalopathy, seizures or neuropathy and persistent dermatitis/alopecia; approximately >=30% each in clinically manifest disease, varying by cause.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurologic dysfunction is a characteristic manifestation across inherited and acquired clinical biotin deficiency, estimated at >=30%; psychiatric symptoms alone do not qualify.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent dermatitis and alopecia are characteristic direct manifestations of clinical biotin deficiency, estimated at >=30% across its usual symptomatic course.

basis: Brachydactyly is a developmental skeletal abnormality affecting the digits.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder with blistering and hyperkeratosis; ocular lesions occur in only 5-29%.
Neoplasm of the erythroid blood-cell lineage and bone marrow; subtype-specific complications are not generalized.
Inherited skeletal muscle disorder with abnormal contractions, stiffness, hypertrophy and elevated creatine kinase; no established peripheral nerve disease.
Bony osteophytes of the distal interphalangeal joints.
Defined by hearing dysfunction arising in central nervous system auditory pathways, supporting both neurologic and hearing axes.
Segmental lower motor neuron degeneration causes arm weakness and denervation atrophy.
Dermatophyte infection causes granulomatous inflammation of hair follicles and surrounding dermis.
Infection of the amniotic cavity and membranes supplies the mechanism axis; the obstetric site has no anatomical axis.
Peripheral resistance to thyroid hormone defines an endocrine signalling disorder.
Complete gonadal dysgenesis causes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and absent secondary sex characteristics; no evidence supports the cardiomyopathy ancestor.
Occlusive disease of pulmonary venules causing pulmonary vascular hypertension and impaired lung gas exchange.
Metabolic myopathy and optic atrophy define disease; leukoencephalopathy is a defining CNS feature qualifying by the diagnostic exception. Supplied HPO frequencies conflict with the phenotype.

decisions.neurologic: involved: defining leukoencephalopathy qualifies by the diagnostic-feature exception; three primary slots retain metabolic myopathy and optic atrophy.
decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is explicitly syndrome-defining; the inconsistent 1-4% annotation does not negate its primary status.

basis: Inherited thyroid iodide-trapping defect causes deficient thyroid hormone synthesis; lasting extra-thyroid damage is not established as common.
Isolated inherited hair-shaft disorder; abnormal hair texture and growth occur in all annotated patients.
Congenitally shortened/malrotated intestine causes intestinal failure. Acidosis (3/3) accompanies diarrhoea/dehydration; persistent additional metabolic dysfunction is not established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: acidosis in 3/3 establishes frequency, but intestinal losses and dehydration can cause transient acidosis; persistent metabolic injury or a defining metabolic disorder is not established.

basis: Inherited phosphate dysregulation causes rickets and intrinsic dentin hypomineralization in over 30%; renal phosphate wasting alone does not establish kidney injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intrinsic dentin mineralization defects affect over 30% and directly compromise teeth; this does not rely on separately diagnosed dental abscesses.

basis: Inherited heme-synthesis defect causes sideroblastic anemia; hepatic abnormalities and glucose intolerance are occasional (5-29%).
Inherited oxalate-handling disorder with hyperoxaluria and calcium oxalate stones; obstruction and acute kidney injury are documented in the reported patient.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the inherited oxalate-handling abnormality is supported by hyperoxaluria in 1/1 reported patients, beyond the gene name alone.

basis: Defective vitamin D activation causes hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia and defining rachitic bone disease; renal enzyme location alone does not imply kidney injury.
Cerebral vascular malformations define this cerebrovascular disease. Retinal, hepatic and skin involvement lack qualifying frequency evidence.
Anemia is the defining blood disorder; organs affected by the underlying chronic disease are not attributed to the anemia.
MUC1 deposition causes progressive renal tubulointerstitial injury; anemia and hypertension are secondary complications of kidney disease.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; microcephaly 2/2, encephalopathy/seizures 1/2, and heart failure/pulmonary arterial hypertension 1/2. Hypotonia alone does not establish myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: microcephaly in 2/2 and encephalopathy/seizures in 1/2 establish common CNS damage; the defining disease is mitochondrial metabolic deficiency.

basis: Inherited renal tubular urate transport defect causes urinary urate wasting and hypouricemia; stones and kidney injury remain within the renal axis.
Defining B-cell maturation arrest with absent/decreased B cells in 7/7; neutropenia 6/19 (~32%). Pneumonias are separate infections; bronchiectasis 3/19 (~16%).

decisions.haematologic: primary: defining B-cell developmental failure with decreased B cells in 7/7 is a blood-cell disease; neutropenia is additional evidence, not the reason for tier.

basis: Familial median nerve entrapment neuropathy; tenosynovitis has unspecified frequency. TTR association alone does not establish systemic amyloid organ damage.
Arthropod-transmitted viral infection umbrella; specific organ damage varies substantially between infections.
Congenital joint fusion defines disease; stapes ankylosis with conductive hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%.
Adrenal cortisol excess causes myopathy/bone loss (~50-80%) and skin atrophy/striae (~50-70%) in overt Cushing syndrome; hypertension is separately diagnosed. Subtype estimates are limited.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension (~70-85% in overt Cushing syndrome) is a separately diagnosed disease; common intrinsic cardiac or vascular injury is not established.

basis: Inherited hair shaft abnormality characterized by pili canaliculi and uncombable dry hair.
Optic atrophy with visual impairment in 6/6; intellectual disability and ataxia each occur in 2/6, supporting neurologic involvement at approximately 33%.
Congenital skin creases, intellectual disability and cleft palate define syndrome; microphthalmia reported in 1/3, just above the frequency threshold.
Disordered vitamin D metabolism causes hypercalcemia; medullary nephrocalcinosis 10/10 with polyuria 7/10 supports direct renal involvement.
Defining immunodeficiency, sweat-gland/hair defects and dental anomalies. Bronchiectasis in 2/2 is secondary to recurrent infections, a separate complication.
audit_reason: Remove pulmonary: bronchiectasis follows recurrent infections and is a separately diagnosed complication of immunodeficiency. Its annotated frequency does not satisfy the direct-damage and separate-disease rules.

basis: ALDH7A1 metabolic defect causes epilepsy; strabismus (1/2) does not establish direct ocular damage; neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus in 1/2 establishes misalignment, but does not demonstrate direct ocular damage distinct from the neurologic disorder.

basis: Acute leukemia involving hematopoietic blasts of mixed lineage; no other organ has established common direct damage.
Intermittent atrioventricular conduction failure defines a cardiac conduction disorder.
Inherited cardiac calcium-release dysfunction causes ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.
Skeletal fusions and contractures define the syndrome together with cutaneous pterygia; webbed neck occurs in 5/9. Cleft palate occurs in only 1/10.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: pterygia are defining congenital skin webs; webbed neck is present in 5/9, supporting cutaneous involvement beyond uncommon antecubital webs.

basis: Plant sterol disorder; hemolysis/platelet abnormalities around 30%, supported by HPO; atherosclerosis separately coded; xanthomas/arcus do not establish functional damage.
Sterol transport disorder; xanthomas lack demonstrated functional damage; atherosclerosis is separately coded; hematologic damage lacks clear >=30% evidence.
Bone cysts and progressive sclerosing leukoencephalopathy with dementia define the disease; both occur in 6/6 reported patients.
Defined by sclerosing leukoencephalopathy and cystic osteodysplasia with osteopenia and pathological fractures.
Catecholamine synthesis defect causing cardiovascular and autonomic dysfunction; decreased GFR 2/2. Anemia 2/2 omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia in 2/2 qualifies, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining autonomic dysfunction and renal functional impairment.
decisions.neurologic: primary: inherited failure of autonomic noradrenergic neurotransmission defines the orthostatic disorder and represents neurologic loss of function.

basis: Coronavirus infection is predominantly a respiratory tract disease across the umbrella; extrapulmonary injury is not universal or defining.
ACTG2 visceral myopathy causes intestinal and bladder smooth-muscle dysfunction; bladder involvement occurs in ~90% across the spectrum, beyond the small historical 1/6 series.
audit_reason: Add renal to primary: ACTG2 visceral myopathy characteristically affects intestinal and bladder smooth muscle. Bladder dysfunction is common across the spectrum; the small 1/6 urinary-retention series does not establish its overall frequency.

basis: Inherited neurologic channelopathy causing hemiplegic migraine, sometimes with progressive cerebellar dysfunction; visual aura does not indicate eye damage.
Migraine syndrome with motor aura; no additional organ damage is established.
Squamous carcinoma confined to the skin epidermis.
Squamous cell carcinoma in situ arising in the epidermis.
Developmental brain malformation with severe developmental impairment, spastic tetraplegia and dystonia; feeding difficulty alone adds no GI damage.
Intellectual disability defines the neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus 26/48 and hearing impairment 13/24 support eye and ear involvement; scoliosis 6/24 is below threshold.
Congenital peripheral hypomyelination; denervation amyotrophy and scoliosis each reported in 1/1 assessed patients, supporting common muscle and skeletal damage.
Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy; fixed talipes in 1/3 supports musculoskeletal involvement. Respiratory failure may be neurogenic, without direct airway or lung damage.
Cauda equina nerve-root injury with defining persistent neurogenic bladder dysfunction; bowel dysfunction is not required or quantified.
Inherited hearing loss defines this umbrella; additional organ disease is not shared across its subtypes.

Neurodevelopmental syndrome; tooth agenesis 2/2, strabismus/blepharophimosis 1/2 and hearing loss 1/2 support involvement. Mild skeletal findings omitted by cap; infections do not prove immune deficiency.
Cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy define disease; distal muscle wasting in 1/1 reflects denervation, without evidence of direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: wasting and weakness are downstream effects of neuropathy; direct skeletal-muscle pathology or common structural skeletal injury is not established.

basis: Cerebellar ataxia and axonal peripheral neuropathy define this group; DNA repair ancestry alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Cerebrospinal fluid leakage reflects failure of the CNS coverings; nasal drainage alone does not establish airway damage.
Intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%; ptosis/strabismus, hearing impairment and dental abnormalities each occur in 30-79%; recurrent infections do not establish immunodeficiency.

Defining severe neurodevelopmental phenotype 3/3; limb undergrowth 3/3 and glaucoma 1/3 support involvement. Cardiac defects and neutropenia, each 1/3, omitted by cap; renal functional injury unproven.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe developmental impairment, intellectual disability, seizures and microcephaly each occur in 3/3 and constitute the defining clinical phenotype.

basis: Bacterial infection umbrella with variable tissue sites; no additional organ is consistently affected across the group.
Glycosylation disorder with defining severe NDD and seizures in 2/2; contractures 2/2 and optic atrophy 1/2. Respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of intrinsic lung damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures in 2/2, with structural CNS abnormalities, constitute the defining clinical presentation.

basis: Defining cone-rod retinal degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss; visual impairment in 3/3 and hearing impairment in 2/2 assessed.
Developmental dysfunction of skeletal cartilage.
NAD(P)HX repair deficiency causes metabolic encephalopathy and myelopathy; respiratory failure reflects neurologic dysfunction without established direct lung damage.
Chronic inflammation of gingiva defines the disease. Plaque association alone does not establish an infectious or autoimmune diagnosis for this broad concept.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: local gingival inflammation, commonly plaque-associated, does not itself establish infection, immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease.

basis: Cutaneous capillary malformations in 48/50 patients define the vascular skin disorder; organ-specific arteriovenous complications are a minority.
Vascular malformations and characteristic cutaneous capillary malformations define CMAVM2. Vein of Galen malformation occurs in only 1-4%.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: persistent cutaneous capillary malformations are a defining disease location. The damage requirement for involved organs does not exclude a defining cutaneous lesion.

basis: Defining hypomagnesemia with developmental disability in 6/6 and seizures in 5/6; no additional structural renal damage established.
Hypomagnesemia, seizures and developmental disability define the syndrome; renal magnesium wasting in 2/2 demonstrates common intrinsic tubular dysfunction.

decisions.renal: involved: renal magnesium wasting in 2/2 establishes direct tubular loss of function accompanying the defining electrolyte and neurologic phenotype.

basis: OCLN-related brain malformation with seizures and developmental impairment; patent ductus arteriosus in 2/5 (40%); ocular and renal findings are occasional.
Brainstem abnormalities and progressive scoliosis define disease. Hyperopic astigmatism affects 1/2 annotated patients (50%), supporting ocular involvement; frequency estimate is uncertain.
audit_reason: Add ocular involvement: hyperopic astigmatism occurs in 1/2 annotated patients, meeting the supplied frequency threshold independently of central gaze palsy. The small sample warrants medium confidence.

basis: Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy causing corneal opacities, photophobia and possible visual impairment.
Skeletal growth disorder with increased vertebral height, severe short stature and coxa vara.
Oculopharyngodistal myopathy; ptosis 52/53 and pharyngeal dysphagia 40/54. Pharynx maps to pulmonary. Brain atrophy 3/3 imaged; sparse cardiac findings omitted by cap.
Invasive adenocarcinoma arising in colorectal epithelium; no additional common organ involvement established.
Growth restriction with delayed skeletal maturation defines the phenotype; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Growth restriction, skeletal asymmetry and digital abnormalities define SRS1. Hypoglycemia occurs in roughly 25-30%; consistent endocrine gland disease is not established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: syndromic growth restriction alone is not endocrine disease; hypoglycemia occurs in roughly 25-30% and is not a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Decompression bubbles occupy joint tissues and obstruct vessels. Direct spinal cord or cerebral injury occurs in roughly 30-50% of clinical cases, varying by series.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurologic decompression injury affects roughly 30-50% in clinical series; it is common but does not define every case of this umbrella condition.

basis: Inherited parathyroid hormone deficiency causes hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia; hypocalcemic seizures do not establish direct brain damage.
Epidermal basal cell tumors account for most patients across this umbrella; salivary gland tumors are a minority site-specific subtype.
CNS myelin destruction defines the organ axis. Immune-mediated disease predominates across patients, including both listed subtypes, MS and MOG-antibody-associated disease.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immune-mediated disorders predominate across this umbrella and both listed subtypes; the umbrella rule requires applicability to most patients, not every cause.

basis: Malignant epithelial tumor arising in the rectum.
Basal cell carcinoma overwhelmingly arises in skin; exceptional extracutaneous sites do not define this umbrella.
Benign basal epithelial tumor, provisionally assigned to skin; the supplied definition leaves the anatomical site unspecified.
Cardiac conduction block originating at the sinoatrial node.
Gonadal sex cord-stromal tumour involving Sertoli and/or Leydig endocrine cell lineages; no common direct extra-gonadal organ damage established.
Testicular reproductive neoplasm presenting as a mass. Clinically relevant hormonal dysfunction is neither defining nor established as common.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: Sertoli-cell hormone secretion alone does not make this mass-defined reproductive tumor an endocrine disorder; a defining hormonal phenotype is absent.

basis: Localized gonadal sex cord-stromal tumor; endocrine dysfunction is not established by the definition.
Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; encephalopathy/developmental impairment common across subtypes (>30%); hepatic, renal and cardiac damage vary by subtype.
Structural tooth damage exposes dental pulp; susceptibility to bacterial invasion does not itself establish infection.
Benign reproductive testicular Sertoli cell tumor; hormonal dysfunction is not defining or established as common.
Miliaria is a cutaneous sweat-duct disorder.
Odontogenic cyst arising around an unerupted tooth; teeth and their supporting oral structures belong to gastrointestinal.
Miliaria is a cutaneous sweat duct obstruction disorder.
Dental dentin maps to gastrointestinal; the supplied definition describes normal dentin formation rather than pathological organ damage.
Sheldon-Hall syndrome subtype defined by congenital distal joint contractures and skeletal deformities.
Infantile sweat duct obstruction causing miliaria in the skin.
Inflammation of the diaphragm, a skeletal muscle; lung or airway damage and an autoimmune cause are not established.
Vertebral and limb skeletal defects, congenital cardiac anomalies and renal malformations define the syndrome.
Inherited alpha-globin abnormality causes methemoglobinemia and impaired blood oxygen carriage; cyanosis does not establish lung injury.
Oocyte maturation and pronucleus formation defect causing female infertility; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection of the anterior nasal airway; systemic toxin complications are not common in this localized form.
Alveolar proteinosis and immunodeficiency define disease. Splenomegaly 4/4 and leukocytosis do not establish destructive hematologic disease.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, ataxia and cerebellar atrophy; visual impairment is very rare (1-4%).
Diphtheritic conjunctival infection supported by name, synonyms and conjunctivitis ancestors; the definition's reference to colitis appears erroneous.
Mitochondrial extraocular and skeletal myopathy; neuropathy and cerebellar atrophy/ataxia 1/1. Cardiac dysfunction and hearing loss each 1/1 omitted at cap.
Severe intellectual disability and developmental delay in 5/5; spasticity is neurologic. The carbohydrate-transport ancestor does not establish a metabolic phenotype.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; other functional organ abnormalities occur below 30%.
Osteopetrosis with anemia and tooth loss/gingivitis each reported in 1/1; marrow compromise and oral damage qualify, but prevalence evidence is limited to one case.
RIPK1 immunodeficiency with autoinflammation; colitis in 4/4 and gastritis in 3/4; bronchiectasis in 2/4 supports direct pulmonary injury.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; myopia 2/3, atrial septal defect 1/3 and finger contractures 1/3. Renal hypospadias 1/3 omitted under the four-organ cap.
audit_reason: Retain the organ lists, but note renal involvement omitted under the four-organ cap: hypospadias in 1/3 meets the supplied threshold and qualifying capped organs must be mentioned in basis.

basis: Spermatogenic failure and cryptorchidism affect reproductive function; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Isolated sperm structural abnormality and male infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Inherited encephalopathy with myelin vacuolization and seizures in 9/9; no established infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Renal sodium transport disorder defined by hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and hypertension; hypertension and hypokalemia each reported in 7/7.
Isolated failure of sperm production with azoospermia; no endocrine dysfunction or other organ disease is established.
MYSM1-related marrow failure includes cytopenias and intrinsic immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia and recurrent infections.
Ovarian endocrine failure: low estradiol and elevated gonadotropins in 3/4 patients; reproductive anatomy adds no separate axis.
ATP synthase metabolic defect; seizures/developmental impairment, rhabdomyolysis/myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/2 patients.
Corynebacterial infection of the fauces/pharyngeal airway; toxin-related cardiac or neurologic complications do not meet the common-involvement threshold.
Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection of the larynx; myocarditis and neuropathy are minority complications.
Corynebacterial infection of the nasopharynx; myocarditis and neuropathy are minority complications.
Organism-defined bacterial infection spanning intestinal, urinary and other sites; no single anatomical site applies across the umbrella.
Congenital additional digits on the postaxial side of hands or feet.
Joint contractures, skeletal fusions and congenital cutaneous pterygia define this multiple-pterygium syndrome.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the named pterygia are congenital skin webs forming a defining structural component of the syndrome.

basis: Fungal infection directly involving ocular structures; possible routes of spread do not establish other organ involvement.
Parasitic infection directly occupies and damages the eye or ocular adnexa.
Viral infection directly affecting ocular structures, including conjunctiva, cornea, iris, retina or eyelids.
Filarial infection; no additional organ has established direct damage in at least 30%; microfilaremia alone does not establish blood-cell injury.
Gonococcal infection directly inflames the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
Inflammatory granulation-tissue mass in the larynx; no intrinsic infectious or autoimmune mechanism established.
Granulomatous prostatitis includes infectious and immune-mediated inflammation. The prostate itself lies outside the organ axes.
Localized hamartomatous malformation of cutaneous hair follicles and sebaceous glands.
Congenital skin and hair-associated hamartoma; subsequent melanoma is a separate disease risk.
Structural rupture of myocardium, cardiac septum, valves or associated supporting tissues.
Inherited persistence of fetal hemoglobin production is a hemoglobin phenotype, usually without additional organ damage.
Inherited iron overload with predominant hepatic deposition; iron-related arthropathy affects ~30–50% of clinically affected patients; cardiac injury is less common.
Congenital fusion of digits defines this skeletal developmental disorder; additional organs vary across syndromic subtypes.
Congenital additional digits define the skeletal disorder; other organ abnormalities are subtype-dependent.
Developmental shortening of digital bones defines the group; other organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Limb and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; cognitive impairment and ptosis each 30-79%. Skin hyperextensibility alone does not establish damage; dental defects are <30%.
Autoimmune coagulation disorder defined by thrombophilia and vascular thrombosis; accompanying autoimmune disease is not attributed to this syndrome.
Carcinoma originates in salivary glands, included in the gastrointestinal axis.
Malignant lymphatic endothelial tumour originating in skin; lymphatic origin does not make it a lymphoma.
Hereditary chorea with motor developmental impairment; thyroid and pulmonary disease are not established for this isolated phenotype.
Brittle abnormal hair and nail dystrophy define ectodermal disease; global developmental delay occurs in 20/20. Ocular and cardiac defects are occasional.
Defined by synaptic dysfunction within the nervous system, including neuromuscular junction disease.
DNAJB6 skeletal muscular dystrophy; dysphagia and dysarthria reflect muscle weakness. The definition specifies absence of characteristic cardiac or respiratory disease.
Inherited melanin/melanosome disorder with foveal hypoplasia and impaired vision; freckling and giant melanosomes do not establish damaging skin disease.
Absent hepatic bilirubin conjugation defines the metabolic defect; bilirubin neurotoxicity/kernicterus is reported in 80-99%. Hearing loss is under 30%.
Skeletal hyperostosis commonly (>30% each over the course) causes cranial neuropathy, optic damage and hearing loss. Choanal stenosis (1/1) omitted at the cap.

decisions.pulmonary: none: choanal stenosis (1/1) qualifies as airway involvement, but is omitted at the cap in favor of common severe cranial nerve, visual and hearing damage.
decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive cranial nerve compression with facial palsy and intracranial hypertension is characteristic and common (>30%) over the course.

basis: Inherited glycinergic startle disorder. Stiffness is neurologic; reflux, hiatus hernia and esophagitis reported at 80-99% are separate conditions rather than direct gut involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: despite HPO frequencies of 80-99%, reflux/hiatus hernia and consequent esophagitis are separate diagnoses, not direct gastrointestinal injury by hyperekplexia.

basis: Androgen hormone resistance is an endocrine disorder; reproductive anomalies and reduced androgen-dependent hair do not establish additional organ damage.
Familial cirrhosis establishes hepatic fibrosis; supplied evidence does not identify the antigen or establish a viral or immune-mediated cause.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: antigenemia is unspecified; the supplied definition and ancestry do not establish hepatitis B infection or an immune mechanism.

basis: Hereditary abnormalities of epidermal appendages; additional organs are not established across this umbrella.
Inherited abnormality of cutaneous sebaceous glands.
Varicella-zoster reactivation causes dermatitis specifically involving eyelid skin; persistent neural damage is not established as common.
VZV causes direct cutaneous infection; pain and neuronal latency alone do not establish additional damage, and postherpetic neuralgia is a minority complication.
Alopecia and severe intellectual disability both occur in 7/7 and define the syndrome.
Persistent follicular keratin plugging is confined to skin.
Tumor family primarily arising in bone or soft connective tissues; neural differentiation does not establish nervous-system origin.
Malignant mesenchymal tumor arising in soft connective tissues; neural differentiation does not establish nervous-system origin.
Pancreatic tumor umbrella predominantly comprises exocrine neoplasms; endocrine origin is restricted to a minority of subtypes.
Fibroblastic neoplasm arising in the pleura.
Glial tumor arising in the brain or spinal cord; no additional organ involvement applies to most patients across the group.
Umbrella chiefly represented by breast fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumors, outside the axes; fibrous histology alone does not imply locomotor disease or justify the renal subtype.
Neoplasm arising in breast parenchyma; breast has no axis.
Neoplasm originating in breast tissue, which is outside the specified axes.
Localized mast-cell neoplasm, usually a solitary cutaneous lesion; systemic mastocytosis is not implied.
Vulvar neoplasm is classified by its reproductive organ origin; this umbrella does not establish disease of another axis.
Vaginal neoplasms originate in a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in parasympathetic paraganglia; usually nonsecretory. Ear and vascular involvement depend on the anatomical subtype.
Tumor of parasympathetic carotid-body chemoreceptor paraganglia. Neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease; carotid proximity adds no vascular axis.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the tumor originates in carotid-body parasympathetic paraganglia, part of the peripheral autonomic sensory system.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the tumor arises in parasympathetic chemoreceptor tissue; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish an endocrine-gland or metabolic disorder.

basis: Sarcoma originates in bone; no additional organ involvement is established across this umbrella.
Colorectal adenomatous polyposis defines FAP; bone osteomas occur in 30-79% per HPO. CHRPE usually spares vision; thyroid nodules and cancers are separate diagnoses.
Colorectal adenomatous polyposis defines disease; gastric and duodenal polyps share this axis. Retinal pigment hypertrophy generally does not impair vision; other tumors are separate risks.
Defined by colorectal adenomas; additional intestinal lesions remain on the same axis, while extracolonic tumors and other lesions are variable or separate diseases.
Neurodevelopmental, cutaneous and congenital cardiac abnormalities characterize the major RASopathies; cardiac lesions are defining features of Noonan-related syndromes.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital heart defects and cardiomyopathy are defining manifestations across major Noonan-related RASopathies, although less characteristic of NF1.

basis: Hereditary neural-tumor syndrome; cutaneous neurofibromas and pigmentary lesions characterize NF1, which accounts for most patients. Hearing and ocular injury vary by subtype.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the colon; lymphoma is only one subtype, and distant metastatic involvement is not universal.
Tumor originates in parasympathetic paraganglia at the skull base and middle ear; clinically significant hormone secretion is uncommon.
Neoplastic occupation of the pleura; other primary sites or metastatic destinations cannot be inferred across this group.
Neoplasms occupying kidneys or urinary collecting and outflow structures, all covered by the renal axis.
Extragonadal tumour originates in mediastinum, outside the specified axes; thoracic location alone does not establish lung, airway or pleural origin or damage.
Ovarian neoplasm is a reproductive-organ tumor; endocrine dysfunction is not a defining feature across this umbrella.
Malignancy originating in endocrine glands; additional organs are not consistently affected across this umbrella.
Carcinoma originates in the sublingual salivary gland, within the gastrointestinal axis.
Neoplasm arising in the larynx, an upper respiratory airway included in the pulmonary axis.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in sympathetic paraganglia or adrenal medulla; catecholamine-related hypertension alone does not establish direct cardiovascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension is a common secretory effect; direct cardiovascular injury in at least 30% is not established.

basis: Site-unspecified neoplastic polyp; gastrointestinal assignment reflects the usual adenomatous polyp setting, but no anatomical site is supplied.
Neoplasm originates in exocrine pancreatic epithelium.
Neoplasm arising from arteries or veins; other anatomical sites vary across subtypes.
Neoplasm arising in a Meckel diverticulum of the ileum.
Congenital ocular motor dysinnervation causes fixed ophthalmoplegia, secondary extraocular muscle fibrosis and ptosis.
Defined by impaired vision; neurologic causes occur in subtypes but are not shared across the umbrella.
Benign or malignant neoplasm involving the stomach.
Neoplasm originates in gingiva, which belongs to the oral gastrointestinal axis.
Primary meningeal tumour within the central nervous system.
Malignancy originates in peripheral or autonomic nervous tissue; anatomical sites and metastatic organ involvement vary across subtypes.
Carcinoma originates in breast tissue, outside the axes; intracellular lipid does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Neoplasm of the fallopian tube; reproductive tissue has no axis.
Skeletal, hair/nail and dental dysplasia define CED1; CKD in 2/2 assessed supports renal involvement. Hepatic fibrosis and retinal dystrophy each 1/10.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: hypodontia/anodontia and microdontia are characteristic defining ectodermal defects; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Defined by deficient cellular or humoral immunity; infections and organ damage vary across this broad group.
Defined by basal ganglia motor pathway dysfunction; rigidity and tremor do not establish primary muscle damage.
Benign tumour arising in mammary ducts; breast tissue lies outside the specified axes.
Intraductal papillomatosis predominantly denotes mammary duct papillomas; the supplied subtype is breast disease, outside the axes.
Neoplasm of breast parenchyma; breast has no axis. Metastases are not defining or common across this benign/malignant umbrella.
Tumor originates in the appendiceal wall; peptide production alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Tumour originates in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; urinary-system ancestry does not establish urinary tract damage.
Alcohol-induced lipid accumulation in hepatocytes; no independent systemic metabolic disorder is established.
Steatotic liver disease; metabolic associations do not independently establish an endocrine or systemic metabolic disorder.
Heterogeneous nuclear-lamina disease umbrella with prominent muscle and skeletal disorders; cardiac, metabolic and neurologic disease varies by subtype.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy and conduction disease characterize particular laminopathies, not most patients across this broad umbrella.

basis: Central sleep-wake regulation disorder; an autoimmune mechanism is not established across all included forms.
Inflammation of the brain or spinal meninges; infection accounts for most cases across this umbrella.
Benign urothelial neoplasm arising in the bladder or other urinary tract sites.
Benign neoplasm originating in cutaneous sweat glands; labels reflect the usual sites across the umbrella.
Benign or malignant tumor directly occupying the ureter.
Scrotal malignancies predominantly affect scrotal skin, most commonly as squamous carcinoma; this supports dermatologic origin across the umbrella.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the scrotum is a cutaneous sac, and most scrotal cancers arise in its skin despite classification under reproductive-system cancers.

basis: Failure of pulmonary gas exchange; underlying causes and possible downstream hypoxic injuries are not universal components.
Neoplasm of a female reproductive gland; Bartholin gland has no axis.
Molecular subtype of a breast carcinoma; breast has no axis, and estrogen receptor expression does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Carcinoma arising in breast, which has no axis; estrogen receptor expression does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Neoplasm occupying the lung; additional organs and lymphoma mechanisms do not apply across this umbrella.
Neoplasm originates in or occupies the small or large intestine.
Neoplasm originating in endocrine tissue; absence of a hormonal syndrome does not change its organ axis.
Hormone-producing endocrine neoplasm with a defining hormonal syndrome; additional organ effects vary across tumour types.
Neoplasm of vascular endothelial cells and vascular channels; organ sites vary across subtypes.
Malignant tumor originating in bone; neuroectodermal differentiation does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Reproductive infertility umbrella; an endocrine disorder is not established across the group.
Congenital or developmental reduction in eyeball size; additional organs depend on the particular syndromic subtype.
Inherited disruption of sphingolipid biosynthesis; no shared extra-metabolic organ damage is established for this umbrella.
Ependymal tumor located in the frontal lobe of the brain.
Autonomous parathyroid hormone excess; chronic high-turnover bone loss is common, exceeding about 30%; underlying renal disease is antecedent rather than direct involvement.
Acquired coagulation factor XIII deficiency; immune inhibitors are one cause, but an immune mechanism is not universal.
Acquired coagulation factor X deficiency; the supplied definition describes a commonly associated circulating factor X inhibitor.
Malignancy originates in or infiltrates bone marrow; marrow involvement does not itself establish skeletal damage.
Acquired rippling myopathy is generally immune-mediated; associated myasthenia gravis is a separate disease and does not establish neurological involvement.
Most melanocytic neoplasms arise in skin; ocular and CNS origins occur in minority subtypes and are not shared across the umbrella.
Ovarian epithelial tumor arises in a reproductive organ; no endocrine dysfunction is specified.
Defined neurological pain disorder; no additional organ damage applies across this broad group.
Anatomically unrestricted developmental umbrella with no shared organ axis; empty labels indicate an unassignable umbrella rather than exclusively outside-axis anatomy.
Neoplasms arise in female reproductive organs, which have no axis; endocrine function is not a defining feature of this umbrella.
Umbrella concept explicitly defined by disease of the dermis.
Inherited degeneration of retinal cone and rod photoreceptors.
Pituitary inflammation, predominantly immune-mediated, directly affects an endocrine gland; its location does not itself establish neurologic damage.
Gonococcal infection of the cervix; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism qualifies.
Gonococcal infection of the epididymis and testis; reproductive inflammation does not establish endocrine gonadal dysfunction.
Gonococcal infection of the fallopian tubes; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis, but infection supplies the mechanism axis.
Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection of the urinary bladder.
Gonococcal infection establishes the mechanism axis; the prostate is reproductive, and urinary tract damage is not established.
