Anophthalmia and esophageal atresia define the syndrome; cryptorchidism has no applicable axis.
Inflammation localized to the trachea and bronchi; this broad diagnosis does not specify an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Post-traumatic heterotopic bone formation in skeletal muscle or adjacent soft tissue; not an autoimmune myositis.
Trypanosomal infection commonly progresses to CNS invasion and meningoencephalitis over its untreated course; skin chancre is uncommon and transient.
Species-defined fungal infection; pulmonary and ear infections occur, but the broad definition establishes neither site in most patients.
Rhodesian sleeping sickness; CNS invasion with meningoencephalitis is a characteristic progressive stage, affecting well over 30% over the untreated course.
A mass-forming tuberculous infection; the anatomical site is unspecified and may vary.
Defined by auditory nerve transmission dysfunction causing hearing loss and impaired speech perception.
Defined by impaired hearing; central auditory dysfunction occurs in a subset and does not justify neurologic labeling across the umbrella.
Mycobacterial infection directly involves the skin; pulmonary involvement is not inherent to cutaneous tuberculosis.
Autoimmune destruction of ovarian steroid-producing tissue causes primary ovarian endocrine insufficiency; associated autoimmune diseases are separate.
Progestogen hypersensitivity typically manifests as dermatitis or urticaria; episodic bronchospasm does not establish lasting pulmonary damage.
Lung parenchymal fibrosis directly attributable to pulmonary tuberculosis.
Nonsyndromic congenital opacity of the lens nucleus; confined to the ocular axis.
Defining features include megalencephaly/developmental disability, short limbs and hearing loss.
Hydrocephalus and cerebral aqueductal dysgenesis define brain involvement; craniosynostosis defines skeletal involvement.
Hamartoma of cutaneous pilosebaceous structures with comedones, cysts and epidermal atrophy.
Disease of hair, nails and skin with hypotrichosis, leukonychia and progressive palmoplantar keratoderma.
Defining brachytelephalangy and skeletal abnormalities occur with congenital optic atrophy.
Water and sodium imbalance causing dilutional hyponatremia; lasting neurologic damage is not established in most cases.
Neurological movement syndrome typically associated with third-ventricular cysts and hydrocephalus.
Spontaneous transmural esophageal rupture defines the disease; secondary infection and pleural complications are not intrinsic defining lesions.
Definition identifies intellectual disability and seizures, skin lesions and hearing loss as core manifestations.
HPV-associated dysplastic papules of genital squamous epithelium; malignant transformation is uncommon.
Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy with defining multiple joint contractures.
Persistent lentiviral infection; the umbrella does not establish direct damage to any additional organ in at least 30%.
Malignant lymphoid-cell neoplasm; no particular extranodal organ is established as commonly damaged.
Defining craniosynostosis, limb and cervical skeletal abnormalities with pulmonary valve stenosis; genital defects have no axis.
Odontogenic epithelial tumor; approximately 90-95% grow within jaw bone, causing direct occupation and local invasion. Skin ancestry conflicts with the definition.
Corpus callosum agenesis and ocular coloboma define the syndrome; amenorrhea alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Severe intellectual disability and delayed sexual maturation define the syndrome, supporting neurologic and endocrine axes; proportionate dwarfism alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Progressive generalized skin hyperpigmentation without other symptoms defines universal acquired melanosis.
Lobular capillary proliferation arising in skin or oral mucosa/gingiva; reactive inflammation does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Recurrent pleural air accumulation causes lung collapse; association with menstruation does not establish endocrine disease.
Prostate inflammation has no anatomical axis; infection or an autoimmune mechanism is not required across this concept.
Permanent destruction and scarring of scalp hair follicles; an autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Visual-release hallucinations reflect neurologic dysfunction. The visual loss comes from a separate underlying eye, optic nerve or brain disorder.
Syndrome characterized by tibial/radial skeletal anomalies, osteopenia, fractures and developmental disability.
Disorder of cutaneous sweat glands causing colored sweat.
Partial 11q trisomy commonly causes developmental delay and intellectual disability. Cardiac, skeletal and other structural abnormalities vary with the duplicated interval.
Developmental delay/intellectual disability is a core manifestation; other structural abnormalities vary by duplicated segment without established umbrella-wide frequencies.
Cardiac and skeletal malformations characterize affected trisomy 16 phenotypes; sparse record and variability between complete and mosaic forms limit assignment.
Chronic erosive injury of gastric mucosa; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established.
Immune-mediated pustular inflammation of the skin; no additional organ damage is established across localized and generalized forms.
Crystal deposition causes joint disease; the umbrella does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder or autoimmune mechanism.
Dorsal midbrain dysfunction causes vertical gaze palsy and pupillary abnormalities; these central ocular-motor signs do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Congenital cerebral white-matter underdevelopment produces disproportionate enlargement of the occipital ventricular horns.
Defined by disease of penile blood vessels, including arterial disease, venous dysfunction and vascular tumors.
Progressive degeneration of cerebral cortex and basal ganglia causes cognitive and motor dysfunction.
Ectodermal dysplasia with osteosclerosis and a craniosynostosis parent supports cutaneous and skeletal axes; other organ involvement is not established.
Fragile, sparse hair and photosensitive skin with nonprogressive intellectual disability define the syndrome; no demonstrated metabolic disorder.
Beta-ketothiolase deficiency disrupts isoleucine and ketone metabolism; permanent neurologic injury affects a minority.
Allergic contact dermatitis due to 2-HEMA is an immune-mediated skin disorder.
Supplied ancestry identifies both an inborn metabolic disorder and an intestinal disorder; aciduria alone does not establish renal damage.
Classified as an inborn error of metabolism; no supplied phenotype evidence supports additional organs.
Historical AIDS-associated dysmorphic syndrome; the supplied record lacks evidence establishing common damage to additional organs.
Histiocytic neoplasm; nervous system infiltration affects about half of reported patients. Other organ involvement varies substantially across presentations.
Congenital absence of a brain structure; associated septo-optic dysplasia does not establish intrinsic ocular or endocrine involvement.
Congenital absence of the heart directly defines the cardiovascular malformation.
The disease is defined by acute lymphoblastic leukemia together with congenital absence of the iris.
Intraepithelial neoplasia of the uterine cervix is confined to a reproductive organ; HPV association does not make the lesion itself an infection.
Congenital absence of the tongue directly affects the oral cavity; situs inversus alone does not establish visceral damage.
Defined by structural malformations of the cerebral cortex.
Neuronal migration disorder defined by cortical and other brain malformations.
Endocrine syndrome with gonadotropin deficiency and estrogen insufficiency causing amenorrhea and galactorrhea.
Retinal ciliopathy umbrella is defined by retinal disease; neurologic ancestry and a deafness-associated subtype do not establish common extraocular injury.
Congenital alopecia and hereditary palmoplantar keratoderma affect hair and skin.
Lysosomal storage disease with characteristic intrinsic immunodeficiency; cognitive and hearing impairment are common (>30%). Major skeletal abnormalities are generally absent in mild type 1.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: intrinsic immune dysfunction is a characteristic component of alpha-mannosidosis, including the mild phenotype; this is more than susceptibility to a separate infection.

basis: Aluminum-associated pulmonary interstitial fibrosis with possible bullous emphysema; no additional organ involvement is established.
Persistent pulmonary vascular hypertension and right-to-left shunting define the disease; hypoxemia alone does not establish lung tissue damage.
Defining syndrome includes hypotrichosis, nail dysplasia and hyperkeratosis together with kyphoscoliosis and cataract.
Defined by poorly controlled childhood diabetes with glycogenic hepatopathy and growth impairment.
Amyloidosis is a protein metabolism/proteostasis disorder; bronchopulmonary deposits occupy airway walls or lung parenchyma and can cause stenosis.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: amyloidosis is a protein metabolism/proteostasis disorder, and its metabolic mechanism remains applicable alongside bronchopulmonary localization.

basis: Benign vascular and smooth-muscle hamartoma, usually within an inguinal lymph node; neither lymphoma nor a skeletal-muscle lesion.
Malignancy arising from vascular endothelium in scalp skin. Lung spread is possible, but the supplied evidence does not establish involvement in >=30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the tumour originates in vascular endothelium, directly involving cutaneous blood vessels; capillaries are included in this axis.

basis: Ankle malformations and short stature identify a skeletal syndrome; no evidence supports additional axes.
Defining congenital anomalies involve eyelid fusion and an imperforate anus.
Congenital cutaneous constriction bands and nail deformities, with hand malformations included in the defining syndrome.
Anophthalmia, cleft palate and mandibular hypoplasia define the syndrome; defining hypospadias is retained as urethral involvement after the three-primary cap.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a defining urethral malformation; urethra belongs to renal. Three primary slots retain the named ocular, palatal and jaw abnormalities.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: micrognathia is defining mandibular skeletal hypoplasia, explicitly named and included in the definition.

basis: Anophthalmia and esophageal atresia define the syndrome; cryptorchidism affects reproductive organs outside the axes.
Defined by absent external ear, congenital facial nerve absence with paralysis, and congenital structural heart disease.
TAP2 antigen-presentation immunodeficiency with defining chronic granulomatous skin ulcers; chronic bronchiectatic airway damage commonly exceeds 30%. Metabolic ancestry is misleading.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: chronic destructive airway disease and bronchiectasis affect >30% over the usual course, beyond isolated episodes of respiratory infection.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: nonhealing ulcerative granulomatous skin lesions are a defining disease manifestation.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: TAP2 deficiency impairs antigen presentation; the supplied metabolic classification does not establish a metabolic disorder.

basis: Arterial dissection and medial degeneration with multiple cutaneous lentigines define the syndrome.
Aortic valve narrowing in childhood directly affects the heart.
Inherited apolipoprotein A-I deficiency disrupts HDL metabolism; premature atherosclerosis is a separate disease risk.
Defined by arthrogryposis, skeletal dysostosis and psychomotor delay; recurrent infections alone do not establish an intrinsic immune defect.
Congenital contractures, CNS dysfunction, and calcification of nervous tissue and skeletal muscle define the syndrome.
Spinal motor neuron disease with congenital joint contractures defining arthrogryposis.
Congenital absence of the sternum; occasional breathing symptoms and associated heart anomalies do not establish common additional organ damage.
Fusion of the atlas and axis involves cervical vertebrae and their articulation; neurologic injury is not intrinsic.
Localized dermal atrophy with depressed plaques; possible relationship to morphea or Borrelia does not establish an immune or infectious mechanism.
Autoimmune injury of the inner ear causes progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Autoimmune inflammation directly damages the myocardium.
BK polyomavirus directly infects and damages renal tissue; the supplied hantavirus parent is inconsistent with the named infection.
Carotidynia is classified here as a carotid artery disorder; facial pain alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Keratotic lesion of gingival oral mucosa; malignant transformation is a later risk.
Supplied definition describes autoimmune thyroid disease driven by TSH-receptor autoimmunity; the name alone does not establish direct CNS damage.
Craniofacial/cervical bone dysplasia and severe periodontal destruction define this syndrome. [Case report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7811426/)

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: severe destruction of the periodontium is a defining feature of craniofaciocervical osteoglyphic dysplasia; gums and tooth-supporting oral tissues are gastrointestinal.

basis: Oculocerebral malformation syndrome; microphthalmia and optic nerve dysplasia establish ocular disease, with cerebellar disease supported by ancestry.
Inflammatory vasculitis of CNS blood vessels defines neurologic, vascular and immune involvement.
Extrauterine smooth-muscle tumour nodules predominantly occupy the lungs; uterine origin is outside the axes. Heart and spinal involvement are rare.
The cataract parent establishes ocular disease; supplied information does not establish additional organ involvement.
Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia is a cardiac rhythm disorder; no underlying systemic cause is specified.
Both kidneys are absent; consequent prolonged oligohydramnios causes severe pulmonary hypoplasia in most affected pregnancies.
Intrahepatic bile duct atresia causes biliary obstruction and cholestatic liver damage.
Intrahepatic bile duct atresia defines hepatic disease; the unspecified syndromic designation does not establish another affected organ.
Bilirubin directly injures the neonatal brain; persistent auditory neuropathy/hearing loss is a major diagnostic feature of chronic kernicterus. No intrinsic hepatic disease is implied.

decisions.otologic: involved: persistent auditory neuropathy/hearing loss is a major diagnostic feature of chronic bilirubin brain injury, supporting inclusion without a numerical frequency.

basis: Carcinoma arising in the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
Defining blepharophimosis and lacrimal duct anomalies affect the ocular axis; thickened facial skin and interdigital webbing affect skin.
The concept and its skeletal dysplasia parent establish a bone disorder; no additional organ involvement is documented.
Skeletal dysplasia and agenesis of the corpus callosum define the syndrome.
Congenital shortening of digits with absent distal phalanges defines skeletal involvement.
Brachydactyly is a digital skeletal malformation; anonychia is congenital absence of nails.
Brachydactyly defines skeletal malformation; short stature and facial anomalies alone do not establish endocrine or additional organ disease.
Brachydactyly and tibial hypoplasia are structural skeletal abnormalities; no other organ involvement is supplied.
Brenner tumor of the vagina affects a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Lethal OI-spectrum bone fragility; pulmonary hypoplasia directly impairs lung function and contributes to respiratory failure in most perinatally lethal cases.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is common in perinatally lethal OI (>30%); structural lung underdevelopment qualifies beyond mechanical chest restriction.

basis: Childhood adenomas/carcinoids arise in the bronchi; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Bronchiectasis is defining structural airway damage; oligospermia affects the reproductive system outside the axes.
Syndrome defined by mesomelic skeletal abnormalities and ectodermal dysplasia affecting skin appendages.
Localized autoimmune scarring pemphigoid, typically affecting scalp and head skin; significant mucosal involvement is generally absent.
Burning mouth syndrome is defined by oral burning pain; psychiatric comorbidity does not remove its oral localization.
Inherited glycosylation disorder establishes the metabolic axis; this unspecified subtype has no supplied phenotype supporting additional organs.
CDK4-associated melanoma is a cutaneous melanocytic malignancy; genetic association alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Defined by camptodactyly, joint contractures and facial skeletal dysplasia; associated clubfoot and dysostosis are skeletal.
Congenital finger contractures and sacral vertebral fusion define skeletal involvement.
Fungal infection defined by its organism; no single anatomical site applies across localized and invasive presentations.
Tentative craniocardioskeletal identification; cutis laxa is characteristic in the original four cases. [Report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7151302/)

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac malformations define the tentatively identified craniocardioskeletal syndrome; exact eponym mapping remains uncertain.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is characteristic of the tentatively identified craniocardioskeletal syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: characteristic cutis laxa in the original four-case description; this assignment does not assume classic Cantu hypertrichosis.

basis: Childhood carcinoids arise predominantly in the appendix/GI tract. Neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine-gland or metabolic disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: neuroendocrine lineage alone does not establish disease of an endocrine gland or a metabolic disorder.

basis: Carcinoma involves the laryngeal vocal fold, part of the pulmonary axis.
Echinococcal hydatid cysts directly occupy cardiac tissue and expand into a heart chamber; other infection sites are not established as common in this concept.
Defined by combined cardiomyopathy, encephalopathy and skeletal myopathy; no specific metabolic mechanism is established by this record.
Sparse concept: the name indicates cardiac abnormalities and shortened limbs; no definition or phenotypes support additional axes.
Cardiomelic malformation syndrome defined by congenital cardiac and limb abnormalities; supplied record lacks detailed phenotype frequencies.
Cardiomyopathy and hearing loss define the syndrome; accompanying myopathy and ataxia have no established frequency of at least 30%.
The defining triad comprises cardiomyopathy, diabetes and deafness.
Anthracycline-induced myocardial disease; cardiac damage defines this concept.
Defining manifestations are cardiomyopathy, gonadal hormone deficiency and cutaneous collagenomas.
Cardiomyopathy, endocrine hypogonadism and metabolic abnormalities define this sparsely described metabolic syndrome.
The syndrome is defined by cardiomyopathy and spherocytosis, affecting cardiac muscle and red blood cells.
Recessive carpal and tarsal osteolysis directly destroys bone; the supplied record does not establish common renal or other organ involvement.
Cassava-associated cyanogenic poisoning causes persistent toxic neurologic injury with ataxic neuropathy or spastic motor impairment.
Inherited cataract affects the lens; additional organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Inherited congenital cataract affecting the ocular lens; no established extraocular involvement.
The syndrome name identifies cataract and skeletal anomalies as defining features; no further phenotype details are supplied.
Congenital absence of the cerebellum is a structural central nervous system disorder.
Degeneration of the cerebellum; autoimmune mechanisms apply only to a subset of this etiologically heterogeneous group.
Atrophy of the cerebellum and inferior olivary nuclei directly affects the central nervous system.
Cerebral calcification and cerebellar hypoplasia define a structural brain disorder.
Named syndrome combines cerebral calcifications, abnormal teeth and renal phosphate wasting. No definition establishes systemic phosphate depletion or another metabolic disorder.

decisions.renal: primary: pathological phosphaturia identifies renal phosphate wasting as a defining component of the named syndrome.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: phosphaturia alone does not establish systemic hypophosphataemia or an independent metabolic disorder; renal phosphate loss is already represented.

basis: Cerebral motor-control injury causes dyskinesia; limb movements and feeding difficulty do not independently establish muscle or gastrointestinal damage.
Cerebral motor-system injury causes persistent unilateral spastic weakness; secondary skeletal damage is not established here.
Cerebral motor-system disorder causing spastic paralysis of one limb; no evidence supplied of common structural muscle or joint damage.
Inherited porphyrin metabolism disorder; acute neurovisceral symptoms do not establish lasting neurologic or gastrointestinal damage in at least 30%.
Hindbrain malformation with an occipital or high cervical encephalocele through a defining skull or vertebral defect.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the occipital or upper cervical bony defect containing the encephalocele is a defining structural component of Chiari III.

basis: Congenital cerebellar hypoplasia or aplasia defines this historical Chiari subtype.
Umbrella disorder of cartilage and skeletal development; other organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Chondrodysplasia with deficient steroid sulfate metabolism; steroid sulfatase deficiency typically causes ichthyosis in most affected patients.
Name indicates chorea with amyotrophy and acanthocytosis; no definition or phenotype data establish additional direct organ involvement.
Cyst located in the choroid plexus of the brain.
Umbrella for occupationally caused lung and airway disease; an immune mechanism does not apply uniformly across the group.
Retinal and choroidal degeneration with pituitary hormone deficiency define the syndrome.
Occupational asthma is airway disease; sensitizer-induced immune mechanisms predominate across the group, although irritant-induced forms occur.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: sensitizer-induced immune asthma accounts for >90% of occupational cases in this [review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC151995/); umbrella rules require most, not all.

basis: Inhaled mixed mineral dust causes pulmonary interstitial injury and fibrosis.
Developmental impairment reported with this rare chromosomal syndrome supports a tentative neurologic label; the supplied record lacks phenotype details.
Congenital non-neoplastic skin malformation; neighboring mucosal involvement is not established as common.
Severe Rubinstein-Taybi phenotype supports developmental intellectual impairment and characteristic skeletal/limb malformations; other organ frequencies are unspecified.
Listed constitutional deletion syndromes predominantly affect brain development or peripheral nerves; variable deletion extent prevents consistent additional organ labels.
Rare mosaic chromosomal disorder associated with developmental impairment; supplied data do not establish common damage to other organs.
Vertebral malformations and learning disability characterize the symptomatic phenotype; most prenatal mosaics are normal, making penetrance uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: primary: learning disability characterizes the described symptomatic phenotype; penetrance across predominantly normal prenatal mosaics is uncertain.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: vertebral malformations characterize the described symptomatic phenotype; uncertain penetrance precludes claiming common secondary organ damage.

basis: Rare mosaic monosomy 22 is associated with developmental impairment; absent phenotype data limits confidence and prevents additional organ labels.
Craniofacial skeletal defects, microcephaly and congenital heart disease are defining. Cleft palate is a common major structural feature; ear malformations are omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is explicitly a common major structural feature; retained alongside the three defining skeletal, neurologic and cardiac axes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: midface hypoplasia and other cranial skeletal abnormalities are explicitly part of the defining congenital phenotype.
decisions.otologic: none at cap: common malformed ears are described, but their functional severity is unspecified; major skeletal, brain, cardiac and palatal defects take priority.

basis: Developmental impairment spans major 22q deletion syndromes; cardiac, immune and endocrine abnormalities depend on deletion region, with no established umbrella-wide frequency.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac defects are common in 22q11.2 deletion, but an umbrella-wide frequency of at least 30% is not established.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypoparathyroidism and hypocalcemia are region-specific; persistent endocrine dysfunction is not established as common across this umbrella.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: immunodeficiency characterizes some 22q11.2 deletions, not chromosome 22q deletions generally; no umbrella-wide frequency is established.

basis: Poorly specified chromosome 3 duplication; neurodevelopmental impairment is typical, but duplication extent and additional organ frequencies are unknown.
Typical 4p deletion causes neurodevelopmental impairment; skeletal abnormalities occur in ~60-70%, congenital heart defects ~40-50%, and hearing impairment ~40%.

decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects approximately 40% of the predominant Wolf-Hirschhorn phenotype, supporting common auditory dysfunction.

basis: IgM-associated chronic demyelinating neuropathy is immune mediated; monoclonal IgM alone does not establish blood-cell or marrow damage.
Chronic inflammatory polyradiculoneuropathy affects peripheral nerves and nerve roots, typically through immune-mediated injury.
Airway ciliary dysfunction with structural bronchiectasis defines the concept; other organ involvement is not established by the supplied record.
Congenital localized absence of skin at the scalp vertex.
Named cutaneous keratinization disorder; no evidence supports additional organ involvement.
HHV8-associated vascular endothelial sarcoma predominantly arising in skin. Pulmonary and gastrointestinal spread occur in a minority of classic cases.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the defining vascular endothelial sarcoma arises in cutaneous microvasculature, which falls within the vessel axis.

basis: Cleft lip/palate with lower-lip mucous cysts affects oral structures, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cleft lip and palate establish an oral structural defect; no definition or phenotype evidence supports additional organs.
The syndrome explicitly combines oral clefting, intellectual disability and corneal opacity; no additional organ evidence supplied.

Cleft lip/palate and pituitary hormone deficiency define the syndrome.
Defining cleft lip/palate affects oral structures, while tetraphocomelia is a severe structural defect of all four limbs.
Lower-lip cleft and lateral canthal/chorioretinal abnormalities define the syndrome; additional organ involvement is unsupported.
Defining malformations affect the palate, heart and digits.

The named defining malformations affect the oral palate, heart and limbs; no additional organ involvement is established.
Congenital cleft of the tongue; the tongue belongs to the oral gastrointestinal axis.
Poorly characterized syndrome named for hypotonia and constipation; motor and intestinal dysfunction inferred, with no established endocrine cause.
Pain disorder localized to the coccyx, commonly following local skeletal injury.
Inborn mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex III deficiency; supplied evidence does not establish a common organ-specific injury pattern.
Cold-triggered mast-cell-mediated urticaria defines a skin and immune-mediated disorder; systemic reactions do not establish lasting additional organ damage.
Skeletal cartilage disease defines the group; vitreoretinal abnormalities and high myopia commonly exceed 30% across its major clinical phenotypes.
Reported short broad great toes and intellectual disability define this sparsely documented syndrome. [Description](https://checkorphan.org/disease/collins-sakati-syndrome/)

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: short, broad great toes are reported as a defining skeletal malformation; evidence is sparse.

basis: The defining abnormalities affect the eye, cerebral tissue and urinary collecting system.
Descriptive congenital syndrome defined by ocular colobomata, abnormal lung lobation and a heart defect; detailed phenotype data unavailable.
Colonic malakoplakia is macrophage-rich inflammatory disease associated with defective bacterial clearance; no other organ involvement established.
Complement receptor dysfunction defines an immunodeficiency; no common direct organ damage is established.
Congenital absence of a skeletal neck muscle; no additional organ involvement specified.
Congenital absence of a limb or limb segment is a structural defect of the locomotor system.
Congenital aneurysmal structural disease of the great vessels.
Congenital joint rigidity defines a musculoskeletal disorder; no additional organ involvement is established.
Congenital spinal muscular atrophy identifies a motor neuron disorder; no supplied evidence establishes direct muscle disease or another organ lesion.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: neurogenic muscle wasting results from motor neuron dysfunction; the sparse record provides no evidence of direct skeletal muscle disease.

basis: Congenital abnormal communication within the cardiovascular circulation.
Congenital joint contractures define a disorder of the locomotor system.
Congenital craniosynostosis directly affects skull bones; maternal hyperthyroiditis does not by itself establish endocrine disease in the affected child.
Congenital malformation replacing the developing eye with a cyst; intracranial anomalies are not established across the umbrella concept.
Syndrome explicitly defined by congenital cystic eye and associated intracranial malformations.
Congenital heart disease, hypodontia and craniosynostosis define the syndrome; ptosis is a defining ocular criterion.
Defining triad comprises congenital heart disease, radioulnar bony fusion and intellectual disability.
Congenitally acquired HIV infection with immune dysfunction; additional organ damage is not intrinsic or established as common.
Congenital hypotrichosis and milia affect hair follicles and skin.
Congenital mumps virus infection; supplied ancestry establishes infection but no characteristic damaged organ or common congenital organ sequelae.
The supplied parent identifies inherited obstructive jaundice of infancy, supporting hepatobiliary disease; a specific bilirubin metabolic defect is not established.
Congenital narrowing of the cervical spinal canal is a structural skeletal disorder; cord injury is not established by the supplied record.
Severe Hallermann-Streiff phenotype supports ocular, craniofacial skeletal and skin defects; dental abnormalities are a major diagnostic feature. Evidence is limited to one family.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental abnormalities are a major diagnostic feature of the Hallermann-Streiff phenotype specified by the definition; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: skin atrophy and hypotrichosis are defining features of the Hallermann-Streiff phenotype, of which this is a severe form.

basis: Congenital underdevelopment of one lung directly affects pulmonary anatomy and functional reserve.
Name indicates congenital vagal autonomic reflex dysfunction; sparse record provides no evidence of additional organ damage.
Congenital two-chambered heart malformation.
The named syndrome comprises corneal crystalline pathology, myopathy and neuropathy. No definition or phenotype data clarify the corneal findings or support additional axes.

decisions.ocular: primary: corneal pathology is a defining component of the named syndrome; the record does not establish that these are non-impairing incidental deposits.

basis: Corneal dystrophy, ichthyosis, microcephaly and intellectual disability explicitly define the syndrome.
Descriptive syndrome identifies corneal dystrophy, pigmentary abnormalities and intestinal malabsorption as defining features; detailed phenotype unavailable.
Callosal agenesis and blepharophimosis identify defining brain and eyelid malformations; insufficient detail to assign additional organs.
Congenital dysgenesis of the corpus callosum.

Corpus callosum maldevelopment and pituitary hormone deficiency define the syndrome.
Skeletal and craniofacial developmental defects support musculoskeletal localization; no additional organ involvement is documented.
Craniofacial dysostosis and arthrogryposis define skeletal disease; progeroid appearance alone does not establish direct skin damage.
Craniofrontonasal malformation supports skeletal involvement; no definition or phenotypes establish additional axes.
Concept denotes cataract with premature cranial suture fusion, affecting lens and skull.

Craniosynostosis directly affects skull bones and sutures; common neurologic injury is not established for this subtype.
Descriptive syndrome comprises craniosynostosis, alopecia and brain malformation; supporting clinical details are sparse.
Named syndrome combines cranial bone fusion, joint contractures and cleft palate; the palate belongs to the mouth axis.
Premature fusion of cranial bone sutures; common direct neurologic damage is not established for this umbrella concept.
Defining skull synostosis and joint contractures affect skeleton; cleft lip/palate affects oral structures.
Craniosynostosis and joint contractures define skeletal involvement; associated cleft lip/palate affects oral structures.
Named syndrome combines craniosynostosis and exostoses, cutaneous nevus, and epibulbar dermoid; limited additional characterization.
Named syndrome combines craniosynostosis, intellectual disability and structural heart defects, defining all three axes.
Immune-mediated Crohn inflammation directly affects the esophagus.
Cold-precipitating fibrin proteins cause thrombotic vasculopathy; ischemic skin ulceration or necrosis occurs in roughly half of symptomatic cases. Autoimmunity is not intrinsic.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: occlusive thrombotic vasculopathy is a defining manifestation of pathogenic cryofibrinogen precipitation.

basis: Sclerosis of skin; no evidence establishes an autoimmune mechanism or systemic organ involvement.
Cutis gyratum and acanthosis nigricans affect skin; craniosynostosis is a defining skull bone abnormality.
Named combination of cutis laxa and osteoporosis establishes skin and bone involvement; no evidence supplied for additional organs.
Cutis verticis gyrata with intellectual disability defines both scalp skin and neurodevelopmental involvement.
Cytokine receptor dysfunction classified as an immune-system disorder; no specific extraimmune organ injury is established.
Named constellation comprises a cerebellar malformation, a nasopharyngeal tumor and a congenital defect of the diaphragm, a skeletal muscle.
Conductive deafness and stapedial ear malformation define otologic disease; associated facial palsy establishes facial nerve dysfunction.
Named syndrome combines deafness, thyroid enlargement and stippled skeletal epiphyses; no further descriptive evidence supplied.
Deafness, metacarpal/metatarsal synostosis and urethral hypospadias define syndrome; developmental/intellectual impairment in both reported cases (2/2).

basis: The syndrome is defined by deafness, small-bowel diverticula and neuropathy; no additional organ involvement is documented.

Fanconi tubular solute wasting defines renal and electrolyte/acid-base disease; ichthyosis defines skin involvement. Jaundice and diarrhea alone do not establish additional organ damage.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: Fanconi syndrome entails proximal tubular solute wasting, including phosphate and bicarbonate, constituting an electrolyte/acid-base disorder.

basis: Inherited apolipoprotein B-100 dysfunction causes a lipid metabolic disorder; atherosclerotic disease is a separate consequence.
Dermatocardioskeletal syndrome denotes defining skin, cardiac and skeletal abnormalities; no detailed definition or phenotype frequencies are supplied.
Astrocytic tumor involving cerebral cortex and leptomeninges; isolated hypotropia does not establish common independent ocular damage.
Neuronal-glial tumor arising in cerebral cortex and leptomeninges; hypotropia alone does not establish ocular damage.
Defined by congenital cardiac malposition. Mirror-image abdominal organs do not imply damage; associated heart defects and ciliary disease affect a minority.
Localized benign breast lesions; associated diabetes is a separate disease, and an autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Defining diaphragm and radius defects affect skeletal muscle and bone; omphalocele involves congenital herniation of abdominal viscera. Lung damage frequency is unspecified.
Defined by a diaphragmatic defect, omphalocele with herniated abdominal viscera, and agenesis of the corpus callosum.
Congenital diaphragm and upper-limb defects; direct developmental pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in >30% of typical congenital diaphragmatic hernia, although syndrome-specific data are absent.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: developmental lung hypoplasia from congenital diaphragmatic herniation is common (>30% in the usual course); confidence is limited by absent syndrome-specific frequencies.

basis: Avascular necrosis of the metacarpal head is a localized bone disorder.
Benign vascular tumor arising in and occupying the rectum; both rectal location and blood-vessel origin define it.
Proliferation of pulmonary neuroendocrine cells directly affects the lungs; neuroendocrine lineage does not establish endocrine dysfunction.

Dermal dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans variant containing pigmented dendritic cells.

decisions.dermatologic: none: defining nail or skin abnormalities are not documented for this overlap phenotype; ectodermal-dysplasia ancestry alone does not establish damage.

audit_reason: Add primary haematologic: Neorickettsia directly infects monocytes/macrophages, producing a mononucleosis-like human disease; blood-cell occupation supports the axis.

basis: Disorders of central cognitive processing and perception, including neglect and agnosia; sensory-organ damage is not required.
Inflammation of tendon and ligament insertions into bone; enthesitis alone does not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Contractures define musculoskeletal involvement; short stature and hypotonia alone do not establish endocrine or neurologic disease.
Defined as impaired cognitive processing of sound despite intact auditory pathways; peripheral ear damage is not established.
Central sensory-processing disorder causing perceptual distortions; no intrinsic eye disease.
Neurological mislocalization of sensory stimuli defines the disorder.
Disorder of bilirubin metabolism; hyperbilirubinemia alone does not establish liver injury, and neurologic injury is confined to particular severe forms.
Disease directly involving a peripheral nerve plexus.
Disease is located in the sacral peripheral nerve plexus.
Limb and skeletal malformations define Robinow syndrome; gingival overgrowth and short lingual frenulum each occur in 3/6, retained primary teeth in 2/6.
Congenital iris and anterior chamber angle dysgenesis; associated cerebellar abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Progressive central and peripheral neuroaxonal degeneration; optic atrophy in 4/6 patients supports direct ocular involvement.
Umbrella disorder of vision; neurologic involvement is limited to particular subtypes.
Bacterial infection of the intestine caused by Aeromonas hydrophila.
Benign diffuse proliferation of blood vessels; infectious mechanisms apply to particular subtypes rather than the entire umbrella.
The definition specifies inherited susceptibility rather than existing melanoma or skin damage; future tumour risk does not establish organ involvement.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the concept denotes predisposition only; assigning skin damage would label a later risk as existing disease.

basis: Ovarian dysgenesis causes primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins; osteoporosis frequency is unspecified.
POU1F1-related pituitary hormone deficiency; growth failure reflects endocrine dysfunction; common direct extraendocrine damage is not established.
Inherited surfactant processing/homeostasis disorder causes alveolar and interstitial lung disease. Pulmonary hypertension and developmental delay each affect only 2/17.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: this is an inherited disorder of surfactant metabolism, so the metabolic mechanism axis applies alongside pulmonary.

basis: Isolated congenital facial nerve dysfunction; orbicularis weakness and reduced corneal reflex do not establish intrinsic ocular disease.
Apocrine sweat glands are cutaneous structures; no mechanism applies across all constituent disorders.
Disease of the anterior pituitary endocrine gland; its intracranial location alone does not establish neurologic involvement.
Cartilage-producing mesenchymal neoplasm, represented by osteochondroma, chondroblastoma and chondrosarcoma.
Benign neoplasm arising from cartilage-producing cells.
Renal insufficiency, thrombocytopenia and skin detachment each have HPO frequency 30-79%; detachment indicates tissue damage. Transient exanthem and isolated transaminase elevation excluded.

decisions.haematologic: involved: thrombocytopenia occurs in 30-79%, supporting intrinsic blood-cell involvement during infection.
decisions.cardiovascular: none: endothelial tropism alone does not establish clinically damaging vascular disease; annotated vasculitis occurs in only 1-4%.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: skin detachment occurs in 30-79% and represents tissue injury, beyond a transient exanthem.

basis: Spotted-fever rickettsiae infect vascular endothelium and cause small-vessel vasculitis. The transient exanthem does not establish additional skin damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: vascular endothelium is the principal infected tissue, with direct small-vessel inflammation characteristic of spotted-fever rickettsiosis.

basis: Epithelial neoplasm originating in the rectum.
Neoplasms arise in liver or intrahepatic bile ducts; endocrine and lymphoma labels do not apply across this umbrella.
Site-unspecified umbrella; hepatic assignment is provisional from the usual clinical entity. Hepatic and subcutaneous subtypes limit certainty; mesenchymal histology does not prove locomotor origin.

decisions.hepatic: primary: provisional assignment to the usual hepatic presentation of mesenchymal hamartoma; the site-unspecified umbrella and nonhepatic child make this uncertain.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: mesenchymal histology alone does not establish bone, joint, skeletal muscle or locomotor connective-tissue origin; no such site is specified.

basis: Epithelial neoplasm arising in the colon.
Skin disease specifically involving the eyelid, which is included in the ocular axis.
Umbrella disorder of cutaneous appendages, including hair, nails and skin glands.
Localized hamartomatous malformation of cutaneous eccrine sweat glands.
Hyperplastic proliferation of the urinary tract urothelium.
Hyperplasia of urinary tract urothelium; possible association with later neoplasia does not add another organ axis.
Infectious process directly affecting the nail.
CNS glioma phenotype defines this susceptibility concept; the label identifies its tumor site and does not imply a tumor is present in every carrier.
A vascular neoplasm arising in bone involves osseous tissue and local vascular tissue; no common distant organ damage is established.
Neoplasm originating in the duodenum; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish a separate endocrine disorder.
Neoplasm originates in the appendix; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Neoplasm arising in the gallbladder; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Digestive-system tumor origin defines this umbrella; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease. Pancreatic endocrine tumors are a subset.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: neuroendocrine differentiation is not itself endocrine-gland disease; this umbrella also includes nonfunctional digestive carcinomas.

basis: Serotonin-producing pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor; endocrine origin determines the axis. Liver metastasis and carcinoid syndrome are conditional complications.
Adams-Oliver syndrome is defined by aplasia cutis and terminal limb reduction defects; cardiac and brain anomalies are variable without established >=30% frequency for this subtype.
Isolated aniridia with foveal hypoplasia and other ocular abnormalities; extraocular findings lack evidence of common involvement.
Reflex epilepsy triggered by hot water; no additional organ disease established.
Inherited hidradenitis suppurativa causes chronic autoinflammatory follicular destruction, abscesses and scarring.
Multiple peripheral, spinal or intracranial schwannomas define the disorder; nerve-origin tumors remain neurologic even when superficially located.
Secondary elevation of blood platelets defines the condition; an underlying infection or inflammatory disease is separate and does not make thrombocytosis an immune disorder.
Renal agenesis/hypodysplasia; associated developmental sequence includes pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/3 and structural clubfoot in 3/3.
Congenital renal agenesis or hypodysplasia; renal agenesis reported in 11/14 patients.
Familial aneurysmal disease of the abdominal aortic wall.
Localized cutaneous amyloid deposition with lichenification and pruritus in 16/16; systemic organ involvement is not part of this condition.
Inherited aortic valve malformation, calcification and stenosis; other reported abnormalities are also cardiovascular.
Inherited cutaneous pigmentation disorder characterized by generalized hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules.
Proximal tubular dysfunction causes solute wasting and metabolic acidosis (28/28). Osteomalacia is reported without evidence establishing a frequency of at least 30%.
Seizures/ID 6/6, gingival overgrowth 5/6 and hallmark nail defects define the syndrome; scoliosis 4/6 and distal phalangeal hypoplasia 3/5 support skeletal involvement.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: nail aplasia/hypoplasia is a defining Zimmermann-Laband feature; anonychia occurs in 3/5 assessed patients.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: scoliosis 4/6 and distal phalangeal hypoplasia 3/5; the three primary slots prioritize neurologic, gingival and nail hallmarks.

basis: Fibronectin deposition damages renal glomeruli; secondary hypertension and renal acidosis do not establish additional organ disease.
Mitochondrial myopathy defines ophthalmoplegia; parkinsonism in 2/2 and sensory neuropathy in 1/2 support neurologic involvement, though samples are small.
Familial mitral valve prolapse with regurgitation. Frequencies and functional significance of accompanying skeletal features are not established.
Collagen VI myopathy causes muscle degeneration and contractures. Skin and renal findings in single patients do not establish common damaging involvement.

decisions.dermatologic: none: keratosis pilaris/hyperkeratosis in 1/1 assessed patient does not establish damaging skin involvement in at least 30% of this subtype.

basis: Tubular aggregates, muscle fiber atrophy and weakness define skeletal myopathy; ophthalmoplegia 2/11 and respiratory insufficiency are below 30%.
Syndrome combines ear malformations and hearing loss with characteristic craniofacial, cervical and shoulder skeletal abnormalities.
Pulmonary arterial remodeling and hypertension with right-heart injury are cardiovascular; no separate lung parenchymal disease is established.
KRT5-related reticulate skin pigmentation disorder; no evidence of systemic metabolic disease or other organ dysfunction.
Interferonopathy with defining skeletal disease and aortic/valvular calcification; dental damage ~90%; glaucoma 50% omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Adrenal ACTH resistance causes cortisol deficiency and hypoglycemia; pigmentation and acute hypoglycemic events do not establish other organ damage.
Riboflavin transporter deficiency causes pontobulbar neuropathy; sensorineural deafness is a defining BVVL feature despite hearing loss recorded in only 2/9 here.
Primary brain calcification disorder; local calcification does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder or additional vascular dysfunction.
Inherited chorioretinal degeneration; choriocapillaris atrophy is local ocular pathology, not systemic vascular disease.
Long-QT cardiac channelopathy and congenital sensorineural hearing loss are defining features, both documented in 9/9 patients.
Defining enteropathy, hepatic fibrosis 14/27 and immunodeficiency 11/12; neurodevelopmental delay 10/16 (~63%). Hair-shaft disease 22/22 omitted at cap in favor of more severe organ dysfunction.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic disease is named and defining; fibrosis occurs in 14/27 (~52%).
decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in 10/16 (~63%); retained for its functional severity.
decisions.dermatologic: none: defining hair-shaft defects occur in 22/22, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of enteropathy, immunodeficiency, hepatic fibrosis and neurodevelopmental impairment.

basis: Cerebellar hypoplasia, ataxia and intellectual disability define it; persistent strabismus in 4/4; pes planus in 4/4 does not alone establish damaging skeletal dysfunction.
Corneal thinning and rupture define disease; joint laxity/scoliosis affect most, and hearing impairment occurs in approximately 30-50%.
Dysferlin-related dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle; reduced reflexes do not establish a separate neuropathy.
Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy features periosteal bone and joint disease with pachydermia; cardiac involvement is not established at 30%.
Pancreatic agenesis directly eliminates exocrine and endocrine function; exocrine insufficiency and neonatal insulin deficiency are defining manifestations.
Inherited skin barrier disorder with peeling and erythroderma; elevated IgE and eosinophils do not establish immune deficiency. Asthma occurs in only 1/4.
Isolated congenital small eye with coloboma.
Skeletal dysplasia; hearing impairment in 6/9 and intellectual disability in 10/30 support involvement; absent sinuses alone do not establish airway dysfunction.
Primary immunodeficiency with B-cell lymphoproliferation; HLH and lymphoma are separate complications. Hepatomegaly alone does not prove injury; liver failure reported in 17%.
Defining linear skin defects (11/11) and microphthalmia (10/11); neurologic, cardiac and hearing abnormalities are minority findings.
Defining myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia; intellectual disability 1/2. Retinopathy 1/2 omitted at cap; restrictive ventilation may reflect myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 1/2 supports direct neurodevelopmental impairment; prioritized at the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: none: pigmentary retinopathy in 1/2 qualifies, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of substantial neurodevelopmental impairment.

basis: D2HGDH-related organic acid metabolic disorder; developmental delay and seizures each occur in 2/2 annotated patients. Cardiomyopathy is not established as common in type 1.
Cerebral white-matter disease with subcortical cysts, seizures, ataxia and developmental impairment.
DEPDC5-related focal epilepsy, often with cortical dysplasia; all established defining injury is neurologic.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration and movement disorder; abnormal eye movements are neurologic. Hypogonadism and skeletal abnormalities are occasional.
Radioulnar fusion and deficient marrow megakaryocytes with thrombocytopenia define the syndrome; hearing-loss frequency is unestablished.
Familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection; cardiac and vascular abnormalities share this axis. Stroke is occasional.
Patent ductus arteriosus is a congenital cardiovascular malformation.
Inherited macular retinal dystrophy causing visual impairment; no established extraocular disease.
Inherited cardiac conduction disorder with sinus node dysfunction, bradycardia and other rhythm abnormalities.
Brain and retinal disease define syndrome; pathological fractures 8/12, GI telangiectasia with bleeding ~46%. Anemia and nail dystrophy ~38% omitted by cap.
Ectodermal dysplasia involves hair, nails and tooth enamel/shape; syndactyly defines the limb component.
Inherited febrile seizure disorder; additional reported findings remain neurologic.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; optic atrophy and joint contractures each reported in 2/2, scoliosis in 1/2; these establish eye and skeletal involvement.
Recurrent infantile hepatic failure defines the syndrome; anemia and neurodevelopmental impairment are common, each in roughly >30%.
Optic atrophy defines disease; mitral prolapse in 3/5 and auditory dysfunction in 3/5, with sensorineural hearing impairment reported.
GCM2-related primary hyperparathyroidism; osteopenia occurs in 3/19 and kidney stones in 4/19, both below 30%. Stones are also separately diagnosed.
Umbrella for disorders arising from AIDS-related immunodeficiency; no single additional organ is consistently affected across its subtypes.
Umbrella of disorders arising in immunodeficiency; no specific damaged anatomical organ is shared across the group.
Inherited hypertrophy of cardiac muscle; syndromic children do not establish extracardiac involvement across this umbrella.
Von Willebrand factor deficiency or dysfunction causes a coagulation disorder. Bleeding sites do not establish separate organ damage.
Obstetric umbrella concept; no organ axis applies consistently across its diverse pregnancy-related subtypes.
Umbrella for male reproductive organ tumors; endocrine dysfunction and damage to an included organ are not defining across the group.
Muscular dystrophy, cataracts and intellectual disability define the syndrome; cataracts occur in 12/12; respiratory insufficiency is occasional.
Carcinoma arising in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes. HPV is a risk factor and does not make the carcinoma an infectious disease.
Defined by parasitic infection or infestation affecting the skin.
Neoplasm occupying the orbital region; skull ancestry alone does not establish a bone-origin tumour across this group.
Manic phase of a psychiatric mood disorder; no covered organ disease is intrinsic.
Depressive episode of bipolar disorder is psychiatric without defined organ damage.
Purely psychiatric depressive disorder without specified damage to an organ axis.
T-cell/NK-cell lymphoid malignancy umbrella includes leukemias and lymphomas; no additional organ is consistently involved across subtypes.
Tympanic membrane inflammation defines the disease. The umbrella includes noninfectious forms; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: the definition establishes inflammation, without establishing infection, autoimmunity or another immune-mediated disease across the umbrella.

basis: Usually a localized cutaneous histiocytic proliferation; extracutaneous disease is uncommon. Tissue histiocyte lineage alone does not establish blood or marrow disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: localized tissue histiocyte proliferation does not establish a disease of circulating blood cells, marrow or coagulation.

basis: Poliovirus infection is usually asymptomatic or mild; destructive neurologic disease occurs in a small minority across this infection umbrella.
Infection directly affects the brain, spinal cord or their coverings.
Poliovirus infection directly inflames the central nervous system meninges.
Adenocarcinoma arising from follicular cells of the thyroid endocrine gland.
Defined anatomical umbrella for ear, nose and throat disease; nose, pharynx and larynx belong to the pulmonary axis.
Disease of the lacrimal gland; immune mechanisms and other organ involvement are subtype dependent.
Functional disease of phagocytic blood cells causes immunodeficiency; abnormal counts are not required for the blood-cell axis. Other affected sites vary across subtypes.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a disease of phagocytic blood-cell function; the rule includes blood-cell diseases without requiring cytopenias, marrow failure or coagulopathy.

basis: Functional disorder of phagocytic white blood cells and host defense; no additional organ damage applies across the umbrella.
Intrinsic dysfunction of phagocytic blood cells impairs chemotaxis and innate immunity; no specific additional organ damage established.
Defective opsonization is an immune-function disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
Defined by chronic hypertension with resultant renal vascular and glomerular damage.
Anatomical umbrella for diseases involving the large intestine; no additional mechanism applies across the group.
Umbrella defined by disease of the small intestine; no additional mechanism or organ applies across subtypes.
Defined by inflammation of a cardiac layer; an infectious, autoimmune or immune-mediated etiology is not established by inflammation alone.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: generic cardiac inflammation does not establish infection or an autoimmune/immune-mediated mechanism across this umbrella.

basis: Malignancy arising in connective and soft tissues; no additional organ is consistently affected across this umbrella.
Gastrin-secreting pancreatic endocrine tumor; acid-mediated gastroduodenal ulceration occurs in most patients and defines its Zollinger-Ellison functional syndrome.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in gastric mucosa; serotonin production alone does not establish endocrine disease, and carcinoid syndrome is occasional.
Neuroendocrine tumor originates in the stomach; endocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Umbrella disorder of heart muscle; immune mechanisms do not apply across the group.
Insufficient myocardial blood supply causes cardiac dysfunction and potentially myocardial necrosis.
Calculi occupy the urinary tract; no metabolic disorder is inherent to the umbrella diagnosis.
Meningeal tumour of the CNS visual pathway; central visual dysfunction alone does not establish direct ocular damage.
Astrocytoma of the CNS optic tract; visual loss from tract injury does not itself establish direct eye damage.
Drug-induced loss of bone mass and strength defines this disease; an intrinsic endocrine disorder is not required.
Corticosteroid-induced loss of bone mass defines this disease; drug causation does not exclude its defining bone involvement.
Embryonic cyst confined to the fallopian tube or adjacent reproductive structures; no covered organ axis.
Neoplasm of skull bones; neural, sinus and orbital sites occur in subtypes and do not apply across the umbrella.
Disorder of skull structures under bone disease; other organ axes apply only to particular subtypes.
Immune-mediated rheumatic inflammation of the pericardium.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the colon or rectum; gastrointestinal origin and lymphoma mechanism define the axes.
Sarcoma arising in extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
HHV8-associated Kaposi sarcoma arising in the colon or rectum; endothelial histology alone does not establish cardiovascular organ involvement.
Tubulovillous epithelial adenomas predominantly arise in the colon, small intestine or stomach.
Adenomatous neoplasm originating in colonic or rectal mucosa.
Primary cutaneous meningioma arises in skin; meningioma histology alone does not establish CNS involvement.
Hypertension defines vascular involvement despite its pregnancy-associated setting.
Genital sexual differentiation abnormality; no specific endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement established for this broad concept.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in skin; infectious causation applies only to particular subtypes.
Cutaneous lymphatic-vessel tumor; skin location and vascular origin are both defining. No additional organ involvement is established.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular to primary: the lesion arises from lymphatic vessels, retaining its parent's defining vascular origin. Dermatologic also remains primary because the tumor arises in skin.

basis: Usually apical lung malignancy with defining brachial plexus and vessel compression; direct invasion of thoracic bones is usual over the course (>30%).

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the supplied definition includes thoracic-outlet vessel obstruction/compression, with impaired drainage and extremity edema.

basis: Wilms tumor arising in the adult kidney; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ involvement.
Childhood Wilms tumor arises in the kidney; metastatic sites are not defining organ involvement.
Insulin-producing tumor of endocrine pancreatic beta cells; hypoglycemic symptoms do not establish common permanent brain injury.
Philadelphia-positive malignant myeloid proliferation affects blood and bone marrow; leukemia alone does not imply immune-mediated disease.
Locally infiltrating synovial and tendon sheath tumor causing joint destruction; ear involvement is reported in only 5-29%.
Malignant mixed epithelial stromal tumor arising in the kidney.
Benign tumor arising in synovium or tendon sheath.
Neoplasm originates in the brain's choroid plexus.
Umbrella for neoplasms arising in the heart, pericardium or vessels; no other organ is consistently affected across subtypes.
ELF4 autoinflammation with oral ulcers 4/4 and gastritis 2/2; arthritis 1/1 assessed, with uncertain prevalence. Iron deficiency anemia is secondary; rash lacks established damage.
Primary skeletal myopathy with fatty replacement, abnormal muscle fibers and progressive weakness; no evidence of nerve or ear involvement.
Intellectual and language impairment define the disorder; high myopia affects 1/2 reported patients. Recurrent otitis is a separate infection.
Gonadal dysfunction includes decreased testosterone in 3/7 patients, supporting a hormonal component beyond reproductive failure; elevated FSH alone would not suffice.
Immunodeficiency/autoinflammation with neutropenia 6/6, thrombocytopenia 5/6 and marrow failure; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining autoimmune cytopenias; hepatic nodular regenerative hyperplasia and aphthous mucosal ulceration each occur in 2/4. Bronchiectasis occurs in only 1/5.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: aphthous ulcers in 2/4 constitute direct oral mucosal injury associated with the immune disorder, rather than an isolated transient inflammatory sign.

basis: Neoplasm originating in the brainstem.
Neoplasm originates in the apical lung; associated Pancoast syndrome does not establish common nerve or skeletal invasion across this umbrella.
Extragonadal teratomas arise at diverse sites; this site-unspecified umbrella establishes no single organ axis.
Mixed teratoma-seminoma is typically a testicular germ cell tumor; reproductive organs have no axis, and no extragonadal organ of origin is specified.
Primary melanoma of the posterior uvea; small tumor size does not establish damage to other organs.
Melanoma originating in the posterior uvea.
Carcinoma occupies the adrenal medulla; the distant primary site is unspecified.
Carcinoma originating in the clitoris, a reproductive organ outside the specified axes.
Disease located in a tendon sheath; no additional organ applies across this umbrella.
Neoplasm of the clitoris, a reproductive organ outside the specified axes.
Site-unspecified malignancy umbrella; no particular organ axis applies across the group. Empty labels reflect unspecified anatomy.
Carcinoma directly occupies bone; the primary site is unspecified and cannot be assigned an additional axis.
Malignant epithelial tumour arising in the ovary; reproductive origin has no axis.
Benign serous adenofibroma of female reproductive organs, represented by ovarian and fallopian tube subtypes.
Definition specifies a female reproductive system neoplasm arising from mesonephric remnants; the kidney parent does not establish renal origin.
Definition specifies a benign female reproductive-system neoplasm from mesonephric remnants; this overrides the conflicting kidney parent.
Neoplasm arising from pineal parenchymal cells in an intracranial endocrine gland.
Noninfectious inflammation of the meninges; autoimmune causation is not established across this umbrella.
Localized soft-tissue amyloid deposition defines the mass and its proteostasis disorder; systemic organ involvement is not established.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine for the defining amyloid proteostasis disorder. Localization limits additional organ involvement but does not remove the metabolic mechanism; retain musculoskeletal for the soft-tissue site.

basis: Larval tissue invasion causes characteristic hepatic inflammation and frequent pneumonitis; both are in the disease definition. Reactive eosinophilia is not blood-organ damage.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: frequent pneumonitis is explicitly part of the defining visceral larval disease, alongside hepatomegaly.

basis: Umbrella of benign ovarian/testicular stromal tumors, including fibrous tumors; reproductive origin alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Distal, ocular and pharyngeal myopathy define disease; direct tongue weakness affects oral function in 30-79%. Hearing loss is occasional; aspiration pneumonia is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: tongue muscle weakness occurs in 30-79% and directly impairs oral function; this adds evidence beyond pharyngeal dysphagia alone.

basis: Umbrella of tick-transmitted infections; no single damaged organ applies across most subtypes.
Neurodevelopmental disease; VSD 60%, hypospadias 50% (urethral malformation), skeletal defects 30-40%; hypodontia 30% omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias affects 5/10 (50%) and directly malforms the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: hypodontia in 3/10 (30%) qualifies but is omitted at the cap in favor of more frequent urethral and skeletal malformations and cardiac defects.

basis: Epileptic encephalopathy with severe developmental impairment; apnea does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Nephrolithiasis is a defining component, reported in 3/3 assessed patients; reproductive obstruction has no axis.
Parvoviridae infection umbrella; clinically significant marrow or other organ damage is not established in most patients across the group.
ZC4H2-associated spectrum combines congenital arthrogryposis and muscle abnormalities with motor and neurodevelopmental impairment.
Antibody-mediated type II hypersensitivity defines an immune disease; target organs vary across the category.
Autoimmune disease defined by recurrent cutaneous urticaria.
Thrombotic dermal vasculopathy directly causes recurrent ulcers and scarring; associated autoimmunity and thrombophilia are separate conditions.
Occupational allergic asthma causes immune-mediated airway inflammation and airflow limitation.
Chlamydial infection of the lungs causing pneumonia.
Axonal neuropathy with demonstrated mitochondrial respiratory-chain dysfunction; fixed pes cavus in 37/44 (84%). Bladder dysfunction only 1/44.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: mitochondrial respiratory-chain dysfunction is demonstrated by reduced complex activities in 2/3, supporting an energy-metabolism disorder.

basis: Deficiency of corneal limbal stem cells impairs ocular surface maintenance and vision; manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
Microcephaly, epilepsy and diabetes each present in 6/6 patients; developmental delay in 5/6.
Inherited central movement disorder with dystonia in 19/19; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability 12/12; strabismus 5/12 supports ocular dysfunction. Constipation alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
CNS hypomyelination defines disease; refractive errors and strabismus occur in 3/3, optic disc pallor in 1/3; fixed flexion contractures in 3/3.
Bladder and intestinal dysfunction define MMIHS2. Pulmonary and cardiovascular findings each have singleton assessments; these do not establish prevalence of at least 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: aneurysm, PDA and elevated pulmonary pressure each have 1/1 annotations; selected singleton observations do not establish common involvement across the syndrome
decisions.pulmonary: none: hypoplasia and bronchomalacia each have 1/1 annotations; these singleton observations do not establish involvement in at least 30% of patients

basis: PLG-associated angioedema characteristically affects skin and oral tissues; recurrent tongue swelling occurs in about 78%. Bradykinin mediation does not establish immune disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: recurrent tongue and oral mucosal angioedema is a defining presentation of PLG-associated disease; tongue swelling affects about 78%.

basis: Hereditary bradykinin-mediated cutaneous/subcutaneous angioedema; transient facial and lip swelling does not establish additional organ damage.
Residual ovarian tissue causes a reproductive and pelvic disorder; retained normal hormonal activity does not establish endocrine disease.
Defining intestinal hypoperistalsis and microcolon with dysfunctional enlarged urinary bladder; visceral smooth muscle disease.
Chronic neuroimmune inflammatory skin disease with excoriated nodules; associated systemic disorders are separate conditions.
Familial skewing of X inactivation does not itself establish damage to an organ axis; associated reproductive consequences fall outside the axes.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; neurologic dysfunction in 3/3, rod-cone dystrophy in 1/3 and progressive sensorineural hearing loss in 1/3. Small cohort limits certainty.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder with metabolic acidosis; congestive heart failure reported in 1/1 patient. Redundant skin alone does not establish damage.
STAG2 neurodevelopmental syndrome. Ear defects, cleft palate, VSD and scoliosis are single-patient observations; their population frequencies are not established.
audit_reason: Remove otologic, gastrointestinal and cardiovascular: findings reported in 1/1 assessed patients do not establish prevalence of at least 30% or major diagnostic criteria across this syndrome.

basis: Defining intellectual disability and developmental delay; weakness in 2/5 does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
Syndromic developmental impairment; high myopia and microtia each 2/2; incontinence does not establish urinary damage, and metabolite elevations alone do not define metabolic disease.
Inherited glomerular disease causing steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, glomerulosclerosis and kidney failure.
Congenital glycosylation disorder; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2. Hepatomegaly in 1/2 alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Universal neurodevelopmental impairment with progressive spasticity. Constipation (9/16) and reflux (8/16) do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage; neonatal hypoglycemia is transient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation (9/16) and reflux (8/16) are common, but the record does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage or disease-specific loss of gut function.

basis: Congenital central hypothyroidism defines an endocrine disorder; the supplied findings do not establish common damage to another organ.
IRS4-related congenital central hypothyroidism; thyroid hypoplasia in 9/17. No established additional organ damage.
Developmental disorder in 10/10; skeletal involvement includes scoliosis 6/10 and contractures 4/10; mitral regurgitation reaches 3/10.
Defining neurodevelopmental impairment, spasticity and congenital joint contractures with muscle weakness; no established common damage to additional organs.
Forebrain malformation and neurodevelopmental impairment define disease; individual cardiac, hearing and palatal defects occur in 25% or fewer; overlap is unknown.
Glycosylation disorder with immunodeficiency; liver dysfunction and cutis laxa each reported in 3/3 patients.
TLR7-related immunodeficiency; severe SARS-CoV-2 infections do not establish intrinsic chronic pulmonary damage.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; atrial septal defect in 3/10 (~30%); isolated skeletal and GI reports do not establish cohort prevalence.
Autoinflammation with marrow dysfunction; inflammatory skin lesions ~80-90%, pulmonary infiltrates 72%. Cap omits auricular chondritis 64% and vascular manifestations.
HPV-associated locally destructive anogenital skin or mucosal tumor; anal canal disease is a site-specific subtype, not universal involvement.
HHV-6 infection directly inflames the brain.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; MT-ND3 deficiency commonly causes Leigh-spectrum encephalopathy, exceeding 30%. Other organ injury is less consistent.
Mitochondrial ATP synthase deficiency; encephalopathy, ataxia or neuropathy affect most mitochondrial type 1 presentations. Retinal and muscle damage vary by phenotype.
Destructive xanthogranulomatous inflammation affects salivary glands; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established.
Dyskeratosis congenita is defined by marrow failure, nail/skin abnormalities and oral leukoplakia; pulmonary fibrosis is variable.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; hypermetropia 41/41, strabismus 24/76, atrial septal defect 16/23 and hearing impairment 38/119 support involvement.
Cutis laxa with defining neurologic and cardiac disease; hip dislocation occurs in 2/3. Ocular abnormalities, including entropion in 2/3 and cataract in 1/3, omitted by the four-axis cap.
Cutis laxa with cardiac and glycosylation defects; pneumothorax 2/3. Cap omits hip dysplasia 2/3, entropion 6/6, cleft palate 2/2 and nephrocalcinosis 1/2.
Fluorouracil poisoning chiefly causes mucosal injury, diarrhea and marrow suppression. Cardiac and neurologic toxicity are minority manifestations.
Abacavir toxicity chiefly denotes immune-mediated hypersensitivity; transient rash and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish lasting organ damage.
Interpreted as severe hypersensitivity toxicity; renal worsening ~85%, hepatitis ~68% ([series summary](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK548098/)).
Characteristic cisplatin toxicity directly injures renal tubules, cochlear hair cells and peripheral axons; these are sites of the toxicity itself.
Codeine poisoning depresses the CNS and medullary respiratory drive; respiratory suppression alone is not direct lung damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory depression is centrally mediated; direct pulmonary injury is not a defining or established common feature.

basis: Efavirenz neurotoxicity characteristically causes cerebellar ataxia and encephalopathy; hepatic and skin injury are not consistent defining manifestations.
Recognized flucloxacillin toxicity predominantly causes cholestatic liver injury; the supplied record provides no additional organ phenotype.
Irinotecan toxicity principally manifests as intestinal injury with severe diarrhea and marrow suppression with neutropenia.
Congenital kidney and urinary tract malformations, particularly ureteropelvic junction obstruction.
Acute isoniazid poisoning is characterized by seizures, coma and metabolic acidosis; hepatotoxicity is a distinct exposure-related presentation, not established as common in acute poisoning.
Motor neuron degeneration; dysphagia and muscle wasting reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct gastrointestinal or muscle disease.
Voriconazole toxicity causes hepatic injury and CNS toxicity; transient visual symptoms and variable chronic skin or bone effects do not establish common lasting damage.
Heterogeneous inherited serpin protein-processing and accumulation disorders; hepatic, pulmonary, coagulation and neurologic damage vary by subtype.
Generalized adipose loss defines a subcutaneous and metabolic disorder; associated fatty liver and diabetes are separately diagnosed diseases.

basis: Renal tubular sodium transport disorder defined by hypertension, hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis; all reported in 2/2.

Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss.

Developmental delay and intellectual disability in 6/6; feeding difficulty and hypotonia do not establish separate gastrointestinal or muscle damage.

basis: Developmental encephalopathy with structural brain abnormalities; optic nerve hypoplasia and impaired fixation occurred in 1/1 annotated patient.

basis: Inherited heme-synthesis defect with characteristic neonatal hemolytic anemia; photosensitivity frequency is uncertain. Hemolytic jaundice alone does not establish liver injury.

basis: Intellectual and language impairment with frequent seizures; constipation in 9/15 and joint hypermobility in 3/9 do not establish direct bowel or joint damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: generalized amyotrophy (2/2) establishes wasting, but direct muscle pathology is not demonstrated; secondary wasting does not meet the direct-damage rule.

basis: Sorbitol dehydrogenase deficiency is an inborn metabolic disorder causing motor and sensory axonal neuropathy; weakness is neurogenic.

GRIA2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability and global developmental delay in 28/28 patients.

Inherited right ventricular cardiomyopathy with ventricular arrhythmias and structural cardiac disease.

SCN2A-related episodic cerebellar dysfunction and seizures; central vertigo and nystagmus do not establish ear or eye disease.
Defining callosal and developmental abnormalities, congenital cardiac defects and ocular malformations; genital abnormalities have no axis.
Intrinsic phagocyte oxidative-burst defect; CGD-associated granulomatous colitis occurs in 4/8. Pulmonary fibrosis is 1/8; infections alone do not establish direct lung involvement.

basis: Mandibulofacial dysostosis and hearing loss 5/6; cleft palate 3/6 and airway failure 3/6. Eyelid coloboma 3/6 omitted at cap in favor of feeding/airway damage.

decisions.ocular: none: eyelid coloboma occurs in 3/6, but feeding and ventilatory impairment take priority under the four-axis cap.
