Cardiac laterality abnormality with dextrocardia in 5/7; situs inversus alone does not imply visceral damage. Asplenia occurs in 1/7 and otitis in 1/6.

Defined by growth and skeletal abnormalities; developmental impairment in 3/5. Blue sclerae, thin skin and sweating do not establish additional organ damage.

basis: Pontocerebellar and other brain malformations with severe developmental impairment; neutropenia and thrombocytopenia each occur in 2/9, below 30%.
Brainstem and cerebellar hypoplasia with severe developmental impairment; neutropenia and thrombocytopenia each 2/9, below threshold.

basis: Hypomyelinating brain disease; hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, hypodontia and optic atrophy each occur in 1/2 reported patients.

Neurodevelopmental disorder with cerebellar degeneration and ataxia; occasional biochemical elevations do not establish a separate metabolic disorder.

basis: Cutis laxa with core skull/limb malformations; learning disability 3/7 (43%) and hearing impairment 3/8 (38%). Proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.

basis: Inherited hepatobiliary metabolic disorder with cholestasis and periportal fibrosis; diarrhea and bleeding do not establish direct intestinal or blood-organ injury.

basis: Type I interferonopathy defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment and destructive cerebral white-matter disease; nystagmus is neurologic.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation defect with defining CNS/liver dysfunction; amyotrophy 8/8 and arthritis 3/9 support muscle/joint involvement. Anemia 4/4 omitted by cap.

basis: Portal venous hypertension; hepatic nodular regenerative hyperplasia 2/5 (40%); splenomegaly 9/9 with thrombocytopenia 8/9 (~89%). Esophageal varices are vascular.

basis: Inherited sideroblastic anemia with ring sideroblasts and additional cytopenias; disease of marrow and blood cells.

basis: Isolated spermatogenic failure and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Inherited retinal degeneration with reduced visual acuity in 4/4 patients; no extraocular involvement established.

Developmental impairment, intellectual disability and epilepsy; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage.

basis: Axonal neuropathy with persistent vocal cord paresis in 8/8, causing laryngeal dysfunction; structural foot deformity, pes cavus, occurs in 6/8.

basis: Joubert brain malformation and neurodevelopmental impairment; polydactyly in 5/5 and optic nerve hypoplasia in 2/4. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic.

basis: Isolated defective spermatogenesis and sperm motility cause male infertility; no endocrine or other covered organ disorder is established.

Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures and developmental impairment; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle disease.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with common cortical malformation; hip dysplasia and ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Ciliary airway disease with chronic sinusitis in 3/3 and recurrent middle-ear inflammation in 2/2. Situs inversus and dextrocardia alone do not establish organ damage.

basis: Cardiac septal/canal defects in 1/3; chronic sinusitis 2/2, chronic otitis 2/3 and intestinal atresia/malrotation 1/3 support involvement; situs reversal alone is not damage.
Defining nephropathy and microcephalic brain disease; congenital hypothyroidism occurs in 3/3 reported patients. Arachnodactyly alone does not establish locomotor damage.

basis: Immunodeficiency with autoimmunity. Microcytic anemia (2/2) may be secondary; bronchiectasis/bullae (1/2) do not establish direct immune lung injury. Crohn disease and asthma are separate diagnoses.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis/bullae in 1/2 meet the frequency threshold, but direct immune-mediated injury is unestablished; infection-related bronchiectasis and asthma are separate diseases.

basis: Inherited dystonia with brain atrophy; dysphagia and laryngeal dystonia reflect neurologic motor dysfunction.

Inherited epidermal fragility with generalized blistering; oral mucosal blisters affect 14/14 patients.
Isolated oocyte maturation failure causing female infertility; no endocrine dysfunction is established.

basis: Inherited cholestasis classified under inborn bilirubin metabolism disorders; hepatic fibrosis in 4/5. Pruritus alone does not establish skin damage.

Isolated spermatogenic failure with azoospermia and infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement established.

basis: Central respiratory/autonomic failure defines disease; achalasia and intestinal dysmotility occur in 3/3; scoliosis and kyphosis each occur in 1/3.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural spinal deformity is documented as scoliosis and kyphosis, each in 1/3, meeting the supplied 30% threshold.

basis: Inherited dystonia with tremor and myoclonus; pursuit abnormalities and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: hypoventilation and respiratory failure (2/2) arise from central drive failure; direct lung or airway disease is not demonstrated.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental delay 4/8 and intellectual disability 3/8. Hearing loss 2/8 is below 30%; absent acoustic reflex alone is insufficient.

Klebsiella bacterial infection directly involving the lungs.

Cystic nephroblastoma arising in the kidney.

Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness, visual-field loss and pigmentary retinopathy.

IFIH1-related antiviral immunodeficiency; recurrent viral pneumonia is a separate infection rather than intrinsic pulmonary disease.
Hypogammaglobulinemic immunodeficiency; multicystic kidney dysplasia in 2/5 (40%). Macrocytosis alone does not establish blood-cell damage.

Autoimmune inflammation of the renal glomeruli.

Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis causing macrocytic dyserythropoietic anemia.

audit_reason: Add pulmonary to primary: pharyngeal dysfunction is a defining component, supported by dysphagia in 8/10. The pharynx belongs to pulmonary even when its dysfunction is myopathic.

Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; complete AV block and limb contracture each occur in 1/1 assessed patient. Very small denominators limit frequency certainty.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome; hepatic failure, renal hypoplasia and ASD/hypertension each 1/3. Ocular and limb defects also 1/3, omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 1/3 meets the frequency threshold, but is omitted at the cap in favor of hepatic failure, renal hypoplasia and cardiovascular disease.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder; muscle atrophy and esotropia each reported in 1/1 patient, supporting muscle and ocular involvement, with limited sampling.

Isolated defective spermatogenesis and globozoospermia cause male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction is established.

Deglycosylation disorder with defining brain malformations and developmental disability; tongue hamartoma 2/6 (33%). Microtia 2/5 lacks established impairment; hearing loss 1/4 is below threshold.

decisions.otologic: none: microtia in 2/5 establishes ear morphology, not functional damage; documented hearing impairment is 1/4 (25%).

basis: Restrictive skin disease; skeletal malformations include short clavicles in 2/2. Rectal prolapse occurs in 1/2. Respiratory distress and proptosis alone do not establish organ damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: short clavicles occur in 2/2 and abnormal long bones in 1/2; these are associated skeletal malformations of the defining restrictive skin disorder.

basis: Intellectual disability, developmental delay, seizures and cortical malformation establish a neurologic disorder; renal stones occur in only 1/12.

Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration; the supplied phenotype is confined to the eye.
Immunodeficiency with defining autoimmune cytopenias; autoimmune melanocyte loss causing vitiligo reported in 1/1. Recurrent infections alone do not establish chronic lung damage.
Hepatic ductal-plate malformation and fibro-obliterative cholangiopathy define this disorder; congestive splenomegaly does not establish blood-organ damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ZFYVE19 disease is a developmental cholangiopathy/ciliopathy; the broad bilirubin-metabolism ancestor does not establish an intrinsic metabolic defect.

basis: Inherited marrow disorder characterized by monosomy 7, myelodysplasia and cytopenias, with possible myeloid leukemia.
Cerebellar degeneration with frequent peripheral neuropathy; nystagmus and diplopia reflect neurologic dysfunction without established intrinsic eye damage.
Isolated sperm flagellar defects and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other organ disease is established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the supplied ancestry explicitly places this inherited hepatobiliary transport disorder under inborn bilirubin metabolism disorders.

basis: VZV-specific immunodeficiency with cerebral vasculitis in 2/2; vascular inflammation supports cardiovascular involvement; brain parenchymal damage is not documented.
Inherited intrahepatic cholestatic disorder of bile handling, with elevated bile acids and hepatocellular injury markers.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with azoospermia and male infertility; reproductive dysfunction has no axis, without evidence of hormonal disease.

Isolated inherited platelet disorder characterized by large platelets and thrombocytopenia.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with axonal neuropathy; pigmentary retinopathy in 5/6 and hearing impairment in 11/19. Scoliosis occurs in only 4/25.

Inherited thyroid hormone metabolism abnormality with elevated reverse T3 and rT3/T3 ratio in 8/8; no common damage to another organ is documented.
Constitutional DNA repair cancer-predisposition syndrome; hematologic, brain and intestinal cancers are separate diseases whose risk is increased.

decisions.neurologic: none: brain tumors are separate diseases within the predisposition spectrum, not established neurologic damage from this syndrome.

basis: Characteristic cutaneous phenotype includes cafe-au-lait macules in 6/6; associated cancers are separately diagnosed diseases, not assumed organ damage. Lisch nodules are non-damaging.

decisions.neurologic: none: astrocytoma and glioblastoma are separately diagnosed tumors; their risk or occurrence does not establish intrinsic neurologic involvement of the syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic cafe-au-lait macules in 6/6 and axillary freckling in 2/2 establish the syndrome's cutaneous phenotype.

basis: Callosal agenesis in 3/3 and heterotopia in 2/3 document CNS malformations. Cancer predisposition alone is excluded; polyposis frequency is unspecified.

basis: Isolated sperm production and flagellar abnormalities cause infertility; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction established.

Intellectual disability and axonal neuropathy define the disorder; structural kyphoscoliosis occurs in 4/9 (~44%); muscle wasting is neurogenic.

Hereditary motor neuron degeneration; persistent thenar and distal leg muscle atrophy is characteristic in most patients (>50%), with associated foot deformity.

basis: Cerebellar and cardiac malformations are core 3C features; skeletal dysplasia and chorioretinal coloboma each occur in 2/2. Cardiac defect occurs in 1/2; samples are very small.

decisions.ocular: involved: chorioretinal coloboma in 2/2 establishes common structural ocular involvement; microphthalmia is also documented in 1/2.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal phalangeal shortening and epiphyseal stippling each occur in 2/2, establishing common skeletal malformation.

Vertebral and rib malformations plus defining oral clefts; cleft lip and palate each reported in 2/6. Helix shape alone does not establish ear dysfunction.

Pontocerebellar and brainstem malformation with developmental impairment; respiratory insufficiency (5/8) and dysphagia (4/6) do not establish intrinsic lung or gut damage.

decisions.otologic: primary: deafness is an explicitly named disease manifestation, supported by congenital sensorineural hearing impairment in 7/7.

basis: Marrow failure and intellectual disability define AMED; isolated short stature and pigmentation do not establish skeletal or skin damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: prominent cranioskeletal malformations characterize the syndrome, including trigonocephaly 12/13 and multiple common limb abnormalities.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral malformation reported in 2/3 patients; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia 2/2, hearing impairment 2/3, rod-cone dystrophy 1/2; central hypothyroidism 1/2 omitted by cap. Recurrent infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Syndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay 12/12 and seizures 5/6; isolated skeletal and ocular findings do not establish common damage.

Intellectual disability and developmental delay are nearly universal; obesity in 6/18 is a separate condition, and facial dysmorphism does not establish organ damage.
Intellectual disability, seizures and spasticity define neurologic disease; scoliosis and structural foot deformities each occur in 1/3 reported patients.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; feeding difficulties alone do not demonstrate gastrointestinal damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 7/7; constipation in 2/7 is below 30% and does not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
ASH1L neurodevelopmental disorder with universal reported ID; isolated ocular, hearing and skeletal findings lack reliable evidence of >=30% prevalence.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.
CAMK2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder; constipation (4/10) does not establish direct gut damage, and apnea (3/10) does not establish lung damage.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy, ataxia and tremor define a neurologic disorder.
CLTC-related intellectual disability and developmental delay; hearing and visual impairment each occur in only 1/12.
Inherited degeneration of frontal-temporal brain regions and/or motor neurons; muscle involvement does not apply across the entire umbrella.
Proteasome-associated autoinflammation; hypertriglyceridemia in 1/1 lacks evidence of persistent metabolic dysfunction. Rash and organomegaly alone do not establish additional damage.

basis: Oocyte maturation failure and infertility affect reproduction without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short fingers and clinodactyly each occur in 2/5, but minor skeletal shape differences alone do not establish damage or loss of function.

basis: Developmental delay in 24/24 and seizures in 15/24 establish neurologic disease; dermatitis and infections are uncommon.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: polydactyly in 2/5 (40%) establishes an anatomical variant, but the record does not demonstrate skeletal functional impairment.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with near-universal developmental delay; feeding difficulty and facial dysmorphism do not establish additional organ dysfunction.

Progressive myoclonus epilepsy with ataxia and cognitive deterioration; all established damaging manifestations are neurologic.
Complex II defect; developmental encephalopathy, cardiomyopathy and visual impairment with optic pallor each 1/1; hepatomegaly alone is not hepatic injury; aspiration is secondary.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with azoospermia; reproductive function without demonstrated endocrine disease.
Ovarian endocrine failure with low sex hormones and elevated gonadotropins; gonads as hormone organs belong to the endocrine axis.
Inherited keratinization disorder with palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, hair changes, nail dystrophy and anhidrosis.
Lysosomal neurodegeneration with bladder loss of function in 2/3; respiratory insufficiency in 3/3 does not establish intrinsic lung injury, and cortical visual loss is neurologic.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 3/3 establishes impaired ventilation but does not demonstrate direct lung or airway damage from the disease.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines disease. Dental crowding 12/15 lacks demonstrated damage or dysfunction; enamel hypoplasia 4/15 is below 30%. Cardiac and developmental abnormalities are uncommon.

basis: Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; feeding difficulties, drooling and motor signs do not establish separate organ injury.

basis: Intellectual and developmental impairment define disease; fifth-finger contractures affect 5/9 and toe syndactyly 3/9. Isolated 1/1 reports do not establish cohort prevalence.

Immunodeficiency, developmental delay and defining autoimmune cytopenias (75-83%); bronchiectasis 3/6 (50%). Recurrent otitis alone does not establish lasting ear damage.

basis: Inborn sulfide oxidation defect with lactic acidosis; encephalopathy 3/3 and coma 2/3 establish neurologic injury. Elevated CK alone does not establish myopathy.

Premature ovarian insufficiency is loss of gonadal endocrine function; amenorrhea and infertility are accompanying reproductive manifestations.
Acantholytic blistering defines disease of oral and laryngeal mucosa; oral erosions and blisters are documented in 1/1 patients.
Vertebral and tracheoesophageal defects predominate (fistula 6/12); developmental delay 3/9. Defining renal defects (2/9) and cardiac defects (2/11) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: none under cap: renal agenesis is defining but reported in 2/9; retain the more frequent developmental impairment (3/9) after skeletal and tracheoesophageal defects.
decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay occurs in 3/9 (33%), meeting the frequency threshold for direct neurodevelopmental dysfunction.

basis: Defined by developmental impairment and dental anomalies; developmental delay affects 35/36 and intellectual disability 28/31 assessed patients. Teeth are gastrointestinal.
Isolated male infertility with abnormal sperm morphology; reproductive function has no axis and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy dominate; dental abnormalities are under 30%. Dysphagia in 5/15 does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Inherited bile-acid conjugation defect with hepatobiliary disease: jaundice 7/7 and elevated transaminases 3/7. Rickets occurs in 2/7, just below 30%, and is excluded.
Dental, skeletal and motor abnormalities define SOFM; hypothyroidism and impaired GH response each 2/3. Ocular and hearing abnormalities each 1/3 omitted by cap.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; functional abnormalities of other organs are reported below 30%.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; absent thumb 1/1, cleft palate 1/3 and cardiac defects 1/3 support involvement. Very small denominators limit certainty.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: absent thumb is a structural limb defect reported in 1/1 assessed patients; supplied frequency supports inclusion, with substantial uncertainty.

basis: Developmental delay and intellectual disability occur in 17/17. Joint hypermobility in 8/17 does not establish joint damage; hearing impairment occurs in only 3/17.
Inherited platelet production and function defect with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; bleeding symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Complex I metabolic defect; developmental/structural brain disease, seizures 2/3; pulmonary arterial hypertension 2/2 and skeletal muscle atrophy 1/2.

decisions.neurologic: involved: severe developmental impairment and brain atrophy are common; seizures occur in 2/3. The concept is defined by complex I deficiency.

basis: Nonsyndromic congenital hearing loss with cochlear and vestibular malformations.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and cerebral atrophy define the disorder; other findings are minor dysmorphism or below 30%.
Developmental delay defines disease; hearing loss 2/3, strabismus 3/6, renal agenesis/reflux 1/3. Skeletal defects and ASD (1/3) omitted by cap; leukemia is separate.
Vitreoretinal degeneration and retinal detachment with defining phalangeal epiphyseal dysplasia.
Severe developmental impairment and cataracts occur in 6/6; kyphosis in 2/6 (~33%) supports skeletal involvement. Reported immunodeficiency lacks a qualifying frequency.
Inherited loss of NTCP-mediated hepatic bile-acid uptake; osteopenia in 3/8 (~38%) supports skeletal involvement.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the defining transport defect is loss of hepatic bile-acid uptake; primary location does not require additional evidence of hepatocellular injury.

basis: Neurodegeneration and optic atrophy define this mitochondrial metabolic syndrome; organic aciduria 2/2, cardiomyopathy 3/3. Hepatic glycogen alone does not establish liver damage.
Skeletal dysplasia, retinal degeneration and neurodevelopmental/CNS abnormalities define syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 4/4 (100%), filling the fourth axis.
Inherited podocyte disease causing steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; secondary lipid changes and hypercoagulability do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect; bruising and mucosal bleeding do not establish separate skin, airway or gastrointestinal organ disease.
Skeletal dysplasia, diabetes and deafness define disease; dentin defects occur in 4/4. Mild intellectual disability (4/4) omitted at cap; diabetic retinopathy is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dentinogenesis imperfecta in 4/4 and tooth loss in 2/4; retained as the fourth axis under the primary cap.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss is a named defining feature, present in 4/4.

basis: Defined neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability and developmental delay; nystagmus and cosmetic or dental features do not establish additional organ damage.
Autoimmune inflammation of the uvea; the erroneous ENT ancestry does not establish ear or airway disease.
Autoimmune inflammation of the optic nerve; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Autoimmune destruction of gastric body/fundic mucosa; pernicious anaemia is a separate disease, and gastric carcinoma is a later risk.
Hereditary corticospinal dysfunction with spastic paraplegia and intellectual disability; associated lumbar lordosis does not establish direct skeletal disease.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define encephalopathy; visual impairment in 1/2 lacks evidence of intrinsic ocular damage.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy and pituitary insufficiency define it; retinal dystrophy occurs in only 1/7, and nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Inherited immunodeficiency with invasive staphylococcal susceptibility; destructive skin manifestations are reported, but a frequency of at least 30% is not established.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay in 5/5; nystagmus does not establish ocular damage; joint hypermobility in 1/4.
Cerebral capillary malformations define a neurovascular disorder; scoliosis (30-79%) lacks evidence of direct skeletal pathology; ocular and skin vascular lesions occur in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is annotated at 30-79%, but direct skeletal involvement by the vascular disorder is not established; neurologic sequelae alone do not qualify.

basis: Inherited intrahepatic cholestasis with bilirubin-metabolism ancestry; proteinuria indicates renal involvement in 3/3; prolonged aPTT alone does not establish a blood disorder.
Central lymphatic vascular malformation; chylothorax in 6/6 and respiratory distress in 4/7 demonstrate common pleural and respiratory dysfunction.
Inherited circadian sleep timing disorder characterized by an abnormally early sleep phase.
Distal joint contracture disorder: camptodactyly in 12/12 and restricted forearm rotation in 7/11.
Myopia, skeletal deformities and sensorineural hearing loss define this collagen disorder; intellectual disability reported in 3/3 supports neurologic involvement.
Developmental and epileptic brain dysfunction defines disease; ocular misalignment occurs in 3/8 (~38%), supporting ocular functional involvement.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis defines pulmonary disease; middle-ear dysfunction with recurrent otitis occurs in 1/1 annotated patient and commonly in PCD.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy defines the disease. Visual impairment in 1/1 has no established ocular localization; feeding difficulty does not establish gut damage.
Skin/nail disease and diagnostic oral leukoplakia (4/10); IgA deficiency (4/9) with recurrent infections (3/10) supports immunodeficiency. Anemia occurs in only 1/10.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: documented antibody deficiency (IgA low in 4/9) and recurrent infections (3/10) support immunodeficiency; applicable mechanism axes belong in primary.

basis: Microcephaly, seizures and developmental impairment define disease; strabismus 2/2. Renal ultrasound changes in 1/2 lack established damaging pathology or functional impairment.

decisions.renal: none: echogenicity and reduced corticomedullary differentiation in 1/2 do not establish damaging renal disease or functional impairment.

basis: Inherited nephrotic syndrome with glomerular injury; nephrotic syndrome occurs in 6/6 annotated patients.
Renal cysts 16/17 and renal insufficiency 10/19. Hypertension (9/18) is a separately diagnosed secondary condition.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; structural Achilles tendon contractures in 2/3 and scoliosis in 1/3 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Red-cell aplasia; intellectual disability 4/6, skeletal abnormalities 4/6, aortic regurgitation 1/3 assessed. Cardiac frequency rests on a small sample.
Isolated defective spermatogenesis and sperm motility cause male infertility; reproductive function is outside the axes.
Isolated spermatogenic failure affects reproductive function; elevated FSH reflects impaired spermatogenesis without establishing a separate endocrine disorder.
Inherited dental enamel defect; amelogenesis imperfecta and enamel hypoplasia in 10/10 patients.
ADCY5-related neurologic movement disorder; orofacial movements do not establish oral tissue or skeletal muscle damage.
Spondylometaphyseal skeletal dysplasia with characteristic dental abnormalities; hearing loss and diabetes belong to a specific subtype.
Inherited interstitial lung disease; metabolic, immune and marrow manifestations are subtype-specific rather than shared across the umbrella.
Hereditary neurodevelopmental syndrome; no supplied evidence establishes common direct involvement of another axis.
Defining skin restriction, contractures and lung hypoplasia; oral restriction/cleft palate 80-99%. PDA/vascular anomalies and entropion (80-99%) omitted by cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none under cap: PDA/vascular anomalies are annotated 80-99%; severe oral restriction and palatal defects take priority for direct functional impairment.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: microstomia and cleft palate occur in 80-99%, with persistent oral structural and feeding impairment.

basis: The syndrome's defining neoplastic manifestations are hematologic malignancies, brain tumors and colorectal tumors/polyposis; no additional organs assigned from future risk.
Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy; encephalopathy or leukodystrophy affects >30% across major nuclear forms. Cardiomyopathy varies by subtype.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct encephalopathy, Leigh disease or leukodystrophy occurs in >30% across the major nuclear forms.

basis: Familial panic disorder is psychiatric; hereditary neurological ancestry does not establish neurological injury.
Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema; tachycardia and leukocytosis are reactive signs, and concomitant cerebral edema is a separate condition.
Bowed-bone dysplasia and dysautonomia define the syndrome; corneal ulceration/opacities affect approximately 45% of longer-term survivors.

decisions.ocular: involved: corneal injury/opacities affect approximately 45% of survivors beyond age two, supporting involvement over the course. [Evidence](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9034487/)

basis: Three eyes and forebrain duplication define it; cleft palate and laryngomalacia each occur in 80-99%. Nonspecific skin and skull findings omitted under the cap.
Developmental defects or dysplasia of cardiac valves directly affect the heart.
Skeletal anomalies and impaired intellectual development define the syndrome.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate organ damage. Intracranial hemorrhage is uncommon overall.
Inherited deglycosylation defects; developmental impairment and central neurologic dysfunction affect most (>80%) reported patients across subtypes.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment affects most (>80%) reported patients across subtypes; it is a consequence of the defining metabolic defect.

basis: Familial Behcet-like autoinflammation with characteristic recurrent oral mucosal ulceration; other organ damage varies across subtypes.
Congenital cardiac defects, acral skeletal abnormalities and neurodevelopmental impairment characterize the principal subtypes.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay and intellectual impairment are defining features across the principal cardioacrofacial dysplasia subtypes.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome umbrella; no shared additional organ involvement is established.
Ankylosis 80-99%; dental defects and sensorineural hearing impairment each 30-79%. These fill the four-axis cap.
Lysosomal storage; skeletal and neurologic dysfunction each common (~30%+ across major forms). Vision-threatening disease is subtype-dependent; ocular deposits may spare function.

decisions.ocular: none: visual loss is concentrated in ML IV and sialidosis; an umbrella frequency >=30% is not established, and corneal/cherry-red deposits alone do not establish damage.

basis: Hereditary abnormalities of thyroid hormone metabolism define this endocrine disorder.
Skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; cardiac anomalies are variable, with no established frequency supporting inclusion across the group.
Inherited hepatobiliary bile-acid handling disorder; fat malabsorption reflects altered bile availability without established intestinal injury. Rickets frequency is unspecified.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: fat malabsorption and steatorrhea reflect impaired bile availability; direct intestinal damage or an intrinsic intestinal absorptive defect is not established.

basis: Isolated inherited thrombocytopenia with enlarged platelets; no syndromic extra-haematologic involvement is established.
Microcephaly, epileptic encephalopathy and permanent neonatal diabetes define the syndrome; other organ abnormalities are occasional.
Severe inherited lymphocyte deficiency or dysfunction defines SCID; secondary organ infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: SCID is a disease of lymphocytes, which are blood cells; the rules require the haematologic mechanism axis as well as infectious_immune.

basis: Inherited skeletal dysplasia characterized by bent bones; no common extraskeletal injury is established across subtypes.
Developmental delay and sparse hair define the syndrome; short stature and facial dysmorphism alone do not establish skeletal damage.
MED13-related neurodevelopmental disorder with universal developmental delay; constipation in 4/13 does not establish intrinsic bowel damage; Duane anomaly in 2/13.
Cerebellar degeneration with ataxia and cognitive decline; dysphagia and incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Lymphatic malformation and protein-losing enteropathy define disease; strabismus 2/2 and spontaneous pneumothorax 1/2 support ocular and pulmonary involvement. Estimates rely on two patients.
audit_reason: Add pulmonary: spontaneous pneumothorax affects the pleura and is reported in 1/2 patients (50%), meeting the supplied frequency threshold. Neurologic involvement is not established for this subtype.

basis: Defining external ophthalmoplegia with congenital rib and vertebral abnormalities; scoliosis 4/4 and short ribs 3/3.
Cholesterol synthesis defect with profound neurodevelopmental disease; optic nerve hypoplasia and knee contractures each 2/3; skin findings 3/3 and bicuspid valve 1/3 omitted by cap.
Isolated pituitary growth hormone deficiency; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation do not establish separate skeletal damage.
Congenital pituitary growth hormone deficiency with anterior pituitary hypoplasia; short stature and delayed bone maturation reflect hormone deficiency.
Joubert brain malformations and developmental impairment; rod-cone dystrophy with night blindness in 4/4. Renal lesions each 1/4, below threshold.
Skeletal dysplasia/immunodeficiency; developmental delay/Chiari and asthma each 2/2. Eczema 2/2, cardiac defects and annular pancreas 1/2 omitted at cap; cohort is very small.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: asthma and allergic rhinitis each occur in 2/2 reported patients, supporting persistent inflammatory airway involvement in this syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: eczematoid dermatitis occurs in 2/2, but neurologic abnormalities and inflammatory airway disease take priority.

basis: Heart, developmental and digital abnormalities define syndrome; hearing impairment 26/49. Eyelid malformations 33/42 omitted at cap in favor of functional hearing loss.

decisions.ocular: none: eyelid malformations occur in 33/42, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of functionally significant hearing impairment in 26/49.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: digital skeletal abnormalities are a defining component; clinodactyly 3/7 and pectus carinatum 17/42 support skeletal involvement.

basis: Marrow failure with hypogammaglobulinemia in 2/2; developmental disability in 2/2 and hypogonadism in 1/1. Pigmentation alone does not establish skin damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: hypogammaglobulinemia in 2/2 supports syndromic humoral immunodeficiency; the immune mechanism axis belongs in primary.

basis: Osteochondrodysplasia with malformed digits, scoliosis and joint dysfunction; absent skin creases reflect digit malformation rather than skin damage.
WNT2B-associated congenital enteropathy causes persistent diarrhea and intestinal villous atrophy.
ARL3-related retinal degeneration with night blindness, reduced acuity and visual field loss.
Congenital cortical and other brain malformations cause epilepsy and severe neurodevelopmental impairment.
Inherited glomerular disease with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and frequent kidney failure.
Inherited nephrotic syndrome with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and kidney failure; no immune mechanism established.
Inherited nephrotic syndrome with proteinuria, glomerulosclerosis and chronic kidney dysfunction.
Primary microcephaly, cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and intellectual disability define neurologic disease. Clinodactyly alone does not establish functional skeletal damage.
Hair and tooth abnormalities define the disorder; hypodontia and sparse hair occur in 5/5, hypohidrosis in 4/5.
Protein-losing enteropathy; renal dysplasia and coloboma each reported in 1/1 patient. Effusions, low immunoglobulins and electrolyte changes reflect secondary losses.
Neuronal migration disorder with developmental delay, seizures and other central nervous system abnormalities.
Ovarian endocrine failure with low estradiol defines disease; osteoporosis reported in 1/1, consistent with sustained estrogen deficiency.
Transient neonatal hyperparathyroidism with skeletal undermineralization; osteopenia in 2/6 patients (~33%); motor delay alone does not establish neural damage.
PPCS deficiency is an established inborn defect of coenzyme A biosynthesis presenting with dilated cardiomyopathy; elevated lactate alone would not justify the metabolic axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this specific disorder is PPCS enzyme deficiency impairing coenzyme A biosynthesis, an inborn metabolic disorder, rather than merely a cardiomyopathy with elevated lactate.

basis: Intellectual disability and degenerative retinal disease define the syndrome; both documented in 4/4 patients.
Presynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction causes fatigable weakness; ptosis and bulbar weakness do not establish intrinsic eye or muscle damage.
Presynaptic neuromuscular-junction disorder; fixed arthrogryposis and limb contractures in 1/1 assessed support musculoskeletal involvement.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with regression, cortical atrophy and spasticity; contractures and respiratory distress are very rare.
Combined immune-cell deficiency; recurrent infections and cutaneous abscesses are separately diagnosed complications rather than established intrinsic organ damage.
Developmental and speech impairment define the syndrome; hypermetropia 38% and strabismus 30%. Joint hypermobility 40% lacks documented joint damage; feeding difficulty is nonspecific.
Defining enterocolitis, immunodeficiency and encephalopathy; cerebral atrophy and bloody diarrhea occur in 3/3. Blood count changes do not establish intrinsic blood disease.
Nonsyndromic congenital extra digits; hand polydactyly is present in all three reported patients.
Intellectual disability and developmental language impairment define the disorder; joint hypermobility in 3/10 does not establish joint damage.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect; gliosis, dystonia and abnormal brain structure in 1/1 annotated patient support neurologic damage. Cardiac frequency is unknown.
Vertebral anomalies, endocrine and T-cell dysfunction define syndrome; cleft palate 3/4. Ectopia pupillae 2/4 lacks demonstrated functional damage.
Complex I metabolic defect; encephalopathy/regression and ataxia (1/2) support common neurologic dysfunction; hepatomegaly lacks established injury or frequency.
Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; brain atrophy and seizures in 3/3. Blindness in 1/1 assessed and strabismus in 2/3 support ocular involvement, with limited sampling.

decisions.neurologic: involved: brain atrophy and seizures occur in 3/3; the concept is defined by respiratory-chain deficiency rather than a specific neurologic syndrome.

basis: Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; ataxia 2/3 and destructive brain abnormalities; strabismus/ptosis 2/3 and optic atrophy 1/3; hepatomegaly alone excluded.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; motor delay/neurologic dysfunction in 3/6 and cardiomyopathy in 2/6; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 2/2 and encephalopathy in 1/1 support heart and brain involvement.
Complex I metabolic defect with encephalopathy/dystonia; neurologic disease, optic pallor and structural kyphoscoliosis reported in 1/1. Very small denominators limit certainty.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy, dystonia and tetraparesis are manifestations of the metabolic defect; axial dystonia is documented in 1/1.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural kyphoscoliosis is documented in 1/1, supporting lasting skeletal involvement, although prevalence rests on a single patient.

basis: Mitochondrial complex I deficiency with lactic acidosis; severe neonatal encephalopathy is typical (>30%). Hypotonia and hypoventilation alone add no muscle or lung damage.
Complex I metabolic defect; developmental delay/encephalopathy and optic atrophy reported in 1/1. Central hypoventilation does not establish lung injury.
Complex I metabolic defect; developmental impairment, cardiomyopathy/heart failure and pigmentary retinopathy each reported in 1/1. Cap excludes unquantified myopathy.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism defect; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 7/7, developmental delay 4/4 and brain atrophy 2/2; apnea alone does not establish lung damage.
Complex I metabolic defect; encephalopathy 6/6 and dystonia 5/5 establish neurologic damage. Cardiomyopathy 1/6 is below threshold; optic atrophy frequency unknown.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy occurs in 6/6, with dystonia and CNS injury; these are consequences of the defining mitochondrial metabolic defect.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; developmental impairment and caudate atrophy in 2/2 establish neurologic damage. Scoliosis accompanies spasticity; diaphragm aplasia is an isolated report.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability, movement disorders and caudate atrophy occur in 2/2; these are direct consequences of the metabolic defect.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis in 2/2 accompanies severe spasticity; diaphragm aplasia in one assessed patient does not establish direct muscle or skeletal disease in >=30% overall.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; basal ganglia necrosis 3/3 and developmental regression 4/4 establish neurologic injury. Weakness alone does not establish intrinsic myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: basal ganglia necrosis 3/3 and regression 4/4 demonstrate common direct brain injury from the defining mitochondrial metabolic defect.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; neurologic involvement includes hypertonia in 3/5 and developmental delay. Renal anomalies 1/5; respiratory failure lacks evidence of intrinsic lung damage.
Complex I metabolic deficiency; developmental impairment/cerebellar atrophy and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/1 assessed. Tiny samples limit certainty; optic atrophy 1-4% excluded.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment and cerebellar atrophy demonstrate direct CNS involvement in 1/1 assessed; the defining disorder is complex I metabolic deficiency.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; leukodystrophy/developmental impairment and myopathy with ragged-red fibers reported in 1/1. Ocular motor signs alone do not establish intrinsic eye injury.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus and nystagmus in 1/1 can reflect central motor dysfunction; no direct eye, retinal or optic nerve injury is established.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; developmental impairment and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each in 1/1 reported patient; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of intrinsic lung damage.
Mitochondrial energy metabolism defect; dystonia and motor delay indicate neurologic dysfunction in 1/1; skeletal muscle atrophy and scoliosis also occur in 1/1.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain metabolic disorder. Hypotonia alone does not establish direct neurologic or skeletal muscle damage.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect with lactic acidosis; encephalopathy and biopsy-supported myopathy each reported in 1/1 phenotyped patient.
Complex I deficiency; brain atrophy/movement disorder, rod-cone dystrophy and hearing impairment each reported in 1/1; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of lung injury.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with developmental delay in 2/2; optic atrophy in 1/2 supports ocular damage. Neurogenic bladder in 1/2 does not establish direct urinary-organ injury.
audit_reason: Remove renal: neurogenic bladder reflects neurologic dysfunction; the evidence does not establish direct urinary-organ damage. Optic atrophy in 1/2 supports ocular involvement despite the small cohort.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; developmental delay/pyramidal dysfunction, optic atrophy and hearing impairment each occur in 2/2 reported patients.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay and pyramidal dysfunction occur in 2/2 patients; they are consequences of the defining respiratory-chain metabolic defect.

basis: Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; myopathic exercise intolerance in 3/3 and proximal weakness in 2/3. Renal and cardiac damage frequencies unspecified.
Mitochondrial complex I disorder; developmental impairment 3/3, muscle atrophy 2/3 and sensorineural hearing impairment 1/3 support involvement; hearing estimate is borderline.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental delay in 2/2 and cerebral atrophy in 1/2 support neurologic involvement; skeletal muscle atrophy in 1/2.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; encephalopathy with seizures in 2/4 and optic atrophy in 2/4. Reported lung disease affects only 1/4.
Primary respiratory ciliary dysfunction; double-outlet right ventricle and recurrent middle-ear inflammation each reported in 2/2 patients; estimates have small denominators.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 4/4.
Congenital motor pathway disorder producing involuntary mirror movements.
Arthrogryposis, craniosynostosis, cleft palate and intellectual disability define syndrome; reflux and hydronephrosis each reported in 1/2 patients.
Cerebellar and brainstem hypoplasia define PCH12. Individual skeletal abnormalities occur in 1/4 patients, below threshold.
Hair abnormalities, cholestasis and neurodevelopmental disease define THNS; hip dysplasia 3/3 and dislocation 2/3 support skeletal involvement. Ptosis 4/4 and PDA 2/4 omitted at cap.
Congenital abnormalities of kidneys and urinary tract, including reflux, renal hypoplasia and ectopia.
Structural brain malformations with intellectual disability, severe developmental impairment and sometimes seizures.
Inherited hair-growth disorder with sparse scalp hair in 6/6; the LSS gene alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Cerebellar degeneration and motor axonal neuropathy; muscle atrophy in 6/13 is neurogenic, without established direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy in 6/13 reflects motor denervation; common secondary wasting does not establish direct muscle involvement.

basis: Neurodegeneration, pulmonary fibrosis and cerebral angiomatosis define FINCA; chronic hemolytic anemia 3/3. Malabsorption/diarrhea 3/3 omitted at cap; liver dysfunction transient.

decisions.haematologic: involved: chronic hemolytic anemia in 3/3 demonstrates direct, persistent blood-cell damage.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cerebral angiomatosis is a named defining vascular lesion; vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: malabsorption with diarrhea in 3/3 qualifies, but omitted at the four-organ cap, prioritizing defining cerebropulmonary/vascular disease and chronic hemolysis.

basis: Defining cardiac and urinary malformations; pulmonary hypoplasia 2/2 and intestinal malrotation 1/2 support involvement. Diaphragmatic and digit defects (1/2 each) omitted by cap; small cohort.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/2 and tracheobronchomalacia in 1/2 establish common direct respiratory malformations beyond the named cardiac-urinary phenotype.
decisions.renal: primary: urinary anomalies are part of the defining urogenital phenotype; patent urachus and urethral hypospadias each occur in 1/2. Genital anomalies alone would not qualify.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: diaphragmatic hernia and toe syndactyly each occur in 1/2; omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of cardiac, urinary, pulmonary and intestinal involvement.

basis: Immunodeficiency with defining eczema; intellectual disability in 6/8. Pneumonia 2/11 and oral thrush 3/11 fall below threshold; recurrent otitis lacks demonstrated lasting damage.
Progressive ocular atrophy with visual impairment; phthisis bulbi and reduced visual acuity reported in 3/3 patients.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability, dystonia and cataracts define the syndrome; cataracts reported in 4/4.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; congenital contractures occur in 13/30 patients (~43%), establishing common structural musculoskeletal involvement.
Intellectual disability and language delay in 18/18, with macrocephaly and occasional structural brain abnormalities; hypotonia does not establish myopathy.
RELA-associated immune deficiency and dysregulation with defining chronic oral ulcers in 4/4; ileitis in 1/4 is below threshold; cytopenias lack established frequency.
Motor neuron disease with muscle atrophy; contractures and clubfeet in 2/2. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Developmental impairment, hypotonia and ataxia define neurologic dysfunction; minor skeletal and dental morphology does not establish organ damage.
Intellectual developmental disorder; sensorineural hearing impairment affects 12/21 (~57%). Hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; scoliosis and fixed flexion contractures each reported in 1/1 assessed patient, with limited sampling.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with chronic rhinitis and sinusitis (4/4); cardiac defects occur in 20-25%, while situs inversus alone causes no damage.
Intellectual disability, seizures and cerebellar atrophy; pes planus 2/2 and maxillary hypoplasia 3/5 do not establish functional skeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent skeletal morphology alone, including pes planus 2/2 and maxillary hypoplasia 3/5, does not establish damaging locomotor involvement.

basis: Inherited marrow disorder with erythroid and granulocytic hypoplasia, anemia and neutropenia in 2/2 patients.
Inherited red-cell production failure; erythroid hypoplasia and anemia occur in 2/2 reported patients.
Congenital erythroid hypoplasia defines DBA20; acetabular dysplasia and anomalous pulmonary venous return each affect 1/3 reported patients (~33%); very small sample.
Developmental disability, congenital heart defects and generalized hypertrichosis define syndrome; scoliosis occurs in 3/10 patients; ocular abnormalities below 30%.
Primary brain calcification with movement, cerebellar and cognitive dysfunction; localized calcification does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Lissencephaly and complex brainstem malformations define disease; strabismus affects 3/5. Optic nerve hypoplasia is occasional; cortical visual loss is neurologic.
Glutaminase deficiency causes developmental epileptic encephalopathy; respiratory failure in 3/4 lacks evidence of direct lung injury.
Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; cerebellar atrophy 4/4, liver dysfunction 2/2, optic atrophy 3/3. Hearing loss 2/3 and cardiomyopathy 1/2 omitted by cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: liver dysfunction and steatosis each occur in 2/2 assessed patients, as direct manifestations of the defining mitochondrial metabolic disorder.
decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebellar atrophy in 4/4 and developmental delay in 3/3 establish common direct neurologic injury secondary to the metabolic defect.

basis: Global developmental delay occurs in 9/9 and intellectual disability in 6/9. Hypotonia does not establish muscle disease; cardiac findings lack clear aggregate frequency.
Progressive encephalopathy and recurrent skeletal muscle destruction define the syndrome; cerebral visual impairment originates in the brain.
Metaphyseal dysplasia, adrenal hypoplasia and immunodeficiency define IMAGE-I; microcephaly alone does not establish brain dysfunction, and seizures occur in 3/15.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly (10/10) alone does not establish neurologic injury in this growth disorder; seizures occur in 3/15 (20%).

basis: Glutamate metabolism disorder with cataracts and developmental impairment; keratotic skin lesions in 1/1; kyphoscoliosis in 1/1 omitted by cap.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Defining intellectual developmental disorder; hearing loss 2/3, hypodontia 2/5 and esodeviation 1/3 support additional axes, with small denominators.
Polymicrogyria defines disease; vascular/valvular defects, abnormal scarring and clubfeet occur in 1/1 annotated case. Sparse evidence; gingival recession omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: vascular EDS is optional, while vascular/valvular abnormalities occur in 1/1 annotated case; not defining across the whole concept.

basis: Inherited rod-cone degeneration with progressive night blindness and reduced visual acuity in 2/2 patients.
Brain malformations, profound developmental delay and seizures define disease; joint contractures in 2/2 and optic atrophy in 1/2 support involvement.
Renal failure in 11/12 and microcephaly/developmental impairment define the syndrome; eczematoid dermatitis in 2/3 supports skin involvement.
Defining nephropathy and neurodevelopmental disease; strabismus 4/4 and hearing impairment 2/4 support involvement. Enamel hypoplasia 2/4 omitted under cap.
Primary microcephaly, callosal hypoplasia and intellectual developmental impairment; additional spinal findings remain on the neurologic axis.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental delay in 16/16; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage; cardiac and ocular abnormalities are uncommon.
Central and peripheral neurologic dysfunction defines the disorder; respiratory distress and infections do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Developmental delay in 15/15; scoliosis and ptosis each in 5/15 (~33%) support skeletal and eyelid involvement. Hypertrichosis alone does not establish skin damage.
Skeletal dysplasia and defective dental enamel define the disorder; hearing impairment occurs in 4/4 annotated patients.
Folate-metabolism defect with epilepsy and CNS hypomyelination. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; short stature and short bones alone do not establish skeletal dysfunction.
Cerebellar degeneration and ataxia; dysphagia and abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct gastrointestinal or ocular damage.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with cerebral atrophy; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic. Astigmatism and esotropia each in 1/2 do not establish direct ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: cerebral visual impairment localizes to the brain; astigmatism and esotropia each in 1/2 meet a frequency threshold but do not establish direct ocular damage.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental impairment and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each 1/1 reported patient; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct lung disease.
Developmental impairment, hypertrichosis and gingival overgrowth define syndrome; optic nerve hypoplasia 2/3; skeletal anomalies in at least 1/3 omitted by cap.
Intellectual disability and language delay in 9/9; ataxia, spasticity and brain abnormalities are neurologic. No established common extra-neurologic damage.
Inherited dicarboxylate transport disorder causing biochemical abnormalities and cerebral white-matter dysfunction; urinary metabolites do not establish renal damage.
Inherited dental enamel hypocalcification; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia; cataract occurred in the single annotated patient (1/1), supporting ocular involvement with limited evidence.
Immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis (2/3) follows infections, while Crohn/ulcerative colitis (1/3 each) are separate diagnoses. Diarrhea alone does not establish direct bowel damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 2/3 is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections; direct immune-mediated lung injury lacks a frequency.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis (1/3 each) are separately diagnosed diseases; diarrhea in 3/3 alone does not demonstrate direct bowel damage.

basis: Developmental impairment and epilepsy define this encephalopathy; nystagmus alone does not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Mitochondrial encephalopathy; congenital contractures 2/2 and optic disc pallor 30-79%; frequent bradycardia omitted by cap.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; hepatic steatosis in 4/11 (~36%), with reported transaminase elevation, supports intrinsic hepatic involvement.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define this neurodevelopmental disorder; incontinence and drooling do not establish urinary or gastrointestinal damage.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy caused by defective sphingolipid metabolism; central nystagmus and feeding difficulty do not establish additional organ damage.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 7/7 patients.
Glutaminase deficiency causes disordered glutamine metabolism with developmental delay and progressive cerebellar ataxia in 3/3 patients.
Inherited cataract with impaired vision; reported manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
Metabolic crises with lactic acidosis, neurologic regression and intrinsic mitochondrial myopathy define the disorder.
Hereditary corticospinal tract disease causes spastic paraplegia; urinary urgency in 11/30 is a neurologic symptom without evidence of urinary tract damage.
Gonadal dysgenesis, retinal dystrophy and myopathy define disease; sensorineural hearing loss 2/3. Hypodontia 4/4, renal agenesis 2/4 and reported ID omitted by cap.
Isolated spermatogenic failure affects reproduction; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 12/12 patients.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment and movement abnormalities; seizures and ataxia are common.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities causing male infertility; no evidence of endocrine dysfunction or disease outside reproductive organs.
Defined neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis in 1/2 annotated patients supports skeletal involvement, with substantial uncertainty from the small sample.
Recurrent placental hydatidiform moles and infertility are confined to reproductive and obstetric organs.
Recurrent hydatidiform mole affects placental trophoblast and reproduction; no covered organ damage is established.
Sperm structural defects and infertility are reproductive; respiratory ciliary ultrastructure alone does not establish common airway damage.
Nonsyndromic bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in 4/4 patients; vestibular dysfunction also belongs to the otologic axis.
Distal arthrogryposis defined by congenital joint contractures and limb deformities.
Distal joint contractures and limb deformities define Sheldon-Hall syndrome; facial morphology alone adds no organ axis.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; hepatic dysfunction and cardiomyopathy occur in 1-4%; optic atrophy frequency is unspecified.
Fixed foot deformities and amyotrophy 2/2; ovarian insufficiency 1/1 assessed female; visual acuity loss 1/2. Frequencies derive from a very small series.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability in 13/13; hypotonia is neurologic. Scoliosis 4/26 and individual ocular or gastrointestinal abnormalities are below 30%.
Cardiac repolarization disorder with QT prolongation in 15/15; this nonsyndromic CACNA1C phenotype does not establish Timothy syndrome features.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes bronchiectasis and sinus disease; intrinsic middle-ear clearance failure with chronic otitis/hearing dysfunction is common (>30%) in PCD.
Early neurodegeneration and microcytic hypochromic anemia define the syndrome; both documented in the reported patient.
Intellectual developmental impairment and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; arrhythmia has no documented qualifying frequency.
Developmental delay in 24/24 defines disease; nail dysplasia in 8/24 (~33%). Individual renal and cardiac defects are below 30%; overlap is unspecified.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis documents lasting airway damage in 2/2 patients. Autoimmune thrombocytopenia is a separately diagnosed disease.
Inherited platelet dysfunction causes bleeding. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage (1/2) does not itself establish direct gastrointestinal tissue disease.
Inherited HDL/apolipoprotein disorder; coronary atherosclerosis (2/5) is a separate associated disease. Cataract and tendon xanthomas each occur in only 1/5.
Paragangliomas arise in neuroendocrine paraganglia of the autonomic nervous system; hypertension frequency is unspecified.
Developmental impairment, epilepsy and structural brain abnormalities define ACTL6B encephalopathy; feeding difficulty and central hypotonia add no organ axis.
Severe intellectual, speech and motor developmental impairment define the disease. Short distal phalanges in 4/9 are dysmorphic, without demonstrated skeletal dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short distal phalanges occur in 4/9, but frequency alone does not establish functional skeletal damage; hypotonia and ambulation defects are neurologic.

basis: Tumours arise in adrenal chromaffin tissue and autonomic paraganglia; pheochromocytoma occurs in 3/8 and paraganglioma in 6/8.
Defining brain abnormalities and neurodegeneration with dysosteosclerosis; optic atrophy and visual impairment only 1/4.
Inborn metabolic disorder with elevated urinary uridine and cytidine; urinary excretion alone does not indicate renal damage.
Defined by cerebellar malformations and developmental impairment with structural eye disease; genital abnormalities have no axis.
Defining neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and abnormal tone; constipation alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Inherited sensorineural hearing loss with vestibular dysfunction; both affect the inner ear.
Genetic epilepsy with seizures in 19/19 and intellectual disability in 13/19 patients.
Congenital myopathy and joint contractures; strabismus and hypermetropia reported in 1/1; restrictive ventilation reflects muscle/chest mechanics.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, structural brain abnormalities, severe intellectual disability and seizures.
Defining neurodevelopmental and ocular dysfunction; joint contractures in 4/4-6/6. Central hypoventilation is neurologic; obesity alone does not establish endocrine damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: hypoventilation reflects central respiratory control dysfunction; recurrent pneumonia is separate, and intrinsic lung or airway damage is not established.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease with defining digital anomalies. Central visual impairment is neurologic; swallowing symptoms and separate reflux/apnea do not prove direct organ injury.
Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia in 2/2 and autoimmune hemolytic anemia in 1/2; diarrhea alone does not establish damaging enteropathy.
Inherited aortic valve disease with frequent aortic root aneurysm; all established lesions fall within the cardiovascular axis.
Epileptic neurodevelopmental disorder; conductive hearing impairment in 1/3 (~33%) supports otologic involvement. Cerebral visual impairment and ocular motor signs do not establish eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; strabismus in 3/6 and nystagmus in 2/6 do not establish direct damage to ocular tissues or the optic nerve.

basis: Nonsyndromic postaxial polydactyly is a structural skeletal anomaly of the hands and feet.
Noonan cardiac/skeletal phenotype; developmental delay 3/3 and sensorineural hearing loss 1/1 support involvement. Ptosis and cutis laxa, each 1/2, omitted at cap; small samples.

decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay in 3/3 supports common neurodevelopmental dysfunction; it is not a defining diagnostic organ for this Noonan subtype.
decisions.otologic: involved: bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment in 1/1 assessed patient supports direct hearing loss under the supplied HPO evidence; denominator is very small.

basis: Brain malformations and pancreatic agenesis define disease; diabetes 3/3 and exocrine insufficiency 2/3. Gallbladder agenesis affects 2/3.
Cerebellar degeneration, seizures and developmental impairment define the disorder; eye movement findings are neurologic.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability in 7/7; seizures in 6/7. Renal and cardiac anomalies each occur in only 1/7.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and distal skeletal anomalies define it; ptosis in 3/3 supports eyelid dysfunction. Other systemic findings mostly have single-patient denominators.
Developmental delay/intellectual disability and characteristic fifth-finger skeletal abnormalities occur in 4/4; cardiac and laryngeal defects each occur in 1/4, below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic fifth-digit skeletal abnormalities are a defining Coffin-Siris feature; clinodactyly occurs in all four reported CSS10 patients.

basis: Hereditary sensorimotor neuropathy with defining optic atrophy; pes cavus and hammertoes occur in 5/5, claw hand deformity in 3/5.
KMT2E-related neurodevelopmental syndrome with global developmental and speech delay; no other axis has established common direct damage.
Inherited retinal degeneration causing congenital visual impairment; optic disc abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Intellectual developmental disorder; myopia and strabismus reported in 1/1 patient. Short extremities alone do not establish locomotor damage.
Bronchiectasis, skeletal abnormalities and eczema each reported in 1/1; neurodevelopmental delay, keratitis, otitis and GI abnormalities omitted at cap. Evidence is a tiny cohort.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with weakness, contractures and scoliosis. Myopathy-associated tremor does not establish a separate neurologic disorder.
Ichthyotic skin disease and CNS hypomyelination; hearing loss in 2/2, optic disc pallor and visual field loss in 1/2; xerostomia in 1/2 omitted at cap.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with hepatic failure; corpus callosum hypoplasia in 1/1 reported patient supports neurologic involvement, with limited frequency evidence.
Gingival overgrowth 3/3 and dental defects 1/2; bicuspid aortic valve and developmental delay each 1/3 (~33%), based on a small series. Proptosis alone does not establish eye damage.
Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Inherited immunodeficiency; autoimmune cytopenias, lymphoma and bronchiectasis are separately diagnosed diseases. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: autoimmune hemolytic anemia (2/2), thrombocytopenia (1/2) and lymphoma (2/2) are separately diagnosed diseases arising with the immunodeficiency.

basis: Hair, sweat-gland and skin abnormalities define this ectodermal dysplasia; inflammatory blepharitis occurs in 2/2 annotated patients.
Hypopigmentation, myelination defects/cerebellar atrophy and hepatomegaly in 2/2 define HOD; reduced visual acuity 1/2. Renal imaging changes do not establish functional damage.

decisions.renal: none: reduced corticomedullary differentiation in 1/2 is an imaging finding without established renal functional injury.
decisions.ocular: involved: reduced visual acuity documents visual loss in 1/2 reported patients; frequency meets threshold, with substantial small-cohort uncertainty.

basis: Hair-shaft disorder with brittle, tiger-tail-banded hair and ichthyosis; no systemic damage is established for this subtype.
Neurodevelopmental and brain abnormalities with defining visual disease: optic atrophy 4/7 and rod-cone dystrophy 3/7. Other organ findings are below 30%.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis defect with developmental epileptic encephalopathy; isolated renal and intrinsic ocular reports do not establish >=30% involvement. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
audit_reason: Remove renal and ocular: cysts/reflux and alacrima/ptosis are isolated 1/1 reports without established >=30% frequency or defining diagnostic status. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.

basis: Oocyte maturation failure and infertility affect reproductive cells without evidence of gonadal endocrine dysfunction.
Congenital stationary retinal dysfunction causing night blindness; no separate neurologic involvement established.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; hypotonia and cerebral visual impairment reflect nervous-system dysfunction.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, intellectual disability and structural brain abnormalities.
Inherited cerebral small-vessel disease with defining pontine leukoencephalopathy; white matter abnormalities in 18/18.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; cerebral/cerebellar atrophy, seizures and hepatic failure occurred in 1/1 reported patient, supporting both organs with limited evidence.
Neurodevelopmental disease with intellectual disability in 8/8 and spasticity in 7/8; skeletal anomalies individually affect fewer than 30%.
Developmental disability and cataracts define syndrome; renal dysplasia 1/3 and cleft palate 1/3 (33%) support involvement. Unspecified heart morphology and minor skeletal features lack clear damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is a structural oral defect in 1/3 assessed patients (~33%); it is part of the syndrome rather than a separate acquired disease.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease with cerebellar hypoplasia, seizures and spasticity; optic atrophy causes direct ocular damage in 2/3 patients.
TRH resistance causes central hypothyroidism; neurodevelopmental delay occurs in 30-79%. Delayed bone maturation and dry skin alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Structural brain anomalies and severe developmental impairment define disease; scoliosis reported in 2/5 patients (40%).
Congenital progressive skeletal myopathy with scoliosis; eyelid dysfunction with ptosis in 4/4. Respiratory and renal abnormalities each 1/5, below threshold.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with developmental epileptic encephalopathy; hearing impairment 7/14 (50%). Small nails 5/14 do not establish damaging skin/nail disease.

decisions.dermatologic: none: small nails in 5/14 establish a morphological finding, without demonstrated tissue injury or loss of function.

basis: Intellectual disability and epilepsy define the disease; hypotonia and ataxia reflect neurologic dysfunction without established primary myopathy.
GPI biosynthesis defect with severe neurodevelopmental impairment; scoliosis 5/5; strabismus 5/5 and hypermetropia 2/5. Hypertrichosis alone does not establish skin damage.
Inherited podocyte disease causing steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, mesangial sclerosis and kidney failure.
Progressive spastic tetraplegia, pyramidal signs and cerebellar atrophy establish neurologic disease; fasciculations and axial hypotonia do not establish primary muscle damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus in 11/15 and visual impairment in 5/15. Hypotonia and feeding difficulty do not establish primary muscle or GI damage.
Developmental delay in 19/19 and intellectual disability in 10/10 define the disorder; hypotonia and external ear shape do not establish muscle disease or hearing impairment.
Pontocerebellar malformation and severe developmental impairment; strabismus 3/3 supports ocular dysfunction. Liver dysfunction in one assessed patient cannot establish prevalence.

decisions.hepatic: none: decreased liver function in 1/1 assessed patient is an isolated observation, insufficient to establish involvement in >=30% of this syndrome.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with defining skeletal anomalies; hearing impairment occurs in 1/4, below threshold. Hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
Congenital lower urinary tract obstruction; reflux and urethral abnormalities remain within the renal axis.
Retinal degeneration with progressive visual loss in 3/3; retinal vessel attenuation remains within the ocular axis.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia; structural laryngeal stenosis in 1/3 supports airway involvement, with stridor in 2/3.
Ptosis, neurodevelopmental impairment and metopic/craniosynostosis abnormalities define the syndrome; hearing impairment and cardiac defects are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental impairment is a core syndrome feature, supported by frequent developmental, speech and motor delays.

basis: Inherited obesity-metabolic syndrome with defining hypertension in 26/35 (~74%). Coronary atherosclerosis and myocardial infarction are separately diagnosed sequelae.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertension is a core metabolic-syndrome feature and occurs in 26/35 (~74%); coronary disease and infarction are separate sequelae.

basis: Brain malformations, developmental impairment and arthrogryposis define disease; neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish direct lung damage.
Congenital heart disease defines the Noonan phenotype; strabismus affects 3/9 patients (~33%). Reported neurodevelopmental and skeletal abnormalities individually fall below 30%.
Usher syndrome defines combined sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and retinal disease; left ventricular hypertrophy reported in 2/5 patients (40%).
Myopathy, leukoencephalopathy and ocular dysfunction define disease; ptosis 6/6 and ophthalmoplegia 3/4. Dysphagia and respiratory failure reflect muscle dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular dysfunction is a named, defining component; ptosis occurs in 6/6 and external ophthalmoplegia in 3/4.

basis: Infantile hepatic failure; vertebral and femoral epiphyseal abnormalities in 3/3 support skeletal involvement. Prolonged PT reflects hepatic dysfunction.
Isolated sperm flagellar dysfunction and male infertility; no endocrine failure or other organ disease established.
Bone fragility disorder; permanent tooth agenesis in 2/5 (40%). Motor delay alone does not establish neural injury; blue sclerae do not establish ocular damage.
IRF9-associated antiviral immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis and mucosal disease are reported, but their frequency is insufficiently established for additional axes.
Brain anomalies and optic atrophy define disease; hearing impairment and hip dislocation/contractures in 2/2. VSD in 1/2 omitted under cap.
Defining neurodevelopmental disease, ocular malformations (4/5) and cardiac defects (3/5); sensorineural hearing impairment in 2/4 supports otologic involvement.
Defining intellectual and language impairment; strabismus and hypermetropia each affect 3/4. PFO and an aberrant artery alone do not establish cardiac dysfunction.
Congenital structural skeletal myopathy; cardiomegaly and congestive heart failure in 1/2 patients support cardiac involvement. Respiratory weakness does not establish lung injury.
Distal skeletal myopathy with muscle weakness, atrophy and abnormal muscle histology; cardiac involvement is not established for this subtype.
Developmental impairment, gingival overgrowth and nail hypoplasia define disease; PDA in 2/3; skeletal abnormalities in ≥1/3 omitted by cap.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and distal skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; joint hypermobility occurs in 8/18. Hearing impairment is 4/19, below threshold.
Congenital intestinal dysfunction causes malabsorptive diarrhea in 9/9; villous atrophy occurs in 3/9.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with peripheral neuropathy; sensorineural hearing impairment in 5/6. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and male infertility; sperm motility abnormalities do not establish airway or endocrine disease.
METTL5-related intellectual disability with microcephaly and developmental impairment. Strabismus occurs in 2/7 (~29%), just below threshold; cardiac defects in 1/7.
Congenital communicating hydrocephalus with ventriculomegaly, seizures and neurodevelopmental delay affects the brain.
Isolated sperm structural and motility defects cause male infertility; no endocrine or other axis involvement is established.
Intellectual and speech developmental impairment define the disorder; strabismus occurs in 4/16 (25%), below threshold.
Telomere biology disorder defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or hypocellular bone marrow failure.
Cortical malformations, severe intellectual disability and developmental delay in all reported patients; seizures are common.
Pancreas-specific hereditary cancer susceptibility defines the target axis; susceptibility does not establish existing pancreatic damage or melanoma involvement.
ATP synthase deficiency causes regression in 4/4 and ataxia in 3/4. Ophthalmoplegia in 2/4 does not establish intrinsic ocular damage; cardiomyopathy in 1/4 is below threshold.

decisions.ocular: none: ophthalmoplegia occurs in 2/4, but ocular motor dysfunction can arise from neurologic disease; direct damage to the eye is not established.

basis: Developmental delay and severe intellectual disability in 5/5; seizures in 3/5. Hypotonia accompanies neurologic disease; visual impairment only 1/5.
CNS hypomyelination defines the disorder; associated myopia affects 3/4 (~75%); optic atrophy occurs in only 1/4 and nystagmus may be central.
Airway ciliary dysfunction causes bronchiectasis and chronic sinonasal disease; recurrent infections are secondary, separately diagnosed conditions.
Inherited retinal and choroidal degeneration causing visual field loss.
Airway ciliary dysfunction causes chronic sinusitis and bronchiectasis (6/6); noncommunicating hydrocephalus also occurred in 6/6.
Defining skeletal growth delay and microcephaly; hypermetropia 2/2; delayed thelarche 1/1 with reported delayed puberty. Nail hypoplasia 1/2 omitted at cap.

decisions.dermatologic: none: nail hypoplasia in 1/2 qualifies by frequency but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of visual and pubertal dysfunction.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: delayed thelarche in 1/1 assessed female and reported delayed puberty support endocrine dysfunction; genital anatomy alone would not.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental disease; strabismus affects 4/5. Flat feet/joint laxity (3/5) lack demonstrated functional injury; constipation alone does not establish gut damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes planus and joint hypermobility occur in 3/5, but neither documented skeletal injury nor impaired musculoskeletal function is established.

basis: Developmental impairment and brain malformations define disease; vertebral anomalies 4/15 (<30%) excluded.
Central neurodevelopmental disorder with regression and absent speech; hypotonia and weakness do not establish primary muscle damage.
Congenital bladder enlargement affects the urinary tract; individual cardiac abnormalities occur in fewer than 30%, with overlap and aggregate frequency unknown.
GOT2-related malate-aspartate shuttle deficiency causes epileptic encephalopathy, hyperammonemia and elevated lactate; recurrent infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Ovarian endocrine failure with reduced estradiol and elevated FSH; gonadal hormone dysfunction belongs to the endocrine axis.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay in 7/7 define the syndrome; clinodactyly in 4/7 and tapered fingers in 3/7 do not establish impaired skeletal function.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: clinodactyly occurs in 4/7, but minor digit-shape variants without demonstrated functional impairment do not establish skeletal damage.

basis: Named ectodermal, ocular and brain abnormalities; scarring alopecia and dental defects each occur in 3/7. Acral skeletal anomalies omitted under the four-axis cap.
Skeletal dysplasia with short long bones, vertebral flattening and hip/knee deformity in 4/4 patients.
Cortical malformations, developmental impairment, epilepsy and spasticity reflect central nervous system disease.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the disorder; blindness and scoliosis each affect 2/5 patients (40%), supporting visual and skeletal involvement.
CSNK2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, motor delay and seizures; hypotonia alone does not establish myopathy.
