Neuromuscular/neurodevelopmental disease with defining ocular or auditory anomalies. Individual retinal and hearing findings are reported in 1/4; destructive muscle findings also 1/4.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular anomalies are a defining named component, with structural retinal abnormalities documented; individual 1/4 findings do not establish total ocular frequency.
decisions.otologic: primary: auditory anomalies are a defining named alternative, with sensorineural hearing impairment documented in 1/4; the involved-organ frequency threshold does not govern primary features.

basis: Intracranial arterial-wall disease; subarachnoid hemorrhage in 7/17 (~41%) is a separately diagnosed rupture complication.

decisions.neurologic: none: subarachnoid hemorrhage affects 7/17 (~41%), but is a separately diagnosed complication; intracranial arterial location alone is cardiovascular.

basis: Brain abnormalities and intellectual disability with defining craniosynostosis; strabismus in 5/9 and ptosis in 3/9 support ocular dysfunction.
Cortical malformation syndrome with pachygyria, microcephaly and developmental impairment; optic atrophy and cerebral visual impairment each reported in 1/5.
Developmental impairment, epilepsy and brain atrophy define the disorder; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 2/6 patients (~33%).
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; structural genu valgum occurs in 4/12 (~33%). Constipation and feeding difficulties do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: genu valgum is a structural skeletal abnormality reported in 4/12 (~33%); the supplied evidence does not establish that it is merely a transient postural finding.

basis: Sperm flagellar abnormalities cause male infertility without established endocrine or other axis involvement.
Intellectual disability defines syndrome. Myopia 6/12 and strabismus 4/12 support ocular involvement; congenital heart defects affect about half. Hearing impairment 3/12 is below 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects collectively affect about half of reported CDK8 cases; individual HPO lesion frequencies should not be summed because they can overlap.

basis: Sperm flagellar abnormalities cause male infertility; reproductive dysfunction alone has no axis.
Neutropenic immunodeficiency; exocrine pancreatic insufficiency 2/3 and neurodevelopmental features including autistic behavior 2/2. Raised transaminases alone do not prove liver damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, hypotonia and movement abnormalities define disease; visual impairment in 3/5 is cerebral rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Joubert neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus and ptosis in 4/4, and structural hand polydactyly in 4/4; hearing loss only 1/4.
Congenital joint contractures and corpus callosum agenesis define the syndrome; optic atrophy occurs in 4/4 assessed patients.
Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy with recurrent corneal erosions.
Spastic paraplegia with neurodevelopmental impairment; reduced visual acuity occurs in 2/4, with retinal abnormalities. Hearing loss and cleft palate each occur in 1/4.
Neurodegenerative spastic paraplegia; reduced visual acuity in 4/4 supports ocular functional loss, although optic atrophy is documented in only 1/4.
Congenital lymphatic vascular malformation causing hydrops. Effusions and edema alone do not establish persistent pulmonary, cardiac or skin injury.
Developmental disability and brain abnormalities define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 16/20. Facial morphology alone does not establish other organ damage.
Mitochondrial defect; cardiomyopathy 2/2, thrombocytopenia 2/2, weakness 2/2 with elevated CK support heart, blood and muscle involvement. Alopecia 2/2 omitted at cap.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect with lactic acidosis 3/3; neurologic disease includes infantile spasms/hypsarrhythmia in 1/3. Optic damage frequency is unspecified.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 4/4 patients.
Developmental delay in 5/5 and intellectual disability in 4/4; small hands and high palate do not establish functional damage; esophageal atresia 1/5.
Congenital cardiac and great-vessel malformations define the disease; anxiety and depression have no organ axis.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes bronchiectasis in 9/9; otitis media occurs in only 2/9, below threshold.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with prolonged QT, bradycardia and atrioventricular block.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 4/4 patients.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; hypotonia and feeding support reflect neurologic dysfunction without established separate muscle or gut damage.
Neurodevelopmental synaptopathy; scoliosis in 3/3 and strabismus in 2/3 support skeletal and ocular involvement, although the cohort is small.
LACC1-associated inflammatory arthritis; reactive leukocytosis and thrombocytosis do not establish intrinsic blood disease; rash alone does not establish skin damage.
Severe neurodevelopmental disease; vesicoureteral reflux and gingival overgrowth each 2/4. Neonatal distress alone does not establish lung damage; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.

decisions.pulmonary: none: neonatal respiratory distress (4/4) alone does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage; tracheomalacia and laryngomalacia are each reported in only 1/4.

basis: Congenital cerebellar disorder; optic atrophy in 1/3 supports ocular damage near the threshold, although the sample is small.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 2/4 and chronic rhinitis; infertility has no axis. Recurrent infections do not imply immunodeficiency.
Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis is an HPV-associated airway disease; keratosis pilaris and atrophodermia in 2/2 establish skin involvement.
Metabolic enzyme deficiency; cataracts in 3/4. Neurodevelopmental/CNS impairment is a common core feature (>30%); hepatic, cardiac and pancreatic injury each 1/4.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment with CNS abnormalities is a common syndrome manifestation (estimated >30%); supplied HPO entries lack a precise frequency.

basis: Infantile T-cell lymphopenia defines the blood/immune disorder; nail dystrophy in 10/25 (40%). Pneumonia in 20% does not support pulmonary involvement.
Developmental impairment and ataxia define disease; elevated LDL in 2/2 and developmental cataract in 1/3 support additional axes, with small-sample uncertainty.
Mitochondrial encephalopathy; cardiomyopathy 8/15 (~53%) and brittle hair 6/11 (~55%). Respiratory failure reflects neuromuscular dysfunction; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency reflects neurologic or neuromuscular failure; direct lung or airway disease is not established.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: brittle hair in 6/11 (~55%) represents persistent structural damage to hair shafts.

basis: Mitochondrial depletion with axonal degeneration; weakness and wasting in 1/1 can be neurogenic. Direct myopathy, pulmonary injury and attributable blood disease are unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: wasting and weakness accompany axonal degeneration; scoliosis in one reported patient does not establish common direct skeletal or muscle damage.

basis: Corneal opacity and cardiomyopathy define phenotype; lactic acidosis 3/5 supports metabolic dysfunction; encephalopathy/seizures 2/5 (40%); contractures 2/5 omitted at cap.
Brain malformations and developmental delay define neurologic disease; hypospadias in 4/4 males is a urethral malformation. Other genital findings are reproductive.

decisions.renal: primary: hypospadias affects the urethra, explicitly covered by renal, and occurs in 4/4 reported males.

basis: Rhizomelia defines skeletal disease; delayed myelination, stage 1 CKD and laryngomalacia each reported in 1/2 patients; frequencies rest on a very small series.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with fractures; respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness. Obstructive sleep apnea (3/3) is separately diagnosed and does not prove intrinsic airway injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory muscle weakness belongs to musculoskeletal disease; separately diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea in 3/3 does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

basis: Congenital skeletal muscle disease with proximal weakness and minicore lesions; no common independent damage to another axis is established.
Pathological brain calcification with ataxia, parkinsonism and cognitive deterioration; no systemic mineral metabolism disorder is established.
Intellectual developmental disorder; scoliosis in 4/8 patients supports musculoskeletal involvement.
Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness, reduced visual acuity and retinal vascular attenuation.
Inherited ocular growth/refractive disorder with increased globe axial length and high myopia.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; hearing impairment 2/2, vesicoureteral reflux 1/2 and optic nerve hypoplasia 1/2 support involvement; small cohort.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; hypothyroidism and structural external-ear hypoplasia each occur in 2/5 (40%). Cardiac defect is 1/5; apnea/reflux do not prove direct organ injury.

decisions.otologic: involved: microtia is structural hypoplasia of the external ear in 2/5 (40%), rather than merely an unusually positioned ear.

basis: PKHD1-associated cystic kidney disease; hepatic fibrosis occurs in 13/16. Hypertension in 12/16 is a separately diagnosed secondary condition.
Nephrocerebral syndrome with developmental impairment, brain atrophy and glomerular disease; optic atrophy occurs in 13/14 patients.
Nephrotic renal failure and microcephalic neurodevelopmental disease occur in 3/3; scoliosis in 1/3 supports skeletal involvement, although the sample is small.
Nephrotic glomerular disease and neurodevelopmental impairment define GAMOS; microphthalmia 2/2 and aortic coarctation 1/2; skeletal findings omitted by cap.
Nephrotic syndrome and primary microcephaly in 4/4; developmental delay in 3/4. Skin findings occur in only 1/4.
Microcephaly/developmental impairment and steroid-resistant glomerular disease define GAMOS5 (2/2); hearing impairment occurs in 1/2 patients.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder with hyperkeratosis and erythroderma; no established additional organ damage.
Inherited keratinization disorder with persistent skin plaques and erythema in 8/8.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder with palmoplantar keratoderma, hyperkeratosis and nail changes.
Defining keratinization disease with inherited platelet-disorder parents; the definition establishes an enzymatic defect of sphingolipid metabolism.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the definition establishes deficient sphingolipid synthesis from impaired enzyme function, supporting an inborn metabolic disorder beyond the gene name alone.

basis: Hyperkeratosis and nail abnormalities define the skin disorder; joint stiffness in 4/4 does not establish direct joint or muscle damage.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy with spastic ataxia; fixed joint contractures 4/5 and scoliosis 2/3 support musculoskeletal damage. Oculomotor signs are neurologic.
Encephalocele/cerebellar malformations and cystic renal dysplasia define the Meckel phenotype; retinopathy frequency is unspecified.
Orofacial/tongue abnormalities, digital malformations and neurodevelopmental impairment define this subtype; developmental delay and polydactyly reported in 1/1; retinopathy frequency unknown.
Meier-Gorlin skeletal and external-ear malformation syndrome; renal hypoplasia in 1/1 reported patient, with very limited subtype evidence.
Perrault syndrome combines sensorineural hearing loss (2/2) and primary ovarian endocrine insufficiency; uterine hypoplasia has no axis.
Congenital ichthyosis with scaling and hyperkeratosis in 6/6; no established extracutaneous damage.
Inherited congenital ichthyosis with epidermal hyperkeratosis; fungal nail infection is a separate infection and does not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Cerebellar ataxia with cerebellar hypoplasia and developmental delay; nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction without established ocular damage.
Cerebellar degeneration with sensorimotor neuropathy; abnormal eye movements and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease with retinal folds, degeneration and detachment; neurodevelopmental involvement is not established for this specific subtype.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy and pes cavus in 4/4, with fatty muscle replacement in 3/3.
Curariform poisoning blocks neuromuscular junction transmission; respiratory paralysis reflects this blockade rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Statin toxicity predominantly manifests as skeletal muscle toxicity; clinically significant hepatic injury is uncommon.
These poisonings chiefly cause CNS dysfunction, including ataxia, nystagmus and depressed consciousness; cardiac toxicity is not consistently common across both drugs.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 2/2 patients.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 2/2 patients.
Congenital sensorineural deafness defines disease; structural iris coloboma occurs in 1/2 reported patients, supporting ocular involvement with limited sampling.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment in all annotated patients.
Nonsyndromic congenital sensorineural hearing loss with semicircular canal malformation.
SGPL1 metabolic disease with nephrotic and endocrine dysfunction; ichthyosis 4/5 and developmental delay 3/8 support involvement; lymphopenia 2/8 excluded.
Respiratory ciliopathy with bronchiectasis; hearing impairment occurs in 1/1 annotated patient and commonly (>=30%) in PCD. Thyroid disease is not established as intrinsic.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypothyroidism and goiter in one patient do not establish a causal thyroid manifestation of this ciliopathy; coincident thyroid disease is excluded.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment, present in 11/11 reported patients.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 7/7 patients.
NLRP3-associated deafness involves cochlear autoinflammation; optional systemic inflammatory symptoms do not establish common lasting extra-ear damage.
Inherited steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia in 3/3 patients.
Inherited nephrotic syndrome with proteinuria and minimal-change glomerular disease in 3/3; genetic disease does not establish an immune mechanism.
DZIP1L-related renal cystic dysplasia; hypertension (5/7) is a secondary, separately diagnosed disease; hepatosplenomegaly occurs in only 1/7.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder with leukodystrophy; hearing impairment 30-79%. Retinopathy <30%; isolated strabismus does not establish intrinsic ocular damage.
Inherited nonsyndromic hearing loss.
Cerebellar malformation and developmental disability define disease; eyelid dysfunction with ptosis occurs in 7/10. Retinal dystrophy 2/9 is below threshold.
Joubert brain malformation; hand polydactyly 3/4 and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 1/2. Oculomotor apraxia and nystagmus reflect central dysfunction.
Molar tooth malformation and developmental delay in 4/4; individual ocular abnormalities occur in 1/4, below threshold.
Hindbrain malformation causes developmental delay and ataxia; oculomotor apraxia and central apnea do not establish direct eye or lung damage.
Schizophrenia is a psychiatric disorder; cognitive impairment in 4/26 does not establish common neurologic involvement.
Congenital hypomyelination of peripheral nerves; secondary weakness does not establish primary muscle damage.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy defines CNS dysfunction; hypotonia does not independently establish skeletal muscle disease.
Progressive developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; visual impairment lacks evidence of intrinsic eye disease, and elevated CK alone does not establish myopathy.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, intellectual disability and developmental regression.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with an inherited GPI-anchor biosynthesis defect; hypermobility alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage; contracture frequency unspecified.
audit_reason: Remove musculoskeletal: hypermobility alone does not establish direct tissue damage or functional loss, despite its frequency. Contractures have no frequency establishing the 30% threshold.

basis: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; structural scoliosis reported in 2/4 patients supports skeletal involvement.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, profound developmental impairment and structural brain abnormalities.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy in 2/4 establishes common ocular damage. Feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with severe intellectual and motor impairment; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, profound developmental impairment and brain atrophy.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with cerebral atrophy; optic atrophy occurred in 1/1 reported patient. Apnea does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
SCN3A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; dysphagia and cerebral visual impairment occur in only 1/6.
Epileptic neurodevelopmental disorder; cleft palate, strabismus and conductive hearing loss each affect 1/3 reported patients. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ocular alignment dysfunction (strabismus) is reported in 1/3 patients, meeting the frequency threshold in this small cohort.

basis: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with universal seizures and intellectual disability; hypotonia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy directly affects brain function; seizures and absent speech occur in 4/4 patients. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Oral/digital malformations define OFD17; tetralogy of Fallot and CNS hypomyelination each 1/1. Renal hypoplasia and hearing impairment also 1/1, omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none at cap: renal hypoplasia occurs in 1/1, but documented cardiac and CNS abnormalities have greater demonstrated functional severity.
decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS hypomyelination and ventriculomegaly occur in 1/1; retained with severe cardiac disease under the four-axis cap.

basis: Inherited cerebellar degeneration with ataxia; tinnitus in 3/7 is a symptom without established ear injury. Abnormal saccades are neurologic.
Inherited cerebellar degeneration with atrophy and ataxia; downbeat nystagmus reflects cerebellar dysfunction.
Cerebellar degeneration and sensory neuropathy; abnormal eye movements are neurologic manifestations rather than intrinsic ocular damage.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; occasional diplopia does not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Inherited erythrocytosis; elevated erythropoietin does not itself establish endocrine-organ disease.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia with defining pulmonary hypoplasia/respiratory failure; ventricular septal defect reported in 1/2 patients. Cardiac frequency rests on a very small cohort.
Inherited CNS hypomyelination and neurodegeneration. Hearing loss and blindness are reported at 1-4%; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct common pulmonary injury.
ARID2-related neurodevelopmental impairment; short stature and minor digital variants do not establish skeletal damage. Isolated 1/1 hepatic reports do not establish prevalence.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short stature (8/8), tapered fingers and isolated clinodactyly do not establish a defining skeletal dysplasia or substantial skeletal dysfunction.

basis: Gingival fibromatosis in 9/9 defines oral disease; nonspecific sternal morphology in 3/9 (~33%) does not establish skeletal damage or dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: abnormal sternal morphology in 3/9 (~33%) meets the frequency threshold, but the unspecified finding does not establish damaging skeletal involvement.

basis: Mitochondrial energy metabolism disorder; developmental delay, seizures and white matter abnormalities in the sole reported patient; arrest alone excludes cardiac inference.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; decreased liver function reported in 1/1 annotated patients, with limited sample size.
Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; hepatic injury, cataract and sensorineural hearing loss each reported in 1/1; skeletal abnormalities omitted by cap.
Immunodeficiency with mycobacterial susceptibility; anemia in 2/2 accompanies infection without established intrinsic blood injury. Hepatosplenomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia in 2/2 during mycobacterial disease does not establish direct blood damage from the immunodeficiency; marrow injury or hemolysis is not documented.

basis: Defined immunodeficiency; supplied data do not establish common direct ocular, gastrointestinal or skin damage. Associated infections and celiac disease are separate diagnoses.
Congenital retinal synaptic dysfunction; developmental language impairment 4/6 and ataxia 2/6; associated glucose dysregulation/hyperglycemia 3/4.
Mitochondrial disorder with defining severe encephalopathy; hearing impairment and microcytic anemia each reported in 1/1. Muscle DNA depletion alone does not establish myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: structural brain abnormality, seizures and severe motor dysfunction define the reported encephalopathic phenotype (1/1).

basis: Multivitamin transport defect with infantile neurodegeneration; reduced IgG in 2/2 supports humoral immune dysfunction. Nystagmus alone does not establish eye damage.
Defining myopathy/respiratory phenotype; lung hypoplasia 2/3. Cleft palate 3/3; urinary obstruction/hydronephrosis 1/3, renal hypoplasia 1/1. Ocular findings omitted at cap; tiny cohort.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: respiratory insufficiency defines the syndrome, with direct lung hypoplasia in 2/3 rather than respiratory muscle weakness alone.

basis: Hereditary optic degeneration; hearing loss 4/22 and neurologic abnormalities generally below 30% in larger cohorts.
Immunodeficiency with autoinflammation and established bronchiectatic lung damage in 4/5 patients (80%); hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish organ dysfunction.

Intrinsic leukocyte dysfunction and cytopenias define immunodeficiency. Bronchiectasis in 1/3 supports pulmonary involvement; chronic obstruction and fibrosis are also reported. Small samples limit certainty.
audit_reason: Add pulmonary: bronchiectasis occurs in 1/3, with chronic obstruction and fibrosis also reported, and belongs to the named parent syndrome. Requiring primary immune lung injury excludes qualifying structural damage.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with intrinsic neutrophil dysfunction and reduced B cells; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic pulmonary damage.
Congenital glycosylation disorder with muscular dystrophy and impaired neurodevelopment; seizures and white-matter abnormalities support neurologic involvement.
Familial immune hyperinflammation with hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; hepatitis and intellectual disability each reported in 1/1 patient; subtype evidence is limited.
Immune dysregulation with eosinophilia; dermatitis 4/4 supports skin involvement. Colonic eosinophilia 1/1 and food allergy do not establish common damaging gut disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: food allergy does not establish intestinal damage; colonic eosinophilia in one assessed patient establishes neither dysfunction nor prevalence of at least 30%.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder defined by developmental impairment, seizures and language delay; dysmorphic features do not establish other organ damage.
Complex I metabolic deficiency; cardiomyopathy, pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary hypoplasia each reported in 1/1 patient; evidence is limited to one case.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; reduced hemoglobin in 3/9 supports hematologic involvement. Constipation lacks evidence of direct gut injury.
Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness and progressive visual field loss; retinal vessels remain within the ocular axis.
Oocyte and early embryonic developmental failure causing female infertility; purely reproductive, without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Oocyte maturation arrest causes female infertility without established endocrine dysfunction; reproductive function has no axis.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental impairment and muscle weakness occur in 2/2, with documented brain injury. Ophthalmoplegia does not establish intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: external ophthalmoplegia (1/1) reflects extraocular muscle or neural dysfunction; nystagmus does not establish intrinsic eye injury.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation disorder presenting as mitochondrial myopathy; progressive weakness and diagnostic muscle pathology occur in the single annotated patient.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myopathy is the defining clinical presentation, supported by progressive weakness, ragged-red fibers and respiratory-chain abnormalities in muscle.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic deficiency; developmental impairment, dystonia and callosal malformation in 1/1; hip dysplasia in 1/1. Adrenal insufficiency shares the endocrine axis.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment, dystonia and callosal malformation occur in 1/1; the defining disorder is oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.

basis: ALG14 glycosylation disorder defined by intellectual disability, epilepsy and abnormal CNS myelination.
Progressive CNS disorder; muscle-fibre abnormalities in 3/5 and contractures in 5/12 support musculoskeletal involvement. Visual and respiratory impairment may be neurogenic.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 8/12 does not localize damage to the eye or optic nerve; cerebral visual impairment remains possible.

basis: Hereditary corticospinal tract disease causing spastic paraplegia; muscle spasms reflect neurologic dysfunction.
CoQ10 biosynthesis disorder; encephalopathy, developmental delay, seizures and ataxia affect 3/3. Eye movement abnormalities are neurologic; muscle fiber predominance alone is not muscle damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy, developmental delay, seizures and ataxia occur in 3/3, documenting CNS damage from the metabolic defect.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental delay in 34/37 and intellectual disability in 23/32; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle disease.
Congenital glycosylation disorder defined by myopathy, epilepsy and progressive cerebral atrophy; neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Inherited myofibrillar muscle disease; left ventricular hypertrophy in 2/4 patients supports cardiac involvement.
Motor neuron disease; denervation causes muscle weakness/atrophy in most reported patients and scoliosis in 2/3. Respiratory weakness does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Isolated sperm production and structural defects cause male infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; visual impairment occurs in 6/15 (40%). Joint hypermobility in 7/13 lacks documented joint injury or functional loss.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypermobility in 7/13 establishes laxity, but does not by itself establish joint damage or loss of function.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; cerebral atrophy/regression, optic atrophy and hearing impairment each reported in 1/1. Aspiration does not establish intrinsic pulmonary disease.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral atrophy, thalamic lesions and regression in 1/1 establish brain injury; the concept is defined by its metabolic defect.

basis: Respiratory-chain defect; ataxia 2/2, weakness 1/1 with abnormal muscle fibers 3/3, cardiomyopathy 1/2; cap omits anemia and hearing loss, each 1/2.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; hepatic steatosis, ventricular hypertrophy/heart failure and brain atrophy each reported in 1/1 phenotyped patients; evidence is sparse.
Respiratory-chain disorder; leukodystrophy/cognitive decline 2/2, muscle weakness with abnormal fibers 2/2, cardiomyopathy 1/1 assessed. Small series; visual loss may be cerebral.
Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; intellectual disability 5/5 and basal ganglia lesions 3/3; optic atrophy 2/3. Abnormal muscle enzyme staining alone does not establish myopathy.
Respiratory-chain defect; abnormal CNS myelination, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and renal hypoplasia each 1/1. Microphthalmia, also 1/1, omitted at cap.
Disordered vitamin D metabolism causes defective skeletal mineralization; metaphyseal flaring and cupping occur in 2/2.
Defining cleft palate, retinopathy and developmental delay; chronic dermatitis 2/2. Hearing impairment 2/3 omitted by the four-axis cap.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic atopic dermatitis in 2/2 assessed patients supports direct skin inflammation; retained under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment in 2/3 qualifies by frequency but is omitted under the cap, favoring the more frequent chronic skin disease.

basis: Polyamine metabolic disorder with neurodevelopmental abnormalities and alopecia; ptosis affects 2/4 (50%). Hearing loss in one assessed patient does not establish prevalence.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis is eyelid dysfunction reported in 2/4 (50%), corroborated by a frequent bilateral-ptosis annotation.
decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing impairment in one assessed patient is insufficient to establish occurrence in at least 30% of the syndrome population.

basis: CARD8-associated immune-mediated intestinal inflammation with Crohn-like mucosal injury, chronic diarrhea and occasional stricture; no established extraintestinal damage.
Microcornea, cataract and rod-cone dystrophy with reduced vision occurred in 4/4 patients; all defining abnormalities are ocular.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain metabolic defect; neurologic damage is common, with ataxia in 3/3 and cerebellar vermis atrophy in 2/2 assessed.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect; seizures in 9/11 support neurologic involvement. Renal and liver-synthetic abnormalities were reported in one patient only.
Respiratory-chain defect; neuropathy/developmental impairment and COX-negative muscle fibers with exercise intolerance each reported in 1/1 patient.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: COX-negative muscle fibers plus exercise intolerance in 1/1 support clinically consequential muscle dysfunction, beyond an isolated enzyme result.

basis: Respiratory-chain defect; brain atrophy/seizures, retinopathy and pulmonary arterial hypertension each reported in 1/1. Skeletal findings omitted at cap; sepsis is separate.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment, seizures and brain atrophy occur in 1/1; the concept is defined by complex IV deficiency rather than a specific neurologic syndrome.

basis: Mitochondrial respiratory-chain deficiency; cerebral/cerebellar atrophy, regression and epileptic spasms each reported in 2/2 patients.
COA8-related respiratory-chain metabolic defect; cavitating leukodystrophy in 6/6 and regression in 5/6 establish neurologic damage. Muscle staining alone does not establish myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: leukodystrophy occurs in 6/6, regression in 5/6 and neuropathy in 3/6; the concept itself is defined by the respiratory-chain metabolic defect.

basis: Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; weakness and pathological muscle fibers establish myopathy in 2/2. Neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: weakness and biopsy-confirmed muscle pathology occur in 2/2; muscle is directly affected by the defining mitochondrial metabolic disorder.

basis: Mitochondrial deficiency with developmental regression in 2/2; protein-losing enteropathy in 1/2 supports gastrointestinal involvement; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.
Respiratory-chain disorder; pulmonary arterial hypertension in 2/2 and hepatic enzyme elevation in 2/2 with hepatomegaly support vascular and liver injury; small cohort.
Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; language delay in 4/4 and dystonia in 3/4 support neurologic involvement. Muscle biochemical findings alone do not establish clinical myopathy.
Hypomyelination and neurodegeneration define disease. Scoliosis and ptosis, each 1/1, do not establish direct extra-neural damage rather than consequences of severe motor dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis in 1/1 is compatible with neurological motor dysfunction; direct ocular injury or impaired vision is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis in 1/1 accompanies severe spastic tetraplegia; evidence does not establish direct skeletal or muscle disease.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder defined by seizures and brain atrophy; no additional organ has established common direct damage.
Brain malformation, seizures and severe developmental delay in 3/3; flexion contractures in 2/3; exotropia in 2/3 and optic disc pallor in 1/3 support ocular involvement.
Defining neurodevelopmental, intestinal/salivary and hearing dysfunction; lacrimal failure in 2/2. Airway obstruction/mucus plugging and skeletal anomalies omitted at the four-organ cap.

decisions.pulmonary: none under cap: recurrent mucus plugging and choanal atresia qualify, but lacrimal failure in 2/2 has stronger frequency evidence than airway findings in 1/1.
decisions.ocular: involved: alacrima in 2/2 represents persistent loss of lacrimal function; retained as the fourth axis.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 8/8; motor delay in 2/8 is below the involvement threshold.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment and sensorineural deafness; cardiac and tracheoesophageal defects each occur in 1/6.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 19/19 patients.
Developmental delay 7/7; structural heart defects are a Noonan diagnostic feature (ASD/MVP each 2/7, ~29%); ptosis 6/7 and pes planus 3/7 support ocular and skeletal involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital structural heart defects are a major Noonan diagnostic feature; ASD and mitral prolapse each occur in 2/7 (~29%), approximately the threshold, with overlap unknown.

basis: Nonsyndromic autosomal recessive sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 3/3 patients.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement established.
Duane ocular motility anomaly, congenital myopathy and severe early scoliosis define the syndrome.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; no endocrine or other organ dysfunction established.
Defining skeletal dysplasia, T-cell immunodeficiency and developmental impairment; renal malformation occurs in fewer than 30%.
Marrow failure, B-cell deficiency and skeletal dysplasia define; cerebral hypoplasia/developmental disability 30-79%; cardiomyopathy 5-29%, heart failure may reflect anemia.
Cerebellar hypoplasia/degeneration causes congenital ataxia and developmental impairment. Liver dysfunction is occasional (5-29%); nystagmus is neurologic.
Isolated eyelid disorder with recurrent swelling leading to eyelid tissue atrophy and laxity.
Isolated splitting of the iris stroma; confined to the eye.
Chronic recurrent corneal epithelial disease without systemic involvement; an immune mechanism is not established.
Corneal degeneration with marginal thinning and astigmatism.
Fungal infection directly inflames and damages the cornea.
Radiation-induced damage to brachial or lumbosacral peripheral nerve plexuses; treatment causation defines this disease itself.
Radiation-induced necrosis of mandibular bone defines this disease; separate oral mucosal injury is not established.
Copper-metabolism disorder causing axonal neuropathy; muscle atrophy and ocular motor findings occur in 30-79% but do not establish direct muscle or eye injury.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and exotropia (30-79%) can reflect motor neuropathy; direct damage to ocular structures is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and atrophy (30-79%) accompany chronic denervation; primary muscle pathology or fixed skeletal damage is not established.

basis: Sterol-biosynthesis disorder with defining cataracts and severe neonatal hepatopathy; global developmental delay is a defining neurologic feature, retained within the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay is a defining feature; retained here because metabolic mechanism, cataracts and hepatopathy fill the three primary slots.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this syndrome is an established CYP51A1-related sterol-biosynthesis disorder, so the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Reported family has myopathy/joint disease, skin fragility and retinal degeneration; malabsorption is a defining feature. Hypothyroidism omitted at cap; nephroptosis alone is not renal damage.
Autoimmune injury of intestinal mucosa defines this enteropathy.
SYT1 neurodevelopmental syndrome with defining oculomotor abnormalities, frequent strabismus and impaired visual behavior; reflux is a separate disorder.
Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; encephalopathy and skeletal myopathy each occur commonly (~30%+) across major forms. Cardiac and renal damage vary by subtype.
Autoimmune thyroid hyperfunction. Proptosis is annotated 30-79%, but damaging orbitopathy is separately diagnosed; tachycardia and enzyme elevations alone do not establish organ injury.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent proptosis and eyelid signs do not establish damaging ocular disease; thyroid-associated orbitopathy is separately diagnosed.

basis: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder, explicitly outside the axes; nutritional complications do not define additional organ disease here.
Marrow injury defines usual acute radiation syndrome; dermal atrophy occurs in 80-99%. Common vomiting/diarrhea do not establish destructive gastrointestinal syndrome.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: vomiting and diarrhea occur in 30-79%, but destructive intestinal injury is a higher-dose manifestation without evidence of a >=30% frequency.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: direct cutaneous injury is supported by dermal atrophy in 80-99%; skin injury does not define the usual systemic syndrome.

basis: Cutaneous angioedema with inherited complement-regulatory deficiency. Bowel/airway edema is episodic; isolated neuropathy reports do not establish common nerve damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: C1-inhibitor deficiency is an inherited complement-regulatory immune defect; bradykinin mediates the swelling.

basis: Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency causes recurrent subcutaneous angioedema, often through immune mechanisms; transient visceral swelling adds no involved axis.
Clonal mast cell disorder with immune mediator activation; episodic flushing, gastrointestinal symptoms and hypotension do not establish lasting organ injury.
Inborn immune dysregulation with defining bowel inflammation and lymphopenia; arthritis is a defining manifestation supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Inborn immune deficiency defined by inflammatory bowel disease and recurrent infections of the sinuses and lungs.
Ependymal glial tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Myopathy, weakness and joint abnormalities define the disorder; atrophic scars in 3/5 support common skin damage. Ocular abnormalities are occasional.
Congenital peripheral axonal neuropathy with encephalopathy; respiratory and swallowing dysfunction are neurogenic; other structural findings have uncertain frequency.
Combined immunodeficiency with intrinsic lymphoproliferation; lymphoma is a separate disease. Organ enlargement alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome defined by optic atrophy, peripheral neuropathy, ataxia and developmental impairment; optic atrophy occurs in 80-99%.
Infection-related HUS causes hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and AKI; vascular endothelial injury/thrombosis is intrinsic (~all). Neurologic involvement (30-79%) omitted by cap.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular for defining microvascular endothelial injury and thrombosis. Remove neurologic under the four-axis cap: intrinsic vascular damage takes priority over neurologic involvement annotated at 30-79%.

basis: Epileptic neurodevelopmental disorder; contractures/scoliosis 3/3, sensorineural hearing loss 2/2, cataract 1/3. Cerebral visual impairment belongs to neurologic.
Congenital skeletal muscle disease; respiratory failure in 2/2 reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct pulmonary damage.
Defined by renal proximal tubular dysfunction and neonatal hyperinsulinism.
Metabolic encephalopathy; blistering skin injury occurs in 30-79%, pancytopenia in 3/6. Myopathy (30-79%) omitted because of cap; cardiac injury is occasional.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; supplied HPO annotations report oral mucosal blisters in 30-79%, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Pancreatic agenesis with exocrine deficiency, neonatal diabetes and forebrain malformation; gallbladder agenesis reported in 30-79%.
Leukoencephalopathy and skeletal dysplasia define the disorder; parents establish leukodystrophy and osteopetrosis.
Cataracts, developmental delay and dental defects define it; scoliosis 5/5. Cap omits endocrine dysfunction (2/3), hearing loss (3/5) and nephrocalcinosis (30-79%).
Inherited glutamine metabolism disorder defined by neurologic dysfunction causing spasticity, ataxia and dysarthria.
Idiopathic loss of normal gastric emptying; no established systemic neurologic disease implied.
Autoimmune hepatitis/cholangitis damages liver and bile ducts; associated colitis is occasional and separately diagnosed.
Sodium-losing enteropathy causes defining electrolyte/acid-base disturbances; syndromic choanal atresia and recurrent corneal erosions each occur in >30%.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: choanal atresia is a characteristic structural airway obstruction reported in >30% of syndromic cases.
decisions.ocular: involved: recurrent corneal erosions directly injure the cornea and occur in >30% of syndromic cases.

basis: Hepatic dysfunction occurs in 30-79%; marrow, renal and lung injury are occasional. Vomiting and abdominal pain alone do not establish gut damage.
THRA resistance directly causes neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal dysplasia in >30% each; anemia occurs in 77% of reported evaluable cases. Constipation alone does not establish gut damage.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic anemia occurred in 23/30 evaluable cases (77%), supporting common impaired erythropoiesis ([analysis](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7947725/)).

basis: Mast-cell-mediated inducible urticaria/angioedema of skin and subcutis; occasional laryngeal swelling does not establish common lasting airway damage.
Defined by skeletal overgrowth, dysplasia and progressive deformities; reported aortic root dilatation lacks evidence of frequency reaching 30%.
Congenital loss of intestinal-wall collagen impairs bowel motility; the enteric nervous system is normal or near-normal, so no additional neurological axis.
Defining abnormalities involve the oesophagus, stomach and vertebral column; diaphragmatic herniation does not establish intrinsic lung disease.
Congenital eyelid inversion; associated corneal injury remains within the ocular axis.
Medically transmitted prion infection causes progressive cerebral neurodegeneration.
Isolated foveal developmental abnormality impairs visual acuity; definition excludes concomitant systemic pathology.
Neoplasm of the exocrine pancreatic ductal system.
Intellectual disability, cardiac anomalies and joint/skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; coloboma occurs in 30-79%. Hearing impairment (30-79%) omitted because of the cap.
Congenital cafe-au-lait macules define the syndrome; developmental delay, cardiomyopathy and reflux lack qualifying frequency data.
Inherited serine biosynthesis deficiency is a neurometabolic disorder with defining neurologic dysfunction.
Thrombosis directly occupies the splenic vein; the location does not itself establish splenic blood-cell disease.
Thrombosis occupies mesenteric veins. Gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish common bowel injury; intestinal infarction is not demonstrated in at least 30%.
Defining craniofacial skeletal and limb malformations; obstructive choanal atresia, CNS malformations and cardiac defects are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.pulmonary: none: external nasal shape and nasal-bone dysplasia do not establish airway dysfunction; choanal atresia occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Brain/eye anomalies define syndrome; thyroid hypoplasia/hypothyroidism and sensorineural hearing loss each 30-79%. Renal, vascular and skeletal anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: congenital thyroid hypoplasia with hypothyroidism occurs in 30-79%; it is a syndromic organ manifestation rather than the defining disease mechanism.

basis: Defining diaphragm, bowel and splenic defects; pulmonary hypoplasia is common (>30%) with congenital diaphragmatic hernia, although syndrome-specific frequency is unknown.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: congenital diaphragmatic hernia commonly (>30%) directly impairs lung development, causing pulmonary hypoplasia; syndrome-specific frequency is unavailable.

basis: Acute myeloid leukemia affects hematopoietic cells and marrow; no common additional organ infiltration is established.
Clonal myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm of hematopoietic cells associated with JAK2 rearrangement; lymphoma is not universal across presentations.
Skin hypopigmentation, ocular and brain anomalies define the syndrome; defining acral skeletal malformations support musculoskeletal involvement despite unavailable frequencies.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular anomalies are explicitly part of the defining syndrome name; no contradictory definition is supplied.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: acral skeletal malformations and craniofacial asymmetry are defining components; included by the diagnostic-feature exception.

basis: Defining developmental disability and obesity; strabismus 2/3, refractive impairment 30-79%, hip dysplasia 1/3. Laryngeal cleft 1/3 omitted at cap; pigment spots do not impair skin.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: hip dysplasia in 1/3 meets the supplied approximately 30% threshold and represents structural joint disease; evidence comes from a small sample.

basis: Schwann-cell neoplasm of the nervous system; melanin production does not establish skin involvement.
Peripheral vascular syndrome with neuropathy annotated in 80-99%. Erythema is transient and ulcers occur in 5-29%; underlying blood disorders and diabetes are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: peripheral neuropathy is annotated in 80-99%, supporting common neural dysfunction within the neurovascular syndrome; the defining vascular axis remains primary.

basis: Developmental disability defines syndrome; obesity 80-99%, skeletal deformities and progressive hearing loss 30-79%. Myopia/ptosis and dental anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: myopia/ptosis occur in 30-79%, but more frequent obesity and substantial skeletal/hearing abnormalities take priority.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: syndromic truncal obesity occurs in 80-99%; it is a direct metabolic phenotype, without requiring a separate endocrine-gland lesion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: scoliosis, limb/joint and skeletal anomalies occur in 30-79%; these are associated structural manifestations of the neurodevelopmental syndrome.

basis: Sperm structural defects cause infertility; reproductive function alone has no axis.
Congenital cystic tumor occupying the central nervous system; ectopic skin components do not establish cutaneous disease.
Neuroserpin inclusions cause progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Defining neurodevelopmental impairment; hydronephrosis, cardiac malformations and GI dysmotility each 80-99%. Skeletal defects (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Bradykinin-mediated angioedema predominantly affects skin and oral tissues, especially tongue. Normal-C1-inhibitor PLG disease is not an immunodeficiency; airway attacks are a minority.
Immune-mediated neutrophilic skin disease causing destructive ulcers and scars; arthralgia and myalgia do not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Persistent sterile neutrophilic skin inflammation is immune-mediated; associated inflammatory bowel disease is a separate disease.
Immune-mediated neutrophilic skin disease causing bullae and necrotic ulcers; associated lymphoproliferative diseases are separate conditions.
Immune-mediated neutrophilic skin inflammation causes an ulcerated plaque; associated systemic diseases are separate conditions.
Complement-mediated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define aHUS; microvascular endothelial injury and thrombosis are defining, essentially universal.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: direct complement-mediated endothelial injury and microvascular thrombosis define the disease and occur in essentially all affected patients.

basis: Pneumococcal infection-associated thrombotic microangiopathy defined by hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury.
Congenital ureteral dilatation with reflux and obstruction; ureters belong to the renal axis.
Localized fibrohistiocytic inflammatory mass in hepatic parenchyma; the definition establishes neither an endocrine tumor nor an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Localized hepatic inflammatory mass with IgG4-related lymphoplasmacytic infiltration and fibrosis; systemic organ involvement is not established for this concept.
Aldosterone synthesis deficiency with electrolyte and acid-base disturbances; sodium wasting and hypotension do not establish kidney or vascular injury.
Aldosterone deficiency with electrolyte and acid-base abnormalities; renal sodium wasting does not establish intrinsic kidney damage.
Defined by impaired ocular movement from congenital cranial dysinnervation together with congenital hearing loss.
Bilirubin neurotoxicity defines encephalopathy; auditory injury/hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Hemolysis is an antecedent separate condition; jaundice does not establish hepatic injury.
Bilirubin brain injury; hearing loss 30-79%; dental enamel dysplasia is a classic diagnostic tetrad component. Hemolysis is antecedent; jaundice does not establish hepatic damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: deciduous enamel dysplasia is structural dental damage and a classic diagnostic tetrad component. [Diagnostic review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20116355/)

basis: Localized inherited skin blistering with nail dystrophy or loss; systemic damage of severe generalized forms does not apply.
Letrozole inhibits aromatase and estrogen synthesis; endocrine disruption is the best-supported axis. No specific toxic organ injury is described.
Disease of intrahepatic portal venules and sinusoids, defining both hepatic and vascular involvement.
Genetically caused immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease directly affects the intestine.
ALPI-related inflammatory bowel disease directly affects the intestine and is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder.
Postinfectious immune inflammation; cardiac dysfunction occurs in roughly 40-60%. Inflammatory gastrointestinal involvement exceeds 30% and is a major diagnostic category; transient rash excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: inflammatory intestinal involvement is common (>30%) and a major diagnostic category; enterocolitis represents direct gut involvement.

basis: Immune-mediated interface hepatitis; concurrent autoimmune diseases are separate conditions.
Absence of major brain structures and the cranial vault defines anencephaly; adrenal hypoplasia is frequent (30-79%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: absence of the cranial vault is a defining skeletal malformation of anencephaly.

basis: Exposed malformed brain with absent or deficient cranial vault defines exencephaly; proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
Synonym and ancestry identify a benign ovarian serous cystadenoma; reproductive-site tumour without specified endocrine dysfunction.
Benign ovarian epithelial neoplasm; reproductive origin without a defining endocrine disorder.
Benign ovarian epithelial tumor; reproductive ovarian tissue has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not described.
Dermatobia larvae infest skin and subcutaneous tissue, producing furuncular lesions.
Cordylobia larvae infest the skin and produce furuncular lesions.
Cordylobia larvae infest skin and produce furuncular lesions.
Isolated congenital absence of the tongue; oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Isolated congenital underdevelopment of the tongue; tongue and oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Myocardial/coronary triglyceride storage; skeletal myopathy in 80-99%; leukocyte vacuoles and hepatomegaly alone do not establish functional blood or liver damage.
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%; biliary atresia is occasional.
Autoinflammation, immunodeficiency, neutrophil dysfunction and bleeding diathesis define disease; additional organ damage meeting 30% is not established.
Inherited small-platelet thrombocytopenia with bleeding; petechiae and mucosal bleeding do not establish separate organ damage.
Mast-cell leukemia involving marrow; absence of organ damage defines this chronic form. Later progression does not justify additional axes.
Multiple hepatocellular adenomas occupy the liver; malignant transformation and hemorrhage are complications, not additional organ axes.
Developmental absence or severe deficiency of the telencephalon; the affected organ is the brain.
Congenital absence of the prosencephalon is a structural brain malformation.
Navicular osteonecrosis with bone collapse, deformity and secondary joint changes; vascular necrosis of bone does not establish systemic vascular disease.
Nephrotic syndrome defines glomerular dysfunction; no established immune mechanism or common direct extrarenal injury.
Idiopathic nephrotic glomerular disease; sensitivity to intensified immunosuppression supports an immune-mediated mechanism.
Primary lymphatic vessel hypoplasia causes chronic limb lymphedema; skin infections and venous insufficiency occur in only 5-29%.
Immunodeficiency, persistent HPV warts and chronic subcutaneous lymphedema define it; anogenital dysplasia does not establish common anal involvement specifically.
Lymphatic vascular dysplasia with impaired drainage, sometimes accompanied by atrial septal defect or varicose veins; edema alone adds no other axis.
Primary lymphatic vessel and valve dysfunction causes persistent limb lymphedema; mapped to the vascular axis. Swelling alone does not establish separate skin damage.
Congenital lymphatic vascular malformation causes persistent lower-limb lymphedema; nail changes reflect local edema.
Human poisoning predominantly follows ingestion, directly injuring gastrointestinal mucosa. Lung and injection-site injury depend on uncommon exposure routes; systemic organ failure is variable.

decisions.pulmonary: none: direct lung injury characterizes inhalational exposure, an uncommon route accounting for well under 30% of typical human cases.

basis: Defining eyelid abnormalities with frequent lacrimal dysfunction and amblyopia; ovarian endocrine dysfunction is occasional (5-29%), below threshold.
Defined by congenital eyelid abnormalities and premature ovarian endocrine failure.
Congenital eyelid malformation syndrome; this subtype explicitly lacks premature ovarian failure.
Congenital microcephaly and limb abnormalities with primordial dwarfism define the spectrum.
Chromaffin neuroendocrine tumour; catecholamine-mediated hypertension occurs in most patients (~60-80%). Severe cardiomyopathy and vascular events are minority complications.
Acquired infectious prions cause progressive central nervous system degeneration.
Noninfectious immune-mediated chorioretinal inflammation causes atrophic scars, neovascularization and visual loss.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: punctate inner choroidopathy is a noninfectious inflammatory chorioretinopathy within the immune-mediated posterior uveitis spectrum.

basis: Peripheral nerve hyperexcitability causes cramps and fasciculations; these do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Infiltrating facial adipose overgrowth; tongue/parotid involvement and maxillary/mandibular overgrowth each occur in 30-79%. Tonsil enlargement alone does not establish airway injury.
B-lymphoblast malignancy involving blood/marrow or lymphoid tissue; the lymphoma designation also requires the infectious_immune axis.
Fatal cerebral neurodegeneration caused by a transmissible prion agent; sleep and oculomotor abnormalities reflect CNS disease.
Acute leukemia involving marrow and blood-cell lineages; mixed lineage does not make it lymphoma or establish an immune-mediated disease.
Acute leukemia of mixed lineage involving blood and marrow; neither the FLT3 gene nor the erroneous connective-tissue ancestor establishes another organ.
Congenital muscle dystrophy; CNS dysfunction 30-99% and conduction defects 30-79%. Respiratory distress reflects muscle weakness; cataract is occasional.
Muscle dystrophy; childhood CNS deficits common, lifetime conduction disease and cataracts >30%; gastrointestinal dysmotility omitted by cap.
Juvenile DM1 causes myopathy; cognitive/learning impairment affects >50%; conduction disease and cataracts commonly exceed 30% over the lifetime.
Muscle dystrophy; conduction disease ~60-80%, cataracts >50%, GI muscle dysmotility >50%. Endocrine/CNS features omitted at cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent swallowing and intestinal dysfunction reflect direct muscle/enteric disease; dysphagia 59%. [Adult cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42556295/)
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: endocrine involvement is variable; independently coded diabetes is excluded. More consistent cardiac, ocular and gastrointestinal dysfunction takes priority at the four-axis cap.

basis: Late-onset myotonic muscle disease; cataracts occur in most mild late-onset cases. Common cardiac damage is less certain in this subtype.
Choanal obstruction, thyroid abnormalities and hearing loss define the syndrome. Lacrimal anomalies lack established functional impairment; amblyopia and microphthalmia each occur in 1/9.

decisions.ocular: none: unspecified lacrimal duct anomalies do not establish impaired drainage; damaging ocular findings, amblyopia and microphthalmia, each occur in only 1/9.

basis: AQP4-associated autoimmune disease defined by CNS inflammation and optic neuropathy; optic nerve involvement belongs to ocular.
Antibody-mediated inflammatory demyelination defined by CNS disease and optic neuritis; optic nerve injury is ocular under these axes.
Seronegative immune-mediated inflammatory disease defined by CNS and optic nerve attacks; absent antibodies do not exclude its immune mechanism.
Anti-MOG-associated immune-mediated inflammation and demyelination of the spinal cord; optic neuritis is a separate manifestation, not intrinsic to this concept.
Isolated inflammatory, typically immune-mediated optic neuropathy; absence of anti-MOG antibodies does not exclude an immune mechanism.
Anti-MOG immune-mediated inflammation of the optic nerve; isolated optic neuritis does not establish additional CNS disease.
Anti-MOG-associated immune-mediated inflammatory demyelination of the central nervous system.
Immune-mediated inflammatory demyelination of the central nervous system; absence of anti-MOG antibodies does not change the affected organ or mechanism.
Long-QT arrhythmia and syndactyly define TS1; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in approximately 65%, and structural dental defects in approximately 35%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: structural dental abnormalities, including enamel or tooth developmental defects, are reported in approximately 35%; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

basis: Severe long-QT arrhythmia defines TS2; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in >30%, probably over half. Syndactyly is absent; endocrine frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment is common (>30%) but is not required to define this long-QT subtype.

basis: Portosinusoidal vascular disease with intrahepatic septal fibrosis and abnormal hepatic vascular architecture.
Microcephaly and severe intellectual disability define this neurodevelopmental syndrome; other congenital anomalies are unspecified.
Blepharophimosis, intellectual disability and patellar abnormalities define this overlap syndrome; other organ involvement is insufficiently documented.
Hereditary skin/subcutaneous angioedema; normal-C1-inhibitor disease does not establish immunodeficiency; episodic mucosal swelling adds no lasting organ damage.
Autoantibodies inhibit coagulation factor VIII, causing acquired bleeding; bleeding sites do not establish additional chronic organ involvement.
Acquired factor IX inhibition causes an autoimmune coagulation disorder.
Acquired coagulation disorder typically caused by inhibitory autoantibodies against factor V.
Acquired deficiency of a coagulation factor; no additional organ damage intrinsic to this diagnosis.
Acquired haemophilia due to factor XI inhibitors is an immune-mediated coagulation disorder; bleeding sites do not establish additional organ disease.
Factor V isoform-related coagulation dysfunction defines a bleeding disorder; bleeding sites do not establish common lasting damage to other organs.
Inherited factor V-associated coagulation disorder causing bleeding; no specific additional organ is consistently damaged.
Factor V-related coagulation protein disorder causing bleeding; no additional organ involvement established.
Immune-complex deposition defines the renal disease; hypertension is a secondary complication, and extra-renal inflammatory manifestations are uncommon.
Immune-mediated idiopathic nephrotic syndrome acquiring steroid resistance; hyperlipidemia and hypercoagulability do not establish additional organ damage.
Severe intellectual disability and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; facial dysmorphism alone adds no organ axis.
Combined deficiency of coagulation factors VII and X.
Intrahepatic cholestasis directly impairs liver function. Villous atrophy relates to parenteral feeding rather than direct cholestatic injury; splenomegaly alone is insufficient.
Defining congenital fistula connects the rectum and bulbar urethra, directly involving both organ systems.
Congenital fistula directly connects the malformed rectum with the prostatic urethra; both structures define the disease.
Defining neurodevelopmental disease and anemia; cataracts 80%, retinal dystrophy 60%, hearing loss 40%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury; steatosis 20%.
Congenital abnormal position of the female urethral opening; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.
KLHL7-related developmental syndrome with severe neurodevelopmental impairment and congenital contractures; retinal involvement frequency uncertain.
Neurodevelopmental/autonomic dysfunction and congenital contractures characterize disease; retinal degeneration affected 2/2 assessed survivors.

decisions.ocular: involved: early retinal degeneration in 2/2 assessed survivors ([series](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5005468/)).
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital camptodactyly and joint contractures are characteristic structural features.

basis: Manifesting carriers have skeletal muscle myopathy; respiratory involvement is variable and not established above 30% for this subgroup.
Immune-mediated systemic lymphoproliferative disease; additional organ damage is variable and not reliably present in at least 30% across the group.
Ivermectin poisoning chiefly targets the CNS. Gastrointestinal upset and hypotension do not establish additional organ damage.
Organ-unspecified toxicity/dose-selection category; the supplied evidence establishes no affected organ. Haematologic damage cannot be inferred from possible drug adverse effects.
audit_reason: Remove haematologic: the organ-unspecified toxicity/dose-selection concept establishes no blood-cell or marrow disease. A possible adverse effect cannot justify an organ label.

basis: Localized chronic inflammatory dermatosis with immune-mediated cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis; vascular involvement qualifies even when confined to skin.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis is part of the lesion itself; the cardiovascular axis includes vessels regardless of their location.

basis: Placental intervillous inflammation is an obstetric disorder; an autoimmune mechanism is suspected but not established.
Progressive motor neuron disease causing unilateral pyramidal dysfunction; weakness does not establish primary muscle damage.
Prenatal serine synthesis deficiency with severe brain malformations and ichthyosis; characteristic limb malformations and contractures occur commonly (>30%).
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma is a blood-cell malignancy; the lymphoma designation also supports the immune mechanism axis.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma; blood-cell malignancy and lymphoma mechanism apply.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma; hematologic malignancy with the lymphoma mechanism axis.
B-cell precursor leukemia/lymphoma; blood-cell neoplasm with lymphoma mechanism axis.
B-lymphoblast neoplasm involving blood/marrow or lymphoid tissue; lymphoma component warrants the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
B-lymphoblastic blood/marrow malignancy with a lymphoma component; no other common organ damage established.
Developmental and skeletal abnormalities define KAT6B disorders; heart defects >50% ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK114806/)); ocular involvement ~50-60%.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis 11/18 (61%) and blepharophimosis 8/16 (50%) support common eyelid involvement ([cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8580094/)).

basis: Altered transthyretin binding causes euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia, a thyroid-hormone transport abnormality without established additional organ damage.
Defining coloboma (4/5), developmental delay (3/5) and anorectal malformation (2/5). Renal, cardiac and skeletal defects each occur in only 1/5.
Parkinsonism and peripheral polyneuropathy directly affect the nervous system; the mitochondrial gene alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
FAR1 superactivity disrupts ether-lipid metabolism; spastic paraparesis and cataracts occur in 12/12. Constipation (5/12) alone does not establish direct intestinal damage.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia defines a severe neurologic disorder; associated hypotonia and respiratory insufficiency do not establish intrinsic muscle or lung disease.
ATAD3-cluster deletion disease disrupts mitochondrial metabolism and causes pontocerebellar hypoplasia. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine: ATAD3-cluster deletion disease is an inherited mitochondrial metabolic disorder. Neurologic remains defining; respiratory insufficiency alone does not establish pulmonary damage.

basis: Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness, retinal pigmentation and optic disc pallor in 4/4.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; renal dysplasia, hydrocephalus and intestinal malrotation each reported in 1/2 patients. Frequencies derive from a very small series.
Inherited sensorimotor neuropathy with structural pes cavus in 3/6 patients (50%); hearing impairment in 1/6 is below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: pes cavus in 3/6 represents persistent structural foot deformity intrinsic to the neuropathy, rather than weakness alone.

basis: Site-unspecified cancer umbrella; treatment resistance does not identify any shared organ axis.
Childhood malignant neoplasm arising in the kidney; no common additional organ involvement established across the group.
Neoplasm affecting the adrenal cortex, an endocrine gland; functional hormone secretion is not required for this axis.
Ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor involving hormone-producing Sertoli-Leydig tissue, commonly with androgen excess; gonadal endocrine tissue belongs to this axis.
Definition includes benign tumors originating in skeletal or cardiac muscle.
Neoplasm occupying the spleen, mapped to the blood-organ axis; the umbrella includes nonlymphomatous tumors, so an immune mechanism is not universal.
Neoplasm originates in lymphatic vessels and is classified as a vascular neoplasm; lymphatic vessel origin does not imply lymphoma or immune disease.
Benign ovarian epithelial tumour; gastrointestinal resemblance does not establish gastrointestinal origin or endocrine disease.
Inherited epidermal keratinization and pigmentation disorder; no evidence of other organ involvement.
Tumor arises from hormone-producing Leydig cells, the endocrine compartment of the gonad; hormonal symptoms are not required.
Benign tumor arising in breast or rarely prostate; both sites are outside the organ axes.
Phyllodes tumors arise predominantly in breast, with prostate variants; neither has an axis. Lung and skeletal metastases are minority complications.
Germ cell tumor arising in lung tissue.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by intellectual disability and abnormal movements, both reported in 80-99%.
Childhood testicular neoplasm is a reproductive organ tumour; endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Splenic congestion with blood-cell destruction and pancytopenia defines the concept. Underlying portal hypertension or cirrhosis is a separate condition, not organ damage caused by splenomegaly.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: portal hypertension is an underlying, separately diagnosed cause of splenic congestion; the definition does not establish an intrinsic vascular disorder.

basis: Theca-type gonadal stromal tumor arises from steroid-producing endocrine cells and is commonly estrogenic; associated reproductive cancers are separate diseases.
Tumor of ovarian steroidogenic theca cells, the endocrine component of the gonad; estrogen production is characteristic.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: thecoma arises from hormone-producing gonadal stromal cells, placing its origin within the endocrine axis.

basis: Most transitional cell neoplasms arise in urinary urothelium; the umbrella also includes ovarian Brenner tumors, whose origin has no axis.
Epithelial tumor of the ovary, a reproductive organ; no endocrine dysfunction or common direct damage to an included organ is established.
Pseudomonas infection directly damages lung parenchyma, causing pneumonia with hemorrhage and necrosis.
Malignancy originates in sebaceous glands, which are skin appendages; anatomical subtypes vary.
Neoplasm originates in infratentorial brain parenchyma.
The tumor originates in peritoneal fibroblastic tissue, outside the explicitly covered organs; direct involvement of bowel or another covered organ is not established.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: peritoneal origin alone does not establish disease of the listed gastrointestinal organs; bowel involvement is not documented.

basis: Malignant neoplasm involving the cauda equina nerve roots.
Benign neoplasm occupying cauda equina nerve roots.
Malignant neoplasm originates in the CNS; mesenchymal histology does not establish locomotor involvement.
Gynecologic stromal neoplasms arising in reproductive organs, which have no axis.
Mediastinal soft tissue lies outside the specified axes; origin in lung, pleura, heart, vessels or locomotor connective tissue is not established.
Neoplasm arises in the retromolar oral region; the broad jaw-neoplasm ancestry does not establish bone involvement.
Connective soft tissue neoplasm with fibromyxoid stroma; no additional organ involvement is established.
Primary vaginal malignancy affects a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes; mesenchymal differentiation does not establish musculoskeletal origin.
Lipoprotein metabolism disorder; atherosclerosis and pancreatitis are separate diseases whose risks vary across subtypes.
Defined by disrupted carbohydrate metabolism; no additional organ damage applies consistently across this umbrella.
Defined by disrupted glycerol metabolism; no specific organ damage is established across this umbrella.
Disordered porphyrin metabolism; cutaneous, neurologic and hepatic manifestations vary by subtype and are not universal across the umbrella.
Defined by disrupted purine metabolism; specific organ injury varies across subtypes and is not established across the umbrella.
Disease of intervertebral joints; infectious and immune mechanisms apply to particular subtypes rather than the whole umbrella.
Inherited fatty acid oxidation defects; hepatic, cardiac, muscle and neurologic damage vary by subtype and are not established across most of the umbrella.
Disruption of valine metabolism defines this metabolic disease umbrella; no shared organ damage is specified.
Umbrella for disrupted amino acid metabolism; additional organ injury varies across constituent diseases.
Bordetella infections predominantly affect respiratory airways, including pertussis and parapertussis.
Defined by disrupted pyrimidine metabolism; no additional damaged organ is shared across the umbrella.
Umbrella for inherited aspartate-family amino acid metabolic disorders; no additional organ damage is established across the group.
Heme synthesis disorders; cutaneous forms, dominated by PCT, comprise over half of clinically manifest cases and cause photosensitive skin injury. Neurologic injury is restricted to acute forms.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous porphyrias, chiefly PCT, comprise >50% of clinically manifest porphyria and directly damage skin; not a minority subtype complication.

basis: Umbrella for inherited auditory system disorders; additional organ disease is subtype-specific.
Inherited GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with defining intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures, each reported in 3/3 patients.
Arthrochalasia EDS is defined by severe joint laxity/dislocations and abnormal skin extensibility or fragility; bladder diverticulum is very rare.
Familial adrenal glucocorticoid deficiency; hyperpigmentation in 5/7 reflects hormonal stimulation rather than skin damage.
Defining eyelid abnormalities and dental agenesis affect 3/3; cleft lip in 2/3. Cutaneous syndactyly is very rare.
Glutathione-metabolism umbrella; hemolysis, neurologic injury and skeletal disease vary substantially by subtype, without established ≥30% involvement across the group.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorder defined by ocular hypopigmentation and visual dysfunction; generalized skin involvement is not required.
Oculocutaneous albinism defines ocular dysfunction and cutaneous hypopigmentation from disordered melanin metabolism.
Historical G6PD class V denotes increased enzyme activity without established hemolysis; metabolic classification retained without inferring anemia from synonyms.

decisions.haematologic: none: historical class V variants have increased G6PD activity without established hemolytic disease; erythrocyte enzyme measurement alone is insufficient.

basis: Extragonadal malignant germ cell tumor located in the abdominal peritoneum.
Psychosexual dysfunction without specified structural or endocrine disease in an organ axis.
Benign myofibroblastic connective-tissue neoplasm, classified on the soft-tissue musculoskeletal axis; the umbrella includes sites beyond breast.
Malignant neoplasm originates in the great vessels; pulmonary artery or vein origin remains cardiovascular.
Invasive carcinoma originates in urinary tract urothelium, including bladder, renal pelvis and ureter.
Carcinoma arising in urinary tract urothelium, including bladder, ureter, urethra and renal pelvis.
Inflammation of a synovial bursa; neither infection nor an autoimmune mechanism is established.
Destructive scleral inflammation, usually immune mediated; associated systemic autoimmune diseases are separately diagnosed.
Congenital benign cystic tumor occupying the orbit.
C. fetus bacterial infection often presents systemically; enteritis, vascular infection and other focal organ damage are not consistently defining or common.
Bacterial infection umbrella covering multiple anatomical sites; no individual organ is consistently affected across the group.
Latent mycobacterial infection without active organ disease; subsequent active tuberculosis is a risk, not current pulmonary damage.
Behavioral excessive drinking without established organ damage; electrolyte complications are not intrinsic defining features.
Psychiatrically driven excessive drinking; electrolyte disturbance or direct organ damage is not inherent in the definition.
Nonpsychiatric primary polydipsia is a disorder of thirst and water balance; no intrinsic renal damage is established.
Latent Treponema pallidum infection; no common organ damage defines the early latent stage.
Persistent asymptomatic syphilis infection; latent status does not establish neurologic, cardiovascular or cutaneous damage.
Latent treponemal infection without active organ lesions; previous skin lesions and possible later complications do not establish current involvement.
Bacterial infection; direct skin/soft-tissue infection, typically bite-associated cellulitis, accounts for the majority (>50%) of human presentations.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: skin and soft-tissue infection is the predominant human presentation (>50%), with direct tissue inflammation.

basis: Persistent neuropathic pain reflects sensory nerve injury after herpes zoster; the antecedent infection does not establish an ongoing infectious mechanism.
Purely psychiatric anxiety and depressive disorder; no intrinsic organ damage within the thirteen axes.
Central retinal venous occlusion is a vascular disorder producing retinal injury and macular edema.
Necrotizing Pseudomonas infection of the external ear commonly extends into temporal/skull-base bone (>30%), causing contiguous bone destruction.
Narrowing or obstruction of peripheral arteries defines the disease; tissue necrosis is not universal.
Disorder located in the urinary bladder neck and sphincter mechanism.
Neuroendocrine mediator crisis defined by severe hemodynamic instability; transient flushing and bronchospasm do not establish additional organ damage.
Immune-mediated photodermatosis with a delayed hypersensitivity response to ultraviolet exposure.
Cutaneous lupus with characteristic erythema multiforme-like lesions; systemic lupus organ damage is not established as common across this syndrome.
Myocardial injury caused by diphtheria infection and its toxin; respiratory or neurologic involvement is not established for this subtype.
