Acid-base disorders belong to the metabolic axis; an underlying renal or pulmonary cause is not established by this umbrella concept.
Focal epilepsy originating in the primary motor cortex.
Acute necrosis of the renal papillae; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to the concept.
Acute epiglottitis is typically an infection of the upper airway.
Toxic injury to the optic nerve causes visual loss; optic nerve disease belongs to the ocular axis.
Malignant tumor occupies the colon by definition; the primary tumor site is unspecified.
Colon is the tumour origin; liver metastases directly occupy hepatic tissue in roughly 60-70% of metastatic colorectal cancers. This is spread of the same disease.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic metastases occur in roughly 60-70% of metastatic colorectal cancer; the unspecified destination does not negate common direct hepatic occupation.

basis: Obstetric pregnancy outcome without a defining disease of any covered organ axis.
Yersinia infection of mesenteric lymph nodes; nodal location alone does not establish damage to the intestine or blood cells.
Systemic Yersinia pseudotuberculosis infection with intestinal and mesenteric inflammation; transient rash does not establish skin damage.
Acute coronary arterial occlusion causes myocardial infarction; other organ complications are not defining or consistently common.
Mycobacterial infection defined by infiltrated skin lesions and peripheral nerve injury; internal organ damage is only described as possible.
Mycobacterial infection defined by anesthetic skin lesions and early peripheral nerve impairment.
Abnormal placental vascular connections produce reversed arterial perfusion and an acardiac twin; immune disease is not intrinsic.
Defined by abnormal iris behavior during surgery.
Mycobacterial infection predominantly located in the lungs across this umbrella; drug resistance changes treatment susceptibility rather than organ distribution.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the lungs are the usual site of tuberculosis across the group; drug resistance does not change that principal disease location.

basis: Gram-negative bacterial infection directly inflames the meninges.
Gram-negative bacterial infection of the lung parenchyma.
Staphylococcus aureus infection directly affects lung tissue.
Gonococcal infection directly affects the joint and synovium.
Bile duct fibrosis directly affects the biliary tract, included in the hepatic axis.
Characteristic toxic axonal neuropathy and hair-follicle injury; common acute gastrointestinal symptoms alone do not establish direct mucosal injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea are characteristic, but symptoms alone do not establish common gastrointestinal tissue injury.

basis: Disseminated Candida infection; organ seeding varies, with no individual additional organ established here as damaged in at least 30%.
Yersinia enterocolitica primarily causes intestinal infection and enterocolitis; systemic complications are uncommon.
Fungal infection of the endocardium; embolic complications do not establish common damage to any particular additional organ.
Typically infectious inflammation of the uterine lining and muscle; the uterus itself has no organ axis.
Tertiary yaws is a treponemal infection characterized by destructive skin lesions and osteoperiostitis.
Adult worms invade small-intestinal mucosa; larvae invade skeletal muscle and cause myositis. Both are defining infection sites; cardiac and CNS complications are minorities.
audit_reason: Add gastrointestinal to primary: adult Trichinella directly occupy and invade small-intestinal mucosa. Intestinal infection and skeletal-muscle invasion are defining sites of this infection.

basis: Disseminated fungal infection; cutaneous nodules and ulcers occur commonly, approximately >=30%; bone, lung and CNS involvement varies.
Infection within a joint directly causes articular inflammation and damage.
Hereditary mixed polyposis affects the intestinal mucosa; subsequent cancer risk does not add an axis.
Carcinoma confined to the uterine cervical epithelium; reproductive organs have no axis, and no infection is specified by this concept.
Cestode infection; intestinal adult-tapeworm infections constitute most cases across the umbrella. Tissue-invasive larval forms affect variable organs.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal infections account for most patients across cestodiases; extraintestinal larval infections do not establish another shared organ.

basis: Congenital neutrophil maturation failure causes severe neutropenia and innate immunodeficiency; recurrent infections are separate diseases.
Neoplasia confined to uterine cervical epithelium, a reproductive site outside the axes; HPV association does not make the neoplasm an infection.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the stomach; lymphoma requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Childhood melanoma predominantly originates in skin; leptomeningeal and other extracutaneous origins are uncommon subtypes.
Arteriosclerosis directly affects retinal arteries and the retina.
Ergot alkaloid poisoning has defining vasospastic ischemic and convulsive neurological forms; fungal toxin ingestion does not itself establish infection.
Ingested fungal toxins cause gastrointestinal toxicity; other target organs vary by toxin. Definition describes poisoning, not fungal infection.
Inherited infantile epilepsy; ictal apnea and cyanosis do not establish intrinsic pulmonary or cardiovascular disease.
DAZ1 deletion causes spermatogenic failure and male infertility without an established endocrine gland disorder.
Prostatic malacoplakia with abscess is an infection-associated inflammatory disorder; prostate and seminal vesicles have no anatomical axis here.
Cortical malformation, pseudobulbar dysfunction and intellectual disability define a neurologic syndrome.
Teratoma of the sacrococcygeal region, localized to the coccyx and classified as a vertebral column disorder; adjacent-organ damage is not established as common.
Sacral cutaneous hemangiomas are vascular endothelial tumors involving skin and blood vessels. Associated congenital abnormalities are unspecified.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangiomas arise from blood vessels, which fall within this axis; localized cutaneous vascular tumors need not cause systemic cardiovascular disease.

basis: Syndrome defined by hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and frontoparietal alopecia, affecting endocrine function and hair.
Abnormally positioned spleen from deficient supporting ligaments; torsion and infarction are potential complications.
Neurodegenerative Machado-Joseph subtype defined by levodopa-responsive parkinsonism.
Inherited structural or functional disease of the mitral valve.
Immune-mediated rheumatic injury of the mitral valve.
Developmental impairment is common across partial chromosome 12 duplications; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common defining manifestations; other organ abnormalities vary with the duplicated region.
Definition establishes disordered enzyme activity and metabolic disease; supplied evidence does not establish a common organ-specific manifestation.
Congenital Herpesviridae infection umbrella includes HSV and CMV; organ injury varies, with no additional axis reliably meeting 30% across the group.
Meningococcal bloodstream infection; bacteremia alone is not blood-cell disease. DIC, tissue necrosis and meningitis are variable complications.
Inherited abnormal bone sclerosis; marrow failure and cranial nerve injury are not established across most patients in this umbrella.
Parainfluenza virus infection principally occupies and inflames the respiratory tract.
Vitamin deficiency disorder; affected organs vary across B-vitamin deficiencies, with no additional organ consistently damaged across the umbrella.
Multiple familial trichoepitheliomas are cutaneous hair-follicle tumors; all 13 reported patients have these lesions.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy defined by hypokalemia and episodic paralysis; fixed myopathy is reported only occasionally (5-29%).
Rigid-akinetic variant of Huntington disease, with primary neurodegeneration.
Structural narrowing of the aortic valve obstructs cardiac outflow.
GATA2 deficiency causes immunodeficiency and hematopoietic cytopenias. Direct pulmonary disease is variable; opportunistic infections and later neoplasms do not add organ axes.
Defined by nervous-system and skin malformations or neoplasms; additional organs vary substantially among subtypes.
Inherited cutaneous acanthosis; insulin resistance or another endocrine disorder is not established for this familial form.
Severe leptospirosis classically causes jaundice, renal failure and hemorrhagic diathesis; coagulation/platelet abnormalities are common and bleeding is defining.
Microcephaly and intellectual disability accompany severe hand/foot syndactyly. Short stature and the endocrine-growth parent do not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
The defining constellation includes aniridia/lens dislocation, abnormal upper incisors and intellectual disability; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defined by neuroaxonal degeneration and renal tubular dysfunction causing metabolic acidosis.
Described syndrome combines gonadal/metabolic dysfunction, cardiomyopathy, blindness and deafness; hearing loss is a defining feature, satisfying the diagnostic-criterion exception.
Defining cranial synostosis, digit malformations and congenital jejunal obstruction.
Defining external-ear malformation and middle-ear ossicular abnormalities cause conductive hearing loss; micrognathia alone does not establish additional functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic denervation causes lasting distal muscle loss and deformity in most symptomatic patients (>30%); these are intrinsic manifestations, not separate diseases.

basis: Menstrual cycle-linked fever without established organ injury or immune-mediated mechanism; occasional cortisol elevation does not establish endocrine disease.
Primary palmoplantar epidermal disorder; cystic fibrosis and other associated conditions do not establish involvement of their organs.
Primary osteoporosis with reduced bone mineral density; ocular disease cannot be inferred from LRP5 alone.
Congenital multiple joint contractures define this arthrogryposis syndrome; no additional organ involvement established.
Immune-mediated inflammation damages the optic nerve, assigned to ocular; extra-optic neurologic disease is not shared across this umbrella.
Immune-mediated recurrent optic nerve inflammation with visual loss; optic nerves belong to the ocular axis.
Immune-mediated inflammatory damage to the optic nerve causes visual dysfunction; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis and systemic disease is excluded.
Recurrent immune-mediated optic nerve head inflammation causes cumulative visual loss; the optic nerve is included in the ocular axis.
Immune-mediated orbital inflammation targeting the optic nerve sheath and impairing vision; optic nerve is assigned to ocular.
Encephalopathy and hearing loss define disease; scoliosis 3/3 and optic atrophy 1/3 (~33%). Neurogenic bladder 1/3 omitted by cap; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Syndromic intellectual disability and congenital nervous system abnormalities define the disorder.
Intellectual disability and brain abnormalities define it; hearing impairment and skeletal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%.
Progressive neurodegeneration with cerebral atrophy and motor regression. Common dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction without established direct gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital auditory canal defects with hearing impairment; eyelid ptosis in 3/4 patients supports ocular involvement; microphthalmos only 1/4.
Squamous carcinoma of the oropharynx; pharyngeal tissues belong to the pulmonary axis under these rules.
Origin is paranasal sinus mucosal epithelium, within the pulmonary axis; the bone-carcinoma ancestor does not establish skeletal involvement.
Developmental malformation of cochlear and vestibular ear structures.
Squamous carcinoma originates in the lip or oral cavity, including buccal mucosa, tongue and gums.
Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy with cerebellar disease; pigmentary retinopathy is defining. Hearing impairment (30-79%) omitted at cap; hyperthyroidism is separately coded.
Ancestry establishes a variable intellectual disability syndrome; no supplied phenotype evidence supports additional organ axes.
Ceramide metabolic leukodystrophy; optic disc pallor and neurogenic bladder each 2/2. Joint contractures (2/2) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: neurogenic bladder in 2/2 establishes loss of bladder function as part of the disorder; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: joint contractures occur in 2/2, but ocular and bladder dysfunction take priority alongside the two defining primary axes.

basis: Immune-mediated skin injury with epidermal detachment; erosive oral mucositis affects most patients with the major form.
Cerebellar degeneration, neuropathy and vestibular failure define CANVAS; optic atrophy is annotated at 30-79%. Neurogenic weakness/contractures do not establish direct musculoskeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contractures are annotated at 30-79%, but the record does not establish direct joint or muscle pathology beyond consequences of neuropathy.

basis: LAT immune deficiency/dysregulation; autoimmune cytopenias directly affect blood in 2/3. Bronchiectasis/chronic lung disease (2/3) follows separate infections, so pulmonary is excluded.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis/chronic lung disease is reported in 2/3, but represents damage mediated by separate recurrent infections rather than direct pulmonary involvement by LAT deficiency.

basis: Organic aciduria with encephalopathy, cerebral atrophy and seizures (2/5). Respiratory failure (4/5) may be neurogenic; direct lung disease is not established.
Organic aciduria with defining epileptic developmental encephalopathy; optic atrophy in 2/4 supports ocular involvement. Weakness alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Combined immunodeficiency with neutropenia and lymphopenia in 5/5; eczematoid dermatitis occurs in 3/5. Diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Zinc-transport disorder with neurodegeneration and nephropathy; ocular dysfunction: ptosis 4/4, strabismus 3/3; hypertension/hearing findings omitted at four-axis cap.
Pancreatic carcinoma with both exocrine and endocrine malignant components; metastatic organ involvement is not specified.
Phospholipid biosynthesis disorder with spastic paraplegia; retinal abnormalities with reduced acuity and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%.
Developmental and intellectual impairment define the syndrome; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Feeding problems lack direct GI pathology; hydronephrosis occurs in 25%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: feeding difficulty and oropharyngeal dysphagia accompany neurologic dysfunction; direct gastrointestinal damage is not established.

basis: Immune-mediated epidermal necrosis; destructive oral mucositis occurs in >80% and ocular epithelial injury in roughly 50–80%, beyond transient conjunctival injection.
Squamous carcinoma originating in salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited epidermolytic keratinization disorder affecting skin.
Malignancy occupies the major salivary glands, which belong to gastrointestinal. Lymphoma is only one possible histology, not the umbrella mechanism.
Deficiency of a coagulation contact-system protein; associated infections and other causes are separate conditions.
Traumatic injury to nervous system structures; ocular injuries are particular subtypes rather than involvement across the umbrella.
Congenital retinal signaling disorder with stationary night blindness and reduced visual function; no separate CNS disease is established.
Lassa virus infection; most infections are mild or asymptomatic. Organ failure and permanent hearing loss do not meet 30% across all infections.
Chronic intestinal dysfunction defines this umbrella; no specific infectious, immune or metabolic cause applies across the group.
Structural narrowing of the lumbar vertebral canal. Pain or claudication alone does not establish common lasting nerve damage.
Abnormal bowel motility impairs intestinal absorption and causes diarrhea; no other organ damage is inherent.
Bowel dysmotility causes stasis, malabsorption and diarrhea; bacterial overgrowth does not itself establish an infectious disease.
Benign tumour of the intracranial choroid plexus; vascular ancestry does not establish a cardiovascular tumour origin.
Defined by renal glomerular protein loss resistant to corticosteroids; heterogeneous causes do not support a universal immune mechanism.
Tumour arising in the adrenal medulla; cardiovascular injury is not established as common intrinsic organ damage.
Tumor arises from neuroendocrine paraganglia associated with the vagus nerve; usually nonsecretory. Dysphagia and vocal cord paralysis do not establish additional organ damage.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: this is an extra-adrenal paraganglionic neuroendocrine tumor, even when nonsecretory. Its vagal location also supports neurologic primary.

basis: Hypergonadotropic ovarian insufficiency is failure of gonadal endocrine function; genomic instability alone does not establish another organ injury.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with low estradiol and elevated gonadotropins; hormone-producing gonads fall within the endocrine axis.
B-cell lymphoma, usually localized to lymph nodes; splenic, hepatic and marrow abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Childhood steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome is an immune-mediated glomerular disorder; the supplied definition overrides the contradictory parent.
Ulceration directly damages the esophageal wall.
Carcinoma originates in breast tissue, which has no axis in this scheme.
Generic benign connective soft tissue neoplasm; the supplied definition does not establish a cardiac or other organ-specific origin.
Melanoma arising in the skin; histologic neurotropism alone does not establish common functional nerve damage.
Neoplasm arising in the exocrine pancreas; invasion of other organs is not a defining or common feature.
Squamous carcinoma originates in nasal or paranasal sinus mucosa, included in the pulmonary airway axis.
Carcinoma arising from large intrahepatic bile ducts.
Sweat-gland carcinoma arising in digital skin; possible lung metastasis does not establish common pulmonary involvement.
Combined tumour originates in hepatocytes and intrahepatic bile ducts, both covered by the hepatic axis.
Congenital melanocytic skin lesion; neurologic complications occur in fewer than 30%; melanoma is a separate subsequent disease.
Benign melanocytic proliferation occupying the epidermal-dermal junction and dermis.
Benign melanocytic proliferation arising in skin.
Benign melanocytic skin nevus with epithelioid melanocytes.
Benign cutaneous melanocytic nevus composed of spindle-shaped melanocytes.
Benign cutaneous melanocytic nevus with desmoplastic stroma.
Benign melanocytic skin nevus with fibrous stroma.
Inherited central movement disorder; additional organ disease varies across subtypes and is not shared by most patients.
Primary torsion dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contraction does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Inherited neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal-muscle disease.
Dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle damage.
Dystonic movement disorder arising from abnormal nervous system motor control; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle damage.
Acquired dystonic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not independently establish skeletal muscle disease.
Task-specific focal dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; muscle contraction does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Disorder of sympathetic or parasympathetic nerves; autonomic symptoms do not establish direct damage to the organs they regulate.
Clonal marrow malignancy causing ineffective hematopoiesis and cytopenias.
Childhood myelodysplastic neoplasm causing persistent cytopenia and abnormal marrow hematopoiesis.
Disease of the smallest coronary arteries and their endothelium.
Immune-mediated cerebellar degeneration defines the disease. The triggering malignancy is separate; nystagmus and diplopia do not establish direct ocular damage.
Cystic epithelial neoplasm arising in the exocrine pancreas; ovarian-type stroma does not indicate ovarian involvement.
Cystic neoplasm of the exocrine pancreas, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Umbrella of hematopoietic cell neoplasms. Lymphoma is a subset, so its immune axis is not universal; no extranodal site is commonly affected across the group.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the pharyngeal tonsil; lymphoma warrants the immune axis. Pharyngeal location maps to pulmonary.
Benign adipose neoplasm arising in the tonsil, within the pharyngeal airway.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the central nervous system; lymphoma also requires the immune mechanism axis.
Malignant mature B-cell lymphoma; blood-cell origin and lymphoma mechanism both apply.
Fibrous replacement of bone marrow defines the condition; common damaging involvement outside marrow and spleen is not established across this umbrella.
Benign urothelial neoplasm arising in the urinary bladder.
Malignant tumour directly occupies the spinal cord; unspecified primary site cannot supply another axis.
Malignant tumour occupies the eye; the originating organ is unspecified.
Carcinoma originates in salivary ducts; variable metastatic sites do not establish common involvement of another axis.
Malignant rhabdoid tumor arising in soft tissues; the supplied definition identifies a soft-tissue sarcoma rather than a renal or CNS primary.
Precursor T-cell lymphoma. Mediastinal masses do not establish pulmonary invasion; common pleural effusions do not establish direct pleural infiltration in >=30%.

decisions.pulmonary: none: neither mediastinal location nor effusion alone establishes direct lung or pleural damage; qualifying involvement in >=30% is not established.

basis: Malignant neoplasm occupying the renal pelvis; other organ involvement is not intrinsic to this concept.
Atypical lymphoid proliferation is a hematologic lesion; this nonspecific concept does not establish lymphoma, immunodeficiency or an immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: atypical lymphoid hyperplasia does not itself establish lymphoma or immune dysfunction; broad immune-disorder ancestry is insufficient.

basis: Acute malignant proliferation of myeloid cells in blood and bone marrow.
Carcinoma originates in oral mucosa or salivary tissue, within the gastrointestinal axis.
Carcinoma arises in the oropharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis under the supplied mapping.
Malignant epithelial tumour originating in the rectum.
Carcinoma arising in the paranasal sinus; salivary-type histology does not change its organ of origin.
Carcinoma originates in minor salivary glands of the oral cavity.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism disease; neurologic impairment and skeletal myopathy each affect >30% across the group; other organ damage varies by subtype.
Disorder of eosinophilic blood cells; the umbrella does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism or a common extracirculatory target organ.
Non-IgE hypersensitivity involving mast-cell or other inflammatory effector activation; no consistently damaged target organ defines this umbrella.
Non-IgE-mediated hypersensitivity commonly involving mast-cell activation; transient skin and airway reactions do not establish additional organ damage.
Benign adipose neoplasms are predominantly subcutaneous lipomas; deep tissue locations vary and do not define most patients across the group.
Disorder of the nasolacrimal duct, part of the ocular lacrimal apparatus.
Broad lymphoid immune-system disorder umbrella; no specific blood-cell, airway or other organ lesion applies consistently across its subtypes.
Defined as disease of the upper digestive tract; no additional organ or mechanism applies across the umbrella.
Disease of the oral mucosa, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defined by involvement of the sympathetic nervous system; endocrine involvement is not shared across the umbrella.
Defined by involvement of the parasympathetic nervous system; no additional organ damage is shared across the umbrella.
Disease of the cerebral cortex; no other organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Defined by disease of the midbrain.
Disease involving a cardiac ventricle.
Disease of vertebral bone; neurologic injury is not inherent across the umbrella.
Scrotal reproductive-system disorder; no covered organ is specified across this umbrella.
Disease of skeletal ligaments, which belong to the locomotor connective tissues.
Disrupted cholesterol metabolism defines this broad metabolic umbrella; additional organ damage varies by subtype.
Inborn glycoprotein metabolic disorder umbrella; direct neurodevelopmental dysfunction affects most patients (>50%) across major glycosylation/deglycosylation groups.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental dysfunction affects most patients (>50%) across the major glycosylation and deglycosylation disorders; isolated non-neurologic forms are exceptions.

basis: Disordered epidermal keratinization; ancestry and subtypes establish skin as the affected organ.
Umbrella disorder of steroid metabolism; additional organ damage varies across subtypes.
Extraembryonic membrane disease is obstetric and outside the axes; infection is not inherent to the entire umbrella.
BH4 metabolic defects impair neurotransmitter synthesis; dystonia or neurodevelopmental dysfunction affects most patients across the listed disorders.
Disrupted carbohydrate transport defines a metabolic disease group; neurologic and other organ damage depend on the specific transport disorder.
Defined by disrupted cholesterol catabolism; organ damage associated with a specific subtype is not assumed throughout this umbrella.
Cholesterol synthesis disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment affects most patients in the major subtypes, Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome and desmosterolosis.
Creatine biosynthesis disorder; cerebral creatine deficiency causes developmental and cognitive impairment in most patients with AGAT or GAMT deficiency.
Disorder of breast lactation; no endocrine gland disease is established for this umbrella concept.
Umbrella disorder of glycine metabolism; no additional organ damage established across most subtypes.
Defined by disrupted organic acid metabolism; no additional organ damage applies consistently across the umbrella.
Acquired adrenal steroid hormone disorder; reproductive manifestations do not establish another covered organ axis.
Noninfectious intestinal disease defined by diarrhea; no specific immune mechanism or additional organ damage is established.
Congenital intestinal epithelial or transport dysfunction causes secretory diarrhea; downstream fluid and electrolyte losses do not establish another primary organ disorder.
Systemic opportunistic fungal infection; affected anatomical organs vary across subtypes, with no additional organ established in most patients.
Opportunistic fungal infection, normally involving skin; invasive visceral disease is not established in most patients.
Fungal infection of skin and subcutaneous tissue; gastrointestinal disease is a different clinical form.
Disseminated Basidiobolus fungal infection; the supplied record does not establish any particular organ as directly damaged in at least 30%.
Disease of the uterine broad ligament, a reproductive supporting structure rather than locomotor connective tissue.
Selective antibody immunodeficiency; associated respiratory infections are separately diagnosed diseases.
Inherited disruption of thyroid hormone metabolism; no additional organ damage common across this umbrella.
Immune-mediated granulomatous nervous system disease; pulmonary sarcoid involvement accompanies neurosarcoidosis in roughly 50-70%, although isolated neurologic disease occurs.
Pregnancy-associated hypertension with defining proteinuria reflects vascular and renal glomerular dysfunction; obstetric context does not negate these axes.
Advanced cataract directly affects the ocular lens.
Cataract affects the nucleus of the ocular lens.
Cataract directly affects the lens cortex.
Benign bone-forming neoplasm.
Bone-forming neoplasm encompassing osteoma, osteoblastoma and osteosarcoma.
Grade II tumour arising from the meninges; recurrence remains within the same organ axis.
Acute cerebral dysfunction affecting attention, orientation and cognition; delirium is explicitly included in the neurologic axis.
Corticotropin-producing neoplasm originates in the pituitary endocrine gland; separately diagnosed consequences of hypercortisolism are excluded.
Carcinoma arising in the breast, which has no organ axis in this scheme.
Cribriform ductal carcinoma in situ confined to the breast; breast has no axis.
Carcinoma originates in major salivary glands; direct perineural tumour invasion is common, roughly 40-60%, and can damage nerves.
Carcinoma originates in minor salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis; invasion and metastasis are not assumed.
Carcinoma originates in minor salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Melanoma originating in the digestive tract; gallbladder origin is a minority subtype, and cutaneous origin is excluded.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma: skin origin, neoplastic lymphocytes and lymphoma mechanism; extracutaneous occupation is not common across variants.
Defined by ectopic hormone secretion; tumor origin and additional organ damage vary across this umbrella.
High myopia affects all 15 reported patients; no extraocular disease is established.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 6/6; facial and external-ear morphology do not establish additional organ damage.
Bone fragility, osteopenia and recurrent fractures in 8/8 patients; blue sclerae are uncommon and do not establish ocular damage.
Peroxisomal disorder; developmental impairment, seizures/spasticity, cataract and nephrocalcinosis with bladder dysfunction each reported in 1/1 patient.
Inherited osteonecrosis directly destroys the femoral head; local ischemia does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Inherited osteonecrosis directly destroys the femoral head; reported in 4/4 patients.
Glycosylation defect; severe CNS abnormalities in 1/1 reported patient; decreased liver function and coagulation abnormalities each frequent (30-79%).
Skeletal dysplasia; aortic stenosis 2/2, tongue/dental malformations 2/2, and intellectual disability or cord compression 1/2 support additional axes; very small samples.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: macroglossia and microdontia each occur in 2/2, supporting persistent developmental involvement of tongue and teeth, both within this axis.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia with metaphyseal and vertebral abnormalities; dental, hair and nail findings are only occasional.
Defining rib, pelvic and limb skeletal malformations; pulmonary or renal tissue disease is not established for this subtype.
Inherited platelet production and function disorder; bleeding does not establish independent organ damage. Skin and infectious findings are very rare.
Defining anorectal, ear/hearing and thumb malformations; renal malformations or dysfunction occur in roughly 40%. Developmental delay 23/89 is below threshold.
Microtia (5/5) and anorectal malformation (atresia 2/6) characterize syndrome; renal ectopia and vesicoureteral reflux each occur in 2/5 (~40%). Skeletal abnormalities lack common-frequency evidence.

decisions.renal: involved: renal ectopia and vesicoureteral reflux each occur in 2/5 (~40%); associated urinary malformations rather than the defining ear/anorectal phenotype.

basis: Developmental delay and loose anagen hair define syndrome; pectus deformity 4/7, joint hypermobility 4/8; pulmonic stenosis 1/3 supports cardiac involvement, with small samples.
Defining developmental disability; skeletal abnormalities commonly reported: brachydactyly 3/3, kyphoscoliosis and foot deformities 2/2. Cardiac/urinary frequency unclear.
Congenital microcephaly and intellectual disability occur in all 10 reported patients.
Adenoma originates in the pituitary endocrine gland; the gene alone does not establish hearing involvement.
Brain commissural and brainstem malformations with developmental disability and progressive scoliosis; supranuclear gaze palsy reflects central neurologic dysfunction.
Sperm flagellar abnormalities cause isolated male infertility; no respiratory or endocrine disease is established by this record.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy; strabismus 8/14 (~57%). Constipation and dental spacing/retention do not establish destructive or disabling GI disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation 14/22 and dental spacing/retention do not establish direct GI tissue injury or substantial loss of oral function; feeding difficulty alone is insufficient.

basis: Loose anagen hair, developmental disability and heart defects characterize it; ptosis 24/33 and strabismus 15/30 support ocular involvement. Common skeletal findings omitted at the cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis occurs in 24/33 and strabismus in 15/30; persistent eyelid and ocular motor dysfunction merit the fourth axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility (5/5) and sternal anomalies (17/32) qualify less strongly by severity than ocular dysfunction and are omitted at the four-axis cap.

basis: Mitochondrial Leigh encephalopathy; fixed contractures occur in 3/6 and kyphoscoliosis in 2/6. Strabismus alone does not establish ocular injury; optic atrophy occurs in 1/5.

decisions.neurologic: primary: Leigh or Leigh-like neurodegeneration is the defining clinical presentation, beyond an incidental complication. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5544391/)
decisions.ocular: none: strabismus/exotropia in 2/6 can reflect neurologic motor dysfunction without direct ocular injury; documented optic atrophy is only 1/5.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed joint contractures in 3/6 and kyphoscoliosis in 2/6 establish common structural impairment of joints and spine.

basis: Adenoma originates in the pituitary endocrine gland; hormone excess does not establish direct damage to additional organs.
Ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins in 4/4 and reduced estradiol in 3/4; uterine hypoplasia is reproductive.
Pontocerebellar malformation and severe developmental impairment define disease; ocular coloboma occurs in 2/6 (~33%); pes planus 2/7 is below threshold.
Mitochondrial disorder; cardiomyopathy 4/4, ophthalmoplegia/ptosis 2/4. Exercise intolerance alone cannot establish muscle damage; renal, hepatic and hearing findings each 1/4.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: exercise intolerance 2/4 can reflect cardiomyopathy; myopathy has no frequency, and CK elevation occurs in only 1/4.

basis: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia with vertebral, hip and limb skeletal abnormalities in the reported patients.
Combined antibody deficiency; psoriasiform dermatitis affects 1/3 (~33%). Diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal damage; recurrent sinusitis is a separate infection.
Congenital structural skeletal myopathy with scoliosis; reduced vital capacity occurs in only 1/5 and does not establish direct lung disease.
RELB-associated immunodeficiency with impaired T-cell function; recurrent infections are separate diseases, with no documented chronic organ damage.
Immunodeficiency with dermatitis in 8/8; asthma (5/8) and pneumonia (4/8) are separate diseases; bronchiectasis occurs in only 1/8.
Autoinflammation, chronic skin/fat loss and contractures (12/12) define disease; hepatic injury in 8/9. Reported arrhythmias (2/3) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Autoinflammatory panniculitis/lipodystrophy; characteristic myositis and contractures affect roughly >=30% in PRAAS. Subtype-specific metabolic dysfunction frequency is uncertain.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: lipodystrophy supports skin involvement; hypertriglyceridemia lacks a frequency establishing common intrinsic metabolic involvement.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: inflammatory myositis, arthritis and contractures are characteristic PRAAS manifestations, collectively expected in >=30%; subtype frequencies are limited.

basis: Autoinflammation/immunodeficiency with neutrophilic skin disease; thrombocytopenia 2/2. Seizure in 1/2 does not establish persistent CNS damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: seizure occurs in 1/2, but direct CNS injury or persistent neurologic dysfunction is not established.

basis: Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; kyphosis occurs in 2/6 (~33%), supporting skeletal involvement.
Inherited retinal degeneration with progressive visual loss in 6/6. Developmental delay and skeletal abnormalities are reported only at 1-4%.
Primary microcephaly with brain malformations and severe developmental impairment; cerebral visual impairment originates in the brain.
Skeletal dysplasia with brachydactyly and joint restriction; subglottic stenosis in 2/3 and mitral regurgitation in 1/3; skin thickening has no supplied frequency.
Isolated male infertility from abnormal sperm flagella and motility; reproductive dysfunction has no axis.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; no established endocrine or other axis involvement.
Isolated defective spermatogenesis and male infertility; reproductive function is outside the axes, with no documented endocrine dysfunction.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with azoospermia and infertility; no demonstrated gonadal hormone disorder.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm morphology and motility; reproductive function has no axis.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with testicular atrophy and infertility; reproductive dysfunction without established gonadal hormone deficiency.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm morphology and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility affect reproductive function outside the axes; no endocrine dysfunction is described.
Testicular failure includes low testosterone in 1/3 and elevated LH in 2/3; endocrine classification is borderline because only three patients were reported.
Isolated male infertility with immotile sperm and non-obstructive azoospermia; reproductive organs have no axis.
Microcephaly in 3/6 and developmental delay in 2/6 support neurodevelopmental involvement. Wilms tumours are separately diagnosed predisposed cancers.
Cryptophthalmos, cutaneous syndactyly and urinary anomalies are major criteria; airway lesions occur in 2/2. Hearing loss, clefts and seizures (1/2 each) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: laryngeal stenosis in 2/2 and pulmonary hyperplasia in 2/3 establish common structural airway/lung involvement; primary axes capped at three.
decisions.renal: primary: renal and urinary tract malformations are major Fraser diagnostic criteria; renal malformations occur in roughly 40%.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous syndactyly is a major diagnostic criterion and represents congenital skin fusion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the recorded syndactyly is explicitly cutaneous; independent bone, joint or muscle disease is not established.

basis: Cryptophthalmos, urinary tract agenesis and syndactyly are major Fraser features, each reported in ~75%; individual intestinal and airway defects occur in 25%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: cutaneous syndactyly is a congenital digital fusion assigned to musculoskeletal; it does not establish an additional independent skin disorder.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: syndactyly is a major diagnostic feature of Fraser syndrome and occurs in 3/4 patients, including its cutaneous form.

basis: Cryptophthalmos and renal agenesis 2/3; syndactyly is defining. Tracheal atresia 1/3 supports pulmonary involvement; hydrocephalus 1/3 omitted at cap.
Defining eyelid, cleft-lip and dental abnormalities; persistent ectodermal abnormalities include sparse hair in 7/8 and nail dysplasia in 5/8.
Mitochondrial disorder with congenital deafness 2/2; hepatic steatosis 2/2, liver failure 1/2 and pancytopenia 1/2; renal dysfunction markers 1/2 omitted by cap.
Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; developmental delay, epileptic encephalopathy and spasticity in 1/1 support neurologic involvement. Optic disc hypoplasia 1-4%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay, epileptic encephalopathy and spasticity in 1/1; these are consequences of the defining mitochondrial metabolic defect.

basis: Hepatic cysts in 5/5 establish liver disease; renal cystic structural involvement occurs in 4/5, although renal function may remain preserved.
BRCA1-related Fanconi subtype has characteristic microcephaly and developmental disability; marrow failure is not characteristic. Cancer predisposition adds no organ axis.
audit_reason: Remove haematologic: marrow failure is not characteristic of this BRCA1-related subtype, despite its Fanconi anemia classification. Move neurologic to primary for the characteristic microcephaly and developmental disability.

basis: Multiple bony synostoses define the disorder; otosclerosis is reported but its frequency is insufficiently established for an otologic label.
Primary microcephaly with intellectual disability; optic nerve hypoplasia and microphthalmia each occur in 2/6, strabismus in 4/6. Individual urinary anomalies are <30%.
Inherited metabolic neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation and cerebellar degeneration; nystagmus and dysphagia do not establish intrinsic ocular or gastrointestinal damage.
Inherited iron-metabolism disorder defined by brain iron accumulation and neurodegeneration; reported manifestations are neurologic.
Localized cutaneous amyloid deposition with pigmentary lesions and dry skin in 9/9; no systemic organ injury established.
Defined by limb and skeletal malformations together with oral anomalies; no established common damage to other axes.
Corneal thinning and ectasia cause reduced visual acuity.
Familial focal epilepsy; associated developmental and autonomic abnormalities remain within the neurologic axis.
Inherited erythrocyte membrane disorder causing elliptocytosis and hemolytic anemia; hemolytic jaundice does not establish liver damage.

Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental disability and sensorineural hearing loss in 2/2, muscle weakness/exercise intolerance in 1/2. Isolated transaminase elevations insufficient for hepatic damage.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy with regression and brain atrophy; optic atrophy occurs in 3/4 patients. Hearing impairment is below threshold at 1/4.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining early neurodegeneration: regression in 5/5 and cerebellar atrophy in 3/5. Visual loss occurs in 2/5 (40%); optic atrophy is documented.

decisions.neurologic: primary: early neurodevelopmental regression and encephalopathy define the clinical syndrome; regression occurs in 5/5 and seizures in 4/5.

basis: CNS hypomyelination with developmental and motor dysfunction; nystagmus is neurologic, while optic disc pallor occurs in only 1/4 patients.
Congenital hydrocephalus with structural brain abnormalities; hydrocephalus in 4/5 and cerebellar agenesis in 2/5.
Inherited erythrocytosis with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit in 17/17 patients; no other common direct organ damage documented.
Inherited erythrocytosis directly affects red blood cells; no common additional organ damage is established.
Primary congenital microcephaly with intellectual disability and absent speech; short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Primary microcephaly with neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Skin fragility and joint/bone abnormalities define this EDS subtype; mitral valve prolapse occurs in 4/6. Isolated dental and vascular reports do not establish prevalence.
Hypomyelinating neurodevelopmental disease; contractures and kyphoscoliosis each 2/4; gingival overgrowth 2/4 supports oral involvement.
Developmental disability and nail/digital hypoplasia define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 4/8. Constipation alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; chronic distal muscle atrophy and fixed foot deformity affect >30% over the course, representing tissue loss and structural impairment beyond weakness alone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: characteristic chronic distal amyotrophy and fixed pes cavus affect >30%; these are lasting structural consequences integral to CMT.

basis: Dopamine transporter dysfunction causes developmental impairment and parkinsonism-dystonia. Feeding and eye-movement abnormalities do not establish separate organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; ptosis 2/2, strabismus/myopia 1/2 support ocular dysfunction; scoliosis, kyphosis and contracture 1/2 support skeletal involvement; small sample.
Familial cardiomyopathy defines cardiac damage; sparse, selectively assessed extracardiac findings do not establish the 30% threshold.
audit_reason: Remove pulmonary, gastrointestinal and musculoskeletal: feature-specific counts of 1/1–2/2 do not establish involvement in at least 30% of CMH27 patients or major diagnostic criteria.

basis: DNAJB11 disease causes renal cysts and progressive renal dysfunction. Hepatic cysts occur in 9/20 (45%), but impairing hepatic involvement is unestablished; hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic cysts occur in 45%, but the evidence does not establish liver injury, impaired function or clinically significant cystic occupation.

basis: Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease. Hearing loss is annotated 1-4%; chronic otitis frequency is unspecified. Situs inversus alone is not cardiac damage.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia with motor-neuron/axonal disease; weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation. Contractures in 1/3 do not demonstrate direct muscle or joint disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy and contractures (each 1/3) are secondary to neurologic dysfunction; intrinsic muscle or joint damage by the disease process is not established.

basis: Developmental impairment and epilepsy occur in 14/14; anemia in 4/13 (~31%) supports blood involvement. Individual functional ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Familial myoclonic epilepsy with cortical myoclonic tremor; no established direct extra-neurologic damage.
Familial cortical myoclonic tremor and epilepsy are neurologic disorders, even when overt seizures are infrequent.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease causing direct intestinal inflammation; associated extraintestinal diseases are not established for this subtype.
Ovarian endocrine failure: hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and absent puberty in 5/5; therefore an endocrine axis applies.
Inherited epidermal barrier disorder with peeling, scaling and dermatitis; associated atopic dermatitis does not establish a separate systemic immune disorder.
Sensorineural hearing loss in 2/2; vestibular dysfunction in 1/2 is covered by the same otologic axis.
Severe intellectual disability, developmental delay, seizures and spasticity define a neurodevelopmental disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated FSH and reduced AMH. No marrow dysfunction is established by the phenotype; FANCM alone does not justify it.
Mitochondrial/peroxisomal metabolic disease defining encephalopathy; optic atrophy is variable, without an established >=30% frequency across this umbrella.

decisions.ocular: none: optic atrophy is variably reported; neither a >=30% frequency across the umbrella nor a required diagnostic criterion is established.

basis: Fatal cardiac rhythm disorder; no additional organ disease is established.
Gastroschisis variant defined by an abdominal wall defect with herniation of abdominal viscera, typically bowel.
Distal small-intestinal obstruction by impacted meconium; underlying cystic fibrosis is a separate condition.
Skeletal muscle membrane excitability disorder causing myotonia; peripheral nerve or CNS disease is not intrinsic.
Isolated failure of sperm production affects reproductive function; endocrine gland dysfunction is not established.
Urinary tract obstruction directly causes kidney damage and impaired renal function.
Brain malformations and developmental impairment define disease; ocular dysfunction includes strabismus in 2/2 and amblyopia or optic disc pallor in 1/2.
Umbrella disorder of the vermiform appendix, part of the large intestine.
Disorder explicitly located in synovial tissue; umbrella includes inflammatory and noninflammatory conditions.
Disease located in a synovial bursa of the locomotor system.
Umbrella disorder of sulfur compound metabolism; no additional organ injury is established across most subtypes.
Benign neoplasms of the peripheral nervous system; endocrine or other organ origins occur only in particular subtypes.
Benign tumor arising in a peripheral nerve.
Squamous carcinoma originates in the lung; metastatic sites are not uniformly involved.
Breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Hormone resistance does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Prostate carcinoma originates in a reproductive organ outside these axes. Hormone resistance does not establish endocrine organ disease or metastatic involvement.
Carcinoma originates in intrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Vulvar reproductive-site carcinoma has no axis; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease.
Carcinoma originates in the rectum.
Carcinoma arising in the skin; glandular differentiation does not establish another organ of origin.
Carcinoma originates in nasal cavity or paranasal sinus epithelium, included in the airway axis.
Neoplasm occupies the nasal cavity or paranasal sinuses; lymphoma is only one possible subtype.
Historical congenital hypotonia syndrome with documented skeletal muscle atrophy; a specific peripheral nerve or spinal lesion is not established.
Inherited red-cell destruction causes hemolytic anemia; jaundice and dark urine do not establish liver or urinary tract damage.
Diffuse cerebral degeneration causes dementia and spastic paraplegia; hearing impairment and blindness lack frequency and localization evidence.
Autoinflammation, arthritis and keratosis in 3/3; ocular inflammation in 1/3 (~33%). Hemolytic anemia and thyroiditis each 1/3 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Hypomyelinating neuropathy with congenital contractures; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 3/9 (~33%). Ocular findings in one assessed patient do not establish common involvement.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and strabismus are documented in one assessed patient among at least nine known; a frequency of >=30% is not established.

basis: Reproductive developmental disorder with ovotestes and genital anomalies; endocrine dysfunction is not established by the supplied findings.
Joint contractures 7/8 and scoliosis 30-79%; optic atrophy 2/4 and cataract 3/9; respiratory insufficiency does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment, involuntary movements and frequent epilepsy; no established common damage outside the nervous system.
Neurodevelopmental disease with deafness; muscle fiber atrophy 3/3, generalized amyotrophy 5/6 and contractures 2/5. Dysphagia alone does not establish GI damage.
Progressive brain disease defines the disorder; joint contractures and kyphosis occur in 7/7, and optic atrophy in 4/4. Hirsutism does not establish skin damage.
Retinal dystrophy with visual dysfunction and staphyloma; isolated short stature or truncal obesity in 1/3 does not establish another damaged organ.
Developmental disability and skeletal overgrowth/deformities characterize syndrome; cataract and myopia reported in 1/1, with limited frequency evidence.
Inherited defect of tyrosine catabolism; often biochemically detected without established liver or kidney damage.
Heart and skeletal defects define syndrome; developmental delay 2/6 and recurrent pneumothoraces 2/6; dental crowding 2/6 omitted by cap.
Defined by microcephaly and limb malformations; microcephaly occurs in 29/29 and intellectual disability/developmental delay in 15/29.
Congenital kidney and urinary tract malformations define the syndrome; hearing impairment and global developmental delay each occur in 2/5 patients.
Inherited skeletal digit malformation; postaxial foot polydactyly occurs in 4/4 reported patients.
Cerebellar atrophy, developmental delay and seizures define a neurologic disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish intrinsic muscle damage.
Named vertebral, cardiac, renal and limb defects; sensorineural hearing loss 2/2. Cap excludes neurologic abnormalities, airway malformations and palatal cleft reported in 1/2.
NAD biosynthesis disorder with defining vertebral and renal malformations; cardiac defects each reported in 1/2. Speech delay (1/2) omitted at cap; cardiac tier reflects the three-primary limit.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypoplastic left ventricle and PDA each occur in 1/2; retained as the fourth axis under the three-primary limit.
decisions.renal: primary: renal hypoplasia/agenesis defines the syndrome; chronic kidney disease is reported in 1/2.
decisions.neurologic: none: speech delay in 1/2 supports involvement, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of metabolic, skeletal, renal and cardiac disease.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is a KYNU-related NAD biosynthesis disorder; elevated 3-hydroxykynurenine in 3/3 supports the metabolic defect.

basis: Joint laxity, short stature and high myopia define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 2/5 patients (40%).
Severe developmental encephalopathy with structural brain abnormalities and defective intermediary metabolism causing lactic acidosis; respiratory insufficiency lacks intrinsic lung disease.
Renal tubulopathy with hypermagnesemia (6/6) and anhidrosis (13/13); lacrimal dysfunction causes alacrima (13/13). Salivary dysfunction/xerostomia (13/13) omitted at cap.
Developmental delay and speech apraxia define the syndrome; immunodeficiency occurs in 2/5 (40%). Dermal translucency alone does not establish skin damage.
Developmental disability, microcephaly, ataxia and seizures define neurologic disease; weakness alone does not establish intrinsic muscle damage.
Mitochondrial neurodevelopmental disorder with movement abnormalities and frequent lactic acidosis; isolated ocular and platelet findings do not establish common involvement.
Mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction defined by auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy; hearing and visual impairment in 8/8 patients.
Chronic eczema/cutaneous inflammation is characteristic; colitis in 1/3. Cap prioritizes skin and bowel over vascular, lung, ocular and CNS inflammation.
Motor axonal neuropathy occurs in 7/7 patients; muscle wasting and weakness reflect denervation without evidence of intrinsic muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and amyotrophy in 7/7 are consequences of motor denervation, without direct skeletal muscle pathology.

basis: Defining congenital facial palsy, eyelid ptosis and velopharyngeal functional failure; pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Defining immunodeficiency, developmental delay and amino-acid abnormality; ASD in 2/4. Recurrent infections do not establish chronic lung or skin damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and distal limb malformations define the syndrome; broad hallux occurs in 5/10 and clinodactyly in 3/10.
Folate metabolic disorder with combined immunodeficiency and megaloblastic anemia; intellectual disability, seizures and hippocampal hypoplasia reported in 1/1.
Cortical atrophy and neurodevelopmental impairment define disease; myopic astigmatism, conductive hearing loss and ankle contracture each affect 1/2 assessed. Small denominators limit certainty.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment; strabismus affects ocular alignment in 6/12. Joint hypermobility in 6/12 lacks documented joint damage; feeding difficulty alone is insufficient.
Defining brain and developmental disorder; hip dysplasia 4/5; strabismus 2/4 and hypermetropia 2/5 support ocular dysfunction.
GPI biosynthesis disorder with developmental impairment and cerebellar atrophy; osteopenia in 8/8 and myopia in 30-79% support bone and ocular involvement.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with movement abnormalities and seizures; strabismus affects ocular alignment in 1/2 assessed patients, with limited sampling.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus is persistent dysfunction of ocular alignment, reported in 1/2 assessed patients; the frequency estimate is uncertain.

basis: Developmental impairment, epilepsy and brain atrophy define disease; strabismus (4/6) and nystagmus (3/6) do not establish direct damage to ocular structures.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus (4/6) and nystagmus (3/6) establish ocular motor abnormalities, but not direct eye damage distinct from the neurologic disorder.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability and developmental delay in 5/5; optic nerve hypoplasia and joint contractures each only 1/5.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; esotropia in 3/7 supports ocular dysfunction. Reflux in 4/7 is a separately diagnosed condition without documented direct gastrointestinal damage.
Retinal degeneration with congenital visual impairment and sensorineural hearing loss; both defining and present in 6/6 patients.
GABBR2-associated neurodevelopmental disorder with severe intellectual disability, language impairment and developmental regression.
Inherited Diamond-Blackfan-like red-cell production disorder; pure red-cell aplasia and steroid-responsive anemia reported in 1/1 patient.
Inherited structural heart disease, predominantly ventricular septal defects; supplied phenotypes are confined to the cardiovascular axis.
Developmental disorder, cataracts and renal defects define it; osteopenia and skeletal dysplasia occur in ~33%. Vascular abnormalities (~33%) omitted by cap; reflux is separately coded.
Neurodevelopmental/cerebellar dysfunction and enamel hypoplasia define the syndrome; nonspecific muscle fiber variation in 2/4 does not establish direct myopathy.
Developmental delay defines disease; hearing impairment and hypermetropia each 2/2, congenital hypothyroidism 1/2. Hip dysplasia (1/2) omitted at cap; evidence is limited.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: congenital hypothyroidism occurs in 1/2 reported patients (50%); clinically important thyroid dysfunction is retained within the cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hip dysplasia and joint abnormalities occur in 1/2 patients (50%), but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of thyroid dysfunction.

basis: Inherited impairment of thyroid hormone metabolism causing euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia; no established additional organ damage.
Phenytoin poisoning primarily causes CNS and cerebellar dysfunction. The poisoning parent supports this interpretation; the related fetal hydantoin synonym does not define additional organs.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses; supplied phenotypes are skeletal.
Severe neurodevelopmental disease with structural brain abnormalities; fixed joint contractures in 5/6 (~83%) establish musculoskeletal involvement.
Developmental disability defines syndrome; skeletal defects 2/2, great-artery transposition 1/2 and ptosis 1/3 support involvement, with small denominators.

decisions.ocular: involved: structural eyelid dysfunction (ptosis) in 1/3 assessed patients meets ~30%; estimate is uncertain because the denominator is small.

basis: The defining triad comprises hearing loss (6/7), congenital cardiovascular defects including pulmonary artery stenosis (5/7), and posterior embryotoxon (7/7).

decisions.ocular: primary: posterior embryotoxon is an explicit defining component of the named syndrome (7/7); primary diagnostic localization does not require visual impairment.

basis: Phosphate metabolism disorder with subcutaneous calcific masses; radial bowing reported in 1/1. Nephrocalcinosis in 1/1 lacks demonstrated renal impairment; singleton frequencies remain uncertain.

decisions.renal: none: nephrocalcinosis is reported in 1/1, but impaired renal function or damaging renal consequences of the deposits are not established.

basis: Inherited phosphate disorder with defining periarticular/tendon calcinosis and skeletal disease. Cerebral calcification in 1/1 lacks demonstrated neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: periarticular/tendon calcinosis is the defining lesion, supported by Achilles calcification and skeletal abnormalities in 1/1.

basis: An inborn glycosylation disorder; developmental neurologic impairment is common (>30%) across the defective-fucosylation subtypes.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with seizures and callosal dysplasia in 2/2 patients. Chronic otitis and osteomyelitis are separate conditions; minor skin findings do not establish damage.
Heme metabolism disorder with defining cutaneous phototoxicity in 3/3. Iron deficiency anemia in 1/3 is separately diagnosed; no common hepatic damage documented.
Limb absence and bilateral lung agenesis define this subtype; cleft palate directly affects the mouth in 6/7 (~86%). Pulmonary vein hypoplasia 2/7 (~29%) is below threshold.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: bilateral lung agenesis defines this subtype (5/7); [OMIM summary](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/conditions/C4747923/).

basis: Defining limb-bone hypoplasia and radial/tibial deficiencies; diaphragmatic hernia occurs in only 1/4 reported patients.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy or ataxia; strabismus in 6/13 (~46%) supports ocular functional involvement; other organ abnormalities are uncommon.
Neurodevelopmental impairment with abnormal tone and seizures; poor growth is nonspecific, and esotropia is reported in only 2/8.
Developmental cerebellar disorder; strabismus affects 3/4 patients. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic; minor digit anomalies do not establish locomotor damage.
Regressive neurodevelopmental disease with seizures and movement disorder; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated intrinsic GI damage.
FBXO11-related intellectual developmental disorder; strabismus in 8/8 assessed patients supports ocular involvement; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.
Developmental impairment, epilepsy and corpus callosum hypoplasia define the disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.
Developmental disability and T-cell dysfunction define disease; oligodontia/microdontia each 5/12. Asthma is a separately diagnosed associated disease.
Oral clefts and renal agenesis each 2/3; choanal atresia 1/3 with reported lung hypoplasia. Ocular, adrenal and splenic anomalies at 1/3 omitted at cap; tiny series.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: choanal atresia in 1/3 meets the threshold; reported pulmonary hypoplasia supports prioritizing potentially lethal respiratory malformations.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: cataract and microphthalmia each occur in 1/3; renal, oral and respiratory malformations take priority.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none at cap: adrenal agenesis occurs in 1/3; renal, oral and respiratory malformations take priority.

basis: Most patients across this broad lesion group have cutaneous skin tags; gastrointestinal, urinary and reproductive sites are distinct site-specific subtypes.
Polypoid lesion arising in the anus, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Localized fibroepithelial lesion of the gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Polyp arising from vaginal tissue; reproductive organs have no axis.
Benign polyp confined to the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction causes defining phosphate, bicarbonate and other solute losses with electrolyte and acid-base disturbance.
Acquired proximal tubular dysfunction causes renal solute wasting, including phosphate depletion and bicarbonate loss.
Acquired proximal tubular injury from degraded tetracycline; generalized solute wasting defines the renal defect.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: proximal tubular reabsorption failure defines this renal syndrome; urinary solute losses alone do not establish a metabolic or endocrine disorder.

basis: Premalignant disorder of hematopoietic cells; other organ involvement is not shared across this umbrella.
Inherited steroidogenesis defect causes severe adrenal cortisol deficiency; electrolyte disturbances remain within the endocrine/metabolic axis.
Intellectual disability is the shared defining feature; ocular and skeletal findings vary across subtypes.
IgE-mediated alpha-gal allergy; episodic urticaria, gastrointestinal symptoms and anaphylaxis do not establish lasting damage to other organs.
Food-protein-triggered, non-IgE immune inflammation directly affects the colon and rectum.
Immune activation disorder of mast cells, a leukocyte lineage; episodic mediator symptoms do not establish lasting damage to other organs.
Immune-mediated mast-cell activation is a leukocyte disorder. Episodic mediator symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the disease is defined by abnormal activation of mast cells, a leukocyte lineage; clonal proliferation is not required.

basis: Food-triggered, non-IgE-mediated immune inflammation of the intestines defines the disease.
Congenital structural heart disease defines this umbrella; pancreatic hypoplasia and diabetes occur in a minority of GATA4-related cases.
Disease directly involving tendons.
Chronic tendon degeneration without inflammation; no immune mechanism established.
Inflammation confined to the tendon paratenon; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Inflammation around a tendon with degeneration within the tendon.
Autoimmune retinal injury causing progressive visual-field and central vision loss.
Isolated focal or segmental dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Generalized dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal contractions alone do not establish skeletal muscle injury.
Immune-mediated inflammatory keratinization disorder affecting skin, hair and nails; no common damaging extracutaneous involvement established.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: PRP is an immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis, although its initiating cause and mechanisms vary across subtypes.

basis: Adult-onset PRP is an immune-mediated inflammatory papulosquamous skin disorder; no additional common organ damage is established.
audit_reason: Add infectious_immune to primary: adult-onset pityriasis rubra pilaris is an immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis, so the mechanism-axis rule applies alongside dermatologic.

basis: ECHS1 enzyme deficiency is an inborn metabolic disorder presenting here with exercise-induced dystonic movements.
Childhood epilepsy with centrotemporal discharges and associated neuropsychological or motor dysfunction.
Focal epilepsy arises in the occipital cortex; visual triggering does not indicate ocular damage.
Epilepsy beginning in neonatal or infantile life; the umbrella includes self-limited and encephalopathic forms without a shared additional organ axis.
A neonatal epilepsy syndrome; remission and typical development do not change its neurologic classification.
Infantile epilepsy syndrome; remission does not change its neurologic classification. Later epilepsy or dyskinesia adds no other axis.
Epilepsy syndrome with myoclonic status and typically severe neurological and developmental impairment.
Epilepsy is defined by immune-mediated CNS inflammation.
Epilepsy defined by antibody-mediated immune dysfunction of the brain.
Epilepsy defined by an underlying metabolic abnormality; both neurologic disease and metabolic mechanism apply.
Disordered cerebral folate transport or metabolism causes a neurologic syndrome; folate metabolism outside the nervous system is normal.
Epilepsy associated with a structural brain abnormality; underlying causes do not automatically add other axes.
Juvenile pityriasis rubra pilaris is a cutaneous keratinization disorder; autoimmune disease is not established by this diagnosis.
Defined by multiple CNS developmental phenotypes; additional organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
CDKL5 deficiency causes a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; no common direct additional organ damage is established here.
Developmental encephalopathy; strabismus in 80–99% and visual impairment in 30–79% support ocular involvement; cortical visual deficits remain neurologic.
Excess precursor load overwhelms trimethylamine metabolism; liver enzyme involvement does not imply liver injury, and malodor does not imply skin damage.
Disorder of cardiac electrical conduction.
Skeletal dysostosis with obligate intellectual disability (100%), a defining syndrome feature. Damaging ocular, hearing and dental findings are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: obligate intellectual disability (100%) is a defining feature of this dysostosis syndrome.

basis: Usher type 1 is defined by congenital sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive retinal degeneration.
Disordered activation of mast cells, a hematopoietic immune-cell lineage; episodic skin, gut and cardiovascular symptoms do not establish lasting organ damage.
Systemic hypersensitivity; airway compromise and circulatory failure are major diagnostic criteria. Transient rash and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypotension/circulatory failure is a major anaphylaxis diagnostic criterion, rather than evidence of a separate cardiac disease.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: acute airway edema and bronchospasm with respiratory compromise are major diagnostic criteria.

basis: Systemic hypersensitivity disorder; acute airway, circulatory and skin manifestations do not establish lasting organ damage.
Primary intraosseous rhabdomyosarcoma directly occupies and damages bone.
Exercise-triggered systemic hypersensitivity; transient cutaneous, respiratory and circulatory manifestations do not establish lasting organ damage.
Food-dependent systemic allergic reaction triggered by exercise; transient skin, airway and circulatory manifestations do not establish lasting organ damage.

Branched-chain amino acid metabolic defect; headache, mild memory complaints and reflex signs in 1/1 do not establish lasting neurologic damage. Isolated ALT elevation does not establish liver injury.

decisions.neurologic: none: headache, mild memory complaints and reflex signs in one reported patient do not establish persistent direct neurologic injury or a typical damaging course.

basis: Persistent asymptomatic blood eosinophilia; the definition excludes eosinophil-mediated organ injury. Restrictive cardiomyopathy ancestry does not establish cardiac involvement.
Congenital spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma is a malignant soft-tissue tumor with skeletal-muscle differentiation.
Purine-synthesis enzyme deficiency defines a spectrum encompassing peripheral neuropathy and sensorineural hearing loss; optic atrophy is subtype-dependent.

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss defines the nonsyndromic hearing-loss presentation and is characteristic across the Arts/CMTX5 spectrum.

basis: Genetic neurodevelopmental disorder defined by developmental impairment and epileptic encephalopathy; extra-neural findings vary by subtype.
Mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm; perivascular growth and proposed pericytic differentiation do not by themselves establish a blood-vessel neoplasm or vascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: perivascular growth alone does not establish a vessel-wall origin or direct vascular disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: classified as a mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm, fitting the connective-tissue axis without another specified organ of origin.

basis: Inherited dopamine synthesis defect defined by dystonia, parkinsonism or encephalopathy.
An inborn neurotransmitter synthesis disorder defined by infantile parkinsonism and delayed motor development.
Infantile encephalopathy caused by an inborn defect of neurotransmitter metabolism; treatment-induced dyskinesias add no axis.
Childhood sarcoma of skeletal muscle differentiation; no specific additional organ of origin is supplied.
Glycosylation disorder with skeletal dysplasia and defective enamel; hearing impairment is a defining feature; mild intellectual impairment omitted because of cap.
Syndromic hearing loss; sperm abnormalities and male infertility involve reproductive functions outside the axes, without established endocrine dysfunction.
Defined by disease of hormone-secreting neuroendocrine glands; neural regulation and ontology ancestry do not establish nervous-tissue disease across this umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: none: responding to neural stimuli does not establish nervous-tissue injury; neurologic disease is not shared across this broad gland-defined group.

basis: Definition explicitly links cardiac disease with abnormalities of skin and/or hair.
Neonatal diabetes, congenital sensorineural deafness and cataracts are the three defining manifestations; additional neurodevelopmental findings vary.
Infection by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus; the broad concept does not specify a consistently damaged organ.
Norovirus infection causes gastroenteritis; intestinal mucosa is the primary affected site.
Idiopathic structural curvature of the juvenile spine; pulmonary impairment is confined mainly to severe curves.
Definition establishes defective alveolar development and atelectasis; the venous anomaly ancestry does not establish a cardiac lesion.
Treatment-resistant arterial hypertension; renal disease and other target-organ complications require separate evidence and diagnoses.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; cerebral visual impairment originates in the brain.
Defined by cardiomyopathy with cutaneous or hair abnormalities, including keratoderma and woolly hair.
Disordered sleep regulation and sleep stages constitute neurologic dysfunction; no other organ damage consistently applies across this umbrella.
Lentigines and cardiac disease define it; ptosis occurs in 8/9 and structural pectus deformities in about 50% or more. Hearing loss usually remains below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: pectus carinatum/excavatum and other structural skeletal abnormalities affect about half or more of patients with Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines.

basis: Inherited thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction; bruising reflects bleeding, not primary skin damage. Malignancy predisposition adds no organ.
ACTA1 skeletal muscle disease; respiratory dysfunction reflects muscle weakness rather than intrinsic pulmonary damage; cardiac involvement is rare.
Malignant neoplasm involving an upper-limb long bone.
Inherited cerebral neurodegeneration causing progressive dementia.
Inherited impairment of erythroid, megakaryocytic and sometimes neutrophil development causes cytopenias and bleeding.
Congenital alveolar maldevelopment defines lung disease; cardiac ancestry alone does not establish a cardiac or vascular lesion.
Elastic-fiber mineralization defines disease of skin, ocular Bruch membrane and arteries; gastrointestinal bleeding is uncommon.
Familial cortical myoclonus is a CNS movement disorder; no separate muscle disease is established.
Familial cortical movement disorder with action myoclonus in 11/11; falls and insomnia do not establish damage to additional organs.
Physical gastrointestinal syndrome defined by recurrent cyclic vomiting associated with cannabis exposure.
Stress-triggered neurodegeneration; respiratory insufficiency in 6/12 does not establish direct lung damage; hearing impairment in 3/25 is below threshold.
SARS-CoV-2 infection primarily affects respiratory epithelium; transient smell/taste loss does not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Congenital alveolar maldevelopment defines the disease; the supplied record does not establish common additional cardiovascular damage.
Tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis disorder causing neurotransmitter deficiency, dystonia and motor delay, even with minimal hyperphenylalaninemia.
Failure of retrograde upper esophageal sphincter relaxation causes inability to belch and impaired gastrointestinal gas evacuation.
SELENON skeletal myopathy; reduced vital capacity 14/14 and hypoventilation 10/17 arise from respiratory muscle weakness and spinal restriction, without direct lung or airway disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: frequent ventilatory failure reflects diseased respiratory skeletal muscles and chest restriction; direct pulmonary tissue or airway involvement is not established.

basis: Neuromuscular dysfunction, contractures and pulmonary hypoplasia define the sequence; hypoplasia occurs in 13/13. Cleft palate occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary hypoplasia is a defining component of fetal akinesia deformation sequence and occurs in 13/13 reported patients.

basis: RAPSN-related neuromuscular-junction dysfunction causes akinesia and contractures; cleft palate occurs in 1/2. Respiratory insufficiency in 2/2 does not establish intrinsic lung damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 2/2 can arise from neuromuscular weakness; pulmonary hypoplasia or other direct lung pathology is not documented for this subtype.

basis: DOK7-related neuromuscular-junction failure causes fetal akinesia and fixed deformities; pulmonary hypoplasia is a major FADS feature, although subtype-specific frequency is unquantified.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is a major defining malformation of fetal akinesia deformation sequence; DOK7-specific frequency is unquantified.

basis: Arthrogryposis in 5/5 and muscle atrophy in 3/5 define skeletal and muscle involvement; direct neural injury not established; pleural effusion 1/5.
Cerebral vessel fragility with hemorrhagic brain injury, leukoencephalopathy and porencephaly defines this cerebrovascular disorder.
Early infantile seizures and progressive psychomotor impairment define a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
Primary skeletal muscle disorder. Motor delay reflects weakness; occasional respiratory involvement does not establish common intrinsic lung injury.
Unilateral renal agenesis is a defining component; seminal vesicle and ejaculatory duct abnormalities are outside the axes.
Adenoviral infection directly affecting the kidney.
