TRIM8-related syndrome defined by glomerular disease and neurodevelopmental impairment; feeding difficulties do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal injury.
Peroxisomal lipid-metabolism disorder defined by elevated VLCFAs, retinal dystrophy, cerebral white-matter disease and psychomotor delay.
Defined by hearing loss with variable keratoderma or ichthyosis; keratitis belongs to a subset and is not established across most of the spectrum.
Macular degeneration with retinal atrophy directly affects the eye.
Spinal gray-matter injury defines AFM. Viral associations do not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism for the entire syndrome.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: AFM is defined as a spinal cord syndrome without an established cause; infection or autoimmunity is not required.

basis: MERS coronavirus infection primarily injures the respiratory tract; renal injury is concentrated in severe cases and is not established as common across all patients.
Umbrella for genetically determined skin diseases; extracutaneous involvement is not shared across most subtypes.
Vitreoretinal disease; interstitial lung abnormalities and enamel hypoplasia each 2/2; encephalocele and developmental impairment 1/2. PDA (1/2) omitted at cap; tiny sample.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalocele, seizures and developmental impairment occur in 1/2 (50%); these support associated CNS injury rather than a universal defining feature.

basis: Defined by vector-transmitted infection; no additional organ is consistently damaged across this broad group.
Congenital skeletal muscle channelopathy; neuromuscular-junction disease occurs in a subtype rather than across the entire umbrella.
Lysosomal disorder with defining skeletal dysplasia/arthropathy; progressive cardiac valve disease is common (>30%); neurologic severity varies across subtypes.
Toxic injury and inflammation of the bronchioles; no infectious or immune-mediated mechanism established.
Syndromic neurodevelopmental impairment; cardiac defects or arrhythmias affect roughly 30-50%; hypotonia and variable skeletal dysmorphism alone add no axis.
Drug-induced psychiatric perceptual disorder; visual phenomena do not establish ocular damage or a separate neurologic lesion.
Proline/ornithine metabolic defect defines neurodevelopmental and spastic motor syndromes; cutis laxa, cataracts and skeletal findings vary by subtype across this umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental impairment and spastic motor syndromes define the disease spectrum, rather than representing downstream complications.

basis: Toxic injury causes obliteration of bronchioles; no infectious or autoimmune mechanism is specified.
Concurrent infections by multiple pathogens; no particular anatomical organ is shared across the concept.
Intracranial arachnoid cyst is a central nervous system malformation.
Acute alveolar-capillary injury causes pulmonary edema and respiratory failure; associated sepsis and systemic complications do not establish additional direct organ disease.
Acute pulmonary parenchymal injury with edema and respiratory failure. Infection is a possible trigger, not an intrinsic mechanism in all cases.
Carcinoma arises from intrahepatic bile ducts, within the hepatic axis.
Complex I metabolic defect; encephalopathy, cardiomyopathy and myopathy each 80-99%. Renal tubulopathy, optic neuropathy and hearing loss also 80-99%, omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy/leukodystrophy occur in 80-99%; neural injury is a manifestation of the metabolic defect, not required across all complex I deficiency subtypes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: mitochondrial myopathy occurs in 80-99%; muscle injury is a common manifestation rather than the defining biochemical defect of this heterogeneous umbrella.

basis: Mitochondrial respiratory-chain metabolic defect; neurologic dysfunction is common (>30%) across symptomatic presentations. Muscle, cardiac and ocular involvement vary by subtype.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causing recurrent seizures and cognitive and motor impairment.
Bone marrow failure and pulmonary fibrosis are core telomere disease manifestations; hepatic and cutaneous disease vary across subtypes without a reliable umbrella frequency >=30%.
Mitochondrial myopathy with defective energy metabolism, lactic acidosis and defining cognitive impairment.
Defined by cerebellar hypoplasia and abnormal locomotion from developmental nervous system disease.
Neurologic dysfunction spans the principal phenotypes; liver failure, glycosylation defects and recurrent infections are subtype-dependent.
Defined by intellectual and speech disability with characteristic dental and palatal abnormalities; additional bone disease is not established as common.
Neurodevelopmental disorder defined by intellectual disability, autism and epilepsy.
Spastic paraplegia, neuropathy and cognitive impairment; ancestors identify a phospholipid metabolic disorder. Additional endocrine deficits lack established frequency.
Primary skeletal muscle channelopathy; respiratory and ocular-motor weakness reflect affected muscles. Common direct lung or neural injury is not established.
Renal cystine storage disease; corneal keratopathy commonly impairs ocular function, with crystals in 187/187. Myopathy 22/86 is <30%; rickets 2/3 is secondary to renal phosphate wasting.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: direct myopathy occurs in 22/86 (~26%); hypophosphatemic rickets 2/3 is a separately diagnosed consequence of renal phosphate wasting, not direct skeletal storage injury.

basis: Dyskeratosis congenita combines marrow failure with diagnostic nail/skin abnormalities and oral leukoplakia. Pulmonary fibrosis affects a minority.
Tubulin-related developmental disorder defined by cortical, basal ganglia and corpus callosum malformations.
Defined by brain and axonal developmental abnormalities and/or congenital extraocular muscle fibrosis with impaired ocular motility.
Retinal dystrophy, cerebellar/peripheral neurologic disease and pituitary hormone deficiencies define this PNPLA6 syndrome group.
Inherited intestinal B12 malabsorption causes megaloblastic anemia; renal tubular protein reabsorption dysfunction produces proteinuria in about 50%.
Inherited intestinal B12 malabsorption causes deficiency and megaloblastic anemia; renal tubular protein-reabsorption dysfunction causes proteinuria in 7/8 despite preserved filtration.
Prenatal neuromuscular-junction dysfunction defines the disorder; typical contractures, vertebral anomalies and cutaneous pterygia establish skeletal and skin axes.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: typical, defining pterygia are congenital skin webs. Neuromuscular-junction dysfunction and structural skeletal abnormalities retain their primary axes.

basis: Persistent elevation of pulmonary arterial pressure; pulmonary vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.
Acute ketoacidosis defines an acid-base/metabolic disorder; vomiting and abdominal pain do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Defective distal tubular electrolyte transport defines renal dysfunction with hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis.
Immunodeficiency with defining ectodermal dysplasia in ~70-80%; dental developmental defects affect >30%. Osteopetrosis is confined to a minority subtype.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: ectodermal dysplasia is a named, defining component affecting most (~70-80%), with impaired sweating and hair development.

basis: Postinfectious immune inflammation with defining myocardial/coronary injury; gastrointestinal inflammation is common (~70-90% involvement); rash often transient.
Beta-cell failure defines PNDM. Neurologic HPO findings cluster in syndromic subsets; >=30% CNS injury across the umbrella is unestablished. Diabetic retinal and renal disease are separate.

decisions.neurologic: none: the 30-79% HPO annotations reflect syndromic presentations; established neurologic injury is not demonstrably >=30% across the PNDM umbrella.

basis: Glucokinase deficiency causes permanent neonatal insulin-secretory failure and hyperglycemia; this genetic diabetes is not autoimmune.
Genetically defined intellectual disability and neurodevelopmental disorder; no other organ involvement is established.
Desmoid tumor arises in deep musculoaponeurotic connective tissue.
Chronic immune-mediated demyelination directly damages peripheral nerves.
Umbrella of inherited neurodevelopmental disorders defined by intellectual disability; additional organs vary by subtype.
Inherited susceptibility defined specifically by myeloid blood-cell malignancy. The primary axis classifies the predisposition; it does not assert existing leukemia or marrow damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the susceptibility concept is defined by myeloid blood-cell neoplasia. Future leukemia is not counted as involved organ damage.

basis: Inherited structural skeletal myopathy. Cardiac disease varies across subtypes without an established umbrella frequency; respiratory weakness does not establish direct lung damage.
Neurodevelopmental and progressive spastic disorder with brain abnormalities. Hypotonia and spasticity are neurologic; structural joint and ocular abnormalities are rare.
Radioulnar bony fusion with restricted forearm rotation; synostosis documented in 22/22 annotated patients.
BH4 synthesis deficiency is a metabolic disorder whose clinical spectrum is defined by central neurotransmitter deficiency, dystonia and encephalopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: dystonia and encephalopathy from central neurotransmitter deficiency define the clinical disease spectrum.

basis: Immune-mediated inflammatory syndrome following immune restoration; affected anatomical organs vary with the underlying antigen.
BH4 synthesis defect causes hyperphenylalaninemia and neurotransmitter deficiency; developmental delay 2/2, dystonia and seizures 1/1 indicate common CNS dysfunction.
Opioid-induced impairment of intestinal motility defines this bowel disorder.
Inherited apolipoprotein deficiency causing abnormal HDL metabolism; atherosclerotic disease is a separate downstream risk.
Metaplastic alteration of gastric mucosa; subsequent cancer is a risk rather than current organ involvement.
Umbrella of inherited kidney or urinary-system abnormalities; no extra-renal axis applies across most patients.
Defined by loss of liver function; encephalopathy is separately diagnosed, and extrahepatic complications vary across acute and chronic forms.
Chronic hepatic failure commonly (>30%) impairs coagulation-factor synthesis and coagulation function. Encephalopathy and hepatorenal syndrome are separate diagnoses.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic impairment of clotting-factor synthesis causes coagulation dysfunction in well over 30% of patients with established chronic liver failure.

basis: Metabolic bone disorder causing reduced bone strength and fragility fractures during late pregnancy or lactation.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disorder, and pregnancy association does not remove that defining mechanism. Musculoskeletal remains primary for bone loss and fragility fractures.

basis: Defined by syndromic intellectual disability and pituitary hormone deficiency.
Primary skeletal muscle myopathy with weakness, atrophy and variable contractures; neurological ancestry does not establish nerve disease.
Parainfluenza virus infection directly involves respiratory tract epithelium.
Inherited encephalopathy defines brain dysfunction; extracerebral manifestations vary across subtypes.
Gastric cancer defines the gastrointestinal component; breast disease is outside the axes; optional clefting adds no additional axis.
Defined by abnormal brain growth and neurodevelopment; the definition excludes common non-brain manifestations.
Degeneration of lumbar intervertebral disks; direct neurologic damage is not established across the disease.
Parainfluenza type 1 infects respiratory epithelium, characteristically producing upper airway disease and croup.
Parainfluenza type 2 causes respiratory tract infection, commonly involving upper airways and the larynx.
Parainfluenza type 4 causes respiratory tract infection.
Epilepsy beginning within the first year of life; additional organ involvement is not shared across this umbrella.
Familial neonatal-infantile epilepsy; remission and generally normal development do not change its neurologic location.
Growth hormone resistance defines endocrine dysfunction; immune dysregulation is a defining component.
Growth hormone resistance with immune dysregulation; pulmonary fibrosis/chronic lung disease and eczematoid dermatitis each occur in 30-79%.
Ichthyosis, alopecia and ocular surface disease define IFAP; intellectual disability/seizures occur in 80-99%, immunodeficiency in 30-79%.
Follicular ichthyosis, atrichia and ocular photophobia define IFAP; ectrodactyly in 4/13 (~31%). Other BRESHECK organ abnormalities fall below 30%.
Inherited interstitial lung disease with defining cerebral calcifications and associated neurologic abnormalities.
Brain, lung and liver disease define the syndrome; anemia in 7/7 supports blood involvement. Thin bone cortices and delayed skeletal maturation, each 7/7, omitted under the cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia in 7/7 demonstrates common blood dysfunction and is retained as the fourth axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: thin bone cortices and delayed skeletal maturation each occur in 7/7; omitted under the cap in favor of established blood dysfunction.

basis: Defining organ spectrum comprises pulmonary cysts/pleuropulmonary blastoma, thyroid neoplasia and cystic nephroma; penetrance varies.
audit_reason: The defining pulmonary, thyroid and renal manifestations fall within the axes, so no_axis is inappropriate. Assign their defining sites as primary; variable tumor risks do not justify additional involved organs.

basis: Developmental delay and sparse hair occur in 3/3; ventricular septal defect in 1/3 (~33%). Minor digit and tooth morphology does not establish functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: brachydactyly and adducted thumb each occur in 1/3, but direct locomotor impairment is not established; short stature alone is insufficient.

basis: Congenital joint contractures with hypertonia 5/5 and tremor 4/4; ocular motility impairment/strabismus reported in 4/4. Other organ findings are isolated reports.
Growth hormone resistance and immune dysregulation define the syndrome; eczematoid dermatitis occurs in 2/3. Thyroiditis and celiac disease each occur in 1/9.
ILD and developmental brain disease define it; hepatic steatosis and pituitary/thyroid failure each 1/1; skeletal abnormalities and anemia omitted by the four-axis cap.
Defining follicular ichthyosis and alopecia with integral ocular disease: blepharitis 8/12, keratitis 4/12 and cataract 4/12.

Immune dysregulation; recurrent oral/GI ulceration affects >60%. Joint complaints (~30-40%) combine arthralgia and arthritis, so destructive/inflammatory joint involvement is not established at >=30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: reported joint involvement (~30-40%) includes arthralgia; inflammatory arthritis alone is not established in >=30%.

basis: Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; encephalopathy/Leigh-spectrum neurologic damage affects >30%; cardiac and intrinsic muscle disease vary across subtypes.
Inherited mitochondrial myopathy; CNS dysfunction is common (developmental delay 1/1, basal ganglia lesions 1/2); hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 1/2. Apnea does not establish intrinsic lung damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay 1/1 and basal ganglia lesions 1/2 support common CNS injury; supplied ancestry defines metabolic disease and myopathy.

basis: Collagen VI defects directly affect skeletal muscle and joints; respiratory weakness varies by severity and does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Neurologic parasomnia involving abnormal motor behavior during non-REM sleep.
ALS2-related degeneration of motor neurons; weakness and spasticity reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than primary muscle disease.
Skeletal-muscle dystrophy with common demyelinating peripheral neuropathy, estimated >30% across predominantly congenital cases; white-matter MRI changes alone would not qualify.

decisions.neurologic: involved: peripheral nerve demyelination with slowed conduction is common, especially in complete laminin deficiency; estimated >30% across the usual disease spectrum.

basis: Plasmalogen biosynthesis disorder with defining neurologic disease; early cataracts occur in most reported patients (>80%).

decisions.ocular: involved: early cataracts are characteristic structural eye disease, reported in >80% of affected patients.

basis: Postinfectious COVID-19 syndrome; fatigue, dyspnea and brain fog do not establish direct structural or functional organ damage in >=30% across the umbrella.
Inherited ventricular electrical instability causes fibrillation despite the absence of structural heart disease.
Developmental malformation of the eye's anterior segment; extraocular findings are not established across this umbrella.
Defined by inherited ocular dysgenesis; additional systemic features are subtype-dependent.
Inherited loss of skin elasticity defines the umbrella; pulmonary, vascular, skeletal and visceral disease vary substantially by subtype.
Inherited generalized proximal tubular failure is defined by renal solute wasting, including phosphate, electrolyte and bicarbonate losses with metabolic disturbances.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: electrolyte wasting and acid-base disturbances are defining components of generalized Fanconi syndrome, rather than occasional extra-renal complications.

basis: Inherited hypertrophy of the pylorus causes gastric outlet obstruction; additional syndromic features do not apply across the umbrella.
Inherited coagulation abnormality predisposes to thrombosis; actual vascular thrombosis is a separate event rather than universal organ damage.
Inherited platelet deficiency; additional organ involvement belongs to particular syndromic subtypes rather than most patients across this umbrella.
Inherited susceptibility specifies future glioma risk, without an existing tumor or established organ dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: none: susceptibility alone establishes future risk, not an existing CNS tumor or neurologic damage.

basis: Clonal haemolytic marrow disorder; intrinsic thrombosis and haemolysis-related chronic kidney damage each reported in 30-79%; no autoimmune mechanism.
Developmental impairment, hypotonia and epilepsy define this group of inherited GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorders, which are inborn metabolic disorders. Other organ anomalies vary by subtype.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the group comprises inherited GPI-anchor biosynthesis deficiencies, a class of congenital glycosylation and metabolic disorders.

basis: Immune-mediated cerebral vasculitis directly affects vessels and causes multiple defining CNS infarctions.
Testosterone deficiency is part of the definition, with male hypogonadism in 80–99%; this establishes gonadal endocrine dysfunction.
SRY-positive 46,XX testicular development commonly entails primary gonadal endocrine failure, supported by elevated LH and FSH; reproductive anatomy adds no axis.
Inherited phosphate metabolic disorder defined by periarticular and subcutaneous calcific masses and the related hyperostosis phenotype.
Phosphate metabolism disorder with subcutaneous calcified masses; hyperostosis in 2/2 supports skeletal involvement. Renal and vascular damage frequencies unspecified.
Limb reduction and clefts define syndrome; developmental disability and cataract each 30-79%. Sparse hair (80-99%) and cardiovascular anomalies (30-79%) omitted by cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataract occurs in 30-79%; retain its potential for substantial visual loss under the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: none: sparse hair occurs in 80-99%, but its lower functional impact gives it lower priority than neurologic and ocular impairment under the cap.

basis: Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy, ataxia and other cerebral or cerebellar dysfunction; no established common extracerebral damage.
Metabolic encephalopathy with liver dysfunction; muscle atrophy 2/2 and CK elevation 3/6 support myopathy. Hearing loss and ASD each 2/6 omitted by cap.
Organ-specific hereditary gastric cancer syndrome; breast has no axis. Predisposition alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Umbrella of single-protein peroxisomal metabolic defects; neurologic, hepatic, renal and skeletal damage varies by subtype and is not established across most patients.
PHYH deficiency causes classic Refsum disease: retinopathy >90%, neuropathy ~70%, hearing loss ~60%; ichthyosis ~35-50% omitted at cap.
Neurologic and hepatic dysfunction affect most Zellweger-spectrum patients; hearing loss 14/14. Dental defects and retinal disease omitted at the four-axis cap.
Liver dysfunction and retinal degeneration each estimated >30%; common hearing loss omitted by cap. [ZSD](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1448/).

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic dysfunction commonly exceeds 30% across the Zellweger spectrum, although severity varies.
decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental impairment or progressive neurologic dysfunction characterizes the spectrum.
decisions.ocular: involved: function-impairing retinal degeneration commonly exceeds 30%; retained for severity under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing loss is common but omitted under the four-axis cap.

basis: Peroxisomal disorder with defining neurologic dysfunction; hepatopathy and sensorineural hearing loss each commonly exceed 30%. Retinal degeneration also qualifies but is omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental neurologic dysfunction and progressive neurologic injury are defining features of Zellweger spectrum disorders.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal degeneration commonly exceeds 30%, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of neurologic, hepatic and hearing impairment.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss is a common intrinsic manifestation across the Zellweger spectrum, exceeding 30%.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease; neurologic dysfunction, hepatopathy and damaging retinal/optic disease each commonly exceed 30%. Common hearing loss is omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal degeneration and optic disease commonly exceed 30% across Zellweger spectrum; potentially severe visual loss merits retention under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing loss commonly exceeds 30% and qualifies clinically, but is omitted under the cap after neurologic, hepatic and ocular damage.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease commonly damages CNS and liver; hearing loss 4/4. Cap omits retinal disease and enamel defects (4/4); nail lines/color alone do not establish injury.
Peroxisomal metabolic defect; neurologic disease in most, hepatic and retinal injury commonly >=30%. Common hearing loss omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurologic dysfunction affects most patients across the spectrum; the PEX10 umbrella is defined by its peroxisomal metabolic defect.

basis: Peroxisomal plasmalogen disorder with defining chondrodysplasia and cataracts; developmental brain dysfunction affects most classic RCDP cases.
Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurologic, hepatic and retinal damage each affect >30%. Sensorineural hearing loss also commonly exceeds 30%, omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal degeneration commonly exceeds 30% across Zellweger spectrum; potentially profound visual loss supports retaining it under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: sensorineural hearing loss commonly exceeds 30%, but neurologic, hepatic and severe retinal disease occupy the available axes.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurologic dysfunction affects most, hepatopathy >30% and hearing loss most; common retinal disease omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatopathy commonly exceeds 30% across Zellweger spectrum; severity varies across PEX13 subtypes.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental or progressive neurologic dysfunction affects most across the spectrum; the peroxisomal metabolic defect defines this umbrella.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal degeneration is common (>30%), but hearing loss is more frequent and retained at the four-axis cap.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects most Zellweger-spectrum patients and causes substantial functional loss.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease; brain injury, liver dysfunction and retinal disease are each common (>30%). Common sensorineural hearing loss omitted at the four-axis cap.
Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurologic dysfunction is common (>30%). Hepatic and ocular damage vary across PEX16 phenotypes; qualifying frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic injury is not established in >=30% across the PEX16 spectrum, which includes milder neurologic phenotypes.
decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment or progressive neurologic dysfunction occurs commonly (>30%) across the spectrum.
decisions.ocular: none: damaging retinal or other ocular disease is not established in >=30% across PEX16 phenotypes.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease with defining CNS/liver pathology; retinal damage commonly >30%, extrapolated from spectrum. Common hearing loss omitted by cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: intrinsic liver disease is a defining component of the inherited Zellweger-spectrum phenotype.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental brain disease, seizures and progressive neurologic dysfunction characterize Zellweger-spectrum disease.
decisions.ocular: involved: retinal damage exceeds 30% in the parent spectrum; subtype extrapolation. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4710674/)
decisions.otologic: none under cap: sensorineural hearing loss commonly exceeds 30%; retained CNS, hepatic and retinal disease prioritize severe functional damage.

basis: Neurologic impairment, hearing loss and retinal degeneration each commonly exceed 30%; hepatic disease also qualifies but is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: none: common hepatic involvement is omitted at the four-axis cap; neurologic and sensory dysfunction are retained across the PEX26 spectrum.
decisions.ocular: involved: retinal degeneration with visual impairment commonly exceeds 30% across the Zellweger spectrum.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; predominant rhizomelic forms commonly cause skeletal dysplasia, neurodevelopmental impairment and cataracts; Refsum forms share nerve and retinal damage.
GNPAT plasmalogen deficiency typically causes RCDP2; skeletal dysplasia, cataracts and severe neurodevelopmental impairment affect most patients.
AGPS plasmalogen deficiency typically produces RCDP3; skeletal dysplasia, congenital cataracts and neurodevelopmental impairment occur in most (>80%) classic cases.
Plasmalogen metabolic disorder; neurologic impairment/spasticity and congenital cataracts are characteristic common manifestations (>30%) across FAR1 defects.
An inborn organelle-fission disorder; encephalopathy and developmental impairment characterize most described patients and the listed subtype.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy affects most described cases, but the umbrella concept itself is defined by defective organelle fission rather than brain disease.

basis: Refsum-spectrum alpha-oxidation defects cause retinopathy (~100%), neuropathy (~70%) and hearing loss (~60%); ichthyosis omitted under the cap.
AGXT, glyoxylate parent and hyperoxaluria child support renal oxalate injury in most; the definition's plasmalogen wording is inconsistent.
Peroxisome biogenesis disorder; intellectual disability, congenital cataracts and sensorineural hearing loss are common in reported PEX11B cases; series are small.
Marrow lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with IgM paraprotein; not an inborn metabolic disorder. Pulmonary lesions are <30%; respiratory insufficiency alone does not prove direct lung damage.
IgM-producing lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma involving marrow; neuropathy is below 30%, and the metabolic ancestor does not define this disease.
Umbrella predominantly comprising cerebral malformations and neurodevelopmental disorders; limb, skin and vascular overgrowth vary by subtype.
Defined by intellectual disability; additional syndromic organ involvement is unspecified.
Extrahepatic bile duct obliteration causes obstruction and progressive hepatic injury; bile ducts and gallbladder belong to the hepatic axis.
RSV infection directly inflames the bronchioles.
Defined by colorectal polyposis and colorectal cancer; no additional organ damage established.
Inherited retinal degeneration with abnormal cone function, night blindness and visual loss.
Vitreoretinal dystrophy with retinal degeneration, retinoschisis and impaired vision.
Multiple serrated colonic polyps define this gastrointestinal condition; subsequent cancer risk adds no axis.
Acute leukemia of immature T-lineage blood/marrow cells; T-cell lineage alone does not establish an immune mechanism axis.
Developmental malformation of the diaphragm, a skeletal muscle; associated lung damage is not established across this umbrella.
Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy; neurologic deterioration and cardiomyopathy each frequent (30-79%). Frequent visual impairment omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Mutilating palmoplantar and periorificial keratoderma; corneal abnormalities <30% and autoamputation 1/6 do not meet the involvement threshold.
Defining skeletal/cardiac syndrome; dental malocclusion 5/10 and conductive hearing loss 4/11 support involvement. Separately diagnosed sleep apnea excluded.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac anomalies are an explicitly named defining component, although variably expressed; arrhythmia occurs in 3/9 and structural heart defects are documented.

basis: Developmental defect of the abdominal wall and its musculofascial structures; associated bowel injury varies by subtype.
Defined by B-cell developmental arrest with lymphopenia and hypogammaglobulinemia, alongside autism and neurodevelopmental abnormalities.
Predisposition targets infantile capillary vascular tumors, predominantly arising in skin; no additional organ damage follows from susceptibility alone.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the predisposition specifically targets tumors of capillary blood vessels, which fall within the cardiovascular axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: infantile capillary hemangiomas predominantly arise in skin, making skin a usual target of this defined predisposition.

basis: Defining lacrimal, auditory and dental/salivary defects; digital malformations are also defining, with thumb phalanx duplication in 11/14.
Epidermal keratinization disorder with ichthyosis, blistering and skin erosions.
Inherited bile acid conjugation defect; malabsorption reflects deficient bile salts rather than intrinsic intestinal injury; common hepatic damage is not established.
Inherited bile acid conjugation enzyme deficiency. A hepatic metabolic reaction does not by itself establish common structural or functional liver damage.
Umbrella for peroxisomal oxidative enzyme/protein defects; additional organ damage is not shared across the diverse subtypes.
Phytanic acid disorder; retinopathy >90%, neuropathy ~70% and hearing loss ~60%; ichthyosis omitted under the four-axis cap.
Defined as a nervous system disorder causing impaired coordination; nystagmus does not establish separate intrinsic ocular damage.
Inherited atactic disorders primarily affect nervous system function; additional organs vary across subtypes and are not established across the umbrella.
Inherited cerebellar dysfunction or degeneration; additional organ disease is subtype-specific across this umbrella.
Ataxia caused by sensory system dysfunction; vestibular disease is only one subtype and does not justify an umbrella otologic label.
Vestibular system dysfunction defines the ataxia; vestibular function belongs to the otologic axis, with no established additional CNS lesion.
Glomerular podocyte injury and segmental sclerosis; heterogeneous causes do not establish an immune mechanism across the group.
Glycogen metabolism disorder; skeletal myopathy affects most patients across its principal subtypes. Cardiac involvement is less common.
ABCD1 metabolic disease presents with adrenal failure; neurologic disability usually (>50%) develops by middle age as part of the same disease's natural history.

decisions.neurologic: involved: the definition explicitly states neurologic disability usually (>50%) develops by middle age; this is evolution of ABCD1 disease, not a separate coincidental disorder.

basis: Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder causing ventricular arrhythmias; syncope does not establish neurologic damage.
Postinfectious inflammation with defining cardiac dysfunction/shock; acute kidney injury occurs in roughly 40% as part of multisystem dysfunction. GI symptoms alone do not establish damage.

decisions.renal: involved: acute kidney injury occurs in approximately 40% and represents renal functional injury during the multisystem inflammatory illness.

basis: Postinfectious SARS-CoV-2 disease umbrella; no additional organ has established direct damage in at least 30% across its heterogeneous subtypes.
Peroxisome biogenesis disorder; neurologic and damaging ocular disease affect most. Rhizomelic forms predominate (>50%) and cause skeletal dysplasia; Refsum forms lack this feature.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: rhizomelic chondrodysplasia predominates among these PEX5/PEX7 disorders, making skeletal involvement common overall despite its absence in Refsum disease.

basis: Inherited renal tubular disorders of aldosterone response or electrolyte handling; salt, potassium and acid-base disturbances define the group.
Primary podocyte injury and glomerular scarring define the disease; proposed circulating permeability factors alone do not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Defining skeletal dysplasia and dentinogenesis imperfecta; pulmonary hypoplasia in 4/10 (40%). Renal disease reported in 1/10.
Inherited platelet aggregation disorder; epistaxis, gingival bleeding and bruising do not establish direct damage to additional organs.
Inherited bile-acid metabolism or transport disorder; elevated circulating bile acids do not establish hepatic injury across this heterogeneous group.
Microcephaly and epilepsy establish neurologic disease; diabetes is a defining endocrine component.
Umbrella for initial viral infections; no single anatomical organ applies across the group.
Viral infection defined by reactivation; this umbrella does not establish common lasting injury to a particular anatomical organ.
Nerve agents cause cholinergic nervous-system and neuromuscular dysfunction; respiratory paralysis does not by itself establish direct pulmonary damage.
Local anesthetic toxicity principally causes central nervous system dysfunction and cardiac conduction or contractile toxicity.
Allelic umbrella principally encompassing tubulointerstitial kidney disease and antibody deficiency; neutropenia is an alternative presentation without evidence of predominance.

decisions.haematologic: none: congenital neutropenia is an alternative allelic presentation; the record does not establish that it applies to most patients across this umbrella.

basis: Infection of the urinary tract, which is covered by the renal axis.
Neurodegeneration; cardiomyopathy, scoliosis/foot deformities and optic atrophy each 30-79%; bowel inflammation represents separate colitis; hearing impairment <30%.
Progressive neurodegeneration; cardiomyopathy in ~60-70% and scoliosis in ~60-80%. Visual impairment is under 30%; diabetes is a separate disease.
Fire ant venom causes local cutaneous injury with characteristic sterile pustules; allergic systemic reactions are a minority.
Definition specifies a malignant CNS glial tumour; anomalous child entries do not establish other organ involvement.
Renal tubular salt-wasting disorder defined by hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis; nephrocalcinosis remains within the renal axis.
Intestinal lactase deficiency causes defective lactose digestion and carbohydrate malabsorption.
Congenital impairment of brain growth with intellectual disability; short stature alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine disease.
Hormone excess defines the syndrome. Diarrhea and flushing do not establish tissue damage; underlying tumors are separate. Cardiac lesions are annotated at 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: frequent secretory diarrhea does not establish intestinal tissue damage; intestinal carcinoid tumors are separately diagnosed.

basis: Central and peripheral neurodegeneration; gait impairment and hypotonia do not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Cerebellar malformation, hepatic fibrosis and ocular coloboma define syndrome; nephropathy reported in 30-79%; central apnea does not establish lung damage.
Hereditary motor neuronopathy; muscle wasting in 30-79% is secondary to denervation rather than direct muscle pathology. Structural foot deformities occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent muscle atrophy (30-79%) is a denervation consequence, not direct muscle disease; skeletal deformities are occasional (5-29%).

basis: PRRT2-associated paroxysmal neurologic movement disorder.
HHV-7 infection; transient exanthem does not establish skin damage, and neurologic complications are uncommon.
Defined by bladder dysfunction with megacystis and intestinal hypoperistalsis with microcolon; visceral smooth muscle disease does not imply skeletal muscle involvement.
WNT10A-related ectodermal dysplasia principally affects teeth and cutaneous appendages; severity of skin, hair and nail disease varies across subtypes.
HSV-1 predominantly causes mucocutaneous herpes, especially labial lesions. Encephalitis and keratitis are distinct minority manifestations; oral mucosal involvement varies.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic to primary: HSV-1 disease predominantly affects mucocutaneous epithelium, including recurrent cutaneous lip lesions. Viral typing does not remove this defining site; neurologic and ocular complications remain minority manifestations.

basis: HSV-2 infection typically causes genital mucocutaneous lesions; neural latency does not establish neurologic damage, and CNS complications affect a minority.
HSV-1 labialis characteristically affects the external lip vermilion and adjacent skin; intraoral mucosal infection is not required.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: herpes labialis does not require oral mucosal involvement; characteristic lesions affect external lip vermilion.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: infectious vesicles and ulcers of the lip vermilion and adjacent skin define herpes labialis.

basis: HSV-2 herpes labialis affects lip vermilion and adjacent skin; intraoral mucosal disease is not specified.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: herpes labialis localizes to external lip/vermilion; intraoral mucosal infection is not established.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic vesicular and ulcerative HSV lesions affect the lip vermilion and adjacent skin.

basis: HSV-2 infection produces genital mucocutaneous lesions; neuronal latency alone does not establish neurologic damage.
HSV-1 infection producing characteristic genital mucocutaneous lesions; neurologic complications are uncommon.
Storage-disorder umbrella; skeletal and valvular damage occur in most (>50%), CNS damage in >30%; corneal disease omitted at cap.
Hydrocephalus and posterior fossa malformations accompany a defining cutaneous capillary malformation. Eyelid nevus does not establish ocular dysfunction.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by biallelic RPE65 variants.
Acute viral infection of the liver; constitutional symptoms and arthralgia do not establish extrahepatic damage.
Acute hepatitis C infection directly affects the liver; subsequent chronic infection does not add an organ axis.
Peroxisomal transport metabolic disorders; neurologic degeneration exceeds ~30% across predominant ALD and ACBD5 disease. Hepatic and retinal damage are subtype-dependent.

decisions.neurologic: involved: ALD dominates this umbrella and commonly causes myelopathy or cerebral disease over its course; ACBD5 deficiency also causes neurodegeneration, supporting >30% overall.

basis: Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood; the chromosome inversion does not establish additional organ involvement.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disorder of myeloid blood cells and bone marrow.
Acute myeloid leukemia involving marrow and blood; associated coagulopathy remains on the haematologic axis.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow defined by t(9;11); no established common additional organ damage.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of myeloid blood and marrow cells; the translocation defines its subtype.
Acute myeloid leukemia involving blood and bone marrow.
Acute malignant myeloid blood/marrow disease defined by its chromosomal translocation; no established common additional organ injury.
Acute myeloid leukemia involving myeloid blood and marrow cells; the translocation defines its subtype.
Acute malignant myeloid proliferation in blood and marrow; no additional organ damage established as common for this cytogenetic subtype.
Acute myeloid leukemia affects myeloid blood cells and bone marrow; the translocation does not establish another organ site.
Cytogenetically defined acute myeloid leukemia involving blood and marrow; no common additional organ damage established.
Acute myeloid leukemia involving myeloid blood and marrow cells; the translocation does not establish additional organ involvement.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a marrow and blood-cell malignancy; the translocation does not establish additional organ damage.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood; the translocation does not establish common damage to another organ.
Acute myeloid leukemia affects marrow and myeloid blood cells; monosomy 7 specifies its cytogenetic subtype.
Acute myeloid malignancy involving blood and bone marrow; monosomy 5 does not establish additional organ involvement.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of myeloid blood cells and marrow; trisomy 8 does not establish another affected organ.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow; der12p specifies its cytogenetics.
Acute myeloid leukemia affects myeloid blood cells and bone marrow; the translocation does not establish another organ.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood; translocation does not establish additional organ involvement.
Blood and marrow AML; direct leukemic skin infiltration occurs in approximately 30-50% of reported t(8;16) cases, with higher frequencies in childhood presentations.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: leukemia cutis is characteristic of this cytogenetic subtype, reported in approximately 30-50%; it represents direct tumour infiltration.

basis: Marrow/blood myeloid malignancy; infant t(1;22) leukemia commonly infiltrates the liver with marked hepatomegaly (>30%), representing direct malignant occupation.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly is common (>30%) in infant t(1;22) disease; direct tumor occupation qualifies even without liver failure.

basis: Acute myeloid leukemia involving marrow and myeloid blood cells; the specified translocation does not establish another commonly damaged organ.
Genetically defined acute myeloid leukemia affecting marrow and myeloid blood cells.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow; the defining translocation does not establish another affected organ.
Acute myeloid malignancy of hematopoietic cells defined by a chromosome 3 inversion.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of myeloid blood cells and marrow; the translocation does not establish another organ.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by its cytogenetic translocation; malignant myeloid cells affect blood and marrow.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by a chromosome 5 deletion; malignant myeloid cells occupy blood and marrow.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by a chromosomal deletion; malignant myeloid cells occupy marrow and blood.
Acute myeloid leukemia affects marrow and myeloid blood cells; chromosome 17p loss does not establish another organ involvement.
KMT2A-rearranged acute myeloid neoplasm of blood and marrow; no established common direct extrahematologic involvement.
Acute myeloid leukemia originates in hematopoietic cells and marrow; the rearrangement does not establish common additional organ injury.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow defined by the specified chromosomal inversion.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disorder of myeloid blood cells and bone marrow.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by a chromosomal translocation; malignant myeloid cells and marrow are the disease compartment.
Acute myeloid neoplasm of blood and bone marrow; the translocation does not establish other common organ damage.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by FUS-ERG-associated translocation; malignant myeloid cells and marrow are the primary compartment.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood; CEBPA mutation specifies the molecular subtype.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood cells; CEBPA status does not establish common damage to another organ.
Acute malignant myeloid disease of marrow and blood; CEBPA mutation defines the leukemia subtype.
FLT3-ITD acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant blood and marrow disorder; no other common direct organ damage is established.
Acute malignant proliferation of myeloid blood and marrow cells; FLT3 mutation does not establish another organ axis.
WT1-mutated acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant blood and marrow disorder; the mutation does not imply kidney disease.
Acute myeloid leukemia involving marrow and myeloid blood cells; the KIT mutation does not establish another affected organ.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant marrow and blood-cell disease; KIT mutation does not establish another organ axis.
Acute myeloid leukemia affects marrow and myeloid blood cells; other KIT-associated tumors are separate diseases.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood-forming cells and bone marrow; GATA1 mutation does not establish additional organ involvement.
Acute myeloid malignancy involving marrow and blood; RUNX1 mutation does not establish additional organ involvement.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disorder of marrow myeloid cells; the mutation does not establish additional organ involvement.
NRAS-mutated acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant blood and marrow disorder; mutation does not establish additional organ damage.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of marrow myeloid cells; KRAS mutation adds no organ axis.
Fazio-Londe disease is a bulbar motor neuropathy within riboflavin transporter deficiency. Dysphagia, stridor and diaphragmatic weakness reflect denervation.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: Fazio-Londe disease belongs to riboflavin transporter deficiency, an inherited vitamin transport and metabolism disorder.

basis: Pregnancy-associated hepatic bile transport dysfunction; pruritus does not establish skin damage, and fetal complications are not maternal organ involvement.
Fibrosis directly affects liver tissue; the broad endocrine ancestor does not establish endocrine disease.
Primary neurologic migraine disorder; neurovascular physiology does not establish structural cardiovascular disease.
Defining B-cell depletion and cardiomyopathy; absent B cells 3/3, neutropenia 2/3. Bronchiectasis is a separate secondary disease; neurologic findings are not reliably attributable.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 1/3 is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections, rather than direct pulmonary involvement by FNIP1 deficiency.

basis: Constitutional platelet disorder with defining neurodevelopmental impairment (6/7); hearing loss and patent ductus arteriosus occur in only 1/7.
Defined by excessive erythrocytosis and chronic hypoxemic respiratory dysfunction; pulmonary hypertension is variable and thrombosis is a risk.
Myotonic myopathy and skeletal dysplasia define disease; blepharophimosis in 1/3 does not establish impaired eyelid or visual function.

decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis is reported in 1/3, but narrowing alone does not demonstrate damaging eyelid dysfunction; cataract frequency is unspecified.

basis: CRYGC-related cataract directly affects the ocular lens; associated visual abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Inherited retinal degeneration; sino-oto-pulmonary manifestations occur in a minority of RPGR-related disease.
Inherited AIPL1-related retinal degeneration; no evidence of extraocular disease.
Hepatic phosphorylase kinase deficiency causes liver glycogen storage; erythrocyte activity is normal.
Dominant GUCY2D-associated retinal dystrophy directly damages the retina.
RP2-related inherited retinal degeneration; neurologic ancestry does not establish separate brain or peripheral nerve disease.
Inherited retinal dystrophy confined to the ocular axis; retinal disease does not independently establish neurologic involvement.
RLBP1-related inherited retinal dysfunction and degeneration; no extraocular involvement established.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by biallelic LCA5 variants; retinal disease belongs to the ocular axis.
Inherited retinal dysfunction caused by biallelic CNGB3 variants; no established extraocular involvement.
Inherited retinal disease caused by biallelic ATF6 variants; no extraocular disease is established.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by biallelic RAB28 variants; no additional organ disease is established.
Retinal degeneration and ataxia in most patients are explicitly defining manifestations.
Inherited inflammatory vitreoretinopathy with immune-mediated uveitis and progressive retinal damage; neurologic findings occur only in some patients.
Retinal dystrophy predominates across CEP290-related disease; renal and cerebellar damage are subtype-dependent and not established in most patients across this umbrella.
Dominant RPE65-related retinal degeneration; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular neurological disease.
Biallelic GUCY2D-related retinal dysfunction or degeneration defines this retinopathy.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; the retinal disease is ocular despite a broad neurologic ancestor.
Neonatal seizures, abnormal cerebral electrical activity, encephalopathy and persistent developmental impairment define the disorder.
Profound neonatal encephalopathy, myoclonus and persistent developmental impairment define the disease; hypoventilation is central without established intrinsic lung damage.
Inherited esophageal achalasia; associated arthritis and sicca findings do not establish common direct extraesophageal damage.
Marrow failure/thrombocytopenia and radioulnar skeletal abnormalities define the variable syndrome; other organ abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Male infertility defined by absent sperm; no endocrine disorder or other axis involvement is inherent.
ACAN-related skeletal growth and cartilage disorder; short stature, accelerated skeletal maturation and joint abnormalities remain within one axis.
Inherited cobalamin-processing disorder; developmental impairment and neurologic dysfunction commonly affect symptomatic patients (~30%+), with variation among subtypes.
Lysosomal storage with defining hepatosplenic disease (>80%); pulmonary infiltration/insufficiency affects >50%. Neurologic degeneration varies by subtype and is omitted under the cap.

decisions.haematologic: primary: splenic storage/infiltration with hepatosplenomegaly defines both major forms; spleen is explicitly included in the blood-organ axis.
decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic storage and hepatomegaly are defining manifestations across both neurovisceral and chronic visceral forms, rather than incidental complications.

basis: Defined by multiple central nervous system developmental abnormalities; no other organ is consistently specified across the group.
Retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy causing progressive visual loss.
Preeclampsia is defined by gestational hypertension with renal proteinuria or other organ dysfunction; eclamptic brain injury, hepatic injury and cytopenias affect minorities.
Congenital nonprogressive skeletal myopathy; an unspecified nervous-system annotation does not establish separate neural damage.
Isolated congenital loss of smell; smell belongs to the neurologic axis. No structural airway disease is specified.
Airway reactivity with cough, wheeze and breathlessness; the nonspecific diagnosis does not establish infection or an immune-mediated disease.
Vitamin deficiency defined by low circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D; rickets and osteomalacia are separate diagnoses and not universal consequences.
Defined by cortical lissencephaly or pachygyria with complex brainstem and neural tract malformations.
Inherited disruption of peptide or amine metabolism; no organ damage is consistent across this umbrella.
Mild inherited disorder of epidermal keratinization; no additional organ damage established.
Severe ichthyosis affects epidermal keratinization and the skin barrier.
Inherited methylamine metabolic defect; no additional organ damage is established across the umbrella.
Named brain and urinary tract malformations; reflux is frequent (30-79%). Metopic craniosynostosis is reported in 1/1, supporting skeletal involvement with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.renal: primary: urinary tract malformations are explicitly named and described as a characteristic component; vesicoureteral reflux occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: metopic synostosis is a structural skull abnormality reported in 1/1 annotated patient; the frequency estimate has substantial sampling uncertainty.

basis: Tuberculosis is a mycobacterial infection predominantly located in the lungs; rifampicin resistance does not establish additional organ involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: lungs are the predominant site of tuberculosis; antimicrobial resistance does not change its usual anatomical classification.

basis: Autoimmune destruction of adrenal cortex; pigmentation, hypotension, gastrointestinal symptoms and salt wasting do not establish direct extra-adrenal organ damage.
Active mycobacterial infection; direct pulmonary infection and tissue injury occur in approximately 80% of cases, while extrapulmonary sites vary.
Tuberculosis is an infection predominantly located in and damaging the lungs; drug resistance does not define additional organ involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: lungs are the predominant anatomical site of tuberculosis, including extensively drug-resistant disease.

basis: Drug-resistant tuberculosis predominantly arises in and damages the lungs; resistance does not establish additional organ involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the lungs are the predominant disease site; drug resistance changes susceptibility, not the principal anatomical location.

basis: Inherited disease of the vitreous and retina; a broad neurological ancestor does not establish additional nervous system disease.
Definition includes neurodevelopmental disability, common nail aplasia/hypoplasia and gingival enlargement. Less frequent skeletal anomalies do not establish umbrella involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: gingival enlargement is explicitly a common defining feature of this spectrum; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: absent or hypoplastic nails are explicitly common defining structural abnormalities; nails belong to the dermatologic axis.

basis: Acne affects cutaneous pilosebaceous units; adult onset does not establish an endocrine or infectious disease.
Inherited platelet production and function disorder. Mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish independent damage to those organs.
Hereditary cancer syndrome defined by diffuse gastric cancer susceptibility; breast has no axis. No additional organ damage is inferred from risk.
Isolated breast/nipple aplasia or hypoplasia has no axis; choanal atresia occurs only occasionally (5–29%).
Immune-mediated pustular skin disease; psoriatic arthritis is separately coded. Geographic tongue and cheilitis do not establish lasting gastrointestinal damage.
45,X Turner phenotype with gonadal failure; congenital cardiac defects ~30-50%, renal anomalies ~30-40%, and intrinsic hearing loss >30% over life. Additional skeletal features omitted at cap.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss directly reflects cochlear dysfunction and affects more than 30% over the typical lifetime course.

basis: Recessive titin-related skeletal myopathy. Cardiomyopathy varies substantially by subtype and is not established at >=30% across this umbrella; respiratory weakness is muscular.
Defined as dominant TTN-related myopathy. Cardiomyopathy and respiratory failure characterize particular subtypes; neither is established as common across the full myopathy umbrella.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy subtypes are included, but their presence among children does not establish cardiac disease in most patients across the umbrella.

basis: Distal skeletal muscle dystrophy with progressive lower-limb weakness; cardiac involvement cannot be inferred from titinopathy alone.
Inherited skeletal muscular dystrophy with weakness and joint contractures; definition explicitly excludes cardiomyopathy.
Congenital titin myopathy is defined by muscle weakness, contractures and fractures, with cardiac abnormalities explicitly included in its defining spectrum.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac abnormalities are explicitly included in the disease definition, although variably expressed.

basis: Inherited porphyrin metabolic disorder with defining cutaneous photosensitivity and fragility; liver damage is variable and not established in at least 30% across the spectrum.
Developmental motor impairment and hypotonia span the umbrella. Major thoracic skeletal defects characterize Kagami-Ogata; small hands and feet alone do not establish locomotor damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: major structural skeletal disease is subtype-dependent; growth restriction and small extremities do not establish common locomotor damage across the umbrella.

basis: Genetic neurodevelopmental disease umbrella; additional organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Major abdominal wall defect with severe kyphoscoliosis and pelvic and limb malformations; no specific visceral damage established.
Fungal infection directly involves the toenail.
Allergic immune-mediated inflammation of skin triggered by ingested food; ingestion does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment, ocular anomalies and contractures define spectrum; progressive hearing loss affects >50% of Cockayne patients, extrapolated to this severe spectrum.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive hearing loss affects >50% across Cockayne spectrum; severe-subset frequency is less certain. [Study](https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2015.110).

basis: Temple syndrome is defined by growth and endocrine abnormalities with characteristic infantile hypotonia and developmental impairment; small hands and feet alone do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: characteristic infantile hypotonia and developmental impairment form part of the defining Temple syndrome phenotype.

basis: Primary breast carcinoma with salivary-type histology; breast has no axis, and histologic resemblance does not imply salivary gland involvement.
Retinal dystrophy and renal ciliopathy are core recessive IFT140 presentations. Skeletal dysplasia varies by subtype; isolated retinal forms occur and umbrella renal frequency is uncertain.

decisions.renal: primary: renal ciliopathy is a core, common presentation of recessive IFT140 disease, including Mainzer-Saldino syndrome; isolated retinal forms make umbrella prevalence uncertain.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia affects vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses; subtype-specific extraskeletal findings do not define the umbrella.
Sudden loss of cardiac activity due to arrhythmia; hypoxic brain injury is a separately diagnosed complication.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by hepatic and cerebral involvement; renal disease belongs to a narrower subtype.
Bronchiectasis 7/10, ileitis 2/2 and vasculitis 2/2 support direct injury. Cap omits small-series skin/joint/thyroid findings; splenomegaly alone lacks blood-organ dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenomegaly 6/6 does not establish blood-organ dysfunction; isolated lymphopenia 1/1 has weaker cohort support and is omitted under the cap.
decisions.cardiovascular: involved: vasculitis directly injures vessels and is reported in 2/2 assessed patients; retained for severity despite the small denominator.

basis: Carcinoma of the ovary, a reproductive organ; no defining endocrine dysfunction or other qualifying organ involvement.
Congenital abnormal motor pathway development causes mirror movements and/or corpus callosum agenesis.
Defined by multiple CNS developmental abnormalities and neurologic motor dysfunction; motor signs alone do not establish primary muscle disease.
Lysosomal sphingolipid disorder; neurodegeneration or leukodystrophy occurs in most constituent phenotypes; visceral involvement varies by subtype.
ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder, included in the neurologic axis; inheritance does not add another organ.
Chorea and thyroid dysfunction characterize the spectrum; intrinsic surfactant-related lung disease affects approximately half of patients.
Defined by skeletal fusions, stapes ankylosis with conductive hearing loss, and ocular abnormalities including hyperopia and strabismus; expression varies by subtype.
Inherited hypotrichosis affects scalp and body hair, eyebrows and eyelashes; eyelash sparsity alone does not establish ocular damage.
SPAST-associated corticospinal and other neurological dysfunction; spasticity alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Ceramide storage disorder; destructive Farber arthropathy and SMA-associated muscle wasting commonly (>30%) affect the locomotor system. Other organ frequencies vary across this umbrella.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive arthropathy in Farber disease and muscle wasting in SMA-PME make locomotor impairment common (>30%) across the spectrum.

basis: The syndrome definition explicitly includes neurodevelopmental impairment, ophthalmologic conditions and orthopaedic abnormalities; frequencies are not supplied.
Bone dysplasia; neuronal migration defects and lung hypoplasia each 80-99%. Urinary abnormality is unspecified; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish damage.

decisions.renal: none: urinary abnormality is reported in 80-99%, but no specific malformation or functional impairment establishes direct urinary-organ damage.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease with defining hypogonadism; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Constipation and reflux do not establish direct intestinal damage; asthma is a separate disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation and reflux occur in 30-79%, but intrinsic gut damage is not established; feeding difficulties may reflect neurologic impairment.

basis: Photosensitive epilepsy with stereotyped seizures and impaired consciousness; light sensitivity does not imply ocular damage.
Inherited alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation disorder causes skeletal myopathy; brain and eye anomalies are subtype-dependent, with no umbrella frequency established.
Emery-Dreifuss disease is defined by skeletal muscle wasting, early contractures and cardiac conduction disease/atrial arrhythmias.
Inherited susceptibility defined by intracerebral hemorrhage as its target; actual hemorrhage or additional organ damage is not established.
Carcinoma originating in the renal medulla. Sickle cell trait is an association, not blood involvement caused by the carcinoma.
Congenital absence of teeth with orofacial cleft; teeth and oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Missing teeth and orofacial cleft affect structures included in the gastrointestinal axis.
Dysfunctional plasminogen causes an inherited fibrinolytic protein disorder; thrombosis and ligneous mucosal disease are not established common manifestations of type II.
Inherited qualitative plasminogen defect affecting fibrinolysis; thrombotic risk alone does not establish cardiovascular damage.
Neurologic spectrum spanning hemiplegic migraine and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
Congenital cardiac malformations define the disorder; pancreatic hypoplasia and diabetes are variable, without an established qualifying frequency here.
Congenital structural abnormalities of the heart and great vessels define the disease.
Clonal proliferation of hematopoietic stem-cell descendants; subsequent malignancy and cardiovascular disease are risks, not direct involvement.
Clonal expansion of mutated marrow or circulating blood cells; subsequent malignancy and cardiovascular disease are risks.
Clonal expansion of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells; subsequent malignancy and cardiovascular disease are risks, not direct organ involvement.
Umbrella of inherited nervous system disorders; muscle and other organ involvement varies by subtype and is not shared by most.
The supplied umbrella definition specifies progressive muscle degeneration and weakness; direct peripheral nerve, CNS or neuromuscular junction pathology is subtype dependent.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurological ancestry does not establish neural damage across most patients; the supplied definition specifies muscle degeneration.

basis: Umbrella category defined by inherited cardiovascular abnormalities; other organ involvement varies by subtype.
SERAC1 spectrum includes metabolic encephalopathy; sensorineural deafness occurs in roughly 80% of classic MEGDEL cases, though milder forms vary.
Benign focal hyperplastic lesion of hepatocytes in the liver.
Immune-mediated inflammation of extraocular skeletal muscles; the disease is confined to the orbital muscles.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, motor dysfunction and hearing loss define the syndrome; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle disease.
Inherited amyloid protein disorder with sensorimotor/autonomic neuropathy; nephropathy 80-99%, cardiac disease 30-79%; ocular involvement omitted at cap.
Inherited open-angle glaucoma damages the ocular optic nerve; no extraocular involvement established.
Inherited disorder of central sleep-wake regulation; an immune mechanism is not established across hereditary forms.
Inherited spectrum of movement disorders and seizures affecting nervous-system function.
Defined by congenital structural heart disease caused by RBFOX2 variants.
Microcephaly, cognitive impairment and skeletal dysplasia define the spectrum; other organ manifestations vary across subtypes.
Inherited glycosylation defect; CNS or neuromuscular junction dysfunction spans the major phenotypes (>30%). Skeletal myopathy varies by subtype.
Chronic fibrin-rich conjunctival lesions define the disease. Associated plasminogen deficiency is a separate underlying disorder.
HBA1-related hemoglobin disorder defined by mild microcytic anemia.
HBA2-related globin disorder defined by mild microcytic anemia.
Inherited alpha-globin disorder; extrahematologic damage varies with severity and treatment and is not shared across the spectrum.
Alpha-globin deficiency causes mild microcytic anemia; additional organ damage is not characteristic of this trait.
Inherited alpha-globin disorder; skeletal changes and iron-related organ injury do not apply to most patients across the spectrum.
Infantile myoclonic epilepsy is a neurologic disorder; the definition describes generally preserved development despite conflicting phenotype frequencies.
Recurrent subcutaneous and submucosal angioedema defines the disease; intestinal and laryngeal edema each occur in 30-79%. Bradykinin excess does not establish immune disease.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent upper-airway mucosal edema is a defining manifestation, with laryngeal edema reported in 30-79%.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: recurrent intestinal mucosal edema is a defining manifestation, reported in 30-79%; it is the disease itself rather than a secondary complication.

basis: Short telomere syndrome commonly causes marrow failure. Pulmonary fibrosis and mucocutaneous disease vary by subtype; their frequency across this umbrella is uncertain.
Defined by neurodevelopmental disease and/or exudative vitreoretinopathy; both are core manifestations across the spectrum.
MTOR overgrowth spectrum commonly involves brain overgrowth, cortical malformations, epilepsy and developmental impairment; other tissue involvement varies.
Epilepsy with both focal and generalized seizures is a brain disorder.
Generalized seizures and characteristic EEG abnormalities define a brain disorder.
Genetically determined generalized epilepsy is a brain disorder.
Inherited generalized epilepsy is defined by cerebral seizure activity.
Epilepsy syndromes defined by prominent myoclonic seizures; muscle jerks do not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Defined by infertility, cancer susceptibility and cytotoxic-agent sensitivity; no intrinsic marrow failure or other qualifying organ damage is established.
Cleft lip/palate is a structural defect of the mouth. No additional generalized skeletal disease is established by the facial-skeleton ancestor.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: oral clefting maps to the mouth; the facial-skeleton ancestor does not establish an additional musculoskeletal manifestation.

basis: Epilepsy is defined by persistent brain dysfunction; unknown seizure onset does not change the organ axis.
Abnormal ocular development and dimensions define this eye disorder.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; neuromuscular transmission abnormalities occur in a subset and do not establish common neurologic involvement.
Jeune thoracic dysplasia has defining short ribs, thoracic constriction and pulmonary hypoplasia/restrictive respiratory dysfunction. Renal damage is not established for this subtype.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary hypoplasia and restrictive respiratory dysfunction are defining features of asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy; renal ancestry alone supplies no additional organ label.

basis: Muscular dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle. Extra-muscular manifestations are variable without evidence of a frequency of at least 30%.
Proteoglycan glycosylation disorder with defining skeletal dysplasia/joint laxity; hyperextensible or fragile skin is common (approximately >=30%) across the spectrum.
Defined as an inborn glycosylation disorder; no evidence supplied for additional organ damage.
Defined as an inborn glycosylation disorder; supplied evidence does not establish the frequency of additional organ damage.
Defined congenital glycosylation defect, an inborn metabolic disorder; no specific additional organ phenotype is supplied.
Neurologic dysfunction, contractures/myopathy and cardiomyopathy characterize the core spectrum; cataract, deafness and renal stones lack established common frequencies.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy is a core manifestation in the multisystem disease definition, alongside neurologic and skeletal muscle involvement.

basis: Umbrella of inherited skeletal dysplasias; additional organ damage is not established across the group.
Defined by skeletal dysplasia, including pseudoachondroplasia and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
Defined by chronic axonal damage to peripheral sensory and motor nerves; secondary weakness does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
Recurrent bacterial infection of hair follicles and surrounding skin, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus; associated immunodeficiency is a separate condition.
Bone fragility defines disease; dentinogenesis imperfecta affects roughly 30–50%, and hearing loss roughly 30–50% over adulthood. Blue sclera alone is non-damaging.
Autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorders defined by intellectual impairment; additional organ abnormalities vary across subtypes.
Intellectual disability defines this inherited neurodevelopmental umbrella; other organ abnormalities vary among its constituent syndromes.
COL1A1-related EDS causes joint laxity and connective-tissue abnormalities with skin fragility or hyperextensibility; vascular complications are not universal.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy with ataxia and hypodontia defines this subtype; teeth belong to gastrointestinal. Parental optional hypogonadism is insufficient.
Intellectual disability defines this neurodevelopmental umbrella; additional organ abnormalities vary substantially by syndrome.
Type II collagen skeletal dysplasia; significant myopia and vitreoretinal abnormalities affect roughly 40-50% or more in major forms. Hearing involvement is less consistently >=30%.

decisions.ocular: involved: significant myopia and vitreoretinal abnormalities occur in roughly 40-50% or more in major forms, including SED congenita and Stickler syndrome.

basis: Definition includes neurodevelopmental disease, frequent limb malformations and lymphopenia. Lymphatic vessels lack an axis; lymphopenia alone does not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.haematologic: primary: frequent lymphopenia is an explicit defining blood-cell abnormality, even when caused by altered trafficking rather than cell destruction.
decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic vessels are outside the specified cardiovascular axis; no heart or blood-vessel disease is established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: craniofacial and limb malformations are explicitly included as frequent structural manifestations in the disease definition.

basis: Myopathy is an explicit component of this spectrum; cardiac and neurologic involvement varies by subtype, without a supported frequency of at least 30% across the umbrella.
Defining leukodystrophy, dental abnormalities and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; myopia causes ocular functional impairment in 80-99%.
Joint and skeletal abnormalities with skin hyperextensibility/fragility characterize the group; severe valvular disease is subtype-specific.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 2/2 patients; secondary infections do not make this an immune disorder.
Alkaline phosphatase deficiency impairs skeletal mineralization; premature tooth loss and dental attachment defects affect roughly 30-50% of mild/adult presentations.
ALPL deficiency defines a metabolic mineralization disorder of bones and teeth; defective dental cementum and premature tooth loss are characteristic diagnostic manifestations.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: defective tooth mineralization/cementum and premature tooth loss are defining dental manifestations of hypophosphatasia; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

basis: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder, including presentations without intellectual disability or substantial language impairment.
Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder, covered by the neurologic axis.
Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder; severe functional impairment defines this form.
Defined by abnormal ocular growth; brain and digit abnormalities in a child subtype are not established across the umbrella.
Congenital cardiac malformation defines this umbrella; extracardiac anomalies vary across syndromes without a shared additional organ.
The concept is liver injury associated with intestinal failure and parenteral nutrition; intestinal failure is the underlying separate condition.
Defined as VPS11-related neurological disease, encompassing hypomyelinating leukodystrophy and dystonia.
Epilepsy syndrome defined by seizures beginning at variable ages.
Epilepsy and developmental impairment define a brain disorder.
Acquired brain disorder defined by developmental impairment and epileptic encephalopathy.
Aseptic meningitis and bladder emptying failure define the syndrome; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not established.
Inherited neurodegeneration affecting central or peripheral neurons; respiratory dysfunction in some subtypes does not establish direct lung damage.
Progressive neurocognitive decline beginning in childhood; additional organ involvement depends on the underlying disease.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and microcephaly define disease; optional ocular malformations and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism lack established >=30% frequency here.
Classified as an inborn metabolic condition with inconclusive CF screening; established pulmonary or pancreatic damage is not required.
Susceptibility-only concept; neither manifest marrow disease nor MIRAGE organ abnormalities are established. Future myeloid neoplasm risk does not establish organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: the definition specifies inherited susceptibility, not manifest marrow disease; myelodysplasia/leukemia is a later risk.

basis: Defined umbrella of hereditary nervous system disorders; no other organ is consistently damaged across its subtypes.
Focal epilepsy arising from an acquired structural brain abnormality; its varied underlying causes do not establish another shared organ axis.
Focal epilepsy syndrome producing characteristic motor seizures during sleep.
Major phenotypes share brain abnormalities or neurodegeneration. Dysosteosclerosis belongs to the uncommon recessive subtype, not most patients across the umbrella.
Toxin-induced damage to multiple peripheral nerves; other toxic organ injuries depend on the exposure and are not inherent to this concept.
Traumatic injury directly damages peripheral nerves.
Radiation directly damages peripheral nerves; the resulting neuropathy defines this concept.
Corticosteroid-induced skeletal muscle disease; treatment is the cause of this explicitly defined myopathy.
Drug-induced skeletal muscle disease; drug causation defines this concept's primary muscle injury.
Defined as metabolic skeletal-muscle disease associated with endocrine dysfunction.
Immune-mediated inflammation of nerve-supplying blood vessels directly causes ischemic peripheral nerve damage.
Chronic idiopathic peripheral nerve disease.
Established peripheral nerve damage defines this disease; chemotherapy is its cause, rather than an additional involved-organ manifestation.
Defined as peripheral nerve damage caused by infection.
Peripheral nerve injury caused by a vitamin deficiency; both neuropathy and the nutritional metabolic deficiency define the concept.
Peripheral nerve damage defines the disease; paraproteinemia does not establish a uniform immune mechanism or blood-cell disorder.
Cryoglobulin-mediated peripheral nerve injury; systemic cryoglobulinemia manifestations are not established for this neuropathy concept.
Peripheral neuropathy is explicitly defined by an endocrine etiology; neurologic injury and the endocrine mechanism are integral to this concept.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: endocrine causation is a defining component of this etiologically specified neuropathy, supporting the endocrine mechanism axis.
