basis: Peripheral nerve damage caused by immune-mediated sarcoidosis; other systemic sarcoid sites are not inherent to this concept.
Tumour arises in a uterine ligament, a reproductive structure outside the axes.
Congenital glycosylation disorder; brain, lung and gastrointestinal involvement explicitly define the syndrome, supporting all four axes.
Excessive bacterial growth in the small intestine; classified as a digestive infectious disorder.
Hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis and renal insufficiency constitute the defining triad.
Metabolic bone disease caused by chronic fluoride accumulation, with skeletal remodeling and ligament calcification.
Nutritional follicular hyperkeratosis directly affects skin; other organ damage is not established by this cutaneous diagnosis.
Defined by refeeding-associated electrolyte and fluid disturbances; direct damage to additional organs is not consistently present in >=30%.
Chronic suppurative bacterial infection predominantly involving skin and subcutis; visceral involvement is less frequent and heterogeneous.
Cyclic eosinophilia with immune-mediated subcutaneous angioedema defines the syndrome; transient episodes do not establish additional visceral organ damage.
Fibrin deposition and organizing inflammation directly involve alveoli and small airways; infection or autoimmunity is not intrinsic to this histological pattern.
SEC61B-related autosomal dominant polycystic disease of the liver; renal disease is not defining.
Glutamine metabolic disorder defined by encephalopathy, seizures or spastic ataxia. Respiratory failure does not establish direct pulmonary injury across subtypes.
Infectious syndrome defined by vascular injury and leakage with hemorrhage and impaired coagulation.
Bacterial hemorrhagic fever combines infection, disturbed hemostasis and vascular endothelial injury; other organ damage varies.
audit_reason: Add cardiovascular to primary: endothelial injury and vascular leakage underlie hemorrhagic fever, including bacterial forms. The bacterial subtype retains this defining vascular involvement.

basis: IgE-mediated allergic disease; transient skin or systemic reactions do not establish persistent organ damage.
Immune activation syndrome; hypotension, rash and dyspnea do not establish common lasting organ damage.
ALP deficiency causes severe skeletal hypomineralization; defective dental mineralization and premature tooth loss commonly affect surviving children (>30%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intrinsic dental mineralization and cementum defects with premature tooth loss commonly affect infantile HPP during childhood (>30%).

basis: Inherited metabolic disorder defined by defective bone and dental mineralization with premature tooth loss; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Developmental lung and pulmonary capillary disease defined by severe pulmonary hypertension and refractory hypoxemia.
Developmental pulmonary hypoplasia with absent functional gas exchange.
Acinar dysplasia is developmental failure of pulmonary gas-exchanging structures; the gene alone does not support additional axes.
Pulmonary acinar dysplasia is a developmental lung disorder; FGFR2 alone does not establish additional organ involvement.
Congenital pulmonary acinar dysplasia impairs development of the gas-exchanging lung.
Immune-mediated skeletal muscle disease; interstitial lung disease directly damages lungs in approximately 30-40% overall, with substantial variation by subtype.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: interstitial lung disease occurs in approximately 30-40% across idiopathic inflammatory myopathies and represents direct inflammatory lung injury.

basis: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy directly affects skeletal muscle through immune-mediated inflammation; other organ damage is not established across this group.
Blocked, fluid-distended fallopian tube; reproductive organs have no axis. Infection is not intrinsic to the diagnosis.
Giant bullous emphysema causes irreversible destruction of pulmonary parenchyma.
Congenital structural defects of the right heart and its outflow tract; pulmonary valve disease is cardiovascular.
Defined by reduced lung volume and impaired ventilation; extrapulmonary causes vary across patients.
TCF3-PBX1 lymphoblast neoplasm affects blood/marrow; explicit lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma classification and B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma ancestry support the lymphoma mechanism rule.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: explicit B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma synonyms and B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma ancestry trigger the lymphoma rule, beyond lymphoid lineage alone.

basis: Defined by ALG9-associated polycystic kidney disease; common functionally damaging hepatic involvement is not established.
Autoimmune-associated pulmonary syndrome defined by reduced lung volumes and restrictive ventilatory dysfunction.
Umbrella of ATP1A3-related neurologic disorders; optic and auditory damage characterize particular subtypes rather than most patients across the group.
Obstetric umbrella; no organ axis applies across pregnancy, childbirth and puerperal disorders.
Etiologic umbrella indicating unknown cause; no organ or mechanism axis is shared across its heterogeneous diseases.
Heterogeneous chromosomal umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment is common among pathogenic chromosome 2 imbalances, but no uniform phenotype is supplied.
Broad chromosome 12 anomaly umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment is typical across syndromic subtypes, with no consistent additional organ established.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is shared across the major chromosome 15 syndromes listed; endocrine and structural organ abnormalities are subtype-dependent.
Clinically significant partial chromosome 13 duplications commonly cause neurodevelopmental impairment; variable duplicated segments prevent reliable additional organ assignments.
Down syndrome causes neurodevelopmental impairment; congenital heart defects ~40-50%, hearing impairment ~50-75%, and functional ocular abnormalities >50%.

decisions.ocular: involved: developmental ocular abnormalities causing refractive or visual dysfunction affect >50%; these are common syndromic manifestations.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects ~50-75%, commonly with abnormal external/middle-ear development and persistent conductive dysfunction.

basis: Mosaic Edwards syndrome has variable neurodevelopmental and characteristic limb defects. Congenital heart defects affect roughly 40% of reported mosaic cases; full-trisomy frequencies are not used.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects occur in roughly 40% of reported mosaic cases, meeting the threshold despite variable expression.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic hand/foot malformations and contractures are defining Edwards skeletal features, including in its mosaic presentation.

basis: Severe neurodevelopmental impairment, characteristic limb abnormalities and congenital heart disease define Edwards syndrome; renal malformations affect roughly 30-60%.
Defining severe CNS impairment; heart defects ~80%, ocular malformations ~50-70%, oral clefts ~60%. Common polydactyly/limb anomalies omitted at cap because generally less damaging.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects occur in approximately 80% and directly impair cardiac structure and function.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft lip/palate occurs in approximately 60%, directly affecting oral structure and feeding function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common polydactyly and limb anomalies qualify anatomically but are generally less damaging than the four retained axes; omitted at cap.

basis: Sex cord-stromal tumor of reproductive organs; endocrine hormone dysfunction is not inherent to the umbrella concept.
Testicular stromal neoplasm without established hormone dysfunction; purely reproductive site outside the axes.
Pathologic TDP-43 inclusions directly damage brain and spinal cord neurons and glia; proteostasis ancestry alone does not establish a clinical metabolic disorder.
Urinary tract exstrophy/epispadias and pelvic/anterior abdominal wall defects define the complex; bowel abnormalities chiefly belong to the cloacal subtype.
Defining unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia; maternal ABO alloantibodies cause red-cell hemolysis. Jaundice alone does not establish hepatic injury.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine: unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia defines this concept and its metabolic parent. Retain haematologic and infectious_immune for alloimmune hemolysis; jaundice does not establish hepatic injury.

basis: Hereditary susceptibility to sympathetic neural tumors; the primary axis reflects tumor lineage. Tumors reported in 5% and occasional aganglionosis add no involved axes.
Developmental and intellectual impairment characterize 9p duplication syndromes; digital hypoplasia and skeletal malformations occur in >30% across typical presentations.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: digital hypoplasia and other skeletal malformations commonly accompany the developmental phenotype, affecting an estimated >30% across the spectrum.

basis: Prototheca infection directly infiltrates skin in approximately 50-70% of cases. Bursitis and individual disseminated organ sites generally affect fewer than 30%.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: direct cutaneous infection occurs in approximately 50-70%; this umbrella infection also includes bursal and disseminated presentations.

basis: Physiological withdrawal causes central nervous system dysfunction, including delirium and seizures; rhabdomyolysis is an occasional severe complication.
Osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disorder causing reduced bone strength and fragility fractures; premenopausal onset does not change its defining axes.
audit_reason: Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disorder. This axis includes metabolic disorders and does not require a separate endocrine gland disease.

basis: Palmar and plantar skin injury defines the syndrome. Tingling alone does not establish peripheral nerve damage.
An infectious abscess directly occupies and destroys liver tissue.
Infectious abscess between the anal sphincters.
Disordered fetal brain growth causes microcephaly and usually intellectual disability; short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
KIF1A neurodegenerative spectrum; optic atrophy with visual impairment occurs in approximately 40-50% of reported KAND patients.

decisions.ocular: involved: functionally significant optic atrophy affects approximately 40-50% of reported KAND patients.

basis: Defined as a nervous system disorder with pain as a major feature; pain alone does not establish damage to other organs.
Compression and degeneration of an interdigital peripheral nerve; the definition excludes a true neoplasm.
Acute leukemia is a malignancy of blood-forming cells; X-linked inheritance adds no organ axis.
Muscular dystrophy from defective protein glycosylation; cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-50% in the predominant limb-girdle phenotype; brain/eye disease is subtype-specific.
Skeletal myopathy caused by an inherited O-glycosylation defect; brain, eye and cardiac involvement lack established frequencies across the umbrella.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defective alpha-dystroglycan O-glycosylation establishes an inborn glycosylation disorder, beyond gene association alone.

basis: Glycosylation-related myopathy; brain impairment and damaging eye anomalies each estimated >30% across the predominantly muscle-eye-brain spectrum; mild limb-girdle forms can spare both.

decisions.ocular: involved: muscle-eye-brain disease predominates in POMGNT1 myopathy; structural eye disease and retinal dysfunction are estimated to exceed 30% across the spectrum.

basis: Skeletal myopathy and defective protein O-glycosylation define this umbrella. Brain and eye abnormalities in severe congenital forms lack established >=30% frequencies across the full group.

decisions.neurologic: none: severe congenital dystroglycanopathy can affect the brain, but involvement in >=30% across this broader myopathy umbrella is not established.
decisions.ocular: none: ocular malformations occur in severe congenital forms; no supplied evidence establishes direct ocular damage in >=30% across the umbrella.

basis: Dystroglycan glycosylation disorder with myopathy; developmental/intellectual impairment occurs in >30% across POMT1 forms. Eye anomalies chiefly affect severe subtypes.
Inherited alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation disorder causes myopathy; brain/cognitive involvement exceeds ~30% across the spectrum; eye anomalies chiefly affect severe forms.
ETFA-related MADD: lipid-storage myopathy is common (>30%); hepatic dysfunction estimated >=30%, especially in neonatal disease. Cardiac injury is not reliably >=30%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic dysfunction is common in severe neonatal ETFA-MADD; estimated >=30% across this generally severe gene-defined group.
decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy occurs in severe presentations, but >=30% across ETFA-MADD is not established; cardiomyopathy ancestry alone is insufficient.

basis: ETFB-related fatty-acid/amino-acid oxidation disorder; muscle injury frequency is unestablished for this genetic subtype, so pooled MADD myopathy rates are insufficient.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: ETFB-specific myopathy >=30% is unestablished; late-onset MADD rates cannot be assumed ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK558236/)).

basis: Glycosylation-related dystrophy; neurologic dysfunction spans severe and mild forms (ID in 3/3 reported mild cases). Ocular damage is subtype-dependent; pooled frequency is uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS dysfunction spans severe and mild phenotypes; intellectual disability affected 3/3 mild cases. [Report](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8728375/)
decisions.ocular: none: eye malformations characterize severe type A8 but are absent in reported milder forms; a qualifying frequency across the umbrella is not established.

basis: ETFDH-related metabolic disease usually causes lipid-storage myopathy (>50%); cardiac, hepatic and neurologic injury chiefly affect severe minority forms.
Breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Hormone receptor expression does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Breast carcinoma has no axis; hormone receptor expression does not make it an endocrine-gland disease.
Defined by congenital vascular malformations; additional organ damage varies across subtypes.
Surfactant deficiency causes neonatal alveolar collapse and impaired pulmonary gas exchange.
Down syndrome causes neurodevelopmental impairment; congenital heart defects ~40-50%, hearing impairment ~50-75%, and functional ocular abnormalities >50%.

decisions.ocular: involved: developmental ocular abnormalities causing impaired visual function affect over 50%, beyond characteristic facial appearance.
decisions.otologic: involved: persistent hearing impairment affects approximately 50-75% and is a common functional manifestation of the syndrome.

basis: Inherited dystroglycan glycosylation disorder causing skeletal myopathy; brain and eye abnormalities are confined mainly to severe subtypes.
Usher type 1B is defined by sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal degeneration.
A neurologic movement disorder causing episodic dystonia and choreoathetosis; muscle movements do not establish primary muscle damage.
Inherited neurologic movement disorder; dystonia and choreoathetosis do not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Temporal-lobe epilepsy; auditory, visual and autonomic seizure manifestations do not establish damage to ears, eyes or gastrointestinal organs.
Defined by impaired development of cognitive, motor or social nervous-system functions; additional organs are subtype-specific.
Stated Down syndrome subtype: neurodevelopmental disability; heart defects ~40-50%, hearing impairment ~50-75%, visual dysfunction >50%. Balanced wording makes subtype interpretation uncertain.

decisions.ocular: involved: intrinsic visual dysfunction, including significant refractive errors and strabismus, affects >50% in Down syndrome.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects ~50-75% in Down syndrome, including persistent conductive and sensorineural dysfunction.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental impairment; heart defects ~40-50%. Refractive disorders and otitis-related hearing loss are separate conditions; direct sensory damage >=30% is unproven.

decisions.ocular: none: common refractive errors and strabismus are separate diagnoses; direct sight-damaging lesions are not established in >=30%.
decisions.otologic: none: frequent hearing impairment largely reflects associated otitis/effusion; direct persistent ear injury in >=30% is not established.

basis: Developmental disability and scalp aplasia occur in 3/3; urethral hypospadias in 3/3 supports urinary involvement. Minor digit shape abnormalities do not establish locomotor impairment.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias in 3/3 is a direct congenital urethral defect; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: clinodactyly and overlapping digits establish minor dysmorphism without demonstrated skeletal or locomotor dysfunction; cutaneous syndactyly is a skin finding.

basis: Complex congenital cardiac malformations predominate. Asplenia occurs in 4/14 (~29%), below the frequency threshold; abnormal visceral position alone does not establish damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: asplenia occurs in 4/14 (~29%), below the qualifying frequency and not a required diagnostic feature; this is a borderline exclusion.

basis: Contractile vitreoretinal membranes directly damage retinal structure and function.
Severe congenital cerebral malformation with profound motor and intellectual impairment.
Dopamine transporter dysfunction causes a defined neurologic movement disorder with parkinsonism and dystonia.
Proximal 18q deletion typically causes developmental delay and intellectual disability; no additional organ has sufficiently established common damage here.
Developmental impairment/hypomyelination core; hearing loss ~50-80%, foot deformities ~70%, GH deficiency ~60%. Common ocular abnormalities omitted because of the four-axis cap.
BAF-complex developmental disorders predominantly cause intellectual disability and developmental impairment; additional organ abnormalities vary across subtypes.
BAFopathy is a chromatin-remodeling neurodevelopmental disorder; supplied evidence does not establish other commonly damaged organs.
Defined by developmental delay, structural brain malformations and congenital cardiac defects.
Neurodevelopmental impairment predominates among pathogenic chromosome 21 imbalances; other organ damage is not consistent across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Broad chromosome 18 anomaly umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment predominates among clinical syndromes. Other organ defects vary substantially by rearrangement.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; congenital heart defects affect ~40-50%, persistent ocular dysfunction >50%, and hearing impairment ~40-65% in adults over the typical course.

decisions.ocular: involved: failed ocular emmetropization produces persistent significant refractive dysfunction in approximately 62%, beyond cosmetic findings. [Cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12601024/)
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing-system dysfunction persists into adulthood; hearing loss affected 65% of adults, with premature auditory aging. [Cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28654410/)

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the Down syndrome spectrum; congenital heart defects occur in roughly 30-40% of mosaic cases.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines Down syndrome; congenital heart defects occur in ~40-50%. Common separately diagnosed thyroid, middle-ear and refractive disorders excluded.

decisions.ocular: none: common vision problems largely comprise separately diagnosed refractive errors and strabismus; direct ocular damage in >=30% is not established.
decisions.otologic: none: common hearing impairment largely reflects separately diagnosed middle-ear disease; direct intrinsic ear damage in >=30% is not established.

basis: Mosaic Down syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder; congenital heart defects occur in approximately 40% of mosaic cases, supporting direct cardiovascular involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects affect approximately 40% of mosaic Down syndrome cases, exceeding the 30% threshold.

basis: Partial trisomy 21 classified within Down syndrome supports neurodevelopmental involvement; other organ defects vary with the duplicated segment.
Dopamine transporter dysfunction causes a central movement disorder with parkinsonism and dystonia; no additional organ damage is established.
Delayed endocrine maturation with transient hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; delayed bone age does not establish skeletal damage.
Neonatal bacterial bloodstream infection; bloodstream location alone does not establish disease of blood cells, marrow or coagulation.
Group B streptococcal infection is defined by its infectious cause; no particular organ site applies across the concept.
Malignant cells directly occupy leptomeninges and subarachnoid space; the variable primary cancer site is not assigned.
Broad transplant-associated disease category, chiefly involving immunosuppression, infection or alloimmunity; no particular graft or damaged organ is specified.
Umbrella of transplant-related immune and immunosuppression disorders; no single damaged organ is common across the group.
Inherited skeletal muscle disease umbrella; additional organ involvement depends on subtype and cannot be generalized.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; no evidence of extraocular disease.
Inherited gallbladder disease; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Immune hypersensitivity to food; transient eruptions, gastrointestinal symptoms and shock do not establish persistent damage to additional organs.
Inherited macular retinal dystrophy; no evidence of extraocular disease in this concept.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease; osteoporosis belongs to a subset, with no evidence it affects at least 30% across this umbrella.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; no evidence of common extraocular damage.
Developmental hypoplasia of the retinal fovea, with or without ocular albinism.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease affecting retinal vascular development; no evidence of systemic vascular involvement.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; disease is defined by retinal involvement.
Inherited retinal degeneration defines the disease.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; retinal degeneration defines the disease.
Inherited RD3-associated retinal degeneration; neurologic ancestry does not imply extraocular nervous-system damage.
Bardet-Biedl subtype supports defining retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; renal abnormalities/dysfunction occur in roughly 30-50%. Common neurodevelopmental involvement omitted by cap.
Bardet-Biedl phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity and renal anomalies are major criteria; cognitive impairment affects ~50-60%; common polydactyly omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal structural or functional abnormalities are a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion; this BBS10 umbrella predominantly represents that phenotype.

basis: Dominant BEST1-related disease of the retina.
Biallelic BEST1-associated retinal disease; no established extraocular organ damage.
Inherited retinal dystrophy caused by biallelic IMPG2 variants; retinal damage defines the disease.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; the affected organ is the retina.
CACNA1F-related retinal dysfunction or dystrophy; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular CNS damage.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; the neurological ancestor does not establish extraocular disease.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder with hyperkeratosis and blistering; hypernatremic dehydration occurs in only 1/4.
Defined as an eye developmental disorder caused by defective PAX6 regulation; no other organ disease is specified.
Defined by congenital ocular abnormalities, neurodevelopmental impairment with progressive spasticity, and hypogonadism. Contractures follow neurologic spasticity.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contractures follow progressive neurologic spasticity; the record does not establish direct disease of skeletal muscle, bones or joints.

basis: Inherited epidermolytic ichthyosis with erythroderma, hyperkeratosis and variable blistering.
Epidermal keratinization disorder causing blistering, ichthyosis and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.
SURF1 respiratory-chain disease with characteristic encephalopathy; regression 13/13, optic atrophy 2/2. COX-negative fibers alone do not establish myopathy; respiratory failure may be central.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive encephalopathy characterizes SURF1 disease; developmental regression in 13/13 and ataxia in 11/11 support a defining neurologic phenotype.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: COX-negative fibers in 15/15 demonstrate enzyme deficiency, but do not establish functional myopathy; hypotonia in 11/11 can arise from encephalopathy.

basis: Congenital orofacial cleft affects oral structures and the facial skeleton; the parent and facial-skeleton ancestry support both defining axes.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary: orofacial cleft involves the facial skeleton, including the palate/alveolus. The skeletal defect need not be a separate lesion from the oral cleft.

basis: Defined by paraneoplastic endocrine dysfunction; additional organs vary across the constituent syndromes.
Defined as a paraneoplastic disorder of the hematopoietic system; immune mechanisms and other organ involvement are not universal across the umbrella.
Paraneoplastic dysfunction of the digestive system; the broad definition does not establish an immune mechanism or another affected organ.
Defined by renal dysfunction caused by a paraneoplastic process; immune or endocrine mechanisms are not universal across the umbrella.
Inherited interferon-mediated autoinflammatory disease. Neurologic, skin and retinal involvement varies across subtypes; no reliable group-wide frequency supplied.
Autoinflammatory interferonopathy; AGS-like encephalopathy and neurodevelopmental damage predominate (>30%). Connective-tissue ancestry alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Genetically defined autoinflammatory interferonopathy; damaging AGS-like encephalopathy is the predominant presentation (>30% estimated). Skin frequency is uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: AGS-like encephalopathy predominates (>30% estimated), but this umbrella is defined by interferon dysregulation and permits other phenotypes.

basis: Autoinflammatory interferonopathy; damaging AGS-like encephalopathy is the predominant RNASEH2A phenotype (>30%). Other organ involvement is insufficiently established.
Interferon-mediated disease; destructive AGS-type encephalopathy and chronic chilblain skin injury each affect >30% of the reported SAMHD1 spectrum, despite skin-only presentations.

decisions.neurologic: involved: AGS5 is a major SAMHD1 presentation; destructive encephalopathy affects >30% of the usual reported spectrum, although chilblain-only cases lack it.

basis: Inherited type I interferon-mediated autoinflammatory umbrella; neurologic and cutaneous manifestations depend on subtype, without a shared frequency established.
Inherited interferon-mediated autoinflammation; neurologic, skeletal and vascular damage varies substantially between the included syndromes.
Inherited autoinflammatory interferonopathy. AGS is a possible presentation; the frequency of neurologic damage across this umbrella is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: the definition identifies AGS as one possible phenotype, without establishing neurologic disease in most patients across the umbrella.

basis: Interferon-driven autoinflammatory disease with defining neurologic manifestations; other organ injury varies across subtypes.
Defined by paraneoplastic disease of joints, bones, skeletal muscles or locomotor connective tissue; immune mechanisms are not universal.
Defined by paraneoplastic skin disease; an immune-mediated mechanism is not universal across this umbrella.
Cancer susceptibility, principally involving breast, which has no axis. Neuroblastoma is a later risk, not existing neurologic damage.
Cancer susceptibility without established organ damage; principal predisposed sites are breast and ovary, outside the axes; pancreatic cancer is a later risk.
Cancer predisposition without established organ disease; breast and ovarian sites have no axis, and pancreatic cancer is a risk rather than existing damage.
Cancer susceptibility without an established tumour or intrinsic organ damage; potential future cancer sites are not affected organs.
Inherited cancer susceptibility without intrinsic organ damage; breast, ovarian and pancreatic cancers are separate diseases rather than existing organ involvement.
Predisposition to ovarian and breast cancers, both outside the axes; susceptibility alone does not establish organ damage.
Cancer predisposition involving ovarian and breast sites, both outside the axes; predisposition alone does not establish organ damage.
Hereditary prostate malignancy has a reproductive organ origin; metastatic symptoms do not establish common direct damage to another axis.
Predominant phenotype is hypomyelinating leukodystrophy. Dental, endocrine and progeroid abnormalities vary across subtypes; umbrella-wide frequencies are uncertain.
Both listed subtypes affect central or peripheral myelin; dental and endocrine abnormalities are not shared across the group.
Cerebral palsy with spastic paralysis of three limbs; motor impairment reflects central neurologic injury.
Post-infectious syndrome following Lyme disease; fatigue, pain and cognitive symptoms do not establish common direct damage to additional organs.
Defined by a complex neurodevelopmental disorder; no specific additional organ damage established.
Leukodystrophy, dental abnormalities and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; progressive myopia affects ~80-90%, supporting ocular involvement.
audit_reason: Add ocular involvement: progressive myopia is an intrinsic feature in approximately 80% or more of POLR3-related leukodystrophy patients, meeting the common functional impairment rule within the four-axis cap.

basis: Cerebral motor disorder producing spasticity and ataxia; these do not establish independent skeletal-muscle damage.
Fatty-acid oxidation disorder encompassing CPT1A and CPT2 deficiencies; hepatic, cardiac and skeletal muscle injury vary substantially by subtype.
Dystrophin-related skeletal muscle degeneration; cardiomyopathy affects most over the lifetime. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Adult-onset cerebral white-matter demyelinating disease; no defining extra-neural damage.
Neurodegeneration, retinal dystrophy and deafness define syndrome; fixed limb contractures occur in 1/1 assessed and cubitus valgus in 2/2, supporting structural involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed limb contractures (1/1 assessed) and cubitus valgus (2/2) establish structural impairment beyond weakness; frequency estimates have very small denominators.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency defines the umbrella; additional affected organs vary across its constituent syndromes.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm flagella and infertility; no endocrine or other organ dysfunction established.
Glycogen metabolism disorder predominantly affecting liver across the group; muscle disease is restricted to less common subtypes.
Benign but locally destructive fibrous neoplasm of bone, supported by the bone-neoplasm ancestry.
Hearing loss spans the principal WFS1 phenotypes. Diabetes and optic atrophy characterize syndromic subsets; their prevalence across the umbrella is unestablished.

decisions.ocular: none: optic atrophy defines syndromic subsets but is absent from isolated hearing-loss disease; common involvement across the umbrella is unestablished.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: diabetes defines syndromic subsets but is absent from isolated hearing-loss disease; common involvement across the umbrella is unestablished.

basis: Central and peripheral demyelination with autonomic dysfunction; bladder symptoms, constipation and orthostatic hypotension do not establish direct urinary, gut or vascular damage.
Aflatoxin poisoning primarily causes hepatocellular injury and potentially acute liver failure; toxin exposure is not an infection.
Cobalamin remethylation disorder with megaloblastic anemia; brain atrophy and severe developmental impairment in 1/1 assessed, seizures in 1/2.
Cobalamin-related organic aciduria; intellectual disability and seizures in 1/1 support neurologic damage. Crisis cytopenias lack evidence of sustained blood injury.

decisions.haematologic: none: leukopenia and thrombocytopenia in 1/1 accompany neonatal metabolic decompensation; persistent marrow or blood damage is not established.

basis: Adrenal macronodular hyperplasia causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome; no additional common direct organ damage established.
Achalasia and generalized lipodystrophy; corneal opacity and sensorineural hearing loss each 5/5. Neurologic, skin and skeletal findings omitted by cap; valve disease 1/4.
Progeroid skin/lipodystrophy, hypothyroidism and severe developmental impairment; cataract in 1/1; hepatic injury and contractures omitted by cap.
Traumatic injury of the upper brachial plexus causes arm paralysis; weakness reflects nerve injury rather than primary muscle disease.
FASLG-related autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome is defined by immune dysregulation, defective lymphocyte apoptosis and abnormal lymphocyte accumulation.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the ALPS synonyms identify a disease of lymphocytes with defining nonmalignant lymphoproliferation; this is intrinsic blood-cell pathology.

basis: Hereditary corticospinal disease with frequent peripheral neuropathy and ataxia; weakness and amyotrophy reflect neurologic injury.
Inherited immunodeficiency; the record does not establish common direct damage to another organ.
Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia; structural joint contractures in 11/11 support musculoskeletal involvement.
DNAJC21-related marrow failure and immunodeficiency; skeletal abnormalities reported in roughly half of cases. Pancreatic insufficiency is not a consistent defining feature of this subtype.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: pancreatic insufficiency in classic Shwachman-Diamond syndrome cannot be generalized to DNAJC21 disease; >=30% is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital skeletal abnormalities occur in roughly half of reported DNAJC21 cases; estimates come from small series.

basis: Cardiac channelopathies are the predominant established presentation; neurologic and skeletal findings are subtype-dependent, with no evidence they affect most across this umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurodevelopmental disease is a distinct subtype; neurologic involvement is not established in most patients across the umbrella.

basis: The supplied definition specifies central auditory maladaptive neuroplasticity following an organic cochlear lesion; both auditory and CNS dysfunction define the condition.
SLE: inflammatory arthritis ~80%, skin disease ~70%, nephritis ~30-50%. Cap omits common cytopenias in favor of severe renal injury; C4A-specific frequencies unavailable.

decisions.haematologic: none under cap: cytopenias occur in >50% of SLE, but arthritis, skin disease and potentially severe nephritis receive priority; C4A-specific rates unknown.
decisions.renal: involved: lupus nephritis directly damages kidneys in ~30-50% of SLE and is a major diagnostic domain; subtype-specific rates are unavailable.

basis: Defined by variable craniosynostosis, radioulnar synostosis and congenital aortic valve or other heart disease.
Defining features are high-flow vascular malformations, limb bone/soft-tissue overgrowth and persistent cutaneous capillary malformations; heart failure shares the vascular axis.
Defined immunodeficiency; the supplied evidence does not establish common direct damage to another organ across the group.
Structural or functional injury of glomerular podocytes defines renal disease; immune mechanisms are not universal across this umbrella.
Immunodeficiency defines this PTEN-associated subtype. The supplied record establishes no additional common organ damage; gene association alone is insufficient.
Type I interferonopathy causing inflammatory encephalopathy; chilblains occur in ~40% of AGS overall, but that frequency is not established for this dominant TREX1 subtype.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the approximately 40% chilblain frequency in AGS overall cannot reliably establish at least approximately 30% in this specific dominant TREX1 subtype.

basis: Isolated familial myocardial disease with ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction; extracardiac phenotypes are occasional or excluded by definition.
Extensive carcinoma deposits occupy the abdominal peritoneal lining; the variable original cancer site does not establish another axis.
Renal tubular dysgenesis commonly causes pulmonary hypoplasia through fetal anuria and deficient skull ossification through fetal hypotension; each occurs in >30%.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is common (>30%) in the usual severe congenital course, arising from fetal anuria and oligohydramnios.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: deficient calvarial ossification is a characteristic common (>30%) developmental consequence of fetal renin-angiotensin dysfunction and hypotension.

basis: Defining cutaneous autoinflammation; hepatitis and fasciitis each reported in 1/1 support hepatic and fascial inflammation. Endocarditis is not established as intrinsic disease; sparse samples.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: endocarditis in 1/1 does not establish intrinsic autoinflammatory cardiac injury; a separately diagnosed infection would not qualify.

basis: DNM1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy directly affects brain development and function.
Congenital foreskin/penile malformation; urine trapping and difficult voiding do not establish intrinsic urinary tract damage.
Hair-shaft disorder causing fragile beaded hair, alopecia and follicular hyperkeratosis.
Hair-shaft disorder with brittle beaded hair, alopecia and follicular hyperkeratosis.
Inherited hair-shaft disorder causing brittle, sparse hair and alopecia, sometimes with follicular keratosis or nail abnormalities.
Nephronophthisis is the established core phenotype. Respiratory, retinal and CNS manifestations vary across this broad umbrella; frequencies supporting additional axes are unavailable.
Hereditary pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma syndrome classified as endocrine neoplasia; increased renal carcinoma risk does not establish renal involvement.
Hereditary endocrine tumor predisposition centered on pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma; tumor complications are not assumed in carriers.
Complex II deficiency is a metabolic disorder; the supplied definition identifies neurological and muscular manifestations as its defining organ phenotype.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurological manifestations are explicitly part of the supplied disease definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: muscular manifestations are explicitly part of the supplied mitochondrial disease definition.

basis: Juvenile polyps directly occupy the gastrointestinal tract; cancer predisposition adds no other organ axis.
Defined by ACTN2-related cardiac and skeletal muscle disease, including cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy.
GRIN2B-related neurodevelopmental impairment, including intellectual disability and developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
Neurodegenerative tauopathy with neuronal and glial brain pathology.
Congenital joint contractures and skeletal abnormalities with congenital heart defects or cardiomyopathy define the syndrome.
Intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures define a neurodevelopmental disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Limb and joint malformations, neurodevelopmental disorder and blepharophimosis define the syndrome; hearing impairment affects most. Genitourinary anomalies do not specify renal disease.
Defined neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental delay and hypotonia; less frequent cardiac abnormalities lack evidence of meeting the 30% threshold.
Defined neurodevelopmental disorder affecting speech and language; variable cardiac anomalies lack evidence of frequency reaching 30%.
Developmental disability, seizures and delayed myelination define CNS disease; common strabismus alone does not demonstrate direct eye damage or visual loss.

decisions.ocular: none: common strabismus alone does not establish direct ocular damage or visual loss; it can reflect impaired central control of eye alignment.

basis: Defined by developmental delay and epileptiform brain dysfunction; no other organ damage is established.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and generalized epilepsy.
Developmental delay and central/obstructive apnea define the disorder; skeletal malformations affect most, including contractures, scoliosis and talipes. Cleft frequency is unclear.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and neurodevelopmental behavioural abnormalities.
Defined by global developmental delay or intellectual disability with autism and behavioural abnormalities.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; heart defects and renal agenesis are described as common, supporting approximately >=30% qualitatively; exact rates absent. Eye abnormalities lack damage details.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: the definition describes heart defects as common; accept this qualitative frequency evidence near the 30% threshold, with uncertainty because no denominator is supplied.
decisions.renal: involved: unilateral renal agenesis is direct structural loss and described as common; exact frequency is unavailable, so the 30% judgment remains uncertain.
decisions.ocular: none: unspecified ophthalmological anomalies establish neither a damaging ocular phenotype nor a frequency of such damage at or above 30%.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, developmental delay and brain abnormalities; feeding difficulties alone do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and commonly epilepsy; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle disease.
Developmental impairment and brain abnormalities define the disorder; cardiac abnormalities are less frequent without evidence meeting the threshold.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define a neurodevelopmental disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish skeletal muscle disease.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and brain abnormalities; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and other neurodevelopmental abnormalities.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease; musculoskeletal abnormalities are described as common (~30%+). Unspecified genitourinary findings cannot establish renal damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with severe lactic acidosis; variable seizures, hypotonia and respiratory distress lack established common organ damage.
Mitochondrial disease spectrum explicitly defined by optic atrophy and/or spastic ataxia; ocular and neurologic disease are its two defining presentations.

decisions.neurologic: primary: spastic ataxia is an explicitly defining presentation of the spectrum, rather than a secondary complication.
decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is an explicitly defining presentation of the spectrum, rather than an incidental ocular finding.

basis: Retinal degeneration is shared across the listed CFAP418 phenotypes; systemic Bardet-Biedl manifestations do not apply across the group.
Inherited retinal degeneration spanning cone-rod, macular and retinitis pigmentosa phenotypes.
Inherited cone or cone-rod retinal degeneration.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease; hearing loss and developmental impairment vary between Norrie disease and other NDP phenotypes, with no umbrella frequency established.
Polydactyly or polysyndactyly is shared across the named subtypes; cardiac, retinal, renal and endocrine involvement varies by subtype.
The named SDCCAG8-related syndromes share nephronophthisis/renal disease and retinal degeneration; other Bardet-Biedl features are not universal across this group.
Inherited retinal dysfunction or degeneration, including stationary night blindness and retinitis pigmentosa.
Inherited macular retinal dystrophy within the CDHR1-related retinopathy spectrum.
Hepatic heme-metabolism disorder defined clinically by neurovisceral attacks or childhood encephalopathy. Ocular disease belongs mainly to rare biallelic forms.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neuropathic neurovisceral attacks and biallelic developmental encephalopathy are defining disease manifestations, rather than later complications.

Chronic airway disease driven by type 2 immune inflammation.
Chronic asthma with non-T2 airway inflammation; neutrophilic immune pathways support infectious_immune despite non-atopy and variable granulocyte counts.
audit_reason: Add infectious_immune: T2-low asthma retains an immune-mediated airway disease mechanism, including neutrophilic inflammation. Non-atopy, low granulocyte counts and corticosteroid resistance do not establish exclusion of that mechanism.

basis: Immune-mediated airway disease with severe obstruction and respiratory failure; altered consciousness does not establish separate neurologic damage.
Immune-mediated chronic airway inflammation and airflow impairment worsen at night.
Parkinsonian dysfunction caused by cerebrovascular lesions; both cerebral injury and vascular pathology define the condition.
Malignant astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system.
An astrocytic central nervous system tumour; BRAF mutation does not establish another organ axis.
Supratentorial ependymoma originates in the central nervous system.
This spindle-cell neoplasm typically originates in dermis or subcutis. Neural differentiation does not establish nerve origin; generic connective-tissue ancestry does not establish muscle disease.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the tumor typically arises in dermis or subcutaneous tissue, both covered by this axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: connective-tissue ancestry alone does not establish origin in locomotor connective tissue; muscle involvement is not established as usual.

basis: Defined as a connective tissue neoplasm; no specific visceral or CNS origin is established.
B-cell lymphoma; blood-cell lineage and lymphoma mechanism apply. No extranodal organ involvement is established as common.
B-cell lymphoma qualifies as both blood-cell neoplasia and lymphoma mechanism; molecular subtype does not define another organ site.
Small round cell sarcoma arising predominantly in soft connective tissues; no other organ involvement is established across cases.
Ependymal tumour arising in the supratentorial central nervous system.
Ependymal tumour arising in the supratentorial central nervous system.
Primary CNS ependymal tumor arising in the posterior fossa.
Ependymal CNS tumour arising in the posterior fossa; molecular subgroup features do not add organ axes.
Astrocytic neoplasm diffusely infiltrating the central nervous system.
IDH-mutant astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Primary central nervous system glial tumor; molecular classification does not imply a systemic metabolic disorder.
Grade 3 oligodendroglioma is a primary central nervous system tumour.
Hereditary disease group defined by abnormalities of vision and its neurologic pathways; no additional organ involvement can be established.
Hereditary structural malformation of the brain; no additional organ phenotype is specified.
Childhood autoinflammatory disease umbrella; no particular damaged organ is established across most subtypes.
Isolated degeneration of the retinal macula.
Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define HUS; complement-mediated immune injury predominates. Intrinsic small-vessel thrombosis/endothelial damage occurs in essentially all.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: intrinsic thrombotic microangiopathy damages small vessels in essentially all; three primary slots retain blood, kidney and immune mechanism.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: inherited complement dysregulation causes immune-mediated endothelial injury in the predominant hereditary HUS forms.

basis: Inherited skeletal muscle sodium-channel dysfunction causes abnormal muscle excitability; peripheral nerve or CNS damage is not established.
Inherited skeletal-muscle chloride channel dysfunction; the muscular channelopathy parent supports muscle disease without established nerve or CNS involvement.
Muscular calcium-channel disorder; neuromuscular classification alone does not establish brain or peripheral nerve disease.
Inherited skeletal-muscle channelopathy; the supplied classification does not establish separate brain or peripheral nerve damage.
Glioma originates in midline structures of the central nervous system.
Diffuse glial tumor arising in and infiltrating the central nervous system.
Isolated sperm abnormalities and male infertility affect reproductive function, outside the axes.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease; kyphoscoliosis affects 4/8 (50%). Feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Autoinflammatory vasculitis with interstitial pneumonitis and respiratory failure; cutaneous vasculitis in 1/1 reported patient; organomegaly alone excluded.
Pituitary maldevelopment causes hormone deficiency; strabismus occurs in 3/5 and hypermetropia in 2/5 reported patients.
Brain, eye and renal defects define syndrome; intestinal malrotation 2/3. Pituitary failure and hearing loss each 1/1, and skeletal findings, omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intestinal malrotation in 2/3 assessed patients is direct congenital intestinal pathology, with stronger replication than the endocrine findings.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none under cap: pituitary hormone failure is reported in 1/1; retain defining brain/eye/kidney disease and intestinal malrotation documented in 2/3.

basis: Copper transport defect with neurodegeneration; pulmonary hypoplasia and cardiomegaly/tricuspid regurgitation each reported in 1/1; skeletal anomalies omitted by cap.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; seizures and global developmental delay each reported in 1/2 patients. Diarrhea lacks evidence of direct intestinal damage.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure; low estradiol and elevated FSH in 11/11 patients establish hormone dysfunction.
Developmental brain malformations with seizures and developmental impairment; cerebral visual impairment reflects brain dysfunction, not eye damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental and speech delay, intellectual disability, microcephaly and structural or white-matter brain abnormalities.
Inherited oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation defect causing female infertility; purely reproductive disease without an established endocrine disorder.
Diaphragmatic myopathy occurs in 4/4; respiratory failure in 2/4 reflects muscle dysfunction. Cardiomyopathy is 1/4; isolated brain and lung findings lack reliable prevalence.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure results from diaphragmatic muscle weakness; intrinsic pulmonary disease is not established as common or defining.

basis: Neurodegeneration and defining respiratory failure (6/6); hearing impairment 3/3 and structural joint contractures 4/4. ASD 2/6 omitted by the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none under cap: ASD 2/6 (~33%) qualifies, but defining respiratory failure and more frequent hearing impairment and contractures take priority.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: early respiratory failure is a defining feature explicitly named in this syndrome and documented in 6/6 assessed patients.

basis: RFX7-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability and speech delay; extra-neurologic findings are uncommon or non-damaging dysmorphism.
Immunodeficiency and pancytopenia occur in 4/4; learning/developmental deficits in 3/4 and hemivertebrae in 2/2. Dermatitis in 2/4 omitted at cap; infections are secondary diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: pancytopenia and anemia in 4/4 establish a core blood-cell disorder alongside the immunodeficiency.

basis: Oocyte/embryo maturation failure causes female infertility; purely reproductive without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Inherited oocyte/embryo maturation defect causing female infertility; purely reproductive dysfunction without evidence of endocrine gland disease.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with macular damage and visual dysfunction.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; ophthalmoplegia (2/5) and ptosis (2/2) support ocular involvement. Respiratory muscle weakness does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy in 1/2 supports ocular damage. Feeding difficulty and constipation do not establish direct gut damage.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Isolated sperm motility defect causing male infertility; reproductive function is outside the axes, with no endocrine dysfunction established.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic sinusitis and bronchitis in 4/4 patients; sperm abnormalities have no applicable axis.
Congenital secretory diarrhea; hepatic steatosis with elevated transaminases occurs in 5/5. Hypoglycemia also occurs in 5/5, but intrinsic metabolic/endocrine pathology is not established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: recurrent hypoglycemia occurs in 5/5 but may follow enteropathy and nutritional depletion; frequency alone does not establish direct metabolic/endocrine disease.

basis: ATP synthase deficiency is metabolic; developmental impairment occurs in 3/6 and anemia in 2/3. Chronic diarrhea in 2/3 lacks evidence of direct intestinal injury or established enteropathy.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: chronic diarrhea in 2/3 establishes a common symptom but does not establish direct intestinal damage, malabsorption or enteropathy.

basis: Mitochondrial ATP synthesis disorder; brain atrophy, developmental delay and severe epilepsy occurred in the sole reported patient (1/1).
Inherited low LDL and hypofibrinogenemia define lipid-metabolic and coagulation abnormalities; isolated AST elevation does not establish liver damage.
Telomere syndrome defined by pulmonary disease and/or marrow failure. Premature graying in 3/5 does not establish skin damage; hepatic abnormalities occur in 1/5.
Osteopetrosis with CKD, visual impairment/papilledema and anemia each in 1/1 reported patient; secondary renal electrolyte and parathyroid changes excluded.
Fibrosis and marrow failure define syndrome; hepatic failure with nodular regenerative hyperplasia reported in 1/1 assessed, but frequency is uncertain in this small cohort.
Cerebroretinal microangiopathy defines disease (brain/retinal lesions 2/2); gastrointestinal hemorrhage 1/2 (50%). Recurrent fractures 1/2 (50%) omitted under cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cerebral and retinal microangiopathy directly affect small blood vessels and define the disorder.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: recurrent fractures in 1/2 (50%) support involvement, but omitted under the four-axis cap; gastrointestinal vascular bleeding is prioritized for severity.

basis: Severe congenital skeletal myopathy; structural pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 5/10 patients. Motor delay reflects muscle weakness.
Photosensitive progeroid skin; sicca and delayed permanent dentition each 2/3; dental crowding, anemia and thrombocytopenia each 1/3. Muscle atrophy 1/3 omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia and thrombocytopenia each occur in 1/3 patients, meeting the supplied frequency threshold for blood-cell dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy in 1/3 qualifies, but is omitted at the four-axis cap; long thumbs alone do not demonstrate locomotor impairment.

basis: Hemorrhagic brain injury; retinal hemorrhage/amblyopia 2/2, tracheomalacia 2/2 and hammertoes 3/3. Small denominators limit confidence; isolated cardiac findings omitted.
Urinary sulfate excess with low circulating sulfate supports renal sulfate wasting and disturbed sulfate homeostasis. Kidney stone in 1/1 is separately diagnosed and adds no organ.

decisions.renal: primary: urinary sulfate excess despite low circulating sulfate supports a renal sulfate-reabsorption disorder; the label does not depend on nephrolithiasis.

basis: Inherited skeletal muscle dystrophy; respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness, not direct lung damage. Cardiac dysfunction 1/4 is below threshold.
Systemic autoinflammation with vasculitis; colitis/oral ulcers 2/2 and liver injury 2/2 with cholestasis; arthritis omitted by cap; purpura reflects vascular inflammation.
Inherited peripheral axonal and demyelinating neuropathy; sustained denervation causes characteristic structural skeletal-muscle atrophy in most patients.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic neurogenic muscle wasting affects most patients (>30%); actual structural atrophy is integral to the neuropathy, beyond weakness alone.

basis: Spastic paraplegia and motor delay occur in 20/20; corpus callosum abnormalities reinforce nervous-system involvement.
Inherited oocyte maturation defect causing female infertility; confined to reproductive function.
Auditory neuropathy causes sensorineural hearing dysfunction; no generalized neurologic disease is established.
Structural skeletal myopathy; ventricular myocardial fatty replacement in 3/4 supports cardiac damage. Reduced FVC reflects muscle weakness without proven lung injury.
Structural skeletal myopathy with nemaline bodies. Respiratory insufficiency and dysphagia reflect muscle weakness, without demonstrated intrinsic lung or gastrointestinal damage.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay in 2/2; ventricular septal defect and eczematoid dermatitis each in 1/2. Frequencies derive from only two patients.
Isolated sperm flagellar dysfunction and male infertility; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not demonstrated.
Inherited epidermolytic palmoplantar hyperkeratosis; no established extracutaneous involvement.
Woolly hair in 9/9 and fragile skin in 8/9 establish a skin and hair disorder.
Scoliosis 1/1 and sensorineural hearing loss 1/2; reflux/dysphagia lack demonstrated intrinsic GI injury; port-wine marks lack dysfunction. Very small cohort.
Spastic paraplegia; contracture, sensorineural hearing loss and myopia each reported in 1/1 patient; estimates are limited. Reflux is a separate diagnosis.
Inherited rod-cone retinal dystrophy with macular degeneration and reduced visual acuity in 11/11 patients.
Familial glomerular basement membrane disorder causing persistent microscopic hematuria.
Calcium oxalate stones of the urinary tract; no specific systemic metabolic disorder is established for this umbrella.
Isolated degenerative disease of the choroid and retina.
Glaucoma is an ocular disease causing optic nerve damage; the underlying secondary cause is unspecified.
Glycine metabolism defect with encephalopathy and developmental delay. Isolated liver and cardiac findings lack reliable ≥30% prevalence; apnea can reflect central dysfunction.
Inherited dystonia with striatal lesions and motor disability; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than gastrointestinal damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and brain abnormalities define the disorder alongside ocular defects, including optic atrophy and retinal dystrophy.
Endocrine autoimmunity 2/3; autoimmune hemolysis and vitiligo each 1/3 are syndrome manifestations. Hepatic hemophagocytosis (1/3) omitted at cap.
Airway ciliary dysfunction causes chronic rhinitis, sinusitis and bronchiectasis; infertility has no axis; situs inversus alone is not cardiovascular damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with universal developmental delay; obesity is a separately diagnosed phenotype, and ocular defects are individually below 30%.
All four named organ disorders define the syndrome. Hearing impairment is retained as involved because primary is capped at three; numerical frequencies are unavailable.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: enterocolitis is a named defining intestinal disorder.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is a named defining feature, satisfying the diagnostic-feature exception; placed here under the three-primary cap.

basis: Childhood autoinflammatory periodic fever syndrome; recurrent fever alone does not establish lasting organ damage.
Umbrella includes Blau and infantile panniculitis syndromes, with defining granulomatous skin inflammation and arthritis; uveitis is a major diagnostic feature across these subtypes.
audit_reason: Add dermatologic, musculoskeletal and ocular for defining skin inflammation, arthritis and uveitis across its subtypes: [Blau](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/90340), [panniculitis syndrome](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/251304).

basis: Childhood autoinflammatory interferonopathy umbrella; neurologic, skin, vascular and other organ damage varies substantially among its subtypes.
Borna virus infection causes inflammatory injury of the brain.
Immune-mediated pituitary inflammation with hormone deficiencies; secondary adrenal and thyroid deficiencies remain within the endocrine axis.
B-lymphoblastic blood/marrow malignancy within the leukemia/lymphoma spectrum; lymphoma warrants the immune mechanism axis.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma is a hematopoietic malignancy; the lymphoma designation also warrants the immune mechanism axis.
Psychotic disorder outside the axes; cognitive symptoms belong to the psychiatric syndrome, while structural brain abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
Cortisol excess directly causes myopathy in roughly 40-70% and skin atrophy/fragility in over 50%; associated hypertension is a separate diagnosis.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension affects roughly 70-80%, but is separately diagnosed; direct cardiac or vascular injury is not established in at least 30%.

basis: Raised limb compartment pressure causes muscle ischemic injury; sentinel skin ulceration or necrosis occurs in most neonatal cases. Nerve injury frequency is uncertain.
Primary structural narrowing of pulmonary veins; pulmonary vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.
Inherited ataxia caused by PEX16 deficiency, a peroxisome biogenesis disorder; no evidence establishes common damage to additional organs in this ataxic form.
Hereditary cerebellar ataxia caused by a peroxisomal biogenesis defect; no additional common organ damage is established here.
Closed spinal dysraphism with a myelocystocele above the conus and an associated posterior vertebral defect; neural and spinal skeletal malformations define it.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary: myelocystocele combines spinal cord malformation with a posterior vertebral closure defect. Its non-terminal location does not remove the defining spinal skeletal defect.

basis: Noninflammatory degeneration of arterial media causing dissections, aneurysms and hemorrhage; not an immune-mediated vasculitis.
Open neural and vertebral closure defect with Chiari II. Neurogenic bladder is a separate diagnosis; direct urinary tract injury in >=30% is not established.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder reflects spinal denervation and is separately diagnosed; direct urinary tract damage in >=30% is not established.

basis: Split spinal cord with myelomeningocele and vertebral dysraphism. Neurogenic bladder is a separate diagnosis; common direct urinary tract damage is not established for this subtype.

decisions.renal: none: extrapolated neurogenic bladder frequency does not establish direct urinary tract injury in >=30% of this rare subtype; bladder dysfunction is separately diagnosed.

basis: Autoimmune inflammatory muscle and skin disease; interstitial lung disease affects approximately one-third of patients.
Immune-mediated dermatomyositis without cutaneous manifestations; a >=30% frequency of lung disease is not established for this subtype.
Spontaneous perforation directly disrupts the intestinal wall.
Tuberculous infection of lymph nodes; neither blood or marrow disease nor pulmonary involvement is established by this localized diagnosis.
Primary tuberculosis infection involving the lungs.
Tuberculous infection directly involves bone and joints; pulmonary involvement is not inherent to this localized concept.
Primary tuberculosis infection of the skin; pulmonary disease is not intrinsic to this cutaneous concept.
Multisite tuberculosis; pulmonary infection accompanies roughly half of cases, exceeding 30%. Other organ sites vary.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary infection accompanies approximately 50% of multifocal tuberculosis over its course; lung involvement is common but not required.

basis: Primary tuberculous infection of the digestive tract.
Tuberculous infection of the genitourinary tract includes the urinary system; genital involvement has no additional axis.
Craniosynostosis defines skeletal involvement; Chiari I malformation and developmental/language delay define neurologic involvement.
Persistent common urethral-vaginal channel is a structural urinary tract malformation; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and obesity define the syndrome; ocular abnormalities and reflux are only occasional.
Osteoporosis directly affects bone; pregnancy association does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Idiopathic catatonia is a psychiatric psychomotor syndrome; its behavioral and motor manifestations do not establish direct structural organ damage.
Immune dysregulation with hemolytic anemia in 4/8 and pericarditis in 2/2; diarrhea 3/12 is below threshold; isolated restrictive defect is insufficient.
HUS defines hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and kidney injury; rhizomelic skeletal shortening defines the subtype; global developmental delay occurs in 2/2 reported patients.
GI dysmotility 2/2 and reflux 4/4; urinary tract anomalies include reflux 2/2 and horseshoe kidney 1/3; bicuspid valve 2/3. Scoliosis 2/2 omitted by cap; small denominators.
Immune-mediated pansclerotic skin disease; oral ulcers 4/4 and disabling joint contractures 3/4; cytopenias 3/4 omitted at cap.
Diffuse carcinoma originates in the stomach; no other organ involvement is established as common.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain metabolic disorder explicitly localized to skeletal muscle.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus in 6/11 and scoliosis in 5/10 support additional involvement. Vesicoureteral reflux occurs in 2/7, below threshold.
Cerebral white-matter disease with subcortical cysts, seizures and progressive motor/cognitive deterioration; dysphagia is neurologic.
Cerebral white matter disease with subcortical cysts, seizures and developmental impairment; all reported patients have neurologic involvement.
Combined immune deficiency with low immunoglobulins and abnormal lymphocyte populations; associated infections are separately diagnosed complications.
Intellectual and speech developmental impairment define the disorder. Extra-neural findings reported in isolated 1/1 assessments do not establish ≥30% prevalence in the ≥6-person cohort.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft palate and ankyloglossia each have only 1/1 assessed reports; common intrinsic oral disease across the larger cohort is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal abnormalities each have isolated 1/1 reports; overlap and population frequency are unknown, so ≥30% involvement is unproven.
decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing impairment is reported in 1/1 assessed patient, insufficient to establish ≥30% prevalence across the larger cohort.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; intellectual disability 5/6, myopathic fibers 2/3 with weakness 2/5, and optic atrophy 2/6 support neurologic, muscle and ocular involvement.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability 5/6, with demyelination 2/2 and cerebellar atrophy, supports common CNS damage from the primary mitochondrial metabolic disorder.

basis: Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; established skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 5/10 patients. Respiratory failure occurs in only 1/10.
Generalized dystonia, cerebellar atrophy and cognitive deterioration; laryngeal and ocular movement abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Liver failure/cholestasis 2/2; skeletal defects 2/2; renal agenesis/hydronephrosis 1/2. Cardiac defects 1/2 omitted by cap; low anticoagulants may reflect liver failure.

decisions.haematologic: none: reduced protein C and antithrombin activity in 2/2 may reflect hepatic failure; independent direct coagulation disease is not established.
decisions.hepatic: primary: severe hepatic failure and cholestasis in 2/2 establish the dominant organ phenotype of this glycosylation disorder.
decisions.renal: involved: renal agenesis and hydronephrosis each occur in 1/2 reported patients, meeting the frequency threshold for structural renal involvement.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and seizures; hearing impairment reported in 2/2 assessed patients, with uncertain broader frequency; central hypoventilation is not lung damage.
Inherited adult-onset dystonia with cognitive deterioration and other neurologic signs.
Auricular and mandibular malformations define the syndrome; hearing impairment in 6/6. Narrow mouth and glossoptosis do not establish digestive tissue injury; apnea alone adds no pulmonary axis.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: narrow mouth (8/10) and glossoptosis (4/9) describe craniofacial anatomy without established direct gastrointestinal injury or functional loss.

basis: External ear and mandibular condyle malformations define the syndrome; corpus callosum hypoplasia and central apnea reported in 1/1 assessed patient support neurologic involvement.
Inherited dilated cardiomyopathy; ventricular dysfunction and supraventricular tachycardia are documented.
Pulmonary venous atresia commonly causes affected-lung hypoplasia and chronic congestive interstitial injury, estimated >30%; respiratory infections are separate diagnoses.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: persistent venous obstruction commonly causes lung hypoplasia and chronic interstitial injury (>30% estimated), beyond transient congestion.

basis: Inherited susceptibility specifically targets noise-induced cochlear hearing loss; susceptibility does not establish existing injury.
Inherited infection-triggered encephalopathy in 8/8; cataracts in 2/2 assessed support ocular involvement. Infection susceptibility alone does not establish an immune disorder.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: an infection-triggered inherited encephalopathy is not itself an infection or established immunodeficiency; the record does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.

basis: Cranial dysinnervation and developmental impairment define disease; profound hearing loss in 1/1 and cochlear hypoplasia in 1/2; corneal opacity in 1/2 supports ocular damage.
Congenital smooth muscle hamartoma is a dermal lesion, often with hypertrichosis. Dermal smooth muscle is not skeletal muscle; hemihypertrophy alone is not damage.
Inherited platelet deficiency, with thrombocytopenia in 10/10 patients; reduced thrombopoietin does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Congenital megakaryocyte deficiency causes thrombocytopenia and commonly progresses to hypocellular marrow failure and pancytopenia.
Early-onset hereditary parkinsonism with intellectual disability in 4/4 patients; psychiatric symptoms do not add an organ axis.
Heme synthesis disorder with fragile skin 2/2 and blistering/scarring; neurodevelopmental impairment/neuropathy and high myopia each 1/1. Skeletal findings 1/1 omitted at cap; tiny series.

decisions.ocular: involved: high myopia in 1/1 assessed patient establishes persistent visual dysfunction; confidence is limited by the tiny series.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic childhood blistering, fragility and scarring establish a defining cutaneous disease component; skin fragility occurs in 2/2.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: short digits and delayed skeletal maturation each reported in 1/1; retain neurologic and ocular dysfunction as the more consequential involvement.

basis: Inherited platelet disorder with thrombocytopenia and bleeding; petechiae, bruising and epistaxis do not establish separate skin or airway damage.
Inherited platelet dysfunction and macrothrombocytopenia; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish separate organ damage.
Developmental disorder; visual impairment in 8/15 (~53%) and scoliosis in 5/17 (~29%, near threshold); isolated cardiac/lung observations do not establish common involvement.
Isolated sperm structural and motility defects causing male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ involvement.
Contractures and kyphoscoliosis occur in 2/2 assessed, as do astigmatism and esotropia. Microtia and superficial skin/nail findings lack demonstrated functional injury.

decisions.otologic: none: microtia is reported in 2/2 assessed, but external-ear dysmorphism alone does not demonstrate hearing, vestibular or other functional damage

basis: Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm morphology; reproductive function has no axis.
Acrosomal sperm defect causing male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or organ within the axes is established.
Marrow failure defines syndrome; hypogonadism with elevated FSH in 2/2 supports endocrine dysfunction. Chiari I in 1/2 lacks documented neurologic injury; evidence is limited to two patients.
audit_reason: Remove neurologic: Chiari I in 1/2 patients documents an anatomical finding without demonstrated neural injury or dysfunction. Frequency alone does not satisfy the direct-damage requirement.

basis: Early-onset epilepsy is a neurologic disorder; metabolic causes apply only to particular subtypes.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with language delay in 4/4 and intellectual disability in 2/3; structural ocular and skeletal abnormalities occur in only 1/4.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with frequent brain malformations; extracerebral findings reported in single patients do not establish common involvement.
Inherited ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis; supplied findings are confined to skin and nails.
Skin, immune and pulmonary dysfunction define syndrome; atrial septal defect in 3/4. Neurologic (2/4), eyelid (3/4) and bone (2/4) abnormalities omitted by cap.
Corticospinal dysfunction causes spastic weakness and gait impairment; skeletal deformities occur in only 1/5 and weakness alone does not establish muscle disease.
Inherited immune dysregulation; anemia with bleeding manifestations reported in 1/1 patient supports blood involvement, with very limited ascertainment.
Progressive neurodevelopmental degeneration with motor and cognitive regression, spasticity and brain atrophy; oromotor dysfunction is neurologic.
Cardiomyopathy and ectodermal hair abnormalities define disease; motor delay alone does not establish intrinsic neurologic injury.
Immune dysregulation directly causes dermatitis in 15/16, inflammatory airway disease in 11/16 and gastrointestinal eosinophilic infiltration in 10/16.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: intrinsic atopic dermatitis affects 15/16 (94%); it is a common tissue manifestation of the underlying immune disorder.

basis: Congenital neutrophil deficiency with marrow maturation arrest causes impaired innate immunity; anorectal abscess is a secondary infection.
Developmental delay and structural brain abnormalities define disease; ocular dysfunction (exotropia, ptosis or nystagmus) reported in 1/3, near the threshold.
Inherited glomerular disease with renal insufficiency in 6/6; hearing loss reported in only 1/6, below 30%; no ocular involvement documented.
Genetic developmental epileptic encephalopathy with frequent seizures and developmental impairment; macroglossia in one assessed patient is insufficient.
Corticospinal and cerebellar dysfunction define disease; optic neuropathy in only 2 assessed patients cannot establish population frequency; muscle atrophy is neurogenic.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual, speech and motor impairment, sometimes epilepsy; ocular findings are below 30%.
Contractures and muscle atrophy define disease; sensory loss in 3/5 and strabismus in 2/5 support involvement. Dental crowding/high palate lack documented functional damage.
audit_reason: Remove gastrointestinal: dental crowding and high palate alone do not establish organ damage or loss of function. Persistent sensory loss in 3/5 and strabismus in 2/5 support neurologic and ocular involvement.

basis: Glycosylation disorder; developmental delay 4/4 with seizures and brain abnormalities; muscle atrophy 2/4; strabismus 1/2 and visual impairment 1/3.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with azoospermia and male infertility; no evidence of gonadal hormone dysfunction or another covered organ disorder.
Primary ovarian insufficiency includes gonadal endocrine failure, supported by elevated FSH and decreased AMH in 2/2 patients.
Hereditary optic nerve degeneration; optic pallor, visual field constriction and reduced acuity occur in 2/2 reported patients.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; myopia in 3/5 does not establish direct disease-related eye injury. [Report](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-44259-4)

decisions.ocular: none: myopia occurs in 3/5, but the report describes nonsyndromic hearing loss and does not establish myopia as direct ocular involvement of this disease.

basis: Generalized osteosclerosis with hip dysplasia; global developmental delay in 3/7 (~43%); ASD and VSD each 2/7, with overlap unknown.
Vanishing white matter leukodystrophy; ovarian insufficiency reported in 2/2 and cataract in 1/1 patients support involvement, with substantial small-sample uncertainty.
Vanishing white matter leukodystrophy affects cerebral white matter; hemianopia is central; one amenorrhea report does not establish common endocrine dysfunction.
White-matter degeneration; optic atrophy 2/2. Associated ovarian insufficiency is supported by primary and secondary amenorrhea, each reported in 1/2.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: ovarian insufficiency is a recognized component of vanishing-white-matter disease; primary and secondary amenorrhea each occur in 1/2 annotated patients.

basis: Inherited white-matter disease with progressive neurologic deterioration in 4/4 patients; no additional organ damage established.
COQ7-related CoQ10 deficiency presenting as motor neuropathy; muscle atrophy (5/6) and pes cavus (3/3) reflect denervation and secondary deformity, without established direct muscle disease.
