decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy in 5/6 and pes cavus in 3/3 are consequences of motor denervation; direct muscle or skeletal disease is not established.

basis: Motor axonal neuropathy; fixed skeletal consequences include hammertoes in 5/5 and Achilles contractures in 2/2, supporting common musculoskeletal impairment.
Hereditary motor axonal neuropathy; persistent muscle atrophy in 7/8 and structural pes cavus in 2/3 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Defined by hepatic steatosis with alcohol exposure and cardiometabolic risk factors; those risk factors do not establish additional organ involvement.
Toxic peripheral nerve injury after organophosphate exposure; weakness reflects neuropathy rather than primary muscle disease.
Pneumatoceles, intestinal bleeding and scoliosis each 2/2; ileus/myositis 1/2. Cytopenias, hepatic, renal, skin and neurologic findings each 1/2 omitted by cap.

decisions.haematologic: none: autoimmune cytopenias in 1/2 qualify but are omitted by the four-axis cap; splenomegaly in 2/2 alone does not establish functional damage.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intestinal bleeding in 2/2 supports bowel injury; paralytic ileus in 1/2 adds functional impairment. Celiac disease alone is excluded as separate.

basis: Neurodevelopmental and congenital skeletal phenotype; strabismus 3/7. Macrodontia 4/4 lacks documented functional injury; reflux 1/1 is sparse. VSD 3/17 is below 30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: macrodontia 4/4 does not itself establish functional damage; reflux reported in 1/1 does not establish common direct GI injury in this subtype.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital limb/skeletal malformations belong to the inherited CdLS phenotype; hip dysplasia and scoliosis are each reported in 2/2.

basis: Primary airway ciliary dysfunction; recurrent otitis media in 3/4 and structural cardiac defects in at least 2/6. Situs abnormalities alone are not damage.
Otosclerosis causes conductive or sensorineural hearing impairment; remodeling is localized to the ear.
Optic atrophy with visual loss defines the disease; headache does not establish additional neurologic damage.
Lymphatic vascular malformation causes primary lymphedema; no additional organ damage is documented.
Folate transport defect with immunodeficiency and megaloblastic anemia; developmental delay 3/4, delayed myelination 2/2. Oral ulcers 4/4 and skin ulcers 2/4 omitted by cap.
Hereditary corticospinal tract disease with spasticity, hyperreflexia and Babinski signs in 4/4 patients.
Isolated oocyte/embryo maturation failure causing female infertility; no endocrine dysfunction established.
Optic atrophy causes visual loss; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 2/2 annotated patients. Headache does not establish additional neurologic damage.
Muscle fatty replacement/atrophy, inflammatory dermatitis and intestinal lymphangiectasia occur in at least 50% of reported cases; developmental delay omitted by cap.
Familial dilated cardiomyopathy with severely reduced ventricular function in 3/3 patients.
Cerebellar degeneration and axonal neuropathy define disease. Muscle atrophy in 2/2 and scoliosis in 1/2 reflect secondary neuromotor effects rather than direct muscle or bone disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy in 2/2 is attributable to denervation; scoliosis in 1/2 is secondary. Neither establishes direct musculoskeletal pathology.

basis: Bone fragility and skeletal dysplasia define disease. Acanthosis nigricans in 3/5 and blue sclerae in 4/5 do not establish functional damage; insulin resistance is only 1/5.

decisions.dermatologic: none: acanthosis nigricans occurs in 3/5, but thickening and pigmentation alone do not establish substantial skin damage or loss of function.

basis: Ciliary airway dysfunction; pulmonary hypertension 2/3 and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia 1/3 support involvement. Small series; situs inversus alone is not damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; developmental delay 2/3, cardiomyopathy/heart failure 1/3 and retinal degeneration 1/3. Small cohort; cholelithiasis is a separate disease.
Mitochondrial myopathy with ophthalmoplegia/ptosis (5/5); gastrointestinal dysmotility 2/5 (40%). Neuropathy and hearing loss each 1/5, below threshold.
Diabetes, deafness and developmental delay each 2/2; high myopia 1/2 supports ocular dysfunction. Scoliosis and alopecia, each 1/2, omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: high myopia affects 1/2 reported patients, with functional visual impairment; small sample limits confidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: scoliosis occurs in 1/2, but unspecified severity gives it lower priority than high myopia and the three defining axes.

basis: Intellectual disability and cortical malformation define the disorder; optic atrophy reported in 1/3 (~33%), with uncertainty from the small sample.
Thrombocytopenia with defining developmental impairment; aortic aneurysm 2/4, renal agenesis 1/2; skeletal anomalies and tracheomalacia omitted by cap.
Skeletal dysplasia; microtia in 2/2 assessed supports otologic involvement. Cardiac findings and reflux each have single-patient reports; prevalence >=30% is unestablished.
audit_reason: Remove cardiovascular and renal: findings in single assessed patients do not establish the 30% threshold across at least four reported patients. Retain otologic because microtia is documented in two patients.

basis: Spastic ataxia caused by impaired coenzyme Q biosynthesis; visual impairment in 1/3 is not localized to ocular structures.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment occurs in 1/3 assessed patients, but ocular injury is not established and central visual dysfunction remains possible.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this COQ4-associated ataxia results from defective coenzyme Q biosynthesis, an inborn metabolic mechanism.

basis: IRF1 immunodeficiency; pulmonary infections are separately diagnosed consequences. Cytopenias in 1/2 lack evidence of persistent intrinsic blood disease.
Inherited iron-handling disorder with brain iron accumulation and neurodegeneration; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated intrinsic bowel damage.
Antibody deficiency defines the disease; recurrent respiratory and ear infections are separately diagnosed complications, without documented chronic organ damage.

Neutrophil maturation failure causes immunodeficiency; renal hypoplasia and recurrent aphthous mucosal ulceration each occur in 1/1 reported patient. Singleton estimates are uncertain; infections excluded.

decisions.renal: involved: renal hypoplasia is direct structural kidney involvement reported in 1/1; this is the available subtype-specific frequency evidence, with substantial uncertainty.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent aphthous stomatitis and ulcers occur in 1/1 and represent intrinsic neutropenia-associated mucosal injury; secondary infections are excluded.

basis: CNS hypomyelination and degeneration define disease; optic atrophy occurs in 2/4. Scoliosis/pes cavus in 1/2 each do not establish direct skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis and pes cavus each occur in 1/2, but may result from neurologic dysfunction; hypermobility alone does not establish direct musculoskeletal damage.

basis: Partial subcutaneous fat loss with metabolic dysfunction defines lipodystrophy. Hypertension and sleep apnea are separate diseases; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss with insulin resistance and dyslipidemia; hepatic steatosis in 2/2 with elevated transaminases supports direct hepatic involvement.
Inherited immunodeficiency; BCG disease is a separately diagnosed infection. Hepatosplenomegaly and osteomyelitis each occur in 2/7, below 30%.
Metabolic lipodystrophy with subcutaneous fat loss; hepatic steatosis 7/7 and demyelinating neuropathy 5/5. Skeletal abnormalities in 3/7 omitted at cap.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated FSH and depleted follicular reserve; hormonal dysfunction warrants the endocrine axis.
Congenital hip dislocation and acetabular hypoplasia define a skeletal joint-development disorder.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is universal, with frequent seizures and hypotonia; premature adrenarche alone does not establish endocrine damage.
Open spinal cord malformation with exposed neural placode and defective posterior vertebral arches; Chiari II remains within the neurologic axis.
Inherited iron overload characteristically targets liver; iron-related arthropathy affects roughly 30-50% in hereditary hemochromatosis. Digenic-specific frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.hepatic: primary: characteristic hepatic iron accumulation and injury are central to the hereditary hemochromatosis phenotype
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: iron-related structural arthropathy affects roughly 30-50% in hereditary hemochromatosis; digenic-specific data are limited

basis: Oral cleft, congenital cardiac malformation and intellectual disability are the three defining components.
Isolated congenital supernumerary kidneys; kidney-disorder ancestry supports the renal axis.
Progressive cerebral white matter disease and early sensorineural deafness define the disorder; reported visual impairment has no established common frequency.
Mature T-cell lymphoma is a haematologic malignancy and qualifies for the lymphoma mechanism axis; common extranodal damage is not established.
Mature T-cell lymphoma arising in and infiltrating intestinal epithelium.
Congenital aneurysm of the superior vena cava; directly affects a major vein.
Aneurysmal dilation of the inferior vena cava is a structural venous disorder.
Fibrotic narrowing of the subglottic airway directly impairs airway patency.
Lymphocytic mastitis is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory breast disorder. Breast has no structural axis; associated diabetes and thyroid disease are separate diagnoses.
Inherited Alport nephritis; sensorineural hearing loss is a major Alport diagnostic feature; damaging ocular involvement is less consistently established.
Sensory and autonomic dysfunction causes pain and temperature insensitivity; decreased corneal reflex does not establish eye damage, and fractures result from injury.
Cutaneous occlusive vasculopathy defines disease; ischemic intestinal involvement occurs in approximately half across the benign/systemic spectrum. CNS injury is less frequent.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: direct intestinal vascular occlusion causes ischemic bowel injury in approximately 50% overall; benign cutaneous cases are included in that estimate.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency and bent-bone dysplasia ancestry establish immune and skeletal involvement; no other common organ damage is supplied.
Eczema and skeletal abnormalities occurred in both initial recessive partial-deficiency cases (2/2). [Study](https://haematologica.org/article/view/8818/62225).

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent eczema/atopic dermatitis affected both initially described recessive partial-deficiency patients, supporting >30%; small sample.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: craniosynostosis and scoliosis affected both initially described patients, supporting common intrinsic skeletal abnormalities; small sample.

basis: Immunodeficiency; eczema >50%, retained teeth needing extraction >50%, scoliosis >30%; lung disease is secondary. [Cohort](https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20191804).

decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic eczema affects >50% in the AD IL6ST cohort; direct immune dysregulation causes persistent dermatitis.

basis: IL6R immunodeficiency with chronic eczematous dermatitis in most reported patients (>50%); recurrent infections alone do not establish lasting damage to other organs.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent eczematous dermatitis affects most reported IL6R-deficient patients (>50%); intrinsic immune dysregulation, not a transient rash.

basis: Embryonal tumor originates in the central nervous system, usually intracranially.
ERBIN immune dysregulation includes chronic eczema; >30% is inferred from sparse familial reports. Additional organ injury frequencies are unestablished.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic eczema is a recurrent core phenotype, inferred >30% from sparse reports. [NIH](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/RCV001984044.6/).

basis: Small-fiber nerve injury defines disease; keratoconjunctivitis sicca affects the ocular surface in 30-79%. Xerostomia and sweating changes alone do not establish other organ damage.
Anomalous pulmonary artery origin defines defect; direct tracheobronchial compression with airway obstruction occurs in roughly half or more, independent of intrinsic tracheal stenosis.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: the anomalous artery directly compresses the tracheobronchial airway, causing functional obstruction in roughly half or more; intrinsic tracheal stenosis is not required.

basis: Transplant-associated immune injury causes fibrotic obliteration of small airways, including chronic rejection or graft-versus-host disease.
Fibrotic obliteration of small airways; this umbrella does not establish a uniform infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Contiguous deletion form of Greig syndrome combines polysyndactyly with substantial neurodevelopmental impairment; facial spacing alone does not establish ocular damage.
Defined by early-onset autoimmunity and immune dysregulation; no specific organ damage established by the supplied record.
Inherited early-onset immune dysregulation; supplied evidence does not establish additional organ damage in at least 30%.
Tick-borne Borrelia infection; mening CNS involvement is uncommon, and transient cytopenias or elevated liver enzymes do not establish common organ damage.
Burkholderia cepacia syndrome is a fulminant infection characterized by necrotizing pneumonia and systemic infection.
Sarcoma arising in bone or mesenchymal soft tissues; genetic alteration does not establish additional organ involvement.
Mesenchymal sarcoma arising in bone or soft tissue; fusion status does not establish additional organ involvement.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma defines hematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes; functionally damaging hepatic involvement at >=30% is not established for this subtype.

decisions.hepatic: none: generic ALL hepatomegaly/infiltration estimates do not establish functionally damaging liver involvement in >=30% of PAX5 P80R cases.

basis: DUX4-rearranged B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma is a precursor lymphoid malignancy of blood and marrow; lymphoma classification adds the immune axis.
Malignant notochordal tumor arising in the axial skeleton, commonly the skull base or spine; location alone does not establish neural invasion.
Anaplastic sarcoma arising in the kidney.
Skin lesions, odontogenic jaw keratocysts and characteristic skeletal anomalies define PTCH1-related Gorlin syndrome; rib anomalies occur in ~50-60%. Falx calcification is non-damaging.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: bifid, fused or markedly splayed ribs are major diagnostic criteria; characteristic skeletal anomalies are intrinsic to the syndrome.

basis: Craniofacial skeletal and ear defects define the syndrome. Limbal dermoids occur in 11/18 and developmental delay in 3/8; cap omits transverse facial clefts (3/8).
Skeletal muscle dystrophy with defining eyelid and pharyngeal muscle dysfunction; ptosis 6/6 and dysphagia 3/7. The supplied mapping places the pharynx under pulmonary.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pharyngeal muscle degeneration defines oculopharyngeal dystrophy; the guide explicitly assigns the pharynx to pulmonary.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia reflects defining pharyngeal myopathy, mapped to pulmonary; separate oral, esophageal or intestinal injury is not established.

basis: Autoinflammatory sterile osteomyelitis; bone inflammation documented in 6/6 patients; pustulosis frequency is unspecified.
Hearing loss 12/13, cataracts 10/15 and nephrotic syndrome 6/15; enterocolitis affects 6/15 (40%). Marrow hypocellularity is below threshold at 3/15.
Glycine metabolism disorder defined by encephalopathy, seizures and developmental impairment; hyperglycinuria does not establish renal damage.
Retinal phototransduction recovery defect causes bradyopsia and reduced visual acuity in all reported patients.
Fatty-acid oxidation disorder with myopathy; peripheral neuropathy in 11/14 and dilated cardiomyopathy in 8/11; isolated transaminase elevation does not establish hepatic damage.
Classical complement deficiency causing immunodeficiency; glomerulonephritis is occasional (5-29%), and lupus is a separate disease.
Hereditary optic neuropathy from mitochondrial complex I dysfunction; central scotoma in 24/29. Retinal vascular findings remain within the ocular axis.
Epidermolytic ichthyosis causes epidermal fragility and abnormal keratinization; no additional organ involvement is established.
Fatty-acid oxidation defect with recurrent muscle breakdown (15/15); peripheral neuropathy 7/13 and dilated cardiomyopathy 7/20. Isolated transaminase reports do not establish liver damage.
Familial glomerular basement-membrane disease presenting with microscopic hematuria in 9/9 patients.
Complement deficiency; discoid lesions 4/4, arthritis 1/3 and bronchiectasis 1/3 support skin, joint and airway damage. An isolated oral ulcer does not establish persistent mucosal damage.
audit_reason: Add pulmonary: bronchiectasis in 1/3 (~33%) establishes structural airway damage meeting the frequency threshold. The resulting four axes fit the cap.

basis: Classical complement immunodeficiency; discoid lupus in 2/2 and meningitis in 1/1 assessed patients are separately diagnosed associated diseases.

decisions.dermatologic: none: discoid lupus is a separately diagnosed autoimmune disease associated with C1q deficiency; its reported 2/2 frequency does not override that exclusion.

basis: Basal cell tumors and palmoplantar pits define disease. CNS tumors are separate predisposition outcomes; hydrocephalus in 1/2 does not establish independent common neurologic involvement.

decisions.neurologic: none: medulloblastoma and meningioma are separately diagnosed predisposition outcomes; hydrocephalus in 1/2 may be secondary, and falx calcification is non-damaging.

basis: Inherited retinal response dysfunction causing bradyopsia and reduced visual acuity in all reported patients.
Inherited calcium oxalate stone disease with nephrocalcinosis; urinary oxalate and citrate abnormalities do not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
AMT glycine-cleavage deficiency causes hyperglycinemia and encephalopathy. Respiratory failure in 14/14 reflects central respiratory dysfunction, not intrinsic lung damage.
Nephrotic syndrome, cataracts and enterocolitis each 2/2; hearing impairment is syndrome-defining. CNS hypoplasia/hypomyelination (1/2) omitted by cap.
External-ear malformation occurs in 10/10; craniofacial skeletal hypoplasia is defining, with micrognathia in 3/10. Palatal defects in 1/10 fall below the involvement threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: craniofacial skeletal hypoplasia defines craniofacial microsomia; micrognathia in 3/10 corroborates this axis rather than representing a separate complication.

basis: Dystrophy affects skeletal, eyelid/extraocular and pharyngeal muscles; ptosis/ophthalmoplegia 11/11, dysphagia 9/9, dysphonia 5/5. Pharynx maps to pulmonary.
audit_reason: Add pulmonary to primary: pharyngeal muscle disease is defining, with dysphagia in 9/9 and dysphonia in 5/5. The specified pulmonary axis includes the pharynx; intrinsic lung disease is not required for direct pharyngeal dysfunction.

basis: Early-onset epilepsy with frequent developmental delay and intellectual disability defines nervous system disease.
Inherited mitochondrial complex I deficiency manifests as optic neuropathy; visual loss and optic atrophy occur in 3/3 patients. Optic nerve involvement is ocular.
Abnormal glycogen metabolism causes progressive myoclonic epilepsy and dementia; visual symptoms are cerebral; common hepatic injury is not established.
Nonsyndromic intellectual developmental disorder; intellectual disability in 3/3.
Progressive cerebral arterial stenosis; direct ischemic brain injury with stroke and persistent deficits affects roughly 30-50% in moyamoya, with limited subtype data.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with universal developmental delay and intellectual disability; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; myopia causes ocular functional impairment in 6/9 patients. Hypotonia alone does not establish myopathy.
Isolated male infertility from abnormal sperm flagella and motility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Porphyria-related encephalopathy; cataracts 2/3 and optic hypoplasia 1/1; anemia 1/3 with splenomegaly 2/3. Kyphosis 1/3 omitted by cap; hepatomegaly alone lacks functional damage.
Porphyria-related white matter disease; optic atrophy in 2/2 and hearing impairment in 1/3 support involvement, though cohorts are tiny. Hepatic porphyria does not establish liver injury.
Polydactyly defines disease; developmental delay 1/2, autism 2/2, structural ocular defects 1/2 and ASD 1/1 assessed. Renal agenesis 1/3 omitted by cap; very small samples.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: structural atrial septal defect is reported in 1/1 assessed; retained under the cap using the supplied frequency, with substantial sampling uncertainty.
decisions.renal: none under cap: renal agenesis 1/3 qualifies, but neurologic, ocular and cardiovascular abnormalities have higher reported frequencies.

basis: Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing impairment, reported in 2/2 patients.
Vascular bleeding disorder; no blood-cell or coagulation defect is established. Gastrointestinal bleeding in 2/4 identifies a bleeding site without establishing intrinsic gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.haematologic: none: supplied evidence establishes vascular pathology but no disease of blood cells, marrow or coagulation; bleeding alone does not establish this axis.

basis: Oral clefts and polydactyly define syndrome; callosal agenesis 2/4 (50%) and atrioventricular canal defect 2/5 (40%) support brain and cardiac involvement; small series.
Defining neurodevelopmental disease; skeletal deformities include clinodactyly in 3/3, and eyelid ptosis occurs in 3/5. Estimates derive from a small cohort.
Nonsyndromic bilateral sensorineural hearing loss; tinnitus belongs to the same ear axis.
Collagen VI-related skeletal myopathy with muscle fiber pathology, weakness and joint contractures; no additional organ damage established.
Collagen VI-related skeletal myopathy causes weakness and joint contractures; kyphosis is within the same axis.
Collagen VI muscular dystrophy damages skeletal muscle and causes contractures; ventilatory failure results from respiratory muscle weakness.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure (1/1 annotated) is neuromuscular; common ventilatory insufficiency does not establish direct lung or airway damage.

basis: Congenital collagen VI myopathy with weakness, contractures and joint hypermobility. Respiratory muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Inherited ferritin/hepcidin dysregulation indicates an iron metabolism abnormality; no blood-cell disorder or iron-overload organ damage is established.
Isolated developmental eye disorder with coloboma, optic disc abnormalities and impaired vision.
Defining neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and structural brain abnormalities; skeletal muscle atrophy and pes cavus each occur in 2/4 patients.
Familial atrial cardiomyopathy with atrial enlargement and fibrosis in 2/2 patients.
Isolated sperm motility impairment and male infertility; reproductive function lies outside the axes.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by destructive skin inflammation and axial inflammatory arthritis.
Defining immune-mediated arthritis and inflammatory skin disease include psoriatic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, acne and hidradenitis.
Adrenal cortisol excess causes muscle/bone loss and dermal atrophy/striae, each in roughly 50-80%. Hypertension is a separately diagnosed associated disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension occurs in roughly 70-80%, but is separately diagnosed; common direct cardiac or vascular structural damage is not established.

basis: Closed spinal cord dysraphism with an abnormal connecting stalk; dermal elements do not establish common functional skin damage across the group.
Lipomatous mass occupies the spinal cord region in spinal dysraphism; no additional common organ damage is established.
Isolated nodular disease of the adrenal cortex; separately coded consequences of cortisol excess are excluded.
Micronodular disease of the adrenal cortex; an endocrine gland disorder.
Infection directly inflames and damages the ocular sclera.
Idiopathic scleritis is immune-mediated inflammation of the sclera.
Immune-mediated inflammation of the sclera defines both ocular and immune axes.
Isolated congenital bronchial branching malformation.
Isolated congenital atresia of a bronchus directly affects the lower respiratory airway.
Isolated congenital bronchial laterality abnormality; no evidence of associated cardiac or splenic disease.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central activation alone does not establish brain damage.
Defining cleft palate, congenital heart malformation and intellectual disability affect oral structures, heart and neurodevelopment.
Skin-limited occlusive small-vessel disease causing atrophic papules; benign form lacks systemic organ involvement.
Segmental maldevelopment of the spinal cord and vertebral column defines the disorder; direct urinary tract damage in at least 30% is not established.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder can accompany cord dysfunction, but direct urinary tract injury in at least ~30% is not established; secondary urologic diagnoses do not suffice.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment in 8/8; macrocephaly in 1/8 does not establish neurologic disease.
Developmental impairment and brain malformations define disease; ankle contractures occur in 2/5 (40%). Recurrent infections do not prove intrinsic lung damage.
Megalencephaly and polydactyly define syndrome; hydronephrosis 1/1, VSD 1/2. Tracheomalacia 1/3 omitted at cap; estimates derive from very small samples.
BCOR-altered mesenchymal sarcoma, typically arising in soft tissue; the molecular subtype alone does not establish other organ involvement.
Mesenchymal sarcoma arising predominantly in bone or soft tissue; no additional organ involvement established.
BCOR-altered sarcoma arises in mesenchymal tissues, typically bone or soft tissue.
Mesenchymal sarcoma arising in bone or soft connective tissues; childhood onset does not establish another organ.
Fusion-defined sarcoma arising predominantly in bone or soft connective tissue.
Fusion-defined round cell sarcoma arising in soft connective tissues; no common additional organ damage established.
Fusion-defined round cell sarcoma arising in bone or soft tissue.
Renal epithelial malignancy defined by a TFEB rearrangement.
Childhood renal cell carcinoma arising in the kidney; MiT translocations specify the tumour subtype.
Developmental disability; scoliosis 4/4, myopia 4/4 with visual impairment, sensorineural hearing loss 6/18; cap omits patent ductus arteriosus 5/15.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, parkinsonism and axonal neuropathy define disease. Distal wasting in 2/2 assessed patients reflects denervation; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy in 2/2 assessed patients is neurogenic; direct skeletal muscle disease is not established.

basis: Inherited epilepsy defined by generalized seizures and frequent febrile seizures; no substantial extra-neurologic involvement established.

An inherited sialic-acid biosynthesis defect impairs platelet sialylation, production and survival. Myopathy is optional without evidence of >=30%; bleeding sites do not establish other organ disease.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the definition establishes impaired sialic-acid biosynthesis causing defective platelet sialylation, an inborn metabolic defect rather than evidence from the gene name alone.

basis: Inherited macular retinal degeneration, with macular dystrophy in 8/8 and reduced visual acuity in 7/8 patients.
Microcephaly, cortical malformations and skeletal growth abnormalities define syndrome; patent ductus arteriosus occurs in 2/4 (50%).
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus 9/18 and cardiac dysrhythmias 8/18 support involvement ([original cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10932913/)).

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus affects 9/18 (~50%) in the original cohort; esotropia 4/18 is a subset and should not replace the overall strabismus frequency.

basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy in 2/2 establishes common ocular damage. Reflux is a separate diagnosis.
Developmental regression, intellectual disability and epilepsy define disease; extracerebral findings are reported in only 1/4 patients.
Congenital neuromuscular dysfunction, extensive contractures and developmental impairment define disease. Ptosis in only 2 assessed patients does not establish >=30% prevalence.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis is reported in 2/2 assessed patients within a series of at least 10; this limited sampling does not establish common ocular dysfunction.

basis: Macrothrombocytopenia with marrow dysplasia; intellectual disability 2/4, cerebral hemorrhage 3/5, cataract 2/4 and mitral prolapse 4/9. Hypergalactosemia omitted under cap.
Pulmonary vascular disease; alveolar septal thickening, ground-glass opacities (2/3) and respiratory insufficiency (3/4) support additional lung involvement.
Cutis laxa defines disease; joint laxity 4/4 with skeletal deformities, GI diverticula 2/2, high myopia 3/4 and ectropion 3/3. Bladder diverticula 3/4 omitted at cap; small cohorts.

decisions.renal: none under cap: bladder diverticula affect 3/4; retain widespread skeletal disease, GI wall defects/prolapse and ocular dysfunction.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: gastric and colonic diverticula each occur in 2/2 assessed patients, with rectal prolapse also documented; direct visceral connective-tissue disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint hypermobility 4/4, pectus deformity 3/4 and scoliosis 2/4 establish common skeletal involvement; skin laxity defines the disease.

basis: Congenital absence of optic nerve and retinal structures is ocular. CNS malformations accompany bilateral cases, but involvement in at least 30% overall is not established.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by destructive skin inflammation and sterile pyogenic arthritis.
Congenital spinal dysraphism with an epithelial dermal tract extending into the intrathecal space. Meningitis is a risk rather than established infection.
Defined by a congenital fibroneural connection between the spinal cord and a skin lesion.
Dysraphic fatty infiltration of the filum terminale with abnormal spinal conus; associated vertebral and anorectal anomalies lack qualifying frequencies.
Dysraphic fatty infiltration of the filum terminale; associated extraspinal abnormalities are not established as common.
Closed spinal dysraphism with persistent rudimentary spinal cord; typically isolated.
Dysraphic lipomatous malformation attached to the spinal cord; associated vertebral abnormalities have no established frequency.
Dysraphic lipomatous malformation occupies the conus of the spinal cord.
Split spinal cord and open hemicord myeloschisis define neural injury; the spina bifida aperta classification also establishes a vertebral closure defect.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: this open spinal dysraphism is a subtype of spina bifida aperta, with a defining vertebral closure defect as well as spinal cord malformation.

basis: Open spinal neural tube defect with exposed neural placode, spina bifida and Chiari II malformation.
Muscular dystrophy with weakness and joint contractures/laxity; uniform respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle dysfunction rather than intrinsic lung disease.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central origin does not imply structural brain damage.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; secondary causes do not establish additional organ damage.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central origin alone does not imply neurologic damage.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; an underlying neurologic lesion is not specified.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay and reported cerebellar hypoplasia; no demonstrated extracerebral organ damage.
Language impairment and neurodevelopmental dysfunction define the disorder; hearing loss and strabismus each occur in 25%, below threshold.
Developmental encephalopathy with brain atrophy; optic nerve hypoplasia 1/1 and nystagmus 2/2 support ocular involvement in a small series. Dysphagia is neurologic.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and optic atrophy define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in only 1/4 reported patients.
Hereditary epidermal disease causing palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and epidermolysis.
Inherited renal tubular urate-handling disorder causing hypouricemia; stones and exercise-related acute kidney injury are minority complications.
Defective dental enamel mineralization; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Agenesis of olfactory bulbs and tracts causes congenital anosmia; smell belongs to the neurologic axis.
Malignant B-cell lymphoma; no particular extranodal organ is established as commonly damaged across this group.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive central movement dysfunction; incontinence and upgaze palsy do not establish separate urinary or ocular damage.
Brain calcification with common ataxia, seizures and movement disorders; extracerebral abnormalities are individually uncommon.
Scalp aplasia 10/11, enamel hypoplasia 9/9 and developmental delay 7/9 define the syndrome; cataracts directly affect the eye in 5/10.
Inherited neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and seizures; structural scoliosis occurs in 1/2 reported patients, supporting musculoskeletal involvement in a small cohort.
Otosclerosis affects the otic capsule and sound transmission; hearing impairment occurred in 7/7 patients.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment documented in 4/4 patients.
Immune dysregulation; colitis/parotitis, chronic otitis media and arthritis each occur in 1/2 (50%). Hepatomegaly and glycogen accumulation alone do not establish hepatic injury.
Autoinflammation; myositis 3/3, pulmonary arterial hypertension 3/3 and pancytopenia 2/3. Cirrhosis 1/3 omitted by cap; brain calcification alone does not prove functional damage.
Dysraphic lipomatous malformation directly involving the conus spinal cord.
Dysraphic lipomatous malformation attached to the conus; possible neurogenic bowel, bladder and limb effects lack qualifying frequencies.
Stalk-containing spinal meningocele defines neural/meningeal dysraphism; the spina bifida cystica ancestry establishes a vertebral closure defect.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the vertebral arch closure defect of spina bifida cystica is part of this congenital spinal malformation.

basis: Closed spinal dysraphism with a defining midline cutaneous abnormality connected to the spinal cord by a fibroneural stalk.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central origin does not imply neurologic injury.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central origin alone does not establish neurological damage.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm morphology and motility; no endocrine dysfunction established.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism disorder with characteristic CNS lesions and developmental regression; optic atrophy is not established in >=30%.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with profound delay and hypomyelination; occasional low glutamine does not establish a separate metabolic phenotype.
Poikiloderma, cataracts and skeletal dysplasia define the phenotype. GH deficiency occurs in 6/6 and hypothyroidism in 5/6; developmental delay is below 30%.
Intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures define the disorder; cardiac defects individually affect <=2/9, with overlap unknown.
Isolated sperm structural and motility defects causing infertility; reproductive function has no axis and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Lipoma occupying the spinal conus region; neural compression or tethering belongs to the neurologic axis.
Lipoma occupies the conus region of the spinal cord.
Lipoma involving the conus spinal cord region; renal or skeletal damage is not established as common for this subtype.
Closed spinal dysraphism defined by a cutaneous defect, subcutaneous lipoma and fibroneural attachment to the spinal cord.
Congenital spinal dysraphism defined by an abnormal connection between spinal cord and a focal cutaneous defect through a fibroneural stalk.
Terminal spinal cord malformation with herniation through a spinal dysraphic defect; associated anorectal and genitourinary anomalies are not established in >=30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the spinal dysraphic defect permitting cord herniation is part of the malformation; optional sacral agenesis is not the basis for this label.

basis: Spinal cord dysraphism and meningocele through a vertebral arch defect define this subtype; epithelial covering alone does not establish skin damage.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary: this saccular spinal dysraphism includes a vertebral closure defect underlying the meningocele, retaining its parent's defining skeletal involvement.

basis: Spinal dysraphism defined by an abnormally attached, stretched spinal cord within a meningeal sac.
Combined immunodeficiency; neutropenia reported in 1/1 patient supports blood involvement. Recurrent infections are separately diagnosed conditions.
Combined immunodeficiency; hearing impairment 2/2 and intellectual disability 2/4 support involvement. Bronchiectasis 1/1 assessed is a separately coded infection-related complication.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis is separately diagnosed damage from recurrent infections; its 1/1 assessed frequency does not overcome the separate-disease exclusion.

basis: Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins and reduced ovarian hormones; this is hormonal dysfunction rather than isolated infertility.
Hearing loss, neurologic abnormalities and malformed teeth define the syndrome; ptosis in 2/2 supports ocular involvement; weakness lacks proven primary muscle disease.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease established.
Immunodeficiency with inflammatory erythroderma in 6/6 and alopecia in 4/5; diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal damage, and colitis occurs in 1/6.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities cause male infertility; no endocrine or other axis involvement is established.
Hereditary TTR protein deposition with neuropathy; cardiac infiltration commonly exceeds 30% across variants; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 2/4 supplied cases, a limited sample.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis is an inherited disorder of protein folding and metabolism producing systemic amyloid deposition.

basis: CIITA-related combined immunodeficiency; gastrointestinal findings lack frequencies establishing intrinsic enteropathy in ≥30%, and infections are separate diseases.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea, malabsorption and villous injury may accompany separately diagnosed enteric infections; intrinsic enteropathy in ≥30% is not established.

basis: TAP1 immunodeficiency commonly causes chronic destructive airway disease/bronchiectasis; granulomatous skin ulceration occurs in roughly 30-50%. Ear involvement is unquantified.
Developmental and ocular abnormalities define syndrome; congenital cardiac and kidney defects are common (~30-50%); hearing/skeletal findings omitted at four-axis cap.
Hereditary protein-deposition disorder; renal amyloid 3/3, cardiac amyloid 4/4 with heart failure, hepatic amyloid 3/3 with failure; cutaneous findings omitted at cap.
Renal amyloidosis 4/4, hepatic amyloidosis 3/3; LYZ disease is usually non-neuropathic. Isolated sicca and heart failure do not establish common direct organ injury.
Inherited amyloid proteopathy; nerve amyloid 4/4, chronic gastrointestinal dysfunction 3/3 and cardiac amyloidosis 1/1. Hepatic deposits lack documented functional injury.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary B2M amyloidosis is an inherited protein-folding and protein-metabolism disorder.

basis: TAP2-related immunodeficiency; chronic sinusitis and bronchitis occur in 3/3, bronchiectasis in 1/1; recurrent GI infection alone does not establish lasting intestinal damage.
MHC class I immunodeficiency; glomerulonephritis directly damages kidneys and is reported in 1/1 patients, with substantial small-sample uncertainty.
MHC-II immunodeficiency; recurrent pneumonia represents secondary infection, and diarrhea alone does not establish enteropathy. Neurologic damage is not consistently common.
MHC-II immunodeficiency; recurrent infections and infection-mediated bronchiectasis (1/3) are secondary diseases rather than direct organ involvement.
MHC II combined immunodeficiency. Delay/ataxia each 1/3 and brain atrophy 1/1 assessed do not establish direct CNS injury independent of infection; recurrent infections are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: delay/ataxia each 1/3 meet the numerical threshold, but direct neurologic injury from this immune defect, independent of separate infections, is not established.

basis: MHC class II immunodeficiency with reduced immunoglobulins; pneumonia in 1/2 is a separately diagnosed infection, and febrile seizure establishes no brain damage.
Endogenous ethanol production defines an acquired metabolic disorder; fermentation sites do not establish local injury, and intoxication is transient.
Acquired metabolic disorder defined by ethanol fermentation within the bladder; intoxication and systemic organ injury are absent.
Carcinoma arising within the thyroid gland; thymic differentiation does not establish immune disease.
Carcinoma arising in the thyroid gland.
Carcinoma originating in thyroid medullary and follicular cells.
Carcinoma arising in the thyroid, an endocrine gland.
Defining developmental brain disorder; strabismus in 2/6 and craniosynostosis in 1/3 support ocular and skeletal involvement, with small denominators.
Joint/tendon disease and atrophic scars define EDS; venous insufficiency in 2/2 and aneurysm in 1/1 support vascular involvement. Bruising alone adds no blood axis.
PRC2-related overgrowth spectrum combines developmental/intellectual impairment with characteristic skeletal overgrowth and advanced bone maturation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal overgrowth and advanced bone maturation characterize PRC2-related overgrowth syndromes; this is a defining skeletal phenotype.

basis: Isolated inflammatory optic neuropathy affects the optic nerve, assigned to ocular; no additional neurologic disease is established.
Recurrent isolated inflammatory optic neuropathy; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Squamous neoplasia originates in the ocular surface.
Chronic Bartonella infection produces persistent cutaneous vascular proliferations with possible ulceration and scarring.
Defined by intellectual developmental impairment, language impairment and dystonia-parkinsonism.
Neurometabolic dystonia; hearing impairment and structural foot deformities, including pes cavus and talipes equinovarus, are each annotated at 30-79%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: HPO explicitly reports pes cavus and talipes equinovarus at 30-79%, supporting structural foot involvement beyond dystonic movement alone.

basis: Orofacial clefting and cardiac anomalies define the syndrome; the intellectual disability parent supports neurologic involvement; phenotype details are limited.
Inherited folate transport disorder defined by folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia and immunodeficiency.
Deletion-associated Phelan-McDermid syndrome is defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, severe speech delay and hypotonia; other organ damage is variable.
SHANK3-related neurodevelopmental syndrome characterized by developmental disability, severe speech impairment and hypotonia.
Leukodystrophy with episodic memory impairment; disease of cerebral white matter.
Nontraumatic atlantoaxial subluxation involving cervical joints and ligaments; preceding ENT infection does not make the subluxation itself an infection.
Congenital duplication of the stomach is a structural gastrointestinal disorder.
Congenital duplication of the gallbladder; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Congenital duplication of the colon.
Congenital duplication of the gastric pylorus.
Congenital duplication of the small intestine.
Obstetric abnormality of fetal vessels traversing the membranes over the cervical opening; outside the organ axes.
Acute myeloid leukemia of megakaryocytic lineage directly involves blood-forming cells and marrow.
Congenital oral palatal defect; associated maxillary hypoplasia is annotated in 30-79% and represents structural bone involvement.
Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia affects vertebral and epiphyseal skeletal development; the gene association alone does not establish vascular involvement.
Polyvalvular cardiac abnormalities and neurodevelopmental impairment characterize this deletion syndrome; other common organ damage is not established.
audit_reason: Add neurologic to primary: developmental delay/intellectual disability is a defining component of the 6q25.1 microdeletion phenotype alongside polyvalvular heart disease.

basis: Nicolau syndrome causes injection-associated ischemic necrosis of skin and subcutis; deeper muscle injury is not consistently common.
Thrombosis of renal veins directly affects the renal circulation and kidney.
Congenital malformation of the cardiac arterial outflow tract.
Congenital common arterial trunk and interrupted aortic arch are cardiovascular malformations.
Isolated congenital structural malformation of the femur.
Carcinoma arising within the oral cavity; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis regardless of basal-cell histology.
Benign neoplasm arising from vascular tissue; a cutaneous location is not universal across the umbrella.
Vascular neoplasm of intermediate behavior; no additional organ site is established across the group.
Astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Explicitly a bone disorder; no additional organ involvement or systemic metabolic disorder is established.
Retinal racemose hemangioma is a retinal arteriovenous malformation, directly involving the eye and its vessels; isolated disease does not imply CNS involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: this is an arteriovenous malformation of retinal vessels; arteries and veins fall within the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Localized aneurysmal retinal capillary lesion with exudation defines both ocular and vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: retinal capillaries are vessels; their defining aneurysmal pathology qualifies without systemic vascular disease.

basis: Congenital localized retinal pigment epithelial abnormality of the macula.
Angioid streaks are structural breaks in Bruch's membrane of the eye.
Parasitic infection damages the retina and ocular optic nerve.
Idiopathic inflammatory outer-retinal disease; inflammation and a suspected immune trigger do not establish infectious or autoimmune causation.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: immune-mediated pathogenesis is proposed, but inflammatory classification alone does not establish infection or an autoimmune/immune-mediated disease.

basis: Choroidal disorder confined to the eye; no systemic involvement is established by the supplied record.
Benign ossifying tumor originates in the ocular choroid; its bone composition does not establish skeletal-system disease.
Paraneoplastic uveal melanocytic proliferation directly causes ocular dysfunction; the associated cancer is a separate disease.
Segmental infantile hemangioma is a regional cutaneous vascular tumor; isolated disease does not establish associated internal malformations.
Congenital marrow fibrosis and pancytopenia, intellectual disability/neurologic abnormalities, and ophthalmic abnormalities define the syndrome; detailed phenotypes unavailable.
Intellectual disability and progressive hypotonia define the neurologic phenotype; supplied ancestry establishes an inborn lysosomal metabolic disorder.
Mesothelial tumour arising in the pleura, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Malignant mesothelioma arising in the pleura.
Malignant mesothelioma arising in the pleura.
In situ mesothelial neoplasm of the pleura.
Corticospinal and peripheral nerve disease; distal amyotrophy in 9/11 is secondary to denervation, without evidence of direct muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy in 9/11 is neurogenic; denervation-related muscle wasting does not establish direct muscle involvement.

basis: Motor neuronopathy with spasticity defines disease; distal muscle atrophy occurs in 85-100%, fatty muscle replacement in 2/4 and fixed foot deformities in about 46-69%.
SCID with developmental delay 2/2, alopecia/erythroderma 1/1 and sensorineural hearing loss 1/2. Enamel hypoplasia 1/2 omitted at cap; bronchiectasis follows separate infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 1/2 is downstream of recurrent respiratory infections, separately diagnosed diseases promoted by the immunodeficiency.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment in 1/2 patients supports persistent hearing loss above the 30% threshold, although the sample is very small.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 4/4; speech delay follows hearing impairment and does not establish independent neurologic damage.
Hepatic porphyrin metabolism disorder defined by cutaneous manifestations; no evidence establishes additional commonly damaged organs.
Hereditary prostate cancer predisposition; the prostate is a reproductive organ outside the axes, and AR alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Muscular dystrophy with cerebellar atrophy 5/9 and cataracts 6/18 (~33%). Hearing loss 1/1 does not establish prevalence; respiratory impairment reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.otologic: none: hearing loss in one assessed patient does not establish occurrence in at least 30% of the broader disease cohort or a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: RNU4-2 neurodevelopmental disease with structural brain abnormalities; strabismus 32/56 (~57%); constipation and feeding symptoms lack established intrinsic GI damage.
Autoinflammation with arthritis and vasculitis; seizures 3/3 and developmental impairment 2/4 support neurologic involvement; skin/renal findings omitted by cap.
Mitochondrial disease defined by optic atrophy and/or auditory neuropathy; encephalopathy 3/3 and cortical atrophy 6/6 support neurologic involvement. Other findings lack reliable prevalence.

decisions.neurologic: involved: associated encephalopathy occurs in 3/3 and cortical atrophy in 6/6; the three primary slots retain metabolic and defining sensory axes.
decisions.otologic: primary: auditory neuropathy is explicitly part of the disease definition; its defining status supports inclusion despite unquantified frequency.

basis: Inherited dilated cardiomyopathy with myocardial fibrosis in 4/4 patients and ventricular arrhythmias.
Ovarian dysgenesis causes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, low estradiol and impaired puberty; gonadal endocrine failure is defining.
Immunodeficiency with defining persistent HPV-related cutaneous verrucosis; recurrent otitis is a separate infection without established lasting ear damage.
Inherited cystic renal disease; kidney failure in 13/14. Hypertension (16/20) is separately diagnosed; secondary ventricular hypertrophy does not establish direct cardiac disease. Liver cysts 10%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension (16/20) is a separately diagnosed renal consequence; ventricular hypertrophy (2/2) does not establish direct cardiovascular involvement.

basis: Arterial disease, bone fragility and inherited cutis laxa define it; hydronephrosis 4/6. Seizures 2/6 omitted at cap; retinal tortuosity alone does not establish eye damage.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: inherited cutis laxa is an explicit parent and a structural skin manifestation of defective elastogenesis; cutis laxa occurs in 3/6.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and external/inner-ear abnormalities define the syndrome; visual impairment 3/5 (60%) and cleft palate 1/2 (50%) support involvement.
Neurodevelopmental disease with defining brittle/sparse hair; scoliosis and foot/chest deformities in 2/2; strabismus and ptosis in 2/2 support ocular dysfunction.
Spastic paraplegia with peripheral neuropathy; amyotrophy is neurogenic. Urinary urgency alone does not establish urinary tract damage; hearing loss occurs in 20%.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and impaired motility cause reproductive failure; no endocrine or other axis involvement is established.
Immunodeficiency with anemia 3/3, leukopenia 2/3 and hypocellular marrow 1/1; otosclerosis and conductive hearing loss 2/2. Cholangitis is a separately diagnosed infection.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia 3/3, leukopenia 2/3 and marrow hypocellularity 1/1 support direct blood/marrow involvement beyond isolated immune-cell deficiency.
decisions.hepatic: none: cholangitis (3/3) is a separately diagnosed infectious complication; independent chronic hepatic injury is not established.

basis: Brain abnormalities, severe developmental delay and intellectual disability define this MEF2C-related neurodevelopmental syndrome.
Vascular neoplasm arising from the endothelial lining of splenic red-pulp sinuses.
Benign vascular neoplasm; no specific additional organ site established.
Endothelial vascular neoplasm commonly occupies skin/subcutis (>50%) and skeletal muscle/bone (~40% or more); occupation directly damages these tissues.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: dermal/subcutaneous tumor occupation occurs in more than half of patients and represents direct tissue involvement.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal muscle involvement occurs in roughly 40%, with additional bone lesions; direct tumor occupation exceeds the 30% threshold.

basis: Cutaneous hamartoma defined by proliferation of eccrine sweat glands and capillary vessels; its vascular component is intrinsic to the lesion.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: proliferating capillary vessels are a defining component, supported by the benign vascular tumor parent; this is intrinsic vascular pathology.

basis: Reactive proliferation of endothelial cells within cutaneous vessels produces persistent skin lesions; associated systemic diseases are separate conditions.
Benign vascular neoplasm; no specific visceral site is established by this concept.
Benign cutaneous vascular neoplasm composed of small dermal blood vessels; its site and vascular origin support both axes.
Benign cutaneous blood-vessel proliferation, typically arising in sun-damaged skin.
Anemia 2/2 with erythroid dysplasia supports blood damage; small cohort limits certainty. Bronchiectasis 2/2 is a separately diagnosed postinfectious complication.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia in 2/2 reported patients, with erythroid dysplasia in 1/1, supports blood involvement; estimates are based on few patients.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease; weakness 3/3 with skeletal defects, microdontia 1/1 and ptosis 3/3; hypertriglyceridemia 1/1 omitted by cap.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia with common developmental regression and brain abnormalities; ocular findings and systemic lactic acidosis are below 30%.
Defining marrow disease, developmental impairment and ocular malformations; hip dysplasia 3/3, osteopenia 2/3. Tracheomalacia 2/3 and hypertriglyceridemia 3/3 omitted by cap.
Inherited cobalamin metabolic disorder; encephalopathy, profound developmental impairment and seizures in 1/1. Refractive error and esotropia alone provide uncertain evidence of direct ocular damage.
Brain/renal defects define syndrome; marrow failure and Peters anomaly each 1/1 assessed. Pulmonary hypoplasia accompanies anhydramnios; sparse evidence and four-axis cap.

decisions.pulmonary: none: hypoplasia in 1/1 accompanies anhydramnios and may be secondary; documented marrow and anterior-eye defects take priority at the cap.
decisions.ocular: involved: Peters anomaly in 1/1 assessed is a structural anterior-eye defect with potential visual impairment; evidence is sparse.

basis: Hereditary cerebellar disease with ataxia and dysarthria in 5/5; dysphagia and ocular motor findings occur in only 1/5.
Hereditary acute encephalopathy with impaired consciousness and neurological signs; vomiting, abdominal pain and diplopia do not establish other organ damage.
Foveal developmental abnormality with reduced visual acuity, nystagmus and refractive abnormalities.
Mitochondrial myopathy with weakness and elevated CK in 4/4; learning disability in 4/4 supports neurologic involvement. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: pervasive myopathy defines the supplied phenotype, with proximal/axial weakness, elevated CK and Achilles contractures in 4/4 patients.

basis: Inherited cholestatic metabolic disease with cirrhosis in 5/5; intrinsic glomerulosclerosis in 2/2 assessed and developmental delay in 3/3 support renal and neurologic involvement.
Congenital myopathy; ophthalmoplegia and ptosis each 3/3, cleft palate 2/2. Reduced ventilation is attributable to muscle weakness; isolated developmental delay is insufficient.
Congenital ocular malformations define disease. Global developmental delay occurs in 1/1 assessed patient; supplied HPO frequency supports involvement, with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay is reported in 1/1 assessed patient; use the supplied HPO frequency, while acknowledging the very small denominator.

basis: Hereditary short stature with skeletal abnormalities; the supplied subtypes support a primary skeletal disorder.
Congenital multiple joint contractures define the disorder; pulmonary hypoplasia and fetal hydrothorax each reported in 1/1. Skin edema is not lasting damage.
Defining digital/oral malformations and pituitary disease; GH deficiency 6/7. Developmental delay 4/5 with structural brain defects. Ptosis 2/6 omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay affects 4/5, with recurrent structural brain malformations; retained alongside the three defining primary axes.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: pituitary malformations and hormone deficiencies characterize this subtype; GH deficiency occurs in 6/7 and TSH deficiency in 4/7.

basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay with structural brain abnormalities; vertigo does not establish peripheral vestibular disease.
Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia; hepatic dysfunction supported by conjugated hyperbilirubinemia 8/8, elevated ALT 7/8 and AST 6/8; gallstones are separate.
Skeletal myopathy with elevated CK and biopsy abnormalities; learning and behavioral findings occur in only 10–20%, without common additional organ damage.
Defined immunodeficiency; pulmonary tuberculosis in 2/2 patients is a separately diagnosed infection, not intrinsic pulmonary involvement.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy causes cerebral white-matter dysfunction and developmental regression; nystagmus reflects neurological disease.
Bronchiectasis and chronic sinonasal disease define the syndrome; recurrent middle-ear inflammation in 7/7 supports otologic involvement.
Neurodevelopmental impairment affects 4/4. Isolated ocular and skeletal reports do not establish >=30%; atopic dermatitis is a separate condition.

decisions.ocular: none: cataract/high myopia reported in one assessed patient; >=30% prevalence is not established across the syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: none: atopic dermatitis in 2/2 assessed patients does not establish direct skin damage from this neurodevelopmental syndrome.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis and foot deformity are isolated reports; small assessed denominators do not establish >=30% prevalence.

basis: Neurodegeneration and optic atrophy define disease. Amyotrophy in 4/4 reflects neurologic dysfunction; respiratory findings do not establish common direct lung injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy in 4/4 establishes common wasting, but not direct muscle disease; denervation and profound neurologic disability explain it.

basis: Developmental delay in 15/15 with frequent neurologic abnormalities; cardiomyopathy reported in one assessed patient does not establish prevalence across the cohort.
Pancreatic aplasia causes exocrine insufficiency (10/10) and diabetes (15/15). Anemia and low immunoglobulins in single assessed patients do not establish common involvement.
Rod-cone retinal dystrophy with visual field loss in all reported patients; neurologic findings occur in only 1/61.
Hereditary gingival fibromatosis directly affects the gums, documented in 12/12 patients.
Isolated spermatogenic failure causing male infertility; reproductive function lies outside the axes, with no endocrine dysfunction established.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated FSH and reduced ovarian hormone markers in 2/2 patients.
Glycosylation disorder; severe developmental impairment 4/4, hearing loss 3/3, knee contractures 3/4. Corneal erosion 1/1 omitted by cap; cholestasis only 1/4.
Single-patient evidence: alveolar hemorrhage/respiratory failure, endocrine autoimmunity and marrow hypocellularity each 1/1. Arthritis 1/1 omitted at cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: diabetes with anti-insulin antibodies and hypothyroidism occur in 1/1; endocrine autoimmunity is a direct manifestation of this immune dysregulation syndrome.

basis: Myopathy 8/8 with neuropathic/CNS disease; sensorineural hearing loss 3/3. Hepatic failure and cataract each have single-patient evidence without established cohort frequency.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic failure in one assessed patient (1/1) does not establish >=30% prevalence across the eight-patient myopathy cohort.

basis: B-lymphoblastic leukemia is a malignant disorder of blood and marrow lymphoid precursors.
B-lineage acute leukemia involving hematopoietic cells and marrow; no additional organ damage is established as common.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia is a blood and marrow malignancy; the leukemic diagnosis does not itself establish lymphoma or immune disease.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia involving blood and bone marrow; B-cell lineage alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
Precursor B-cell leukemia of blood and bone marrow; no additional organ damage meeting the frequency threshold is established.
B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia is a blood and marrow neoplasm; no common additional organ damage is established.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of myeloid blood cells and bone marrow.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by FUS-ERG fusion; malignant myeloid cells and marrow are the disease site.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of marrow and myeloid blood cells; this fusion does not establish other organ involvement.
Acute myeloid neoplasm of blood and marrow; no defining common extramedullary organ damage supplied.
Defining severe neurodevelopmental and brain abnormalities; optic atrophy 3/3. Isolated pancreatic insufficiency and urethral valve reports do not establish common involvement.
audit_reason: Remove gastrointestinal and renal: isolated pancreatic insufficiency and urethral valve reports do not establish common involvement. Their 1/1 annotations cannot establish 1/3 cohort prevalence. Ocular involvement is supported by optic atrophy in 3/3.

basis: Brain calcification with cognitive and motor impairment; isolated ANA positivity does not establish immune-mediated disease.
Neurodevelopmental disease with bile-acid dysregulation; hepatic cholestasis in 4/11 and urinary reflux in 6/8. Ptosis (4/13) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: conjugated hyperbilirubinemia in 4/11, elevated aminotransferases in 31-46%, and hepatomegaly in 5/12 support direct hepatic dysfunction.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: familial hypercholanemia represents the defining inherited disturbance of bile-acid metabolism and transport.

basis: Intellectual disability, epilepsy and dental anomalies define the named syndrome; facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
Degeneration of the inferior olivary nucleus is a central nervous system lesion.
Chromosomal deletion syndrome with developmental and intellectual impairment. Other congenital anomalies are variable; no additional axis has established >=30% involvement here.
Mesothelioma originates in the tunica vaginalis surrounding the testis, a reproductive structure outside the axes.
Combined immunodeficiency defines the disease; TBX1 alone does not establish additional organ involvement.
Immune-mediated hypersensitivity causes inflammatory injury of the lung parenchyma, even without fibrosis.
Immune response to inhaled antigens directly causes chronic lung inflammation and fibrosis.
Classified as a nervous system disorder with persistent neurologic complaints after exposure; evidence does not establish another commonly damaged organ.
Persistent sexual sensory dysfunction, including genital sensory loss; explicitly classified under nervous system disorders.
Congenital cholesteatoma directly occupies and can damage the middle ear.
DiGeorge-2 deletion phenotype includes developmental impairment, parathyroid and thymic deficiency; congenital heart defects are a major diagnostic feature, supporting cardiovascular involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac malformations are a major feature of the DiGeorge-2 phenotype associated with this deletion; diagnostic significance supports inclusion despite variable frequency.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hypoparathyroidism from parathyroid hypoplasia is a defining component of the DiGeorge-2 deletion phenotype.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: thymic hypoplasia with T-cell immunodeficiency is a defining DiGeorge-2 component; the immunodeficiency mechanism axis applies.

basis: Clonal dendritic-cell disorder; destructive bone lesions account for most unifocal presentations (>30%). Other sites vary.
Clonal Langerhans-cell neoplasm; single-system multifocal disease most commonly involves multiple bones, supporting skeletal infiltration in >30%.
Clonal histiocytic neoplasm; destructive bone lesions ~70%, skin infiltration ~50%, and liver involvement ~30-40% in multisystem cases.

decisions.hepatic: involved: direct hepatic infiltration occurs in approximately 30-40% of multisystem cases.

basis: Malformation of venous channels within the spleen; no established impairment of blood cells or splenic hematologic function.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenic location of malformed vessels alone does not establish disease of the spleen as a blood organ.

basis: T-B- SCID defines severe immunodeficiency with deficient T- and B-lymphocyte lineages; additional organ damage is not established.
audit_reason: Add haematologic: T-B- SCID entails deficiency of T- and B-lymphocyte lineages, meeting the blood-cell disease rule. Additional agranulocytosis or marrow failure is not required.

basis: Distal myopathy with muscle enzyme elevation and possible rhabdomyolysis; renal damage is not established as common.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia establishes motor pathway degeneration; IFIH1 alone does not establish an additional immune or systemic phenotype.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia defines corticospinal tract disease; the gene alone does not establish immune involvement.
Acquired disorder of energy regulation causing obesity; antecedent hypothalamic injury is the cause rather than neurological damage produced by this metabolic condition.

decisions.neurologic: none: the underlying hypothalamic injury is an antecedent lesion; obesity does not itself establish additional brain damage.

basis: Odontogenic epithelial tumor arising within the jaw, involving dental tissues and jaw bone.
Spastic paraplegia occurs in 10/10 and peripheral conduction abnormalities in 9/9. Weakness is neurogenic; no distinct metabolic abnormality is established by the supplied evidence.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: mitochondrial inheritance alone does not establish an inborn metabolic disorder; the supplied evidence establishes central and peripheral neurologic disease.

basis: Cerebral vascular malformations define the disease in 43/43 patients; intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 11/43.
Inherited autoinflammatory disease defined by inflammatory injury of skin and subcutaneous fat.
ID, metaphyseal dysplasia and optic atrophy occur in 2/2; GI atresia/bleeding in 1/2. Cutaneous vascular findings and thyroid dysfunction omitted at cap; tiny series.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cutaneous telangiectasia occurs in 2/2, but retained neurologic, skeletal, ocular and gastrointestinal disease has stronger evidence of consequential damage; cap applied.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: anal atresia and gastrointestinal hemorrhage each occur in 1/2; these establish direct structural or bleeding involvement.
decisions.ocular: primary: eye abnormalities are explicitly defining, with optic atrophy in 2/2 and documented visual impairment.

basis: Isolated spermatogenic failure and sperm structural abnormalities affect reproductive function without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Low testosterone with elevated LH and FSH in 2/2 establishes endocrine testicular dysfunction beyond reproductive failure.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with cortical malformations and seizures; visual impairment in 2/7 is below 30%; isolated additional findings do not establish common organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and hypomyelination define disease; visual impairment is cerebral. Single-case cardiac and skeletal annotations do not establish prevalence of at least 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: individual cardiac defects have single-case annotations in a cohort of at least four; involvement in at least 30% is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hip and foot abnormalities have single-case annotations; neither major diagnostic status nor prevalence of at least 30% is established.

basis: Defining microcephaly and developmental impairment; laryngomalacia in 3/3 selected patients does not establish ≥30% prevalence across the broader 21-patient cohort.

decisions.pulmonary: none: laryngomalacia in 3 assessed patients and singleton lung findings have selected denominators; common pulmonary involvement across the disorder is unestablished.

basis: Cleft lip/palate, heart defects and deafness define syndrome; hearing loss 4/7. Ocular involvement includes high myopia 6/7 and structural lesions. Skeletal anomalies omitted under cap.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with low estradiol and elevated gonadotropins; gonadal hormone dysfunction belongs to this axis.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis in 2/3 and structural foot deformities in 2/4; cataract in 1/2 assessed patients. Small denominators limit certainty.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and agammaglobulinemia define disease; optic atrophy affects 2/4. Hypothyroidism in one assessed patient has uncertain syndrome-wide frequency.
audit_reason: Remove metabolic_endocrine: central hypothyroidism reported in one assessed patient does not establish involvement in at least 30% of the syndrome or a major diagnostic criterion. Optic atrophy in 2/4 supports ocular involvement.

basis: Mitochondrial myopathy with immunodeficiency 2/2 and reduced CD4 cells 3/4; ptosis 3/3 and ophthalmoparesis 1/3. Possible hepatic involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.hepatic: none at cap: transaminases 3/4 may partly reflect myopathy; steatosis is reported in 1/1 assessed. Persistent ocular dysfunction has stronger evidence.
decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ptosis affects 3/3 and ophthalmoparesis 1/3, supporting direct eyelid and ocular motor dysfunction.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: intrinsic immunodeficiency is documented in 2/2 with reduced CD4 cells in 3/4; the immunodeficiency mechanism axis belongs in primary.

basis: Defining myofibrillar muscle degeneration and axonal motor neuropathy. Isolated hearing, bladder and respiratory reports do not establish population frequency >=30%.

Defining cardiac/visceral malformations: cardiac defects 2/2, asplenia and malrotation each 1/1; developmental delay 1/1 supports neurologic involvement. Bronchial isomerism alone adds no lung damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: splenic maldevelopment, including asplenia reported in 1/1, is a defining visceral heterotaxy abnormality; spleen belongs to the haematologic axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal malrotation is part of the defining visceral malformation pattern, reported in 1/1. [Case](https://doi.org/10.1101/mcs.a006248)

basis: Heterotaxy with congenital cardiac malformations; asplenia in 2/3 and hydronephrosis in 2/2 support splenic and renal involvement. Small denominators limit certainty; situs alone is not damage.

decisions.renal: involved: hydronephrosis is structural urinary-tract pathology, reported in 2/2 assessed patients; the supplied frequency supports inclusion with limited certainty.

basis: Corneal pterygia and digital keloid/fibromatous skin lesions define the syndrome; each is documented in 3/3 patients.
Inherited oocyte maturation failure causing infertility; reproductive dysfunction without endocrine disease has no axis.
Inherited adult-onset demyelination of central nervous system white matter.
Hereditary motor neuronopathy; structural muscle wasting in 7/8 and biopsy atrophy in 2/3; left ventricular hypertrophy in 2/6 (~33%). Cardiac estimate has a small denominator.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: actual muscle loss, not weakness alone, is documented by distal amyotrophy in 7/8 and muscle-fiber atrophy in 2/3.

basis: Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle fatty replacement and distal amyotrophy each reported in 2/2 assessed patients, with distal leg weakness in 5/7. Small denominators limit certainty.
IRF4-related antibody deficiency; isolated inflammatory findings in single assessed patients do not establish >=30% prevalence. Recurrent infections are separate diseases.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: large-intestinal inflammation is reported in one assessed patient; this does not establish >=30% prevalence across the disorder.
decisions.dermatologic: none: dermatitis is documented in one assessed patient; premature graying in 3/3 does not establish functionally damaging skin disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: synovial hyperplasia is documented in one assessed patient, without evidence of >=30% prevalence; arthralgia alone is insufficient.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia involving vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses, with common joint limitation and reduced bone density.
Intellectual disability and seizures define the disorder; conductive hearing impairment reported in 2/2 assessed patients, although the denominator is small.
Sensorineural deafness and ovarian endocrine failure affect 3/3; intellectual disability affects 2/2 evaluated patients, supporting neurological involvement.
Developmental disability, progressive spasticity, neuropathy and brain abnormalities; isolated cardiac and metabolic reports do not establish ≥30% prevalence.
Inherited kidney disease with tubular atrophy and fibrosis; hypertension, gout and hypercholesterolemia are separate diagnoses reported in single patients.
Inherited neurodegeneration with parkinsonism, cerebral atrophy and cognitive decline; dysphagia and gaze palsy reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Glycosylation disorder with immune dysfunction; neurodevelopmental deficits 1/1 and anemia 2/2; ocular, joint, vascular and hepatic findings omitted at cap.
Holoprosencephaly is a congenital forebrain malformation; additional endocrine involvement is not established for this subtype.
Severe CNS developmental disorder; optic atrophy in 2/3 and fixed limb joint contractures in 4/4 support ocular and musculoskeletal involvement.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures; atrial septal defect in 2/3 assessed patients and joint contractures in 2/5 support additional axes, with small denominators.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and structural brain abnormalities define disease; isolated non-neurologic reports do not establish a typical frequency >=30%.
Congenital intestinal dysfunction with diarrhea and parenteral nutrition dependence in 2/2 patients.
Congenital intestinal dysfunction causing diarrhea and dependence on parenteral nutrition; treatment-related complications are excluded.
Core skeletal, nail and renal dysplasia (CKD 2/2); retinal dystrophy with progressive visual loss 1/1 assessed. Dental defects 2/2 omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: inherited renal tubular disease is part of the defining ancestry; tubulointerstitial nephritis and stage 3 CKD occur in 2/2 assessed patients.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental delay in 14/14. Isolated eye and limb anomalies lack evidence of involvement in at least 30% of the cohort.
Rag nutrient-sensing/metabolic signalling disorder; end-organ disease varies across subtypes. [Review](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-50034-4)
Defined by interconnected cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic disease.
Inherited retinal degeneration with pigment epithelial atrophy, night blindness and visual field loss.
Inherited retinal degeneration; the broad hereditary neurological ancestor does not establish extraocular neurologic damage.
Leukodystrophy, cerebellar abnormalities and developmental impairment define disease; sensorineural hearing loss in 1/2. Oculomotor signs do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Defining hepatic and cardiac disease; palatal defects in 4/4 and hearing loss in 2/2. Renal and spinal abnormalities in small samples omitted by cap.
Isolated spermatogenic dysfunction and male infertility; reproductive function lies outside the axes.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; learning disability in 9/9 supports neurologic involvement. Ocular and renal findings have small assessed denominators; prevalence >=30% is unestablished.
audit_reason: Remove ocular and renal: organ-specific counts of 1/1 or 2/2 do not establish involvement in >=30% of a population with at least nine patients; neither organ is established as a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Monogenic diabetes; retinopathy, albuminuria and polyneuropathy represent separately diagnosed diabetic complications.
