Neurodevelopmental disease with ataxia and brain abnormalities; optic atrophy in 3/3 assessed patients and sensorineural hearing loss in 2/2.
Brain anomalies, seizures and developmental impairment define disease; hearing impairment in 2/2 and retinopathy in 1/1 assessed support involvement, with small denominators.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinopathy demonstrates direct retinal pathology; supplied frequency is 1/1 assessed, supporting inclusion despite sparse evidence.

basis: Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and impaired motility cause male infertility; no endocrine or other axis involvement is established.
Developmental delay in 3/3; strabismus and pes planus each in 2/2 assessed, with additional skeletal anomalies. Cardiac findings lack robust frequency evidence.
Isolated congenital duplication of the duodenum, a segment of the small intestine.
Congenital duplication of the jejunum and ileum directly affects the small intestine.
Localized mesothelial tumour arising in the peritoneal lining of the abdomen.
Isolated congenital duplication of the anal canal is an anorectal malformation.
Inherited cerebral white matter degeneration with brain atrophy, seizures and cognitive decline; isolated other findings do not establish common organ damage.
Ectodermal hair, skin and dental defects; oligodontia in 5/14. Limb involvement includes short thumbs in 4/11 and osseous finger syndactyly in 2/3.
Structural skeletal myopathy with fatty muscle replacement in 2/2; ophthalmoparesis in 1/1 and ptosis in 1/2 support ocular functional involvement.
Spastic cerebellar/pyramidal disease; myopathic EMG in 3/6 supports muscle involvement. Bladder dysfunction 9/24 is neurogenic; cirrhosis 2/12 is below 30%.

decisions.renal: none: bladder dysfunction in 9/24 is attributable to neural dysfunction; direct urinary-organ injury is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: explicitly myopathic EMG abnormalities in 3/6 support intrinsic muscle dysfunction beyond neurologic weakness.

basis: Oocyte and early embryonic maturation failure causes infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other qualifying organ involvement is established.
Oocyte/embryo maturation failure and female infertility affect reproductive function without an endocrine or other covered organ disorder.
Syndromic hypothyroidism 3/3, arthritis 2/2 and recurrent aphthous ulceration 2/2 support involvement. Respiratory infections and their separate sequelae are excluded; small cohort.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 1/1 is a separately diagnosed sequel of recurrent respiratory infection, rather than established direct pulmonary autoimmunity.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent aphthous stomatitis in 2/2 represents intrinsic immune-mediated oral mucosal ulceration; mouth belongs to this axis.

basis: Infantile multisystem autoimmunity with diabetes 2/2; intellectual disability and seizures 1/2 support neurologic involvement. Airway findings do not establish direct autoimmune injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: asthma and bronchiolitis each reported in 1/2, but neither establishes direct pulmonary damage from the autoimmune syndrome.

basis: Familial dilated cardiomyopathy with severe ventricular dysfunction; sparse hepatic and coagulation findings do not establish direct extra-cardiac disease.
Pulmonary arterial disease and associated cardiac dysfunction affect the cardiovascular axis; isolated airway diagnoses do not establish intrinsic lung involvement.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; macrocytic anemia in 5/5 assessed supports common blood involvement; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; retinal dystrophy only 1 case.
Familial dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular enlargement in 5/5 patients; additional cardiac findings remain within the same axis.
Cataracts, skin/hair disease and oral inflammation define syndrome; myopathy in 1/1 assessed; developmental delay in 1/2 omitted by cap.
Marrow disorder; thumb defects 3/3, renal agenesis 3/4 and hydrocephalus 3/4. GI atresias (~67%) and cardiac/endocrine anomalies omitted by cap; small samples.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive limb malformations are common (absent thumbs 3/3), but skeletal abnormalities are not required to define Fanconi anemia.

basis: Defining short ribs and pulmonary hypoplasia (2/2); pyloric stenosis causes gastrointestinal obstruction and is reported in 1/1 assessed patient, with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: pyloric stenosis is documented in 1/1 assessed patient; supplied HPO frequency supports inclusion, although the sample is very small.

basis: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe ventricular dysfunction; hydrops and effusions reflect cardiac failure. Developmental delay in 1/2 lacks established direct neurologic injury.
Marrow/red-cell disorder; skeletal anomalies ~50-60%, hearing loss 1/2, palatal clefts ~29-33%. Small denominators limit certainty; singleton autism does not establish a common phenotype.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: submucous cleft palate in 1/3 and cleft palate in 2/7 support an approximately 30% rate of permanent oral structural defects.
decisions.neurologic: none: autism and ADHD are singleton observations without a representative frequency; common intrinsic neurodevelopmental damage is not established.

basis: Neurodevelopmental and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; high myopia/amblyopia and pituitary hypothyroidism each occur in 1/1 assessed. Ear positioning alone does not impair function.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: pituitary hypothyroidism represents endocrine loss of function in 1/1 assessed; the very small denominator limits confidence.
decisions.otologic: none: low-set ears are positional dysmorphism; recurrent otitis is a separate infection, without established intrinsic hearing or vestibular damage.

basis: Septal defects 3/5 and 2/5; sensorineural hearing loss 2/4; congenital hypothyroidism 1/3. Ocular and airway anomalies omitted under cap; all estimates use small subsets.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: congenital hypothyroidism in 1/3 meets the supplied frequency threshold, although the denominator is small.

basis: Hereditary skeletal muscle disease with myalgia, elevated creatine kinase and possible rhabdomyolysis; renal injury is not established as common.
Chronic granulomatous inflammation directly affects anogenital skin/subcutis; isolated disease does not establish intestinal or urinary injury.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: Crohn-like immune-mediated granulomatous skin inflammation can occur without intestinal disease. [Case report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31451228/)

basis: Cerebral vascular malformation with chronic parenchymal ischemia and progressive neurological deficits explicitly defining the disease.
Defective triglyceride metabolism causes myocardial lipid deposition, heart failure and diffuse arterial disease.
Combined immunodeficiency and defective neutrophil chemotaxis define immune and blood-cell dysfunction; bronchiectasis defines pulmonary disease. Cancer predisposition is risk only.
audit_reason: Add haematologic to primary: defective neutrophil chemotaxis defines both listed subtypes and constitutes blood-cell dysfunction. Retain pulmonary for defining bronchiectasis and infectious_immune for combined immunodeficiency.

basis: Congenital fistula between hepatic arterial and portal venous vessels; both its vascular nature and intrahepatic location define the lesion.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the lesion is explicitly located within the liver; primary location does not require additional evidence of secondary hepatic injury.

basis: Defined as hereditary spastic paraplegia, a neurodegenerative motor pathway disorder; no additional organ involvement is established.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the urinary tract, which belongs to the renal axis.
Large abdominal-wall defect with congenital bowel herniation; pulmonary hypoplasia affects roughly 30-50% of giant cases. Liver herniation alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia directly impairs lung development in roughly 30-50% of giant omphaloceles, independent of treatment.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: congenital extra-abdominal herniation of bowel is part of the defining abdominal-wall/bowel malformation; primary localization does not require bowel necrosis.

basis: Abdominal-wall closure defect defined by bowel herniation into an umbilical sac; the wall defect and displaced intestine are primary locations.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: bowel herniation into the umbilical sac defines omphalocele; additional intrinsic intestinal injury is not required for a primary location label.

basis: Cystic transformation of pancreatic acinar tissue involves the exocrine pancreas; endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Sickling hemoglobinopathy affecting erythrocytes and spleen; nephropathy, osteonecrosis and acute chest syndrome are separately diagnosed complications.
Compound sickling and beta-plus-thalassemia hemoglobinopathy; additional organ damage is variable and not established as common for this subtype.
Combined immunodeficiency is defined by impaired immune function; no common additional organ damage is supplied.
Combined immunodeficiency due to ICOSL deficiency; no evidence supplied for common direct damage to another organ.
The supplied parent establishes syndromic intellectual disability; evidence is insufficient to assign additional organs to this deletion syndrome.
Vitreoretinal B-cell lymphoma; direct CNS dissemination by the same lymphoma occurs in roughly 50-80% over the disease course, rather than representing an unrelated later malignancy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS dissemination of the same lymphoma occurs in most patients over its course. [AAO](https://eyewiki.aao.org/Primary_Vitreoretinal_Lymphoma).

basis: Generalized congenital subcutaneous fat loss with metabolic dysfunction; hepatic steatosis affects most generalized lipodystrophy patients (>50%); subtype-specific data limited.
Emergomyces fungal infection; disseminated series show skin lesions in about 95% and pulmonary involvement in over 70%; frequencies vary by species and host.
Benign lymphoepithelial cyst of the pancreas; neither endocrine dysfunction nor an immune-mediated disease is established.
Combined immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia and skeletal anomalies defines the syndrome.
IKAROS-related combined immunodeficiency with low immunoglobulins; no specific additional organ damage is established.
Inherited glycosylation disorder whose recognized subtypes are defined by intellectual disability or developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental dysfunction defines both recognized subtypes and therefore the usual phenotype across this umbrella

basis: Congenital accessory peritoneal membrane encapsulating bowel; a developmental gastrointestinal structural disorder.
Structural lesion of the carotid arterial intima; associated ischemic stroke is a separately diagnosed complication.
Annular cutaneous eruption; no established systemic organ disease.
Congestive liver injury and fibrosis associated with Fontan circulation; antecedent congenital heart disease is a separate condition.
Combined immunodeficiency with reduced immunoglobulins; no additional commonly damaged organ is established.
Inborn immunodeficiency with immune dysregulation; no additional common organ damage is established by the supplied record.
Necrotizing bacterial infection of skin and subcutaneous tissue.
Venous malformation with defining fibro-adipose infiltration of skeletal muscle, causing atrophy, contractures and joint deformity.
Bacterial infection causing necrosis of skeletal muscle.
Infantile CLN1 is a lysosomal storage neurodegenerative disease; progressive retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients.
Lysosomal storage disease causing progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss occur in most patients over the course.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss are common (>30%) in juvenile CLN1.
Lysosomal storage disorder causing adult-onset neurodegeneration; retinal disease is not a consistent feature of adult neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neuronal degeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients over the course.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients over the typical course.
Neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disease; retinal degeneration with visual loss commonly develops over the course (>30%), although timing varies in juvenile CLN2.

decisions.ocular: involved: progressive retinal degeneration with visual loss is common over the CLN2 course (>30%); juvenile onset can delay ocular manifestations.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease defined by progressive neurodegeneration and early retinal degeneration; visual loss occurs in nearly all classic juvenile CLN3 cases.

decisions.ocular: primary: early progressive retinal degeneration and visual loss are defining clinical features of classic juvenile CLN3 disease.

basis: CLN3 lysosomal storage disease defined by early retinal degeneration and visual loss, followed by unusually slow neurologic deterioration.

decisions.ocular: primary: early retinal degeneration and progressive visual loss are defining features of protracted juvenile CLN3 disease.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease causing progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients (>50%) over the course.
Lysosomal storage disorder causing progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients (>50%).
Adult-onset neuronal lysosomal storage disorder with neurodegeneration; retinal damage is not established as common in this adult subtype.
Parentage establishes syndromic intellectual disability; no additional organ involvement is documented.
Compound sickling hemoglobinopathy. Extrahematologic damage varies substantially by partner variant; no additional organ meets the common-damage threshold across this group.
Inherited hemoglobin disorder affecting red blood cells; no common direct damage to other organs established.
Hereditary chronic inflammation and destruction of the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is a separately diagnosed disease.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is a separately diagnosed disease.
Inherited distal skeletal myopathy predominantly affecting the upper limbs; TARDBP alone does not establish neurologic involvement.
Blepharophimosis affects eyelids and intellectual disability establishes neurodevelopmental involvement; both define the named syndrome.
Autosomal dominant distal skeletal myopathy causing asymmetric thumb and handgrip weakness.
Distal skeletal myopathy with calf weakness and gastrocnemius atrophy.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients over the childhood course.
Neuronal lysosomal storage causes progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration with visual loss is common in juvenile CLN6, exceeding ~30%.
Lysosomal storage neurodegeneration; progressive retinal degeneration with visual loss occurs commonly (>30%) in late-infantile CLN8 disease.
Congenital CLN10 is a lysosomal degradation disorder causing severe congenital neurodegeneration; common functionally significant retinal disease is not established in this neonatal form.
Lysosomal metabolic disease with progressive neurodegeneration; damaging retinal involvement at a frequency of at least 30% is not established for this specific form.

decisions.ocular: none: the supplied evidence does not establish retinal degeneration or visual loss in at least 30% of late-infantile CLN10 patients.

basis: Defining immunodeficiency and ectodermal dysplasia; motor delay 4/4 and speech delay 5/5; conical teeth 1/1 support dental involvement, with limited sampling.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: conical teeth are structural dental abnormalities, reported in 1/1 assessed patients; frequency evidence is limited.

basis: Inherited vitreoretinal disease with retinal neovascularization, folds and detachment; retinal vessels belong to the ocular axis.
Spermatogenic failure affects reproduction. Low testosterone in 1/1 assessed among four reported patients does not establish common persistent endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: low testosterone in one assessed patient does not establish persistent gonadal endocrine failure in at least 30% of this reproductive disorder.

basis: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 20/21; muscle pathology in only 2/2 assessed patients does not establish skeletal involvement in >=30% across the subtype.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: direct myopathy is documented, but 1-2 muscle-assessed cases do not establish >=30% prevalence across the broader cardiomyopathy subtype.

basis: Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness, visual-field constriction and severely impaired electroretinographic responses.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with near-universal developmental impairment and frequent seizures; isolated 1/1 findings do not establish common additional organ injury.
Developmental delay 5/5 and intellectual disability 4/4 establish the neurodevelopmental phenotype. Single-patient ocular observations do not establish common involvement.

decisions.ocular: none: cataract and retinopathy each have only a 1/1 assessed observation; prevalence of at least 30% across this syndrome is not established.

basis: Eye and vertebral defects define syndrome; hearing loss and hypothyroidism each 2/3. Renal agenesis 2/7 is below 30%; isolated mitral prolapse 1/1 omitted under cap.
Cerebral arteriopathy with infarcts and white-matter disease; retinopathy reported in 2/2 evaluated patients; isolated scoliosis has insufficient prevalence evidence.
Developmental hip dysplasia and congenital hip dislocation affect the hip joint.
Cerebral small-vessel disease directly affects vessels and brain, with lacunar strokes, hemorrhage and cognitive impairment.
Defined by neurodevelopmental disease, achalasia and alacrima (3/3); myopathy 2/2 supports muscle involvement; hyperkeratosis 2/2 omitted by cap.
Hereditary Wilms tumor subtype; nephroblastoma is a primary renal neoplasm, reported in 5/5 patients.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual/developmental and speech impairment; other organ anomalies vary. [NIH](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/conditions/C6065891/)
Defined by cerebral small-vessel disease with brain injury and osteoporosis; lacunar strokes and white-matter lesions occur in 7/7.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; unilateral renal agenesis reported in 21/21. Infection is a trigger; an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism is not established.
Skeletal and ectodermal dysplasia; hepatic injury in 5/5 and hydrocephalus in 3/3. Cardiac abnormalities and probable renal concentrating defects omitted under cap.
Local hydroxyapatite deposition causes periarticular inflammation; no systemic metabolic or immune disorder is established.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with abnormal muscle histology. Transaminase and CK-MB elevations alone do not establish hepatic or cardiac damage.
Severe developmental impairment, absent speech and epilepsy establish neurologic disease. Isolated skeletal and skin findings have very small assessed denominators.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with vertebral, pelvic and epiphyseal abnormalities; microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction.
Hereditary congenital ptosis affects the eyelids.
Cerebellar neurodevelopmental disease; ankle contractures in 5/5 assessed and multiple contractures in 3/3 support musculoskeletal involvement. Visual impairment is chiefly cerebral.

decisions.ocular: none: cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; abnormal ERG in one tested patient does not establish retinal damage in >=30% of the 18-patient cohort.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; Pierre-Robin sequence with mandibular malformation is reported in 9/9. Pigmentation and minor facial features do not establish additional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: Pierre-Robin sequence establishes mandibular malformation, but cleft palate or independent gastrointestinal tissue damage is not documented.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: Pierre-Robin sequence in 9/9 includes mandibular hypoplasia, a consequential congenital skeletal malformation.

basis: Molybdenum cofactor deficiency causes sulfite-related destructive encephalopathy and developmental impairment; dysmorphic features do not establish other organ damage.
Named immune, neurodevelopmental and colitic defects; dermatitis 2/2. Ocular lesions (1/2), reduced bone density (1/1) and cholangitis (1/2) omitted under cap.
Neurodevelopmental impairment in most; strabismus in 4/6 (~67%); isolated skeletal findings lack reliable cohort frequency; reflux/infections are separate diagnoses.
Named neurocardiorenal malformations define three axes; CNS disease is documented. Microdontia (2/2) alone does not establish oral functional injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: microdontia (2/2) is a minor structural finding without established functional damage; feeding difficulties alone do not demonstrate gastrointestinal injury.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with severe developmental delay in 9/9 and absent speech in 7/7. Cardiac, renal, ocular and pulmonary malformations have isolated reports without reliable prevalence.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac malformations have single-case annotations; 1/1 assessed does not establish prevalence of at least 30% across the reported disease population.
decisions.renal: none: renal dysplasia and hydronephrosis have single-case annotations; population prevalence of at least 30% is not established.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental disorder; camptodactyly 2/2, strabismus/ptosis 1/1 and hearing impairment 1/1 support additional involvement, with very limited assessed samples.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus and ptosis are reported in 1/1 assessed patients; supplied frequencies support involvement, although ascertainment is very limited.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is direct auditory dysfunction, reported in 1/1 assessed patients; the frequency estimate is highly uncertain.

basis: Cerebellar hypoplasia in 9/9 defines neurologic disease; scoliosis 6/10, strabismus 6/9 and severe periodontitis 2/2 support additional involvement.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm morphology and motility; reproductive function has no axis.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define the disorder. Constipation alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage; isolated cardiac reports do not establish common involvement.
Brain malformations define disease; contractures occur in 4/6 and clubfoot in 3/3. Eye and cardiac defects each have only 1/1 assessed, insufficient to establish >=30% across the series.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: VSD is reported in only 1/1 assessed; one affected patient among at least six reported cases does not establish a frequency of >=30%.
decisions.ocular: none: ocular abnormalities have only 1/1 assessed annotations; these isolated observations do not establish >=30% involvement across at least six reported cases.

basis: Cerebral microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy define CARASAL; hearing loss in 1/1 annotated patient does not establish involvement in >=30% across the disease.

decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing loss is documented in one annotated patient; its frequency across patients is insufficiently established at >=30%.

basis: Ichthyosis, deafness and atopy define syndrome; chronic rhinitis/asthma occur in 2/2; hyperthyroidism (1/2) is a separate thyroid disease.
Genetic cardiac conduction and atrial rhythm disease, with variable dilated cardiomyopathy.
Retinal degeneration and pigment epithelial atrophy define the disease; hypertension in one patient does not establish direct systemic vascular involvement.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal platelets; intracranial hemorrhage affects a minority, below 30%.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal or neonatal platelets; intracranial hemorrhage is a minority complication.
Maternal alloantibodies cause fetal or neonatal platelet destruction. Intracranial hemorrhage is a minority complication.
Developmental delay 8/8; ankyloglossia 4/7 with feeding difficulties 6/7 supports oral dysfunction; ptosis 2/5 (40%) affects eyelid function. Weakness does not establish myopathy.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis in 2/5 (40%) is impaired eyelid elevation, within the ocular axis; visual loss is not required to establish eyelid dysfunction.

basis: Developmental delay with named cardiac and renal malformations; sensorineural hearing loss in 5/5. Ptosis in 4/4 omitted under the four-axis cap; other findings sparsely assessed.
Developmental impairment and sleep apnea define disease: central apnea 7/8, obstructive apnea 3/8. Skeletal involvement includes clubfeet in 2/5; GI symptoms lack intrinsic organ injury.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: sleep apnea defines the syndrome; obstructive airway dysfunction occurs in 3/8, alongside central apnea in 7/8.

basis: Anemia 2/2; hepatitis/hepatic failure 1/1; cardiomyopathy 1/1 assessed. Very small series; respiratory infections alone do not establish lasting airway damage.
Shared defining phenotype is syndromic neurodevelopmental disability; gastrointestinal, ocular and other manifestations vary across Pitt-Hopkins and Pitt-Hopkins-like subtypes.
Left ventricular pump dysfunction defines disease; congestion and reduced perfusion alone do not establish direct damage to other organs.
Defined by renal arterial sclerosis together with glomerulosclerosis, cortical fibrosis and tubular loss.
Psychiatric body dysmorphic disorder; perceived inadequate muscularity does not indicate skeletal muscle disease.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease. Skeletal abnormalities in 2/2 selected patients among a larger cohort do not establish a frequency of at least 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis, camptodactyly and pes cavus each occur in only two reported patients; selected 2/2 denominators do not establish prevalence across the roughly 15-patient cohort.

basis: Cerebral small-vessel disease with porencephaly and severe neurodevelopmental impairment; visual impairment is cortical rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with motor dysfunction and brain abnormalities; asthma and reflux are separate diseases, and nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
An apolipoprotein deficiency classified as a disorder of lipoprotein metabolism; no direct organ injury is established.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease; brachydactyly 2/4 and scoliosis 2/2 assessed. Isolated renal/cardiac reports lack reliable cohort prevalence.
White matter disease with cognitive and neurologic dysfunction defines condition. Hypertension is 1/5; hypertensive retinopathy is secondary rather than direct leukodystrophy damage.
Respiratory-chain disorder; neurologic regression 1/2, severe progressive visual loss 1/1, muscle fiber atrophy 1/2. Cardiac and gastric findings omitted by cap.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with rigid spine and scoliosis; reduced vital capacity in 5/5 reflects respiratory muscle weakness, without direct lung disease.
Bacterial-associated inflammatory destruction of the periodontal tissues supporting the teeth.
Inherited lymphoma susceptibility specifies future risk, without established lymphoma, blood-cell disease or immune dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: none: susceptibility to a blood malignancy does not establish existing blood-cell or marrow disease.

basis: Dental root and pulp-chamber dysplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Infiltrative fibrofatty neoplasm of extremity connective tissue, typically involving subcutaneous fat and fibrous soft tissue.
Defined by microcephaly, abnormal cortical development and cerebellar hypoplasia; eye and skeletal findings in isolated assessed patients do not establish >=30%.
Neutropenia with lymphocyte deficiency; stomatitis 3/3, gingivitis 2/3 and intellectual disability 2/3; dermatitis 2/2 omitted by cap; infections are separate diagnoses.
Defining distal, ocular and pharyngeal myopathy: ptosis 24/24, ophthalmoplegia 14/20 and dysphagia 17/22. Pharynx maps to pulmonary; swallowing-muscle disease does not establish GI injury.
audit_reason: Add pulmonary to primary: pharyngeal myopathy is a defining component, and the axis explicitly includes the pharynx. Dysphagia affects 17/22 patients and reflects loss of pharyngeal muscle function.

basis: Osteopetrosis defines the skeletal disease; permanent-incisor agenesis occurs in 3/4; spinal stenosis alone does not establish neural damage.
Brain calcification and leukoencephalopathy define the disease; cataract, tinnitus and thrombocytopenia are each reported in only 1/5 patients.
Scoliosis/contractures 2/2, strabismus 2/2 and sensorineural hearing loss 1/1 support involvement. Respiratory failure alone does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure in 2/2 may arise from neuromuscular dysfunction; direct lung injury is unestablished and aspiration pneumonia is a separate complication.
decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus in 2/2 represents persistent ocular alignment dysfunction; retained alongside skeletal and hearing impairment.

basis: Developmental impairment, seizures and movement abnormalities define CNS disease; sparse reflux and hepatomegaly reports do not establish common direct organ damage.
Intellectual disability, seizures and spastic diplegia define neurologic disease; lumbar hyperlordosis and genu valgum occur in the reported patient (1/1).
Neurodevelopmental white matter disorder; persistent strabismus and scoliosis each reported in 4/4 assessed patients. Isolated mitral prolapse lacks support for common involvement.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, developmental impairment and brain abnormalities; isolated constipation does not establish direct bowel damage.
Cerebral arterial stenosis defines moyamoya; ischemic brain injury occurred in 2/2. Glaucoma in 1/2 is a separately diagnosed eye disease; hemianopia reflects brain injury.

decisions.neurologic: involved: arterial stenosis is the defining lesion; downstream ischemic stroke directly damages brain tissue and occurred in 2/2 patients.
decisions.ocular: none: glaucoma in 1/2 is a separate eye disease without established direct injury from moyamoya; hemianopia localizes to cerebral injury.

basis: Inherited peripheral neuropathy; distal muscle wasting occurs in 16/17 and foot deformities in ~50%; an isolated mitral regurgitation report does not establish common heart disease.
Oocyte and embryo maturation failure causes female infertility; purely reproductive disease outside the axes.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and cardiac defects define syndrome; ocular dysfunction 2/2, renal cyst 1/1. Skeletal and hearing findings omitted by cap; samples small.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; hearing impairment occurs in 1/3 (~33%). Muscle atrophy in 3/5 can be secondary to neurologic disability; intrinsic muscle or lung disease is unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy in 3/5 accompanies severe spastic neurologic disability; direct myopathy rather than secondary denervation or disuse is not established.

basis: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy defines metabolic, brain and muscle disease; optic disc pallor in 1/2 supports ocular involvement.
Defining developmental disability, seizures and motor dysfunction; joint contractures occur in 2/6 patients (~33%), meeting the threshold with limited evidence.
Motor-sensory axonal neuropathy; distal amyotrophy 3/3 supports common muscle loss, with fatty replacement and structural foot deformities also reported.
Respiratory-chain defect; neuropathy/developmental impairment, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and muscle involvement occur in the single reported patient (1/1).
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle wasting in 7-8/8 and fixed foot deformities in 4-6/6 support musculoskeletal involvement. Diabetes is a separate disease.
Hair growth and shaft disorder with sparse, brittle hair and patchy alopecia.
Skeletal abnormalities (5/5-6/6) and dental crowding (4/4); CNS defects/delay in assessed 1/1-2/2 and pulmonary artery stenosis 2/2. Sparse endocrine, renal and airway findings omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: pulmonary artery stenosis in 2/2 assessed patients, with other major cardiac and arterial abnormalities reported; denominators are small.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay and structural CNS abnormalities recur in assessed subsets of 1/1-2/2; skeletal and dental findings establish the core phenotype.

basis: Craniosynostosis/scoliosis define syndrome; ID 3/3, hearing loss 2/2 and severe visual loss 1/1. Cap omits dental/anal anomalies; single-case anemia does not establish an intrinsic blood disorder.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 3/3 and motor delay in 4/4 establish common neurologic dysfunction; neither is established as a defining diagnostic criterion here.

basis: Photosensitive skin disease with scarring; developmental delay, microcephaly and intellectual disability reported in 1/1. Photophobia alone does not establish ocular damage.
Inherited epilepsy with seizures, abnormal EEG and developmental delay; all supported manifestations fall within the neurologic axis.
Optic nerve hypoplasia 11/12, scoliosis 5/5 and contractures 2/2, hearing impairment 4/5. Precocious puberty 5/5 omitted by cap; respiratory findings lack proven lung injury.
Microcephaly and developmental impairment define disease; thyroid hormone deficiency occurs in 2/5 (40%), supporting endocrine dysfunction. Celiac disease is a separate diagnosis.
Microtia 8/8 and patellar aplasia 3/5 define skeletal/ear disease; immune dysfunction with infections 5/7; neutropenia 5/6. Intellectual disability 2/2 omitted at cap.
audit_reason: Add otologic to primary for defining microtia (8/8). Move haematologic to involved for associated neutropenia (5/6). Omit neurologic at the four-axis cap, prioritizing defining ear defects and common immune/blood dysfunction.

basis: Noninflammatory arterial wall disease; cervical and intracranial location does not itself establish brain injury.
Structural disease of the renal arteries; renal parenchymal damage is not established in ≥30% and is not required for diagnosis.
Fibromuscular dysplasia directly affects the coronary arterial walls.
Noninflammatory dysplasia of visceral arterial walls; downstream organ ischemia is not established as common.
Fibromuscular dysplasia affects arterial walls in the extremities; it is a noninflammatory vascular disorder.
Compound HbS/Hb Lepore hemoglobinopathy causes sickling and hemolytic blood disease; no additional organ damage is established as common for this subtype.
HbS/HbO-Arab hemoglobinopathy causes red-cell sickling and hemolysis; specific organ complications vary and are often separately diagnosed.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; endocrine failure is a separately diagnosed complication.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is a separate diagnosis.
Dilated cardiomyopathy with myocardial fibrosis and conduction disease; antibody positivity and symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Vertebral/rib dysplasia and T-cell deficiency; cardiac defects and cleft palate each 1/1. Respiratory findings lack demonstrated pulmonary damage; tethered cord omitted by cap. Tiny samples.
audit_reason: Remove pulmonary: respiratory distress and failure with thoracic deformity do not establish direct lung or airway damage. Add gastrointestinal: cleft palate (1/1) is a structural oral defect and now fits within the cap.

basis: Cerebellar/caudate degeneration defines disease. Hearing findings in two assessed patients and ocular/skeletal singletons do not establish >=30% prevalence across the 11-patient series.

decisions.ocular: none: cataract and progressive visual loss are singleton observations; their prevalence across the 11-patient series is not established at >=30%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contracture and scoliosis are singleton observations, without established >=30% prevalence or evidence that they define this disorder.
decisions.otologic: none: hearing loss is reported in only two assessed patients; the 2/2 annotation does not establish >=30% prevalence across the 11-patient series.

basis: Congenital myopathy with contractures; cardiomyopathy in 8/8. Speech and motor delay may reflect muscle weakness; independent CNS damage is insufficiently established.
Congenital contractures with peripheral neuropathy; vocal cord paresis/respiratory failure and corneal scarring each reported in 1/1 assessed. Very small cohort.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; ocular dysfunction includes strabismus in 3/3 assessed. Hearing, renal, cardiac and skeletal anomalies are too sparsely reported to establish 30%.
Skeletal malformations and microcephaly (7/7) characterize this subtype. Hearing impairment in 1/1 supports otologic involvement, although population frequency is uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: primary: microcephaly in 7/7 and reported intellectual disability characterize the subtype's neurodevelopmental phenotype.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is reported in 1/1; this supports involvement with limited confidence, rather than establishing a defining ear phenotype.

basis: Hereditary cerebellar degeneration with ataxia and cerebellar atrophy; nystagmus and pursuit abnormalities reflect central motor dysfunction, not eye damage.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with speech delay, intellectual disability and motor delay; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Retinal degeneration with night blindness and visual loss; CLN3 alone does not establish neurologic disease in this isolated retinal subtype.
Developmental delay in 5/5 and seizures in 3/4 establish neurologic disease. Joint hypermobility in 2/2 lacks demonstrated tissue injury; other organ abnormalities are isolated reports.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypermobility in 2/2 does not establish damaging joint dysfunction; isolated skeletal findings do not establish common direct injury.

basis: Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; no additional organ disease is established.
Destructive arterial infection and keratitis each account for roughly one-third or more of major human case series; cutaneous infection is less common.
Defined as human infection with Aleutian mink disease parvovirus; no specific human organ injury is established by the supplied record.
High-grade glioma arising in the childhood central nervous system.
Autoimmune cutaneous disease; ILD affects ~60–90%. Objective inflammatory muscle involvement affects roughly 30–50%, despite frequent amyopathic presentations.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal involvement: anti-MDA5 disease includes objective inflammatory muscle injury in roughly 30–50%, including hypomyopathic cases. Frequent amyopathic presentations do not exclude involvement across this broader subtype.

basis: Autoimmune inflammatory myopathy with characteristic dermatitis; interstitial lung disease is uncommon in the anti-Mi2 subtype.
Autoimmune skin and muscle disease; dysphagia (~40-60%) reflects swallowing-muscle myopathy. ILD is generally below 30% in this subtype.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: common dysphagia reflects swallowing-muscle weakness; common direct gastrointestinal tissue damage is not established.

basis: Autoimmune inflammatory muscle and skin disease; interstitial lung disease is uncommon in the anti-TIF1 subtype. Associated cancer is a separate disease.
Autoimmune skin and muscle disease; ILD occurs in roughly 30-50% in several anti-SAE cohorts, with substantial geographic variation. Dysphagia can reflect muscle involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: direct interstitial lung disease reaches roughly 30-50% in several anti-SAE cohorts, although estimates vary considerably by population.

basis: Immune-mediated dermatomyositis with skin disease and objective subclinical myositis; interstitial lung disease affects roughly 30-50% of clinically amyopathic cases.
Autoimmune cutaneous dermatomyositis without clinical muscle weakness; interstitial lung disease affects roughly 30-50%, varying by population and antibody status.
Definition specifies a hereditary neurologic disorder; retinal disease is subtype-specific, and the gene alone does not establish a metabolic axis.
Congenital heart disease, particularly PDA, defines the spectrum; hand anomalies and other extracardiac defects vary across Char syndrome and isolated PDA subtypes.
Severe hypothyroidism with defining cerebral dysfunction, altered consciousness or coma; systemic slowing alone does not establish other organ damage.
Defined cardiac dysfunction and refractory heart failure caused by hypothyroidism.
Defined renal pain and hematuria syndrome; pain alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Isolated reduced skeletal growth defines the phenotype; an endocrine or metabolic cause is not established.
Autoimmune melanocyte loss causes persistent cutaneous depigmentation.
Autoimmune destruction of cutaneous melanocytes causes persistent widespread depigmentation.
Inflammation of the abdominal peritoneum. Infection or an autoimmune mechanism is not required by the umbrella definition.
Fibrocollagenous peritoneal encasement directly obstructs the small intestine.
Inherited cerebral white-matter disease; subtype-specific extracerebral findings do not establish involvement across the umbrella.
Congenital structural heart disease caused by PLD1 variants.
Definition includes neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and visual/ocular abnormalities; altered intracellular lipid signaling alone adds no metabolic axis.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction; chronic middle-ear disease with hearing impairment affects >30% in primary ciliary dyskinesia. CFAP46-specific frequency is uncertain.
Benign neoplasm arising from skeletal muscle tissue.
Cerebral vasculopathy, brain injury and ocular dysgenesis define the spectrum; myopathy and renal pathology are subtype-dependent without established umbrella-wide frequency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: myopathy is recognized, especially in particular COL4A1 phenotypes, but involvement in at least 30% across COL4A1/A2 disorders is not established.

basis: Primary skeletal myopathy with muscle fiber atrophy and weakness; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Inherited mineralization disorder defined by osteomalacia, fractures, arthropathy and dental abnormalities; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Alkaline-phosphatase deficiency impairs skeletal mineralization; premature primary-tooth loss is common, exceeding 30%; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Enzyme deficiency causes defining rickets; dental mineralization defects and premature tooth loss commonly affect >30% over the course. Renal and neurologic frequencies are uncertain.
audit_reason: Add gastrointestinal involvement: defective dental mineralization and premature tooth loss commonly occur over the disease course, directly damaging dentition. Infantile onset does not exclude later dental manifestations.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency; no specific additional organ damage established.
Defined combined immunodeficiency; no additional organ damage is documented.
Defined combined immunodeficiency; no common direct damage to another organ is established.
Combined immunodeficiency; supplied evidence establishes no additional organ damage.
Combined immunodeficiency is defining; no additional direct organ damage is established by the supplied record.
Coloboma, ear defects and cardiac malformations are defining; intellectual disability annotated in 47/47. Choanal atresia (~49%) and endocrine defects omitted by cap.
Insulin-deficient diabetes from underdeveloped endocrine pancreatic tissue; no evidence of common direct exocrine pancreatic damage.
Monogenic disorders of cardiac rhythm and conduction.
Inherited cardiac electrical dysfunction causing arrhythmias and conduction disorders; normal cardiac morphology does not negate functional disease.
Premenstrual mood disorder without direct organ damage; psychiatric and menstrual conditions have no axis.
Macular retinal degeneration and local capillary abnormalities impair central vision; no systemic vascular or neurologic involvement established.
Defined by retinal capillary incompetence and dilatation with progressive central visual loss; the affected vessels fall within the cardiovascular axis.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: retinal capillary dysfunction and telangiectasia define this disease; the cardiovascular axis includes capillaries without requiring systemic involvement.

basis: Immune destruction of transplanted tissue; the affected organ varies with the graft and cannot be assigned across this umbrella.
Pre-existing antidonor antibodies cause complement-mediated vascular injury and thrombosis; the affected graft organ is unspecified.
Immune-mediated graft injury; the transplanted organ is unspecified, so no individual organ axis applies across the concept.
Immune-mediated destruction of transplanted tissue; the graft organ is unspecified.
Inherited cardiomyopathy affecting cardiac muscle, with variable ventricular morphology and arrhythmias.
Hereditary neuromyopathy encompasses skeletal muscle disease and neurologic dysfunction, including spastic paraplegia.
Oocyte and early embryonic maturation failure causes infertility; purely reproductive disease without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Inherited medulloblastoma susceptibility alone establishes no organ injury; a future CNS tumor is a separate diagnosis, not an existing neurologic manifestation.

decisions.neurologic: none: the definition establishes inherited tumor risk, not an existing medulloblastoma, brain malformation or neurologic dysfunction.

basis: Tick-borne infectious illness; the transient erythema migrans-like rash does not establish lasting skin damage.
Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and polycystic kidney disease are both defining features.
Developmental proximal femoral epiphyseal disease causes femoral-head necrosis, cystic changes or sclerosis; other collagenopathy manifestations are not established for this group.
Bacterial infection umbrella encompassing different sites; pulmonary or neurologic damage is not established across most patients.
Recurrent viral meningitis, frequently associated with HSV-2, directly affects the meninges.
Basaloid follicular hamartomas, pigmentary skin lesions and acral skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; other organ involvement is not quantified.
Severe hypertension without acute target-organ damage by definition.
Incomplete mitral valve closure causes regurgitation; disease is defined by cardiac valve dysfunction.
Sustained atrial rhythm disorder; stroke and heart failure are separately diagnosed complications.
Narrowing directly affects a precerebral artery; cerebral infarction or neurologic injury is not inherent in stenosis.
Intermittent atrial fibrillation is a cardiac rhythm disorder; embolic complications are separate diseases.
Acquired porphyrin metabolism disorder, predominantly sporadic PCT; chronic blistering skin injury occurs in most symptomatic cases; liver dysfunction is not universal.
Multiple peripheral nerve sheath tumors define the disease; skin ancestry does not establish common independent skin involvement.
Spectrum defined by ectodermal abnormalities, limb malformations and orofacial clefting/dental defects; no additional organ consistently qualifies across subtypes.
Spectrum defined by segmental soft-tissue/skeletal overgrowth and vascular malformations; cerebral malformations affect a subset, not most across the umbrella.
Defined by developmental impairment, sometimes epilepsy; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage, and visual impairment is less frequent.
PIK3R2-related disease predominantly causes megalencephaly, cortical malformations and neurodevelopmental impairment; polydactyly varies across the spectrum.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage; eye and heart defects are less frequent.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and cardiac anomalies are explicit defining features; hypotonia alone does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Congenital unilateral destruction or absence of cerebral cortex; presumed prenatal vascular disruption does not establish systemic vascular disease.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and dilated cardiomyopathy explicitly define the disorder.
TRIP11-related skeletal dysplasia spectrum; dental and respiratory manifestations vary by subtype and are not established across most patients.
IRF6 spectrum predominantly affects oral development through lip pits and cleft lip/palate; popliteal skeletal abnormalities do not characterize most patients across the group.
Dissection directly damages the vertebral artery wall; cerebral infarction is a separately diagnosed complication.

decisions.neurologic: none: associated posterior-circulation infarction is a separate disease, regardless of its frequency in symptomatic series.

basis: Definition identifies neurologic dysfunction, intestinal malformations/inflammation and combined immunodeficiency as the defining spectrum; their combinations vary across subtypes.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the disorder; strabismus in 2/2 assessed patients supports ocular alignment dysfunction, with uncertainty from the small sample.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus documents ocular alignment dysfunction in 2/2 assessed patients; supplied frequency supports inclusion, although the sample is small.

basis: Sepsis directly causes acute renal dysfunction in roughly 35-50%, as part of its organ-failure syndrome. Transient hypotension does not establish cardiac damage; intrinsic myocardial injury varies.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypotension alone does not establish organ damage; intrinsic myocardial dysfunction is not securely >=30% across the full sepsis population.
decisions.renal: involved: direct sepsis-associated acute renal dysfunction affects roughly 35-50% and constitutes the disease's acute organ-failure syndrome.

basis: Narrowing directly affects a cerebral artery; brain infarction or functional injury is not inherent to stenosis.
An abnormal intestinal communication defines the disease; the destination and any additional organ damage vary.
Defined by complex CNS neurodevelopmental impairment; other congenital abnormalities are unspecified.
Enterococcal bacterial infection; this umbrella concept specifies no consistently affected organ.
Bacterial infection; no particular organ site or common organ injury is specified.
CHRNE-related postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder.
Proteoglycan-linker glycosylation defects underlie defining skeletal, joint and cutaneous connective-tissue abnormalities. Cardiac, ocular and developmental damage varies across subtypes.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic cutaneous connective-tissue abnormalities form part of the group's defining phenotype, although severity varies.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: linkeropathies are inborn defects of proteoglycan glycosylation, establishing a metabolic mechanism beyond the presence of an associated gene.

basis: Mitochondrial complex I dysfunction defines the metabolic spectrum; cardiac, neurologic, ocular and skin abnormalities vary by subtype without established umbrella frequencies.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy is a recognized presentation, but involvement in at least 30% across the heterogeneous umbrella is not established.

basis: Antibody-mediated demyelination defines the disease; optic neuritis is explicitly a core diagnostic presentation and directly damages the optic nerve, assigned to ocular.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic neuritis is explicitly a core demyelinating event in the diagnostic definition; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.

basis: Metastatic tumour directly occupies the brain; the original tumour site is unspecified.
Defined by joint instability and secondary musculoskeletal dysfunction; systemic symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Inherited retinal disease; retinal involvement belongs to the ocular axis.
Arthritis and colitis/parotitis each 1/2; hepatic deposits lack proven dysfunction; otitis mechanism uncertain. [Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38609546/)

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: biopsy-proven inflammatory colitis and parotitis in 1/2 reported patients (~50%) are direct manifestations of autoinflammation; small cohort limits certainty.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: severe inflammatory arthritis in 1/2 reported patients (~50%), with synovial inflammation and impaired ambulation, directly damages joint function.

basis: DYNC1H1 spectrum primarily affects central and peripheral neurons. Independent muscle disease or retinal damage is not established in most patients across the spectrum.
Defining limb shortening, syndactyly and nail malformations; brain and urinary abnormalities are variable and not established in most across subtypes.
Congenital skeletal muscle dystrophy; cerebellar atrophy and white-matter abnormalities reported in 30-79%, despite preserved intellect and often mild imaging findings.
Inherited retinal dystrophy directly damages the retina; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular nervous-system disease.
Inherited retinal dysfunction; the neurological ancestor does not establish disease outside the eye.
Inherited retinal disease; the neurologic ancestor does not establish extraocular nervous system involvement.
Autosomal recessive retinal dystrophy directly affects the retina; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular nervous-system disease.
Inherited retinal degeneration defines the disease.
Predominant classic OFD1 presentations have defining oral, digital and CNS malformations; cystic renal disease occurs in roughly 50%. Isolated retinal/airway presentations are minority subtypes.

decisions.renal: involved: cystic renal disease affects roughly 50% over time in the predominant classic OFD1 phenotype; renal involvement varies across rarer subtypes.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral malformations are defining features of the predominant classic orofaciodigital presentation; mouth and teeth belong to this axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: digital skeletal malformations define the predominant classic orofaciodigital presentation; isolated retinal and airway forms are minority subtypes.

basis: Explicitly isolated inherited retinal disease; the gene does not establish systemic storage disease.
FZD4-related disease of retinal vascular development with vitreoretinal degeneration; no systemic vascular involvement is established.
Bardet-Biedl spectrum: retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly define disease; renal abnormalities ~30-50%. Cognitive impairment (~60%) omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: none at cap: cognitive impairment occurs in roughly 60% of the Bardet-Biedl spectrum; retain defining retinal, endocrine, skeletal and renal disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: postaxial polydactyly is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion, occurring in roughly 70-80%.

basis: BBS1 spectrum includes retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; renal dysplasia is a major BBS criterion. Learning impairment (~30-60%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: renal dysplasia/dysfunction is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion, despite lower renal penetrance in BBS1.
decisions.neurologic: none: common learning impairment (~30-60%) qualifies but is omitted at the four-axis cap, retaining the defining features and potentially severe renal disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: postaxial polydactyly is a defining skeletal malformation and major diagnostic criterion of the predominant Bardet-Biedl phenotype.

basis: BBS4-associated Bardet-Biedl phenotype includes retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly. Renal disease is a major BBS criterion; neurodevelopmental involvement omitted under the cap.

decisions.renal: involved: structural or functional renal disease is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion; BBS4-specific frequency is uncertain.
decisions.neurologic: none: cognitive or developmental impairment can qualify in Bardet-Biedl syndrome, but is omitted under the cap; subtype-specific frequency is uncertain.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: postaxial polydactyly is a cardinal diagnostic feature of the Bardet-Biedl phenotype represented by this concept's child.

basis: Bardet-Biedl phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and renal disease are major criteria; cognitive impairment affects ~60%+. Polydactyly omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal developmental/parenchymal disease is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion and an important feature of BBS12 disease.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental/cognitive impairment affects roughly 60% or more; retained under the cap because of substantial functional impairment.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: polydactyly qualifies as a major feature but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of visual, metabolic, renal and neurodevelopmental disease.

basis: BBS phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; cognitive impairment ~60% across BBS. Renal disease (~50%) omitted at cap; subtype-specific frequencies remain uncertain.

decisions.renal: none at cap: renal disease affects ~50% across BBS; cognitive impairment is more frequent. LZTFL1-specific frequencies are uncertain.
decisions.neurologic: involved: cognitive impairment is a major BBS feature, affecting ~60% overall; extrapolation to this sparsely described subtype warrants medium confidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is a major defining feature of the Bardet-Biedl phenotype represented by this concept.

basis: BBS features include retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; renal disease ~50%. Cognitive impairment (~60%) omitted at the cap, prioritizing severe renal damage; BBS5 frequencies uncertain.
audit_reason: Replace neurologic involvement with renal involvement: common renal malformation/dysfunction (~50% across BBS) warrants priority for severe organ damage at the four-axis cap.

basis: Syndromic BBS predominates: retinal dystrophy, obesity and cognitive impairment (~50-60%) are major criteria; intrinsic renal disease ~30-50%. Polydactyly omitted by cap; isolated RP is rare.

decisions.renal: involved: intrinsic renal abnormalities or dysfunction affect approximately 30-50% of the predominant syndromic phenotype.
decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental/cognitive impairment (~50-60%) is a major BBS diagnostic feature; rare isolated retinopathy does not determine this umbrella's labels.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: obesity (~70-90%) is a major diagnostic feature of the predominant Bardet-Biedl phenotype; isolated BBS2 retinopathy is a minority presentation.

basis: Retinal degeneration is shared by isolated retinitis pigmentosa and Bardet-Biedl subtypes; renal and metabolic disease are not shared across the umbrella.
Polydactyly is common across McKusick-Kaufman and Bardet-Biedl phenotypes; retinal, renal and metabolic damage is not established across the umbrella.
Inherited retinal degeneration encompassing retinitis pigmentosa and Leber congenital amaurosis.
Inherited retinal disease caused by recessive PROM1 variants.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by dominant PROM1 variants.
Neurologic and retinal damage each inferred in >=30% across major forms; pooled frequency uncertain. [CDG network](https://fcdgc.rarediseasesnetwork.org/diseases-studied/dhdds-cdg).

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal degeneration defines the recessive form; 30-40 reported families versus 59 dominant neurologic cases suggests >=30% across this umbrella, with ascertainment uncertainty.

basis: Inherited PRPH2-related degeneration is localized to the retina.
PROM1-related inherited retinal degeneration; retinal disease belongs to the ocular axis despite the hereditary neurological ancestor.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; retinal disease belongs to the ocular axis despite the neurological ancestor.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; the retinal disease does not establish additional neurologic involvement.
Retinal degeneration is shared by Bardet-Biedl syndrome 3 and retinitis pigmentosa 55; other organ involvement is subtype-dependent.
Inherited retinal degeneration directly damages the retina.
CNS and renal malformations characterize major subtypes; polydactyly estimated >30% across the spectrum. Retinal and hepatic injury vary by subtype; aggregate frequencies uncertain.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: polydactyly is common (~50-80%) in major Meckel/Bardet-Biedl phenotypes; >30% across this spectrum is an estimate, with lower penetrance in Joubert.

basis: Inherited retinal degeneration; both listed subtypes primarily damage the retina.
Bacterial infection of beard and moustache hair follicles, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
Autoantibodies damage the postsynaptic neuromuscular junction; muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction disease defined by extraocular and eyelid dysfunction, with ptosis and ophthalmoplegia.

decisions.ocular: primary: eyelid and ocular motor dysfunction define this subtype; loss of function qualifies without intrinsic globe injury.

basis: Autoantibody-mediated neuromuscular junction dysfunction; weakness does not establish primary muscle or lung disease.
Autoimmune neuromuscular junction dysfunction; ocular and respiratory weakness do not establish eye or lung damage.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction disease; generalized weakness reflects impaired transmission rather than primary muscle damage.
Inherited oxysterol metabolic disorder; progressive spastic paraplegia is the predominant presentation (>50% of reported cases). Hepatic disease characterizes a much rarer subtype.

decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive corticospinal degeneration in spastic paraplegia is the predominant CYP7B1 phenotype (>50%), rather than a rare subtype complication.

basis: Neurodevelopmental encephalopathy; visual dysfunction and abnormal ocular movements occur in 30-79%. Central hypoventilation does not establish direct lung damage.
Spectrum defined by skin fragility and muscular dystrophy; pyloric atresia belongs to a specific subtype.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and brachydactyly type E define the haploinsufficiency syndrome; obesity alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Intrinsic cytopenias, marrow failure and cerebellar ataxia characterize the defined spectrum. Myeloid neoplasm susceptibility adds no further organ.

decisions.neurologic: primary: ataxia is an explicitly defining clinical component of the supplied spectrum, rather than an organ inferred from the gene or future cancer risk.

basis: Ulceration is confined to vulva/vagina; association with preceding infection does not establish direct infection or a defined autoimmune disease.
Retinal degeneration with early deafness is the established syndromic phenotype. Respiratory ciliary disease is variant-dependent; its frequency across the umbrella is unestablished.

decisions.pulmonary: none: primary ciliary dyskinesia is an alternative variant-associated presentation; common airway involvement across this umbrella is not established.
decisions.otologic: primary: early-onset deafness is a defining component of the established retinal-deafness phenotype represented by the named child concept.

basis: Mitochondrial disease with defining optic atrophy; neuropathy, ataxia or developmental impairment affect most patients; auditory neuropathy/hearing loss occurs in roughly 40-50%.

decisions.otologic: involved: auditory neuropathy or hearing loss affects roughly 40-50% across reported FDXR disease cohorts, exceeding the threshold.

basis: Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment and corpus callosum abnormalities.
Mitochondrial aconitase disorder causing optic atrophy; neurologic disease varies by genotype and is not established in >=30% across this umbrella.
Defined by kidney and/or liver cystic disease, with variable penetrance and severity.
GRIN1-related developmental brain dysfunction with frequent seizures and movement abnormalities; hypotonia and feeding difficulty do not establish other organ damage.
Congenital obstruction or absence of the laryngeal or tracheal airway defines CHAOS.
Exogenous glucocorticoid excess defines the endocrine syndrome. Additional steroid-induced skin, muscle and bone effects are excluded by the explicit treatment-effect rule.

decisions.dermatologic: none: skin atrophy and striae can be common, but in this exogenous syndrome they result from corticosteroid treatment and fail the treatment-effect exclusion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: steroid myopathy and bone loss can be common, but are effects of corticosteroid treatment and fail the treatment-effect exclusion.

basis: Orofacial clefting affects oral structures and the facial skeleton, including the palate and alveolus; no syndromic organ involvement is established.
audit_reason: Add musculoskeletal to primary: orofacial clefting includes structural palatal and alveolar skeletal defects, retaining the parent's defining skeletal axis alongside the oral gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Cardiovascular disease caused by atherosclerotic arterial damage; no specific downstream organ injury is required.
Immunodeficiency and autoimmunity are explicit defining mechanisms; skeletal and metabolic abnormalities vary between SHORT and immunodeficiency subtypes.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal abnormalities characterize SHORT presentations, but substantial skeletal damage in most patients across this umbrella is not established.

basis: NMDA receptor-related neurodevelopmental disorders defined by developmental impairment, epilepsy and other central nervous system dysfunction.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy, language dysfunction and movement disorders.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy directly affects brain function.
Defined by epilepsy, speech dyspraxia and neurodevelopmental impairment.
GRIN2A-related focal epilepsy and associated neurodevelopmental dysfunction define a neurologic disease.
Digenic retinal degeneration causes progressive vision loss.
Congenital retinal dystrophy causing severe visual impairment.
FGFR1-related Pfeiffer syndrome is defined by craniosynostosis and characteristic thumb/toe skeletal abnormalities.
Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define Pfeiffer syndrome; hearing loss affects ~50%; structural upper airway obstruction affects an estimated 40-60%. Eye/brain injury varies.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: congenital upper airway narrowing from midface hypoplasia commonly causes persistent obstruction, estimated 40-60% across Pfeiffer syndrome.

basis: Nasal turbinate loss and persistent nasal airway dysfunction define disease; cognitive and psychiatric symptoms do not establish another damaged organ.
Genetic skeletal growth and cartilage disorder; short stature does not establish endocrine disease.
Cardiac and aortic abnormalities anchor this spectrum; skin, limb and brain abnormalities vary by phenotype and are not established in most patients across the umbrella.
Psychotic and mood disorder without defining structural or functional damage to a covered organ axis.
Purely psychiatric schizoaffective disorder with depressive episodes.
Subcutaneous lipomatous overgrowth with partial lipodystrophy; peripheral neuropathy is optional and its frequency is not established.
Skeletal ciliopathy defined by polydactyly, oral tongue nodules and developmental delay.
Defined by central movement abnormalities with optional neurodevelopmental impairment.
Inherited distal tubular acidification failure causes renal acid-base dysfunction; hearing and skeletal complications vary across subtypes.
Acquired distal tubular acidification defect defines both renal dysfunction and metabolic acidosis; underlying diseases are not additional organ involvement.
Inherited neutrophil deficiency is both a blood-cell disorder and an innate immunodeficiency; secondary infections do not establish additional organ involvement.
Defined by autoimmune injury to hepatocytes and red blood cells, causing giant cell hepatitis and hemolytic anemia.
Hereditary immune checkpoint dysregulation confers SPTCL/HLH susceptibility. Blood-cell injury and subcutaneous infiltration belong to the separately manifest diseases, not predisposition alone.

decisions.haematologic: none: susceptibility to lymphoma or HLH does not establish blood-cell, marrow or coagulation disease in the predisposition state.

basis: Diffuse glioma arising in midline central nervous system structures.
Defining skeletal dysplasia; hypoparathyroidism with hypocalcemia is common (>30%) across its principal Kenny-Caffey and osteocraniostenosis subtypes.
Umbrella of FLNB-related skeletal dysplasias; bone and joint malformations are shared, while additional organ findings vary across subtypes.
C1q-associated autoimmune lupus causes cutaneous disease in ~90% and nephritis in ~30-40%; arthritis is reported in roughly 20-25%, below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: arthritis in C1q-associated lupus is approximately 20-25%; the higher joint involvement of ordinary SLE should not be transferred to this subtype.

basis: Inherited SLE; skin and inflammatory joint involvement generally >50%, renal involvement ~30-50% in SLE. C1S-specific frequencies are sparse.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; hypotonia and cerebral visual impairment reflect neurologic dysfunction, without established separate muscle or eye disease.
The supplied definition and parent classify this as an autoimmune nervous system disorder with acute neurologic and psychiatric manifestations.

Developmental disorder with defining joint and eye abnormalities; tracheomalacia 1/1 and sleep apnea 3/3 support airway involvement. Hearing loss (1/1 assessed per type) omitted at cap; small samples.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: structural airway disease (tracheomalacia 1/1 assessed), with sleep apnea in 3/3; respiratory involvement retained at cap.
decisions.otologic: none: hearing loss is reported in 1/1 assessed per type, but omitted at cap in favor of respiratory disease supported by apnea in 3/3.

basis: Glioblastoma arising in the brain stem.
Propionate metabolism defect; developmental impairment and neurologic injury affect over 30%, often roughly half or more. Cardiomyopathy generally affects under 30%.
Propionate metabolism defect; developmental and cognitive neurologic impairment affects over 50%. Cardiomyopathy generally affects fewer than 30%.
Erythrocytosis supplies the defining blood axis; pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility does not establish endocrine organ disease.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the definition specifies predisposition to endocrine tumors, not an existing endocrine tumor or gland dysfunction.

basis: Nephritis 4/4, cytopenias 2/2 and pericardial effusion 3/3 assessed patients; skin and joint findings omitted by cap. Small denominators limit frequency estimates.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia and leukopenia each reported in 2/2 assessed patients; hematologic injury is a manifestation of systemic autoimmunity.
decisions.renal: involved: nephritis 4/4 and urinary abnormalities 5/5 establish common direct renal injury in this systemic autoimmune disorder.

basis: Skin plaques reflect chronic T-cell-mediated inflammation; immune involvement does not require lymphoma. Rare lymphoma progression adds no organ.
audit_reason: Add infectious_immune to primary: small plaque parapsoriasis is an immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis. Absence of lymphoma does not exclude the immune mechanism axis.

basis: Chronic scaly cutaneous patches and plaques; progression to mycosis fungoides is a future risk, not established lymphoma.
Hereditary amyloid-processing disease, classified under inborn errors of metabolism, with defining deposition in brain parenchyma and cerebral vessel walls.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the record identifies a hereditary amyloid-processing disorder within inborn errors of metabolism; the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Bardet-Biedl/Joubert subtype spectrum supports neurologic involvement; supplied evidence does not establish common retinal, renal or skeletal damage across the umbrella.
Defined by intellectual disability, developmental brain abnormalities and sometimes seizures; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular tissue damage.
CASK-related intellectual disability with developmental and brain abnormalities; nystagmus alone does not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Defective lymphocyte homeostasis causes autoimmune lymphoproliferation, commonly with splenic enlargement and cytopenias; lymphoma is a separate subsequent disease.
Congenital cardiac malformations define the disease; visceral malposition alone is not damage, and substantial extracardiac dysfunction is not established as common.
Cerebral vascular obstruction produces ischemic brain dysfunction or infarction.
Cerebrovascular hemorrhage into brain tissue or surrounding spaces directly causes neurologic injury.
Excess thyroid hormone production arises within the thyroid; autoimmune causation does not apply across all subtypes.
Excess thyroid hormone driven by hypothalamic or pituitary endocrine pathology; no necessary damage to another axis.
Thyroid adenoma autonomously produces excess thyroid hormone; additional organ damage is not intrinsic to the definition.
The definition explicitly locates the causal pathology in the hypothalamus, with excessive pituitary stimulation and thyroid hormone production.

decisions.neurologic: primary: hypothalamic brain pathology is an explicit defining location; additional neurological symptoms are not required for a primary label.

basis: Menstrual abnormalities are reproductive; the umbrella does not establish an endocrine disorder or blood-cell disease.
Menstrual pain is a reproductive condition outside the organ axes.
Primary menstrual pain without underlying pelvic pathology; reproductive condition outside the axes.
Menstrual pain associated with reproductive pelvic pathology; no organ within the 13 axes is intrinsically affected.
Menstrual disorder; an endocrine cause or endocrine gland damage is not inherent in this symptom-defined concept.
Menstrual absence is a reproductive disorder; this umbrella does not establish an endocrine cause.
Functional hypothalamic suppression causes hypogonadotropic endocrine dysfunction; bone loss varies with duration and underlying energy deficiency.
Gonadal dysgenesis and premature ovarian failure define endocrine gonadal dysfunction; isolated infertility subtypes do not negate this defining axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: gonadal dysgenesis and ovarian failure involve gonads as hormone organs; adrenal disease is not inferred from NR5A1.

basis: Spectrum explicitly defined by myofibrillar myopathy, cataract and cardiomyopathy; individual presentations may involve only one component.
Subretinal drusenoid deposits define a localized retinal condition.
Umbrella disorder of gametogenesis causing infertility; ovarian endocrine failure belongs to the female subtype rather than the whole group.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and brain malformations define disease; renal TMA is variable, and common renal, cardiac or pulmonary damage is not established.
Anterior pituitary inflammation defines endocrine disease; xanthomatous histology alone does not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: pathogenesis is uncertain; inflammatory infiltrates alone do not establish autoimmune, immune-mediated or infectious disease.

basis: Xanthogranulomatous inflammation and fibrosis affect the pituitary; histology alone does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: macrophages, giant cells and fibrosis establish inflammation, but do not by themselves establish infection or an autoimmune or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Necrotizing inflammatory hypophysitis damages the pituitary; lymphoplasmacytic inflammation supports an immune-mediated process.
Congenital spinal cord splitting; associated structural scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
Congenital splitting of the spinal cord within a single dural sac.
Both spinal-cord splitting and an incomplete osseous spur are defining congenital malformations of this subtype.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the incomplete bony spur is a defining skeletal malformation intrinsic to this subtype; a separate skeletal diagnosis is unnecessary.

basis: Defined immune signalling deficiency with growth hormone insensitivity; lymphoma susceptibility is a risk, not existing organ damage.
Defined skeletal myopathy with weakness and contractures; possible cardiomyopathy lacks frequency evidence, and respiratory weakness does not establish lung damage.
Primary ovarian insufficiency/dysgenesis establishes an endocrine phenotype; male gametogenic failure is reproductive; tumour predispositions are risks.
C1q-associated lupus causes cutaneous disease in ~90% and nephritis in ~30-40%; inflammatory arthritis occurs in ~20%, below the threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: inflammatory arthritis occurs in approximately 20% of C1q-associated lupus, below the 30% threshold; typical SLE arthritis frequencies should not be substituted.

basis: C1q-associated lupus commonly damages skin (~90%) and kidneys (~30-40%); joint and CNS involvement are less consistently above 30%.
Acute nicotine poisoning causes autonomic nervous system dysfunction; nausea and vomiting do not establish gastrointestinal tissue injury.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, leukodystrophy and optic atrophy are defining features. Hypopigmentation occurs only in some patients and does not establish common skin damage.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is expressly included among the disorder's defining features and constitutes direct optic nerve damage on the ocular axis.

basis: Predisposition is specifically to tumors of the endocrine pituitary gland; actual tumor development or other organ damage is not assumed.
Congenital sensory neuropathy impairs pain perception; injuries and their complications are secondary consequences rather than direct involvement of other organs.
Neurodevelopmental umbrella defined by intellectual and language impairment; cardiac and other abnormalities are subtype dependent.
Inherited platelet activation and aggregation defect causing bleeding; no common additional organ damage is established.
