GJB2 disorders predominantly cause hearing loss; skin and corneal disease occur in minority syndromic subtypes.
Inherited platelet adhesion defect with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate skin or oral-organ disease.
Inherited platelet adhesion defect with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate skin or gastrointestinal disease.
Inherited platelet adhesion defect with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; bleeding sites do not establish additional organ disease.

Mitochondrial translation/oxidative-phosphorylation disorder. Leukoencephalopathy and infantile cardiomyopathy define different presentations; their frequencies across this umbrella are unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: none: leukoencephalopathy defines one presentation; its frequency across the entire AARS2-related umbrella is not established at >=30%.

basis: Ectodermal dysplasia affects sweat glands, skin and hair, with characteristic tooth agenesis; hoarseness alone does not establish airway damage.
Defined spectrum of cerebellar ataxia, developmental delay and epileptic encephalopathy.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with cerebellar hypoplasia.
Defined neuronal channel disorder causing neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy or episodic ataxia.
Permanent neonatal diabetes and accompanying liver dysfunction define this syndrome. Explicit hepatic loss of function supports primary hepatic despite its transient course.

decisions.hepatic: primary: liver dysfunction is explicitly named and described in the definition; it represents organ dysfunction, rather than a nonspecific transient sign.

basis: Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment and movement disorders. The enzyme's role in purine synthesis alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Molecular subtype of an atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor arising in the central nervous system.
MYC-activated subtype of atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Molecular subtype of a central nervous system atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor; melanosomal gene expression does not imply skin involvement.
Primary intracranial CNS mesenchymal tumor; rare metastases do not support additional axes.
The supplied definition and parent identify a pineal-body neoplasm: a brain tumor involving an endocrine gland.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the definition explicitly identifies a pineal-body neoplasm; the pineal gland is an endocrine gland, irrespective of hormonal secretion by the tumor.

basis: Primary intraventricular central nervous system tumour.
Ovarian epithelial carcinoma originates in a reproductive organ outside the axes; ovarian origin alone does not indicate endocrine disease.
Phenylalanine metabolism disorder; sustained untreated hyperphenylalaninemia causes brain injury and intellectual disability in most patients.
PAH metabolic deficiency spans benign hyperphenylalaninemia through PKU; common neurologic injury across the entire spectrum is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: untreated PKU can injure the brain, but this umbrella includes benign mild hyperphenylalaninemia; persistent neurologic injury at >=30% across the spectrum is not established.

basis: Benign fibro-osseous neoplasm originating in bone; adjacent sinus or orbital extension is site-dependent.
Bone-forming neoplasm arising predominantly in the jaw; tooth displacement alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Bone-forming fibro-osseous neoplasm; regional extension into adjacent organs is not established as common.
Neural tumors, including schwannomas and meningiomas, are central to this predisposition; renal and other tumor sites are not universal across its subtypes.
Persistent severe neutrophil deficiency causes impaired antibacterial immunity; infection sites vary and do not establish additional organ damage.
Severe persistent neutrophil deficiency affects blood cells and constitutes quantitative innate immunodeficiency; secondary infections add no organ labels.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: severe chronic neutrophil deficiency directly impairs innate immunity; an immunodeficiency need not have autoimmune causation.

basis: Autoantibody-mediated destruction of circulating neutrophils causes severe neutropenia; serious infections are infrequent.
Across the spectrum, skeletal fibrous dysplasia predominates; endocrine hyperfunction and skin pigmentation characterize subsets rather than most patients.
Ischemic injury of the posterior optic nerve causes visual loss; optic nerve is included in the ocular axis.
Traumatic injury directly damages the optic nerve, explicitly included in the ocular axis; associated brain injury is not required.
Radiation necrosis directly damages the optic nerve and causes irreversible visual loss; optic nerve disease belongs to the ocular axis.
Compression damages the optic nerve or chiasm and causes visual loss; optic nerve disease belongs to the ocular axis.
Ophthalmic arterial obstruction directly causes ischemia of the globe and potentially permanent visual loss.
Vitreous adhesion directly distorts and damages the macula; retinal anatomy belongs to the ocular axis.
Traumatic full-thickness defect of the retinal macula; retinal injury belongs to the ocular axis.
Immune-mediated uveal inflammation defines this manifestation; the underlying arthritis is a separately diagnosed disease.
Secondary glaucoma is an eye disease; its heterogeneous causes do not establish another shared organ axis.
Pigment obstructs aqueous outflow, causing elevated intraocular pressure and glaucomatous optic nerve damage.
Secondary glaucoma directly damages the ocular optic nerve. The definition includes heterogeneous inflammatory and steroid-related pathways without a universal infectious or autoimmune cause.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation-associated glaucoma does not itself establish infection or immune-mediated disease; underlying uveitis has heterogeneous causes.

basis: Degenerated intraocular red cells obstruct aqueous outflow and cause glaucoma; this does not establish a systemic blood disorder.
Secondary glaucoma from intraocular obstruction by erythrocyte debris; local hemolysis does not establish a systemic blood disorder.
Secondary glaucoma associated with aniridia directly affects the eye and threatens optic nerve function.
Abnormal ciliary-body configuration obstructs ocular aqueous outflow and causes angle-closure glaucoma.
Exfoliation-associated glaucoma causes ocular pressure-related optic nerve damage.
Skeletal dysplasia defines the umbrella; airway, cardiac and ocular disease vary substantially among its subtypes and are not established in most patients.
Defined as a CAMK2A-related neurodevelopmental disorder; no other common organ damage established.
The umbrella predominantly comprises developmental, epileptic and movement disorders; metabolic glycosylation disease belongs to the rarer biallelic subtype.
Wormian skull bones and brachydactyly define skeletal malformations; the definition distinguishes this from the allelic syndrome with congenital heart defects.
Developmental brain malformations and intellectual disability define the tubulinopathy; skin creases characterize a subtype, without established frequency across the umbrella.
Skin-defined immune-mediated reaction to infection or vaccination; associated viral hepatitis is a separate disease, not intrinsic hepatic involvement.
Adenocarcinoma arising in salivary glands, predominantly minor glands of the palate.
Psychiatric eating disorder; nutritional consequences do not establish common direct damage to a covered organ.
Insulin-deficient diabetes from CF-associated pancreatic fibrosis; other manifestations belong to the underlying cystic fibrosis.
Defined organ-specific forms include bronchiectasis and pancreatitis; neither implies multisystem CF. The CBAVD form is reproductive and has no axis.
Defined hepatobiliary injury from CFTR dysfunction; other manifestations of cystic fibrosis are outside this liver-specific concept.
Ontology grouping class rather than a specific disease; no consistent affected organ can be assigned across its members.
Defined by hepatocellular retention of abnormal fibrinogen with variable liver injury and inherited hypofibrinogenemia, a coagulation disorder.
Skin hyperextensibility and fragility plus generalized joint hypermobility define this EDS group; bruising alone does not establish a blood disorder.
Kyphoscoliosis/joint instability define kEDS. Skin fragility/scarring and hypermetropia each occur in 30-79%; arterial events and hearing loss lack >=30% support.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: skin fragility and abnormal scarring occur in 30-79%; they are additional manifestations, whereas the defining kEDS criteria are musculoskeletal.

basis: Brainstem dysgenesis with deafness in 26/29; carotid artery hypoplasia in 3/4 assessed. Central hypoventilation and supranuclear gaze palsy reflect brainstem dysfunction.
Infection directly occupies and damages the intervertebral disc space.
Staphylococcal infection directly inflames and damages an intervertebral disc.
Escherichia coli infection of an intervertebral disc.
Pneumococcal infection of an intervertebral disc.
Salmonella infection directly involves an intervertebral disc.
Fungal infection directly inflames and damages an intervertebral disc.
Defining immunodeficiency, neutropenia/myelokathexis and persistent warts; pneumonia is a separate infection, while bronchiectasis occurs in only 5-29%.
Defined by intellectual disability, cataracts and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; skeletal deformities and femoral epiphyseal osteonecrosis occur in 2/2 reported patients.
Autoimmune hypercoagulability with defining arterial/venous thrombosis. Stroke is separately diagnosed despite HPO frequency of 30-79%; livedo alone does not establish skin damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: ischemic stroke is a separately diagnosed thrombotic complication, excluded by the separate-disease rule despite its 30-79% HPO frequency.

basis: Enteric neuropathy; hypogammaglobulinemia 80-99%; ear canal atresia 6/6 and hearing loss 3/3. Cardiac defects (80-99%) and contractures (3/6) omitted by cap.
Neurologic, endocrine and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction define disease; hepatic fibrosis in 2/2. Hearing loss (2/2) and muscle fibrosis (1/2) omitted under cap.
Noncirrhotic intrahepatic portal vascular disease; varices 7/8 are vascular. Splenomegaly 8/8 alone does not establish splenic dysfunction.
Autoimmune coagulation disorder defined by arterial/venous thrombosis; listed ocular findings lack frequencies supporting common involvement.
Absent or dysgenetic testes cause loss of gonadal endocrine function, low testosterone and absent puberty; the anomalous cardiomyopathy ancestor is unsupported.
Peripheral vestibular disorder; oscillopsia and imbalance reflect vestibular dysfunction rather than separate ocular or neurologic damage.
Inherited peripheral vestibular disorder; vestibular function belongs to the otologic axis.
Immune dysregulation with autoimmune cytopenias and lymphoproliferation; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage. Lymphoma is a later risk.
Immune lymphoproliferation with splenic involvement; renal failure 1/3; hepatosplenomegaly 2/2 with raised transaminases 1/1. Arthritis and alopecia, each 1/3, omitted by cap.
